de bzhin du byang chub sems dpa' de dag dang / 'jig rten gyi dbang po byang chub la mngon par mos pa de dag sangs rgyas kyi byin gyi rlabs rgya chen po dang / rang gi dge ba'i rtsa ba'i stobs ma nor bar shin tu bsags pa dang / thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du smon lam shin tu mngon par bsgrubs pa dang / de bzhin gshegs pa'i yon tan thams cad la shin tu zhugs pa dang / byang chub sems dpa'i lam bkod pa chen po dang ldan pa la shin tu gnas pa dang / thams cad mkhyen pa'i ye shes kyi chos nyid dang / yan lag rnam pa thams cad du shin tu rdzogs pa dang / byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po'i spyod pa'i khyad par dang / smon lam yongs su rdzogs par bya ba rnam par dag pa dang / byang chub sems dpa'i sa thams cad kyi ye shes kyi dkyil 'khor yongs su non pa dang / byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin gyis rnam par spyod pa thams cad la rnam par rtse ba dang / byang chub sems dpa'i ye shes kyi spyod yul thams cad la chags pa med par rnam par spyod pas bsam gyis mi khyab pa'i sangs rgyas kyi khyu mchog gi mthu phyung ba de dag dang / sangs rgyas kyi rnam par rol pa de dag mthong zhing khong du chud la/ nyams su myong bar gyur kyang / nyan thos chen po mchog gi zung dang / bzang po'i zung la sogs pa de dag la byang chub sems dpa'i mig med pas mthong bar ma gyur/ shes par ma gyur to/ /

In the same way, those bodhisattvas, those lords of the world who aspire to enlightenment, who had received the vast blessing of the Buddha, who had obtained the unmistaken power of their roots of merit, who had made prayers of aspiration for omniscience, who understood well all the qualities of the tathāgatas, who were well established in the vast array of the bodhisattva path, and who were highly accomplished in the Dharma of the aspects of omniscient wisdom[129]‍—they had completely excellent bodhisattva conduct, had the pure fulfillment of their prayers of aspiration, had reached the domain of wisdom of all the bodhisattva levels, enjoyed all practices through bodhisattva samādhi, and practiced without impediment the entire range of bodhisattva wisdom, so that they could see, perceive, and experience the inconceivable supremacy of the Buddha and the displays of the Buddha. However, the great śrāvakas, the supreme pair, the good pair, and so on did not see them or know of them, because they did not have the vision of the bodhisattvas.

In the same way the enlightening beings and the world rulers on the verge of enlightenment, by virtue of the tremendous power of the Buddha, by the attainment of their own roots of goodness, by their own undertaking of the vow for omniscience, by development of the qualities of all buddhas, by stabilization in the magnificent path of enlightening beings, by accomplishment of the outgrowths of the teachings of all aspects of omniscient knowledge, by fulfillment and purification of the higher aspirations of the acts of the Universally Good enlightening being, by entering the spheres of knowledge of all the stages of enlightening beings, by mastery of all the states of concentration of enlightening beings, and by unhindered contemplation of all the spheres of knowledge of enlightening beings, saw the inconceivable power and mastery of the Buddha, understood and comprehended, whereas the great disciples, the best of the best, did not see or understand, because they did not have the eye of enlightening beings.

'di lta ste/ dper na/ ri'i rgyal po kha ba can/ sman gyi 'byung gnas kyis gang ba la/ sngags dang / rig sngags dang / sman gyi tshul dang / blang ba'i rgyus shes shing / rig sngags grub pa'i skyes bu gnas pa/ sman gyi cho ga thams cad shes pa/ sman blang ba'i las byed kyang / ri bo'i dbang po de nyid la gnas pa'i phyugs dang / ba lang dang / ra lug 'tsho ba dang / rngon pa dang / de ma yin pa'i mi sman gyi tshul mi shes pa gzhan dag gis sman de dag gi cho ga dang / sman gyi ro dang / mthu dang / yon tan dang / byin dang / thabs dang / 'phrod pa mi shes so/ / de bzhin du byang chub sems dpa' de bzhin gshegs pa'i ye shes kyi yul la zhugs pa/ byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par 'phrul ba'i yul gyis byung ba/ de dag gis de bzhin gshegs pa'i ting nge 'dzin gyi rnam par 'phrul ba'i yul de dag mthong yang / nyan thos chen po mchog gi zung dang / bzang po'i zung la sogs pa rang gi dgos pas tshim par gyur pa/ gzhan gyi dgos pa yal bar gzhog pa/ btang snyoms can de dag dze ta'i tshal de nyid na gnas kyang / tshe 'di la bde bar spyod pas bde zhing dga' bar gnas pa las/ phar de bzhin gshegs pa'i ting nge 'dzin gyi rnam par 'phrul pa'i yul de dag khong du mi chud do/ /

By analogy, the Himalaya, the king of mountains, is filled with places that are the sources of herbs. Those individuals who have acquired the knowledge of mantras, medicine, and herbs and are accomplished in that science,[130] and who are learned in the usage of all herbs, carry out there the task of collecting those herbs. Others who dwell on that king of mountains and who are herders of animals, cattle, goats, and sheep; those who are hunters; and other people who do not know the science of herbs do not know the taste, power, effects, locations, usages, and application of herbs. In the same way, the bodhisattvas who perceive[131] the range of activity of the Tathāgata, who have perfected[132] the range of bodhisattva miracles, can see[133] the range of miracles of the Tathāgata’s samādhi. The great śrāvakas, the supreme pair, the good pair, and others who were content concerning what had to be done for themselves, who were indifferent concerning what had to be done for others, who were uncaring‍—although they were present in Jetavana, they did not perceive the range of miracles of the Tathāgata’s samādhi.

On the snowy king of mountains are many medicinal herbs, which someone who is expert in secret lore and medicine, knowing all the principles of herbal medicine, may go and pick, while herders and hunters on the same mountain, ignorant of herbal medicine, do not know the essence, energy, results, efficacy, or method of application of the herbs. In the same way, those enlightening beings who had entered the sphere of knowledge of buddhas and produced the transformed perceptions of enlightening beings were aware of the transfigured perceptions of the concentration of Buddha, while the great disciples, even though they were there in the same Jeta grove, being satisfied with their own task and having no desire to work for others, being indifferent, dwelt in the feeling of bliss because they were in a condition of bliss in their present state and so were not aware of the perceptions of the concentration and miraculous transfiguration of Buddha.

'di lta ste/ dper na/ sa chen po rin po che thams cad kyi 'byung gnas phun sum tshogs pa/ gter brgya stong du mas gang ba/ rin po che sna tshogs rnam pa tha dad pas yongs su gang ba 'di la'ang rin po che'i 'byung gnas dang / gter gyi rgyus la mkhas shing byang ba'i mi/ rin po che brtag pa'i gtsug lag gi blo shin tu byang ba/ gter gyi gtsug lag dang / rgyus dang / dan rtags gya nom par lobs pa/ bsod nams rgya chen po'i stobs kyis bstan pa dag /de las rin po che ci 'dong bar blangs shing bdag kyang yongs su tshim par byed/ pha dang ma la yang legs par rim gro byed/ bu pho smos kyang legs par gso bar byed cing / de ma yin pa'i sems can rga ba dang / na ba dang / dbul ba dang / nyam nyes pa dang / kha zas dang / gos kyis mi 'byor pa rnams la btud cing khyad par bgo bsha' byed pa/ nor gyi dga' ba sna tshogs nyams su myong bar byed kyang sems can rin po che'i 'byung gnas dang / gter gyi rgyus mi shes pa/ bsod nams ma byas pa/ rin po che la shes pa'i mig yongs su ma dag pa/ de dag de nyid na 'khod kyang rin po che'i 'byung gnas de dag dang; rin po che'i gter de dag khong du mi chud mi shes pas/ rin po che yang blang du med do/ / rin po che'i don kyang byar med do/ /

For example, this great earth is the perfect source of all jewels. It is filled with many hundreds of thousands of treasures. It is completely filled with different kinds of various jewels. A man who is skilled in the knowledge of the sources[134] of jewels and treasure, is educated in the science of examining jewels, has knowledge of the science of treasures, is well trained in the craft of jewelry,[135] and is supported by the power of vast merit will obtain whatever jewels he desires, and he will completely satisfy himself, support his father and mother, care for his sons and daughters, and also distribute his wealth among other beings who are old, sick, poor, suffering misfortune, or in need of food and clothes, bringing others various kinds of happiness from wealth. However, those beings who have no knowledge of treasures or the source of jewels and who have not created merit do not have the pure vision of the knowledge of jewels. Even though they are at the very location, they do not perceive that there is precious treasure and a source of jewels, and without that knowledge they do not obtain jewels, nor do they make use of the jewels.

This earth is abundantly endowed with mines of jewels of all kinds, with hundreds of thousands of deposits, filled with endless supplies of various jewels. Someone who has acquired knowledge of precious substances, sees where the deposits are, has thoroughly studied the appropriate science and technology, and is supported by immense virtue and strength, then can take jewels and enjoy himself as he wishes, properly honor his parents, support his wife and children, and also distribute them evenly to the old, the poor, the destitute, the unfortunate, those without food and clothing. On the other hand, those who do not know about the deposits of jewels, who have not done good works, and have not clarified the eye of knowledge of the precious, do not discover the jewel mines in spite of the fact that they are walking on them—they do not take the jewels and do not do what can be done with jewels.

de bzhin du byang chub sems dpa' de bzhin gshegs pa'i yul bsam gyis mi khyab pa la ye shes kyi mig shin tu rnam par dag pa/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i ye shes kyi yul bsam gyis mi khyab pa la zhugs pa de dag dze ta'i tshal na 'khod cing; sangs rgyas kyi rnam par 'phrul pa de dag mthong la/ chos kyi tshul rgya mtsho la 'jug cing / ting nge 'dzin gyi phyag rgya yongs su sgrub ste/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i mchod pa dang / rim gro la brtson zhing / dam pa'i chos yongs su gzung ba la mngon par brtson te/ bsdu ba'i dngos po bzhis sems can de dag yongs su sdud kyang / nyan thos chen po de dag gis de bzhin gshegs pa'i rnam par 'phrul pa de dag dang / byang chub sems dpa'i tshogs chen po kun nas 'dus pa de lta bu yang ma mthong / ma shes so/ /

In the same way, the bodhisattvas had the pure vision of wisdom concerning the inconceivable range of the Tathāgata, and they perceived the inconceivable range of the wisdom of the Tathāgata. They were present in Jetavana and saw the miracles of the Buddha, perceived an ocean of the ways of the Dharma, had applied the seal of samādhi, were engaged in making offerings to the Tathāgata, were dedicated to possessing the Dharma, and gathered beings through the four methods of gathering pupils. The great śrāvakas did not see those miracles of the Tathāgata or that gathering of the great assembly of bodhisattvas.

Similarly, the enlightening beings in the Jeta grove who had clarified the eye of knowledge of the inconceivable sphere of Buddha and who had entered the sphere of the inconceivable knowledge of Buddha saw the miraculous transfigurations of Buddha, entered the oceans of principles of the Buddha teachings, attained oceans of concentrations, engaged in the service of the buddhas, took to embracing all truths, took all beings into their care with the four means of integration. The great disciples, however, did not see or notice the transfigurations of the Buddha or the great assembly of the enlightening beings.

'di lta ste/ dper na/ skyes bu la la zhig mig gnyis gos kyi bkab ste/ rin po che'i gling du phyin par gyur na/ des rin po che'i gling der phan tshun 'gro ba dang / 'greng ba dang / 'dug pa dang / nyal ba byas kyang rin po che'i 'byung gnas mi mthong ngo/ / rin po che'i shing dang / gos kyi rin po che dang / spos kyi rin po che dang / rin po che thams cad kyang mi mthong la/ rin po che de dag gi spyod yul lam/ rin thang ngam/ yongs su spyad pa'i rgyus kyang mi shes pas/ de ni rin po che de dag len kyang mi len la/ rin po che'i don kyang nyams su myong bar mi byed do/ / gang gi mig la bsgribs pa med pa de dag gis ni de dag thams cad mthong zhing shes so/ /

By analogy, a man who is blindfolded arrives at an island of jewels. He walks around that island of jewels, stands on it, sits on it, and lies down on it, but he does not see that source of jewels. He does not see the trees of jewels, the clothing of jewels, the incense of jewels, or all the jewels. He does not know the scope, the value, or the use of those jewels. He does not acquire the jewels. He does not understand what could be done with the jewels. Those who are not blindfolded see and know all those jewels.

It was, again, as if a man came to a land of jewels with his eyes blindfolded by a rag: he might walk around, stand, sit, and lie there, but he would not see the masses of jewels, he would not see the jewel trees, jewel clothes, jewel fragrances, or any of the other jewels. Furthermore, he would not know the use, value, or enjoyment of those jewels. He would not take the jewels and would not know what to do with the jewels. Someone whose eyes were uncovered, however, would see and distinguish them all.

de bzhin du byang chub sems dpa' chos rin po che'i gling chen por phyin pa de dag gis/ bla na med pa'i de bzhin gshegs pa'i rin po che/ 'jig rten thams cad kyi rgyan du gyur pa mngon du gyur te/ dze ta'i tshal na bzhugs shing / sangs rgyas kyi rnam par 'phrul pa bsam gyis mi khyab pa yongs su ston pa mthong yang / nyan thos chen po de dag de bzhin gshegs pa'i zhabs kyi drung de nyid na gnas shing spyod kyang / de bzhin gshegs pa'i ting nge 'dzin gyi yul rnam par 'phrul ba'i cho 'phrul de dag ma mthong ngo/ / byang chub sems dpa'i tshogs mang po de lta bu'i rin po che'i 'byung gnas chen po yang mthong par ma gyur to/ /

In the same way, the bodhisattvas had reached the island of the jewels of the Dharma and saw before them the supreme jewel of the Tathāgata, the adornment of the entire world, present in Jetavana and demonstrating the inconceivable miracles of a buddha. The great śrāvakas were present, staying at the feet of the Tathāgata, but did not see manifested miracles from the range of the Tathāgata’s samādhi. They did not see the great assembly of the bodhisattvas who were like a source of jewels.

In the same way, those enlightening beings, having come to the land of jewels of truth, where the unsurpassed jewel of the enlightened, adornment of all worlds, was right before them, standing in the Jeta grove, saw the Buddha displaying inconceivable miraculous transfigurations. The great disciples, however, were standing at the Buddha’s feet and gazing at the Buddha, but they did not see the miraculous occurrence emanating from the sphere of the Buddha’s concentration, and did not see the great treasury of jewels which was the great assembly of enlightening beings.

de ci'i phyir zhe na/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i ting nge 'dzin gyi khyu mchog gi mthu phyung ba dang / cho 'phrul bsam gyis mi khyab pa de dag bltar thams cad mkhyen pa nyid dang mi mthun pa'i phyogs kyi ma rig pa'i gos kyis ye shes kyi mig bkab pa de dag la/ byang chub sems dpa'i ye shes kyi mig yongs su dag pa de lta bu med do/ / de dag gis chos kyi dbyings gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa la 'jug pa de lta bu khong du ma chud do/ /

Why was that? Because their eyes of wisdom were blindfolded by the ignorance that is contrary to omniscience. They did not have the purified eyes of wisdom of the bodhisattvas, and they had not realized the comprehension of the lineage of the Dharma’s domain, through which one could see the inconceivable manifestation of miracles from the supremacy of the Tathāgata’s samādhi.[136]

Why? They were inimical to omniscience, their eyes covered with the rag of ignorance, and they had not clarified the eye of unobstructed knowledge of enlightening beings, and they did not realize that all things interpenetrate, which is how they could have seen the miracle produced by the inconceivable power of the Buddha’s concentration.

'di lta ste/ dper na/ mig yongs su dag pa rdul dang bral bas rab tu snang ba dang ldan pa zhes bya ba/ rab rib dang / mun pa thams cad dang mi 'grogs pa yod de/ de mi la la zhig gis thob par gyur na/ de rdul dang bral bas rab tu snang ba dang ldan pa'i mig yongs su dag pa dang ldan pas mtshan mo mun pa'i mun nag shin tu gnag par gyur pa'i nang na/ sems can bye ba khrag khrig brgya stong kun nas 'dus pa dang / cho ga dang / spyod lam rnam par sna tshogs dang ldan zhing / mun pa'i rab rib kyis mig yongs su 'khrugs par gyur pa'i mi'i khrod na 'dug cing / rnam par rgyu la phan tshun 'gro ba dang / 'greng ba dang / spyod lam rnam pa sna tshogs kyis spyod kyang; mi de dag gis skyes bu spyod lam sna tshogs kyis spyod pa de mi mthong / mi shes so/ / skyes bu des ni 'gro ba'i tshogs chen po/ spyod lam dang cho ga sna tshogs kyis rnam par spyod pa; phyogs tha dad du mngon par bltas pa/ dbyibs kyi rnam pa tha dad pa/ kha dog gi rnam pa tha dad pa/ dmigs pa'i tshul tha dad pa thams cad kyang mi mthong ba med do/ / de bzhin du de bzhin gshegs pa byang chub sems dpa'i tshogs kyi 'khor mnga' ba/ rnam par dag cing chags pa mi mnga' ba'i spyan dang ldan pas/ 'jig rten thams cad mkhyen cing gzigs te/ sangs rgyas kyi ting nge 'dzin gyi rnam par 'phrul pa dang / cho 'phrul chen po bstan pa mdzad kyang / nyan thos chen po de dag gis de bzhin gshegs pa'i ye shes dang / ting nge 'dzin gyis rnam par sprul pa'i cho 'phrul chen po de dag mthong bar ma gyur to/ / byang chub sems dpa' chen po'i tshogs chen po de lta bu yang mthong bar ma gyur te/

By analogy, there is the completely purified sight called stainless brilliance, which does not experience any darkness. If a man who has obtained that purified sight named stainless brilliance were to go in the completely black darkness of a dark night among a gathering of a quintillion people who have various[137] practices and conduct and whose sight is overwhelmed by darkness, he would move, stand, sit down,[138] and act among them in various ways, but those people will not see or know of that man’s various kinds of activity. However, when that man looks in the different directions at the various practices and conduct that the great gathering of beings is performing, he sees their various shapes, their various colors, with none of those various sights unseen. In the same way, the Tathāgata, who has an entourage of an assembly of bodhisattvas, possesses the sight that is pure and unimpeded so that he sees and knows the entire world. He demonstrates the manifestation of the great miracles of a buddha’s samādhi, but the great śrāvakas do not see those great miracles manifested by the samādhi and wisdom of the Tathāgata. Nor do they see that great assembly of the great bodhisattvas.

Again, it is as if there is an eye-purifier called “possessed of undefiled brilliance,” which is incompatible with any darkness or obscurity: suppose someone obtained it and with that eye-clarifier “possessed of undefiled brilliance” went in the dark of night among a huge crowd of people in various postures unable to see in the darkness, and walked around, stood there, sat down, and so on—those people would not see this person or distinguish what he was doing. On the other hand, this person would see the crowd of people, their various postures, positions, locations, appearances, and dress. In the same way, the Buddha, together with his company of enlightening beings, having the pure unobstructed eye of knowledge, discerns and sees all beings. Buddha shows the miracle emanated from the great concentration of Buddha, but the great disciples did not see the miracle emanated from the concentration of great knowledge of Buddha, or the great company of the assembly of enlightening beings.

'di lta ste/ dper na/ dge slong la la zhig skye bo mang po'i tshogs kyi dbus su sas khyab pa'i ting nge 'dzin la snyoms par zhugs sam/ chus khyab pa'am/ mes khyab pa'am/ rlung gis khyab pa'am/ sngon pos khyab pa'am/ ser pos khyab pa'am/ dmar pos khyab pa'am/ dkar pos khyab pa'am/ lhas khyab pa'am/ sems can sna tshogs kyi lus kyis khyab pa'am/ sgra dang dbyangs kun gyis khyab pa'am; dmigs pa thams cad kyis khyab pa'i ting nge 'dzin la snyoms par zhugs na/ 'gro ba mang po'i tshogs de dag gis chu'i phung po de mi mthong ngo/ / me'i snang ba de yang mi mthong ngo/ / sems can sna tshogs kyi lus kyis khyab pa dang / dmigs pa thams cad kyis khyab pa'i bar du yang mi mthong ste/ ting nge 'dzin de la snyoms par zhugs shing / rnam par spyod pa rnams ni ma gtogs so/ / de bzhin du de bzhin gshegs pas sangs rgyas kyi ting nge 'dzin gyis yul gyi rnam par sprul pa bsam gyis mi khyab pa de dag yongs su bstan pa mdzad na/ nyan thos chen po de dag gis mthong zhing shes par ma gyur te/ byang chub sems dpa' de bzhin gshegs pa'i lam la zhugs pa de dag gis ni/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i yul de dag mthong ngo/ / khong du chud do/ /

By analogy, it is like when a bhikṣu in the center of an assembly of many beings rests in the samādhi of the pervasion of earth or rests in the samādhi pervaded by water or the samādhi pervaded by fire, pervaded by air, pervaded by blue, pervaded by yellow, pervaded by red, pervaded by white, pervaded by devas, pervaded by the bodies[139] of various beings, pervaded by all sounds and voices, or pervaded by all perceptions. That assembly of many beings does not see a mass of water, does not see the light of fire, does not see the pervasion by the bodies of various beings, and so on up to not seeing the pervasion by all perceptions. It only sees him practicing and resting in the samādhis. In the same way, when the Tathāgata manifests inconceivable miracles that are the range of a buddha’s samādhi, the great śrāvakas do not see or know them. The bodhisattvas who are following the path of the tathāgatas see and comprehend that range of activity of the tathāgatas.

Also, it is as if a monk in the midst of a large group of people attained the concentration of total absorption in earth or water or fire or wind, or total absorption in blue, yellow, red, or white, or total absorption in heaven, or in the bodies of various beings, or in all sounds, or in all objects, that group of people would not see the body of water, would not see the realm of fire, would not see the various bodies or totality of objects in which the monk’s mind was absorbed, except for those who had themselves attained those states of concentration. In the same way, the great disciples did not see the Buddha’s revelation of the inconceivable wonder of the sphere of the concentration of Buddha, while the enlightening beings who had attained the path of the Buddha entered into the sphere of the Buddha.

'di lta ste/ dper na/ sku ba grub pa'i mi ni mig gnyis bskus ma thag tu/ skye bo mang po thams cad kyis lus mi mthong ngo/ / des ni 'gro 'am; 'dug gam/ 'greng yang rung ste/ skye bo mang po thams cad mthong ngo/ / de bzhin du de bzhin gshegs pa 'jig rten las 'das pa/ 'gro ba thams cad kyi yul las yongs su 'das pa/ thams cad mkhyen pa'i ye shes kyi yul du zhugs pa/ byang chub sems dpa'i ye shes kyi mig gis shes par bya ba des 'gro ba thams cad gzigs kyang / nyan thos chen po de dag gis de bzhin gshegs pa'i rnam par 'phrul pa de dag ma mthong ngo/ /

For example, as soon as a man who creates ointments smears it on his two eyes, an entire multitude of beings cannot see his body, but he can see the bodies of the entire multitude of beings. Whether he is walking, sitting, or standing, he sees the entire multitude of beings. In that same way, the Tathāgata has transcended the world, has passed beyond the range of perception of all beings, and has attained the range of omniscient wisdom but can be perceived by the vision of the wisdom of the bodhisattvas. He can see all beings, but the great śrāvakas do not see the miracle of the Tathāgata.

Again, it is as if there were an ointment, which simply by being applied to one’s eyes makes one invisible to others while one is able to see others. In the same way Buddha, beyond the world, beyond the spheres of all beings, having entered the sphere of omniscience, can be discerned by the eye of knowledge of enlightening beings, and sees all beings in the world, but the great disciples could not see those miracles of the Buddha.

'di lta ste/ dper na/ mi'i tsher 'grogs pa'i lha rtag tu rjes su 'brang ba ni des mi de mthong yang / mis lha de mi mthong ngo/ / de bzhin du de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad mkhyen pa'i ye shes kyi yul la zhugs pa/ byang chub sems dpa'i tshogs kun nas 'dus pa chen po'i dbus su; sangs rgyas kyi rnam par 'phrul pa chen po yongs su bstan pa mdzad kyang / nyan thos chen po de dag gis de bzhin gshegs pa'i rnam par 'phrul pa dang / cho 'phrul chen po dang / byang chub sems dpa'i 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor gyi rnam par 'phrul pa de dag kyang ma mthong / ma shes so/ /

For example, a deity who accompanies a human for his entire life is always following him. The deity sees the human, but the human does not see the deity. In the same way, the Tathāgata has attained the range of perception of the wisdom of omniscience, and he manifests miracles in the middle of the great gathering of the assembly of bodhisattvas, but the great śrāvakas do not see and do not know of the Tathāgata’s great manifestation of miracles or the miracle of the assembled circle of bodhisattvas.

It is also like the case of the celestial spirit born together with a person and always associated with the person—the spirit sees the person, but the person does not see the spirit. In the same way, the Buddha, in the sphere of omniscience, manifested great miraculous transfigurations of Buddha in the midst of the great assembly of enlightening beings, but the great disciples did not see, did not notice, the miracle of the transfiguration of the Buddha or the magical manifestation of the circle of enlightening beings.

'di lta ste/ dper na/ dge slong sems thams cad la dbang gi dam pa'i pha rol tu phyin pa'i mchog thob pa/ 'du shes dang / tshor ba 'gog pa la snyoms par zhugs pa ni/ shes pa med la tshor ba med pas dbang po drug gis kyang bya ba gang yang nyams su mi myong ste/ mya ngan las 'das pa yang ma yin la/ 'jig rten gyi rnam par spyod pa thams cad gnas de na yod kyang / snyoms par zhugs pa de nyid kyi byin gyi rlabs dang mthus des mi shes/ mi mthong ngo/ / de bzhin du nyan thos chen po de dag dze ta'i tshal de na yang rnam par spyod la/ de dag la dbang po drug kyang yod de/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i ting nge 'dzin dang / rnam par 'phrul pa dang / khyu mchog gi mthu phyung ba dang / cho 'phrul de dag mthong bar ma gyur/ khong du chud par ma gyur/ shes par ma gyur to/ / byang chub sems dpa'i cho 'phrul chen po de dag dang / byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par 'phrul pa de dag kyang khong du ma chud/ ma mthong / ma shes so/ /

Consider, for example, a bhikṣu who has reached the perfection of power over his entire mind[140] and rests in a meditation in which all perception and sensation has ceased. Through his being without perception[141] or sensation, his six senses do not experience anything. He has not attained nirvāṇa, and worldly events are continuing and present, but through the power and might of being in that meditation, he does not perceive them and does not see them. In the same way, the great śrāvakas were present in Jetavana, and they had all the six sensory faculties, but they did not see, did not perceive, and did not know of the manifestation of miracles and supremacy from the samādhi of the Tathāgata.

Again, it is like the case of a monk who has attained perfect control of mind and has reached extinction of perception and sensation: he neither perceives nor cognizes and does nothing with his six sense organs, but still is not totally extinct. All the ordinary events of the world are going on there where he is, but he does not perceive or cognize them, because of the overmastery of the power of his concentration. In the same way, the great disciples were in the Jeta grove and had the six sense faculties, but they did not see, penetrate, perceive, or discern the miracle of the power emanated from the concentration of the Buddha, nor did they gain access to, see, or cognize the great gathering of the enlightening beings, the miracle of the enlightening beings, the transfiguration of the enlightening beings.

de ci'i phyir zhe na/ sangs rgyas kyi yul ni zab cing yangs la tshad med de/ blta bar dka' zhing rtogs par dka' ste/ khong du chud par dka' la 'jig rten thams cad las yongs su 'das pa'o/ / sangs rgyas kyi yul ni bsam gyis mi khyab pa ste/ nyan thos dang / rang sangs rgyas thams cad kyis mi 'dus pa'o/ / de bas na nyan thos chen po de dag dze ta'i tshal de nyid na 'khod cing / bcom ldan 'das kyis zhabs kyi drung na spyod kyang / sangs rgyas kyi rnam par 'phrul pa de dag dang / byang chub sems dpa'i tshogs chen po de dag kyang ma mthong ngo/ / dze ta'i tshal 'jig rten gyi khams grangs med pa/ bsam gyis mi khyab pa rnam par dag pa'i yon tan dang / bkod pa yongs su 'dus pa de yang ma mthong ma shes te/ de ni snod du ma gyur pa'i phyir ro/ /

Why is that? The range of activity of the Buddha is profound, vast, immeasurable, difficult to see, and difficult to understand. The Buddha’s range of activity is inconceivable and is inaccessible to the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas. Therefore, the great śrāvakas were assembled in Jetavana and were present at the feet of the Bhagavat, but they did not see the Buddha’s miracles or the great gathering of bodhisattvas. They also did not see or perceive the accumulation in Jetavana of the qualities and adornments of countless, innumerable pure world realms, because they were not worthy of it.

Why? The sphere of Buddha is indeed profound, vast, immeasurable, difficult to see, difficult to realize, difficult to plunge into, completely beyond all worldlings: for all disciples and individual illuminates, the sphere of Buddha is unthinkable and ungraspable. Therefore, the great disciples, even though they were there in the Jeta grove at the feet of the Buddha, did not see the transfigurations of the Buddha, and they did not see or apprehend the great gathering of enlightening beings or their concentration of the arrays of qualities of enlightening beings or their concentration of the arrays of qualities of inconceivable, innumerable purified worlds in the Jeta grove, because they did not have the capacity to do so.
de nas byang chub sems dpa' rnam par snang mdzad kyi smon lam gyi gtsug gi 'od zer rab tu snang bas sangs rgyas kyi byin gyi rlabs kyis de'i tshe tshigs su bcad pa 'di dag smras so/ /
At that time, the bodhisattva Vairocanapraṇidhānanābhiraśmiprabha recited these verses:
At that time the enlightening being Light from the Origin of the Vows of the Illumination, by the power of Buddha, looked over the ten directions and then spoke these verses:
ltos shig sems can dam pa yi; ; sangs rgyas byang chub bsam mi khyab/ / rgyal bas sangs rgyas rnam 'phrul pa/ / dze ta'i rgyal mtshan 'di bstan to/ /
“See the inconceivable enlightenment, The buddhahood of the supreme being! The Jina has manifested the miracles Of a buddha in this Jetadhvaja. {1}
See how inconceivable is the enlightenment of Buddha, the best of beings: In the Jeta grove he shows the Victor’s transfiguration of the enlightened.
rang byung rnams kyi byin gyi rlabs/ / bgrang du med par 'byung ba la/ / sangs rgyas chos tshul mi shes pa'i/ / 'jig rten kun kyang mgo rmongs so/ /
“There appears the self-arising, Incalculable power of transformation That the world, not knowing the way Of the Dharma, is ignorant of. {2}
He exercises incalculable independent power, Whereat the world is confused, not knowing Buddha’s qualities.
chos kyi rgyal po'i cho 'phrul dag / tshad med bsam gyis mi khyab cing / / shin tu zab pa 'byung ba ni/ / de la 'jig rten 'babs mi nus/ /
“There are the profound, Immeasurable, inconceivable Miracles of the Dharma kings That the world does not fathom. {3}
Profound is the miracle worked by the Spiritual Sovereign, Infinite, inconceivable, beyond the range of the world.
rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas kha dog mdog / mtshan gyis shin tu rnam par klubs/ / yang dag sangs rgyas bskyed pa yi/ / chos rab de dag mtshan nyid med/ /
“The buddhas have infinite splendor[142] And are adorned by characteristics. The Dharmas that the buddhas produce Are without characteristics. {4}
The buddhas are adorned with infinite attributes, But the truths revealed by the buddhas are signless.
rnam 'phrul mtha' dang dbus med pa/ / tshig gi lam gyis brjod dka' ba'i/ / rnam 'phrul shin tu zab pa dag / rgyal bas dze ta'i tshal du bstan/ /
“In the grove that is named Jeta The Jina demonstrates miracles That are without center or edge And difficult to describe in words. {5}
The Victor shows transfigurations in the Jeta grove, Boundlessly deep, most hard to put into words.
rgyal sras bdag nyid che ba'i rnams/ / zhing rnams bsam yas bye ba nas/ / rgyal ba'i zhal ltar mos dga' ste/ / kun nas 'dus pa'i tshogs la ltos/ /
“See the assembly of great beings, Of bodhisattvas, who have assembled From countless millions of realms Wishing to look upon the Jina.[143] {6}
The enlightening beings do not look at the assembly of saints, Having come from innumerable lands to see the Buddha.
smon lam yongs su phun sum tshogs/ / spyod lam spyod pa chags med pa/ / de dag bsam pa shes par ni/ / 'jig rten kun gyis mi nus so/ /
“The entire world is unable To know or think of that Fulfillment of prayers And that unimpeded conduct. {7}
They have attained the sphere of unobstructed, unattached action By their determination; no one in the world can know their will.
de dag sems dang spyod yul dang / / spyod pa dag kyang nyan thos dang / / rang rgyal thams cad yongs kyis kyang / / rnam pa kun tu shes mi nus/ /
“The pratyekabuddhas And the śrāvakas do not know Anything about their conduct Or the range of[144] their minds. {8}
All those enlightened on their own and the disciples all around Do not know their doings or their state of mind.
rgyal sras shes rab chen po'i rnams/ / gzhan gyis thub dka' pham bya la/ / dpa' ba'i rgyal mtshan ma 'dres shing / / ye shes sa la gzhol gyur pa/ /
“Those with great wisdom, the bodhisattvas, Are invincible and undefeatable,[145] Banners of heroism, unadulterated, And they have reached the level of wisdom. {9}
The enlightening beings, great in wisdom, are invulnerable, invincible, Paragons of heroism, undefiled, certain of the stage of knowledge;
ting 'dzin dpag tu tshad med la/ / grags chen mnyam par bzhag pa rnams; / chos dbyings thams cad rgyas bkang zhing / / rnam par 'phrul pa kun kyang ston/ /
“They have great renown And have attained immeasurable samādhis. They demonstrate miracles that pervade The entire domain of phenomena.” {10}
Beyond measure, of great fame, they have attained concentration And display a miracle extending throughout the cosmos.
de nas byang chub sems dpa' thub par dka' ba'i brtson 'grus kyi shugs kyi rgyal pos sangs rgyas kyi byin gyi rlabs kyis/ phyogs bcur rnam par bltas nas de'i tshe tshigs su bcad pa 'di dag smras so/ /
Then the bodhisattva Duryodhanavīryavegarāja, through the blessing of the Buddha, looked into the ten directions and recited these verses:
Then the enlightening being King of Invincible Energy, by the power of Buddha, looked over the ten directions and spoke these verses:
bsod nams snying po shes rab che/ / byang chub spyod pa'i tshul rtogs shing / / 'jig rten kun la bde byed pa'i/ / bde gshegs sku las skyes pa ltos/ /
“See those who are born from the sugatas, They who bring happiness to the world, Who have the essence of merit, great wisdom, And who have realized the conduct of a bodhisattva. {11}
Full of virtue and great knowledge, gone to the goal of enlightening practice, Givers of security to all worlds—behold these, the offspring of Buddha,
yid gzhungs blo gros mtha' yas shing / / shin tu mnyam gzhag sems ldan pa; ; mtha' dang dbus med zab pa yi/ / ye shes rgya chen spyod yul can/ /
“They are learned, with infinite knowledge. Their minds are in a perfect state of meditation. They have the range of a vast wisdom That is profound and without center or limit. {12}
Intelligent, with boundless wisdom and well-concentrated minds, In the realm of boundlessly deep and broad knowledge.
rgyan rab mang pos mdzes byas pa'i/ / dze ta'i nags tshal rgya che ba/ / byang chub sems dpa' kun rgyas shing / / bde gshegs bzhugs pa'i gnas gyur par/ /
“See the numerous oceans Of they who have no dwelling, no basis, Who are assembled from the ten directions And seated upon lotus seats {13}[146]
The great grove called Jeta, where the perfect Buddha sojourns, Is adorned with magnificent arrays and filled with enlightening beings.
gnas med mi gnas gyur pa rnams/ / phyogs rnams bcu nas kun 'dus te/ / pad+mo'i stan la 'khod pa dag / rgya mtsho mang la lta ba gyis/ /
“In the great forest named Jeta That is beautified by many adornments, That is completely filled with bodhisattvas And is the hermitage of the Sugata. {14}
See the Great Oceans, nonreliant, independent, Sitting on lotus thrones, having come from the ten directions:
gnas med len pa med pa rnams/ / spros pa med cing mi rten la/ / rdul bral chags pa'i sems med pa/ / chos kyi dbyings la gzhol ba dang / /
“They are without basis, without acquisition, Without elaboration, without foundation, With unimpeded minds, stainless, Focused on the essence of phenomena. {15}
Not resting on anything, not grasping, free from falsehood, without abode, With unattached minds, dispassionate, set on the reality realm.
ye shes rgyal mtshan rab dpa' ba/ / rdo rje'i sems ni mi g.yo zhing / / grub pa med pa'i chos rnams la/ / mya ngan 'da' bar gang ston pa/ /
“They are banners of wisdom, Great heroes who have vajra minds. They are unshakable and teach nirvāṇa Within unceasing qualities.[147] {16}
Exemplars of knowledge, great heroes, with unshakable adamant minds, In the midst of unperishing truths, they make a show of nirvana.
phyogs bcu'i zhing mang bye ba rnams/ / grangs kyis mi chod kun nas 'dus/ / yang dag sangs rgyas drung du lhags/ / gnyis kyi 'du shes rnam par spangs/ /
“They have gathered from numerous millions Of realms beyond number in the ten directions And have arrived before the Buddha And are free from dualistic perception. {17}
They have come together from countless worlds in the ten directions, Come to the Buddha, without any notions of duality.
rang byung shAkya seng ge yi/ / rnam par 'phrul pa 'di dag mthong / / de yi byin rlabs dam pa yis/ / byang chub sems dpa' 'di dag lhags/ /
“They see these miracles Of the self-arisen Lion of the Śākyas, And it is through his blessing That these bodhisattvas have gathered. {18}
They see the miraculous transfiguration of the autonomous Buddha, By the power of which these enlightening beings have come.
sangs rgyas chos la 'byed pa med/ / chos dbyings gzhi la'ang de bzhin te/ / spyod pa tsam du yongs 'byed pa'i/ / pha rol phyin pa rgyal ba'i sras/ /

“The offspring of the jinas, they who have attained perfection, Do not distinguish between the Buddha’s Dharmas On the level of the essence of phenomena But make distinctions merely in terms of terminology. {19}
They are nondiscriminatory in regard to Buddha teachings and the plane of realities; The offspring of Buddha have thoroughly realized that distinctions are merely mundane conventions.
chos kyi dbyings la dbyer med pa'i/ / mtha' la thug pa de dag gnas/ / tshig rnams yongs su zad med pas/ / chos la dbye ba'ang rab tu byed/ /
“They are established in the ultimate conclusion Of the indivisibility of the essence of phenomena, But they make distinctions between phenomena Through producing unceasing words.” {20}
The buddhas stand in the undifferentiated ultimate limit of the reality realm, Yet show the differentiation of things by inexhaustible sayings.
de nas byang chub sems dpa' dpal kun nas 'phags pa'i gzi brjid rgyal pos sangs rgyas kyi byin gyi rlabs kyis phyogs bcur rnam par bltas te/ de'i tshe tshigs su bcad pa 'di dag smras so/ /
Then the bodhisattva Samantaśrīsamudgatatejorāja, through the blessing of the Buddha, looked into the ten directions and recited these verses:
Then the enlightening being King of Fiery Energy of Universal Splendor, by the power of Buddha, looked over the ten directions and spoke these verses:
ltos shig sems can dam pa yi/ / ye shes dkyil 'khor shin tu yangs/ / dus dang dus min mkhyen mdzad cing / / sems can rnams la chos kyang ston/ /
“See the vast circle of wisdom Of the one who is supreme among beings. He knows when it is timely and untimely And then teaches the Dharma to beings. {21}
See the immense sphere of knowledge of the best of beings; Knowing when is the right time and when not, he teaches the truth to people.
mu stegs ldan pa tshogs 'dus pa'i; ; rgol ba thams cad rab tu 'joms/ / sems can bsam pa ji bzhin du/ / rnam par 'phrul pa yongs su ston/ /
“He completely defeats all opposition From gathered assemblies of tīrthikas. He demonstrates miraculous acts According to the wishes of beings. {22}
Destroying the various arguments marshaled by heretics, He shows beings’ spiritual transfigurations according to their dispositions.
phyogs na mi bzhugs bde gshegs rnams/ / sangs rgyas yul gyi rjes mi bzhud/ / tshad med pa dang tshad yod las/ / thub pa chen po 'das pa min/ /
“The Sugata does not dwell in a direction;[148] The Buddha does not go to a realm.[149] The great Muni is always both[150] Ascertainable and unascertainable. {23}
Buddha is not finite or infinite: The great sage has transcended finitude and infinity.
nyi ma mkha' las 'gro ba ni/ / nyin bar 'grangs pa smos pa byed/ / de bzhin mkhyen pas mkhas ston pa/ / dus gsum chags pa med pas brjod/ /
“The sun moving through the sky Demarcates the number of days. Thus the Teacher, wise with knowledge, Demarcates the three times without impediment. {24}
Like the sun coursing through the sky giving light every day, So does the sagacious guide appear, independent of past, present, and future.
zla ba nye ba'i mtshan mo la/ / zla ba'i dkyil 'khor 'phags par snang / / de bzhin chos dkar yongs rdzogs pa'i/ / mgon po rnams kyang mthong ba yin/ /
“On the night of a full moon The moon’s disk is the brightest light. In that way, the Lord[151] Full of white Dharma is seen. {25}
As the sphere of the full moon shines at night, So does one see the guide, full of pure qualities.
bar snang nam mkha'i dbyings 'di las/ / nyi ma'i dkyil 'khor rgyu ba ni/ / gar yang thogs pa med par 'gro/ / sangs rgyas rnam 'phrul de bzhin no/ /
“Just as the disk of the sun Moves through the sky Without being stopped‍— Thus are the Buddha’s miracles. {26}
As the globe of the sun courses through space without stopping, Such is the transfiguration of the Buddha.
ji ltar nam mkha' phyogs rnams kyi/ / zhing rnams kun la mi gnas pa/ / de bzhin 'jig rten sgron ma yi/ / sangs rgyas rnam 'phrul shes par bya/ /
“Just as space is not dependent On the worlds in the directions, In that way, the buddha miracles Of the Lamp of the World are to be known. {27}
Just as space is independent of all land, So is the Buddha transfiguration of the Lamp of the World to be known.
ji ltar sa ni 'jig rten na/ / lus can kun gyi gnas yin pas/ / 'jig rten sgron ma'i 'jig rten na/ / chos kyi 'khor lo de ltar gnas/ /
“Just as in the world the earth Is the support for all beings, In that way, in the world the Dharma wheel Of the Lamp of the World is a support. {28}
As the earth is the support of all corporeal beings in the world, In the same way is the wheel of teaching of the Lamp of the World steadfast.
ji ltar rlung ni chags med par/ / mkha' la mgyogs par rab rgyu ba/ / de bzhin sangs rgyas chos nyid kyang / / 'jig rten khams su rab tu rgyu/ /
“Just as the wind, without impediment, Moves swiftly through the sky, In that way, the Buddha’s nature Moves through the world realms. {29}
As the wind blows swiftly through the sky, not sticking to anything, In the same way does the nature of Buddha operate in the world.
ji ltar chu yi phung po la/ / zhing rnams 'grangs pa kun gnas pa/ / de bzhin dus gsum sangs rgyas kyang / / ye shes tshogs la rab tu gnas/ /
“Just as the numbers of worlds Are based on accumulations of water, In that way, the buddhas of the three times Are based on accumulations of wisdom.” {30}
Just as all lands are founded on a mass of water, So are the buddhas of all times founded on a mass of knowledge.
de nas byang chub sems dpa' dpal gyi snying po chags pa med pa'i rgyal pos sangs rgyas kyi byin gyi rlabs kyis phyogs bcur rnam par bltas te/ de'i tshe tshigs su bcad pa 'di dag smras so/ /
Then the bodhisattva Asaṅgaśrīgarbharāja, through the blessing of the Buddha, looked into the ten directions and recited these verses:
Then the enlightening being King of Unobstructed Splendor, by the power of Buddha, looked over the ten directions and spoke these verses:
ji ltar rdo rje ri rab brag / zang yag shin tu mtho yod pa/ / de ltar 'jig rten kun skyob pa'i/ / sangs rgyas mngon par 'phags pas mtho/ /
“Just like high mountains and cliffs That are made of vajras, The Buddha, the protector of all worlds, Is the highest in the world. {31}
Like a lofty mountain made of diamond Does Buddha emerge in the world, savior of all beings.
ji ltar rgya mtsho'i chu chen dag / tshad med rnyog pa med pa ltar/ / sangs rgyas mthong ba'ang de bzhin te/ / 'jig rten kun gyi skom pa gcod/ /
“Just as the great water of the ocean Is immeasurable and unpolluted, In that way, the sight of the Buddha Dispels the thirst of the world. {32}
Like the water of the ocean, immeasurable, pure, Does the sight of Buddha stop the thirst of the world.
rgya mtsho'i chu las 'phags pa yi/ / ri bo ri rab ci 'dra bar/ / de bzhin 'jig rten sgron ma yang / / chos kyi mtsho las mngon par 'phags/ /
“Just as Mount Meru Is higher than the ocean’s water, In that way, the Lamp of the World Is higher than the ocean of phenomena. {33}
Just as the polar mountain emerges from the ocean water, So does the Light of the World emerge from the ocean of truth.
rin chen kun gyi 'byung gnas kyis/ / rgya mtsho rgyas pa ji bzhin du/ / rang byung ye shes de bzhin te/ / mi zad skad cig rab tu mkhyen/ /
“Just as the vast ocean Is the source of all jewels, The Self-Arisen One’s wisdom Is unending instantaneous knowledge. {34}
Like an ocean filled with deposits of jewels Is the Independent One’s instant awareness of endless knowledge.
mgon po'i ye shes shin tu zab/ / tshad med de bzhin bgrang du med/ / de bas sangs rgyas rnam 'phrul ba/ / bsam gyis mi khyab tshad med ston; ;
Profound is the Guide’s knowledge, incalculable, infinite, By which he shows infinite inconceivable Buddha transfigurations.
sgyu ma'i mtshan nyid ston pa yi/ / sgyu mkhan mkhas pa ci 'dra ba/ / de ltar sangs rgyas mkhyen dbang yang / / rnam par 'phrul ba rab tu ston/ /
“Just as a skilled magician Manifests the qualities of illusions, In that way, the Buddha, who has the power Of knowledge, manifests miracles. {36}
As an expert magician shows illusory forms, Buddha, master of knowledge, displays transfigurations.
yid bzhin nor bu rnam dag pa; ; bsam don rdzogs byed ji lta ba/ / de bzhin bsam pa dag pa la/ / rgyal ba smon lam rdzogs pa mdzad/ /
“Just as a pure wish-fulfilling jewel Fulfills the wishes that are made, In that way, the Jina fulfills The pure aspirations of beings. {37}
As a pure wish-fulfilling jewel grants what is desired, The Victor fulfills the aspirations of those whose intentions are pure.
'od snang gsal ba byed pa yi/ / rin chen rnam snang ji lta ba/ / de ltar thams cad mkhyen pa dag / 'gro ba'i bsam pa gsal bar mdzad/ /
“Just as a shining jewel Shines with lights, In that way, pure omniscience Illuminates the aspirations of beings. {38}
Like a luminous jewel shining, Omniscience, pure, illumines beings’ minds.
ji ltar phyogs la mngon lta ba'i/ / rin chen zur brgyad rab gnas pa/ / de bzhin chags med sgron ma yang / / chos dbyings rab tu snang ba mdzad/ /
“Just as a jewel with eight facets Remains facing all directions, In that way, the unimpeded Lamp Illuminates the realm of phenomena. {39}
Like an octagonal jewel facing all directions, The Unobstructed Lamp illumines the cosmos.
chu rin chen 'od gsal ba/ / ji ltar dri med chu byed/ / de bzhin sangs rgyas mthong bas kyang / / 'gro ba'i dbang po dag par 'gyur/ /
“Just as the bright water-purifying jewel Makes turbid water clear, In that way, the sight of the Buddha Purifies the senses of the world.” {40}
Like a water-clarifying light purifying water, Vision of Buddha purifies people’s senses.

de nas byang chub sems dpa' chos kyi dbyings su smon lam rab tu 'phrul ba'i zla ba'i rgyal pos/ /sangs rgyas kyi byin gyi rlabs kyis phyogs bcur rnam par bltas te/ de'i tshe tshigs su bcad pa 'di dag smras so/ /
Then the bodhisattva Dharmadhātupraṇidhisunirmitacandrarāja, through the blessing of the Buddha, looked into the ten directions and recited these verses:
Then the enlightening being Supreme Moon of Vows Emanated throughout the Cosmos, by the power of Buddha, looked over the ten directions and spoke these verses:
phyogs 'di in+d+ra nI la yis/ / kha dog mdog gcig byas pa ltar/ / sangs rgyas mthong bas skye dgu rnams/ / de bzhin byang chub mdog tu 'gyur/ /

“Just as looking through a sapphire[152] transforms A direction in this world into the color of the sapphire, In the same way, seeing the Buddha Transforms beings into the color[153] of enlightenment. {41}
As everywhere is made one hue by an emerald, Vision of Buddha makes beings the hue of enlightenment.
sangs rgyas rdul phran re re la/ / rnam par 'phrul ba sna tshogs rnams/ / tshad kyis gzhal du med pa ston/ / byang chub sems dpa' rnam dag mdzad/ /
“The Buddha manifests immeasurable Miracles of various kinds, Within each single atom, That purify the bodhisattvas. {42}
In each atom Buddha shows transformation of various kinds, Beyond measure, purifying the enlightening beings.
de ni rmad byung shin tu zab/ / mtha' yas bsgrub pa dga' ba ste/ / blo ldan ye shes yul de la/ / 'jig rten rnams ni 'bab mi nus/ /
“They are marvelous, profound, Infinite, difficult to accomplish, In the scope of the wisdom of the wise, And inaccessible to the world. {43}
That is extremely profound, unlimited, hard to approach, In the realm of knowledge of the wise, inaccessible to worldlings.
byang chub sems dpa' bsgrub don du/ / bkod pa phun sum tshogs pa dang / / sangs rgyas tshul gyis rnam sbyangs pa'i/ / chos kyi dbyings la 'jug pa ston/ /
“For the consummation of the bodhisattvas There is the perfected display, The purification of the Buddha’s activity That teaches entering the realm of the Dharma.[154] {44}
The full arrays of adornments purified by the works of Buddha Are perceived by enlightening beings entering the reality realm.
sangs rgyas zhing rnams bsam yas pa/ / blo ldan bskor ba'i sangs rgyas kyis/ / kun nas gang bar gyur pa yang / / rgyal ba de la ston pa mdzad/ /
“The Jina manifests In countless buddha realms That are completely filled By buddhas encircled by the wise. {45}
The inconceivable buddha-lands where the Victor appears Are filled with buddhas surrounded by the wise, everywhere.
chos kun mnga' sgyur ston pa ste/ / shAkya'i khyu mchog skyes par gyur/ / de yi cho 'phrul tshad med pa/ / 'di dag rab tu byung ba yin; ;
“The Teacher with dominion over all Dharma teachings, The supreme one of the Śākyas, has appeared. These miracles of his, which are Beyond measure, have occurred. {46}
The Teacher, master of all truths, the Hero of the Shakyas, has come forth: It is his immeasurable miracle that has appeared.
brtan pa'i spyod pa sna tshogs rnams/ / tshad med rnam par gzigs gyur nas/ / rnam par 'phrul ba mtha' yas pa/ / tshad med gzi can ston pa mdzad/ /
“You see[155] this immeasurable variety Of the activities of the constant one. He who has immeasurable splendor Manifests infinite miracles. {47}
You see the variety of the infinite deeds of the resolute: The one of infinite splendor shows endless transformations.
'jig rten mgon po rgyal sras rnams/ / chos kyi dbyings la slob pa mdzad/ / chos rnams thams cad yongs la yang / / chags med ye shes spyod yul 'gyur/ /
“The Lord of the World teaches The Jina’s children in the essence of the Dharma, And they become those who have The unimpeded range of wisdom in all Dharmas. {48}
The Leader of the World teaches the offspring of Buddha about the reality realm; And they develop the range of knowledge unattached in all things.
skyes bu dbang po'i byin rlabs kyis/ / cho 'phrul brgya dang rab ldan zhing / / 'jig rten thams cad rnam sbyong ba'i/ / chos kyi 'khor lo rab tu bskor/ /
“The lord of[156] humans through his powers Turns the wheel of the Dharma, Manifesting hundreds of miracles And purifying[157] the entire world. {49}
Buddha’s wheel of teaching turns by spiritual power, Filled with hundreds of miracles, purifying all worlds.
sems can gtso bo'i yul la yang / / ye shes dkyil 'khor yongs sbyangs shing / / shes rab chen po'i klu chen rnams/ / 'jig rten thams cad 'grel bar 'gyur/ /
“In the domain of the supreme among beings There is the purified circle of knowledge, The great nāgas with enormous wisdom, Who bring liberation[158] from the entire world.” {50}
In the realm of the Best of Beings, their sphere of knowledge purified, The Great Dragons, rich in wisdom, liberate all beings.
de nas byang chub sems dpa' chos kyi don gyi blo gros gzi brjid rgyal pos/ bcom ldan 'das kyi byin gyi rlabs kyis phyogs bcur rnam par bltas te/ de'i tshe tshigs su bcad pa 'di dag smras so/ /
Then the bodhisattva Dharmārciṣmattejorāja, through the blessing of the Buddha, looked into the ten directions and recited these verses:
Then the enlightening being King of Fiery Energy of Truth, by the power of Buddha, looked over the ten directions and spoke these verses:
drang srong dam pa'i mchog rnams kyi/ / dus gsum nyan thos gang byung ba/ / de dag kun gyis bde gshegs kyi/ / gshegs thabs 'jog 'deg mi shes so/ /
“The śrāvakas of the supreme ṛṣi Who appear[159] in the three times Are without the knowledge Of the footsteps the Sugata[160] takes. {51}
The disciples trained in past, present, and future, foremost sages, Do not even know a footstep of a perfect buddha.
dus gsum ma lus thams cad kyi/ / ma nor rang rgyal gang byung ba/ / de dag gis kyang mgon po yi/ / gshegs thabs 'jog 'deg mi rig go /
“The entirety of the pratyekabuddhas Free of error, who appear in the three times, Are also without the knowledge Of the footsteps the Protector takes. {52}
Even all individual illuminates Do not know a footstep of the Protector.
ma rig mun pas bsgribs pa rnams/ / khyi ltar ltong la brgyus pa yi/ / sems can de 'dra kun gyis ni/ / mgon po mi shes smos mi dgos/ /
“It goes without saying that all beings, Obscured by the darkness of ignorance And like dogs tied to a leash, Have no knowledge of the Guide. {53}
How much less could ordinary beings know the Guide, As they are bound in chains and wrapped in the dark of ignorance.
rgyal ba tshad mas gzhal ba min/ / de ni shes par mi nus te/ / sangs rgyas chags med ye shes can/ / tshig gi lam las shin tu 'das/ /
“The Jina cannot be known. He cannot be measured by any measure. The Buddha has unimpeded knowledge. He has transcended the path of words. {54}
Unquantifiable, the Victor cannot be known by any scales; Endowed with unobstructed knowledge, Buddha transcends the path of words.
zla ba nya rgyas 'od mnga' ba/ / brtan pa mtshan gyis rnam par bris/ / de ni bskal pa dpag yas par/ / rnam 'phrul thog med spyod pa mdzad/ /
“The constant one has the light of the full moon, And he is beautified[161] by his features. For countless kalpas he performs Unimpeded miraculous actions.[162] {55}
Radiant as the full moon, steady, adorned with a multitude of qualities, He passes infinite eons creating transformations.
tshul sgo re res sangs rgyas la/ / shin tu mnyam gzhag bsams byas kyang / / bskal pa bye ba bsam yas pa/ / brjod du med pa zad 'gyur gyi/ /
“Though one contemplates with a focused mind The Buddha in this and that way For countless millions of kalpas, He will remain indescribable. {56}
Thinking of the Buddha in every way with perfect concentration, Even after untold billions of eons Buddha would still be inconceivable.
rang byung rnams kyi yon tan las/ / phyogs gcig cha yi mthar mi phyin/ / sangs rgyas de yi zhal bltas kyang / / sangs rgyas chos ni bsam mi khyab/ /
“One will not completely understand A single aspect of the self-arisen qualities. Even when the Buddha is gazed upon, The Buddha’s Dharmas are inconceivable. {57}
One cannot understand the limit of even a single attribute of the Independent, Even while gazing on Buddha, for the qualities of Buddha are inconceivable.
gang zhig de la smon byed cing / / gang zhig yid kyis dga' mos pa/ / de dag kun kyang de 'dra ba'i/ / spyod yul blta dka' 'thob par 'gyur/ /
“All such fields of activity as those, Which are difficult to see, will appear To those who have the aspiration, To those whose minds delight in them. {58}
Those who are intent on this, and whose minds delight therein, Will attain these realms, which are so hard to see.
bsod nams ye shes mtha' yas shing / / tshogs chen yangs pas rnam gnon la/ / dri med blo ldan sems gnas pa/ / de dag 'di yi tshul la 'jug /
“Those who maintain an unstained, wise mind And have an overpowering, great[163] accumulation Enter into this way Of infinite merit and wisdom. {59}
Valiant ones of great resources, intelligent, pure-minded, stable, Enter into this teaching, made of endless virtue and knowledge.
de dag smon lam rgya che bas/ / sems dang sdom pa rgya che ste/ / rgyal ba'i spyod yul thob gyur cing / / byang chub rgya chen gnon par 'gyur/ /
“Those with vast aspirations, Vast motivation, and vows Will reach the field of activity of the jinas And attain vast enlightenment.” {60}
Great is their aspiration, great their discipline of mind; They will attain great enlightenment, having arrived at the sphere of the Victor.

de nas byang chub sems dpa' bdud kyi dkyil 'khor rnam par 'thor ba'i ye shes rgyal mtshan gyi rgyal pos/ sangs rgyas kyi byin gyi rlabs kyis phyogs bcur rnam par bltas te/ de'i tshe tshigs su bcad pa 'di dag smras so; ;
Then the bodhisattva Sarvamāramaṇḍalavikiraṇajñānadhvajarāja, through the blessing of the Buddha, looked into the ten directions and recited these verses:
Then the enlightening being Standard of Knowledge Scattering All Bands of Demons, by the power of Buddha, looked over the ten directions and spoke these verses:
chags med ye shes sku mnga' bas/ / rang byung rnams ni sku med de/ / bsam yas ye shes yul mnga' bas/ / de dag bsam par mi nus so/ /
“They have bodies of unimpeded wisdom, And therefore the self-arisen ones have no body. The scope of their wisdom is inconceivable, And therefore one cannot conceive of them. {61}
Being the body of unobstructed knowledge, the Independent is incorporeal; In the realm of inconceivable knowledge, that cannot be conceived.
'phrin las dkar po bsam yas pas/ / sangs rgyas sku rab bsgrub pa'i phyir/ / de la 'jig rten gsum mi 'go / mtshan dang dpe byad bzang pos mdzes/ /
“A buddha’s body is obtained Through inconceivable acts of goodness, And therefore it is unstained by the three worlds And beautified by a supreme being’s features and signs. {62}
The buddha-body is realized by inconceivable pure deeds; Undefiled by the triple world, it shines with distinctive embellishments.
chos kyi dbyings kyis rnam sbyangs pas/ / 'jig rten kun tu snang ba mdzad/ / sangs rgyas byang chub sgo yin te/ / ye shes kun gyi gnas chen no/ /
“He completely illuminates the world And is purified of the realm of phenomena. He is the gateway to the enlightenment of buddhahood And is the great source of all wisdom. {63}
Universal light of the world, having clarified the reality realm, It is also the door of enlightenment, the mine of all knowledge.
chags pa thams cad rnam spangs pas/ / rdul med spros pa mi mnga' 'o/ / ye shes 'od zer rab 'gyed pas/ / 'jig rten kun tu nyi ma 'dra/ /
“Unsullied and pristine, Free of all clinging, A sun for the world Radiating rays of wisdom, {64}
Dispassionate, free from falsehood, having shed all hindrances, As the sun of the world Buddha radiates lights of knowledge.
khams gsum thams cad rnam sbyong bas/ / srid pa'i 'jigs pa rnam par gcod/ / byang chub sems dpa' sgrub pa mdzad/ / byang chub 'byung gnas de bzhin no/ /
“Eliminating the terrors of existence Through purification of the three realms, And bringing bodhisattvas to perfection, He is the source of the enlightenment of buddhahood.[164] {65}
That which removes the fears of existence and purifies those in the triple world, The development of enlightening beings is thus the mine of buddhas’ enlightenment.
kha dog mtha' yas ston mdzad kyang / / kha dog kun la gnas pa med/ / sems can kun gyis bsam yas pa'i/ / kha dog tshad med yongs su ston/ /
“Although he manifests infinite colors, He is devoid of all colors. He manifests the countless, endless[165] Colors because of all beings. {66}
Buddha shows infinite forms without sticking to any form, And shows those inconceivable forms through all living creatures.
skad cig gcig la sangs rgyas kyis/ / byang chub bsam yas sbyangs pas na/ / de yi ye shes mthar phyin par/ / brtag par sus kyang mi nus so/ /
“There is no one who can fully Understand[166] the Buddha’s wisdom, Which in each instant purifies The enlightenment of buddhahood. {67}
No one can reach the end of the knowledge of Buddha, By which inconceivable enlightenment is instantly clarified.
ye shes brtan pa zad mi shes/ / rang bzhin rnam par 'gyur ba med/ / de la dus gsum rgyal ba kun/ / skad cig gcig gis rab tu brjod/ /
“The unceasing teaching of wisdom Is by its nature unchanging. In a single instant it describes All the jinas of the three times. {68}
Inexhaustible exposition of knowledge, wherein are the buddhas of all times, Is produced in a single instant, without any change in essence.
rtag par las gzhan yongs btang ste; ; shes ldan byang chub don gnyer bas/ / sems la sems shes bya bar yang / / de la sems skye med par bsam/ /
“The wise one who is dedicated to enlightenment, Constantly forsaking all other activity, Although his mind is called mind, In his mind no mind arises.[167] {69}
The wise seeker of enlightenment, engaged in endless action, should always think— Although it be thought, no thought is born in this thought.
gang gis sangs rgyas bskyed pa yi/ / sangs rgyas chos rnams bsam mi khyab/ / de dag brjod pa'i yul ma yin/ / shin tu zab pas tshig lam spangs/ /
“The qualities of buddhahood That the buddhas manifest Are inconceivable, are a field beyond description, Are profound, and are beyond the scope of words.” {70}
The inconceivable elements of buddhahood realized by the perfectly enlightened Are profound beyond all telling, beyond the scope of words.

de nas byang chub sems dpa' rnam par snang mdzad kyi smon lam dpal gyi rgyal mtshan gyis; sangs rgyas kyi byin gyi rlabs kyis phyogs bcur rnam par bltas te/ de'i tshe tshigs su bcad pa 'di dag smras so/ /
Then the bodhisattva Vairocanapraṇidhānaketudhvaja, through the blessing of the Buddha, looked into the ten directions and recited these verses:
Then the enlightening being Flames of Knowledge of Vows of the Illuminator, by the power of Buddha, looked over the ten directions and spoke these verses:
dran pa rmongs med dag pa rnams/ / chos 'dzin shin tu nges rtags shing / / blo gros bsam gyis mi khyab la/ / byang chub rgya mtsho mi zad pa/ /
“Those who are pure and with unconfused recollection, Who possess the Dharma with complete certainty, Who have inconceivable understanding, Are an unending ocean of enlightenment. {71}
Those of unerring recollection, pure, born of truth, of certain mind And inconceivable wisdom, are inexhaustible oceans of enlightenment.
de dag yid ni 'di la nges/ / de dag spyod pa'i spyod yul yin/ / de dag shes pa 'dir mi g.yo/ / de dag 'di la the tshom 'chad/ /
“Their minds have certainty concerning this. This is their realm of practice. Their wisdom is unshakable. They have eliminated doubt. {72}
This is the sphere of action of those whose minds are resolved hereon; Their knowledge is unshakable, they have ended doubt.
de dag skyo bar mi 'gyur te/ / de dag yid kyang zhum mi 'gyur/ / sangs rgyas chos la rab gzhol bar/ / de dag sems kyang rab tu 'byung / /
“They do not become disheartened. They do not become despondent. They maintain the aspiration Of devotion to the Buddha’s Dharma. {73}
They do not become depressed or dejected; Their minds are on the way to buddhahood.
de dag dad pa rting tshugs shing / / yang dag 'phags pa rab tu skye/ / dmigs med gnas pa med pa yi/ / ye shes 'di la de dag dga'/ /
“They have the deepest faith, And they develop what is truly superior. They delight in the wisdom That has no object and no fixation. {74}
bskal pa bye bar bsags pa yi/ / yongs su rdzogs pa dge ba'i chos/ / ye shes 'di 'dod mtshungs med pa/ / de dag thams cad yongs su bsngo/ /
“They are filled with virtuous qualities Created during millions of kalpas. All of that is completely given away By these unequaled seekers of wisdom. {75}
Filled with good qualities realized over countless eons, The peerless seekers of knowledge dedicate them all.
'khor ba'i nang na rnam rgyu yang / / 'khor ba dag la gnas pa min/ / sangs rgyas chos rnams rab rtogs pas/ / sangs rgyas yul la rab tu rtse/ /
“Although they are active within saṃsāra, They are not based within saṃsāra. They have realized the Buddha’s Dharma And so delight in the Buddha’s field of activity. {76}
They think about the course of life but do not take refuge in it— They take refuge in the Buddha teachings, sporting in the realm of Buddha.
sems can khams na ji snyed du/ / 'jig rten phun sum tshogs rgyu ba/ / de dag thams cad brtan pas spangs/ / sangs rgyas phun sum tshogs la gnas/ /
“Whatever worldly good fortune there is That occurs within the realms of beings, The resolute ones renounce it all, And they remain in the Buddha’s good fortune. {77}
Whatever mundane fortune takes place in the world of sentient beings, The resolute relinquish it all, for they are set on the attainment of buddhahood.
sangs rgyas rtag tu 'byung gyur kyang / / 'jig rten don med rab tu gnas/ / chags med spyod pa de dag ni/ / rtag tu sems can don la gnas/ /
“The world remains fruitless, Continuously in bondage.[168] Those whose conduct is free from attachment Are continuously fixed on benefiting beings. {78}
Vainly clinging, the world is always fettered— There, those of unobstructed action are always set on the welfare of beings.
de dag spyod pa mtshungs med de; ; lus can kun gyis bsam mi khyab/ / 'jig rten bde ba kun sems pas/ / de dag sdug bsngal rnam par bzlog /
“Their unequaled conduct Is inconceivable for all beings. They who think of the world’s happiness Bring an end to suffering. {79}
Unequaled in their action, inconceivable to all beings, They consider the happiness of the world, whereby suffering is repelled.
'jig rten kun la snying brtse zhing / / byang chub ye shes rnam dag pas/ / de dag 'jig rten snang bar gyur/ / 'jig rten thams cad rab tu 'grel/ /
“They have compassion for the whole world And have the pure wisdom of enlightenment. They are a light for the world And bring liberation to the entire world.” {80}
They have purified knowledge of enlightenment and are sympathetic to all beings, As lights of the world, emancipating all beings.
de nas byang chub sems dpa' sgrib pa thams cad rnam par 'thor ba'i rgyal pos/ sangs rgyas kyi byin gyi rlabs kyis phyogs bcur rnam par bltas te/ de'i tshe tshigs su bcad pa 'di dag smras so/ /
Then the bodhisattva Sarvāvaraṇavikiraṇajñānavikrāntarāja,[169] through the blessing of the Buddha, looked into the ten directions and recited these verses:
Then the enlightening being Valiant One with Knowledge to Disperse All Barriers, by the power of Buddha, looked over the ten directions and spoke these verses:
bskal pa bye ba phrag brgyar yang / / sangs rgyas sgra ni rab dkon na/ / the tshom thams cad gcod pa yi/ / dam pa mthong ba ci zhig smos/ /
“Even the word buddha is a great rarity For thousands of millions[170] of kalpas, Let alone seeing a supreme one Who eliminates all doubts. {81}
The name of Buddha is hard to come by even in a billion eons— How much more so the sight of Buddha, supreme, which ends all desires.
chos kun thugs su chud rtogs pa/ / 'jig rten gsum po'i bsod nams stegs/ / sems can thams cad rnam sbyong ba'i/ / 'jig rten sgron ma mthong gis dga'/ /

“He has gained the realization of all Dharmas. He is the object of veneration[171] for the three worlds. He brings purification to all beings. He is a light for the world that brings joy when seen.[172] {82}
Buddha appears as the light of the world, gone to the goal of all truth, Worthy of the offerings of the three worlds, purifier of all beings.
sems can gtso bo ma smad pa'i/ / gzugs kyi sku ni mthong gyur na/ / bskal pa bye ba khrag khrig tu/ / ngoms shing tshim pa skyer mi btub/ /
“One will never have enough Of seeing the form body Of the supreme blameless being, Even in a quintillion kalpas. {83}
Those who regard the physical form of the impeccable best of beings Never tire of it even in countless eons.
mi yi dbang po'i sku gzugs la/ / rgyal ba'i sras rnams blta blta zhing / / rang gi dge ba chags med pa/ / gzhan don brtson pa byang chub bsngo/ /
“The bodhisattvas[173] are continually gazing At the form body of the lord of humans. They have no attachment, and they dedicate Their own virtues to enlightenment for the benefit of others. {84}
Offspring of the Victor looking at the form body of the Lord of Humans, Unattached, dedicate themselves purely to enlightenment, seeking the highest goal.
thub pa chen po'i gzugs kyi sku/ / de las tha dad yang dag shes/ / chags med ye shes 'byung 'gyur bas/ / de ni sangs rgyas byang chub sgo/ /
“The form body of the great Muni Is this gateway to the enlightenment of buddhahood, From which comes unimpeded and Unceasing[174] discriminating knowledge. {85}
This is the door to enlightenment, the corporeal embodiment of the Great Sage, Whence issue unhindered, inexhaustible analytic intellectual powers.
sems can bsam yas tshad med pa/ / snang bas mdzad de theg chen la/ / btsud nas thub pa chen po'i mchog / byang chub dam par lung yang ston/ /
“The supreme great Muni illuminates Countless, innumerable beings, Brings them into the Mahāyāna, And prophesies their supreme enlightenment. {86}
Having illumined infinite beings, the Great Sage foretells their supreme Enlightenment, having led them into the Great Vehicle.
bsod nams chen po'i rang bzhin zhing / / ye shes dkyil 'khor shar cing 'byung / / 'jig rten tshad mad [*med?] kun tu snang / / bsod nams phung po rnam 'phel mdzad/ /
“He illuminates an infinite world, A realm that has the nature of great merit, A domain of wisdom that has arisen and appeared,[175] And he multiplies accumulated merit. {87}
The great field of blessings, a sphere of knowledge, has emerged And illuminates infinite beings, increasing the mass of virtue.
sdug bsngal dra ba rab tu gcod/ / ye shes phung po rnam par sbyong / / gang gis rgyal ba bsnyen bkur pa; ; de dag ngan song 'jigs pa med/ /
“He cuts through the net of suffering And purifies[176] the aggregation of wisdom. Those who please the Jina Have no fear of the lower realms. {88}
There is no fear of evil ways for those who associate now with Buddha, The one who cuts through the net of misery and purifies the mass of knowledge.
rkang gnyis dam pa mthong gyur na/ / shin tu yangs pa'i sems skye ste/ / 'od snang gsal ba'i shes rab mthu/ / grangs med pa yang skye bar 'gyur/ /
“On seeing the supreme two-legged being, An extremely vast motivation develops. The incalculable power of wisdom Creates an illuminating radiance.[177] {89}
A great mind is born in those who see the Buddha, Immeasurable wisdom and power is born, radiant as the moon.
sangs rgyas skyes bu'i mchog mthong zhing / / byang chub dam par nges par 'gyur/ / de bzhin gshegs par 'gyur bya zhes/ / de dag kun kyang nges par sems/ /
“Those who see the Buddha, the supreme human, Will certainly attain supreme enlightenment. They will have certainty, thinking, ‘I shall become a tathāgata.’ ” {90}
They will be sure of enlightenment, having seen the Buddha, And will be certain that they will become buddhas themselves.
de nas byang chub sems dpa' chos kyi dbyings kyi smon lam gyi gzhi rab tu rtogs pas/ sangs rgyas kyi byin gyi rlabs kyis de'i tshe tshigs su bcad pa 'di dag smras so/ /
Then the bodhisattva Dharmadhātupraṇidhitalanirbheda,[178] through the blessing of the Buddha, looked into the ten directions and recited these verses:
Then the enlightening being King of Superknowledge Discerning the Differentiations of the Plane of the Cosmos, by the power of Buddha, looked over the ten directions and spoke these verses:
yon tan mtha' yas phun ldan pa/ / shAkya'i khyu mchog thub mthong nas/ / yongs su bsngo ba byed pa'i sems/ / theg pa che la rnam par 'dag /
“Having seen the Muni who is the foremost Śākya, Who possesses a perfection of infinite qualities, Those with minds that make dedications Are purified within the Mahāyāna. {91}
Having seen the Sage endowed with infinite virtues, The minds of those dedicated to the Great Vehicle are purified.
sems can kun gyi don gyi phyir/ / thugs rje mnga' ba brtan pa'i rnams/ / chos kyi 'khor lo bskor mdzad pa/ / de bzhin gshegs pa 'byung bar 'gyur/ /
“The constant ones who have great compassion, Who turn the wheel of the Dharma, The tathāgatas Appear for the sake of all beings. {92}
The buddhas appear for the welfare of all beings, Universally compassionate, steadfast, turning the wheel of the teaching.
bskal pa khrag khrig phrag brgyar yang / / sems can don la brtson mdzad pa'i/ / sangs rgyas rnams la lus can rnams/ / kun gyis lan glan cis kyang nus/ /
“How could all beings Be able to repay the buddhas, Who for trillions of kalpas Have been dedicated to benefiting beings? {93}
How can all creatures requite the buddhas’ Countless eons of dedication to their welfare?
ngan song gsum po mi bzad par/ / bskal pa bye bar btsos bla yi/ / chags pa thams cad zlog mdzad pa'i/ / ston pa mi mthong ma yin no/ /
“It is better to be cooked for ten million kalpas In the three unendurable lower existences Than to not see the Teacher, Who dispels all attachment. {94}
It is better to burn in the fearsome three evils for eons Than not to see the Teacher, who quells all attachments.
sems can kun gyi rgyud rnams na/ / sdug bsngal phung po ci yod pa/ / ma lus nyams su bzod nus kyi/ / sangs rgyas mi mthong ma yin no/ /
“However great the aggregation of suffering That exists within the minds of all beings, One can endure the experience of all of it, But not being deprived of seeing the Buddha. {95}
All the mass of suffering that takes place in all realms of being Is tolerable, but not deprivation of the sight of Buddha.
'jig rten 'di dag thams cad na/ / tha dad ngan song rgyud yod pa/ / de dag yun ring gnas bla yi/ / sangs rgyas mi thos ma yin no/ /
“It is better to remain for a long time In all these different states of being That are in the lower existences in this world Than to be deprived of hearing[179] the Buddha. {96}
It is better to live long in every miserable way in the world Than not to hear the buddhas.
sems can dmyal ba re rer yang / / bskal pa tshad med gnas bla yi/ / mtha' yas rgyal bas brnyes pa yi/ / byang chub mchog las ring gnas min/ /
“It is better to remain for countless kalpas In each of the hell realms Than to remain far from the supreme enlightenment That has been attained by infinite jinas. {97}
Each eon spent even in hell is better Then elsewhere apart from Buddha, distant from enlightenment.
ci zhig phyir ni ngan song du/ / yun ring gnas par 'dod ce na/ / rgyal ba'i dbang po mthong ba ni/ / ye shes 'phel ba'i rgyur 'gyur phyir/ /
“For what reason would one wish to remain For a long time in the lower realms? One would do so as a cause of seeing The lord of jinas, which increases wisdom. {98}
What is the reason for wanting to live long amid calamities? It is to see the Buddha and increase in Knowledge.
rgyal ba 'jig rten mchog mthong na/ / sdug bsngal thams cad 'chad par 'gyur/ / rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas spyod yul gyi/ / ye shes khong du chud pa 'byung / /
“All suffering is eliminated Through seeing the Jina, the Lord of the World, And there is the realization of the wisdom Of the field of activity of the perfect buddhas. {99}
All miseries are ended once the Buddha has been seen, And entry into knowledge takes place, into the sphere of the enlightened.
sangs rgyas mi yi mchog mthong zhing / / sgrib pa thams cad zad par 'gyur/ / byang chub gang gis 'thob pa yi/ / bsod nams tshad med 'phel bar 'gyur/ /
“By seeing the Buddha, the supreme human, All obscurations are brought to an end. It causes the increase of immeasurable merit Through which enlightenment is attained. {100}
All obstructions are removed when Buddha is seen, Increasing measureless virtue, whereby enlightenment is attained.
sangs rgyas mthong bas sems can rnams/ / the tshom yid gnyis chad par 'gyur/ / 'jig rten 'das dang 'jig rten gyi/ / bsam pa'ang yongs su rdzogs par 'gyur/ /
“Seeing the Buddha eliminates The doubts and uncertainties of beings, And both worldly and unworldly Wishes are completely fulfilled.” {101}
Sight of Buddha severs all doubts of sentient beings And fulfills all purposes, mundane and transcendental.
[kun tu bzang po]
Chapter 2. Samantabhadra
Universally Good

de nas byang chub sems dpa' sems dpa' chen po kun tu bzang pos byang chub sems dpa'i tshogs thams cad la rnam par bltas te/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i ting nge 'dzin seng ge rnam par bsgyings pa 'di nyid de bas kyang rnam par dbye ba dang / rgya cher brjod pa dang / gsal bar bya ba dang / rab tu brjod pa dang / yang dag par bstan pa dang / shin tu snang bar bya ba dang / rab tu gsal bar bya ba dang / man ngag bstan pa'i phyir chos kyi dbyings kyi tshul nam mkha'i dbyings dang mnyam pas dus gsum mnyam pa nyid dang / chos kyi dbyings mnyam pa nyid dang / sems can gyi khams mnyam pa nyid dang / 'jig rten thams cad mnyam pa nyid dang / las kyi rgyud thams cad mnyam pa nyid dang / sems can gyi bsam pa mnyam pa nyid dang / sems can gyi mos pa mnyam pa nyid dang / chos kyi snang ba mnyam pa nyid dang / sems can yongs su smin par bya ba'i dus mnyam pa nyid dang / 'gro ba thams cad kyi dbang po mnyam pa nyid kyis de bzhin gshegs pa'i ting nge 'dzin seng ge rnam par bsgyings pa 'di nyid/ byang chub sems dpa' de dag la bstan pa'i tshul bcus yang dag par rab tu ston te/

Then the bodhisattva mahāsattva Samantabhadra looked upon the great assembly of bodhisattvas, and in order to categorize, teach extensively, clarify, illuminate, and give instructions on the Tathāgata’s samādhi called the gaping lion, he taught those bodhisattvas in ten ways the Tathāgata’s samādhi called the gaping lion through the equality of the nature of the realm of phenomena with the element of space, the equality of the three times, the equality of the realm of phenomena, the equality of the realms of beings, the equality of all worlds, the equality of the continuum of karma, the equality of the thoughts of all beings, the equality of the aspirations of beings, the equality of the appearances of phenomena, the equality of the times for ripening beings, and the equality of the faculties of all beings.
