illumined with the knowledge of the sphere of buddhas,
gya nom par snang ba'i ting nge 'dzin la rtag tu mnyam par bzhag pa/
they constantly remained in magnificent samādhi;
always in the concentration of good vision,
chags pa med pa'i mtha'i chos thams cad rab tu dbye ba'i ye shes la mngon par mkhas pa/
they were at the unimpeded summit of being wise in the knowledge that differentiates between all phenomena;
having the superknowledge that discerns the differences among all things while being ultimately unattached,
chos thams cad las khyad par du 'phags pa'i rnam par 'phrul ba'i yul la ye shes kyis rnam par rtse ba/
they disported themselves with wisdom within the domain of liberation that is superior to all phenomena;
master of knowledge of the sphere of liberation, the highest of all states,
dmigs pa thams cad la rgyan bzang por byin gyis rlob pa/
they had transformed all sense objects into excellent adornments;
causing all objects to appear in pure arrays,
chos kyi dbyings phyogs med pa la phyogs kyi rjes su 'brang bas rab tu zhugs pa/
they had followed and entered every direction[248] in the realm of phenomena;
entering into the universes of the ten directions wherever they are,
phyogs thams cad rnam par dbye bas chos kyi dbyings las yang dag par gzhol ba
they had entered[249] the realm of phenomena through all the different directions;
entering into the different universes in all directions,
shin tu phra ba ste/ yangs pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba la byang chub tu rnam par 'tshang rgya ba
they had awakened to enlightenment in the minute, in the vast, in atoms;[250]
conscious of enlightenment in atomic particles subtle and gross,
rang bzhin kha dog thams cad yongs su ston pa/
their nature was colorless[251] yet they manifested every color;
showing all colors beautiful in nature,
phyogs gcig la yang dag par gzhol ba
they had brought together everything in one direction;
concentrating the totality in one space,
de lta bu'i yon tan dang ye shes mtha' yas pas yang dag par bskyed de/ bsod nams dang ye shes kyi snying po dang ldan par gyur pa/
they had an essence of wisdom and merit that developed infinite qualities and wisdom in one form;[252]
treasuries of knowledge and virtue mature in the knowledge of infinite qualities of one form,
sangs rgyas thams cad kyis bstod pa/ bsngags pa/ bkur ba;
they were praised and eulogized by all the buddhas;
praised by all buddhas,
tshig dang / yi ge mi zad pas yon tan dang legs pa brjod du yod pa'i
and they described qualities and excellences with unceasing words and terms.
having qualities that can never be fully told—
byang chub sems dpa' dze ta'i tshal du 'dus te 'khod pa/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i yon tan rgya mtsho la 'jug pa/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i 'od zer gyis rab tu snang bar gyur pa
The bodhisattvas who had gathered and were assembled in Jetavana had entered the ocean of the qualities of the Tathāgata and were illuminated by the light rays of the Tathāgata.
those enlightening beings who had gathered at the Jeta grove and were sitting there immersed in the ocean of qualities of Buddha, illumined by rays of light from the buddhas,

de dag gi lus thams cad dang / khang pa brtsegs pa de dag dang / byang chub sems dpa'i longs spyod de dag dang / byang chub sems dpa'i stan de dag dang / dze ta'i tshal thams cad nas kyang / dga' ba chen po'i shugs rab tu thob pa'i chos nyid dang / byang chub sems dpa'i chos snang ba bsam gyis mi khyab pa rab tu thob pas/ dga' ba'i shugs las byung ba'i rnam par 'phrul pa chen po'i rgyan mngon par 'thon nas/ chos kyi dbyings thams cad rgyas par khyab par gyur to/ /

Through the nature of their attainment of great joy, and through their attainment of the inconceivable splendor of bodhisattva qualities, an array of miraculous manifestation that originated from great joy issued forth from all their bodies, the kūṭāgāras, the bodhisattva enjoyments, the bodhisattva thrones, and the entirety of Jetavana, and it spread throughout the entire realm of phenomena.

as they were in a state of great ecstasy, having attained the light of the inconceivable state of enlightening beings, from their ecstasy emanated great arrays of mystical projections pervading all universes, issuing from all of their bodies, their towers, their paraphernalia and their thrones, from everywhere in the Jeta grove:
'di lta ste/ sems kyi skad cig re re la 'od zer gyi dra ba'i sprin shin tu yangs pa/ 'gro ba thams cad yongs su tshim par byed pa mngon par 'thon te/ phyogs bcu rgyas par khyab par gyur to/ /
It was like this: in each instant of the mind there issued forth vast clouds of networks of light rays that brought satisfaction to all beings and pervaded the ten directions;
in each successive mental moment they emanated vast clouds of webs of light beams, pleasing to all worlds, suffusing the ten directions;

rin po che sna tshogs kyi dril bu'i sprin mngon par 'thon te/ dus gsum gyi de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi yon tan dang / legs pa rab tu brjod pa'i sprin gyi nga ro rjes su bsgrags pas phyogs bcu rgyas par khyab par gyur to/ /

there issued forth clouds of bells made of a variety of precious materials, from which resounded praises of the qualities and excellences of all the tathāgatas in the three times and which pervaded the ten directions;
they filled the ten directions with clouds of bells of all jewels ringing with sounds bespeaking the virtues and qualities of the buddhas of past, present, and future;

dmigs pa thams cad las 'gro ba thams cad kyi rol mo'i sprin mngon par 'thon te/ sems can thams cad kyi las dang rnam par smin pa/ rol mo'i sgra snyan par blang bas rjes su sgrog cing / phyogs bcu rgyas par khyab par gyur to/ /

there issued forth from all sensory objects clouds of the music of[253] all beings that possessed the beautiful sounds of the music of the ripening of the karma of all beings, and it resounded and pervaded throughout the ten directions;
they filled the ten directions with clouds of voices of all beings, issuing from all objects, making sweet sounds telling of the fruits of all beings’ actions;

byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi smon lam dang / byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa sna tshogs yang dag par ston pa'i tshul gyi sprin mang po mngon par 'thon nas/ byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi smon lam gyi sgra dbyangs rab tu sgrog pas phyogs bcu rgyas par khyab par gyur to/ /

there issued forth a multitude of clouds that manifested all the ways of bodhisattva prayers and the variety of bodhisattva conduct, and they pervaded throughout the ten directions; they resounded with the sound of the prayers of all bodhisattvas and pervaded throughout the ten directions;

they filled the ten directions with clouds of forms showing the vows of all enlightening beings and the various practices of enlightening beings, emanating voices telling of the undertakings of all enlightening beings;

de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi sprul pa dang / rnam par 'phrul pa'i sprin mang po mngon par 'thon nas/ de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi gsung gi dbyangs rjes su brjod cing / phyogs bcu rgyas par khyab par gyur to/ /
there issued forth a multitude of clouds of the emanations and manifestations of all the tathāgatas, speaking with the voices of all the tathāgatas, which pervaded throughout the ten directions;

byang chub sems dpa'i lus mtshan dang dpe byad bzang pos rnam par brgyan pa'i sprin mang po mngon par 'thon nas/ zhing thams cad du byung ba'i sangs rgyas skye ba gcig nas skye ba gcig tu brgyud pa rab tu brjod cing / phyogs bcu rgyas par khyab par gyur to/ /

there issued forth a multitude of clouds of the adorning characteristics and features of the bodies of bodhisattvas, which described the successive births of buddhas in all realms and pervaded throughout the ten directions;
they emanated clouds of beatified embodiments of enlightening beings filling the ten directions telling of the succession of buddhas in all lands;

dus gsum gyi de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad dang mnyam pa'i snying po byang chub kyi sprin mang po mngon par 'thon nas/ de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad mngon par byang chub pa'i rgyan byung ba yongs su ston cing / phyogs bcu sangs rgyas par khyab par gyur to/ /

there issued forth a multitude of clouds of the enlightenment that is equally the essence of all the tathāgatas in the three times, and they taught the appearance of the array of the attainment of buddhahood by all the tathāgatas and pervaded throughout the ten directions;

they emanated clouds of sites of enlightenment like those of all buddhas of past, present, and future, filling the ten directions, showing magnificent displays of the transcendent enlightenment and emancipation of all buddhas;
dmigs pa thams cad las klu'i dbang po'i lus kyi sprin mang po mngon par 'thon nas; spos sna tshogs kyi char rab tu 'bebs shing / phyogs bcu rgyas par khyab par gyur to/ /
there issued forth a multitude of clouds of the bodies of the lords of nāgas from all sensory objects, which let fall a rain of various kinds of perfume and pervaded throughout the ten directions;
from all objects they emanated clouds of bodies of ruling water spirits, showering rain of all fragrances throughout the ten directions;

'gro ba thams cad kyi dbang po'i lus dang 'dra ba'i sprin mang po mngon par 'thon nas/ byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po'i spyod pa yongs su brjod pa byed cing / phyogs bcu rgyas par khyab par gyur to/ /
there issued forth a multitude of clouds of bodies that resembled the lords of beings, described the completely good bodhisattva conduct, and pervaded the ten directions;
they emanated clouds of bodies like the rulers of all worlds, pervading the ten directions, telling of the conduct of the enlightening being Universally Good;

zhing yongs su dag pa rin po che thams cad kyi rang bzhin yongs kyi gzugs brnyan gyi sprin mang po mngon par 'thon nas/ de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi chos kyi 'khor lo bskor ba mngon par ston cing / phyogs bcu rgyas par khyab par gyur to; ;

there issued forth a multitude of clouds of images of the pure realms that had the nature of all precious materials, made visible the turning of the Dharma wheel by all tathāgatas, and pervaded the ten directions;

from all objects they sent forth clouds of reflections of all perfectly pure buddha-lands, made of all jewels, filling the ten directions, showing the turnings of the wheels of teachings of all buddhas.

de dag la sogs pa byang chub sems dpa' de dag gi byin gyi rlabs dang / chos kyi snang ba rgya mtsho bsam gyis mi khyab pa rab tu thob pa'i chos nyid kyi rgyan chen po rnam par sprul pa'i sprin; sangs rgyas kyi zhing brjod du med pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed byung bar gyur to/ /

and there issued forth other such clouds of vast arrays of miraculous manifestations as numerous as the atoms in buddha realms beyond enumeration through the transformative power of those bodhisattvas and from their nature of having attained the radiance of an inconceivable ocean of qualities.

They emanated as many such clouds of magical displays of great magnificent arrays as atoms in untold buddha-lands, by the mystic power of those enlightening beings, and by virtue of their state of attainment of illumination of the inconceivable ocean of truths.

de nas byang chub sems dpa' 'jam dpal gyis sangs rgyas kyi byin gyis rlabs kyis rnam par 'phrul pa de dag yongs su ston pa byed cing / phyogs bcur rnam par bltas nas de'i tshe tshigs su bcad pa 'di dag smras so/ /
The bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, seeing in the ten directions all those manifestations of miracles through the miraculous power of the Buddha, recited these verses:
Then the enlightening being Manjushri, empowered by Buddha, observing all those mystical apparitions appearing throughout the ten directions, uttered these verses:
dze ta'i tshal du sangs rgyas byin gyi rlabs/ / mtha' yas rgya chen yongs su byung la ltos/ / dmigs pa kun las lus kyi sprin chen rnams/ / mngon par 'thon cing phyogs rnams kun tu khyab/ /
“Observe the appearance of the vast, infinite, Miraculous power of the Buddha in Jetavana. There have issued forth from all sensory objects Clouds of bodies that have pervaded all directions. {11}
Observe the infinite, vast power of Buddha arisen in the Jeta grove, Having emanated clouds of bodies as sense objects that pervade all directions.
bde gshegs sras po rnams kyi sna tshogs rgyan/ / kha dog mtha' yas rgya chen rnam dag pa/ / stan dang dmigs pa yongs su bcas pa la/ / de dag thams cad gzugs brnyan byung ba snang / /
“The vast, completely pure, infinite forms Of the various displays of the Sugata’s offspring Are perceived as images appearing From the thrones and from sensory objects. {12}
The vast, pure arrays of offspring of Buddha, various, of infinite forms, Are all seen reflected from the thrones, which contain the objects of sense.
rgyan rnams sna tshogs rin chen 'od 'phro'i sprin/ / bde gshegs sras po rnams kyi spu rtse las/ / sangs rgyas gsung rnams rab tu sgrog byed cing / / zhing rnams kun gyi dbyings su khyab par 'phro/ /

“A variety of displays, clouds of jewel light rays, From the tips of the body hairs of the sons of the sugatas Are emanated, spreading within all the realms And resounding with the words of the buddhas. {13}
Clouds of jewel radiance, in various arrays, pervade the land, pouring forth From the pores of the offspring of Buddha, emitting the sounds of Buddha.
tshangs pa'i dbang po'i gzugs 'dra lus rnams dang / / spyod lam rab tu zhi ba dag pa'i gzugs/ / zhing gi me tog kun las mngon 'thon te/ / bsam gtan yan lag brjod cing kun tu 'dong / /
“Bodies that resemble the forms of Brahmakāyika devas With pure bodies and peaceful conduct Issue forth from the blossoms on the trees,[254] Describing the aspects of dhyāna as they go. {14}
Forms like Brahma and Indra, with pure bodies and tranquil deportment, Emerging from the trees and flowers, go forth telling of meditation.
kun tu bzang po 'dra ba'i rgyal ba'i sras/ / mtshan rab dpe byad bzang pos brgyan pa'i lus/ / grangs med bsam yas bde gshegs pa spu las/ / sprul pa de 'dra thogs pa med par 'byung / /

“From the Sugata’s pores issue forth, Without impediment, innumerable, countless emanations Who are bodhisattvas that resemble Samantabhadra, Their bodies adorned by the characteristics and features. {15}
Enlightening beings like Universally Good, adorned with embellishing marks, Inconceivable, countless, are produced from the Buddha’s pores.
bde gshegs sras po dus gsum byung ba rnams/ / yon tan rgya mtsho'i legs pa brjod pa dag / rgya mtsho che mnyam rgyan sprin de dag kun/ / dze ta'i tshal na gnas shing rab tu brjod/ /

“The great ocean of the emanated qualities Of the sugatas’ sons who have appeared in the three times, Who are clouds of displays of an ocean of qualities, Proclaim those who are seated in Jetavana.[255] {16}
Those clouds of adornments of the Oceans of Virtue bespeak the qualities Of the enlightening beings of all times, gathered in the Jeta grove.
phyogs rnams kun gyi sems can yongs kyi las/ / rgya mtsho chen po sna tshogs ma lus par/ / dze ta'i tshal gyi shing gi gzugs rnams kyi/ / gseb nas byung bar gyur pa kun tu grags/ /
“A vast ocean of the variety, without exception, Of the karma of beings in all directions Is proclaimed, issuing forth from within The forms of the trees in Jetavana. {17}
All the varied oceans of deeds of groups of beings in all directions Are heard, radiating from within the trees in the Jeta grove.
dus gsum 'byung ba'i rgyal ba thams cad kyi/ / zhing rnams kun gyi ma lus rnam 'phrul pa/ / zhing rnams rgya mtsho'i rdul snyed de dag kyang / / so so dmigs kyi dmigs par gyur pa snang / /
“The miracles in all the realms, without exception, Of all the jinas who appear in the three times, Appear as each and every sensory object As numerous as the atoms in an ocean of realms.[256] {18}
Transfigurations of all buddhas of past, present, and future in every land Appear from the ground, in every single object, numerous as atoms.
sangs rgyas phyogs kyi zhing rnams rgya mtsho'i sprin/ / spu rtse re rer sna tshogs rnams phye ba'i/ / sangs rgyas gnas rnams skad cig re rer snang / / de dag la yang sangs rgyas sprin mang bzhugs/ /

“Clouds of oceans of buddhas in the realms in the directions Disseminate from each of their pore hairs, In each instant, a variety of the abodes of buddhas, Within which reside multitudes of clouds of buddhas. {19}
At each and every point various oceanic clouds of buddhas Continuously reveal the abodes of the Victors and the masses of buddhas there.
'gro dang mnyam par phyogs rnams kun bkang zhing / / sems can thabs kyis yongs su smin par byed/ / de dag 'od las spos kyi 'od 'phro dang / / me tog phal chen rgya mtsho sprin kyang 'byung / /

“They pervade every direction, wherever there are beings, And through skillful methods ripen those beings. From their light there issue forth vast clouds Of oceans of perfumes, light rays,[257] and flowers. {20}
As many as beings, pervading everywhere, as they develop beings by expedient means, From their auras emerge oceanic clouds of fragrant flames and masses of flowers.
mkha' ltar tshad med rin chen gzhal med khang / / ma lus rgyan rab kun gyis rnam mdzes pa/ / de dag thams cad phyogs rnams kun khyab byed/ / zhing dang snying po byang chub de bzhin no/ /
“The precious divine palaces as immeasurable as space Are beautified with every adornment without exception. Those realms and their bodhimaṇḍas Pervade every direction. {21}
Precious mansions, measureless as the sky, adorned with all realities, Fill the lands in all directions, and all sites of enlightenment.
dus gsum byung ba'i rgyal ba'i sras rnams kyis/ / kun tu bzang po'i spyod pa'i rnam tshul du/ / zhing rnams rgya mtsho rnam par dag byas pa'i/ / rgyan rab sna tshogs 'gro ltar tshad med pa/ /
“The sugatas’ sons who appear in the three times Purify the ocean of realms Through the practice of completely good conduct,[258] And their various displays, as limitless as beings, {22}
All the lands of the offspring of Buddha in past, present, and future, great healers, Purified by means of the practice of universal good,
phyogs rnams dus gsum kun tu gang byung rnams/ / bskal pa rgya mtsho chen por rnam sbyangs pa/ / de dag kun kyang dze ta'i nags tshal gyi/ / bar snang mkha' la gzugs brnyan tshul du snang / /
“Fill all directions and the three times. They have been purified in a great ocean of kalpas, And they all appear like reflections In the expanse of the sky above Jetavana.” {23}
Their various arrays, purified over oceans of eons, infinite as beings, Are all seen by reflection in the sky of the Jeta grove.

de nas byang chub sems dpa' sangs rgyas kyi ting nge 'dzin gyis rgyud shin tu snang bar byas pa de dag las; ;byang chub sems dpa' re res kyang / snying rje chen po'i sgo sangs rgyas kyi zhing brjod du med pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed du zhugs par gyur nas/ de dag de bas kyang 'gro ba thams cad la phan pa dang / yongs su bsdu ba'i don du zhugs par gyur te/ de ltar mnyam par bzhag pa de dag gi ba spu'i sgo re re nas kyang 'od zer sangs rgyas kyi zhing brjod du med pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed mngon par 'thon par gyur te/ 'od zer de dag gi sgo re re nas kyang / byang chub sems dpa'i 'phrul pa'i sprin/ 'jig rten gyi dbang po thams cad dang 'dra ba'i lus dang / 'gro ba thams cad la mngon par blta ba'i lus dang / sems can thams cad yongs su smin par bya ba dang / 'phrod pa'i las dang ldan pa mngon par 'thon te/ mngon par 'thon nas kyang / phyogs thams cad kyi chos kyi dbyings rgyas par bkang nas/ sems can thams cad yang dag par bskul zhing yongs su smin par bya ba dang / gdul bar byed do/ /

Those bodhisattvas were continuously illumined by the samādhi of the Buddha. Each of those bodhisattvas had entered gateways of great compassion as numerous as the atoms in innumerable buddha realms and brought even more benefit for beings. Resting in meditation in that way there issued from each of their body hairs light rays as numerous as the atoms in innumerable buddha realms, and from the tips of each of those light rays there issued clouds of bodhisattvas’ emanations, emanated bodies that resembled the bodies of the Indras of all worlds, bodies that looked upon all beings and ripened all beings. Having issued forth, they pervaded the realm of phenomena in all directions. They inspired all beings, ripened them, and guided them.

At that point, each of those enlightening beings, illuminated by the light of the concentration of Buddha, entered as many gates of great compassion as atoms in untold buddha-lands, and attained even greater capability to treat all beings beneficially. Thus concentrated, from each of their pores came forth as many rays of light as atoms in untold buddha-lands; from each ray of light came forth as many multitudes of phantom enlightening beings, bodies like those of all world rulers, bodies appearing to all beings, bodies adapted to the development of all beings. Having pervaded the cosmos with their emanations,

lha'i gnas nas shi 'phos pa yongs su bstan pa'i sgo dang / 'jig rten gyi khams thams cad du skye ba yongs su bstan pa'i sgo dang / byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa'i dkyil 'khor yongs su bstan pa'i sgo dang / rmi lam yongs su bstan pa'i sgo dang / sangs rgyas kyi zhing brjod du med pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyis sems can yongs su bskul ba byed do/ /
byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi smon lam gyis 'byung ba'i sgo dang /
with the gateways that arose from aspirations of all bodhisattvas;
by means of release through the vows of all enlightening beings;
'jig rten gyi khams yongs su bskyod pa'i sgo dang /
with the gateways that shook the world realms;
by means of perfect knowledge of the world;
sbyin pa'i pha rol tu phyin pa'i spyod pa yongs su bstan pa'i sgo dang /
with the gateways that taught the conduct of the perfection of generosity;
by means of showing the practice of transcendent giving;
de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi yon tan la nan tan du bya ba dang rab tu bsgrub pa'i sgo dang /
with the gateways that were dedicated to and accomplished the qualities of all the tathāgatas;
by means of the positive and negative spheres of the virtues of all buddhas, what they cultivate and what they efface;
yan lag dang nying lag gcod pa'i bzod pa'i pha rol tu phyin pa yongs su bstan pa'i sgo dang /
with the gateways that taught the perfection of patience when one’s limbs and various body parts are cut off;
by means of showing transcendental forbearance, even if dismembered;
byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par 'phrul pa chen pos brtson 'grus kyi pha rol tu phyin pa yongs su bstan pa'i sgo dang /
with the gateways that taught the perfection of diligence through the great miracles of the bodhisattvas;
by means of transcendent energy of the great spiritual metamorphosis of enlightening beings;

byang chub sems dpa'i bsam gtan dang / rnam par thar pa dang / ting nge 'dzin dang / snyoms par 'jug pa thams cad dang / sangs rgyas kyi ye shes kyi lam gyi dkyil 'khor snang ba rab tu brjod pa'i sgo dang /
with the gateways that described the dhyānas, liberations, and samādhis of the bodhisattvas and the radiance of the domain that is the path of the wisdom of the buddhas;
by means of shining light of the sphere of the path of buddha-knowledge by the meditations, liberations, concentrations, and attainments of all enlightening beings;
sangs rgyas kyi chos thams cad yongs su btsal ba'i phyir chos kyi tshig dang / yi ge re re'i phyir lus grangs med pa yongs su gtong ba yongs su bstan pa'i sgo dang /
with the gateways that taught the sacrificing of countless bodies for the sake of seeking all the Dharmas of the buddhas and for the sake of each word and letter of the Dharma;
by means of showing the relinquishment of countless bodies in quest of the meaning of each phrase of the teachings in order to find out all buddha-teachings;
de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi drung du 'gro zhing chos thams cad yongs su dri ba'i sgo dang /
with the gateways of going into the presence of all the tathāgatas and asking questions concerning all the Dharmas;
by means of approaching all buddhas and asking about all the teachings;

dus la ji ltar 'bab pa dang bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du 'gro ba'i drung du 'gro zhing thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du yongs su smin par 'gyur ba thob par bya ba'i tshul rgya mtsho snang ba'i rnam par dmigs par bya ba'i sgo dang /

with the gateways of being focused on the radiance of an ocean of the ways of attaining going into the presence of beings when the time is right and, in accordance with their aspirations, ripening them for omniscience;
by means of communicating the light of the ocean of methods and principles of approaching and guiding beings according to the right timing and according to their mentalities, fulfilling omniscience;
byang chub sems dpa'i bsod nams dang / ye shes kyi tshogs thams cad bdud dang phas kyi rgol bas mi tshugs pa'i stobs kyi rgyal mtshan yongs su bstan pa'i sgo dang /
with the gateways that teach the victory banner of the power of the invincibility of the merit and wisdom of bodhisattvas in the face of māras and adversaries;
by means of showing the light of power of the stores of knowledge and virtue of all enlightening beings, which are invulnerable to demons and disputers;
bzo thams cad shes shing mkhas pa dang ldan pa'i ye shes kyis yongs su bstan pa'i sgo dang /
with the gateways that teach the level[259] of the wisdom that has knowledge and understanding of all crafts;
by means of showing the stage of knowledge which includes knowledge of all practical arts and mystic knowledge;
'gro ba thams cad las khyad par du 'phags par shes shing / mkhas pa dang ldan pa'i ye shes kyis yongs su bstan pa'i sgo dang /
with the gateways that teach the level[260] of knowledge and understanding that is superior to that of all beings;
by means of showing the stage of knowledge which includes knowledge and mystic knowledge of the differences among all beings;
sems can thams cad kyi bsam pa'i khyad par shes shing / mkhas pa dang ldan pa'i ye shes kyis yongs su bstan pa'i sgo dang /
with the gateways that teach the level[261] of the wisdom that has the knowledge and understanding of the different aspirations of all beings;
by means of showing the stage of knowledge which includes knowledge and mystic knowledge of the differences in the mentalities of all beings;

sems can thams cad kyi dbang po la 'jug pa'i thabs kyis nyon mongs pa dang bag chags sna tshogs yang dag par gzhom pa la shes shing / mkhas pa dang ldan pa'i ye shes kyis yongs su bstan pa'i sgo dang /

with the gateways that teach the level[262] of the wisdom that has the knowledge and understanding of the capabilities, entrances, engagements, and various kleśas and predispositions of all beings;[263]

by means of showing the stage of knowledge which includes knowledge and mystic knowledge of the faculties, procedures, and practices of all beings and the destruction of their various afflictions and habits;
and with the gateways that teach the level of the wisdom that has the knowledge and understanding of the variety of karma and practices of all beings.[264]
by showing the stage of knowledge which includes knowledge and mystic knowledge of the various results of deeds of all beings—

de dag la sogs pa'i sems can yongs su smin par bya ba dang / gdul ba'i thabs dang / bsdu ba'i sgo sangs rgyas kyi zhing brjod du med pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyis byang chub sems dpa' de dag sems can thams cad kyi gnas su phyin par snang ste/

With other such gateways as numerous as the atoms in innumerable buddha realms that contained methods for ripening and guiding beings, those bodhisattvas went to the abodes of all beings and appeared there.

with as many such means of developing and guiding beings as atoms in untold buddha-lands, those enlightening beings were seen to have come to the abodes of all sentient beings in all states of existence;

la la ni lha'i gnas su phyin par snang ngo/ / la la ni klu'i gnas su phyin par snang ngo/ / la la ni gnod sbyin gyi gnas su phyin par snang ngo/ / la la ni dri za'i gnas su phyin par snang ngo/ / la la ni lha ma yin gyi gnas su phyin par snang ngo/ / la la ni nam mkha' lding gi gnas su phyin par snang ngo/ / la la ni mi'am ci'i gnas su phyin par snang ngo/ / la la ni lto phye chen po'i gnas su phyin par snang ngo/ / la la ni tshangs pa'i dbang po'i gnas su phyin par snang ngo/ / la la ni mi'i gnas su phyin par snang ngo/ / la la ni gshin rje'i gnas su phyin par snang ngo/ / la la ni yi kyi gnas thams cad du phyin par snang ngo/ / la la ni sems can dmyal ba'i 'jig rten thams cad du phyin par snang ngo/ / la la ni yi kyi skye gnas kyi rgyud thams cad du phyin par snang ste/

Some went to the abodes of devas and appeared there. Some went to the abodes of nāgas and appeared there. Some went to the abodes of yakṣas and appeared there. Some went to the abodes of gandharvas and appeared there. Some went to the abodes of asuras and appeared there. Some went to the abodes of garuḍas and appeared there. Some went to the abodes of kinnaras and appeared there. Some went to the abodes of mahoragas and appeared there. Some went to the abodes of the lords of Brahmā deities and appeared there. Some went to the abodes of humans and appeared there. Some went to the realms[265] of Yamas and appeared there. Some went to all the abodes of pretas and appeared there. Some went to the worlds of the hells and appeared there. Some went to births as animals[266] and appeared there.

mthong bas 'dul ba'i sems can dang / thos pas 'dul ba dang / rjes su dran pas 'dul ba dang / dbyangs kyi dkyil 'khor gyi 'dul ba dang / ming gi chu klung gi sgras 'dul ba dang / 'od kyi dkyil 'khor gyis 'dul ba dang / 'od zer gyi dra ba rab tu dgye bas 'dul ba dang / sems can rnams kyi bsam pa'i tshul ji lta ba bzhin du yongs su smin par bya ba dang / gdul ba'i phyir snying rje chen po tha mi dad pa dang / smon lam tha mi dad pa dang / ye shes tha mi dad pa dang / sems can yongs su bsdu ba tha mi dad pa'i tshul du/ byang chub sems dpa' de dag dze ta'i tshal nas rnam par 'phrul ba'i rgyan pa sna tshogs kyis/ 'jig rten gyi khams 'byams klas pa thams cad dang / sems can gyi khams 'byams klas pa thams cad rgyas par 'gengs pa byed par snang yang / de bzhin gshegs pa'i zhabs kyi drung nas mi g.yo ste/

In order to ripen and guide with undivided great compassion, with undivided aspiration, with undivided wisdom, with an undivided attraction of beings, and in accordance with the aspirations of beings, those beings who are guided by seeing them, guided by hearing them, guided by remembering them, guided by the scope of their voices, guided by the sound of the river of their names, guided by their halos, or guided by their emanating a net of light rays‍—those bodhisattvas in Jetavana filled with an array of various emanations the entire extent of world realms and the entire extent of the realms of beings without moving from the feet of the Tathāgata.

with nondiscriminatory great compassion, with nondiscriminatory commitment, with nondiscriminatory knowledge, with nondiscriminatory effort to save all beings, for the purpose of fully developing beings according to their mentalities, beings who could be guided by seeing them, by hearing them, by their halos, by the sound of their names, by their auras, by radiating nets of light beams, the enlightening beings in the Jeta grove were seen by various arrays of projections pervading all realms of beings in all oceans of worlds, yet without leaving the presence of the Buddha:
la la ni rang gi gnas dang / khang pa brtsegs pa dang / stan dang / 'khor du bcas pas phyogs bcu rgyas par byed par snang yang / de bzhin gshegs pa'i zhabs kyi drung nas mi g.yo'o/ /
Some made their own dwellings, kūṭāgāras, thrones, and retinues appear throughout the ten directions without moving from the feet of the Tathāgata.
some appeared pervading the ten directions, their bodies on their thrones in their towers surrounded by their associates, yet without becoming absent from the presence of Buddha;

la la ni sprul pa'i sprin rab tu 'gyed par snang / la la ni sems can yongs su smin par bya ba'i don du gcig pu gnyis su med par 'gro bar snang yang / de bzhin gshegs pa'i 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor nas mi g.yo'o/ /
Some sent forth clouds of emanations, while some appeared to go alone, with no companion, in order to ripen beings, without moving from the circle of the Tathāgata’s entourage.
some appeared emanating clouds of apparitions to develop beings, yet without becoming absent from the assembly around the Buddha;

la la ni dge sbyong gi gzugs/ la la ni tshangs pa'i gzugs/ la la ni brtul zhugs can thams cad kyi cha byad dang / cho ga dang / chu zheng gi gzugs/ la la ni sman pa'i gzugs/ la la ni tshong pa'i gzugs/ la la ni snyan pas 'tsho ba'i gzugs/ la la ni gar mkhan gyi gzugs/ la la ni lha khyer ba'i gzugs/ la la ni bzo thams cad dang ldan pa'i gzugs su grong dang / grong khyer dang / grong rdal dang / ljongs dang / khams dang / rgyal po'i pho brang 'khor du phyin par snang ste/

Some appeared in the form of śramaṇas, some in the form of Brahmās, some in the form of those adorned all over with all emblems,[267] some in the form of physicians, some in the form of merchants, some in the form of disciples, some in the form of dancers, some in the form of devotees to deities, and some in the form of those skilled in all crafts, all of them appearing in villages, towns, market towns, regions, and capitals.

some appeared in the form of mendicants, some in the form of priests, some in bodies adorned head to foot with particular emblematic signs, some in the forms of scholars, scientists, doctors, some in the form of merchants, some in the form of ascetics, some in the form of entertainers, some in the form of pietists, some in the form of bearers of all kinds of arts and crafts—they were seen to have come, in their various forms, to all villages, cities, towns, communities, districts, and nations.

dus kyi dbang gis dus kyi rjes su 'brang zhing / ming dang / gzugs dang / lus mngon par bsgrub pa tha dad pa dang / lus kyi kha dog dang / dbyibs tshul dang 'dra ba dang / dbyangs rnam pa tha dad pa dang / skad rnam pa tha dad pa dang / spyod lam rnam pa tha dad pa dang / gnas rnam pa tha dad pas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa dang / 'gro ba thams cad mig 'phrul lta bur shes pa dang / bzo'i 'khor thams cad rab tu brjod pa dang / 'gro ba thams cad kyi shes pa brjod pas snang ba'i sgron ma dang / bde ba thams cad kyi byin gyi rlabs kyis brgyan pa dang / las thams cad snang bar byed pa'i 'od dang ldan pa dang / phyogs thams cad theg pa la gnas pas rab tu sbyong ba dang / byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa chos thams cad kyi dkyil 'khor rab tu snang ba la spyod cing / sems can yongs su smin par bya ba dang / gdul ba'i don du grong dang / grong khyer dang / grong rdal dang / ljongs dang / khams dang / rgyal po'i gnas dag tu phyin par snang ngo/ /

They appeared at the times that were the appropriate times, assuming different appropriate bodies, with different colors and body shapes, different voices, different languages, different kinds of conduct, and different kinds of residence. They practiced the bodhisattva conduct in which all beings are known to be illusions, which illuminated the entire realm of crafts, which was a bright lamp that revealed the knowledge of all beings, which was adorned with the blessing of all truths,[268] which had the light that illuminated all Dharmas,[269] and which purified beings in the yānas in all directions, and they practiced the bodhisattva conduct that illuminated the entire domain of the Dharma. In order to ripen and guide beings, they appeared in villages, towns, market towns, regions, and capitals.

With mastery of proper timing, proceeding according to the time, by modification of adapted forms and appearances, modifications of tone, language, deportment, situation, carrying out the practices of enlightening beings, which are like the cosmic network of all worlds, illumine the spheres of all practical arts, are lamps shedding light on the knowledge of all beings, are arrays of mystical displays of all realities, radiate the light of all truths, purify the establishment of vehicles of liberation of all places, and light up the spheres of all truths, they were seen to have come to all villages, towns, cities, districts, and nations for the purpose of leading sentient beings to perfection.
['jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pa]
Chapter 3. Mañjuśrī
Manjushri

de nas 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pa gnas pa med pa'i khang pa brtsegs pa na 'dug 'dug pa las/ bskal pa mthun pa'i byang chub sems dpa' de dag dang / rtag tu phyi bzhin 'brang ba'i lag na rdo rje dag dang / 'jig rten thams cad kyi nyams blta ba la brtson zhing / sangs rgyas thams cad bsnyen bkur bar smon pa'i sems dang ldan pa'i lus kyi rigs su gtogs pa'i lha dag dang / sngon gyi smon lam gyis rjes su 'brang ba'i rkang gis 'gro ba'i rigs su gtogs pa'i lha dag dang / chos mnyan pa la mngon par mos pa'i sa'i lha dag dang / snying rje chen po la brtson pa'i lu ma dang / mtsho dang / mtshe'u dang / rdzing bu dang / khron pa dang / chu klung gi lha dag dang / shes rab kyi 'od snang bas rab tu gsal ba'i me'i lha dag dang / rin po che'i cod pan thogs pa'i rlung gi lha dag dang / chos kyi phyogs snang bar khong du chud pa'i phyogs kyi lha dag dang / ma rig pa'i mun pa bsal ba la brtson pa'i mtshan mo'i lha dag dang / de bzhin gshegs pa'i nyi ma mngon par bsgrub pa la brtson pa'i nyi ma'i lha dag dang / chos kyi dbyings thams cad kyi nam mkha' brgyan pa la brtson pa'i nam mkha'i lha dag dang /

Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta was residing[270] in his kūṭāgāra together with bodhisattvas who had the same conduct; vajrapāṇis who constantly followed him; devas with physical bodies whose minds aspired to serve all the buddhas and were dedicated to bringing power to the entire world; devas who walked on foot following their past aspirations; devas of the earth who aspired to hear the Dharma; devas of pools, lakes, ponds, reservoirs, wells, and rivers who were dedicated to great compassion; devas of fire who brought illumination through the light of wisdom; devas of the air who wore precious crowns; devas of the directions who illuminated the directions with wisdom; devas of the night who were dedicated to eliminating the darkness of ignorance; devas of the day who were dedicated to producing the daylight of the tathāgatas; devas of the sky who were dedicated to orbiting[271] in the sky of the entire realm of phenomena;

At that time Manjushri, in the form of a youth, was in his tower together with enlightening beings of equivalent practice, perpetually attendant thunderbolt bearers, physical deities who had undertaken the making of power for all worlds and were willingly committed to attendance on all buddhas, footstep-following deities committed to past vows, earth deities intent on hearing the Teaching, greatly compassionate deities of springs, lakes pools, reservoirs, and rivers, deities of fire shining with the radiance of the power of the light of wisdom, crowned deities of wind, area deities with knowledge illumining all regions, night deities involved in dispelling the darkness of ignorance, day deities involved in bringing forth the day of those who arrive at Thusness, sky deities engaged in the adornment of the space of all elements of reality,

'gro ba thams cad srid pa'i rgya mtsho las bsgral bar brtson pa'i gangs chen mtsho'i lha dag dang / thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du tshogs yang dag par bsags pa la brtson zhing / dge ba'i rtsa ba'i sgo mngon par 'phags pa'i sems dang ldan pa'i ri'i lha dag dang / 'gro ba thams cad kyi lus brgyan par brtson zhing sangs rgyas thams cad kyi kha dog dang / byin gyi rlabs la smon cing brtson pa'i chu klung gi lha dag dang / 'gro ba thams cad kyi sems kyi grong rdal yongs su bskyang bar brtson pa'i grong gi lha dag dang / thams cad mkhyen pa'i chos kyi grong khyer du smon cing mos pa'i klu'i dbang po dag dang / sems can thams cad yongs su bsrung ba la zhugs pa'i gnod sbyin gyi dbang po dag dang / sems can thams cad kyi dga' ba'i shugs rnam par 'phel bar bya ba la brtson pa'i dri za'i dbang po dag dang / yi kyi rgyud thams cad rnam par bzlog pa la brtson pa'i grul bum gyi dbang po dag dang /

devas of the ocean[272] who were dedicated to rescuing beings from the ocean of existence; devas of mountains who were dedicated to gathering the accumulation of omniscience and whose minds had ascended to the summit[273] of the roots of merit; devas of rivers who were dedicated to adorning all beings and who were dedicated to aspiring to the characteristics and supernatural power of all the buddhas; devas of towns who were dedicated to caring for the towns that are the minds of all beings; nāga lords who were devoted to and longed for the town of the omniscient Dharma;[274] yakṣa lords who were engaged in protecting all beings; gandharva lords who were dedicated to increasing the power of joy in all beings; kumbhāṇḍa lords who were dedicated to preventing rebirth as pretas;

ocean deities involved in rescuing all beings from the ocean of existence, mountain deities involved in gathering the store of all knowledge with a mind based on transcendentally lofty virtue, river deities engaged in adorning the bodies of all beings with the vow to cause all the qualities of buddhas to appear, city deities engaged in protecting the city of the mind of all beings, and with dragon chiefs devoted to the city of all truths, spirit chiefs able to protect all beings, celestial musician chiefs engaged in increasing the bliss of all beings, demon chiefs engaged in repulsing all ghostlike tendencies,

sems can thams cad srid pa'i rgya mtsho nas gdon pa'i smon lam gyis zhugs pa'i nam mkha' lding gi dbang po dag dang / 'jig rten thams cad las 'phags pa'i de bzhin gshegs pa'i sku dang / stobs yongs su bsgrub par smon lam yongs su bskyed pa'i lha ma yin gyi dbang po dag dang / de bzhin gshegs pa mthong bas dga' bar gyur cing / lus rab tu 'dud pa'i lto 'phye chen po'i dbang po dag dang / 'khor ba las skyo ba'i yid dang ldan zhing ngor lta ba'i lha'i dbang po dag dang / rim gro chen po rab tu byed cing lus rab tu 'dud pa'i tshangs pa'i dbang po dag dang /

garuḍa lords who were engaged in aspiring to bring all beings out of the ocean of existence; asura lords who had the aspiration to attain the body and power of the Tathāgata, which have transcended the entire world; mahoraga lords who rejoiced in seeing the Tathāgata and bowed down to him; deva lords who had been saddened by saṃsāra and gazed with admiration; and lords of Brahmakāyika devas who bowed down with great respect.

bird chiefs committed to taking all beings up out of the ocean of existence, titans resolved to perfect the power of the body of those who arrive at Thusness, which is beyond all worlds, serpent chiefs with bowed bodies who had attained the joy of the vision of Buddha, celestial chiefs appalled by the whirl of birth and death who looked to what is higher, and most respectful Brahma chiefs in attitudes of reverence;

lhan cig tu de dag gis rim gro chen pos mngon par bstod de mchod cing / de lta bu'i byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par gnon pa'i rgyan phun sum tshogs pa dang ldan par rang rang gi gnas nas byung ste/ bcom ldan 'das la g.yas phyogs su bskor ba lan brgya phrag du ma zhig tu byas nas/ mchod pa rnam pa du mas mchod de/ bcom ldan 'das kyi spyan snga nas phyir byung nas/ lho phyogs logs su yul rgyu zhing song ngo// //

Mañjuśrī, together with them, displaying the prowess of a bodhisattva, respectfully made praises and offerings. Then he came out of his abode and circumambulated the Bhagavat many hundreds of times, keeping him to his right, and made many offerings. He then left the presence of the Bhagavat and departed to the land of the southern region.

with a parade of such enlightening beings, the enlightening being Manjushri came forth from his place, circled the Buddha hundreds of times to his right, made many offerings to Buddha, then left the presence of the Buddha and went south on a journey in the human realm.
bam po brgyad cu rtsa dgu pa/

de nas sangs rgyas kyi byin gyi rlabs kyis/ tshe dang ldan pa shA ti'i bus/ 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pa byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par 'phrul ba'i rgyan phun sum tshogs pa de 'dra bas dze ta'i tshal nas byung ste/ lho phyogs logs su 'gro ba mthong nas de 'di snyam du gyur te/ bdag kyang 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur ba dang lhan cig tu yul rgyu zhing 'gro'o snyam nas/

Through the blessing of the Buddha, Brother Śāriputra saw Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, who, with that display of bodhisattva miracles, departed from Jetavana and went to the southern region. He thought, “I will go with Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta to that land.”

Then the venerable Shariputra, by the power of Buddha, seeing the young Manjushri with this transfigured array of enlightening beings having left the Jeta grove and going south, conceived the desire to go on the journey to the human world with Manjushri.

de dge slong drug cu tsam gyis bskor cing mdun du byas te/ rang gi gnas nas byung nas/ bcom ldan 'das gang na ba der song ste/ bcom ldan 'das kyi zhabs gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal nas bcom ldan 'das la zhus te/ bcom ldan 'das kyis gnang ba dang / bcom ldan 'das la lan gsum bskor ba byas nas/ bcom ldan 'das kyi spyan snga nas phyir byung ste/ 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pa gang na ba der/ dge slong lhan cig tu spyod pa rab tu byung nas ring po ma lon pa gsar du zhugs pa sha stag ste/ 'di ltar dge slong rgya mtsho'i blo dang / legs par byin pa chen po dang / bsod nams kyi 'od dang / bu chen po dang / kun khyab sbyin pa dang / rnam dag spyod pa dang / lha'i dpal dang / dbang po'i blo gros dang / tshangs pa'i dam pa dang / dge slong zhi ba'i blo gros dang / de dag la sogs pa'i dge slong drug cu tsam

Leading his following of sixty bhikṣus, he left where he was sitting, approached the Bhagavat, bowed his head to the Bhagavat’s feet, and asked for the Bhagavat’s permission. When the Bhagavat had given it, Śāriputra circumambulated him three times, left the presence of the Bhagavat, and went to where Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta had gone, together with his following of sixty bhikṣus who had all newly and not long before entered homelessness. They were the bhikṣus Sāgarabuddhi, Mahāsudata, Puṇyaprabha, Mahāvatsa, Vibhudatta, Viśuddhacārin, Devaśrī, Indramati, Brahmottama, Praśāntamati, and others.

With a group of sixty monks he went forth from where he was and approached the Buddha. Going up to the Buddha, he bowed his head to the Buddha’s feet, then gazed at the Buddha; given permission by the Buddha, he circled the Buddha three times to his right, and went to Manjushri, accompanied by those sixty monks, who were staying with him and who were novices, having but recently left home. Among those sixty monks were Sagarabuddhi, Mahasudatta, Punyaprabha, Mahavatsa, Vibhudatta, Vishuddhacarin, Devashri, Indramati, Brahmottama, Prashantamati, and others.

kun kyang / sngon gyi rgyal ba la bya ba byas pa/ dge ba'i rtsa ba skyed pa/ mos pa zab mor gyur pa; dad pa'i mig yongs su dag pa/ sems rgya chen pos yongs su spyod pa/ sangs rgyas kyi chos rnam par blta ba la mthu yod pa/ chos kyi ngo bo nyid dang rang bzhin nges par rtogs pa'i sems dang ldan pa/ gzhan la phan par gyur pa'i blo can de bzhin gshegs pa'i yon tan la mngon par mos pa/ 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pa'i chos bstan pas 'dul ba sha stag dang 'grogs shing mdun du byas te/ sngon du bdar nas/ 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pa gang na ba der dong ngo/ /

They had all served jinas in the past, planted[275] the roots of merit, had profound aspiration, had the purified eyes of faith, practiced with a vast mentality, had the power to see the buddhas in the directions, had realized the nature and character of the Dharma, had the intention to benefit others, aspired to the qualities of the Tathāgata, and had been guided by the Dharma teaching of Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta. Leading those followers, Śāriputra went to where Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta had gone.

All those monks had served past buddhas, had planted roots of goodness, had far-reaching zeal, had thoroughly purified faith and reason, were great in understanding and action, were capable of viewing the realm of Buddha and comprehended the inherent nature of things, were intent on the welfare and development of others, and sought the qualities of those who arrive at Thusness. They were guided by the teaching of Manjushri.
de nas tshe dang ldan pa shA ri'i bus/ de ltar lam du zhugs te 'dong ba'i tshe/ dge slong de dag kun la bltas nas/ dge slong rgya mtsho'i blo la smras pa/

When Brother Śāriputra was on the way, he looked at all those bhikṣus and said to the bhikṣu Sāgarabuddhi, “Sāgarabuddhi, regard the bodhisattva Mañjuśrī upon a path that has a checkerboard pattern[276] and displays of his path as he walks along it.
At that point the venerable Shariputra, on the way, looked at all the monks and said to Sagarabuddhi,

rgya mtsho'i blo/ byang chub sems dpa' 'jam dpal gyi lus mtshan dang dpe byad bzang pos rnam par brgyan cing yongs su dag pa/ lha dang mir bcas par bsam gyis mi khyab pa dang / 'od kyi dkyil 'khor yongs su dag cing sems can tshad med pa'i dga' ba yongs su skyed pa dang / 'od zer gyi dra ba'i rgyan sems can dpag tu med pa'i sdug bsngal rab tu zhi bar byed pa dang / 'khor phun sum tshogs pa sngon gyi dge ba'i rtsa ba yongs su bzung ba dang /

“His pure body is inconceivable to devas and humans. It is beautified by the signs and features of a great being. It has a pure halo of light. It emits a display of a network of light rays that brings joy to countless beings. It brings to an end the sufferings of countless beings. It is accompanied by a perfect entourage, and it is in possession of past roots of merit.

“See the inconceivable purity of form of Manjushri, along with the celestial and earthly beings, his variety of marks and embellishments, the purity of his sphere of radiance, his web of light beams developing countless beings, extinguishing all miseries, his wealth of followers, embraced by past virtues, arraying the path, which is eight steps wide.

lam gyi rgyan mgron lam mig mangs ris su gnas pa dang / lam rnam par gnon pa'i rgyan phyogs kyi dkyil 'khor thams cad la mngon par lta bar gnas pa dang / bsod nams phun sum tshogs pa'i rgyan g.yas g.yon nas gter chen po mngon par 'thon pa dang /
“The displays of the prowess of his path are directed toward the domain of every direction; the displays of his perfection of merit issue forth to the right and left as great treasures.
See the magnificent arrays of the procession on the path, facing the realms in all directions as they go, with overflowing great treasuries, auspicious and fair arrays, on the left and right;

sngon gyi sangs rgyas la rim gro byas pa'i dge ba'i rtsa ba dang rgyu mthun pas shing gi gseb thams cad nas rgyan mang po 'byung ba dang / 'jig rten gyi dbang po thams cad la mchod pa'i sprin gyi char mngon par 'bebs shing btud de phyag 'tshal ba dang / phyogs bcu nas de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyis 'od zer gyi dra ba'i dkyil 'khor mang po bkye ba sangs rgyas kyi chos thams cad rab tu sgrog cing spyi bor 'char ba la ltos shig ces/

“These displays emerge from within all the trees as the result of his roots of merit from serving past buddhas. All the lords of the world bow down to him and send down a rain of clouds of offerings. All the tathāgatas in the ten directions emanate[277] multitudes of disks composed of nets of light rays that resound with all the Dharma of the buddhas and descend[278] onto the crown of his head.”

magnificent arrays of adornments emerge from within all the trees growing out of the roots of goodness of attendance on past buddhas; all the world chiefs are showering clouds of offerings in respect; from the curl of hair between the eyebrows of all buddhas from the ten directions, spheres of networks of light beams emanate, uttering all teachings of buddhas, and enter Manjushri’s head.”

de dag la sogs pa tshe dang ldan pa shA ri'i bus 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pa lam du zhugs pa'i yon tan gyi rgyan tshad med pa dag dge slong de dag la yongs su bstan to/ / brjod do/ / bshad do/ / smos so/ / bkrol lo/ / rab tu brjod do/ / rnam par phye'o/ / gsal bar byas so/ /

Beginning with the above, Brother Śāriputra described, explained, announced, narrated, related, elucidated, and brought illumination to the bhikṣus concerning Mañjuśrī’s measureless displays of the qualities of following the path.
Beginning with these, Shariputra revealed and described to the monks measureless arrays of qualities of the procession of Manjushri,

de ltar gnas brtan shA ri'i bus 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pa'i yon tan ji tsam du brjod pa de tsam du dge slong de dag gi sems rnam par dag par gyur to/ / rab tu dang bar gyur to/ / dga' ba'i shugs rnam par 'phel bar gyur to/ / mos pa skyes par gyur to/ / de dag gi sems kyi rgyud las su rung bar gyur to/ / dbang po rab tu dang bar gyur to/ / yid bde ba rnam par 'phel bar gyur to/ / yid mi bde ba rab tu byang bar gyur to; ;sems kyi skyon dang bral bar gyur to/ / sgrib pa thams cad phyir ldog par gyur to/ / sangs rgyas blta ba la mngon par mos par gyur to/ / sangs rgyas kyi chos la sems rab tu gzhol bar gyur to/ / byang chub sems dpa'i dbang po yongs su dag par gyur to/ / byang chub sems dpa'i dad pa'i shugs skyes par gyur to/ / snying rje chen po 'byung bar gyur to; ;pha rol tu phyin pa'i dkyil 'khor gnon par gyur to/ / snying rje chen po yongs su skyes par gyur to/ / phyogs bcu'i sangs rgyas rgya mtsho yongs su snang bar gyur to/ /

The more that Sthavira Śāriputra described Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta’s qualities, the more the minds of the bhikṣus became purified and became clearer, the strength of their joy increased, delight arose, the continuum of their minds became adept, their faculties became clearer, their happiness increased, they cast off unhappiness, they became free of the mind’s faults, they repelled all obscurations, they became intent on seeing the Buddha, their minds turned to the Buddha’s Dharma, their bodhisattva faculties were purified, the power of their bodhisattva faith developed, great compassion arose, they gained the prowess of the domain of the perfections, they fully developed great compassion, and they perceived the ocean of buddhas in the ten directions.

and as Shariputra spoke of the qualities of Manjushri, the minds of the monks were purified, calmed, and delighted; they were thrilled, their mental states became suitable for religious practice, their senses became clear and tranquil, their gladness increased and their depression vanished, all obstructions disappeared, they came face to face with the vision of Buddha, they dedicated their minds to the buddha-teachings, their enlightening faculties were clarified, the power of faith of enlightening beings rose in them, great compassion developed in them, they entered the sphere of the transcendences, they conceived great vows and came to perceive the oceans of buddhas in the ten directions:
de ltar de dag thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du mos pa'i shugs thob par gyur nas 'di skad 'dzer to/ / mkhan po/ bdag cag kyang skyes bu dam pa de'i drung du phyin par mdzad du gsol zhes nas/
Having attained the power of aspiration to omniscience, they spoke these words: “Upādhyāya, we pray that we too may be able to go into the presence of that supreme being.”
with this supreme power of faith in omniscience, they said to Shariputra, “Teacher, lead us to the presence of that wise person.”

de nas tshe dang ldan pa shA ri'i bu dge slong de dag dang 'grogs te/ 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pa gang na ba der song nas 'di skad ces smras so/ / 'jam dpal/ dge slong 'di dag ni khyod la blta bar 'dod pa dag go /
Then Brother Śāriputra, together with the bhikṣus, went to where Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta was and said these words: “Mañjuśrī, these bhikṣus wish to see you.”
Then Shariputra went together with the monks to Manjushri and said, “O Manjushri, these monks want to see you.”
de nas 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pas dge slong de dag dang / 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor gyi sa'i phyogs de tsam dang bcas pa glang po'i lta stangs kyi sa gzi dang ldan par khyab par bltas pa dang /
Then Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, together with the entire circle of his followers, turned[279] and looked upon the bhikṣus with the majestic gaze of an elephant.
Then Manjushri, who was together with a great host of transfigured enlightening beings, turned with the gaze of an elephant and looked at the monks.

de'i rjes la dge slong de dag gis 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pa'i rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal nas/ thal mo sbyar te 'di skad ces smras so/ / skyes bu dam pa khyod mthong ba dang / khyod la phyag 'tshal ba'i dge ba'i rtsa ba 'di dang / bdag cag gi dge ba'i rtsa ba gzhan khyod kyis mkhyen pa dang / mkhan pos thugs su chud pa dang / gang yang bcom ldan 'das de bzhin gshegs pa shAkya thub pas mngon du gzigs pa'i dge ba'i rtsa ba des khyod ci 'dra bar de 'dra bar gyur te/ rnam pa 'di 'dra ba'i lus thob par shog cig /rnam pa 'di 'dra ba'i dbyangs dang / rnam pa 'di 'dra ba'i mtshan dang / 'di lta bu'i rnam par 'phrul pa dag kyang khyod ji lta ba bzhin thob par shog cig ces/

The bhikṣus bowed their heads to the feet of Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, and then with their palms together in reverence they said, “Holy being, through the roots of merit from seeing you and paying homage to you, and also our other roots of merit that you know we have, that our upādhyāya knows we have, and that the Bhagavat Tathāgata Śākyamuni sees we have, may we become like you. May we obtain bodies that are the same as yours, voices the same as yours, and features the same as yours, and may we attain miraculous powers the same as yours.”

The monks then bowed their heads to the feet of Manjushri, saluted him, and said, “By this root of goodness, witnessed by the blessed Shakyamuni Buddha—by the root of goodness may we become like you, may we attain bodies, voices, embellishments, and spiritual transfigurations like you.”

dge slong de dag gis de skad du smras pa dang / 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pas/ dge slong de dag la 'di skad ces smras so/ / dge slong dag /yongs su mi skyo ba'i sems bskyed pa bcu dang ldan pa'i rigs kyi bu'am/ rigs kyi bu mo theg pa chen po la zhugs pa ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i sa lta smos kyang ci smos kyi/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i sa yang gnon par 'gyur ro/ / bcu gang zhe na/

When the bhikṣus had said this, Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta said to the bhikṣus, “Bhikṣus, the noble man or noble woman with the ten unflagging motivations who enters the Mahāyāna will ascend to the level of a tathāgata, and therefore, it goes without saying,[280] to the level of a bodhisattva. What are those ten?

To this Manjushri replied, “A man or woman setting out on the Great Vehicle imbued with ten indefatigable determinations will enter the stage of realization of Thusness, to say nothing of the stage of enlightening beings. What are the ten?

'di lta ste/ de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad blta ba dang / bsnyen bkur ba dang / mchod pa dang / rim gro bya ba la yongs su mi skyo ba'i sems bskyed pa dang / dge ba'i rtsa ba thams cad bsags pa las phyir mi ldog cing / yongs su mi skyo ba'i sems bskyed pa dang / chos thams cad btsal ba la yongs su mi skyo ba'i sems bskyed pa dang / byang chub sems dpa'i pha rol tu phyin pa thams cad sbyor ba la yongs su mi skyo ba'i sems bskyed pa dang / byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin thams cad yongs su bsgrub pa la yongs su mi skyo ba'i sems bskyed pa dang / dus gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa thams cad du 'jug pa la yongs su mi skyo ba'i sems bskyed pa dang / phyogs bcu'i sangs rgyas kyi zhing rgya mtsho rgyas par dgang zhing yongs su dag par bya ba la yongs su mi skyo ba'i sems bskyed pa dang / sems can gyi khams thams cad yongs su smin par bya ba dang / gdul ba la yongs su mi skyo ba'i sems bskyed pa dang / zhing dang bskal pa thams cad du byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa mngon par bsgrub pa la yongs su mi skyo ba'i sems bskyed pa dang / sangs rgyas kyi zhing thams cad kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi pha rol tu phyin pa sbyar bas/ sems can gcig yongs su smin par bya ba'i tshul du sems can thams cad yongs su smin par bya bas/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i stobs gcig yongs su bsgrub pa la yongs su mi skyo ba'i sems bskyed pa'o/ /

They are (1) the unflagging motivation to see, pay homage to, offer to, and serve all the tathāgatas; (2) the unflagging motivation to never abandon accumulating all roots of merit; (3) the unflagging motivation to seek all Dharmas; (4) the unflagging motivation to practice all the bodhisattva perfections; (5) the unflagging motivation to accomplish all the bodhisattva samādhis; (6) the unflagging motivation to enter all successive times; (7) the unflagging motivation to purify the extensive oceans of buddha realms in the ten directions; (8) the unflagging motivation to ripen and guide all realms of beings; (9) the unflagging motivation to accomplish the conduct of a bodhisattva in all realms and kalpas; and (10) the unflagging motivation to accomplish one power of the tathāgatas by ripening all beings in the way that one would ripen one being through the practice of perfections as numerous as the atoms in all buddha realms.

The indefatigable resolution to see, attend, and serve all buddhas; to build up all roots of goodness without retreating; to seek all truths; to practice all the transcendent ways of enlightening beings; to fully accomplish all concentrations of enlightening beings; to enter successively into all ages; to thoroughly purify all oceans of buddha-lands in the ten directions; to lead all realms of sentient beings to perfect development; to carry out the practices of enlightening beings in all lands and ages; to fully attain each power of buddhas by maturing all beings through the process of practicing as many transcendent ways as atoms in all buddha-lands to mature each being.

dge slong dag /yongs su mi skyo ba'i sems bskyed pa bcu po 'di dag dang ldan pa'i rigs kyi bu'am/ rigs kyi bu mo dad pa dang ldan pa ni/ dge ba'i rtsa ba thams cad la yongs su 'grub par 'gyur ro/ / 'khor ba'i rgyud thams cad las phyir ldog par 'gyur ro/ / 'jig rten gyi rgyud thams cad las gyen du 'phags par 'gyur ro/ / nyan thos dang / rang sangs rgyas kyi sa thams cad las yongs su 'da' bar 'gyur ro/ / de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi rigs dang rgyud du 'byung bar 'gyur ro/ / byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi smon lam la yang dag par 'grub par 'gyur ro/ / de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi yon tan gyi nan tan la rnam par dag par 'gyur ro/ / byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa thams cad la yongs su dag par 'gyur ro/ / de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi stobs la yang dag par 'byung bar 'gyur ro/ / bdud dang phas kyi rgol ba thams cad rab tu 'dul bar 'gyur ro/ / byang chub sems dpa'i sa yongs su gnon par 'gyur ro/ / de bzhin gshegs pa'i sa dang shin tu nye bar 'gyur ro/ /

“Bhikṣus, the noble man or noble woman with faith who has these ten unflagging motivations will accomplish all roots of merit, will turn away from all existences in saṃsāra, will transcend all the worldly existences, will transcend all the levels of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, will become a member of the family of all the tathāgatas, will accomplish the aspirations of all bodhisattvas, will purify the practice of the qualities of all the tathāgatas, will purify all bodhisattva conduct, will have the strength of all tathāgatas, will subdue all māras and adversaries, will ascend to the level of bodhisattvas, and will approach the level of the tathāgatas.”

Men or women with faith who are imbued with these ten indefatigable determinations grow in all roots of goodness, leave all compulsive, routine mundane tendencies, drop out of all social castes, go beyond all stages of individual emancipation, are born in the family of all buddhas, fulfill the vows of enlightening beings, become pure with the attainment of all qualities of the enlightened, become clarified in all the practices of enlightening beings, develop all the powers of buddhas, overcome all demons and challengers, progress through all the stages of enlightening beings, and reach buddhahood.”

de nas dge slong de dag gis chos kyi tshul 'di thos nas/ sangs rgyas thams cad rnam par mthong ba la chags pa med pa'i mig gi yul zhes bya ba'i ting nge 'dzin thob par gyur to/ / de'i mthus phyogs bcu mtha' yas mu med pa'i 'jig rten gyi khams na bzhugs pa'i de bzhin gshegs pa'i 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor mthong bar gyur to/ / 'jig rten gyi khams de dag gi 'gro ba'i rgyud du skyes pa'i sems can de dag kyang ma lus par mthong bar gyur to/ / 'jig rten gyi khams de dag gi sems can rnams kyang ma lus par mthong bar gyur to/ / 'jig rten gyi khams de dag kyang rnam par phye ba sna tshogs su mthong bar gyur to/ / 'jig rten gyi khams de dag na rdul shin tu phra ba ji snyed yod pa de dag kyang bgrang ba'i tshul gyis rab tu shes par gyur to/ / sems can de dag gi rin po che'i gnas dang longs spyod de dag kyang mthong bar gyur to/ / de bzhin gshegs pa de dag gi dbyangs kyi yan lag rgya mtsho yang thos par gyur to/ / chos bstan pa de dag kyang tshig dang / yi ge dang / nges pa'i tshig dang / skad dang / ming dang / brdas yongs su shes par gyur to/ / sems can de dag gi sems dang / dbang po dang / bsam pa la yang rnam par lta bar gyur to/ / sngon gyi mtha' dang / phyi ma'i mtha'i tshe rabs bcu yang rjes su dran par gyur to/ / de bzhin gshegs pa de dag gi chos kyi 'khor lo bcu'i nges pa'i tshig mngon par bsgrub pa la yang rab tu zhugs par gyur to/ / rdzu 'phrul gyis rnam par 'phrul pa mngon par bsgrub pa bcu la yang rab tu zhugs par gyur to/ / bstan pa'i tshul mngon par bsgrub pa bcu la yang rab tu zhugs par gyur to; ;rjes su bstan pa'i tshig mngon par bsgrub pa bcu la yang rab tu zhugs par gyur to/ / de bzhin gshegs pa de dag gi tha dad pa yang dag par mkhyen pa'i tshul mngon par bsgrub pa bcu la yang rab tu zhugs par gyur to/ /

When the bhikṣus heard this way of the Dharma, they attained the samādhi the unimpeded vision that sees all the buddhas. Through its power they saw all the tathāgatas and the circles of their assemblies that were present in infinite, endless world realms in the ten directions. They also saw every being that had been reborn into an existence in those world realms. They saw every being in those world realms.[281] They saw the various divisions of those world realms. They knew the number of atoms in those worlds. They saw the residences and adornments made of jewels[282] that those beings enjoyed. They heard the ocean of the aspects of speech of those tathāgatas. They knew those Dharma teachings through their words, letters, definitions, languages,[283] names, and symbols.[284] They viewed the minds, faculties, and aspirations of those beings. They knew ten lifetimes back into the past and ten lifetimes into the future. They comprehended the explanations of ten turnings of Dharma wheels by those tathāgatas. They comprehended ten attainments of manifestations of miraculous powers. They comprehended the accomplishment of ten ways given in the teachings. They comprehended ten explanations of the words of the teachings. They comprehended ten accomplishments of the analytic knowledge of those tathāgatas.

Then the monks, having heard this teaching, attained a concentration called sphere of the unobstructed eye of vision of all buddhas, by the experience of which they saw the circles of assemblies of the buddhas in all worlds throughout the ten directions. They also saw all the beings in those worlds, and they also saw the various differentiations in those worlds. They also knew how many atoms were in these worlds. They also saw all the dwellings and furniture of those beings, made of various precious substances. They also heard the oceans of the qualities of the voice and the buddhas in those worlds, and understood the various statements, allusions, expressions, mystic formulae, terminology, and concepts of their teachings. They also discerned the minds, faculties, and dispositions of the beings in those worlds, and called to mind the events of ten lives past and future. They also comprehended the utterance of ten cycles of teaching of those buddhas. They also comprehended ten states produced by mystical powers, ten productions of guiding principles, and ten productions of instructive statements. They also comprehended ten accomplishments of analytic knowledge of those buddhas.

ting nge 'dzin de thob ma thag tu byang chub kyi sems kyi yan lag stong phrag bcu yang yongs su rdzogs par gyur to/ / ting nge 'dzin stong phrag bcu yang yongs su non par gyur to/ / pha rol tu phyin pa'i yan lag stong phrag bcu yang rnam par dag par gyur te/ snang ba chen po rab tu thob cing shes rab chen po'i dkyil 'khor gyis snang bar gyur pa de dag gis/ byang chub sems dpa'i mngon par shes pa bcu rab tu thob par gyur to/ /

As soon as they attained that samādhi, they perfected ten thousand aspects of the aspiration to enlightenment, they attained ten thousand samādhis, they purified ten thousand aspects of the perfections, they attained a great radiance, they illuminated the domain of great wisdom, and they attained ten bodhisattva clairvoyances.

When they attained this concentration, they developed ten thousand qualities of the determination of enlightenment, entered ten thousand concentrations and purified ten thousand aspects of transcendence; having attained great illumination, being illumined by the sphere of great wisdom, they attained ten mystic knowledges of enlightening beings.

de ltar mngon par shes pa'i myu gu gzhon zhing shin tu phra ba thob ste/ byang chub tu sems skyes pa brtan pa la gnas pa de dag 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pas/ byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po'i spyod pa la yang dag par bskul nas rab tu bkod do/ /

They who had thus attained the small young seedlings of clairvoyance and had gained the resolute aspiration to enlightenment were then inspired to and established in completely good bodhisattva conduct[285] by Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta.
Manjushri exhorted and led them, now with soft and delicate sprouts of mystic knowledge and firm determination for enlightenment, into the practice of the universally good enlightening being.

de ltar byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po'i spyod pa la rab tu gnas pa de dag smon lam chen po rgya mtsho la zhugs shing mngon par bsgrub par gyur to/ / de ltar smon lam chen po rgya mtshos mngon par bsgrubs pa'i sems rnam par dag pas lus yongs su dag pa rab tu thob par gyur to/ / lus rnam par dag pas lus yang ba rab tu thob par gyur to/ / de ltar lus rnam par dag pa dang / lus yang bas mngon par shes pa'i sgo de dag shin tu yangs par byed pas mi nyams shing / rjes su 'brang ba'i mngon par shes pa rab tu thob par gyur to/ / mngon par shes pa de dag thob pas/ 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pa'i rkang pa'i drung nas kyang mi g.yo la/ sangs rgyas kyi chos thams cad yongs su bsgrub pa'i phyir phyogs bcur yang de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi sku'i 'phrin las kyi sprin mngon par bsgrub par gyur to/ /

They who were thus established in completely good bodhisattva conduct entered an ocean of great aspirations and fulfilled them. Through fulfilling an ocean of great aspirations with a pure motivation they attained purity of the body. Through purity of the body they attained lightness of body. Through that purity of body and lightness of body they vastly increased their entrances to clairvoyances. They attained everlasting clairvoyances. Through that attainment of clairvoyance, while constantly remaining at the feet of Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta and in order to accomplish all the Dharmas of the buddhas, they created clouds of the activities[286] of the bodies of all the tathāgatas in the ten directions.

Based on the practice of the universally good enlightening being, they entered into the oceans of great vows and began to carry them out. By undertaking the oceans of great vows, and by purification of mind, they attained purity of body; by physical purity they gained physical lightness, by which physical purity and lightness they opened wide the doors to mystic knowledge and attained undiminishing mystic knowledge. By this attainment of mystic knowledge they appeared in multitudes of bodies to all the buddhas in the ten directions for the sake of accomplishing all Buddha teachings, yet without leaving the presence of Manjushri.

de nas 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pas/ dge slong de dag bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu bkod nas/ mthar gyis yul rgyu zhing lho phyogs logs skyid pa'i 'byung gnas zhes bya ba'i grong rdal chen po gang na ba der logs su song ste phyin nas/ grong rdal chen po skyid pa'i 'byung gnas kyi shar phyogs logs na nags tshal chen po sA la sna tshogs kyi rgyal mtshan gyi rgyan ces bya ba sngon gyi sangs rgyas bzhugs bzhugs pa'i mchod rten/ sems can smin par mdzad pa'i don du de bzhin gshegs pas byin gyis brlabs pa/ zhing mtha' yas par ming gi sgra rjes su grags pa/ sngon chad bcom ldan 'das byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa mdzad pa'i tshe/ yongs su btang bar dga' ba du ma yongs su btang ste/ sa'i phyogs de na lha dang / klu dang / gnod sbyin dang / dri za dang / lha ma yin dang / nam mkha' lding dang / mi'am ci dang / lto 'phye chen po dang / mi dang / mi ma yin pa rnams rtag tu rgyun mi 'chad par mchod pa la brtson pa'i gnas yod pa der/ 'khor dang bcas te phyin nas/

Then Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, having established those bhikṣus in the aspiration to the highest, complete enlightenment, traveled to the southern region and came to the great city called Dhanyākara. Having reached there, he and his entourage went the east of Dhanyākara, where there was a great forest called Vicitrasāladhvajavyūha.[287] It was a sacred place where buddhas of the past had dwelled. It had been consecrated by the tathāgatas for the ripening of beings. Its name was renowned throughout endless realms. It was a place where the Bhagavat, when he was practicing bodhisattva conduct in the past, performed many difficult actions of generosity. It was a place where devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, and nonhumans constantly engaged in making offerings.

Then Manjushri, having set those monks on the foundation of unexcelled true enlightenment, continued his journey to the human realm and came to a great city in the south named Dhanyakara. There he stayed with his retinue in a forest called Array of Various Standards of Strength, to the east of the city, at a shrine where past buddhas had dwelt, established by buddhas for the sake of perfecting sentient beings, the repute of which resounded in infinite lands, a place where the Buddha, in the past, carrying out the practice of an enlightening being, relinquished many things that are difficult to relinquish, a place where gods, dragons, goblins, nymphs, titans, birds, centaurs, serpents, humans, and nonhumans always presented offerings to the earth.

der 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pas mdo sde chos kyi dbyings kyi tshul rab tu snang ba zhes bya ba mdo sde bye ba khrag khrig brgya stong phrag bcu 'byung ba bstan to/ / de bstan pa'i tshe/ rgya mtsho chen po nas klu bye ba khrag khrig brgya stong du ma nye bar lhags te/ de dag gis chos kyi tshul de thos nas/ klu'i rgyud la rnam par smod cing de bzhin gshegs pa'i yon tan la mos par gyur nas klu'i rgyud rnam par bzlog ste/ lha dang mir skya ba yongs su 'dzin par gyur nas/ der klu stong phrag bcu bla na med par rdzogs pa'i byang chub las phyir mi ldog par gyur to/ / chos de bstan pa'i tshe/ sems can gyi khams mtha' dang dbus med pa theg pa gsum gyis dus gzhan dang gzhan du rnam par dul bar gyur to/ /

There Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta taught the sūtra called The Radiance of the Way of the Essence of Phenomena, from which arose a septillion[288] sūtras. During that teaching, many hundred thousand quintillions of nāgas came from the great ocean. When they had heard that way of the Dharma, they became disgusted with their existences as nāgas and aspired to have the qualities of a tathāgata. They abandoned their nāga existences and gained rebirth as devas or humans. Ten thousand nāgas attained irreversibility from the highest, complete enlightenment. During the time he taught that Dharma, endlessly numerous realms of beings were guided through the three yānas.

There Manjushri expounded a scripture called Illumination of the Principles of the Cosmos, whence flowed ten hundred thousand trillion scriptures. As he was expounding the scripture, many tens of hundreds of thousands of trillions of dragons came to him from the ocean; having heard this teaching, disdaining the condition of dragons and desiring the qualities of buddhahood, they left the state of dragons and gained birth as celestial or human beings. There ten thousand dragons became irreversible in their progress toward supreme perfect enlightenment. And during his exposition of the teaching, innumerable beings were edified through the Three Vehicles.

de nas skyid pa'i 'byung gnas kyi mi rnams kyis/ 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pa'i skyid pa'i 'byung gnas kyi grong rdal du phyin te/ sA la sna tshogs kyi rgyan gyi gzhi 'di nyid na rnam par spyod do zhes thos nas/
The people in Dhanyākara heard that Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta had come to Dhanyākara and was dwelling in the sacred Vicitrasāladhvajavyūha.
Now the people of the city heard that Manjushri had come and was staying at the shrine in the forest. Having heard this,

dge bsnyen tshong dpon shes rab chen po la sogs pa dge bsnyen pha dang / dge bsnyen ma dang / khye'u dang / bu mo mang po dag so so nas 'khor lnga brgya lnga brgya dang bcas te/ skyid pa'i 'byung gnas kyi grong rdal nas byung nas/ 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pa gang na ba dar dong ngo/ /

The leading[289] upāsaka Mahāprajña and upāsakas, upāsikās, sons, and daughters, each accompanied by an entourage that numbered five hundred, came out from Dhanyākara city and went to where Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta was.
pious men and women, boys and girls, each a company of five hundred, led by Mahaprajna, the foremost of the pious men, went from the city to where Manjushri was.

de la dge bsnyen shes rab chen po ni/ dge bsnyen bzang pos byin dang / lhas byin dang / bsod nams 'od dang / grags pa'i lha dang / grags pas byin dang / zla ba'i dpal dang / zla ba dga' bo dang / blo gros bzang po dang / blo gros chen po dang / sgra gcan bzang po dang / dge bsnyen bzang po'i dpal dang / de dag la sogs pa dge bsnyen lnga brgyas ba skor cing mdun du byas te; 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pa gang na ba der dong nas/ 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pa'i rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te/ 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pa la lan gsum du bskor ba byas nas phyogs gcig tu 'khod do/ /

The upāsaka Mahāprajña, with other upāsakas such as Sudatta, Vasudatta, Puṇyaprabha, Yaśodeva, Somaśriti, Somanandi, Sumati, Mahāmati, Rāhulabhadra, Bhadraśrī, and so on, each with an entourage of five hundred upāsakas, came to where Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta was, bowed their heads to his feet, circumambulated Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta three times, and sat to one side.

Then the pious man Mahaprajna, with a company of five hundred pious men such as Sudatta, Vasudatta, Punyaprabha, Yashodeva, Somashri, Somanandi, Sumati, Mahamati, Rahulabhadra, and Bhadrashri, went to Manjushri, bowed their heads to his feet, circled him three times, and then sat to one side.

de la dge bsnyen ma shes rab chen mo ni/ dge bsnyen ma 'od bzang mo dang / lus bzang mo dang / dge ba yod pa dang / dge ba'i dpal dang / zla ba'i 'od dang / dpal gyi 'od dang / dpal bzang mo dang / dge bsnyen ma mig bzang mo dang / de dag la sogs pa dge bsnyen ma lnga brgyas bskor cing mdun du byas te/ 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pa gang na ba der dong nas/ 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pa'i rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te/ 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pa la lan gsum du bskor ba byas nas phyogs gcig tu 'khod do/ /
