The upāsikā named Mahāprajñā, with other upāsikās such as Suprabhā, Sugātrā, Subhadrā, Bhadraśrī, Candraprabhāsā, Ketuprabhā, Śrībhadrā, and Sulocanā and so on, each with an entourage of five hundred upāsikās, came to where Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta was, bowed their heads to his feet, circumambulated Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta three times, and sat to one side.

Then a pious woman named Mahaprajna, with a company of five hundred pious women including Suprabha, Sugatra, Subhadra, Bhadrashri, Candraprabhasa, Ketuprabha, Shribhadra, and Sulocana, went to Manjushri, bowed to him and circled him, and then sat to one side.

de la tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang ni tshong dpon gyi bu brtul zhugs bzang po dang / tshul khrims bzang po dang / ngang tshul bzang po dang / rnam par gnon pa bzang po dang / bsam pa bzang po dang / blo gros bzang po dang / blo bzang po dang / mig bzang po dang / lag pa bzang po dang / tshong dpon gyi bu 'od bzang po dang / de dag la sogs pa tshong dpon gyi bu lnga brgyas bskor cing mdun du byas te/ 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pa gang na ba der dong nas/ 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pa'i rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te/ 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pa la lan gsum du bskor ba byas nas phyogs gcig tu 'khod do/ /

The head merchant’s son[290] Sudhana, with other sons of head merchants such as Suvrata, Suśīla, Svācāra, Suvikrāmin, Sucinti, Sumati, Subuddhi, Sunetra, Subāhu, Suprabha, and so on, each with an entourage of five hundred sons of head merchants, came to where Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta was, bowed their heads to his feet, circumambulated Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta three times, and sat to one side.

Then Sudhana, an outstanding boy, together with a company of five hundred outstanding boys including Suvrata, Sushila, Svacara, Suvikrami, Sucinti, Sumati, Subuddhi, Sunetra, Subahu, and Suprabha, went to Manjushri, bowed to him and circled him, and then sat to one side.

de la khyim bdag shes rab chen po'i bu mo dge ba bzang mo ni/ bu mo bzang mo dang / yid du 'ong ba'i bzhin dang / brtan pa'i blo gros dang / dpal bzang mo dang / tshangs pas byin pa dang / dpal gyi 'od dang / bu mo 'od bzang mo la sogs pa bu mo lnga brgyas bskor cing mdun du byas te/ 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pa gang na ba der dong nas/ 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pa'i rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te/ 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pa la lan gsum du bskor ba byas nas phyogs gcig tu 'khod do/ /

Subhadrā, the daughter of the layman Mahāprajña, with other daughters such as Bhadrā, Abhirāmavartā, Dṛḍhamatī, Śrībhadrā, Brahmadattā, Śrīprabhā, Suprabhā, and so on, each with an entourage of five hundred daughters, came to where Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta was, bowed their heads to his feet, circumambulated Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta three times, and sat to one side.

Then the girl Subhadra, daughter of the householder Mahaprajna, together with a group of five hundred girls including Bhadra, Abhiramavarta, Drdhamati, Brahmadatta, Shribhadra, Shriprabha, and Suprabha, went to Manjushri, bowed to him and circled him, and then sat to one side.

de nas 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pas skyid pa'i 'byung gnas kyi grong rdal nas skyes pa dang / bud med dang / khye'u dang / bu mo de dag 'dus te 'khod par shes nas/ bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du bstan pa'i byin gyis zil gyis gnan te/ byams pa chen po'i byin gyis sim par byas nas/ snying rje chen po'i byin gyis chos bstan pa mngon par bsgrubs te/ ye shes kyi byin gyis sems dang bsam pa rnam par phye nas tha dad pa yang dag par shes pa chen pos chos bstan par dga' ste/ tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la bltas so/ /

Then Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, knowing that the men, women, boys, and girls from Dhanyākara had gathered and assembled, overwhelmed them with the magnificence of his teaching in accordance with their wishes, comforted them with the magnificence of his great love, accomplished the teaching of the Dharma through the magnificence of his great compassion, and investigated their minds and aspirations through the magnificence of his wisdom. Delighting in teaching the Dharma with his great discernment, he observed Sudhana, the head merchant’s son.

Then Manjushri, seeing that the women, men, boys and girls from the city had gathered and were seated, according to their dispositions overwhelmed them with his power over appearance, soothed them with his power of great benevolence, undertook to teach them with his power of great compassion, considered their mentalities with his power of knowledge, and, imbued with great analytic intelligence, wishing to expound the truth, he observed the outstanding boy Sudhana:

tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang zhes bya ba/ ci'i phyir nor bzang zhes bya zhe na/ tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang zhes bya ba/ thog ma ma'i mngal du zhugs ma thag tu khyim de'i 'khor kun nas rnam par phye ba'i rin po che sna bdun gyi sdong po 'thon par gyur to/ / rin po che'i sdong po de dag gi 'og na rin po che'i gter bdun yod de/ gser dang / dngul dang / bai DUr+ya dang / shel dang / mu tig dmar po dang / asma gar b+ha dang / mu sa ra gal pa dang / rin po che de bdun gyi rin po che'i sdong po de dag kyang gter de dag nas skyes te/ sa'i gzhi brtol nas mngon par 'thon par gyur to/ /

He said, “Why is Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, called Sudhana? The instant that Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, entered his mother’s womb, all around his home seven precious sprouts[291] emerged. Beneath those precious sprouts there were seven treasures of precious substances. Those precious sprouts made of those seven precious substances rose up through the ground from those treasures, which were gold, silver, beryl, crystal, red pearls, emeralds, and white coral.

“Why is Sudhana called Sudhana, which means ‘Good Wealth’? When Sudhana was conceived in his mother’s womb, there appeared in the house sprouts of seven precious substances, evenly distributed throughout the house. Beneath those precious sprouts were seven great treasuries, from which those sprouts emerged, splitting the surface of the earth as they grew, treasuries of gold, silver, sapphire, crystal, ruby, emerald, and coral.

de yan lag dang nying lag thams cad yongs su rdzogs te/ zla ba bcu lon nas btsas pa dang / de'i tshe gter chen po bdun po de dag kyang chu zheng dang / rngams su khru bdun tsam du sa'i steng nas mngon par 'phags te snang bar byung nas rnam par snang zhing mdzes par gyur to/ / khyim der rin po che sna tshogs kyi snod lnga brgya yang byung bar gyur te/ 'di ltar mar gyi snod dang / til mar gyi snod dang / sbrang rtsi'i snod dang; mar gsar gyi snod dang / gzhan dag kyang so so nas yo byad sna tshogs thams cad kyis yongs su gang ba dag ste/ 'di ltar rdo rje'i snod spos sna tshogs kyis yongs su gang ba dang / spos kyi snod gos sna tshogs kyis yongs su gang ba dang / man shel gyi snod kha zas dang spyan gzigs sna tshogs ro mchog tu zhim pas yongs su gang ba dang; nor bu'i snod rin po che sna tshogs kyis yongs su gang ba dang / gser gyi snod dngul sil mas yongs su gang ba dang / dngul gyi snod gser phyes yongs su gang ba dang / phra men gyi snod nor bu rin po che bai DUr+yas yongs su gang ba dang / shel gyi snod mu sa ra gal pas yongs su gang ba dang / mu sar gal pa'i snod rin po che shel gyis yongs su gang ba dang / asma gar b+ha'i snod mu tig dmar pos yongs su gang ba dang / mu tig dmar po'i snod asma gar b+has yongs su gang ba dang / nor bu rin po skar ma'i rgyal mtshan gyi snod nor bu rin po che chu 'dang gis yongs su gang ba dang / nor bu rin po che chu 'dang gi snod nor bu rin po che skar ma'i rgyal mtshan gyis yongs su gang ba dang / de dag la sogs pa rin po che'i snod lnga brgya 'thon par gyur to/ /

“After ten months, when his limbs and body parts were completely formed, he was born. At that time, those seven great treasures became visible, rising up above the ground to the height and breadth of seven cubits, bright and beautiful. Inside the house appeared five hundred pots made of various kinds of precious substances. There were pots filled with ghee, pots filled with sesame oil, pots filled with honey, and pots filled with butter. There were individual pots filled with whatever was necessary. There were diamond pots filled with every kind of perfume, pots of aromatic wood filled with various kinds of cloth, crystal pots filled with various kinds of enjoyable food delicious with perfect flavors, jewel pots filled with various kinds of precious substances, gold pots filled with silver powder, silver pots filled with gold dust, pots of silver and gold filled with beryl jewels, quartz pots filled with white coral, white-coral pots filled with quartz jewels, emerald pots filled with red pearls, red-pearl pots filled with emeralds, cat’s-eye-jewel pots filled with moonstone jewels, moonstone-jewel pots filled with cat’s-eye jewels, and so on. Five hundred such precious pots appeared.

When his limbs were perfectly formed and he was born after ten months, those treasuries, which were seven spans high, wide, and long, rose to the surface of the earth, opened, glittered, and shone. Five hundred vessels made of precious substances also appeared in the house—vessels of clarified butter, sesame oil, honey, and fresh butter, each equipped with all the necessary utensils; there also appeared diamond vessels filled with all kinds of perfumes, fragrant vessels filled with various cloths, crystal vessels filled with various foods and drinks, pearl vessels filled with various jewels, gold vessels filled with silver powder, silver vessels filled with gold powder, gold and silver vessels filled with agates, crystal vessels filled with sapphires, sapphire vessels filled with crystal jewels, emerald vessels filled with rubies, ruby vessels filled with emeralds, star sapphire vessels filled with water-clarifying jewels, water-clarifying jewel vessels filled with star sapphires. Five hundred such precious vessels appeared in the storerooms of the house

tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang de btsas ma thag tu khyim dang / bang ba dang / mdzod thams cad du nor dang / 'bru dang / dbyig dang / gser dang / rin po che sna tshogs kyi char mngon par bab par gyur to/ /
“As soon as that Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, was born, there fell a rain of wealth, grain, money, gold, and all kinds of jewels in all the storerooms and granaries in the house.
simultaneously with the birth of Sudhana, raining money, grain, gold, and various other valuables.

de la bram ze'i bltas pa dang / pha dang / ma dang / gnyen gyi tshogs kyis 'di btsas ma thag tu nor mang po phun sum tshogs pa byung bar gyur pas na/ nor bzang / nor bzang zhes de ltar ming du btags te/

“The brahmin prognosticators, his parents, and his relatives said, ‘As soon as he was born there appeared this perfection of much wealth,’ and they gave him the name Sudhana, meaning Excellent Wealth.
Because of this great prosperity that appeared in the house by his mere birth, the fortune-tellers and priests and his parents and kin called him Sudhana, ‘Good Wealth.’”

tshong dpon gyi bu nor bu bzang de ni/ sngon gyi rgyal ba la bya ba byas pa'o/ / dge ba'i rtsa ba bskyed pa'o/ / mos pa rgya chen po dang ldan pa'o/ / dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi rjes su 'brang ba'i bsam pa can no/ / lus dang ngag dang yid kyi spyod pa kha na ma tho ba med pa'o/ / byang chub sems dpa'i lam yongs su sbyang ba la rab tu brtson pa'o/ / thams cad mkhyen pa la mngon par mos pa'o/ / sangs rgyas kyi chos kyi snod du gyur pa'o/ / bsam pa'i nam mkha' yongs su dag pa'o/ / byang chub kyi sems chags pa med pa yongs su rdzogs pa'o/

“This Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, has served past jinas, has planted roots of merit, possesses a vast aspiration, and is motivated to follow kalyāṇamitras. His physical, vocal, and mental actions are irreproachable. He is dedicated to purifying the bodhisattva path. He is focused on omniscience. He is a worthy vessel for the Dharma of the buddhas. He has a pure manner[292] of aspiration. He has perfected an unimpeded aspiration for enlightenment.”

Sudhana, furthermore, having served past buddhas and planted roots of goodness, imbued with great zeal and devotion, intent on following spiritual benefactors, impeccable in word, thought, and deed, engaged in clarification of the path of enlightening beings, heading for omniscience, having become a vessel of the Buddha teachings, his course of mind purified, had achieved an unhindered, unattached determination for enlightenment.

de nas 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pas/ tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la bltas te/ dga' ba'i gtam byas nas/ de la 'di lta ste/ sangs rgyas kyi chos thams cad las kyang brtsams/ sangs rgyas kyi chos thams cad yang dag par bsdu zhing thob par bya ba las kyang brtsams/ sangs rgyas thams cad gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa las kyang brtsams/ sangs rgyas gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa thams cad shes par bya ba las kyang brtsams/ sangs rgyas thams cad kyi 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor rnam par dag pa las kyang brtsams/ sangs rgyas thams cad kyi chos kyi 'khor lo dang sprul pa'i rgyan las kyang brtsams/ sangs rgyas thams cad kyi gzugs kyi sku'i mtshan dang dpe byad bzang po rnam par dag pa las kyang brtsams/ sangs rgyas thams cad kyi chos kyi sku yongs su grub pa las kyang brtsams/ sangs rgyas thams cad kyi gsung rnam par phye ba las kyang brtsams/ sangs rgyas thams cad kyi 'od kyi dkyil 'khor gyi rgyan rnam par dag pa las kyang brtsams/ sangs rgyas thams cad kyi mnyam pa nyid las kyang brtsams te/ chos kyang bstan par gyur to/ /

Then Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta looked upon Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, welcomed him, and taught him the Dharma. He taught the Dharma through teaching on the Dharma of all the buddhas, on uniting and attaining the Dharma of all the buddhas, on the infinity of all the buddhas,[293] on the successive appearance of all the buddhas, on the pure circles of the followers of all the buddhas, on the display[294] of the Dharma wheels and emanations[295] of all the buddhas, on the pure characteristics and features of the bodies of all the buddhas, on the accomplishment of the Dharma body of all the buddhas, on the display of the speech of all the buddhas, on the pure display of the auras of all the buddhas, and on the equality of all the buddhas.

At that point Manjushri, having regarded Sudhana, greeted him in a friendly manner and expounded the Teaching to him, dealing with all elements of buddhahood, the cultivation and attainment of all elements of buddhahood, the infinity of all buddhas, the successive appearance of all buddhas in the world, the purification of the congregations surrounding all buddhas, the achievement of the reality-body of all buddhas, the magnificent arrays of wisdom and eloquence of all buddhas, the purification of the array of spheres of light of all buddhas, and the equality of all buddhas.

de nas 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang dang / skye bo'i tshogs chen po de dag chos dang mthun ba'i gtam gyis bstan te/ yang dag par bskul nas spro ba bskyed de dga' bar byas nas/ bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed du btsud de/ sngon gyi dge ba'i rtsa ba yongs su dran par byas nas/

Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, through speaking about the Dharma, taught, motivated, encouraged, and inspired Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, and that great assembly of beings, and made them develop the aspiration to the highest, complete enlightenment and remember their past roots of merit.

Then Manjushri, having edified, inspired, sharpened, and delighted Sudhana and the great crowd of people with his talk on the Teaching, having caused them to set their minds on perfect enlightenment and made them remember their past roots of goodness,
skyid pa'i 'byung gnas kyi grong rdal de'i sems can rnams kyi bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du chos bstan pas byin gyis brlabs te/ bde bar byas nas de nas song ngo/ /
He blessed and made happy[296] the beings from the city of Dhanyākara by teaching them the Dharma according to their wishes, and he departed.
stopped his teaching there, given as it was to the people in accord with their mentalities, and left.

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis/ 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pa las/ rnam pa de lta bu'i sangs rgyas kyi yon tan dang / che ba nyid thos nas bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu mos shing brtson pas phyi bzhin du 'brang ste/ 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pa la tshigs su bcad de mngon par bstod do/ /

Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, having heard from Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta the nature of the greatness and[297] qualities of the buddhas, aspired to the highest, complete enlightenment. He diligently followed behind Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, reciting these verses of praise to him:

Then Sudhana, having heard from Manjushri of such magnificence of the qualities of Buddha, with the quest for supreme perfect enlightenment uppermost in his mind, uttered these verses as he watched Manjushri going:
blo gros chen po mtha' yas spyod yul can/ / khyod kyi mthus ni sems can sman slad du/ / bdag kyang byang chub mchog tu zhugs par gyur/ / de la nges pa gang mchis bdag la gson/ /
“Oh wise one! Through your power I am set on enlightenment for the benefit[298] of beings. You who have an infinite range of activity,[299] Hear from the certainty that I have. {1}
By your power, Great Sage, I am set on enlightenment for the good of all beings, Resolved on this, with an endless vista; hear what is on my mind.
dga' ba'i chus bkang 'obs kyis kun nas bskor/ / nga rgyal dregs pa'i ra ba mtho bar brtsegs/ / sems can lam rgyud sgo rnams btsud cing gdangs/ / de 'dra'i khyim ni srid gsum ming ldan che/ /

“The great city of the three realms of existence Is encircled by a moat of the water of delight, Has the raised walls of pride and conceit, And has the gateways into all[300] the states of beings. {2}
Moats filled with the water of delight, with high walls of conceit and pride, Its doors the conditions of all beings—that is how the great city of existence is.
de ni gti mug ma rig gzings pas khebs/ / 'dod chags zhe sdang me lces rab tu gdungs/ / rtag par bdud kyi dbang po'i dbang du gyur/ / de la byis pa ma rig rten kyang 'cha'/ /
Shrouded in the great darkness of ignorance, burnt by the fire of lust and hate, Ever under the sway of the lord of demons, the abode of the unenlightened.
sred pa'i sgrog dang zhags pas shin tu glags/ / g.yo dang sgyu yi skyon gyis mtho brtsams shing / / the tshom yid gnyis dag gis mig mdongs pa/ / log pa phyin phyogs lam la rab tu zhugs/ /

“Confined in the fetters and chains of craving, Rendered powerless by the defects of deception and deceit, Their eyes blinded by doubt and uncertainty, They are on the path that leads in the wrong direction. {4}
Completely bound by the ropes and chains of craving, made desolate by the wastelands of deceit, Blinded by doubt and confusion, standing on the ground of falsehood.
phrag dog ser sna'i thag pas btags shing bcings/ / yi byol song sems dmyal mi khom rgyu/ / rga shi na dang skye bas rab tu mnar/ / mgo rmongs lam rgyun 'bar lo kun tu 'khor/ /

“Bound tightly by the ropes of envy and greed, They go to the unfortunate states of pretas, animals, and hells. Tormented by aging, death, illness, and rebirth, Bewildered they go around on the wheel of existences. {5}
Bound up in envy and jealousy, becoming ghosts, animals, and fiends, Oppressed by birth, sickness, age, and death, they wander lost in the wheel of transmigration.
de la khyod ni thugs rje rnam dag pa'i/ / dkyil 'khor ye shes 'od zer snang ba mdzad/ / nyon mongs rgya mtsho skam par shar te 'phags/ / nyi ma 'dra bas bdag la snang ba mdzod/ /
“You shine the light rays of wisdom From the disk of your pure compassion, Which come forth[302] to dry up the ocean of kleśas. You who are a sun, shine upon me! {6}
May the pure orb of your compassion for them, a sun radiating the light of knowledge, Risen to evaporate the sea of afflictions, shine on me like the sun.
byams pa bsgoms pas dkyil 'khor rdzogs shing nya/ / bsod nams zla 'od bde ba'i zer 'gyed pa/ / sems can kun gyi gnas su shar gyur gyi/ / zla ba nya ba lta bus bdag snang mdzod/ /
“The full disk of your meditation of love, The moonlight of your merit brings happiness, Shining on the dwellings of all beings: You who are like a full moon, shine upon me! {7}
Orb full of the power of love, radiating moonbeams of virtue, grant happiness; You give light like the full moon appearing in the abodes of all beings.
dkar mthus thams cad yongs bsags bskor mnga' zhing / / chos dbyings mkha' la chags pa mi mnga' ba/ / chos kyi 'khor lo rin chen sngon 'dren pas/ / rgyal por gyur pas bdag la bstan du gsol/ /

“You possess the treasure of good karma’s power And fly freely through the sky of the essence of phenomena.[303] You bear the precious wheel of the Dharma. You who are a king, give me your command! {8}
Endowed with all virtues and powers, your mind is in the sky of the reality realm; Instruct me, O King, with the jewel of the wheel of the teaching.
byang chub theg pa'i smon lam mthu mnga' ste/ / bsod nams ye shes shin tu yangs bsags shing / / sems can kun la phan pa'i don bzhugs pa'i/ / ded dpon chen pos bdag kyang bskyang du gsol/ /

“You have the courageous resolution[304] for the path to enlightenment. You have accumulated vast merit and wisdom, And you set forth for the benefit of all beings. Caravan leader, give me your protection! {9}
Boldly advancing, resolute, on the vehicle of enlightenment, having developed great virtue and knowledge, O Caravan Leader arising to benefit all beings, protect me.
bzod pa brtan zhing sra ba'i go mnabs te/ / ye shes spyan mnga' thugs rje'i phyag ring bas/ / bdud kyi dmag dpung tshogs rnams mngon 'gyur bar/ / dpa' ba chen pos bdag gi sel yang mdzod/ /
Girt with the armor of forbearance, strength, and firmness, wielding the sword of knowledge in the hand of compassion, Facing the band of demons in battle, lead me to safety, O Hero.
chos kyi ri rab spo la brtan bzhugs shing / / ting 'dzin mchog gi lha mos kun nas bskor/ / nyon mongs sgra gcan lha min 'dul mdzad pa/ / brgya byin gyur pas bdag kyang gzigs su gsol/ /
“You dwell on the summit of the Dharma Meru, Encircled[306] by the apsarases of supreme samādhi, Subjugating the asura Rāhu of the kleśas. You who are Śakra, look upon me! {11}
Dwelling on the peak of the polar mountain of truth, surrounded by the archangels of concentration, Destroyer of the titans of affliction, look upon me, O Mighty One.
byis pa'i gnas gyur khams gsum khang pa na/ / nyon mongs las rnams rnam par bsal ba mkhyen/ / rgyu yi sa dang lam rgyud 'khor rmongs par/ / me mar 'dra bas bdag kyang shul bstan gsol/ /

“In the residence of the three realms where the foolish live, Your knowledge clears away kleśa and karma. In the obscurity of the wheel of existences and the level of causes You are a lamp; reveal to me the way to proceed! {12}

In the city of existences, the abode of the unaware, your guidance out of afflictive action is definitive; Amid the confusion of the cycle of transmigration on the ground of cause, as a lamp reveal to me the Way.
ngan 'gro'i lam rnams rnam par zlog mdzad cing / / bde bar 'gro ba'i lam rnams rnam sbyong ba/ / 'jig rten kun gyi lam gyi rgyud las 'das/ / bdag la'ang thar pa'i sgo ni bstan du gsol/ /

“You turn from the path that leads to the lower existences. You make pure the path that leads to the happy existences. You have transcended all worldly paths. Show me the[307] gateway to liberation! {13}
Turning away from the paths of woe, purifying the paths of bliss, Transcender of all worldly states, lead me to the door of liberation.
rtag dang bdag dang bde bar 'du shes ldan; ; log 'dzin sgo re'i skyabs kyis bcad gyur gyi/ / bden pa'i ye shes spyan rno mchog mnga' bas/ / thar sgo bdag la'ang myur du dbye bar gsol/ /

“You close and block[308] the gateway to the false beliefs That have the conceptions of permanence, self, and happiness. You possess the sharp eyes with the power[309] of the wisdom of truth. Quickly open for me the gateway to liberation! {14}
I am stuck to the notions of permanence, self, and pleasure, blocked by falsehood and grasping— With the sharp eye of truth, knowledge, and power, quickly open the door of liberation for me.
yang dag log pa'i lam la mkhas gyur cing / / lam gyi rgyus dang tshul la bsnyengs mi mnga'/ / lam rnams kun gyis 'dul ba thugs chud pa/ / bdag la byang chub shul ni bstan du gsol/ /
“You know what are the right and the wrong paths. Skilled[310] in the practices and knowledge of the paths, You have mastered the ways of all paths. Teach to me the path to enlightenment! {15}
Knower of the paths of truth and falsehood, fearless in the varied knowledge of the Way, Certain of the guidance of all paths, show me the Way to enlightenment.
yang dag lta ba'i sa yi thang la bzhugs/ / sangs rgyas kun gyi yon tan chab kyis bskrun/ / sangs rgyas chos legs me tog char 'bebs pa/ / byang chub shul ni bdag la bstan du gsol/ /

“You reside upon the plain of the level of the true view, Bring the water of the qualities of all the buddhas, And rain down the flowers of the Buddhadharma’s qualities. Teach to me the path to enlightenment! {16}
Tree of right insight standing firm on the ground, nourished by the water of the virtues of all buddhas, Showing flowers of virtues of buddha-teaching, show me the Way to enlightenment.
rgyal ba gang 'das ma byon gang rnams dang / / da ltar byung ba'i rgyal ba snang mdzad pa/ / sems can gtso bo legs par gshegs pa'i phyogs/ / de yang lam ston mdzad pas bdag bstan gsol/ /
“Revealer[311] of the path, show me The jinas of the past and the future And the jinas who appear in the present, The sugatas, the principal beings in all directions. {17}
O teacher of the Way, show me the buddhas of the past, future, and present, Makers of light, best of beings, gone to bliss.
las kyi 'khrul 'khor tshul la mi bsnyengs pa/ / chos theg shing rta'i 'khrul 'khor mkhyen gyur cing / / ye shes theg pa'i tshul la rnam nges pa/ / byang chub theg pa bdag la bshad du gsol/ /

“You who are skilled[312] in employing the apparatus of karma, Proficient in the apparatus of the Dharma vehicle’s chariot, And skilled[313] in employing the apparatus of wisdom, Teach to me the vehicle for enlightenment! {18}
Familiar with the various mechanics of action, expert in the mechanics of the vehicle of religion, Sure of the various vehicles of knowledge, show me the vehicle of enlightenment.
mos shing smon pa'i 'khor lo'i mu khyud can/ / bzod pa rdo rje snying rje srog shing brten/ / dad pa'i gnya' shing rin chen legs spras pa'i/ / byang chub theg la bdag kyang bskyon du gsol/ /

“Bring me up onto the vehicle of enlightenment That has the circling wheels of aspiration and resolution, Has the stable axle of patience and vajra compassion, And is beautified by the precious shafts of faith. {19}
Put me on the vehicle of enlightenment, driven by faith, studded with jewels of virtue, A globe with wheels of prayer and vows, steeled by forbearance, resting on the axle of compassion.
gzungs rnams kun gyis rnam dag dkyil 'khor can/ / byams pa brtsegs pa'i dga' bas rab brgyan pa/ / tha dad yang dag shes pa'i dril phreng can/ / theg mchog bzang pos bdag la bstan du gsol/ /
“Carry[314] me in the excellent, supreme vehicle That has the wheels of all mental retentions, Is adorned by a covering roof of love, And is beautified by the strings of bells of discernment. {20}
Orb of all memory, purified, with a roof of kindness, well adorned, And a beautiful bell-garland of analytic powers—put me in this supreme vehicle.
tshangs pa'i spyod pa'i lam gyis mngon par brgyan/ / ting 'dzin bud med khrag khrig kun nas rgyu/ / chos kyi rnga yi dbyangs chen rab bsgrags pa/ / theg pa'i dam pa bdag la bstab tu gsol/ /
“Lead me onto the royal[315] vehicle Adorned with a bed[316] of celibacy, Crowded[317] with a hundred billion women of samādhi, And resounding with the sound of Dharma drums. {21}
Adorned with a couch of pure conduct, filled with millions of concentration-ladies, With the drum of truth resounding—bring me to this royal vehicle.
bsdu ba bzhi yi mi zad mdzod ldan pa/ / ye shes rin chen yon tan phreng gis brgyan/ / khrel yod dul ba'i 'phreng bas mchog bsdams pa'i/ / theg pa'i dam pa bdag la bstan du gsol/ /

“Reveal to me the excellent vehicle That has the unending treasure of the four methods of gathering pupils And is adorned by strings of qualities, the jewels of wisdom, Tied with the supreme thongs of self-control and a sense of shame. {22}
With an infinite chamber of the four integrative methods, adorned with jewels of knowledge and pearls of virtue, Harnessed with the finest rope of modesty—show me the chief of vehicles.
sbyin pa'i 'od zer dkyil 'khor bzang po can/ / tshul khrims tsan dan snying rje'i byug ldan zhing / / bzod pa'i gzer gyis mtshams rnams dam sbyar ba'i/ / theg pa'i mchog la myur du bdag gzhag gsol/ /

“Quickly place me on the supreme vehicle That has the excellent wheels of the light rays of generosity And is anointed with compassion and the sandalwood of good conduct, Its parts held together by the strong nails[318] of patience. {23}

It has the radiance of the pure sphere of light of relinquishment, the sandalwood of morality, the perfume of compassion, With the lance of forbearance, and is held together by firmness—place me on the supreme vehicle.
sems can thams cad 'dul las mi ldog pa/ / bsam gtan ting 'dzin kha khyer mthor sgron cing / / shes rab thabs gnyis 'byor mthun 'gro rgyu ba'i/ / chos kyi theg pa mchog la bdag gzhag gsol/ /
“Bring me onto the supreme Dharma vehicle That never turns back from guiding beings, Has a carriage of dhyāna built high with samādhi, And is pulled along by the union of wisdom and method. {24}
It guides all beings, never turning back; its frame of meditation is set up on concentration, It is drawn by the team of wisdom and means—place me on that eminent vehicle of truth.
smon lam 'khor los lam gyi 'khor sbyong ba/ / chos kyi gzugs dam mthu brtan che ldan zhing / / ye shes 'khrul 'khor legs sbyangs legs byas pa'i/ / chos kyi theg pa de la bdag bskyon gsol/ /

“Bring me up onto the vehicle of the Dharma That has the circling of the pure wheels of aspiration, Has the great strength[319] of the firm retention of the Dharma, And is the perfectly well-made device of wisdom. {25}
Vows set the course and alignment of its wheels; it holds the truth steadfastly, having great power; It is well made by the dynamics of knowledge, expertly—lift me onto the vehicle of truth.
kun tu bzang po'i spyod pas rab sbyangs shing / / sems can lta bas rgyu la thogs med pa/ / kun tu bzang po'i spyod pas gnon gyur pa'i/ / ye shes theg pas bdag la bsdud du gsol/ /
“Lead me onto the vehicle of completely good conduct That has purified completely good conduct And proceeds unhesitatingly[320] to care for beings With overpowering completely excellent conduct. {26}
It is refined by Universally Good action, proceeding slowly with concern for beings: Bring me to that vehicle of knowledge, of valor in pure conduct everywhere.
de ni brtan pas rdo rje bzhin gnas pa/ / ye shes sgyu mas legs sbyangs legs byas shing / / sgrib dang chags pa thams cad gcod pa yi/ / bzang po'i theg la bdag kyang bskyon par gsol/ /

“Bring me up onto the excellent vehicle That is enduring, having the nature of a diamond, With perfectly arranged, exquisitely[321] made garlands of wisdom, And cuts through all obstructions[322] and impediments. {27}
Put me on that vehicle which cuts through all obstructions, Steady and firm as the finest steel, adorned with garlands of knowledge.
'gro mnyam dri med shin tu yangs gyur pa/ / sems can thams cad skyob pas bde sgrub cing / / chos dbyings shin tu rgya chen rnam snang ba'i/ / byang chub theg la bdag kyang bskyon du gsol/ /

“Bring me up onto the vehicle of enlightenment, Which is vast, unstained, as extensive as beings, And a refuge for all beings, bringing them happiness And illuminating the vastness of the realm of phenomena. {28}
It is spacious, clean, impartial toward people, a refuge for all beings, bringing happiness: Put me on that vehicle of enlightenment, which sheds light throughout the cosmos.
sdug bsngal phung po rab byung gcod byed pa/ / nyon mongs las kyi rdul mang sbyong sel cing / / bdud dang phas kyi rgol ba kun 'joms pa'i/ / chos kyi theg la bdag kyang bskyon du gsol/ /

“Bring me up onto the vehicle of the Dharma, Which cuts through the arising of the mass of suffering, Cleans away the dust circles[323] of karma and kleśas, And crushes all[324] māras and adversaries. {29}
Its advance cuts through the mass of suffering, clears the sphere of dust of afflictions of action, And subdues all demons and challengers—put me on that vehicle of truth.
phyogs rnams kun tu ye shes rab snang ba/ / chos dbyings nam mkha' rnam par klubs byed cing / / sems can kun gyi bsam pa rdzogs byed pa'i/ / chos kyi theg la bdag kyang bskyon du gsol/ /

“Take me on the vehicle of the Dharma, Which has all directions as the scope of its wisdom[325] And is displayed[326] throughout the space of the realm of phenomena, Fulfilling the aspirations of all beings. {30}
Its scope is universal knowledge, it arrays the sky of the reality realm; Bring me to that vehicle of truth, which fulfills the aspiration of all beings.
rnam dag mkha' ltar tshad med mi zad pa/ / sred dang ma rig lta ba'i skyon med cing / / sems can kun la phan par rab gnas pa'i/ / chos kyi theg la bdag kyang bskyon du gsol/ /

“Bring me up onto the vehicle of the Dharma, Which is measureless and inexhaustible like pure space, Without the defects of craving and the views of ignorance, And remains so as to benefit all beings. {31}
Put me on that spiritual vehicle, pure and infinite as space, Unstained by the ignorance and obscurity of views, serving all sentient beings.
rlung chen langs pa'i shugs kyi shugs ldan pas/ / smon lam mthu yis 'jig rten kun 'dzin cing / / zhi ba'i gnas rab kun sar skyel byed pa'i; ; chos kyi theg la bdag kyang bskyon du gsol/ /

“Bring me up onto the vehicle of the Dharma, Which is as fast as the speed of a great wind, Seizes the world with the power of the wind[327] of aspiration, And brings it to the level of the city[328] of peace. {32}
Put me on that spiritual vehicle, swift as the wind, Sustaining the world by the wind-power of vows, establishing the ground of all citadels of peace.
sa chen bzhi yi stobs kyi stobs ldan pa/ / snying rje'i mthu dang shugs kyis khur khyer zhing / / ye shes lo tog 'gro ba nyer 'tsho ba'i; ; theg pa'i mchog la bdag kyang bskyon du gsol/ /

“Bring me up onto the supreme vehicle, Which is as unshakable as the great surface of the earth,[329] Carrying its load with the powerful speed of compassion And nourishing beings with the harvest of wisdom. {33}
Put me on the supreme vehicle, unshakable as the earth, carrying its cargo By the intense power of compassion, full of knowledge, beneficial to the world.
nyi ma lta bur 'gro ba nyer 'tsho zhing / / bsdu ba rab yangs 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor can/ / gzungs kyi stobs mchog dag pa'i 'od bzang ba'i/ / ye shes nyi ma bdag la bstan du gsol/ /
“Reveal to me the sun of wisdom That sustains beings like the sun, An attracting disk with vast light rays,[330] Radiant with supremely pure retention. {34}
It is like the sun, giving life to the world, a concentrated orb of great lights, Radiant with supreme purity of mental command; show me the sun of knowledge.
bskal pa mang po du mar rab bslabs pa/ / rgyu yi tshul dang sa kun mkhas gyur pa/ / gang gis 'dus byas grong khyer gzhom 'gyur ba'i/ / shes brtan rdo rje 'phags pas bdag la stsal du gsol/ /

“You are wise in the nature of causes and all levels Through having trained for a multitude of numerous kalpas. Give me the sublime strong thunderbolt of knowledge That will destroy the city of the composite. {35}
Give me that mighty thunderbolt of knowledge, O Noble One, which is learned over many eons, Knows the reasons and grounds of all causes, and smashes the fortress of conditioning.
sangs rgyas legs kun bslab pa phun sum gyis/ / ye shes rgya mtsho yangs pa gang zhig la/ / tshad med rgya mtsho'i blo mang bslab gyur pa/ / de legs ci 'dra 'phags pas bka' stsal gsol/ /
“Within a vast ocean of wisdom You acquired an ocean of unequaled understanding. Ārya, describe to me the nature of that excellence‍— That perfect training in all the qualities of the buddhas. {36}
As you have learned a vast ocean of knowledge, an unequaled ocean of awareness, Imbued with all qualities of buddhas, tell me what it is like.
gang na yang dag spyan mnga' khyod bzhugs shing / / ye shes rgyal po'i cod pan legs brgyan te/ / chos kyi dbu thod dam pas dbu bcings pa'i/ / chos kyi rgyal po'i pho brang bdag kyang ston/ /
“May I see[331] the city[332] of the Dharma king Where you reside possessing perfect eyes, Adorned by the royal crown of wisdom, Your head bound with the supreme turban of the Dharma.” {37}
As you have highly developed vision and are graced with the crown of the king of knowledge, Your head wrapped in the turban of truth, look into the city of the spiritual sovereign.

de nas 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pas/ glang po'i lta stangs kyis bltas te/ /tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la 'di skad ces smras so/ / rigs kyi bu/ de ltar khyod kyis bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed de/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi rjes su 'brang zhing / byang chub sems dpa'i lam yongs su rdzogs par bya bar 'dod de/ byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa yongs su dri bar bsam pa legs so/ / legs so/ /

Then Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta looked with the gaze of an elephant upon Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, and said to him, “Noble one, it is excellent, excellent, that you have developed the aspiration for the highest, complete enlightenment, wish to follow a kalyāṇamitra and complete the path of a bodhisattva, and wish to ask about bodhisattva conduct.

Then Manjushri, gazing like an elephant, said to Sudhana, “It is good that you follow spiritual benefactors, having set your mind on supreme enlightenment, that you think you should inquire into the practice of enlightening beings, wishing to fulfill the path of enlightening beings.

rigs kyi bu/ 'di lta ste/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen rnams la bsnyen cing bsten pa dang / rim gror bya ba 'di ni thams cad mkhyen pa nyid yongs su grub par 'gyur ba'i gzhi yin te/ 'di ni mthun pa'i rgyu yin gyi/ rigs kyi bu/ de bas na khyod kyis dge ba'i bshes gnyen bsnyen bkur bas yongs su ma skyo bar gyis shig /

“Noble one, it is like this: serving, following, and attending to a kalyāṇamitra is the basis and the corresponding cause for the attainment of omniscience. “Therefore, noble one, you should not tire of serving and honoring a kalyāṇamitra.”
Attending and serving spiritual friends is the beginning, the logical course, for the accomplishment of omniscience. Therefore you should tirelessly attend spiritual benefactors.”

nor bzang gis smras pa/ 'phags pa/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bgyi/ ji ltar nan tan du bgyi/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa brtsam par bgyi/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la spyad par bgyi/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa yongs su rdzogs par bgyi/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa yongs su sbyang bar bgyi/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la 'jug par bgyi/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa mngon par bsgrub par bgyi/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa'i rjes su 'brang bar bgyi/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la lhag par dmigs par bgyi/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa rgyas par bgyi/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas kun tu bzang po'i spyod pa'i dkyil 'khor yongs su rdzogs par 'gyur ba rgya cher bstan du gsol/

Sudhana said, “Ārya, teach me in detail‍—how does a bodhisattva train in bodhisattva conduct? In what way does a bodhisattva practice it? How does a bodhisattva commence with bodhisattva conduct? How does a bodhisattva practice bodhisattva conduct? How does a bodhisattva perfect bodhisattva conduct? How does a bodhisattva purify bodhisattva conduct? How does a bodhisattva enter into bodhisattva conduct? How does a bodhisattva attain bodhisattva conduct? How does a bodhisattva follow bodhisattva conduct? How does a bodhisattva gain hold[333] of bodhisattva conduct? How does a bodhisattva increase bodhisattva conduct? How does a bodhisattva perfect the domain of completely good conduct?”

Sudhana said, “Noble One, please give me a full explanation of how an enlightening being is to study the practice of enlightening beings, how an enlightening being is to accomplish it. How is an enlightening being to initiate the practice of enlightening beings? How is an enlightening being to carry out the practice of enlightening beings? How is an enlightening being to fulfill the practice of enlightening beings? How is an enlightening being to purify the practice of enlightening beings? How is an enlightening being to comprehend the practice of enlightening beings? How is an enlightening being to effect the practice of enlightening beings? How is an enlightening being to follow the practice of enlightening beings? How is an enlightening being to keep to the practice of enlightening beings? How is an enlightening being to expand the practice of enlightening beings? How can an enlightening being fulfill the sphere of the universally good practice?”
de nas 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pas/ tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la tshigs su bcad de smras pa/
Then Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta recited these verses to Sudhana, the head merchant’s son:
Then Manjushri spoke to Sudhana in verse:
dge ba'i bsod nams gangs chen mtsho/ / de ltar khyod ni nga yi drung du nyer phyin te; ; snying rje'i snying brtse rgya chen gyi/ / yid ldan byang chub dam pa tshol bar legs/ /
“Your coming into my presence Is like an ocean of good merit. It is excellent that you seek supreme enlightenment With a mind that has vast loving compassion. {38}
Bravo, ocean of pure virtues, who has come to me; With a mind of vast compassion, you seek supreme enlightenment.
'gro ba thams cad dgrol don du/ / spyod pa mtshungs med don du smon lam rab 'debs shing / / 'gro ba kun gyi skyabs 'gyur ba/ / byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa'i tshul 'di yin/ /
“You have aspired to the unequaled conduct In order to liberate all beings. You will become a protector of all beings‍— That is the way of bodhisattva conduct. {39}
You are committed to the peerless course of conduct for the sake of the liberation of all beings; You will become a savior of the world—this is the principle of enlightening beings’ practice.
byang chub sems dpa'i brtan pa rnams/ / 'khor ba'i nang na skyo med yid kyis spyod byed pa/ / de dag kun tu bzang po yi/ / spyod pa thub med chags med 'thob par 'gyur/ /
“Those bodhisattvas who are completely resolute, Who have untiring minds in saṃsāra, Attain the conduct that is completely good, That is invincible and unimpeded. {40}
Enlightening beings who are steadfast and indefatigable work within the mundane— They attain universal good, invincible and unobstructed.
bsod nams 'od can bsod nams dpal/ / de ltar khyod ni kun tu bzang po'i spyod pa la/ / 'gro la phan phyir smon byed pa/ / bsod nams rgya mtsho dge zhing dag pa'i mtshan/ /

“In order to benefit beings, you aspire To the conduct that is completely good, Which has the radiance[334] of merit, the splendor[335] of merit, An ocean of merit, and the emblems of virtue and purity.[336] {41}
Light of virtue, star of virtue, mine of virtue, ocean of virtue, pure— You are committed to universal good in practice, for the welfare of the world.
mtha' dang dbus med tshad med pa'i/ / phyogs bcu'i 'jig rten sangs rgyas kun kyang mthong bar 'gyur/ / dran pa'i mthu dang stobs kyis kyang / / de dag chos kyi sprin kyang yongs su 'dzin par 'gyur/ /
“In the worlds in the ten directions, you will see the buddhas Who are beyond measure, without center or end. You will possess their clouds of Dharma Through the power and might of your memory. {42}
You will see infinite buddhas, in the worlds of the ten directions: And you will hold their clouds of teachings by the power of memory.
de ltar khyod kyis phyogs bcu yi/ / sangs rgyas zhing rnams kun tu rgyal ba mthong nas kyang / / byang chub spyod pa'i don gyi phyir/ / de dag kun la smon lam rgya mtsho dag byed 'gyur/ /
“In that way, you will see the jinas In all the buddha realms in the ten directions. And within[337] bodhisattva conduct You will fulfill[338] an ocean of their aspirations. {43}
As you see the buddhas in the buddha-lands of the ten directions, You will clarify their ocean of vows in enlightenment practice.
'jig rten gtso la slob byed cing / / gang rnams sangs rgyas sa la gnas ni bcas byas shing / / 'di tshul rgya mtshor zhugs gyur pa/ / de dag kun kyang thams cad gzigs par 'gyur/ /
“Those who enter into an ocean of this way And are established on the level of buddhahood Train under the lords of the world, And thereby they all become omniscient. {44}
Those who enter this ocean of principles and stand on the ground of buddhahood Will become all-seers, learning from the Guides of the world.
khyod ni 'byams klas zhing kun du/ / bskal mang zhing rdul snyed du kun tu bzang po yi; ; spyod pa'i dam pa spyod byas shing / / byang chub dam pa zhi ba 'thob par 'gyur/ /
“You will practice the completely good conduct Throughout the vastness of realms For as many kalpas as numerous as atoms And attain the peace of enlightenment. {45}
Having practiced the conduct of universal good throughout all lands, for as many eons as there are atoms in the lands, You will reach enlightenment, the abode of peace and bliss.
zhing rnams mtha' dang dbus med pa/ / ma lus kun tu bskal pa rgya mtshor spyad par gyis/ / kun tu bzang po'i spyod mchog phyir/ / smon lam rgya chen yongs su rdzogs par byos/ /
“You should practice for an ocean of kalpas Throughout all the realms, which are without end, And you should fulfill your aspiration For the completely good conduct. {46}
You should practice for boundless oceans of eons in all lands And fulfill this undertaking of the conduct of universal higher good.
khyod kyi smon lam thos gyur nas/ / sems can khrag khrig dga' ba yongs su skyes gyur cing / / kun tu bzang po'i ye shes kyis/ / byang chub mchog tu smon pa byed la ltos/ /
“Observe a hundred billion beings Who are delighted on hearing your prayer: They aspire to supreme enlightenment Through completely good wisdom.” {47}
Behold the millions of beings who are happy to hear your vow, Who seek enlightenment by the knowledge of universal good.

de nas 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pas/ tshigs su bcad pa de dag smras nas/ tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang po la 'di skad ces bsgo'o/ / rigs kyi bu/ de ltar khyod bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed cing / byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa yongs su btsal bar sems dpa' legs so/ / legs so/ /

Then Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, having recited those verses, said to Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, “Noble one, it is excellent, excellent, that you have in that way developed the aspiration to enlightenment and have the intention to seek for bodhisattva conduct!
Then Manjushri, having uttered these verses, said to Sudhana, “It is good that you think, having set your heart on supreme enlightenment, that you should find out the practice of enlightening beings.

rigs kyi bu/ 'di ltar bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed pa de lta bu'i sems can yang rab tu dkon te/ de bas kyang gang gis bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed nas/ byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa yongs su tshol ba de lta bu'i sems can ni ches dkon no; ;

“Noble one, in that way, the beings who develop the aspiration for the highest, complete enlightenment are very rare. Even more rare are the beings who, having developed the aspiration for the highest, complete enlightenment, then seek for bodhisattva conduct.

It is hard to find beings who set their hearts on supreme enlightenment. It is even harder to find beings who, once they have set their minds on enlightenment, seek the practice of enlightening beings.

rigs kyi bu/ de bas na byang chub sems dpas thams cad mkhyen pa'i ye shes thob par bya ba'i phyir/ yang dag pa'i dge ba'i bshes gnyen las gdon mi za bar rtogs pa thob par gyis shig /dge ba'i bshes gnyen yongs su btsal ba la yongs su skyo ba'i yid med par gyis shig /dge ba'i bshes gnyen blta ba la ngoms pa med par gyis shig ;dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyis bstan pa la mthun par 'dzin par gyis shig /dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyis thabs mkhas pa'i spyod pa la khong khro ba med par gyis shig/

“Therefore, noble one, bodhisattvas should gain certain knowledge from true kalyāṇamitras. They should be tireless in their search for kalyāṇamitras. They should never have enough of looking at the kalyāṇamitras. They should successfully master the teachings of the kalyāṇamitras. They should not become angered by the kalyāṇamitras’ conduct of skillful methods.

An enlightening being is to attain certainty through true spiritual friends, spiritual benefactors, for the realization of omniscience. One should indefatigably seek spiritual benefactors and be tireless in seeing spiritual benefactors. One should respectfully follow the appropriate instructions of spiritual benefactors and should carry out the techniques skillfully devised by spiritual benefactors, without interruption.

rigs kyi bu/ lho phyogs kyi rgyud 'di nyid na/ yul mi mo gya nom mchog ces bya ba yod de/ de na mgul legs pa zhes bya ba'i ri zhig yod pa de la/ dge slong sprin gyi dpal zhes bya ba 'dug gi /de'i gan du song la ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bya ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bya ba dang / ji ltar byang chub sems dpas/ byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa brtsam par bya ba dang / ji ltar byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la spyad par bya ba dang / ji ltar byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa yongs su rdzogs par bya ba dang / ji ltar yongs su dag par bya ba dang / ji ltar 'jug par bya ba dang / ji ltar mngon par bsgrub par bya ba dang / ji ltar rjes su 'brang bar bya ba dang / ji ltar lhag par dmigs par bya ba dang / ji ltar rgyas par bya ba dang / ji ltar byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po'i spyod pa'i dkyil 'khor yongs su rdzogs par 'gyur ba dris shig dang / dge ba'i bshes gnyen de khyed la kun tu bzang po'i spyod pa'i dkyil 'khor ston to/ /

“Noble one, in this southern region there is a land named Rāmāvarānta, in which there is a mountain called Sugrīva, where there lives a bhikṣu by the name of Meghaśrī. Go to him and ask him, ‘How do bodhisattvas train in bodhisattva conduct? How do bodhisattvas practice it? How do bodhisattvas commence with bodhisattva conduct? How do bodhisattvas practice bodhisattva conduct? How do bodhisattvas perfect bodhisattva conduct? How do they purify it? How do they enter it? How do they attain it? How do they follow it? How do they maintain[339] it? How do they increase it? How do bodhisattvas perfect the domain of completely good conduct?’ “Then that kalyāṇamitra will teach you the domain of completely good conduct.”

South of here is a country called Ramavaranta; there is a mountain there called Sugriva, where a monk named Meghashri lives. Go to him and ask how an enlightening being should learn the conduct of enlightening beings, and how to apply it; how one is to fulfill, purify, enter into, carry out, follow, keep to, and expand the practice of enlightening beings, and how an enlightening being is to fulfill the sphere of universally good action. That spiritual friend will tell you about the sphere of universally good conduct.”

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang dga' rangs te/ mgu zhing nyams bde la/ tshim zhing yid bde ba skyes nas/ 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pa'i rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te/ 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pa la/ lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas/ lan brgya brgya stong du mar phyir bltas te/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen yid du 'ong ba'i sems dang ldan pas dge ba'i bshes gnyen mi mthong ba mi bzod de/ gdong mchi mas gang bar du zhing; 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pa'i drung nas song ngo/ /

Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, filled with joy, delighted, elated, pleased, and happy, bowed his head to the feet of Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta. He circumambulated Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta many hundreds of thousands of times, keeping him to his right, and, looking back at him many hundreds of thousands of times, with his mind enraptured by that kalyāṇamitra, unable to endure not seeing that kalyāṇamitra, with his face covered in tears and weeping, he departed from Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta.

Then Sudhana, pleased, enraptured, transported with joy, delighted, happy, and cheerful, laid his head at the feet of Manjushri in respect, circled Manjushri hundreds and thousands of times, and looked at him hundreds and thousands of times, with a mind full of love for the spiritual friend, unable to bear not seeing the spiritual friend, with tears streaming down his face as he wept, and left Manjushri.
[dge slong sprin gyi dpal]
Chapter 4. Meghaśrī
Meghashri

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang mthar gyis yul mi mo gya nom mchog ces bya ba der song ste/ phyin nas yul mi mo gya nom mchog nas rnam par rgyus te/ sngon gyi dge ba'i rtsa bas byung zhing las rgya chen byin gyis brlabs pa'i longs spyod yid du 'ong ba la yongs su spyod cing / ri mgul legs pa gang na ba der phyin nas/ mgul legs pa'i ri la 'dzegs te/ dge slong sprin gyi dpal tshol tshol zhing shar phyogs logs su byung ngo/ / de bzhin du lho dang / nub dang / byang dang / byang shar gyi phyogs mtshams dang / shar lho'i phyogs mtshams dang / lho nub kyi phyogs mtshams dang / nub byang gi phyogs mtshams su'ang byung ste/ bla 'og tu'ang lta zhing dge slong sprin gyi dpal tshol tshol ba las/

Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, eventually arrived at the land called Rāmāvarānta. Having arrived there, he traveled through the land of Rāmāvarānta. Enjoying the delightful pleasures that arose from his past roots of merit and through the power of vast karma, he came to Sugrīva Mountain. He climbed Sugrīva Mountain and, seeking the bhikṣu Meghaśrī, he went to its eastern side. In the same way, he went to its southern, western, northern, northeastern, southeastern, southwestern, and northwestern sides, looking up and down for the bhikṣu Meghaśrī.

Then Sudhana proceeded by stages to the country of Ramavaranta. Having reached Ramavaranta, reflecting on and tasting the mentally pleasing enjoyments based on higher action born of past roots of goodness, he went to Mount Sugriva, climbed the mountain, and looked in every direction for the monk Meghashri.
des zhag bdun lon pa dang / dge slong sprin gyi dpal ri rtse zhig gi sman ljongs na 'chag cing 'dug pa mthong nas/
After seven days had passed, he saw the bhikṣu Meghaśrī walking on a plateau[340] on the summit of another mountain.
Finally, after seven days, he saw the monk walking on the plateau of another peak.

dge slong sprin gyi dpal gang na ba der song ste/ dge slong sprin gyi dpal gyi rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal nas/ dge slong sprin gyi dpal la g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas te/ mdun du 'dug nas thal mo sbyar te/ 'di skad ces smras so/ / 'phags pa thugs su chud par mdzad du gsol/ /bdag gis bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed na/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bgyi ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bgyi ba dang / ji ltar byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa brtsam pa dang / ji ltar byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la spyad par bgyi ba dang / ji ltar byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa yongs su spyod pa rdzogs par bgyi ba dang / ji ltar yongs su dag par bgyi ba dang / ji ltar 'jug par bgyi ba dang / ji ltar rjes su 'brang bar bgyi ba dang / ji ltar mngon par bsgrub par bgyi ba dang / ji ltar lhag par dmigs par bgyi ba dang / ji ltar rgyas par bgyi ba dang; ji ltar byang chub sems dpas kun tu bzang po'i spyod pa'i dkyil 'khor yongs su rdzogs par 'gyur ba ma 'tshal te/

He went to where the bhikṣu Meghaśrī was and bowed his head to the bhikṣu Meghaśrī’s feet. He circumambulated the bhikṣu Meghaśrī, keeping him to his right. He sat before him and with palms pressed together said, “Ārya, I wish to know this: When bodhisattvas have developed the aspiration to the highest, complete enlightenment, how do bodhisattvas train in bodhisattva conduct? How do bodhisattvas practice it? How do bodhisattvas commence in bodhisattva conduct? How do bodhisattvas practice bodhisattva conduct? How do bodhisattvas perfect bodhisattva conduct? How do they purify it? How do they enter it? How do they attain it? How do they follow it? How do they maintain[341] it? How do they increase it? How do bodhisattvas perfect the domain of completely good conduct?

He went to Meghashri, paid his respects, and said, “O noble one, I have determined to seek supreme enlightenment, but I do not know how an enlightening being should learn the conduct of enlightening beings, or how one should accomplish it, or how to begin the practice of enlightening beings, how to carry it out, fulfill it, purify it, comprehend it, realize it, follow it, keep to it, and expand it, or how an enlightening being is to fulfill the sphere of universally good action.

'phags pa khyod ni/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams la gdams ngag dang / rjes su ston pa mdzad ces thos na/ 'phags pa ji ltar byang chub sems dpa' bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu 'byung bar 'gyur ba bdag la bstan du gsol/ de skad ces smras pa dang /
“Ārya, I have heard that you give instruction and teachings to bodhisattvas! Therefore, Ārya, teach me how bodhisattvas set out for the highest, complete enlightenment!”
I hear that you give instruction for enlightening beings, so please tell me how enlightening beings proceed to supreme perfect enlightenment.”

dge slong sprin gyi dpal gyis/ tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la 'di skad ces smras so/ / rigs kyi bu/ de ltar khyod kyis bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed cing / byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa yongs su dri ba legs so/ / legs so/ /

The bhikṣu Meghaśrī said to Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, “Noble one, it is excellent, excellent, that you have developed the aspiration for the highest, complete enlightenment and are asking about the bodhisattva conduct.
The monk Meghashri replied to Sudhana, “It is good that you ask about the practice of enlightening beings, having set your mind on supreme perfect enlightenment.

rigs kyi bu/ 'di lta ste/ byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa yongs su btsal ba dang / byang chub sems dpa'i spyod yul yongs su btsal ba dang / byang chub sems dpa'i 'byung ba rnam par dag pa yongs su btsal ba dang / byang chub sems dpa'i lam rnam par dag pa yongs su btsal ba dang / byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa rgya chen po rnam par dag pa yongs su btsal ba dang / byang chub sems dpa'i mngon par shes pa bsgrub pa rnam par dag pa yongs su btsal ba dang / byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa yongs su bstan pa dang / byang chub sems dpa'i snang ba'i snying rje'i rgyud yongs su bstan pa dang / byang chub sems dpa'i 'gro ba'i bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du rjes su 'brang ba dang / byang chub sems dpas 'khor ba dang / mya ngan las 'das pa'i sgo yongs su bstan pa dang / byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi 'dus byas dang / 'dus ma byas kyi skyon dang / 'jigs pas mi gos pa'i rgyud yongs su btsal ba 'di ni dka'o/ / shin tu dka'o/ /

“Noble one, it is like this: these are difficult, extremely difficult‍—seeking the bodhisattva conduct, seeking the bodhisattva’s scope of activity, seeking the bodhisattva’s pure setting-forth, seeking the bodhisattva’s pure path, seeking the bodhisattva’s pure, vast conduct, seeking the bodhisattva’s pure attainment of the higher cognitions, manifesting the bodhisattva’s liberations, manifesting the bodhisattva’s continuum[342] of compassion for the world,[343] the bodhisattva’s compliance with the aspirations of beings, the bodhisattva’s revelation of the gateways to saṃsāra and nirvāṇa, and seeking the bodhisattva’s activities that are unstained by composite defects, noncomposite defects, and fear.

It is difficult, most difficult, to seek the practice of enlightening beings, to seek the sphere of enlightening beings, to seek the purification of emancipation of enlightening beings, to seek the purification of the path of enlightening beings, to seek the far-ranging purification of the conduct of enlightening beings, to seek the purification of the accomplishment of mystic knowledge of enlightening beings, to show the liberation of enlightening beings, to show enlightening beings’ exercise of compassion for the world, to oblige people according to their mentalities in the manner of enlightening beings, to show enlightening beings’ mundane and transcendental faces, to seek the thought and action of enlightening beings undefiled by the ills and fears of the created and the uncreated.

rigs kyi bu/ kho bo ni mos pa'i stobs kyi dbang gis/ mig gi blo gros dang / dad pa'i mig rnam par dag pas/ kun tu mngon par blta ba'i ye shes kyi 'od snang ba phyin phyogs med pa dang / yul kun la thogs pa med cing bsgribs pa thams cad dang bral ba'i lhag mthong la mkhas pa dang / mig gi yul kun nas yongs su dag pa'i lus rnam par dag pa dang / phyogs kyi rgyud 'byams klas pa thams cad du mngon par 'dud pa'i lus kyis 'dud pa la mkhas pa dang / sangs rgyas thams cad kyi chos kyi sprin yongs su 'dzin pa'i gzungs kyi stobs kyis/ phyogs kyi rgyud thams cad kun nas mngon du gzigs pa'i de bzhin gshegs pa rnams mthong ste/

“Noble one, through the power and might of my aspiration, through having the pure eyes of wisdom and the pure eyes of faith, and by looking straight ahead with the illumination of the light of wisdom, perceiving everything before me, the entire unobstructed field of vision, with a sight that is free of all obscuration, with astute observation, with a completely pure field of vision, and with a pure body, and bowing down toward the extent of every direction with a skillful bowing-down of the body, with the power of retaining the clouds of Dharma of all the buddhas, and with the might of the power of retention, I see the tathāgatas in the realms in every direction before me.

Son, by virtue of mastery of the power of devotion, purity of the eye of perceptive faith, illumination of the light of knowledge without aversion, purity of the universal eye looking in all directions with unobstructed universal perspective and unobstructed vision skillfully observing, skillfulness in obeisance, bowing in all directions in a state of physical purity, and the power of memory command perfectly holding the masses of teachings of all buddhas, I see the buddhas in all the lands of the ten directions.

'di ltar shar phyogs kyi de bzhin gshegs pa gcig kyang mthong ngo/ / sangs rgyas gnyis dang / bcu dang / sangs rgyas brgya dang / sangs rgyas stong dang / sangs rgyas brgya phrag stong dang / sangs rgyas bye ba dang / sangs rgyas bye ba brgya dang / sangs rgyas bye ba stong dang / sangs rgyas bye ba brgya phrag stong dang / sangs rgyas bye ba khrag khrig brgya phrag stong nas/ de bzhin gshegs pa tshad med pa/ dpag tu med pa/ grangs med pa/ bsam gyis mi khyab pa/ mtshungs pa med pa/ kun tu mtha' yas pa/ sa mtshams med pa/ gzhal du med pa/ brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa dag kyang mthong ngo/ /

“In that way, I see one tathāgata in the eastern direction; I see two buddhas, ten buddhas, a hundred buddhas, a thousand buddhas, a hundred thousand buddhas, ten million buddhas, a billion buddhas, ten thousand million buddhas, a trillion buddhas, a quintillion buddhas, and so on up to limitless, immeasurable, countless, inconceivable, unequaled, infinite, endless, incalculable, and more indescribable than indescribable numbers of buddhas.

That is, in the east I see one buddha, two buddhas, three buddhas, a hundred buddhas, a thousand buddhas, a hundred thousand buddhas, a million buddhas, a hundred million buddhas, a billion buddhas, a hundred billion buddhas, a quintillion buddhas—I see incalculable, immeasurable, uncountable, inconceivable, incomparable, incomprehensible, unlimited, ungraspable, inestimable, unutterable numbers of buddhas.

de bzhin gshegs pa 'dzam bu'i gling gi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyang mthong ngo/ / de bzhin gshegs pa gling bzhi pa'i 'jig rten gyi khams rdul shin tu phra ba snyed dang / stong dang / stong gnyis pa dang / stong gsum gyi stong chen po'i 'jig rten gyi khams na sangs rgyas kyi zhing gi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyang mthong ngo/ /

“I see tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms in Jambudvīpa, tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms in the world realm of four continents, in the world realm of a thousand four-continent worlds, in the world realm of a million four-continent worlds, and in the world realm of a billion four-continent worlds.

I see as many buddhas as atoms in this continent; I see as many buddhas as atoms in the land masses of the four continents; I see as many buddhas as atoms in thousand-world, million-world, and billion-world buddha-lands;

de bzhin gshegs pa sangs rgyas kyi zhing bcu'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyang mthong ngo/ / de bzhin gshegs pa sangs rgyas kyi zhing brgya'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed dang / sangs rgyas kyi zhing stong gi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed dang / sangs rgyas kyi zhing brgya phrag stong gi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed dang / sangs rgyas kyi zhing bye ba'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed dang / sangs rgyas kyi zhing bye ba phrag brgya'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed dang / sangs rgyas kyi zhing bye ba phrag stong gi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed dang / sangs rgyas kyi zhing bye ba brgya phrag stong gi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed dang / sangs rgyas kyi zhing bye ba khrag khrig brgya phrag stong gi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed nas/ sangs rgyas kyi zhing brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed dag kyang mthong ste/

“I see buddhas as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha realms. I see buddhas as numerous as the atoms in a hundred buddha realms. I see buddhas as numerous as the atoms in a thousand buddha realms. I see buddhas as numerous as the atoms in a hundred thousand buddha realms. I see buddhas as numerous as the atoms in ten million buddha realms. I see buddhas as numerous as the atoms in a billion buddha realms. I see buddhas as numerous as the atoms in ten billion buddha realms. I see buddhas as numerous as the atoms in a trillion buddha realms. I see buddhas as numerous as the atoms in a quintillion buddha realms. I see buddhas as numerous as the atoms in more indescribable than indescribable numbers of buddha realms.

shar phyogs logs su ji lta ba de bzhin du/ lho phyogs dang / nub phyogs dang / byang phyogs dang / byang shar gyi phyogs mtshams dang / shar lho'i phyogs mtshams dang / lho nub kyi phyogs mtshams dang / nub byang gi phyogs mtshams dang / 'og dang / bla'i phyogs kyi de bzhin gshegs pa gcig kyang mthong ba nas/ de bzhin gshegs pa sangs rgyas kyi zhing brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed dag kyang mthong ba'i bar du ste/

“Just as I see in the east, in the south, in the west, in the north, in the northeast, in the southeast, in the southwest, in the northwest, below, and above, I see one tathāgata and so on up to tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms in more indescribable than indescribable numbers of buddha realms.

I see as many buddhas as atoms in ten buddha-lands; I see as many buddhas as atoms in a hundred buddha-lands; I see as many buddhas as atoms in a thousand buddha-lands; I see as many buddhas as atoms in a hundred thousand buddha-lands; I see as many buddhas as atoms in a million buddha-lands; I see as many buddhas as atoms in a hundred million buddha-lands; I see as many buddhas as atoms in a billion buddha-lands; I see as many buddhas as atoms in a hundred billion buddha-lands; I see as many buddhas as atoms in a quintillion buddha-lands; I see as many buddhas as atoms in untold numbers of buddha-lands.

phyogs re rer rnam par bltas kyang de bzhin gshegs pa kha dog sna tshogs mnga' ba dang / dbyibs sna tshogs mnga' ba dang / rnam par 'phrul pa sna tshogs mnga' ba dang / khyu mchog gi mthu dang / rnam par rol pa sna tshogs mnga' ba dang / 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor gyi rgyan rnam pa sna tshogs mnga' ba dang / 'od zer gyi dra ba snang ba kha dog du ma can dang / kha dog mtha' yas pa rab tu 'gyed pa dang / sangs rgyas kyi zhing rnam par dag pa dang / pho brang dang rgyan sna tshogs mnga' ba dang; sku tshe'i tshad rnam par dag pa sna tshogs mnga' ba dang / 'gro ba'i bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du rnam par dmigs par mdzad pa dang / mngon par 'tshang rgya ba rnam par dag pa'i sgos rnam par 'phrul pa rnam pa sna tshogs mnga' ba dang / sangs rgyas kyi khyu mchog dang / seng ge'i nga ro rnam par sgrog pa mang po mthong ngo/ /

“In each direction I see tathāgatas of various colors, of various shapes, with various miraculous powers, with various majestic miracles, with various assemblies of followers, shining with networks of many light rays in many colors, in infinite colors, in an array of different pure buddha realms and palaces, with different kinds of pure lifespans, addressing[344] beings in accordance with their aspirations, manifesting different kinds of miracles through the pure attainment of buddhahood, and resounding with the majestic lion’s roar of the buddhas.

As in the east, in the same way I see untold buddhas in all the other directions as well; looking in each direction, I see buddhas with various appearances, I see buddhas with various forms, various transfigurations, various exercises of power, various congregations, radiating light in networks of rays of many colors, with various arrays of states of purity in their buddha-lands, various life spans, showing magical projections of various ways of purification of enlightenment to beings according to their mentalities, roaring the mighty lion roar of buddhas.
de ltar rigs kyi bu/ kho bos ni sgo kun nas dmigs pa thams cad rnam par rig pa la yang dag par gzhol ba'i sangs rgyas rjes su dran pa 'di thob par zad na/
“In that way, noble one, I have attained mindfulness of the buddhas through beholding the aggregation of the knowledge of all objects of perception from all sides.
“Son, from this universal light in which is concentrated the information of all sense objects, I have attained mindfulness of the buddhas:

byang chub sems dpa' ye shes kyi dkyil 'khor rnam par dag pa gang gis de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi dkyil 'khor dang / sangs rgyas kyi zhing dang / pho brang rnam par dag pa'i rgyan mngon par mthong bas/ sangs rgyas rjes su dran pa'i sgo nas kun nas snang ba'i dkyil 'khor rab tu thob pa dang /

“But how could I know the conduct or describe the qualities of the pure domain of the infinite[345] wisdom of the bodhisattvas who have attained the gateway of mindfulness of the buddhas called the completely radiant domain through seeing before them the domains of all the tathāgatas, all the displays of pure buddha realms and palaces?

but how can I know the practice, or tell of the virtues, of the enlightening beings who have purified the sphere of endless knowledge, who have attained the means of mindfulness of buddhas in the sphere of universal illumination, by seeing right before their eyes the pure arrays of abodes in all buddha-lands in the spheres of all buddhas;
bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du rnam par dmigs par/ de bzhin gshegs pa mthong ba rnam par dag pas; sangs rgyas rjes su dran pa'i sgo 'gro ba thams cad du sgro btags pa rab tu thob pa dang /

“They are the ones who have attained the gateway of mindfulness of the buddhas called all beings through their pure vision of the tathāgatas addressing beings[346] in accordance with their aspirations.
gang gis de bzhin gshegs pa'i stobs bcu tshad med pa'i rjes su 'brang bas/ sangs rgyas rjes su dran pa'i sgo stobs kyis sgro btags pa rab tu thob pa dang /
“They are the ones who have attained the gateway of mindfulness of the buddhas called the ten strengths[347] through following the immeasurable ten strengths of the tathāgatas.
who have attained the means of mindfulness of buddhas in which the ten powers are developed, by following the infinite ten powers of the enlightened;
gang gis chos mnyan pa'i rnam pas de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi sgo'i sprin la blta bas/ sangs rgyas rjes su dran pa'i sgo chos kyis sgro btags pa rab tu thob pa dang /
“They are the ones who have attained the gateway of mindfulness of the buddhas called the Dharma through listening to the Dharma while looking upon clouds of the bodies of all the tathāgatas.
who have attained the means of mindfulness of buddhas in which the truth is displayed, by observation of the clouds of bodies of all buddhas as sources from which the truth is heard;
gang gis phyogs rgya mtsho thams cad kyi sangs rgyas mtsho tha mi dad pa la 'jug pas; sangs rgyas rjes su dran pa'i sgo phyogs rnam par snang ba'i snying po rab tu thob pa dang /

“They are the ones who have attained the gateway of mindfulness called the essence of the illumination of the directions through entering an undifferentiated ocean of buddhas in the ocean of all the directions.
who have attained the means of mindfulness of buddhas which is the seed of illumination of all realms, by plunging into the undivided ocean of buddhas in all oceans of realms;

gang gis de bzhin gshegs pa'i rnam par 'phrul pa dang / khyu mchog gi mthu phyung ba la rab tu phra bar dmigs shing 'jug pas/ sangs rgyas rjes su dran pa'i sgo phyogs thams cad du 'jug pa rab tu thob pa dang /

“They are the ones who have attained the gateway of mindfulness of the buddhas called entering the ten directions through perceiving the subtle objects of perception that are the majestic miracles of the tathāgatas.
who have attained the means of mindfulness of buddhas throughout the ten directions, by comprehending the majesty of projections of all buddhas in all microcosms;
bskal pa thams cad du de bzhin gshegs pa mthong zhing rnam par dmigs pa dang mi 'bral bas/ sangs rgyas rjes su dran pa'i sgo bskal par sgro btags pa rab tu thob pa dang /
“They are the ones who have attained the mindfulness of the buddhas called the kalpas through perceiving the vision of never being apart from the tathāgatas of all the kalpas.
who have attained the means of mindfulness of buddhas in all ages, by communication of the inseparable vision of Buddha in all ages;
gang gis dus thams cad du de bzhin gshegs pa mthong zhing 'grogs pa dang mi 'bral bas/ sangs rgyas rjes su dran pa'i sgo dus su sgro btags pa rab tu thob pa dang /
“They are the ones who have attained the gateway of mindfulness of the buddhas called time through never being separated from the companionship of the vision of the tathāgatas of all times.
who have attained the means of mindfulness of buddhas in all times, by seeing buddhas according to the time in all times and living with them inseparably;

gang gis sangs rgyas kyi zhing thams cad nas mngon par 'phags shing / zil gyis mi non pa'i sangs rgyas kyi sku yongs su mthong zhing rnam par rig pas sangs rgyas rjes su dran pa'i sgo zhing du sgro btags pa rab tu thob pa dang /

“They are the ones who have attained the gateway of mindfulness of the buddhas called the realms through perceiving the vision of the superior buddha realms and the unsurpassable bodies of the buddhas.
who have attained the means of mindfulness of buddhas in all fields, by communication of the vision of the transcendent, unsurpassed body of buddhas in all buddha-fields;
gang gis dus gsum gyi de bzhin gshegs pa'i dkyil 'khor rang gi sems dang bsam par yang dag par gzhol bas/ sangs rgyas rjes su dran pa'i sgo dus gsum du sgro btags pa rab tu thob pa dang /

“They are the ones who have attained the gateway of mindfulness of the buddhas called the three times through their own motivations and aspiration conjoining within the domains of the tathāgatas of the three times.

gang gis dmigs pa thams cad la de bzhin gshegs pa gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa yang dag par tshogs pa mthong zhing dmigs pas/ sangs rgyas rjes su dran pa'i sgo dmigs par sgro btags pa rab tu thob pa dang /
“They are the ones who have attained the gateway of mindfulness of the buddhas called locations through perceiving the vision of the arrival of the succession of the tathāgatas in all locations.
who have attained the means of mindfulness of buddhas in all sense objects, by communication of vision of successive emergence of buddhas in all objects;

gang gis skad cig gcig la 'jig rten gyi khams thams cad du de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad yongs su mya ngan las 'da' ba rnam par dmigs pas sangs rgyas rjes su dran pa'i sgo zhi bas sgro btags pa rab tu thob pa dang /
“They are the ones who have attained the gateway of mindfulness of the buddhas called peace through perceiving in each instant the passing into nirvāṇa of all tathāgatas in all world realms.
who have attained the means of mindfulness of buddhas by which peace is developed, through revelation of the ultimate extinction of all buddhas in all worlds in a single instant;
gang gis nyin gcig tu gnas thams cad du de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad gshegs par rnam par dmigs pas/ sangs rgyas rjes su dran pa'i sgo 'bral bas sgro btags pa rab tu thob pa dang /
“They are the ones who have attained the gateway of mindfulness of the buddhas called separation through perceiving in one day in all places the departure of all the tathāgatas.
who have attained the means of mindfulness of buddhas by which detachment is developed, by revelation of all buddhas going forth from all abodes in one day;

gang gis de bzhin gshegs pa re re skyil mo krung du bzhugs pas kyang / chos kyi dbyings thams cad du rgyas par khyab ba'i sangs rgyas kyi sku rnam par dmigs pas/ sangs rgyas rjes su dran pa'i sgo shin tu yangs pas sgro btags pa rab tu thob pa dang /
“They are the ones who have attained the gateway of mindfulness of the buddhas called vastness through perceiving the body of each tathāgata while sitting cross-legged filling the realm of phenomena.
who have attained the means of mindfulness of buddhas in the past, by revelation of the bodies of buddhas, each buddha sitting cross-legged filling the cosmos;
gang gis skra'i rtse mo gcig la sangs rgyas brjod du med pa byung ba mnyes par bya ba la 'jug pas/ sangs rgyas rjes su dran pa'i sgo shin tu phra bas sgro btags pa rab tu thob pa dang /

“They are the ones who have attained the gateway of mindfulness of the buddhas called subtle through discerning the accomplishment[348] of the appearance of countless buddhas on the tip of a single hair.
who have attained the means of mindfulness of buddhas in the minute, by entering into the service of untold buddhas appearing in a single point;

skad cig gcig la 'jig rten gyi khams thams cad du mngon par 'tshang rgya zhing rnam par 'phrul pa ston pa rnam par dmigs pas/ gang gis sangs rgyas rjes su dran pa'i sgo rgyan du sgro btags pa rab tu thob pa dang /

“They are the ones who have attained the gateway of mindfulness of the buddhas called display through perceiving the vision in one instant of the manifestation of the miracles of the attainment of buddhahood in all world realms.
who have attained the means of mindfulness of buddhas in supernal manifestations, by communication of visions of mystical displays of attainment of enlightenment in all worlds in one instant;

sangs rgyas byung ba thams cad kyi chos kyi 'khor lo dang / rnam par 'phrul pa dang / ye shes snang ba rab tu thob pas/ gang gis sangs rgyas rjes su dran pa'i sgo bgos par sgro btags pa rab tu thob pa dang /

“They are the ones who have attained the gateway of mindfulness of the buddhas called equality through attaining the radiance of the wisdom and miraculous display of the wheel of the Dharma by all the buddhas who have appeared.
