who have attained the means of mindfulness of buddhas in religious actions, by attainment of the illumination of knowledge of the miracle of all buddhas coming forth and teaching;
rang gis sems dang bsam pa la bltas nas/ de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad rab tu snang ba thob pas/ sangs rgyas rjes su dran pa'i sgo sems kyis sgro btags pa rab tu thob pa dang /
“They are the ones who have attained the gateway of mindfulness of the buddhas called mind through the vision of their own mind and thoughts attaining the radiance of all the tathāgatas.
who have attained the means of projected mindfulness of buddhas, by apprehending appearances of all buddhas seen as they wish;
'gro ba thams cad kyi las rnam pa ji lta bur bsags pa'i gzugs brnyan yongs su ston pas gang gis sangs rgyas rjes su dran pa'i sgo las kyis sgro btags pa rab tu thob pa dang /
“They are the ones who have attained the gateway of mindfulness of the buddhas called karma through the vision of the images of the karma that has been accumulated by all beings.
who have attained the means of mindfulness of buddhas in deeds, by showing reflected images according to the deeds that all beings have done;

chos kyi dbyings ma lus pa thams cad pad+mo'i tshal gyis rgyas par sangs rgyas rnam par 'phrul pa rgya chen po ston pa/ phyogs kun tu mngon sum du dmigs pas gang gis sangs rgyas rjes su dran pa'i sgo rnam par 'phrul pas sgro btags pa rab tu thob pa dang /

“They are the ones who have attained the gateway of mindfulness of the buddhas called miracles through the direct perception in all directions of the vision of the buddhas miraculously filling the entirety of the realm of phenomena with a vast bed of lotuses.

who have attained the means of mindfulness of buddhas in mystic projections, by means of the ubiquitous manifestation of visions of tremendous projections of buddhas on lotus blossoms blooming in all phenomenal and noumenal realms;

de bzhin gshegs pa'i sku gzugs brnyan gyi sprin dbyangs sgrog pas chos kyi dbyings dang nam mkha' kun nas snang ba/ gang gis sangs rgyas rjes su dran pa'i sgo nam mkha' sgro btags pa rab tu thob pa de dag gi spyod pa shes pa'am/ yon tan brjod par nus re skan/

“They are the ones who have attained the gateway of mindfulness of the buddhas called space through seeing the formation of clouds of the forms of the tathāgatas, resounding with their voices,[349] throughout space in the realm of phenomena.
who have attained the means of mindfulness of buddhas in space, by vision of the space of the cosmos adorned by clouds of images of buddhas?

song / rigs kyi bu/ lho phyogs kyi rgyud 'di nyid na; phyogs kyi ljongs rgya mtsho'i sgo zhes bya ba yod pa de na/ dge slong rgya mtsho'i sprin ces bya ba 'dug gi de'i gan du song la/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bya ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bya ba dris shig dang /

“Depart, noble one. In this southern region there is a district called Sāgaramukha. There dwells a bhikṣu by the name of Sāgaramegha. Go to him and ask him, ‘How does a bodhisattva train in bodhisattva conduct? How does a bodhisattva practice it?’

“Go, son—south of here is a place called Sagaramukha, where there lives a monk named Sagaramegha. Go to him and ask him how an enlightening being is to learn and accomplish the conduct of enlightening beings.

rigs kyi bu/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen de khyod la/ dge ba'i rtsa ba'i tshogs dang / rgyu yongs su ston par 'gyur ro; ;tshogs kyis rgya chen po yang khong du chud par byed do/ / dge ba'i rtsa ba'i stobs dang / shugs rgya chen po yang yongs su skyed par byed do/ / byang chub kyi sems kyi tshogs dang / rgyu rgya chen po yang yongs su brjod par 'gyur ro/ / theg pa chen po rab tu 'thob pa dang / snang bar 'gyur ba'i rgyu rgya chen po yang skyed par byed do/ / pha rol tu phyin pa'i tshogs kyi stobs rgya chen po yang rab tu ston par byed do/ / spyod pa rgya mtsho la 'jug pa'i tshul rgya chen po yang rab tu brjod par 'gyur ro/ / smon lam gyi dkyil 'khor rgya chen po yang yongs su sbyong bar 'gyur ro/ / sgo kun nas 'byung ba'i rgyan rgya chen po yang rnam par sbyong bar 'gyur ro/ / snying rje chen po'i stobs rgya chen po yang yongs su 'phel bar byed do/ /

“Noble one, that kalyāṇamitra will explain it to you.[350] He will reveal to you the cause of the accumulation of merit. He will make you understand the level[351] of vast accumulation. He will describe the vast power and might of roots of merit. He will make known to you the vast cause for the accumulation of the aspiration to enlightenment. He will provide the basis for the cause of the great radiance of the Mahāyāna. He will enable in you the vast power of the accumulation of the perfections. He will enable you to purify your entry into the vast ocean of conduct. He will enable you to purify a vast domain of aspirations. He will enable you to develop vast displays that emerge from everywhere. He will augment the vast power of great compassion.”

He will reveal to you a spiritual benefactor; he will introduce you into the cause of accumulation of roots of goodness; he will get you to develop the vast ground of provisions for enlightenment; he will tell you of the immense, intense power of roots of goodness; he will inform you of the great cause of preparation of the determination for enlightenment; he will establish in you the great cause of the illumination of the vehicle of universal salvation; he will cause you to develop the great power of the set of transcendent ways; he will get you to purify extensive means of entry into the ocean of religious practice; he will get you to purify the vast sphere of vows; he will get you to develop extensive systems of all-sided emancipation; he will get you to develop the immense power of compassion.”

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis dge slong sprin gyi dpal gyi rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal nas/ dge slong sprin gyi dpal la lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas te/ lan brgya stong du mar phyir bltas nas/ dge slong sprin gyi dpal gyi drung nas song ngo// //

Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, bowed his head to the feet of the bhikṣu Meghaśrī, circumambulated the bhikṣu Meghaśrī a hundred thousand times, keeping him to his right, and, looking back a hundred thousand times, departed from the bhikṣu Meghaśrī.
Then Sudhana paid his respects to the monk Meghashri and left.
bam po dgu bcu tham pa/
[dge slong rgya mtsho'i sprin]
Chapter 5. Sāgaramegha
Sagaramegha

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi gdams ngag de rjes su bsam pa dang / ye shes snang ba de rjes su dran par bya ba dang / byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa de rnam par dpyad pa dang / byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin gyi tshul de rjes su sbyang ba dang / byang chub sems dpa' rgya mtsho'i tshul de blta ba dang / sangs rgyas kyi dkyil 'khor de la mngon par mos par bya ba dang / sangs rgyas kyi blta ba'i phyogs de la mngon par spro bar bya ba dang / sangs rgyas rgya mtsho de la rjes su bsam pa dang / sangs rgyas gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa de rjes su dran par bya ba dang / sangs rgyas kyi tshul rtogs par bya ba de khong du chud par bya ba dang / sangs rgyas kyi nam mkha' de la rjes su blta bar bya ba byed cing

Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, contemplated the instruction of that kalyāṇamitra. He remembered the radiance of his wisdom.[352] He analyzed that bodhisattva’s liberation. He reflected on[353] the bodhisattva’s way of samādhi. He looked at the way of an ocean of bodhisattvas. He aspired toward the domain of buddhahood. He delighted in the direction of the vision of the buddhas. He contemplated the ocean of buddhas. He remembered the succession of buddhas. He comprehended that which is understood in the way of the buddhas.[354] He looked into the sky of the buddhas.

Then Sudhana, reflecting on the instructions of that spiritual benefactor, pondering that enlightening liberation, polishing that enlightening method of concentration, peering into that conductor into the ocean of the essence of enlightenment, intent upon the sphere of buddhahood, seeking that direction to the vision of Buddha, thinking about that ocean of buddhas, remembering the succession of buddhas, following that approach to the means of enlightenment, looking throughout that sky of the enlightened,

mthar gyis phyogs kyi ljongs rgya mtsho'i sgo gang na ba dang / dge slong rgya mtsho'i sprin gang na ba der phyin nas/ dge slong rgya mtsho'i sprin gyi rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te/ dge slong rgya mtsho'i sprin la lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas/ dge slong rgya mtsho'i sprin gyi mdun du 'dug ste/ tham mo sbyar nas 'di skad ces smras so/ /

Eventually he arrived in the area called Sāgaramukha and went to where the bhikṣu Sāgaramegha was. He bowed his head to the feet of the bhikṣu Sāgaramegha, circumambulated him many hundreds of thousands of times, keeping him to his right, sat before him, and with palms together said,
went gradually to the monk Sagaramegha in the region of Sagaramukha. When he got there, he paid his respects to Sagaramegha and said,
'phags pa/ bdag ni bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu mngon par zhugs te/ bla na med pa'i ye shes rgya mtsho la 'jug par 'tshal na/
“Ārya, I am set on the highest, complete enlightenment. I seek to enter the ocean of the highest wisdom.
“O noble one, I have set out for supreme perfect enlightenment and want to enter the supreme ocean of knowledge;
ji ltar byang chub sems dpa' rnams 'jig rten gyi rgyud las phyir ldog cing / de bzhin gshegs pa'i rigs su 'grub par 'gyur ba dang /
However, I do not know how bodhisattvas turn away from worldly existences and attain[355] the family of the tathāgatas;
but I do not know how enlightening beings get out of the host of worldlings and into the host of the enlightened,
'khor ba'i rgya mtsho las brgal zhing / thams cad mkhyen pa'i rgya mtshor 'jug par 'gyur ba dang /
how they cross the ocean of existence and enter the ocean of omniscience;
emerge from the ocean of the mundane whirl and enter the ocean of omniscience,
byis pa so so'i skye bo'i sa las gyen du 'phags par 'gyur zhing / de bzhin gshegs pa'i rigs su 'grub par 'gyur ba dang /
how they transcend the level of foolish, ordinary beings and attain the family of the tathāgatas;
die away from the state of ignorant sentient beings and are born in the family of buddhas,
'khor ba'i rgyud las ldog par 'gyur zhing / byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa'i rgyud du 'jug par 'gyur ba dang /
how they turn away from the flow[356] of saṃsāra and enter the flow of bodhisattva conduct;
withdraw from the stream of the mundane whirl and follow the stream of enlightening practice,
'khor ba'i rgya mtsho'i rgyud kyi 'khor lo las phyir ldog cing / byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa dang / smon lam gyi 'khor lor 'jug par 'gyur ba dang /
how they turn back from the wheel of the continuum of saṃsāra’s ocean and enter[357] the wheel of bodhisattva conduct and aspiration;
escape from the wheel of transmigration in the mundane whirl and turn to the wheel of practice and vows of enlightening beings,
bdud kyi dkyil 'khor thams cad rab tu 'joms shing / sangs rgyas kyi dkyil 'khor 'byung ba thams cad rab tu ston pa dang /
how they defeat all the domains of the māras and manifest the arising[358] of all the domains of the buddhas;
destroy the gang of all demons and make manifest the light of the host of all buddhas,
srid pa'i rgya mtsho yongs su skems shin snying rje chen po'i mtsho rnam par 'phel bar byed pa dang /
how they dry up the ocean of existences and expand the ocean of great compassion;
evaporate the ocean of craving and increase the water of great compassion,
mi khom pa dang / ngan song dang / ngan 'gro dang / log par ltung ba thams cad kyi sgo gcod cing mtho ris dang mya ngan las 'das pa'i sgo 'byed pa dang /
how they shut the gateway to all unfortunate existences, lower existences, and downfalls and open the gateway to the higher existences and nirvāṇa;
close all doors of decadence and miserable states and evils which are inopportune for enlightenment and open the door of heaven and nirvana,
khams gsum gyi grong khyer gyi sgo rnam par gcod cing / thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi pho brang gi sgo rnam par 'byed pa dang /
how they destroy the gateway to the city of the three realms and open the gateway to the palace of omniscience;
break through the door of the city of the mundane and enter the door of the city of omniscience,
yo byad thams cad kyi sred pa rnam par spong zhing 'gro ba thams cad bsdu ba'i smon lam yongs su bskyed par 'gyur ba ma 'tshal to/ /
how they reject craving for all things and develop the aspiration to gather all beings.”
give up craving for all luxuries and give rise to the determination to care for all being.”

de skad ces smras pa dang / dge slong rgya mtsho'i sprin gyis; tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la 'di skad ces smras so/ / rigs kyi bu/ khyod kyis de ltar bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed pa legs so/ / legs so; ;rigs kyi bu/ dge ba'i rtsa ba ma bskyed pa'i sems can rnams ni/ byang chub tu sems kyang mi skye'o/ /

After he had said that, the bhikṣu Sāgaramegha said to Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, “Noble one, it is excellent, excellent, that you have developed the aspiration for the highest, complete enlightenment. “Noble one, the beings who have not planted roots of merit do not develop the aspiration for enlightenment.[359]
To this Sagaramegha replied, “It is good that you have set your mind on supreme perfect enlightenment. The will for enlightenment is not developed by people who have not planted roots of goodness;

dge ba'i rtsa ba sgo kun tu snang ba rab tu thob dang / thabs kyi snying po dang ldan pa'i lam gyi ting nge 'dzin gyi ye shes snang bas rab tu snang bar 'gyur ba dang / bsod nams rgya mtsho'i tshogs rgya chen po bsags pa dang / dkar po'i tshogs thams cad kyi rgyun mi 'chad pa dang / dge ba'i bshes gnyen thams cad bkur bas yongs su skyo ba med pa dang / lus dang srog la phangs par mi rtsi ba dang / dngos por 'dzin pa thams cad dang bral ba dang / mthon dman med pa'i sa ltar sems mnyam pa dang / rang bzhin gyis snying rje che zhing byams par sems pa dang ldan pa dang / srid pa'i lam gyi rgyud thams cad du gnas par 'dug pa dang / de bzhin gshegs pa'i yul la mngon par mos pa'i sems can rnams byang chub tu sems skye ste/

“The aspiration for enlightenment is developed by those beings who have attained the complete illumination, by the roots of merit, of all gateways, who are illuminated by the light of the wisdom of the samādhi of the path that has the essence of methods, who have accumulated a vast accumulation of an ocean of merit, who have a continuity of all good actions, who never tire of relying on all the kalyāṇamitras, who have no concern for their own bodies or lives, who are free from all fixation on things, whose minds are as even as completely level ground, who possess a nature of compassion and kindness, who are focused[360] on all those dwelling in the states of existence, and who long for the scope of activity of the tathāgatas.

the will for enlightenment is produced by those who have attained the illumination of all-sided roots of goodness, who are illumined by the light of knowledge of concentration on the path containing the means of enlightenment, who have accumulated a vast ocean of virtue as provisions for the path to enlightenment, who ceaselessly practice all that is pure and good, who tirelessly apply the methods set up by all spiritual benefactors, who are not worried about their physical subsistence, who are free from clinging to material things, whose minds are equanimous as the earth, without high or low, who are by nature compassionate and friendly, who face up to all states of being, who seek the sphere of those who realize Thusness.

'di ltar sems can thams cad yongs su bskyab pa'i phyir snying rje chen po'i sems dang / 'gro ba thams cad la snyoms par nan tan du bya ba'i phyir byams pa chen po'i sems dang / 'gro ba thams cad kyi sdug bsngal kyi phung po zhi bar bya ba'i phyir bde ba'i sems dang / mi dge ba'i chos thams cad las rnam par bzlog pa'i phyir phan pa'i sems dang / 'jigs pa thams cad las yongs su bsrung ba'i phyir snying brtse ba'i sems dang / sgrib pa thams cad rnam par bzlog pa'i phyir chags pa med pa'i sems dang / chos kyi dbyings thams cad rgyas par dgang ba'i phyir rgya chen po'i sems dang / nam mkha'i dbyings kun tu gzhol zhing kun tu 'gro bar bya ba'i phyir mtha' yas pa'i sems dang / de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad mthong zhing rnam par dmigs par bya ba'i phyir dri ma med pa'i sems dang / dus gsum gyi dmigs pa ma lus par ye shes kyis rgyas par dgang ba'i phyir rnam par dag pa'i sems dang / thams cad mkhyen pa'i ye shes rgya mtsho la 'jug par bya ba'i phyir ye shes kyi sems kyang skye bar 'gyur ro/ /

“In other words, they have developed a motivation of great compassion so as to protect all beings. They have developed a motivation of great love so as to treat all beings equally. They have developed the motivation to bring happiness so as to bring to an end the mass of suffering of all beings. They have developed the motivation to bring benefit so as to turn beings away from all bad qualities. They have developed the motivation of sympathy so as to protect from all fear. They have developed the motivation of nonattachment so as to eliminate all obscurations. They have developed a vast motivation so as to pervade the entire realm of phenomena. They have developed an infinite motivation so as to extend throughout and be present everywhere in the realm of space. They have developed a stainless motivation so as to perceive the vision of all the tathāgatas. They have developed a pure motivation in order for their wisdom to extend throughout the three times without exception. They have developed a motivation for wisdom in order to dispel wisdom’s obscurations[361] and enter into an ocean of omniscient wisdom.

In such people arises the mind of enlightenment—the mind of great compassion, for the salvation of all beings; the mind of great kindness, for unity with all beings; the mind of happiness, to stop the mass of misery of all beings; the altruistic mind, to repulse all that is not good; the mind of mercy, to protect from all fears; the unobstructed mind, to get rid of all obstacles; the broad mind, to pervade all universes; the infinite mind, to pervade all spaces; the undefiled mind, to manifest the vision of all buddhas; the purified mind, to penetrate all knowledge of past, present, and future; the mind of knowledge, to remove all obstructive knowledge and enter the ocean of all-knowing knowledge.

rigs kyi bu/ kho bos ni phyogs kyi ljongs rgya mtsho'i sgo 'dir lo bcu gnyis su rgya mtsho chen po 'di la dmigs te/ mngon du byas nas 'di ltar rgya mtsho rgya che zhing tshad med pa rjes su bsam pa dang / dri ma med cing dang ba dang / zab cing gting dpag dka' ba dang / bags kyis gzhol zhing legs par gnas pa dang / rin po che'i 'byung gnas du mas rnam par brgyan pa dang / chu'i phung po tshad med pa dang / kha dog rnam pa tha dad pa mang zhing bsam gyis mi khyab pa dang / 'byung po mtha' yas pa'i gnas su gyur pa dang / srog chags mang po sna tshogs kyi rten du gyur pa dang / sprin chen po'i char yongs su 'dzin pa dang / gang zhing 'bri bar 'gyur ba med pa la rjes su sems pa byed cing gnas gnas te/

“Noble one, for twelve years I have dwelled in this area called Sāgaramukha. I focused on the great ocean, facing it, and I contemplated the ocean in this way: ‘It is vast and immeasurable; it is stainless and clear; it is deep and unfathomable; it becomes steadily deeper and stays perfectly the same; it is a source of a variety of many jewels; it is a limitless mass of water; it has many different colors and is inconceivable; it has infinite spirits; it is the dwelling place of a multitude of various creatures; it receives the rain from great clouds; and it is neither filled nor diminished.’

“Son, I have been living here in Sagaramukha (‘Ocean-Door’) for twelve years, having focused my mind on the ocean and kept it present in my awareness, reflecting on the measureless vastness of the great ocean, its pure clarity, its unfathomable depth, its gradual deepening, its variety of deposits of precious substances, the measurelessness of its body of water, its infinity, its being the dwelling place of various immense creatures, its being covered by great clouds, and how it neither increases nor decreases.

rigs kyi bu/ de la kho bos 'di snyam du bsams so/ / 'jig rten gyi khams 'di na rgya mtsho chen po 'di bas kyang 'phags par rgya che la 'di bas kyang yangs shing / 'di bas kyang tshad med la 'di bas kyang ngo mtshar dang ldan pa la la zhig yod dam snyam ste/
“Noble one, I thought, ‘Is there anything in this world realm that is greater than this ocean? Is there something that is vaster, more measureless, deeper,[362] or more marvelous?’
I think: is there anything else in the world as vast as the great ocean, as broad, as measureless, as deep, as various?

de de ltar kho bos tshul bzhin du bsam pa yid la byed pa la brtson par gnas pa'i tshe/ rgya mtsho chen po'i 'og gi gzhi las pad+ma chen po nor bu rin po che in+d+ra nI la thub pa med cing rdo rje lta bur sra ba'i chu ba can/ nor bu rin po che bai DUr+ya dam pa'i rgyan dang ldan pa/

While I was engaged in attention to this through contemplation, there appeared a great lotus from under the great ocean. It had a stem of unsurpassable precious sapphire jewels that was as hard as diamond. It was adorned with great precious beryl jewels.
While I was engaged in these thoughts, an enormous lotus from the bottom of the ocean appeared before me. Its stem was of unsurpassed jewels, sapphires, and diamonds, with a wreath of agate;

'dzam bu chu klung gi gser ltar dri ma med pa'i lo ma rgya chen po can/ dus dang mthun pa'i tsan dan gyi snying po'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa/ rin po che asma gar b+ha'i ze ba can/ rgya mtsho tsam du yangs shing rgya che ba/
It had vast leaves of stainless Jambu River gold. It displayed a yellow sandalwood pericarp[363] and stamens of emerald jewels. It was as vast and large as the ocean.
lha ma yin gyi dbang po brgya stong phrag bcus sdong po'i lhun nas bzung ba/
A gathering of a million[364] asura lords held the stem.
its calyx was on a stem held by a million titan chiefs,
rin po che sna tshogs brgya phrag stong gi dra bas kun nas yog pa/
It was covered from above by a network of a million various jewels.
it was covered by a net of a million various jewels,
klu'i dbang po brgya stong phrag bcus spos chu'i char mngon par phab pa/
A million nāga lords sent down a rain of incense.
sprinkled by rain from clouds of fragrant water by a million chief water spirits,
nam mkha' lding gi dbang po brgya stong phrag bcus dar dang rin po che'i lda ldi dang / sen mo do mang po mchus gzung zhing rab tu dbyangs pa/
A million garuḍa lords hung from their beaks streamers of silk and strings of jewels.
with a million bird chiefs trailing silks and strings of jewels over it,
mi'am ci'i dbang po brgya stong phrag bcus phan pa'i sems kyis kun nas blta ba/
A million kinnara lords looked on with a wish to benefit.
a million centaur chiefs gazing at it benevolently,
lto 'phye chen po'i dbang po brgya stong phrag bcus 'khor nas mngon par 'dud pa/
A million mahoraga lords encircled the lotus and bowed down to it.
a million serpent chiefs bowing to it in respect,
srin po'i dbang po brgya stong phrag bcus lus btud cing mngon par mchod pa/
A million rākṣasa lords bowed down and made offerings to it.
a million goblin chiefs honoring it with bowed bodies,
dri za'i dbang po brgya stong phrag bcus rol mo dang glu sna tshogs snyan pas bstod cing mchod pa/
A million gandharva lords played music and sang various melodious songs in praise and as an offering.
a million celestial musician chiefs celebrating it with music and song,

lha'i dbang po brgya stong phrag bcus lha rdzas kyi me tog dang / spos dang / phreng ba dang / bdug spos dang / byug pa dang / phye ma dang / gos dang / gdugs dang / rgyal mtshan dang / lha'i ba dan gyi sprin gyi char mngon par phab pa/
A million deva lords sent down rain from clouds of divine flowers, perfume, garlands, incense, ointments, powders, clothing, parasols, banners, and divine flags.
a million celestial leaders raining on it clouds of heavenly flowers, fragrances, garlands, incenses, perfumes, aromatic powders, cloths, parasols, banners, and pennants,
tshangs pa'i dbang po brgya stong phrag bcus spyi bos gtugs te phyag 'tshal zhing mchod pa/
A million Brahmakāyika lords reverently bowed their heads, paid homage, and made offerings.
a million Brahma chiefs bowing their heads in respect,
gnas gtsang ma'i ris kyi lha brgya stong phrag bcus thal mo sbyar cing phyag bya ba/
A million Śuddhāvāsa devas placed their palms together and paid homage.
a million celestial beings of the pure abodes paying respect with joined palms,
mi'i dbang po 'khor los bsgyur ba brgya stong phrag bcus rin po che sna bdun gyis bsu zhing mngon par mchod pa/
A million cakravartins, lords of humans, welcomed it with an offering of the seven jewels,
a million human rulers making offerings of precious substances,
rgya mtsho'i lha brgya stong phrag bcus mngon par 'thon cing phyag bya ba/
and a million ocean devas rose up and paid homage to it.
a million ocean deities emerging to pay respect;

nor bu rin po che skar ma'i ngad brgya stong phrag bcu'i 'od zer gyi rgyan gyis rab tu snang bar byas pa/ nor bu rin po che bsod nams kyis dag pa brgya stong phrag bcus mkhos su phebs par 'phel bas rab tu brgyan pa/ nor bu rin po che rnam par snang ba brgya stong phrag bcus snying po rab tu gsal bar byas pa/ nor bu rin po che dpal gyi snying po brgya stong phrag bcus dpal chen po shin tu 'bar bar gyur pa/ nor bu rin po che mdzod sna tshogs brgya stong phrag bcus mtha' yas par snang bar byas pa/ nor bu rin po che 'dzam bu'i chu klung brgya stong phrag bcus yongs su ston par gnas pas rab tu brgyan pa/ nor bu rin po che rdo rje'i seng ge brgya stong phrag bcus thub pa med par brgyan pa/ nor bu rin po che nyi ma'i snying po brgya stong phrag bcus rgya cher gsal ba bsgrubs pa/ nor bu rin po che 'bar ba brgya stong phrag bcus kha dog sna tshogs su brgyan pa/ nor bu rin po che yid bzhin gyi rgyal po brgya stong phrag bcus mi zad pa'i rgyan dang / 'od 'bar bar byas pa byung ste/

“A million precious asteria jewels displaying light rays adorned it. A million perfectly arranged precious jewels of pure merit[365] beautified it. A million radiant[366] precious jewels were its stainless center. It blazed with a million glorious precious jewels. It had the infinite shining of a million variegated treasures of precious jewels. It was beautified by a perfectly arranged display of a million precious Jambudvīpa[367] jewels. It had an unsurpassable display of a million precious diamond[368] jewels. It had a plenitude of illustrious blazing precious sunstone jewels. It had an arrangement of a million radiant precious jewels of various colors. It had the unceasingly brightly shining display of a million precious wish-fulfilling kings of jewels.

it was illumined by arrays of light beams from a million luminous jewels, adorned with a million pure jewels in orderly arrays, containing a million radiant jewels, blazing with the great splendor of a million dazzling jewels, shining endlessly with a million jewels from various sources, adorned with a million jewels symbolic of earth arrayed all around, incomparably arrayed with a million of the finest diamonds, brilliantly covered with a million sun-containing jewels, decorated with a million beautiful jewels in various colors, blazing with the light of an endless array of a million wish-fulfilling jewels.

pad+mo chen po de ni/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i 'jig rten las 'das ba'i dge ba'i rtsa ba las byung ba'o/ / byang chub sems dpa'i bsam pas yongs su brtan pa'o/ / phyogs thams cad du mngon par dmigs su yod pa'o/ / sgyu ma'i rnam pa'i chos kyis byung ba'o/ / rjen pa'i dri ma med pa'i las kyis byung ba'o/ / nyon mongs pa med pa'i chos kyi tshul gyis brgyan pa'o/ / rmi lam lta bu'i chos nyid kyis yongs su byung ba'o/ / mngon par 'du bya ba med pa'i chos kyi tshul gyis rgyas btab pa'o/ / chags pa med pa'i chos kyi tshul dang ldan pa'o/ / phyogs kyi khams kun tu chos kyi dbyings rgyas par 'gengs pa'o/ / sangs rgyas kyi yul brjod pa dang mthun pa ste/ de'i rnam pa dang / yon tan dang / dbyibs dang / kha dog dang / rgyan gyi mthar phyin par ni/ bskal pa brgya stong grangs med par yang khong du chud par mi nus te/

“That great lotus had arisen from a tathāgata’s transcendent roots of merit and remained through the aspiration of bodhisattvas. It could be perceived in all directions. It had come forth as an illusory phenomenon. It had been created from pure, stainless actions. It was the display of the unalloyed true nature. It was produced like a phenomenon in a dream. It was sealed as being a noncomposite phenomenon. It possessed the nature of being free of attachment. It pervaded the domains of the directions throughout the vast realm of phenomena. It accorded with the majestic radiance[369] of the domain of buddhahood. It would be impossible to fully comprehend its display of form, qualities, shape, and colors even in hundreds of thousands of asaṃkhyeya kalpas.

That great lotus is born from the transcendental roots of goodness of the enlightened; it appears everywhere, directed to the will of enlightening beings; it comes forth from the principle of illusoriness; it is produced by pure deeds; it is adorned by the principle of the state of noncontention; it is a presentation of the nature of being equal to a dream; it is marked by the principle of nonfabrication; it accords with the principle of nonattachment; it pervades all universes everywhere; it is in the realm of illumination by the light of the sphere of Buddha. It would be impossible to reach the end of the array of characteristics, qualities, forms, and appearances of that lotus even in countless hundreds of thousands of eons.

pad+mo chen po de yang de bzhin gshegs pa'i sku skyil mo krung du bzhugs pas khyab cing / yongs su rgyas par mthong ngo/ / de bzhin gshegs pa sku de yang 'di nas bzung ba nas/ srid pa'i rtse mo'i bar gyi mthas klas par mthong ngo/ / de bzhin gshegs pa de'i gdan gyi rgyan bsam gyis mi khyab pa'ang mthong ngo/ / 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor gyi rgyan bsam gyis mi khyab pa dang / 'od kyi dkyil 'khor gyi rgyan bsam gyis mi khyab pa dang / mtshan phun sum tshogs pa bsam gyis mi khyab pa dang / dpe byad bzang bzang po sna tshogs bsam gyis mi khyab pa dang / sangs rgyas kyi khyu mchog gi mthu dang / sangs rgyas kyi rnam par 'phrul ba bsam gyis mi khyab pa dang / de bzhin gshegs pa'i sku mdog rnam par dag pa bsam gyis mi khyab pa dang / spyi gtsug ltar mi mthong ba bsam gyis mi khyab pa dang / ljags yangs pa bsam gyis mi khyab pa yang mthong ngo/ /

“I saw the clear image of the body of a tathāgata sitting cross-legged on that great lotus and filling it. I saw that tathāgata’s body extending from here up to the summit of existence. I saw the inconceivable display of that tathāgata’s seat. I saw the inconceivable circle of his followers, the inconceivable extent of his halo, his inconceivable perfect primary signs of a great being, his inconceivable various secondary features of a great being, his inconceivable majesty and power, his inconceivable miracles of buddhahood, the inconceivable color of the tathāgata’s body, the inconceivable invisible crown of his head,[370] and his inconceivable vast tongue.

Also I saw an embodiment of Buddha clearly manifest sitting cross-legged on that great lotus, completely filling it; I saw that embodiment of Buddha reaching from here to the very summit of being. I also saw the inconceivable adornments of the Buddha’s throne, the inconceivable adornments of the Buddha’s congregation, the inconceivable adornments of his aura of light, his inconceivable marks of greatness, various embellishments, and inconceivable majesty, the inconceivable projection of Buddha, the inconceivable purity of appearance of the Buddha;

sangs rgyas kyi gsung gi rgyan bsam gyis mi khyab pa dang / dbyangs kyi dkyil 'khor bsam gyis mi khyab pa yang thos so/ / stobs tshad med pa bsam gyis mi khyab pa dang / mi bsnyems pa'i rgyan rnam par dag pa bsam gyis mi khyab pa dang / tha dad pa yang dag par mkhyen pa'i stobs mngon par bsgrub pa bsam gyis mi khyab pa yang rjes su shes so/ / sngon byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa yang dag par bsgrub pa bsam gyis mi khyab pa yang rjes su dran no/ / mngon par rdzogs par byang chub pa'i rnam par 'phrul pa bsam gyis mi khyab pa yang mthong ngo/ / chos kyi sprin gyi 'brug sgra mngon par bsgrags pa bsam gyis mi khyab pa dang / yongs su bstan pa rnam par dmigs pa'i gnas dang / rgyan bsam gyis mi khyab pa yang thos so/ / g.yas g.yon gyi sku'i rnam par tshad med pa bsam gyis mi khyab pa dang / sems can gyi don dang / dgos pa bsam gyis mi khyab pa yongs su grub par gyur pa yang mthong ngo/ /

“I heard the inconceivable display of that buddha’s speech and the inconceivable range of his voice. I comprehended his inconceivable limitless strength, his inconceivable display of fearlessness, and his inconceivable accomplishment of the power of discernment. I remembered his inconceivable past accomplishment of bodhisattva conduct. I saw the inconceivable miracle of his complete enlightenment. I heard the inconceivable resounding of the thunder of Dharma and the inconceivable array of the perceived communication of the complete teaching. I saw the inconceivable, immeasurable right and left parts of his body and the inconceivable accomplishment of a body that benefits beings.

I heard the Buddha’s inconceivable eloquence and drew near to the inconceivable infinity of Buddha’s power, the inconceivable purity of his adornments of expertise, and his inconceivable accomplishment of the power of analytic knowledge; I recalled his past consummation of practices as an enlightening being, I saw the inconceivable transformation of the attainment of enlightenment, I heard of the inconceivable array of senses conveying universal insight and saw the inconceivable infinite division of his body into left and right and his consummate attainment of physical being beneficial to all creatures.

de bzhin gshegs pa des kyang phyag g.yas pa brkyang zhing / kho bo'i mgo la byugs nas/ chos kyi rnam grangs kun nas mig ces bya ba/ de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi yul byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa rab tu brjod pa/ chos kyi dbyings kyi gzhi dang / rnam pa tha dad pa thams cad rab tu snang ba/ chos thams cad kyi dkyil 'khor la yang dag par gzhol zhing snang bar byed pa/ zhing gi dkyil 'khor dang / rnam pa thams cad rnam par dag pas yongs su snang ba/ phas kyi rgol ba'i dkyil 'khor thams cad rnam par 'thor ba/ bdud kyi dkrugs ma'i dkyil 'khor thams cad rab tu 'joms pa/ sems can gyi khams thams cad shin tu tshim par byed pa/ sems can thams cad kyi sems kyi thibs po rab tu snang bar byed pa/ sems can thams cad kyi bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du rnam par dmigs pa/ sems can thams cad kyi dbang po'i 'khor lo'i rgyud dang mthu snang bar byed pa yang dag par bstan te/ kho bos kyang kun nas mig gi chos kyi rnam grangs de blangs so/ / bzung ngo/ / spel to/ / bsams so/ /

“That tathāgata extended his right hand and stroked my head and taught me a Dharma teaching called All-Seeing Eyes, which is the field of all the tathāgatas, reveals the conduct of bodhisattvas, illuminates the different bases of the realm of phenomena,[371] illuminates the compiled[372] field of all Dharmas, is the pure vision of the forms of the range of all realms, scatters the entire range of adversaries, defeats the entire range of the discord of the māras, brings satisfaction to all realms of beings, illuminates the darkness in the minds of all beings, communicates[373] in accord with the thoughts of all beings, and illuminates the turning wheel of the faculties of all beings. “I acquired, possess, follow, and contemplate this Dharma teaching called All-Seeing Eyes.

“Then the Buddha extended his right hand, rubbed my head, and revealed to me a teaching called universal eye, which is the sphere of all buddhas, revealing the practice of enlightening beings, showing the differentiation of the planes of all universes, showing the spheres of all truths together, the light purifying all lands, dispersing all challengers, crushing all demons and devils, making all beings happy, illumining the hidden recesses of all beings’ minds, communicating to all beings in accord with their mentalities, illuminating the turning of the wheels of the senses of all beings. And I have taken up that teaching of the universal eye, keep it in mind, apply it, and contemplate it,

de ltar bzung ba de la yang bri na ni snag tsha rgya mtsho chen po'i chu'i phung po tsam dang / smyu gu'i phung po ri rab ri'i rgyal po tsam zad par gyur kyang chos kyi rnam grangs de las le'u re re dang / sgo re re dang / chos kyi tshul re re dang / chos kyi tshig rnam par phye ba re re las kyang zad pa'am/ 'grib pa'am/ 'byang ba'am/ mthar thug pa'am/ mtha' zad par 'gyur ba dmigs par mi rung ngo/ /

“Having thus acquired it, if one were to use a volume of ink equal to the great ocean and a heap of pens the size of Sumeru, the king of mountains, to write it out, one would not be able reach the end of a single chapter, a single gateway, a single Dharma way, or a single category of words from that Dharma teaching, nor could one diminish what is to be written, complete it, finish it, or reach the end.

taking it in this way—even if it were being written by a collection of pens the size of the polar mountains with as much ink as water in the oceans, it could never be finished; it would be impossible to finish even a part of a single line of a single formula of a single principle of a single doctrine of a single chapter of the teaching—it cannot be even partially exhausted, let alone fully exhausted or comprehended.

rigs kyi bu/ de ltar bdag gis lo bcu gnyis tshang bar chos kyi rnam grangs kun nas mig ces bya ba 'di la nyi ma gcig cing yang thos pa 'dzin pa'i gzungs kyi 'od snang bas le'u grangs med pa zhig khong du chud do/ / zhi ba'i sgo'i gzungs kyi 'od snang bas le'u grangs med pa zhig la zhugs so/ / glong mtha' yas pa'i gzungs kyi 'od snang bas le'u grangs med pa zhig la yang dag par 'jug go / sa la rnam par dpyod cing rjes su rtogs par byed pa'i gzungs kyi 'od snang bas le'u grangs med pa zhig rnam par bsgom ste rnam par dbye ba byas so; ;gzi brjid dang ldan pa'i gzungs kyi 'od snang bas le'u grangs med pa zhig yongs su blangs so/ / pad+mo'i rgyan gyi gzungs kyi 'od snang bas le'u grangs med pa zhig mngon par bsgrubs so/ / dbyangs kyi tshul gyi gzungs kyi snang bas le'u grangs med pa zhig yang dag par bshad do/ / nam mkha'i snying po'i gzungs kyi 'od snang bas le'u grangs med pa zhig rab tu phye'o/ / skar ma brtsegs pa'i gzungs kyi 'od snang bas le'u grangs med pa zhig shin tu rgyas par byas so/ / rgya mtsho'i snying po'i gzungs kyi 'od snang bas le'u grangs med pa zhig yongs su bkod do/ /

“Noble one, in that way I have possessed this Dharma teaching called All-Seeing Eyes for an entire twelve years. Having thus acquired it, in a single day I can understand countless chapters through the illumination of the light of the power of retention called remembering what is heard. I can comprehend countless chapters through the illumination of the light of the power of retention called the gateway to peace. I can fathom countless chapters through the illumination of the light of the power of retention called endless revolving. I can consider and investigate countless chapters through the illumination of the light of the power of retention called examining and analyzing the levels. I can conclude countless chapters through the illumination of the light of the power of retention called majestic. I can accomplish countless chapters through the illumination of the light of the power of retention called array of lotuses. I can elucidate countless chapters through the illumination of the light of the power of retention called distinct voice. I can distinguish countless chapters through the illumination of the light of the power of retention called the essence of space. I can expand on countless chapters through the illumination of the light of the power of retention called the multitude of stars. I can arrange countless chapters through the illumination of the light of the power of retention called the essence of the ocean.

“So, son, having taken up this teaching of the universal eye for a full twelve years—taking it up in this way: in one day I master countless chapters by the light of mental command to retain what is heard; I penetrate countless chapters by the light of mental command that is a way of access to tranquillity; I plunge into countless chapters by the light of mental command that progresses endlessly; I contemplate and investigate countless chapters by the light of mental command that is imbued with fiery energy; I put countless chapters into practice by the light of mental command adorned with lotuses; I elucidate countless chapters by the light of mental command that is beyond words; I analyze countless chapters by the light of mental command that is a mass of brightness; I arrange countless chapters in order by the light of mental command containing the ocean—

kho bo'i drung du shar phyogs logs nas/ lha dang lha'i dbang po'am/ klu dang klu'i dbang po'am/ gnod sbyin dang gnod sbyin gyi dbang po'am/ dri za dang dri za'i dbang po'am/ lha ma yin dang lha ma yin gyi dbang po'am/ nam mkha' lding dang nam mkha' lding gi dbang po'am/ mi'am ci dang mi'am ci'i dbang po'am/ lto 'phye chen po dang lto 'phye chen po'i dbang po'am/ mi dang mi'i dbang po'am/ tshangs pa'am tshangs pa'i dbang po'am/ sems can gang su 'ongs kyang rung ste/ de dag thams cad de bzhin gshegs pa dang / byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa snang ba'i chos kyi rnam grangs kun nas mig ces bya ba 'di nyid la rab tu bkod cing btsud do/ / de dag kun kyang kun nas mig gi chos kyi rnam grangs 'di nyid la mos par byas so/ / rtog tu btsud do/ / yongs su bstan to/ / yang dag par brjod do/ / yongs su gsal bar byas so/ / rnam par phye'o; ;rgyas par byas so/ / mngon par bstan to/ / rnam par bkrol lo/ / rab tu phye'o/ / shin tu snang bar byas so/ /

“Beings have arrived before me to the east. There are devas and deva lords, nāgas and nāga lords, yakṣas and yakṣa lords, gandharvas and gandharva lords, asuras and asura lords, garuḍas and garuḍa lords, kinnaras and kinnara lords, mahoragas and mahoraga lords, humans and human lords, brahmins and brahmin lords. I establish them in and bring them all into this Dharma teaching called All-Seeing Eyes that illuminates the conduct of the tathāgatas and bodhisattvas. For all of them I clarify, delineate, elucidate, describe, teach,[374] categorize, expand, reveal, expound, and illuminate this Dharma teaching called All-Seeing Eyes.

whatever beings come to me from the ten directions, I direct and introduce them all into this teaching of the universal eye, the manifestation of the practice of enlightened and enlightening beings; to all of them I elucidate, represent, illumine, describe, show, analyze, expound upon, open up, explain, unlock, and clarify the teaching of the universal eye.

de ltar shar phyogs la ji lta ba de bzhin du lho phyogs dang / nub phyogs dang / byang phyogs dang / byang shar gyi phyogs mtshams dang / shar lho'i phyogs mtshams dang / lho nub kyi phyogs mtshams dang / nub byang gi phyogs mtshams dang / 'og dang / bla'i phyogs nas sems can gang su 'ongs kyang rung ste/ kun la yang snga ma bzhin no/ /
“As in the east, it is the same for the beings who arrive to the south, the west, the north, the northeast, the southeast, the southwest, the northwest, above, and below.
[whatever beings come to me from the ten directions]

rigs kyi bu/ de ltar kho bos ni chos kyi rnam grangs gcig cig shes par zad na/ byang chub sems dpa' smon lam yongs su dag pa dang ldan pas/ byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa rgya mtsho thams cad la zhugs pa dang / bskal pa thams cad du gnas pa rgyun mi gcad pa'i phyir smon lam rgya mtsho thams cad la zhugs pa dang / bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du rjes su 'brang bar bya ba'i phyir sems can rgya mtsho thams cad la zhugs pa dang / stobs bcu'i ye shes chags pa med pa'i snang ba yongs su bskyed pa'i phyir 'gro ba thams cad kyi sems rgya mtsho la zhugs pa dang / yongs su smin par bya ba dang gdul ba'i dus las mi 'da' bar bya ba'i phyir sems can thams cad kyi dbang po rgya mtsho la zhugs pa dang / zhing thams cad rnam par dag par bya ba'i smon lam mngon par bsgrubs pas zhing rgya mtsho thams cad la zhugs pa dang / de bzhin gshegs pa la mchod cing rim gro byed pa'i stobs kyis sangs rgyas rgya mtsho thams cad la zhugs pa dang / ye shes rnam par rig pas chos rgya mtsho thams cad la zhugs pa dang / nan tan dang ldan pas yon tan rgya mtsho thams cad la zhugs pa dang / brjod pa thams cad du chos kyi 'khor lo bskor ba mngon par bsgrub pa'i phyir 'gro ba'i skad rgya mtsho thams cad la zhugs pa rnams kyi spyod pa shes pa'am/ yon tan brjod par nus re skan/

“Noble one, in this way I know but one Dharma teaching. How could I know the conduct or describe the qualities of bodhisattvas? They have entered the ocean of bodhisattva conduct in order to gain pure aspiration; they have entered the ocean of all aspirations in order to remain continuously throughout all kalpas; they have entered the ocean of all beings in order to follow a conduct that accords with their wishes; they have entered the ocean of the minds of all beings in order to communicate wisdom; they have entered the ocean of all good qualities[375] in order to develop the unimpeded radiance of the wisdom of the ten strengths; they have entered the ocean of the faculties of all beings in order not to miss the time for ripening and guiding them; they have entered the ocean of realms in order to fulfill the aspiration to purify all realms; they have entered the ocean of buddhas in order to serve and make offerings to the tathāgatas; they have entered the ocean of Dharma in order to communicate[376] wisdom; they have entered the ocean of good qualities in order to reach attainment; and they have entered the ocean of the languages of beings in order to turn the wheel of the Dharma in all languages.

“I know this teaching, son, but how can I know the practice or tell of the virtues of the enlightening beings who have entered into the ocean of all enlightening beings’ practices in accord with pure vows; who have entered into the ocean of all vows, to remain in the world through all ages; who have entered into the mundane whirl of all beings, to act appropriately according to their mentalities; who have entered the ocean of minds of all beings, to communicate knowledge; who have entered the ocean of all virtues, to produce the vision of the knowledge of the ten powers without obstruction; who have entered the ocean of all beings’ faculties, to guide them to maturity and perfection with appropriate timing; who have entered the ocean of all lands, by carrying out the vow to purify all lands; who have entered the ocean of all buddhas, by the power of the vow to honor and attend all enlightened ones; who have entered the ocean of all truths, for the communication of knowledge; who have entered the ocean of all virtues by pursuing their realization; who have entered the ocean of languages of all beings, to carry out the turning of the wheel of the teaching in all languages?

song / rigs kyi bu/ 'di nas dpag tshad drug cu 'das pa'i lho phyogs kyi gnas 'di nyid na/ lang+ka'i gnas rgya mtsho'i dogs zhes bya ba yod de/ de na dge slong shin tu brtan pa zhes bya ba 'dug gi /de'i gan du song la ji ltar byang chub sems dpa' byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa yongs su sbyang bar bya ba dris shig /

“Depart, noble one. Sixty yojanas from here on the road south, there is a place named Sāgaratīra on the road to Laṅka. There dwells a bhikṣu by the name of Supratiṣṭhita. Go to him and ask him, ‘How does a bodhisattva train in bodhisattva conduct?’ ”

“Go, son, to a place called Sagaratira, in the region of Sri Lanka, sixty leagues south of here. A monk named Supratishthita lives there; go to him and ask how a great enlightening being is to purify enlightening practice.”

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis/ dge slong rgya mtsho'i sprin gyi rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te/ dge slong rgya mtsho'i sprin la lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas yang dang yang bltas te/ dge slong rgya mtsho'i sprin gyi drung nas song ngo/ /

Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, bowed his head to the feet of the bhikṣu Sāgaramegha, circumambulated the bhikṣu Sāgaramegha many hundreds of thousands of times, keeping him to his right, and, looking back again and again, departed from the bhikṣu Sāgaramegha.
Then Sudhana, paying his respects, departed from the presence of Sagaramegha.
[dge slong shin tu brtan pa]
Chapter 6. Supratiṣṭhita
Supratishthita

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi gdams ngag de dang / kun nas mig gi chos kyi rnam grangs de yang rjes su dran par byed cing / de bzhin gshegs pa'i rnam par 'phrul pa de yang rjes su bsam pa dang / chos kyi tshig dang yi ge'i sprin de dag kyang yongs su gzung ba dang / chos kyi sgo rgya mtsho'i tshul de dag la'ang 'jug par bya ba dang / chos kyi tshul de la'ang rjes su rnam par blta ba dang / chos kyi le'u dang / glong gi tshul de dag la 'jug par bya ba dang / chos kyi nam mkha' de la yang dag par gzhol bar bya ba dang / chos kyi dkyil 'khor de yang rjes su sbyar bar bya ba dang / chos rin po che'i gling de yang rjes su sems shing mthar gyis lang+ka'i gnas rgya mtsho'i ngogs zhes bya ba gang na ba der phyin nas/ dge slong shin tu brtan pa mthong bar dga' zhing shar phyogs su bltas so/ / de bzhin du lho phyogs dang; nub phyogs dang / byang phyogs dang / byang shar gyi phyogs mtshams dang / shar lho'i phyogs mtshams dang / lho nub kyi phyogs mtshams dang / nub byang gi phyogs mtshams dang; bla dang / 'og tu yang dge slong shin tu brtan pa mthong bar dga' ste kun tu bltas pa dang /

Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, remembering the instructions of the kalyāṇamitra and the Dharma teaching called All-Seeing Eyes, contemplating the miracles of that tathāgata, keeping in his mind the clouds of the words and terms of that Dharma, comprehending that ocean of Dharma gateways, observing the precepts of that Dharma, entering[377] those ways of turning toward[378] the Dharma, absorbed into the sky of that Dharma, purifying the range of that Dharma, and meditating on the precious continent[379] of that Dharma, eventually arrived at Sāgaratīra in the Laṅka region.[380] Wishing to see the bhikṣu Supratiṣṭhita, he looked for him in the eastern direction. In the same way, wishing to see the bhikṣu Supratiṣṭhita, he looked for him everywhere: in the southern direction, in the western direction, in the northern direction, in the northeastern direction, in the southeastern direction, in the southwestern direction, in the northwestern direction, above, and below.

Then Sudhana, remembering that spiritual benefactor’s teaching of the universal eye, reflecting on that projection of buddhahood, keeping in mind those multitudes of statements of the Teaching, entering into those oceans of entries into the Teaching, pondering that method of teaching, plunging into the principles of that whirlpool of teaching, entering fully into the space of that teaching, clarifying that sphere of teaching, and contemplating that treasure island of teaching, gradually made his way to Sagaratira in Lanka, where he looked in all directions, desiring to see the monk Supratishthita.
des dge slong shin tu brtan pa nam mkha'i dbyings la lha brgya stong grangs med pas yongs su bskor cing phan tshun du 'chag pa mthong ngo/ /
Then he saw the bhikṣu Supratiṣṭhita walking back and forth in the sky accompanied by countless hundreds of thousands of devas.
He saw Supratishthita walking in the sky, surrounded by countless hundreds of thousands of celestial beings.

nam mkha'i dbyings de yang lha'i dbang po rnams kyis/ dge slong shin tu brtan pa la mchod pa'i las su bya ba'i phyir lha rdzas kyi me tog sil ma'i sprin gyis yog pa dang / lha rdzas kyi rol mo'i sprin gyi sgra dang / dar gyi ba dan grangs med pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan par mthong ngo/ /

He saw deva lords in the sky making offerings to the bhikṣu Supratiṣṭhita with clouds of scattered divine flower petals, the sound of countless clouds of divine music, and countless adorning streamers and banners.

He also saw the sky covered with clouds of celestial flowers, with the sound of countless clouds of heavenly music and countless streamers and banners offered by the chief celestials to the monk Supratishthita as tokens of respect.
klu'i dbang po rnams kyis nam mkha' de la/ a ka ru nag po'i spos mngon par 'thul ba'i sprin shin tu mtho ba las 'brug sgra bsam gyis mi khyab pa 'byung bar byas pa mthong ngo/ /
He saw that nāga lords in the sky had created high clouds, made of the spreading incense smoke of black agarwood, from which came inconceivable claps of thunder.
He also saw inconceivable clouds of black aloe-scented water thundering in the sky, raised on high by the chief water spirits.

mi'am ci'i dbang po rnams kyis nam mkha'i de la lha rdzas kyi ngag snyan pa'i rgyud kyis bstod pa'i rol mo brdung ba dang / dkrol ba dang / glur blang ba'i dbyangs thams cad sbyar cing blangs ba thos par gyur to/ /
He heard kinnara lords offering their divine beautiful voices in songs of praise and the sounds of a concert with all musical instruments being played.
He also heard countless sounds of pleasing celestial music and song coming from the sky with words of reverence and hymns of praise, performed by supernatural beings;

lto 'phye chen po'i dbang po rnams kyis nam mkha' de la gos shin tu phra zhing mdog bzang pa'i sprin bsam gyis mi khyab pa dag yid dga' bas bkye ste/ dge slong shin tu brtan pa la dad cing mos pa'i gzugs su phyung ba mthong ngo/ /

He saw mahoraga lords in the sky joyfully and with faith bringing forth an inconceivable cloud of fine clothing in beautiful colors,[381] with the appearance of delighting in the bhikṣu Supratiṣṭhita.
he also saw inconceivable clouds of fine cloths spread out in the sky by joyous serpent chiefs out of respect for Supratishthita.

lha ma yin gyi dbang po rnams kyis kyang nam mkha' de la/ nor bu rin po che'i sprin bsam gyis mi khyab pa byin gyis brlabs te/ yon tan bsam gyis mi khyab pa'i rgyan snang ba dang ldan par byas pa mthong ngo/ /
He saw asura lords in the sky conjuring an inconceivable cloud of precious jewels shining with an inconceivable display of qualities.
He also saw inconceivable clouds of jewels set in the sky by the chief titans, with the light of the magnificent array of their inconceivable qualities.

nam mkha' lding gi dbang po mang po yang mi'i gzugs dang / kha dog dang / dbyibs su 'khod cing / nam mkha' lding gi dbang po'i bu mos kun nas bskor te gsod pa med la dga' zhing thal mo sbyar te gnas pa bsam gyis mi khyab pa mthong ngo/ /

He saw a gathered multitude of garuḍa lords in human form, color,[382] and shape, encircled by the daughters of the garuḍa lords, delighting[383] in nonviolence[384] and with their palms together in homage.
He also saw inconceivable hosts of bird girls, standing in the sky with their hands joined in gestures of respect, with noninjury uppermost in their minds.

gnod sbyin gyi dbang po brgya stong 'khor dang bcas pa bsam gyis mi khyab pa dag kyang nam mkha' de la shin tu mi sdug pa'i gzugs su/ dge slong shin tu brtan pa la byams pa'i mthu dang ldan par 'khor ba mthong ngo/ /
He saw an inconceivable hundred thousand yakṣa lords, arranged with their retinues in the sky, who had very ugly bodies and the power of love toward the bhikṣu Supratiṣṭhita.
He also saw inconceivable hundreds of thousands of goblin chiefs in the sky with their retinues, their bodies transfigured, directed there by goodwill toward the monk Supratishthita.
srin po'i dbang po brgya stong 'khor dang bcas pa bsam gyis mi khyab pa dag kyang / nam mkha' de la dge slong shin tu brtan pa yongs su srung ba byed cing kun tu rgyu ba mthong ngo/ /
He saw an inconceivable hundred thousand rākṣasa lords with their retinues in the sky who circled around the bhikṣu Supratiṣṭhita, guarding him.
He also saw inconceivable numbers of demigod chiefs with their retinues circling in the sky to protect Supratishthita.
tshangs pa'i dbang po brgya stong bsam gyis mi khyab pa dag kyang nam mkha' de la thal mo sbyar cing dga' ba dang yid du 'ong ba'i tshig gi rgyud kyis bstod pa rab tu brjod pa mthong ngo/ /
He saw an inconceivable hundred thousand Brahmakāyika lords with their retinues in the sky with their palms together in homage, engaged in singing his praises with beautiful, melodious voices.
He also saw inconceivable hundreds of thousands of Brahma chiefs in the sky making salutations, uttering pleasant words of respect and songs of praise.

gnas gtsang ma'i lha brgya stong bsam gyis mi khyab pa dag kyang nam mkha' de la dge slong shin tu brtan pa la mchod pa'i las su bya ba'i phyir/ thal mo sbyar cing gzhal med khang na gnas pa mthong ngo/ /
He saw an inconceivable hundred thousand Śuddhāvāsa devas in their aerial palaces in the sky making offerings to the bhikṣu Supratiṣṭhita.
He also saw inconceivable hundreds of thousands of celestial beings of the pure abodes in their palaces in the sky, paying their respects to the monk Supratishthita.

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis dge slong shin tu brtan pa de ltar nam mkha'i dbyings la 'chag cing 'dug pa mthong nas dga' rangs te mgu zhing nyams bde la tshim zhing yid bde ba skyes nas/ dge slong shin tu brtan pa la thal mo sbyar te/ phyag 'tshal nas 'di skad ces smras so/ /
Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, on seeing the bhikṣu Supratiṣṭhita walking in the sky, was filled with joy, delighted, elated, pleased, and happy. He placed his palms together in homage and said,
Then Sudhana, seeing the monk Supratishthita walking in the sky, was pleased, enraptured, transported, overjoyed, happy; he saluted and greeted Supratishthita and said to him,

'phags pa/ bdag gis bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed nas/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas sangs rgyas kyi chos btsal bar bgyi ba dang / ji ltar byang chub sems dpas sangs rgyas kyi chos yongs su bsgrub par bgyi ba dang / ji ltar byang chub sems dpas sangs rgyas kyi chos yongs su bsdu bar bgyi ba dang / ji ltar byang chub sems dpas sangs rgyas kyi chos bstan par bgyi ba dang / ji ltar byang chub sems dpas sangs rgyas kyi chos bsgom par bgyi ba dang / ji ltar byang chub sems dpas sangs rgyas kyi chos kyi rjes su 'brang bar bgyi ba dang / ji ltar byang chub sems dpas sangs rgyas kyi chos yongs su brtul bar bgyi ba dang / ji ltar byang chub sems dpas sangs rgyas kyi chos yongs su bsgom par bgyi ba dang / ji ltar byang chub sems dpas sangs rgyas kyi chos rnam par dag par bgyi ba dang / ji ltar byang chub sems dpas sangs rgyas kyi chos yongs su sbyang bar bgyi ba dang / ji ltar byang chub sems dpas sangs rgyas kyi chos khong du chud par bgyi ba ma 'tshal te/

“Ārya, I have developed the aspiration for the highest, complete enlightenment, but I do not know this‍—how should a bodhisattva seek for the Buddhadharma? How should a bodhisattva obtain the Buddhadharma? How should a bodhisattva compile the Buddhadharma? How should a bodhisattva serve[385] the Buddhadharma? How should a bodhisattva protect[386] the Buddhadharma? How should a bodhisattva follow the Buddhadharma? How should a bodhisattva accumulate[387] the Buddhadharma? How should a bodhisattva pervade[388] the Buddhadharma? How should a bodhisattva purify the Buddhadharma? How should a bodhisattva train in the Buddhadharma?[389] How should a bodhisattva understand the Buddhadharma?

“Noble one, I have set my mind on supreme enlightenment, but I do not know how an enlightening being is to seek the qualities of buddhas, how an enlightening being is to acquire the qualities of buddhas, how an enlightening being is to accumulate the qualities of buddhas, how an enlightening being is to cultivate the qualities of buddhas, how an enlightening being is to actualize the qualities of buddhas, how an enlightening being is to act in accord with the qualities of buddhas, how an enlightening being is to assemble the qualities of buddhas, how an enlightening being is to contemplate the qualities of buddhas, how an enlightening being is to clarify the qualities of buddhas in order to accomplish all the tasks of enlightening beings, how an enlightening being is to approach and follow the qualities of buddhas.

'phags pa ni/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams la gdams ngag dang / rjes su bstan pa mdzad do/ /zhes bdag gis thos na/ 'phags pa/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas sangs rgyas kyi chos la nan tan du bgyi/ ji ltar nan tan du bgyis na yang dag pa ji lta ba bzhin dang / skol bar mi 'gyur ba'i slad du sangs rgyas mthong ba dang mi 'bral ba dang / byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi dge ba'i rtsa ba dang tshul gcig tu 'gyur ba'i slad du byang chub sems dpa' mthong ba dang mi 'bral ba dang / ye shes rtogs par 'gyur ba'i slad du sangs rgyas kyi chos dang mi 'bral ba dang / byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi don yongs su thob par bgyi ba'i slad du byang chub sems dpa'i smon lam thams cad dang mi 'bral ba dang; bskal pa thams cad du gnas pas yongs su mi skyo bar bgyi ba'i slad du byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa dang mi 'bral ba dang / 'jig rten gyi khams thams cad yongs su dag par bgyi ba'i slad du sangs rgyas kyi zhing thams cad rgyas par dgang ba dang mi 'bral ba dang / de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi rnam par 'phrul pa thams cad rnam par dmigs par bgyi ba'i slad du sangs rgyas kyi rnam par 'phrul pa mthong ba dang mi 'bral ba dang / byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa sprul pa lta bus srid pa'i rgyud thams cad du skye zhing shi 'pho ba'i skye mched rang gi lus kyis nyams su myong bar bgyi ba'i slad du 'dus byas kyi gnas dang mi 'bral ba dang / de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi chos kyi sprin yongs su gzung ba'i slad du chos mnyan pa dang mi 'bral ba dang / dus gsum gyi ye shes khong du chud cing rjes su 'brang bar bgyi ba'i slad du ye shes snang ba dang mi 'bral bar 'gyur ba de bdag la bstan du gsol/

“Ārya, I have heard that you give instruction and teachings to bodhisattvas! Therefore, Ārya, teach me how bodhisattvas should practice the Buddhadharma so that while practicing they will not lack the sight of the Buddha in order to not become separated from the truth; will not lack the vision of the bodhisattvas in order to have the same way[390] as the roots of merit of all bodhisattvas; will not lack the Buddhadharma in order to realize wisdom; will not lack the bodhisattva aspiration in order to attain all the goals of the bodhisattvas; will not lack bodhisattva conduct in order to never become weary of remaining throughout all kalpas; will not lack the pervading of all buddha realms in order to purify all world realms; will not lack seeing the miracles of buddhas in order to perceive all the miraculous manifestations of all the tathāgatas; will not lack a composite presence so that through bodhisattva conduct that is like a magical creation they will experience as their own bodies the āyatanas that are born and pass away within all existences; will not lack hearing the Dharma in order to obtain the clouds of Dharma of all the tathāgatas; and will not lack the light of wisdom in order to gain and use the knowledge of the three times.”[391]

Noble one, I hear that you give instructions to enlightening beings: please tell me how an enlightening being is to set to work on the Buddha teachings, not to lose sight of Buddha whatever one is doing, not to lose sight of enlightening beings so as to be always in contact with reality, always to be involved with the Buddha teachings so as to be at one with the roots of goodness of all enlightening beings, always to be involved with the vows of enlightening beings so as to accord with knowledge, always to be involved in the practices of enlightening beings so as to accomplish the task of all enlightening beings, always to be pervading all buddha-fields so as to live continuously through all ages, to remain in the conditional for the manifestation of the projections of all buddhas, always to be hearing the Teaching in order to visit in one’s own body the places of death and birth of all buddhas by the emanationlike action of enlightening beings, and to always be in contact with the light of knowledge so as to receive the teachings of all buddhas and accord with knowledge of past, present, and future.”
de skad ces smras pa dang /

dge slong shin tu brtan pas/ tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la 'di skad ces smras so/ / de ltar khyod kyis bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed de/ sangs rgyas kyi chos dang / thams cad mkhyen pa'i chos dang; rang byung gi chos 'dri ba legs so/ /legs so/ /

When he had said this, the bhikṣu Supratiṣṭhita said to Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, “Noble one, it is excellent, excellent, that you have developed the aspiration for the highest, complete enlightenment and that you ask questions about the Buddha’s Dharma, the Dharma of omniscience, the self-arisen Dharma.

To this, Supratishthita replied, “It is good that you have set your mind on supreme perfect enlightenment and ask about the qualities of buddhahood, the qualities of omniscience, the qualities of independence.

rigs kyi bu/ kho bos ni byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa thogs pa med pa'i sgo thob pa ste/ rigs kyi bu/ byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa thogs pa med pa'i sgo de kho bos blangs te/ yongs su bzung nas rjes su 'brang zhing rnam par dbye ba dang / rnam par dpyad pa dang / rnam par brtag pa dang; snang bar bya ba dang / rab tu snang bar byas pas thogs pa med pa'i mtha' zhes bya ba'i ye shes snang ba thob bo/ / de thob pas kho bos ni sems can thams cad kyi sems dang / spyod pa khong du chud par bya ba la thogs pa med do/ / sems can thams cad kyi skye ba dang / 'chi 'pho yongs su shes par bya ba la thogs pa med do/ / sngon gyi gnas rjes su dran par bya pa'i sgor 'jug pa la thogs pa med do/ / phyi ma'i mtha'i bskal par 'gro ba thams cad dang 'grogs par bya ba la thogs pa med do/ / da ltar byung ba'i dus gyi 'gro ba thams cad rnam par rig par bya ba la thogs pa med do/ / sems can thams cad kyi sgra skad dang / kun rdzob yongs su shes par bya ba la thogs pa med do/ / sems can thams cad kyi the tshom gcad par bya ba la thogs pa med do/ / sems can thams cad kyi dbang po tha dad par khong du chud par bya ba la thogs pa med do/ / sems can thams cad yongs su smin par bya ba dang / gdul ba'i dus su 'gro bar bya ba la thogs pa med do/ / nyin mtshan dang / skad cig dang / yud tsam dang / thang cig dang / dus kyi ming du bya ba khong du chud par bya ba la thogs pa med do/ / dus gsum rgya mtsho'i rgyud du 'jug par bya ba la thogs pa med do/ / phyogs bcu'i sangs rgyas kyi zhing rang gi lus kyis rgyas par 'gengs par bya ba la thogs pa med do/ / de ni de ltar dngos po med pa la gnas shing mngon par 'du bya ba med pa'i rdzu 'phrul thob pa'i phyir te/

“Noble one, I have the attainment of the unimpeded gateway, the liberation of a bodhisattva. I have acquired, followed, categorized, analyzed, examined, and elucidated this unimpeded gateway, this liberation of a bodhisattva, and I have attained the light of wisdom called the unimpeded apex. Having attained that, I have no impediment in perceiving the minds and conduct of all beings; I have no impediment in knowing the births and deaths of all beings; I have no impediment in entering the gateway of remembering past lives; I have no impediment in dwelling with all beings in future kalpas; I have no impediment in perceiving all the beings of the present time; I have no impediment in knowing the relative languages of all beings; I have no impediment in cutting through the doubts of all beings; I have no impediment in comprehending the different faculties of all beings; I have no impediment in acting at the right time to ripen and guide all beings; I have no impediment in identifying days, nights, seconds, hours,[392] and periods of time; I have no impediment in entering into the ocean of the three times;[393] and I have no impediment in incorporeally[394] pervading the buddha realms in the ten directions, because I am present without substance and have attained noncomposite miraculous powers.

I have attained the enlightening liberation ‘unobstructed door.’ Going in and out of this ‘unobstructed door’ liberation, practicing it, analyzing it, examining it, investigating it, and clarifying it, I have attained a light of knowledge called ‘ultimate nonobstruction,’ whereby I am free from obstruction in awareness of the mental actions of all sentient beings, knowing where all sentient beings die and are born, entries into the channels to memory of past states, associations with all beings in future ages, communications to all sentient beings of the present time, knowledge of the conventions of languages of all sentient beings, cutting off the doubts of all sentient beings, comprehending the differences in the faculties of all sentient beings, approaching all sentient beings at appropriate times to guide them to full development, comprehension of time divisions as being conceptual, and in noncorporeal pervasion of the buddha-fields in the ten directions, all by the attainment of nonbeing, nonabiding, and nondoing.

rigs kyi bu/ dngos po med pa la gnas shing / mngon par 'du bya ba med pa'i rdzu 'phrul de'i byin gyis kho bo nam mkha'i dbyings 'di las phan tshun du 'gro zhing 'dug pa dang / bsnyes pa dang / spyod lam sna tshogs su spyod do/ / mi snang bar byed do/ / snang bar 'byung ngo/ / du ba 'thul bar byed do/ / me lce 'bar bar byed do/ / gcig tu byas shing mang por bsgyur ro/ / mang por byas shing gcig tu bsgyur ro/ / snang ba dang mi snang ba'ang nyams su myong bar byed do/ / rtsig pa la'ang thag thogs med pa dang / ra ba la'ang thag thogs med par 'gro ste/ dper na/ nam mkha' la bya ba bzhin no/ / nam mkha' la'ang skyil mo krung gis 'gro ste/ dper na/ 'dab chags bya bzhin no/ / sa la yang byi'u zul dang steng du 'byung ba byed de/ dper na/ chu la bya ba bzhin no/ / chu la yang 'bying ba med par 'gro ste/ dper na sa la bya ba bzhan [*bzhin?] no/ / du ba 'thul ba dang / me lce 'bar bar byed de/ dper na/ me'i phung po chen po bzhin no/ / sa yang yongs su g.yos par byed do/ / nyi ma dang zla ba 'di gnyis de ltar rdzu 'phrul che zhing de ltar mthu che la/ de ltar gzi brjid che yang lag pas kun nas yongs su nyug go / tshangs pa'i 'jig rten gyi bar dag tu'ang lus kyis dbang bsgyur ro/ / 'jig rten spos kyi dud pa na bun du chags pa'i sprin gyis kun nas khebs par byas shing rab tu 'bar bar byed do/ / rin po che thams cad kyi 'od zer gyi sprin gyi dra bas 'jig rten kun nas khebs par byas shing / 'gro ba thams cad dang 'dra ba'i sprul pa'i sprin rab tu 'gyed do/ /

“Noble one, because I am present without substance and have the power of noncomposite miraculous powers, I can walk back and forth, stand,[395] sit, lie down, and perform various activities in the sky. I can become invisible. I can reappear. I can become smoke. I can become a fire. I can transform from one into many. I can transform from many into one. I can be both visible and invisible. I can pass without impediment through walls and without impediment through city ramparts, as if through space.[396] I travel cross-legged through the air, as a bird does. I can plunge into the earth and reappear the way a bird does in water. I can walk on water without sinking like a bird on the ground. I can produce smoke and flames the way a great fire does. I can make the ground shake. I can wipe clean with my hands this sun and this moon that have such great miraculous power, great mightiness, and great brilliance. My body can dominate everywhere up to and including the world of Brahmā. I can cover the world with a mist formed from clouds of incense smoke and then make it shine. I can cover the world with a network of clouds of light rays from all jewels. I can send forth a cloud of emanations that resemble all beings.

By the realization of this mystic power of nondoing I walk, stand, sit, and lie down in the sky, disappear and appear, produce smoke and flame. Being one, I become many; being many, I become one. I become now visible, now invisible. I go through walls unhindered, as through empty space. While sitting cross-legged I travel in space, like a bird on the wing. I go in and out of the earth as if in water. I walk on water unhindered as on the earth. I smoke and flame like a great conflagration. I cause even the earth to quake. With my hand I polish even the sun and moon, those bodies of great potency, power, and light. I envelop even up to the Brahma world in my body. Covering the world with clouds of lights the colors of all jewels, I emit clouds in the forms of all beings.

kha dog mtha' yas pa'i 'od kyi dra ba'i sprin rab tu bkye zhing / phyogs kun tu'ang 'gro ste/ 'di ltar shar phyogs su'ang 'gro'o/ / lho phyogs dang / nub phyogs dang / byang phyogs dang / byang shar gyi phyogs mtshams dang / shar lho'i phyogs mtshams dang / lho nub kyi phyogs mtshams dang / nub byang gi phyogs mtshams dang; 'og dang / bla'i phyogs su'ang 'gro'o/ / sems kyi skad cig re re yang shar phyogs logs su 'jig rten gyi khams gcig kyang 'da'o/ /

“I can emanate clouds of networks of lights of infinite colors that go to all directions and realms. In that way, they go to the east, to the south, to the west, to the north, to the northeast, to the southeast, to the southwest, to the northwest, downward, and upward. In one instant of mind, they go beyond one world realm in the east.
Emanating clouds of webs of light of infinite colors, I go forth in all directions: in each moment of thought I pass one world to the east,

'jig rten gyi khams gnyis dang / bcu yang 'da'o; /'jig rten gyi khams brgya dang / 'jig rten gyi khams stong dang / 'jig rten gyi khams brgya phrag stong dang / 'jig rten gyi khams bye ba dang / 'jig rten gyi khams bye ba phrag brgya dang; 'jig rten gyi khams bye ba phrag stong dang / 'jig rten gyi khams bye ba brgya phrag stong dang / 'jig rten gyi khams bye ba khrag khrig brgya phrag stong dang / 'jig rten gyi khams tshad med pa dang / 'jig rten gyi khams dpag tu med pa dang / 'jig rten gyi khams grangs med pa dang / 'jig rten gyi khams bsam gyis mi khyab pa dang / 'jig rten gyi khams mtshungs pa med pa dang / 'jig rten gyi khams gzhal du med pa dang / 'jig rten gyi khams kun tu mtha' yas pa dang / 'jig rten gyi khams mu med pa dang / 'jig rten gyi khams sa mtshams med pa dang / 'jig rten gyi khams brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa dag kyang 'da' bar byed de/

“They go beyond two world realms and ten world realms. They go beyond a hundred world realms. They go beyond a thousand world realms, a hundred thousand world realms, ten million world realms, a billion world realms, a trillion world realms, a quintillion world realms, an incalculable number of world realms, a measureless number of world realms, innumerable world realms, an inconceivable number of world realms, an unequaled number of world realms, an unfathomable number of world realms, an infinite number of world realms, an endless number of world realms, limitless world realms, and an inexpressible number of world realms.

I pass two worlds, three worlds, a hundred worlds, a thousand worlds, a hundred thousand worlds, a million worlds, a hundred millions worlds, a billion worlds, a hundred billion worlds, a quintillion worlds, countless, measureless, endless, incomparable, inconceivable, incalculable, untold, unspeakably unspeakable numbers of worlds;

'jig rten gyi khams de dag na/ sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das ji snyed cig bzhugs shing 'tsho gzhes la/ 'jig rten gyi khams rgya mtsho de dang de dag dang / 'jig rten gyi khams 'byams klas pa de dang de dag dang / 'jig rten gyi khams kyi phyogs de dang de dag dang / 'jig rten gyi khams kyi rgyud de dang de dag dang / 'jig rten gyi khams yongs su 'du ba de dang de dag dang / 'jig rten gyi khams 'byung ba de dang de dag dang / 'jig rten gyi khams su bya ba de dang de dag dang / 'jig rten gyi khams kyi sgo de dang de dag dang / 'jig rten gyi khams kyi bskal par bya ba de dang de dag dang / 'jig rten gyi khams su 'jug pa de dang de dag dang / 'jig rten gyi khams kyi snying po byang chub rnam par bkod pa de dang de dag dang / 'jig rten gyi khams kyi 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor de dang de dag dang / sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das ji snyed cig chos ston pa'i de bzhin gshegs pa de dag las/ de bzhin gshegs pa re re zhing yang sangs rgyas kyi zhing mtha' yas pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi lus sna tshogs dang / lus re re zhing yang sangs rgyas kyi zhing mtha' yas pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi mchod pa'i sprin gyi char 'bebs shing spyan sngar 'gro'o/ / de dag tu phyin nas kyang me tog thams cad dang / spos thams cad dang / phreng ba thams cad dang / phye ma thams cad dang / byug pa thams cad dang / na bza' thams cad dang / rgyal mtshan thams cad dang / lha'i ba dan thams cad dang / bla re thams cad dang / dra ba thams cad dang / gzugs thams cad kyi mchod pa rgyun ma chad par byed do/ /

“All the buddha bhagavats that are present, living, and remaining in those world realms, in that ocean of world realms, in that vast extent of world realms, in the world realms in the directions, in the world realms that are coming to an end, in the world realms that are assembled, in the world realms that are created, in those world realms that are named, in the gateways of those world realms, in the kalpas of those world realms, in the entrances into those world realms, and at the bodhimaṇḍas of those world realms, those buddha bhagavats who are teaching the Dharma in the circle of their assembled followers in those world realms‍—each of the tathāgatas among those tathāgatas has a variety of bodies that are as numerous as the atoms in the infinite buddha realms. I approach each of those bodies while sending down a rain from clouds of offering as numerous as the atoms in the infinite buddha realms. Having approached them, I make a continuous offering of all flowers, all incense, all garlands, all powders, all ointments, all food, all banners, all flags, all canopies, all networks of beads, and all ornaments.[397]

and in those worlds are buddhas living, in each of those oceans of worlds, in each of those streams of worlds, in each region of those worlds, in each age of those worlds, in each set of those worlds, in each occurrence of those worlds, in each expression of those worlds, in each medium of those worlds, in each particular of those worlds, in each sacred place in those worlds, in each site of enlightenment in those worlds, in each assembly in those worlds—I go to each of the buddhas teaching in those worlds with as many bodies as atoms in endless buddha-lands, each body raining as many clouds of offerings as atoms in endless buddha-lands. Going to the buddhas, I ceaselessly make offerings of all kinds of flowers, fragrances, garlands, unguents, robes, banners, pennants, canopies, nets, and ornaments.

sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das de dag gis gang ji snyed du gsungs pa dang / bstan pa dang / brjod pa dang / yang dag par bshad pa dang / yang dag par smos pa dang / yongs su brjod pa dang / man ngag tu gsungs pa dang / shin tu bstan pa dang / rab tu brjod pa de dag thams cad kyang shes shing 'dzin to/ /
“I know and remember whatever all those buddha bhagavats say, teach, utter, explain, describe, elucidate, instruct, proclaim, and disclose.
Those buddhas explain, reveal, and elucidate, and I acknowledge and take up all that they teach.
