sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das de dag gi sangs rgyas kyi zhing yongs su dag pa ji snyed pa de dag thams cad kyang rjes su dran no/ / shar phyogs su ji lta ba de bzhin du lho phyogs dang / nub phyogs dang / byang phyogs dang / byang shar gyi phyogs mtshams dang / shar lho'i phyogs mtshams dang / lho nub kyi phyogs mtshams dang; nub byang gi phyogs mtshams dang / 'og dang steng gi phyogs su yang 'jig rten gyi khams gcig kyang 'da'o/ / 'jig rten gyi khams gnyis dang / bcu yang 'da'o/ / 'jig rten gyi khams brgya nas 'jig rten gyi khams sangs rgyas kyi zhing brjod du med pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed dag kyang 'da'o/ /

“I remember all the pure buddha realms of those buddha bhagavats. As it is in the east, so it is in the south, the west, the north, the northeast, the southeast, the southwest, the northwest, above and below, beyond one world realm, beyond two world realms and ten world realms, beyond a hundred world realms, and so on, up to beyond as many world realms as there are atoms in even more innumerable than innumerable buddha realms.
I also remember the purity of the buddha-lands of those buddhas. As in the east, so also in all directions do I go to innumerable worlds,

'jig rten gyi khams de dag na/ sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das ji snyed cig bzhugs shing 'tsho skyong la/ 'jig rten gyi khams mtsho de dang de dag dang / 'jig rten gyi khams rnam par dag pa de dang de dag nas/ 'jig rten gyi khams kyi 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor de dang de dag na chos ston pa de dag kun kyang mthong ngo; ; de bzhin gshegs pa de dag la'ang me tog thams cad nas/ gzugs thams cad kyi bar gyis mchod pa byed do/ / sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das de dag gis gang ji snyed du gsungs pa nas/ rab tu brjod pa'i bar de dag thams cad kyang yongs su shes shing 'dzin to/ / sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das de dag gi sangs rgyas kyi zhing yongs su dag pa gang ji snyed pa de dag thams cad kyang rjes su dran no/ /

“I see all the buddha bhagavats that are present, living, and remaining in those world realms, in that ocean of world realms, in those pure world realms, who are teaching the Dharma in the circle of their followers. I make offerings to those tathāgatas with all flowers, and so on, up to all ornaments.[398] I know and remember whatever all those buddha bhagavats say, and so on, and what they disclose. I remember all the pure buddha realms that there are of those buddha bhagavats.
see the buddhas teaching there, make offerings to them, acknowledge and take up what they say, and remember the purity of their buddha-lands.

sems can gang gis kho bo mthong bar gyur pa dag/ gang dang 'grogs par gyur pa de dag kun kyang / bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu nges par 'gyur ro/ / sems can phra mo'am/ rags pa'am/ ngan pa'am/ bzang ba'am/ bde ba'am/ mi bde ba gang ji snyed cig kho bos mthong bar gyur pa de dag kun la yang yongs su smin par bya ba dang / 'dul ba'i dus las mi 'da' bar bya ba'i phyir/ khong ta de dag gi lus kyi tshad dang mnyam par lus byin gyis rlob bo/ / sems can ji snyed cig kho bo'i drung du 'ongs pa de dag thams cad kyang / byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa kun tu 'gro ba 'di dang / byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa rnam par gnon pa don yod pa la rab tu gzhog go/

“Whatever being sees me, who associates with me, will definitely attain the highest, complete enlightenment. Whether they are small or huge, good or bad, happy or unhappy beings, however many of them see me, I will bless all of their bodies and I will not let the time to ripen and guide them pass. However many beings come before me, I will establish all of them in this bodhisattva liberation that goes everywhere and has fruitful prowess.

Also, all the beings who see me, to whom I come, are assured of supreme perfect enlightenment. Also, whatever beings I see, small or large, underdeveloped or well developed, happy or unhappy, I adopt a corresponding physical form, in order to guide them to maturity and perfection in the appropriate time. And all beings who come to me I establish in this enlightening liberation, which is everywhere at once and which is the consummation of unerring power.

rigs kyi bu/ kho bos ni byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa thogs pa med pa'i sgo kun tu 'gro ba/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i mchod pa dang / rim gro rab tu sbyor ba/ sems can thams cad yongs su smin par bya ba dang mthun pa 'di shes par zad na

“Noble one, I know only this bodhisattva liberation that goes everywhere, which is dedicated to making offerings and serving the tathāgatas and which is an unimpeded gateway favorable for ripening all beings.
“Son, I know this enlightening liberation ‘unobstructed door,’ which is everywhere at once engaged in the service of the buddhas, appropriate to the development of all beings.

kho bos byang chub sems dpa' snying rje chen po'i ngang tshul can/ theg pa chen po'i ngang tshul can/ byang chub sems dpa'i lam dang mi 'bral ba'i ngang tshul can/ thogs pa med pa'i ngang tshul can/ byang chub sems dpa'i bsam pa'i snying po chud mi gson pa'i ngang tshul can/ byang chub kyi sems yongs su mi gtong ba'i ngang tshul can; sangs rgyas kyi chos la lhag par dmigs pa'i ngang tshul can/ thams cad mkhyen pa yid la bya ba dang mi 'bral ba'i ngang tshul can/ nam mkha' dang mnyam pa'i ngang tshul can/ 'jig rten thams cad la mi gnas pa'i ngang tshul can/ chud mi gson pa'i ngang tshul can/ mnyam pa'i ngang tshul can/ ma god pa'i ngang tshul can/ glags med pa'i ngang tshul can/ ma 'dres pa'i ngang tshul can/ rnyog pa med pa'i ngang tshul can/ 'gyod pa med pa'i ngang tshul can/ rnam par dag pa'i ngang tshul can; byang chub sems dpa' rdul dang bral ba de dag gi spyod pa shes pa'am/ yon tan brjod par nus re skan/

“How could I know or describe the qualities of the bodhisattvas who have the conduct of great compassion, who have the conduct of practicing the Mahāyāna, who have the conduct that is never apart from the path of the bodhisattvas, who have unimpeded conduct, who have the conduct of the essence of bodhisattva motivation that is never lost, who have the conduct that never forsakes the aspiration to enlightenment, who have the conduct that is focused on the Buddhadharma, who have the conduct that is never apart from attention to omniscience, who have the conduct that is as vast as space, who have the conduct that is not based on the world, who have the conduct that is never lost, who have the conduct that never deteriorates, who have the conduct that is never impaired, who have the conduct that is never destroyed, who have the conduct that is never adulterated, who have the conduct that is never polluted, who have the conduct that is without regret, who have pure conduct, and who have bodhisattva conduct that is stainless?

How can I know the practice, or tell the virtues, of the great enlightening beings who act on great compassion, who act in accord with the practice of the Great Vehicle, whose conduct never deviates from the path of enlightening beings, whose conduct is free from attachment, whose conduct always embodies the will of enlightening beings, who always act with the thought of enlightenment, whose action is focused on the way of the enlightened, who always act with the thought of omniscience, whose way of action is like the sky, whose conduct is independent of all mundane realms, whose conduct is flawless, whose conduct is uncorrupted, whose conduct is consistent, whose conduct is faultless, whose conduct is pure, whose conduct is unblemished, whose conduct is free from evil, whose conduct is honest, whose conduct is dispassionate, whose conduct is undefiled?

song / rigs kyi bu/ lho phyogs kyi rgyud 'di nyid na/ dra byi la'i grong rdal rdo rje'i grong khyer ces bya ba yod de/ de na dra byi la sprin ces bya ba 'dug gi de'i gan du song la/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bya ba dang / ji ltar nan tan tu bya ba dris shig /

“Depart, noble one. In this southern region, in the land of Draviḍa, there is a town called Vajrapura. There dwells a Dravidian by the name of Megha. Go to him and ask him, ‘How does a bodhisattva train in bodhisattva conduct? How does a bodhisattva practice it?’ ”
“Go south, son, to the Dravidian city Vajrapura. There lives a grammarian named Megha. Go to him and ask him how an enlightening being is to learn and practice the conduct of enlightening beings.”

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis dge slong shin tu brtan pa'i rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal nas/ lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas te/ yang dang yang du bltas nas/ dge slong shin tu brtan pa'i drung nas song ngo/ /

Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, bowed his head to the feet of the bhikṣu Supratiṣṭhita, circumambulated the bhikṣu Supratiṣṭhita to his right a hundred thousand times, and, looking back a hundred thousand times, departed from the bhikṣu Supratiṣṭhita.
Then Sudhana again paid his respects to the monk Supratishthita and left.

Chapter 7. Megha
Megha

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang chos kyi dad pa'i shugs dang byin gyis non pa sangs rgyas yid la bya ba'i 'du shes dang ldan pa/ dkon mchog gsum gyi gdung mi gcad pa la rab tu brtson pa/ dus gsum snang bas sems snang bar gyur pa smon lam chen po yid la byed pa dang ldan pa/ sems can gyi khams thams cad yongs su bskyab pa'i thabs la zhugs pa/ 'dus byas kyi dga' ba thams cad la mi gnas pa'i sems dang ldan pa/ chos thams cad kyi rang bzhin nges par rtogs par bya ba la brtson pa/ 'jig rten gyi khams thams cad yongs su sbyang ba'i smon lam las mi g.yo ba/ sangs rgyas thams cad kyi 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor na gnas pa med par gnas pa/ chos kyi snang ba rjes su dran par bya ba dang / dge ba'i gshegs gnyen rjes su dran par bya ba dang / 'dod chags dang bral ba'i rigs yongs su rjod par byed cing /

Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, was filled with the power and might of faith in the Dharma. He was focused on the idea of following the Buddha; he was sincerely dedicated to the lineage of the Three Jewels; his mind illuminated the worlds of the three times;[399] he was focused on following the great aspiration; he was continuously dedicated[400] to saving all the realms of beings; his mind did not dwell on composite pleasures;[401] he was devoted to contemplating the nature of all phenomena; he never deviated from the aspiration to purify all world realms; he dwelled without attachment in the circles of the assemblies of all the buddhas; he remembered the light of the Dharma;[402] he remembered his kalyāṇamitras;[403] and he proclaimed the lineage of freedom from desire.[404]

Then Sudhana, mindful of the light of the Teaching, steeped in intensity of faith in the Teaching, his attention focused on thoughts of Buddha, intent on perpetuating the lineage of the three treasures, remembering spiritual friends, his mind having illumined the worlds of past, present, and future, thinking of great vows, striving for the salvation of all beings, his mind unattached to enjoyment of any created things, praising the tradition of dispassion, intent upon contemplation of the instrinsic essence of all things, firm in the commitment to purify all worlds, sojourning without attachment in the congregations of all buddhas,

mthar gyis dra byi la'i grong rdal rdo rje'i grong khyer du phyin nas/ dra byi la sprin yongs su tshol tshol ba las/ grong khyer gyi khams shig na chos bstan pa'i don du/ seng ge'i khri la 'dug cing / srog chags stong phrag bcu tsam zhig la/ chos kyi rnam grangs yi ge'i 'khor lo'i rgyud kyi rgyan ces bya ba yongs su ston cing 'dug pa mthong ngo/ /

Eventually he arrived at Vajrapura in the Draviḍa region. He searched and searched for the Dravidian Megha until he saw him in one of the courtyards in the town. He was seated on a lion throne in order to teach the Dharma, and he was teaching the Dharma teaching called the display of the rotating wheel of syllables to about ten thousand beings.

gradually approached the Dravidian city Vajrapura, looking for the grammarian Megha. He saw Megha at a crossroads in the middle of the city, sitting on a lion seat to talk about the Teaching, elucidating a scripture called Manifestation of Turning of the Wheel of Letters.

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis/ dra byi la sprin gyi rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te/ dra byi la sprin la lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas mdun du 'dug ste/ thal mo sbyar nas 'di skad ces smras so/ / 'phags pa/ bdag gis bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed na/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bgyi ba dang / ji ltar nan tan bgyi ba dang / ji ltar byang chub sems dpa'i byang chub kyi sems srid pa'i lam rgyud thams cad du chab mi 'tshal ba dang / ji ltar yongs su skyo ba ma mchis shing / bsam pa brtan par 'gyur ba dang / ji ltar thub pa ma mchis shing / lhag pa'i bsam pa yongs su dag par 'gyur ba dang / ji ltar yongs su skyo ba ma mchis shing / snying rje chen po'i stobs yang dag par skye bar 'gyur ba dang / ji ltar sgo kun nas rnam par dag cing gzungs kyi stobs gnon par 'gyur ba dang / ji ltar ma rig pa'i rab rib dang sgrib pa rnam par 'thor zhing / shes rab kyi 'od chos thams cad la rab rib ma mchis pa'i snang ba skye bar 'gyur ba dang / ji ltar don dang / chos dang / nges pa'i tshig dang / spobs pa la mkhas pa'i dbyangs kyi dkyil 'khor yongs su rdzogs shing / tha dad pa yang dag par shes pa'i stobs gnon par 'gyur ba dang / ji ltar sangs rgyas thams cad kyi 'khor lo tha mi dad pa yang dag par 'dzin cing dran pa'i stobs yongs su gnon par 'gyur ba dang / ji ltar chos thams cad kyi phyogs rig pa'i snang ba rjes su rtogs shing rig pa'i stobs rnam par dag par 'gyur ba dang / ji ltar byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin gyi stobs chos thams cad kyi don rnam par gdon mi za bar rab tu dbye ba la brtson pas 'grub par 'gyur ba ma 'tshal to/ /

Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, bowed his head to the feet of the Dravidian Megha, circumambulated the Dravidian Megha to his right many hundreds of thousands of times, sat before him, and with palms together said, “Ārya, I have developed the aspiration for the highest, complete enlightenment. However, I do not know how bodhisattvas should train in bodhisattva conduct; how they should practice it; how bodhisattvas do not lose the aspiration to enlightenment; how they keep their motivation firm within all the states of existence so that they do not lose heart;[405] how they purify their resolve so that they do not become oppressed; how they develop the power of great compassion so that they do not lose heart; how they gain the power of retention so that all gateways are purified; how they develop the light of wisdom, the light that frees all phenomena from darkness, so that the darkness that obscures omniscience will be dispersed; how they gain the power of discernment so that they perfect the domain of voice through being skilled in meaning, Dharma, definitions, and eloquence; how they gain the power of memory so that they will possess without differentiation all the Buddha’s Dharma wheels; how they purify states of rebirth[406] so that they will realize and follow the light in all rebirths and phenomena in all directions; and how the power of bodhisattvas’ samādhi is brought forth so as to have the highest certainty and analysis of all the meanings of the Dharma.”

Sudhana went up to him, paid his respects, and said, “Noble one, I have set my mind on supreme perfect enlightenment, but I do not know how an enlightening being is to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings. How is an enlightening being to preserve the determination for enlightenment? How does one develop a will that is firm in all states of existence and is indefatigable? How does one purify one’s intent, in accord with invincibility? How is the power of great compassion produced so that it never flags? How does one acquire mental command that is totally purified? How is the light of wisdom produced, light free from obscurity in regard to meaning, principle, expression, and presence of mind? How does one acquire the power of recollection, keeping in mind the teachings of all buddhas without confusion? How is the power of migration purified, illumining all states of existence with the truth? How is an enlightening being’s power of concentration perfected, intent on the ascertainment and discernment of the meanings of all principles?”

de nas dra byi la sprin gyis byang chub sems dpa' la rim gror bya ba'i phyir seng ge'i khri de las langs te/ babs nas/ tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la lus thams cad kyis phyag byas nas/ tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la gser gyi me tog gi phung pos mngon par gtor to/ / nor bu rin po che rin thang med pa mang po dang / tsan dan gyi phye ma dam pas kyang mngon par gtor to/ / gos tshon sna tshogs rnam pa tha dad pas kha dog bsgyur ba/ brgya stong phrag du mas kyang mngon par bkab bo/ spos kyi me tog kha dog rnam pa tha dad cing yid du 'ong la blta na sdug pa mang pos kyang mngon par gtor nas/ mchod pa rnam pa sna tshogs gzhan dag gis kyang mchod pa dang / rim gro dang / bkur sti dang / bsti stang cher byas te/

Then the Dravidian Megha, in order to show respect to the bodhisattva, rose from his throne, stepped down, and with his entire body prostrated before Sudhana, the head merchant’s son. He scattered a heap of golden flowers toward Sudhana, the head merchant’s son. He scattered many priceless precious jewels and supreme sandalwood powder. He draped him in many hundreds of thousands of cloths that had been dyed in various colors. He scattered many beautiful and delightful perfumed flowers of many different colors. He also made offerings with other kinds of offerings, showing him respect, honor, and veneration.

Now Megha, out of respect for an enlightening being, got off his seat and prostrated himself before Sudhana, then showered Sudhana with golden flowers, precious jewels, and the finest sandalwood powders, covered him with hundreds of thousands of robes dyed in various colors, showered him with beautiful flowers of many various colors with pleasant scents, and honored him with various other offerings,

tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la 'di skad ces smras so/ / rigs kyi bu khyod kyis de ltar bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed pa legs so/ /legs so/ / rigs kyi bu/ gang gis bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed pa de ni/ sangs rgyas thams cad kyi gdung mi gcad pa'i phyir zhugs pa yin/

'dod chags dang bral ba'i rigs yang dag pa ji lta ba bzhin du rnam par rigs par bya ba la brtson pa yin/

de ni de bzhin gshegs pa mang po thams cad kyis byin gyis brlabs pa yin/

des ni sems can gyi khams thams cad kyang ngan song gi lam rgyud gsum po yongs su bcad pa dang / mi khom pa dang / ngan 'gro'i lam thams cad bzlog pa dang /

always seeing spiritual benefactors, consistently listening to the lofty buddha-teaching, purifying the will for enlightenment, cultivating the cause of the thought of enlightenment, gaining the illumination of the path of enlightening beings, following the knowledge of enlightening beings, and dwelling in the stages of enlightening beings.

“Noble one, this is what I think:

byang chub sems dpa' rnams ni dka' ba byed pa ste/ 'byung bar dka' zhing mthong bar dka' ba'o/ /

the bodhisattvas are like Sumeru because of the great height of their roots of merit;
enlightening beings are the polar mountain, by virtue of the height of their roots of goodness;
byang chub sems dpa' rnams ni snying po byang chub tu ye shes kyi zla ba 'char bar 'gyur ba'i phyir zla ba lta bu'o/ /
the bodhisattvas are like the moon because they rise as the moon of the wisdom of the essence of enlightenment;
enlightening beings are a moon, the moon of knowledge of the essence of enlightenment having risen in them;
byang chub sems dpa' rnams ni bdud kyi sde thams cad rab tu 'joms pas dpa' bor gyur pa'o/ /
the bodhisattvas are like warriors because they defeat the armies of the māras;
enlightening beings are warriors crushing the armies of all demons;
byang chub sems dpa' rnams ni rang byung gi chos kyi grong khyer du phyin par byed pas rtul phod pa lta bu'o/ /
the bodhisattvas are like heroes because they reach the self-arisen city of the Dharma;
enlightening beings are heroic, having reached the city of the state of independence;
byang chub sems dpa' rnams ni sems can thams cad kyi bdag la bya mas ba'i rlan yongs su skem pas me lta bu'o; ;
the bodhisattvas are like Agni because they dry up the wetness of the self-love[410] of all beings;
enlightening beings are fire, annihilating the self-love of all sentient beings;
byang chub sems dpa' rnams ni chos sprin rgya chen po'i char mngon par 'bebs pas sprin lta bu'o/ /
the bodhisattvas are like clouds because they send down rain from the vast cloud of the Dharma;
enlightening beings are clouds, causing vast clouds of true teaching to shower;
byang chub sems dpa' rnams ni sems can gyi dbang po dad pa la sogs pa'i myu gu rnam par 'phel bar byed pas char pa lta bu'o/ /
the bodhisattvas are like rain because they increase the sprouts of the faculties, faith, and so on of beings;
enlightening beings are rain, causing the sprouts of faculties such as faith to grow;
byang chub sems dpa' rnams ni chos rgya mtsho'i 'gram yongs su ston pas mnyan pa lta bu'o/ /
the bodhisattvas are like mariners because they reveal the point of embarkation for crossing the ocean of the Dharma;
enlightening beings are navigators, showing the way on the ocean of truth;
byang chub sems dpa' rnams ni sems can thams cad 'khor ba'i rgya mtsho las yang dag par sgrol ba'i phyir zab pa lta bu'o/ /
the bodhisattvas are like a bridge because they enable all beings to cross over the ocean of saṃsāra;
enlightening beings are bridges conveying all sentient beings across the sea of mundane life;
byang chub sems dpa' ni sems can thams cad kyis mngon par bgrod par bya ba'i phyir mu stegs lta bu'o/ /
and the bodhisattvas are like fords because they enable beings to cross over.”
enlightening beings are a pathway to the holy for all sentient beings.”

de ltar dra byi la sprin gyis tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gi mdun du 'dug ste/ tshig gi rgyud de dag gis byang chub sems dpa' rnams la yongs su bsngags pa byas nas/ tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la legs so/ / zhes bsngags so/ /
In that way, Megha the Dravidian, while sitting before Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, praised the bodhisattvas with those words and congratulated Sudhana, the head merchant’s son.
Thus praising enlightening beings to Sudhana in such terms, Megha applauded Sudhana.

de ltar des byang chub sems dpa' yang dag par dga' bar bya ba'i phyir tshig brjod pa'i tshe; kho'i sgo nas 'od 'phro ba'i phung po rnam pa 'di lta bu byung ste/ 'od 'phro ba'i phung po des stong gsum gyi stong chen po'i 'jig rten gyi khams rgyas par gang bar gyur nas/ lha dang / lha rdzu 'phrul chen po'am/ klu dang / klu rdzu 'phrul chen po'am/ gnod sbyin dang / gnod sbyin rdzu 'phrul chen po'am/ dri za dang / dri za rdzu 'phrul chen po'am/ lha ma yin dang / lha ma yin rdzu 'phrul chen po'am/ nam mkha' lding dang / nam mkha' lding rdzu 'phrul chen po'am, mi'am ci dang / mi 'am ci rdzu 'phrul chen po'am/ lto 'phye chen po dang / lto 'phye chen po rdzu 'phrul chen po'am/ mi dang / mi rdzu 'phrul chen po'am/ mi ma yin pa dang / mi ma yin pa rdzu 'phrul chen po'am/ tshangs pa pa dang / tshangs pa rdzu 'phrul chen po'am/ sems can gang sus mthong yang rung ste/ snang ba des yongs su snang bar byas pa de dag /dra byi la sprin gyi drung du 'ongs so/ /

As he was proclaiming those words that brought delight to bodhisattvas, a mass of light rays was emitted from his mouth in this fashion: that mass of light rays spread throughout the billion worlds. Those beings who saw it and were illuminated by that great radiance‍—devas and devas with great miraculous power, nāgas and nāgas with great miraculous power, yakṣas and yakṣas with great miraculous power, gandharvas and gandharvas with great miraculous power, asuras and asuras with great miraculous power, garuḍas and garuḍas with great miraculous power, kinnaras and kinnaras with great miraculous power, mahoragas and mahoragas with great miraculous power, humans and humans with great miraculous power, nonhumans and nonhumans with great miraculous power, Brahmakāyikas and Brahmakāyikas with great miraculous power‍—came into the presence of Megha the Dravidian.

While he was saying these words pleasing to enlightening beings, there issued from his mouth a mass of flames that made a thousand worlds clearly visible; and all the sentient beings who perceived that light came to Megha, illumined by the light;

de nas de ltar dra byi la sprin gyis bsam pa byin gyis brlabs shing thal mo sbyar te gnas pa/ lus dang sems sim par gyur pa/ dga' ba rgya chen po skyes pa/ sri zhu chen po la gnas pa/ nga rgyal gyi rgyal mtshan bcom pa/ g.yo sgyu dang bral ba/ dbang po rnam par dang bar gyur pa de dag la/ dra byi la sprin gyis chos kyi rnam grangs yi ge'i 'khor lo'i rgyud kyi rgyan ces bya ba de nyid rgya cher yang dag par bstan te/ khong du chud pa dang / rtogs pa dang / shes pa dang / rig par byas so/ / de thos nas kyang de dag thams cad bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub las phyir mi ldog par gyur to/ /

Their thoughts were thus blessed by Megha the Dravidian, and they placed their palms together in homage. Their bodies and minds were refreshed, they felt vast joy, they showed great veneration, they had cast down the banner of pride,[411] they were free of deceit, and their senses were serene. Megha the Dravidian taught them extensively the Dharma teaching called The Display of the Rotating Wheel of Syllables. He made it known to them, introduced them to it, led them into it, and caused them to understand it.[412] Having heard it, they all gained irreversible progress toward the highest, complete enlightenment.

to them, their attention commanded by Megha, their hands held forth in respectful supplication, their bodies and minds cooled, enraptured, inspired with reverence, divested of conceit, freed from deception, senses tranquil, Megha expounded and conveyed the teaching of the manifestation of the turning of the wheel of letters, upon hearing which they became irreversible in their progress toward supreme perfect enlightenment.
de nas de'i phyir chos kyi stan la 'dug nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la 'di skad ces smras so/ /
Then Megha the Dravidian sat again upon the Dharma throne and said to Sudhana, the head merchant’s son,
Megha sat back down on the seat of teaching and said to Sudhana,
rigs kyi bu/ kho bo ni dbyangs dang ldan pa'i gzungs thob pa ste/ de'i mthus kho bo stong gsum gyi stong chen po'i 'jig rten gyi khams 'di'i lha rnams kyi lha'i skad kyang shes so/ /
“Noble one, I have attained Sarasvatī’s power of retention. Through its power I know the divine languages of the devas in these world realms of the billion-world universe.
“I have attained the light of the spell of eloquence: I know the speech of all kinds of beings in a billion-world universe;

de bzhin du klu dang / gnod sbyin dang; dri za dang / lha ma yin dang / nam mkha' lding dang / mi 'am ci dang / lto 'phye chen po dang / mi dang / mi ma yin pa dang / tshangs pa rnams kyi tshangs pa'i skad kyang shes so/ /
In the same way, I know the languages of the nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, and nonhumans and the Brahmakāyika language of the Brahmakāyika devas.

lha rnams kyi lha'i skad sna tshogs kyang shes so/ / de bzhin du klu dang / gnod sbyin dang / dri za dang / lha ma yin dang / nam mkha' lding dang / mi 'am ci dang / lto 'phye chen po dang / mi dang / mi ma yin pa dang / tshangs pa rnams kyi tshangs pa'i skad sna tshogs kyang shes so/ /

“I know the various divine languages of the devas, and similarly I know the various languages of the nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, and nonhumans and the various Brahmakāyika languages of the Brahmakāyika devas.
I know the variety of speech of each kind of being;

lha rnams kyi lha'i skad gcig pa yang shes so/ / de bzhin du klu dang / gnod sbyin dang / dri za dang / lha ma yin dang / nam mkha' lding dang / mi'am ci dang / lto 'phye chen po dang / mi dang / mi ma yin pa dang / tshangs pa rnams kyi tshangs pa'i skad gcig pa yang shes so/ /
I know the unity of speech of each kind of being;

lha rnams kyi lha'i skad tha dad pa yang shes so/ / de bzhin du klu dang / gnod sbyin dang / dri za dang / lha ma yin dang / nam mkha' lding dang / mi 'am ci dang / lto 'phye chen po dang / mi dang / mi ma yin pa dang / tshangs pa rnams kyi tshangs pa'i skad tha dad pa yang shes so/ /

“I know the different divine languages of the devas, and similarly I know the different languages of the nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, and nonhumans and the different Brahmakāyika languages of the Brahmakāyika devas.
I know the mixture of speech of each kind of being;

byol song gi skye gnas su skyes pa'i sems can rnams kyi brda dang; skad dang / ming tha dad pa yang shes so/ / sems can dmyal ba pa'i sems can rnams kyi skad dang ming rnams kyang shes so/ / gshin rje'i 'jig rten pa'i sems can rnams kyi skad dang ming rnams kyang shes so/ /

“I also know the different signs, languages, and names of the beings who have been reborn as animals. I also know the different languages and names of the beings who have been reborn in the hells. I also know the different languages and names of the beings in the realm of Yama.[413]
I know the terms, speech, and concepts of all creatures;

'phags pa'i skad dang ming rnams kyang shes so/ / 'phags pa ma yin pa'i skad dang ming rnams kyang shes so/ / byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi tshig dang / brda dang / nges pa'i ngag sems can gyi bsam pa bzhin du 'byung ba yang shes so/ /

I also know the languages and names of the āryas. I also know the languages and names of those who are not āryas. I also know the words, signs, and definitions of bodhisattvas that arise in accordance with the wishes of beings.
I know the ideas of all sages; I know the ideas of all ignoble people; I know the speech of enlightening beings, expressed according to the mentalities and languages of sentient beings;

sems kyi skad cig re re la yang dus gsum du gshegs pa'i de bzhin gshegs pa rnams kyi dbyangs kyi yan lag dang / gsung rgya mtsho sems can thams cad kyi ming dang / gtam gyi sgra dang / tshig tu ldan pa yang rtogs shing khong du chud do/ /

“In each instant of mind, I perceive and comprehend the aspects of the voices and the oceans of speech of all the tathāgatas in the three times, and the words, the sound of conversations, and the languages that are used by all beings.
I enter into and focus on the oceans of utterances addressed to all sentient beings by the buddhas of past, present, and future.

ji ltar stong gsum gyi stong chen po'i 'jig rten gyi khams 'di'i sems can rnams kyi brda dang / nges pa'i tshig dang / skad dang / ming rgya mtsho la 'jug cing shes pa de bzhin du shar phyogs kyi 'jig rten gyi khams bye ba khrag khrig brgya stong tshad med pa/ grangs med pa/ bsam gyis mi khyab pa/ mtshungs pa med pa/ kun tu mtha' yas pa/ mu med pa/ sa mtshams med pa/ gzhal du med pa/ brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa dang / de bzhin du lho phyogs dang / nub phyogs dang / byang phyogs dang / byang shar gyi phyogs mtshams dang / shar lho'i phyogs mtshams dang / lho nub kyi phyogs mtshams dang / nub byang gi phyogs mtshams dang / 'og dang / steng gi phyogs kyi 'jig rten gyi khams bye ba khrag khrig brgya stong tshad med pa nas/ brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa'i bar gyi sems can rnams kyi brda dang / nges pa'i tshig dang / skad dang / ming rgya mtsho thams cad la yang 'jug cing shes te/

“Just as I perceive and know the ocean of terms, definitions, languages, and names of beings in this world realm of a billion worlds, in the same way, I perceive and know the ocean of terms, definitions, languages, and names of beings in a quintillion world realms, a measureless number of world realms, innumerable world realms, an inconceivable number of world realms, an unequaled number of world realms, an infinite number of world realms, limitless world realms, and an inexpressible number of world realms in the eastern direction, and it is the same for the south, the west, the north, the northeast, the southeast, the southwest, the northwest, below, and above.

As in this billion-world universe in each moment of thought I enter into the oceans of all terms, expressions, speech, and concepts of sentient beings, I do the same in untold worlds in each of the ten directions.
'di ltar lha rnams kyi lha'i skad kyang shes so/ / tshangs pa rnams kyi tshangs pa'i skad kyi bar du'ang shes so/ /
“In that way, I know the deva language of the devas, and so on, up to knowing the Brahmakāyika language of the Brahmakāyika devas.

rigs kyi bu/ kho bos ni byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi gzungs snang ba dbyangs dang ldan pa 'di shes par zad na/ kho bos byang chub sems dpa' 'gro ba sna tshogs kyi brda'i rnam pa rgya mtsho la zhugs pa de dag dang / 'gro ba sna tshogs kyi skad dang ming rgya mtsho la zhugs pa de dag dang / 'gro ba sna tshogs kyi ming shin tu bstan pa rgya mtsho la zhugs pa de dag dang / 'gro ba sna tshogs kyi brjod pa rab tu bkod pa dang / rnam par spyod pa rgya mtsho la zhugs pa de dag dang / tshig thams cad kyi mtshams sbyar ba rgya mtsho la zhugs pa de dag dang / tshig lhur blangs te bstan pa rgya mtsho la zhugs pa de dag dang / dus gsum gyi dmigs pa thams cad dmigs pa gcig tu rnam par spyod pa rgya mtsho gangs chen mtsho la zhugs pa de dag dang / tshig gis brtsegs te bstan pa rgya mtsho la zhugs pa de dag dang / tshig gnyis nas brtsegs te bstan pa rgya mtsho la zhugs pa de dag dang / tshig rab tu phye ste bstan pa rgya mtsho la zhugs pa de dag dang / chos thams cad rab tu dbye bas 'dul ba'i tshul bstan pa rgya mtsho la zhugs pa de dag dang / 'gro ba thams cad kyi skad rgya mtsho la zhugs pa de dag dang / dbyangs kyi dkyil 'khor rnam par dag pa'i rgyan thams cad la zhugs pa de dag dang / yi ge'i 'khor lo'i mthar phyin par bya bas rab tu dbye ba las byung ba de dag gi spyod pa shes pa'am, yon tan brjod par nus re skan/

“Noble one, I know the light of Sarasvatī’s power of retention that the bodhisattvas have, but how could I know the conduct or describe the qualities of the entry by the bodhisattvas into an ocean of different terms, their entry into an ocean of terms and languages of various beings, their entry into an ocean of taught names of various beings, their entry into an ocean of an array of descriptions by various beings, their entry into an ocean of conducts, their entry into an ocean of the conjunctions of all words, their entry into an ocean of the literal meaning of words, their entry into an ocean of single terms for perceptions that include all perceptions in the three times, their entry into an ocean of teaching through assembling a single word,[414] their entry into an ocean of teaching through assembling two words,[415] their entry into an ocean of teaching through dividing words, their entry into an ocean of teaching that brings guidance through categorizing the words[416] for all phenomena, their entry into an ocean of the languages of all beings, their entry in the entire pure display of the field of speech, and what arises in the categories of the apex of the wheel of words?

“I know this light of the spell of eloquence of enlightening beings, but how can I know the practice or tell the virtues of the enlightening beings who have entered the ocean of what is in various conceptions, who have entered the ocean of the various conceptions and languages of all people, who have entered the ocean of the various conventions of verbal designation used by all people, who have entered the ocean of logical connections of all statements, who have entered the ocean of literalism, who have entered the ocean of designation of all objects of past, present, and future in one object, who have entered the ocean of teaching which is beyond verbal expression, who have entered the ocean of the teaching of the Buddha, who have entered the ocean of explanations of distinct types of statements, who have entered the ocean of explanation guiding the analysis of statements of all truths, who have entered the ocean of speech of all beings, who have gone into the pure arrays of all spheres of sound, who are conversant with the ultimate distinctions of the wheel of phonemes?

song / rigs kyi bu lho phyogs kyi rgyud 'di nyid na yul nags tshal na gnas pa zhes bya ba yod de/ de na tshong dpon btang brjod ces bya ba 'dug gi /de'i gan du song la/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la brtson par bya ba dang / ji ltar 'byung bar bya ba dang / ji ltar sems nges par gzhag par bya ba dris shig /

“Now depart, noble one. In this southern region, in the land of Vanavāsī, there dwells a head merchant by the name of Muktaka. Go to him and ask him, ‘How should bodhisattvas train in bodhisattva conduct? How should they set forth? How should their minds rest in meditation?’ ”

“Go, son—there is a country south of here called Vanavasin, where there lives a distinguished man named Muktaka. Go ask him how an enlightening being is to undertake the practice of enlightening beings and become familiar with it, and how the mind is to be observed.”

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis/ dra byi la sprin gyi rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te/ chos kyi rim gro byas nas/ dad pa'i mtshan nyid rtsa ba tshugs pa la rab tu brtag pa dang / dge ba'i bshes gnyen las 'ongs pa'i thams cad mkhyen pa nyid la yang dag par lta zhing gdong mchi mas gang bar ngus te/ dra byi la sprin la lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas/ yang dang yang du bltas te phyag 'tshal zhing dra byi la sprin gyi drung nas song ngo// //

Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, bowed his head to the feet of Megha the Dravidian, and showing respect for his Dharma, showing that Megha was the source for the signs of the arising of his faith, and seeing the omniscience that has come from the kalyāṇamitra, weeping, with his face covered in tears, he circumambulated Megha the Dravidian a hundred thousand times, keeping him to his right, and, looking back a hundred thousand times, departed from Megha the Dravidian.

Then Sudhana, having bowed to Megha and paid respect to the teaching, describing the faith rooted in him, observing that all-knowledge comes from following good spiritual benefactors, reluctantly took his leave and went on.
bam po dgu bcu rtsa gcig pa/
[tshong dpon btang brjod]
Chapter 8. Muktaka
Muktaka
de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang byang chub sems dpa'i gzungs snang ba dbyangs dang ldan pa'i rgyan de nyid la rjes su bsam pa dang /
Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, then contemplated that power of retention of the bodhisattvas called the light that is the display of Sarasvatī,
Then Sudhana, reflecting on that array of light of the spell of eloquence of enlightening beings,
byang chub sems dpa'i skad kyi tshul rgya mtsho de nyid la 'jug par bya ba dang /
remembered that particular entry by the bodhisattvas into an ocean of languages,
plunging into that enlightening beings’ ocean of principles of speech,
byang chub sems dpa'i tshul phra mo la 'jug pa de nyid rjes su dran par bya ba dang /
remembered that particular entry by the bodhisattvas into the way of subtlety,[417]
byang chub sems dpa'i sems rnam par byang bas rnam par dag pa de nyid kyi rjes su 'brang bar bya ba dang /
remembered that particular purity of the bodhisattvas through purification of the mind,
remembering that enlightening beings’ mental purification,
byang chub sems dpa' dge ba'i rtsa ba'i bag chags bsdu zhing bsgrub pa mngon par bsgrub pa dang /
accomplished that particular accomplishment by the bodhisattvas of creating the predispositions for roots of merit,
undertaking that enlightening beings’ production of inclination to goodness,
byang chub sems dpa'i yongs su smin par bya ba'i sgo de nyid rnam par sbyang ba dang /
purified that particular bodhisattva gateway for ripening,
clarifying that enlightening beings’ method of perfecting sentient beings,
byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi sems can bsdu ba'i ye shes de nyid shin tu byang bar bya ba dang /
refined that particular bodhisattva wisdom that attracts beings,
purifying that enlightening beings’ knowledge of how to take care of sentient beings,
byang chub sems dpa'i bsam pa'i stobs rnam par dag par bya ba de nyid brtan par bya ba dang /
made firmer that particular pure strength of bodhisattva motivation,
making firm that enlightening beings’ purity of willpower,
byang chub sems dpa'i lhag pa'i bsam pa'i stobs de nyid nye bar brtan par bya ba dang /
stabilized that particular strength of the superior motivation of the bodhisattvas,
establishing that enlightening beings’ power of supreme resolve,
byang chub sems dpa'i mos pa'i rgyud de yang yongs su sbyang ba dang /
purified that lineage of bodhisattva aspiration,
clarifying that body of interest of enlightening beings,
byang chub sems dpa'i sems de nyid gdon mi za bar dge bar bsam pa dang /
developed[418] that particular goodness that is in the minds of the bodhisattvas,
producing that goodness of intent and
byang chub sems dpa'i yi dam chen po de nyid mthar phyin par byed cing /
and entered into that particular commitment of the bodhisattvas.
thought of enlightening beings,
tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang yi dam la brtan zhing smon lam gyi sems kyis yongs su skyo ba med pa'i rgyud kyi rgyan dang ldan pa phyir mi ldog pas rnam par gnon pa'i brtson 'grus can/
Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, displayed a continuity of strong commitment, a mind of aspiration, and indefatigability. He had the heroism[419] of irreversible courage.
evoking that effort of enlightening beings, equipped with a mind of firm commitment and tireless consistency,
yid kyis brtul ba las mi zlog pa/
He had the commitment of an irreversible mind.
with unrelenting energy and determination,
dad pa mi 'phrogs pa'i stobs dang ldan pa/
He possessed the strength of unassailable faith.
imbued with unshakable power of faith,
rdo rje'i mthu bo ches mi phyed pa'i sems dang ldan pa/
His motivation had the indestructibility of the mighty vajra.
with an indestructible mind,
dge ba'i bshes gnyen thams cad kyi gdams ngag mthun par len pa/
He had acquired with reverence the instructions of all kalyāṇamitras.
follower of the instructions of all spiritual benefactors,
shes rab kha ma bab pa'i yul dang ldan pa/
He had an unimpaired scope of wisdom.
with the perspective of sane knowledge,
sgo kun nas rnam par dag pa la mngon du gyur pa/
He faced the completely pure gateways.
on the verge of all-sided purity,
ye shes rnam par dag pa'i spyod yul thogs pa med pa/
He possessed the unimpeded field of pure wisdom.
coursing in the purity of unobstructed knowledge,
kun tu lta ba'i ye shes kyi tshul snang ba dang ldan pa/
He had the illumination of all-seeing wisdom.
imbued with the light of the principle of the universal eye,
sa'i gzungs kun nas snang ba rab tu thob pa/
He had attained the radiance of the retentive power of all levels.
illumined by the mystic formulations of all stages of enlightenment,
chos kyi dbyings kyi gzhi'i bye brag la mngon sum du gyur pa'i sems dang ldan pa/
His mind faced the separate bases of the realm of phenomena.
his mind directed to the differentiations of the planes of the cosmos,
gzhi kun la rten pa'i rgyan rnam par dag pa'i rang bzhin rnam par dmigs pa gnas pa med pa dang /
He perceived the nature of the pure display that is completely without any basis.
aware of the pure essence of forms unfixed anywhere,
bdag gi med pa dang / gnyis su med pa'i spyod yul la rab tu brtson pa/
He was devoted to the unattached, unequaled,[420] nondual field of activity.
intent on the sphere of absolute unity with no attachment,
'du shes thams cad las 'da' bar byed pa'i ye shes kyi sgo rnam par dag pa/
He had the pure gateway of wisdom that surpasses all concepts.
having purified the medium of powerful knowledge of all ideas,
chos kyi phyogs dang gzhi tha dad pa'i phyogs la so sor rtog pa med pa/
He had the discrimination[421] of all[422] the separate directions and families.[423]
having broken through the boundaries of all spaces,
'jig rten gyi gzhi dang phyogs kyi bye brag las phyir mi ldog pa/
He had not annulled the separate bases and directions of the world.
progressively distinguishing the realms of worldly planes,
chos kyi gzhi dang phyogs kyi bye brag las phyir mi ldog pa/
He had not annulled the separate bases and directions of the Dharma.
progressively distinguishing the realms of planes of reality,
sangs rgyas kyi phyogs dang gzhi tha dad pa mthong ba dang / rnam par rig par bya ba la gzhol ba/
He was dedicated to the perception of the vision of the different directions and families[424] of the buddhas.
intent on the manifestation of the vision of the varieties of abodes of Buddha,
dus kyi phyogs dang gzhi'i bye brag khong du chud pa'i ye shes can/
He had the wisdom that comprehended the different directions and bases of time.
knowing about the distinctions of realms of time,
chos kyi 'khor lo yid du 'ong bas yang dag par bsgrubs pa'i blo dang ldan pa/
He had the understanding endowed with the radiance of the wheel of the Dharma.
his intellect bearing the radiant wheel of the teaching,
ye shes kun nas snang ba'i ting nge 'dzin gyi rnam pa snang bas sems gsal bar byas pa/
The light of the complete radiance of wisdom and samādhi illuminated his mind.
his mind illumined by the light of the treasury of concentration of universally radiant knowledge,
yid kyi lus yul kun dang ldan pa'i sa la zhugs pa/
He had the mind and body[425] that had reached the complete levels and ranges.
mentally and physically according with the stage of universal perspective,
de bzhin gshegs pa'i ye shes snang bas rgyud shin tu snang bar byas pa/
He was continuously illuminated by the radiance[426] of the wisdom of the tathāgatas.
his mind illumined by the lightning of knowledge of those who realize Thusness,
thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du dad pa'i dba' rlabs kyi shugs kyis rab tu slob pa/
He had given rise to the power of faith in omniscience.
realizing the exaltation of faith in omniscience,
sangs rgyas kyi chos la mos pa'i shugs dang 'bral ba med pa/
He was never lacking in the power of faith in the Buddhadharma.
never without the exaltation of faith in the buddha-teaching,
de bzhin gshegs pa'i byin gyi rlabs kyis byin du brlabs pa/
He possessed the blessing of the tathāgatas.
filled with the exaltation of the empowerment of Buddha,
sangs rgyas thams cad rang gi sems kyi rgyud du khong du chud pa'i 'od kyis snang bar gyur pa/
He had been illuminated by the light of the approach of his own mind to the buddhas.
illumined by the inherent mental light of all buddhas,
'jig rten gyi khams kyi dra ba thams cad rang gi lus kyis rgyas par dgang ba'i smon lam dang /
He was endowed with the aspiration for his own body pervading the network of all world realms.
hearing the vow to penetrate all networks of worlds with his own body,
chos kyi dbyings thams cad rang gi lus su yang dag par bsdu ba dang mngon par bsgrubs pa la brtson pa de/
He was dedicated to accomplishing the inclusion of the entire realm of phenomena within his own body.
intent on putting all universes at once into his own body,
mthar gyis song song ste/ lo bcu gnyis kyis yul nags tshal na gnas par phyin nas/ des tshong dpon btang brjod de btsal btsal te mthong ngo/ /
After twelve years he eventually arrived at Vanavāsī. He searched for the head merchant Muktaka and saw him.
made his way gradually to the country Vanavasin, arriving there after twelve years. He looked for the noble Muktaka,
mthong nas kyang lus thams cad kyis phab ste/ phyag 'tshal nas mdun du 'dug ste/
When he saw him, he bowed down his entire body onto the ground in homage and sat before him.
saw him, paid his respects,

thal mo sbyar nas 'di skad ces smras so/ / 'phags pa/ bdag de ring dge ba'i bshes gnyen dang mjal bar gyur pa ni/ bdag gis 'thob par bgyi ba legs par thob bo/ / de ci'i slad du zhe na/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen rnams ni mthong bar dka' ba'o/ / 'byung bar dka' ba'o/ / mjal bar dka' ba'o/ / bgrod par dka' ba'o/ / bsnyen bkur bgyi bar dka' ba'o/ / mnyes par bgyi ba dka' ba'o/ / 'grogs par dka' ba'o/ / rim gror bgyi ba dka' ba'o/ / dge ba'i bshes gnyen rnams ni rjes su 'brang bar dka' ba lags na/

With palms together he said, “Ārya, today I have succeeded; I have succeeded well. Why is that? Because I have met the kalyāṇamitra.[427] It is rare to have the opportunity to see the kalyāṇamitras. It is rare to have the opportunity find their appearance. It is rare to have the opportunity arrive where they are. It is rare to have the opportunity to go to where they are, it is rare to have the opportunity to serve them, it is rare to have the opportunity to approach[428] them, it is rare to have the opportunity to dwell with them, it is rare to have the opportunity to train with them, and it is rare to have the opportunity to follow the kalyāṇamitras.

and said, “Noble one, I have made gains, having met the spiritual benefactor Megha. Why do I say this? Spiritual benefactors are hard to get to see, hard to get to encounter, hard to visit, hard to attend, hard to approach, hard to stay with, hard to be perfected by, hard to associate with.
de lta bu'i dge ba'i bshes gnyen dang 'grogs pa de ring bdag gis thob par gyur to/ /
“Today I have succeeded in being with the kalyāṇamitra.[429]
But I have met the spiritual benefactor Megha.
'phags pa/ bdag gis 'di lta ste/ sangs rgyas thams cad la bsnyen bkur ba dang /
Ārya, I have developed the aspiration for the highest, complete enlightenment in order to serve all the buddhas;
Noble one, I have set my mind on supreme perfect enlightenment, to attend all buddhas,

sangs rgyas thams cad la rim gror bgyi ba dang / sangs rgyas thams cad kyi zhal blta ba dang / sangs rgyas thams cad rnam par dmigs par bgyi ba dang / sangs rgyas thams cad dang mnyam pa nyid thob par bgyi ba dang /
to venerate all the buddhas; to see all the buddhas; to perceive all the buddhas; to comprehend the equality of all the buddhas;
to be on good terms with all buddhas, to see all buddhas, to know all buddhas, to approach equality with all buddhas,

sangs rgyas thams cad kyi smon lam khong du chud par bgyi ba dang / sangs rgyas thams cad kyi smon lam yongs su rdzogs par bgyi ba dang / sangs rgyas thams cad kyis yang dag par bsgrub pa'i ye shes snang bar bgyi ba dang / sangs rgyas thams cad rang gi lus su mngon par bsgrub pa dang /
to follow the vows of all buddhas, to fulfill the vows of all buddhas, to view the knowledge attained by all buddhas, to produce all buddhas in my own body,

sangs rgyas thams cad kyis yang dag par bsgrubs pa rang gi spyod par mngon par bsgrub par bgyi ba dang / sangs rgyas thams cad kyi rnam par 'phrul ba mngon sum du rtogs par bgyi ba dang / sangs rgyas thams cad kyi stobs dang mi bsnyengs pa yongs su dag par bgyi ba dang / sangs rgyas thams cad kyi chos bstan pa mnyan pas mi ngoms par bgyi ba dang /

to accomplish the realization of all buddhas in my own practice, to directly know the mystical transformations of all buddhas, to purify the powers and confidences of all buddhas, to hear all true teachings tirelessly,
sangs rgyas thams cad kyi chos brtan pa mnyan cing blang bar bgyi ba dang / sangs rgyas thams cad kyi chos bstan pa yang dag par gzung bar bgyi ba dang /
to hear and adopt the Dharma that is taught by all the buddhas; to truly hold the Dharma that is taught by all the buddhas;
to listen to and take up the teachings of all buddhas, to hold the teachings of all buddhas,
sangs rgyas thams cad kyi chos bstan pa rnam par dbye bar bgyi ba dang / sangs rgyas thams cad kyi chos bstan pa yongs su gzung ba dang /
to distinguish the teachings of all buddhas, to preserve the instructions of all buddhas,

byang chub sems dpa' thams cad dang tshul gcig tu 'gyur bar bgyi ba dang / byang chub sems dpa' thams cad dang skal pa mnyam par bgyi ba dang / byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi spyod pa yongs su dag par bgyi ba dang / byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi pha rol tu phyin pa yongs su rdzogs par bgyi ba dang /
to be one being with all buddhas, to be equal to all enlightening beings, to purify the practice of all enlightening beings, to fulfill the transcendent ways of enlightening beings,

byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi smon lam mngon par bsgrub pa rnam par dag par bgyi ba dang / byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi sangs rgyas kyi byin gyi rlabs kyi mdzod rab tu thob par bgyi ba dang / byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi chos kyi gter dang mdzod mi zad pa'i ye shes snang ba thob par bgyi ba dang / byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi ting 'dzin gyi gter dang mdzod khong du chud par bgyi ba dang /

to purify the accomplishment of the vows of all enlightening beings, to attain all enlightening beings’ store of mystical power of buddhas, to be illumined by the endless knowledge of the treasury of truths of all enlightening beings, to approach the treasury of enlightening beings,

byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi mdzod tshad med pa mngon par bsgrub pa dang / byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi snying rje chen po'i gter dang mdzod sems can 'dul ba'i mthar phyin par bgyi ba dang / byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi rnam par 'phrul ba'i gter dang mdzod rnam par dmigs par bgyi ba dang / byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi dbang gi gter dang mdzod rang gi sems kyi dbang du bgyi ba dang /

to produce the infinite treasury of enlightening beings, to realize the ultimate consummation of guidance of sentient beings with the treasury of great compassion of all enlightening beings, to know the treasury of spiritual transformations of all enlightening beings, to command in my own body the treasury of powers of all enlightening beings,
byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi rnam par dag pa'i gter dang mdzod rnam pa thams cad du brgyan par bgyi ba'i slad du/ bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed nas/
and for the array of all the aspects of all the bodhisattvas’ store of treasure of purity.
to be fully arrayed with the treasury of purities of all enlightening beings.

'phags pa/ de lta bu'i sems kyis bdag 'dir mchis so/ / bsam pa de lta bu dang / yid la smon pa de lta bu dang / mngon par dga' ba de lta bu dang / sems pa de lta bu dang / gdon mi 'tshal bar bsgrub par bsam pa de lta bu dang / spyod yul mngon du bgyi ba de lta bu dang / tshul khong du chud par bgyi ba la mos pa de lta bu dang / rnam par dag pa la gzhol ba de lta bu dang / rnam par dpyod pa'i bsam pa de lta bu dang / rab tu gzhol ba'i sems de lta bu dang / dge ba'i sbyor ba de lta bu dang / mngon du gyur pa'i dbang po de lta bus bdag 'dir mchis te/

“Ārya, I have come here with such a motivation, with such an intention, with such joy,[432] with such delight, with such thoughts, with such an aspiration to accomplish certainty, with such an aspiration to conduct, with such an aspiration to comprehend the way, with such a dedication to purity, with such an intention for analysis,[433] with such an oriented mind, with such a dedication to goodness, and with senses focused in that way.

“Noble one, I have come in such a spirit, with such desires, such wishes, such intentions, such thoughts uppermost in my mind, aiming for such a realm, determined to follow such principles, intent on such purity, seeking such adornments, with such a humble mind, applied to such good, my faculties oriented in this way.
'phags pa ni/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams la gdams ngag dang rjes su ston pa mdzad cing /
“Ārya, I have heard[434] that you give instruction and teachings to bodhisattvas,
Noble one, I hear you give instructions to enlightening beings,
tshul ni nye bar ston pa mdzad/ rtogs par bgyi ba ni snang bar mdzad/ lam ni bstan par mdzad/ mu stegs la ni 'jog par mdzad/
that you teach the way, elucidate the way to understand, teach the path, bring across the ford,
explain principle and clarify procedure, explain the Path, take them across the bridge,
chos kyi sgo ni rnam par 'byed pa mdzad/ the tshom ni yongs su gcod par mdzad/ nem nur ni sel bar mdzad/ yid gnyis kyi zug rngu ni 'byin par mdzad/
open the gateway of the Dharma, cut through doubts, dispel uncertainty, extract the splinter of prevarication,
open the door of the Teaching, cut off doubts, dispel craving, pull out the arrow of confusion,
dogs pa'i dri ma ni sbyong bar mdzad/ sems kyi thibs po ni snang bar mdzad; sems kyi dri ma ni yongs su sel bar mdzad/ sems kyi rgyud ni rab tu dang bar mdzad/
remove hesitancy, illuminate the darkness of the mind, eliminate the stains of the mind, clarify the continuity of the mind,
clear away the grime of uncertainty, light up the obscurity in the mind, remove defilement from the mind, calm the mental flow,
sems kyi g.yo sgyu ni yongs su sel bar mdzad/ sems kyi gdung ba ni yongs su sim par mdzad/
remove the deception of the mind, alleviate the distress of the mind,
remove deviousness from the mind, cool the fever of the mind,
'khor ba las ni sems rnam par bzlog par mdzad/ mi dge ba'i las ni phyir bzlog par mdzad/ sems can dmyal ba las ni ldog par mdzad/
turn the mind away from saṃsāra, lead away from bad actions, dissuade from going to the hells,
turn back the mind revolving in the mundane whirl, turn enlightening beings away from evil, separate them from hells,
gnas dang ni dbral bar mdzad/
bring freedom from existence,
mngon par zhen pa las ni gyen du bskyod pa mdzad/ chags pa thams cad las ni yongs su 'grel ba mdzad/
liberate from attachment, banish all clinging,
free them from attachments, foster nonattachment,

thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du ni bsgrub pa mdzad/ chos kyi grong khyer du 'jug par bgyi ba'i slad du ni mngon du gyur par mdzad/ snying rje chen po la ni rab tu bsgrub pa mdzad/ byams pa chen po la ni rab tu gzhog pa mdzad/
create the aspiration for omniscience, enable entry into the city of the Dharma, bring to great compassion, unite with great love,
direct them toward omniscience, lead them into the city of truth, establish them in great compassion, settle them in great kindness,

byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la ni rab tu sbyor ba mdzad/ ting nge 'dzin gyi sgo bsgom pa la ni 'dzud pa mdzad/ rtogs par 'gyur ba'i sgo la ni gnas par mdzad/ rang bzhin nges par rtogs pa la ni gzhog par mdzad/
conjoin with bodhisattva conduct, cause to enter the meditation of the gateway of samādhi, establish in the gateway of realization, establish in the comprehension of nature,

introduce them into the practice of enlightening beings, cause them to enter into the development of ways of concentration, establish them in means of realization, fill them with contemplation of inherent nature,
stobs dang ldan pas ni khyab par mdzad/ 'gro ba thams cad mnyam pa nyid du ni sems rnam par dbye ba mdzad do
spread the possession of the strengths, and realize the equality of all beings.
and explain mind according to power for the sake of attainment of equanimity toward all beings.

zhes thos na/ 'phags pa/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la brtson par bgyi/ ji ltar sbyar bar bgyi/ ji ltar brtson par bgyis na byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa'i dkyil 'khor rnam par dag par 'gyur ba bdag la bstan du gsol/

“Therefore, now that I have heard that, teach me, Ārya, how bodhisattvas should learn[435] bodhisattva conduct, how they train in it, how they are dedicated to it, and how they quickly[436] purify the domain of bodhisattva conduct.”

Noble one, please tell me how an enlightening being is to learn, commence, and carry out the practice of enlightening beings, and how one so engaged can quickly purify the sphere of practice of enlightening beings.”

de nas tshong dpon btang brjod kyis de'i tshe byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin gyi sgo sangs rgyas kyi zhing thams cad yang dag par 'du ba zhes bya ba gzungs kyi sgo klong mtha' yas pa sngon du 'gro ba la sngon gyi dge ba'i rtsa ba'i shugs dang / de bzhin gshegs pa'i byin gyi rlabs dang / 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pas yang dag par bsams shing / ye shes snang ba nye bar bsgrubs pas snyoms par zhugs so/ /

Then, at that time, the head merchant Muktaka the bodhisattva entered the gateway of samādhi, the foremost gateway to the infinite circling of the power of retention, called the assembly of all buddha realms, through the power of past roots of merit, through the blessing of the tathāgatas, and through the concentration that brings the light of wisdom of Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta.

At that juncture Muktaka entered an enlightening concentration medium called “collection of all buddha-fields,” led by a mystic formula of endless progression, accomplishing entry into this concentration by the power of his past roots of goodness, by the empowerment of the Buddha, and by Manjushri’s attention and gift of the light of knowledge.

tshong dpon btang brjod de ltar snyoms par zhugs ma thag tu gzugs kyi lus yongs su dag pa rnam pa 'di lta bur gnas par gyur te/ lus yongs su dag pa de'i mthus phyogs bcu'i sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das/ sangs rgyas kyi zhing bcu'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed sangs rgyas kyi zhing yongs su dag pa dang bcas/ 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor dang bcas/ 'od rnam par dag pa dang bcas/ sngon spyod pa la zhugs pa dang bcas/ sangs rgyas kyi rnam par 'phrul pa dang bcas/ smon lam gyi tshogs dang bcas/ spyod pa dang 'byung ba'i rgyan rnam par dag pa dang bcas/ mngon par rdzogs par 'tshang rgya ba yongs su ston pa dang bcas/ chos kyi 'khor lo shin tu ston pa dang bcas/ sems can yongs su smin par mdzad pa dang bcas/ chos kyi mu'i mthar thug pa dang bcas par kun kyang lus kyi khong du chud cing 'dus par snang ste/

Immediately, the form of the head merchant Muktaka, who had entered that samādhi, became a pure body. Because of the purity of his body, there appeared within his body the presence of buddha bhagavats as numerous as the atoms in the buddha realms in the ten directions, together with their pure buddha realms, the assemblies of their pupils, their pure halos, their past practice of conduct, their buddha miracles, their accumulation of prayers, their pure display of conduct and setting forth, their demonstration of the attainment of buddhahood, their teaching the wheel of the Dharma, their ripening of beings, and their final conclusion of the Dharma.

As soon as Muktaka had entered that state, his body became pure, and by that purity of body as many buddhas in the ten directions as atoms in ten buddha-lands were visible within his body, along with the adornments of their pure lands, their congregations, their pure lights, their past actions and abodes, their mystical projections, their vows, their pure arrays of liberative practices, their manifestations of attainment of perfect enlightenment, their turnings of the wheel of teaching, their developments of sentient beings, and the ultimate consummation of their teaching.

de dag kyang phan tshun ma 'dres pa dang / phan tshun mchod pa dang / phan tshun shin tu rnam par phye ba dang / phan tshun shin tu rnam par gnas pa dang / tshul sna tshogs su bzhugs pa dang / yang dag pa ji lta ba bzhin du rnam par dmigs pa dang / sangs rgyas kyi zhing rgyan sna tshogs can mnga' ba dang / byang chub sems dpa'i 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor sna tshogs kyi rgyan dang ldan pa dang / sangs rgyas kyi rnam par 'phrul pa sna tshogs su yongs su ston par snang ngo/ /

They were distinct from each other, were not obscuring each other,[437] were perfectly separate from each other, were differentiated from each other, remaining in different ways,[438] and were perceived exactly as they were. Their various arrays of buddha realms, the various adorning assemblies of bodhisattva pupils, and the appearances of various buddha miracles were seen.

All these were visible within Muktaka’s body without mutual confusion, without mutual obstruction, clearly distinct, showing the various individual ages accurately defined, the various arrays of the buddha-lands, the various adornments of the congregations of enlightening beings, and the various miracles of the buddhas.

theg pa sna tshogs rnam par dgod pa mdzad pa dang / smon lam gyi sgo sna tshogs yongs su brjod pa dang / 'jig rten gyi khams la la na ni dga' ldan gyi pho brang du skyes shing / sangs rgyas kyi 'phrin las thams cad mdzad par snang ngo/ / la la na ni dga' ldan gyi pho brang nas 'pho ba dang / la la na ni yum gyi sku na bzhugs shing rnam par 'phrul pa sna tshogs yongs su ston pa dang / la la na ni skye ba dang / la la na ni byis pa'i rtsed mo ston pa mdzad pa dang / la la na ni btsun mo'i 'khor gyi nang na bzhugs pa dang / la la na ni mngon par 'byung ba dang / la la na ni snying po byang chub tu gshegs te rnam par 'phrul ba'i rgyan chen pos bdud kyi sde pham par mdzad pa dang / la la na ni lha dang / klu dang / gnod sbyin dang / dri zas yongs su bskor cing tshangs pa'i dbang pos chos kyi 'khor lo bskor bar gsol ba gdab pa dang / la la na ni chos kyi 'khor lo bskor ba mdzad pa dang / la la na ni sems can thams cad kyi gnas na bzhugs pa dang / la la na ni yongs su mya ngan las 'da' bar snang ngo/ / 'jig rten gyi khams la la na ni de bzhin gshegs pa mya ngan las 'das pa rnams kyi ring bsrel rnam par 'god par snang ngo/ / sangs rgyas kyi zhing la la na ni lha dang mi rnams de bzhin gshegs pa'i mchod rten la rgyan gyis klubs pa byed par snang ste/

They were establishing the various yānas and reciting the various gateways of prayers. They were seen in some worlds being born in a palace in Tuṣita. They were seen to accomplish all the deeds of a buddha: in some worlds they were descending from the palace in Tuṣita; in some they were entering their mothers’ wombs and manifesting various miracles; in some they were being born; in some they demonstrated playing as children; in some they were in the middle of their harems; in some they were setting forth in renunciation; in some they were arriving at the bodhimaṇḍa; in some they were defeating the armies of Māra with vast miraculous manifestations; in some they were encircled by devas, nāgas, yakṣas, and gandharvas, and Brahmā and Indra[439] were supplicating them to turn the wheel of the Dharma; in some they were turning the wheel of the Dharma; in some they were present in the abodes of all beings; and in some they were passing into nirvāṇa. In some world realms there could be seen the distribution of the relics of the tathāgatas that had passed into nirvāṇa, and in some buddha realms devas and humans could be seen covering the caityas of the tathāgatas with adornments.

Some buddhas were seen to be in the heaven of happiness in a world setting forth various means of liberation and illumining various undertakings; some were seen descending from the heaven of happiness doing the duty of buddhas; some were seen in the womb of the mother displaying various miracles; some were seen being born and showing a child’s play; some were seen at home, some leaving home, some gone to the summit of enlightenment defeating the army of demons; some were seen surrounded by deities, spirits, and cherubim, being asked by Brahma and Indra to turn the wheel of the teaching; some were seen turning the wheel of teaching; some were seen in the abodes of all beings; some were seen passing away; in some cases the division of the relics of deceased buddhas in a world was seen, and in some cases people and celestial beings in a buddha-land were seen adorning a buddha’s shrine.

sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das de dag gis sems can gyi ris rnam pa tha dad pa dang / sems can gyi 'jig rten gyi rnam pa tha dad pa dang / sems can gyi lam rnam pa tha dad pa dang / sems can gyi skye gnas rnam pa tha dad pa dang / sems can gyi tshogs rnam pa tha dad pa dang / sems can gyi dge ba'i rtsa ba'i rgyud rnam pa tha dad pa dang / sems can gyi lam gyi rgyud rnam pa tha dad pa dang / sems can gyi bsam pa'i rgyud rnam pa tha dad pa dang / sems can gyi mos pa'i rgyud rnam pa tha dad pa dang / sems can gyi dbang po'i rgyud rnam pa tha dad pa dang / dus kyi rgyud rnam pa tha dad pa dang / sems can gyi las kyi bye brag rnam pa tha dad pa dang / sems can gyi las mi mthun pa rnam pa tha dad pa dang / sems can gyi 'jig rten rnam par dbye ba rnam pa tha dad pa dang / sems can gyi tshul lam dang / spyod pa rnam pa tha dad pa la rnam par spyod pa dang / sems can rgya mtsho bsam pa dang / sbyor ba'i rnam pa tha dad pa dang / dbang po mi mthun pa sna tshogs rnam par dag pa dang / nyon mongs pa dang / bag chags sna tshogs bag la nyal bar gyur pa'i sems can 'byams klas pa rnams la/

Those buddha bhagavats were teaching among the various classes of beings, the various worlds of beings, the various modes of beings, the various births of beings, the various aggregations of beings, the various successive roots of merit of beings, the various successive modes of beings, the various successive thoughts of beings, the various successive aspirations of beings, the various successive sensory faculties of beings, the various successive times of beings, the various particular karmas of beings, the various dissimilar karmas of beings, the various worlds of beings, the various modes and conducts of beings, the various aspirations and conducts in the ocean of beings, the various, different pure faculties, and the various kleśas, predispositions, and propensities in the vast extent of beings.

And what those buddhas said, in various groups of beings, in various beings’ worlds, in various realms of existence, in various assemblies of beings, in various situations according to beings’ virtues, states, inclinations, beliefs, and faculties, in various periods of time, amid various kinds of beings’ activities, in various manifestations of worlds of beings carrying out various intentions, in the midst of beings with various degrees of purity of senses and various afflictions, habits, and propensities,

sangs rgyas kyi rnam par 'phrul pa rnam pa sna tshogs yongs su bstan pa dang / yul sna tshogs kyi nges pa'i tshig dang / dbyangs kyi yan lag dang / gsung rnam pa sna tshogs su bsgrub pa dang / mdo sde sna tshogs kyi tshul rab tu brjod pa dang / gzungs kyi sgo rnam pa tha dad pa'i rgyud dang / tha dad pa yang dag par mkhyen pa'i tshul gyi gzhung sna tshogs dang / 'phags pa'i bden pa'i ming rgya mtsho'i rgyud rnam pa sna tshogs dang / sangs rgyas kyi khyu mchog dang / seng ge'i nga ro rab tu bsgrags pa dang / sems can gyi dge ba'i rtsa ba sna tshogs bstan pa'i cho 'phrul yongs su bstan pa dang / dran pa'i sgo sna tshogs can shin tu bstan pa'i rnam par 'phrul pa dang / byang chub sems dpa' lung bstan pa'i seng ge'i nga ro sna tshogs dang / de bzhin gshegs pa'i chos kyi 'khor lo'i mthu phyung ba

They did so through the demonstration of various kinds of buddha miracles, through the accomplishment of the various word definitions in various worlds, through various aspects of voice and language in various worlds, through relating the ways of various sūtras, through the processes of the various kinds of gateways to the power of retention, through the production of various kinds of discernment, through the processes of an ocean of various names for the truth, through various majestic lion’s roars of the buddhas, through the demonstration of miracles that teach the roots of merit to beings, through miracles that teach the various gateways of memory, through the lion’s roar of various prophecies to bodhisattvas, and through the power that arises from the various Dharma wheels of the tathāgatas.

teaching by various manifestations of buddhas’ transfigurations and projections, by various expressions, various utterances, various enunciations of doctrine, various mystical mnemonic formulae, various intellectual analyses of principles, various stirrings of the ocean of names of truth, various roarings of the mighty lion’s roar of buddhas, various manifestations of magical performances teaching beings bases of goodness, mystic projections showing various facets of memory, various lion roars foretelling the buddhahood of enlightening beings, various manifestations of the wheel of teaching of the enlightened,

rnam pa sna tshogs kyis 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor mtha' dang / dbus med pa mtha' yas par rnam pa tha dad pa phan tshun mchod pa dang / rnam par dag pa'i 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor sna tshogs yangs pa dang / 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor shin tu phra bar 'dus pa dang / dpag tshad gcig gi tshad tsam dang / dpag tshad bcu'i tshad tsam dang / dpag tshad brgya'i tshad tsam nas/ 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor 'jig rten gyi khams sangs rgyas kyi zhing brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi tshad tsam du sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das de dag gis/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i gsungs dbyangs kyi yan lag dang / sgra skad thams cad kyi rjes su 'gro bas chos ji snyed du bstan pa

The buddha bhagavats taught through the aspects of the voice of a tathāgata and in accordance with all languages in the various assemblies of pupils‍—which are limitless, infinitely different, and dependent on one another‍—in the various vast, pure assemblies of pupils, in the gatherings of small assemblies of pupils, among those that are the length of one yojana, the length of ten yojanas, the length of a hundred yojanas, and so on, up to assemblies of pupils that are as many yojanas as there are atoms in even more countless than countless buddha realms.

in infinite assemblies of infinite varieties, all interdependent, in groups variously purified, in large groups contained in small groups, in groups a league deep, ten leagues deep, up to groups the size of as many worlds as atoms in untold buddha-fields—

de dag thams cad kyang tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis thos so/ / blangs so/ / yang dag par bzung ngo/ / bsams so/ / sangs rgyas kyi sa rnam par 'phrul pa de dag kyang mthong ngo/ / byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin gyi khyu mchog gi mthu phyung ba de dag kyang mthong ngo/ /

Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, heard, adopted, kept, and contemplated all those Dharmas that were taught. He also saw those buddha miracles. He saw the power of the majesty of that bodhisattva samādhi.

all that those buddhas taught, Sudhana heard, took in, remembered, undertook, and contemplated. He also saw the mystic projection and the inconceivable power of concentration of the enlightening being.
de nas tshong dpon btang brjod dran zhing shes bzhin du ting nge 'dzin de las langs nas/ tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la 'di skad ces smras so/ /
Then the head merchant Muktaka mindfully and with awareness arose from his samādhi and said to Sudhana, the head merchant’s son,
Then Muktaka, mindful, perfectly cognizant, arose from that concentration and said to Sudhana,
rigs kyi bu/ kho bo ni de bzhin gshegs pa'i rnam par thar pa/ thogs pa med pa'i rgyan ces bya ba yongs su blangs shing 'dzin pa ste/
“Noble one, I have obtained and hold the liberation of the tathāgatas called the unimpeded display.
“I go in and out of a liberation of buddhas which is called ‘unobstructed manifestation.’

rigs kyi bu/ de ltar kho bo de bzhin gshegs pa'i rnam par thar pa thogs pa med pa'i rgyan de la rtog cing dpyod pa'i tshe/ shar phyogs kyi 'jig rten gyi khams 'dzam bu chu klung gi mdog dang ldan pa na/ de bzhin gshegs pa dgra bcom pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas skar ma'i dbang phyug rgyal po zhes bya ba/ byang chub sems dpa' rnam par snang ba'i snying po la sogs pa byang chub sems dpa'i 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor thams cad dang thabs gcig tu bzhugs pa'ang mig lam du snang ngo/ /

“Noble one, when in that way I strove for and attained[440] the liberation of the tathāgatas called the unimpeded display, to my eyes appeared the tathāgata arhat samyaksaṃbuddha named Tāreśvararāja in the eastern world realm called Jāmbūnadaprabhāsavatī. He was accompanied by an assembly that was all bodhisattvas, such as the bodhisattva Vairocanagarbha.

As I go in and out of the ‘unobstructed mainfestation’ liberation of buddhas, to the east I see in the world Golden Light a buddha named Supreme Savior, along with the whole group of enlightening beings there, led by the enlightening being Child of Radiance.

lho phyogs kyi 'jig rten gyi khams stobs thams cad kyi shugs dang ldan pa na/ de bzhin gshegs pa dgra bcom pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas spos kun tu rnam par yangs pa zhes bya ba/ byang chub sems dpa' bsam pa'i rgyal po la sogs pa byang chub sems dpa'i 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor thams cad dang thabs gcig tu bzhugs pa yang mig lam du snang ngo/ /

“To my eyes appeared the tathāgata arhat samyaksaṃbuddha named Samantagandhavitāna in the southern world realm called Sarvabalavegavatī. He was accompanied by an assembly that was all bodhisattvas, such as the bodhisattva Cintārāja.
To the south I see in the world Possessed of All Powers a buddha named Universal Spread of Fragrance, with the whole group of enlightening beings there, led by King of Thought.

nub phyogs kyi 'jig rten gyi khams spos thams cad kyi 'od dang ldan pa na/ de bzhin gshegs pa dgra bcom pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas ri rab mar me'i rgyal po zhes bya ba/ byang chub sems dpa' chags pa med pa'i sems la sogs pa byang chub sems dpa'i 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor thams cad dang thabs gcig tu bzhugs pa yang mig lam du snang ngo/ /

“To my eyes appeared the tathāgata arhat samyaksaṃbuddha named Merupradīparāja in the western world realm called Sarvagandhaprabhāsavatī. He was accompanied by an assembly that was all bodhisattvas, such as the bodhisattva Asaṅgacitta.
To the west I see in the World Possessed of All Fragrances and Beauties a buddha named Supreme Lamp, with the whole group of enlightening beings there, led by Unobstructed Mind.

byang phyogs kyi 'jig rten gyi khams ngur smrig rgyal mtshan na/ de bzhin gshegs pa dgra bcom pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas rdo rje rab tu 'dul ba zhes bya ba/ byang chub sems dpa' rdo rje'i gom pas rnam par gnon pa la sogs pa byang chub sems dpa'i 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor thams cad dang thabs gcig tu bzhugs pa yang mig lam du snang ngo/ /

“To my eyes appeared the tathāgata arhat samyaksaṃbuddha named Vajrapramardana in the northern world realm called Kāṣāyadhvajā. He was accompanied by an assembly that was all bodhisattvas, such as the bodhisattva Vajrapadavikrāmin.
To the north I see in the world Vestment Banner a buddha named Diamond Crusher, with the whole group of enlightening beings there, led by Boldly Advancing on Indestructible Feet.

byang shar gyi phyogs mtshams kyi 'jig rten gyi khams rin po che thams cad rab tu 'bar ba na/ de bzhin gshegs pa dgra bcom pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas mi dmigs pa'i spyan rnam par dmigs pa zhes bya ba/ byang chub sems dpa' dmigs pa med par shin tu sprul pa la sogs pa byang chub sems dpa'i 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor thams cad dang thabs gcig tu bzhugs pa yang mig lam du snang ngo/ /

“To my eyes appeared the tathāgata arhat samyaksaṃbuddha named Anilambhacakṣurvairocana[441] in the northeastern world realm called Sarvaratnarucirā. He was accompanied by an assembly that was all bodhisattvas, such as the bodhisattva Anilambhasunirmita.
To the northeast I see in the world Beauty of All Jewels a buddha named Radiance of the Independent Eye, with the whole group of enlightening beings there, led by Independent Emanation.

shar lho'i phyogs mtshams kyi 'jig rten gyi khams spos kyi 'od zer rab tu snang ba na/ de bzhin gshegs pa dgra bcom pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas spos kyi mar me zhes bya ba/ byang chub sems dpa' chos kyi dbyings kyi gzhi tha dad pa'i dpal gyi rgyal po la sogs pa byang chub sems dpa'i 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor thams cad dang thabs gcig tu bzhugs pa yang mig lam du snang ngo/ /

“To my eyes appeared the tathāgata arhat samyaksaṃbuddha named Gandhapradīpa in the southeastern world realm called Gandhārciḥprabhāsvarā. He was accompanied by an assembly that was all bodhisattvas, such as the bodhisattva Sarvadharmadhātutalabhedaketurāja.[442]
