All around there were a million ponds with yellow sandalwood mud, covered with lotuses of various colors made from all precious materials and filled with stainless water illuminated by the great radiance of the precious lotuses.
There were also ten hundred thousand pools, lined with sandalwood clay, covered with lotuses of various colors made of all kinds of jewels, with pure water shining with lotuses of huge gems.

bza' shing gi ra ba de'i dbus na gzhal med khang chen po rgyal mtshan sna tshogs zhes bya ba sa'i gzhi rin po che rgya mtsho'i snying po las blangs pa/ nor bu rin po che'i ka ba bkye ba/ 'dzam bu chu klung gi gser gyi lhun mngon par 'phags pa nor bu rin po che 'gro bar rnam par snang ba'i spang leb bkye bas brgyan pa/ gzhi nor bu rin po che 'bar ba grangs med pa'i ra bas bres pa/ rin po che'i rgyal po mi pham pa'i spos kyi dris gam yo kun nas bdugs pa/ rin po che'i rgyal po sgra snyan pa 'byin pa'i dri'i ngad kun tu ldang ba; rin po che'i rgyal po dri rnam par gsal bar byed pas/ dbang po rno ba'i bag chags rnam par bsgrubs pa dang ldan zhing

In the center of Samantavyūha Park there was a great aerial palace called Vicitradhvaja. It had a floor made of jewels from within the ocean; it was adorned by beryl[537] jewel pillars, with a high spire of Jambu River gold and with floorboards that were a display of precious jewels that illuminated the world; and it was draped in countless nets of shining precious jewels. It had the scent of the perfume of the invincible kings of jewels that perfume the environs, the scent of the kings of music-emitting jewels that spread everywhere, and the kings of stain-eliminating jewels that establish the propensities for sharp faculties.[538]

In the middle of the park was a large mansion called Multicolored Banner standing on a ground of jewels, adorned with pillars of sapphire, roofed with gold, surfaced with arrays of world-illumining jewels, its base blazing with webs of countless jewels, graced by the scent of unsurpassed jewels of fragrance, perfumed by jewels of compounded fragrances, filled with jewels of awakening fragrance extinguishing the heat of the senses.

gzhal med khang chen po rgyal mtshan sna tshogs der stan grangs med cing tshad med pa bting bar gyur pa 'di lta ste/ pad+mo'i snying po can dang / nor bu rin po che phyogs snang bar byed pa'i pad+mo'i snying po can dang / nor bu rin po che rnam par snang ba'i pad+mo'i snying po can dang / nor bu rin po che 'gro ba yid du 'ong ba'i pad+mo'i snying po can dang / nor bu rin po che mdzod sna tshogs kyi pad+mo'i snying po can dang / nor bu rin po che seng ge'i shing thags pad+mo'i snying po can dang / nor bu rin po che dri ma med pa'i pad+mo'i snying po can dang / nor bu rin po ches brgyan pa'i pad+mo'i snying po can dang; nor bu rin po che sgo kun nas brgyan pa'i pad+mo'i snying po can dang / nor bu rin po che 'od kyi rgyan gyi pad+mo'i snying po can dang / nor bu rin po che rgya mtsho'i gnas rnam par dag pa'i rin po ches rnam par brgyan pa'i 'od zer kun tu 'byung ba'i pad+mo'i snying po can dang / nor bu rin po che rdo rje'i seng ges gnon pa'i pad+mo'i snying po can dag bshams shing bting ba ste/

In this celestial mansion called Vicitradhvaja, countless, innumerable seats, which were lotus pericarps, had been arranged. There had been arranged and set out lotus pericarps of precious jewels that illuminated the directions, lotus pericarps of shining precious jewels, lotus pericarps of precious jewels that illuminated[539] the world, lotus pericarps that were manifold treasuries of precious jewels, lotus pericarps of lion-cage precious jewels, lotus pericarps of stainless precious jewels, lotus pericarps that were a display of precious jewels, lotus pericarps of precious jewels that faced everywhere,[540] lotus pericarps of precious jewels that were a display of lights, lotus pericarps of pure precious jewels from the ocean, which were precious jewels that shone with light rays, and lotus pericarps of overpowering vajra-lion precious jewels.

In that mansion were arranged infinite seats—the calyxes of lotuses, luminous jewel lotuses, radiant jewel lotuses, world-illumining jewel lotuses, lotuses of various treasures, lotuses of pure jewels, lotuses inlaid with jewels, lotuses of omnifaceted jewels, lotuses of jewels with auras of light, lotuses of jewels shining with the radiant lights of arrays of pure jewels of the ocean, jewel lotuses covered with diamond lions.

gzhal med khang chen po rgyal mtshan sna tshogs de'i ba gam mang po yang rin po che bsam gyis mi khyab pa las byas pa/ rin po che sna tshogs kyis rnam par brgyan pa/ kha dog bsam gyis mi khyab par mdzes shing gzugs yod du 'ong ba dag go /
The celestial mansion Vicitradhvaja had many pinnacles made of countless jewels, displaying an array of various jewels that were beautiful, attractive, and delightful, with countless colors.
The many turrets of the mansion were made of inconceivably many jewels, arrayed with varicolored jewels, their forms resplendent with light of inconceivably many colors.

bza' shing gi ra ba kun nas brgyan pa de steng nas bla re chen po brgya stong phrag bcus kun nas khebs pa ste/ 'di ltar gos kyi bla re dang / 'khri shing gi bla re dang / me tog gi bla re dang / phreng ba'i bla re dang / spos kyi bla re dang / nor bu rin po che'i bla re dang / gser gyi bla re dang / rgyan gyi bla re dang / rin po che rdo rje snang ba'i bla re dang / glang po'i shugs dang ldan pas sprul pa'i lha mo'i bla re dang / nor bu rin po che brgya byin mngon par dga' ba'i bla re dang / de dag la sogs pa bla re brgya stong phrag bcus kun nas khebs par byas pa'o/ /

A million great canopies covered the Samantavyūha Park from above. There were canopies of cloth, canopies of creepers, canopies of flowers, canopies of garlands, perfumed canopies, canopies of jewels, canopies of gold, canopies of adornments, canopies of shining diamond jewels, canopies of apsarases conjured by Airāvaṇa the king of elephants,[541] canopies of the precious jewels that are worn[542] by Śakra, and so on‍—a million such canopies completely covered the park.

The park was also covered above by ten hundred thousand canopies, such as canopies of cloth, canopies of plant tendrils, canopies of flowers, canopies of garlands, canopies of fragrances, canopies of jewels, golden canopies, canopies of jewels glittering like diamonds, canopies of nymphs magically produced by the chief of the water spirits, canopies of jewels prized by the king of gods.

rin po che'i dra ba brgya stong phrag bcus kun nas yog pa ste/ 'di ltar rin po che dam pa'i dril bu'i dra ba dang / rin po che'i gdugs kyi dra ba dang / rin po che'i 'bru'i dra ba dang; mu tig rgya mtsho'i snying po'i dra ba dang / nor bu rin po che bai DUr+ya sngon po'i dra ba dang / seng ge'i 'khri shing gi dra ba dang / nor bu rin po che chu shel gyi dra ba dang / spos kyi gzugs kyi dra ba dang / rin po che'i cod pan dang / rin po che'i phreng ba'i dra ba dang / de dag la sogs pa rin po che'i dra ba brgya stong phrag bcus kun nas yog pa/

The park was covered with a million precious networks. There were networks of precious bells; networks of precious parasols; networks of precious images;[543] networks of pearls, the essences of the sea; networks of precious blue beryl jewels; networks of lion-vine ornaments; networks of precious moonstone jewels; networks of perfumed shapes; networks of precious crowns; networks of precious strings of beads; and so on‍—a million such networks completely covered the park.

It was also covered by ten hundred thousand precious nets such as nets of bells with jewels inside, nets of jeweled streamers, nets of jewel figures, nets of pearls, nets of sapphires, nets of moonlike jewels, nets emanating fragrance, nets of jeweled crowns.

snang ba chen po brgya stong phrag bcus kyang kun nas yog pa ste/ 'di ltar nor bu rin po che skar ma'i 'od zer gyi snang ba dang / nor bu rin po che nyi ma'i snying po'i snang ba dang / nor bu rin po che zla ba'i rgyal mtshan gyi snang ba dang / nor bu rin po che spos kyi dud pa 'od 'phro ba'i snang ba dang / nor bu rin po che dpal gyi snying po'i snang ba dang / nor bu rin po che pad+mo'i snying po'i snang ba dang / nor bu rin po che skar ma'i rgyal mtshan gyi snang ba dang / nor bu rin po che sgron ma chen po'i snang ba dang / nor bu rin po che phyogs kun tu rnam par snang ba'i snang ba dang / nor bu rin po che spos kyi sprin chen po'i snang ba dang / glog gi phreng ba 'byung ba'i snang ba dang / de dag la sogs pa nor bu rin po che'i snang ba chen po brgya stong phrag bcus rtag tu snang bar byas pa'o/ /

The park was also covered with a million great radiances. There was the radiance of precious starlight jewels, the radiance of precious sunstones, the radiance of precious moon-banner jewels, the radiance of precious incense-smoke jewels, the radiance of precious lotus-essence jewels, the radiance of precious star-banner jewels, the radiance of precious great-lamp jewels, the radiance of precious all-illuminating jewels, the radiance of precious great-clouds-of-perfume jewels, the radiance of precious garlands-of-lightning jewels, and so on‍—a million such great radiances from precious jewels illuminated the park.

It was also illumined by ten hundred thousand great lights, such as starlight-jewel light, sun-filled-jewel light, moonlike-jewel light, scenting-flame-jewel light, luster-filled-jewel light, lotus-calyx-jewel light, starry-jewel light, great blazing jewel light, radiant jewel light, and the light of jewels like wreaths of lightning emitting great clouds of fragrance.

bza' shing gi ra ba de ni rgyan chen po'i sprin brgya stong phrag bcu'i char 'bab pa'i rgyan dang ldan pa ste/ dus dang mthun pa'i tsan dan gyi sprin brgya stong phrag bcu'i 'brug sgra rab tu 'byung ba lha rdzas las 'das pa'i phreng ba dang lda ldi'i sprin chen po kun tu mched pas rab tu brgyan pa/ lha rdzas las 'das pa'i gos tshon sna tshogs dang ldan pa'i sprin brgya stong phrag bcu'i sprin mngon par 'bab pa/ lha rdzas las 'das pa'i rgyan gyi sprin brgya stong phrag bcus rnam par klubs pa/ lha'i bu brgya stong phrag bcu mthong bar dga' ste/ 'og tu lta zhing rab tu 'dud pa'i phyag char bzhin du 'bab pa/ lha mi'i sprin brgya stong phrag bcu sngon gyi spyod pa'i skal ba mnyam pos rang rang gi lus 'bul ba'i char mngon par 'bab pa/ byang chub sems dpa'i sprin brgya stong phrag bcus chos mnyan pas sgom zhing 'ong ba'i char mngon par 'bab pa ste/

In that park there were a million great clouds of adornments that rained down adornments; there was thunder from a million clouds of yellow sandalwood; there was the beauty of a million clouds of hanging garlands and wreaths that transcended those of the devas; there was the rain from a million clouds of various kinds of clothing that transcended those of the devas; there was the beautification from a million clouds of adornments that transcended those of the devas; there was a cloud of a million devas who, wishing to see, looked downward and bowed their bodies in a rainfall of homage; there was a cloud of a million apsarases, with the same extent of past conduct, who sent down a rain of the offering of their bodies; and there was a cloud of a million bodhisattvas listening to the Dharma and sending down a rain for those who are thirsty.

The park was also adorned by rain from ten hundred thousand great clouds of ornaments; ten hundred thousand sandalwood-scented clouds thundered; it was adorned by ten hundred thousand trailing clouds of garlands surpassing those in the heavens; ten hundred thousand clouds of varicolored cloths surpassing the celestials rained; it was adorned by ten hundred thousand clouds of ornaments surpassing those of the heavens; it was showered by ten hundred thousand celestial beings bowing their heads to see; it was showered by ten hundred thousand clouds of nymphs producing beings of their own kind who did the same things in the past, with bodies like their own; it was showered by ten hundred thousand clouds of enlightening beings who had come to hear the Teaching.

de na dge bsnyen ma yid bzhin gser gyi snying po'i khri chen po la 'dug cing mu tig rgya mtsho'i snying po'i dra bas brgyan pa'i cod pan thogs pa/ lag pa la lha rdzas las 'das pa'i gser gyi dpung rgyan dang / gdu bu thogs pa/ lag pa nor bu rin po che dpal gyi rang bzhin gyi 'od zer gyis rnam par mdzes par gyur pa/ rna cha rin po che mthon thing dri ma med pa rab tu 'phyang ba/ mgo nor bu rin po che'i dra bas mdzes par brgyan pa/ nor bu rin po che seng ge'i gdong gi rna ba'i gong rgyan thogs pa/ nor bu rin po che yid bzhin gyi rgyal po'i mgul 'khor thogs pa/ lus rin po che thams cad kyi dra bas yog cing 'od rab tu 'bar ba;

The upāsikā Āśā was seated there on a great throne of the essence of gold, wearing a crown of a net of pearls, the essences of the sea; wearing on her arms gold armlets and bracelets transcending those of the devas; her arms adorned by precious jewels shining with glorious light rays; wearing precious, stainless, dark blue pendant earrings; her head beautifully adorned by a net of precious jewels; wearing precious lion-face jewels on the upper part of her ears; wearing a necklace of precious king of wish-fulfilling jewels at her throat; her body covered in a brightly shining net of all jewels.

Innumerable living beings in all states of existence came from the ten directions to the laywoman Asha, who was seated on a golden throne, adorned with a net of pearls from the ocean, wearing a tiara, her wrists adorned with bracelets of gold more beautiful than that of the heavens, her arms resplendent with jewels of glorious light, wearing earrings of pure deep blue gems, her head adorned with a veil of all kinds of jewels, her neck draped with a string of wish-fulfilling jewels.

srog chags bye ba khrag khrig gis lus rab tu btud de/ phyag bya ba zhig 'dug ste/ dge bsnyen ma yid bzhin de'i drung du shar phyogs nas tshangs pa chen po'am/ tshangs lha nye phan nam/ tshangs pa'i ris su gtogs pa'am/ dbang byed dam/ gzhan 'phrul dbang byed kyi ris su gtogs pa'am/ rab 'phrul dga'am/ 'phrul dga'i ris su gtogs pa'am/ rab dga' ldan nam/ dga' ldan gyi ris su gtogs pa'am/ rab mtshe ma'am/ mtshe ma'i ris su gtogs pa'am/ lha'i dbang po'am/ sum cu rtsa gsum gyi ris su gtogs pa'am/ gnod sbyin gyi dbang po'am/ gnod sbyin nam/ dri za'i dbang po'am/ dri za'am/ grul bum gyi dbang po'am/ grul bum mam; klu'i dbang po'am/ klu'am/ lha ma yin gyi dbang po'am/ lha ma yin nam/ nam mkha' lding gi dbang po'am/ nam mkha' lding ngam/ mi'am ci'i dbang po'am/ mi'am ci'am/ lto 'phye chen po'i dbang po'am/ lto 'phye chen po'am/ gshin rje'am/ gshin rje'i bu mo'am/ yi rdzu 'phrul chen po'am/ yi sam/ mi'i dbang po'am/ mi yang rung ste/ sems can tshad med grangs med pa dag 'ong ba dang /

A quintillion beings were bowing down to her in homage. In front of this upāsikā, there came from the eastern direction countless, innumerable beings: Mahābrahmās, court priests of Brahmās, and Brahmakāyika devas, Vaśavartins and Paranirmitavaśavartin devas, Sunirmitas and Nirmāṇarati devas, Saṃtuṣitas and Tuṣita devas, Suyāmas and Yāma devas, Devendra and Trāyastriṃśa devas, lords of yakṣas and yakṣas, lords of gandharvas and gandharvas, lords of kumbhāṇḍas and kumbhāṇḍas, lords of nāgas and nāgas, lords of asuras and asuras, lords of garuḍas and garuḍas, lords of kinnaras and kinnaras, lords of mahoragas and mahoragas, Yamas and Yama daughters, pretas with great power and pretas, and lords of humans and humans.

de bzhin du lho phyogs dang / nub phyogs dang / byang phyogs dang / byang shar gyi phyogs mtshams dang / shar lho'i phyogs mtshams dang / lho nub kyi phyogs mtshams dang / nub byang gi phyogs mtshams dang / 'og dang steng gi phyogs nas kyang tshangs pa chen po'am/ tshangs lha nye phan nam/ tshangs pa'i ris su gtogs pa'am/ dbang byed dam/ dbang byed kyi ris su gtogs pa nas/ mi'i dbang po'am/ mi'i bar gyi sems can mang po 'ong ba

In the same way, from the south, the west, the north, the northeast, the southeast, the southwest, the northwest, above, and below there came many beings: Mahābrahmās, court priests of Brahmās, Brahmakāyika devas, Vaśavartins, Paranirmitavaśavartin devas, and so on, up to lords of humans and humans.

de dag nad sna tshogs shig gis btab pas/ nyon mongs pa sna tshogs kyis kun nas 'khor tam/ lta ba'i rnam pa sna tshogs la mngon par zhen tam/ las kyi sgrib pas bsgribs pa zhig yod na'ang / de dag gis dge bsnyen ma yid bzhin de mthong ma thag tu nad thams cad kyang rab tu zhi bar gyur; sems kyi nyon mongs pa'i dri ma dang yang bral bar gyur/ lta ba'i gsal shing yang phyin par gyur/ sgrib pa'i ri thams cad kyang rnam par shigs par gyur/ rnam par dag pa'i dkyil 'khor bsgribs pa med pa yang khong du chud par gyur te/ rnam par dag pa'i dkyil 'khor de yod pas ni dge ba'i rtsa ba thams cad kyang rab tu byang bar 'gyur/ dbang po'i myu gu thams cad kyang rnam par 'phel bar 'gyur/ thams cad mkhyen pa'i ye shes kyi tshul rgya mtsho la'ang yang dag par gzhol bar gyur/ gzungs kyi sgo rgya mtsho thams cad la'ang 'jug par gyur/ ting nge 'dzin gyi sgo dang tshul rgya mtsho thams cad kyang mngon sum du gyur/ smon lam gyi sgo thams cad kyang yang dag par skye bar gyur/ spyod pa'i sgo thams cad kyang rab tu 'byung bar gyur/ yon tan mngon par bsgrub pa'i sgo thams cad kyang rnam par dag par gyur/ sems rgya chen po yang mngon par shes pa thams cad dang ldan pa'i tshul du 'byung bar gyur/ lus thogs pa med pas kyang thams cad du rjes su 'gro bar gyur to/ /

All those who suffered from various illnesses, were mired in various kleśas, were attached to various wrong views, or were obscured by karmic obscurations, as soon as they saw Upāsikā Āśā, were healed of their illnesses, became freed from the kleśas that stained their minds,[544] departed from their erroneous views, had all their mountains of obscurations destroyed, and entered the pure field of freedom from obscurations, and within that pure field they purified all their roots of merit, caused all the seedlings of their faculties to grow, became dedicated to the ocean of the way of omniscient wisdom, entered the entire ocean of the gateways to the power of retention, faced the entire ocean of the gateways of samādhis, developed all the gateways of prayer, gave rise to all the gateways of conduct, purified all the gateways of the accomplishment of qualities, gave rise to the ways of all the clairvoyances of a vast mind, and could go anywhere with unimpeded bodies.

Those who came to her, affected with various sicknesses, filled with various afflictions, immersed in various views, covered by obstructions caused by actions, had their sicknesses alleviated when they saw Asha. Their minds freed from the defilement of afflictions, the thorns of views removed, the mountains of obstructions disintegrated, they entered the sphere of unobstructed purity, in which sphere of purity all their roots of goodness were clarified, the sprouts of spiritual faculties grew, and they entered the ocean of principles of omniscience, they recited the ocean of all mystic spells leading to mental command, came face to face with the ocean of all concentration media, began all holy vows, set all means of practice into operation, purified the means of accomplishing all virtues, proceeded according to wisdom characterized by all higher knowledges with unregressing breadth of mind, and became physically unattached and unobstructed, able to go everywhere.

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzangbza' shing gi ra ba kun nas rnam par brgyan pa'i nang du phyin te bltas na/ dge bsnyen ma yid bzhin khri bzang po la 'dug pa mthong nas de dge bsnyen ma yid bzhin gang na ba der stong ste phyin nas/ dge bsnyen ma yid bzhin gyi rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te/ dge bsnyen ma yid bzhin la lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas/ 'di skad ces smras so/ /

Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, entered the Samantavyūha Park, looked around at everything, and saw the upāsikā Āśā seated on a magnificent throne. He approached the upāsikā Āśā and, having reached her, bowed his head to the feet of the upāsikā Āśā. He circumambulated her, keeping her to his right, many hundreds of thousands of times and then said,
Then Sudhana entered the park, looking all over till he saw Asha sitting there. He went up to her, paid his respects, and said,

'phags ma/ bdag gis bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed na/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas/ byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bgyi ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bgyi ba ma 'tshal te/ 'phags ma ni/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams la gdams ngag dang rjes su bstan pa mdzad do zhes thos na/ 'phags ma/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bgyi ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bgyi ba bdag la bshad du gsol/

“Āryā, I have developed the aspiration for the highest, complete enlightenment, but I do not know how bodhisattvas should train in bodhisattva conduct and in what way they should practice it. Āryā, I have heard that you give instruction and teachings to bodhisattvas! I pray that you explain to me how bodhisattvas should train in bodhisattva conduct and how they should practice it!”

“Noble one, I have set my mind on supreme perfect enlightenment, but I do not know how to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings. I hear you give instructions to enlightening beings, so please tell me how an enlightening being is to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings.”
des smras pa/ rigs kyi bu/ kho mo ni byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa mya ngan med pa/ bde ba'i rgyal mtshan thob pa ste/
The upāsikā Āśā said, “Noble one, I have attained the bodhisattva liberation called the banner of bliss without sorrow.
She said, “I have attained an enlightening liberation called ‘characterized by sorrowless well-being.’
rigs kyi bu/ kho mo ni de'i mthus mthong na don yod pa'o/ / mnyan na don yod pa'o/ / rim gror byas pa don yod pa'o/ / gnas gcig na 'grogs pa don yod pa'o/ / rjes su dran par byas pa don yod pa'o/ /
Noble one, through its power it is beneficial to see me, it is beneficial to hear me, it is beneficial to honor me, it is beneficial to be in one place with me, and it is beneficial to remember me.
It is definitely beneficial to see me, hear me, attend me, live with me, remember me.

rigs kyi bu/ kho mo ni sems can dge ba'i rtsa ba ma bskyed pa/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyis yongs su ma zin pa/ yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas kyis ma dgongs pa rnams kyis mthong zhing rnam par dmigs par mig lam du 'ong bar mi 'gyur te/

“Noble one, when beings who have not developed the roots of merit, have not become pupils of a kalyāṇamitra, and have no intention to attain complete buddhahood look at me, I do not appear within their field of vision.
I am not visible to those who have not developed the bases of goodness, who are not under the tutelage of spiritual benefactors, who are not in the care of the perfect buddhas.
rigs kyi bu/ kho mo mthong btsam gyis ni/ sems can rnams kyang bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub las phyir mi ldog par 'gyur ro/ /
“Noble one, merely through seeing me, beings become irreversible on the path to the highest, complete enlightenment.
Those who see me thereupon become irreversible in progress toward supreme perfect enlightenment.

gzhan yang rigs kyi bu/ kho mo'i drung du shar phyogs nas de bzhin gshegs pa dag byon cing / gdan rin po che'i khri la bzhugs nas chos ston to/ /shar phyogs nas ji lta ba bzhin du phyogs bcu nas kyang de bzhin te/

“Moreover, noble one, tathāgatas come from the east into my presence, and they sit on precious thrones and teach the Dharma. And just as they come from the east, they come in that way from the ten directions.
Furthermore, the buddhas of the ten directions come here and sit on this jewel seat and expound the truth to me.
rigs kyi bu/ de lta bas na kho mo ni de bzhin gshegs pa mthong ba dang mi 'bral ba'o/ / chos mnyan pa dang mi 'bral ba'o/ / byang chub sems dpa' dang 'grogs pa dang mi 'bral ba'o/ /
“Therefore, noble one, I am never without the sight of the tathāgatas, I am never without the teaching of the Dharma, and I am never without the company of bodhisattvas.
I am always seeing buddhas, hearing the truth, and meeting enlightening beings.

rigs kyi bu/ kho mo dang spyod pa'i skal pa mnyam pa'i srog chags bye ba khrag khrig brgya stong phrag brgyad cu rtsa bzhi po bza' shing gi ra ba kun nas rnam par brgyan pa 'di na gnas pa de dag thams cad kyang / bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub las phyir mi ldog pa sha stag go /

“Noble one, eighty-four hundred thousand quintillion beings who have the same level of conduct as me are present in this Samantavyūha Park. They are all irreversibly progressing to the highest, complete enlightenment.
The eighty-four thousand quadrillion beings who live here in this park are all irreversible in progress toward supreme perfect enlightenment, having performed the same practices as I have.

rigs kyi bu/ sems can gzhan gang 'di na gnas pa de dag kyang / bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub las mi ldog pa phyir mi ldog pa'i dge 'dun du gtogs pa sha stag ste/ kho mo dang spyod pa'i skal pa mnyam pa dag go /

“Noble one, all the other beings who are present here will also progress irreversibly to the highest, complete enlightenment and will be included within the irreversible saṅgha and have the same level of conduct as myself.”

Any others who live here too will all be irreversible in progress toward supreme perfect enlightenment, as enlightening beings of the same practice as I who have entered the community of those who cannot regress.”
smras pa/ 'phags ma khyod kyis bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu yun ji srid cig nas thugs bskyed/
Sudhana asked, “Āryā, how long have you had the aspiration to attain the highest, complete enlightenment?”
Sudhana said, “Noble one, how long ago did you set your mind on supreme perfect enlightenment?”

smras pa/ rigs kyi bu/ kho mos ni/ sngon gyi gnas rjes su dran te/ de bzhin gshegs pa dgra bcom pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas mar me mdzad ces bya ba byung ba de bzhin gshegs pa de'i drung na/ kho mos tshangs pa'i spyod pa spyad do/ / de bzhin gshegs pa de kho mos mchod do/ / de bzhin gshegs pa de las chos bstan pa kho mos yongs su bzung ngo/ / de'i snga rol du de bzhin gshegs pa dri ma med ba zhes bya ba byung ste/ de'i bstan pa la'ang kho mo rab tu byung ngo/ / chos kyi 'khor lo yang kho mos bzung ngo; ; de'i snga rol du de bzhin gshegs pa dpal zhes bya ba byung ste/ de yang kho mos bsnyen bkur to/ / de'i snga rol du de bzhin gshegs pa ri rab dpal zhes bya ba byung ngo/ / de'i snga rol du de bzhin gshegs pa pad mo'i snying po zhes bya ba byung ngo/ / de'i snga rol du de bzhin gshegs pa rnam par snang mdzad ces bya ba byung ngo/ / de'i snga rol du de bzhin gshegs pa kun tu gzigs pa zhes bya ba byung ngo/ / de'i snga rol du de bzhin gshegs pa tshangs pa dag pa zhes bya ba byung ngo/ / de'i snga rol du de bzhin gshegs pa rdo rje'i gtsug ces bya ba byung ngo/ / de'i snga rol du de bzhin gshegs pa chu bo'i lha zhes bya ba byung ste/

The upāsikā Āśā answered, “Noble one, I remember my past lives. There was the tathāgata arhat samyaksaṃbuddha named Dīpaṅkara. I took the vows of celibacy in the presence of that tathāgata. I made offerings to that tathāgata. I obtained the teaching of the Dharma from that tathāgata. Before him there was a tathāgata named Vimala. I entered homelessness within his teaching, and I also obtained his wheel of the Dharma. Before him there was a tathāgata named Ketu, and I propitiated him. Before him there was a tathāgata named Meruśrī. Before him there was a tathāgata named Padmagarbha. Before him there was a tathāgata named Vairocana. Before him there was a tathāgata named Samantacakṣu. Before him there was a tathāgata named Brahmaśuddha. Before him there was a tathāgata named Vajranābhi. Before him there was a tathāgata named Varuṇadeva.

She said, “I remember a past state when I cultivated religious practice in the company of the buddha known as the Lamp, whom I served and from whom I received teaching. Before that was a buddha named Undefiled; I went forth from society into the tutelage of that buddha and held the wheel of teaching of that buddha. Before that was a buddha named Star; I propitiated that buddha. Before that was a buddha named Splendor of the Polar Mountain; before that was a buddha named Lotus Calyx; before that was a buddha named Illuminating; before that was a buddha named Universal Eye; before that was a buddha named Purified by Spiritual Knowledge; before that was a buddha named Diamond Navel; before that was a buddha named Deifying the Universe.

rigs kyi bu/ gzhung de ltar tshe gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa dang; bskal pa gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa'i sangs rgyas gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa de bzhin gshegs pa'i mtshams 'dab chags su bsams te dran par byas na; gang kho mos rim gror byas te bsnyen bkur ba dang / mchod pa dang / bsti stang du byas pa dang / gang gi spyan sngar kho mos chos thos par gyur pa dang / gang gi bstan pa la kho mos tshangs pa'i spyod pa spyad pa'i de bzhin gshegs pa chu klung gang+gA sum cu rtsa drug gi bye ma snyed rjes su dran te/

“Noble one, in that way I think of and remember the continuous sequence of one life after another, one kalpa after another, and the successions of one buddha after another, remembering tathāgatas as numerous as the grains of sand in thirty-six Ganges Rivers, whom I served, propitiated, made offerings to, honored, and heard the Dharma from and within whose teaching I practiced the conduct of celibacy.

Remembering back in this way lifetime to lifetime, age to age, as successive buddhas appeared in the world, I remember as many buddhas as grains of sand in thirty-six Ganges Rivers whom I propitiated, attended, served, and honored, from whom I heard spiritual teaching, under whose tutelage I carried out spiritual practice.
rigs kyi bu/ de phan chad du kho mos de bzhin gshegs pa ji snyed cig bsnyen bkur ba ni de bzhin gshegs pa rnams kyis mkhyen to/ /
“Noble one, the tathāgatas know how many tathāgatas beyond that I have honored.
Beyond this, only the buddhas know how many buddhas I propitiated.
rigs kyi bu/ sems dang po bskyed ma thag tu chos kyi dbyings rgyas par 'gengs pas/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams ni tshad med pa'o/ /
“Noble one, the bodhisattvas are immeasurable because they fill the realm of phenomena through developing the aspiration for enlightenment for the first time.
Enlightening beings are infinite because of the aspiration of enlightenment, because of pervading all universes;
rigs kyi bu/ snying rje chen po'i khongs su 'gro pa thams cad chud pas byang chub sems dpa' rnams ni tshad med pa'o/ /
“Noble one, the bodhisattvas are immeasurable because through great compassion they enter into all worlds.
enlightening beings are infinite because of the guidance of great compassion, because of entry into the midst of all beings;
rigs kyi bu/ smon lam chen pos phyogs bcu'i chos kyi dbyings kyi gzhi zad zad du 'gro bas byang chub sems dpa' rnams ni tshad med pa'o/ /
“Noble one, the bodhisattvas are immeasurable because through great prayers they are based upon every level in the ten directions of the realm of phenomena.
enlightening beings are infinite because their great vows go to the end of all universes;
rigs kyi bu/ byams pa chen pos 'gro ba thams cad rgyas par 'gengs pa'i phyir/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams ni tshad med pa'o/ /
“Noble one, the bodhisattvas are immeasurable because through their great love they are spread among all beings.
enlightening beings are infinite because of great love, because of suffusing all beings with love;
rigs kyi bu/ byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pas zhing thams cad du bskal pa thams cad yongs su sdud pas byang chub sems dpa' rnams ni tshad med pa'o/ /
“Noble one, the bodhisattvas are immeasurable because through their bodhisattva conduct they include all kalpas in all realms.
enlightening beings are infinite because of the practice of enlightening beings, because of entering into all ages in all lands;
rigs kyi bu/ ting nge 'dzin gyi stobs kyis byang chub sems dpa'i lam las phyir mi ldog pas byang chub sems dpa' rnams ni tshad med pa'o/ /
“Noble one, the bodhisattvas are immeasurable because through the power of samādhi they are irreversible on the bodhisattva path.
enlightening beings are infinite because of the power of concentration, because of not regressing on the path of enlightening beings;
rigs kyi bu/ gzungs kyi stobs kyis 'gro ba thams cad yongs su 'dzin pa'i gzungs kyi tshul khong du chud par byed pas/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams ni tshad med pa'o/ /
“Noble one, the bodhisattvas are immeasurable because through the power of retention they realize the way of retention that supports all beings.
enlightening beings are infinite because of the power of mental command, because of attainment of the method of mystic spells able to hold the memory of truths for all beings;
rigs kyi bu/ ye shes snang ba'i stobs kyis dus gsum gyi ye shes kyi tshul khong du chud par byed cing / yang dag par 'dzin pas byang chub sems dpa' rnams ni tshad med pa'o/ /
“Noble one, the bodhisattvas are immeasurable because through the power of the radiance of knowledge they realize and possess the way of the knowledge of the three times.
enlightening beings are infinite because of the power of the light of knowledge, because of retaining the realization of the knowledge and wisdom of past, present, and future;

rigs kyi bu/ mngon par shes pa'i stobs kyis zhing thams cad du sems can rnams kyi bsam pa dang; mos pa ji lta ba bzhin du 'od kyi dra ba'i 'khor lo mngon par bsgrub pas byang chub sems dpa' rnams ni tshad med pa'o/ /

“Noble one, the bodhisattvas are immeasurable because through the power of clairvoyance they accomplish wheels of nets of light in accordance with the thoughts and aspirations of beings in all realms.
enlightening beings are infinite because of the power of mystic knowledge, because of ability to produce wheels of nets of light pleasing beings according to their mentalities;
rigs kyi bu/ tha dad pa yang dag par shes pa'i stobs kyis tshig gcig brjod kyang / 'gro ba thams cad shin tu tshim par byed pas byang chub sems dpa' rnams ni tshad med pa'o/ /
“Noble one, the bodhisattvas are immeasurable because through the power of discernment they can satisfy all beings by uttering just one word.
enlightening beings are infinite because of the power of intelligence, because of satisfying all beings with one utterance;
rigs kyi bu/ lus rnam par dag pas sangs rgyas kyi zhing thams cad rang gi lus kyis rgyas par 'gengs pas byang chub sems dpa' rnams ni tshad med pa'o/ /
“Noble one, the bodhisattvas are immeasurable because through the purity of their bodies they pervade all the buddha realms with their bodies.”
enlightening beings are infinite because of purity of body, because of pervading all buddha-fields with their own body.”
nor bzang gis smras pa/ 'phags ma khyod ji srid cig na/ bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu mngon par rdzogs par 'tshang rgya bar 'gyur ro/ /
Sudhana asked, “Āryā, at which twilight will you attain the highest, complete enlightenment of buddhahood?”
Sudhana said, “Noble one, when will you realize supreme perfect enlightenment?”

smras pa/ rigs kyi bu/ 'di lta ste/ sems can gcig la dmigs shing gdul bar bya ba dang / smin par bya ba'i phyir byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi sems byang chub tu skye ba ma yin te/ sems can brgya'i phyir ma yin/ sems can stong gi phyir ma yin/ sems can brgya phrag stong gi phyir ma yin/ sems can bye ba'i phyir ma yin/ sems can bye ba brgya'i phyir ma yin/ sems can bye ba stong gi phyir ma yin; sems can bye ba brgya phrag stong gi phyir ma yin te/ sems can bye ba khrag khrig brgya phrag stong gi don du byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi sems byang chub tu skye ba ma yin/

Āśā answered, “Noble one, it is like this: bodhisattvas do not develop the aspiration for enlightenment with the intention of guiding and ripening one[545] being, or a hundred[546] beings, or a thousand[547] beings, or a hundred thousand[548] beings, or ten million[549] beings, or a thousand million beings,[550] or ten thousand million[551] beings, or a trillion[552] beings; nor does a bodhisattva develop the aspiration for enlightenment for the sake of a hundred thousand quintillion[553] beings.

Asha said, “Enlightening beings do not aspire to enlightenment with the object of leading just one sentient being to perfection, nor for the sake of a hundred or a thousand or a million or a billion sentient beings,

sems can thams thams kyi phyir ma yin/ sems can khrag khrig gi phyir ma yin/ [myad myid] sems can gang+gA'i phyir ma yin/ sems can ban bun gyi phyir ma yin/ sems can phyar phyur gyi phyir ma yin/ [ lcag lcig]

“A bodhisattva does not develop the aspiration for enlightenment for the sake of a kaṅkara[554] of beings, or for the sake of a bimbara[555] of beings, or for the sake of an agara[556] of beings, or for the sake of a pravara[557] of beings, or for the sake of a mapara[558] of beings, or for the sake of an avara[559] of beings, or for the sake of a tapara[560] of beings,
nor for any number of beings,

sems can byang bying gi phyir ma yin/ sems can nyer 'jal gyi phyir ma yin/ sems can phyal phyol gyi phyir ma yin/ sems can yal yol gyi phyir ma yin/ sems can ljad ljod kyi phyir ma yin/ sems can phyod zim gyi phyir ma yin/

or for the sake of a sīma[561] of beings, or for the sake of an anaupama[562] of beings, or for the sake of a nena[563] of beings, or for the sake of an avaga[564] of beings, or for the sake of a mṛgava[565] of beings, or for the sake of a vināha[566] of beings,

sems can phyad phyod kyi phyir ma yin/ sems can ldam ldem gyi phyir ma yin; sems can ya gangs kyi phyir ma yin/ sems can cho ma'i phyir ma yin/ sems can khram khrim gyi phyir ma yin/ sems can nab nub kyi phyir ma yin/ [sang sang] sems can brgyud yas kyi phyir ma yin/ sems can btang yas kyi phyir ma yin/ sems can bkra yar gyi phyir ma yin/

or for the sake of a viraga[567] of beings, or for the sake of an avagama[568] of beings, or for the sake of a vigava[569] of beings, or for the sake of a saṃkrama[570] of beings, or for the sake of a visara[571] of beings, or for the sake of a vibhaja[572] of beings, or for the sake of a vijaṅga[573] of beings, or for the sake of a visota[574] of beings, or for the sake of a vivāha[575] of beings, or for the sake of a vibhakta[576] of beings,

sems can gsal yas kyi phyir ma yin/ sems can gzhal brtag gi phyir ma yin/ sems can mtshungs med kyi phyir ma yin/ sems can lam lum gyi phyir ma yin/ sems can rab rib kyi phyir ma yin/ sems can thab thib kyi phyir ma yin/ sems can 'grigs yol gyi phyir ma yin/ sems can them 'phyo'i phyir ma yin/ sems can bsam phyod kyi phyir ma yin/ sems can 'dra mnyam gyi phyir ma yin/

or for the sake of a vikhata[577] of beings, or for the sake of a tulana[578] of beings, or for the sake of an atula[579] of beings, or for the sake of a varaṇa[580] of beings, or for the sake of a vivaraṇa[581] of beings, or for the sake of an avana[582] of beings, or for the sake of a thavana[583] of beings, or for the sake of a viparya[584] of beings, or for the sake of a samarya[585] of beings, or for the sake of a viturṇa[586] of beings,

sems can brang breng gi phyir ma yin/ sems can bgrod yas kyi phyir ma yin/ sems can rgyas 'dal gyi phyir ma yin/ sems can bsngo yas kyi phyir ma yin/ sems can zang yag gi phyir ma yin/ sems can 'phro ba bkye'i phyir ma yin/ sems can rtse 'phyo'i phyir ma yin/ sems can yong then gyi phyir ma yin/ sems can brug g.yos kyi phyir ma yin/ sems can sang yal gyi phyir ma yin/

or for the sake of a hetura[587] of beings, or for the sake of a vicāra[588] of beings, or for the sake of a visāra[589] of beings, or for the sake of a vyatyasta[590] of beings, or for the sake of an abhyudgata[591] of beings, or for the sake of a viśiṣṭa[592] of beings, or for the sake of a nivala[593] of beings, or for the sake of a haribha[594] of beings, or for the sake of a vikṣobha[595] of beings, or for the sake of a halibha[596] of beings,
sems can thing yug gi phyir ma yin/ sems can snang yal gyi phyir ma yin/ sems can nan pa'i phyir ma yin/ sems can yid 'phyo'i phyir ma yin/ sems can nab neb kyi phyir ma yin/

or for the sake of a harisa[597] of beings, or for the sake of an aloka[598] of beings, or for the sake of a dṛṣṭānta[599] of beings, or for the sake of a hetuna[600] of beings, or for the sake of a durbuda of beings,[601]
or for the sake of a haruṇa[602] of beings,
sems can khrig thams kyi phyir ma yin/ sems can yal yol gyi phyir ma yin/ sems can bgrang yas kyi phyir ma yin/
or for the sake of an ela[603] of beings, or for the sake of a dumela[604] of beings, or for the sake of a kṣemu[605] of beings,
or for the sake of an akṣayamukta[606] of beings,

sems can thug yal gyi phyir ma yin/ sems can yad yud kyi phyir ma yin/ sems can phyo ldog gi phyir ma yin/ sems can brda yas kyi phyir ma yin/ sems can lhub be'i phyir ma yin/ sems can thag thug gi phyir ma yin/ sems can khrig ga'i phyir ma yin/ sems can rig yas kyi phyir ma yin/ sems can snyad med kyi phyir ma yin/ sems can mchog phreng gi phyir ma yin/

or for the sake of an elada[607] of beings, or for the sake of a māluda[608] of beings, or for the sake of a maṇḍumā[609] of beings, or for the sake of a viṣamatā[610] of beings, or for the sake of a samatā[611] of beings, or for the sake of a visada[612] of beings, or for the sake of a pramantā[613] of beings, or for the sake of a pramātra[614] of beings, or for the sake of an amātra[615] of beings, or for the sake of a bhramātra[616] of beings,

sems can nyag 'bru'i phyir ma yin; sems can spu 'phyes kyi phyir ma yin/ sems can 'bru 'brel gyi phyir ma yin/ sems can brjod 'os kyi phyir ma yin/ sems can lhod yas kyi phyir ma yin/ sems can brjod phul gyi phyir ma yin/ sems can zhi snyed kyi phyir ma yin/ sems can ngag thim gyi phyir ma yin/ sems can 'phyo 'gyur gyi phyir ma yin/ sems can nyar nyer gyi phyir ma yin/ sems can phyag phyig gi phyir ma yin/

or for the sake of a gamātra[617] of beings, or for the sake of a namātra[618] of beings, or for the sake of a hemātra[619] of beings, or for the sake of a vimātra[620] of beings, or for the sake of a paramātra[621] of beings, or for the sake of a śivamātra[622] of beings, or for the sake of an ela[623] of beings, or for the sake of a vela[624] of beings, or for the sake of a tela[625] of beings, or for the sake of a śaila[626] of beings, or for the sake of a gela[627] of beings,
or for the sake of a śila[628] of beings,
sems can zal zul gyi phyir ma yin/ [gtad yas]
or for the sake of a śvela[629] of beings, or for the sake of a nela[630] of beings,
or for the sake of a bhela[631] of beings,
sems can sal sul gyi phyir ma yin/ sems can g.yo ldeg gi phyir ma yin/ sems can phan phun gyi phyir ma yin/ sems can brnang ya'i phyir ma yin/
or for the sake of a kela[632] of beings, or for the sake of a sela[633] of beings, or for the sake of a pela[634] of beings, or for the sake of ten septenquinquagintillion beings,
or for the sake of a hela[635] of beings,
sems can rem 'drol gyi phyir ma yin/ sems can rdzi ngad kyi phyir ma yin/ sems can rdzi rdul gyi phyir ma yin/ sems can phun yol gyi phyir ma yin/
or for the sake of a mela[636] of beings, or for the sake of a saraḍa[637] of beings, or for the sake of a māruta[638] of beings, or for the sake of a meruda[639] of beings,

sems can 'ol 'ol gyi phyir ma yin/ sems can ngad ngad kyi phyir ma yin/ sems can bgrang brtsi'i phyir ma yin/ sems can zab bgrang gi phyir ma yin/ sems can dga' rgyang gi phyir ma yin/ sems can grangs mtha'i phyir ma yin/ sems can phyod yal gyi phyir ma yin/ sems can 'ol phyod kyi phyir ma yin/ sems can gdab yas kyi phyir ma yin/ sems can gcal yas kyi phyir ma yin/

or for the sake of a kheluda[640] of beings, or for the sake of a māluda[641] of beings, or for the sake of a samula[642] of beings, or for the sake of an ayava[643] of beings, or for the sake of a kamala[644] of beings, or for the sake of a magava[645] of beings, or for the sake of an atara[646] of beings, or for the sake of a heluya[647] of beings, or for the sake of a veluva[648] of beings, or for the sake of a kajāva[649] of beings,

sems can bgrang yas kyi phyir ma yin/ sems can byi ma 'phyo'i phyir ma yin/ sems can yam me'i phyir ma yin/ sems can bsnyal yas kyi phyir ma yin/ sems can ldab ldeb kyi phyir ma yin/ sems can 'ban chad kyi phyir ma yin/ sems can phan phung gi phyir ma yin/ sems can mtha' rdul gyi phyir ma yin/ sems can rgyud lding gi phyir ma yin/ sems can yun 'gyangs kyi phyir ma yin/ sems can mkha' yal gyi phyir ma yin/

or for the sake of a havava[650] of beings, or for the sake of a havala[651] of beings, or for the sake of a vivara[652] of beings, or for the sake of a bimba[653] of beings, or for the sake of a caraṇa[654] of beings, or for the sake of a carama[655] of beings, or for the sake of a parava[656] of beings, or for the sake of a dhavara[657] of beings, or for the sake of a dhamana[658] of beings, or for the sake of a pramada[659] of beings, or for the sake of a nigama[660] of beings,

sems can bun lob kyi phyir ma yin/ sems can lam lom gyi phyir ma yin/ sems can bsnyad yas kyi phyir ma yin/ sems can lang ling gi phyir ma yin/ sems can ljab ljib kyi phyir ma yin/ sems can mi brtsal gyi phyir ma yin/ sems can 'byams yas kyi phyir ma yin/ sems can nga 'grang gi phyir ma yin/ sems can smos yas kyi phyir ma yin/

or for the sake of an upavarta[661] of beings, or for the sake of a nirdeśa[662] of beings, or for the sake of an akṣaya[663] of beings, or for the sake of a saṃbhūta[664] of beings, or for the sake of an amama[665] of beings, or for the sake of an avada[666] of beings, or for the sake of an utpala[667] of beings, or for the sake of a padma[668] of beings, or for the sake of a saṃkhya[669] of beings,

sems can bkra chal gyi phyir ma yin/ sems can lo rgyas kyi phyir ma yin/ sems can 'bum rdib kyi phyir ma yin/ sems can le lo'i phyir ma yin; sems can phyam phyam gyi phyir ma yin/ sems can bgrang 'phyos kyi phyir ma yin/ sems can bgrang 'phyos la bsgres pa'i phyir ma yin/ sems can dpag yas kyi phyir ma yin/ sems can dpag yas la bsgres pa'i phyir ma yin/ sems can yal 'phyong gi phyir ma yin/ sems can yal 'phyong la bsgres pa'i phyir ma yin/

or for the sake of a gati[670] of beings, or for the sake of an upagama[671] of beings, or for the sake of an aupamya[672] of beings, or for the sake of an asaṃkhyeya[673] of beings, or for the sake of an asaṃkhyeyaparivarta[674] of beings, or for the sake of an aparimāṇa[675] of beings, or for the sake of an aparimāṇaparivarta[676] of beings, or for the sake of an aparyanta[677] of beings, or for the sake of an aparyantaparivarta[678] of beings, or for the sake of an asamanta[679] of beings,

sems can mu yal gyi phyir ma yin/ sems can mu yal la bsgres pa'i phyir ma yin/ sems can bgrang yol gyi phyir ma yin/ sems can bgrang yol la bsgres pa'i phyir ma yin/ sems can mi 'jal gyi phyir ma yin/ sems can mi 'jal la bsgres pa'i phyir ma yin/ sems can bsam phyod kyi phyir ma yin/ sems can bsam phyod la bsgres pa'i phyir ma yin/ sems can mtha' 'byams kyi phyir ma yin/ sems can mtha' 'byams la bsgres pa'i phyir ma yin/ sems can dpag thag gi phyir ma yin/

or for the sake of asamantaparivarta[680] of beings, or for the sake of an agaṇeya[681] of beings, or for the sake of an agaṇeyaparivarta[682] of beings, or for the sake of an atulya[683] of beings, or for the sake of an atulyaparivarta[684] of beings, or for the sake of an acintya[685] of beings, or for the sake of an acintyaparivarta[686] of beings, or for the sake of an aparyanta[687] of beings, or for the sake of an aparyantaparivarta[688] of beings, or for the sake of an amāpya[689] of beings,

sems can dpag thag la bsgres pa'i phyir ma yin/ sems can brjod du med pa'i phyir ma yin/ sems can brjod du med pa la bsgres pa'i phyir ma yin/ sems can brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa'i phyir ma yin/ sems can brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa la bsgres pa'i phyir ma yin/

or for the sake of an amāpyaparivarta[690] of beings, or for the sake of an anabhilāpya[691] of beings, or for the sake of an anabhilāpyaparivarta[692] of beings, or for the sake of an anabhilāpyānabhilāpya[693] of beings, or for the sake of an anabhilāpyānabhilāpyaparivarta[694] of beings.
sems can 'jig rten gyi khams gcig tu gtogs pa rnams kyi phyir ma yin pa nas/ brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa'i 'jig rten gyi khams su gtogs pa'i sems can rnams kyi phyir ma yin/
“The bodhisattvas do not develop the aspiration for enlightenment for the sake of the beings in one world realm, and so on, up to an anabhilāpyānabhilāpyaparivarta of world realms.

gling bzhi pa'i 'jig rten gyi khams kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi 'jig rten gyi khams su gtogs pa'i sems can rnams kyi phyir ma yin/ stong gi 'jig rten gyi khams kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi 'jig rten gyi khams su gtogs pa'i sems can rnams kyi phyir ma yin/ stong gnyis kyi 'jig rten gyi khams kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi 'jig rten gyi khams su gtogs pa'i sems can rnams kyi phyir ma yin/ stong gsum gyi stong chen po'i 'jig rten gyi khams kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi 'jig rten gyi khams su gtogs pa'i sems can rnams kyi phyir ma yin pa nas/ stong gsum gyi stong chen po'i 'jig rten gyi khams brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi 'jig rten gyi khams su gtogs pa'i sems can rnams kyi don du 'di lta ste/ yongs su smin par bya ba dang / gdul ba'i phyir byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi sems byang chub tu skye ba ma yin gyi/

“The bodhisattvas do not develop the aspiration for enlightenment for the sake of beings in world realms as numerous as the atoms in a four-continent world realm, or for the sake of beings in world realms as numerous as the atoms in a thousand such world realms, or for the sake of beings in world realms as numerous as the atoms in a million such world realms, or for the sake of beings in world realms as numerous as the atoms in a billion such world realms, or for the sake of beings in world realms as numerous as the atoms in an anabhilāpyānabhilāpyaparivarta of billion-world great universes. The bodhisattvas do not develop the aspiration for enlightenment in order to guide and ripen that number of beings.
nor for all the sentient beings in as many worlds as atoms in untold, inexpressibly vast numbers of billion-world universes.

'di lta ste/ 'jig rten gyi khams ma lus pa lhag ma med pa mtha' dag thams cad du gtogs pa'i sems can rnams kyi don du yongs su smin par bya ba dang / gdul ba'i phyir byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi sems byang chub tu skye'o/ /
“The bodhisattvas develop the aspiration for enlightenment in order to guide and ripen the beings throughout the entirety of all world realms without exception or remainder.
Enlightening beings aspire to enlightenment for the sake of all sentient beings in all worlds, to lead them to perfection.

'di lta ste/ sangs rgyas gcig bsnyen bkur ba dang / mnyes par bya ba dang / mchod cing rim gror bya ba'i phyir byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi sems byang chub tu skye ba ma yin pa dang / sangs rgyas bcu bsnyen bkur zhing mnyes par bya ba dang / mchod cing rim gror bya ba'i phyir ma yin pa nas; brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa'i 'jig rten gyi khams kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi sangs rgyas bsnyen bkur zhing mnyes par bya ba dang / mchod cing rim gror bya ba'i phyir byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi sems byang chub tu skye ba ma yin/

“The bodhisattvas do not develop the aspiration for enlightenment in order to serve, propitiate, make offerings to, and honor one buddha, or to serve, propitiate, make offerings to, and honor ten buddhas, and so on up to the bodhisattvas do not develop the aspiration for enlightenment in order to serve, propitiate, make offerings to, and honor buddhas as numerous as the atoms in an anabhilāpyānabhilāpyaparivarta of world realms.
Enlightening beings do not aspire to enlightenment to propitiate, honor, and attend one buddha, or even as many buddhas as atoms in untold worlds,

'jig rten gyi khams gcig tu gtogs pa'i sangs rgyas kyi rgyud bsnyen bkur zhing mnyes par bya ba dang / mchod cing rim gror bya ba'i phyir ma yin pa nas/ sangs rgyas kyi zhing brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi 'jig rten gyi khams su gtogs pa'i de bzhin gshegs pa'i rgyud bsnyen bkur zhing mnyes par bya ba dang / mchod cing rim gror bya ba'i phyir byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi sems byang chub tu skye ba ma yin no/ /

“The bodhisattvas do not develop the aspiration for enlightenment in order to serve, propitiate, make offerings to, and honor the succession of buddhas within one world realm and so on up to the bodhisattvas do not develop the aspiration for enlightenment in order to serve, propitiate, make offerings to, and honor the succession of buddhas within world realms as numerous as the atoms in an anabhilāpyānabhilāpyaparivarta of world realms.[695]
or to propitiate, honor, and attend the lineage of buddhas in one world or the lineage of buddhas in as many worlds as atoms in untold buddha-fields.

sangs rgyas kyi zhing gcig yongs su dag par bya ba'i phyir/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi sems byang chub tu skye ba ma yin pa nas/ 'jig rten gyi khams brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi sangs rgyas kyi zhing yongs su dag par bya ba'i phyir/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi sems byang chub tu skye ba ma yin/

“The bodhisattvas do not develop the aspiration for enlightenment in order to purify one buddha realm and so on up to the bodhisattvas do not develop the aspiration for enlightenment in order to purify buddha realms as numerous as the atoms in an anabhilāpyānabhilāpyaparivarta of world realms.
Enlightening beings do not aspire to enlightenment to purify one buddha-land, or even to purify as many buddha-lands as atoms in untold, inexpressible numbers of worlds.

de bzhin gshegs pa gcig gi bstan pa yongs su gzung ba'i phyir/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi sems byang chub tu skye ba ma yin pa nas/ sangs rgyas kyi zhing brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi de bzhin gshegs pa'i bstan pa yongs su gzung ba'i phyir/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi sems byang chub tu skye ba ma yin/

“The bodhisattvas do not develop the aspiration for enlightenment in order to hold the teachings of one tathāgata and so on up to the bodhisattvas do not develop the aspiration for enlightenment in order to hold the teachings of tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms in an anabhilāpyānabhilāpyaparivarta of world realms.
Enlightening beings do not aspire to enlightenment to preserve the teaching of one buddha, or even to preserve the teachings of as many buddhas as atoms in untold, inexpressible numbers of worlds.

sangs rgyas gcig rab tu zhugs pa'i smon lam rnam pa tha dad pa la 'jug pa'i phyir/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi sems byang chub tu skye ba ma yin pa nas/ sangs rgyas kyi zhing brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi sangs rgyas rab tu zhugs pa'i smon lam rnam pa tha dad pa la 'jug par bya ba'i phyir/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi sems byang chub tu skye ba ma yin no/ /

“The bodhisattvas do not develop the aspiration for enlightenment in order to comprehend the different prayers established by one buddha and so on up to the bodhisattvas do not develop the aspiration for enlightenment in order to comprehend the different prayers established by buddhas as numerous as the atoms in an anabhilāpyānabhilāpyaparivarta of world realms.

Enlightening beings do not aspire to enlightenment to enter into the diversity of vows which are the point of departure of one buddha, nor even to enter into the diversity of vows which are the points of departure of as many buddhas as atoms in untold, inexpressible numbers of buddha-fields.

de bzhin gshegs pa gcig gi sangs rgyas kyi zhing gi rgyan la 'jug par bya ba'i phyir/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi sems byang chub tu skye ba ma yin pa nas /sangs rgyas kyi zhing brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi de bzhin gshegs pa'i sangs rgyas kyi zhing gi rgyan la 'jug par bya ba'i phyir/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi sems byang chub tu skye ba ma yin/

“The bodhisattvas do not develop the aspiration for enlightenment in order to enter the displays of one buddha realm and so on up to the bodhisattvas do not develop the aspiration for enlightenment in order to enter the displays of buddha realms as numerous as the atoms in an anabhilāpyānabhilāpyaparivarta of world realms.

Enlightening beings do not aspire to enlightenment to enter into the array of the buddha-field of one buddha, nor even to enter into the arrays of buddha-fields of as many buddhas as atoms in untold, inexpressible numbers of buddha-fields.

sangs rgyas gcig gi 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor rnam par phye ba la 'jug par bya ba'i phyir/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi sems byang chub tu skye ba ma yin pa nas/ sangs rgyas kyi zhing brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi/ 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor rnam par phye ba la 'jug par bya ba'i phyir/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi sems byang chub tu skye ba ma yin/

“The bodhisattvas do not develop the aspiration for enlightenment in order to enter the circle of followers of one buddha and so on up to the bodhisattvas do not develop the aspiration for enlightenment in order to enter the circle of followers of buddhas as numerous as the atoms an anabhilāpyānabhilāpyaparivarta of world realms.

Enlightening beings do not aspire to enlightenment to take part in the assembly of one buddha, nor even to take part in the assemblies of as many buddhas as atoms in untold, inexpressible numbers of buddha-fields.

de bzhin gshegs pa gcig gi chos kyi 'khor lo yongs su gzung ba'i phyir/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi sems byang chub tu skye ba ma yin pa nas/ sangs rgyas kyi zhing brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi de bzhin gshegs pa'i chos kyi 'khor lo yongs su gzung ba'i phyir/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi sems byang chub tu skye ba ma yin/

“The bodhisattvas do not develop the aspiration for enlightenment in order to possess the Dharma wheel of one tathāgata and so on up to the bodhisattvas do not develop the aspiration for enlightenment in order to possess the Dharma wheel of tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms in an anabhilāpyānabhilāpyaparivarta of world realms.

Enlightening beings do not aspire to enlightenment to preserve the wheel of teaching of one buddha, nor to preserve the wheels of teaching of even as many buddhas as atoms in untold, inexpressible numbers of buddha-fields.

sems can gyi sems rgya mtsho gcig khong du chud par bya ba'i phyir/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi sems byang chub tu skye ba ma yin pa nas/ sangs rgyas kyi zhing brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi sems can gyi sems rgya mtsho khong du chud par bya ba'i phyir/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi sems byang chub tu skye ba ma yin/

“The bodhisattvas do not develop the aspiration for enlightenment in order to comprehend the ocean of the mind of one being and so on up to the bodhisattvas do not develop the aspiration for enlightenment in order to comprehend the oceans of the minds of beings as numerous as the atoms in an anabhilāpyānabhilāpyaparivarta of world realms.

Enlightening beings do not aspire to enlightenment to penetrate the ocean of mind of one sentient being, nor to penetrate the oceans of mind of even as many sentient beings as atoms in untold, inexpressible numbers of buddha-fields.

sems can gcig gi dbang po'i 'khor lo yongs su shes par bya ba'i phyir/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi sems byang chub tu skye ba ma yin pa nas/ sangs rgyas kyi zhing brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi sems can gyi dbang po'i 'khor lo yongs su shes par bya ba'i phyir/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi sems byang chub tu skye ba ma yin/

“The bodhisattvas do not develop the aspiration for enlightenment in order to know the wheel of faculties of one being and so on up to the bodhisattvas do not develop the aspiration for enlightenment in order to know the wheels of faculties of beings as numerous as the atoms in an anabhilāpyānabhilāpyaparivarta of world realms.

Enlightening beings do not aspire to enlightenment to know the sphere of faculties of one sentient being, nor to know the faculties of even as many sentient beings as atoms in untold, inexpressible numbers of buddha-fields.

sems can gcig gi dbang po rgya mtsho khong du chud par bya ba'i phyir/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi sems byang chub tu skye ba ma yin pa nas/ sangs rgyas kyi zhing brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi sems can gyi dbang po rgya mtsho khong du chud par bya ba'i phyir/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi sems byang chub tu skye ba ma yin/

“The bodhisattvas do not develop the aspiration for enlightenment in order to know the ocean of faculties of one being and so on up to the bodhisattvas do not develop the aspiration for enlightenment in order to know the ocean of faculties of beings as numerous as the atoms in an anabhilāpyānabhilāpyaparivarta of world realms.

Enlightening beings do not aspire to enlightenment to penetrate the ocean of faculties of one sentient being, nor to penetrate the oceans of faculties of even as many sentient beings as atoms in untold, inexpressible numbers of buddha-fields.

'jig rten gyi khams gcig gi bskal pa gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa la 'jug par bya ba'i phyir/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi sems byang chub tu skye ba ma yin pa nas/ sangs rgyas kyi zhing brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi 'jig rten gyi khams kyi bskal pa gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa la 'jug par bya ba'i phyir/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi sems byang chub tu skye ba ma yin/

“The bodhisattvas do not develop the aspiration for enlightenment in order to enter the succession of kalpas in one world realm and so on up to the bodhisattvas do not develop the aspiration for enlightenment in order to enter the succession of kalpas in world realms as numerous as the atoms in an anabhilāpyānabhilāpyaparivarta of world realms.

Enlightening beings do not aspire to enlightenment to enter into the succession of ages in one world, nor to enter into the succession of ages in even as many worlds as atoms in untold, inexpressible numbers of buddha-fields.

'jig rten gyi khams gcig tu gtogs pa'i sems can thams cad kyi spyod pa'i bag chags kyi mtshams sbyor ba la 'jug bar bya ba'i phyir/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi sems byang chub tu skye ba ma yin pa nas/ sangs rgyas kyi zhing brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi 'jig rten gyi khams su gtogs pa'i sems can thams cad kyi spyod pa'i bag chags kyi mtshams sbyor ba la 'jug par bya ba'i phyir/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi sems byang chub tu skye ba ma yin/

“The bodhisattvas do not develop the aspiration for enlightenment in order to enter an investigation of the propensities for conduct of beings in one world realm and so on up to the bodhisattvas do not develop the aspiration for enlightenment in order to enter an investigation of the propensities for conduct of beings in world realms as numerous as the atoms in an anabhilāpyānabhilāpyaparivarta of world realms.

Enlightening beings do not aspire to enlightenment to comprehend the continuity of actions and habits of the sentient beings in one world, nor to comprehend the continuity of actions and habits of the sentient beings even in as many worlds as atoms in untold, inexpressible numbers of buddha-fields.

'jig rten gyi khams gcig tu gtogs pa'i sems can thams cad kyi nyon mongs pa rgya mtsho thams cad la 'jug par bya ba'i phyir/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi sems byang chub tu skye ba ma yin pa nas/ sangs rgyas kyi zhing brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi 'jig rten gyi khams su gtogs pa'i sems can thams cad kyi nyon mongs pa rgya mtsho thams cad la 'jug par bya ba'i phyir; byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi sems byang chub tu skye ba ma yin/

“The bodhisattvas do not develop the aspiration for enlightenment in order to comprehend the entire ocean of kleśas of all beings within one world realm and so on up to the bodhisattvas do not develop the aspiration for enlightenment in order to comprehend the entire ocean of kleśas of all beings within world realms as numerous as the atoms in an anabhilāpyānabhilāpyaparivarta of world realms.

Enlightening beings do not aspire to enlightenment to comprehend the ocean of afflictions of sentient beings in one world, nor to comprehend the oceans of afflictions of the sentient beings even in as many worlds as atoms in untold, inexpressible numbers of buddha-fields.

'jig rten gyi khams gcig tu gtogs pa'i sems can thams cad kyi las rgya mtsho thams cad la 'jug par bya ba'i phyir/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi sems byang chub tu skye ba ma yin pa nas/ sangs rgyas kyi zhing brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi 'jig rten gyi khams su gtogs pa'i sems can thams cad kyi las rgya mtsho thams cad la 'jug par bya ba'i phyir/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi sems byang chub tu skye ba ma yin/

“The bodhisattvas do not develop the aspiration for enlightenment in order to comprehend the entire ocean of the karma of all beings within one world realm and so on up to the bodhisattvas do not develop the aspiration for enlightenment in order to comprehend the entire ocean of the karma of all beings within world realms as numerous as the atoms in an anabhilāpyānabhilāpyaparivarta of world realms.

Enlightening beings do not aspire to enlightenment to comprehend the ocean of all actions of the beings in one world, nor even to comprehend the oceans of all actions of beings in as many worlds as atoms in untold, inexpressible numbers of buddha-fields.

'jig rten gyi khams gcig tu gtogs pa'i sems can thams cad kyi spyod pa rgya mtsho thams cad khong du chud par bya ba'i phyir/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi sems byang chub tu skye ba ma yin pa nas/ sangs rgyas kyi zhing brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi 'jig rten gyi khams su gtogs pa'i sems can thams cad kyi spyod pa rgya mtsho thams cad khong du chud par bya ba'i phyir/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi sems byang chub tu skye ba ma yin gyi/

“The bodhisattvas do not develop the aspiration for enlightenment in order to comprehend the entire ocean of the conduct of all beings within one world realm and so on up to the bodhisattvas do not develop the aspiration for enlightenment in order to comprehend the entire ocean of the conduct of all beings within world realms as numerous as the atoms in an anabhilāpyānabhilāpyaparivarta of world realms.

Enlightening beings do not aspire to enlightenment to comprehend the ocean of all modes of behavior of all beings in one world, nor even to comprehend the ocean of all modes of behavior of all beings in as many worlds as atoms in untold, inexpressible numbers of buddha-fields.
sems can gyi khams ma lus pa/ lhag ma med pa mtha' dag thams cad yongs su smin par bya ba dang / gdul ba'i phyir byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi sems byang chub tu skye'o/ /
“The bodhisattvas develop the aspiration for enlightenment in order to guide and ripen the beings throughout the entirety of all world realms without exception or remainder.
Rather, enlightening beings aspire to enlightenment to lead all sentient beings without exception to full development—
sangs rgyas ma lus pa thams cad bsnyen bkur zhing mnyes par bya ba dang / mchod cing rim gror bya ba'i phyir byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi sems byang chub tu skye'o/ /
“The bodhisattvas develop the aspiration for enlightenment in order to serve, propitiate, make offerings to, and honor all buddhas without remainder.
they wish to propitiate and honor and attend all buddhas,

'jig rten gyi khams ma lus pa thams cad du gtogs pa'i sangs rgyas kyi rgyud bsnyen bkur zhing mnyes par bya ba dang / mchod cing rim gror bya ba'i phyir byang chub sems dpa' rnams smon lam la mngon par mos pa yin/
“The bodhisattvas make the prayer to serve, propitiate, make offerings to, and honor the succession of buddhas within all world realms without remainder.
to propitiate and honor and attend the successions of buddhas in all worlds;
sangs rgyas kyi zhing ma lus pa thams cad yongs su dag par bya ba'i phyir/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi bsam pa brtan par 'gyur ba yin/
“The bodhisattvas have the firm intention to purify all buddha realms without remainder.
they are determined to purify all buddha-lands;
sangs rgyas kyi bstan pa ma lus pa thams cad yongs su gzung ba'i phyir /byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi sbyor ba 'byung ba yin/
“The bodhisattvas are dedicated to holding the teachings of all tathāgatas without remainder.
they strive to hold the teachings of all buddhas;
de bzhin gshegs pa rab tu zhugs pa'i smon lam rnam pa tha dad pa ma lus pa thams cad kyi rjes su 'brang bar bya ba'i phyir/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi sems kyi shugs drag po skye ba yin/
“The bodhisattvas have the strength of mind to comprehend the different prayers established by all buddhas without remainder.
they are zealously devoted to following the variety of vows which are the points of departure of all buddhas;
de bzhin gshegs pa'i sangs rgyas kyi zhing gi yon tan gyi rgyan ma lus pa thams cad la 'jug par bya ba'i phyir/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi yi dam brtan pa skye ba yin/
“The bodhisattvas are resolved to enter the displays of the qualities of all buddha realms without remainder.
they are determined to enter into the arrays of all buddha-lands;
de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor rgya mtsho ma lus pa thams cad la 'jug par bya ba'i phyir/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi mngon par mos pa 'byung ba yin/
“The bodhisattvas develop aspiration in order to enter the circle of followers of all buddhas without remainder.[696]
they wish to enter the oceans of assemblies of all buddhas;
'gro ba'i sems rgya mtsho ma lus pa thams cad la 'jug par bya ba'i phyir/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi smon lam yongs su skye ba yin/
“The bodhisattvas pray to comprehend the oceans of the minds of all beings without remainder.
they seek to go deeply into the ocean of mind of all sentient beings;
sems can gyi dbang po'i 'khor lo ma lus pa thams cad yongs su shes par bya ba'i phyir/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi mngon par 'dod pa skye ba yin/
“The bodhisattvas long to comprehend the wheels of faculties of all beings without remainder.
they wish to know the spheres of faculties of all sentient beings;
sems can gyi dbang po rgya mtsho ma lus pa thams cad khong du chud par bya ba'i phyir/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi spro ba skye ba yin/
“The bodhisattvas are enthused to comprehend the oceans of faculties of all beings without remainder.
they aspire to penetrate the ocean of faculties of all sentient beings;
'jig rten gyi khams ma lus pa thams cad kyi bskal pa gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa la 'jug par bya ba'i phyir/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi mos pa skye ba yin/
“The bodhisattvas aspire to comprehend the succession of kalpas in all world realms without remainder.
they wish to enter into the succession of ages in all worlds;
sems can ma lus pa thams cad kyi nyon mongs pa'i bag chags kyi mtshams sbyor ba yongs su gcad pa'i phyir/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi brtson 'grus yongs su skye ba yin/
“The bodhisattvas have the determination to eradicate the ocean of kleśas of all beings without remainder.
they are inspired with courage to cut off the continuity of afflictions and habit energies of all sentient beings;
sems can ma lus pa thams cad kyi las dang nyon mongs pa'i rgya mtsho bskam pa'i phyir/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi ye shes chen po'i nyi ma 'char ba yin/
“The bodhisattvas have the rising of the sun of great knowledge in order to dry up the ocean of the karma and kleśas of all beings without remainder.
their sun of knowledge rises to evaporate the ocean of afflictions caused by actions of all sentient beings;
sems can ma lus pa thams cad kyi spyod pa yongs su shes par bya ba'i phyir/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi shes rab kyi snang ba 'byung ba yin/
“The bodhisattvas develop the radiance of wisdom in order to know the conduct of all beings without remainder.
their light of wisdom becomes manifest to know the ways of behavior of all sentient beings;
sems can ma lus pa thams cad kyi sdug bsngal gyi me'i phung po rab tu zhi bar bya ba'i phyir/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi snying rje'i sprin chen po kun nas 'du ba yin/
“The bodhisattvas gather the clouds of great compassion in order to end the mass of suffering of all beings without remainder.
their cloud of great compassion gathers to extinguish the mass of fire of suffering of all sentient beings.
rigs kyi bu/ mdor na de dag la sogs pa byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa'i tshul dang / sgo grangs med pa brgya stong phrag bcu dag /byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyis yongs su bsgrub par bya'o/ /
“Noble one, in brief, the bodhisattvas accomplish these and millions of countless other ways and gateways of bodhisattva conduct.
“To put it briefly, there are ten hundred thousand incalculable numbers of such aspects of the conduct of the practice of enlightening beings, which are to be accomplished by an enlightening being.
rigs kyi bu/ gzhan yang 'di lta ste/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi spyod pa ni ye shes khong du chud par bya ba'i phyir/ chos thams cad la yang dag par gzhol ba'o/ /
“Moreover, noble one, bodhisattva conduct is the acquisition of all Dharmas in order to realize wisdom.
Furthermore, the practice of enlightening beings enters into all things, for the attainment of knowledge;
byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi spyod pa ni yongs su dag par bya ba'i phyir; zhing thams cad la yang dag par gzhol ba'o/ /
Bodhisattva conduct is the acquisition of all realms in order to accomplish their purification.
the practice of enlightening beings enters into all lands, to thoroughly purify them.

rigs kyi bu/ de lta bas na kho mos ni bdag gi smon lam nam mkha'i dbyings rnam par dag pa'i mtha' gang du thug pa de'i mthas klas par shog cig /bdag gi smon lam 'jig rten gyi khams rnam par dag pa'i mtha' gang du thug pa de'i mthas klas par shog cig /bdag gi smon lam ma sems can thams cad kyi nyon mongs pa dang / bag chags kyi mtshams sbyor ba dang / bdag la nyal ba'i mtha' gang du thug pa de'i mthas klas par shog cig ces de ltar smon lam btab bo/

“Therefore, noble one, may my prayers reach their conclusion only when the realm of desire[697] has been completely purified. May my prayers reach their conclusion only when the world realms are purified. May my prayers reach their conclusion only when their connection with the predispositions and propensities for the kleśas of all beings have come to an end.”

Because of this vow of mine, when the purification of the realm of desire is finished, my commitments will be finished; when the purification of the world is finished, my commitments will be finished; when all sentient beings’ propensities to continue afflictive habits are ended, my commitments will be ended.”
smras pa/ 'phags ma/ rnam par thar pa 'di'i ming ci zhes bgyi/
Sudhana asked, “Āryā, what is the name of this liberation?”
Sudhana said, “What is the name of this liberation?”
smras pa/ rigs kyi bu/ rnam par thar pa 'di ni nyon mongs pa med pa/ bde ba'i rgyal mtshan zhes bya ba ste/
Āśā replied, “Noble one, this liberation is called the banner of bliss without sorrow.[698]
Asha said, “This liberation is called ‘characterized by sorrowless well-being.’

rigs kyi bu/ kho mos kyang byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa de gcig pu shes par zad na; byang chub sems dpa'i sangs rgyas kyi chos thams cad yang dag par 'dzin pa'i phyir sems rgya mtsho dang ldan pa/ lhag pa'i bsam pa brtan pa'i phyir ri rab dang 'dra ba/ sems can thams cad kyi nyon mongs pa'i nad rab tu sos par byed pa'i phyir sman gyi rgyal po mthong na legs pa lta bu/ sems can thams cad kyi ma rig pa'i mun pa sel ba'i phyir nyi mar gyur pa /sems can thams cad kyi bsam pa'i gnas su gyur pas ba lta bu'i sems dang ldan pa/ 'gro ba thams cad kyi don byed pa'i phyir rlung du gyur pa/ sems can thams cad la ye shes kyi snang ba 'byin pa'i phyir mar mer gyur pa/ zhi ba'i sgras sangs rgyas kyi chos kyi char yang dag pa ji lta ba bzhin du 'debs pa'i phyir sprin du gyur pa/ bsod nams kyi 'od zer gyi dra ba rab tu 'gyed pa'i phyir zla ba lta bu/ 'gro ba thams cad yongs su bsrung ba la zhugs pa'i phyir brgya phyin lta bu de dag gi spyod pa shes pa'am/ yon tan brjod pa'am/ byang chub sems dpa'i bslab pa bsam gyis mi khyab pa smos pa'am/ byang chub sems dpa'i smon lam gyi rnam pa mtha' dang dbus med pa yongs su bstan par nus re skan/

“Noble one, I know only this bodhisattva liberation. How could I know or describe the qualities of the conduct of bodhisattvas who have minds like an ocean because they have received all the Buddhadharma, who are like Mount Meru because of their firm commitment, who are like beautiful kings of healing because they free all beings from the illness of the kleśas, who are like the sun because they dispel the darkness of ignorance for all beings, who have minds that are like the earth because they support the aspirations of all beings, who are like the air because they benefit all beings, who are like lamps because they bring the light of knowledge to all beings, who are like clouds because they send down with peaceful sounds a rain of the Buddhadharma, who are like the moon because they emit a network of light rays of merit, and who are like Śakra because they are dedicated to the protection of all beings? How could I speak of their inconceivable bodhisattva training? How could I teach the forms of their bodhisattva prayers?

I know this enlightening liberation, but how can I know the practice, tell of the virtues, convey the inconceivable enlightening skills, or show the infinite varieties of enlightening vows of the enlightening beings who have oceanic minds because of seeking all the buddha-teachings, who are like the polar mountain because of steadfast will, who are like the medicine ‘good to see’ because they free all sentient beings from the sicknesses of afflictions, who are like the sun because they eliminate the darkness of ignorance of all sentient beings, whose minds are like the earth because they are a refuge for all sentient beings, who are like air because they benefit all sentient beings, who are lamps producing the light of knowledge for all sentient beings, who are like clouds raining truth with a quiet sound, who are like the moon because they radiate a web of light beams of virtue, who are like gods because they protect all sentient beings?

song / rigs kyi bu /lho phyogs kyi rgyud 'di nyid kyi rgya mtsho rnam par rlob pa 'di na/ yul chu ba gtsang ma zhes bya ba yod de/ de na drang srong 'jigs mchog dbyangs zhes bya ba 'dug gi /de'i gan du song la dris shig dang / des rigs kyi bu khyod la byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa ston par 'gyur ro/ /

“Depart, noble one. In this southern region, in this Samudravetāḍī,[699] there is a land called Nālayu. There dwells a ṛṣi by the name of Bhīṣmottaranirghoṣa. “Go to him and ask him. Noble one, he will teach you the bodhisattva conduct.”
“Go south—there is a district in Samudravetalya called Nalayur where a seer named Bhishmottaranirghosha lives. Go ask him, and he will instruct you in the practice of enlightening beings.”
