de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis/ dge bsnyen ma yid bzhin gyi rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te/ dge bsnyen ma yid bzhin la lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas yang dang yang bltas te/ phyag 'tshal nas ngo mchi mas gang bar ngus te/ byang chub mchog tu dkon pa rjes su sems shing / dge ba'i bshes gnyen rim gro bya ba dkon par rjes su bsdam pa dang / skyes bu dam pa dang 'phrad pa dkon pa rjes su bsam pa dang / byang chub sems dpa'i dbang po thob par bya ba rjes su bsam pa dang / byang chub sems dpa'i bsam pa yongs su dag pa dkon par rjes su bsam pa dang / skal ba mnyam pa'i dge ba'i bshes gnyen dang 'phrad pa dkon par rjes su bsam pa dang / byang chub tu yang dag pa ji lta ba bzhin du mngon par mos shing sems nges par gzhog pa dkon par rjes su bsdam pa dang / mi mnyam pa med pa'i chos kyi tshul rjes su bstan pa'i sbyor ba dkon par rjes su bsdam pa dang / sems dri ma med cing mi 'phrogs pa'i sbyor ba yang dag par bsgrub pa dka' bar rjes su bsam pa dang / thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du shugs drag po rnam par skyed pa'i chos kyi snang ba dkon par rjes su bsam pa byed cing / dge bsnyen ma yid bzhin gyi drung nas song ngo/ /

Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, bowed his head to the feet of the upāsikā Āśā and circumambulated the upāsikā Āśā, keeping her to his right, a hundred thousand times. Looking back again and again, bowing, his face covered with tears, thinking of the rarity of the highest enlightenment, thinking of the rarity of being able to honor a kalyāṇamitra, thinking of the rarity of meeting a superior being, thinking of the rarity[700] of attaining the faculties of a bodhisattva, thinking of the rarity of attaining the pure motivation of a bodhisattva, thinking of the rarity of meeting suitable companions,[701] thinking of the rarity of having in mind the true aspiration for enlightenment, thinking of the rarity of practicing the teaching of the unequaled Dharma, thinking of the rarity of the practice of an unwavering and stainless[702] mind, and thinking of the rarity of the light of the Dharma that creates the power of omniscience, he departed from the presence of the upāsikā Āśā.

Then Sudhana left Asha, after paying his respects, reflecting on the extreme rarity of enlightening beings, on how hard it is to get on good terms with spiritual benefactors, on how very difficult it is to get to meet people of truth, on how hard it is to attain the faculties of enlightening beings, how hard it is to attain the purity of intent of enlightening beings, how hard it is to find colleagues, how hard it is to focus the mind accurately on enlightenment, how hard it is to apply the teachings leading to the state of freedom from distress, how hard it is to find ways to develop invincible goodness of mind, and how hard it is to get to see ways to quickly develop omniscience.
[drang srong 'jigs mchog dbyangs]
Chapter 11. Bhīṣmottaranirghoṣa
Bhishmottaranirghosha

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang / byang chub sems dpa'i gdams ngag gi rjes su song ba'i sems dang ldan pa/ byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa yongs su dag par bya ba'i rjes su song ba'i sems dang ldan pa/ byang chub sems dpa'i bsod nams kyi stobs rnam par 'phel bar bya ba'i sems dang ldan pa/ sangs rgyas blta ba'i shugs drag po rab tu snang bar byas pa'i sems dang ldan pa; chos kyi gter 'thob par bya la shugs drag po skyes pa'i sems dang ldan pa/ smon lam chen po mngon par bsgrub pa'i shugs drag po rab tu 'phel ba'i sems dang ldan pa/ chos thams cad kyi phyogs la mngon du lta ba'i sems dang ldan pa; chos kyi rang bzhin gyi 'od kyis snang bar byas pa'i sems dang ldan pa/ sgrib pa thams cad rnam par 'thor ba'i sems dang ldan pa/ chos kyi dbyings la mun pa med par rnam par lta ba'i sems dang ldan pa/ rdo rje rin po che mthu bo ches mi choms pa ltar dri ma med pa'i sems dang ldan pa/ bdud thams cad kyi dpung gis brgal bar dka' zhing thub par dka' ba'i sems dang ldan pa de/ mthar gyis yul chu ba gtsang ma ga la ba der phyin nas/

Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, thinking of following the bodhisattva instructions, thinking of following the pure conduct of bodhisattvas, thinking of increasing the strength of the merit of bodhisattvas, thinking of the illumination of the power of seeing the buddhas, thinking of developing the power to attain the treasure of the Dharma, thinking of increasing the power of accomplishing the great prayers, thinking of facing every direction in the realm of the Dharma, thinking of the illumination of the nature of the Dharma, thinking of the dispersal of all obscurations, thinking of looking at the realm of Dharma free of darkness, thinking of the motivation[703] that is stainless and unbreakable like Nārāyaṇa’s[704] precious vajra, and thinking of invincibility and unassailability in the face of all the māra armies, eventually arrived in the land of Nālayu.

Then Sudhana, his mind on the instruction of the enlightening being, his mind on the purification of the conduct of enlightening beings, his mind developing the power of virtue of enlightening beings, his mind lit by the energy of the vision of Buddha, with mental energy arising from receiving a treasury of teaching, his mental energy increased by the undertaking of great vows, all things apparent to his mind, his mind aware of the intrinsic essence of things, his mind free from all obstructions, his mind viewing the reality realm without obscurity, his pure will indestructible, his mind invulnerable and immune to the power of all demons, gradually made his way to Nalayur and

drang srong 'jigs mchog dbyangs tshol tshol ba las/ de'i tshe drang song 'jigs mchog dbyangs/ dge ba sbyang ba'i gnas shing dang / shing phran sna tshogs grangs med pa'i nags tshal mdangs dga' ba/ lo mas rgyas pa'i shing gis kun nas 'grigs pa/ rtag tu me tog rgyas pa dang ldan pa'i shing sna tshogs can/ rtag tu shing tog mang po dang ldan pa'i shing tog gi shing dang ldan pa/ nor bu rin po che sna tshogs kyi shing drung / nor bu rin po che'i spang leb kyis rtag tu gshibs pa dang ldan pa/ tsan dan dam pa'i shing kun nas rnam par bres pa/ a ga ru yid du 'ong ba'i shing las spos kyi dri rtag tu 'byung bas rab tu brgyan pa/ phyogs bzhi nas shing pa ta la rnam par mdzes par skyes pas yongs su brgyan pa/ nya gro da'i shing dbyibs yid du 'ong ba dang ldan pa/ 'dzam bu'i shing las rtag tu shing thog smin pa 'brul ba/ me tog gi tshal pad+mo dang / ut+pa la gsar du skyes pas rab tu brgyan pa zhig na 'dug 'dug ste/

He searched and searched for the ṛṣi Bhīṣmottaranirghoṣa. At that time, the ṛṣi Bhīṣmottaranirghoṣa was dwelling in an ashram in a delightful forest of countless different kinds of trees and creepers. In that forest there was a canopy of the leaves of various trees, there were always flowers blossoming on trees of various kinds, and there were fruit trees always laden with fruit. Platforms of precious fruit had formed at the feet of trees that were made of the various kinds of precious materials. There were beautifully proportioned[705] tall sandalwood trees. The forest was made pleasant by the aroma that constantly came from beautiful agarwood trees. It was beautified by scents in all four directions. It was adorned by perfectly proportioned bignonia trees.[706] There were beautifully formed banyan trees. Ripened fruits were constantly falling from jambul trees. It was beautified by fresh red lotuses, blue lotuses, and night lotuses.[707]

sought out the seer Bhishmottaranirghosha. At that time Bhishmottaranirghosha was sojourning in a retreat, a pleasant place with countless diverse trees and plants, shaded by the leaves of various trees, with flowering trees perpetually blooming in various colors and fruit trees perpetually bearing, the ground made of the finest jewel-fruits from various jewel trees, well distributed with great sandalwood trees, graced with fragrance constantly coming from pleasant aloes wood trees, adorned with trumpet-flower trees distributed in the four directions, with beautifully formed fig trees, with perpetually ripe fruits raining from rose apple trees, beautified by fresh water lilies and lotus blossoms.
tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis/ drang srong 'jigs mchog dbyangs/ drang srong stong phrag bcus bskor cing;
Sudhana saw the ṛṣi Bhīṣmottaranirghoṣa and circumambulated the ṛṣi Bhīṣmottaranirghoṣa a hundred thousand times, keeping him to his right.
Sudhana saw the seer Bhishmottaranirghosha

tsan dan gyi yal gshin tu 'brel ba'i bya skyibs shig na/ thor tshugs kyi cod pan can/ pags pa dang / gos gyon pa/ shing shun gyi smad g.yogs can; stan la 'dug pa mthong ngo/ / mthong nas kyang drang srong 'jigs mchog dbyangs ga la ba der stong ste/

The ṛṣi Bhīṣmottaranirghoṣa was seated under a canopy of interlaced sandalwood branches. His hair was bound into a topknot of matted locks, he wore clothing made of skins and grass, with a skirt of bark, and he was seated on a cushion of grass. Sudhana approached the ṛṣi Bhīṣmottaranirghoṣa.

wearing matted hair, sitting on a seat of bark, rags, fragrant grass, and antelope skin on a layer of straw in a hut built at the foot of a sandalwood tree, surrounded by ten thousand seers. Seeing Bhishmottaranirghosha, Sudhana went up to him, and
phyin nas yang dag pa'i dge ba'i bshes gnyen dang phrad pa'i bsam pas/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen ni yang dag pa'i lam ston pas/ thams cad mkhyen pa nyid 'byung ba'i sgo yin par yang dag par lta/
When he had approached him, seeing that omniscience arises from the gateway of the kalyāṇamitra, the genuine kalyāṇamitra that one wishes to find, because the kalyāṇamitra teaches the true path;
thinking he had found a true spiritual benefactor, looking upon spiritual benefactors as the door to omniscience because they guide one on the true path,
thams cad mkhyen pa'i sa la gzhog pas/ thams cad mkhyen pa nyid ni dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi gdams ngag la rag lus par yang dag par lta/
seeing that omniscience is dependent on the instructions of the kalyāṇamitra because they lead one to the level of omniscience;
looking upon omniscience as coming from the teaching of spiritual benefactors because they lead to the stage of all-knowledge,
stobs bcu'i ye shes rin po che'i gling du skyel bas/ thams cad mkhyen pa nyid ni dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi mnyan pa la rag lus par yang dag par lta/
seeing that omniscience is dependent on the friendship of the kalyāṇamitra because they lead one to the island of the jewels of the wisdom of the ten strengths;
looking upon omniscience as coming from the guidance of spiritual benefactors because they lead to the jewel land of the knowledge of the ten powers,
stobs bcu'i ye shes snang ba yang dag par bskyed pas/ thams cad mkhyen pa nyid ni dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi sgron mas snang bar bya ba yin par yang dag par lta/
seeing that omniscience is the illumination from the lamp of the kalyāṇamitra because they create the light of the wisdom of the ten strengths;
looking upon omniscience as illumined by the torch of spiritual benefactors because they produce the light of knowledge of the ten powers,
nyam nyes med par thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi grong du phyin par byed pas/ thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi lam ni dge ba'i bshes gnyen yin par yang dag par lta/
seeing that the kalyāṇamitra is the road to omniscience because they lead one to the city of unimpaired omniscience,
looking upon spiritual benefactors as the path to omniscience leading unbroken to the city of omniscience,
mnyam pa dang mi mnyam pa yongs su ston pas/ thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi mar me ni dge ba'i bshes gnyen yin par yang dag par lta/
seeing that omniscience is the lamp of the kalyāṇamitra because they reveal that which is equal and unequal;
looking upon spiritual benefactors as lamps on the way to omniscience because they show the level and the uneven,
g.yang sa'i 'jigs pa thams cad med par byed pas; thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi stegs ni dge ba'i bshes gnyen yin par yang dag par lta/
seeing that the kalyāṇamitra is the bridge[708] of omniscience because they eliminate all the fear of falling into crevasses;
looking upon spiritual benefactors as a bridge to omniscience because the peril of falling is eliminated,
byams pa chen po'i stobs kyis sim pa yongs su skyed pa'i phyir/ thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi gdugs ni dge ba'i bshes gnyen yin par yang dag par lta/
seeing that the kalyāṇamitra is the parasol of omniscience because they cool through the power of great benevolence;
looking upon spiritual benefactors as parasols of omniscience because they produce coolness by the power of great love,
snying rje chen po yongs su bskyed pas/ thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi shugs drag po ni dge ba'i bshes gnyen yin par yang dag par lta zhing /
seeing that the kalyāṇamitra is the power of omniscience because they create great compassion;
looking upon spiritual benefactors as streams of omniscience because they give rise to great compassion,

chos kyi rang bzhin gyi tshul rab tu snang bar byed pas/ thams cad mkhyen pa nyid gsal bar mthong ba ni/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen la rag las par mthong nas/ lus thams cad kyis phab ste/ phyag byas nas langs te/ drang srong 'jigs mchog dbyangs la lan brgya stong du mar bskor ba byas nas mdun du 'dug ste/ thal mo sbyar nas/ yid du 'ong ba'i tshul gyis yid du 'ong ba'i tshig brjod de/ 'di skad ces smras so; ;

and seeing that reliance on the kalyāṇamitra is the clear vision of omniscience because they illuminate the way of the nature of phenomena, Sudhana threw his body onto the ground before him, prostrating to him. He then rose, circumambulated the ṛṣi Bhīṣmottaranirghoṣa many hundreds of thousands of times, keeping him to his right, and then sat down before him. With his hands together in homage in a pleasing way with pleasing words, he said,

looking upon the satisfaction of the vision of omniscience as coming from spiritual benefactors because they illumine the principle of the inherent nature of phenomena, Sudhana paid his respects to the seer and said,

'phags pa/ bdag gis bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed na/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bgyi ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bgyi ba ma 'tshal te/
“Ārya, I have developed the aspiration for the highest, complete enlightenment. How does a bodhisattva train in bodhisattva conduct? How does a bodhisattva practice it?
“Noble one, I have set my mind on supreme perfect enlightenment, but I do not know how an enlightening being is to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings.

'phags pa ni/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams la gdams ngag dang / rjes su bstan pa mdzad do/ / zhes thos na/ 'phags pa/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bgyi ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bgyi ba bdag la bshad du gsol/ /
“Ārya, I have heard that you teach and give instructions to bodhisattvas. Therefore, Ārya, teach me how bodhisattvas train in bodhisattva conduct and in what way they practice it!”
I have heard you give enlightening beings instruction; please tell me how an enlightening being is to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings.”
de nas drang srong 'jigs mchog dbyangs kyis/ bram ze'i byis pa stong phrag bcu po de dag la bltas te/ 'di skad ces smras so/ /
The ṛṣi Bhīṣmottaranirghoṣa looked at the ten thousand brahmin[709] youths who were there and said,
The seer Bhishmottaranirghosha looked at the ten thousand people surrounding him and said,

byis pa dag /rigs kyi bu'dis bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed de/ sems can thams cad 'jigs pa med pa la mgron du gnyer to/ / rigs kyi bu/ 'di ni sems can thams cad la phan pa dang / bde ba'i don du sta gon du gnas pa ste/ ye shes rgya mtsho mngon du gyur pa'o/ / de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad chos kyi sprin gyi char btung bar 'dod pa'o/ / chos kyi tshul rgya mtsho thams cad la 'jug par 'dod pa'o/ / ye shes kyi snang ba chen po la gnas par 'dod pa'o/ / snying rje chen po'i sprin bsdu bar 'dod pa'o/ / chos kyi char chen po mngon par dbab par 'dod pa'o/ / ye shes chen po'i zla ba 'jig rten du shar bar byas te/ nyon mongs pa'i gdung ba thams cad rab tu gzhil bar 'dod pa'o/ / sems can thams cad kyi dge ba'i rtsa ba rnam par spel bar 'dod pa'o/ /

“Young men, this noble one has developed the aspiration for the highest, complete enlightenment. He has invited all beings to become free of fear. This noble one is prepared to bring happiness and benefit to all beings. He is facing an ocean of wisdom. He longs to drink the rain of the clouds of Dharma of all the tathāgatas. He longs to enter the ocean of all the ways of the Dharma. He longs to be in the great light of wisdom. He longs for the great rain of the Dharma to fall. He longs for the moon of great wisdom to rise over the world and extinguish all the torment of the kleśas. He longs to increase the roots of merit of all beings.”

“This youth has set his mind on supreme perfect enlightenment and has invited all sentient beings to fearlessness. He is aiming for the welfare and happiness of all beings; he is facing the ocean of knowledge; he wants to spread the clouds of teaching of all buddhas; he wants to plunge into the ocean of all principles of the Teaching; he wants to live by the light of knowledge; he wants to bring the cloud of great compassion near; he wants to cause the rain of the great Teaching to shower; he wants to have the moon of great knowledge rise in the world and extinguish the burning of all afflictions; he wants to develop the roots of goodness of all sentient beings.”

de nas bram ze'i byis pa stong phrag bcu po de dag gis/ me tog dri zhim la yid du 'ong zhing / kha dog sna tshogs dang ldan pa mang pos/ tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la gtor to/ / mngon par gtor to/ / rab tu gtor to/ / mngon par phyag 'tshal te/ rab tu btud de phyag 'tshal nas/ g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas te/ tshig 'di skad du brjod do/ / 'di ni sems can thams cad yongs su skyob par 'gyur ro/ / sems can dmyal ba'i sdug bsngal thams cad rab tu zhi bar bgyid par 'gyur ro/ / byol song gi skye gnas kyi lam gyi rgyud thams cad rnam par gcod par 'gyur ro/ / gshin rje'i 'jig rten gyi lam gyi rgyud thams cad rnam par bzlog par 'gyur ro/ / mi khom pa'i sgo thams cad gcod par 'gyur ro/ / sred pa'i rgya mtsho yongs su skem par 'gyur ro/ / sred pa'i 'ching ba gcod par 'gyur ro/ / sdug bsngal gyi phung po rnam par bzlog par 'gyur ro/ / ma rig pa'i mun pa sel bar 'gyur ro/ / bsod nams kyi khor yug gis 'jig rten yongs su bskor bar 'gyur ro/ / ye shes rin po che'i 'byung gnas yongs su ston par 'gyur ro/ / ye shes kyi nyi ma 'char bar bgyid par 'gyur ro/ / chos kyi mig rnam par sbyong bar 'gyur ro/ / 'jig rten rnams la mnyam pa dang / mi mnyam pa yang dag par ston par 'gyur ro/ /

Then the ten thousand brahmin youths scattered beautiful flowers with lovely aromas and in various colors over Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, strewed them over him, covered him with them, paid homage to him, bowed down to him, circumambulated him, keeping him to their right, and then said these words to him: “This one will become a protector of all beings; he will end all the sufferings in the hells, he will block all the pathways to rebirth as animals, he will turn beings away from the path that leads to the world of Yama, he will close the doors to the unfortunate existences, he will dry up the ocean of existences, he will cut through the bondage of existences, he will repel the mass of suffering, he will dispel the darkness of ignorance, he will establish a Cakravāla mountain range of merit around the world, he will reveal the source of the jewels of wisdom, he will cause the sun of wisdom to rise, he will purify the eyes of Dharma, and he will reveal that which is equal and unequal in all the worlds.”

Then those ten thousand people scattered beautiful fragrant flowers over Sudhana, bowed to him, and circled him in respect, and said, “This person will be a savior; he will extinguish all the hellish torments of all beings, he will stop all brutish ways, he will get rid of the ways of the underworld, he will shut the door of all conditions inopportune for enlightenment, he will evaporate the ocean of craving, he will sever the bonds of craving, he will remove the mass of suffering, he will dispel the darkness of ignorance, he will surround the world with mountains of virtue, he will reveal the mine of jewels of knowledge, he will cause the sun of knowledge to rise, he will clarify the eye of truth, he will show what is good and bad in the world.”

de nas drang srong 'jigs mchog dbyangs kyis/ byis pa de dag la 'di skad ces smras so/ / byis pa dag /gang gis bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed pa de ni /byang chub sems dpa'i spyad pa spyod pa'i tshe/ sems can thams cad kyi bde ba rab tu bskyed de/ rim gyis thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyang 'thob par 'gyur ro/ / byis pa dag /rigs kyi bu'dis ni/ bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed pa ste/ de bas na 'di ni/ sangs rgyas kyi yon tan thams cad kyis yongs su sbyong bar 'gyur ro/ /

Then the ṛṣi Bhīṣmottaranirghoṣa said to those youths, “Young men, when someone has developed the aspiration for the highest, complete enlightenment and practices bodhisattva conduct, they create happiness for all beings and will eventually attain omniscience. Young men, this noble one has developed the aspiration for the highest, complete enlightenment, and therefore he will bring to completeness all the qualities of buddhahood.

Then the seer Bhishmottaranirghosha said to those people, “Whoever aspires to supreme perfect enlightenment promotes the happiness of all sentient beings, carrying out the practice of enlightening beings, and will eventually attain omniscience. This youth has set his heart on supreme perfect enlightenment; he will fulfill the stage of complete buddhahood.”

de nas drang srong 'jigs mchog dbyangs kyis/ tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la 'di skad ces smras so/ / rigs kyi bu/ kho bo ni byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa gzhan gyis mi thub pa'i rgyal mtshan thob pa'o/ /
Then the ṛṣi Bhīṣmottaranirghoṣa said to Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, “Noble one, I have attained the bodhisattva liberation called the banner of being invincible to others.”
Then the seer said to Sudhana, “I have attained an enlightening liberation called ‘unsurpassed banner.’”
nor bzang gis smras pa/ byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa gzhan gyis mi thub pa 'di'i yul ji lta bu zhig mchis/
Sudhana asked, “What is the scope of this bodhisattva liberation called the banner of being invincible to others?”
Sudhana said, “What is the scope of this liberation?”
de nas drang srong 'jigs mchog dbyangs kyis lag pa g.yas pa brkyang ste/ tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gi mgo la byugs nas/ lag pa g.yas pas bzung ngo/ /
The ṛṣi Bhīṣmottaranirghoṣa extended his right hand and with it stroked and held the head of Sudhana, the head merchant’s son.
Bhishmottaranirghosha stretched forth his right hand and rubbed Sudhana’s head, then took Sudhana by the right hand.

tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la drang srong 'jigs mchog dbyangs kyis lag pa g.yas pas bzung ma thag tu de'i mod la/ tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis phyogs bcur sangs rgyas kyi zhing brgya stong phrag bcu'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi sangs rgyas kyi zhing mthong bar gyur te/

As soon as the ṛṣi Bhīṣmottaranirghoṣa held the head of Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, with his right hand, Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, saw in the ten directions buddha realms as numerous as the atoms in a million buddha realms;
At that moment Sudhana saw in the ten directions as many buddha-lands as atoms in ten hundred thousand buddha-lands,
de dag gi de bzhin gshegs pa sangs rgyas kyi zhing brgya stong phrag bcu'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi zhabs kyi drung na/ bdag nyid 'dug pa shes par gyur to; ;
he perceived himself to be sitting at the feet of buddhas as numerous as the atoms in a million buddha realms;
and in them he perceived himself at the feet of as many buddhas as atoms in ten hundred thousand buddha-lands.
sangs rgyas kyi zhing de dag kyang / rnam pa grangs med par rnam par dag pa'i rgyan dang ldan par mthong ngo/ /
he saw the countless pure displays of forms within those buddha realms;
He also saw the innumerable features in the pure adornments of those buddha-lands,
de dag na'ang de bzhin gshegs pa'i 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor rgya mtsho kha dog sna tshogs can/ rgyan rnam pa tha dad pa dang ldan pa dag 'khod par mthong ngo/ /
he saw the ocean of the multicolored display of the circles of followers of those tathāgatas;
and he saw the various arrays of the oceans of audiences surrounding the buddhas therein.
'khor gyi dkyil 'khor rgya mtsho de dag na'ang de bzhin gshegs pa'i sku mtshan dang dpe byad bzang po 'bar bas brgyan pa dag bzhugs pa mthong ngo/ /
he saw in the midst of those oceans of the circles of followers the bodies of the tathāgatas, which were adorned with the shining signs and features of a great being;
He also saw the radiant mass of the marks and embellishments of the buddhas’ bodies in the midst of the congregations.
de dag las kyang tshig dang yi ge gcig las kyang / phyir phyogs pa med par chos bstan pa nyan to/ /
he listened to their Dharma teachings without missing a single word or term;
He also heard teaching from the buddhas without missing a single word,
de bzhin gshegs pa'i chos kyi 'khor lo de dag kyang phan tshun ma 'dres par yang dag par 'dzin to/ /
he obtained those Dharma wheels of the tathāgatas, each distinct from the other;
and he remembered the cycles of teachings of those buddhas in order without confusion,
chos kyi sprin gyi char sems can gyi bsam pa sna tshogs la rab ba pa de dag kyang yang dag par 'dzin to/ /
he received the rain of Dharma that fell according to the various aspirations of beings;
and he received the rain of those clouds of teaching as they showered on beings of various mentalities.
de bzhin gshegs pa de dag gi sngon gyi smon lam/ mos pa sna tshogs kyi stobs kyis rnam par sbyangs pa rgya mtsho la yang zhugs so; ;
and he comprehended an ocean of the past prayers of those tathāgatas, which were purified by the power of various aspirations;
He also entered the oceans of past vows of those buddhas, purified by zealous application of various kinds.
sangs rgyas kyi yang dag par bsdu ba smon lam sna tshogs rgya mtshos rnam par dag pa rgya mtsho de dag la'ang zhugs so/ /
he also comprehended those pure oceans of various prayers, which were oceans that had been accumulated by the buddhas;
He also entered oceans of past attainments of the buddhas, purified by oceans of various vows.
sangs rgyas kyi sku mdog sems can gyi bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du tshim par 'gyur bar rnam par dmigs pa de dag kyang mthong ngo/ /
he also saw the perception of the colors of the bodies of the buddhas that satisfied beings in accordance with their wishes;
He also saw the forms of buddhas manifested so as to please all sentient beings according to their mentalities.
sangs rgyas kyi 'od zer gyi dra ba 'dod chags dang bral ba sna tshogs kyis rnam par dag pa'i rgyan gyi dkyil 'khor de dag kyang mthong ngo/ /
he also saw the network of light rays from the buddhas as various passionless, pure displays of halos;
He also saw the nets of light rays of the buddhas, their various cool, pure halos.
sangs rgyas kyi stobs de dag la'ang ye shes snang ba bsgribs pa med pa dang ldan pas zhugs so/ /
and he also perceived the strengths of those buddhas that possessed the unobscured radiance of wisdom.
He also entered into those buddhas’ powers by following the light of unobstructed knowledge.
de ltar byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa gzhan gyis mi thub pa'i rgyal mtshan gyi ye shes kyi 'od kyis snang bar gyur pa/
In that way, he was illuminated by the light of wisdom from the bodhisattva liberation called the banner of being invincible to others;
Thus did he perceive himself with the buddhas, illumined by the light of knowledge of the liberation “unsurpassed banner,”
ting nge 'dzin gyi rnam par snang mdzad kyi snying po snang ba rab tu thob pa/
he attained the illumination of the samādhi called the essence of the sun;
imbued with the light of the concentration filled with sunlike radiance,
ting nge 'dzin ye shes mi zad pa'i rnam par thar pa dang ldan pa/
he possessed the samādhi called the liberation of unceasing wisdom;
reaching absorption in liberation of endless knowledge,
gzungs kyi sgo snang ba/ phyogs kun gyi dra ba rab tu thob pa/
he obtained the sight of the gateway of retention called the network in all directions;
imbued with the light of the mystic formulation of the structure of the universe,
gzungs kyi sgo rdo rje'i snying pos sems rab tu gsal bar byas pa/
his mind illumined by the mystic formulation of the indestructible sphere,
ting nge 'dzin gyi ye shes brtsegs pa rnam par phye ba'i yul la rnam par phye ba rab tu thob pa/
he attained the samādhi called the range of the summit of well-ordered knowledge;[710]
abiding in absorption in the realm of well-ordered bodies of knowledge,
shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa la rnam par spyod pa/ gzhi kun nas rnam par brgyan pa'i snying po yul du gyur pa/
he had the range of dwelling in the perfection of wisdom, which is the path[711] with the complete array of foundations;
intent on the state of transcendent wisdom of the path of adornment of all planes,
ting nge 'dzin gyi snang ba sangs rgyas nam mkha'i snying po'i dkyil 'khor la rab tu zhugs pa/
he gained the light of the samādhi called the buddhas’ domain of the essence of space;
illumined by the light of concentration on the sphere containing the space of the enlightened,
ting nge 'dzin sangs rgyas thams cad kyi chos kyi 'khor lo'i mu khyud kyis sems rab tu snang bar byas pa/
his mind was illuminated by the samādhi called the rim of the Dharma wheel of all the buddhas;
his mind illuminated by concentration on the circumference of the wheel of teaching of all buddhas,
ting nge 'dzin gyi snang ba dus gsum gyi ye shes rin po che mi zad pa'i dkyil 'khor la rab tu brtson pa des/
and he attained the light of the samādhi called the domain of the unceasing precious knowledge of the three times.[712]
imbued with the light of absorption in the inexhaustible sphere of jewels of knowledge of past, present, and future.

de bzhin gshegs pa la la'i zhabs kyi drung du ni nyin zhag gcig lon par shes so/ / la lar ni nyin zhag bdun lon pa snyam/ la lar ni zla ba phyed lon pa snyam/ la lar ni zla ba gcig lon pa snyam/ la lar ni lo gcig lon pa snyam/ la lar ni lo brgya lon pa snyam/ la lar ni lo stong lon pa snyam/ la lar ni lo brgya phrag stong lon pa snyam/ la lar ni lo bye ba lon pa snyam/ la lar ni lo bye ba brgya lon pa snyam/ la lar ni lo byed ba stong lon pa snyam/ la lar ni lo bye ba brgya phrag stong lon pa snyam/ la lar ni lo bye ba khrag khrig lon pa snyam/ la lar ni bskal pa phyed lon pa snyam/ la lar ni bskal pa gcig lon pa snyam/ la lar ni bskal pa brgya lon pa snyam; la lar ni bskal pa stong lon pa snyam/ la lar ni bskal pa brgya phrag stong lon pa snyam/ la lar ni bskal pa bye ba lon pa snyam/ la lar ni bskal pa bye ba phrag brgya lon pa snyam/ la lar ni bskal pa bye ba phrag stong lon pa snyam/ la lar ni bskal pa bye ba brgya phrag stong lon pa snyam/ la lar ni bskal pa bye ba phrag khrig brgya phrag stong lon pa snyam byed pa nas/ de bzhin gshegs pa la la'i zhabs kyi drung du ni/ bskal pa brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa snyed lon par gyur pa snyam byed pa nas/ de bzhin gshegs pa la la'i zhabs kyi drung du ni/ bskal pa 'dzam bu'i gling gi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed lon pa snyam byed pa nas/ bskal pa sangs rgyas kyi zhing brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed lon pa snyam byed par gyur to/ /

He perceived sitting at the feet of some tathāgatas for one day and night, at the feet of some for seven days, at the feet of some for half a month, at the feet of some for one month, at the feet of some for one year, at the feet of some for a hundred years, at the feet of some for a thousand years, at the feet of some for a hundred thousand years,[713] at the feet of some for ten million years, at the feet of some for a billion years, at the feet of some for ten billion years, at the feet of some for a trillion years, at the feet of some for a quintillion years, at the feet of some for half a kalpa, at the feet of some for one kalpa, at the feet of some for a hundred kalpas, at the feet of some for a thousand kalpas, at the feet of some for a hundred thousand kalpas, at the feet of some for ten million kalpas, at the feet of some for a billion kalpas, at the feet of some for ten billion kalpas, at the feet of some for a trillion kalpas, at the feet of some for a quintillion kalpas, at the feet of some for an anabhilāpyānabhilāpyaparivarta of kalpas, at the feet of some tathāgatas for as many kalpas as there are atoms in Jambudvīpa, and so on up to at the feet of some tathāgatas for as many kalpas as there are atoms in an anabhilāpyānabhilāpyaparivarta of buddha realms.

He seemed to be with one buddha for a day and a night, with another for seven days and nights, another for a fortnight, another for a month, another for a year, another for a century, another for a millennium, another for a hundred millennia, another for a million years, another for a hundred million years, another for a billion years, another for a hundred billion years, another for a trillion years, another for half an eon, another for an eon, another for a hundred eons, another for a thousand eons, another for a hundred thousand eons, another for a million eons, another for a hundred million eons, another for a billion eons, another for a hundred billion eons, another for a trillion eons, up to untold, inexpressible numbers of eons, or as many eons as atoms in the continent, or as many eons as atoms in untold buddha-lands.
de nas drang srong 'jigs mchog dbyangs kyis/ tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang btang ba dang / des yang bdag drang srong 'jigs mchog dbyangs kyi mdun na 'dug par shes par gyur to/ /
Then the ṛṣi Bhīṣmottaranirghoṣa released Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, and Sudhana perceived again that he was sitting at the feet of the ṛṣi Bhīṣmottaranirghoṣa.
Then the seer let go of Sudhana, who found himself once again standing before the seer Bhishmottaranirghosha.
de la drang srong 'jigs mchog dbyangs kyis smras pa/ rigs kyi bu/ dran mod/ smras pa/ 'phags pa/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi byin gyi rlabs kyis dran no/ /
The ṛṣi Bhīṣmottaranirghoṣa asked him, “Noble one, do you remember?” Sudhana replied, “Ārya, I remember the blessing of the kalyāṇamitra.”
The seer said, “Do you remember?” Sudhana said, “I remember, noble one, by the empowerment of the spiritual benefactor.”

smras pa/ rigs kyi bu kho bos ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa gzhan gyis mi thub pa'i rgyal mtshan 'di shes par zad na/ byang chub sems dpa' 'gro ba thams cad las khyad par du 'phags pa'i ye shes mngon par shes pa dang ldan pa'i ting nge 'dzin thob pa/ dus thams cad du 'khor lo bskor ba/ sangs rgyas kyi mtshan dang ye shes mngon par sgrub pa la mkhas pa/ de bzhin gshegs pa byung ba'i nyi ma la rnam par dmigs pa'i rgyan rab tu 'god pa/ dus gsum gyi yul skad cig gcig gis ye shes su yang dag par sdud pa/ 'jig rten gyi khams thams cad du lus shin tu rnam par bkram pa/ chos kyi dbyings thams cad la/ ye shes snang ba'i rang bzhin dang ldan pa sems can thams cad kyi bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du mngon sum du mngon par langs pa/ sems can gyi bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du spyod pas rnam par dpyod pa dang mthun pa'i tshul dang ldan pa 'dod pa bzhin du kun tu snang zhing dri ma med la/ 'od dang ldan pa'i ye shes kyi dkyil 'khor rnam par dag pa de dag gi spyod pa shes pa'am/ yon tan brjod pa'am/ smon lam gyi khyad par smos pa'am/ zhing gi mngon par 'du bya ba shes pa'am/ ye shes kyi yul la 'jug par bya ba'am/ ting nge 'dzin gyi spyod yul gyi rjes 'brang bar bya ba'am/ rdzu 'phrul dang rnam par 'phrul pa la 'jug par bya ba'am/ rnam par thar pa'i khyu mchog gi mthu phyung ba dang / rnam par rtse ba'i rjes su 'brang bar bya ba'am/ lus rnam par phye ba'i mtshan ma gzung bar bya ba'am/ dbyangs kyi dkyil 'khor rnam par dag pa brjod pa'am/ ye shes kyi snang ba rab tu bstan par nus re skan/

The ṛṣi Bhīṣmottaranirghoṣa said, “Noble one, I know only this bodhisattva liberation called the banner of being invincible to others. How could I know or describe the qualities, indicate the different prayers, know the formation of realms, comprehend the scope of the wisdom, follow the range of the samādhis, comprehend the miracles and emanations that follow the arising of the might and display of the powerful liberations, grasp the characteristics of the different bodies, describe the pure domain of the voices, or teach the radiance of the wisdom of the bodhisattvas who have attained the samādhis that have the clairvoyant knowledge that is superior to all beings, who have power over the wheel of time,[714] who are skilled in the accomplishment of the knowledge of the signs of buddhahood,[715] who perceive the display of the rising of the sun of the tathāgatas, who have accumulated the knowledge of the single characteristic of the range of the three times,[716] who have bodies that are distributed through all world realms, who have bodies[717] of wisdom that illuminate the entire realm of phenomena, who appear in accordance with the wishes of all beings, who practice an appropriate conduct in a way that is in accordance with the aspirations of beings, who shine in a way that delights, and who have the pure domain of stainless radiant wisdom?

Bhishmottaranirghosha said, “I know this enlightening liberation known as the unsurpassed invincible banner, but how can I know the practice, or tell the virtues, or accurately express the excellence of vows, or know the structure of the lands, or plunge into the sphere of knowledge, or enter into the realm of concentration, or attain the mystic powers, or attain to the freedom of liberation, or take up the various physical manifestations, or reveal the purity of voice, or show the light of knowledge of the enlightening beings who have attained absorption in the mystic knowledge supreme among all creatures, who are masters of all wheels of time, who are skilled in achievement of the knowledge of the characteristics of buddhas, who are supernal manifestations of the incarnation of the buddhas, who have comprehended the knowledge of all objects of past, present, and future as of one characteristic, whose bodies are distributed throughout all worlds, who are embodiments of knowledge in which all realms of reality are revealed, who appear to all sentient beings according to their inclinations, who benefit sentient beings according to their ways of thought and action, who glow with a brightness that illumines everywhere, who have purified the sphere of pure, vast, radiant knowledge?

song / rigs kyi bu/ lho phyogs kyi rgyud 'di nyid na yul yongs su tshol ba zhes bya ba yod de/ de na bram ze rgyal ba'i drod kyi skye mched ces bya ba 'dug gi /de'i gan du song la/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bya ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bya ba dris shing / /

“Depart, noble one. In this southern region, in the land called Īṣāṇa, there dwells a brahmin by the name of Jayoṣmāyatana. Go to him and ask him, ‘How should a bodhisattva train in bodhisattva conduct? How should a bodhisattva practice it?’ ”
“Go south to a land called Ishana, where there lives a priest named Jayoshmayatana. Go ask him how an enlightening being is to learn and apply the practice of enlightening beings.”

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang dga' rangs te/ mgu zhing nyams bde la tshim zhing yid bde ba skyes nas/ drang srong 'jigs mchog dbyangs kyi rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te/ drang srong 'jigs mchog dbyangs la/ lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas/ yang dang yang bltas te/ drang srong 'jigs mchog dbyangs kyi drung nas song ngo// //

Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, was overjoyed, pleased, happy, and content. He bowed his head to the feet of the ṛṣi Bhīṣmottaranirghoṣa, circumambulated the ṛṣi Bhīṣmottaranirghoṣa, keeping him to his right, many hundreds of thousands of times, and, looking back again and again, departed from the ṛṣi Bhīṣmottaranirghoṣa.
Then Sudhana, pleased, uplifted, transported, overjoyed, happy, paid respects to the seer Bhishmottaranirghosha and departed, looking back at him again and again.
bam po dgu bcu rtsa gsum pa/

f.d: [bram ze rgyal ba'i drod kyi skye mched]
Chapter 12. Jayoṣmāyatana
Jayoshmayatana
de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang / byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa gzhan gyis mi thub pa'i rgyal mtshan gyi ye shes kyis snang bar byas pa/
Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, was illuminated by the wisdom of the bodhisattva liberation called the banner of being invincible to others.
Then, illumined by the light of knowledge of the enlightening liberation “unsurpassed banner,”
sangs rgyas kyi yul gyi rnam par 'phrul pa bsam gyis mi khyab pa la mngon sum du rnam par spyod pa/
He dwelled in the direct experience of the inconceivable range of the miraculous manifestations of the buddhas.
directly witnessing the inconceivable miracles of the realm of buddhas,
byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa bsam gyis mi khyab pa'i mngon sum gyi ye shes kyis mngon par shes pa/
He perceived the direct knowledge of inconceivable bodhisattva liberations.
endowed with mystic knowledge directly aware of the inconceivable liberation of enlightening beings,
byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin bsam gyis mi khyab pa'i ye shes kyis sems snang bar gyur pa/
His mind was illuminated by the wisdom of inconceivable bodhisattva samādhis.
his mind illumined by the inconceivable knowledge of concentration of enlightening beings,
dus thams cad du yang dag par 'jug pa'i ting nge 'dzin ye shes snang ba rab tu thob pa/
He had attained the radiance of the wisdom of samādhi that is present at all times.
imbued with the light of knowledge of concentration comprehending all times at once,
'du shes kyi rnam pa thams cad la yang dag par 'jug pa'i ting nge 'dzin gyi yul gyis snang bar gyur pa/
He was illuminated by the range of samādhi, in which all perceptions are present and included.
illumined by the realm of concentration comprehending that all is in perception,
'gro ba thams cad las khyad par du 'phags pa dang ldan pa'i ye shes snang ba thob pa
He had obtained the light of the wisdom that transcends all worlds.
having attained the light of the highest knowledge in all worlds,
thams cad kyi rjes su song ba'i spyod yul la rnam par spyod pa mngon du gyur pa/
He had the direct perception of dwelling in the entire range of the three times.[718]
approaching the state whose scope reaches everywhere in past, present, and future,
gnyis su rnam par rtog pa med pas mnyam pa nyid du bstan pa'i ye shes lhur len pa/
He was devoted to the wisdom that teaches equality without dualistic conceptions.
intent on the knowledge showing nondual equality in differentiation,
dmigs pa thams cad la rab tu 'dal ba'i ye shes snang ba dang ldan pa/
He had the light of wisdom that pervaded[719] throughout all objects of perception.
with the light of knowledge extending to all objects,
mnyam pa thams cad la mngon du gyur pa'i bzod pa rnam par dag pa la mos pa'i mdzod la mkhas pa/
He had mastered the treasury of aspiration for pure patience toward all that is heard.[720]
with skillfulness rich in zeal for the purification of tolerance in the face of people’s beliefs,
rang bzhin gyi chos la bzod pa khong du chud pa'i ye shes mngon par shes pa dang ldan pa/
He had attained the definitive wisdom[721] of patience for natural phenomena.
having attained the light of certain knowledge of acceptance of things in terms of their inherent nature,
byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa'i rang bzhin bsgom pa dang mi 'bral ba'i sems dang ldan pa/
His mind was never apart from meditation on the nature of the bodhisattva conduct[722] of higher cognition.
his mind constantly involved in enlightening beings’ practice of mystic knowledge reaching everywhere, which is meditation on inherent nature,
thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi shugs drag po las phyir mi ldog pa'i sems dang ldan pa/
His mind was irreversibly progressing toward the power of omniscience.
his mind progressing rapidly and irreversibly toward omniscience,
stobs bcu'i ye shes snang ba'i 'od rab tu thob pa/
He had attained the illumination of the knowledge[723] of the ten strengths.
illumined by the lightning of knowledge of the ten powers,
chos kyi dbyings brjod pa la mngon par mos pas ngoms pa med pa'i sems dang ldan pa/
His mind was never content in its aspiration to hear the sound of the words of the realm of Dharma.
his mind tirelessly seeking the sound of the reality realm,
thams cad mkhyen pa nyid la rnam par spyod pa'i spyod yul la 'jug pa khong du chud pa'i sems dang ldan pa/
His mind had gained entry into the field of dwelling in omniscience.
determined to enter the realm of omniscience,
byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa'i rgyan mtha' yas pa mngon par bsgrub pa'i sems dang ldan pa/
His mind had attained the infinite display of bodhisattva conduct.
intent on accomplishing the infinite array of practices of enlightening beings
byang chub sems dpa'i smon lam gyi dkyil 'khor mtha' yas pa rnam par spyad pa'i sems dang ldan pa/
His mind was purified[724] by the infinite domain of great[725] bodhisattva prayers.
and purifying the infinite sphere of great vows of enlightening beings,
'jig rten gyi khams kyi dra ba mi zad pa khong du chud pa'i ye shes mtha' dang dbus med pa mngon du gyur pa'i sems dang ldan pa/
He had the mind with direct perception of the limitless knowledge without limit or center of the unceasing network[726] of world realms.
his mind directed toward endlessly ongoing knowledge of the infinite network of all worlds,
sems can rgya mtsho mtha' yas pa yongs su smin par bya ba dang gdul bar bya ba la zhum pa med pa'i sems dang ldan pa des/
He had the mind that never wearies in ripening and guiding the infinite ocean of beings.
his mind not shrinking from guiding infinite beings to complete development,
byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa'i yul mtha' yas pa la yang dag par blta ba dang /
He saw the infinite range of bodhisattva conduct.
beholding the infinite sphere of practice of enlightening beings,
'jig rten gyi khams kyi rgyud rnam pa tha dad pa mtha' yas pa la yang dag par blta ba dang /
seeing the variety of conditions in infinite worlds,
'jig rten gyi khams rnam par phye ba sna tshogs mtha' yas pa la yang dag par blta ba dang /
He saw the infinite diversity of the different world realms.
seeing the variety of differentiations of infinite worlds,
'jig rten gyi khams mtha' yas pa dmigs pa phra ba dang / yangs pa'i khongs su chud par bya ba la yang dag par blta ba dang /
He saw the small and the vast objects of perception included within the infinite world realms.
seeing infinite worlds within microcosms and macrocosms,
'jig rten gyi khams kyi gzhi mtha' yas pa'i ming gi dra ba sna tshogs yang dag par blta ba dang /
He saw the various networks of names that are the bases for infinite world realms.
seeing the variety of the webs of perceptions and conceptions on which infinite worlds are based,
'jig rten gyi khams su rnam par spyad pa rnam par gdags pa mtha' yas pa'i kun rdzob rnam pa tha dad pa la yang dag par blta ba dang /
He saw the various infinite, differing relative designations and terms for infinite world realms.
seeing the variety of conventional terminology in infinite worlds,
sems can gyi mos pa sna tshogs mtha' yas pa la yang dag par blta ba dang /
He saw the infinite, differing aspirations of beings.
seeing the variety of interests of infinite beings,
sems can rnam par phye ba'i rnam pa tha dad pa mtha' yas pa la yang dag par blta ba dang /
He saw the infinite, differing categories of beings.
seeing the variety of differentiations of infinite beings,
sems can mtha' yas pa yongs su smin par bya ba dang / gdul ba khong du chud par bya ba la yang dag par blta ba dang /
He saw the infinite practices for guiding and ripening beings.
seeing the following of developmental teachings of infinite beings,
sems can dang / phyogs dang / dus mtha' yas pa'i ming gi rnam pa sna tshogs la yang dag par blta ba dang /
He saw the various infinite perceptions[727] of the directions and times of beings.
seeing the variety in perceptions of place and time of infinite beings,
dge ba'i bshes gnyen mngon du bya ba byed cing / mthar gyis yul tshol ba dang ldan pa gang na ba dang / bram ze rgyal ba'i drod kyi skye mched ga la ba der phyin to/ /
Focused on the kalyāṇamitra, Sudhana eventually arrived in the land called Īṣāṇa and went to where the brahmin Jayoṣmāyatana was.
Sudhana, his attention on spiritual benefactors, gradually made his way to the priest Jayoshmayatana in the land of Ishana.

de'i tshe bram ze rgyal ba'i drod kyi skye mched thams cad mkhyen pa nyid bsgrub pa'i gzhir byas shing dka' thub drag po la spyod de/ de'i phyogs bzhi nas me'i phung po ri rab tsam du che ba bus pa dang / ri shin tu mtho ba'i g.yang sa'i lam gyi rgyud spu gri'i sos gshibs pas 'khod par snang ngo/ /

At that time, the brahmin Jayoṣmāyatana was practicing the basis for accomplishing omniscience and practicing extreme asceticism. On all four sides of himself he had lit fires the size of mountains. Towering above was the precipice of a great mountain with a path of razors leading up it.[728]

At that time the priest was practicing an ascetic exercise of enduring fierce heat, with his mind on omniscience; on four sides were huge bonfires like mountains ablaze. Rising above appeared a great mountain precipice, a razor-edge path.

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis/ bram ze rgyal ba'i drod kyi mched kyi rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te; mdun du 'dug nas thal mo sbyar te/ 'di skad ces smras so/ / 'phags pa/ bdag gis bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed na/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la spyad pa dang / ji ltar nan tan du bgyi ba ma 'tshal te/ 'phags pa ni/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams la gdams ngag dang / rjes su bstan pa mdzad do zhes bdag gis thos na/ 'phags pa/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bgyi ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bgyi ba bdag la bshad du gsol/

Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, bowed his head to the feet of the brahmin Jayoṣmāyatana, sat down before him, and with his hands together in homage said, “Ārya, I have developed the aspiration for the highest, complete enlightenment. How does a bodhisattva train in bodhisattva conduct? In what way does a bodhisattva practice it? Ārya, I have heard that you teach and give instructions to bodhisattvas. Therefore, Ārya, teach me how bodhisattvas train in bodhisattva conduct and in what way they practice it!”

Sudhana went up, paid his respects to the priest, and said, “Noble one, I have set my mind on supreme perfect enlightenment, but I do not know how an enlightening being is to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings. I hear you give enlightening beings instruction; please tell me how to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings.”
des smras pa/ rigs kyi bu/ song la spu gri'i so dang ra ba'i ri 'di la 'dzegs te/ me'i 'obs 'dir mchongs shig dang / des khyod kyi byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa yongs su dag par 'gyur ro zhes nas/
The brahmin Jayoṣmāyatana said, “Noble one, go and climb up this mountain on the path of razors and then jump down into this fire. In that way, your bodhisattva conduct will become pure.”
The priest said, “Climb this razor-edge-path mountain and jump from there into the fire—thus will your enlightening practice be purified.”
tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang'di snyam du sems par gyur te/ mi khom pa brgyad las rnam par ldog pa yang shin tu dkon/ mir 'gyur te/
Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, thought, “It is rare to avoid the eight unfavorable existences. It is rare to become a human.[729]
At that point Sudhana thought, “It is hard to avoid the situations that are inopportune for enlightenment; it is hard to get to be human;
khom pa phun sum tshogs shing rnam par dag pa yang shin tu dkon/ sangs rgyas 'byung ba yang shin tu dkon/ dbang po nyams su med pa yang shin tu dkon/
It is rare to have pure good fortune. It is rare to have the appearance of a buddha. It is rare to have unimpaired senses.
it is hard to remove error and doubt about the right opportunity; it is hard to find a buddha in the world; it is hard to have all one’s faculties in order;
sangs rgyas kyi chos thos pa yang shin tu dkon/ skyes bu dam pa dang phrad pa yang shin tu dkon/ yang dag pa'i dge ba'i bshes gnyen yang shin tu dkon/
It is rare to hear the Buddhadharma. It is rare to meet a higher being. It is rare to have the friendship of a true kalyāṇamitra.
it is hard to get to hear the truth; it is hard to meet people of truth; it is hard to find genuine spiritual benefactors;

yang dag pa'i tshul rjes su bstan pas legs par sdud pa yang shin tu dkon/ yang dag par 'tsho bar bya ba yang shin tu dkon/ mi'i 'jig rten na chos dang gnyen ba'i chos la nan tan byed pa yang shin tu dkon na/ de skad zer zhing
It is rare to gain the teaching of the true way. It is rare to have a right livelihood. It is rare in the human world to practice the Dharma and the ancillary Dharmas.
it is hard to get genuine guidance and instruction; it is hard to live right in the human world; it is hard to carry out truth in all respects.

bdag gi dge ba'i bar chad la zhugs la/ de ltar bdag gi srog gcad par brtson pa 'di bdud dam zhig ma yin nam/ bdud kyis byin gyis brlabs pa'am/ bdud kyi ris su gtogs pa'am/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen ltar brdzus pa'am/ byang chub sems dpa' la mi gcags pa byed pa zhig ma yin grang / bdag gi thams cad mkhyen pa nyid la gegs byed par 'dod pa zhig ma yin grang / bdag lam gol ba ngan par gzhug par 'dod pa zhig ma yin grang / bdag gis sangs rgyas kyi chos khong du chud par bya ba'i chos kyi sgo la gegs byed pa zhig ma yin grang snyam nas/

“This person who will create an obstacle to my roots of merit, who urges me to kill myself, is he a māra? Is he blessed by a māra? Is he a follower of Māra? Is he pretending to be a kalyāṇamitra? Is he someone who destroys[730] bodhisattvas? Does he wish to prevent me from attaining omniscience? Does he wish to lead me down a wrong path? Is he creating an obstacle to the gateway of the Dharma through which one realizes the Buddhadharma?”

Might this not be a demon, or someone possessed by a demon, or a cohort of the devil, or an imitation spiritual teacher, or a false enlightening being, who has undertaken to impede my roots of goodness, who is out to destroy my life? Does he not want to prevent me from reaching omniscience? Does he not want to lead me on a wrong path? Does he not want to prevent me from attaining buddhahood?”
de de ltar sems shing yid la byed pa'i tshe/ tshangs pa stong phrag bcu steng gi bar snang la gnas te/ 'di skad ces 'dzer to/ /
When Sudhana had these thoughts, ten thousand Brahmās who were up in the sky said to him,
While he was involved in these thoughts, ten thousand Brahma gods appeared in the sky and said to him,

rigs kyi bu/ de lta bu'i sems mi brtan par ma byed cig /rigs kyi bu/ 'phags pa 'di ni/ ting nge 'dzin rdo rje 'od 'phro ba'i snang ba rab tu thob pa ste/ brtson 'grus ldog pa med pa'o/ / brtsams pa chen po mthar dbyung ba la zhugs pa'o/ /
“Noble one, do not be unrelenting in these thoughts! This ārya has attained the illumination of the samādhi vajra light rays. He has unwavering diligence. He has set out on the greatest undertaking.
“Do not get fixed on such thoughts. This sage has attained the light of the concentration of adamantine flame. He has unrelenting energy and has begun the great undertaking of salvation.
'gro ba thams cad kyi sred pa'i rlan bskam pa la mngon par brtson pa'o/ /
He is dedicated to drying up the moisture of craving in all beings.
He has set out to end the emotional attachments of all sentient beings.
lta ba'i rnam pa dang / dra ba thams cad gtub pa la brtson pa'o/ /
He is dedicated to cutting through the nets of wrong views.
He is striving to dissolve the webs of all views.
nyon mongs pa'i lcag lcig thams cad zad par bsreg pa la sta gon du gnas pa'o/ /
He is prepared to incinerate the forest[731] of kleśas.[732]
He is determined to burn up the deadwood of all afflictions and their actions.
mi khom mi shes pa'i bas mtha'i dgon pa thams cad snang bar bya ba la brtson pa'o/ /
He is dedicated to illuminating all the desolate areas of unfavorable knowledge.[733]
He is working to shed light in the wilderness of all kinds of knowledge that is not conducive to enlightenment.
sems can thams cad kyi rga shi'i g.yang sa dang / 'jigs pa rnam par bzlog pa la yi dam brtan pa'o/ /
He has the resolute commitment to turn all beings away from the terror of the chasm[734] of aging and death.
He is resolved upon eliminating all beings’ fears of old age and death.
dus gsum gyi mun pa bsal pa la mngon par brtson pa'o/ /
He is dedicated to dispelling the darkness in the three times.
He is intent on dispersing the darkness of past, present, and future.
chos thams cad kyi 'od zer dgye ba la zhugs pa'o/ /
He radiates the light rays of the entire Dharma.
He has undertaken to shine beams of light of all truths.

rigs kyi bu/ 'phags pa 'di dka' thub lngas yongs su gdung ba mdzad pa'i tshe/ tshangs pa ji snyed cig mkhan po dang / dbang sgyur ba dang / 'jig rten thams cad kyi gtso bor rang rang rlom zhing / sems pa blta ba'i rnam pa sna tshogs la mngon par zhen pa de dag thams cad/ 'phags pa 'di dka' thub dang / brtul zhugs kyi thugs dam gyi mthus/ rang rang gi gnas na bag dga' ba med cing / de dag bsam gtan gyi ro dga' ba myong ba med pas/ 'phags pa 'di'i drung du 'dong ngo/ / de dag phyin pa dang / 'phags pa 'di'i rdzu 'phrul gyi byin dang / drag shul kyi dka' thub dang / brtul zhugs kyi sa zil gyis mnan te/ lta ba'i rnam pa thams cad rnam par bzlog pa dang / nga rgyal dang; rlom sems thams cad rab tu spang ba'i phyir chos ston to/ / 'gro ba thams cad la byams pa chen po dang / snying rje chen pos khyab par bya ba dang / byang chub kyi bsam pa brtan par bya ba dang / byang chub tu sems bskyed pa shin tu yangs par bya ba dang / sangs rgyas thams cad yang dag par blta ba la mngon par brtson par bya ba dang / sangs rgyas kyi gsung gi dkyil 'khor thob par bya ba yongs su rdzogs par bya ba dang / thams cad du grag pa'i sangs rgyas kyi dbyangs la thogs pa med cing / bsgribs pa med par bya ba'i phyir chos ston to/ /

“Noble one, while this ārya was enduring the ascetic practice of the five heats,[735] through the power of his commitment to asceticism[736] and self-discipline, Brahmās who were accomplished and powerful, who arrogantly thought of themselves as preeminent in all worlds, and who were attached to a variety of incorrect views ceased to take pleasure in their state and no longer enjoyed the taste of their dhyāna, and they came into the presence of this ārya. When they had arrived, through the overpowering might[737] of this ārya’s miracles and his fierce discipline and asceticism, they were all turned away from their wrong views, and he taught them the Dharma so that they would abandon all their pride and arrogance. He taught them the Dharma so that they would have great love and great compassion that spread over all beings, so that they would have an unwavering wish for enlightenment, so that they would develop a vast aspiration for enlightenment, so that they would be dedicated to seeing all the buddhas, so that they would have the complete attainment of the domain of the speech of the buddhas, and so that there would be everywhere without obscuration or impediment the sound of the voices of the buddhas.”

As he mortifies himself with four fires under the blazing sun, even the Brahma gods, who think themselves creators and lords and supreme beings, and are engrossed in various views, do not take pleasure in their own states because of the light given off by this priest’s peerless practice of heat austerity. Not enjoying the pleasure of meditation, they come to the priest, and he overwhelms them by mystic power, and through fierce austerity teaches them to get rid of all their views and destroy all pride and arrogance. He also teaches them so that they may suffuse all worlds with great love and compassion, make their will for enlightenment firm, enlarge their determination for enlightenment, turn to the vision of all buddhas, fully receive the voice of the buddhas, and hear the voice of buddhas everywhere without resistance or obstruction.”

bdud stong phrag bcu yang steng gi bar snang la 'khod nas/ lha rdzas kyi nor bu rin po ches mngon par gtor te/ 'di skad ces 'dzer to/ / rigs kyi bu/ 'phags pa 'di dka' thub lngas yongs su gdung ba mdzad pa'i tshe/ 'od 'phro ba'i phung po 'di las snang ba chen po byung zhing / kho bo cag gi khyim dang / lus dang / rgyan gyi longs spyod thams cad zil gyis gnon to/ / de'i phyir kho bo cag kyang so so'i gnas gnas na bag dga' ba med pas 'khor dang bcas te/ 'phags pa 'di'i drung du 'dong ngo/ / kho bo cag 'di'i drung du phyin nas kyang / 'phags pa 'di ni kho bo cag la ci nas kyang / rang rang gi sems sor chud nas byang chub tu sems bskyed de/ bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub las phyir mi ldog par 'gyur ba/ de lta de ltar chos ston to/ /

Ten thousand māras were also in the sky above, scattering divine precious jewels. They said, “Noble one, while this ārya was enduring the ascetic practice of the five heats, from this mass of light rays came a great radiance that outshone all our residences, bodies, adornments, and possessions. Therefore, we too ceased to take pleasure in our residences, and with our entourages we came into the presence of this ārya. When we had come before him, this ārya taught us the Dharma so that our minds were healed, we developed the aspiration for enlightenment, and we became irreversible on the way to the highest, complete enlightenment.”

Ten thousand demons also stood in the sky, showered celestial jewels, and said, “The light emitted from the flames used by this priest in his heat mortification obscures our abodes, our ornaments, and our paraphernalia. Terrified, we and our cohorts go to the priest, who teaches in such a way that, coming to ourselves and getting back our right minds, we aspire to enlightenment and become irreversible on the way to supreme perfect enlightenment.”

dbang sgyur gyi lha'i rgyal po stong phrag bcus kyang / lha rdzas kyi me tog gis mngon par gtor te/ 'di skad ces 'dzer to/ / rigs kyi bu/ 'phags pa 'di dka' thub lngas yongs su gdung ba byed pa'i tshe/ kho bo cag kyang rang rang gi gnas na dga' ba med de/ de ltar bdag cag kyang rang rang gi skye bo'i 'khor dang bcas te/ 'di'i drung du 'dong ngo/ / bdag cag drung du phyin pa dang / 'di ni bdag cag la rang rang gi sems la dbang bsgyur ba thob par bya ba'i phyir chos ston to/ / nyon mongs pa thams cad la dbang bsgyur ba thob par bya ba dang / bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du skye ba la dbang bsgyur ba thob par bya ba dang / las kyi sgrib pa thams cad rnam par dag pa'i dbang rab tu thob par bya ba dang / snyoms par 'jug pa thams cad la dbang bsgyur ba thob par bya ba dang / yo byad la dbang ba'i rgyan yongs su dag par bya ba dang / bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du tshe la dbang bsgyur ba thob par bya ba'i phyir chos ston to/ /

Ten thousand Vaśavartin deva kings were also in the sky above, scattering divine flowers. They said, “Noble one, while this ārya was enduring the ascetic practice of the five heats, we also ceased to take delight in our residences, and therefore each of us, without entourages, came into the presence of this ārya. When we came into his presence, he taught us the Dharma so that we gained control over our own minds. He taught us the Dharma so that we would have power over all kleśas, so that we would have the power to be reborn wherever we wish, so that we would have the power to purify the obscuration of karma, so that we would have power over all meditative states, so that we would have power over requisites, and so that we would have the power to live as long as we wish.”

Also, ten thousand controlling gods, scattering celestial flowers, said, “While he is mortifying himself with four fires under the fiery sun, we find no pleasure in our own abodes. We and our cohorts go to him, and he teaches us so that we attain control of our own minds, control of afflictions, ability to be born in any state we wish, power to clear away obstructions caused by action, mastery of all concentrations, control of paraphernalia to purify our arrangements, and control conforming to our wishes.”

rab 'phrul dga'i lha'i rgyal po stong phrag bcu yang / steng gi bar snang la 'khod de/ lha rdzas kyi glu yang dag par sbyar ba'i nga ro snyan pa'i dbyangs bsgrags te/ mchod pa byas nas 'di skad ces 'dzer to/ / rigs kyi bu/ 'phags pa 'di dka' thub lngas yongs su gdung ba mdzad pa'i tshe/ me'i phung po 'di las de dang 'dra ba'i 'od byung zhing kho bo cag gi gzhal med khang 'di dag rnam par dag ste/ gsal ba dang / 'od shin tu dang bar 'gyur ro/ / rgyan 'di dag dang / lha'i bu mo 'di dag kyang / rnam par dag cing gsal la 'od shin tu dang bar 'gyur ro/ / de bas na bdag cag kyang lha'i bu dang / lha mo'i tshogs kyi 'khor dang bcas par/ 'dod pa la dga' bar tshor ba med de/ 'dod pa'i bde ba la mngon par dga' ba med pas/ lus dang sems sim par gyur nas/ 'phags pa 'di'i drung du 'dod pa yin te/ 'phags pa 'di ni/ bdag cag de ltar phyin pa rnams la sems rnam par dag par bya ba'i phyir chos ston to/ / sems kyi 'od dang bar bya ba dang / sems shin tu dag par bya ba dang / sems las su rung bar bya ba dang / sems kyi dga' ba yongs su bskyed pa dang / stobs bcu'i ye shes 'thob pa rnam par dag par bya ba dang / chos kyi shugs chen po rnam par 'phel bar bya ba dang / sangs rgyas kyi sku tshad med pa mngon par bsgrub pa'i phyir lus rnam par dag par bya ba dang / de bzhin gshegs pa'i gsung thob par bya ba'i phyir ngag rnam par dag par bya ba dang / thams cad mkhyen pa nyid rab tu thob par bya bar sems rnam par dag par bya ba'i phyir chos ston to/ /

Ten thousand Sunirmita deva kings were also in the sky above, singing out a melodious roar of divine songs. They said, “Noble one, while this ārya was enduring the ascetic practice of the five heats there came from those masses of flames a corresponding light that purified, illuminated, and brightened our aerial palaces. It also illuminated and brightened our adornments and our apsarases. Then we ceased to take delight in our entourage of young devas and apsarases. We ceased to delight in the bliss of desire, and our bodies and minds were left unsatisfied. We came into the presence of this ārya. When we came into his presence, he taught us the Dharma so that our minds would be purified. He taught us the Dharma so that our minds would be brightened, so that our minds would be very pure,[738] so that our minds would be tractable, so that our minds would be joyful, so that we would have the pure attainment of the knowledge of the ten strengths, so as to increase the great power of the Dharma, so as to purify our bodies, so as to attain an immeasurable buddha body, so as to purify our speech, and so as to attain the voice of a buddha.”

Ten thousand gods of pleasant emanations also stood in the sky, presented sweet sounds of celestial music and song, and said, “The fire of the priest is producing such light that our palaces are glowing, being purified and becoming more radiant, and so are the decorations and nymphs here. We and our cohorts of godlings and nymphs no longer find pleasure in desires, and we do not enjoy sensual pleasures. Our minds and bodies cooled, we go to the priest, who teaches us so that our minds will be purified, so that our minds will be radiant, so our minds will be good, so our minds will be malleable, so we will become joyful, so we may purify the realization of the knowledge of the ten powers, so we may grow in enthusiasm for the great Teaching, so we may purify our bodies and produce measureless buddha-bodies, so we may purify our voices and attain the voice of Buddha, so we may purify our minds and attain omniscience.”

rab dga' ldan gyi lha'i rgyal po stong phrag bcu'i lha'i bu dang / lha'i bu mo'i tshogs kyi 'khor dang bcas pa dag kyang / steng gi bar snang la 'khod nas/ spos sna tshogs kyi phye ma'i sprin gyi char mngon par phab pas mchod pa byas te/ phyag 'tshal nas 'di skad ces 'dzer to/ / rigs kyi bu/ 'phags pa 'di dka' thub lngas yongs su gdung ba mdzad pa'i tshe/ bdag cag kyang rang rang gi gnas na dga' ba med de/ de ltar dga' ba med pas 'di'i drung du 'dong ste/ bdag cag phyin pa rnams la/ 'phags pa 'di ni yul thams cad la ltos pa med par bya ba'i phyir chos ston to/ / chog shes pa'i sems su bya ba dang / dge ba'i rtsa ba yang dag par bskyod pa dang / byang chub tu sems bskyed pa rab tu thob par bya ba nas/ sangs rgyas kyi chos thams cad yongs su rdzogs par bya ba'i phyir chos ston to/ /

Ten thousand Saṃtuṣita deva kings were also in the sky with[739] an entourage of deva youths and apsarases, all of whom were paying homage and making an offering of sending down rain from clouds of various scented powders. They said, “Noble one, while this ārya was enduring the ascetic practice of the five heats, we ceased to take delight in our residences. As we had ceased to take delight in them, we came into the presence of this ārya. When we came into his presence, he taught us the Dharma so that we would not be dependent on any sensory object. He taught us the Dharma so that our minds would have contentment, so that we would create the roots of merit, so that we would attain the development of the aspiration for enlightenment, and so that we would be able to fulfill the entire Buddhadharma.”

Ten thousand gods of the heaven of satisfaction, along with their companies of celestial boys and girls, also stood in the sky, showered all kinds of fragrant powders, paying honor and respect, and said, “While he mortifies himself with fire there is no pleasure in our abodes. Being freed from attachment, we go to the priest and he teaches us so that we will be indifferent to all objects of sense, so that we will be perfectly and completely satisfied in mind, so that we will produce roots of goodness, so that we will aspire to enlightenment, and so that we will eventually fulfill all qualities of buddhas.”

rab mtshe ma'i lha'i rgyal po stong phrag bcu lha'i bu dang / lha'i bu mo'i tshogs kyi 'khor dang bcas pa dag gis kyang lha rdzas kyi me tog man da ra ba'i char mngon par phab ste/ 'di skad ces 'dzer to/ / rigs kyi bu/ 'phags pa 'di dka' thub lngas yongs su gdung ba mdzad pa'i tshe/ bdag cag kyang lha rdzas kyi glu snyan pa la dga' ba med de/ de ltar dga' ba med pas 'phags pa 'di'i drung du 'dong ste/ bdag cag phyin nas kyang / 'phags pa 'di ni 'dod pa'i dga' ba thams cad rnam par bzlog par bya ba nas/ sangs rgyas kyi chos thams cad rab tu thob par bya ba'i phyir chos ston to/ /

Ten thousand Suyāma deva kings were also in the sky with an entourage of deva youths and apsarases, all of whom were sending down a rain of divine coral tree flowers. They said, “Noble one, while this ārya was enduring the ascetic practice of the five heats, we ceased to take delight in listening to divine songs. As we had ceased to take delight in them, we came into the presence of this ārya. When we came into his presence, he taught us the Dharma so that we would turn away from all delight in desires and so that we would attain all of the Buddhadharma.”

Ten thousand gods of the heaven of timely portion, along with their celestial sons and daughters, showered a rain of flowers and said, “While this priest is mortifying himself with fire, we have no pleasure in our celestial song. Freed from attachment, we go to the priest and he teaches us so that we will become detached from all sensuality and eventually attain all qualities of buddhahood.”

lha'i dbang po brgya byin stong phrag bcu so so nas nye ba'i dbang po sum cu rtsa gnyis dang; lha'i bu dang / lha'i bu mo'i tshogs kyi 'khor dang bcas pas/ lha rdzas kyi gos dang / rin po che'i rgyan dang / me tog gi sprin gyi char mngon par phab ste/ 'di skad ces 'dzer to/ / rigs kyi bu/ 'phags pa 'di dka' thub lngas yongs su gdung ba mdzad pa'i tshe/ bdag cag kyang brgya byin gyi khang pa dang / bza' shing gi ra ba dang / rtse ba'i nags tshal dang / lha rdzas kyi rol mo brdung zhing dkrol ba dang / gam yo na glu len pa'i longs spyod la dga' ba med/ de ltar bdag cag dga' ba med pas 'di'i drung du 'dong ngo/ / bdag cag der phyin nas kyang / 'phags pa 'di ni kho bo cag la 'dod pa'i dga' ba thams cad yongs su spang pa'i phyir chos ston to/ / 'di dag thams cad ni rtag pa ma yin te/ mi brtan zhing 'jig par 'gyur ba'i chos can no zhes bya ba'i tshig brjod do/ / dregs pa dang / bag med pa thams cad yongs su gcad pa dang / bla na med pa'i byang chub tu spro ba bskyed pa'i phyir chos ston to/ /

Ten thousand Śakras, lords of devas, each with their thirty-two secondary lords and an entourage of deva youths and apsarases, were also in the sky. They were dropping down rain from clouds of divine clothing, precious adornments, and flowers. They said, “Noble one, when this ārya was enduring the ascetic practice of the five heats, we ceased to take delight in Śakra’s palace, park, pleasure groves, the playing of divine music, attendants, and songs. As we had ceased to take delight in them, we came into the presence of this ārya. When we came into his presence, he taught us the Dharma so that we would renounce all delight in desires. He said, ‘All these have the qualities of being impermanent, unstable, and decaying.’ He taught us the Dharma so that our arrogance and carelessness would end and we would develop the aspiration for the highest enlightenment.

Ten hundred thousand celestial beings of the thirty-three-fold heavens, each with thirty-two siblings, along with their celestial sons and daughters, showered rain from clouds of celestial cloths, jewels, ornaments, and flowers, then said, “While this priest is mortifying himself with fire, we have no pleasure in our palaces, parks, and groves, or in such enjoyments as music, dance, and song. Freed from attachment, we go to the priest, and he teaches us to remove all sensuality. He tells us this is all impermanent, unstable, bound to perish. He teaches us to thoroughly cut off all arrogance and heedlessness, to increase our desire for supreme enlightenment.

rigs kyi bu/ gzhan yang 'dis bltas pa tsam gyis ri rab kyi rtse mo thams cad kyang g.yo bar 'gyur te/ des bdag cag gshigs pas sems skyo bar gyur nas thams cad mkhyen pa'i sems brtan pas/ thams cad mkhyen pa'i ye shes su smon lam mngon par sgrub bo/ /

“Moreover, noble one, just by his gaze these peaks of Meru are shaken. We became alarmed on being shaken, and as the omniscient mind cannot be disturbed, we made the prayer to attain omniscient wisdom.”
Furthermore, at the sight of this priest, these peaks of the polar mountain quake. Terrified, we commit ourselves to reach omniscience, that we may be firm in our aspiration for omniscience.”

klu'i rgyal po shugs ldan dang / dga' bo dang / bsnyen dga' bo la sogs pa klu brgya stong phrag bcu dag kyang steng gi bar snang la gnas shing; dus dang mthun pa'i lha rdzas kyi tsan dan gyi sprin dang / klu'i bu mos blangs pa'i nga ro snyan pa'i dbyangs dang / lha rdzas kyi spos chu'i rgyun rab tu 'bab pa'i char mngon par phab ste/ 'di skad ces 'dzer to/ / rigs kyi bu/ 'phags pa 'di dka' thub lngas yongs su gdung ba mdzad pa'i tshe/ me'i phung po chen po 'di las 'od chen po 'byung ste; des klu'i gnas thams cad snang bar byas nas/ bye ma'i char dang / nam mkha' lding gi 'jigs pa yongs su sel to/ / khro ba 'byung ba yang zhi bar byas te/ lus sim par byas nas yid shin tu mos par byed do/ / de ltar sems shin tu mos par gyur nas/ 'phags pa 'di ni bdag cag la chos ston te/ /'di ltar klu'i lam gyi rgyud ngan pa rnam par smad pa dang / sgrib pa'i las thams cad rab tu spang ba'i phyir nyes pa 'chags su btsud cing / bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed du btsud de/ thams cad mkhyen pa nyid la rab tu 'god do/ /

Ten thousand nāgas such as the nāga kings Airāvata, Nanda, and Upananda were also in the sky above. They were sending down rain from clouds of divine yellow sandalwood, the pleasant sound of a chorus of nāga maidens, and rain that was a flow of divine scented water. They said, “Noble one, when this ārya was enduring the ascetic practice of the five heats, from this great fire shone a great light that illuminated all the dwellings of nāgas and eliminated the rains of sand and fear of the garuḍas. It also pacified anger, refreshed our bodies,[740] and made our minds serene.[741] Then when we had serene minds, this ārya taught us the Dharma so that we would repudiate the evil ways of nāgas, renounce all karma that brings obscuration, confess transgressions, develop the aspiration for the highest, complete enlightenment, and be established in omniscience.”

Also, ten thousand rain spirits in the sky showered rain from clouds of celestial sandalwood, along with the sweet sounds of the songs of nymphs, producing clouds of celestial fragrance, and said, “The light emitted from this priest’s fires, illumining the abodes of all the water spirits, removes fears of the hot rain of sand. It also extinguishes anger, and the water spirits become cool and clear in mind. Then, once our minds are clear, the priest teaches us to reject our low state as dragons and to stop all obstructive actions. Having taught us to overcome evil, he inspires us to supreme perfect enlightenment and leads us to omniscience.”

gnod sbyin gyi dbang po stong phrag bcu yang nam mkha'i dbyings la 'khod de/ mchod pa rnam pa sna tshogs kyis bram ze rgyal ba'i drod kyi skye mched dang / tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la mchod pa byas nas/ 'di skad ces 'dzer to/ rigs kyi bu/ 'phags pa 'di dka' thub lngas yongs su gdung ba mdzad pa'i pa'i tshe/ kho bo cag gi 'khor kun kyang mi rnams la byams pa'i sems skye bar gyur te/ gnod sbyin dang / srin po dang / grul bum thams cad kyang byams pa'i sems dang ldan par gyur to/ / de dag byams pa'i sems dang ldan zhing 'tsho ba med pa la zhugs pa rnams kho bo cag gi drung du 'ong ngo/ kho bo cag kyang de ltar byams pa'i dbang gis zil gyis non pas/ rang rang gi gnas de dang / de dag na dga' ba med de/ de ltar bdag cag kyang rang rang gi skye bo'i 'khor dang bcas te/ 'phags pa 'di'i drung du 'dong ngo/ / bdag cag de ltar 'ongs pa rnams la/ 'phags pa 'di'i sku las byung ba'i 'od kyis lus thams cad snang bar byas shing bde bas khyab par mdzad de/ de ltar bdag cag lus dang sems bde bar gyur nas/ 'phags pa 'di ni ci nas kyang bdag cag la gnod sbyin dang / srin po dang / grul bum dang / lus srul po mang po byang chub tu sems skye bar 'gyur ba de ltar chos ston to/ /

Ten thousand yakṣa lords were also in the sky above. They made various kinds of offerings to the brahmin Jayoṣmāyatana and Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, and then they said, “Noble one, when this ārya was enduring the ascetic practice of the five heats, we and all our retinues developed a loving mind toward humans. All yakṣas, rākṣasas, and kumbhāṇḍas also developed loving minds. They came before us with loving minds and without violence. We too were overpowered by the power of love, and each of us ceased to delight in our own residences. In that way, we each went with our retinues to the presence of the ārya. When we arrived, a light came from this ārya’s body, illuminated all our bodies, and filled us with bliss. In that way, both our bodies and minds became blissful. Then he taught us the Dharma so that the multitude of yakṣas, rākṣasas, kumbhāṇḍas, and kaṭapūtanas would develop the aspiration to enlightenment.”
