Also, ten thousand spirit chiefs, standing in the sky, honored the priest Jayoshmayatana and the youth Sudhana with various offerings, then said, “Son, as this priest mortifies himself with fire, goodwill toward human beings is born in our minds, and all spirits, goblins, and demons also become benevolent. Benevolent, now harmless, they come to us; overcome by the dominant power of goodwill, we find no pleasure in our various estates. We all go with our respective companions to the priest; he radiates light from his body, which shines on us and fills our bodies with bliss. Our bodies and minds blissful, he teaches us in such a way that many spirits, goblins, demons, and ghosts are inspired to seek enlightenment.”

dri za'i dbang po stong phrag bcu dag kyang steng gi bar snang la 'khod nas/ 'di skad ces 'dzer to/ / rigs kyi bu/ kho bo cag kyang rang rang gi gnas na 'khod pa'i tshe/ 'phags pa 'di dka' thub lngas yongs su gdung bar mdzad pa'i tshe/ me'i phung po 'di las 'od byung ste/ bdag cag gi gnas snang bar gyur to/ / de ltar bdag cag 'od des phog ste/ bde ba bsam gyis mi khyab pa dang ldan par gyur pas/ 'phags pa 'di'i drung du 'dong ste/ bdag cag drung du phyin nas kyang 'phags pa 'di ni/ bdag cag ci nas kyang bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub las phyir mi ldog par 'gyur ba de ltar chos ston to/ /

Ten thousand gandharva lords were also in the sky above, and they said, “Noble one, while we were each dwelling in our own abodes, and when this ārya was enduring the ascetic practice of the five heats, from this fire came a light that illuminated our abodes. When that light struck us we experienced inconceivable bliss. We went to be in the presence of this ārya, and when we arrived in his presence, he taught us the Dharma so that we would progress irreversibly toward the highest, complete enlightenment.”

Ten thousand chief celestial musicians also stood in the sky and said, “While we are in our abodes too, our abodes are illumined by the light of the priest’s fires; touched by that light, we are filled with inconceivable bliss and we go to the priest, who then teaches us in such a way that we become irreversible in progress toward supreme perfect enlightenment.”

lha ma yin gyi dbang po stong phrag bcu dag kyang rgya mtsho'i nang nas mngon par 'thon te/ nam mkha' la pus mo g.yas pa'i lha nga btsugs te/ thal mo sbyar nas phyag 'tshal zhing 'di skad ces 'dzer to/ / rigs kyi bu/ 'phags pa 'di dka' thub lngas yongs su gdung ba mdzad pa'i tshe/ kho bo cag gi lha ma yin gyi 'jig rten rgya mtsho dang rir bcas pa'i sa chen po'i dkyil 'khor rab tu g.yo bar gyur te/ bdag cag kun gyi nga rgyal dang / rlom sems dang / dregs pa thams cad brtul zhugs dang dka' thub kyi zil gyis non te/ 'phags pa 'di'i drung du 'dong ngo/ / der phyin nas kyang 'phags pa 'di ni/ bdag cag la g.yo sgyu thams cad rab tu spang ba dang / chos zab mo'i bzod pa dang / mi g.yo ba'i chos nyid la rab tu dgod pa dang / stobs bcu'i ye shes yongs su grub par bya ba'i phyir chos ston to/ /

Ten thousand asura lords rose up from the ocean, high into the sky, where they knelt on their right knees, and with hands together in homage they paid homage, saying, “Noble one, when this ārya was enduring the ascetic practice of the five heats, our asura world, a great circle of earth with its oceans and mountains, shook. All our arrogance and pride was overwhelmed by his self-discipline and asceticism. We went to be in the presence of this ārya, and when we arrived in his presence, he taught us the Dharma so that we would abandon all deception, enter the patience of the profound Dharma, be established in the unshakable true nature of phenomena, and attain the knowledge of the ten strengths.”

Ten thousand titan kings rose from the ocean, knelt on their right knees, joined their palms in salutation, and said, “As this priest mortifies himself by fire, all our titan worlds, including the oceans, mountains, and land spheres, quake: we are all thereby divested of arrogance, heedlessness, and conceit; overwhelmed by the heat of his religious practice, we go to him, and he teaches us so that we may do away with all deceitfulness and guile, enter into acceptance of the profound truth, abide in the state of imperturbability, and perfect the knowledge of the ten powers.”

nam mkha' lding gi dbang po shugs chen po 'dzin pa la sogs pa nam mkha' lding gi dbang po stong phrag bcus kyang / bram ze'i bu shin tu sdug gu'i gzugs su mngon par sprul te/ /'di skad ces 'dzer to/ / rigs kyi bu/ 'phags pa 'di dka' thub lngas yongs su gdung ba mdzad pa'i tshe/ me'i phung po 'di dag las 'od chen po byung ste/ bdag cag gis gnas snang bar byas nas yongs su g.yo bar byed do/ / des bdag cag kyang 'jigs shing skrag ste/ skyo ba'i yid dang ldan par gyur nas 'phags pa 'di'i drung du 'dong ngo/ 'phags pa 'di yang bdag cag la chos ston cing / byams pa chen po la yang dag par sbyor bar mdzad do/ / snying rje chen po la yang dag par dgod pa mdzad do/ / 'khor ba'i rgya mtshor 'jug pa la yang yang dag par sbyor ba mdzad do/ / 'dod pa'i 'dam du bying ba'i sems can mngon par gdon par bya ba la yang yongs su sbyor ba mdzad do/ / lhag pa'i bsam pa'i sgo rnam par dag par bya ba la yang rab tu sbyor ba mdzad do/ / shes rab dang thabs shin tu gsal ba la yang yang dag par sbyor ba mdzad do/ / rnam pa ji lta bur yongs su smin par bya ba'i sems can rnams gdul bar bya ba la yang rab tu sbyor ba mdzad do/ /

Ten thousand garuḍa lords such as the garuḍa lord Mahāvegadhārin manifested in the form of handsome brahmin[742] youths and said, “Noble one, when this ārya was enduring the ascetic practice of the five heats, a great light came from these great masses of fire and illuminated and shook our abodes. We were frightened, terrified, and dismayed, and so we went to be in the presence of this ārya. This ārya taught us the Dharma so that we would practice great love, so that we were established in great compassion, so that we would apply ourselves to plunging into the ocean of saṃsāra, so that we would apply ourselves to saving beings who are sinking in the swamp of desire, so that we would apply ourselves to the pure gateway of the higher motivation for enlightenment,[743] so that we would apply ourselves to sharp[744] wisdom and methods, and so that we would apply ourselves to guiding beings in whatever way will ripen them.”

Also ten thousand bird kings, assuming splendid human forms, said, “Son, the light from the flames of the priest’s fires, shining on our abodes, causes them to quake. Frightened and agitated, we go to him, and by teaching us he exhorts us to great benevolence and compassion, he urges us to plunge into the ocean of mundane life to serve sentient beings sunk in the mud of desire, he urges us to purify our will for enlightenment, he exhorts us to keenness of wisdom and skill in means, and gets us to work at guiding sentient beings according to their maturity.”
mi'am ci'i dbang po stong phrag bcu yang steng gi bar snang la 'khod do/ / 'di skad ces 'dzer to/ /
Ten thousand kinnara lords were also in the sky. They said,
Ten thousand centaur kings also stood in the sky and said,
rigs kyi bu/ 'phags pa 'di dka' thub lngas yongs su gdung ba mdzad pa'i tshe/
“Noble one, when this ārya was enduring the ascetic practice of the five heats,
“As this priest mortifies himself by fire,

kho bo cag gi gnas na 'khod pa'i shing ta la'i phreng ba las dril bu'i dra ba rin po che'i srad bus lda ldir brgyus pa'i sil snyan dang / rol mo'i yo byad dang / rin po che'i rgyan dang / khyim gyi longs spyod thams cad las sangs rgyas kyi sgra 'byung ngo/ /

the sound of the word Buddha, the word Dharma, the words irreversible bodhisattva Saṅgha, and the words the prayer to reach enlightenment came from the rows of palm trees, the music of the garlands of strings of networks of little bells on our trees,[745] the musical instruments, the precious jewelry, the enjoyed possessions in the homes, and the blowing of the breezes[746] in our domain.

the voice of Buddha comes forth from the rows of palms, the trees hung with nets of bells, strings of jewels, garlands, and musical instruments, and the houses and furniture with all kinds of musical instruments and jewelry in our abodes as they are blown by the wind;
chos kyi sgra dang / phyir mi ldog pa'i byang chub sems dpa'i dge 'dun gyi sgra dang / byang chub tu yang dag par zhugs pa'i smon lam gyi sgra 'byung ngo/ /
the voice of the Teaching, the voice of the host of nonregressing enlightening beings, and the voice of the vows on which enlightening beings act also emerge,
'jig rten gyi khams kyi grangs su bya ba che ge mo zhig na ni/ byang chub sems dpa' ming 'di zhes bya ba zhig byang chub tu smon lam 'debs so/ /
There came the words that said that in this and that particular world a bodhisattva named such and such is praying to attain enlightenment;
saying that in such-and-such a world the enlightening being so-and-so is vowing to attain enlightenment,
'jig rten gyi khams kyi grangs su bya ba che ge mo zhig na ni/ byang chub sems dpa' ming 'di zhes bya ba zhig dka' ba yongs su gtong ba byed do/ /
in this and that particular world a bodhisattva named such and such is accomplishing a difficult renunciation;
in such-and-such a world the enlightening being so-and-so is giving up that which is difficult to give up,
'jig rten gyi khams kyi grangs su bya ba che ge mo zhig na ni/ byang chub sems dpa' ming 'di zhes bya ba zhig /thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi ye shes kyi dkyil 'khor yongs su sbyong ba byed do/ /
in this and that particular world a bodhisattva named such and such is purifying the domain of omniscient wisdom;
in such-and-such a world the enlightening being so-and-so is purifying the sphere of universally aware knowledge,
'jig rten gyi khams kyi grangs su bya ba che ge mo zhig na ni/ byang chub sems dpa' ming 'di zhes bya ba zhig snying po byang chub tu 'gro'o/ /
in this and that particular world a bodhisattva named such and such is going to the bodhimaṇḍa;
in such-and-such a world the enlightening being so-and-so is going to the summit of enlightenment,

'jig rten gyi khams kyi grangs su bya ba che ge mo zhig na ni/ byang chub sems dpa' ming 'di zhes bya ba zhig dpung dang bzhon par bcas pa'i bdud rab tu pham par byas te/ bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu mngon par 'tshang rgya'o/ /
in this and that particular world a bodhisattva named such and such has defeated Māra, and his army is attaining the highest, complete enlightenment of buddhahood;
in such-and-such a world the enlightening being so-and-so has conquered the demon hordes and is becoming supremely and perfectly enlightened,
'jig rten gyi khams kyi grangs su bya ba che ge mo zhig na ni/ de bzhin gshegs pa mtshan 'di zhes bya ba zhig chos kyi 'khor lo bskor ba mdzad do/ /
in this and that particular world a tathāgata named such and such is turning the wheel of the Dharma;
in such-and-such a world the buddha so-and-so is turning the wheel of the teaching,

'jig rten gyi khams kyi grangs su bya ba che ge mo zhig na ni/ de bzhin gshegs pa mtshan ni che ge mo zhig sangs rgyas kyi 'phrin las ma lus par mdzad nas/ phung po ma lus pa'i dbyings su yongs su mya ngan las 'da' ba mdzad do zhes bya ba'i sgra 'byin te/

in this and that particular world a tathāgata named such and such, having accomplished all the deeds of a buddha without remainder, is passing away into the state of nirvāṇa without any remaining skandhas.
in such-and-such a world the buddha so-and-so has finished all the tasks of buddhas and is passing away into absolute nirvana.

rigs kyi bu; 'dzam bu'i gling gi dang / shing dang / yal ga dang / lo ma dang / 'dab ma thams cad rdul shin tu phra ba'i char blags pa'i mur thug par ni rung yang srid kyi/ de bzhin gshegs pa de dag gi mtshan dang / byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi smon lam dang / byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la 'jug pa'i khyad par gang kho bo cag gi gnas na yod pa'i shing ta la'i phreng ba las rol mo'i yo byad dang / rin po che'i rgyan dang / khyim gyi longs spyod rlung gis bskyod pa'i sgra 'byung zhing / nga ro 'byin pa dang / rna lam du grag pa'i mtha' ni thug par mi rung ngo/ /

“Noble one, it is possible that there could be an end to the number of atoms from all the plants, wood, branches, leaves, and petals in Jambudvīpa, but there is no end to the number of the names of tathāgatas, of the bodhisattva prayers, and of the different engagements in bodhisattva conduct that come from, resound from, and are heard from the rows of palm trees and so on up to[747] the musical instruments, the precious jewelry, the enjoyed possessions in the homes, and the blowing of the breezes in our domain.

There may be an end to the particles of every tree and plant, limb and leaf, on this continent, but there is no end to those names of the buddhas and the vows of enlightening beings, the lofty points of departure of the conduct of enlightening beings, which are heard to sound from the rows of palms and all the musical instruments, jewelry, houses, and furniture in our abodes as they are blown by the wind, producing the voices of Buddha, the Teaching, and enlightenment.

de ltar bdag cag kyang sangs rgyas dang / chos dang / dge 'dun dang / byang chub sems dpa' rab tu 'jug pa'i smon lam dang; spyod pa dang / mtshan gyi chu klung gi sgras dga' ba chen po'i shugs drag pos nyams bde ba skyes te/

“In that way, we experienced bliss through the intense joy of hearing the sound of a river[748] of the words Buddha, Dharma,[749] and Saṅgha, the prayers and conduct engaged in by bodhisattvas, and their names.
Ecstatically joyful at the sound of the names of the buddhas and the community of enlightening beings and the vows and practices they proceed upon,

'phags pa 'di'i drung du 'dod do/ / de ltar bdag cag phyin par gyur nas kyang / 'phags pa 'di ni bdag cag la ci nas kyang kho bo cag gi 'khor gyi sems can du ma zhig /bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub las phyir mi ldog par 'gyur ba de lta bur chos ston pa mdzad do/ /

“We each went to be in the presence of the ārya. When we arrived in his presence, this ārya taught us the Dharma so that we would become irreversible in our progress to the highest, complete enlightenment.”
we go to the priest, and he teaches us so that we and the many beings around us become irreversible in progress toward supreme perfect enlightenment.”

'dod pa la spyod pa'i lha'i bu stong phrag dpag tu med pa/ kha dog shin tu mdzes pa dag kyang nam mkha' la 'khod cing / yid kyis sprul pa'i mchod pa byas nas 'di skad ces 'dzer to/ / 'phags pa 'di dka' thub lngas yongs su gdung ba mdzad pa'i tshe/ me'i phung po 'di dag las rnam pa 'di lta bu'i 'od 'byung ste/ 'od des mar na mnar med pa yan chad du sems can dmyal ba rnams snang bar byas nas/ sems can dmyal ba pa'i sems can thams cad kyi sdug bsngal rtse zil bar byas te/ 'od de nyid kyis 'phags pa 'di bdag cag gi mig lam du snang bar bstan pas/ de'i phyir kho bo cag kyang 'phags pa 'di la sems mos par gyur nas 'dod pa la spyod pa'i lha'i ris nyams su bde bar skyes so/ / de ltar bdag cag kyang 'phags pa 'di'i mdzad pa la drin du gzo zhing mthong bas mi ngoms pas/ 'dod pa'i dga' ba thams cad yongs su spangs te/ 'phags pa 'di'i drung du 'dong ngo/ / der bdag cag phyin nas kyang / 'phags pa 'di ni ci nas kyang sems can tshad med pa rnams byang chub tu smon lam 'debs par 'gyur ba de ltar chos ston pa mdzad do/ /

Countless thousands of desire-realm devas with beautiful bodies[750] were also in the sky, making offerings with mentally emanated offerings. They said, “Noble one, when this ārya was enduring the ascetic practice of the five heats, a light came from these great masses of fire. That light illuminated beings as far down as the Avīci hell and extinguished the sufferings of all the beings in the hells. That light brought the image of this ārya to our eyes, and therefore we yearned for this ārya and experienced the bliss of the realm of desire devas.[751] In that way, we were grateful to him, never ceased wanting to see him, and renounced delighting in desires. We went to be in the presence of this ārya. This ārya taught us the Dharma so that we would pray for the enlightenment of limitless beings.”

Innumerable gods of the realm of desire with magnificent appearances also stood in the sky, presented mental offerings, and said, “As this priest mortifies himself with heat, his bonfires give off such light that it illumines all the hells all the way to the uninterrupted hell, and the pains of all the creatures in hell cease. He also is visible to us by the same light. We above him, our minds clarified, have been born in the heavens of the realm of desire we wished for. Grateful to him, never tired of seeing him, we give up all sensuality and go to him, and he teaches us in such a way that innumerable sentient beings resolve to realize enlightenment.”

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis chos kyi tshul rnam pa 'di lta bu thos nas dga' rangs te/ mgu zhing nyams bde la/ tshim zhing yid bde ba skyes te/ bram ze rgyal ba'i drod kyi skye mched la yang dag pa'i dge ba'i bshes gnyen du 'du shes bskyed; bram ze rgyal ba'i drod kyi skye mched kyi rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te/ 'di skad ces smras so/ / 'phags pa/ de ltar bdag gis dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi bka' dang 'gal bar bgyis pa'i nongs pa la nongs par bshags so/ /

Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, on hearing this way of the Dharma, was overjoyed, pleased, happy, and content. He recognized the brahmin Jayoṣmāyatana to be a true kalyāṇamitra. He bowed his head to the feet of the brahmin Jayoṣmāyatana and said, “Ārya, I confess my transgression of having disobeyed a kalyāṇamitra’s instruction.”

Then Sudhana, pleased, enraptured, transported, overjoyed, happy, having heard this teaching, considered the priest Jayoshmayatana to be a true spiritual benefactor, and prostrated himself at the priest’s feet and said, “I confess my error, noble one, in not recognizing you as a spiritual benefactor.”
de nas bram ze rgyal ba'i drod kyi skye mched kyis/ tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la tshigs su bcad pa 'di dag smras so/ /
Then the brahmin Jayoṣmāyatana recited this verse to Sudhana, the head merchant’s son:
Thereupon the priest spoke a verse to Sudhana:

byang chub sems dpa' gang zhig rjes su bstan dang mthun byed cing / / dran pa nye bar bzhag ste bla ma'i ngag gcog mi byed na/ / de'i phyir de yi don rnams thams cad mthun par 'grub par 'gyur/ / mthun pa'i sangs rgyas ye shes byang chub drung du 'tshang yang rgya/ /

“The bodhisattva who successfully follows the instructions And who is mindful not to disobey the guru’s words[752] Will successfully accomplish all goals and successfully Attain the wisdom of buddhahood, enlightened under the Bodhi tree.”

An enlightening being who follows instructions Has no doubts, his mind at one with the teachers. All benefits will be his, and they will be auspicious; Sure of buddha-knowledge too, he awakens at the foot of the enlightenment tree.

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis/ ri g.yang sa'i lam spu gri'i so gshibs pa la 'dzegs te/ me'i phung po chen po der mchongs so/ / de de ltar mchongs pa'i tshe/ byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin shin tu brtan pa zhes bya ba thob par gyur to/ / me des reg nas kyang byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin rab tu zhi ba'i bde ba mngon par shes pa zhes bya ba thob par gyur nas/

Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, climbed the path of razors up the mountain precipice and jumped down into the great mass of fire. When he jumped, he attained the bodhisattva samādhi called completely stable. When he landed in the fire, he attained the bodhisattva samādhi called perceiving the bliss of peace.

Then Sudhana climbed the path up the cliff of the mountain, a mass of razor edges, and threw himself into the fire. As he was falling he attained an enlightening concentration called “well established.” On contact with the fire he attained an enlightening concentration called “mystic knowledge of the bliss of tranquillity.”
des 'di skad ces smras so/ / 'phags pa/ me'i phung po la de ltar reg na bde ba dang / ri'i lam spu gris gtams pa 'di yang de ltar reg na bde ba de ni ngo mtshar che'o/ /
Sudhana said, “I am astonished, Ārya! The touch of the fire was blissful, and the mountain path of razors was also blissful to the touch.”
He said, “How wonderful is the pleasant feeling of this fire and this razor-edge mountain.”

des smras pa/ rigs kyi bu/ kho bo ni byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa dkyil 'khor yongs su mi zad pa thob pa ste/ rigs kyi bu/ kho bos ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa dkyil 'khor yongs su mi zad pa 'di shes par zad na/ kho bos byang chub sems dpa' me'i phung po lta bu/ 'gro ba thams cad kyi nyon mongs pa dang / lta ba'i rnam pa thams cad yongs su zad par bya ba'i smon lam can/ ru mtshon phyir mi ldog pa dang ldan pa/ sems la thub pa med cing / sems dma' ba med pa dang ldan pa/ yid zhum pa med pa can rdo rje'i snying po dang ldan pa'i mthu bo che lta bu/ brtsams pa chen po mthar phyin par bya ba la sgyid lug pa med pa/ sbyor ba lhod pa med pa rlung gi dkyil 'khor lta bu/ 'gro ba thams cad kyi don du brtson pa/ brtson 'grus phyir mi ldog pa dang ldan pa/ phyir mi ldog pa'i go cha bgos pa de dag gi spyod pa shes pa'am/ yon tan brjod par nus re skan/ /

The brahmin Jayoṣmāyatana said, “Noble one, I have attained the bodhisattva liberation called the unceasing domain. However, noble one, I know only this bodhisattva liberation called the unceasing domain. How could I know or describe the qualities of the bodhisattvas who are like masses of fire, who pray to eliminate all the kleśas and wrong views of all beings, who have an ensign[753] that is never in retreat, who have invincible minds, who have minds that never despair, who have minds that are never despondent, who are like Nārāyaṇa possessing the vajra essence, who reach the conclusion of their great undertakings, who have no despondency, who never slacken, who are like whirlwinds, who are dedicated to the benefit of all beings, who have irreversible diligence, and who wear the armor of irreversibility?

The priest said, “I have attained the enlightening liberation in which one is not overcome. I know this liberation, but how can I know the practice or tell the virtues of the enlightening beings whose resolve is like rays of fiery energy, determined to end all beings’ afflictions and views, who are eminent leaders who never turn back, whose hearts are never exhausted or overcome, whose minds are never depressed, whose spirits never cringe or cower, whose resolve is adamant, who are never dejected in carrying out their great undertakings, who never slacken in their efforts, who are like whirlwinds, who work for the benefit of all beings, whose vigor never recedes?

song; rigs kyi bu/ lho phyogs kyi rgyud 'di nyid na/ grong khyer seng ge rnam par bsgyings pa zhes bya ba yod de/ de na rgyal po seng ge'i dpal gyi bu mo byams ma zhes bya ba/ bu mo lnga brgya'i 'khor dang bcas pa 'dug gi /de'i gan du song la/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bya ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bya ba dris shig/

“Depart, noble one. In this southern region there is a city called Siṃhavijṛmbhita. There dwells Maitrayaṇī, the daughter of King Siṃhaketu, with her entourage of five hundred maidens. Go to her and ask her, ‘How does a bodhisattva train in bodhisattva conduct? How does a bodhisattva practice it?’ ”

“Go south, to a city called Simhavijurmbhita, where there lives a girl named Maitrayani, daughter of the rajah Simhaketu; go ask her how an enlightening being is to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings.”

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis/ bram ze rgyal ba'i drod kyi skye mched kyi rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te/ bram ze rgyal ba'i drod kyi skye mched la lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas/ yang dang yang bltas te/ bram ze rgyal ba'i drod kyi skye mched kyi drung nas song ngo/ /

Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, bowed his head to the feet of the brahmin Jayoṣmāyatana, circumambulated the brahmin Jayoṣmāyatana, keeping him to his right, many hundreds of thousands of times, and, looking back again and again, departed from the presence of the brahmin Jayoṣmāyatana.
Then Sudhana paid his respects and left the priest Jayoshmayatana.
[bu mo byams ma]
Chapter 13. Maitrayaṇī
Maitrayani

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang / dge ba'i bshes gnyen la rim gro bsam gyis mi khyab pa la zhugs pa mos pa rgya chen pos rnam par dag pa/ theg pa chen po la mngon du phyogs pa/ sangs rgyas kyi ye shes la mngon par mos pa/ sangs rgyas kyi chos la yang dag par zhugs pa/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi rjes su 'brang bar spro ba/ chos kyi rim gro la rnam par spyod pa/ chags pa med pa'i ye shes la mngon du gyur pa/ yang dag pa'i mtha' shin tu rtogs pa/ ye shes kyi mtha' la mi gnas pa'i yul dang ldan pa/ dus gsum skad cig gi cha shas la khong du chud par byed pa/ nam mkha'i mtha' gnyis su med pa mngon du gyur pa/ mi gnyis pa'i mtha' rnam par gdon mi za ba thob pa; chos kyi dbyings kyi mtha' la rnam par mi rtog par gnas pa/ bsgribs pa med pa'i mthas gdul ba khong du chud par bya ba la zhugs pa/ chos kyi mtha' dang mi 'gal bar bya ba la gzhol ba/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i mtha' la mtha' med par khong du chud pa/ sangs rgyas thams cad kyi mtha' la rnam par mi rtog par gnas pa/ sems can thams cad kyi 'du shes kyi dra ba rnam par gtor ba'i ye shes la gzhol ba/ zhing la mngon par chags pa thams cad dang bral ba/ sangs rgyas kyi 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor thams cad la chags pa med pa'i sems dang ldan pa/ sangs rgyas kyi zhing thams cad yongs su dag par bya ba la gnas pa med par spyod pa/ sems can thams cad la bdag med pa dang / sems can med pa'i 'du shes dang ldan pa/ sgra thams cad tshig gi lam lta bur khong du chud pa/ gzugs thams cad gzugs kyi gzugs brnyan dang mnyam par rnam par rig par bya ba la gzhol ba

Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, with inconceivable respect[754] for kalyāṇamitras, with a pure, vast[755] aspiration, intent on the Mahāyāna, aspiring to the wisdom of buddhahood, following the Buddhadharma, longing to follow the kalyāṇamitras, practicing veneration of the Dharma,[756] intent on unimpeded wisdom, with conviction in the highest goal, being within the range of the apogee of wisdom, comprehending the three times in a fraction of an instant, intent on the nondual apogee of space, having attained certainty in the apogee of nonduality, dwelling in the nonconceptual apogee of the realm of the Dharma, having entered the comprehension of the way that is the apogee of being free of obscurations, dedicated to the harmony that is the apogee of action,[757] realizing that the apogee of the tathāgatas is without an apogee, dwelling in the nonconceptuality that is the apogee of the buddhas,[758] and dedicated to the wisdom that disperses the network of conceptualizations of all beings, had a mind free from all attachment to realms, free from attachment to all the circles of followers of the buddhas, and practiced, without dwelling in any location, the purification of all buddha realms; he had the recognition that there is no self and no beings within all beings, comprehended that all sounds are like echoes,[759] and was dedicated to the realization that all forms are the same as reflections of forms.

Then, with inconceivable respect for spiritual benefactors, the great zeal purified, ready for the Great Vehicle, seeking enlightened knowledge, absorbed in the way to enlightenment, seeking association with spiritual friends, dwelling in the sphere of the Teaching, approaching unhindered knowledge, certain of the supreme truth, intent on ultimate knowledge, realizing that past, present, and future are ultimately one instant, aware of ultimate nonduality like space, sure of the ultimacy of nonduality, dwelling in the ultimate nondifferentiation of the reality realm, devoted to discipline whose goal is freedom from obstruction, intent on ultimate harmony in action, dwelling on the ultimate nondifference of those who realize Thusness, intent on the knowledge to tear apart the net of conceptions of all sentient beings, free from attachment to any land, his mind not attached to the congregations of the buddhas or to the purities of the buddha-lands, perceiving all sentient beings as void of self or inherent identity, realizing that all sounds are like echoes and eminently aware that all forms are like reflections,

de mthar gyis seng ge rnam par bsgyings pa'i grong khyer gang na ba der phyin te/ bu mo byams ma tshol zhing yongs su rmed rmed pa las/ rgyal po seng ge'i dpal gyi bu mo byams ma; 'khor bu mo lnga brgya dang ldan pa de khang pa rnam par snang ba'i snying po zhes bya ba'i nang na/ khri tsan dan sprul gyi snying po'i rkang pa can/ gser gyi lcags bod kyi dra bas legs par blas pa/ lha rdzas kyi stan bting ba la 'dug cing chos ston to zhes thos nas/

Sudhana eventually arrived at the city of Siṃhavijṛmbhita. He searched for and sought the maiden Maitrayaṇī and heard that Maitrayaṇī, the daughter of King Siṃhaketu, with her entourage of five hundred maidens, was in a palace called Vairocanagarbha. She was teaching the Dharma while seated on a throne that had uragasāra sandalwood legs, was draped in a network of threads of gold, and had a cushion made of divine material.

Sudhana gradually made his way to the city Simhavijurmbhita, looking for the girl Maitrayani. He was told, “The girl Maitrayani, daughter of the rajah Simhaketu, with a retinue of five hundred girls, is up on the roof of a palace of radiant jewels, sitting on a seat set on sandalwood legs and draped with nets of strings of jewels and arrayed with celestial cloth, expounding spiritual teaching.” Hearing this,

seng ge rnam par bsgyings pa'i grong khyer du song ste/ rgyal po seng ge'i dpal gyi gnas gang na ba der phyin nas/ rgyal po'i phyi sgo'i sgo khang na/ bu mo byams ma mthong bar dga' ba'i phyir sdod cing 'dug 'dug pa dang /
Sudhana entered the city of Siṃhavijṛmbhita and went to the residence of King Siṃhaketu. He sat at the king’s outer gate hoping to see the maiden Maitrayaṇī.
Sudhana entered the city, went to the house of the rajah, and stood at the outer foyer, desirous of seeing the girl Maitrayani.
des der srog chags brgya phrag du ma dang / srog chags stong phrag du ma dang / srog chags brgya stong phrag du ma 'dong ba mthong nas/
Sudhana saw many hundreds of people, many thousands of people, many hundreds of thousands of people there.
There he saw hundreds of thousands of people going in.

khyed gang nas 'ong / da gang du 'dong zhes dris pa dang / de dag na re/ ded ni bu mo byams ma'i drung du chos mnyan pa'i phyir 'dong ngo zhes nas/ des bsams pa/ 'dir ni su 'gro yang dag pa med pa lta zhig snyam ste/ de yang nang du phyin to/ /

He asked them, “Where have you come from? Where are you going?” They replied, “We have come to hear the Dharma from the maiden Maitrayaṇī.” Sudhana thought, “It seems as if everyone is allowed to go in,” and he went inside.

He asked them where they were going and why they had come, and they told him they were going to Maitrayani to hear the Teaching. He thought to himself, “No one is prevented from going in.” So he went in.

de ltar phyin te bltas na; khang pa rnam par snang ba'i snying po can de yang / gzhi shel du 'dug pa'i sa las blangs te/ bai DUr+ya'i ka ba bkye ba/ rtsig pa rdo rje las byas pa/ 'dzam bu chu klung gi lhun dang ldan pa'i ba gam brgya phrag stong gis brgyan pa nor bu rin po che grangs med pas rnam par bris pa/ rin po che stong gi snying po'i me long gi dkyil 'khor gyis shin tu spa bar byas pa/ nor bu rin po che 'gro ba'i yid du 'ong bas rnam par brgyan pa/ rin po che'i shing rta grangs med pas yongs su bskor ba/ gser gyi dril bu brgya stong shin tu 'khrol ba'i sgra snyan pa bsam gyis mi khyab pa'i rgyan dang ldan par 'dug par mthong ngo/ /

When he had gone inside and looked around, he saw that the Vairocanagarbha palace had the inconceivable display of a floor that was made of crystal, pillars made of beryl, and walls made of diamonds; it was adorned with hundreds of thousands of pinnacles made of solid gold, was furnished with round mirrors made of the essence of a thousand precious materials, and was adorned with countless precious jewels; it was arrayed with precious jewels that delighted beings and was strewn with countless nets of jewels;[760] and there was the melodious sound from hundreds of thousands of jingling golden bells.

Having gone in, he saw the palace of radiant jewels set on a crystal base, with pillars of lapis lazuli and walls of diamond, ornamented with a hundred thousand projections of gold, furnished with countless jewel mirrors, arrayed with world-illumining jewels, spread with countless jewel nets, graced with inconceivable arrays of beautiful sounds from a hundred thousand golden bells shaken by the breeze.
bu mo byams ma de yang mig dkar nag 'byes pa/ skra mthon mthing du 'dug pa/ mdog gser gyi kha dog ltar 'dug pa mthong nas/
He saw the maiden Maitrayaṇī, who had deep black eyes,[761] deep black hair, and golden skin.
He also saw the girl Maitrayani, with dark eyes, black hair, and golden skin.
des de'i rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te/ lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas thal mo sbyar te/ mdun du 'dug nas

Sudhana bowed his head to the feet of the maiden Maitrayaṇī, circumambulated her, keeping her to his right, many hundreds of thousands of times, and with his hands together in homage sat down before her.
Sudhana paid his respects to her and

'di skad ces smras so/ / 'phags ma/ bdag gis bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed na/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bgyi ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bgyi ba ma 'tshal te/

Sudhana said, “Āryā, I have developed the aspiration for the highest, complete enlightenment, but I do not know how bodhisattvas should train in bodhisattva conduct and in what way they should practice it.
said, “Noble one, I have set my mind on supreme perfect enlightenment, but I do not know how an enlightening being is to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings.”

'phags ma ni/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams la gdams ngag dang rjes su bstan pa mdzad do zhes bdag gis thos pa; 'phags ma/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bgyi ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bgyi ba bdag la bshad du gsol/
“Āryā, I have heard that you give instruction and teachings to bodhisattvas! I pray that you explain to me how bodhisattvas should train in bodhisattva conduct and how they should practice it!”
smras pa/ rigs kyi bu; kho mo'i gnas kyi rgyan la ltos shig ces nas/
Maitrayaṇī said, “Noble one, look at the display of my residence!”
She said, “Look at the adornments of my palace.”

des kun tu yul te bltas pa dang / rtsig pa re re dang / ka ba re re dang / me long gi dkyil 'khor re re dang / rnam pa'i bye brag re re dang / dbyibs re re dang / nor bu rin po che re re dang / gser gyi dril bu re re dang / rin po che'i shing re re dang / ba sbu'i bu ga re re dang / rin po che'i sen mo do re re dag las kyang / chos kyi dbyings thams cad na bzhugs pa'i de bzhin gshegs pa/ thog ma thugs bskyed pa dang bcas pa/ spyod pa dang smon lam gyi yul dang bcas pa/ 'byung ba'i rgyan dang bcas pa/ mngon par 'tshang rgya ba'i rnam par 'phrul pa dang bcas pa/ chos kyi 'khor lo bskor ba dang bcas pa/ yongs su mya ngan las 'da' ba ston pa dang bcas par gzugs brnyan gyi tshul du mthong bar gyur to/ / dmigs pa de dag re re las/ ji lta ba de bzhin du dmigs pa thams cad las kyang mthong bar gyur to/ / 'di lta ste/ dper na/ chus yongs su gang ba'i mtsho dang zhing rnyog pa med pa la rnam par gsal ba la ni/ nam mkha' nyi zla dang / skar ma'i tshogs kyis brgyan pa gzugs brnyan gyi tshul du yongs su snang ngo; ; de bzhin du khang pa rnam par snang ba'i snying po 'di dmigs pa re re las kyang / chos kyi dbyings kun na bzhugs pa'i de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad gzugs brnyan gyi tshul du yongs su snang bar gyur te/ de ni bu mo byams ma'i sngon gyi dge ba'i rtsa ba'i rgyu'i phyir te/

Sudhana looked all around and saw in each wall, each pillar, each round mirror, each form, each shape, each precious jewel, each golden bell, each precious tree, each pore, and each string of jewels the images of the tathāgatas in all the realm of phenomena first developing their aspiration for enlightenment, their conduct and the scope of their prayers, the display of their setting forth, their manifestation of the attainment of buddhahood, their turning the wheel of the Dharma, and their demonstration of passing into nirvāṇa. What he saw from one object of perception he saw from all the objects of perception. For example, there appeared in a lake filled with water that was unpolluted and clear the reflection of the sky, the sun, the moon, and the constellations of stars. In the same way, in every object of perception within the Vairocanagarbha palace appeared the reflections of all the tathāgatas present in the entire realm of phenomena as the result of the maiden Maitrayaṇī’s previous roots of merit.

Looking all around, in each wall, each pillar, each mirror, each figure, each formation, each jewel, each golden bell, each jewel tree, each girl’s body, each jewel necklace, he saw reflected images of the buddhas in the cosmos, with their first inspirations, spheres of practice and vows, manifestations of emergence in the world, mystical transformation on attainment of enlightenment, turnings of the wheel of teaching, and displays of ultimate extinction. This he saw in each and every object. Just as the sun, moon, and stars in the sky are seen reflected in a clear, limpid pool of water, so did all the buddhas of the cosmos appear reflected in each object of the luminous jewel palace, this as a result of the girl Maitrayani’s past roots of goodness.
des de ltar rnam par bltas nas/ sangs rgyas mthong ba'i rgyan gyi mtshan ma de yongs su bzung ste thal mo sbyar nas/ bu mo byams ma'i gdong du bltas pa dang /
When Sudhana had seen and remembered the features of this display of the vision of the buddhas, with his hands together in homage he looked at Maitrayaṇī’s face.
Having viewed this, holding in mind the features of this supernal array of visions of Buddhas, Sudhana joined his hands in a gesture of respect and turned his attention to Maitrayani’s words.

des smras pa/ rigs kyi bu/ kho mo ni shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa'i sgo'i rgyud kun nas rnam par brgyan pa zhes bya ba thob pa ste/ shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa'i sgo'i rgyud 'di ni/ kho mos de bzhin gshegs pa chu klung gang+gA sum cu rtsa drug gi bye ma snyed las yongs su btsal ba ste; de bzhin gshegs pa de dag gis kyang / shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa'i sgo'i rgyud kun nas rnam par brgyan pa 'di/ sgo sna tshogs kyi khong du chud par bya bas rtogs par mdzad de; gcig gis gang du gsungs pa de yang gnyis kyis ma gsungs so/ /

She said to him, “Noble one, I have attained the teaching[762] of the gateway to the perfection of wisdom called the complete display. I sought this teaching of the gateway to the perfection of wisdom called the complete display from as many tathāgatas as there are grains of sand in three hundred and sixty million Ganges Rivers. Those tathāgatas, through making me enter various gateways, made me realize the teaching of the gateway to the perfection of wisdom called the complete display. What was taught by any one of them was not taught by another of them.”

She said, “I have attained the means of access to perfect wisdom from the arrangement of the totality. I sought this from buddhas as numerous as grains of sand in thirty-six Ganges Rivers, and those buddhas introduced me to the means of access to perfect wisdom by way of the arrangement of the totality through various ways of entry into it, each different.”
smras pa/ 'phags ma/ shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa'i sgo'i rgyud kun nas rnam par brgyan pa 'di'i yul ji lta bu zhig mchis/
Sudhana asked, “Āryā, what is the scope of this teaching of the gateway to the perfection of wisdom called the complete display?”
Sudhana said, “What is the sphere of this means of access to perfect wisdom by way of the arrangement of the totality?”

smras pa/ rigs kyi bu/ shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa'i sgo'i rgyud kun nas rnam par brgyan pa 'di la/ kho mo mngon du byed cing / sems pa dang / rjes su 'brang bar bya ba dang / rnam par dpyod pa dang / rjes su sems pa dang / dran par bya ba dang / yongs su gzung ba dang / rnam par brtags pa dang / mngon par bsgrub pa dang / yang dag par brgyan par bya ba dang / rab tu rnam par dbye ba byed pa'i tshe/ gzungs kun nas sgo zhes bya ba yongs su skye ste/ gzungs kyi dkyil 'khor der ni chos kyi sgo brgya stong grangs med pa phrag bcu yongs su 'du'o/ / khong du chud do/ / mngon du 'gyur ro/ / mngon par 'du'o/ / khongs na 'khod do/ /

Maitrayaṇī answered, “Noble one, having been made to face, reflect on, follow, practice, contemplate, approach,[763] grasp, display, attain, adorn, and analyze this teaching of the gateway to the perfection of wisdom called the complete display, there arose the power of retention called the complete gateways. Countless millions of Dharma gateways are present, are included, are manifest, are collected, and are arranged[764] within the range of that power of retention.

She said, “Focusing my attention on this means of access to perfect wisdom by way of the arrangement of the totality, meditating on it, following it, pondering it, contemplating it, making it familiar, keeping it in mind, putting it in order, putting it into effect, perfecting it, thoroughly examining it, I developed a mental control called ‘facing in all directions,’ in the sphere of which mental control incalculable tens of hundreds of thousands of media of the Teaching operate, assemble, become visible, become accessible, and develop—
'di lta ste/ sangs rgyas kyi zhing gi sgo dang / sangs rgyas kyi sgo dang / chos kyi sgo dang / sems can gyi sgo dang /
“There is the gateway to the buddha realms, the gateway to the buddhas, the gateway to the Dharma, the gateway to beings,
for example, the medium of buddha-lands, the medium of buddhas, the medium of doctrines, the medium of all beings,
'das pa'i sgo dang / ma 'ongs pa'i sgo dang / da ltar byung ba'i sgo dang / gnas pa'i mtha' sgo dang;
the gateway to the past, the gateway to the future, the gateway to the present, the gateway to the highest state,
the medium of the past, the medium of the future, the medium of the present, the medium of the limit of duration,
bsod nams kyi sgo dang / bsod nams kyi tshogs kyi sgo dang / ye shes kyi sgo dang / ye shes kyi tshogs kyi sgo dang /
the gateway to merit, the gateway to the accumulation of merit, the gateway to wisdom, the gateway to the accumulation of wisdom,
the medium of virtue, the medium of provisions of virtue, the medium of knowledge, the medium of provisions of knowledge,
smon lam gyi sgo dang /
the gateway to the forms of prayer,
the medium of vows,
smon lam gyi rnam pa'i sgo dang;
the medium of differentiation of vows,
spyod pa'i sgo dang / spyod pa rnam par dag pa'i sgo dang /
the gateway to conduct, the gateway to pure conduct,
the medium of practices, the medium of purification of practices,
spyod pa yongs su 'byung ba'i sgo dang / spyod pa yongs su rdzogs par bya ba'i sgo dang / las kyi sgo dang / las dang mi 'gal pa'i sgo dang /
the gateway to the creation of conduct, the gateway to the perfection of conduct, the gateway to karma, the gateway to the illumination[765] of karma,
the medium of accumulation of practices, the medium of fulfillment of practices, the medium of actions, the medium of harmony of actions,
las kyi rgyun gyi sgo dang / lam mngon par 'du bya ba'i sgo dang / * mi mnyam pa'i las yongs su spang pa'i sgo dang /
the gateway to the continuum of karma, the gateway to the creation of karma, the gateway to the range of karma,[766] the gateway to the avoidance of bad karma,
the medium of streams of actions, the medium of performance of actions, the medium of fields of actions, the medium of rejection of evil actions,
yang dag pa'i las la nan tan du bya ba'i sgo dang / las la dbang bsgyur ba'i sgo dang / legs par spyad pa'i sgo dang / legs par spyad pa yang dag par blang ba'i sgo dang /
the gateway to the practice of good karma, the gateway to power over karma, the gateway to good behavior, the gateway to the adoption of good behavior,
the medium of undertaking of proper actions, the medium of control of actions, the medium of morality, the medium of guidance to right ethics,
ting nge 'dzin gyi sgo dang / ting nge 'dzin khong du chud par bya ba'i sgo dang / ting nge 'dzin la rnam par spyad pa'i sgo dang / ting nge 'dzin spyod yul gyi sgo dang /
the gateway to samādhi, the gateway to engagement in samādhi, the gateway to the procedure of samādhi, the gateway to the range of samādhi,
the medium of concentration, the medium of practice pursuant to concentration, the medium of contemplation in concentration, the medium of spheres of concentration,
ting nge 'dzin las ldang ba'i sgo dang / mngon par shes pa'i sgo dang / sems rgya mtsho'i sgo dang / sems kyi rnam grangs kyi sgo dang /
the gateway to arising from samādhi, the gateway to clairvoyance, the gateway to the ocean of the mind, the gateway to the processes of the mind,
the medium of emerging from concentration, the medium of mystic knowledge, the medium of the ocean of mind, the medium of ways of thought,
sems kyi rgyud yongs su dag par bya ba'i sgo dang / sems kyi thibs po snang bar bya ba'i sgo dang / sems kyi mtsho dang bar bya ba'i sgo dang; sems 'byung ba'i sgo dang /

the gateway to the purification of the continuum of the mind, the gateway to illuminating the darkness of the mind, the gateway to clarifying the lake of the mind, the gateway to the arising of the mind,

the medium of clearing away entanglements of mind, the medium of illumining the obscure recesses of the mind, the medium of calming and clearing the pool of the mind, the medium of capacities of the mind,
sems rnam par rgyu ba'i sgo dang / sems can kun nas nyon mongs pa rgyu ba'i sgo dang / nyon mongs pa'i bag chags kyi sgo dang / nyon mongs pa'i sbyor ba'i sgo dang; mos pa'i sgo dang /
the gateway to the activities of the mind, the gateway of the kleśas in beings, the gateway to the propensity for the kleśas, the gateway to the engagement of the kleśas,
the medium of the actions of the mind, the medium of the occurrence of sentient beings’ afflictions, the medium of defiling habit energies, the medium of the acting out of afflictions,
sems can gyi spyod pa'i sgo dang / sems can gyi spyod pa rnam pa tha dad pa'i sgo dang / 'jig rten 'byung ba'i sgo dang /
the gateway to aspiration,[767] the gateway to the conduct of beings, the gateway to the different conducts of beings, the gateway to the creation of worlds,
the medium of interests, the medium of the conduct of sentient beings, the medium of the variety of conduct of sentient beings, the medium of the productions of the world,
sems can gyi bsam pa'i sgo dang / sems can gyi 'du shes kyi rnam pa'i sgo dang / phyogs kyi sgo dang / chos kyi phyogs kyi sgo dang /
the gateway to the thoughts of beings, the gateway to the form of the conceptualizations of beings, the gateway to the directions, the gateway to the direction of the Dharma,
the medium of the inclinations of sentient beings, the medium of what is in the conceptions of sentient beings, the medium of places, the medium of the realms of phenomena,
snying rje chen po'i sgo dang / byams pa chen po'i sgo dang / zhi ba'i sgo dang / ngag gi lam gyi sgo dang /
the gateway to great compassion, the gateway to great love, the gateway to peace, the gateway to the path of speech,
the medium of great compassion, the medium of great kindness, the medium of tranquillity, the medium of speech,
tshul gyi sgo dang / khong du chud par bya ba'i sgo dang / rnam par phye ba'i sgo dang / yang dag par 'du ba'i sgo dang /

the medium of reason, the medium of attainments, the medium of distinctions, the medium of unity,
