rigs kyi bu/ de ltar kho mos shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa'i sgo'i rgyud dran pas kun nas rnam par brgyan pa 'di shes par zad na/ kho mos byang chub sems dpa' nam mkha'i dbyings dang mnyam pa/ blo gros chos kyi dbyings ltar yangs pa/ rgyud bsod nams kyi tshogs kyis brtan pa/ 'jig rten las 'das pa'i lam du zhugs pa/ 'jig rten gyi chos yongs su mi rgyu ba/ ye shes snang ba'i mig rab rib med pa rab tu thob pa/ chos kyi dbyings thams cad mun pa med par khong du chud pa/ blo nam mkha' ltar tshad med pa dang ldan pa/ dmigs pa thams cad kyi rjes su song ba'i mig can/ chags pa med pa'i sa snang ba'i snying po dang ldan pa/ chos thams cad kyi don rab tu dbye ba la mkhas pa zil gyis gnon la/ 'jig rten kun gyis zil gyis mi non pa/ 'jig rten gyi spyod pa'i tshul la rnam par spyod pa/ 'jig rten gyi lam gyi rgyud thams cad na kha na ma tho med pa/ 'jig rten gyi don byed pa la brtson pa/ 'gro ba thams cad kyi rten du gyur pa/ 'gro ba thams cad kyi ngag gi tshul dang rnam pa la mkhas pa/ 'gro ba thams cad du gnas pa'i bsam pa dang ldan pa/ bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du rnam par dmigs pa ston pa/ dus kyi 'khor lo thams cad la dbang bsgyur ba de dag gi spyod pa shes pa'am/ yon tan brjod par nus re skan/

“However, noble one, I know only this teaching of the gateway to the perfection of wisdom called the complete display of memory. How could I know or describe the qualities of the bodhisattvas whose minds are as vast as the realm of space, whose understanding is as vast as the realm of phenomena, whose continuum is supported by an accumulation of merit, who follow a path that transcends the world, who do not engage with worldly qualities, who have attained the undimmed radiance of wisdom, who have comprehended the entire realm of Dharma free of darkness, who have an understanding that is as limitless as space, who have the eyes that follow every object of perception, who possess the essence of unimpeded radiance, who are skilled in differentiating the words[770] and meaning of all the Dharma, who overpower[771] without being overpowered by the world, who have a conduct that accords with the ways of worldly conduct, who do not commit any transgression in any of the worldly ways, who are dedicated to the benefit of all[772] worlds, who are a support for all beings, who are skilled in the speech and behavior of all beings, who have the intention to dwell with all beings, who appear in whatever way they are wished to be perceived, and who have power over all the wheels of time.

“I know this means of access to perfect wisdom which is the array of total mindfulness; how can I know the practice orteil the virtues of the enlightening beings whose minds are like space, whose intellects are broad as the cosmos, whose mental flow is based on accumulated virtue, who have attained transmundane understanding, who do not practice worldly ways, who have attained the eye of the light of knowledge without obscurity, who clearly discern all realms of reality, whose awareness is infinite as space, whose eyes are mindful of all objects, who are filled with the light of the state of nonobstruction, who are skilled in analyzing all doctrines, meanings, and statements, who are not overcome by any world, who conduct themselves well according to worldly standards and are irreproachable in any worldly state, who are intent on the well-being of all worlds, who are a refuge for all beings, who know the manners and courtesies of speech of all worlds, who can give the appearances of dress and habitation of all worlds as they wish, and who are masters of all wheels of time?

song / rigs kyi bu/ lho phyogs kyi rgyud 'di nyid na/ yul mig gsum pa zhes bya ba yod de/ de na dge slong blta na sdug pa zhes bya ba 'dug gi/ de'i gan du song la; ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bya ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bya ba dri sa shig /

“Depart, noble one. In this southern region there is a land called Trinayana. There dwells a bhikṣu by the name of Sudarśana. Go to him and ask him, ‘How does a bodhisattva train in bodhisattva conduct? How does a bodhisattva practice it?’ ”
“Go south, to the land called Trinayana, where a monk named Sudarshana lives. Go ask him how an enlightening being is to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings.”

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis/ bu mo byams ma'i rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te/ bu mo byams ma la lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas/ yang dang yang bltas te/ bu mo byams ma'i drung nas song ngo//

Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, bowed his head to the feet of the maiden Maitrayaṇī, circumambulated the maiden Maitrayaṇī, keeping her to his right, many hundreds of thousands of times, and, looking back again and again, departed from the presence of the maiden Maitrayaṇī.
Then Sudhana paid his respects to Maitrayani and left.
[dge slong blta na sdug pa]
Chapter 14. Sudarśana
Sudarshana

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang byang chub sems dpa'i ye shes kyi rnam par spyod pa zab mo rjes su bsam pa dang / chos kyi dbyings kyi gzhi zab mo khong du chud par bya ba rjes su bsam pa dang / sems can gyi ye shes shin tu phra zhing zab pa rjes su bsam pa dang / 'jig rten gyi 'du shes kyi rnam pa zab mo rjes su bsam pa dang / mngon par 'du bya ba med pa'i dbyings zab mo rjes su bsam pa dang / sems kyi rgyud kyi dbyings zab mo rjes su bsam pa dang / rten cing 'brel par 'byung ba'i dbyings zab mo rjes su bsam pa dang / rang bzhin gyis bden pa'i dbyings zab mo rjes su bsam pa dang / 'gro ba thams cad kyi rnam par spyod pa bden pa'i dbyings zab mo rjes su bsam pa dang / chos kyi dbyings brgyan pa'i rgyan gyi dbyings zab mo rjes su bsam pa dang / lus kyi 'khrul 'khor shugs kyis 'khor ba'i dbyings zab mo rjes su bsam pa dang / las kyis sna tshogs su gyur pa'i dbyings zab mo rjes su bsam pa byed cing /

Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, contemplated the profound conduct of wisdom of the bodhisattvas, contemplated reaching the profound basis of the realm of phenomena, contemplated all[773] profound subtle wisdom, contemplated the profound aspect of worldly conceptualization, contemplated the profound ground[774] that is without creation, contemplated the profound ground of the stream of the mind, contemplated the profound ground of dependent origination, contemplated the profound true[775] ground of nature, contemplated the profound true ground of the terminology[776] of beings, contemplated the profound ground of the adorning array of the realm of phenomena, contemplated the profound ground of dependence on the processes of the body, and contemplated the profound ground of the various transformations of the body.

Then, contemplating the profound discernment of enlightening beings’ knowledge, the profound attainment of the base of the reality realm, the profound knowledge of all subtleties, the profundity of the conceptuality of the world, the profundity of the base of nondoing, the profundity of the base of the mental stream, the profundity of the base of interdependent origination, the profundity of the plane of truth in terms of inherent nature, the profundity of the plane of truth in terms of the conventions of sentient beings, the profundity of the ground of adornment of the cosmos, the profundity of the plane of observation of the operation of the body, and the profundity of the ground of the world of action and thought,

mthar gyis yul mig gsum pa gang na ba der phyin te/ yul gyi 'khor dang / grong khyer gyi 'khor dang / tshong 'dus kyi 'khor dang / grong rdal gyi 'khor dang / yul gru'i 'khor dang / lhas kyi 'khor dang / drang srong dge ba spyod pa'i gnas kyi 'khor dang / yul dang / phyogs kyi 'khor dang / chu'i rgyud kyi 'khor dang / ri'i sal sul gyi 'khor dang / nags tshal chen po'i 'khor dag tu dge slong blta na sdug pa yongs su tshol tshol ba las/ des dge slong blta na sdug pa nags tshal stug po zhig na

Eventually he arrived at the land of Trinayana. He searched for the bhikṣu Sudarśana throughout the land, throughout the towns, throughout the cities, throughout the marketplaces, throughout the villages, throughout the cattle pens, throughout the ashrams of ṛṣis, throughout the regions and districts, throughout the banks of rivers, throughout mountain caves, and throughout great forests until he saw the bhikṣu Sudarśana inside a thick forest.

Sudhana made his way to the land of Trinayana. Looking for the monk Sudarshana in towns and cities, marketplaces and villages, in herding stations, in hermitages, in the provinces, in mountains, caves, and forests, he saw Sudarshana walking around in a certain woods,
gzhon zhing dar la bab pa/ gzugs mdzes shing sdug la blta na yid du 'ong ba/
The bhikṣu Sudarśana was a young adult, handsome, good looking, and attractive.
young and handsome,

skra mthon mthing g.yas phyogs su 'khyil ba dang ldan pa/ mgo gdugs ltar 'dug pa; gtsug tor gyi spyi bo can dpral ba yangs pa/ mig dkar nag 'phyes shing ril la/ rdzi ma ba'i rdzi ma ltar 'dug pa/ sna'i dbyibs legs shing bzang la ran par mdzes pa dang ldan pa/ mchu mtshal ltar mdog bzang zhing shin tu legs pa dang ldan pa/ so mnyam zhing thags bzang la shin tu dkar ba bzhi bcu tshang ba dang ldan pa/ 'gram pa'i lha nga seng ge ltar 'dug pa/ mkhur ba shas gang zhing rgyas pa/ smin tshugs gzhu ltar 'dug cing ring la shin tu mdzes pa/ mdzod spu'i zla ba'i kha dog ltar 'dug pa'i thig le can/ rna shal ring zhing lhod par 'phyang ba/ zla ba nya ba ltar bzhin mdangs dang ldan zhing shin tu bzang ba/ mgul zlum zhing dung ltar mdzes pa/ snying ga dpal gyi be'us brgyan pa/ ro stod seng ge'i stod ltar 'dug pa/ thal gong shin tu rgyas pa/ dpung mgo'i lhun legs shing zlum pa/ lag pa ring ba dra bar 'brel ba'i sor mo can/ rkang lag 'khor los brgyan pa/ rkang lag 'jam zhing gzhon la shas rgyas pa/ bdun shin tu mtho ba/ rkang pa rdo rje ltar 'dug pa/ lus che zhing drang ba/ brla zlum pa/ pho mtshan gsang ba'i sbubs na 'dug pa/ byin pa ri e na ya'i byin pa ltar 'dug pa/ sor mo ring ba/ rkang pa'i rting pa yangs pa/ 'od 'dom gang ba dang ldan pa/ mdog gser gyi kha dog ltar 'dug pa/ ba spu re re nas g.yas phyogs su gyen du 'khyil ba/ shing nya gro da'i rgyal po ltar chu zheng gab pa/

His deep black hair curled to the right. His head was like a parasol. There was an uṣṇīṣa on the crown of his head. His forehead was broad. His eyes were wide and deep black. His eyelashes were like the eyelashes of a cow. His nose was lovely, high, and prominent.[777] His lips were the beautiful color of vermilion and perfectly proportioned. His teeth were even, without gaps, very white, and a full forty in number. He had jaws like a lion. His cheeks were full and wide. His eyebrows were long, beautiful, and curved like a bow. He had the mark of the ūrṇā hair the color of the moon. His earlobes were long and hung loosely. His face was bright and beautiful like the full moon. His throat was round and as beautiful as a conch. His heart area was adorned by the śrīvatsa. His upper body was like the upper body of a lion. His flesh between the shoulder blades was muscular. His shoulders were bulky and rounded. His arms were long. His fingers were webbed. His hands and feet were adorned by wheels. His hands and feet were soft, young, and thick. He had the seven prominences. His waist was slim like a vajra’s. His body was big and straight. His thighs were round. His penis was retracted into his body. His calves were like the calves of a female blackbuck. His fingers were long. The heels of his feet were wide. He had a halo a fathom in width. He was golden in color. Each of his body hairs was curled upward to the right. He had the circular symmetry[778] of a king banyan tree.
lus mtshan dang / dpe byad bzang pos shin tu brgyan pa/
He was adorned with the signs and features of a superior being.
with the physical marks and embellishments of a great man,

mig mi 'gebs shing mi rgod pa/ dran pa nye bar gnas pa; ri'i rgyal po kha ba can ltar dang / nags tshal dang / sman dang / shing phran sna tshogs kyis brgyan pa/ blo shin tu yangs pa/ ye shes kyi spyod yul dang / yul la thub pa med pa; dbyangs kyi dkyil 'khor gyi rgyan sprin gyi sgra lta bu dang ldan pa/ g.yo ba dang / rlom sems dang / g.yeng ba dang / spros pa thams cad dang bral ba'i sems dang ldan pa/ ye shes kyi spyod yul ma 'dres pa/ sangs rgyas kyi yul rgya chen po'i snang ba thob pa/ sems can thams cad yongs su smin par bya ba dang / gdul ba'i bsam pa rgyun mi 'chad pa/ snying rje chen po'i dkyil 'khor shin tu yangs pa skyes pa/

His eyes did not blink or waver. He remained in a state of mindfulness. He was like the Himalayas, the king of mountains, adorned with various grasses, forests, herbs, and vines. His intellect was vast. He had an invincible range and scope of wisdom. The display of the field of his voice was like thunder from the clouds. His mind was free of all vacillation, conceit, instability, or frivolity. He had an unalloyed range of wisdom. He had attained the illumination of the vast range of the wisdom[779] of buddhahood. He was continuously motivated to ripen and guide all beings. He had developed the vast[780] field of great compassion.

his gaze steady, mindful, of vast intelligence, intent on the sphere of insuperable knowledge, his mind free from all vacillation, vain imagination, idle fancies, and false ideas, abiding in pure knowledge, aware of the vast range of enlightened knowledge, firmly resolved to guide all beings to full development, with a vast sphere of great compassion,

de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi chos kyi tshul yongs su gzung ba dang / sems can thams cad kyi ye shes snang ba yang dag par bskyed pa'i phyir/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i tshul rjes su dran zhing / 'gro ba thams cad kyi don du 'chag pa la zhugs te/ drag dal med cing pad ral med la/ shin tu mdzes par 'chag pa/ gnas gtsang ma'i lha'i gos dang ldan pa/

He was dedicated to possessing the way of the Dharma of all the tathāgatas. He was dedicated to bringing the light of wisdom to all beings. He was mindful of the way of the tathāgatas. He was on the meditation walkway. He was walking neither too fast nor too slow, serenely and steadily.[781] He was dressed like the Śuddhāvāsa devas.

aiming to bear the eye of the teachings of all buddhas, aiming to produce the light of knowledge in all sentient beings, ever-mindful of the way of the enlightened, treading it for the sake of all sentient beings, walking quietly and steadily, neither quickly nor slowly, dressed like the deities of the pure abodes,

lha dang / klu dang / gnod sbyin dang / dri za dang / lha ma yin dang / nam mkha' lding dang / mi'am ci dang / lto 'phye chen po dang / brgya byin dang / tshangs pa dang / 'jig rten gyi mgon po dang / mi dang / mi ma yin pas bskor cing 'dug pa
He was encircled by devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, Śakra, Brahmā, the world guardians, humans, and nonhumans.
surrounded by all kinds of beings.
mthong ngo/ /
[…thus seen]
[…thus seen]

dge slong blta na mdzes pa de 'chag pa'i tshe/ phyogs mngon du gyur pa'i phyogs kyi lha rnams phyogs kyi dkyil 'khor yongs su sgrub par byed do/ / rkang gis 'gro ba'i lha rnams rin po che'i pad mos gom pa 'dor ba'i tshe/ yongs su blang ba byed do/ / me'i lha snang ba'i dkyil 'khor zad mi shes pa rnams kyang mun pa dang / rab rib rnam par sel to/ / 'dzam bu rgyal mtshan gyi nags tshal gyi lha rnams kyang me tog mang po char mngon par 'bebs so/ / sa'i lha mi g.yo ba'i snying po can rnams kyang rin po che'i 'byung gnas mang po ston to/ / nam mkha'i lha kun nas snang ba'i dpal dang ldan pa rnams kyang nam mkha'i dbyings yongs su brgyan pa byed do/ / rgya mtsho'i lha dpal kun nas 'byung ba rnams kyang rin po che dam pa mang pos mngon par 'thor to/ / ri rab gyi lha dri ma med pa'i snying po can rnams kyang thal mo sbyar cing phyag 'tshal lo/ / rlung gi lha thogs pa med pa'i stobs can rnams kyang spos dang / bdug spos dang / me tog 'thor ba'i rlung rab tu 'gyed do/ / mtshan mo'i lha gnas par byed pa lus shin tu brgyan pa rnams kyang lus shin tu btud cing phyag 'tshal lo/ / nyin mo'i lha rtag tu sad par byed pa'i dkyil 'khor can rnams kyang nor bu rin po che phyogs snang bar byed pa'i rgyal mtshan thogs shing / snang ba bskyed pa'i phyir nam mkha'i dbyings la 'khod do/ /

When Sudarśana was going to change the direction in which he was walking, the devas of the directions turned[782] the field of directions around. The devas of walking received his footsteps on precious lotuses. The devas who cause fire, who have unceasing disks of light, dispelled obscuring darkness. The devas of the forest of Jambudhvaja sent down a rain of many flowers. The devas of the earth, who have the essence of stability, revealed many sources of jewels. The devas of the sky, who have the splendor of complete brightness, adorned the surface of the sky. The devas of the ocean, who are the source of splendor, scattered great precious jewels. The devas of Sumeru, who have the essence of stainlessness, placed their hands together and paid homage. The devas of the air, who have unimpeded power, spread breezes that scattered perfume, incense, and flowers. The devas of the night,[783] with their bodies bedecked in jewelry, bowed down in homage. The devas of the daytime, who have the disk that always causes beings to wake were holding banners of precious jewels that illuminated the directions and standing in the sky in order to create light.

Furthermore, in front of Sudarshana as he walked were deities of direction who caused the world to turn; footstep-following deities received his steps on jewel lotuses; fire deities with inexhaustible spheres of light dispelled the darkness; forest deities showered rain of flowering plants; earth deities, the source of stability, revealed jewel mines; sky deities, their splendor illumining everywhere, adorned the sky; glorious ocean deities scattered great jewels over him; polar mountain deities, full of purity, folded their hands in respectful salutation; wind deities of unobstructed power gave off a fragrant flowery breeze; springlike night deities prostrated their beautifully adorned bodies in respect; ever-awakening daylight deities hovered in the sky holding banners of radiant jewels to produce light.

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang / dge slong blta na sdug pa gang na ba der phyin nas/ dge slong blta na sdug pa'i rkang pa'i bol gnyis la/ spyi bos gtugs te phyag 'tshal nas/ dge slong blta na sdug pa'i rkang pa'i bol gnyis la bzhin sbyar te/ legs par phyis nas

Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, approached the bhikṣu Sudarśana and bowed his head onto the surface of the bhikṣu Sudarśana’s feet, covered the surface of the bhikṣu Sudarśana’s feet with kisses,[784] and wiped[785] them well.
Sudhana went up to the monk Sudarshana, paid his respects, and

mdun du 'dug ste/ thal mo sbyar nas 'di skad ces smras so/ / 'phags pa/ bdag ni bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu yang dag par zhugs nas/ byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa yongs su tshol ba zhig lags te/
Then Sudhana sat down before the bhikṣu Sudarśana and with his hands placed together said, “Ārya, I am set on the highest, complete enlightenment and am seeking bodhisattva conduct.
said, “Noble one, I have set out for supreme perfect enlightenment and seek the practice of enlightening beings.

'phags pa ni byang chub sems dpa' rnams la gdams ngag dang / rjes su bstan pa mdzad do/ /zhes bdag gis thos na/ 'phags pa/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bgyi ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bgyi ba bdag la bshad du gsol/
“Ārya, I have heard that you give instruction and teachings to bodhisattvas! Explain to me how bodhisattvas should train in bodhisattva conduct and how they should practice it!”
I have heard you give enlightening beings instruction, and I ask you to tell me how an enlightening being is to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings.”
des smras pa/ rigs kyi bu/ kho bo ni tshes btab na dar la bab pa/ rab tu byung bas btab na gsar du zhugs pa ste/
The bhikṣu Sudarśana said, “Noble one, having reached adulthood, I am newly entered into the homeless life.
Sudarshana said, “I am young, and have only recently become a monk.

rigs kyi bu/ kho bos ni tshe de 'dra ba gcig gis/ de bzhin gshegs pa chu klung gang+gA sum cu rtsa brgyad kyi bye ma snyed kyi drung du tshangs pa'i spyod pa spyad de/ bdag gis de bzhin gshegs pa la la'i zham ring du nyin zhag gcig tu tshangs pa'i spyod pa spyad do/ /la lar ni nyin zhag bdun du/ la lar ni zla ba phyed du/ la lar ni zla ba gcig tu/ la lar ni lo gcig tu/ la lar ni lo brgyar/ la lar ni lo stong du/ la lar ni lo brgya phrag stong du/ la lar ni lo bye bar/ la lar ni lo bye ba khrag khrig tu/ la lar ni lo brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med par/ la lar ni bskal pa bar mar/ la lar ni bskal pa phyed du/ la lar ni bskal par bdag gis de bzhin gshegs pa la la'i zham ring du ni/ bskal pa brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med par tshangs pa'i spyod pa spyad de/ bskal pa bgrang ba'i tshul 'di nyid kyis de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad las chos bstan pa thos te/ gdams ngag dang / rjes su bstan pa yang dag par blangs so/ /

“Noble one, I have in this one lifetime practiced celibacy before as many tathāgatas as there are grains of sand[786] in thirty-eight Ganges Rivers. I practiced celibacy with some for a day and night. I practiced celibacy with some for seven days. I practiced celibacy with some for half a month. I practiced celibacy with some for a month. I practiced celibacy with some for a year. I practiced celibacy with some for a hundred years. I practiced celibacy with some for a thousand years. I practiced celibacy with some for a hundred thousand years. I practiced celibacy with some for ten million years. I practiced celibacy with some for a quintillion years. I practiced celibacy with some for an anabhilāpyānabhilāpyaparivarta of years. I practiced celibacy with some for an intermediate kalpa. I practiced celibacy with some for half a kalpa. I practiced celibacy with some for a kalpa. I heard the Dharma from all those tathāgatas and received their instructions and teachings.

At that, in one life I have performed religious practice in the company of as many buddhas as grains of sand in thirty-eight Ganges Rivers. With some I performed spiritual practice for a day and a night, with some for a week, with some for a fortnight, with some for a month, with some for a year, with some for a century, with some for a millennium, with some for a hundred millennia, with some for a million years, with some for a trillion years, with some for untold, inexpressible numbers of years, with some for an intermediate eon, with some for half an eon, with some for an eon, with some for as long as untold, inexpressible numbers of eons, and from all those buddhas I heard explanation of the Teaching and received instruction.
smon lam gyi rgyan yongs su sbyangs so/ / yang dag par bsgrub pa'i yul la zhugs so/ / spyod pa'i dkyil 'khor yongs su sbyangs so/ /
“I have purified an array of prayers. I have purified the field of conduct that enters the range of realization.[787]
My vows were purified, my sphere of practice entering into the realm of realization was purified,

pha rol tu phyin pa rgya mtsho yongs su rdzogs par byas so/ / mngon par rdzogs par 'tshang rgya ba'i rnam par 'phrul pa yongs su shes par byas so/ / de dag gis chos kyi 'khor lo 'khor ba phan tshun ma 'dres pa dag kyang yongs su gzung ngo/ /
“I have completed an ocean of the perfections. I have perceived the miraculous manifestations of complete buddhahood. I have held their wheels of Dharma each distinct from another.
the oceans of transcendent ways were fulfilled, I perceived their mystical transformations on attainment of enlightenment, I remembered their successive cycles of teaching without confusion,
de dag gi stobs mnyam pa nyid kyang khong du chud par byas so/ / de dag gi bstan pa yang dam pa'i chos zad pa'i mthar thug gi bar du yongs su bzung ngo/ /
“I have realized the equality of their strengths. I have held their teachings for as long as their Dharma remained.
I realized the equality of their powers, and I preserved their instructions till the end of the right doctrine.

kho bos de bzhin gshegs pa de dag thams cad kyi sngon gyi smon lam rnams kyang / smon lam gyi dkyil 'khor gyi ting nge 'dzin mngon par bsgrub pa'i stobs kyis/ rang gi sangs rgyas kyi zhing yongs su dag par bya ba'i phyir mngon par bsgrubs so/ /
“I have accomplished, through the power of the accomplishment of the samādhi of the field of prayer, the previous prayers of all those tathāgatas for the purification of my own buddha realm.
“I also realized all those buddhas’ past vows for the purification of their buddha-lands, by the power of accomplishment of concentration on the sphere of vows.

kho bos de bzhin gshegs pa de dag thams cad kyi sngon gyi byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa rnams kyang / spyod pa thams cad la 'jug pa'i ting nge 'dzin thob pa'i rang gi spyod pa yongs su dag par bya ba'i phyir mngon par bsgrubs so/ /
“I have accomplished, through the power of entering the samādhi of entering all conducts, the past practice of bodhisattva conduct by all those tathāgatas for the purification of my own conduct.
I also realized all those buddhas past enlightening practices for the purification of their own practice, by the power of attainment of concentration entering into all practices.
kho bos de bzhin gshegs pa de dag thams cad kyi pha rol tu phyin pa rnam par dag pa'ang / kun tu bzang po'i spyod pas 'byung ba'i stobs kyis mngon par bsgrubs so/ /
“I have accomplished, through the power of setting forth on completely good conduct, the pure perfections of all those tathāgatas.
I realized all those buddhas’ purification of the transcendent ways, by the power of setting out on universally good practice.
gzhan yang rigs kyi bu/ kho bo 'chag sa 'di na 'chags pa'i tshe/ phyogs kyi rgyud kyi sgo thams cad kyang shin tu rnam par lta ba'i ye shes kyi sgos mngon du 'gyur ro/ /
“Moreover, noble one, because of the gateway of the perfectly observant wisdom, while I am walking on this meditation walkway there come toward me the gateways of the continuums of all directions.
“Furthermore, as I walk here, all realms flow toward me because of keenly observant knowledge being brought to the fore:

'jig rten gyi khams kyi rgyud kyi sgo thams cad kyang / smon lam chen po mngon par bsgrubs pa'i stobs kyis sems bskyed pa gcig la 'jig rten gyi khams brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa 'da' zhing / yongs su dag par bya ba'i phyir rnam par 'grub par 'gyur ro/ /

“Through the arising of a single aspiration, the gateways of the continuums of all world realms are moving further away in order to purify the transcendence of an anabhilāpyānabhilāpyaparivarta of world realms through the power of accomplishing great prayers.
all worlds flow away from me for the purification of passing over untold worlds in a single thought, by the power of accomplishment of great vows.

sems kyi skad cig gcig la sems can gyi spyod pa'i tshul gyi sgo brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa dag kyang / byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po'i spyod pa dang / smon lam mngon par bsgrubs pa'i stobs kyis stobs bcu'i ye shes yongs su rdzogs par bya ba'i phyir mngon sum du 'gyur ro; ;

“In one instant of mind, through the power of accomplishing the bodhisattva’s completely good conduct and prayers, I directly perceive an anabhilāpyānabhilāpyaparivarta of gateways of the ways of conduct among beings in order to complete the wisdoms of the ten strengths.

In a single thought untold practical principles for sentient beings appear to me, for the fulfillment of the knowledge of the ten powers, by the power of carrying out the vows of practice of universally good enlightening beings.

sems bskyed pa gcig la sangs rgyas brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa mthong ba rnam par dag pa dag kyang snga phyi'i de bzhin gshegs pa rnams la mchod pa'i smon lam mngon par bsgrubs pa'i stobs kyis de bzhin gshegs pa sangs rgyas kyi zhing brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed la mchod pa dang / bsnyen bkur ba dang; rim gro bya ba'i phyir mngon du 'gyur ro/ /

“Through the arising of a single aspiration, through the power of accomplishing the prayers to make offerings to past and future buddhas, I directly perceive the vision of an anabhilāpyānabhilāpyaparivarta of buddha realms[788] in order to make offerings to, serve, and honor tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms in an anabhilāpyānabhilāpyaparivarta of buddha realms.

In a single thought the purities of visions of untold buddha-lands appear to me, so I may honor, attend, and serve as many buddhas as atoms in untold buddha-lands, by the power of carrying out the vow to serve former and future buddhas.

sems bskyed pa gcig la de bzhin gshegs pa brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa'i chos kyi sprin gyi char rnams kyang / chos kyi 'khor lo yongs su 'dzin pa'i gzungs dang / smon lam mngon par bsgrubs pa'i stobs kyis chos kyi tshul grangs med pa rnam par 'tshang rgya zhing khong du chud par bya ba'i phyir bsam pa la mngon par 'bab bo/ /

“Through the arising of a single aspiration, there falls rain from the clouds of Dharma of an anabhilāpyānabhilāpyaparivarta of tathāgatas through the power of accomplishing the prayers for[789] the mental retention of holding the Dharma wheels that[790] follow countless ways of the Dharma.

In a single thought the teachings of untold buddhas occur to my mind, by the power of carrying out the vow to remember wheels of teaching accompanied by countless ways of proceeding with the teachings in action.

sems bskyed pa gcig la byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa rgya mtsho brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa dag kyang / byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa mig 'phrul lta bu yongs su rdzogs par bya ba'i smon lam mngon par bsgrubs pa'i stobs kyi spyod pa'i dkyil 'khor thams cad yongs su dag par bya ba'i phyir mngon du 'gyur ro; ;

“Through the arising of a single aspiration, through the power of the accomplishment of the prayers to fulfill the bodhisattva conduct that are like magical illusions,[791] I directly perceive the ocean of the conduct of an anabhilāpyānabhilāpyaparivarta of bodhisattvas in order to purify all fields of conduct.

In a single thought, untold oceans of enlightening practices appear to me, for the purification of all spheres of practice, by the power of carrying out the vow to fulfill the practices of enlightening beings, which are all interrelated.

sems bskyed pa gcig la ting nge 'dzin rgya mtsho brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa dag kyang / ting nge 'dzin gyi sgo gcig tu/ ting nge 'dzin gyi sgo thams cad yang dag par 'du bar bya ba'i smon lam mngon par bsgrubs pa'i stobs kyis ting nge 'dzin gyi dkyil 'khor thams cad yongs su dag par bya ba'i phyir mngon du 'gyur ro/ /

“Through the arising of a single aspiration, through the power of the accomplishment of the prayer to concentrate all the fields of samādhi through a single samādhi, I directly perceive the ocean of an anabhilāpyānabhilāpyaparivarta of samādhis in order to purify all fields of samādhi.

In a single thought, untold oceans of concentrations become manifest to me, for the purification of all spheres of concentration, by the power of carrying out the vow to comprehend all ways of concentration in one way of concentration.

sems bskyed pa gcig la dbang po rgya mtsho brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa dag kyang / dran pa'i mthar phyin pa'i dbang po thob par bya ba'i smon lam mngon par bsgrubs pa'i stobs kyi dbang po'i 'khor lo dang / dus kyi 'khor lo thams cad kyi rjes su 'brang bar bya ba'i phyir mngon du 'gyur ro/ /

“Through the arising of a single aspiration, through the power of the accomplishment of the prayer to attain the power of the highest mindfulness, I directly perceive the ocean of an anabhilāpyānabhilāpyaparivarta of powers in order to manifest all the wheels of the powers and the wheels of time.
In a single thought untold oceans of faculties appear to me, for adaptation to all faculties and times, by the power of carrying out the vow to attain the faculty of ultimate mindfulness.

sems bskyed pa gcig la dus kyi 'khor lo brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa dag kyang / sems can zad mi shes pa zad par bya ba'i smon lam mngon par bsgrubs pa'i stobs kyis dus thams cad du chos kyi 'khor lo rab tu bskor ba'i phyir mngon du 'gyur ro/ /

“Through the arising of a single aspiration, through the power of the accomplishment of the prayer for the end of endless beings, I directly perceive an anabhilāpyānabhilāpyaparivarta of wheels of time in order to turn the wheels of Dharma in all times.
In a single thought, untold wheels of time are manifest to me, for conveying timely teachings, by the power of carrying out the endless vow to continue till the end of sentient beings.

sems bskyed pa gcig la dus rgya mtsho brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa thams cad kyang / dus gcig tu rnam par dgod pa'i tshul khong du chud pa'i ye shes snang ba'i smon lam mngon par bsgrubs pa'i stobs kyis/ 'jig rten gyi khams thams cad kyi dus gsum rnam par dgod pa'i phyir mngon sum du 'gyur te/

“Through the arising of a single aspiration, through the power of the accomplishment of the prayer for the light of the wisdom of realization, I directly perceive an anabhilāpyānabhilāpyaparivarta of oceans of all three[792] times in order to establish the three times in all world realms in a single time.[793]

In a single thought, untold oceans of all pasts, presents, and futures appear to me, for the definition of past, present, and future in all worlds, by the power of carrying out the vow for illumination of comprehensive knowledge.

rigs kyi bu/ kho bos ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa shin tu zhi bar mi 'gyur ba'i sgron ma zhes bya ba 'di shes par zad na/ kho bos byang chub sems dpa' bsam pa rdo rje lta bu dang ldan pa/ de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi rigs su rigs dang ldan par byung ba/ srog gi dbang po la rgyun chad pa med pa/ ye shes kyi sgron ma zhi bar 'gyur ba med pa/ mi shigs mi phyed pa'i lus dang ldan pa/ sgyu ma'i rnam pa lta bu'i gzugs shin tu grub pa rgyu'i chos mnyam pa'i yan lag dang nying lag tu ldan pa'i lus can; 'gro ba rnams kyi bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du/ rnam par dmigs par byed pa'i lus dang ldan pa/ 'gro ba thams cad dang 'dra ba'i gzugs dang / lus dang / kha dog dang dbyibs dang / chu zheng yongs su ston pa/ me mdag dang / me lce dang / dug dang / mtshon gyis mi tshugs pa'i lus dang ldan pa/ rdo rje ltar sra zhing khor yug ltar thub pa med pa'i lus can; bdud dang phas kyi rgol ba thams cad kyi stobs kyi stobs med par byed pa/ 'dzam bu chu klung gi gser gyi ri bo dang 'dra bar 'gro ba kun las mngon par 'phags pa'i lus dang ldan pa/ 'gro ba thams cad du rnam par dmigs pa'i gzhi dang ldan pa/ sgo thams cad du rnam par dmigs shing thos par 'gyur ba/ 'gro ba thams cad kyis ngor blta ba/ chos thams cad kyi sprin gyi 'byung gnas su gyur pa/ phyogs kun du rnam par snang ba/ sgrib pa'i ri thams cad rnam par gtor bas blta na mdzes pa/ mi dge ba'i rtsa ba thams cad shin tu 'joms pas shin tu dpa' bar snang ba/ dge ba'i rtsa ba rgya chen po'i rgyu mthun pa las byung bas blta na dga' ba/ 'byung bar shin tu dka' zhing dkon pas me tog u dum wA ra lta bu de dag gi spyod pa shes pa'am/ yon tan brjod par nus re skan/

“However, noble one, I know only this bodhisattva liberation called the never-extinguished lamp of wisdom.[794] How could I know or describe the qualities of the bodhisattvas whose aspiration is like a vajra; who have been born into the family that is the family of all the tathāgatas; who have the power of unceasing life; who have a lamp of wisdom that is never extinguished; who have indestructible, unbreakable bodies; who have accomplished a physical form that is like an illusion; who have bodies that have the limbs and smaller physical parts that accord with being phenomena dependent on causes; who have bodies that are perceived in accordance with the wishes of beings; who demonstrate forms, bodies, colors, shapes, and circumferences that are like those of all beings; who have bodies that are unharmed by burning embers, flames, poison, or weapons; whose bodies are as hard as vajras and as invincible[795] as the Cakravāla mountain range; who make the power of all māras and adversaries ineffective; who resemble a mountain of Jambu River gold; who have bodies that are superior to those of all beings; who are perceived as a refuge[796] by all beings; who are perceived and heard from all sides; who are looked up to with admiration by[797] all beings; who are the source of the clouds of all the Dharma; who illuminate every direction; who appear beautiful as a result of destroying the mountains of obscurations; who appear as supreme heroes because they defeat all the roots of demerit; who are a joy to see because they originate from vast roots of merit; and who are as rare as fig flowers?”

“So I know the enlightening liberation ‘the lamp of knowledge which is never extinguished.’ How can I know the practice or tell the virtues of the enlightening beings with adamantine will, who are born in the families of all buddhas, who have undying life-roots, whose light of knowledge is never extinguished, who have indestructible bodies, whose magical forms are without end, who embody the principle of relativity, who appear to sentient beings according to their mentalities, whose bodies appear like those of all beings in color, form, and size, whose bodies are not harmed by fire, poisons, or weapons, whose beings are invulnerable as adamantine mountains, who vitiate the power of all demons and opponents, who shine like mountains of gold, whose bodies stand out among all beings, whose bodies are perceived by all beings, who are heard of everywhere, who are looked up to by all sentient beings, who are mines of the earth of all truths, who illumine all quarters, who are seen without opposition because they have destroyed the mountains of obstructions, who are seen as supreme heroes because they extirpate all roots of evil, who are a welcome sight because they are products of many virtues, who are like udumbara flowers because they very rarely appear?

song / rigs kyi bu/ lho phyogs kyi rgyud 'di nyid na/ yul dge sbyong gi dkyil 'khor zhes bya ba na/ grong khyer sgo bzang po zhes bya ba yod de/ de na khye'u dbang po'i dbang phyug ces bya ba 'dug gi/ de'i gan du song la/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyad pa la bslab par bya ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bya ba dris shig /

“Depart, noble one. In this southern region there is a city called Sumukha in the land called Śramaṇamaṇḍala. “There dwells a boy by the name of Indriyeśvara. Go to him and ask him, ‘How does a bodhisattva train in bodhisattva conduct? How does a bodhisattva practice it?’ ”

“South of here, in the land of Shramanamandala, is a city called Sumukha, where a boy named Indriyeshvara lives. Go ask him how an enlightening being is to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings.”

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang / byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par gnon pa dang / nan tan rnam par dag par bya ba la brtson pa/ byang chub sems dpa'i stobs snang bas sems shin tu snang bar gyur pa/ byang chub sems dpa'i brtan pa/ gzhan gyis mi thub cing / brgal thag chad pa'i snying dang ldan pa/ byang chub sems dpa'i smon lam gyi go cha bzang pos sems zhum pa med pa/ byang chub sems dpa'i bsam pa brtan pas kun tu gnas shing / yongs su 'phel bar 'gyur ba la brtson pa/ byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa'i sprin gyi char yongs su 'dzin pa'i bsam pa dang ldan pa/ byang chub sems dpa'i chos kyi sprin gyi char yongs su mi ngoms pa'i rgyud dang ldan pa/ byang chub sems dpa' yon tan thams cad la 'jug pa'i smon lam mngon du gyur pa/ 'gro ba thams cad kyi kha lo sgyur bas yongs su sdud par bdag nyid yongs su gtong bar 'dod pa/ 'gro ba thams cad 'khor ba'i bas mtha'i dgon pa pa chen po las bzla bar 'dod pa/ dge ba'i gshes gnyen blta ba dang / mnyan pa dang / bsnyen bkur bas yongs su mi ngoms pa/ chos kyi rim gro tshad med pa bskyed pa dang ldan pa

Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, was dedicated to the pure prowess and practice of the bodhisattvas. His mind was illuminated by the light of the power of the bodhisattvas. In his heart he had mastered the unconquerable fortitude of the bodhisattvas. His mind was indefatigable because of the excellent armor of the resolution of the bodhisattvas. He was dedicated to the stability and vastness of the resolute aspiration of the bodhisattvas. He had the aspiration to possess all the rain from the clouds of bodhisattva conduct. He had the continuity of never having enough of the rain from the clouds of Dharma of the bodhisattvas. He had the aspiration directed toward realizing all the qualities of the bodhisattvas. He longed to send himself to be the embodiment of the charioteers for all beings. He longed to lead beings out beyond the great forest of saṃsāra. He never had enough of gazing upon, listening to, and honoring kalyāṇamitras. He had developed an immeasurable veneration for the Dharma.

Then, intent on purifying attainment of the valor of enlightening beings, his mind illumined by the light of the power of enlightening beings, with the invincible energy of enlightening beings in his heart, his mind girded with the armor of the steadfast vows of enlightening beings, the breadth of the firm basis of intent of enlightening beings on his mind, determined to maintain the multitude of practices of enlightening beings, never tiring of the ways of enlightening beings, resolved to attain all qualities of enlightening beings, desiring to offer himself as a charioteer for all beings, desiring to bring all beings across the wasteland of the mundane whirl, never tiring of seeing, listening to, and attending spiritual benefactors, with immeasurable respect for the Teaching,

des/ dge slong blta na sdug pa'i rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te/ dge slong blta na sdug pa la lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas/ yang dang yang bltas te/ dge slong blta na sdug pa'i drung nas song ngo// //

Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, bowed his head to the feet of the bhikṣu Sudarśana, circumambulated the bhikṣu Sudarśana many hundreds of thousands of times, keeping him to his right, and, looking back again and again, departed from the presence of the bhikṣu Sudarśana. [B1]
Sudhana paid his respects to the monk Sudarshana and left.
bam po dgu bcu rtsa bzhi pa/

Chapter 15. Indriyeśvara
Indriyeshvara

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang dge slong blta na sdug pa de'i gdams ngag rjes su zlos shing / spel ba dang / bstud pa dang / rab tu dbye ba dang / bshad pa dang / so sor rnam par sgom pa dang / brjod pa dang / yang dag par bstan pa dang / rjes su bsam pa dang / mngon par 'jug pa bya ba dang; bkur ba dang / khong du chud par bya ba dang / yang dag par gzhol bar bya ba dang / yang dang yang bzlas pa dang / shin tu rtogs par bya ba dang / rab tu bstan pa dang / snang bar bya ba dang / rjes su rnam par lta bar byed cing /

Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, recited,[798] promulgated, presented,[799] investigated, elucidated, reflected on, described, taught, contemplated, bestowed, understood, was immersed in, repeated again and again, realized, propounded, illuminated, and surveyed the teaching of the bhikṣu Sudarśana.

Thinking about the instruction of Sudarshana, applying it, passing it on, investigating it, talking about it, revealing it, contemplating it, approaching it, following it, reflecting on the principle of his teaching, entering into it, bringing it near, analyzing it, explaining it, elucidating it, pondering it,
lha dang / klu dang / gnod sbyin dang / dri za'i 'khor dang bcas pa de mthar gyis yul dge sbyong gi dkyil 'khor gyi grong khyer sgo bzang po gang na ba der phyin te/
He eventually, with an entourage of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, and gandharvas, arrived at the city of Sumukha in the land called Śramaṇamaṇḍala.
Sudhana, surrounded by celestial beings, spirits, and cherubim, made his way to the city of Sumukha in the land of Shramanamandala,

khye'u dbang po'i dbang phyug yongs su tshol tshol ba las/ de'i steng gi bar snang las/ lha dang / klu dang / gnod sbyin dang / dri za rnams kyis bos pa/ rigs kyi bu/ khye'u'i dbang po'i dbang phyug ni chu klung gi chu 'dus dang nye ba zhig na/ byis pa stong phrag bcu tsam gyis bskor te/ bye ma la rtse bas rtse zhing 'dug go /

He searched for the boy Indriyeśvara until the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, and gandharvas in the sky above called down, “Noble one, the boy Indriyeśvara, accompanied by ten thousand other children, is playing in the sand at the conflux of the rivers.”
looking for the boy Indriyeshvara.

zhes nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang grong khyer sgo bzang po dang nye ba'i chu klung gi chu 'dus gang na ba der song ste/ phyin pa dang / des khye'u dbang po'i dbang phyug byis pa stong phrag bcu tsam gyis bskor cing / bye ma la rtse bas rtse ba mthong ngo/ /

Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, went into the city of Sumukha toward the confluence of the rivers. When he arrived there, he saw the boy Indriyeśvara accompanied by ten thousand children, playing in the sand.
Then, when Sudhana got to the city Sumukha, near a river junction, he saw Indriyeshvara, surrounded by ten thousand boys, playing in the sand.

mthong nas kyang khye'u dbang po'i dbang phyug ga na ba der song ste/ khye'u dbang po'i dbang phyug gi rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal nas/ khye'u dbang po'i dbang phyug la lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas/ khye'u dbang po'i dbang phyug gi mdun du 'dug ste thal mo sbyar nas/ 'di skad ces smras so/ /

When he saw the boy Indriyeśvara, he approached him, bowed his head to the boy Indriyeśvara’s feet, circumambulated the boy Indriyeśvara many hundreds of thousands of times, keeping him to his right, and then sat down before the boy Indriyeśvara. He placed the palms of his hands together and said,
He went up to Indriyeshvara, paid his respects, and said,

'phags pa/ bdag gis bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed na/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bgyi ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bgyi ba ma 'tshal te/
“Ārya, I have developed the aspiration for the highest, complete enlightenment. How does a bodhisattva train in bodhisattva conduct? In what way does a bodhisattva practice it?”
“Noble one, I have set my mind on supreme perfect enlightenment, but I do not know how an enlightening being is to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings.”

'phags pa ni/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams la gdams ngag dang / rjes su bstan pa mdzad do zhes bdag gis thos na/ 'phags pa/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bgyi ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bgyi ba bdag la bshad du gsol/
“Ārya, I have heard that you teach and give instructions to bodhisattvas. Therefore, Ārya, teach me how bodhisattvas train in bodhisattva conduct and in what way they practice it!”

smras pa/ rigs kyi bu/ kho bo ni 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pas/ yi ge dang / grangs dang / brda dang / rtsis kyi tshul bslabs te/ bzo thams cad mngon par shes pa dang ldan pa zhes bya ba'i ye shes kyi sgor bcug go /

Indriyeśvara said, “Noble one, Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta has taught me writing, numbers, symbols, and counting so that I entered through the gateway called the wisdom that possesses clairvoyance in all crafts.
Indriyeshvara said, “I have been taught writing and mathematics by Manjushri, and have been led into the door of knowledge encompassing higher knowledge of all practical arts.
de ltar rigs kyi bu/ kho bos ni 'jig rten na yi ge dang / ming gi rnam pa dang /
“Thus, noble one, I know all writing and terminology in this world;
So I know all the various arts and crafts and sciences in the world dealing with writing,
grangs dang / rtsis dang / brda dang / shol thabs shes par bya ba dang / bzo sna tshogs shes par bya ba dang /
all numbers, calculations, symbols, the knowledge of dice throwing,[800] and the knowledge of the various crafts;
mathematics and symbols,
khams kyi cho ga dang /
physiology;
physiology,
dug gso ba'i thabs dang /
methods to cure poisoning;
rhetoric,
skem pa dang / brjed byed dang / 'byung po'i gdon gyis btab pa gso ba dang /
exorcising śoṣas, apasmāras, bhūtas, pretas, and demons;
physical and mental health,
grong dang / grong khyer dang / tshong 'dus dang / bza' shing gi ra ba dang / dka' thub kyi nags tshal dang / gnas rnam par dgod pa shes par bya ba dang /
the knowledge of where to establish villages, towns, marketplaces, cities,[801] parks, and forest groves for ascetics;
city planning,
ra ba dang / khang pa dang / skar khung dang / khang pa brtsegs pa'i tshad shes par bya ba dang /
the knowledge of the measurements of walls, houses, windows, and kūṭāgāras;
architecture and construction,
'khrul 'khor dang / shing rta sbyar ba'i tshul sna tshogs shes par bya ba dang /
the knowledge of how to make various machines and chariots;
mechanics and engineering,
dge mi dge dang / 'jigs mi 'jigs kyi ltas dang / mtshan ma shes par bya ba dang /
the knowledge of good and bad omens, omens of danger and safety;
divination,
rmos dang / tshong dang / rnam par spyad par sbyar ba'i cho ga shes par bya ba dang /
the knowledge of the practices of farming and business;
agriculture and commerce,
sems can gyi yan lag dang / nying lag gi mtshan gyi rgyud dang / rgyus dang / rnam par spyad pa shes par bya ba dang /
the knowledge of the analysis of the signs of the movement and characteristics of the limbs and the minor extensions of the body;
conduct and manners,
bde 'gro dang / ngan song gi las kyi lam rnam par dag par bya ba'i tshul shes par bya ba dang /
the knowledge of the ways of purifying the path of karma that leads to the higher realms or the lower existences;
good and bad actions,
dge ba dang mi dge ba'i chos dang / tshogs mchod pa shes par bya ba dang /
the knowledge of good and bad groups and offerings;
good and bad principles,
bde 'gro dang / ngan song gi tshogs shes par bya ba dang /
the knowledge of the accumulations that lead to the higher existences or to the lower existences;
what makes for felicity and what for misery,
nyan thos dang / rang sangs rgyas kyi theg pa'i tshogs shes par bya ba dang /
the knowledge of the accumulations that lead to the Śrāvakayāna and Pratyekabuddhayāna;
what is necessary for the vehicles of buddhas, disciples, and individual illuminates,
de bzhin gshegs pa'i sa'i tshogs shes par bya ba dang /
the knowledge of the accumulations that lead to the level of the tathāgatas;
what is necessary for buddhahood, and
rgyu dang / byed pa dang / sbyor ba'i rgyud shes par bya ba
and the knowledge of the processes of application to causes and actions.
behavior linking reason and action.
ji snyed pa de dag thams cad shes te/

I know all these sciences,

de dag la sems can yongs su gzung bar byed do/ / rab tu dgod par byed do/ / yongs su gzhog par byed do/ / slob tu 'dzud do/ / sbyong du 'dzud do/ / brtan par byed do/ / lhur len par byed do/ / rdzogs par byed do/ / yongs su sgrub par byed do/ / yongs su spyod par byed do/ / gsal bar bstan par byed do/ / rnam par 'phel bar byed do/ / mtshan mar byed do/ / mthar phyin par byed do/ / rnam par sbyong bar byed do/ / dri ma med par byed do/ / shin tu dag par byed do/ / 'od gsal zhing dang bar byed do/ / shin tu yangs par byed do/ /

“I make all beings enter into those knowledges, settle them in those knowledges, establish them in those knowledges, make them study those knowledges, make them practice those knowledges, make them stable in those knowledges, make them dedicated to those knowledges, make them complete those knowledges, make them accomplished in those knowledges, make them use those knowledges, make them elevate those knowledges, make them increase those knowledges, make those knowledges effective, bring those knowledges to their conclusion, make them purify those knowledges, make those knowledges stainless, make those knowledges shine, make those knowledges bright and clear, and make those knowledges vast.
and I also introduce and teach them to people, and get people to study and practice them, to master and develop them, using these as means to purify, refine, and broaden people.
de ltar rigs kyi bu/ kho bos byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi rtsis kyi tshul shes pa de gang zhe na/
“Thus, noble one, I know the way of calculations of the bodhisattvas. What is it?
“I myself know enlightening beings’ method of reckoning, which goes like this:

brgya stong phrag brgya na bye ba'o/ / bye ba bye ba na khod khod do/ / khod khod khod khod na tha da dgu'o/ / thad dgu thad dgu na khrig khrig go / khrig khrig khrig khrig na thams thams so/ / thams thams thams thams na myad myid do/ / myad myid myad myid na gang ya'o/ / gang ya gang ya na ban bun no/ /

“A hundred thousand times a hundred is ten million.[802] Ten million times ten million is an ayuta.[803] An ayuta times an ayuta is a niyuta.[804] A niyuta times a niyuta is a bimbara.[805] A bimbara times a bimbara is a kiṃkara.[806] A kiṃkara times a kiṃkara is an agara.[807] An agara times an agara is a pravara.[808] A pravara times a pravara is a mapara.[809]
ban bun ban bun na phyar phyur ro/ /
A mapara times a mapara is an avara.[810]
phyar phyur phyar phyur na lcag lcig go /
An avara times an avara is a tapara.[811]
a mapara squared is a tapara;

lcag lcig lcag lcig na byang bying ngo/ / byang bying byang bying na chem chem mo/ / chem chem chem chem na phyal phyol lo/ / phyal phyol phyal phyol na khyud khyud do/ / khyud khyud khyud khyud na zar zer ro/ /
A tapara times a tapara is a sīma.[812] A sīma times a sīma is a yāma.[813] A yāma times a yāma is a nena.[814] A nena times a nena is an avaga.[815] An avaga times an avaga is one mṛgava.[816]
One mṛgava times one mṛgava is one vināha.[817]
zar zer zar zer na khrib khrib bo/ /

khrib khrib khrib khrib na ya gangs so/ /

a viraga squared is a vigava;
ya gangs ya gangs na cho ma'o/ / cho ma cho ma na khram khrim mo/ / khram khrim khram khrim na nab nub bo/ /
A vigava times a vigava is a saṃkrama.[821] A saṃkrama times a saṃkrama is a visara.[822] A visara times a visara is a vibhaja.[823]
nab nub nab nub na sang sang ngo/ / sang sang sang sang na brgyud yas so/ / brgyud yas brgyud yas na btang yas so/ / btang yas btang yas na bkra yar ro/ / bkra yar bkra yar na gsa' yas so/ /

gsa' yas gsa' yas na mtshungs med do/ / mtshungs med mtshungs med na lam lum mo/ / lam lum lam lum na yal yol lo/ /
A tulana times a tulana is an atula.[830] An atula times an atula is a varaṇa.[831] A varaṇa times a varaṇa is a vivaraṇa.[832]
yal yol yal yol na khral khrul lo/ / khral khrul khral khrul na thud thud do/ /
A vivaraṇa times a vivaraṇa is an avana.[833] An avana times an avana is a thavana.[834]
an ilana squared is an avana; an avana squared is a thavana;

a thavana squared is a viparya;
thud thud thud thud na bsam phyod do/ /

a viparya squared is a samaya;
A samarya times a samarya is a viturṇa.[837]
a samaya squared is a viturna;
bsam phyod bsam phyod na brang breng ngo/ / brang breng brang breng na bgrod yas so/ /
A viturṇa times a viturṇa is an hetura.[838] A hetura times a hetura is a vicāra.[839]
a viturna squared is a hetura; a hetura squared is a vicara;
A vicāra times a vicāra is a visāra.[840]

bgrod yas bgrod yas na bsngo yas so/ / bsngo yas bsngo yas na zang yag go/ zang yag zang yag na 'phro bkye'o/ / 'phro bkye 'phro bkye na rtse 'phyo'o/ / rtse 'phyo rtse 'phyo na yong tan no/ / yong tan yong tan na brug g.yos so/ /

A visāra times a visāra is a vyatyasta.[841] A vyatyasta times a vyatyasta is an abhyudgata.[842] An abhyudgata times an abhyudgata is a viśiṣṭa.[843] A viśiṣṭa times a viśiṣṭa is a nivala.[844] A nivala times a nivala is a haribha.[845] A haribha times a haribha is a vikṣobha.[846]
brug g.yos brug g.yos na sang yal lo/ / sang yal sang yal na 'thing yug go /

a vikshoba squared is a halita; a halita squared is a hari;

a hari squared is an aloka;
'thing yug 'thing yug na yid 'phyo'o/ / yid 'phyo yid 'phyo na nab neb bo/ /

an aloka squared is a drshvanta; a drshvanta squared is a hetuna;

A haruṇa times a haruṇa is an ela.[854] An ela times an ela is a dumela.[855] A dumela times a dumela is a kṣemu.[856]
A kṣemu times a kṣemu is an akṣayamukta.[857]
bgrang yas bgrang yas na thug yal lo/ /
An akṣayamukta times an akṣayamukta is an elada.[858]
a kshemu squared is an eluda;
thug yal thug yal na shang shang ngo/ /
An elada times an elada is a māluda.[859]
an eluda squared is a bhaluda;
A māluda times a māluda is a maṇḍumā.[860] A maṇḍumā times a maṇḍumā is a viṣamatā.[861]
shang shang shang shang na yag yag go / yag yag yag yag na tham thim mo/ /
A viṣamatā times a viṣamatā is a samatā.[862] A samatā times a samatā is a visada.[863]
a bhaluda squared is a samata; a samata squared is a visada;
tham thim tham thim na rlom bsnyal lo/ /
A visada times a visada is a pramantā.[864]
rlom bsnyal rlom bsnyal na gzhal 'phyos so/ / gzhal 'phyos gzhal 'phyos na gzhal yal lo/ /
A pramantā times a pramantā is a pramātra.[865] A pramātra times a pramātra is an amātra.[866]
a visada squared is a pramatra; a pramatra squared is an amantra;
gzhal yal gzhal yal na gzhal med do/ / gzhal med gzhal med na gzhal 'khor to/ / gzhal 'khor gzhal 'khor na gzhal thim mo/ /
An amātra times an amātra is a bhramātra.[867] A bhramātra times a bhramātra is a gamātra.[868] A gamātra times a gamātra is a namātra.[869]
gzhal thim gzhal thim na gar gzhal lo/ / gar gzhal gar gzhal na gzhal sangs so/ / gzhal sangs gzhal sangs na gzhal thag go / gzhal thag gzhal thag na gzhal phul lo/ /
A namātra times a namātra is a hemātra.[870] A hemātra times a hemātra is a vimātra.[871] A vimātra times a vimātra is a paramātra.[872] A paramātra times a paramātra is a śivamātra.[873]
gzhal phul gzhal phul na gzhal zhi'o/ / gzhal zhi gzhal zhi na 'phyo 'gyur ro/ /
A śivamātra times a śivamātra is an ela.[874] An ela times an ela is a vela.[875]
a shivamantra squared is a delu; a delu squared is a velu;
'phyo 'gyur 'phyo 'gyur na nyar nyer ro/ /
A vela times a vela is a tela.[876]
A tela times a tela is a śaila.[877]
nyar nyer nyar nyer na phyag phyig go /

a velu squared is a gelu;

phyag phyig phyag phyig na zal zul lo/ /

a gelu squared is a khelu;

a khelu squared is a nelu; a nelu squared is a bhelu;
zal zul zal zul na sal sal lo/ / sal sal sal sal na g.yo ldeg go / g.yo ldeg g.yo ldeg na phan phun no/ /
A bhela times a bhela is a kela .[883] A kela times a kela is a sela.[884] A sela times a sela is a pela.[885]
phan phun phan phun na brnang ya'o/ /

brnang ya brnang ya na rem 'drol lo/ / rem 'drol rem 'drol na rdzi ngad do/ /

a pelu squared is a melu; a melu squared is a sarada;
rdzi ngad rdzi ngad na rdzi rdul lo/ /

rdzi rdul rdzi rdul na phun yol lo/ /
A māruta times a māruta is a meruda.[890]
a sarada squared is a bherudu;

a bherudu squared is a kheludu;
phun yol phun yol na ngad ngad do/ / ngad ngad ngad ngad na bgrang brtsi'o/ / bgrang brtsi bgrang brtsi na zab bgrang ngo/ / zab bgrang zab bgrang na dga' rkyang ngo/ /
A kheluda times a kheluda is a māluda.[892] A māluda times a māluda is a samula.[893] A samula times a samula is an ayava.[894] An ayava times an ayava is a kamala.[895]
dga' rkyang dga' rkyang na gzhung 'dal lo/ / gzhung 'dal gzhung 'dal na khrug phyad do/ /

a kamala squared is an agava; an agava squared is an ataru;

an ataru squared is a helura;

bgrang yas bgrang yas na byim 'phyo'o/ /

byim 'phyo byim 'phyon ya me'o/ /

ya me ya me na bsnyal yas so/ / bsnyal yas bsnyal yas na ldab ldeb bo/ / ldab ldeb ldab ldeb na 'ban chad do/ /
A vivara times a vivara is a bimba.[904] A bimba times a bimba is a caraṇa.[905] A caraṇa times a caraṇa is a carama.[906]
'ban chad 'ban chad na phang phung ngo/ /

phang phung phang phung na khye'u tsang ngo/ /

khye'u tsang khye'u tsang na zhung zung ngo/ / zhung zung zhung zung na mchog yal lo/ / mchog yal mchog yal na mtha' rdul lo/ / mtha' rdul mtha' rdul na yun 'gyangs so/ /
A dhamana times a dhamana is a pramada.[910] A pramada times a pramada is a nigama.[911] A nigama times a nigama is an upavarta.[912] An upavarta times an upavarta is a nirdeśa.[913]
yun 'gyangs yun 'gyangs na bun lob bo/ / bun lob bun lob na lam lom mo/ / lam lom lam lom na bsnyad yas so/ /
A nirdeśa times a nirdeśa is an akṣaya.[914] An akṣaya times an akṣaya is a saṃbhūta.[915] A saṃbhūta times a saṃbhūta is an amama.[916]

bsnyad yas bsnyad yas na lang ling ngo/ / lang ling lang ling na ljab ljib bo/ / ljab ljib ljab ljib na mi brtsal to/ / mi brtsal mi brtsal na 'byams yas so/ / 'byams yas 'byams yas na nga 'grang ngo/ /

An amama times an amama is an avada.[917] An avada times an avada is an utpala.[918] An utpala times an utpala is a padma.[919] A padma times a padma is a saṃkhya.[920] A saṃkhya times a saṃkhya is a gati.[921]
nga 'grang nga 'grang na smos yal lo/ /
A gati times a gati is an upagama.[922]
a gati squared is an upama;
smos yal smos yal na bkra chal lo/ / bkra chal bkra chal na lo rgyas so/ / lo rgyas lo rgyas na 'bum rdib bo/ / 'bum rdib 'bum rdib na gam gum mo/ / gam gum gam gum na la lo'o/ /
An upagama times an upagama is an aupamya.[923]
an upama squared is an aupamya;
la lo la lo na bgrang 'phyos so/ /
An aupamya times an aupamya is an asaṃkhyeya.[924]
an aupamya squared is incalculable;
bgrang 'phyos bgrang 'phyos na bgrang 'phyos la bsgres pa'o/ /
An asaṃkhyeya times an asaṃkhyeya is an asaṃkhyeyaparivarta.[925]
'grang 'phyos la bsgres pa bgrang 'phyos la bsgres pa na/ dpag yas so/ /
An asaṃkhyeyaparivarta times an asaṃkhyeyaparivarta is an aparimāṇa.[926]
an incalculable to the fourth power is measureless;
dpag yas dpag yas na dpag yas la bsgres pa'o/ /
An aparimāṇa times an aparimāṇa is an aparimāṇaparivarta.[927]
a measureless to the fourth power is boundless;

dpag yas la bsgres pa dpag yas la bsgres pa na/ yal phyod do/ / yal phyod yal phyod na yal phyod la bsgres pa'o/ / yal phyod la bsgres pa yal phyod la bsgres pa na/ mu yal lo; ; mu yal mu yal na/ mu yal la bsgres pa'o/ / mu yal la bsgres pa mu yal la bsgres pa na/ bgrang yol lo/ / bgrang yol bgrang yol na/ bgrang yol la bsgres pa'o/ /

An aparimāṇaparivarta times an aparimāṇaparivarta is an aparyanta.[928] An aparyanta times an aparyanta is an aparyantaparivarta.[929] An aparyantaparivarta times an aparyantaparivarta is an asamanta.[930] An asamanta times an asamanta is an asamantaparivarta.[931] An asamantaparivarta times an asamantaparivarta is an agaṇeya.[932] An agaṇeya times an agaṇeya is an agaṇeyaparivarta.[933]
bgrang yol la 'gres pa bgrang yol la bsgres na/ mi 'jal to/ /
An agaṇeyaparivarta times an agaṇeyaparivarta is an atulya.[934]
a boundless to the fourth power is incomparable;
mi 'jal mi 'jal na/ mi 'jal la bsgres pa'o/ /
An atulya times an atulya is an atulyaparivarta.[935]
mi 'jal la bsgres pa mi 'jal la bsgres na/ bsam phyod do/ /
An atulyaparivarta times an atulyaparivarta is an acintya.[936]
an incomparable to the fourth power is uncountable;
bsam phyod bsam phyod na/ bsam phyod la bsgres pa'o/ /
An acintya times an acintya is an acintyaparivarta.[937]
an uncountable to the fourth power is unequaled;
bsam phyod la bsgres pa bsam phyod la bsgres na/ mtha' 'byams so/ /
An acintyaparivarta times an acintyaparivarta is an aparyanta.[938]
an unequaled to the fourth power is inconceivable;
An aparyanta times an aparyanta is an aparyantaparivarta.[939]
mtha' 'byams mtha' 'byams na/ dpag thag go;
An aparyantaparivarta times an aparyantaparivarta is an amāpya.[940]
an inconceivable to the fourth power is immeasurable;
dpag thag dpag thag na/ dpag thag la bsgres pa'o/ /
An amāpya times an amāpya is an amāpyaparivarta.[941]
dpag thag la bsgres pa dpag thag la bsgres na/ brjod du med pa'o/ /
An amāpyaparivarta times an amāpyaparivarta is an anabhilāpya.[942]
an immeasureable to the fourth power is unspeakable;
brjod du med pa brjod du med pa na/ brjod du med pa la bsgres pa'o/ /
An anabhilāpya times an anabhilāpya is an anabhilāpyaparivarta.[943]
an unspeakable to the fourth power is unspeakably unspeakable;
An anabhilāpyaparivarta times an anabhilāpyaparivarta is an anabhilāpyānabhilāpya.[944]
brjod du med pa la bsgres pa brjod du med pa la bsgres na/ brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa la bsgres pa shin tu bstan pa'o/ /
An anabhilāpyānabhilāpya[945] times an anabhilāpyānabhilāpya is an anabhilāpyānabhilāpyaparivarta.”[946]
and unspeakably unspeakable squared is untold.”

de'i mdun na bye ma'i phung po chen po dpag tshad du ma'i tshad dang ldan pa zhig 'dug 'dug pa las 'di la bye ma'i 'bru 'di snyed cig yod do/ /zhes bya ba nas/ bye ma'i 'bru brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa la bsgres pa 'di snyed cig yod do/ /zhes rab tu phye nas bgrang brtsis te grangs su bcad do/ /

In front of Indriyeśvara there was a heap of sand that was many yojanas high. He counted how many grains of sand there were in that heap, beginning with “the number of grains of sand in this mound” and continuing until he said, “there are an anabhilāpyānabhilāpyaparivarta of grains of sand in this heap.”
He counted out the grains of sand in the miles-wide mass of sand before him, telling how many grains of sand there were, and how many unspeakable numbers of grains of sand there were;
des bye ma'i phung po de rtsis kyi brdar bstan pas shin tu bstan nas 'di skad ces smras so/ /
Having taught Sudhana through the teaching that stipulated the number of grains of sand in that heap of sand, he said,
then, having indicated this by these conventions of enumeration, he said,
rigs kyi bu/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi bgrang ba'i tshul 'di ni/ 'jig rten gyi khams gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa kun na'ang yod do/ /
“Noble one, this method of counting of the bodhisattvas continues from one world realm to another.
“This counting device serves enlightening beings for the succession of worlds;

byang chub sems dpa' rnams ni bgrang ba'i tshul 'dis/ shar phyogs kyi 'jig rten gyi khams 'byams klas pa dag kyang bgrang zhing brtsi'o/ / de bzhin du lho phyogs dang / nub phyogs dang / byang phyogs dang / byang shar gyi phyogs mtshams dang / shar lho'i phyogs mtshams dang / lho nub kyi phyogs mtshams dang / nub byang gi phyogs mtshams dang / 'og dang / steng gi phyogs su'ang byang chub sems dpa' rnams bgrang ba'i tshul 'dis/ 'jig rten gyi khams 'byams klas pa dag kyang bgrang zhing brtsi'o /

With this method of counting of the bodhisattvas, one can calculate the number of the entire extent of world realms in the eastern direction. In the same way, with this method of counting of the bodhisattvas, one can calculate the number of the entire extent of world realms in the southern direction, in the western direction, in the northern direction, in the northeastern direction, in the southeastern direction, in the southwestern direction, in the northwestern direction, in the upward direction, and in the downward direction.
by this method of counting they count the multitudes of worlds in the ten directions.

rigs kyi bu/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi bgrang ba'i tshul 'di ni/ phyogs bcu'i 'jig rten gyi khams kyi ming du bya ba/ gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa bstan du yod pa thams cad na'ang yod do/ / byang chub sems dpa' rnams ni bgrang ba'i tshul 'dis phyogs bcu'i 'jig rten gyi khams kyi ming gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa bgrang zhing brtsi'o /

“Noble one, with this method of counting of the bodhisattvas, the entire extent of the succession of the names of world realms in the ten directions are taught; with this method of counting of the bodhisattvas, the entire extent of the succession of the names of world realms in the ten directions is counted.

This method of counting serves enlightening beings in indicating the worlds in the ten directions in an orderly continuum. By this method of counting, enlightening beings count the string of names of the worlds in the ten directions.

ji ltar 'jig rten gyi khams kyi ming gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa bstan du yod pa de bzhin du/ phyogs bcu'i bskal pa'i ming gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa bstan du yod pa dang / sangs rgyas kyi mtshan gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa bstan du yod pa dang / chos kyi ming gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa bstan du yod pa dang / sems can gyi ming gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa bstan du yod pa dang; las kyi ming gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa bstan du yod pa kun la'ang 'jug ste/

“Just as the entire extent of the succession of world realms in the ten directions is taught, in the same way the succession of names of kalpas in the ten directions is taught, the succession of the names of buddhas is taught, the succession of the names of Dharmas is taught, the succession of the names of beings is taught, and the succession of the names of actions is taught, so that all these are comprehended.

As in the case of indications of the string of names of worlds, in the same way this method of counting serves enlightening beings in indicating the successions of names of eons, buddhas, doctrines, sentient beings, actions, and indeed everything in the ten directions.
byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi bgrang ba'i tshul 'di nyid ni/ phyogs bcu na ming du bya ba gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa bstan du rung ba ji snyed pa thams cad la'ang 'jug ste/
“With this method of counting of the bodhisattvas, the entirety of however many successions of names that can be taught and that are in the ten directions is comprehended in full.
byang chub sems dpa' rnams ni bgrang ba'i tshul 'dis/ phyogs bcu na ming gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa ji snyed yod pa thams cad kyang bgrang zhing brtsi'o/ /
“With this method of counting of the bodhisattvas, the entirety of however many successions of names that can be taught and that are in the ten directions is counted in full.

de ltar rigs kyi bu/ kho bo pa ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i ye shes snang ba chos thams cad shes par bya ba'i bzo mngon par shes pa dang ldan pa 'di shes par zad na/ kho bos byang chub sems dpa' 'gro ba thams cad kyi grangs la zhugs pa/ chos kyi tshul thams cad kyi grangs la zhugs pa/ dus gsum gyi grangs la zhugs pa/ sems can thams cad kyi grangs la zhugs pa/ chos kyi phung po thams cad kyi grangs la zhugs pa/ sangs rgyas dang / byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi grangs la zhugs pa/ chos thams cad kyi ming gi 'khor lo dbang bsgyur ba de dag gi spyod pa shes pa'am/ yon tan brjod pa'am/ spyod yul smos pa'am/ yul brjod pa'am/ stobs bsngags pa'am/ bsam pa bstan pa'am/ tshogs yongs su brjod pa'am/ smon lam bshad par bya ba'am/ spyod pa yongs su bstan pa'am/ pha rol tu phyin pa yongs su dag pa mngon par brjod pa'am/ yang dag par bsgrub pa yongs su dag pa'am/ yang dag par bstan pa'am/ ting nge 'dzin gyi khyad par smos pa'am/ ye shes snang ba khod du chud par nus re skan/

“However, noble one, in that way I know only this light of bodhisattva wisdom that is the possession of the clairvoyance of crafts that is the knowledge of all phenomena. How could I know the conduct of the bodhisattvas who engage with the number of all beings, who engage with the number of all the accumulations of Dharmas, who engage with the number of all the buddhas and bodhisattvas, and who have power over the wheel of the names of all the Dharmas? How could I describe their qualities? How could I reveal[947] the range of their activity? How could I elucidate the scope of their knowledge? How could I praise their strengths? How could I proclaim their resolute intentions? How could I cast light[948] on their accumulations? How could I explain their prayers? How could I teach their conduct? How could I speak of their pure perfections? How could I make clear their pure attainments? How could I describe the range[949] of their samādhis? How could I comprehend the light of their wisdom?

“I know this light of knowledge of enlightening beings which is characterized by higher knowledge of all arts and sciences. How can I know the practice, tell of the virtues, indicate the range, show the sphere, describe the power, show the will, elucidate the preparation, explain the commitment, show the conduct, illumine the purity of transcendent ways, expound the purity of accomplishment, tell of the sphere of concentration, or approach the light of knowledge of the enlightening beings who know the number of all worlds, who know the number of all modes of spiritual practice, who know the number of pasts, presents, and futures, who know the number of all sentient beings, who know the number of all bodies of doctrine, who know the number of enlightenments of all buddhas, and who command the wheel of names of all the teachings?”

song / rigs kyi bu/ lho phyogs kyi rgyud 'di nyid na/ grong khyer rgya mtsho brtan pa zhes bya ba yod de/ de na dge bsnyen ma phul du byung ba zhes bya ba 'dug gi/ de'i gan du song la ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bya ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bya ba dris shig /

“Depart, noble one. In this southern region there is a town called Samudrapratiṣṭhāna, where dwells an upāsikā by the name of Prabhūtā. Go to her and ask her, ‘How should a bodhisattva train in bodhisattva conduct? How should a bodhisattva practice it?’ ”
“South of here is a city called Samudrapratishthana, where lives a lay devotee named Prabhuta. Go ask her how an enlightening being is to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings.”

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi tshig thos nas spu g.yos te/ dga' ba chen po'i shugs skyes nas/ rab tu dga' ba'i yid dang ldan par gyur pa/ ngo mtshar gyi bsam pa rin po che rab tu dkon pa thob pa/ 'gro ba mang po la phan pa'i sems dang / bsam pas byung ba/ sangs rgyas skyes pa gcig nas gcig tu brgyud par 'gro ba la dbang bsgyur ba/ chos kyi dkyil 'khor rnam par dag pa'i blo gros la rten pa/ thams cad du rjes su song ba'i rigs rnam par phye bas 'byung ba bstan pa la brtson pa/ dus gsum gyi dbyings su ma 'dres pa'i sangs rgyas gyi yul dang ldan pa/ bsod nams mi zad pa'i rgya mtsho las byung ba'i sems dang ldan pa/ ye shes kyi snang ba chen po la dbang bsgyur ba khams gsum gyi khyim du sdud pa'i sgo shin tu gcod pa drung nas song ngo/ /

When Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, heard the words of the kalyāṇamitra, the hairs on his body rose, he felt a powerful great happiness, and he had great joy in his mind. He had obtained this rare, wonderful jewel of motivation. He had developed the motivation of intending to benefit many beings. He had the power to encounter the successive appearances of the buddhas. He was dedicated to understanding the pure field of the Dharma. He was dedicated to demonstrating setting forth to liberation in different ways appropriate to all places.[950] He knew the distinct ranges of activity of the buddhas in the levels of the three times. He had a state of mind that had arisen from an inexhaustible ocean of merit. He had the power of the illumination of great wisdom. He had broken open the gate that sealed beings within the city[951] of the three realms.

Having heard the words of the spiritual benefactor, Sudhana was thrilled and overjoyed; he paid his respects and took leave of Indriyeshvara, having obtained the treasure of will that is rare and most difficult to obtain, setting out to act benevolently toward all, freely able to perceive the succession of emergence of buddhas, intent on the wisdom to clarify the sphere of the Teaching, intent on showing the various means of emancipation everywhere, aware of past, present, and future without confusion, his mind an inexhaustible ocean of virtue, in control of the light of great knowledge, having broken open the doors of confinement in the city of mundane existence.

des/ khye'u dbang po'i dbang phyug gi rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal nas/ khye'u dbang po'i dbang phyug la lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas/ yang dang yang bltas te/ khye'u dbang po'i dbang phyug gi

Sudhana bowed his head to the feet of the boy Indriyeśvara, circumambulated the boy Indriyeśvara many hundreds of thousands of times, keeping him to his right, and, looking back again and again, departed from the boy Indriyeśvara.

d.crumb: [dge bsnyen ma phul du byung ba]

f.d: [dge bsnyen ma phul du byung ba]
Chapter 16. Prabhūtā
Prabhuta
de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang / dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi gdams ngag gi sprin gyi char yongs su 'dzin pa byed cing /
Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, had obtained the rain from the cloud of the instructions of the kalyāṇamitras.
Then, receiving the multitude of teachings of spiritual benefactors

gangs chen mtsho ltar sprin chen po'i char gyis ngoms mi shes pa/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi nyi ma'i ye shes kyi 'od zer gyis/ dge ba yongs su smin par byas pa'i sa gzhi las dbang po'i myu gu 'thon cing skyes pa/

He was like the ocean that never has too much rain from the clouds. The light from the sun of the wisdom of the kalyāṇamitras had caused the seedling of his powers to sprout from the ground of his ripened good karma.
as the ocean receives torrential rains without being filled, the sprouts of his faculties raised from clear ground and developed by the rays of light of knowledge of sunlike spiritual benefactors,
dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi zla ba nya zhing rgyas pa'i gdams ngag gi 'od zer kyi dra bas/ lus dang sems shin tu tshim par byas pa/
The net of light rays from the full moon of the instructions of the kalyāṇamitras had brought ease to his mind and body.
his body and mind cooled by the aura of light of teaching of the full moon of spiritual benefactors,
dpyid kyi nyi ma'i 'od kyis gdungs pa'i ri kyi tshogs gsal zhing bsil ba'i gangs chu la 'thung bar 'dod pa ltar dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi gdams ngag gi chu la 'thung bar 'dod pa/

Like the herds of deer who wish to drink the clear, cooling water from the Himalayas when they are tormented by the heat of the summer[952] sun, he longed to drink the water of the instructions of the kalyāṇamitras.
having drunk the water of the teachings of spiritual benefactors like a herd of animals burnt by the heat of the summer sun,
bung ba mang po 'khor zhing lding bas rgyas par gyur pa'i pad mo dang ldan pa'i pad mo'i mtsho ltar dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi gdams ngag gis/ sems kyi me tog puN+Da ri ka kha bye ba/
The white lotuses of his mind had blossomed through the instructions of the kalyāṇamitras to become a lotus pond like a pond with a bed of blossomed lotuses over which hovers a swarm of bees.
the lotuses of his mind opened like a blooming lotus pond by the instructions of spiritual benefactors like water flowing from the snowy mountains,
rin po che sna tshogs kyis yongs su rgyas pa'i rin po che'i gling ltar dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi gdams ngag rin po che 'phel ba'i snang bas sems shin tu snang bar byas pa/
The jewels of the instructions of the kalyāṇamitras, like the island of jewels that is completely filled with all kinds of jewels, continuously illuminated the mind.
his being illumined by the practice of the precious instructions of spiritual benefactors,
'dzam bu'i shing chen po me tog dang 'bras bu'i tshogs chen po dang ldan pa ltar dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi gdams ngag /bsod nams dang ye shes kyi tshogs su gyur pa phun sum tshogs pa dang ldan pa/
Like the great accumulation of flowers and fruit on the great Jambu tree, the instructions of the kalyāṇamitras have a perfect accumulation of merit and wisdom.
like a treasure island covered with jewels, successful in accumulating knowledge and virtue according to the instructions of spiritual benefactors,
