klu'i dbang po chen po rtsed mo dam pas rtse ba las byung ba'i nam mkha'i sprin chen po ltar dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi gdams ngag thos pa'i tshogs su gyur pa'i rnang shin tu che ba/ sum cu rtsa gsum pa'i 'jig rten gyis brgyan pa'i sna tshogs kyi spo ltar dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi gdams ngag las byung ba'i chos dri ma med pa sna tshogs brtsegs pa'i spor gyur pa /sum cu rtsa gsum pa'i tshogs kyi 'khor gyis bskor ba'i brgya byin/ lha ma yin gyi dbang po'i tshogs rab tu 'joms pa ltar dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi gdams ngag las byung ba'i yon tan dri ma med pa'i tshogs kyis yongs su bskor cing zil gyis mi non la/ gzhan la zil gyis gnon pa de/

Like the great clouds in the sky born from the sublime play of the great lords of serpents,[953] the accumulation of instructions heard from the kalyāṇamitras expanded.[954] The towering mass of the various stainless Dharmas of the instructions of the kalyāṇamitras was like the variegated summit of the Trāyastriṃśa paradise.[955] Just as Śakra and his entourage of the host of Trāyastriṃśa devas defeat the hosts of the lord of the asuras, the entourage of the host of the stainless qualities that arise from the instructions of the kalyāṇamitras cannot be surpassed but overwhelm others.

like a great tree laden with flowers and fruits, having an abundant store of learning of instructions of spiritual benefactors, like a great cloud in the sky produced by the sport of dragons, a radiant mountain peak of various virtues arising from the instruction of spiritual benefactors like the wonderful peak of the world of the thirty-three heavens, full of pure qualities produced by the instructions of spiritual benefactors, overpowering and invincible like the god Indra surrounded by the deities of the thirty-three heavens who conquers the leaders and hordes of titans,

mthar gyis grong khyer rgya mtsho brtan pa gang na ba der phyin te/ dge bsnyen ma phul du byung ba yongs su tshol tshol ba las/ de la skye bo mang pos bstan te/ rigs kyi bu/ dge bsnyen ma phul du byung ba de/ grong khyer gyi dbus kyi rang gi khyim na 'dug go zhes nas/

Eventually he arrived at the town called Samudrapratiṣṭhāna. When he was searching for the upāsikā Prabhūtā, a great crowd of people told him, “Noble one, the upāsikā Prabhūtā is in her house in the middle of the city.”
Sudhana made his way to the city Samudrapratishthana, looking for the devotee Prabhuta. He was told by the people there that Prabhuta was in her house in the middle of town.
tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang dge bsnyen ma phul du byung ba'i gnas gang ba der song ste/ thal mo sbyar nas sgo khang na sdod sdod pa dang /
Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, went to the home of the upāsikā Prabhūtā, and with his palms together in homage, he stood at the door.
Sudhana went to Prabhuta’s house and stood before the entrance with his hands joined in respectful salutation.

des dge bsnyen ma phul du byung ba'i khyim de shin tu rgya che la yangs shing rin po che'i ra bas yongs su bskor ba/ phyogs bzhi nas sgo shin tu mdzes pa rnam par phye ba/ rin po che tshad med grangs med pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa/ bsod nams kyi rnam par smin pas mngon par grub pa mthong nas/

He saw that the upāsikā Prabhūtā’s house was encircled by a large and extensive precious wall. It had a gateway in each of the four directions and was adorned with countless measureless jewels that had been created from the ripening of merit.
He saw that her house was very large, covered with precious ornaments, with doors on all four sides, arrayed with countless jewels, the result of the development of inconceivable virtues.

de khyim der song ste kun tu bltas na/ dge bsnyen ma phul du byung ba/ na chung shin tu gzhon la/ thog ma dar la bab pa/ gzugs mngon zhing mdzes la blta na sdug pa/ kha dog dam pa pri ya pa shin tu rgyas pa dang ldan pa/ skra phye mar bzhag pa/ lus la rgyan med pa/ gos dang / smad g.yogs dkar po bgos pa/ rin po che'i khri la 'dug pa mthong ste/

Sudhana entered the house, looked around, and saw the upāsikā Prabhūtā seated on a precious throne. She was a very young maiden who had newly become an adult, having just reached puberty. She was surpassingly beautiful, attractive, and lovely to look at. Her skin was an excellent, perfect color. Her hair hung loose. She wore no jewelry. She wore a white robe and skirt.

Entering the house and looking around, he saw the devotee Prabhuta in a jeweled chair, young, slim, fresh, in the blossom of youth, radiantly beautiful, her hair hanging loose, wearing no ornaments on her body, clothed in pure white garments.
sangs rgyas dang / byang chub sems dpa' ma gtogs par de'i lus sam/ sems kyi dbang ngam/ gzi brjid dam/ kha dog gis zil gyis mngon pa'i sems can ni khyim de na gang yang med de/
Apart from buddhas and bodhisattvas, everyone else who came into that house was overwhelmed by her body, the power of her mind, her majesty, and her color.
Except for buddhas and enlightening beings, no one came to that house whom she did not overwhelm by her appearance, her mastery of mind, her radiance, her voice, or her splendor.
lha'am mi'ang rung ste/ sems can gang gis dge bsnyen ma phul du byung ba mthong bar gyur pa de dag thams cad kyis kyang / dge bsnyen ma phul du byung ba la ston pa'i 'du shes su bsam pa zhig /
Every being who saw the upāsikā Prabhūtā, whether deva or human, conceived of the upāsikā Prabhūtā as being their teacher.
All who saw Prabhuta, whether human or celestial beings, thought of her as a teacher.
rin po che'i khri la 'dug pa mthong ngo/ /
[…thus seen]
[…thus seen]
gzhan yang khyim de na/ stan lha rdzas dang / mi'i rdzas las shin tu 'phags pa/ byang chub sems dpa'i las kyi rnam par smin pas yongs su grub pa bye ba stong phrag bcu bting ba dang /
Also, a hundred trillion[956] seats had been arranged in that house. They were superior to any human or deva seat. They had been created through the ripening of a bodhisattva’s karma.
Also, in her house were arrayed ten million seats, superior to those of celestials and humans, perfected by the deeds of enlightening beings.
mdun du phru ba gcig cig bzhag pa las kha zas dang / skom gyi bag gam/ gos dang / rgyan gyi longs spyod kyi bag gzhan ci'ang mi snang ngo/ /
Sudhana did not see any store of food or drink in the house, nor did he see any store of clothing, jewelry, or possessions apart from a single small pot placed before her.
There were no provisions of food or drink, or clothing or jewelry or other accoutrements to be seen in the house, except for a vessel placed before her.

bud med stong phrag bcu tsam zhig mdun na 'dug par mthong na'ang / de dag thams cad kyang lha'i bu mo'i kha dog dang ldan pa/ lha'i bu mo'i gzugs dang ldan pa/ lha'i bu mo'i tshul dang ldan pa/ lha'i bu mo'i spyod pa dang ldan pa/ lha'i bu mo'i longs spyod dang ldan pa/ lha'i bu mo'i tshul du shis pa dang ldan pa/ lha rdzas kyi gos yid bzhin du gyon pa/ lha rdzas kyi lhab lhub kyis shin tu klubs pa/ lha'i bu mo'i skad lta bu'i dbyangs snyan pa dang ldan pa/ lha'i bu mo'i chu zheng mdzes pa dang ldan pa sha stag ste/

Sudhana saw ten thousand maidens in front of her. They all had the skin color of apsarases, the bodies of apsarases, the manner of apsarases, the behavior of apsarases, the pleasures of apsarases, the courtesy of apsarases, the divine[957] clothing of apsarases, the jewelry of apsarases, and the beautiful-sounding voices of apsarases, and their waists[958] were like those of apsarases.
He also saw ten thousand ladies like goddesses standing before her, wearing celestial clothing and ornaments, with pleasing voices like goddesses. Those ladies,

de'i 'khor gyi bud med kyang / nges ci bsgo ba bzhin du byed cing mdun na 'khod do/ / rim gro byed do/ / bkur sti byed do/ / gdong du lta'o/ / ci bsgo ba nyan cing gnas so/ / rje sar 'khod do/ / yongs su lta'o/ / rnam par lta'o; ; 'dud do/ / rab tu 'dud do/ / phyag 'tshal lo/ /

Her entourage of maidens was stationed before her, fulfilling all her instructions, gazing upon her, honoring her, venerating her, showing her respect, facing her, listening to her, looking upon her, gazing upon her, bowing down to her, making obeisance to her, and paying homage to her.
her attendants, responding to her word, waited on her, watched her, kept their attention on her, respectfully saluted her, looked at her, bowed to her, and expressed their reverence for her.

de dag gi lus las spos kyi ngad ldang pas ni/ grong khyer de'i 'khor thams cad du dri zhim pos khyab par 'dug ste/ sems can gang gis dri de tshor bar 'gyur ba de dag thams cad kyang gnod sems med pa'i sems dang / shar gnyer med pa'i sems dang / 'tshe ba med pa'i sems dang / phrag dog dang; 'jungs pa dang bral ba'i sems dang / sgyu dang g.yo med pa'i sems dang / chags pa dang / khong khro ba med pa'i sems dang / zhum ba dang / gzengs mtho ba med pa'i sems dang; byams pa'i sems dang / phan pa'i sems dang / sdom pa la gnas pa'i sems dang / gzhan gyis yongs su bzung ba la re ba med pa'i sems su gyur te/

The perfume that emanated from their bodies filled the entire surrounding town with its pleasant aroma, and when beings smelled that aroma, they all ceased to have malice in their minds, ceased to have animosity in their minds, ceased to have aggression in their minds, ceased to have jealousy and greed in their minds, ceased to have deception and deceit in their minds, ceased to have craving and anger in their minds, ceased to go back and forth between low and high spirits, and had loving minds, altruistic minds, self-controlled minds, and minds that did not wish to acquire the possessions of others.

The fragrance from their bodies perfumed the whole city, and all who smelled the fragrance became free from malice, free from hostility, nonviolent, free from envy and jealousy, free from guile and deceitfulness, disciplined, mentally unobstructed, free from depression and elation, even-minded, kind, altruistic, restrained in mind, charitable.
gang gis de dag gi skad thos pa de dag thams cad kyang dga' ba dang / mos pa dang / dul ba'i sems dang ldan par 'gyur ro/ /
All those who heard the voices of those maidens became delighted, reverent, and subdued.[959]
And whoever heard their voices became happy, joyful, and humble in mind.
gang gis de dag mthong bar gyur pa de dag kyang 'dod chags dang bral ba tsam du rang rang gis shes par 'gyur ro/ /
And whoever saw them felt themselves freed of lust.
de ltar mthong nas/
Having seen this,

tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis/ dge bsnyen ma phul du byung ba'i rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te; dge bsnyen ma phul du byung ba la lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas/ mdun du 'dug ste thal mo sbyar nas 'di skad ces smras so/ /

Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, bowed his head to the feet of the upāsikā Prabhūtā, circumambulated her many hundreds of thousands of times, keeping her to his right, and sat before her. With his palms together in homage, Sudhana said,
Then Sudhana paid his respects to Prabhuta and politely said to her,

'phags ma/ bdag gis bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed na/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bgyi ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bgyi ba ma 'tshal te/ 'phags ma ni/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams la gdams ngag dang rjes su bstan pa mdzad do/ /zhes bdag gis thos na/ 'phags ma/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bgyi ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bgyi ba bdag la bshad du gsol/

“Āryā, I have developed the aspiration for the highest, complete enlightenment, but I do not know how bodhisattvas should train in bodhisattva conduct and in what way they should practice it. Āryā, I have heard that you give instruction and teachings to bodhisattvas! I pray that you explain to me how bodhisattvas should train in bodhisattva conduct and how they should practice it!”

“Noble one, I have set my mind on supreme perfect enlightenment, but I do not know how to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings. I hear you give enlightening beings instruction, so I beg of you to tell me how an enlightening being is to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings.”
smras pa/ rigs kyi bu/ kho mo ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa bsod nams kyi mdzod mi zad pa'i rgyan ces bya ba thob ste/
The upāsikā Prabhūtā said, “Noble one, I have attained the bodhisattva liberation called the unceasing display of the treasure of merit.
She said, “I have attained an enlightening liberation which is an inexhaustible treasury of manifestations of good.

rigs kyi bu/ kho mo ni phru ba gcig po 'di las mos pa sna tshogs can rnams/ kha zas ci la dga' ba bzhin du tshod ma sna tshogs dang / ro sna tshogs dang / kha dog sna tshogs dang / dri sna tshogs kyis tshim par byed de/
“Noble one, from this small pot, beings[960] with different wishes are satisfied by whatever foods they enjoy, with various kinds of broths, various flavors, various colors, and various aromas.
From this one vessel I satisfy sentient beings of various tastes with food conforming to their wishes, with various sauces and spices, of various colors and aromas.

rigs kyi bu; de ltar kho mo ni phru ba gcig po 'di las ci la dga' ba'i kha zas kyis sems can brgya'ang yongs su tshim par byed do/ / sems can stong dang / sems can brgya phrag stong dang / sems can bye ba dang / sems can bye ba phrag brgya dang / sems can bye ba phrag stong dang / sems can bye ba brgya phrag stong dang / sems can bye ba khrag khrig brgya phrag stong nas/ sems can brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa/ mos pa sna tshogs can rnams kyang / ci la dga' ba'i kha zas kyis yongs su tshim par byed do/ / yongs su stob par byed do/ / yongs su dga' bar byed do/ / yongs su mgu bar byed do/ / yongs su spro bar byed do/ / shin tu tshim par byed do/ / yid bde bar byed do/ / 'on kyang phru ba 'di las 'god par 'gyur ba med de/ 'grib pa med do/ / dma' bar mi 'gyur ro/ / zad par mi 'gyur ro/ / 'bri bar mi 'gyur ro/ / sa mtshams yod par mi 'gyur ro/ / mthar thug par mi 'gyur ro/ / mur thug par mi 'gyur ro/ /

“Noble one, in that way, with this one small pot I can satisfy a hundred beings with the foods they enjoy. I can satisfy with the foods they enjoy a hundred thousand beings, ten million beings, a billion beings, a trillion beings, a quintillion beings, and an innumerably-beyond-an-innumerable number of beings with different wishes. I strengthen them, make them joyful, please them, delight them, make them content, and make them happy. Nevertheless, this small pot is never diminished, depleted, emptied, used up, exhausted, spent, or finished, nor does it ever come to an end.

From this one vessel I satisfy even a hundred beings with whatever food they wish, even a thousand beings, a hundred thousand, a million, a billion; I satisfy untold numbers of sentient beings of various tastes with whatever foods they wish, gratifying and pleasing them and making them happy—and yet this vessel does not diminish or run out.

rigs kyi bu/ gzhung de dang 'dra bar sems can 'dzam bu'i gling gi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed dang / de bzhin du gling bzhi pa'i 'jig rten gyi khams gyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed dang / stong gi 'jig rten gyi khams kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed dang / stong gnyis kyi 'jig rten gyi khams kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed dang / stong gsum gyi stong chen po'i 'jig rten gyi khams kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed nas/ sems can mos pa sna tshogs can/ sangs rgyas kyi zhing brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed cig 'ongs kyang ci la dga' ba'i kha zas tshod ma sna tshogs dang / ro sna tshogs dang / kha dog sna tshogs dang / dri sna tshogs kyis yongs su tshim par byed do/ / yongs su dga' bar byed do/ / nyams bde bar byed do/ / shin tu tshim par byed do/ / yid shin tu bde bar byed do/ /

“Noble one, in the same way, I can satisfy, make joyful, please, delight, make content, and make happy, with whatever foods they enjoy and with various kinds of broths, various flavors, various colors, and various aromas, beings with different wishes who are as numerous as the atoms in a world realm of four continents, as numerous as the atoms in a world realm of a thousand four-continent worlds, as numerous as the atoms in a world realm of a million four-continent worlds, as numerous as the atoms in a world realm of a billion four-continent worlds, and as numerous as the atoms in innumerably more numerous than innumerable buddha realms.

In this way, even if as many sentient beings as atoms in a continent, or four continents, or a thousand-world universe, or a million-world universe, or a billion-world universe, or even if as many sentient beings as atoms in untold buddha-lands come to me with various tastes, I satisfy, please, and delight them with foods according to their wishes, with various sauces, spices, colors, and aromas—

'on kyang phru ba 'di las 'god par 'gyur ba med de/ 'grib pa med do; ; dma' bar mi 'gyur ro/ / zad par mi 'gyur ro/ / sa mtshams yod par mi 'gyur ro/ / mthar thug par mi 'gyur ro/ / mur thug par mi 'gyur ro/ /
“Nevertheless, this small pot is never diminished, depleted, emptied, used up, exhausted, spent, or finished, nor does it ever come to an end.
yet this vessel never diminishes or runs out, it is never depleted or exhausted.

rigs kyi bu/ gal te phyogs bcu'i 'jig rten gyi khams thams cad du gtogs pa'i sems can mos pa sna tshogs can dang / bsam pa sna tshogs can thams cad 'ong bar gyur na yang / de dag thams cad ci la dga' ba'i kha zas kyis yongs su tshim par byed pa nas yid bde bar bya ba'i bar du byed do/ / kha zas sna tshogs kyis ji lta ba de bzhin du btung pa rnam pa sna tshogs dang / ro rnam pa sna tshogs dang / stan sna tshogs dang / mal cha sna tshogs dang / bzhon pa sna tshogs dang / gos sna tshogs dang / me tog sna tshogs dang / phreng ba sna tshogs dang / spos sna tshogs dang / bdug spos sna tshogs dang / byug pa sna tshogs dang / phye ma sna tshogs dang / rin po che sna tshogs dang / rgyan sna tshogs dang / rin po che'i shing rta sna tshogs dang / gdugs sna tshogs dang / rgyal mtshan sna tshogs dang / lha'i ba dan sna tshogs dang / yo byad kyi yul rnam pa sna tshogs kyis yongs su tshim par byed pa nas/ yid dga' bar 'gyur ba'i bar du byed do/ /

“Noble one, if the beings in all world realms in the ten directions, all with different wishes and aspirations, were all to come here, they would all be satisfied and so on up to made happy by the food they enjoy. Just as it would be with various kinds of food, they would all be satisfied and so on up to made happy by various kinds of drinks, by various kinds of flavors, by various kinds of seats, by various kinds of beds, by various kinds of steeds, by various kinds of clothing, by various kinds of flowers, by various kinds of garlands, by various kinds of perfume, by various kinds of incense, by various kinds of ointments, by various kinds of powders, by various kinds of jewels, by various kinds of jewelry, by various kinds of precious carriages, by various kinds of parasols, by various kinds of banners, by various kinds of flags, and by various kinds from among the entire range of utensils.

Even if all the beings in all worlds in the ten directions, with various tastes and desires, should come to me, I would satisfy them all with whatever food they wished. And as with food, so also would I satisfy and please them with various kinds of drinks, various delicacies, various couches, various clothing, various flowers, various garlands, various fragrances, various incenses, various unguents, various aromatic powders, various jewels, various ornaments, various conveyances, various parasols, various banners, various pennants, and various kinds of utensils.

rigs kyi bu/ gzhan yang shar phyogs kyi 'jig rten gyi khams gcig na nyan thos dang / rang sangs rgyas sku'i tha ma 'dzin pa gang ji snyed gcig bzhugs pa de dag thams cad kyang / kho mo'i kha zas las gsol cing / nyan thos dang / rang sangs rgyas kyi byang chub kyi 'bras bu brnyes par mdzad do/ /

“Moreover, noble one, all the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas in a single world realm in the east, who are in their final life, attain the result of the śrāvaka and pratyekabuddha enlightenments by eating my food.

“Furthermore, any Buddhist disciples or individual illuminates in their last embodiment in one world in the east who attain the fruit of discipleship or individual illumination all do so after having eaten my food.

shar phyogs kyi 'jig rten gyi khams gcig na ji lta ba de bzhin du 'jig rten gyi khams brgya dang / 'jig rten gyi khams stong dang / 'jig rten gyi khams brgya phrag stong dang / 'jig rten gyi khams bye ba dang / 'jig rten gyi khams bye ba phrag brgya dang / 'jig rten gyi khams bye ba phrag stong dang / 'jig rten gyi khams bye ba brgya phrag stong dang / 'jig rten gyi khams bye ba khrag khrig brgya phrag stong dang / 'jig rten khams 'dzam bu'i gling gi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed dang / gling bzhi pa'i 'jig rten gyi khams kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed dang / stong gi 'jig rten gyi khams kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed dang / stong gnyis kyi 'jig rten gyi khams kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed dang / stong gsum gyi stong chen po'i 'jig rten gyi khams kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed nas/

Just as it is in one realm in the east, so it is in a hundred world realms, a thousand world realms, a hundred thousand world realms, ten million world realms, a billion world realms, ten billion world realms, a hundred billion world realms, a quintillion world realms, and world realms as numerous as the atoms in the world realm of Jambudvīpa, as the atoms in a world realm of four continents, as the atoms in a world realm of a thousand four-continent worlds, as the atoms in a world realm of a million four-continent worlds, and as the atoms in a world realm of a billion four-continent worlds.

And as this is true in one world in the east, so it is true in a hundred worlds, a thousand, a million, a billion, a trillion, a quadrillion, in as many worlds as atoms in a continent, as many worlds as atoms in four continents, as many worlds as atoms in a thousand-world universe, as many worlds as atoms in a million-world universe, as many worlds as atoms in a billion-world universe, up to as many worlds as atoms in untold buddha-lands—

de bzhin du shar phyogs kyi sangs rgyas kyi zhing brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi 'jig rten gyi khams na/ nyan thos dang / rang sangs rgyas sku'i tha ma 'dzin pa ji snyed cig bzhugs pa de dag thams cad kyang / kho mo'i kha zas las gsol cing / nyan thos dang; rang sangs rgyas kyi 'bras bu brnyes par mdzad do/ /

“In the same way, all the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas in world realms as numerous as the atoms in innumerably more numerous than innumerable buddha realms in the east, who are in their final life, will attain the result of the śrāvaka and pratyekabuddha enlightenments by eating my food.
all those who realize the fruit of discipleship or individual illumination do so after having eaten my food.

shar phyogs na bzhugs pa ji lta ba de bzhin du lho phyogs dang / nub phyogs dang / byang phyogs dang / byang shar gyi phyogs mtshams dang / shar lho'i phyogs mtshams dang / lho nub kyi phyogs mtshams dang / nub byang gi phyogs mtshams dang / 'og dang / steng gi phyogs na ji snyed cig bzhugs pa de dag thams cad kyang de bzhin no/ /

“Just as it is for those who are in the east, so it is for all of those who are in the south, in the west, in the north, in the northeast, in the southeast, in the southwest, in the northwest, below, and above.
And as this is true in so many worlds to the east, so it is true in the worlds in all ten directions.

rigs kyi bu/ shar phyogs kyi 'jig rten gyi khams gcig tu sku tshe gcig gis thogs pa'i byang chub sems dpa' ji snyed cig bzhugs pa de dag thams cad kyang / kho mo'i kha zas las gsol cing / snying po byang chub tu bzhugs nas/ bdud sde dang bcas pa pham par mdzad de/ bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu mngon par 'tshang rgya'o/ /

“Noble one, all those who are bodhisattvas in their last life in a single world realm in the east will, by eating my food, be seated at the bodhimaṇḍa, defeat Māra and his armies, and attain the highest, complete enlightenment of buddhahood.

“The enlightening beings in one world in the east who are bound to attain enlightenment in one life all sit on the site of enlightenment, conquer the demons, and realize supreme perfect enlightenment after having eaten my food.

shar phyogs kyi 'jig rten gyi khams gcig na bzhugs pa ji lta ba de bzhin du/ 'jig rten gyi khams brgya dang / 'jig rten gyi khams stong dang / 'jig rten gyi khams brgya phrag stong dang / 'jig rten gyi khams bye ba dang / 'jig rten gyi khams bye ba brgya dang / 'jig rten gyi khams bye ba stong dang / 'jig rten gyi khams bye ba brgya phrag stong dang / 'jig rten gyi khams bye ba khrag khrig brgya phrag stong dang / 'jig rten gyi khams 'dzam bu'i gling gi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed dang / gling bzhi pa'i 'jig rten gyi khams kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed dang / stong gi 'jig rten gyi khams kyi rdul shin tu phra pa snyed dang / stong gnyis kyi 'jig rten gyi khams kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed dang / stong gsum gyi stong chen po'i 'jig rten gyi khams kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed nas/ shar phyogs kyi sangs rgyas kyi zhing brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi 'jig rten gyi khams na/ byang chub sems dpa' sku tshe gcig gis thogs pa ji snyed cig bzhugs pa de dag thams cad kyang / kho mo'i kha zas las gsol cing snying po byang chub la bzhugs nas/ bdud sde dang bcas pa pham par mdzad de/ bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu mngon par 'tshang rgya'o/ /

“Just as it is for those in one realm in the east, so it is in a hundred world realms, a thousand world realms, a hundred thousand world realms, ten million world realms, a billion world realms, ten billion world realms, a hundred billion world realms, a quintillion world realms, and world realms as numerous as the atoms in the world realm of Jambudvīpa, as the atoms in a world realm of four continents, as the atoms in a world realm of a thousand four-continent worlds, as the atoms in a world realm of a million four-continent worlds, and as the atoms in a world realm of a billion four-continent worlds. Those and others up to all those who are bodhisattvas in their last life in world realms as numerous as the atoms in innumerably more numerous than innumerable buddha realms in the east will, by eating my food, be seated at the bodhimaṇḍa, defeat Māra and his armies, and attain the highest, complete enlightenment of buddhahood.
The same is true of the enlightening beings to realize enlightenment in one life in up to as many worlds as atoms in untold buddha-lands in each of the ten directions—

shar phyogs na bzhugs pa ji lta ba de bzhin du/ lho phyogs dang / nub phyogs dang / byang phyogs dang / byang shar gyi phyogs mtshams dang / shar lho'i phyogs mtshams dang / lho nub kyi phyogs mtshams dang / nub byang gi phyogs mtshams dang / 'og gi phyogs dang / steng gi phyogs kyi 'jig rten gyi khams gcig na/ byang chub sems dpa' sku tshe gcig gis thogs pa ji snyed cig bzhugs pa de dag thams cad kyang / kho mo'i kha zas las gsol cing snying po byang chub tu bzhugs te/ bdud sde dang bcas pa rab tu pham par mdzad nas/ bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu mngon par 'tshang rgya'o/ /

“Just as it is for those who are in the east, in the same way all those who are bodhisattvas in their last life in one world realm in the south, in the west, in the north, in the northeast, in the southeast, in the southwest, in the northwest, below, and above will, by eating my food, be seated at the bodhimaṇḍa, defeat Māra and his armies, and attain the highest, complete enlightenment of buddhahood.
they all sit on the site of enlightenment, conquer the demons, and realize supreme perfect enlightenment after having eaten my food.”

shar phyogs kyi 'jig rten gyi khams gcig na bzhugs pa ji lta ba de bzhin du/ 'jig rten gyi khams brgya dang / 'jig rten gyi khams stong dang; 'jig rten gyi khams brgya phrag stong dang / 'jig rten gyi khams bye ba dang / 'jig rten gyi khams bye ba brgya dang / 'jig rten gyi khams bye ba stong dang; 'jig rten gyi khams bye ba brgya phrag stong dang / 'jig rten gyi khams bye ba khrag khrig brgya phrag stong dang / 'jig rten gyi khams 'dzam bu'i gling gi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed dang / gling bzhi pa'i 'jig rten gyi khams kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed dang / stong gi 'jig rten gyi khams kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed dang / stong gnyis kyi 'jig rten gyi khams kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed dang / stong gsum gyi stong chen po'i 'jig rten gyi khams kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed nas/ rigs kyi bu/ steng gi phyogs kyi 'jig rten gyi khams sangs rgyas kyi zhing brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed na/ byang chub sems dpa' sku tshe gcig gis thogs pa ji snyed cig bzhugs pa de dag thams cad kyang / kho mo'i kha zas las gsol cing snying po byang chub tu bzhugs nas/ bdud sde dang bcas pa pham par mdzad de/ bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu mngon par 'tshang rgya'o/ /

“Just as it for all those who are bodhisattvas in their last life and so on up to those in one realm in the upward direction,[961] so it is in a hundred world realms, a thousand world realms, a hundred thousand world realms, ten million world realms, a billion world realms, ten billion world realms, a hundred billion world realms, a quintillion world realms, and world realms as numerous as the atoms in the world realm of Jambudvīpa, as the atoms in a world realm of four continents, as the atoms in a world realm of a thousand four-continent worlds, as the atoms in a world realm of a million four-continent worlds, as the atoms in a world realm of a billion four-continent worlds, and so on, up to all those who are bodhisattvas in their last life in world realms in the upward direction that are as numerous as the atoms in innumerably more numerous than innumerable buddha realms in the east. All those who are bodhisattvas in their last life will, by eating my food, be seated at the bodhimaṇḍa, defeat Māra and his armies, and attain the highest, complete enlightenment of buddhahood.
rigs kyi bu khyod kyis kho mo'i 'khor bud med stong phrag bcu po 'di dag mthong ngam/ smras pa/ 'phags ma/ bdag gis mthong ngo/ /
“Noble one, do you see these ten thousand maidens?” Sudhana replied, “Āryā, I see them.”
“Do you see these ten thousand women, my companions?
smras pa/ rigs kyi bu/
The upāsikā Prabhūtā said, “Noble one,
bud med 'di dag la sogs pa brgya stong grangs med pa phrag bcu kho mo dang skal pa mnyam par spyod pa/
myself and these maidens and countless millions of others have the same conduct,
Beginning with these, there are countless tens of hundreds of thousands of women whose practice is the same as mine,
smon lam gcig pa/ dge ba'i rtsa ba gcig pa/ 'byung ba'i rgyan gcig pa/ mos pa'i lam rnam par dag pa gcig pa/
the same prayer, the same roots of merit, the same display of setting forth, the same pure path of aspiration,
who are one in vows, one in roots of goodness, one in ways of emancipation, one in purity of devotion,
kho mo dang skal pa mnyam par dran pa rnam par dag pa/ skal pa mnyam par blo rnam par dag pa/ skal pa mnyam par blo tshad med par gyur pa/ skal pa mnyam par dbang po rab tu thob pa/
the same pure mindfulness, the same pure mode of being,[962] the same measureless realization, the same attainment of the highest faculties,
equal in purity of mindfulness, one in purity of deportment, equal in infinity of understanding, equal in attainment of spiritual faculties,
skal pa mnyam par sems kyis rgyas par 'gengs pa/ skal pa mnyam par spyod yul gyi yul dang ldan pa/ skal pa mnyam par chos kyi tshul la zhugs pa/ skal pa mnyam par don nges par rtogs pa/
the same pervasion of mind, the same range of the scope of conduct, the same way of the Dharma, the same ascertainment of meaning,
equal in pervasive awareness, equal in range of sphere of action, equal in penetration of spiritual principles, equal in ascertainment of meanings,
skal pa mnyam par chos kyi don ston pa/ skal pa mnyam par gzugs rnam par dag pa/ skal pa mnyam par stobs tshad med pa/
the same teaching of the meaning of the Dharma, the same pure form, the same measureless strengths,
equal in elucidation of doctrines and meanings, equal in purity of form, equal in infinity of power,
skal pa mnyam par brtan pa gzhan gyis mi thub pa/
equal in unsurpassed energy,
skal pa mnyam par chos kyi sgra sgrogs pa/ skal pa mnyam par dbyangs rnam par dag pa/
the same voicing of the words of the Dharma, the same pure voice in all our communication,[963]
equal in voicing truth, equal in purity of voice,
tshad med pa'i yon tan brjod du yod pas rnam par spyod pa thams cad la skal pa mnyam par yon tan rnam par dag pa/
the same pure qualities in all our conduct because we are praised for limitless qualities,
equal in purity of qualities in all manners by manifesting infinite virtues,
las kyi rnam par smin pa la kha na ma tho ba med cing / rnam par dag pas bskal pa mnyam par las kyi rnam par smin pa rnam par dag pa/
the same purity of karma because of having the pure ripening of faultless karma,
equal in purity of action by virtue of purity of results of irreproachable actions,
'gro ba thams cad yongs su skyob pa/ skal pa mnyam par byams pa chen pos rgyas par 'gengs pa/
the same all-pervasive great love because of our protection of all beings,
equal in pervasive kindness by virtue of saving all sentient beings,
'gro ba thams cad yongs su smin par byed pas mi skyo ba'i phyir/ skal pa mnyam par snying rje chen pos rgyas par 'gengs pa/
the same pervasive great compassion because of our tireless ripening of all beings,
equal in pervasive compassion by virtue of tirelessly developing all sentient beings,
bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du sems can thams cad tshim par byed pa'i lus yongs su ston pas skal pa mnyam par lus kyi las rnam par dag pa/
the same pure karma of body because we manifest the bodies that satisfy beings according to their wishes,
equally pure in physical action by virtue of appearing to all sentient beings in forms that please them,
chos kyi dbyings kyi nges pa'i tshig tha snyad la skal pa mnyam par ngag gi las rnam par dag pa/
the same pure karma of speech in communicating the meaning of the words in the realm of the Dharma,
equally pure in speech in usage expressing the realm of realities,
sangs rgyas thams cad kyi 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor du skal pa mnyam par 'dod pa/
the same arrival into the circles of the followers of all the buddhas,
equal in going to the assemblies of all buddhas,
sangs rgyas la mchod cing rim gror bya ba'i phyir sangs rgyas kyi zhing thams cad du skal pa mnyam par rgyu ba/
the same eagerness for all the buddha realms in order to serve and make offerings to all the buddhas,
equal in speeding to all buddha-lands to attend all the buddhas,
chos thams cad kyi tshul khong du chud par bya ba la skal pa mnyam par mngon sum du gyur pa'i ye shes dang ldan pa/
the same directly perceived knowledge in comprehending all the ways of the Dharma,
equal in direct knowledge in understanding the principles of all doctrines,
byang chub sems dpa'i sa thams cad thob par bya ba la skal pa mnyam par spyod pa rnam par dag pa sha stag cig kyang yod de/
and the same pure conduct in attaining all the bodhisattva levels.
equal in purity of practice in attainment of all the stages of enlightening beings.

rigs kyi bu/ bud med stong phrag bcu po 'di dag kyang skad cig gcig tu 'di lta ste/ byang chub sems dpa' sku tshe gcig gis thogs pa rnams la zhal zas yongs su dbul ba'i phyir/ phyogs bcu rgyas par 'dong ngo/ / phru ba 'di nyid nas kha zas blangs shing srid pa tha ma pa dang; nyan thos dang / rang sangs rgyas kyi theg pa pa rnams la bsod snyoms dbul ba'i phyir phyogs bcur rgyas par 'dong ngo/ / phru ba 'di nyid nas kha zas blangs shing phyogs bcu rgyas par bkang ste/ yi kyi tshogs thams cad kha zas kyis yongs su tshim par byed do/ /

“Noble one, these ten thousand maidens, within one single instant, travel throughout the ten directions in order to offer food to the bodhisattvas in their final life. They take food from this small pot and go throughout the ten directions in order to offer it as alms to śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas in their final life. They take food from this small pot and go throughout the ten directions in order to satisfy all the hosts of pretas with the food.

“These ten thousand women pervade the ten directions in a single instant to present food to the enlightening beings who are bound to become enlightened in one lifetime, giving them food from this same vessel. They pervade the ten directions to give food and drink to the saints and individual illuminates who are in their last existence. They go everywhere and satisfy all hungry ghosts with food.

rigs kyi bu/ de ltar kho mo ni phru ba 'di nyid nas lha rnams ni lha'i kha zas kyis yongs su tshim par byed do/ / klu rnams ni klu'i kha zas kyis/ gnod sbyin rnams ni gnod sbyin gyi kha zas kyis/ dri za rnams ni dri za'i kha zas kyis/ lha ma yin rnams ni lha ma yin gyi kha zas kyis; nam mkha' lding rnams ni nam mkha' lding gi kha zas kyis/ mi'am ci rnams ni mi'am ci'i kha zas kyis/ lto 'phye chen po rnams ni lto 'phye chen po'i kha zas kyis/ mi rnams ni mi'i kha zas kyis/ mi ma yin pa rnams ni mi ma yin pa'i kha zas kyis yongs su tshim par byed do/ /

“Noble one, in that way I satisfy the devas with divine food from this small pot, and I satisfy nāgas with nāga food, yakṣas with yakṣa food, gandharvas with gandharva food, asuras with asura food, garuḍas with garuḍa food, kinnaras with kinnara food, mahoragas with mahoraga food, humans with human food, and nonhumans with nonhuman food.

I also satisfy all the celestial beings with celestial food from this same vessel: I satisfy dragons with dragon food, spirits with spirit food, cherubim with cherub food, titans with titan food, birds with bird food, centaurs with centaur food, serpents with serpent food, humans with human food, and nonhumans with nonhuman food.
rigs kyi bu/ yud tsam zhig sdod dang / de'u re mngon du 'gyur ro/ /
“Noble one, stay a moment and you will see a sight.”
Come here and in a moment you shall see with your own eyes.”

dge bsnyen ma phul du byung ba des tshig de brjod ma thag tu de'i mod la 'di lta ste/ dge bsnyen ma phul du byung bas sngon gyi smon lam gyis pos pas/ sems can grangs med pa zhig shar phyogs kyi sgo nas nang du 'ongs par gyur to/ / de bzhin du 'di lta ste/ dge bsnyen ma phul du byung ba'i sngon gyi smon lam gyis bos pas/ sems can grangs med pa zhig lho phyogs dang / nub phyogs dang / byang phyogs kyi sgo nas nang du 'ongs par gyur te/ de ltar 'ongs pa de dag dge bsnyen ma phul du byung bas/ stan de dag la bkod de/ so so nas ci dga' ba'i kha zas tshod ma sna tshogs dang / ro sna tshogs dang / kha dog sna tshogs dang / dri sna tshogs dang ldan pas yongs su tshim par byas so/ / yongs su bstabs par byas so/ / yongs su dga' bar byas so/ / yongs su mgu bar byas so/ / yongs su spro bar byas so/ / shin tu tshim par byas so/ / yid bde bar byas so/ /

As soon as the upāsikā Prabhūtā said those words, at that moment, having been invited by the upāsikā Prabhūtā in the prayers she made in the past, countless beings came in through the eastern door. In the same way, countless beings, invited by the upāsikā Prabhūtā in the prayers she made in the past, came in through the southern, the western, and the northern doors. Seated on her throne, the upāsikā Prabhūtā satisfied, made joyful, pleased, delighted, made content, and made happy those beings who had arrived with whatever foods they enjoyed, in various kinds of broths, with various flavors, various colors, and various aromas.

No sooner had Prabhuta said these words than immeasurable numbers of such beings came in through the four doors of her house, invited by Prabhuta’s standing vow. Prabhuta seated them in the places prepared and satisfied them with whatever kind of foods they wished, pleasing and delighting them.

kha zas sna tshogs kyis ji lta ba de bzhin du btung ba rnam pa sna tshogs dang / ro rnam pa sna tshogs dang / stan sna tshogs dang / mal cha sna tshogs dang / bzhon pa sna tshogs dang / gos sna tshogs dang / me tog sna tshogs dang / phreng ba sna tshogs dang / spos sna tshogs dang / bdug spos sna tshogs dang / byug pa sna tshogs dang / phye ma sna tshogs dang / rin po cha [*che?] sna tshogs dang / rgyan sna tshogs dang / rin po che'i shing rta sna tshogs dang / gdugs sna tshogs dang / rgyal mtshan sna tshogs dang / lha'i ba dan sna tshogs dang / yo byad kyi yul rnam pa sna tshogs kyis yongs su tshim par byas pa nas/ yid dga' bar 'gyur ba'i bar du byas so/ /

Just as with the food, she satisfied them and so on up to made them happy with various kinds of drinks, various kinds of flavors, various kinds of seats, various kinds of beds, various kinds of steeds, various kinds of clothing, various kinds of flowers, various kinds of garlands, various kinds of perfume, various kinds of incense, various kinds of ointments, various kinds of powders, various kinds of jewels, various kinds of jewelry, various kinds of precious carriages, various kinds of parasols, various kinds of banners, various kinds of flags, and various kinds from among the entire range of utensils.

In the same way she also satisfied and pleased them with various drinks, delicacies, seats, couches, conveyances, clothes, flowers and garlands, perfumes and incenses, unguents and aromatic powders, ornaments, jeweled chariots, parasols, banners, pennants, and utensils.

lha rnams ni lha'i kha zas kyis yongs su tshim par byas so/ / klu dang / gnod sbyin dang / dri za dang / lha ma yin dang / nam mkha' lding dang / mi'am ci dang / lto 'phye chen po dang / mi dang / mi ma yin pa rnams kyang / mi ma yin pa'i kha zas kyis yongs su tshim par byas pa nas/ yid bde bar 'gyur ba'i bar du byas so/ /
She satisfied and so on up to made happy devas with divine food, and she and satisfied nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, and nonhumans with their food.
She satisfied all the various kinds of beings with their various kinds of food,
'on kyang phru ba de las god par gyur pa med/ 'grib pa med/ dmas pa med/ zad par gyur pa med/ sa mtshams su gyur pa med/ mthar thug pa med/ mur thug pa med do/ /
Nevertheless, her small pot was never diminished, depleted, emptied, used up, exhausted, spent, or finished, and it never came to an end.
yet the vessel was not depleted or exhausted; it never ran out.

de nas dge bsnyen ma phul du byung ba des/ tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la 'di skad ces smras so/ / rigs kyi bu/ kho mos ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa bsod nams kyi mdzod mi zad pa'i rgyan ces bya ba 'di shes par zad na/ byang chub sems dpa' bsod nams chen po'i rgya mtsho mi zad pas/ mi zad pa'i bsod nams dang ldan pa/ bsod nams kyi tshogs rgya chen po shin tu bsags pas nam mkha' lta bur gyur pa/ 'gro ba thams cad kyi smon lam yongs su rdzogs par byed pas/ nor bu rin po che yid bzhin gyi rgyal po lta bu/ 'gro ba thams cad kyi dge ba'i rtsa ba yongs su bsrung bas/ bsod nams chen po'i khor yug dang ldan pa/ 'gro ba thams cad du rin po che snyim pa nas char ltar 'thor bas/ bsod nams chen po'i sprin du gyur pa chos kyi grong khyer gyi sgo 'byed pas/ bsod nams chen po'i mdzod la mngon sum du lta ba/ 'gro ba thams cad kyi phongs pa'i mun pa sel bas/ bsod nams chen po'i sgron mar gyur pa de dag gi spyod pa shes pa'am/ yon tan brjod par nus re skan/

Then the upāsikā Prabhūtā said to Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, “I know only this bodhisattva liberation called the unceasing display of the treasure of merit. How could I know or describe the qualities of the conduct of bodhisattvas who have an inexhaustible ocean of merit, who possess inexhaustible merit, who have accumulated a vast accumulation of merit and are therefore like space, who fulfill the prayers of all beings and are therefore like the king of wish-fulfilling jewels, who protect the roots of merit of all beings and are therefore like a Cakravāla mountain range of merit, who send down a rain of jewels from their hands and are therefore like a great cloud of merit, who open the gate to the city of the Dharma and are therefore like the direct vision of a treasure of great merit, and who dispel the darkness of the poverty of all beings and are therefore like a lamp of great merit?

Then Prabhuta said to Sudhana, “I know this enlightening liberation, which is an inexhaustible treasury of manifestations of good; how can I know the practice or tell the virtues of enlightening beings whose goodness is inexhaustible because of the endlessness of the ocean of good, who are like the sky in that they have produced a vast store of good, who are like wish-fulfilling jewels in that they fulfill the wishes of all sentient beings, who are mountains of good because they protect the roots of goodness of all beings, who are great clouds of good as they shower jewel rain on all beings, who are superintendents of the great treasury of good in that they open the door of the city of truth, who are great lamps of good in that they dispel the darkness of destitution for all sentient beings?

song / rigs kyi bu/ lho phyogs kyi rgyud 'di nyid na/ grong khyer 'byung ba chen po zhes bya ba yod de/ de na khyim bdag mkhas ba zhes bya ba 'dug gi/ de'i gan du song la/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bya ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bya ba dris shig /

“Depart, noble one. In this southern region there is a town called Mahāsaṃbhava. There dwells a householder by the name of Vidvān. Go to him and ask him, ‘How should a bodhisattva train in bodhisattva conduct? How should a bodhisattva practice it?’ ”
“South of here is a city called Mahasambhava, where a householder named Vidvan lives. Go ask him how an enlightening being is to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings.”

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang dge bsnyen ma phul du byung ba'i rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te/ dge bsnyen ma phul du byung ba la lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas/ yang dang yang bltas te/ dge bsnyen ma phul du byung ba'i drung nas blta bas mi ngoms bzhin du song ngo/ /

Sudhana bowed his head to the feet of the upāsikā Prabhūtā, circumambulated the upāsikā Prabhūtā, keeping her to his right, many hundreds of thousands of times, and, looking back again and again, departed from the upāsikā Prabhūtā.
Then Sudhana, paying his respects to the devotee Prabhuta, looking at her again and again without tiring of the sight of her, took his leave and departed.
[khyim bdag mkhas ba]
Chapter 17. Vidvān
Vidvan

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang / bsod nams kyi mdzod mi zad pa'i rgyan gyi rnam par thar pa'i snang ba rab tu thob pa de/ bsod nams rgya mtsho de la ni rjes su sems/ bsod nams kyi nam mkha' de la ni kun tu lta/ bsod nams kyi phung po de ni yongs su 'dzin/ bsod nams kyi ri bo de la ni mngon par 'dzeg /bsod nams kyi tshogs de ni yang dag par sdud/ bsod nams kyi chu bo de la ni yongs su 'bog /bsod nams kyi mu stegs de la ni rab tu 'bab/ bsod nams kyi dkyil 'khor de ni yongs su sbyong / bsod nams kyi gter de la ni yang dag pa blta/ bsod nams kyi tshul de la ni rjes su dran par byed/ bsod nams kyi chos de ni yongs su 'dzin/ bsod nams kyi rgyud de ni yongs su sbyong ba byed cing /

Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, had obtained the light of the liberation called the unceasing display of the treasure of merit. He contemplated that ocean of merit. He viewed that sky of merit. He obtained that heap of merit. He climbed that mountain of merit. He accumulated that store[964] of merit. He immersed himself in that river of merit. He descended the steps into the bathing place of that merit. He purified that field of merit. He looked at that treasure of merit. He thought of that way of merit. He paid attention[965] to that tradition[966] of merit. He purified that lineage of merit.

Then, having gained the illumination of that enlightening liberation which is an inexhaustible treasury of goodness, reflecting on that ocean of good, gazing into that sky of good, climbing that mountain of good, gathering that mass of good, plunging into that stream of good, crossing that bridge of good, purifying that sphere of good, viewing that treasury of good, recalling that principle of good, contemplating that eye of good, purifying that multitude of good,
mthar gyis grong khyer 'byung ba chen po gang na ba der phyin nas/
Eventually he arrived at the town called Mahāsaṃbhava and searched, sought, and looked around[967] for the householder Vidvān.
Sudhana made his way to the city of Mahasambhava and looked all around for Vidvan, seeking a spiritual benefactor.

dge ba'i bshes gnyen 'dod cing / dge ba'i bshes gnyen blta bas bsgos pa'i sems kyi rgyud dang / dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyis byin gyis brlabs pa'i bsam pa dang / dge ba'i bshes gnyen la thogs pa med pa'i sbyor ba dang / dge ba'i bshes gnyen la rim gro bya bas skyo ba med pa'i brtson 'grus dang / dge ba'i bshes gnyen la rag lus pa'i dge ba'i rtsa ba thams cad dang / dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyis nges par gyur pa'i bsod nams kyi tshogs thams cad dang / dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyis rnam par spel ba'i thabs mkhas pa'i spyod pa dang / gzhan gyi dring mi 'jog par dge ba'i bshes gnyen la rim gro bya ba la mkhas pa dang / rnam par 'phel ba'i dge ba'i rtsa ba thams cad dang / rnam par dag par 'gyur ba'i byang chub sems dpa'i lhag pa'i bsam pa dang / yang dag par 'phel ba'i byang chub sems dpa'i dbang po dang / yongs su smin par 'gyur ba'i dge ba'i rtsa ba thams cad dang / yang dag par 'phel ba'i smon lam chen po mngon par bsgrub pa dang / shin tu yangs par 'gyur ba'i snying rje chen pos bdag nyid thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du nye bar gyur par yang dag par mthong nas/ sangs rgyas thams cad las byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po'i spyod pas/ chos kyi snang ba yang dag pa blang ba dang / de bzhin gshegs pa'i stobs bcu snang ba rnam par 'phel bar byed cing /

He searched for the householder Vidvān while longing for kalyāṇamitras, with his being transformed by seeing kalyāṇamitras, with an aspiration that was the blessing of the kalyāṇamitras, with dedication to following[968] kalyāṇamitras, with diligence in tireless service of the kalyāṇamitras, with all the roots of merit of relying on kalyāṇamitras, with all the accumulation of merit through being faithful to the kalyāṇamitras, with the practice of the skillful methods increased by the kalyāṇamitras, with skill in serving the kalyāṇamitras without relying on anyone else, and while increasing all his roots of merit, purifying the bodhisattva motivation, increasing the bodhisattva faculties, ripening all roots of merit, increasing the fulfillment of great prayers, making great compassion vast, seeing himself as coming close to omniscience, receiving the Dharma radiance of the completely good bodhisattva conduct from all the buddhas, and increasing the illumination of the ten strengths of the tathāgatas.

Looking for Vidvan, his whole being perfumed by the sight of spiritual benefactors, finding strength in spiritual benefactors, relying on spiritual benefactors, striving to follow spiritual benefactors, with tireless vigor in attending spiritual benefactors, all his roots of goodness due to spiritual benefactors, all his stores of virtue sustained by spiritual benefactors, his practice of skill in means developed by spiritual benefactors, all his roots of goodness growing by skill in attendance of spiritual benefactors without depending on others, his will for enlightenment becoming purified, his enlightening faculties developing, all his roots of goodness maturing, his accomplishments of great vows growing, his great compassion broadening, seeing himself near omniscience, receiving the light of teaching of all buddhas by the practice of Universally Good enlightening beings, the manifestations of the ten powers of buddhas increasing,
khyim bdag mkhas pa yongs su tshol tshol ba las/
[…thus sought]
[…thus sought]

grong khyer gyi dbus lam gyi bzhi mdo zhig na/ rin po che sna bdun gyi stegs bu zhig la/ rin po che grangs med pa las byas pa'i khri/ nor bu rin po che'i rkang pa rdo rje dang / in+d+ra nI la sna tshogs kyis spras pa bkye ba/ gser gyi lcag pod kyi dra bas legs par blas pa/ nor bu rin po che dri ma me pa'i snying po can rin po che lnga brgya tsam gyis gzugs legs par brgyan pa/ lha rdzas kyi stan sna tshogs bting ba/ gam yo na sa lha rdzas kyi gos kyi rgyal mtshan dang / ba dan mang po bsgreng ba/ rin po che du ma'i dra bas kun nas yog pa/ rin po che'i bla re chen po bres pa/ bla nas gser dang / rin po che'i me tog gi lda ldi mang po bkye ba zhig la 'dug cing /

He saw the householder Vidvān at the crossroads in the center of the town. He was upon a dais made of the seven precious materials. He was seated upon an excellent throne made of countless jewels. Its legs of precious jewels were adorned with various diamonds and sapphires. It was covered with a network of strings of gold. It contained stainless precious jewels. Its form was decorated with five hundred jewels. Various cushions of divine material were set upon it. Around it stood streamers, banners, and flags made of divine cloth. It was covered by a net of strings of many jewels. Overhead was a great bejeweled canopy, from which hung wreaths of flowers of gold and jewels.

Sudhana saw Vidvan at a crossroads in the middle of the city, on a seat on a high pedestal made of innumerable jewels, set on legs of diamonds and emeralds, with a web of white cowries on golden strings, set in pure jewels, with five hundred ornamental jewel figurines, arrayed with multicolored celestial cloth, with celestial banners and pennants flying above, covered with many nets of jewels, overspread with a great canopy of jewels, with garlands of gold and jewels hanging from it.

'dzam bu chu klung gi gser gyi gdugs yu ba dri ma med pa bai DU r+ya las byas ba ni drung na bsgreng zhing bzung / rin po che'i g.yag rnga dri ma med pa'i rdul yab ngang pa'i rgyal po lta bus ni legs par g.yab/ spos kyi rim gro yo byad sna tshogs kyis ni bdugs shing bsangs/

A parasol of Jambu River gold was held aloft[969] by its stainless handle made of beryl. Vidvān was being fanned by precious stainless fans made of the feathers of the king of geese,[970] and censers of various incenses perfumed the air around him.
A golden parasol with a handle of pure lapis lazuli was held over Vidvan, and he was being fanned by plumes made of pure white goose feathers while various incenses perfumed the air around him.

rol mo brdung ba dang / dkrol ba lha rdzas kyi dbyangs las 'das par sgra 'byin pa lnga brgya tsam ni g.yas g.yon nas brdungs shing dkrol/ grong khyer 'byung ba chen po na 'khod pa'i sems can rnams shin tu dga' bar bya ba'i don du/ lha rdzas kyi me tog gi sprin gyi char ni kun nas 'bab par gyur/ g.yog srog chags stong phrag bcu tsam sngon dge ba'i rtsa ba skal pa mnyam par spyod spyod pa/ ngag nyan cing ci dga' bar byed pa/ lha rdzas las 'das pa'i rgyan gyis shin tu brgyan pa/ byang chub sems dpa'i bsam pa yongs su grub pa/ lha dang mi'i gzugs las shin tu 'das pa sha stag gis kun nas bskor cing 'dug pa

There was an entourage of five thousand musicians to the right and left who played and beat on musical instruments, emitting a beautiful music that transcended that of the devas and filled the town of Mahāsaṃbhava in order to bring delight to beings. These ten thousand beings let fall a rain from clouds of divine flowers. Their bodies surpassed those of devas and humans. They had the complete bodhisattva motivation and were adorned with jewelry that surpassed that of the devas.

He was attended by ten thousand people of equally virtuous past conduct, finer in appearance than celestials or humans, perfect in the will of enlightening beings, adorned with ornaments superior to those of the gods, playing music sweeter than that of the heavens to please all the people in the city, and showering celestial flowers.
mthong nas/
[…thus seen]
[…thus seen]

tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang / khyim bdag mkhas pa gang na ba der song ste phyin nas/ khyim bdag mkhas pa'i rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te/ khyim bdag mkhas pa la lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas mdun du 'dug ste; thal mo sbyar nas 'di skad ces smras so/ / 'phags pa/ bdag ni 'di lta ste/ sems can thams cad kyi sdug bsngal zhi bar bgyi ba dang / sems can thams cad shin tu bde ba la dgod pa dang / sems can thams cad 'khor ba'i rgya mtsho nas mngon par gdon pa dang / sems can thams cad chos rin po che'i gling du yang dag par bskyal ba dang / sems can thams cad kyi sred pa'i rlan shin tu bskam pa dang / sems can thams cad kyi snying rje'i rlan yang dag par bskyed pa dang / sems can thams cad kyi 'dod pa'i dga' ba dang / sred pa rnam par bzlog pa dang / sems can thams cad sangs rgyas kyi ye shes la mos shing bsgrub par bgyi ba dang / sems can thams cad 'khor ba'i dgon pa las yang dag par bzla ba dang / sems can thams cad sangs rgyas kyi yon tan dang / chos la dga' zhing mos pa yang dag par bskyed pa dang / sems can thams cad khams gsum gyi grong brdal nas gdon pa dang / sems can thams cad thams cad mkhyen pa'i pho brang du gzung par sems can thams cad kyi don du bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu zhugs kyis kyang /

Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, approached the householder Vidvān and, having come up to him, bowed his head to Vidvān’s feet, circumambulated him, keeping him to his right, many hundreds of thousands of times, and sat down before him. With his palms together in homage, Sudhana said, “Ārya, I have set out to attain the highest, complete enlightenment in order to end the suffering of all beings, in order to bring all beings to happiness, in order to save all beings from the ocean of saṃsāra, in order to take all beings across to the island of the jewels of the Dharma, in order to dry up the moisture of the cravings of all beings, in order to create the moisture of compassion in all beings, in order to expel all delight and craving of desire from all beings, in order to make all beings gain a craving for the wisdom of buddhahood, in order to make all beings pass through the jungle of saṃsāra, in order to make all beings develop a delight and desire for the Dharma and the qualities of the buddhas, in order to make all beings depart from the city of the three realms, and in order to lead all beings to the city[971] of omniscience.

Seeing Vidvan, Sudhana went up to him, paid his respects, and said, “Noble one, I have set out for supreme perfect enlightenment for the benefit of all beings—to extinguish the sufferings of all beings, to lead them to ultimate happiness, to rescue them from the ocean of the mundane whirl, to deliver them to the island of jewels of truth, to evaporate their cravings, to produce great compassion in them, to divert their craving for sensual pleasure and arouse in them craving for enlightened knowledge, to help them all cross over the wildness of the mundane whirl, to develop in them a taste for the way of buddhahood, to lead them out of the city of mundane states and lead them to the city of omniscience.

ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bgyi ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bgyi ba ma 'tshal te/ 'phags pa ni/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams la gdams ngag dang rjes su bstan pa mdzad do zhes bdag gis thos na/ 'phags pa/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bgyi ba dang / ji ltar bslabs na byang chub sems dpa' rnams sems can thams cad kyi rten du 'gyur ba bdag la bshad du gsol/ /de skad ces smras pa dang /

“However, I do not know how bodhisattvas should train in bodhisattva conduct and in what way they should practice it. Ārya, I have heard that you give instruction and teachings to bodhisattvas! I pray that you explain to me how bodhisattvas should train in bodhisattva conduct and how having trained in it they become supports for all beings!”

But I do not know how an enlightening being is to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings. Noble one, I hear that you give enlightening beings instruction, so I ask you to tell me how an enlightening being is to learn the practice of enlightening beings, and how enlightening beings in the course of learning become a refuge for all sentient beings.”

khyim bdag mkhas pas/ tshong dpon gyi bu nor bu bzang la 'di skad ces smras so/ / rigs kyi bu/ de ltar khyod kyis bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed pa legs so/ / legs so/ /
The householder Vidvān said to Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, “Noble one, it is excellent, excellent, that you have developed the aspiration for the highest, complete enlightenment!
Vidvan replied, “It is good that you have aroused the aspiration for supreme perfect enlightenment.

rigs kyi bu/ sems can gang bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed cing byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa yongs su tshol ba dang / dge ba'i bshes gnyen blta bas mi ngoms pa dang / dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi drung du 'gro bas mi skyo ba dang / dge ba'i bshes gnyen la rim gro bya bas sgyid lug pa med pa dang / dge ba'i bshes gnyen btsal bas yid mi bde ba mi skyed pa dang / dge ba'i bshes gnyen btsal ba las phyir mi ldog pa dang / dge ba'i bshes gnyen la mos shing dad pa'i yid las rnam par mi ldog pa dang / dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi ngor blta ba las phyir mi zlog pa dang / dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi gdams ngag gi tshul la zhum pa med pa dang / dge ba'i bshes gnyen la rim gro dang / bsnyen bkur bya bas mi skyo ba de lta bu ni shin tu dkon no/ /

“Noble one, it is rare to find a being who develops the aspiration for the highest, complete enlightenment, who seeks the bodhisattva conduct, who never has enough of gazing upon a kalyāṇamitra, who never tires of coming into the presence of a kalyāṇamitra, who never becomes dispirited in serving a kalyāṇamitra, who never becomes unhappy with seeking a kalyāṇamitra, who never turns back from seeking a kalyāṇamitra, who never ceases to sincerely yearn for and be attracted to a kalyāṇamitra, who never turns away from gazing upon a kalyāṇamitra, who is never despondent in following the instructions of a kalyāṇamitra, and who never wearies of serving and honoring a kalyāṇamitra.

Rare are those who aspire to supreme perfect enlightenment, and rare are those who, having aspired to enlightenment, are tireless in seeking the practices of enlightening beings by meeting spiritual benefactors, who do not weary of going to spiritual benefactors, who are not pained by attendance on spiritual benefactors, who are not depressed by the difficulty of approaching spiritual benefactors, who do not give up seeking spiritual benefactors, who do not turn away from the sight of the countenance of spiritual benefactors, who do not get discouraged in the path taught by spiritual benefactors, who do not tire in the service of spiritual benefactors.
rigs kyi bu/ khyod kyis kho bo'i 'khor 'di dag mthong ngam/ smras pa/ 'phags pa/ mthong ngo/ /
“Noble one, do you see those in my entourage?” Sudhana replied, “Yes, Ārya, I see them.”
Do you see my companions?

smras pa/ rigs kyi bu/ 'di dag kun kyang kho bos bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed bdag ste/ 'di dag ni kho bos de bzhin gshegs pa'i rigs su bskyed pa'o/ / 'di dag ni kho bos pha rol tu phyin pas bstud de/ gsos pa'o/ / 'di dag ni kho bos chos dkar po thams cad kyis bskyed pa'o/ / 'di dag ni kho bos de bzhin gshegs pa'i stobs bcu la rnam par bskyed pa'o/ / 'di dag ni kho bos 'jig rten gyi rigs las gyen du bskyod pa'o/ / 'di dag ni kho bos de bzhin gshegs pa'i rigs la bkod pa'o/ / 'di dag ni kho bos 'jig rten gyi lam gyi 'khor lo las bzlog pa'o/ / 'di dag ni kho bos chos kyi 'khor lo bskor ba la btsud pa'o/ / 'di dag ni kho bos ngan song gsum gyi rgyud du ltung ba las yongs su bzung ba'o/ / 'di dag ni kho bos chos nyid khong du chud par bya ba la bkod pa ste/

Vidvān said, “Noble one, I made all of them develop the aspiration for the highest, complete enlightenment. I have caused them to be reborn in the family of the tathāgatas. I have nourished them through the accumulation of the perfections. I have made them practice all the good qualities. I have made them develop the ten strengths of the tathāgatas. I have made them transcend the family of the world. I have established them in the family of the tathāgatas. I have made them turn away from the wheel of worldly existences. I have made them enter into the turning of the wheel of the Dharma. I have saved them from falling into lives in the three lower existences. I have established them in the understanding of the true nature of phenomena.

I inspired them all to seek supreme perfect enlightenment; I caused them to be born in the family of buddhas; I nourished them by providing them with the ways of transcendence; I got them to live in good ways; I developed them in the ten powers of buddhas; I lifted them out of worldliness; I established them in the ranks of the enlightened; I removed them from the circle of mundane states; I started them in the cycle of enlightening teaching; I saved them from falling into bad conditions; I led them to realization of equality of things:
rigs kyi bu/ de ltar na byang chub sems dpa' rnams sems can thams cad kyi skyabs su gyur pa yin no/ /
“Noble one, it is in that way that bodhisattvas become a refuge for all beings.
for thus do enlightening beings become saviors of all sentient beings.
rigs kyi bu/ kho bo ni yid kyi mdzod nas byung ba'i bsod nams mang po thob pa ste/
“Noble one, I have attained the bodhisattva liberation called[972] the merit that arises from the treasury of mind.
“I have attained good works produced from the treasury of mind:
de'i mthus kho bo ni zas 'dod pa rnams la zas kyi sbyin pa byed do/ / btung ba 'dod pa rnams la btung ba dang /
Through its power I give food to those who wish for food; drink for those who wish for drink;
to those who need food I give food, to those who need drink I give drink,

ro dam pa 'dod pa rnams la ro'i dam pa dang / bza' ba 'dod pa rnams la bza' ba dang / bca' ba 'dod pa rnams la bca' ba dang / bldag pa 'dod pa rnams la bldag pa dang / mur pa 'dod pa rnams la mur ba dang /
gos 'dod pa rnams la gos dang / me tog 'dod pa rnams la me tog dang / phreng ba 'dod pa rnams la phreng ba dang / spos 'dod pa rnams la spos dang / bdug pa 'dod pa rnams la bdug pa dang /
to those who need clothing I give clothing, to those who need flowers I give flowers, to those who want garlands I give garlands, To those who need perfumes or incenses I give perfumes or incenses,
byug pa 'dod pa rnams la byug pa dang / phye ma 'dod pa rnams la phye ma dang /
ointments to those who wish for ointments; powders to those who wish for powders;

rgyan dang lhab lhub 'dod pa rnams la rgyan dang lhab lhub dang / rin po che 'dod pa rnams la rin po che dang / gser 'dod pa rnams la gser dang / dngul 'dod pa rnams la dngul dang / mu tig 'dod pa rnams la mu tig dang /

to those who need ornaments I give ornaments, to those who need jewels I give jewels, to those who need gold I give gold, to those who need silver I give silver, to those who need pearls I give pearls,
rten 'dod pa rnams la rten dang /
dwellings to those who wish for dwellings;
stan 'dod pa rnams la stan dang / mal cha 'dod pa rnams la mal cha dang /
seats to those who wish for seats; beds to those who wish for beds;
to those who need chairs I give chairs, to those who need beds I give beds,
na ba'i gsos sman dang / yo byad 'dod pa rnams la na ba'i gsos sman dang yo byad dang /
medicine that heals illness to those who wish for medicine that heals illness; utensils to those who wish for utensils;
to those who need medicine I give medicine,
carriages to those who wish for carriages;[973]
to those who need means of transportation I give means of transportation,

bzhon pa 'dod pa rnams la bzhon pa dang / dga' ba 'dod pa rnams la dga' ba dang / glang po dang / rta dang / shing rta dang / ba lang dang / bong bu dang / ma he dang / ra lug 'dod pa rnams la glang po dang / rta dang / shing rta dang / ba lang dang / bong bu dang / ma he dang / ra lug dang / rgyal mtshan dang / gdugs dang / ba dan 'dod pa rnams la/ rgyal mtshan dang / gdugs dang / ba dan dang / bran pho dang / bran mo 'dod pa rnams la bran pho dang / bran mo dang / 'khor gyi byis pa 'dod pa rnams la 'khor gyi byis pa dang / bud med 'dod pa rnams la bud med dang; bu mo gzhon nu 'dod pa rnams la bu mo gzhon nu dang / cod pan dang / gtsug gi rin po che 'dod pa rnams la cod pan dang / gtsug gi rin po che dang / thor pag dang bcas pa'i gtsug gi rin po che 'dod pa rnams la thor pag dang bcas pa'i gtsug gi rin po che dang / skra mthon mthing dri ma med pa'i dkyil 'khor 'dod pa rnams la/ skra mthon mthing dri ma med pa'i dkyil 'khor gyi sbyin pa byed pa nas/ yo byad sna tshogs thams cad 'dod pa rnams la yang yo byad sna tshogs thams cad kyi sbyin pa byed do/ /
and so on—whatever the needs, I provide them.
rigs kyi bu/ yud tsam zhig sdod dang / de'u re mngon sum du mthong bar 'gyur ro/ /
“Noble one, stay a moment and you will see a sight.”
Come here, and in a moment you will see for yourself.”
de skad du khyim bdag mkhas pas tshig de brjod ma thag tu de'i mod la/ sems can grangs med pa zhig khyim bdag mkhas pa'i sngon gyi smon lam gyis bos pas/
As soon as the householder Vidvān said those words, at that moment, having been invited by the householder Vidvān in the prayers he had made in the past,
As soon as Vidvan had spoken these words, innumerable beings gathered at his house, summoned by his past vows.

phyogs tha dad pa dang / yul tha dad pa dang / gnas tha dad pa dang / grong khyer tha dad pa dang / grong rdal tha dad pa dang / tshong 'dus tha dad pa dang / ljongs tha dad pa dang / 'khor gyi grong tha dad pa dang / khyim tha dad pa dang / sems can gyi rgyud tha dad pa dang / sems can gyi rigs tha dad pa dang / sems can rnam pa mi mthun pa tha dad pa dang / lam gyi rgyud tha dad pa dang / gnas kyi rnam pa dang / ming du bya ba tha dad pa dang /

there came countless beings from different directions, from different lands, from different districts, from different towns, from different markets, from different cities, from different villages, from different hamlets, from different houses, from different castes, from different families, from different levels of families, from different ways of life, and from different classifications of stations in life.
They came from various regions, various nations, various cities, various towns, and various groups, of various conditions, various states of consciousness,

sems can skye mched rnam par dag pa sna tshogs dang ldan pa kha zas sna tshogs don du gnyer ba/ kha zas sna tshogs 'dod pa/ bsam pa tha dad pa bza' ba dang btung ba gtsang ba 'dod pa dang / sha 'dod pa dang / kha zas rnam pa tha dad pa sna tshogs don du gnyer ba/ lam gyi rgyud rnam pa sna tshogs kyi khyad par du skyes pa'i skye mched la gnas pa 'di lta ste/ mi'i nang nas 'bras chan dang / sran chan dang / 'khur ba dang / skyo ma dang / nya dang / sha la sogs pa/ kham gyis bza' ba'i kha zas sna tshogs don du gnyer ba dang /

These beings had various different sensory perceptions, wishing for various kinds of food, desiring various kinds of food, with various aspirations, desiring different aspirations and desires, desiring pure food and drink, desiring meat, wishing to consume contrasting kinds of different food, and remaining in various kinds of distinct sensory perceptions and different ways of life. In other words, among humans there were those who wished for such various kinds of food as boiled rice, sour gruel, broths, fish, and meat.
various degrees of purity of sense, desiring various kinds of food, having various inclinations, needing diverse kinds of sustenance according to their states of being.

mi'i nang nas ji lta ba bzhin du 'gro ba'i rgyud thams cad rnam par spyod pa dag las kyang / kha zas dang btung ba sna tshogs don du gnyer ba dag de ltar byang chub sems dpa'i mthu dang / byang chub sems dpa'i sbyin pa thogs pa med par gtong ba'i rnga'i sgra dang / byang chub sems dpa'i sngon gyi smon lam gyis bos pas kun kyang 'ongs par gyur te/ 'ongs nas kyang khyim bdag mkhas pa la slong mo 'debs so/ / gdong du lta'o/ / sdod do/ / gsol ba 'debs so/ /

Whatever were the different kinds of food and drink that were wished for by those with different ways of life among human beings, through the power of the bodhisattva, the drumbeat of the unimpeded generosity of the bodhisattva, and the invitation made by the past prayers of the bodhisattva, all those human beings came there, and when they had arrived they entreated the householder Vidvān. They looked upon him, observed him, and addressed him.

They were invited by the vow of the enlightening being, by the power of the enlightening being, by the sounds of the drums of unattached giving; they came to Vidvan, looked at him, and made requests of him.

de nas khyim bdag mkhas pas/ slong ba de dag kun nas 'dus par shes nas yud tsam du bsams te/ nam mkha' la bltas pa dang / nam mkha'i dbyings nas kha zas dang / btung ba rnam pa sna tshogs/ ro sna tshogs dang ldan pa/ kha dog sna tshogs dang ldan pa/ dri sna tshogs dang ldan pa mang po 'thon te/ lag mthil du 'ongs par gyur to/ / des de dag yongs su blangs shing de ltar kun nas 'dus pa'i slong mo pa mos pa sna tshogs dang ldan pa de dag ci 'dod pa'i zas dang / btung ba'i rnam pa dang / yo byad kyi khyad par thams cad kyis yongs su tshim par byas so/ / ci 'dod pa yongs su byin no/ / rab tu dga' bar byas so/ / shin tu tshim par byas so/ / dga' ba shin tu skye bar byas so/ / nyams shin tu bde bar byas so/ / yid rab tu dga' bar byas so/ /

The householder Vidvān, knowing that the petitioners had all gathered there, thought for a moment and then looked up into the sky. From the realm of the sky there came into the palms of his hands a great number of various kinds of food and drink, with various kinds of flavors, various kinds of colors, and various kinds of aromas. He gave these different kinds of food, drink, and utensils to all the petitioners gathered there, who had different aspirations and desires, in accordance with what they desired, so that they were satiated, pleased, contented, delighted, joyful, and overwhelmed with happiness.

Seeing them gathered there begging, Vidvan thought for a moment, then looked at the sky. From the sky various kinds of food and drink streamed into his hand, and this Vidvan gave to the beggars according to their various tastes and desires, satisfying and delighting them with the food and drink they wanted, with the best kinds of all means of subsistence.

de ltar de dag shin tu tshim par byas nas/ des kyang mchog ste/ de'i 'og tu chos bstan pa 'di lta ste/ ye shes kyi tshogs rgya chen po bsags pa'i rgyu yongs su brjod de/ chos bstan to/ / phongs pa thams cad 'byung mi srid pa'i rgyu yongs su brjod pa dang / skyid pa chen po yongs su 'grub pa'i rgyu yongs su brjod pa dang / chos kyi ye shes kyi tshul 'thob pa 'byung ba'i rgyu yongs su brjod pa dang / bsod nams kyi tshogs rgya chen po bsags pa'i rgyu yongs su brjod pa dang / dga' ba bza' ba'i zas rab tu 'thob pa 'byung ba'i rgyu yongs su brjod pa dang / mtshan dang / dpe byad bzang pos shin tu brgyan pa'i lus 'thob pa 'byung ba'i rgyu yongs su brjod pa dang / thub pa med pa'i stobs rnam par dag pa 'thob pa 'byung ba'i rgyu yongs su brjod pa dang / bla na med pa'i kha zas yongs su shis pa 'thob pa 'byung ba'i rgyu yongs su brjod pa dang / bdud kyi dpung thams cad rab tu 'joms pa'i bsod nams kyi stobs mi zad pa rab tu 'thob pa 'byung ba'i rgyu'ang yongs su brjod pa byas te chos ston to/ /

Having concluded satisfying them in that way, afterward he taught them the Dharma. He taught the Dharma that elucidated the cause of gathering a vast accumulation of wisdom, elucidated the cause that made it impossible for poverty to occur, elucidated the cause of the arising of perfect great enjoyment, elucidated the cause of the arising of the attainment of the Dharma’s way of wisdom, elucidated the cause of the arising of gathering a vast accumulation of merit, elucidated the cause of the arising of the attainment of the enjoyment of the food of happiness, elucidated the cause of the arising of the attainment of a body adorned by the signs and features of a great being, elucidated the cause of the arising of the attainment of invincible strength, elucidated the cause of the arising of the attainment of the unsurpassable[976] food of wisdom, and elucidated the cause of the arising of the attainment of the inexhaustible strength of merit that defeats the strength[977] of all the māras.

Then, after satisfying them, he expounded the Teaching to them: that is, he elucidated means of accumulating a great store of knowledge, means of eliminating all poverty, means of producing all enjoyments, means of finding ways to knowledge of truth, means of accumulating a vast store of virtue, means of being able to feed on joy, means of attaining a body adorned with the marks and embellishments of greatness, means of attaining purity of invincible power, means of attaining knowledge of uninterrupted livelihood, and means of attaining inexhaustible good powers overcoming the power of all demons.

de kha zas don du gnyer cing 'ongs pa rnams la nam mkha'i dbyings nas kha zas rnam pa sna tshogs blangs shing tshim par byas te/ de dag la tshe dang / mdog dang / stobs dang / bde ba dang / spobs pa phun sum tshogs pa thob par bya ba'i phyir chos bstan to/ /

When all those who came wishing for food were satisfied through having obtained various kinds of food from the realm of the sky, the householder Vidvān taught them the Dharma so that they could attain perfect lifespans, color, strength, happiness, and eloquence.
As for those who came for food, once they were satisfied by the various foods from the sky, he taught them to attain intelligence for life, health, and strength.

des btung ba don du gnyer cing 'ongs pa rnams la/ btung ba mang po zhim pa kha na ma tho ba med pa/ yid shin tu dga' ba byed pa de dag gis tshim par byas nas/ de dag la 'khor bas skom zhing 'khor ba la dga' ba las rnam par bzlog pa dang / sangs rgyas kyi chos la dga' zhing sangs rgyas kyi chos la mos pa yongs su bskyed pa'i phyir chos bstan to/ /

When all those who came wishing for drink were satisfied and delighted through having obtained many kinds of delicious, nontransgressive drinks, the householder Vidvān taught them the Dharma so that they would turn away from thirsting for saṃsāra, from delighting in saṃsāra, and would develop a delight in the Buddhadharma, a thirst[978] for the Buddhadharma.

As for those who came for drink, once they were satisfied by the various fine, good, and pleasant drinks, he taught them to put an end to mundane cravings and develop craving for the pleasure of the way of enlightenment.

des ro'i mchog don du gnyer zhing 'ongs pa rnams la ro'i mchog sna tshogs mngar ba dang / skyur ba dang / lan tsha dang / tsha ba dang / kha ba dang / bska ba rnam pa tha dad pas yongs su tshim par byas te/ de'i 'og tu skyes bu chen po'i mtshan ro bro ba'i mchog thob par bya ba'i phyir chos bstan to/ /

After all those who came wishing for excellent flavors had been satisfied by the different excellent flavors of sweetness, sourness, saltiness, spiciness, bitterness, and astringency, the householder Vidvān taught them the Dharma so that they would attain the supreme flavor of the physical signs of a great being.
Those who came for delicacies he satisfied with sweets, and then taught them to attain the refined characteristics of great people.
