Some see it small, some large; some see a ground of earth, some see a ground spread with lapis lazuli; some see clay walls, some see it surrounded by walls covered with the finest cloth, banners, and jewels; some see it full of gravel and sand, uneven, with a lot of ravines; some see the ground spread with large jewels, decorated and flat as the palm of the hand; some see it beautifully arrayed with mansions and palaces, with round windows, nets, crescents, jewels, and various other adornments.

grong khyer gyi phyi rol na gnas pa'i sems can sngon ngas byang chub sems dpa'i spyad pa spyod pa'i tshe/ bsdu ba'i dngos po bzhis yongs su bsdus pa/ bsam pa dag pa/ dge ba'i rtsa ba bskyed pa/ sangs rgyas mang po la bsnyen bkur ba/ thams cad mkhyen pa nyid la mngon par mos pa/ thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du rab tu gzhol ba de dag la yang rin po che las byas par snang ngo/ / de ma yin pa gzhan dag la ni sa las byas par snang ste/

“Among the beings who live outside the city, there are those who, when I was practicing bodhisattva conduct in past lives, gathered around me as pupils through the four methods of gathering pupils. They have pure motivation, have created the roots of merit, have served many buddhas, aspire to omniscience, and are set on omniscience. To them the city appears to be made of jewels. To the others it appears to be made of earth.

Even among those who live outside the city, those whose minds are pure, who have made roots of goodness, who have attended many buddhas, who are aiming for omniscience, and who make omniscience their ultimate goal, see it as made of jewels. Those whom I took care of in the course of past enlightening practice by means of charity, kindness, assistance, and cooperation see it this way, while others see it as made of clay.

rigs kyi bu/ nga'i khams na gnas pa'i sems can yul dang / phyogs dang / grong khyer dang / grong rdal dang / ljongs dang / khams dang / rgyal po'i pho brang dag na/ rnyog pa lnga dang ldan pa'i 'jig rten gyi dus kyi rang bzhin gyis dkrugs te/ mi dge ba bcu'i las kyi lam zhig byed par 'dod par gyur na yang / de'i tshe nga de dag la phan par bya ba'i sems kyis/ byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin 'jig rten gyi dbang po'i glong zhes bya ba/ byams pa chen po sngon du 'gro ba la snyoms par 'jug ste/

“Noble one, when the beings who live in my realm, in the districts and subdistricts, in the villages, towns, and markets, in the country and the capital, are disturbed by the nature of the times in a world that has the five degenerations and want to practice the path of the ten bad actions, then at that time, wishing to benefit them, I enter the bodhisattva samādhi called exercising power over the world through being motivated by great love.

“Whenever the inhabitants of my domain want to do anything wrong in the degenerate world, their natures disturbed by the times, in order to save them I go into an enlightening concentration guided by great benevolence called ‘adapting to the faculties of the world,’

rigs kyi bu; de ltar nga ting nge 'dzin de la snyoms par zhugs pa dang / de nyid kyi mod la sems can de dag gi 'jigs pa de dag dang / mi bde ba de dag dang / shar gnyer ba de dag dang / 'thab mo dang / rtsod pa de dag dang / sems kyi 'khrug pa de dag dang / 'tshe ba'i sems de dag kyang byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin 'jig rten gyi dbang po'i glong byams pa chen po sngon du 'gro ba de'i chos nyid thob pas rab tu zhi bar gyur to/ / nye bar zhi bar gyur to/ / rnam par ldog par gyur to/ / 'gag par gyur to/ /

“Noble one, as soon as I rest in that samādhi, the fears, misfortunes, hostilities, disputes, mental disturbances, and violent intentions of those beings cease, are extinguished, are eliminated, and are brought to an end through their attaining the nature of the bodhisattva samādhi called exercising power over the world through being motivated by great love.

whereupon their fears, misfortunes, animosities, quarrels, agitations, and hostilities cease. That happens as a matter of course by the achievement of the nature of the enlightening concentration adapting to the faculties of the world, which is guided by great benevolence.

rigs kyi bu/ yud tsam zhig sdod dang / de'u re mngon sum du 'gyur ro/ / de nas rgyal po 'od chen pos de'i tshe/ byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin byams pa chen po sngon du 'gro ba 'jig rten gyi dbang po'i glong la mnyam par bzhag go /
“Noble one, stay a moment and you will see a sight.” Then King Mahāprabha entered the bodhisattva samādhi called exercising power over the world through being motivated by great love.
Come here and you shall see for yourself in a moment.” At that point the king entered that concentration,

de ltar rgyal po 'od chen pos/ byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin byams pa chen po sngon du 'gro ba 'jig rten gyi dbang po'i glong la mnyam par bzhag ma thag tu/ de'i mod la grong khyer chen po 'od bzang po'i yul dang phyogs su bcas pa/ grong khyer dang / grong rdal dang / ljongs dang / khams dang / rgyal po'i pho brang gi 'khor dang bcas par rnam pa drug tu g.yos so/ /

As soon as he entered the bodhisattva samādhi called exercising power over the world through being motivated by great love, the great city of Suprabha and its districts and subdistricts, its villages,[1043] towns, and markets, the land and the kingdom, the capital, and its environs all shook in six ways.
whereupon the whole city as well as the provinces of the kingdom quaked.

de g.yos pa'i tshe rin po che'i ra ba de dag dang / rin po che'i khang pa dang / rin po che'i snying po dang / rin po che'i khyim dang; rin po che'i gnas dang / rin po che'i gzhal med khang dang / rin po che'i khang pa brtsegs pa dang / rin po che'i ba gam dang / rin po che'i pu shu dang / rin po che'i skar khung dang / rin po che'i stegs bu dang / rin po che'i rta babs dang / rin po che'i zla gam dang / rin po che'i seng ge'i dra ba dang / rin po che'i lan kan dang / rin po che'i 'bru dang / rin po che'i bla re dang / rin po che'i srad bus brgyus pa'i dril bu g.yer ka'i dra ba dang / rin po che'i dril bu dang / rin po che'i rgyal mtshan dang / rin po che'i ba dan dang / rin po che'i ta la de dag kyang rab tu g.yos te sgra 'byin to/ / rab tu 'khrol lo/ / de dag de ltar sgra 'byin cing / yid du 'ong la snyan pa dang / mnyan na dga' ba'i dbyangs brjod cing / rgyal po 'od chen po gang na ba der 'dud de phyag 'tshal lo/ /

When they shook, the precious walls, precious mansions, precious interiors, precious houses, precious dwellings, precious aerial palaces, precious kūṭāgāras, precious spires, precious balustrade rooftops, precious round windows, precious balconies, precious toraṇas, precious crescents, precious lattices of lion adornments, precious railings, precious disks, precious canopies, precious strings of little spherical bells, precious bells, precious banners, precious flags, and precious palm trees also shook, made loud sounds, and jingled. When they resounded, they emitted beautiful, delightful sounds, so that those people bowed and made obeisance in the direction of King Mahāprabha.

As they shook, the jewel walls, jewel temples, jewel treasuries, jewel houses, jewel mansions, jewel palaces, jewel towers, jewel windows, jewel balconies, jewel arches, jewel crescents, jewel domes, jewel statues, jewel canopies, jewel bells, jewel banners, and jewel trees gave off beautiful, pleasant sounds and bowed toward King Mahaprabha.

grong khyer chen po 'od bzang po'i nang na/ sems can ji snyed cig gnas pa de dag thams cad kyang dga' ba dang / rangs pa'i sems kyis yongs su rgyas nas/ rgyal po 'od chen po gang na ba de logs su mngon du bltas te/ lus thams cad kyis phab cing phyag 'tshal lo/ /

All those beings who dwelled within the great city of Suprabha experienced increased happiness and joy, turned to face the direction of King Mahāprabha, and prostrated their entire bodies on the ground in homage.
The inhabitants of the city Suprabha, ecstatic, prostrated themselves in the king’s direction.

de'i khams kyi grong dang / grong khyer dang / ljongs dang / yul dang / khams dang / rgyal po'i pho brang 'khor na gnas pa de dag thams cad kyang lus dang sems bde bar gyur te/ dga' zhing rangs pa skyes nas/ rgyal po 'od chen po gang na ba de logs su phyag 'tshal lo/ /

Those beings who lived in the villages, the towns, the marketplaces, the land, the kingdom, the capital, and its environs all became blissful in mind and body, and with happiness and joy they bowed down in the direction of King Mahāprabha.
The inhabitants of the rest of the domain, refreshed and joyful, bowed toward the king.

byol song gi skye gnas su gtogs pa'i sems can de dag thams cad kyang / gcig la gcig byams pa'i sems dang / phan pa'i sems su ldan par gyur nas/ rgyal po 'od chen po gang na ba de logs su blta zhing mngon par 'dud do/ /
The beings who had been reborn as animals all became kind toward one another and wished to help one another. They all turned to look in the direction of King Mahāprabha and bowed down to him.
Even the animals, in friendship and harmony with each other, bowed toward the king.
ri dang sgang mthon po'i sa'i phyogs thams cad kyang / rgyal po 'od chen po gang na ba der mngon par 'dud do/ /
Even the land, all the mountain peaks, and the other lofty lands bowed toward King Mahāprabha.
Even the mountains and hills all bowed toward the king.

me tog gi shing dang / 'bras bu'i shing dang / lo ma'i shing dang / sa bon gyi tshogs dang / 'byung po'i tshogs dang / lo tog dang / ldum bu dang / rtswa dang / gel pa dang / sman dang / nags tshal thams cad kyang / rgyal po 'od chen po gang na ba de logs su lta zhing mngon par 'dud par gyur to/ /

All the flowering trees, fruit trees, leafy trees, edible plants,[1044] vegetation,[1045] crops,[1046] grasses, bushes, herbs, and forests turned in the direction of King Mahāprabha and bowed down toward him.
All the trees and plants also bowed toward the king.

de'i khams na mtsho dang / mtshe'u dang / lu ma dang / lteng ka dang / 'bab chu dang / chu klung dang / rdzing dang / khron pa ji snyed pa de dag thams cad kyang / rgyal po 'od chen po gang na ba de logs su mngon par gzhol zhing rlabs kyi sgra 'byin par gyur to/ /
All the springs,[1047] lakes, ponds, reservoirs, waterfalls, rivers, lotus ponds, and wells in his realm turned and made the sounds of flowing in the direction of King Mahāprabha.
All the lakes, ponds, streams, and rivers in the domain flowed toward the king.

klu'i rgyal po stong phrag bcu yang a ga ru nag po'i bdug spos kyi dud pa na bun du 'grigs pa'i spos kyi sprin las glog sna tshogs 'gyu ba'i 'od kyis snang bar byed cing / 'brug sgra sgrog pa dang / spos chu'i char gyi rgyun shin tu phra ba mngon par 'bebs par gyur to/ /

Ten thousand nāga kings caused a mass of smoke of great black-agarwood incense to form a cloud of perfume, from which came the illumination of bright streaks of lightning, the roar of thunder, and a fine rain of perfumed water that fell in all four directions.[1048]
Ten thousand water spirits sent subtly aromatic rains from clouds of fragrant water, with thunder and lightning.
brgya byin dang / rab mtshe ma dang / rab dga' ldan dang / rab 'phrul dga' dang / dbang sgyur gyi lha'i rgyal po la sogs pa/ lha'i bu stong phrag bcus kyang steng gi bar snang la 'khod do/ /
Ten thousand devas, such as the deva lords Śakra, Suyāma, Saṃtuṣita, Sunirmita, and Vaśavartin gathered in the sky facing him and made offerings to King Mahāprabha:
Ten thousand celestial beings adorned the sky
nam mkha'i dbyings thams cad lha rdzas kyi rol mo'i sil snyan gyi sprin bye ba khrag khrig brgya stong gi sgra phyung bas/ dbyangs snyan pa rgya cher bsgrags pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa dang /
The entire expanse of the sky resounded with the vast melodious sound from clouds of a quintillion divine musical instruments.
with countless clouds of celestial music,
lha'i bu mo grangs med pa/ lha'i glu snyan pa len pa'i sprin gyi sgra bsgrags pa'i dbyangs snyan cing yid du 'ong ba'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa dang /
A gathering of countless apsarases created the adornment of sweet, beautiful sounds from clouds of divine songs.
goddesses sweetly singing,
lha rdzas kyi rin po che'i me tog sna tshogs kyi sprin grangs med pa'i char rab tu 'bab pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa dang /
There was the adornment of the rain that fell from clouds of a variety of countless divine, precious flowers.
clouds raining celestial jewel flowers,
lha rdzas kyi spos kyi sprin kha dog sna tshogs kyi sprin grangs med pa'i char rab tu 'bab pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa dang /
There was the adornment of the rain that fell from clouds of a variety of countless divine incenses of various colors.
clouds raining various celestial fragrances,
lha rdzas kyi rin po che'i phreng ba sna tshogs kyi sprin grangs med pa'i char rab tu 'bab pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa dang /
There was the adornment of the rain that fell from clouds of a variety of countless divine, precious garlands.
garlands,
lha rdzas kyi phye ma kha dog sna tshogs kyi sprin grangs med pa'i char rab tu 'bab pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa dang;
There was the adornment of the rain that fell from clouds of a variety of countless divine powders of various colors.
aromatic powders,
lha rdzas kyi rin po che'i lhab lhub sna tshogs kyi sprin grangs med pa'i char rab tu 'bab pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa dang /
There was the adornment of the rain that fell from clouds of a variety of countless divine, precious jewelry.
jewelry,
lha rdzas kyi gos sna tshogs dri ma med cing 'jam pa/ kha dog rnam pa tha dad pa'i sprin grangs med pa'i char rab tu 'bab pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa dang /
There was the adornment of the rain that fell from clouds of a variety of countless divine, delicate,[1049] stainless clothing.
robes,
lha rdzas kyi rin po che'i gdugs rnam par phye ba sna tshogs kyi sprin grangs med pa'i char rab tu 'bab pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa dang /
There was the adornment of the rain that fell from clouds of a variety of countless divine parasols of different kinds.
parasols,
lha rdzas kyi rin po che'i seng ge yid du 'ong ba'i rgyal mtshan gyi sprin grangs med pa'i char rab tu 'bab pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa dang;
There was the adornment of the rain that fell from clouds of beautiful lion banners.
banners,

lha rdzas kyi rin po che 'bab ba'i lce shin tu 'phro ba'i rin po che'i ba dan gyi sprin grangs med pa'i char rab tu 'bab pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan par rgyal po 'od chen po la mchod pa bya ba'i phyir byin gyis brlabs so/ /
There was the adornment of the rain that fell from clouds of countless precious flags shining with the blazing light of divine jewels.
and pennants blazing with the radiance of jewels, presenting these to the king as tokens of respect.

glang po'i rgyal po chen po shugs 'dzin gyis kyang / glang po'i dbang po'i khyu mchog gi mthu phyung ba dang / rnam par 'phrul ba'i mthus nam mkha'i dbyings thams cad lha rdzas kyi rin po che sna tshogs kyi pad+mo'i sprin grangs med pas kun nas yog par byin gyis brlabs so/ /

Airāvaṇa and all the kings of elephants were in the sky, and through the inconceivable miraculous powers of the lords of the elephants, the leaders of the herds, they manifested in the sky clouds of a variety of countless divine, precious lotuses that covered the entire expanse of the sky;
The chief of the water spirits also adorned the sky with a covering of countless clouds of celestial jewel lotuses,
lha rdzas kyi nor bu rin po che'i se mo do grangs med pa rab tu 'phyang ba dang /
of countless divine, precious hanging strings of jewels;
countless trailing ornaments of celestial jewel necklaces,
lha rdzas kyi rin po che'i snam bu'i lda ldi dang / chun po grangs med pa rab tu 'phyang ba dang /
of countless divine, precious hanging clusters of streamers and wreaths;
streamers,
lha rdzas kyi rin po che sna tshogs kyi phreng ba'i rgyud grangs med pa mngon par 'phyang ba'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa dang /
of hanging adornments of countless varieties of divine, precious flower garlands;
garlands,
lha rdzas kyi rin po che sna tshogs kyi lhab lhub dang / phreng ba grangs med pa mngon par 'phyang ba'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa dang /
of hanging adornments of countless varieties of divine, precious strings of jewelry;
ornaments,
lha rdzas kyi rin po che sna tshogs kyi me tog gi lda ldi grangs med pa mngon par bres pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa dang /
and of hanging adornments of countless varieties of divine, precious wreaths of flowers;
and leis,
lha rdzas kyi spos kyi rgyal po kha dog sna tshogs phyogs thams cad du dri zhim pos rgyas par 'gengs pa'i sprin grangs med pas kun nas khengs pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa dang /
the adornment of sky-covering clouds of perfume composed of countless varieties of divine, precious kings of scents of different colors that filled all directions with a lovely aroma;
countless clouds of all-pervading celestial fragrances,
lha rdzas kyi rin po che'i gos kha dog sna tshogs kyi sprin grangs med pa'i char rab tu 'bab pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa dang /
the adornment of rain from clouds of divine, precious clothing of various colors;
countless clouds raining celestial cloths,
lha rdzas kyi bdug spos kyi dud pa na bun du 'khrigs pa'i sprin grangs med pa'i char rab tu 'bab pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa dang /
the adornment of rain from clouds of a divine mass of incense smoke;
incense balls,
lha rdzas kyi phye ma kha dog sna tshogs kyi sprin grangs med pa'i char phra mo rab tu 'bab pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa dang /
the adornment of a delicate rain from clouds of divine powders of different colors;
and aromatic powders,

lha'i bu mo'i tshogs lha rdzas kyi rol mo byed pa dang / glu snyan pa'i dbyangs yid du 'ong bar len cing / bstod pa'i sprin gyis kun nas yog pa'i char mngon par 'bebs pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan par nam mkha'i dbyings byin gyis brlabs so/ /
and the adornment of rain from sky-covering clouds of the sweet and melodious music and songs of praise by a host of apsarases.
and countless clouds of nymphs playing sweet music and singing hymns of praise, producing these in the sky by the inconceivable power of the chief water spirit.

srin po'i dbang po brgya stong grangs med pa rgya mtsho la gnas pa dang / gling bzhi pa'i 'jig rten gyi khams kyi rten gyi sa'i gzhi la gnas pa/ kha zas su sha dang khrag 'thung zhing za la/ chu la spyod pa dang / ri dang / phyugs dang / bya dang / ba lang dang / rta dang / glang po dang / bong bu dang / skyes pa dang / bud med kyi tshogs kyi mdangs 'phrog pa/ zhe sdang ba'i yid kyi rnam par rtog pa dang ldan pa/ rtag tu 'gro ba la 'tshe zhing / mtho 'tsham pa la zhugs pa rnams kyang / byams pa dang phan pa'i sems dam pa dang ldan zhing / bzhin gyi mdog shin tu dang ba dang / 'gro ba thams cad la mi 'tshe zhing / mtho 'tsham pa med pa la zhugs te/ 'jig rten pha rol la blta bar gyur nas/ thal mo sbyar cing shin tu dga' ba'i sems kyis rgyal po 'od chen po gang na ba de logs su btud nas phyag 'tshal bar gyur te/ lus dang sems kyi bde ba rgya chen po mtshungs pa med pa yang myong bar gyur to/ /

Countless hundreds of thousands of rākṣasa lords who dwell in the sea and on the land, who dwell in our world realm of four continents, whose food is flesh and whose drink is blood, who steal the vitality of those creatures that live in the water and of deer, cattle, birds, oxen, horses, elephants, donkeys, men, and women, whose minds have thoughts of anger and who always harm and injure beings, all gained the highest motivation of love and altruism; their faces having become serene, they became dedicated to not causing violence or injury to any being, their thoughts upon the next world after death, and with their palms together in homage, with the highest happiness, they bowed in the direction of King Mahāprabha, experiencing an unequaled vast bliss of mind and body.

Also, countless hundreds of thousands of sea and land goblins, malevolent beings who feed on flesh and blood and consume the vitality of fish, birds, animals, and humans, all became benevolent, placid, intent on not harming any creatures, and sympathetic to other beings; they joined their hands in respect and most joyfully bowed to the king, experiencing mental and physical bliss.

gnod sbyin dang / grul bum dang / sha za dang / 'byung po'i dbang po brgya stong du ma yang byams pa dang / phan pa'i sems dam pa dang ldan zhing / bzhin gyi mdog shin tu dang ba dang; 'gro ba thams cad la mi 'tshe zhing / mtho 'tsham pa med pa la zhugs te/ 'jig rten pha rol la blta bar gyur nas/ thal mo sbyar cing shin tu dga' ba'i sems kyis/ rgyal po 'od chen po gang na ba der 'dud cing phyag 'tshal bar gyur te/ lus dang sems kyi bde ba rgya chen po mtshungs pa med pa yang myong bar gyur to/ /

Hundreds of thousands of lords of yakṣas, mahoragas, piśācas, and bhūtas with the highest motivation of love and altruism, their faces having become serene and their thoughts upon the next world after death, became dedicated to not causing violence or injury to any being. With their palms together in homage, with the highest happiness, they bowed in the direction of King Mahāprabha, experiencing an unequaled vast bliss of mind and body.

Hundreds of thousands of other kinds of fiends and malevolent spirits, also becoming benevolent, placid, intent on not harming any creature, and sympathetic to other beings, joined their hands in respect and most joyfully bowed to the king, experiencing physical and mental bliss.

de ltar gling bzhi pa'i 'jig rten gyi khams thams cad kyi sems can kun gyi 'jigs pa dang / gnod pa dang / mi bde ba dang / shar gnyer ba dang / 'thab mo dang / rtsod pa dang / sems kyi 'khrug pa dang / 'tshe ba'i sems thams cad rab tu zhi bar gyur to/ / rnam par zhi bar gyur to/ / rnam par log par gyur to/ / 'gag par gyur to/ / phyir log par gyur to/ /

In the same way, for all beings in the four-continent world realm, fear, misfortune, hostility, disputes, mental disturbances, and violent intentions ceased, were extinguished, were eliminated, were brought to an end, and were eradicated.
In this way all the fears, misfortunes, animosities, quarrels, agitations, and hostilities of all creatures on earth ceased.

gling bzhi pa'i 'jig rten gyi khams 'dir ji lta ba de bzhin du/ stong gsum gyi stong chen po'i 'jig rten gyi khams thams cad nas/ phyogs bcur 'jig rten gyi khams bye ba khrag khrig brgya stong phrag bcu'i bar gyi sems can kun gyi 'jigs pa dang / gnod pa dang / mi bde ba dang / shar gnyer ba dang / 'thab mo dang / rtsod pa dang / sems kyi 'khrug pa dang / 'tshe ba'i sems thams cad kyang / byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin byams pa chen po sngon du 'gro ba 'jig rten gyi dbang po'i glong gi chos nyid thob pa'i phyir rab tu zhi bar gyur to/ / rnam par zhi bar gyur to/ / rnam par log par gyur to/ / 'gag par gyur to/ / phyir log par gyur to/ /

In the same way as it was for the four-continent world realm, so it was that for all beings throughout the great universe of a billion worlds, throughout a quintillion world realms in the ten directions, all fear, misfortune, hostility, disputes, mental disturbances, and sinful and violent intentions ceased, were extinguished, were eliminated, were brought to an end, and were eradicated through their attaining the nature of the bodhisattva samādhi called exercising power over the world through being motivated by great love.

And as this happened on earth, so did it also happen throughout the galaxy, in as many as ten duodecillion worlds. This was by the achievement of the nature of the enlightening concentration adapting to the faculties of the world, which is guided by great benevolence.

de nas rgyal po 'od chen po ting nge 'dzin de las langs te/ tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la 'di skad ces smras so/ / rigs kyi bu/ ngas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa'i ye shes snang ba'i sgo byams pa chen po'i rgyal mtshan 'di shes par zad na/
Then King Mahāprabha arose from that samādhi and said to Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, “Noble one, I know only this wisdom of bodhisattva conduct called the banner of great love.
Then King Mahaprabha came out of that concentration and said to Sudhana, “I know this medium of the light of knowledge of practice of enlightening beings which is characterized by great benevolence.
ngas byang chub sems dpa' 'jig rten gyi khams thams cad bde ba'i bsam pas rgyas par 'gengs pa/ byams pa chen po'i gdugs tshad med pa dang ldan pa/
“How could I know the conduct or describe the qualities of the bodhisattvas who hold the immeasurable parasol of great love; who pervade all the world realms with their motivation to bring happiness;
How can I know the practice, tell the virtues of the enlightening beings who are like immeasurable umbrellas of great benevolence, filling all beings with happiness;
'khor mi phyed pa dang ldan pas/ 'gro ba thams cad 'khor du gyur pa/
who are attendants for all beings through continual attendance to them;
who are inseparable companions to all beings;
dbang po rab dang 'bring dang tha ma'i sbyor bas 'gro ba thams cad yongs su bskyab pa la zhugs pa/
who are dedicated to the protection of all beings applied equally to the highest, the middling, and the lowest beings;
who have set out to save all beings, working equally with the superior, inferior, and middling;
'gro ba thams cad yongs su gzung ba la zhugs pas/ byams pa'i sems lta bu dang ldan pa/
who have a loving motivation that is like the earth, for it is engaged in supporting all beings;
whose benevolence is as impartial as the earth, supporting all beings;
bsod nams dang ye shes kyi 'od zer 'gro ba thams cad du 'byung bas zla ba nya zhing rgyas pa lta bur gyur pa/
who are like the disk of the full moon sending the light rays of merit and wisdom equally to all beings;
who are impartial as the full moon, shining the light of virtue and knowledge equally on all beings;
shes bya thams cad ye shes kyi 'od kyis snang bar byed pa'i phyir nyi ma'i dkyil 'khor lta bur gyur pa/
who are like the disk of the sun because they shine the light of wisdom on everything that is to be known;
who are impartial as the sun, illumining the world with knowledge of all that can be known;
sems can thams cad kyi sems kyi mun pa thibs po rab tu sel bas sgron ma chen po lta bur gyur pa/
who are like lamps because they dispel the deep darkness in the minds of all beings;
who are like great lamps, dispelling the darkness in the recesses of all beings’ minds;
sems can thams cad kyi sems kyi rgya mtsho'i g.yo sgyu'i rnyog pa dang bar byed pas nor bu rin po che chu 'dang dang 'dra ba;
who are like the precious jewel that purifies water because they clear away the turbidity of deceit and deception in the lakes of the minds of all beings;
who are like water-clarifying jewels, removing the turbidity of deceit and guile from the water of beings’ minds;
'gro ba thams cad kyi bsam pa dang / smon lam yongs su rdzogs par byed pa nor bu rin po che yid bzhin gyi rgyal po dang 'dra ba/
who are like the king of wish-fulfilling jewels because they fulfill the aspirations and prayers of all beings;
who are like wish-fulfilling jewels, fulfilling the aspirations of all beings;

'gro ba thams cad ting nge 'dzin dang / snyoms par 'jug pa'i khang pa dang / thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi pho brang chen por gzhog pas/ rlung dmar chen po dang 'dra ba de dag gi spyod pa shes pa'am/ yon tan brjod pa'am/
who are like a great wind because they make them live in the dwelling place of resting in samādhi, which is the great city[1050] of omniscience?
who are like a gale, driving all beings into the citadel of omniscience with its houses of concentration and equilibrium?

bsod nams kyi ri bo gzhal ba'am/ yon tan gyi skar ma'i tshogs kyis brgyan pa'i nam mkha' la blta ba'am/ smon lam chen po'i rlung gi dkyil 'khor las mtshams gcad pa'am/ chos mnyam pa nyid kyi stobs la tshad gzung ba'am/ theg pa chen po'i rgyan gyis bsngags pa yongs su brjod pa'am/ kun tu bzang po'i spyod pa'i tshul gyi khyad par brjod pa'am/ byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin chen po bsgom pa'i sgo dbye ba'am/ snying rje chen po'i sprin yongs su smos par nus re skan/

“How could I measure their mountain of merit? How could I view the sky that is adorned by the myriads of stars of their qualities? How could I know the circle of air[1051] that is their great prayers? How could I measure their power of the equality of all phenomena? How could I explain their praises of the array of the Mahāyāna? How could I describe their special way of completely good conduct? How could I reveal the gateway to the great samādhi of the bodhisattvas? How could I describe their clouds of great compassion?

measure the mountain of merit, view the myriad stars of virtuous qualities, encompass the atmosphere of great vows, measure the power of impartiality toward things, clarify the forms of arrangements of the vehicle of universal salvation, express the excellences of the principles of universally good practice, open the doors of cultivation of great enlightening concentrations or describe the clouds of great compassion?

song / rigs kyi bu/ lho phyogs kyi rgyud 'di nyid na rgyal po'i gnas brtan pa zhes bya ba yod de/ de na dge bsnyen ma mi g.yo ba zhes bya ba 'dug gi/ de'i gan du song la ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bya ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bya ba dris shig /

“Depart, noble one. In this southern region there is a capital city called Sthirā. There dwells an upāsikā by the name of Acalā. Go to her and ask her, ‘How should a bodhisattva train in bodhisattva conduct? How should a bodhisattva practice it?’ ”
“South of here is a kingdom called Sthira where a devotee named Achala lives. Go ask her how to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings.”

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis/ rgyal po 'od chen po'i rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag byas nas/ rgyal po 'od chen po la lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas te/ yang dang yang bltas nas/ rgyal po 'od chen po'i drung nas song ngo// //

Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, bowed his head to the feet of King Mahāprabha, circumambulated King Mahāprabha many hundreds of thousands of times, keeping him to his right, and, looking back again and again, departed from King Mahāprabha.
So Sudhana paid his respects to King Mahaprabha and left.
bam po dgu bcu drug pa/
[dge bsnyen ma mi g.yo ba]
Chapter 22. Acalā
Achala

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang / grong khyer chen po 'od bzang po nas byung ste/ yud tsam du lam gyi mgo btsal nas/ rgyal po 'od chen po'i gdams ngag de la rjes su bsam pa byed cing / byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa'i tshul byams pa chen po'i rgyal mtshan de rjes su dran par bya ba dang /

Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, left the city of Suprabha, and having followed the road for a little while, he contemplated the instruction given to him by King Mahāprabha: he remembered the way of bodhisattva conduct called the banner of great love;
Then Sudhana left Suprabha city and shortly set forth on the road; reflecting on the teaching of King Mahaprabha, remembering the principle of enlightening practice of great benevolence,
ting nge 'dzin gyi sgo 'jig rten gyi dbang po'i glong gi snang ba chen po de yongs su bsgom pa dang /
he meditated on the light of the great samādhi called exercising power over the world;
thinking of the light of that method of great concentration adapting to the faculties of the world,
byang chub sems dpa'i lus rnam par dag pa bsam gyis mi khyab pas brgyan pa'i seng ge'i khri'i rgyan rnam par phye ba rnam pa sna tshogs de dag mngon par bsgrub pa dang /
he realized[1052] the variegated display of the lion throne and adornments of the pure bodhisattva body;
byang chub sems dpa'i smon lam dang / bsod nams kyi dbang dang / stobs bsam gyis mi khyab pa de dag rjes su spel ba dang /
he increased the inconceivable power and strength of bodhisattva aspiration and merit;
developing the inconceivable power commanding the goodness of the vows of enlightening beings,
byang chub sems dpa'i sems can yongs su smin par bya ba'i ye shes kyi tshul bsam gyis mi khyab pa de shin tu bstan par bya ba dang /
he made firm[1053] the inconceivable way of bodhisattva wisdom that ripens beings;
stabilizing the inconceivable wisdom of enlightening beings, knowing how to develop and perfect sentient beings,
byang chub sems dpa'i longs spyod kyi bdag nyid che ba thun mong du gyur pa bsam gyis mi khyab pa de la rjes su bsam pa dang /
he reflected upon the inconceivable greatness of the general enjoyments of the bodhisattvas;
contemplating the inconceivable unique greatness of experience of enlightening beings,
byang chub sems dpa'i gnas rnam pa tha dad pa bsam gyis mi khyab pa de dag kyang mtshan mar bya ba dang /
he considered the inconceivable different aspects[1054] of the bodhisattvas;
aiming for the inconceivable measurelessness of enlightening beings,
byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi sems can yongs su smin par bya ba rnam par dag pa bsam gyis mi khyab pa de rjes su dran par bya ba dang /
he remembered the inconceivable pure ripening of beings by bodhisattvas;
remembering enlightening beings’ inconceivable purity of development of sentient beings,
byang chub sems dpa'i 'khor phun sum tshogs shing yongs su dag pa de la brtag pa dang /
he thought about the inconceivable pure and perfect bodhisattva assembly of pupils;
thinking of the inconceivability of the purity of company of enlightening beings,
byang chub sems dpa' sems can gyi don bsam pa snang ba'i tshul bsam gyis mi khyab pa de la yid ches par byed byed pas/
he had conviction in the inconceivable radiance of the bodhisattvas’ dedication to their duty to beings;
focusing on enlightening beings’ inconceivable way of considering and seeing what to do for sentient beings,

sems dga' zhing mos pa'i shugs dang / sems kyi nyams bde ba dang / sems shin tu tshim pa dang / sems khong nas dga' ba dang / sems rnyog pa med pa dang / sems 'od dad pa dang / sems brtan pa dang / sems rgya che ba dang / sems mi zad pa thob ste/
and he attained happiness, powerful attraction, delight, contentment, deep joy, clarity of mind, brightness of mind, stability of mind, vastness of mind, and inexhaustibility of mind.
Sudhana became joyful and happy, his mind became clear, light, steadfast, broad, and invincible.
de de ltar dge ba'i bshes gnyen rjes su dran zhing yid la byed pa la brtson pas
He was in that way dedicated to remembering and thinking of the kalyāṇamitra.
Weeping as he thought of his memories of spiritual benefactors,
gdong mchi mas gang nas rjes su sems pa/ kyi hud; dge ba'i bshes gnyen mthong ba 'di ni/ yon tan rin po che thams cad kyi 'byung gnas su gyur pa'o/ /
With his face covered in tears, he thought “Ah! Oh! Seeing the kalyāṇamitra is the source of all precious qualities.
he thought, “Meeting spiritual benefactors is a mine of jewels of all virtues;
byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa thams cad yongs su dag pa dang / yongs su rdzogs par 'gyur ba'i rgyur gyur pa'o/ /
It perfects and purifies all bodhisattva conduct.
it brings about the purification and fulfillment of all enlightening practices;
byang chub sems dpa'i dran pa thams cad rnam par dag par byed pa'o/ /
It makes pure all bodhisattva mindfulness.
it purifies the mindfulness of all enlightening beings;
byang chub sems dpa'i gzungs kyi dkyil 'khor thams cad yongs su sbyong ba'o/ /
It purifies all the domains of bodhisattva retention.
it purifies all enlightening beings’ sphere of mental command;
byang chub sems dpa'i ting 'dzin gyi snang ba thams cad yongs su bskyed pa'o/ /
It gives rise to the radiance of all bodhisattva samādhis.
it generates the light of concentration of all enlightening beings;
sangs rgyas thams cad mthong bar 'gyur ba yongs su bsgrub pa'o/ /
It accomplishes seeing all buddhas.
it fosters accomplishments of the vision of all buddhas;
sangs rgyas kyi chos thams cad kyi sprin gyi char rab tu 'bebs pa'o/ /
It brings down the rain from the Dharma clouds of all[1055] the buddhas.
it causes the clouds of teachings of all buddhas to rain;
byang chub sems dpa'i smon lam gyi tshul thams cad brjod pa'o/ /
It indicates the way of all bodhisattva prayers.
it reveals the principles of the vows of all enlightening beings;
shes rab dang / ye shes kyi snang ba bsam gyis mi khyab pa yang dag par bskyed pa'o/ /
It gives rise to the inconceivable light of knowledge and wisdom.
it generates the inconceivable light of wisdom and knowledge;
byang chub sems dpa'i dbang po brtan pa'i myu gu skyed par byed pa'o/ /
It grows the sprouts[1056] of stable bodhisattva faculties.
it strengthens and develops the sprouting faculties of enlightening beings.
dge ba'i bshes gnyen rnams ni bdag ngan song gi g.yang sa thams cad nas skyob pa'o/ /
The kalyāṇamitras save me from falling into the chasm of the lower existences.
Spiritual benefactors save me from falling into evil ways;
dge ba'i bshes gnyen rnams ni bdag chos mnyam pa nyid kyi tshul khong du chud par bya ba la gzhog pa'o/ /
The kalyāṇamitras have brought me to the realization of the way of the equality of phenomena.
they guide me according to the principle of equality of things;
dge ba'i bshes gnyen rnams ni bdag la lam bde ba dang / mi bde ba ston pa'o/ /
The kalyāṇamitras have shown me the paths to happiness and to unhappiness.
they show me which paths are safe and which dangerous;
dge ba'i bshes gnyen rnams ni bdag la theg pa chen po yongs su ston pa'o/ /
The kalyāṇamitras have taught me the Mahāyāna.
they elucidate the way of universal enlightenment;
dge ba'i bshes gnyen rnams ni bdag la byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po'i spyod pa'i gdams ngag gis 'doms pa'o/ /
The kalyāṇamitras have given me the instructions on the completely good bodhisattva conduct.
they explain to me universally good enlightening conduct;
dge ba'i bshes gnyen rnams ni bdag la thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi grong khyer gyi lam ston pa'o/ /
The kalyāṇamitras have shown me the road to the city of omniscience.
they tell me the way to the citadel of omniscience;
dge ba'i bshes gnyen rnams kyi bdag thams cad mkhyen pa'i gnas su phyin par skyel ba'o/ /
The kalyāṇamitras have guided me on the way to the town of omniscience.
they lead me into the stronghold of omniscience;
dge ba'i bshes gnyen rnams ni bdag chos kyi dbyings kyi tshul rgya mtsho la 'jug par byed pa'o/ /
The kalyāṇamitras have made me enter the ocean of the ways of the realm of the Dharma.
they plunge me into the ocean of principles of the cosmos;
dge ba'i bshes gnyen rnams ni bdag la dus gsum gyi shes bya rgya mtsho'i tshul rab tu ston pa'o; ;
The kalyāṇamitras have taught me the ways of an ocean of what is to be known in the three times.
they illumine for me the way into the ocean of what can be known in past, present, and future;
dge ba'i bshes gnyen rnams ni bdag la 'phags pa'i tshogs kyi dkyil 'khor thams cad rab tu ston pa'o/ /
The kalyāṇamitras have shown me all the circles of ārya assemblies.[1057]
they show me the multitude of spheres of all goals;
dge ba'i bshes gnyen rnams ni bdag gi dkar po'i chos thams cad rnam par 'phel bar byed pa'o/ /
The kalyāṇamitras have increased all my good qualities.”
they cause me to develop all good qualities.”

zhes de de ltar ngu zhing smre sngags 'don pa'i tshe/ nam mkha'i dbyings la 'khod pa'i lha'i tshogs dang / rtag tu phyi bzhin 'brang zhing yang dag par bskul ba dang / sangs rgyas kyi pho nya ltar gyur pa'i byang chub sems dpa' rnams 'di skad 'dzer to/ /
While he thus wept and wailed, the devas who were assembled in the sky, who were bodhisattva devas, emissaries of the buddhas who continually followed him and inspired him, called down to him,
As Sudhana wept, a group of celestial enlightening beings in the sky, envoys of the buddhas who were always following Sudhana to inspire him, said,

rigs kyi bu/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi gdams ngag la zhugs pa'i byang chub sems dpas ni/ sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das rnams kyang thugs shin tu dgyes par 'gyur ba yin/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi tshig dang mi 'gal bar gnas pa'i byang chub sems dpas ni/ thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du'ang shin tu bsnyen pa yin/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi tshig la the tshom mi za ba'i byang chub sems dpa' la ni dge ba'i bshes gnyen rnams kyang nye bar bsnyen pa yin/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen yid la bya ba dang mi 'bral ba'i byang chub sems dpa' la ni don thams cad kyang mngon du 'gyur ba yin gyi/

“Noble one, the bodhisattvas who follow the instructions of the kalyāṇamitras greatly please the buddha bhagavats. The bodhisattvas who never go against the words of the kalyāṇamitras come close to omniscience. The bodhisattvas who do not doubt the words of the kalyāṇamitras come close to the kalyāṇamitras. The bodhisattvas who always have the kalyāṇamitras in their minds are approaching all their goals.

“The buddhas are pleased with an enlightening being who puts the instruction of spiritual benefactors into practice. An enlightening being who obeys the word of spiritual benefactors is close to omniscience. An enlightening being who does not doubt the word of spiritual benefactors becomes near to spiritual benefactors. An enlightening being who always pays attention to spiritual benefactors is within sight of all goals.
rigs kyi bu/ rgyal po'i pho brang brtan par dge bsnyen ma mi g.yo ba gang na ba der song zhig dang / de las byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa thos par 'gyur ro/ /
“Noble one, go to the upāsikā Acalā in the royal capital of Sthirā! You will hear the bodhisattva conduct from her.”
Go to the devotee Achala in the kingdom of Sthira, and you will hear from her of the practice of enlightening beings.”
de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang ting nge 'dzin gyi ye shes snang ba las langs nas/ mthar gyis rgyal po'i pho brang brtan par dge bsnyen ma mi g.yo ba gang na ba der song nas/
Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, emerged from samādhi’s light of wisdom and eventually arrived at Sthirā, where the upāsikā Acalā was.
Then Sudhana emerged from the light of concentration knowledge and made his way to the kingdom of Sthira,

dge bsnyen ma mi g.yo ba yongs su tshol zhing rmed rmed pa las/ de la 'gro ba mang pos bstan pa/ rigs kyi bu/ dge bsnyen ma mi g.yo ba de ni; rang gi khyim na pha ma dang 'phrogs shing gzhon nur gyur pa ste/ rang gi gnyen bshes kyi tshogs kyis yongs su bskor cing / skye bo'i tshogs chen po la chos ston to/ /

He searched and looked for the upāsikā Acalā, and many people said to him, “Noble one, the upāsikā Acalā is young and lives with her parents at home, where, surrounded by her family, she teaches the Dharma to a great gathering of people.”
looking for the devotee Achala. People told him, “The devotee Achala is a girl living at home with her parents and relatives; she gives spiritual teaching to a large group of people.”

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang dga' ba chen po dang mos shing spro bas yongs su rgyas pa'i sems dang ldan pa de dge bsnyen ma mi g.yo ba'i khyim gang na ba der song ste phyin nas/ dge bsnyen ma mi g.yo ba'i khyim gyi sgo na sdod pa'i tshe/ des khyim de thams cad 'od lus dang sems shin tu bde bar byed pa/ gser gyi kha dog tu 'dug pa zhig gis khyab cing gsal bar gyur nas/

Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, his mind filled with great happiness, enthusiasm, and joy, went to the home of the upāsikā Acalā. After arriving there, while he was waiting at the door he saw[1058] the entire house shining with a pervading golden light that brought ease to mind and body.
Filled with joy, Sudhana went to Achala’s house. Standing in the door, he saw the whole house lit up with a soothing golden light.

'od des tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la phog par gyur ma thag tu tshor ba thams cad la dbang bsgyur ba'i ting nge 'dzin gyi sgo mang po dang / zhi ba'i gnas kyi ting nge 'dzin gyi sgo mang po dang / 'gro ba thams cad dang bral ba'i ting nge 'dzin gyi sgo mang po dang / kun du lta ba'i btang snyoms dang ldan pa'i ting nge 'dzin gyi sgo mang po dang / de bzhin gshegs pa'i mdzod kyi ting nge 'dzin gyi sgo mang po la sogs pa ting nge 'dzin gyi sgo lnga brgya tsam la zhugs par gyur te yongs su skyes so/ / de dag kyang shin tu phra zhing gzhon pa ste/

The instant the light touched Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, he entered, and there arose five hundred subtle and newly developed entrances to samādhi such as entrances to the samādhi called power over all sensations,[1059] entrances to the samādhi called the region of peace, entrances to the samādhi called apart from[1060] all beings, entrances to the samādhi called the all-seeing equanimity, and entrances to the samādhi called the treasure of the tathāgatas.

The moment Sudhana was touched by the light, five hundred subtle trances descended upon him, beginning with a trance characterized by power over all sensations, trance absorption in the realm of tranquillity, absorption in the welfare of all beings, absorption in the equanimity of the universal eye, and absorption in the matrix of realization of Thusness.
'di ltar dper na/ thog ma mngal du zhugs pa'i rnam par shes pa lta bu ste/ ting nge 'dzin de dag kyang shin tu phra zhing gzhon par skyes par gyur to/ /
Those samādhis were very subtle and newly developed like a consciousness that has just entered the womb.
The feeling of those trances was as subtle as the consciousness of a half-day old embryo.

des dri zhim po zhig tshor na yang / de ni lha la yang med/ lha'i bu mo la yang med/ klu la yang med/ klu'i bu mo la yang med/ gnod sbyin la yang med/ gnod sbyin gyi bu mo la yang med/ dri za la yang med/ dri za'i bu mo la yang med/ lha ma yin la yang med/ lha ma yin gyi bu mo la yang med/ nam mkha' lding la yang med/ nam mkha' lding gi bu mo la yang med; mi 'am ci la yang med/ mi 'am ci'i bu mo la yang med/ lto 'phye chen po la yang med/ lto 'phye chen po'i bu mo la yang med/ mi la yang med/ mi'i bu mo la yang med cing mi srid pa de lta bu'i dri zhim po tshor bar gyur to/ /

Then Sudhana sensed a lovely scent of such a kind that male devas did not have, that female devas did not have, that male nāgas did not have, that female nāgas did not have, that male yakṣas did not have, that female yakṣas did not have, that male gandharvas did not have, that female gandharvas did not have, that male asuras did not have, that female asuras did not have, that male garuḍas did not have, that female garuḍas did not have, that male kinnaras did not have, that female kinnaras did not have, that male mahoragas did not have, that female mahoragas did not have, that male humans did not have, and that female humans did not have.
He also smelled a scent more beautiful than that of any gods or goddesses or humans or any other creatures of the world,
bud med de'i gzugs dang mnyam pa yang phyogs bcu'i 'jig rten na med na lhag pa lta ga las 'ong /
There was no equal to that girl’s body in the worlds in the ten directions, let alone one that was superior.
and there was to be found in all the world no one even equal to, much less more beautiful than, that girl Achala.

kha dog dang mdog de lta bu yang de bzhin gshegs pa'i sku mdog dang / kha dog dang / byang chub sems dpa' dbang bskur ba'i kha dog dang / mdog ma gtogs par de'i kha dog dang; mdog tu mnyam pa phyogs bcu'i 'jig rten na med na lhag pa lta ga las 'ong /

Apart from the luster of the color of the bodies of the tathāgatas, and the luster of the color of consecrated bodhisattvas, there was no one in the worlds in the ten directions who had a body with a luster of color that equaled the luster of color of her body, let alone one that was superior.
The radiance of her complexion,

lus kyi chu zheng dang / dbyibs de lta bu'ang de bzhin gshegs pa'i sku'i khrun chu zheng dang / dbyibs dang / byang chub sems dpa' dbang bskur ba thob pa'i lus kyi chu zheng dang / dbyibs ma gtogs par de'i lus kyi chu zheng dang / dbyibs su mnyam pa phyogs bcu'i 'jig rten na med na lhag pa lta ga las 'ong /

Apart from the shape and figure of the bodies of the tathāgatas, and the shape and figure of consecrated bodhisattvas, there was no one in the worlds in the ten directions who had a body with a shape and figure that equaled the shape and figure of her body, let alone one that was superior.
the proportions of her body, and

'od kyi rgyan de lta bu yang de bzhin gshegs pa'i 'od kyi rgyan dang / byang chub sems dpa' dbang bskur ba thob pa'i 'od kyi rgyan ma gtogs par de'i 'od kyi rgyan dang mnyam pa phyogs bcu'i 'jig rten na med na lhag pa lta ga las 'ong /

Apart from the aura of light of the tathāgatas, and the aura of light of consecrated bodhisattvas, there was no one in the worlds in the ten directions who had an aura of light that equaled her aura of light, let alone one that was superior.
the magnificence of her aura were such that none in the world, save buddhas and coronated enlightening beings, even equaled, much less surpassed them.

de'i kha'i drod kyi dri zhim po dang mnyam pa'i dri de lta bu yang phyogs bcu'i 'jig rten gyi lha'i gnas sam/ klu dang / gnod sbyin dang / dri za dang / lha ma yin dang / nam mkha' lding dang / mi 'am ci dang / lto 'phye chen po dang / mi dang / mi ma yin pa'i gnas na med na lhag pa lta ga las 'ong /

Apart from the tathāgatas and the consecrated bodhisattvas, there was no one in the worlds in the ten directions, in the realms of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, or nonhumans, who had a scent that equaled the scent of the breath that came from her mouth, let alone one that was superior.
Her scent was unequaled and unsurpassed by any celestial, preternatural, or human beings.

khyim gyi rgyan dang longs spyod de lta bu yang de bzhin gshegs pa'i longs spyod dang / byang chub sems dpa' dbang bskur ba thob pa'i longs spyod ma gtogs par/ de'i khyim gyi rgyan dang longs spyod dang mnyam pa yang phyogs bcu'i 'jig rten na med na lhag pa lta ga las 'ong /

Apart from the displays and enjoyments of the abodes of the tathāgatas, and the displays and enjoyments of the abodes of the consecrated bodhisattvas, there was no one in the worlds in the ten directions who could equal the displays and enjoyments of her abode, let alone anyone who could be her superior.
The furnishings of her abode were unequaled and unsurpassed in all the world, except by the accoutrements of buddhas and coronated enlightening beings.

g.yog 'khor phun sum tshogs pa de lta bu yang de bzhin gshegs pa'i 'khor phun sum tshogs pa dang / byang chub sems dpa'i 'khor phun sum tshogs pa ma gtogs par de'i g.yog 'khor phun sum tshogs pa dang mnyam pa yang phyogs bcu'i 'jig rten na med na lhag pa lta ga las 'ong ste/

Apart from the perfect entourage of attendants of the tathāgatas and the perfect entourage of attendants of the consecrated bodhisattvas, there was no one in the worlds in the ten directions who could equal her perfect entourage of attendants, let alone anyone who could be her superior.
Her company was also unequaled and unsurpassed by any in the world, except for the companies of buddhas and coronated enlightening beings.
dge bsnyen ma mi g.yo ba de la 'dod chags dang ldan pa'i sems kyis blta bar nus pa'i sems can de lta bu yang phyogs bcu'i 'jig rten gyi sems can gyi ris na med do/ /
There was no being among the classes of beings in the worlds in the ten directions who could look upon the upāsikā Acalā with desire.
There was no one in all the world who could look upon Achala with lust—
dge bsnyen ma mi g.yo ba de mthong ma thag tu nyon mongs pa zhi bar mi 'gyur ba de lta bu'i sems can yang phyogs bcu'i 'jig rten gyi sems can gyi ris na med de/
There was no being among the classes of beings in the worlds in the ten directions whose kleśas did not cease as soon as they saw the upāsikā Acalā.
there was no one in the world whose afflictions did not cease the moment he beheld her.

'di lta ste/ dper na/ tshangs pa chen po stong phrag bcu la dbang bsgyur ba la ni/ 'dod pa la spyod pa'i nyon mongs pa rnams mi rgyu'o/ / de bzhin du dge bsnyen ma mi g.yo ba yang mthong ma thag tu sems can rnams kyi nyon mongs pa mi rgyu'o/ /

Just as the Mahābrahmās who have power over a million desire realms[1061] do not have kleśas arising within them, in the same way, the beings who saw the upāsikā Acalā did not have kleśas arising within them.
Just as gods with controlling power who live in the realm of desire do not activate afflictions, similarly people who saw Achala did not act on afflictions.
dge bsnyen ma mi g.yo ba de la blta bas ngoms par 'gyur ba'i sems can de lta bu yang / shes rab kyis ngoms pa ma gtogs par phyogs bcu'i 'jig rten gyi khams kyi sems can gyi ris na med do/ /
There was no being among the classes of beings in the worlds in the ten directions who had enough of looking upon the upāsikā Acalā, apart from those who had the contentment of wisdom.
There was no one in the world who became satiated with the sight of Achala, except those who were sated with wisdom.

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis/ dge bsnyen ma mi g.yo ba'i lus kyi byin bsam gyis mi khyab pa dang / gzugs dang; kha dog dang / dbyibs dang / chu zheng bsam gyis mi khyab pa dang / sa'i gzhi dang / grong khyer dang / rin po che thams cad la thogs pa med pa'i 'od zer gyi dra ba'i rgyan bsam gyis mi khyab pa dang / sems can gyi don bsam gyis mi khyab pa sgrub pa mthong ste/

Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, saw the inconceivable majesty of the upāsikā Acalā’s body and her inconceivable form, color, shape, and figure; he saw the inconceivable network of unimpeded light rays from the entirety of the ground, city, and jewels; and he saw the accomplishment of inconceivable benefits for beings.

Then Sudhana, in an attitude of reverence, seeing Achala’s inconceivable physical majesty, her inconceivable appearance, and her inconceivable aura of light, which could not be blocked by all the cities and mountains on the face of the earth,

ba spu'i bu ga thams cad nas byung ba'i dri zhim po tshor nas/ 'khor rgya mtsho phun sum tshogs pa mtha' yas pa mthong ste/ khyim dang / gzhal med khang gi rgyan phun sum tshogs pa mi 'phrogs pa mthong nas/ yon tan rgya mtsho tshad med pa khong du chud de/ dge bsnyen ma mi g.yo ba la tshigs su bcad pa 'dis bstod do/ /

He smelled the lovely scent that arose from all her pores, saw the infinite perfect assembly of her attendants, saw the perfect, unassailable display of the aerial palace that was her home, perceived the measureless ocean of its qualities, and praised the upāsikā Acalā with this verse:

sensing the inconceivable beneficial fragrance coming from her pores, looking over her endless company of followers, noticing the matchless adornment of her abode, immersed in the measureless ocean of her virtues, eulogized Achala with this verse:

khyod kyis rtag tu tshul khrims dri med yongs bsrungs te/ / bzod pa shin tu yangs pa'ang yongs su bsgoms mdzad cing / / brtson 'grus brtan pa rdo rje lta bu bsgrubs pas na/ / ri bo'i rgyal po lta bur 'gro bar 'phags shing 'bar/ /

“You continually maintain a stainless good conduct. You are completely pervaded[1062] by vast patience. You are established in diligence as firm as a vajra. You are superior among beings like the shining lord[1063] of mountains.”[1064] {1}
Who keeps conduct pure, Develops great tolerance, And makes vigor enduring as diamond Stands out in the world like a mountain of light.

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis/ dge bsnyen ma mi g.yo ba la tshigs su gcad pa des mngon par bstod de/ 'di skad ces smras so/ / 'phags ma/ bdag gis bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed na/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bgyi ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bgyi ba ma 'tshal te/ 'phags ma ni/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams la gdams ngag dang / rjes su bstan pa mdzad do zhes bdag gis thos nas/ 'phags ma/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bgyi ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bgyi ba bdag la bshad du gsol/

After Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, had praised the upāsikā Acalā with that verse, he said to her, “Āryā, I have developed the aspiration for the highest, complete enlightenment, but I do not know how bodhisattvas should train in bodhisattva conduct and in what way they should practice it. Āryā, I have heard that you give instruction and teachings to bodhisattvas! I pray that you explain to me how bodhisattvas should train in bodhisattva conduct and how they should practice it!”

Then Sudhana said to her, “Noble one, I have set my mind on supreme perfect enlightenment, but I do not know how to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings. I hear that you give instruction to enlightening beings, so I ask you to tell me how an enlightening being is to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings.”

de nas dge bsnyen ma mi g.yo bas/ byang chub sems dpa'i ngag 'jam zhing yid du 'ong la nyams su bde bas/ tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la dga' bar 'gyur ba'i tshig tu brjod nas/ 'di skad ces smras so/ /
The upāsikā Acalā spoke with a gentle, beautiful, delightful voice to Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, with words that brought him joy, saying,
In the affectionate, pleasing, charming words of an enlightening being, Achala greeted Sudhana and said,
rigs kyi bu/ de ltar khyod kyis bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed pa legs so/ / legs so/ /
“Noble one, it is excellent, excellent, that you have developed the aspiration for the highest, complete enlightenment.
“It is good that you aspire to supreme perfect enlightenment.

rigs kyi bu/ kho mo ni byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa thub par dka' ba'i ye shes kyi snying po thob pa ste/ byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa'i sgo yi dam brtan pa la slob pa/ chos thams cad mnyam pa nyid kyi sa'i gzungs kyi sgo thob pa'o/ /

“Noble one, I have attained the bodhisattva liberation called the essence of wisdom that is difficult to attain. I train in the gateway of bodhisattva conduct that possesses a strong commitment. I have attained the gateway of the power of retention of the level of the equality of all phenomena.

I have an enlightening liberation containing invincible knowledge, and I cultivate enlightening beings’ way of practice of firm resolve. I have also attained mental command of the stage of equanimity in all things,
kho mo ni spobs pa'i ye shes snang ba chos kyi gzhi thams cad snang bar brjod pa thob pa'o/ /
I have attained the gateway called the light of the wisdom of eloquence that elucidates the basis[1065] of all phenomena,
and I am imbued with the light of knowledge to clarify the true state of all phenomena.
kho mo ni chos thams cad yongs su btsal bas mi skyo ba'i rgyan gyi ting 'dzin gyi sgo thob pa'o/ /
and I have attained the gateway of the samādhi called the display of the tireless search for the Dharma.”
I have also attained concentration of tireless search for truth.”

smras pa/ 'phags ma/ byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa thub par dka' ba'i ye shes kyi snying po de'i yul ni ji lta bu zhig mchis/ yi dam la brtan pa'i byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa'i sgo dang / chos thams cad mnyam pa nyid kyi sa'i gzungs kyi sgo dang / chos kyi gzhi thams cad snang bar brjod pa'i spobs pa snang ba'i sgo dang / chos yongs su btsal bas mi skyo ba'i rgyan gyi ting nge 'dzin gyi sgo'i yul ni ji lta bu zhig mchis/

Sudhana asked, “Āryā, what is the scope of the bodhisattva liberation called the essence of the wisdom that is difficult to attain? What is the scope of the gateway of bodhisattva conduct with a strong commitment, of the gateway of maintaining the level of the equality of all phenomena, of the gateway of the light of the wisdom of eloquence that elucidates the basis[1066] of all phenomena, and of the gateway of the samādhi called the display of the tireless search for the Dharma?”
Sudhana asked her about the sphere of these attainments,
smras pa/ rigs kyi bu/ gnas 'di ni yid ches par dka'o/
Acalā answered, “Noble one, this is a subject that is difficult to believe.”[1067]
and she said her state was hard to believe.

smras pa/ 'phags ma/ bstan du gsol/ sangs rgyas kyi byin dang / dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyis yongs su bzung na yid ches par mchi grang / rtogs pa dang / 'tshal pa dang / rnam par rtogs pa dang / rjes su rtogs pa dang / rig pa dang / dmigs su phebs pa dang / goms pa dang / mi 'gal ba dang / rnam par mi rtog pa dang / sgro 'dogs pa ma mchis pa dang / mnyam par bgyid par yang mchi grang /

Sudhana said, “Āryā, please teach me. Through the power of the buddhas and being in the care of the kalyāṇamitras, I will believe it, comprehend it, know it, understand it, discern it, cognize it, reflect upon it as a focus of my attention, contemplate it, not deny it, not conceptualize it, not add to it, and be in accord with it.”

Sudhana urged her to tell him, assuring her that by the power of Buddha and the help of spiritual benefactors he would believe in it, enter into it, investigate, contemplate, follow, and cultivate it, and would not quarrel or make up arbitrary ideas or assumptions about it, but would strive to equal it.
de nas dge bsnyen ma mi g.yo bas/ tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la 'di skad ces smras so/ /
Then the upāsikā Acalā said to Sudhana, the head merchant’s son,
Achala then said to Sudhana,

rigs kyi bu/ sngon 'das pa'i dus shig na dri ma med pa'i 'od kyi bskal pa la de bzhin gshegs pa phyag rab tu brkyang pa zhes bya ba 'jig rten du byung ste/ kho mo yang de'i tshe rgyal po glog gis byin pa'i bu gcig ma zhig tu gyur nas/
“Noble one, in the past, during a kalpa called Stainless Light, appeared the tathāgata named Pralambabāhu. At that time I was the only daughter[1068] of King Vidyuddatta.
“A long time ago, in a past eon called Undefiled Light, a buddha named Arms Extended Downward appeared in the world. I was the daughter of a king named Vidyuddatta.

de'i tshe nub mo mi nyal tsam zhig na rgyal po'i sgo yang bcad/ pha dang ma yang nyal/ skyes pa dang bud med dag kyang gnyid kyis log /rol mo brdung ba dang dkrol ba'i sgra yang zhi/ lhan cig spyod pa'i bud med lnga brgya tsam dag kyang nyal bar gyur pa zhig na/ kho mo mal gyi steng na 'dug cing / nam mkha'i dbyings la rgyu ba'i skar ma'i tshogs kyi phreng ba rnam par 'khod pa la lta lta ba las/ steng gi bar snang la/ bcom ldan 'das de bzhin gshegs pa dgra bcom pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas phyag rab tu brkyang pa ri'i rgyal po ri rab ltar lha dang / klu dang / gnod sbyin dang / dri za dang / lha ma yin dang / nam mkha' lding dang / mi 'am ci dang / lto 'phye chen po'i 'khor mang pos bskor ba/ byang chub sems dpa'i tshogs grangs med pas yongs su bskor ba/ phyogs thams cad du 'od zer gyi dra ba thogs pa med pas rgyas par khyab pa'i sku bzhugs pa mthong ngo/ /

One night when I was not sleeping,[1069] the door of the royal residence[1070] was shut, my parents were asleep, the staff of men and women had gone to sleep, the sound of music being played had ceased, and the five hundred women that I spent time with were sleeping, I sat on my bed, looking at the constellations of stars in the sky. In the sky above I saw the Tathāgata Arhat Samyaksaṃbuddha Pralambabāhu, who was like Sumeru, the lord of mountains. He was accompanied by an entourage of many nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas. His body spread a network of unimpeded light rays throughout all directions.

One quiet night, as my parents slept in the inner apartments of the palace, and the men and women of the court were fast asleep, and the sounds of music had all stopped, and my five hundred girl companions were all in bed, as I gazed up at the starry night sky I saw up there the Buddha, like the polar mountain, surrounded by many celestial beings, spirits, preternatural creatures, and countless enlightening beings, his body pervading everywhere with an aura of unobstructed light.
de bzhin gshegs pa de'i sku'i ba spu'i bu ga thams cad nas kyang dri zhim po rnam pa 'di lta bu byung ste/ des kho mo'i lus dang sems shin tu bde bar gyur/ yid shin tu dga' bar gyur te/
From all the pores of the tathāgata’s body came a beautiful scent that brought ease to my mind and body and great happiness to my mind.
From his pores came a fragrance that soothed my body and mind and made me happy.

mal gyi steng nas langs nas/ sor mo bcu'i thal mo sbyar te sa la babs nas; bcom ldan 'das de bzhin gshegs pa phyag rab tu brkyang pa de la phyag 'tshal te/ de'i spyi gtsug la bltas na yang mtha' thug par ma rung / g.yas g.yon gyi tshad kyang zin par ma rung / mtshan dang dpe byad phun sum tshogs pa la bsams na yang ngoms par ma rung ste/ de'i tshe kho mo 'di snyam du bsams so/ /

“I arose from my bed and stood on the floor, and with my ten fingers placed together in homage, I bowed down to the Tathāgata Pralambabāhu. As I looked at the crown of his head there seemed to be no end to it, and I could not grasp his extent to the right or left. I could never have enough of contemplating his perfect signs and features of a great being.

Getting up from bed, I saluted the Buddha; looking at him, I found I could not determine any limit to the extent of his height and breadth. As I reflected on his marks and embellishments of greatness,

las ji lta bu zhig byas na; lus phun sum tshogs pa 'di lta bu ni 'thob par 'gyur/ mtshan dang dpe byad bzang po phun sum tshogs pa ni skye bar 'gyur/ 'od kyi rgyan phun sum tshogs pa ni 'byung bar 'gyur/ 'khor phun sum tshogs pa ni 'grub par 'gyur/ yid kyi rang bzhin gyi gnas dang longs spyod phun sum tshogs pa ni 'byung bar 'gyur/ bsod nams phun sum tshogs pa ni skye bar 'gyur/ ye shes phun sum tshogs pa ni rnam par dag par 'gyur/ ting nge 'dzin gyi rnam par 'phrul pa bsam gyis mi khyab pa phun sum tshogs pa ni yang dag par 'grub par 'gyur/ gzungs phun sum tshogs pa ni yongs su rdzogs par 'gyur/ spobs pa phun sum tshogs pa ni dbang du 'gyur snyam pa dang /

“At that time, I wondered, ‘Through what kind of karma can one obtain such a perfect body? Give rise to the perfect signs and features of a great bring? Have such a perfect display of light? Attain such a perfect entourage? Have such a perfect residence and requisites that are of the nature of the mind? Develop such a perfection of merit? Have such purified wisdom? Attain such perfect, inconceivable miracles from samādhi? Complete such perfect powers of retention? And have the power of such perfect eloquence?’

I thought, ‘By performing what kind of action is such a body obtained? How are the marks and embellishments of greatness attained? How is the aura of light attained? How does the retinue of followers develop? How do the mentally produced dwelling and furniture appear? How is virtue developed? How is knowledge purified? How are the inconceivable meditative projections accomplished? How is mental command perfected? How is eloquence mastered?’
rigs kyi bu/ de nas bcom ldan 'das de bzhin gshegs pa phyag rab tu brkyang pa des/ kho mo'i bsam pa thugs su chud nas 'di skad ces bka' stsal to/ /
“Noble one, the Bhagavat Tathāgata Pralambabāhu knew my thought and said,
“Reading my mind, that Buddha said to me,

bu mo khyod kyis nyon mongs pa thams cad gzhom pa'i phyir thub pa med pa'i sems skyed cig /mngon par zhen pa thams cad bsal ba'i phyir pham pa med pa'i sems skyed cig /chos zab mo'i tshul khong du chud par bya ba'i phyir zhum pa med pa'i sems skyed cig /sems can bsam pa mi bzad pa dang ldan pa'i rgya mtsho'i klong du ltung bas mi sgul ba'i sems skyed cig /srid pa'i lam gyi rgyud thams cad du skye ba'i skye mched du mgo rmongs pa med pa'i sems skyed cig /sangs rgyas thams cad blta bar mos pa rgyun mi gcad pa'i phyir ngoms mi shes pa'i sems skyed cig/ sangs rgyas thams cad kyi chos kyi sprin yongs su gzung ba'i phyir chog mi shes pa'i sems skyed cig /sangs rgyas thams cad kyi chos kyi tshul snang ba rtogs par bya ba'i phyir nges par rtogs pa'i sems skyed cig /de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi chos kyi 'khor lo gzung ba'i phyir yang dag par gzung ba'i sems skyed cig /de bzhin gshegs pa'i zhal nas byung ba shes par bya ba lta la ci smos kyi chung ngu na brdar byas pa tsam la yang 'khrul pa med pa'i sems skyed cig /bu mo khyod kyis sems can rnams kyi bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du chos rin po che rnam par dbye ba'i phyir rnam par dbye ba'i sems skyed cig ces byung ste/

‘Girl, develop an invincible motivation for the defeat of all the kleśas. Develop an undefeatable motivation for eliminating all attachment. Develop an unwearying motivation for comprehending the way of the profound Dharma. Develop an unshakable motivation for descending into the whirling ocean of the range[1071] of the thoughts of beings. Develop an unconfused motivation for the rebirth in all the states of existence within saṃsāra. Develop a never-satisfied motivation for the continuous aspiration to see all the buddhas. Develop a never-satiated motivation in order to obtain the clouds of Dharma of all the buddhas. Develop a realized motivation in order to realize the light of the way of the Dharma of all the buddhas. Develop an acquisitive motivation for acquiring the Dharma wheels of all the buddhas. Develop a motivation to be without delusion concerning even a small gesture, let alone to know that which comes from a tathāgata’s mouth. Girl, you should develop the motivation to distribute the precious Dharma in accordance with the aspirations of beings.’

‘Daughter, you should produce an invincible mind to destroy afflictions, an indomitable mind to get rid of all clinging, an intrepid mind to enter into the profound truth, a mind unshakable while descending into the whirlpool of the ocean of sentient beings who are attached to objects, a mind undeluded in the midst of all states of being, a mind tireless in seeking vision of all buddhas, a mind receiving the multitudes of teachings of all buddhas without complacence, a contemplative mind to attain the light of wisdom of all buddha-teachings, a retentive mind remembering the cycles of teaching of all buddhas, a mind free from forgetfulness even in regard to conventional terms, to say nothing of knowledge arising from the word of buddhas; and you should develop a mind of sharing, to distribute the jewels of the Teaching to all sentient beings according to their mentalities.’

de ltar rigs kyi bu/ kho mos bcom ldan 'das de bzhin gshegs pa dgra bcom pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas phyag rab tu brkyang pa las/ chos kyi tshul gyi gdams ngag gi sgo rnam pa de lta bu dag thos nas/ thams cad mkhyen pa'i ye shes la ni mngon par mos par gyur/
“Noble one, I heard from the Bhagavat Tathāgata Arhat Samyaksaṃbuddha Pralambabāhu, that king of the gateways of instruction to the way of the Dharma, and I longed to attain omniscient wisdom.
“Having heard such principles of the Teaching from the Buddha, desiring omniscience,
stobs bcu'i rang bzhin la ni mngon par smon par gyur/
I aspired to the nature of the strengths.
aiming for the development of the ten powers,
sangs rgyas kyi gsung la ni mngon par dad par gyur/
I wished for the words of the Buddha.
seeking the eloquence of a buddha,
sangs rgyas kyi 'od kyi rgyan ni yongs su sbyang bar dga'/
I wanted to have the purified display of light of a buddha.
wishing to purify in myself the aura of light of a buddha,
sangs rgyas kyi sku phun sum tshogs pa ni yongs su bsgrub par dga'/
I wanted to attain the perfect body of a buddha.
wishing to perfect a body like a buddha,
sangs rgyas kyi mtshan dang dpe byad bzang po rnam par dag pa la ni mngon par mos par gyur/
I longed to have a buddha’s pure signs and features of a great being.
desiring the purity of marks and embellishments of greatness of a buddha,
sangs rgyas kyi 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor phun sum tshogs pa la ni mngon par smon par gyur/
I aspired to have the perfect assembly of followers of a buddha.
aiming to gain a congregation like a buddha,
sangs rgyas kyi zhing rnam par dag pa la ni mngon par dad par gyur/
I wished for[1072] the pure realms of a buddha.
seeking purification of a buddha-land,
sangs rgyas kyi spyod lam phun sum tshogs pa la ni mngon par mos par gyur/
I longed for the perfect conduct of a buddha.
wishing to accomplish the deportment of a buddha,
sangs rgyas kyi sku tshe'i tshad phun sum tshogs pa la ni mngon par dga' nas/
I rejoiced in the perfect lifespan of a buddha.
wanting to attain the span of life of a buddha,
rdo rje ltar ri dang mtshon cha thams cad kyi mthus thub par dka' ba'i sems nyon mongs pa thams cad dang / nyan thos dang / rang sangs rgyas thams cad kyis mi phyed mi tshugs pa bskyed de/

I had developed the motivation that could not be impaired by all the kleśas or by the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, which like a vajra could not be defeated even by the strength of all mountains and weapons.
developing a mind that neither afflictions nor anyone concerned with self-liberation alone could break down, like indestructible adamant,

rigs kyi bu/ de nas nye bar bzung ba tshun chad du sems bskyed pa de'i mthus/ bskal pa 'dzam bu'i gling gi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed cig tu yid kyi dgu las kyang 'dod pa la spyad par mi dran na/ gnyis kyis gnyis 'du ba lta ci smos/

“Noble one, from that time until now, through the power of having developed that motivation, throughout as many kalpas as there are atoms in Jambudvīpa, I do not remember[1073] ever in my mind enjoying pleasures, let alone copulation.
I do not remember the arising of a single thought of enjoyment of desires—much less engaging in sexual intercourse—for as many eons thereafter as atoms in this continent.
rigs kyi bu/ de nas nye bar bzung ba tshun chad du rang gi gnyen bshes la'ang khong khro bo'i sems gcig ma bskyed na/ de ma yin pa'i sems can ma nyes pa gzhan lta la ci smos/
“Noble one, from that time until now, I have never had one thought of anger toward a kalyāṇamitra, let alone offended any other being.
I do not remember a single thought of anger toward my relatives, much less toward innocent others.

de nas nye bar bzung ba tshun chad du bdag tu lta ba dang ldan pa'i sems bskyed pa gcig tsam yang bskyed par mi dran na/ de ma yin pa'i yo byad gzhan la bdag gir byas te mngon par chags pa lta ci smos/

“Noble one, from that time until now, I do not remember having ever given rise to a single thought that holds the view that there is a self, let alone having attachment to things that I think of as being mine.
I do not remember a single thought related to the idea of self, much less having considered anything my own.
shi 'pho dang / mngal na gnas pa'i tshe 'ang sems rmongs pa'am/ 'du shes sna tshogs sam/ lung du ma bstan pa'i sems kyang byung du mi dran na/ legs par bsam shing gnas pa lta ci smos/

“Even when I died and was reborn inside a womb, I do not remember being in a state of stupidity, having various concepts, or having a neutral state of mind, let alone having a state of mental fixation.
I do not remember any confusion, or any notion of difference, or yet any indifference, even while in the womb between death and birth, much less while focusing my attention.
bskal pa de snyed cig tu sangs rgyas gcig kyang chung ngu na rmi lam du mthong ba'i rnam par dmigs par yang rjes su mi dran na/ byang chub sems dpa'i mig bcus mthong bar gyur pa lta ci smos/

“Throughout those kalpas I do not remember ever forgetting[1074] seeing a buddha, even down to the perception of the sight of a buddha in a dream, let alone the perception of the visual images of the ten levels of bodhisattvas.
In all those eons I did not forget a single vision of a buddha, not even a dream vision, much less those appearing to the ten eyes of an enlightening being.

de nas nye bar bzung ba tshun chad du de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi chos kyi sprin yang dag par 'dzin kyang chung ngu na ming du bya ba'i rnam pa tsam gyi chos kyi tshig dang / yi ge gcig kyang brjod par mi dran na/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i zhal gyi mdzod nas byung ba lta ci smos/

“From that time until now, while holding the clouds of Dharma of all the tathāgatas, I do not remember forgetting[1075] in my mind even a single word or term of the Dharma, even down to a single syllable, let alone what has emerged from the treasure of the mouths of the tathāgatas.
de nas nye bar bzung ba tshun chad du chos kyi rgya mtsho de snyed cig 'thung 'thung yang chung ngu na 'jig rten pa'i chos rnams la tshig 'ga' yang ma bsam ma brtags par mi dran no/ /
“From that time until now, while I drank and drank from the ocean of the Dharma, I do not remember ever ignoring and not contemplating even any words of the worldly Dharmas.
Ever since that original inspiration I have been imbibing the ocean of the Teaching, contemplating and reflecting on every single statement, even in the context of worldly phenomena.

de nas nye bar bzung ba tshun chad du de snyed cig gis chos kyi tshul rgya mtsho las kyang chung ngu na 'jig rten pa'i bzo'i rgyus dang tshul yang rung ste/ chos kyi tshul gyi sgo gang la yang kho mos ting nge 'dzin mngon par ma bsgrubs pa de lta bu med do/ /

“From that time until now, I do not remember not accomplishing the samādhi of a single gateway to the ways of the Dharma from among the ocean of the ways of the Dharma, even down to the ways of the knowledge of worldly crafts.
There is not a single facet of the Teaching that I have not become absorbed in, even in the context of worldly arts and sciences.

de nas nye bar bzung ba tshun chad du de bzhin gshegs pa de snyed kyi chos kyi 'khor lo bzung yang / ji ltar yongs su bzung ba las/ sems can 'dul ba'i dbang du bya ba ma gtogs par chung ngu na rjes su brgyud pa'i rgyus tsam gyi tshig dang / yi ge 'ga' yang por bar mi dran no/ /

“From that time until now, while I held the wheels of Dharma of the tathāgatas in order to guide beings, I do not remember leaving out a single word or even a single syllable that was transmitted to me.

Ever since that first inspiration, while holding the wheel of teaching of the buddhas, I have never omitted even a single word as I learned it, even in following logic, except to regulate the guidance of others.

de nas nye bar bzung ba tshun chad du sangs rgyas rgya mtsho de snyed cig mthong yang / chung ngu na sprul pa'i sangs rgyas kyi smon lam gyi rgyud kyang rung ste/ smon lam 'ga' yang kho mos sems can rgya mtsho thams cad rnam par dag par bya ba'i phyir mngon par ma bsgrubs pa med do/ /

“From that time until now, there is not a single prayer from the ocean of the visions of buddhas that I have not accomplished in order to purify the ocean of beings, even down to carrying out the prayer of a buddha who was an emanation.
There is not a single vow I have not undertaken in the presence of the buddhas I have met since then to purify the ocean of all sentient beings, even carrying out vows made to phantom buddhas.

de nas nye bar bzung ba tshun chad du/ sangs rgyas rgya mtsho de snyed cig gi sngon gyi byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa rgya mtsho las byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa 'ga' tsam yang / kho mos bdag gi spyod pa yongs su dag par bya ba'i phyir mngon par ma bsgrubs pa de lta bu mi dran no/ /
“From that time until now, I do not remember not practicing any bodhisattva conduct from the ocean of the past bodhisattva conduct of the ocean of buddhas in order to purify my conduct.
There is not a single enlightening practice from the ocean of past enlightening practices of the oceans of buddhas that I have not undertaken to purify my own practice.
de nas nye bar bzung ba tshun chad du/ sems can gang kho mos bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu ma bskul pa de lta bu gcig kyang mig lam du 'ongs par mi dran no/ /
There is not a single sentient being I have seen since then that I have not established in the determination for supreme enlightenment.
de nas nye bar bzung ba tshun chad du/ nyan thos dang / rang sangs rgyas yid la bya ba dang ldan pa'i sems bskyed pa gcig kyang mngon par bsgrubs su mi dran no/ /
“From that time until now, I do not remember creating a single motivation that was focused on being a śrāvaka or a pratyekabuddha.
I do not remember even having a thought of individual liberation since then.
