rigs kyi bu/ de nas nye bar bzung ba tshun chad du/ bskal pa 'dzam bu'i gling gi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed cig lon yang / tshig dang yi ge 'ga' la yang the tshom bskyed pa'am/ gnyis kyi 'du shes sam/ rnam par rtog pa'i 'du shes sam/ sna tshogs kyi 'du shes sam; rab kyi 'du shes sam/ bzang ngan gyi 'du shes sam/ sdug mi sdug gi 'du shes bskyed du mi dran no/ /

“Noble one, from that time until now, throughout as many kalpas as there are atoms in Jambudvīpa, I do not remember ever having given rise to doubts, dualistic identification, conceptualized identification, variegated identification, obdurate[1076] identification, identification as inferior,[1077] or identification as appropriate or inappropriate concerning any single word or syllable.

I do not remember ever conceiving any doubt, any notion of duality, any false discriminations, any notion of variety, any idea of grasping or rejection, any concept of inferior or advanced, or any thought of attachment or resistance, in regard to so much as even a single word or letter of the Teaching, for as many eons as atoms in this continent.
rigs kyi bu/ kho mo ni de phyin chad du sangs rgyas byung ba dang ma bral lo; ;
“Noble one, since that time, I have never been separated from the appearance of a buddha.
“Ever since then I have never been apart from buddhas,
sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das rnams dang ma bral lo/ /
I have never been separated from the buddha bhagavats.
byang chub sems dpa' rnams dang ma bral lo/ /
I have never been separated from the bodhisattvas.
enlightening beings,
yang dag pa'i dge ba'i bshes gnyen rnams dang ma bral lo/ /
I have never been separated from the true kalyāṇamitras.
and true spiritual benefactors.
sangs rgyas kyi smon lam thos pa dang ma bral lo/ /
I have never been separated from hearing the prayers of the buddhas.
I have always been hearing of the vows of buddhas,
byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa thos pa dang ma bral lo/ /
I have never been separated from hearing of the conduct of the bodhisattvas.
the practices of enlightening beings,
byang chub sems dpa'i pha rol tu phyin pa'i tshul thos pa dang ma bral lo/ /
I have never been separated from hearing the way of the perfections of the bodhisattvas.
the transcendent ways of enlightening beings,
byang chub sems dpa'i sa'i ye shes snang ba'i tshul thos pa dang ma bral lo/ /
I have never been separated from hearing the way of the light of the wisdom of the level of the bodhisattvas.
the light of knowledge of the stages of enlightening beings,
byang chub sems dpa'i gzungs dang / ting nge 'dzin mi bzad pa'i mdzod dang gter thos pa thob pa dang ma bral lo/ /
I have never been separated from the attainment of hearing the inexhaustible treasures and treasuries of the retentions and samādhis of the bodhisattvas.
the inexhaustible treasury of mental command and concentration of enlightening beings,
mtha' dang dbus med pa'i 'jig rten gyi khams kyi dra ba la 'jug cing / khong du chud par bya ba'i tshul thos pa dang ma bral lo/ /
I have never been separated from hearing of the comprehension of and entry into the centerless and endless network of world realms.
the way to enter the infinite network of worlds,
mtha' dang dbus med pa'i sems can gyi khams 'byung ba'i rgyu thos pa thob pa dang ma bral lo/ /
I have never been separated from the attainment of hearing the causes for the arising of the centerless and endless realms of beings.
the original causes of the infinite realms of sentient beings.
'gro ba thams cad kyi nyon mongs pa'i dra ba'i dkyil 'khor yongs su zad par bya ba'i ye shes snang ba dang ma bral lo/ /
I have never been separated from the light of the wisdom of the cessation of the domain of the network of the kleśas of all beings.
I have never left the light of knowledge removing the web of afflictions of all beings.
sems can thams cad kyi dge ba'i rtsa ba 'byung ba'i rgyu'i ye shes thob pa dang ma bral lo/ /
I have never been separated from the attainment of the wisdom of the causes that give rise to the roots of merit of all beings.
I have always been acquiring knowledge of the productive causes of the roots of goodness of all beings.
sems can thams cad kyi bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du lus yongs su ston pa dang ma bral lo/ /
I have never been separated from the manifestation of bodies in accordance with the aspirations of all beings.
I have always been appearing to all beings according to their mentalities.
sems can thams cad shes par byed pa'i dbyangs kyi dkyil 'khor rnam par dag pa dang ma bral lo/ /
I have never been separated from the pure domain of the speech that brings knowledge to all beings.
I have always been purifying the verbal range to instruct all beings.

rigs kyi bu/ kho mos byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa'i sgo thub par dka' ba'i ye shes kyi snying po 'di dang / chos thams cad yongs su btsal bas mi skyo ba'i rgyan gyi ting nge 'dzin gyi sgo 'di la snyoms par zhugs te/ byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa'i sgo yi dam la brtan pa 'di rnam par phye ba dang / gzungs kyi sgo chos thams cad mnyam pa nyid kyis 'di dang / slobs pa'i ye shes snang ba'i sgo chos kyi gzhi thams cad snang bar brjod pa 'di rnam par phye ba dang / cho 'phrul bsam gyis mi khyab pa yod na/ rigs kyi bu khyod mngon sum du blta bar 'dod dam/

“Noble one, I have accomplished this gateway of the bodhisattva liberation called the essence of the wisdom that is difficult to attain and the gateway of the samādhi called the display of the tireless search for the Dharma; I have reflected on the gateway to bodhisattva conduct with a firm commitment; I have contemplated the gateway called the power of retention of the level of the equality of all phenomena and the gateway called the light of the wisdom of eloquence that elucidates the basis of all phenomena; and therefore miraculous powers have arisen. Noble one, do you wish to see them?”

“Having attained this enlightening liberation containing invincible knowledge and this concentration of tireless searches for all truths, accumulating this enlightening way of practice of firm resolve, contemplating this method of mental command of the stage of equanimity in all things and this medium of the light of knowledge clarifying the basis of all things, I am capable of inconceivable miracles. Do you want to witness them?”
smras pa/ 'phags ma/ 'tshal lo/ /
Sudhana answered, “I wish to do so.”
Sudhana said, “I do.”

de nas dge bsnyen ma mi g.yo ba de na de ltar 'dug bzhin du/ byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa'i sgo thub par dka' ba'i ye shes kyi snying po la sogs pa dang / ting nge 'dzin gyi sgo thams cad yongs su btsal bas mi skyo ba'i rgyan la sogs pa dang / ting nge 'dzin gyi sgo don yod pa'i dkyil 'khor gyi rgyan la sogs pa dang / ting nge 'dzin gyi sgo stobs bcu'i ye shes kyi dkyil 'khor mngon du 'gyur ba la sogs pa dang / ting nge 'dzin gyi sgo sangs rgyas kyi rigs mi zad pa'i mdzod la sogs pa ting nge 'dzin gyi sgo brgya stong phrag bcu la rnam par blta ba dang / rnam par spyad pa dang / rjes su 'jug pa dang / nges par rtogs par byas so/ /

The upāsikā Acalā viewed, analyzed, followed, and realized gateways of bodhisattva liberations such as the essence of wisdom that is difficult to attain and many millions of gateways of samādhis: gateways of samādhis such as the display of the tireless search for the Dharma, samādhis such as the display of the unfailing domain, samādhis such as facing the display of the domain of the wisdom of the ten strengths, and samādhis such as the inexhaustible treasure of the buddha family.

Then, as she sat there, Achala looked into, passed through, followed, and meditated on ten hundred thousand doors of concentration, beginning with the door of enlightening liberation containing invincible knowledge, the door of concentration of tireless searches for all truths, the door of concentration on the arrangement of the sphere of efficacy, the door of concentration on the sphere of the ten powers, and the door of liberation through concentration on the inexhaustible source of all buddhas.

de ltar dge bsnyen ma mi g.yo ba snyoms par zhugs ma thag tu/ tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis/ phyogs bcur 'jig rten gyi khams sangs rgyas kyi zhing brjod du med pa phrag bcu'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed rnam pa drug tu g.yos pa dang / bai DUr+ya yongs su dag pa'i rgyu las gyur par gnas par mthong ngo/ / 'jig rten gyi khams re re'i gling bzhi pa bye ba phrag brgya brgya na/ de bzhin gshegs pa bye ba phrag brgya brgya bzhugs par mthong ste/ la la ni dga' ldan gyi gnas na bzhugs pa nas/ la la ni yongs su mya ngan las 'da' ba mdzad pa'i bar du'ang mthong ngo/ / de'ang 'jig rten gyi khams bai DUr+ya'i rang bzhin de dag yongs su dag cing sgrib pa med pa'i phyir te/ de bzhin gshegs pa de dag so so nas 'od zer dang / 'od kyi dkyil 'khor chos kyi dbyings thams cad du rgyas par khyab par mda' ba dang / de bzhin gshegs pa de dag so so'i 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor shin tu rnam par phye ba rgya mtsho yang mthong bar gyur to/ / de bzhin gshegs pa de dag re re'i gsung gi dkyil 'khor chos kyi 'khor lo thams cad brjod pa/ sems can thams cad kyi rna lam du rnam par grag pa'ang thos par gyur to/ /

As soon as the upāsikā Acalā rested in those samādhis, Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, saw world realms as numerous as the atoms in ten anabhilāpya buddha realms in the ten directions shake in six ways, and he saw that they were formed of pure beryl. He saw in each world realm a billion tathāgatas in a billion four-continent world realms. He saw some dwelling in Tuṣita and so on, up to some passing away into nirvāṇa. He saw that because those completely pure world realms of beryl were unobscured, each of those tathāgatas pervaded the entire realm of phenomena with their light rays and halos; each of those tathāgatas had their own ocean of separate assemblies of followers; and each of those tathāgatas taught the wheel of the entire Dharma, which was heard by all beings, who listened to the domains of their speech.

As soon as Achala had reach these concentrations, Sudhana saw as many worlds as atoms in ten inexpressible numbers of buddha-lands quaking, and appearing made of clear lapis lazuli. He also saw in each world a billion sets of four continents and a billion buddhas. He saw some of the buddhas in the heaven of satisfaction, some descending to be born on earth, some in the womb, some first-born, some leaving home for ascetic practice, some sitting under the tree of enlightenment, some defeating the demons, some realizing enlightenment, some teaching, some entering final extinction—this was because there was no obstruction to vision in the worlds made of clear lapis lazuli. He also saw the aura of light of each buddha pervading all universes, and he saw the orderly congregations of each buddha. He also heard the voice of the individual buddha communicating all the cycles of the Teaching to all sentient beings.
de nas dge bsnyen ma mi g.yo ba ting nge 'dzin de las langs nas/ tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la 'di skad ces smras so/ /
Then the upāsikā Acalā rose from that samādhi and said to Sudhana, the head merchant’s son,
Then Achala emerged from concentration and said to Sudhana,
rigs kyi bu khyod kyis mthong ngam/ thos sam/ shes sam/
“Noble one, did you see that? Did you hear that? Did you discern that?”
“Did you see? Did you hear? Did you understand?”
smras pa/ 'phags ma/ mthong ngo/ /thos so/ /rig go /
He answered “I saw it. I heard it. I discerned it.”
Sudhana said, “I saw, I heard, I understood.”
The upāsikā Acalā said,
Achala said,
rigs kyi bu/ kho mo ni de ltar byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa yi dam brtan pa la slob cing /
“Noble one, I have trained in the gateway of the bodhisattva conduct called possessing a strong commitment;
“In this way, learning enlightening beings’ practice of firm resolve,
chos thams cad yongs su btsal bas mi skyo ba'i rgyan gyi ting nge 'dzin la mnyam par bzhag ste/
I have rested in the samādhi called the display of the tireless search for the Dharma;
absorbed in tireless search for all truths,
byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa'i sgo thub par dka' ba'i ye shes kyi snying po la gnas nas/
I have dwelled in the gateway of bodhisattva liberations called the essence of the wisdom that is difficult to attain;
established in enlightening beings’ way of liberation by invincible knowledge,

chos thams cad mnyam pa nyid kyi sa'i gzungs khong du chud pa dang / spobs pa'i ye shes snang ba chos kyi gzhi thams cad snang bar brjod pa la mkhas pa'i legs par bshad pas/ sems can thams cad yongs su tshim par byed par zad na/

I have realized the power of retention of the level of the equality of all phenomena; and through being skilled in describing the light of the wisdom of eloquence that elucidates the basis of all phenomena, I have taught beings and brought them satisfaction.

I satisfy all sentient beings with good explanation by following mental command of the stage of equanimity in all things, using the skill of the light of knowledge of how to elucidate the basis of all things.
kho mos byang chub sems dpa' yon tan tshad med pa bsam gyis mi khyab pa dang ldan pa nam mkha'i dbyings la 'dab chags khyu mchog 'khod pa ltar gnas med par spyod pa/

“However, how could I know the conduct or describe the qualities of the bodhisattvas who possess measureless, inconceivable qualities; whose activity has no fixed location, like the lord of birds in the sky;
How can I know the practice or tell the virtues of the enlightening beings who are imbued with inconceivable, measureless virtues,

nam mkha' lding gi dbang po chen po ltar yongs su smin pa'i byang chub sems dpa' gdon pa'i phyir/ sems can thams cad kyi rgya mtsho la 'jug pa/ tshong pa ltar stobs bcu'i ye shes rin po che mngon par 'dod cing / thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi rin po che'i gling du rgyu ba/

who, like the great lord of the garuḍas, dive into the ocean of beings in order to extract the ripened bodhisattvas; who, like merchants, go the island of the jewels of omniscience, longing for the jewel that is the wisdom of the ten strengths;

who are like eagles soaring independently through the sky, who plunge into the sea of sentient beings to take out the mature enlightening beings, who search the treasure island of omniscience for the jewels of knowledge of the ten powers,

mthu dang ldan pa'i nya pa ltar yid du 'ong ba'i chos kyi dkyil 'khor gyi rgya dang ldan pa'i lag pas sred pa'i chu las byung ba'i sems can yongs su smin par mngon par gdon pa'i phyir chos kyi rgya mtsho la rnam par rgyu ba/ lha'i dbang po ltar nyon mongs pa'i lha ma yin gyi g.yul chen po gdul ba bzlog pa'i phyir khams gsum gyi gnas yongs su bkang zhing rnam par rgyu ba/ nyi ma'i dkyil 'khor ltar sems can gyi sred pa'i chu dang nyon mongs pa'i 'dam shin tu bskam pa'i phyir chos kyi dbyings kyi nam mkha'i dbyings la yang dag par 'phags pa/

who, like strong fishermen, go onto the ocean of saṃsāra[1078] with the beautiful net of the domain of the wheel of the Dharma in their hands in order to draw ripened beings out from the water of craving; who, like the lord of the devas,[1079] move throughout the three realms, filling them in order to repel and subjugate the attacks of the asuras of the kleśas; who, like the disk of the sun, rise high in the sky of the realm of the Dharma in order to dry the water of the craving of beings and the mud of the kleśas;

who go like strong fishers into the sea of the mundane whirl with the net of the Teaching to mature beings born amid craving and pull them out of it, who go like titan kings throughout all realms of existence quelling the titanic disturbances and agitations of afflictions, who rise like the sun in the sky of the reality realm to evaporate the water of beings’ cravings and dry up the mud of afflictions,

zla ba nya zhing rgyas pa ltar 'dul ba'i yid kyi me tog ku mu da rnam par kha dbye ba'i phyir ye shes kyi nam mkha' la mngon par shar ba; sa'i gzhi ltar 'gro ba thams cad kyi dge ba'i dbang po'i myu gu bskyed cing rnam par spel ba'i phyir/ byams mi byams dang / mthon dman med par 'jig rten na mnyam par gnas pa/ rlung dmar ltar sems can thams cad kyi nyon mongs pa dang / lta ba'i shing dang / shing phran gyi nags tshal dang / kun dga' rtsa ba nas gdon pa'i phyir chags pa med par phyogs thams cad du rnam par rgyu ba/ 'khor los bsgyur ba ltar bsdu ba'i dngos po'i yo byad dang rkyen gyis 'gro ba thams cad yongs su bsdu ba'i phyir/ 'jig rten na rnam par spyod pa de dag gi spyod pa shes pa'am/ yon tan brjod par nus re skan/

who, like the full moon, shine in the sky of wisdom in order to cause the night lotuses of the minds of those to be guided to blossom; who, like the surface of the Earth, support all equally without any distinction between those who are friends and not friends, or those who are high and those who are low, in order to cause the sprouts of the power of goodness in all beings to rise and grow; who, like a tempest, move everywhere without impediment in order to uproot the trees, vines, forests, and groves of the kleśas and false views of all beings; who, like a cakravartin, act within the world in order to gather all beings through conditions and requisites as methods of gathering pupils?

who rise like the full moon in the sky to awaken the water lilies of the minds of the teachable, who support all beings equally, whether friendly or hostile, high or low, to plant and grow the sprouts of roots of goodness in all sentient beings, who go everywhere unhindered like the wind to uproot the afflictions and views of all sentient beings, who go through the world like sovereigns uniting all beings with generosity, kindness, assistance, and cooperation?

song / rigs kyi bu/ lho phyogs kyi rgyud 'di nyid kyi yul dga' 'dzin tshad med pa na/ grong khyer dga' ba 'dzin pa zhes bya ba yod de/ de na kun du rgyu thams cad du 'gro ba zhes bya ba 'dug gi /de'i gan du song la/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bya ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bya ba dris shig /

“Depart, noble one. In this southern region, in a land called Amitatosala, there is a town named Tosala. There dwells the parivrājaka by the name of Sarvagamin. Go to him and ask him, ‘How should a bodhisattva train in bodhisattva conduct? How should a bodhisattva practice it?’ ”
“South of here is a city called Tosala in a land called Amitatosala. There is a mendicant named Sarvagamin living there. Go ask him how to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings.”

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis/ dge bsnyen ma mi g.yo ba'i rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te/ dge bsnyen ma mi g.yo ba la lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas yang dang yang bltas te/ dge bsnyen ma mi g.yo ba'i drung nas song ngo/ /

Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, bowed his head to the feet of the upāsikā Acalā, circumambulated the upāsikā Acalā a hundred thousand times, keeping her to his right, and, looking back again and again, departed from the presence of the upāsikā Acalā.
So then Sudhana paid his respects to Achala and left.

d.crumb: [kun du rgyu thams cad du 'gro ba]

f.d: [kun du rgyu thams cad du 'gro ba]
Chapter 23. Sarvagamin
Sarvagamin

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang / dge bsnyen ma mi g.yo ba mngon du byas te/ dge bsnyen ma mi g.yo ba'i gdams ngag rjes su dran par byed cing / dge bsnyen ma mi g.yo bas bstan pa dang / yang dag par bstan pa dang / bsgrags pa dang / bshad pa dang / brjod pa dang / yang dag par brjod pa dang / bzhag pa dang / rnam par phye ba dang / smos pa dang / rgya cher bstan pa de dag thams cad la gdon mi za bar yid ches shing / rjes su 'brang bar bya ba dang / rjes su bsam pa dang / khong du chud par bya ba dang / bsgom pa dang / yongs su bsgom pa dang / gzhan du mi 'gyur ba dang / rtogs par bya ba dang / snang bar bya ba dang / mnyam par bya ba byed cing

Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, visualizing in his mind the upāsikā Acalā, remembering the instruction of the upāsikā Acalā, with conviction in and no doubt about what the upāsikā Acalā had taught, proclaimed, instructed, described,[1080] sanctioned, established, explicated, stated, and elaborated upon it; he followed it, contemplated it, comprehended it, meditated on it, was absorbed in it,[1081] was fixed upon it, understood it, illuminated it, and became equal to it.[1082]

His mind on the devotee Achala, remembering her teaching, absorbing what she had shown him, what she had told him, what she had described to him, what she had enjoined on him, what she had shared with him, what she had disclosed to him, what she had set forth to him, following it, reflecting on it, entering into it, cultivating it, embodying it, contemplating it, clarifying it, living up to it,
mthar gyis gnas nas gnas dang / yul nas yul du brgyu ste/ rgyu zhing song song nas yul dga' 'dzin tshad med pa gang na ba der phyin nas/
Eventually, traveling from district to district, going from land to land, Sudhana arrived at the land called Amitatosala.
Sudhana made his way from place to place, finally reaching the land of Amitatosala.

grong khyer dga' ba 'dzin pa rmed cing tshol tshol te/ nyi ma nub tu cha ba zhig na/ grong khyer dga' ba 'dzin par phyin nas/ grong khyer dga' ba 'dzin pa'i nang du song ste/ grong khyer gyi lam gyi bzhi mdo'i dbus shig tu phyin nas/ srang gi sgo nas srang gi sgo dang / lam gyi bzhi mdo nas/ lam gyi bzhi mdo dang / grong phrag nas/ grong phrag tu kun du rgyu thams cad du 'gro ba tshol zhing rmed rmed pa dang / mtshan mo mi nyal tsam zhig na/ grong khyer dga' ba 'dzin pa'i byang phyogs logs na ri shin tu mod pa zhes bya ba zhig yod pa de'i rtse mo dang / gel ba dang / sman sna tshogs dga' dga' ltar skyes pas brgyan pa/ 'od chen po dang ldan pa nyi ma shar ba lta bur gnas pa mthong ngo/ / des snang ba de mthong nas/ dga' ba'i shugs chen po skyes te/ 'di snyam du bsams so/ / bdag gis dge ba'i bshes gnyen ri'i rtse mo 'di la gdon mi za bar mthong bar 'gyur ba lta zhig snyam nas/

He searched for the town named Tosala, and at sunset he arrived at the town of Tosala. He entered the town of Tosala and went to the crossroads in the center of the town. He wandered from one street to another, from one crossroads to another, from one lane to another, searching and inquiring. When it was night and people were asleep, he saw to the north of the town of Tosala a hill called Sulabha. Its summit was adorned by a delightful variety of grasses, bushes, and herbs, and it shone as brightly as the sun. Seeing that light, he felt a powerful joy and thought, “I will without doubt see the kalyāṇamitra on the summit of that hill.”

There he sought out and found the city of Tosala. Entering the city at sunset, he went from block to block, street to street, looking for the mendicant Sarvagamin. In the still of the night, he saw a mountain called Sulabha, north of the city. The mountain peak was adorned with thickets and groves of various plants and trees and was as bright as the sun. Seeing that light, Sudhana was ecstatic: he thought to himself, “I will undoubtedly see the spiritual benefactor on this mountaintop.”

grong khyer de nas byung ste/ ri shin tu mod pa gang na ba der phyin pa dang / ri shin tu mod pa de la 'dzegs nas/ ri'i rtse mo snang ba chen po can gang na ba der phyin pa dang / rgyang yang ring po zhig nas/ kun tu rgyu thams cad du 'gro ba tshangs pa chen po las kyang lhag pa'i kha dog dang ldan pa dpal gyis shin tu 'bar ba zhig /tshangs pa stong phrag bcus kun nas bskor te/ 'chags na 'chag cing 'dug pa mthong nas

He came out of the town and went to Sulabha Hill, and he climbed up Sulabha Hill and arrived at the very bright summit of the hill. He saw in the distance the parivrājaka Sarvagamin, who shone with splendor and whose appearance was superior even to that of Mahābrahmā, and ten thousand brahmins were walking in circumambulation around him.

Sudhana went out of the city to the mountain and climbed to the shining peak, where he saw the mendicant Sarvagamin from afar. The appearance of the mendicant was superior to that of the great god Brahma, glorious and radiant; he was walking around surrounded by ten thousand brahmic gods.
de'i dung du phyin te/ rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal nas/ de la lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas te/ mdun du 'dug nas thal mo sbyar te 'di skad ces smras so/ /
Sudhana approached him, bowed his head to his feet, circumambulated him many hundreds of thousands of times, and sat down before him. With his hands placed together in homage, he said,
Sudhana went up to Sarvagamin, paid his respects, and said,

'phags pa/ bdag gis bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed na/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bgyi ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bgyi ba ma 'tshal te/
“Ārya, I have developed the aspiration for the highest, complete enlightenment, but I do not know how bodhisattvas should train in bodhisattva conduct and in what way they should practice it.
“Noble one, I have set my mind on supreme perfect enlightenment, but I do not know how an enlightening being is to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings.

'phags pa ni/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams la gdams ngag dang / rjes su bstan pa mdzad do/ / zhes bdag gis thos na/ 'phags pa/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bgyi ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bgyi ba bdag la bshad du gsol/
“Ārya, I have heard that you give instruction and teachings to bodhisattvas! Explain to me how bodhisattvas should train in bodhisattva conduct and how they should practice it!”
I hear that you give enlightening beings instruction, so please tell me how to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings.”
smras pa/ rigs kyi bu/ de ltar khyod bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu zhugs pa legs so/ /legs so/ /
Sarvagamin said, “Noble one, it is excellent, excellent, that you have in that way set out upon the highest, complete enlightenment!
Sarvagamin said, “It is good that you have set out for supreme perfect enlightenment.

rigs kyi bu/ kho bo ni thams cad du 'gro ba ste/ thams cad kyi rjes su song ba'i byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la gnas pa'o/ / sgo thams cad du rnam par spyod pas snang ba'i ting 'dzin gyi sgo dang / dngos po med pa la gnas pas/ mngon par 'du bya ba med pa'i rdzu 'phrul dang / chos kyi dbyings kun gyi gzhir thug par thal ba'i shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa'i ye shes snang ba'i sgo dang ldan pa'o/ /

“Noble one, I, Sarvagamin, remain within the all-pervading bodhisattva conduct. I am endowed with the gateway of the samādhi called the light of the practice of all gateways, with being established in the absence of existence, with noncomposite miraculous powers, and with the gateway of the knowledge of the perfection of wisdom that has reached the basis of the entire realm of the Dharma.

I am established in the enlightening practice of going everywhere, I have attained concentration of all-observing vision, and I am imbued with the light of knowledge of transcendent wisdom which distinguishes all planes of the cosmos without effort, based on nonbeing.
rigs kyi bu/ de ltar kho bo ni sems can gyi snod kyi 'jig rten gyi rgyud thams cad dang / sems can gyi lam gyi rgyud thams cad dang /
“Noble one, in that way I benefit beings in the entire array of worlds inhabited by beings, in all the states of existences that beings are in,
In wandering through all worlds of living beings and inanimate objects, in wandering through the realms of existence of all beings,
sems can gyi shi 'pho'i sgo thams cad dang / sems can gyi skye ba'i sgo thams cad dang / srid pa'i lam gyi rgyud tha dad pa thams cad dang /
in all the gateways of the deaths of beings, in all the gateways of the births of beings, in all the different existences,
in the occasions of death of all sentient beings, in the occasions of birth of all sentient beings, in all kinds of conditions of existence,
skye ba'i skye mched sna tshogs kyi 'jig rten gyi gnas rnam pa tha dad pa dag gi
in the various different abodes, and in the worlds that are habitations‍—
in the various places of birth, the worlds and abodes, of
sems can kha dog dang / dbyibs dang / chu zheng rnam pa sna tshogs dang ldan pa/
beings who have various colors, shapes, heights,
sentient beings of various appearances, forms, and sizes,
skye ba kun du 'brel pa rnam pa sna tshogs dang ldan pa/ sbyor ba sna tshogs dang ldan pa/ mos pa sna tshogs/ can 'di lta ste/
and widths and who have entered various kinds of rebirths, have different practices, and have different aspirations, which means
bound to various kinds of existence, with various aims,

lha'i lam gyi rgyud du gtogs pa dang / klu'i lam gyi rgyud du gtogs pa dang / gnod sbyin gyi lam gyi rgyud du gtogs pa dang / dri za'i lam gyi rgyud du gtogs pa dang / lha ma yin gyi lam gyi rgyud du gtogs pa dang / nam mkha' lding gi lam gyi rgyud du gtogs pa dang / mi'am ci'i lam gyi rgyud du gtogs pa dang / lto 'phye chen po'i lam gyi rgyud du gtogs pa dang / sems can dmyal ba'i lam gyi rgyud du gtogs pa dang / byol song gi skye gnas kyi lam gyi rgyud du gtogs pa dang / gshin rje'i 'jig rten gyi lam gyi rgyud du gtogs pa dang / mi'i lam gyi rgyud du gtogs pa dang / mi ma yin pa'i lam gyi rgyud du gtogs pa dang /

those within existence as a deva, those within existence as a nāga, those within existence as a yakṣa, those within existence as a gandharva, those within existence as an asura, those within existence as a garuḍa, those within existence as a kinnara, those within existence as a mahoraga, those within existence as a hell being, those within existence as an animal, those within existence in the world of Yama, those within existence as a human, those within existence as a nonhuman,
lta ba'i rnam pa sna tshogs la gnas pa dang / nyan thos kyi theg pa la mos pa dang / rang sangs rgyas kyi theg pa la mos pa dang / theg pa chen po la mos pa'i
those who have various false views, those who aspire to the Śrāvakayāna, those who aspire to the Pratyekabuddhayāna, and those who aspire to the Mahāyāna‍—
wedded to various views and courses of action, believing in various forms of religion,
sems can rnams kyi don thabs sna tshogs dang / ye shes kyi tshul dang / sbyor ba sna tshogs kyis byed de/
benefiting them through various methods and through various introductions to the way of wisdom.
I work for the benefit of sentient beings by various means and various applications of knowledge.
'di ltar sems can la la la ni bzo'i rgyud tha dad pa thams cad dang ldan pa'i gzugs snang bas 'jig rten gyi bzo sna tshogs bslabs shing don byed do/ /
“This means that I benefit some beings with the light of the power of mental retention[1083] that possesses all the knowledge of the various crafts so that they will learn the various worldly crafts.
Some I help by teaching various worldly arts, by means of the light of mental command of all kinds of arts.
sems can la la la ni 'di lta ste/ thams cad mkhyen pa'i ye shes bstabs pa'i phyir/ bsdu ba'i dngos po bzhis yongs su bsdu ba'i thabs kyi don byed do/ /
“I benefit some beings through the application of the four methods of gathering pupils, which means leading them to omniscient wisdom.
Some I help by charity, kindness, assistance, and cooperation, to lead them to omniscient knowledge.
sems can la la la ni 'di lta ste/ thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du 'gyur ba'i ye shes kyi sgo snang ba yongs su bskyed pas/ pha rol tu phyin pa yang dag par brjod cing don byed do/ /
“I benefit some beings by describing the perfections, thus generating the light of the gateway[1084] of the wisdom that transforms into omniscience.
Some I help by describing the ways of transcendence, generating the light of knowledge of dedication to omniscience.
sems can la la la ni 'di lta ste/ byang chub kyi sa bon chud mi za bar brtan zhing yongs su bskyed pas byang chub sems dpa'i sems yongs su brjod cing don byed do/ /
“I benefit some beings by describing the aspiration to enlightenment, thus developing an imperishable, strengthened seed of enlightenment.
Some I help by praising the aspiration for enlightenment, producing a basis for preservation of the seed of enlightenment.

sems can la la la ni 'di lta ste/ sangs rgyas kyi zhing thams cad yongs su dag par bya ba dang / sems can thams cad yongs su smin par bya ba'i smon lam yongs su bskyed pa'i phyir/ byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa rnam pa thams cad du yang dag par brjod pas don byed do/ /
“I benefit some beings by describing all the aspects of bodhisattva conduct, thus generating the aspiration to purify all buddha realms and ripen all beings.
Some I help by describing all facets of the practices of enlightening beings, fostering the commitment to purify all buddha-lands and perfect all beings.

sems can la la la ni 'di lta ste/ ngan du spyad pa'i rnam par smin pa dang mthun pa'i rgyus sems can dmyal ba'i lam gyi rgyud kyi sdug bsngal gyi tshor ba myong bar 'gyur ba yongs su bstan pas/ skyo ba yongs su bskyed cing don byed do/ /
“I benefit some beings by causing dismay, by teaching the sufferings experienced by beings in the hells caused by the ripening of their bad conduct.
Some I help by frightening them, showing them the misery and pain resulting from evil actions.

sems can la la la ni 'di lta ste/ de bzhin gshegs pa la bskyed pa'i yon tan thams cad ni gdon mi za bar thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi 'bras bu'i mthar thug par 'gyur bar brjod pas dga' ba chen po bskyed cing don byed do/ /
“I benefit some beings by causing delight, by describing all the qualities that arise in the tathāgatas,[1085] which are the ultimate result of definite omniscience.
Some I help by delighting them, telling them about the fruit of omniscience ultimately developing from giving gifts to all buddhas.

sems can la la la ni 'di lta ste/ sangs rgyas kyi yon tan dang / sku la mngon par mos pas thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du smon lam 'debs par bya ba'i phyir/ de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi yon tan dang bsngags pa yang dag par brjod pas don byed do/ /
“I benefit some beings by speaking praises of the qualities of all the tathāgatas, thus generating the aspiration to omniscience and the longing for the qualities and body of a buddha.
Some I help by describing the virtues and qualities of all buddhas, to generate desire for the qualities of buddhas and determination for omniscience.

sems can la la la ni 'di lta ste/ mi zlog cing lhun gyis grub pa dang / rgyun chad pa med par sangs rgyas kyi 'phrin las nan tan du mdzad pa'i mthu dang ldan pa'i sangs rgyas kyi sku 'thob par mos pa bskyed pa'i phyir/ sangs rgyas kyi bdag nyid che ba brjod pas don byed do/ /

“I benefit some beings by describing the greatness of the buddhas, thus generating the longing to attain the body of a buddha that possesses the power to undertake continuous, irresistible buddha activity.
Some I help by eulogizing the greatness of buddhas, to generate the desire to embody buddhahood and be constantly engaged in spontaneous, ceaseless buddha-work.

sems can la la la ni 'di lta ste/ tshur zil gyis gnon la/ phar zil gyis mi non pa'i sangs rgyas kyi sku phun sum tshogs pa 'thob par mos pa bskyed pa'i phyir sangs rgyas kyi mnga' chen po yongs su brjod cing don byed do/ /
“I benefit some beings by describing the dominance of the buddhas, thus generating the aspiration to attain the perfect body of a buddha, which cannot be surpassed but surpasses all others.
Some I help by showing the mastery of buddhas, to generate the desire to attain supreme buddhahood.

rigs kyi bu/ gzhan yang kho mo ni grong khyer dga' ba 'dzin pa 'di yi bzhi mdo'i phongs thams cad dang / srang thams cad dang / lam gyi sum mdo thams cad dang / grong mtshams thams cad dang khyim thams cad dang / mthun par 'dus pa'i rdal thams cad dang / grong thams cad dang / grong gi rgyud thams cad du rnam pa ji ltar tshogs shing 'dus pa'i bud med dang / skyes pa dang / khye'u dang / bu mo rnams kyi bsam pa ji lta ba dang / sbyor ba ji lta ba dang / mthu ji lta ba dang / rnam par spyod pa ji lta ba bzhin du de dag dang mthun pa'i lus kyi chu zheng dang dbyibs mngon par bsgrubs shing chos ston kyang / sems can de dag gis de sum bstan pa dang / de ga las 'ongs pa mi shes te/ gzhan du na thos nas ma nor bar nan tan du byed pa ni med pa'ang ma yin no/ /

“Moreover, noble one, I manifest a body of the size and shape that accords with the aspirations, activities, powers, and conducts of all the men, women, boys, and girls who are gathered in all the crossroads, streets, junctions, side streets, houses, trades, districts, and dwellings in the districts of this town of Tosala, and I teach them the Dharma. Those beings do not know who has taught them or where he has come from, but otherwise having heard me, they all practice correctly.[1086]

“Furthermore, in every street, every block, every house, every district, every family and group, I assume forms like the men and women, boys and girls, and expound the Teaching to them according to their dispositions, aims, powers, and thoughts; they do not know who is teaching them or where I am from; they just practice truthfully what they have heard.

gzhan yang / rigs kyi bu/ 'dzam bu'i gling 'di na zhags pa 'thub pa lta ba rnam pa sna tshogs la mngon par zhen pa dgu bcu rtsa drug 'khod pa de dag thams cad kyi nang du yang / sems can lta ba'i rnam pa sna tshogs la chags pa rnams yongs su smin par bya ba'i phyir thams cad dang mthun par gnas te/
“Moreover, noble one, I go everywhere in this Jambudvīpa in order to ripen those who are attached to the ninety-six varieties of heretical[1087] views.
And I go everywhere on this continent to those who are immersed in the views of false doctrines, in order to mature those who cling to various views.

rigs kyi bu/ ji ltar kho bo grong khyer dga' ba 'dzin pa 'di na/ sems can gyi don byed cing 'dug pa de bzhin du/ 'dzam bu'i gling gi grong dang / grong khyer dang / ljongs dang / yul dang / khams dang / rgyal ba'i pho brang 'khor thams cad na yang sems can gyi don byed do/ /
“Noble one, in the same way that I benefit beings in this town of Tosala, I benefit beings in all the villages, markets,[1088] towns, lands, kingdoms, and capitals in Jambudvīpa.
'dzam bu'i gling na ji lta ba de bzhin du gling bzhi pa'i 'jig rten gyi khams thams cad dang / de bzhin du stong dang / stong gnyis pa dang / stong gsum gyi stong chen po'i 'jig rten gyi khams dang /

In the same way that I benefit beings in Jambudvīpa, I do so in the entire four-continent world realm, and in a thousand such world realms, and in a million, and in the great world realms of a billion such world realms.
And just as I do so throughout the continent, so also do I work for the benefit of all beings on earth, in the galaxy, in the universe,

de bzhin du phyogs bcu'i 'jig rten gyi khams sems can gyi rten du bya ba thams cad dang / sems can gyi gnas su bya ba thams cad dang / sems can gyi gzhir bya ba thams cad dang / sems can gyi khams su bya ba'i ming du gtogs pa thams cad dang / sems can yongs su rgyu ba thams cad dang / sems can yongs su 'du ba thams cad dang /

In the same way, I benefit beings according to their aspirations in all the world realms in the ten directions, in all the habitations of beings, in all the dwellings of beings, in all the locations of beings, in all that are known as the abodes of beings, in all the residences of beings, in all the congregations of beings,
in infinite worlds, in the paths of all beings, in the abodes of all beings, in the thoughts in which all beings rest, in the groups of all beings,

sems can rgya mtsho na gnas pa thams cad dang / sems can gyi rgyud gnas pa thams cad dang / sems can gyi phyogs su bya ba thams cad dang / sems can gyi phyogs mtshams su bya ba thams cad dang / sems can spyod pa'i gnas thams cad du'ang thabs sna tshogs dang / tshul sna tshogs dang / sgo sna tshogs dang / rigs pa sna tshogs dang / phrad pa sna tshogs dang / thabs kyi tshul sna tshogs dang / bya ba sna tshogs kyis sems can rnams kyi don byed do/ /

in all the oceans of beings, in all the lineages of beings, in all the directions of beings, in all the intermediate directions of beings, and in all the conducts of beings. I benefit beings through various methods, various ways, various gateways, various kinds of logic, various connections, various ways of methods, and various actions.

in the masses of all beings, in all races of beings, among all types of beings, wherever they be, helping them according to their mentalities and inclinations, through various means, various methods, various approaches, various efforts, various devices, various expedients, various activities,
gzugs dang kha dog sna tshogs yongs su bstan cing mos par bya ba dang / tshig gi lam sna tshogs brjod pas kyang sems can rnams kyi don byed do/ /
I benefit beings through the manifestation of various attractive physical forms and colors. I benefit beings through speaking in various languages.
assuming various forms, and speaking in various languages.

rigs kyi bu kho bos ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa thams cad du 'gro ba thams cad kyi rjes su song ba 'di shes par zad na/ kho bos byang chub sems dpa' 'gro ba thams cad dang mnyam pa'i lus dang ldan pa/ bdag dang sems can gyi lus su tha mi dad pa'i ting nge 'dzin thob pa/ 'phrul pa'i 'khor lo rgya chen pos srid pa'i lam gyi rgyud thams cad du khyab pa/ 'jig rten gyi skye ba thams cad rang gi lus la rjes su spyod la/ 'gro ba thams cad kyis blta na dga' zhing yid du 'ong ba'i sprul pa'i 'khor lo la brtson pa/ 'gro ba thams cad kyi rigs dang / rgyud dang / cher skye ba rab tu ston pa/ bskal pa thams cad du gnas pa la thogs pa med pa'i smon lam gyi 'khor lo dang ldan pa/ mig 'phrul lta bu'i spyod pa rnam par phye ba'i snang ba rab tu thob pa; 'gro ba thams cad kyi don byed kyang gos pa med par gnas pa la brtson pa/ dus gsum gyi 'gro ba'i dbyings mnyam pa nyid khong du chud pa/ ye shes kyi dbyings bdag med pa dang ldan pas snang bar byas pa'i snying rje chen po mtha' yas pa'i snying po dang ldan pa/ 'gro ba thams cad kyi dge ba'i rtsa ba yongs su bskyed pa la mngon par brtson pa de dag gi spyod pa shes pa'am/ yon tan brjod par nus re skan/

“Noble one, in that way, I know this bodhisattva conduct that is all-pervasive[1089] and omnipresent, but how could I know the conduct or describe the qualities of those bodhisattvas who possess bodies that are the same as those of all beings; who have attained the samādhi called identical to the bodies of all beings; who pervade all the classes of existence with a vast wheel of emanations; who perform in their own bodies all worldly births; who are dedicated to the wheel of beautiful emanations that all beings delight to see; who manifest births in the families, clans, and lives of all beings; who possess the unimpeded wheel of aspiration to dwell in all kalpas; who have attained the radiance of the display of conduct that is like an illusion; who are dedicated to benefiting all beings and yet remain stainless; who have realized the equality of all the realms of beings in the three times; who possess the essence of infinite compassion illuminated by the realm of the wisdom of selflessness; and who are dedicated to generating the roots of merit of all beings?

“I know this enlightening practice of going everywhere. How can I know the practice or tell of the virtues of the enlightening beings with bodies equal to all beings, who have attained concentration in which their own bodies and all bodies are indivisible, whose vast sphere of emanation adapts to all states of existence, who pass through existence in all worlds in their own bodies, who are intent on mystical projections pleasing to the sight of all beings, who appear to be born in all races, who carry out their vows unimpeded in all ages, who can manifest the interrelated cosmic network of practices, who are devoted to working for the welfare of all beings while living together with them without becoming defiled, who realize the basic equality of the worlds of past, present, and future, who are imbued with endless great compassion appearing in the realm of selfless knowledge, who aim to foster good in all beings?

song / rigs kyi bu/ lho phyogs kyi rgyud 'di nyid na/ yul khams chen po zhes bya ba yod de/ de na spos 'tshong gi tshong dpon longs spyod ut+pa la zhes bya ba 'dug gi/ /de'i gan du song la/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bya ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bya ba dris shig /

“Depart, noble one. In this southern region, in a land called Pṛthurāṣṭra, there dwells a perfume-seller head merchant by the name of Utpalabhūti. Go to him and ask him, ‘How should a bodhisattva train in bodhisattva conduct? How should a bodhisattva practice it?’ ”
“South of here is a land called Prthurashtra, where there lives an eminent perfumer named Utpalabhuti. Go ask him how to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings.”

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis/ kun tu rgyu thams cad du 'gro ba'i rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te/ kun tu rgyu thams cad du 'gro ba la lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas/ yang dang yang bltas te/ kun tu rgyu thams cad du 'gro ba'i drung nas song ngo/ /

Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, bowed his head to the feet of the parivrājaka Sarvagamin, circumambulated the parivrājaka Sarvagamin a hundred thousand times, keeping him to his right, and, looking back again and again, departed from the presence of the parivrājaka Sarvagamin.
So Sudhana paid his respects to the mendicant Sarvagamin and left.

d.crumb: [spos 'tshong gi tshong dpon longs spyod ut+pa la]

f.d: [spos 'tshong gi tshong dpon longs spyod ut+pa la]
Chapter 24. Utpalabhūti
Utpalabhuti
de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang lus dang srog la mi lta/
Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, had no regard for his life or body;
Unconcerned with body and life,
srid pa'i longs spyod dang / yongs su zin pa dang / nye bar blangs pa mngon par chags pa'i gnas thams cad la ni mi sems/
he had no regard for engaging in dedication to obtaining and possessing the pleasures of existence;
unconcerned with any material things,
sems can gyi yul gyi dga' ba thams cad la ni mi lta/
he had no regard for the objects of perception that beings delight in;
unconcerned with enjoyment of any people or places,
gzugs dang / sgra dang / dri dang / ro dang / reg bya thams cad la ni mi lta/
he had no regard for forms, sounds, smells, tastes, and textures;
unconcerned with objects of the senses,
g.yog 'khor dang / longs spyod dang / nye bar spyad pa thams cad la ni mi lta ste/
he had no concern for enjoying retinues and pleasures;
unconcerned with enjoying the experiences that go along with having followers,
rgyal srid dang / dbang phyug gi dbang gi bde ba thams cad la ni mi lta la/
he had no regard for any of the pleasures of the power of kingship and sovereignty;
unconcerned with kingship, dominion, or power,
sangs rgyas kyi zhing bla na med par yongs su dag pa mngon par bsgrubs pas/ sems can thams cad yongs su smin par bya ba dang / gdul ba dang / yongs su dag par bya ba la blta ba/
he was focused on attaining the highest purification of a buddha realm for the pure ripening and guiding of all beings;
concerned with developing, guiding, and purifying all sentient beings, with achieving supreme purity of a buddha-land,
mchod pa dang / bsnyen bkur ba dang / rim gror bya bas mi ngoms pas de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad la blta ba dang /
he was focused on never being satisfied with the extent of his offering to, honoring, and serving all the tathāgatas;
with tirelessly attending and serving all buddhas,
rang bzhin med pa yongs su shes pa'i ye shes khong du chud par bya ba'i phyir chos thams cad la blta ba/
he was focused on all phenomena with the wisdom that knows their nature;[1090]
with knowing and according with the inherent nature of all things,
yon tan rgya mtsho thams cad kyi don du nan tan bya ba las nyams pa med par bya ba'i phyir/ byang chub sems dpa'i yon tan thams cad la blta ba dang /
he was focused on the qualities of bodhisattvas so that there would be no decline in his practice, which had the entire ocean of those qualities as its goal;
with permanently attaining the virtues of all enlightening beings,
bskal ba thams cad du byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la yang dag par gnas par bya ba'i phyir/ byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi smon lam chen po la lta ba/
he was focused on the great prayers of all bodhisattvas so as to maintain bodhisattva conduct throughout all kalpas;
with carrying out the vows of enlightening beings through all ages,
de bzhin gshegs pa'i 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor rgya mtsho thams cad du 'jug par bya ba la lta ba/
he was focused on entering the ocean of the circles of the followers of all tathāgatas;
with entering the ocean of congregations of all buddhas,

ting nge 'dzin gyi sgo re rer/ byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin grangs med pa thams cad gzud pa la rnam par 'phrul par bya ba'i phyir/ byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin gyi sgo thams cad la lta ba/
he was focused on all gateways of bodhisattva samādhis so as to manifest the attainment of all countless bodhisattva samādhis through each samādhi gateway;
with entering all concentrations of enlightening beings in each particular mode of concentration by mystic transformation,
de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi chos kyi 'khor lo yang dag par bzung bas/ mi ngoms par bya pa'i phyir chos kyi ye shes snang ba'i 'khor lo thams cad la lta ba de/
he was focused on all the light of wisdom of all Dharma wheels so as to never be satisfied with the extent of his obtaining Dharma wheels from all the tathāgatas;
with tirelessly receiving the light of knowledge of all truths through the cycles of teachings of all buddhas,

sangs rgyas dang byang chub sems dpa'i yon tan 'di dag dang / gzhan dag kyang dge ba'i bshes gnyen las byung ba ste/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen ni/ de dag thams cad kyi 'byung gnas su gyur pa yin par yang dag par lta zhing /
and he was focused on the kalyāṇamitras, who are the source of qualities, because the kalyāṇamitras are the source of the qualities of the buddhas, the bodhisattvas, and others.
pondering these and other virtues of all enlightening beings,
mthar gyis yul khams chen po gang na ba der phyin nas; spos 'tshong gi tshong dpon longs spyod ut+pa la yongs su rmed cing tshol tshol ba las
Sudhana eventually arrived at the land called Pṛthurāṣṭra. He looked and searched for the perfume-seller head merchant by the name of Utpalabhūti.
Sudhana made his way to Prthurashtra, where he sought and found the eminent perfumer Utpalabhuti.

mthong nas/ spos 'tshong gi tshong dpon longs spyod ut+pa la gang na bder phyin te/ drung du song nas spos 'tshong gi tshong dpon spyod ut+pa la'i rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te/ spos 'tshong gi tshong dpon longs spyod ut+pa la la lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas/ spos 'tshong gi tshong dpon longs spyod ut+pa la'i mdun du 'dug ste thal mo sbyar nas/ 'di skad ces smras so/ /

He saw the perfume-seller head merchant Utpalabhūti and approached him. After approaching him, Sudhana bowed his head to the perfume-seller head merchant Utpalabhūti’s feet, circumambulated the perfume-seller head merchant Utpalabhūti many hundreds of thousands of times, and sat down before the perfume-seller head merchant Utpalabhūti. With his hands placed together in homage, he said,
Seeing the perfumer, Sudhana went up to him, paid his respects, and said,
'phags pa/ bdag sangs rgyas thams cad dang mnyam pa'i ye shes 'tshal te/
“Ārya, I seek the wisdom that is the same as that of all the buddhas.
“Noble one, I have set out for supreme perfect enlightenment, seeking the knowledge common to all buddhas,
sangs rgyas thams cad kyi sngon gyi smon lam gyi dkyil 'khor yongs su rdzogs par bgyi bar yang dga';
I rejoice in the fulfillment of the field of prayers made in the past by all the buddhas,
wishing to fulfill the vows fulfilled by all buddhas, wishing to see the embodiments of all buddhas,
sangs rgyas thams cad kyi chos kyi sku yongs su grub par bgyi bar yang dga'/
I rejoice in the accomplishment of the Dharma body of all the buddhas,
wishing to attain the reality body of all buddhas,
sangs rgyas thams cad kyi ye shes kyi sku yongs su 'tshal bar bgyi bar yang dga'/
I seek the wisdom body of all the buddhas,
wishing to know the body of knowledge of truths of all buddhas,
byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa'i dkyil 'khor thams cad yongs su dag par bgyi bar yang dga'/
I rejoice in the purification of all the fields of bodhisattva conduct,
wishing to purify all enlightening practices,
byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin gyi dkyil 'khor thams cad snang bar bgyi bar yang dga'/
I rejoice in the light of all the fields of bodhisattva samādhis,
wishing to manifest the sphere of concentration of all enlightening beings,
byang chub sems dpa'i gzungs kyi dkyil 'khor thams cad yongs su brten par yang dga'/
I rejoice in the stability of all the fields of the bodhisattva power of mental retention,
wishing to master the sphere of mental command of all enlightening beings,
sgrib pa'i dkyil 'khor thams cad rnam par gtor bar yang dga'/
I rejoice in the dispelling of the entire field of kleśas,
wishing to disperse all obstructions,
zhing gi dkyil 'khor thams cad du rnam par rgyu bar yang 'tshal nas/
I seek to travel in all the fields of the realms,
wishing to travel through all lands.
bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu yang dag par zhugs na/
and I have set out upon the highest complete enlightenment,
[…see above]

ji ltar byang chub sems pas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bgyi ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bgyi ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bgyis na/ byang chub sems dpa' thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du 'byung bar 'gyur ba ma 'tshal to/ /
but I do not know how bodhisattvas should train in bodhisattva conduct and how they should practice it, and how through having practiced in that way all bodhisattvas become omniscient.”
But I do not know how an enlightening being is to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings. How does an enlightening being gain access to omniscience?”
smras pa/ rigs kyi bu/ de ltar khyod kyis bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub sems bskyed pa legs so/ /legs so/ /
Utpalabhūti said to him, “Noble one, it is excellent, excellent, that you have developed the aspiration for the highest, complete enlightenment.
Utpalabhuti said, “It is good that you aspire to supreme perfect enlightenment.

rigs kyi bu/ kho bo ni spos thams cad shes te/ spos sbyar ba thams cad dang / bdug spos thams cad dang / bdug spos sbyar ba thams cad dang / byug pa thams cad dang / byug pa sbyar ba thams cad dang / phye ma thams cad dang / phye ma sbyar ba thams cad dang / spos dang byug pa dang / phye ma'i rnam pa thams cad kyang shes te/

“Noble one, I know all perfumes. I know about all combined perfumes, all incenses, all combinations of perfumes and incenses, all ointments, all combined ointments, all powders, all combinations of powders, and all perfumes, ointments, and powders.
I know about all fragrances—perfumes, incenses, ointments, and aromatic powders—and how they are compounded and used. I also know the sources of all fragrances.
lha'i spos kyang shes so/ /klu dang / gnod sbyin dang / dri za dang / lha ma yin dang / nam mkha' lding dang / mi 'am ci dang / lto 'phye chen po dang / mi dang / mi ma yin pa'i spos kyang shes so/ /
I know the perfumes of the devas. I also know the perfumes of the nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, and nonhumans.
I know celestial fragrances, and I also know the fragrances of other types of beings, human and nonhuman. Indeed, I know various kinds of fragrances.

nad gso ba'i spos dang / yid mi bde ba bsal ba'i spos dang / 'jig rten gyi dga' ba yongs su bskyed pa'i spos dang / nyon mongs pa 'bar bar bya ba'i spos dang / nyon mongs pa zhi bar bya ba'i spos dang / 'dus byas kyi dga' ba dang bde ba sna tshogs yongs su bskyed pa'i spos dang / 'dus byas thams cad las skyo ba yongs su bskyed pa'i spos dang / bag bya ba'i gnas thams cad yongs su sel ba'i spos dang / sangs rgyas yid la bya ba'i rgyud yang dag par 'byung ba'i spos dang / chos kyi tshul khong du chud par bya ba'i spos dang /

“I know the perfumes that heal sickness. I also know the perfumes that dispel unhappiness, the perfumes that give rise to worldly happiness, the perfumes that cause the kleśas to blaze, the perfumes that cause kleśas to cease, the perfumes that create various kinds of composite happiness and bliss, the perfumes that create composite sadness, the perfumes that dispel all intoxication and carelessness,[1091] the perfumes that accomplish a continuous focus on the buddhas, the perfumes of understanding the way of the Dharma,

I know fragrances that cure illness, I know fragrances that remove depression, I know fragrances that produce mundane joy, I know fragrances that incite passions, I know fragrances that extinguish passions, I know fragrances that produce pleasure in enjoyment of various created things, I know fragrances that produce rejection of all created things, I know fragrances that remove arrogance and heedlessness, I know fragrances that produce thoughts of Buddha, I know fragrances that accord with the principles of the Teaching,
'phags pas spyad pa'i spos dang / byang chub sems dpa'i spos rnam pa tha dad pa dang / byang chub sems dpa'i sa thams cad rnam par dgod pa'i spos kyang shes te/
the perfumes of ārya conduct, the various bodhisattva perfumes, and the perfumes of being established on all the bodhisattva levels.
fragrances enjoyable to sages, the variety of fragrances of enlightening beings, and the fragrances of the arrangement of all stages of enlightening beings.
kho bos spos de dag thams cad rnam pa ji lta bu'ang rab tu shes so/ /
I know the aspects of all those perfumes.
I also know the external appearance of all these fragrances,

'byung ba dang / skye ba dang / 'grub pa dang / yongs su rdzogs pa dang / yongs su dag pa dang / yongs su spangs pa dang / rab tu sbyar ba dang / yongs su spyad pa dang / yul dang / mthu dang / las dang / rgyu yang rab tu shes so/ /
I also know their origin, creation, accomplishment, perfection, purification, elimination, combination, usage, object, power, action, and cause.
as well as their source, production, manifestation, perfection, purification, removal, application, use, sphere of action, efficacy, nature, and root.

rigs kyi bu/ mi'i 'jig rten na spos glang po'i snying po zhes bya ba/ klu yongs su 'khrug par byed pa yod de/ de'i ri lu til gyi 'bru tsam gyis kyang / yul khams chen po thams cad spos kyi sprin gyi dra ba shin tu stug pas kun nas khebs par gyur te/ zhag bdun du spos chu'i rgyun shin tu phra ba'i char mngon par 'bab bo/ /

“Noble one, in the world there is the perfume called elephant essence that disconcerts the nāgas.[1092] A pellet merely the size of a sesame seed will pervade the entire land of Pṛthurāṣṭra with a thick net of a cloud of perfume. For seven days there will fall a fine rain of scented water.

“In the human world there is a fragrance said to come from the agitation of water spirits: one grain the size of a sesame seed will cause this whole country to be covered with fragrant clouds that shower fine fragrant rain for seven days.
de'i tshe sems can su'i lus sam/ gos la spos chu'i rgyun de dag gis bab par gyur pa de dag thams cad kyang / me tog gser gyi kha dog tu 'dug pas rnam par brgyan pa'i gos dang / lus su 'gyur ro/ /
At that time, when that scented water falls on any being’s body or clothing, all their bodies and clothing will become adorned with golden flowers. [1093]
Those on whose bodies or clothing that fragrant water falls become as brilliant as golden flowers,
khang pa dang / gzhal med khang dang / khang pa brtsegs pa gang du bab par gyur pa de dag thams cad kyang / me tog gser gyi kha dog lta bus rnam par brgyan par gnas so/ /
and any houses or buildings on which it falls become as brilliant as golden flowers.

sems can khyim gyi nang na gnas par gang gis/ spos kyi sprin gyi dra ba de la rlung gis mngad pa'i dri tshor bar gyur pa de dag thams cad kyang / zhag bdun du dga' ba dang / mos pa chen pos yongs su rgyas par 'gyur te/ lus dang sems la bde ba dang / dga' ba sna tshogs kyang rab tu myong bar 'gyur ro/ /

Those beings who are indoors and smell the scent that is brought in by the breeze from that net of clouds of perfume will all have increased happiness and aspiration for seven days and will experience various kinds of mental and physical happiness and pleasure,
And any who smell the scent of that fragrant water wafting in on the breeze become ecstatic for seven days and experience many kinds of physical and mental pleasure and delight.
de dag gi lus la yang khams 'khrugs pa las gyur pa'am/ gzhan gyis gnod par byas pa las gyur pa'i nad kyang 'byung bar 'gyur ba med do/ /
and they will have no illness that is caused by the disturbance of the elements in their bodies or is the result of harm caused by others.
Furthermore, no illness—whether due to constitutional upset or external trauma—occurs in their bodies,
sems kyi sdug bsngal dang / mi bde ba yang mi 'byung ngo/ /
They will have no suffering or unhappiness.
nor do they suffer any mental distress or depression,
'jigs pa'am/ dngang ba'am/ bag tsha ba'am/ yid 'khrugs pa'am/ gnod sems kyang mi rgyu ste/ de dag thams cad zhag bdun du dga' ba dang bde ba skyes te/ gcig la gcig byams pa'i sems su 'gyur ro; ;
They will have no fear, no terror, no apprehension, no disturbance of mind, and no malice. For seven days there will arise happiness and joy, and they will be kind to one another.
nor do they have any fear, anxiety, fright, agitation, or ill will. They become kind to one another, happy, and joyful.

rigs kyi bu/ kho bo ni de dag de ltar dga' ba dang / nyams bde ba skyes pa rnams la bsam pa dag par bya ba'i phyir/ ci nas kyang bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu nges par 'gyur ba de ltar chos ston to/ /
“Noble one, in order to purify the thoughts of those who are experiencing happiness and joy, I teach them the Dharma so that they will definitely have the highest, complete enlightenment.
When they have become happy and joyful, I begin to purify their minds and teach them in such a way that they become certain of supreme enlightenment.
gzhan yang rigs kyi bu/ rim la ya las 'byung ba'i tsan dan sa steng dam pa zhes bya ba yod de; de lus la bskus na me'i 'obs su mchongs kyang tshig pa med do/ /
“Moreover, noble one, there is sandalwood called gośīrṣa that comes from the Malaya mountains. If you rub it on your body, you can jump into a great fire and you will not be burned.
“There is a kind of sandalwood that comes from the mountains which will protect those anointed with its essence from burning even if they fall into a fire.
rigs kyi bu/ rgya mtsho'i mtha' nas 'byung ba'i spos gzhan gyis thub pa med pa zhes bya ba yod de/ des rnga'am/ dung la bskus na/ de'i sgras gzhan gyi 'khor thams cad pham par 'gyur ro/ /
“Noble one, there is a perfume called invincible that comes from the ends of the ocean. If you rub it on a drum or a horn, its sound will defeat all the followers of others.
The sound of kettledrums or conches smeared with it will drive away all enemy armies.

rigs kyi bu/ mtsho ma dros pa'i ngogs nas 'byung ba'i a ga ru nag po pad+mo'i snying po zhes bya ba yod de/ de'i ri lu til gyi 'bru tsam gcig gi dris kyang / 'dzam bu'i gling thams cad rgyas par gang bar 'gyur te/ sems can gang gis spos kyi dri de tshor ba de dag thams cad kyang sdig pa la smod cing / sdom pa'i sems rab tu 'thob par 'gyur ro/ /

“Noble one, there is the black agarwood called lotus essence that comes from Lake Anavatapta. The smell from a pellet the size of a sesame seed will fill all of Jambudvīpa. Every being that smells that perfume will renounce bad actions and gain a controlled mind.

There is a kind of aloe called ‘lotus calyx’ from the banks of the lake Heatless; a grain of it the size of a sesame seed will fill the whole continent with fragrance such that all who smell it gain a disciplined mind rejecting evil.

rigs kyi bu/ ri'i rgyal po kha ba can las 'byung ba'i spos kyi rnam pa 'od dang ldan pa zhes bya ba yod de/ de'i dri tshor na sems can de dag 'dod chags dang bral ba'i sems su 'gyur te/ kho bo ni de dag la ci nas kyang rdul dang bral ba'i dkyil 'khor ces bya ba'i ting nge 'dzin thob par 'gyur ba de ltar chos ston to/ /

“Noble one, there is a kind of perfume called luminescent that comes from the Himalaya, the king of mountains. If one smells its scent, the mind will become freed from desire. I teach them the Dharma so that they will attain the samādhi called the stainless field.

There is a kind of fragrance from the Himalaya Mountains which is such that all who smell it become dispassionate; then I teach them in such a way that they attain a concentration called ‘sphere of dispassion.’

rigs kyi bu/ srin po'i 'jig rten nas 'byung ba'i spos kyi rnam pa rgya mtsho'i snying po zhes bya ba yod de/ de ni 'khor los bsgyur ba'i longs spyod kyi don du 'byung ste/ des bdugs ma thag tu 'khor los bsgyur ba'i rgyal po'i dpung gi tshogs yan lag bzhi pa yang nam mkha'i dbyings la gnas so/ /

“Noble one, there is a kind of perfume called the essence of the sea that comes from the land of the rākṣasas and has been produced for the enjoyment of a cakravartin king. As soon as he is perfumed by it, the cakravartin’s fourfold[1094] army appears in the sky.
There is a kind of fragrance from the world of spirits called ‘ocean storehouse’ which is produced for the use of sovereign rulers; perfumed by it, the ruler and the ruler’s armies stand in the sky.
rigs kyi bu; lha'i 'khor chos bzang po nas 'byung ba'i spos kyi rnam pa rnam par 'byed pa zhes bya ba yod de/ des bdugs ma thag tu lha rnams sangs rgyas kyi dri zhim po dran par 'gyur ro; ;

“Noble one, there is a kind of perfume called array of beauty[1095] that comes from Sudharma, the assembly hall of the devas. As soon as the devas are perfumed by it, they gain the memory of the pleasant aroma of the buddhas.
There is a kind of incense called ‘beautiful array’ originating in the celestial hall of the good doctrine; when it is burned, celestial beings gain awareness of the scent of enlightenment.

rigs kyi bu/ lha'i rgyal po rab mtshe ma'i gnas na spos kyi rnam pa dag pa'i mdzod ces bya ba yod de/ des bdugs ma thag tu mtshe ma'i lha'i bu thams cad lha'i rgyal po rab mtshe ma'i drung du 'dong ngo/ / de dag der phyin nas kyang lha'i rgyal po rab mtshe mas chos kyi gtam bya'o/ /

“Noble one, there is a kind of perfume called pure treasure in the paradise of Suyāma, the king of devas. As soon as they are perfumed by it, all Suyāma’s devas come before deva king Suyāma, and when they are in his presence, the deva king Suyāma talks to them about the Dharma.

There is a kind of incense from the pure treasuries in the palace of the heaven of timely portion; when it is burned, inhabitants of that heaven all go to the ruler of the heaven of timely portion, who then talks to them about the Teaching.

rigs kyi bu/ dga' ldan gyi gnas na spos kyi rnam pa sin du ba ra zhes bya ba yod de/ de'i spos kyi dud pa byang chub sems dpa' tshe gcig gis thogs pa chos kyi stan la 'dug pa'i mdun du phyung na/ spos kyi sprin chen pos chos kyi dbyings thams cad rgyas par gang zhing de bzhin gshegs pa'i 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor thams cad du rgyan rnam pa sna tshogs dang ldan pa'i chos kyi sprin chen po'i char rab tu bab bo/ /

“Noble one, there is a kind of perfume called chaste tree in Tuṣita. When its aroma reaches bodhisattvas with one life remaining and who are upon their Dharma seats, a great cloud of perfume fills the entire realm of phenomena, and from great Dharma clouds that have a variety of adornments a rain falls onto all the circles of followers of the tathāgatas.

There is a kind of incense in the heaven of satisfaction which, when burned before an enlightened being destined to become a buddha in one lifetime who is sitting on the throne of the Teaching, fills the whole cosmos at once with a great fragrant cloud and causes rain from the great cloud of the Teaching to shower in many arrays on the audiences of all buddhas.

rigs kyi bu; lha'i rgyal po rab 'phrul dga'i gnas na/ spos kyi rnam pa yid 'phrog pa zhes bya ba yod de/ des lha'i rgyal po rab 'phrul dga'i gnas su bdugs na/ zhag bdun du chos kyi sprin gyi char bsam gyis mi khyab pa 'bab par 'gyur ro/ /

“Noble one, there is a kind of perfume called captivating in the paradise of the deva king Sunirmita. When there is that aroma in the paradise of the deva king Sunirmita, there falls an inconceivable rain from clouds of Dharma for seven days.

There is a kind of incense called ‘fascinating’ in the palace of the king of the heaven of beautiful emanations which, when burned, causes rain to shower from the cloud of the inconceivable Teaching for seven days.

rigs kyi bu/ kho bos ni spos sbyar ba de shes su zad na/ kho bos byang chub sems dpa' skyon gyi dri ma med pa 'dod pa'i 'jig rten thams cad nas gyen du 'phags pa/ nyon mongs pa'i bdud kyi zhags pa dang bral ba/

“Noble one, I know how to combine perfumes, but how could I know the conduct or describe the qualities of those bodhisattvas who have no stain of faults and have transcended the entire realm of desire, who are free from the noose of the māra of the kleśas,

“I know this art of perfuming. How can I know the practice, tell of the virtues, elucidate the method of purification of conduct, convey the irreproachable action, or explain the malice-free words, thoughts, and deeds of the enlightening beings who are free from foulness, who are void of lusts, who are free from the snares of the demon of afflictions,
srid pa'i lam gyi rgyud thams cad las shin tu 'das pa/
who have transcended all the continuums of the states of existence,
who have transcended all conditions of existence,
ye shes sgyu ma'i rnam pa dang / gzugs kyis rnam par spyod pa/
who perform conduct with bodies and the aspect of the illusion of wisdom,
who proceed with material form as being something in the magic of knowing,
'jig rten thams cad kyis gos pa med pa/
who are unstained by any world,
who are unstained by any world,
chags pa med pa'i ngang tshul can/
who have the state of being without desire,
whose way of life is free from attachment,
sgrib pa med pa'i ye shes kyi dkyil 'khor rnam par dag pa/
who have the pure field of wisdom that is unobscured,
who have purified the sphere of unobstructed knowledge,
thogs pa med pa'i ye shes kyi spyod yul dang /
who have the range and scope of unimpeded wisdom,
who are in the realm of unimpeded knowledge,
yul du ldan pa/ kun gyi gzhi'i gnas thams cad la mi gnas par srid pa'i kun gzhi dang / gnas thams cad du rgyu ba rnams kyi spyod pa shes pa'am/
who do not dwell in any basis or location, and who know the conduct of those who move in all the bases and locations of existence?
who do not take refuge in any abode or rely on anything in existence?

yon tan brjod pa'am/ tshul khrims kyi spyod pa rnam par dag pa'i sgo yongs su smos pa'am kha na ma tho ba med pa'i spyod pa'am/ gnod par spyod pa med pa'i lus dang / ngag dang / yid kyi rgyud bstan par nus re skan/

How could I elucidate the gateway of their pure practice of correct conduct? How could I describe their faultless conduct? How could I teach their continuum of body, speech, and mind that is devoid of harmful conduct?

song / rigs kyi bu/ lho phyogs kyi rgyud 'di nyid na; grong khyer khang pa brtsegs pa zhes bya ba yod de/ de na mnyan pa dpa' bo zhes bya ba 'dug gi /de'i drung du song la/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bya ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bya ba dris shig /

“Depart, noble one. In this southern region, there is a town named Kūṭāgāra. There dwells a mariner by the name of Vaira. Go to him and ask him, ‘How should a bodhisattva train in bodhisattva conduct? How should a bodhisattva practice it?’ ”
“South of here is a city called Kutagara, where there lives a mariner named Vaira. Go ask him how to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings.”

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis/ spos 'tshong gi tshong dpon longs spyod ut+pa la'i rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal nas/ spos 'tshong gi tshong dpon longs spyod ut+pa la la lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas/ yang dang yang bltas te/ spos 'tshong gi tshong dpon longs spyod ut+pa la'i drung nas song ngo/ /

“Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, bowed his head to the feet of the perfume-seller head merchant Utpalabhūti, circumambulated the perfume-seller head merchant Utpalabhūti a hundred thousand times, keeping him to his right, and, looking back again and again, departed from the presence of the perfume-seller head merchant Utpalabhūti.
So then Sudhana paid his respects to Utpalabhuti and left.
[mnyan pa dpa' bo]
Chapter 25. Vaira
Vaira

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang grong khyer khang pa brtsegs par 'gro ba'i lam du 'jug pa'i tshe/ lam gyi gyen thur dang / lam mnyam pa dang / lam gyi thag thug dang / lam rdul yod pa dang / lam rdul med pa dang / lam bde ba dang / lam mi bde ba dang / lam dog pa dang / lam gegs med pa dang; lam 'khyug pa dang / lam 'khyug pa med pa la rnam par spyod de/ bltas nas 'dri snyam du bsams so/ / 'di ltar bdag dge ba'i bshes gnyen de'i drung du 'gro ba 'di ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i lam gyi nan tan gyi rgyur 'gyur ro/ / pha rol tu phyin pa'i lam gyi nan tan gyi rgyur 'gyur ro/ / sems can la phan gdags pa'i lam gyi nan tan gyi rgyur 'gyur ro/ / sems can thams cad byams sdang dang / mthon dman du gyur pa'i g.yang sa las rnam par bzlog pa dang / sems can thams cad mi mnyam pa'i nan tan las bsgyur ba dang / sems can thams cad kyi nyon mongs pa'i rdul rab tu zhi bar bya ba dang / sems can thams cad kyi mi dge ba'i lta ba sna tshogs kyi sdong dum dang / tsher ma dang / gyo mo dang / gseg ma bsal ba dang / chos kyi dbyings bsgribs pa med pa la gzhol bar bya ba dang / thams cad mkhyen pa'i pho brang du thogs pa med par bskyal ba'i rgyur 'gyur ro/ /

When Sudhana set out on the path to Kūṭāgāra, he observed and contemplated how the path could be upward or downward, even or uneven,[1096] dusty or free of dust, safe or hazardous,[1097] difficult or unobstructed, and crooked or straight. He thought, “This journey to a kalyāṇamitra will be a cause for the practice of the bodhisattva path, will be a cause of the practice of the path of the perfections, and will be a cause of the path of benefiting all beings,[1098] which will be a cause for turning all beings away from the precipice of attachment[1099] and aversion, of elation and depression;[1100] will be a cause for turning all beings away from a perception[1101] of inequality; will be a cause for removing the dust of the kleśas from all beings; will be a cause for clearing away the tree trunks, thorns, pebbles, and gravel of the various bad views of all beings; and, through their entering the unobscured realm of the Dharma, will be a cause for bringing them without hindrance to the palace of omniscience.

On the way to the city Kutagara, Sudhana observed where the road was variously low and high, even and uneven, dusty and dust-free, safe and perilous, impassable and unobstructed, crooked and straight. As he went along he thought, “My going to that spiritual benefactor will be a means of accomplishment of the path of enlightening beings, a means of accomplishment of the path of knowledge to assist sentient beings; it will be a means of accomplishment of the path of transcendence, a means of accomplishment of the path of knowledge to assist sentient beings. It will become a means of stopping all beings from falling into attachment and rejection, arrogance and servility; a means of turning all beings away from bad inclinations; a means of ridding all beings of the dust of afflictions; a means of removing the thorns and grit of wrong views from all sentient beings; a means of absorption in the unobstructed reality realm; a means of leading to the eternal citadel of omniscience.
de ci'i phyir zhe na/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen ni/ dge ba'i chos thams cad kyi 'byung gnas so/ / dge ba'i bshes gnyen la ni/ thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi rag lus so zhes/
“Why is that? Because the kalyāṇamitras are the source of all good Dharmas, and the attainment of omniscience is dependent on the kalyāṇamitras.”
Why is that? Spiritual benefactors are mines of all that is good, sources of omniscience.”

de de ltar sems shing yid la byed pas spyod pa thub par dka' ba de mthar gyis grong khyer khang pa brtsegs pa der phyin nas/ mnyan pa dpa' bo yongs su rmed cing tshol tshol ba las/ grong khyer chen po zhig gi sgo rgya mtsho chen po'i ngogs na mnyan pa dpa' bo de tshong pa brgya phrag stong tsam dang / srog chags brgya stong du ma gtam sna tshogs nyan par 'dong pa sha stag gis kun nas bskor cing / rgya mtsho'i gtam yongs su brjod pas/ sangs rgyas kyi yon tan rgya mtsho sems can rnams la ston cing 'dug pa mthong ngo/ /

With his mind focused on those thoughts, and undergoing a difficult journey, he eventually arrived at the city of Kūṭāgāra. He looked and searched for the mariner Vaira and saw him at the shore of the ocean in front of the gate of the great city. He was encircled by a hundred thousand merchants and many hundreds of thousands of people who all wished to listen to his various tales. As he told them tales of the sea, he was teaching the beings about the ocean of qualities of the buddhas.

With these thoughts in mind, with a purpose rarely encountered, he made his way to Kutagara city looking for the mariner Vaira. When he got there, he saw the mariner surrounded by hundreds of thousands of merchants and hundreds of thousands of other people who wished to hear him talk, explaining to them the oceans of virtues of buddhas by talking about the ocean.

mthong nas kyang mnyan pa dpa' bo gang na ba der song ste phyin nas/ mnyan pa dpa' bo'i rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te/ mnyan pa dpa' bo la lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas/ mnyan pa dpa' bo'i mdun du 'dug ste/ thal mo sbyar nas 'di skad ces smras so/ /

When Sudhana saw the mariner Vaira, he approached him. Having approached him, Sudhana bowed his head to the mariner Vaira’s feet, circumambulated the mariner Vaira many hundreds of thousands of times, and sat down before the mariner Vaira. With his hands placed together in homage, he said,
Sudhana went up to Vaira, paid his respects, and said,

'phags pa; bdag gis bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed na/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bgyi ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bgyi ba ma 'tshal te/
“Ārya, I have developed the aspiration for the highest, complete enlightenment, but I do not know how bodhisattvas should train in bodhisattva conduct and in what way they should practice it.
“Noble one, I have set my mind on supreme perfect enlightenment, but I do not know how to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings.

'phags pa ni/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams la gdams ngag dang / rjes su bstan pa mdzad do/ /zhes bdag gis thos na/ 'phags pa; ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bgyi ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bgyi ba bdag la bka' stsal du gsol/
Ārya, I have heard that you give instruction and teachings to bodhisattvas! I pray that you explain to me how bodhisattvas should train in bodhisattva conduct and how they should practice it!”
I hear that you give enlightening beings instruction, and I hope you will tell me how one is to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings.”
