smras pa/ rigs kyi bu khyod kyis de ltar bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed de/ ye shes chen po 'thob pa 'byung ba'i rgyu 'dri ba dang / 'khor ba'i sdug bsngal sna tshogs kyi rgyud 'byung ba'i rgyu dang / thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi gling gi gnas su 'gro ba 'byung ba'i rgyu dang / dbyer med pa'i theg pa chen po 'byung ba'i rgyu dang / nyan thos dang / rang sangs rgyas kyi sar ltung bas 'jigs pa dang bral bar 'gyur ba'i lam gyi nan tan 'byung ba'i rgyu dang / zhi ba'i ting nge 'dzin gyi sgo dang rgyud sna tshogs khong du chud par bya ba'i ye shes kyi lam 'byung ba'i rgyu dang / byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa thams cad du 'gro bas rnam par spyod pa'i smon lam gyis shing rta'i 'khor lo thogs pa med pa'i lam 'byung ba dang / rnam par dag par 'gyur ba'i rgyu dang / byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa'i gzi brjid kyi dba' rlabs kyis rnam par brgyan pa thams cad kyi rang bzhin dang / tshul gyi lam 'byung ba dang / rnam par dag par 'gyur ba'i rgyu dang / chos kyi phyogs dang / sgo thams cad kyi phyi ma'i mtha'i lam 'byung ba dang / rnam par dag par 'gyur ba'i rgyu dang / thams cad mkhyen pa'i rgya mtshor 'jug pa'i lam 'byung ba dang / rnam par dag par 'gyur ba'i rgyu 'di 'dri ba legs so/ /legs so/ /

Vaira said, “Noble one, it is excellent, excellent, that you have developed the aspiration for the highest, complete enlightenment, that you have asked about the cause of[1102] great wisdom, the cause of the continuity of the various sufferings of saṃsāra, the cause of journeying to the island of omniscience, the cause of the indivisible Mahāyāna, the cause of the practice of the path that is free from the fear of falling down to the level of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, the cause of the path of knowledge that comprehends engaging in the gateways of various[1103] samādhis of peace, the cause of the pure[1104] and unimpeded path of the wheels of the chariot of the aspiration to the practice of all-pervasive bodhisattva conduct, the cause of the pure path of the way that is the nature of the display of all the majestic waves of bodhisattva conduct, the cause of the pure ultimate path of all the aspects and gateways of the Dharma, and the cause that gives rise to the pure path for entering the ocean of omniscience.

Vaira said, “It is good that you aspire to supreme perfect enlightenment and ask about the means of attaining great knowledge, about the cause of the various miseries of the mundane whirl, about the means of arriving at the island of omniscience, about the means of producing the indestructible vehicle of universal salvation, about the means of attaining the path leading away from the danger of falling into the state of individual liberation, about the source of the path of knowledge of the way to attain all kinds of tranquil concentrations, about the source of the unobstructed path of the chariot of vows carrying the practice of enlightening beings which goes everywhere, about the means of development and purification of the path guided by the nature of enlightening practice adorned with all waves of energy, about the means of development and purification of the endless path facing all things, the means of development and purification of the path into the ocean of omniscience.
rigs kyi bu; kho bo ni rgya mtsho'i ngogs kyi grong khyer khang pa brtsegs pa 'di na/ byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa snying rje chen po'i rgyal mtshan yongs su sbyong zhing gnas te/
“Noble one, I dwell at the city of Kūṭāgāra on the seashore, purifying the bodhisattva conduct called the banner of great compassion.
“I live in this coastal metropolis of Kutagara, purifying enlightening practice characterized by great compassion.
rigs kyi bu; kho bo ni 'dzam bu'i gling gi sems can phongs pa rnams mthong nas/ de dag gi don du dka' ba spyod de/ de dag gi bsam pa yongs su rdzogs par bya'o/ /
“Noble one, when I see destitute beings in Jambudvīpa, I undergo hardships for their sake, which means I will fulfill all their wishes.
Observing those on this continent who are poor, I practice such spiritual exercises as will cause their wishes to be fulfilled:
'jig rten gyi zang zing gis yongs su bsdu bar bya'o/ /
I will collect worldly goods for them.
I will take care of their mundane needs,
chos kyi longs spyod kyis de dag yongs su tshim par bya'o/ /
I will satisfy them with the enjoyment of the Dharma.
and I will satisfy them with spiritual enjoyments;
de dag la bsod nams kyi tshogs kyi lam man ngag tu bstan par bya'o/ /
I will teach them the instructions for the path of the accumulation of merit.
I will teach them the way to accumulate virtue,
ye shes kyi tshogs rnam par spel bar bya'o/ /
I will cause them to increase their accumulation of wisdom.
I will foster knowledge in them,
dge ba'i rtsa ba'i stobs yongs su spel bar bya'o/ /
I will increase the power of their roots of merit.
I will promote the growth of the power of roots of goodness,
byang chub kyi sems bskyed par bya'o/ /
I will cause them to develop the aspiration for enlightenment.
I will inspire them to seek enlightenment,
byang chub kyi bsam pa rnam par dag par bya'o/ /
I will purify their aspiration for enlightenment.
I will purify their aspiration for enlightenment,
snying rje chen po'i stobs nye bar brtan par bya'o/ /
I will cause them to have the enduring strength of great compassion.
I will firmly establish their power of great compassion,
'khor ba'i sdug bsngal rnam par zhi bar bya'o/ /
I will cause the suffering of saṃsāra to cease.
I will get them to extinguish the misery of the mundane whirl,
'khor ba'i spyod pas yongs su mi skyo ba'i stobs shin tu brtan par bya'o/ /
I will cause them to have an enduring strength for tireless conduct in saṃsāra.
I will firmly establish their power to act in the mundane world without tiring,
sems can rgya mtsho bsdu ba la 'di dag sbyar bar bya'o/ /
I will provide these to the gathering of an ocean of beings.
and I will get them to care for all living beings.
yon tan rgya mtsho'i nan tan gyi sgo la dgod par bya'o/ /
I will bring them into the gateways of the practice of an ocean of qualities.
I will set them at the gate of entry into the ocean of virtue,
'di dag la chos rgya mtsho'i ye shes snang ba nye bar bsgrub par bya'o/ /
I will cause them to obtain the light of the wisdom of the ocean of the Dharma.
I will produce in them the light of knowledge of the ocean of truths,
sangs rgyas rgya mtsho thams cad kyang 'di dag gis mngon par mthong bar bya'o/ /
I will cause them to see[1105] the entire ocean of buddhas.
I will turn them toward the ocean of all buddhas,
thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi rgya mtsho la yang 'di dag gzud par bya'o zhes
I will cause them to enter the ocean of omniscience.
and I will plunge them into the ocean of omniscience.
de lta bu'i bsam pa dang / yid la byed pa la brtson par kho bos rgya mtsho'i ngogs kyi grong khyer khang pa brtsegs pa 'di na gnas so/ /
“Noble one,[1106] it is with such an aspiration and intention that I dwell in the city of Kūṭāgāra on the seashore.
“With these thoughts in mind I roam this city on the edge of the ocean.
rigs kyi bu/ kho bo ni de ltar 'gro ba la phan pa dang / bde bar brtson pas rgya mtsho chen po'i rin po che'i gling thams cad kyang shes so/ /
“Noble one, dedicated in that way to the benefit and happiness of beings, I know all the islands of jewels in the great ocean.
Thus committed to the welfare and happiness of the world, I know all the treasure islands in the ocean.
rin po che'i 'byung gnas thams cad dang / rin po che'i rigs thams cad dang / rin po che'i gtos thams cad kyang rab tu shes so/ /
I know all the jewel mines, all the classes of jewels, and all the sources[1107] of jewels.
I know all the deposits of precious substances, all the types of precious substances, and all the sources of precious substances.
I know how to refine, bore out, extract, and produce all precious substances, and I know all precious vessels, tools, and objects, and the light of all precious substances.

klu'i gnas thams cad dang / klu 'khrug pa thams cad dang / gnod sbyin gyi gnas thams cad dang / gnod sbyin 'khrug pa thams cad dang / srin po'i gnas thams cad dang / srin po'i 'jigs pa thams cad rab tu zhi bar bya ba dang / 'byung po thams cad dang / 'byung po'i bar chad rnam par zhi bar bya ba yang rab tu shes te/

“I know all the residences of the nāgas, all that disconcerts the nāgas, all the residences of the yakṣas, all that disconcerts the yakṣas, all the residences of the rākṣasas, all that allays fear of the rākṣasas, all the residences of the bhūtas, all that allays fear of the bhūtas, and all that eliminates the obstacles created by the bhūtas.

I know the abodes of all water spirits, the agitations of all water spirits, the abodes of all sprites, the agitations of all sprites, the abodes of all goblins, how to alleviate the danger of goblins, the abodes of all ghosts, and how to put an end to obstacles caused by ghosts.
klong yod pa thams cad dang / klong thams cad bkol ba dang / dba' rlabs chen po yongs su spangs pa dang / chu'i kha dog rnam pa tha dad pa'ang rab tu shes so/ /
“I know all whirlpools,[1108] the avoidance[1109] of whirlpools, and the avoidance of great waves.
I know how to avoid all the whirlpools and billows, and I know the colors and depths of all the waters.
nyi zla dang / gza' skar gyi tshogs yongs su 'khor ba dang / nyin zhag dang / skad cig dang / yud tsam dang / thang cig kyang rab tu shes so/ /
“I know the orbits of the sun, moon, planets, and constellations and the seconds, minutes, and hours[1110] of[1111] the days and nights.
I know the cycles of the sun, moon, stars, and planets, and the lengths of the days and nights.

phan tshun du 'gro ba'i shol 'dums dang / bde mi bde dang / gru'i 'khrul 'khor brtan par bya ba dang / gru bzur ba dang / gru phul ba dang / rlung brdo ba dang / rlung bskyed pa dang / gru bsgyur zhing bzlog pa dang / gru rtod pa dang / gru gtang ba'ang rab tu shes so/ /

“I know the particular times to depart and arrive, safety and danger, whether a ship’s rigging is reliable, what ships to reject, what ships to sail, how to catch the winds, the coming of the wind, how to turn a ship, how to turn a ship around,[1112] how to anchor a ship, and how to launch a ship.

I know when to travel and when not to; I know when it is safe and when it is dangerous. I know the performance and soundness of the hull and rigging of ships. I know how to control and steer ships, I know how to catch the wind, I know where the winds rise from, I know how to direct the ship and how to turn it around, I know when to anchor and when to sail.

rigs kyi bu/ de ltar kho bo ni shes pa de lta bu dang ldan pas/ rtag tu sems can gyi don dang; dgos pa byed do/ tshong pa'i tshogs gru brtan pos lam bde zhing nye zhor mi 'gyur la/ mi 'jigs pa nas chos kyi gtam gyis dga' ba dang / spro ba bskyed cing bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du rin po che'i gling du phyin par byas nas/ de dag rin po che thams cad kyis chog ste phun sum tshogs par 'gyur ba dang / phyir yang 'dzam bu'i gling du 'gyed 'gyed kyang /

“Noble one, with that kind of knowledge I am constantly dedicated to necessary benefits[1113] for beings: I bring a group of merchants, just as they wish, to the island of jewels safely,[1114] peacefully,[1115] without fear, and in a reliable ship, and I talk to them about the Dharma in a way that delights them and brings them joy. When they have collected all the jewels and have attained good fortune, I bring them back again to Jambudvīpa.

“With this knowledge, always engaged in working for the benefit of beings, with a sturdy ship, safe, peaceful, without anxiety, I convey merchants to the treasure islands of their choice, pleasing them with spiritual conversation. Having enriched them with all kinds of jewels, I bring them back to this continent.

rigs kyi bu/ kho bo'i gru ni nam yang bub pa'am/ nye zhor gyur ma myong ste/ sems can gang gis kho bo mthong bar gyur pa dang / sems can gang gis kho bo'i chos bstan pa thos pa de dag kyang 'khor ba'i rgya mtsho thams cad du nye zhor 'gyur ba'i 'jigs pa dang bral bar 'gyur ro/ / thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi rgya mtshor 'jug pa'i ye shes kyang mngon sum du 'gyur ro/ /

“Noble one, no ship of mine has ever been in distress.[1116] Any being who sees me and any being who hears me teach the Dharma becomes free from all[1117] fear of sinking[1118] in the ocean of saṃsāra, and they turn toward[1119] the wisdom of entering the ocean of omniscience.

And I have never lost a single ship. All who see me or hear my spiritual instruction are freed from all fears of sinking in the ocean of the mundane whirl; they become aware of the knowledge of how to go into the ocean of omniscience,

srid pa rgya mtsho bskam pa'i don du'ang rab tu 'jug par 'gyur te/ dus gsum rgya mtsho'i ye shes snang ba'ang rab tu 'thob bo/ / sems can thams cad kyi sdug bsngal rgya mtsho zad par bya ba'i phyir yang mngon par mos par 'gyur ro/ / sems can thams cad kyi sems rgya mtsho'i rnyog pa dang bar bya ba'i phyir yang rab tu brtson par 'gyur ro/ /

They become dedicated to drying up the ocean of craving, attain the light of the knowledge of the ocean of the three times, and make the aspiration to eliminate the ocean of the suffering of all beings. They become dedicated to purifying away the pollution in the ocean of the minds of all beings.

they learn how to evaporate the ocean of craving, they are illumined with knowledge of the ocean of past, present, and future, they become capable of annihilating the ocean of suffering of all sentient beings, they undertake to clear the turbidity of the ocean of minds of all sentient beings,

zhing rgya mtsho thams cad rnam par dag par bya ba'i phyir brtson 'grus rtsom par 'gyur ro/ / phyogs rgya mtsho thams cad rgyas par dgang ba las kyang phyir mi ldog par 'gyur ro/ / 'gro ba thams cad kyi dbang po rgya mtsho tha dad pa'ang khong du chud par 'gyur ro/ / sems can thams cad kyi spyod pa rgya mtsho'i rjes su'ang 'brang bar 'gyur ro/ / 'gro ba'i bsam pa rgya mtsho ji lta ba bzhin du'ang gzugs brnyan 'byung bar 'gyur ro/ /

They become dedicated to purifying the ocean of all realms. They never turn back from spreading throughout the ocean of all directions. They comprehend the ocean of the different capabilities of all beings. They follow the ocean of the conducts of all beings. They manifest appearances that accord with the ocean of the wishes of all beings.

they begin the heroic effort to purify the ocean of all lands, they never turn back from going throughout the ocean of all places, they penetrate the variety in the ocean of faculties of all sentient beings, they adapt to the ocean of actions of all sentient beings, and they appear in the ocean of the world intentionally according to the mental set.

rigs kyi bu/ kho bo ni byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa mthong ba dang / thos pa dang / 'grogs pa dang / rjes su dran pa'i chu klung gi dbyangs zhes bya ba thob par zad na/ kho bos byang chub sems dpa' 'khor ba'i rgya mtsho thams cad du rnam par spyod pa/ nyon mongs pa'i rgya mtsho thams cad kyis gos pa med pa/ lta ba'i rnam pa'i rgya mtsho thams cad kyi chags pa'i chu srin gyi 'jigs pa dang bral ba/ chos rgya mtsho thams cad kyi rang bzhin dang gzhi las rnam par rgyu ba/ 'gro ba rgya mtsho thams cad bsdu ba'i dngos pos yongs su sdud pa'i rgya mtsho dang ldan pa/ thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi rgya mtsho dang 'grogs pa/ sems can gyi mngon par chags pa'i rgya mtsho thams cad rab tu bsrub pa/ dus rgya mtsho thams cad dang tha mi dad par rnam par spyod pa/ 'gro ba rgya mtsho thams cad yongs su smin par bya ba'i dmigs shes pa/ 'gro ba rgya mtsho thams cad kyi 'dul ba'i dbres las mi 'da' ba de dag gi spyod pa shes pa'am/ yon tan brjod par nus re skan/

“Noble one, I have attained the bodhisattva liberation called remembering to abide with the fruitful[1120] hearing and seeing of the banner of great compassion,[1121] but how could I know the conduct or describe the qualities of the bodhisattvas who act within all the oceans of saṃsāra, who are unstained by any of the oceans of saṃsāra, who are free from the fear of the makaras of attachment[1122] in all the oceans of false views, who move among the nature and basis[1123] of all phenomena, who possess an ocean[1124] of the methods of gathering all the oceans of beings, who dwell within the ocean of omniscience, who churn the ocean of the attachments of all beings, who perform their conduct[1125] without differentiation[1126] in the oceans of all times, who have the clairvoyant knowledge of the nature[1127] of ripening the ocean of all beings, and who never miss the time[1128] for guiding the ocean of beings?

“I have attained this enlightening liberation which is characterized by great compassion and the sound of flowing water, and it is beneficial to see me, hear me, live with me, and remember my name; but how can I know the practice or tell of the virtues of the enlightening beings who traverse all the oceans of the mundane whirl, who are unaffected by the ocean of afflictions, who are free from the danger of being engulfed by the ocean of views, who travel the water of inherent nature of the ocean of all phenomena, who travel the ground of inherent nature of the ocean of all beings, who hold the net of means of salvation of all creatures from the oceans of the mundane, who abide in the ocean of omniscience, who pull all sentient beings out of the ocean of attachments, who remain continuously through the ocean of all times, who have true higher knowledge to perfect the ocean of all sentient beings, who do not miss the right occasions to guide the ocean of all sentient beings?

song / rigs kyi bu/ lho phyogs kyi rgyud 'di nyid na grong khyer dga' ba'i phreng ba zhes bya ba yod de/ de na tshong dpon rgyal ba dam pa zhes bya ba 'dug gi/ de'i gan du song la/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bya ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bya ba dris shig /

“Depart, noble one. In this southern region, in the town called Nandihāra, dwells a head merchant by the name of Jayottama. Go to him and ask him, ‘How should a bodhisattva train in bodhisattva conduct? How should a bodhisattva practice it?’ ”
“South of here is a city called Nandihara. An eminent man named Jayottama lives there. Go ask him how to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings.”

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis/ mnyan pa dpa' bo'i rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag byas nas/ mnyan pa dpa' bo la lan brgya stong du mas g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas te/ yang dang yang blta sa nas/ gdong mchi mas bkang ste ngu zhing dge ba'i bshes gnyen blta bas ma ngoms bzhin du mnyan pa dpa' bo'i drung nas song ngo// //

Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, was overjoyed, pleased, happy, and content. He bowed his head to the feet of the mariner Vaira, circumambulated the mariner Vaira many hundreds of thousands of times, keeping him to his right, and, looking back again and again, departed from the mariner Vaira.
Then Sudhana paid his respects and reluctantly left the mariner Vaira.
bam po dgu bcu bdun pa/
[tshong dpon rgyal ba dam pa]
Chapter 26. Jayottama
Jayottama
de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang / byams pa chen pos sems can gyi khams tshad med pa rgyas par dgang ba'i sems dang ldan pa/
Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, whose mind spread great love throughout the immeasurable realm of beings;
His mind filled with great love for the infinite realm of life,
snying rje chen po'i rlan gyis mngon par brlan pa'i rgyud can/ bsod nams dang / ye shes kyi tshogs rgya chen po'i rgyan shin tu bsags pa/
whose being was saturated with the tenderness[1129] of great compassion; who had accumulated a vast array of the accumulations of merit and wisdom;
overflowing with great compassion, having amassed immense stores of virtue and knowledge,
nyon mongs pa'i rdul dang / mun pa dang / dri ma dang / 'dam thams cad dang bral ba/
who had become free of all the dust, darkness, dirt, and mire of the kleśas;
freed from the defilement of ignorance, passion, and all afflictions,
chos mnyam pa nyid khong du chud pas thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi lam gyen thur med pa la zhugs pa/
who had realized the equality of all phenomena; who was devoted to the path that leads[1130] upward to omniscience;
realizing the equality of all things, proceeding equanimously on the path of omniscience,
dge ba'i chos tshad med pa la 'jug pa'i sgor zhugs pa/
who had chosen[1131] the gateway for entering into immeasurable good qualities;
having eradicated the entryways into countless bad tendencies,
mi dge ba thams cad kyis mi shigs pa'i brtson 'grus brtan pa'i mthu sngon du 'dor ba dang ldan pa/
who had the exertion[1132] of firm diligence that is unimpaired by any bad quality;
proceeding heroically by the power of steadfast energy immune to all evils,
byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin bsam gyis mi khyab pa rab tu byang ba/
who was filled[1133] with the vast calmness[1134] of inconceivable bodhisattva samādhis;
filled with great calm by the inconceivable concentrations of an enlightening being,
rgya chen po'i bde ba rab tu thob pa/
shes rab kyi nyi ma'i 'od zer snang bas ma rig pa'i mun pa ma lus bar bsal ba;
who shone with the light of the sun of wisdom that eliminated all the darkness of ignorance;
having thoroughly dispelled the darkness of ignorance by the light of the sun of wisdom,
thabs kyi ser bu bde zhing bsil bas blags pa'i ye shes kyi me tog gis rgyas ba/
who scattered flowers of wisdom brought by the pleasant, cool breezes of methods;
adorned with flowers of knowledge vivified by the moon of bliss and the breeze of means,
smon lam chen po'i rgya mtshor 'byung ba'i ye shes kyi tshul dang mthun pa/
who followed the way of wisdom that emerged from an ocean of great aspirations;
according with the principles of knowledge of liberation through the ocean of great vows,
chos kyi dbyings thams cad du thogs pa med par rgyas par 'gengs pa'i ye shes dang ldan pa/
and who possessed the wisdom that permeated without impediment the entire realm of the Dharma‍—
imbued with knowledge pervading the reality realm unimpeded,
thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi pho brang du thogs pa med par 'gro ba la mngon du gyur pa/ byang chub sems dpa'i lam la mngon par mos pa de/
he had approached entry into the city[1135] of faultless[1136] omniscience, and he yearned for the bodhisattva path.
facing the entrance of the imperishable city of omniscience, seeking the path of enlightening beings,

grong khyer dga' ba'i phreng ba gang na ba der phyin te/ tshong dpon rgyal ba dam pa yongs su rmed cing tshol tshol ba la/ grong khyer dga' ba'i phreng ba'i shar phyogs logs kyi 'dab gcig na/ shing a sho ka'i nags tshal rgyal mtshan sna tshogs zhes bya ba 'dug pa de'i nang na/ khyim bdag stong phrag du ma zhig gis bskor te/ grong khyer gyi bya ba sna tshogs yongs su bgro zhing de las brten te/ bdag tu bya ba thams cad yang dag par gzhom pa dang / yongs su 'dzin pa thams cad yongs su gtang ba dang / dngos por 'dzin pa thams cad rab tu spang ba dang / mngon par zhen pa thams cad shin tu gzhig pa dang / srid pa'i 'ching ba thams cad gcad par bya ba dang / lta ba'i rnam pa thams cad kyi sgo glegs gcag pa dang / the tshom dang / yid gnyis dang / nem nur gyi rab rib thams cad rnam par bsal ba dang / g.yo sgyu'i rnyog pa shin tu gdang ba dang / phrag dog dang ser sna'i dri ma yongs su sbyang ba dang / sems kyi mtsho shin tu gsal bar bya ba dang / sems rnyog pa med pa la sems can rab tu dgod pa dang / dad pa rnyog pa med pa'i stobs bskyed de/ sangs rgyas blta bar mos pa bskyed pa dang / byang chub sems dpa'i stobs bsngags shing sangs rgyas kyi chos yang dag par blangs pa dang / byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa smos te/ byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin gyi stobs yongs su bskyed pa dang / byang chub sems dpa'i shes rab kyi stobs yang dag par ston cing / byang chub sems dpa'i dran pa'i stobs rnam par dag pa'i mthar phyin par bya ba'i phyir/ chos kyi gtam byed cing

He arrived at the town called Nandihāra and looked and searched for the head merchant Jayottama. He saw him on the eastern edge of the town of Nandihāra, in a forest of ashoka trees that was called Vicitradhvaja. He was encircled by many thousands of householders deciding[1137] upon various kinds of civic duties, and in reference to those he talked about the Dharma. He was teaching the Dharma for the sake of eliminating all egotism;[1138] abandoning all possessiveness;[1139] rejecting all attachment; forsaking all fixation on things; destroying all clinging; cutting through all the bondage of craving; breaking down the doors of all views; clearing away the darkness of doubt, uncertainty, and equivocation; cleansing away the dirt of illusion and deceit; purifying the stains of envy and miserliness; clarifying the lake of the mind; bringing beings to a state of unpolluted mentality; giving rise to an unpolluted faith; giving rise to the aspiration to see the buddhas; eulogizing the power of bodhisattvas; receiving the Dharma of the buddhas; aspiring to bodhisattva conduct; giving rise to the power of bodhisattva samādhi; teaching the power of bodhisattva wisdom; and attaining the highest purity of the power of bodhisattva memory.

Sudhana made his way to the city of Nandihara and sought out the eminent Jayottama, whom he saw in a grove at the eastern edge of the city, surrounded by thousands of elders, giving instructions regarding the various affairs of the city, in the course of which he was also talking about spirituality in order to get rid of all egoism, possessiveness, acquisitiveness, clinging to material things, dependency, binding cravings, impeding views, obscuring doubts, beclouding deceit and guile, defiling envy and jealousy, in order to clear and purify everyone’s minds, in order to inspire them to delight in the vision of buddhas by fostering the power of pure faith in them, in order to get them to accept the buddha-teachings by bringing forth the powers of enlightening beings in turn, in order to generate the power of concentration of enlightening beings by revealing to them the practices of enlightening beings, in order to purify enlightening beings’ power of recollection by showing them the power of wisdom of enlightening beings.
'di lta ste/ byang chub tu sems bskyed pa la mngon par mos par bya ba'i phyir chos ston cing 'dug pa mthong ngo/ /
This means that he was teaching the Dharma in order to inspire the aspiration to enlightenment.
Thus he was expounding the Teaching, to inspire them to seek enlightenment.

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis gtam de'i rjes chad chad du bsdad nas/ tshong dpon rgyal ba dam pa'i rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te/ ring mo zhig tu btud nas/ chos la shin tu gus pa'i bsam pas tshig 'di skad du brjod do/ /
Then when the teaching was concluded, Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, approached and bowed his head to the feet of the head merchant Jayottama. He bowed down to him for a long time and said,
Sudhana went up to the grandee Jayottama, bowed to him, and with respect for the Teaching said,

'phags pa/ bdag ni nor bzangnor bzang zhes bgyi ba ste/ byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa yongs su tshol na/ ci nas kyang bdag byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la slob par 'gyur ba dang / bslabs nas kyang ci nas sems can thams cad yongs su smin par bgyi ba dang / gdul ba'i don la mngon du mos par 'gyur ba dang / sangs rgyas thams cad kyi zhal blta ba las mi 'phang ba dang / sangs rgyas thams cad kyi chos thos par 'gyur ba dang / sangs rgyas thams cad kyi chos kyi sprin gyi char yongs su gzung ba dang; sangs rgyas thams cad kyi chos kyi tshul la nan tan du bgyi ba dang / 'jig rten gyi khams thams cad du byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa spyad pa dang / bskal pa thams cad du gnas kyang byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pas yongs su mi skyo ba dang / de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi rnam par 'phrul pa yongs su 'tshal bar 'gyur ba dang / sangs rgyas thams cad kyi byin gyi rlabs yang dag par mnod pa dang / de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi stobs rnams la snang ba thob par 'gyur ba de ltar 'phags pas bdag la bshad du gsol/

“Ārya, I am Sudhana, I am Sudhana! I seek bodhisattva conduct. Instruct me, Ārya, on how I should train in bodhisattva conduct and while training how I should aspire to guide and ripen all beings,[1140] not forsake seeing all the buddhas, hear the Dharma of all the buddhas, possess the rain[1141] from the clouds of the Dharma of all the buddhas, practice in the way of all the buddhas, practice bodhisattva conduct in all world realms, never tire of bodhisattva conduct while dwelling in all kalpas, comprehend[1142] the manifestations of all the tathāgatas, receive the blessing of all the buddhas, and attain splendor in the power of all the tathāgatas.”

“I am Sudhana, O noble one, and I seek the practice of enlightening beings. Please tell me how to learn the practice of enlightening beings, how to orient myself to the disciplines that will perfect all sentient beings while I am learning, how to see all buddhas, how to hear the teaching of all buddhas, how to remember the multitudes of teachings of all buddhas, how to carry out the principles of the teachings of all buddhas, how to perform the practice of enlightening beings in all worlds, how to be indefatigable living in all ages by the practice of enlightening beings, how to perceive the transformation of all who have gone to Thusness, how to receive the empowerment of all buddhas, how to attain knowledge of the powers of all buddhas.”

de nas tshong dpon rgyal ba dam pas/ tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la 'di skad ces smras so/ / rigs kyi bu/ de ltar khyod kyis bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed pa legs so/ / legs so/ /
Then the head merchant Jayottama said to Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, “Noble one, it is excellent, excellent, that you have developed the aspiration for the highest, complete enlightenment.
Jayottama said to Sudhana, “It is good that you aspire to supreme perfect enlightenment.

rigs kyi bu/ kho bo ni 'di lta ste/ dngos po med pa la gnas pas mngon par 'du bya ba med pa'i rdzu 'phrul thob pa'i mthus/ byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa'i sgo thams cad du 'gro ba yongs su spyong ste/
“Noble one, I purify the gateway to omnipresent[1143] bodhisattva conduct through the power of the attainment of noncomposite miracles[1144] while residing in the absence of existence.
I am purifying the method of enlightening practice that goes everywhere, by the power of attainment of nondoing based on nonbeing.
da ltar kho bo byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa yongs su dag pa'i sgo thams cad du 'gro ba 'di la gnas shing /
In that way, remaining in this gateway to omnipresent[1145] bodhisattva conduct,
By this method of purification of enlightening practice going everywhere,

stong gsum gyi stong chen po'i 'jig rten gyi khams thams cad kyi sum cu rtsa gsum gyi lha'i 'jig rten thams cad dang / mtshe ma'i lha'i gnas thams cad dang / dga' ldan gyi lha'i 'jig rten thams cad dang / 'phrul dga'i lha'i 'jig rten thams cad dang / gzhan 'phrul dbang byed kyi lha'i 'jig rten thams cad dang / bdud kyi gnas thams cad dang / 'dod pa'i khams kyi lha'i ris su gtogs pa thams cad dang / lha'i gnas thams cad dang / klu'i 'jig rten thams cad dang / klu'i gnas thams cad dang / gnod sbyin gyi 'jig rten thams cad dang / gnod sbyin gyi gnas thams cad dang / srin po'i 'jig rten thams cad dang / srin po'i gnas thams cad dang / grul bum gyi 'jig rten thams cad dang / grul bum gyi gnas thams cad dang / yi kyi 'jig rten thams cad dang / yi kyi gnas thams cad dang / dri za'i 'jig rten thams cad dang / dri za'i gnas thams cad dang / lha ma yin gyi 'jig rten thams cad dang / lha ma yin gyi gnas thams cad dang / nam mkha' lding gi 'jig rten thams cad dang / nam mkha' lding gi gnas thams cad dang / mi 'am ci'i 'jig rten thams cad dang / mi 'am ci'i gnas thams cad dang / lto 'phye chen po'i 'jig rten thams cad dang / lto 'phye chen po'i gnas thams cad dang / mi'i 'jig rten thams cad dang / mi'i gnas thams cad dang / grong dang / grong khyer dang / grong rdal dang / ljongs dang / khams dang / rgyal po'i pho brang 'khor dang / 'dod pa'i khams su gtogs pa'i sems can gyi rgyud thams cad du

in all billion-world universes, in all the Trāyastriṃśa[1146] paradises, in all the Yāma paradises, in all the Tuṣita paradises, in all the Nirmāṇarati paradises, in all the Paranirmitavaśavartin paradises, in all the abodes of the māras, in all the places that are classed as paradises within all desire realms, in all the nāga worlds, in all the nāga abodes, in all the yakṣa worlds, in all the yakṣa abodes, in all the rākṣasa worlds, in all the rākṣasa abodes, in all the kumbhāṇḍa worlds, in all the kumbhāṇḍa abodes, in all the preta worlds, in all the preta abodes, in all the gandharva worlds, in all the gandharva abodes, in all the asura worlds, in all the asura abodes, in all the garuḍa worlds, in all the garuḍa abodes, in all the kinnara worlds, in all the kinnara abodes, in all the mahoraga worlds, in all the mahoraga abodes, in all the human worlds, in all the human abodes, villages, towns, market towns, districts, countries, and capitals, and for all classes of beings that are within all desire realms
in all realms of being in the universe,

chos ni ston to/ / chos ma yin pa ni bzlog go / rtsod pa ni zhi bar byed do/ / 'thab pa ni rnam par bzlog go / 'khrug pa ni nye bar zhi bar byed do/ / g.yul du lhags pa ni rnam par bzlog go / shags 'gyed pa ni zhi bar byed do/ / mdud par 'dzin pa ni rab tu sel to/ / bcings pa thams cad ni yongs su gcod do/ / brtson ra thams cad ni mngon par 'dral lo/ / 'jigs pa ni rnam par bzlog go / mi dge ba'i las kyi 'du byed ni rgyun gcod do/ /

I teach the Dharma, reject all that is not Dharma, pacify all disputes, dispel all conflict, pacify all quarrels, prevent all battles, pacify wars, pacify hostility, cut through all bondage, break open all prisons, dispel all fear, and end the practice of nonvirtuous activities.
I expound the Teaching I oppose untruth, I stop controversy, conflict, strife, combat, and hostility. I cut through bonds and break prisons apart. I eliminate fears. I put an end to evildoing,

srog gcod pa las ni sems can rnam par bzlog go / ma byin par len pa dang / 'dod pas log par g.yem pa dang / brdzun du smra ba dang / phra ma dang / zhe gcod pa dang / tshig kyal pa dang / chags sems dang / gnod sems dang; log par lta ba las ni sems can rnam par bzlog go /
I turn beings away from killing and from taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, telling lies, slandering, harsh speech, idle speech, avariciousness, maliciousness, and wrong views.
I turn people away from killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, falsehood, slander, harshness, divisive talk, longing, malice, and false views.

mi bya ba thams cad ni byed du mi 'jug go / dge ba'i chos bya ba thams cad ni byed du 'jug go / sems can thams cad ni bzo thams cad la slob tu 'dzud de/ 'jig rten rnams rab tu dga' bar bya ba dang / sems can yongs su smin par bya ba dang / zhags pa 'thub pa thams cad la gong ma'i ye shes khyad par du 'phags pa brjod pa'i phyir rjes su 'brang bar bya ba dang / lta ba'i rnam pa thams cad rnam par bzlog pa dang / sangs rgyas kyi chos thams cad brjod cing bstan pa'i phyir/ 'jig rten la phan par 'gyur ba'i gtsug lag thams cad kyang ston to/ / rnam par 'god do/ / rab tu gsal bar byed do/ / brjod do/ /

I turn beings away from all that should not be done and make them engage in all virtuous Dharma activity, and I make all beings train in all skills. I teach, prepare, elucidate, and present all the treatises that are beneficial to the world, so as to bring happiness to the world, to ripen beings, to follow false doctrines[1147] in order to describe the special higher wisdom, to dispel all wrong views, and to describe and teach all the Buddhadharma.

I get them to stop all compulsive activity and to pursue all right and good actions. I teach everyone all arts and crafts that bring benefit to the world. I elucidate, articulate, explain, and promote all sciences for the happiness of the world. I go along with all false doctrines in order to develop the people involved in them. In order to show the excellence of higher knowledge, to put a stop to all views, to inspire interest in the teaching of all buddhas,
de bzhin du tshangs pa'i 'jig rten gyi bar du gzugs kyi khams kyi lha thams cad zil gyis mnan te chos ston to/ /
I overwhelm and teach the Dharma to all the devas in the form realm as far up as the Brahmā paradise.
I approach all the celestial beings in the realm of form all the way up to the world of Brahma and expound the Teaching to them.

stong gsum gyi stong chen po'i 'jig rten gyi khams 'dir ji lta ba de bzhin du phyogs bcur yang 'jig rten gyi khams sangs rgyas kyi zhing bye ba khrag khrig brgya stong brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed dag tu chos ston te/ sangs rgyas kyi chos kyang ston to/ /

“Just as I teach the Dharma in the world realms of this billion-world universe, I do so in world realms in the ten directions as numerous as the atoms in an indescribable quintillion buddha realms. I teach the Dharma of the buddhas. I teach the Dharma of the bodhisattvas.
And as I teach in this universe, so also do I teach in as many worlds as atoms in ten unspeakable numbers of decillions of buddha-lands. I teach the ways of buddhas, the ways of enlightening beings,
byang chub sems dpa'i chos dang / nyan thos kyi chos dang / rang sangs rgyas kyi chos kyang ston to/ /
I teach the Dharma of the śrāvakas and the Dharma of the pratyekabuddhas.
the ways of Buddhist disciples, and the ways of individual illuminates.

sems can dmyal ba yang ston to/ / sems can dmyal bar 'gro ba'i lam dang / sems can dmyal ba'i sems can gyi mi bde ba'ang ston to/ / byol song gi skye gnas kyang ston to/ / byol song gi skye gnas kyi lam gyi rgyud tha dad pa dang / byol song gi skye gnas kyi lam du 'gro ba'i lam dang / byol song gi skye gnas su skyes pa'i sdug bsngal yang ston to/ / gshin rje'i 'jig rten yang ston to/ / gshin rje'i 'jig rten du 'gro ba'i lam dang / gshin rje'i 'jig rten gyi sdug bsngal yang ston to/ / mtho ris kyi 'jig rten yang ston to/ / mtho ris kyi 'jig rten du 'gro ba'i lam dang mtho ris kyi 'jig rten gyi dga' ba spyod pa dang / longs spyod kyang ston to/ / mi'i 'jig rten yang ston to/ / mi'i 'jig rten gyi lam kyi rgyud du 'gro ba'i lam dang / mi'i 'jig rten gyi bde ba dang; sdug bsngal nyams su myong ba sna tshogs kyang ston to/

I teach the hells. I teach the path that leads to the hells. I teach the unhappiness[1148] of beings in the hells. I teach the animal existences. I teach the different kinds of animal existences, the paths that lead to animal existences, and the suffering of animal existences. I teach the world of Yama. I teach the path that leads to the world of Yama. I teach the suffering in the world of Yama. I teach the higher existences. I teach the path that leads to the higher existences. I teach the practice and enjoyment of happiness in the higher existences. I teach the human world. I teach the path that leads to the human world. I teach the various experiences of happiness and suffering in the human world.

I teach about the hells, what leads to hell, and the motives and actions of beings in hell. I teach about animality, the types who tend toward animality, what leads to animality, and the misery of animalistic life. I teach about the underworld, what leads to the underworld, and the misery of the underworld. I teach about heavens, what leads to heaven, and the enjoyments of heaven. I teach about the human world, what leads to the human world, and the variety of pleasant and unpleasant experiences in the human world.

de ltar rigs kyi bu/ kho bo ni 'jig rten gyi chos kyang ston to/ / 'jig rten kun 'byung ba dang / 'jig rten nub par 'gyur ba dang / 'jig rten gyi kha na ma tho ba dang / 'jig rten nas 'byung ba yang ston to/ /
“In that way, noble one, I also teach the Dharma of the world, the creation of the world, the destruction of the world, the transgressions in the world, and the renunciation of the world.
“Thus I teach about the law of the world, the formation of the world, the decline of the world, the pain of the world, and emancipation from the world;

de yang 'di ltar byang chub sems dpa'i lam yang dag par bstan pa dang / 'khor ba'i skyon rnam par bzlog pa dang / thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi yon tan yang dag par brjod pa dang / srid pa'i lam gyi rgyud du mgo 'khor ba dang / sdug bsngal du gyur pa yang dag par bstan pa dang / sgrib pa med pa'i chos nyid brjod pa dang / 'jig rten rgyu ba'i bya ba yongs su bstan pa dang / 'jig rten 'byung ba dang / ldog pa'i bde ba dang / sdug bsngal thams cad smos pa dang / 'gro ba thams cad gnas kyi ming du bya ba rnam par bsgom pa dang / de bzhin gshegs pa'i chos gnas pa med pa mngon par bstan pa dang / las dang nyon mongs pa'i 'khor lo thams cad rnam par bzlog pa dang / de bzhin gshegs pa'i chos kyi 'khor lo 'khor ba shin tu brjod pa'i phyir chos ston to/ /

“In this way, I teach the Dharma in order to explain the bodhisattva path, reject the faults of saṃsāra, teach the qualities of omniscience, pacify the delusion and sufferings of the existences, describe the unobscured true nature, illuminate the activities of being in the world, describe all the happiness and suffering of being in the world, contemplate the designations of the abodes of all beings, teach the tathāgata qualities that have no location, counter the wheel of all karma and kleśas, and describe the turning of the tathāgata’s wheel of the Dharma.

I expound the Teaching in order to explain the path of practice of enlightening beings, to remove the ills of the mundane world, to show the virtues of omniscience, to extinguish the pain of infatuation with states of being, to elucidate the unimpeded nature of reality, to clarify the ordinary conduct of the world, to point out the happiness and misery of the conduct of all beings in the world, to show the notions on which all worlds are based, to elucidate the independent state of those who realize Thusness, to fend off all active afflictions, and to show the progress of the wheel of teaching of the enlightened.

rigs kyi bu/ kho bo ni byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa rnam par dag pa'i sgo thams cad du 'gro ba/ dngos po med pa la gnas pas mngon par 'du bya ba med pa'i rdzu 'phrul gyi mthus brgyan pa 'di shes par zad na/
“Noble one, I know this gateway to pure, omnipresent[1149] bodhisattva conduct, the stainless[1150] display of the noncomposite miracles[1151] based in the absence of existence,[1152]
“I know this method of purification of enlightening practice that goes everywhere, an undefiled manifestation of nondoing based on illumination.

kho bos byang chub sems dpa' thams cad mngon par shes pa/ zhing gi dbyings thams cad du sgyu ma lta bu'i ye shes kyi lus kyis rgyas par 'gengs pa/ kun du lta ba'i ye shes kyis rab tu thob pa /tshig gi lam dang / sgra thams cad rnam par dmigs pa la shin tu gzhol ba'i rna ba dang ldan pa/ dus gsum rgyas par 'gengs pa'i chos kyi sgo snang ba la dbang rab tu thob pa/

How can I know the practice or tell of the virtues of enlightening beings who have all mystic knowledges, who go throughout all lands with the body of knowledge of illusoriness, who have attained the stage of knowledge of the universal eye, who hear all utterances, who have attained control of the light of the way to truth that pervades past, present, and future,

chos thams cad la yang dag par gzhol ba'i ye shes la dbang bsgyur ba'i skyes bu dpa' bo sems can tshad med bsam gyis mi khyab pa'i bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du rnam par dmigs par bya ba lam 'dres pa'i dbyangs kyi dkyil 'khor dang ldan pa'i lce yangs shing srab la yid du 'ong ba dang ldan pa/ bsam pa tha dad pa'i sems can rgya mtsho'i yid du 'ong ba'i kha dog dang dbyibs su ldan pa'i byang chub sems dpa' thams cad dang mnyam pa'i lus sgyu ma lta bu dang ldan pa/

who are heroic masters of knowledge comprehending all things, who speak with the voice of totality communicating to infinite sentient beings according to their mentalities, who have phantom bodies the same as all enlightening beings pleasing to the masses of sentient beings with their various wishes,

de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad dang mi gnyis pa'i spyod lam gyi bsam gyis mi khyab pa'i lus la gzhol ba/ dus gsum thams cad du rjes su 'brang ba'i ye shes kyi lus dang ldan pa/ nam mkha'i dbyings ltar tshad med pa'i spyod yul dpag tu med pa'i yul dang ldan pa de dag gi spyod pa shes pa'am/ yon tan brjod par nus re skan/
who are intent upon one and the same inconceivable body of all buddhas, whose body of knowledge pervades past, present, and future, whose sphere is as vast and measureless as the sky?

song / rigs kyi bu/ lho phyogs kyi rgyud 'di nyid kyi yul shu ma phyi ma'i mtha' na grong khyer ka ling+ka'i nags tshal zhes bya ba yod de/ de na dge slong ma seng ge rnam par bsgyings pa zhes bya ba 'dug gi /de'i gan du song la/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bya ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bya ba dris shig /

“Depart, noble one. In this southern region, in the land called Śroṇāparānta, there is a city by the name of Kaliṅgavana where dwells a bhikṣuṇī by the name of Siṃhavijṛmbhitā. Go to her and ask her, ‘How should a bodhisattva train in bodhisattva conduct? How should a bodhisattva practice it?’ ”
“South of here, in the land of Shronaparanta, is a city called Kalingavana, where a nun named Sinhavijurmbhita lives. Go ask her how to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings.”

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis/ tshong dpon rgyal ba dam pa'i rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te/ tshong dpon rgyal ba dam pa la lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas yang dang yang bltas te/ tshong dpon rgyal ba dam pa'i drung nas song ngo/ /

Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, bowed his head to the feet of the head merchant Jayottama, circumambulated the head merchant Jayottama many hundreds of thousands of times, keeping him to his right, and, looking back again and again, departed from the head merchant Jayottama.
Then Sudhana paid his respects to Jayottama and left.

d.crumb: [dge slong ma seng ge rnam par bsgyings pa]

f.d: [dge slong ma seng ge rnam par bsgyings pa]
Chapter 27. Siṃhavijṛmbhitā
Sinhavijurmbhita

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang mthar gyis yul shu ma phyi ma'i mtha'i grong khyer ka ling+ka'i nags tshal gang na ba der song ste phyin nas/ dge slong ma seng ge rnam par bsgyings pa yongs su tshol zhing sems can kun la rmed pa'i tshe/ gang nas gang du song ba de dang der/ rogs pa brgya phrag du ma dang / bu mo brgya phrag du ma zhig srang dang / lam gyi bzhi mdo dang; lam gyi sum mdo dag nas tshogs te rjes su 'brang ngo/ / skyes pa brgya phrag du ma dang / bud med brgya phrag du ma zhig gis kyang /

Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, set out for the town of Kaliṅgavana in the land of Śroṇāparānta and then arrived there. Searching for the bhikṣuṇī Siṃhavijṛmbhitā, as he roamed here and there he questioned the people he met. There were many hundreds of young men[1154] and many hundreds of young women assembling and following in the streets, crossroads, and street junctions, together with many hundreds of men and many hundreds of women.

Then Sudhana made his way to the city called Kalingavana in the land of Shronaparanta, where he asked everyone he met the whereabouts of the nun Sinhavijurmbhita. As he was looking for the nun, everywhere he went hundreds of boys and girls came together from the streets and intersections and blocked the way. There were also hundreds of men and women, who told him,

rigs kyi bu/ 'di re/ dge slong ma seng ge rnam par bsgyings pa ni/ grong khyer ka ling+ka'i nags tshal 'di nyid kyi bza' shing gi ra ba chen po rgyal ba'i 'od kyis byin pa nyi ma'i mdog na/ sems can tshad med pa'i don du chos ston cing 'dug go zhes bstan to/ /

They said, “Noble one, the bhikṣuṇī Siṃhavijṛmbhitā is in this town of Kaliṅgavana, sitting in the great park called Sūryaprabha donated by Jayaprabha, where she is teaching the Dharma for the sake of countless beings.”
“the nun Sinhavijurmbhita is in this city, staying in Sunlight Park, which was donated by Jayaprabha, where she is expounding the Teaching for the benefit of countless beings.”

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang / bza' shing gi ra ba nyi ma'i mdog der phyin nas kun tu btsal te bltas na/ bza' shing gi ra ba de na/ shing zla ba shar ba zhes bya ba/ khang pa brtsegs pa'i dbyibs ltar 'dug pa/ 'od sna tshogs kyi kha dog can/ 'od kyi mdog dang ldan pa/ 'khor kun du dpag tshad kyi khyon tsam du 'od kyis rgyas par 'gengs pa mang po dang /

Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, went to Sūryaprabha Park. Walking around it and looking about, he saw in the park many trees called candrodgata that had the shape of kūṭāgāras, had various colors of light, and shone with light, illuminating everywhere around up to a yojana.

So then Sudhana went to this Sunlight Park and looked all around. In the park he saw trees called “moon-risen,” which were covered like pavilions, of flamelike color and blazing radiance, lighting up the space of a league all around.

lo ma'i shing yongs su 'gebs pa zhes bya ba/ gdugs kyi rnam pa dang / dbyibs su 'dug pa'i 'dab mas kun nas khebs pa/ bai DUr+ya sngon po'i kha dog ltar 'dug pa'i sprin gyi mdog dang ldan pa mang po dang /
He saw many leafy trees called saṃpracchada that had the shape of a parasol, and their leaves covered everywhere, like shining clouds the color of blue beryl.
He also saw leafy trees called “completely covering,” which are shaped like parasols, their clustered leaves providing shade, shining like blue crystal clouds.

me tog gi shing me tog gi mdzod ces bya ba/ ri'i rgyal po kha ba can ltar mdangs dga' ba'i dbyibs sna tshogs dang ldan pa/ kha dog sna tshogs kyi me tog mi zad pa'i char rab tu 'bebs pa/ sum cu rtsa gsum gyi lha'i pho brang gi rgyan gyis kun nas 'du ba dang / sus kyang mi shigs pa lta bu mang po dang / shing tog gi shing rtag tu smin pa'i ro dpe med pa'i 'bras bu'i tshogs zhes bya ba/ gser gyi ri bo'i lhun ltar 'dug pa/ rtag tu shing tog phun sum tshogs par gnas pa mang po dang /

He saw many blossoming trees called kusumakośa that had the varied beautiful shape of the Himalaya, king of mountains, and from which fell unceasing flows of a rain of flowers of various colors; they were an accumulation of all the adornments of the Trāyastriṃśa palace[1155] and could not be destroyed by anyone.[1156] He saw many fruit trees called anupamasvāduphalanicita, which had the form of gold mountain peaks[1157] and always had perfect fruit that was always ripe.

He saw flowering trees called “treasury of flowers,” which had various pleasing forms like the Himalaya Mountains and showered endless streams of varicolored flowers, like the trees of paradise adorning the heavens. He also saw ever-ripe sweet fruit trees called “gathering of fruits of indescribable sweetness,” which had the appearance of golden polar mountains and were always bearing fruit.

rin po che'i rgyal po'i shing rnam par snang ba'i mdzod ces bya ba/ rin po che'i rgyal po dpe med pa'i dbyibs ltar 'dug pa/ lha rdzas kyi rin po che'i phreng ba dang / se mo do dang / rgyan rin po che yid bzhin gyi rgyal po'i mdzod nas byung ba ltar phun sum tshogs pa dang ldan pa/ rin po che kha dog grangs med pa'i 'byung gnas su gyur pa mang po dang /

He saw many trees of kings of jewels called vairocanakośa that had the shapes of incomparable kings of jewels and possessed perfect divine strings of jewels, necklaces, and precious adornments that seemed to have come from the treasury of the kings of wish-fulfilling jewels and were the source of jewels of countless colors.

He also saw jewel trees called “treasury of radiance,” which looked like incomparable jewels and bore riches in buds producing garlands and ornaments of celestial jewels and wish-fulfilling gems, and were adorned by jewels of countless colors.
gos kyi shing dga' bar byed pa zhes bya ba/ lha rdzas kyi gos rin po che kha dog sna tshogs kyi tshogs rab tu 'gyed cing 'phyang bas shin tu brgyan pa mang po dang /
He saw many cloth trees called prasādana, which were adorned by being strewn and hung with precious divine cloths of various colors.
He also saw trees of cloth called “soothing,” from which hung precious celestial cloths of various colors.
rol mo'i shing dga' ba bskyed pa zhes bya ba/ lha rdzas las kyang lhag pa'i rol mo yid du 'ong ba'i sgra snyan pa 'byin pa mang po dang /
He saw many music trees called pramodana, which emitted the sounds of beautiful music from instruments superior to those of the devas.
He also saw trees of musical instruments called “pleasing,” which produced music more sweet and pleasant than that of the heavens.
spos kyi shing kun tu zhim pas brgyan pa zhes bya ba/ phyogs thams cad du thogs pa med par rnam pa thams cad du yid du 'ong ba'i spos kyi ngad 'byung ba mang po dag kyang yod par mthong /
He saw many perfume trees called samantaśubhavyūha, from which arose pleasing perfumes of every kind of pleasant aroma spreading freely in all directions.
He also saw trees of fragrance called “gracing everywhere,” which pervaded everywhere with all kinds of pleasing fragrances.

mtshe'u dang / lu ma dang / lteng ka dang / rdzing bu rin po che bdun gyi pha gus mtha' brtsigs pa/ phyogs bzhi nas rin po che'i them skas btsugs pa/ rin po che sna tshogs kyi khri 'phang dus dang mthun pa'i tsan dan gyi dri zhim pos bskus pas kun nas bskor ba/ gzhi rin po che'i rgyal po bai DUr+ya sngon po las legs par blangs pa/ 'dzam bu chu klung gi gser gyi bye ma bdal ba/ yan lag brgyad dang ldan pa'i chu lha rdzas kyi dri yid du 'ong ba can gyis yongs su gang ba/

There were springs, ponds, reservoirs, and pools that had balustrades made of the seven precious materials around them, with precious steps on all four sides, encircled by precious platforms perfumed with the pleasant aroma of yellow sandalwood, with perfectly laid bottoms made of precious blue beryl, the king of jewels, and which were spread with the sand of Jambu River gold and filled with aromatic divine water that had the eight qualities.

There were also cool lotus ponds, with steps made of bricks of seven precious substances arrayed on four sides, surrounded by benches of various jewels painted with sandalwood fragrance, set in ground made of blue lapis lazuli, the bottom covered with gold sand, the ponds filled with water pleasantly scented with celestial fragrance,

rin po che'i pad+mo dang / ut+pa la dang / ku mud dang / me tog pun da ri ka kha dog sna tshogs lha rdzas kyi bsung dang ldan pas chu kun nas yog pa/ bya bran sna tshogs kyi khyu lha rdzas las kyang 'das pa'i gzugs yid du 'ong ba dang ldan pa /sgra snyan pa 'byin cing brjod pas gang ba/ lha rdzas kyi rin po che sna tshogs kyi shing gi phreng ba legs par bkye bas yongs su bskor cing brgyan pa dang ldan pa/

Their waters were covered with the various colors and divine scents of precious lotuses, blue lotuses, night lotuses, and white lotuses; were filled with flocks of various birds, with beauty that transcended the divine, emitting beautiful sounds; and were beautified by being encircled with radiant trees made of various divine jewels.

the surface of the water covered with varicolored lotuses of heavenly scent and texture, the air around them filled with the songs of birds, more lovely than the heavens, all surrounded by rows of beautiful trees of various celestial treasures.

shing sna tshogs de dag gi drung thams cad du'ang / rin po che'i seng ge'i khri sna tshogs yid du 'ong ba'i gzugs dang ldan pa/ rin po che sna tshogs kyi rgyan bsam gyis mi khyab pa du mas brgyan pa/ lha rdzas kyi stan rin po che sna tshogs 'brel bar bting ba/ lha rdzas kyi spos dang / bdug spos kyi rnam pa thams cad kyis bdugs pa/ lha rdzas las kyang 'das pa'i dar rin po che mngon par dpyangs pa/ rin po che sna tshogs kyi bla re bkye ba/ rin po che sna tshogs dang / 'dzam bu chu klung gi gser gyi dra ba sna tshogs kun nas bres pa/ rin po che'i dril gyi dra ba yid du 'ong zhing snyan pa'i sgra 'byin pa mang pos brgyan pa/ 'khor du lha rdzas kyi rin po che'i stan brgya stong phrag du ma bting zhing bshams pa mthong ngo/ /

Arranged at the feet of all those trees of various jewels[1158] were precious lion thrones, with various beautiful forms, arrayed in inconceivable adornments of various jewels, adorned and spread with divine precious cushions,[1159] perfumed by all kinds of scents and incenses, hung with precious, beyond-divine ribbons, canopied by canopies of various jewels, covered by nets[1160] of Jambu River gold and various jewels, adorned by many[1161] precious beautiful nets of bells that emitted beautiful sounds, and accompanied by many hundreds of thousands[1162] of seats made of divine jewels.

At the foot of each of those treasure trees were arranged jewel lion seats of various pleasing forms, adorned with innumerable jewels of various kinds, spread with various precious celestial cloths, perfumed with incenses of all kinds of celestial fragrances, covered with canopies of various jewels hung with precious silks surpassing those of the heavens, enveloped in nets of gold adorned by various jewels, with circlets of bells giving forth pleasant sounds, surrounded by hundreds of thousands of celestial seats.
rin po che'i shing drung la lar ni seng ge'i khri rin po che'i pad+mo snying po can bshams pa mthong ngo/ /
He saw, arranged at the feet of some jewel trees, lion thrones with lotuses in their centers that were made of jewels;
At the foot of one precious tree he saw a lion seat in the calyx of a jewel lotus;
la lar ni seng ge'i khri nor bu rin po che spos kyi rgyal po'i pad+mos snying po byas pa bshams pa mthong ngo/ /
at the feet of some, lion thrones with lotuses in their centers that were made of the precious jewel king of perfumes;
at another, a lion seat in the calyx of a fragrant diamond lotus;
la lar ni seng ge'i khri rin po che'i rgyal po klu'i rgyan gyi pad+mos snying po byas pa bshams pa mthong ngo/ /
at the feet of some, lion thrones with lotuses in their centers that were made of the king of jewels array of nāgas;
at another, a lion seat in the calyx of a diamond lotus ornamented with dragons;
la lar ni seng ge'i khri nor bu rin po che'i rgyal po seng ge'i bya la'i pad+mos snying po byas pa bshams pa mthong ngo/ /
at the feet of some, lion thrones with lotuses in their centers that were made of the king of precious jewels lion’s trunk;[1163]
la lar ni seng ge'i khri rin po che'i rgyal po rnam par snang ba'i pad+mos snying po byas pa bshams pa mthong ngo/ /
at the feet of some, lion thrones with lotuses in their centers that were made of the king of precious jewels the sun;
at another, a lion seat in the calyx of a diamond lotus with clusters of jewel lions;
la lar ni seng ge'i khri rin po che'i rgyal po phyogs rnam par snang ba'i pad+mos snying po byas pa bshams pa mthong ngo/ /
at the feet of some, lion thrones with lotuses in their centers that were made of the king of precious jewels radiance;
at another, a lion seat in the calyx of a lotus of luminous jewels;
la lar ni seng ge'i khri rin po che'i rgyal po dbang po'i rdo rje'i pad+mos snying po byas pa bshams pa mthong ngo/ /
at the feet of some, lion thrones with lotuses in their centers that were made of the king of precious jewels Indra’s vajra;
at another, a lion seat in the calyx of a lotus of the finest diamonds;
la lar ni seng ge'i khri rin po che'i rgyal po 'gro ba'i yid du 'ong ba'i pad+mos snying po byas pa bshams pa mthong ngo/ /
at the feet of some, lion thrones with lotuses in their centers that were made of the king of precious jewels beauty of the world;
at another, a lion seat in the calyx of a lotus of world-illumining jewels;
rin po che'i shing drung la lar ni seng ge'i khri rin po che'i rgyal po mdog dkar po'i pad+mos snying po byas pa bshams pa mthong ngo/ /
and he saw, arranged at the feet of some jewel trees, lion thrones with lotuses in their centers that were made of the king of precious jewels white light.
at another, a lion seat in the calyx of a lotus of jewels of white light.
bza' shing gi ra ba de'i gzhi thams cad kyang rin po che sna tshogs kyis yongs su gang zhing / rgya mtsho chen po ltar rin po che'i gling gis yongs su gang ba mthong ngo; ;
He saw that the entire ground of that great park was covered with various jewels like an ocean covered by islands of jewels.
He saw that the ground of the whole park was scattered with various jewels, just as the ocean is scattered with jewel islands.
bai DUr+ya sngon po'i dam pas spras te/ rin po che thams cad kyis brgyan pa'i sa'i phyogs ka tsa lin da ltar reg na bde zhing 'jam yang / gom pa bor zhing bteg pa'i tshe/ mtho dman med pa
The earth, studded with blue lapis lazuli and inlaid with all kinds of jewels, was soft and pleasant to the touch, and would give way and spring back as one walked on it.
rdo rje rin po che'i mchog gi pad+mo dri yid du 'ong bar zhim zhing reg na bde ba'i sil ma kun tu bkram pa/
its surface was strewn with the petals[1167] of beautifully aromatic lotuses that were pleasant to the touch and made of diamond jewels;
The grounds were covered with diamond lilies, of pleasant texture and lovely scent.
ngang ngur dang / rma bya dang / khrung khrung dang / kun la dang / ka la ping+ka dang / ko ki la dang / dzi ban dzi ba ka sgra snyan cing yid du 'ong ba'i nga ro 'byin pa mang pos gang ba/
it was filled with ruddy shelducks,[1168] peacocks, cranes, snipes, avadavats, cuckoos,[1169] and partridges that emitted beautiful sounds;
The sweet sounds of the calls of various birds were heard,
lha rdzas kyi rin po che'i tsan dan gyi shing mang po'i nags tshal shin tu legs par 'grigs pas mdzes par brgyan pa/
it was adorned by perfectly formed forests of many divine, precious sandalwood trees;
and the park was graced with well-arrayed stands of heavenly precious sandalwood trees.
rin po che sna tshogs kyi pad+mo'i sprin gyi char dang / rin po che'i me tog sna tshogs mi zad pa'i char rgyun du 'bab pa/ 'bres pa'i nags tshal las kyang khyad par du 'phags pa/
there was a continuous rainfall from clouds of lotuses made of various jewels and a rain of various precious flowers; it was superior to Miśrakavana;
There were endless streams of jewel blossoms raining from clouds of various jewel flowers in a magnificent array surpassing the pleasure garden of Indra, chief of gods.
rin po che sna tshogs kyi khang bu brtsegs ma rgyan par bkod pa'i nang nas/ spos kyi rgyal po'i bdug spos rin thang med pa rtag tu 'thul zhing zhim pa/
there were kūṭāgāras made of various jewels arrayed as adornments from within which constantly emanated the unequaled[1170] aromas of the kings of perfumes;
There were well-spaced towers with various incomparably fragrant incenses always burning,
lha'i 'dun sa chos bzang po'i rgyan las kyang lhag pas brgyan pa/
it was a display superior to that of Sudharma, the meeting hall of the devas;
more magnificent than Indra’s hall of justice,
lha rdzas las kyang 'das pa'i rin po che'i dra ba sna tshogs kyis kun tu bres pa/
they were covered with nets of various jewels that were superior to divine jewels;
covered above with nets of various jewels surpassing those of the heavens,

mu tig rin po che'i me tog gi phreng ba dang / lda ldi kun nas bres pas rab tu brgyan pa/ rin po che'i dril bu rnam pa sna tshogs su rnam par bkye ba'i gser gyi dra ba 'bar bas kun nas dkrigs pa/ rol mo'i shing dang /
they were adorned by hanging bundles of pearls, jewels, and flowers;[1171] they were entirely adorned by shining gold nets arrayed with a variety of precious bells.
hung with garlands of pearl flowers spread all over with nets of shining gold arrayed with jewel bells.

rin po che'i ta la las dril bu'i dra ba rlung gis legs par bskyod pas yid du 'ong ba'i sgra snyan pa'i dbyangs 'byung ba dang ldan pa/ dbang sgyur gyi lha'i rgyal po'i lha mo dpe tshul shin tu bzang ba rnams kyis/ glu snyan pa'i sgra rab tu yid du 'ong ba blang ba/

Beautiful and pleasant music came from trees with a variety[1172] of musical instruments, precious palm trees, and nets of bells when they were stirred by the breeze. There arose the perfectly delightful sound of songs like those of the apsarases of the king of the Vaśavartin devas.
Trees of various musical instruments, jewel palm trees with nets of bells, played sweet music as they were stirred by the breeze, and the singing of goddesses was also heard.
lha rdzas kyi yid bzhin gyi gos kha dog sna tshogs kyi sprin gyi char rab tu 'bab pas rnam par mdzes pa/ rgya mtsho chen po ltar kha dog dang / mdog sna tshogs su ldan pas blta na gtang mi bra ba/

The park was beautified by a rain that fell from clouds of divine cloths, of various colors, that fulfilled all wishes. It resembled a vast ocean with a variety[1173] of colors and lusters so that one could not stop looking at it.
The park was splendidly adorned by rain from clouds of radiant celestial cloths, of infinite colors like the ocean, lovely to see.
khang pa brtsegs pa'i rin po che'i rgyan dang ldan pa brgya stong grangs med pas rab tu brgyan pa/ sum cu rtsa gsum gyi lha'i pho brang ltar blta na bzang ba/
It was adorned by countless hundreds of thousands of kūṭāgāras adorned with jewels.[1174] It was as beautiful to behold as the residence[1175] of Indra[1176] in Trāyastriṃśa.[1177]
He saw Sunlight Park adorned with hundreds of thousands of towers arrayed with inconceivable, innumerable jewels, beautiful as the castle of the god Indra.
rin po che sna tshogs rnam par phye bas rnam pa thams cad du brgyan pa'i gdugs shin tu legs pa rnam par bsgreng zhing bkram pas kun nas blta na mdzes pa/
It was adorned by an array of various jewels of every kind. There was the beautiful sight of an array of perfectly formed parasols standing erect.
It was adorned with arrays of all kinds of jewels, everywhere graced with arrays of beautifully formed parasols,
dbang po chen po'i 'jig rten ltar shin tu mdzes pa'i de'u sna tshogs kyis brgyan pa/
It was made beautiful by various pinnacles,[1178] like the realm of great Indra.
yid du 'ong ba'i 'od snang ba chen po rtag par 'byung ba/ tshangs pa chen po'i gzhal med khang ltar nor bu rin po che'i rgyal po 'gro ba'i yid du 'ong ba'i 'od kyis 'bar ba ste/
There shone constantly a great beautiful radiance of light. Like the divine palace of Mahābrahmā, it was radiant with the light of the kings of jewels that brought delight to beings.
always radiating pleasing light, like the abode of the god Brahma, shining with world-illumining light.

bza' shing gi ra ba chen po nyi ma'i mdog ces bya ba de/ dge slong ma seng ge rnam par bsgyings pa'i rdzu 'phrul gyi mthu stobs dang / byin gyi rlabs che zhing bsam gyis mi khyab pas/ 'jig rten gyi khams grangs med pa'i gnas su gyur pa'i nam mkha'i dbyings ltar yangs shing tshad med de/ rgya chen po dang ldan par mthong ngo/ /

That great park called Sūryaprabha, through the bhikṣuṇī Siṃhavijṛmbhitā’s great, inconceivable, miraculous abilities and attainment of power,[1179] was as vast, immense, and extensive as the expanse of the sky over countless world realms.
It was as vast as a space that holds innumerable worlds. Sudhana saw this Sunlight Park by the strength of the mystic power of the nun Sinhavijurmbhita.

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis/ de ltar yon tan tshad med pa bsam gyis mi khyab pa tshogs pa'i bza' shing gi ra ba'i rgyan byang chub sems dpa'i las kyi rnam par smin pas yongs su grub pa/ 'jig rten las 'das pa'i dge ba'i rtsa ba rgya chen po las skyes pa/ sangs rgyas la mchod cing / rim gror byas pa'i rgyu mthun pa bsam gyis mi khyab pa las byung ba/ 'jig rten gyi khams thams cad na yod pa'i dge ba'i rtsa ba ma lus pas mi 'phrogs pa/ chos kyi rang bzhin sgyu ma'i rnam pa lta bus grub pa/ dge ba'i bsod nams dri ma med pa rgya chen pos grub cing byung ba/ dge slong ma seng ge rnam par bsgyings pa'i sngon gyi spyod pa bzang po legs par byas pa dang / rgyu mthun pa'i stobs dang shugs kyis byung ba/ nyan thos dang / rang sangs rgyas thams cad dang thun mong ma yin pa/ mu stegs can dang; phas kyi rgol ba thams cad kyis mi 'phrogs pa/ bdud kyi lam yongs su rgyu ba thams cad kyis mi tshugs pa/ byis pa so so'i skye bo thams cad kyis bltar med par mthong ste

Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, saw in that way the displays in the park of aggregations of measureless, inconceivable qualities, which were accomplished through the ripening of a bodhisattva’s karma; which were born from vast, transcendent roots of merit that appeared as the natural result of inconceivable offering and service to buddhas; which all the roots of merit without exception in all worlds could not surpass; which were present as the illusory nature of phenomena; which originated from the ripening of the merit of vast, stainless virtue; which originated from the strength and power that is the natural result of the conduct perfectly accomplished in the past by the bhikṣuṇī Siṃhavijṛmbhitā; which could not be surpassed by all the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; which could not be destroyed by tīrthikas and opponents; which could not be harmed[1180] by any of the activities of the path of the māras; and which could not be seen at all[1181] by ordinary, foolish beings.

Sudhana looked all over and saw these magnificent adornments of the park, replete with infinite, inconceivable qualities, perfected by the maturation of the work of the enlightening being, born of vast supramundane roots of good, deriving from making offerings to inconceivably many buddhas, unsurpassed by all worldly goodness, sprung forth from the illusory nature of phenomena, composed of the results of extensive pure good works, without contamination, produced by the power deriving from the past virtuous actions of the nun Sinhavijurmbhita, unique, beyond the individually liberated, immune to the destructive influence of false teachers, imperceptible to maniacs and ignoramuses.

shing sna tshogs de dag gi drung gi seng ge'i khri chen po de dag la'ang / dge slong ma seng ge rnam par bsgyings pa lus shin tu mdzes pa/ spyod lam zhi ba/ dbang po zhi ba; yid zhi ba/ shin tu dben pa/ dbang po thul ba/ glang po ltar shin tu dul ba/ mtsho ltar shing gsal la rnyog pa med pa'i sems dang ldan pa/ rin po che'i rgyal po yid bzhin gyi nor bu ltar 'dod pa thams cad sgrub pa/ pad+mo la chus mi chags pa ltar 'jig rten gyi chos kyis ma gos pa/ seng ge ltar 'jigs pa dang / skyi g.ya'i ba med pa/ mi 'jigs pa rnam par dag pas ri'i dbang po chen po ltar mi sgul ba/ tshul khrims rnam par dag pas yid du 'ong ba'i spos kyi rgyal po ltar 'gro ba'i sems tshim par byed pa/ kha ba'i tsan dan ltar nyon mongs pa'i gdung ba rab tu zhi bar byed pa/ sman gyi rgyal po blta na bzang ba ltar 'gro ba thams cad kyi sdug bsngal rnam par zhi bar byed pa/ chu'i lha'i zhags pa ltar blta na don yod pa/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i 'od ltar lus dang sems kyi bag yangs bde ba bskyed pa/ tshangs pa chen po ltar 'dod chags dang / zhe sdang dang / gti mug gi kun nas ldang ba dang bral ba/ rin po che'i rgyal po nor bu chu 'dang ltar nyon mongs pas rnyog pa can du gyur pa'i sems can gyi sems rab tu par byed pa/ zhing gshin pa ltar dge ba'i rtsa ba rnam par 'phel bar byed pa 'dug par mthong ngo/ / 'khor gyi stan de dag la'ang 'khor sna tshogs 'khod par mthong ste/

He saw seated upon lion thrones at the feet of all those various precious trees the bhikṣuṇī Siṃhavijṛmbhitā surrounded by a great assembly.[1182] She had a beautiful body, the peaceful conduct of a mendicant,[1183] pacified senses,[1184] and a peaceful mind; she was perfectly self-controlled[1185] and had conquered her senses; she was as perfectly tamed as an elephant; her mind was as pure, clear, and unsullied as a lake; she fulfilled all wishes like a king of wish-fulfilling jewels; she was as unstained by worldly concerns as a lotus by water; she was as free of fear and trepidation as a lion; because of her perfectly pure confidence she was as unshakable as the great king of mountains; because of her pure discipline she brought delight to beings like the king of entrancing perfumes; like Himalayan sandalwood, she extinguished the burning of the kleśas; like the beautiful king of herbs, she brought an end to the sufferings of all beings; like the noose of Varuṇa, she was a beneficial sight;[1186] like the light from a tathāgata, she brought peace and happiness to body and mind; like Mahābrahmā, she was free from the arising of anger, desire, and ignorance; like the king of jewels that purifies water, she brought delight to the minds of beings that were turbid with kleśas; and like a fertile land, she multiplied the roots of merit. On the surrounding seats a diverse assembly was seated.

In all of those lion seats under the various precious trees he saw the nun Sinhavijurmbhita sitting, surrounded by a great company of followers, calm, composed, her senses and mind quiet, well controlled, her senses subdued, as restrained as an elephant, her mind pellucid and clear as a deep pool, granter of all desires like a wish-fulfilling jewel, unaffected by worldly things as a lotus is not clung to by water, fearless as a lion, with polished expertise, unshakable as a mountain, pure in conduct, soothing the minds of beings like intoxicating perfume, extinguishing the burning of afflictions like sandalwood from the snowy mountains, alleviating the pains of all sentient beings like the medicine “good to see,” beneficial to all who behold her, producing the physical and mental bliss of quiescence like the light of a buddha free from the ills and delusions of passion, clearing the minds of sentient beings polluted by afflictions like the water-purifying crystal, promoting the growth of roots of virtue like a good field. He saw her sitting in those seats, with various audiences in the surrounding seats.

'khor gyi stan la la la ni lha'i bu dbang po chen po la sogs pa gtsang ma'i gnas kyi ris su gtogs pa'i lha'i bu rnams 'khod cing / dge slong ma seng ge rnam par bsgyings pas/ chos kyi sgo rnam par thar pa mi zad pa yang dag par 'byed pa zhes bya ba yang dag par bstan pa mthong ngo/ /

He saw the bhikṣuṇī Siṃhavijṛmbhitā teaching the Dharma gateway called the categories of unceasing liberation to the deva Maheśvara and other inhabitants of the Śuddhāvāsa paradise who were seated upon some of the assembly seats.
In one setting he saw the nun surrounded by gods of the heaven of pure abodes, expounding a doctrine called unity with endless liberation;

'khor gyi stan la la la ni tshangs pa yid du 'ong ba la sogs pa tshangs pa'i ris su gtogs pa'i lha'i bu rnams 'khod cing / dge slong ma seng ge rnam par bsgyings pas/ dbyangs kyi dkyil 'khor rnam par dag pa gzhi kun nas 'byed pa zhes bya ba yang dag par bstan pa mthong ngo/ /

He saw the bhikṣuṇī Siṃhavijṛmbhitā teaching the pure realm of sound called the complete categories of the ground to the deva Rucirabrahmā and the other inhabitants of the Brahmakāyika paradise who were seated upon some of the assembly seats.
in another he saw her surrounded by gods of Brahma’s heaven, expounding a purity of the sphere of the voice called division of the universal ground;

'khor gyi stan la la la ni lha'i rgyal po dbang sgyur la sogs pa gzhan 'phrul dbang byed kyi lha'i bu/ lha'i bu mo'i 'khor dang bcas pa dag 'khod cing / dge slong ma seng ge rnam par bsgyings pas/ chos kyi sgo byang chub sems dpa'i bsam pa rnam par dag pa'i dbang gis rnam par brgyan pa zhes bya ba yang dag par bstan pa mthong ngo/ /

He saw the bhikṣuṇī Siṃhavijṛmbhitā teaching the Dharma gateway called the display of the power of the pure motivation of bodhisattvas to the deva king Vaśavartin and other inhabitants of the Paranirmitavaśavartin paradise who were seated upon some of the assembly seats.
in another he saw her surrounded by gods and goddesses of the heaven of control of others’ emanations, expounding a doctrine called array of powers of purification of mind of enlightening beings;

'khor gyi stan la la la ni lha'i rgyal po rab 'phrul dga' la sogs pa 'phrul dga'i lha'i bu/ lha'i bu mo'i 'khor dang bcas pa rnams 'khod cing / dge slong ma seng ge rnam par bsgyings pas/ chos kyi sgo chos thams cad dge bas rnam par brgyan pa zhes bya ba yang dag par bstan pa mthong ngo/ /

He saw the bhikṣuṇī Siṃhavijṛmbhitā teaching the Dharma gateway called the display of the goodness of all dharmas[1187] to the deva king Sunirmita and other devas and devīs of the Nirmāṇarati paradise who were seated upon some of the assembly seats.
in another he saw her surrounded by gods and goddesses of the heaven of enjoyable emanations, expounding a doctrine called pure array of all phenomena;

'khor gyi stan la la la ni lha'i rgyal po rab dga' ldan la sogs pa dga' ldan gyi ris su gtogs pa'i lha'i bu/ lha'i bu mo'i 'khor dang bcas pa rnams 'khod cing / dge slong ma seng+ge rnam par bsgyings pas/ chos kyi sgo rang gi sems kyi mdzod kyi klong zhes bya ba yang dag par bstan pa mthong ngo/ /

He saw the bhikṣuṇī Siṃhavijṛmbhitā teaching the Dharma gateway called the process of the treasure of one’s own mind to the deva king Saṃtuṣita and the other devas and devīs of the Tuṣita paradise who were seated upon some of the assembly seats.
in another he saw her surrounded by gods and goddesses of the heaven of satisfaction, expounding a doctrine called resorting to the treasury of one’s own mind;

'khor gyi stan la la la ni lha'i rgyal po rab mtshe ma la sogs pa lha'i bu/ lha'i bu mo'i 'khor dang bcas pa rnams 'khod cing / dge slong ma seng+ge rnam par bsgyings pas/ chos kyi sgo rgyan mtha' yas pa zhes bya ba yang dag par bstan pa mthong ngo/ /

He saw the bhikṣuṇī Siṃhavijṛmbhitā teaching the Dharma gateway called the infinite display to the deva king Suyāma and the other devas and devīs of the Yāma paradise who were seated upon some of the assembly seats.
in another he saw her surrounded by gods and goddesses of the heaven of timely portion, expounding a doctrine called endless array;

'khor gyi stan la la la ni lha'i rgyal po brgya byin la sogs pa sum cu rtsa gsum gyi ris su gtogs pa'i lha'i bu/ lha'i bu mo'i 'khor dang bcas pa rnams 'khod cing / dge slong ma seng+ge rnam par bsgyings bas/ chos kyi sgo skyo ba'i sgo zhes bya ba yang dag par bstan pa mthong ngo/ /

He saw the bhikṣuṇī Siṃhavijṛmbhitā teaching the Dharma gateway called the gateway to revulsion to the deva king Śakra and the other devas and devīs of the Trāyastriṃśa paradise who were seated upon some of the assembly seats.
in another he saw her surrounded by gods and goddesses of the thirty-three-fold heaven, expounding a doctrine called the method of rejecting;

'khor gyi stan la la la ni klu'i rgyal po gangs chen mtsho la sogs pa klu'i rgyal po 'od brgya pa dang / dga' bo dang / bsnyen dga' bo dang / yid du 'ong ba dang / shugs ldan dang / ma dros pa la sogs pa klu'i bu mo'i 'khor dang bcas pa/ klu'i byis pa'i 'khor dang bcas pa rnams 'khod cing / dge slong ma seng+ge rnam par bsgyings pas/ chos kyi sgo sangs rgyas kyi rdzu 'phrul dang yul gyi 'od kyi rgyan ces bya ba yang dag par bstan pa mthong ngo/ /

He saw the bhikṣuṇī Siṃhavijṛmbhitā teaching the Dharma gateway called the display of the light of miracles[1188] and the range of activity of the buddhas to the nāga king Sāgara and other nāga kings‍—Śataraśmin, Nanda and Upananda, Manasya, Airāvata, Anavatapta, and so on‍—with their nāga sons and nāga daughters who were seated upon some of the assembly seats.
in another he saw her surrounded by water spirits, nymphs, and sprites, expounding a doctrine called array of lights of the sphere of buddhas;
