f.d: [bcom pa ma lha'i bshes gnyen ma]
Chapter 28. Vasumitrā
Vasumitra
de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang / shes rab kyi snang ba chen po des sems snang bar gyur pa de/ thams cad mkhyen pa'i ye shes snang ba de la ni sems/
Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, with his mind illuminated by that great light of wisdom, focusing upon the light of omniscience,
His mind illumined by the lightning of great vision, meditating on the light of omniscience,

chos nyid kyi rang bzhin gyi stobs snang ba de la ni yang dag par rjes su lta/ sems can thams cad kyi skad rnam par dmigs pa'i mdzod kyi gzungs kyi tshul de ni brtan par byed/ de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi chos kyi 'khor lo yang dag par 'dzin pa'i gzungs kyi tshul de ni shin tu rgya che bar byed/

regarding the light of the power of the true nature, strengthening the way of retention that is the treasure of what was known from the voices of all beings, increasing the way of retention that possesses the Dharma wheels of all the tathāgatas,

observing the manifestation of power of essential nature, making firm the mnemonic command of the treasury of verbal communications of all beings, extending the mnemonic command to retain the cycles of teachings of all buddhas,

snying rje chen po 'gro ba thams cad kyi skyabs su gyur pa'i stobs de ni nye bar ston/ chos thams cad kyi tshul snang ba'i sgo nas yang dag par 'byung ba'i thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi shugs de la ni rab tu rtog/
supporting[1204] the power of the great compassion that is a refuge for all beings, realizing the strength of the omniscience that comes from the gateway of the light of the way of all Dharmas,
establishing the power of great compassion as a refuge for all sentient beings, examining the power of omniscience which is the source of the means of perceiving the principles of all laws,

chos kyi dbyings rgya chen po'i dkyil 'khor rgyas par 'gengs pa'i smon lam yongs su dag pa de'i rjes su ni 'brang / chos thams cad kyi phyogs snang bar byed pa'i ye shes kyi 'od de ni shin tu gsal bar byed/ chos thams cad kyi phyogs bcu'i 'jig rten gyi khams rnam par phye ba rgyas par 'gengs pa'i mngon par shes pa'i stobs de ni mngon par sgrub/ byang chub sems dpa'i lam dang dran pa thams cad nye bar blangs pas brtsams pa mthar dbyung ba'i smon lam de ni yongs su rdzogs par byed cing /

following the pure aspiration that pervades the domain of the vast realm of phenomena, shining with the light of wisdom that illuminates all the directions of phenomena, accomplishing the power of the higher knowledge that pervades the array of world realms in the ten directions of all phenomena, and fulfilling the aspirations of accomplishing undertaking all the practices, memories, and actions[1205] of the bodhisattvas,

following the purity of vows extending throughout the cosmos, clarifying the light of knowledge illumining all things, developing the power of mystic knowledge pervading all phenomena arraying the worlds of the ten directions, fulfilling the vow to remember, undertake, and accomplish all the deeds of enlightening beings,
mthar gyis yul bgrod dka' ba'i grong khyer rin po che'i rgyan gang na ba der phyin te/ bcom pa ma lha'i bshes gnyen ma yongs su tshol tshol ba dang /
eventually arrived at the city of Ratnavyūha in the land of Durga and searched for the courtesan Vasumitrā.
Sudhana made his way to the city of Ratnavyuha in the country of Durga, where he sought out Vasumitra.
de la bcom pa ma lha'i bshes gnyen gyi yon tan mngon par mi shes la/ ye shes kyi spyod yul gyi tshul la mi mkhas pa'i mi ji snyed pa de dag 'di snyam du sems te/
The people there who did not know the qualities of the courtesan Vasumitrā and lacked the knowledge of the scope of wisdom thought,
People there who did not know of Vasumitra’s virtues or the scope of her knowledge said to Sudhana,

mi 'di de ltar zhi zhing dul ba'i dbang po dang ldan la/ de ltar shes bzhin dang ldan te/ de ltar 'khrul pa med cing / de ltar yid 'khrug pa med la/ de ltar gnya' shing gang tsam du lta ste/ de ltar gnod pas mi tshugs shing / de ltar mtshan mar mi 'dzin la gzugs kyi rnam pa thams cad la g.yeng ba med ba'i mig dang ldan te/ yid la brel ba med cing / bsam pa zab la mngon par mdzes te/ rgya mtsho ltar 'dug cing sems mi nyams mi 'khrug pa de la/ bcom pa ma lha'i bshes gnyen mas ko ci zhig bya/

“What does such a man‍—who has pacified and controlled senses, who is mindful, who is unconfused, whose mind is not agitated, who keeps his gaze the length of a yoke before him, whose mind is not overcome by sensations, who is not fixated on external features, whose eyes are averted[1206] from dwelling on any physical form, whose mind is free of preoccupations, who is wise,[1207] who is like an ocean, whose mind is unshakable and without weakness‍—want with the courtesan Vasumitrā?

“What has someone like you—with senses so calm and subdued, so aware, so clear, without confusion or distraction, your gaze focused discreetly right before you, your mind not overwhelmed by sensations, not clinging to appearances, your eyes averted from involvement in all forms, your mind so cool and steady, your way of life profound, wise, oceanic, your mind free from agitation or despondency—what have you to do with Vasumitra?
'di lta bu dag ni 'dod chags la dga' ba med de/ sems phyin ci log dang ldan yang mi srid do/ /
Someone like this does not delight in sensual pleasures, and so his mind cannot possibly go astray.
You should not have any lust for her, your head should not be turned by her,
'di lta bu dag ni sdug cing gtsang ba'i 'du shes yongs su rgyu ba med de/ 'di lta bu dag ni 'dod pas 'khol kyang mi srid do/ /
Someone like this does not engage in impure[1208] thoughts. It is not possible that someone like this would be a slave to desire.
you should not have any such-impure thoughts, you should not be ravaged by such desires,
'di lta bu dag ni bud med kyi dpang du 'gyur ba med de/ 'di lta bu dag ni bdud kyi spyod yul la spyod kyang mi srid do/ /
Someone like this does not fall under the power of a woman. It is not possible that someone like this is engaged in the field of conduct of the māras.
you should not be under the power of a woman, you should not be so bewitched,
'di lta bu dag ni bdud kyi yul la chags pa med de/ 'di lta bu dag ni 'dod pa'i 'dam du bying yang mi srid do/ /
Someone like this does not dwell in the field of conduct of the māras. It is not possible that someone like this is sinking into the mud of desire.
you should not enter the realm of temptation, you should not sink into the mire of sensuality,
'di lta bu dag ni bdud kyi zhags pas bcings par 'gyur ba med de/ mi dgos pa byed kyang mi srid do snyam mo/ /
Someone like this is not bound by the noose of the māras. He is not someone who would do what should not be done.”
you should not be bound by the snares of the devil, you should not do what should not be done.”
gang yang bcom pa ma lha'i bshes gnyen ma'i yon tan gyi khyad par mngon par shes shing / ye shes kyi spyod yul mngon du gyur pa de dag ni 'di skad ces 'dzer te/
Those who did know the special qualities of the courtesan Vasumitrā and directly perceived wisdom’s range of conduct said to him,
Those who knew the excellence of the virtues of Vasumitra, however, and who were aware of the scope of her knowledge, said,
rigs kyi bu/ de ltar khyod bcom pa ma lha'i bshes gnyen ma la yongs su dri bar sems pa ni/ khyod kyang thob par bya ba legs par thob pa ste/ legs so/ / legs so/ /
“It is excellent, excellent, noble one, that you intend to ask questions of the courtesan Vasumitrā; you have perfectly obtained a good outcome.
“Good, good! You have really made gain if you ask about Vasumitra.

khyod ni nges par sangs rgyas su smon pa'o/ / khyod ni bdag nges par sems can thams cad kyi gnas su bsgyur bar 'dod pa'o/ / khyod ni nges par sems can thams cad kyi 'dod chags kyi zug rngu dbyung bar 'dod pa'o/ / khyod ni nges par sdug cing gtsang ba'i 'du shes rnam par gtor bar 'dod pa'o/ /

You are certainly aspiring to buddhahood. You are certainly wishing to become a refuge[1209] for all beings. You are certainly wishing to remove from all beings the pain of desire. You are certainly wishing to dispel conceptions of beauty and purity.

You surely seek buddhahood; you surely want to make yourself a refuge for all sentient beings; you surely want to extract the barbs of passion from all sentient beings; you surely want to transform the notion of purity.
rigs kyi bu/ 'di re/ bcom pa ma lha'i bshes gnyen ma ni grong khyer gyi lam gyi sum mdo'i byang phyogs logs shig na rang gi khyim na 'dug go /
“Noble one, the courtesan Vasumitrā is in her home, which is on the north side of the city’s junction of three streets.”
Vasumitra is in her house, north of the town square.”

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis tshig 'di thos nas/ dga' rangs te mgu zhing nyams bde la tshim zhing / yid bde ba skyes nas bcom pa ma lha'i bshes gnyen ma'i khyim gang na ba der phyin nas/ de'i khyim che zhing yangs la rin po che'i rab rim pa bcus bskor ba/ rin po che'i ta la'i phreng ba rim pa bcus kun nas bskor ba/ 'obs spos chus gang ba/ lha rdzas kyi rin po che'i pad+mo dang / ut+pa la dang / ku mud dang / me tog pun da ri kas chu yongs su khebs pa/ yan lag brgyad dang ldan pa'i chus yongs su gang ba/ gzhi gser gyi bye ma 'dal ba/ spos yid du 'ong ba dang 'dres pa'i chu dri zhim pos gang ba/ rin po che sil ma mang pos shin tu brgyan pa/ rim pa bcus kun nas bskor ba/

Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, on hearing those words, was filled with joy, delighted, elated, pleased, and happy. He went to the home of the courtesan Vasumitrā. He saw that her house was huge and vast and surrounded by ten successive precious walls. It was encircled by ten successive rows of precious palm trees. It was encircled by ten successive moats filled with water and covered with divine, precious red lotuses, blue lotuses, night lotuses, and white lotuses; they were filled with water that possessed the eight good qualities; they had bottoms that were covered with gold dust; they were filled with aromatic water mixed with beautiful scents; and they were adorned by numerous precious fences.[1210]

Hearing this, Sudhana was delighted. He went to Vasumitra’s house and saw that it was surrounded by ten jewel walls, ten circles of jewel trees, and ten moats filled with fragrant water covered by celestial jewel lotuses of various colors, with gold sand spread on the bottom, the rippling waters producing an intoxicating fragrance, the banks adorned by many jewels.

rin po che thams cad las byas pa'i khang pa dang / gzhal med khang dang / khang pa brtsegs pas rnam par dkrigs shing / ba gam dang / rta babs dang / skar khung gi shar bu dang / zla gam dang / seng ge'i shing thags dang / snang ba'i rgyal mtshan la sogs pa/ rin po che sna tshogs kyi 'od kyis 'bar ba/

He saw well-arranged buildings, palaces, kūṭāgāras made from every jewel with high[1211] pinnacles, toraṇas, round windows, lattices, crescents, pavilions, shining banners, and so on, brilliant with various jewels.
The house had well-arranged apartments and towers made of all kinds of precious substances; it had high arched doorways and circular windows, draped with nets and blazing with jewels.

rin po che rnam pa sna tshogs grangs med pa'i 'byung gnas kyis brgyan pa/ rin po che'i dgar bai DUr+ya sa spras pa'i g.yi dang ldan pa/ lha rdzas kyi spos zhim po thams cad kyis 'khor thams cad nas bdugs shing bsangs pa/ a ga ru nag po mchog gi bdug spos kyis dri zhim par bdugs pa; spos kyi byugs pas 'khor kun nas byugs pa/ rin po che sna tshogs kyi lan kan gyis rtsig ngos kun du bres pa/ steng 'dzam bu chu klung gi gser gyi dra ba rin po che sna tshogs kyis rab tu spras pas kun nas bkab pa/

Her house was beautified by walls[1212] of countless various jewels. Its floor was formed of jewels inlaid with beryls. Its environs were perfumed by every aromatic divine incense. It was perfumed by the aroma of supreme black agarwood incense. Its environs were anointed with unguents. Rooftop railings made of various jewels adorned the walls. It was covered above by nets of Jambu River gold inlaid with various jewels.

It was adorned with fences of countless various jewels, and its base was composed of masses of jewels studded with lapis lazuli. It was perfumed with all kinds of fragrant oils. The walls were studded with all kinds of jewels, and the roof was inland with various gems and covered with a gold net.

gser gyi dril gyi dra ba brgya stong rlung gis bskyod cing 'khrol ba'i sgra yid du 'ong zhing snyan pa 'byung ba/ rin po che thams cad kyi me tog gi sprin sil ma kun tu bkram pas rin po che'i me tog gi rgyan dang ldan pa/

A hundred thousand networks of hundreds of golden bells were ringing as they were moved by the breeze, emitting a pleasant, beautiful sound. It was adorned by precious flowers scattered and dispersed[1213] from clouds of flowers made from every jewel.
A hundred thousand webs of gold bells gave off sweet, pleasant sounds as they rustled in the breeze. The house was adorned with sprays of jewel flowers from clouds of flowers of all kinds of jewels.

rin po che sna tshogs thams cad kyi rgyal mtshan bsgreng bas sgo shin tu brgyan pa/ nor bu rin po che sna tshogs kyi 'od kyi dra ba snang ba mu med par brjod du yod pa/ rin po che byu ru'i sdong po dang / rdo rje dang / man shel la sogs pa'i gter brgya stong kun gyis shes pa phun sum tshogs pas mdzod mi zad pa dang ldan pa/ bza' shing gi ra ba chen po bcus brgyan pa mthong ste/

The gateways were adorned by erected multicolored[1214] banners made of all precious materials. The light from the brilliant shining of various precious jewels shone outward without limit. There was an endless treasure of a perfect multitude[1215] of hundreds of thousands of precious trees of coral, diamonds, crystal, and so on,[1216] and it was beautified by ten parks.

The doors were decorated with multicolored banners of all kinds of jewels. The light of lamps of various jewels shone to an endless distance. The house had diamond beams made from the limbs of gigantic brilliant jewel trees, and it was an inexhaustible treasury of hundreds and thousands of riches in full view; it was also adorned with ten large gardens set around it.

de na bcom pa ma lha'i bshes gnyen ma/ gzugs mdzes shing bzang la blta na sdug pa/ gya nom pa'i kha dog dam pa rgyas pa dang ldan pa/ gser gyi kha dog ltar 'dug pa'i mdog can/ skra mthon mthing du 'dug pa/ lus kyi yan lag dang / nying lag tshul dang 'dra bar rnam par grub pa/ 'dod pa'i khams kyi lha dang / mi thams cad las 'phags pa'i kha dog dang / gzugs dang / dbyibs mdzes pa dang ldan pa/ tshangs pa las kyang 'das pa'i dbyangs kyi yan lag dang ldan pa/

Sudhana saw there the courtesan Vasumitrā, who was beautiful, attractive, and delightful to see. She was endowed with a magnificent, perfect color. She had golden skin and deep black[1217] hair. Her limbs and smaller features were all perfectly formed. She had a beautiful color, form, and shape that were superior to those of all humans and devas of the desire realm. The aspects of her voice were superior to those of Brahmā.

There he saw Vasumitra, who was beautiful, with golden skin and black hair, her limbs and body well proportioned, more beautiful in form than all celestial and human beings in the realm of desire, her voice finer even than that of the god Brahma.

sems can thams cad kyi sgra skad kyi tshul la mkhas pa/ rgyan thams cad dang ldan zhing yid du 'ong ba'i dbyangs can/ rnam par thar pa yi ge'i 'khor lo'i rgyan la mkhas pa dang ldan pa/ bzo dang gtsug lag thams cad la mkhas par byung ba/ chos kyi ye shes sgyu ma la mkhas par bslabs pa/ byang chub sems dpa'i thabs dang tshul rnam pa thams cad du thob pa/ rin po che'i lhab lhub sna tshogs kyis rnam par brgyan pa'i lus yid du 'ong ba dang ldan pa/ rin po che thams cad las byas pa'i dra ba 'od shin tu gsal bas lus rab tu brgyan pa/ lha rdzas kyi nor bu rin po che'i rgyan dang / lhab lhub grangs med pas rab tu brgyan pas lus shin tu 'bar ba/

She was skilled in the languages of all beings. She had a beautiful voice that had the array of all sounds.[1218] She possessed the skill of the liberation called the array of the wheel of words. She had become skilled in all arts and treatises. She had trained to become wise in illusions through Dharma wisdom. She had attained all the methods and ways of the bodhisattvas. She had a beautiful body adorned by various kinds of precious jewelry. Her body was adorned by a brightly shining network of all jewels. Her body shone brightly, being adorned by an array of jewelry made of countless divine precious jewels.

She knew the language of all beings; she had a pleasant voice that could pronounce any sound, and was skilled in freedom of phonetic organization. She was well versed in all arts and sciences, she had learned to use the magic of true knowledge, and she had mastered all aspects of the expedient means of enlightening beings. Her beautiful body was decorated with assorted jewelry, draped with a radiant mesh made of all kinds of precious substances, shining with an array of countless celestial jewel ornaments.

nor bu rin po che dam pa yid bzhin gyi rgyal po'i cod pan thogs pa/ rin bo che bai DUr+ya'i phreng ba mdo zungs rdo rje rin po che sna tshogs dang / nor bu rin po che seng ge mdzes pa sna tshogs bkye ba mgul na thogs pa/

She wore tied upon her head a king of wish-fulfilling, supreme, precious jewels. She wore at her throat a string of beryl jewels with its middle adorned by diamonds, a multicolored beautiful lion, and precious jewels.
She wore a tiara of large wish-fulfilling gems, her waist was adorned with diamonds, and she had a lapis lazuli necklace on.
dge ba'i rtsa ba spyad pa la bskal pa mthun pa dang / smon lam gcig pa'i 'khor mang po gzhan gyis mi phyed cing yid du 'ong ba dang ldan pa/
She had a beautiful assembly of followers that could not be divided, that had a single aspiration and a similar share of the practice of the roots of merit.
She had a large, attractive retinue, all with the same virtues, the same practice, and the same vow.
bsod nams dang / ye shes kyi tshogs chen po'i gter mi zad pa'i mdzod dang ldan pa 'dug pa mthong ste/
She possessed an inexhaustible treasury of the treasure of the great accumulations of merit and wisdom.
She was an inexhaustible treasury of goodness and knowledge.

des khyim de dag thams cad dang / rin po che'i gnas dang / gzhal med khang gi rgyan de dag thams cad kyang rang gi lus las byung ba'i 'od dga' bar byed pa/ lus bde ba dang sim pa skyed pa/ sems khong nas dga' bar byed pas gsal zhing snang bar byas pa mthong ngo/ /

Sudhana saw that all those buildings, the entire array of precious dwellings and palaces, were illuminated and made bright by the light that came from her body, which caused delight, physical pleasure and bliss, and joy and happiness in the mind.
He also saw the whole house, with all its jeweled apartments and furnishings lit up by the lovely, refreshing, pleasant, blissful, enrapturing light that emanated from her body.
de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis/ bcom pa ma lha'i bshes gnyen ma'i rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te mdun du 'dug nas thal mo sbyar te 'di skad ces smras so/ /
Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, bowed his head to the feet of the courtesan Vasumitrā, stood before her with hands placed together in homage, and said,
Sudhana went up to Vasumitra, paid his respects, and said,

'phags ma/ bdag gis bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed na/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bgyi ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bgyi ba ma 'tshal te/ 'phags ma ni/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams la gdams ngag dang / rjes su bstan pa mdzad do zhes bdag gis thos na/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bgyi ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bgyi ba 'phags mas bdag la bstan du gsol/

“Āryā, I have developed the aspiration for the highest, complete enlightenment, but I do not know how bodhisattvas should train in bodhisattva conduct and in what way they should practice it. Āryā, I have heard that you give instruction and teachings to bodhisattvas! I pray that you explain to me how bodhisattvas should train in bodhisattva conduct and how they should practice it!”

“Noble one, I have set my mind on supreme perfect enlightenment, but I do not know how to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings. I hear that you give enlightening beings instructions, and I hope you will tell me how an enlightening being is to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings.”
des smras pa/ rigs kyi bu/ kho mos ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa 'dod chags dang bral ba'i mthar phyin pa zhes bya ba thob ste//
Vasumitrā said, “Noble one, I have attained the bodhisattva liberation called the complete attainment of freedom from desire.
She said, “I have attained an enlightening liberation called ‘ultimately dispassionate.’

rigs kyi bu/ de ltar kho mo ni lha rnams la lha mo'i gzugs dang / /ba dog dang / dbyibs dang / chu zheng las kyang lhag par kha dog gsal ba dang / rnam par dag pas ci la mos pa bzhin du snang par byed do/ / de bzhin du klu dang / gnod sbyin dang / dri za dang / lha ma yin dang / nam mkha' lding dang / mi'am ci dang / lto 'phye chen po dang / mi dang / mi ma yin pa rnams la yang bud med kyi gzugs dang / kha dog dang / dbyibs dang / chu zheng lhag par 'od gsal zhing rnam par dag pas ci la mos pa bzhin du snang bar byed do/ /

“Noble one, in this way I appear to the devas in accordance with their wishes in the form, color, shape, and size of an apsaras with a brighter and purer color. In the same way, I appear in accordance with their wishes in a female form, color, shape, and size with a brighter and purer color to the nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, and nonhumans.

To gods, in accord with their inclinations and interests, I appear in the form of a goddess of surpassing splendor and perfection; and to all other types of beings I accordingly appear in the form of a female of their species, of surpassing splendor and perfection.

sems can gang 'dod chags kyis kun nas 'khor ba'i sems dang ldan pa dag kho mo'i drung du 'ongs na yang / de dag thams cad la kho mo ni 'dod chags dang bral bar 'gyur ba'i phyir chos ston te/ de dag gis chos de thos nas kyang 'dod chags dang bral ba thob par 'gyur ro/ / byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin chags pa med pa zhes bya ba yang rab tu 'thob bo/ /

“When beings whose minds are encircled by desire come before me, I teach all of them the Dharma so that they will become free from desire. When they hear the Dharma, they attain freedom from desire. They attain the bodhisattva samādhi called the realm[1219] of nonattachment.

And all who come to me with minds full of passion, I teach them so that they become free of passion. Those who have heard my teaching and attain dispassion achieve an enlightening concentration called ‘realm of nonattachment.’
la la ni kho mo mthong ma thag tu 'dod chags dang bral bar 'gyur te/ byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin dga' ba dang ldan pa zhes bya ba yang rab tu 'thob bo/ /
Some become free from desire the instant they see me, and they attain the bodhisattva samādhi called joyfulness.
“Some attain dispassion as soon as they see me, and achieve an enlightening concentration called ‘delight in joy.’
la la ni gtam byas pa tsam gyis 'dod chags dang bral ba thob par 'gyur te/ byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin chags pa med pa'i dbyangs zhes bya ba yang rab tu 'thob bo/ /
Some attain dispassion merely by talking with me, and achieve an enlightening concentration called ‘treasury of unimpeded sound.’

la la ni lag nas bzung ba tsam gyis 'dod chags dang bral ba thob bar 'gyur te/ byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin sangs rgyas kyi zhing thams cad du rjes su 'gro zhing gnas pa zhes bya ba yang rab tu 'thob bo/ /
Some become free from desire when they hold my hand, and they attain the bodhisattva samādhi called going to and residing in all the buddha realms.
Some attain dispassion just by holding my hand, and achieve an enlightening concentration called ‘basis of going to all buddha-lands.’
la la ni gcig tu 'grogs pa tsam gyis 'dod chags dang bral ba thob par 'gyur te/ byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin bral bas snang ba zhes bya ba yang rab tu 'thob bo/ /
Some become free from desire when they are alone in my company, and they attain the bodhisattva samādhi called the light of detachment.
Some attain dispassion just by staying with me, and achieve an enlightening concentration called ‘light of freedom from bondage.’
la la ni bltas pa tsam gyis/ 'dod chags dang bral ba thob par 'gyur te/ byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin rab tu zhi ba'i rnam par brgyan ces bya ba yang rab tu 'thob bo/ /
Some become free from desire just by gazing upon me, and they attain the bodhisattva samādhi called the display of the form of peace.
Some attain dispassion just by gazing at me, and achieve an enlightening concentration called ‘tranquil expression.’
la la ni glal ba tsam gyis 'dod chags dang bral ba thob par 'gyur te/ byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin phas kyi rgol ba rnam par 'thor ba zhes bya ba yang rab tu 'thob bo/ /
Some become free from desire just by yawning, and they attain the bodhisattva samādhi called the disarraying of adversaries.
la la ni mig btsums pa tsam gyis 'dod chags dang bral ba thob par 'gyur te/ byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin sangs rgyas kyi yul snang ba zhes bya ba yang rab tu 'thob bo/ /
Some become free from desire just by closing their eyes, and they attain the bodhisattva samādhi called the light of the buddha domains.

la la ni pang du khyud pa tsam gyis 'dod chags dang bral ba thob par 'gyur te/ byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin 'gro ba thams cad yongs su sdud cing mi gtong ba'i snying po zhes bya ba yang rab tu 'thob bo/ /
Some become free from desire just by embracing me, and they attain the bodhisattva samādhi called the essence of gathering and not abandoning all beings.
Some attain dispassion just by embracing me, and achieve an enlightening concentration called ‘womb receiving all sentient beings without rejection.’

la la ni 'o byas pa tsam gyis 'dod chags dang bral ba thob par 'gyur te/ byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin 'gro ba thams cad bsod nams kyi mdzod la reg par byed pa zhes bya ba yang rab tu 'thob bo/ /
Some become free from desire just by kissing me, and they attain the bodhisattva samādhi called touching the treasure of the merit of all beings.
Some attain dispassion just by kissing me, and achieve an enlightening concentration called ‘contact with the treasury of virtue of all beings.’

de ltar kho mo ni sems can gang ji snyed cig kho mo'i drung du 'ong ba de dag thams cad kyang / byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa 'dod chags dang bral ba'i mthar phyin pa/ thams cad mkhyen pa'i sa chags pa med pa la mngon du gyur pa 'di nyid la rab tu 'god do/ /

In that way, I establish all the beings who come to me in the bodhisattva liberation called the complete attainment of freedom from desire and the manifestation of the attachment-free level of omniscience.”
All those who come to me I establish in this enlightening liberation of ultimate dispassion, on the brink of the stage of unimpeded omniscience.”
smras pa/ 'phags ma khyod de lta bu'i phun sum tshogs pa dang ldan pa de/ khyod kyis dge ba'i rtsa ba ni gang du bskyed/ 'phrin las ni ji lta bu zhig bzhugs/
Sudhana asked, “Āryā, what roots of merit did you develop? What kinds of activities did you accumulate so that you have attained this kind of perfection?”
Sudhana asked her, “Where did you plant roots of virtue, and what kind of deeds did you accumulate, that you got to be this way?”

smras pa/ rigs kyi bu/ kho mos dran na 'das pa'i dus shig na/ de bzhin gshegs pa dgra bcom pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas mkhyen pa dang zhabs su ldan pa/ bde bar gshegs pa/ 'jig rten mkhyen pa/ bla na med par skyes bu 'dul ba'i kha lo sgyur ba/ lha dang mi'i ston pa sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das shin tu mtho bar gshegs pa zhes bya ba 'jig rten du byung ste/

Vasumitrā replied, “Noble one, I remember that in a past time, there had appeared in the world a tathāgata, an arhat, a samyaksaṃbuddha, one with wisdom and conduct,[1220] a sugata, one who knows the world’s beings, an unsurpassable guide who tames beings, a teacher of devas and humans, a buddha, a bhagavat named Atyuccagāmin.
She replied, “I recall that in a past age a buddha named Reaching the Heights appeared in the world.

de bzhin gshegs pa shin tu mtho bar gshegs pa de/ sems can rnams la thugs brtse ba'i sku don du/ rgyal po'i gnas sgo bzang po zhes bya bar gshegs nas/ sgo'i them pa la zhabs kyis non pa'i tshe/ grong khyer de thams cad kyang rab tu g.yos nas/ yangs shing rgya che la/ rin po che du ma las byas par yongs su grub par gyur te/ steng gi bar snang yang rin po che mang po'i 'od kyis rnam par brgyan pa dang / rin po che'i me tog sna tshogs kyis yongs su gang ba dang / lha rdzas kyi rol mo sna tshogs kyi sgra rab tu 'byung ba dang / lha'i lus kyi sprin tshad med par rgya che bas khebs par gyur to/ /

“The Tathāgata Atyuccagāmin, because of his love for beings, went to the capital city named Sumukhā. When he placed his foot upon the threshold of its gateway, the entire city shook and became huge, vast, and made of many jewels. In the sky above, there was the light of a display of many jewels; it was filled with various precious flowers, emitted the sound of various divine musical instruments, and was pervaded by vast, measureless clouds of deva bodies.

When the buddha went to the royal capital out of compassion for the people, as he crossed the threshold the whole city quaked and appeared to-be vastly extended and made of jewels, adorned with the luster of many jewels, strewn with flowers of various jewels. A variety of celestial musical instruments played, and the sky appeared covered by high, immeasurable clouds of celestial beings.

rigs kyi bu/ kho mo yang de'i tshe/ tshong dpon gyi chung ma zhig tu gyur te/ blo gros bzang mo zhes bya'o/ / de nas kho mo cho 'phrul gyis yang dag par bskul nas/ khyim thab dang lhan cig tu dong dong ste/ de bzhin gshegs pa grong bar gyi srang du gshegs pa la dad pa rgya chen po skyes te/ kho mos rin po che'i dril bu gcig cig phul lo/ /

“Noble one, at that time, I was the wife of a head merchant, and my name was Sumati. Inspired by the miracles of the Buddha,[1221] my spouse and I ran and came to the Tathāgata in a street in the middle of the city. Developing a fast faith, I offered to him one precious bell.[1222]
At that time I was the wife of a grandee. Impelled by the miracle of the buddha, I went with my husband in a state of exalted serenity and presented a coin to the buddha on the street.

de'i tshe 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pa yang / bcom ldan 'das de bzhin gshegs pa shin tu mtho bar gshegs pa'i zham 'bring na 'dug ste/ des kho mo bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed do/ /
“At that time, Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta was an attendant of the Bhagavat, the Tathāgata Atyuccagāmin. Through him I developed the aspiration to the highest, complete enlightenment.
At that time Manjushri was an attendant of that buddha; it was by him that I was inspired to seek supreme perfect enlightenment.

rigs kyi bu/ kho mos byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa 'dod chags dang bral ba'i mthar phyin pa 'di shes par zad na/ kho mos byang chub sems dpa'i thabs dang / ye shes mtha' yas pa la gnas pa/ bsod nams rgya che zhing yangs pa'i mdzod dang ldan pa/ ye shes kyi yul la thub pa med pa de dag gi spyod pa shes pa'am/ yon tan brjod par nus re skan/

“Noble one, I know only this bodhisattva liberation called the complete attainment of freedom from desire. How could I know the conduct or describe the qualities of those bodhisattvas[1223] who dwell in infinite method and wisdom, who have a vast, immense treasure of merit, and who are invincible in their scope of wisdom?

“I know this enlightening liberation of ultimate dispassion, but how can I know the practice or tell the virtues of the enlightening beings who are endowed with the skill of endless means and knowledge, who are vast, inexhaustible treasuries of good, who are in the realm of invincible knowledge?

song / rigs kyi bu/ lho phyogs kyi rgyud 'di nyid na/ grong khyer dge ba'i pha rol tu phyin pa zhes bya ba yod de/ de na khyim bdag nan khugs zhes bya ba/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i mchod rten tsan dan gyi khri 'phang can la mchod pa byed pa zhig 'dug gi /de'i gan du song la/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bya ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bya ba dris shig/

“Depart, noble one. In this southern region there is a city called Śubhapāraṃgama. There dwells a householder by the name of Veṣṭhila who makes offerings to a sandalwood chair that is a tathāgata shrine. Go to him and ask him, ‘How should a bodhisattva train in bodhisattva conduct? How should a bodhisattva practice it?’ ”

“South of here is a city called Shubhaparamgama, where a householder named Veshthila is presenting offerings to the shrine of the buddha Sandalwood Throne. Go ask him how to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings.”

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis/ bcom pa ma lha'i bshes gnyen ma'i rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te/ bcom pa ma lha'i bshes gnyen ma la lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas/ yang dang yang bltas te/ bcom pa ma lha'i bshes gnyen ma'i drung nas song ngo/ /

Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, bowed his head to the feet of the courtesan Vasumitrā, circumambulated the courtesan Vasumitrā many hundreds of thousands of times, keeping her to his right, and, looking back again and again, departed from the courtesan Vasumitrā.
So Sudhana paid his respects to Vasumitra and left.
[khyim bdag nan khugs]
Chapter 29. Veṣṭhila
Veshthila

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis/ grong khyer dge ba'i pha rol tu phyin par khyim bdag nan khugs kyi khyim gang na ba der phyin nas/ khyim bdag nan khugs kyi rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te/ mdun du 'dug nas thal mo sbyar te 'di skad ces smras so/ /
Then Sudhana went to the town of Śubhapāraṃgama and approached the householder Veṣṭhila. He bowed his head to his feet, stood before him, and, with his hands placed together in homage, said,
Then Sudhana went to Veshthila’s house in the city of Shubhaparamgama. Paying his respects to the householder, he said,

'phags pa/ bdag gis bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed na ji ltar byang chub sems dpas/ byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bgyi ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bgyi ba ma 'tshal te/
“Ārya, I have developed the aspiration for the highest, complete enlightenment, but I do not know how bodhisattvas should train in bodhisattva conduct and in what way they should practice it.
“Noble one, I have set my mind on supreme perfect enlightenment, but I do not know how to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings.

'phags pa ni byang chub sems dpa' rnams la gdams ngag dang / rjes su bstan pa mdzad do zhes bdag gis thos na/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bgyi ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bgyi ba 'phags pas bdag la bshad du gsol/ /
“Ārya, I have heard that you give instruction and teachings to bodhisattvas! Explain to me how bodhisattvas should train in bodhisattva conduct and how they should practice it!”
I hear that you give enlightening beings instruction; please tell me how to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings.”
des smras pa/ rigs kyi bu/ kho bo ni byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa yongs su mi zad pa thob pa ste/
Veṣṭhila said, “Noble one, I have attained the bodhisattva liberation called the attainment of the summit of inexhaustibility.
Veshthila said, “I have attained an enlightening liberation called ‘not ultimately exhausted.’

“Noble one, from my mind’s viewpoint, a tathāgata has not passed into nirvāṇa, does not pass into nirvāṇa, and will not pass into nirvāṇa in any world other than as a way to bring beings who are to be guided under his control, not as a way to enter truly complete nirvāṇa.
To my way of thinking, no buddha in any world ever has, does, or will become finally extinct, except as a docetic device.

rigs kyi bu/ de ltar kho bo ni de bzhin gshegs pa'i mchod rten tsan dan gyi khri 'phang gi sgo 'byed pa ste/ kho bo mchod rten gyi sgo 'byed 'byed pas/ byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin/ sangs rgyas kyi rigs mi zad pa'i rgyan ces bya ba thob bo/ /

“Noble one, in that way, when I opened the door of the sandalwood-throne shrine of the Tathāgata, I attained, by opening the door of the shrine, the bodhisattva samādhi called the display of the unceasing family of the buddhas.
When I opened the door of the shrine of the buddha Sandalwood Throne, I attained an enlightening concentration called ‘manifestation of the endless lineage of buddhas.’
rigs kyi bu/ kho bo ni ting nge 'dzin 'di nyid la sems kyi skad cig skad cig tu mnyam par gzhog ste/ sems kyi skad cig thams cad la'ang khyad par gyi rnam pa du ma rab tu 'thob bo/ /
“Noble one, in each instant of mind I rest in this samādhi, and I attain many special features.”
I enter this concentration in each mental moment, and every moment understand many kinds of excellence.”
smras pa/ 'phags pa/ ting nge 'dzin de'i yul ji lta bu zhig mchis/
Sudhana asked, “Ārya, what is the scope of that samādhi?”
Sudhana asked, “What is the sphere of this concentration?”

smras pa/ rigs kyi bu; kho bo ni ting nge 'dzin 'di la snyoms par zhugs pa'i tshe/ 'jig rten gyi khams kyi rgyud 'di sangs rgyas gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa/ bsod skyabs la sogs pa de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad dang /

Veṣṭhila replied, “Noble one, when I am resting in this samādhi, there appear to me all the tathāgatas, such as Kāśyapa, in a continuous succession of one buddha after another within the lineage of this world: all the tathāgatas such as
Veshthila replied, “When I am in this concentration, all the successive buddhas of this world-system—beginning with Kashyapa,

gser thub dang / log par dad sel dang / thams cad mnga' ba dang / gtsug tor can dang / rnam par gzigs dang / rgyal dang / rdzogs mdzad dang / grags mchog dang / pad+mo'i bla la sogs pa/ de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyang /
Kanakamuni, Krakucchanda, Viśvabhuk, Śikhin, Vipaśyin, Tiṣya, Puṣya, Yaśottara, and Padmottara.
Kanakamuni, Krakucchanda, Vishvabhuj, Shikhin, Vipashyin, Tishya, Pushya, Yashottara, and Padmottara—appear to me.
sangs rgyas mthong ba'i mtshams 'brel bas/ sangs rgyas gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa rgyun mi 'chad pa'i tshul gyis mngon sum du mthong ste/ sems kyi skad cig gcig la sangs rgyas brgya'ang mthong ngo/ /
I see in the consecutive appearances of the buddhas the unceasing succession of one buddha after another, a hundred buddhas in one instant of mind.
In the continuity of vision of buddhas, by the continuity of the succession of buddhas, in one mental moment I see a hundred buddhas;

de'i 'og ma'i sems kyis sangs rgyas stong yang mthong ngo/ / de'i 'og ma'i sems kyis sangs rgyas brgya phrag stong yang mthong ngo/ / de bzhin du sangs rgyas bye ba dang / sangs rgyas bye ba phrag brgya dang / sangs rgyas bye ba phrag stong dang / sangs rgyas bye ba brgya phrag stong dang / sangs rgyas bye ba khrag khrig dang / sangs rgyas bye ba dung phyur dang / sangs rgyas bye ba thams cad dang / sangs rgyas bye ba khrag khrig dang /

In the next instant of mind I perceive a thousand buddhas. In the next instant of mind I perceive a hundred thousand buddhas. In the same way I see ten million buddhas, a thousand million[1224] buddhas, ten thousand million[1225] buddhas, a million million buddhas,[1226] ten million billion buddhas,[1227] ten million million billion[1228] buddhas, a hundred thousand million billion[1229] buddhas, and ten million million billion[1230] buddhas, and so on,
in the next moment of awareness I find a thousand buddhas, then a hundred thousand buddhas, a million buddhas, a hundred million, a billion, a trillion, a quadrillion, a quintillion;

de'i 'og ma'i sems kyis sangs rgyas 'byung ba gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa/ brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa dag kyang mthong ngo/ / de'i 'og ma'i sems kyis de bzhin gshegs pa 'dzam bu'i gling gi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyang mthong ngo/ / de'i 'og ma'i sems kyis de bzhin gshegs pa sangs rgyas kyi zhing brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa'i bar gyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyang mthong ste/

until in a subsequent moment of mind I perceive an inexpressible number of inexpressible numbers of buddhas appearing in succession. In the next instant of mind I see tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms in Jambudvīpa. In the next instant of mind I see tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms in an inexpressible number of inexpressible numbers of buddha realms.
I immediately become aware of the succession of appearance of untold numbers of buddhas, of as many buddhas as atoms in the continent, as many as atoms in untold buddha-lands.

de bzhin gshegs pa de dag gis thugs dang po bskyed pa'i tshogs gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa la'ang 'jug go / thugs dang po bskyed pas thob pa'i rnam par 'phrul pa la'ang 'jug go / smon lam rnam pa tha dad pa mngon par bsgrub pa rnam par dag pa la'ang 'jug go / spyod pa rnam par dag pa la'ang 'jug go / pha rol tu phyin pa yongs su rdzogs par mdzad pa la'ang 'jug go / byang chub sems dpa'i sa thams cad yongs su bsgrub pa la'ang 'jug go / bzod pa brnyes pa rnam par dag pa la'ang 'jug go /

“I also perceive the successive accumulations for the first development of the aspiration to enlightenment by those tathāgatas. I perceive the miraculous powers they attain through their first development of the aspiration to enlightenment. I perceive their pure fulfillment of their different prayers. I perceive their pure conduct. I perceive their complete accomplishment of the perfections. I perceive their attainment of all the bodhisattva bhūmis. I perceive their pure attainment of patience.

I also comprehend the order of preparations of those buddhas’ initial aspiration, their spiritual transformation on achieving the aspiration for enlightenment, the purity of execution of their various vows, their purification of action, their fulfillment of the transcendent ways, their attainment of all the stages of enlightening beings, their perfection of attainment of tolerance,
bdud kyi dkrugs ma rnam par 'thor ba'i khyu mchog gi mthu phyung ba la'ang 'jug go / mngon par rdzogs par 'tshang rgya ba'i rnam par 'phrul ba'i rgyan la'ang 'jug go /
I perceive their roaring[1231] that disperses the disturbances of the māras. I perceive the display of the miracles of their complete buddhahood.
their conquering of demons, the supernal manifestation of their spiritual transfiguration on becoming perfectly enlightened,

sangs rgyas kyi zhing rnam par dag par mdzad pa rnam pa tha dad pa la'ang 'jug go / sems can yongs su smin par mdzad pa rnam pa tha dad pa la'ang 'jug go / 'khor kun nas 'dus pa rnam pa tha dad pa la'ang 'jug go /
I perceive the purification of their different buddha realms. I perceive their different ripening of beings. I perceive their different gatherings of followers.
the variety of purity of their buddha-lands, the variety of their development of sentient beings, the variety of their audiences,

'od kyi dkyil 'khor rnam pa tha dad pa la'ang 'jug go / chos kyi 'khor lo bskor ba'i khyu mchog gis mthu phyung ba la'ang 'jug go / sangs rgyas kyi rdzu 'phrul dang / rnam par 'phrul pa dang / cho 'phrul la'ang 'jug go /

I perceive their different halos of light. I perceive their supremacy in turning the wheel of the Dharma. I perceive their attainment of the miraculous powers, miracles, and miraculous manifestations of buddhahood.
the variety of their auras of light, the majesty of their teaching activities, and their accomplishment of the miracles of buddhas.

de bzhin gshegs pa de dag gis chos bstan pa'ang shin tu rnam par gsal ba dang / ma 'dres par dran te yang dag par 'dzin to/ / dran pas yongs su bcangs so/ / rig pas rab tu shes par byed do/ / blo gros kyis shin tu rnam par 'byed do/ / blos rtogs par byed do/ / shes rab kyis snang bar byed do/ /

“I remember and keep the Dharma teachings of these tathāgatas clearly and distinctly. Through my memory I possess them. With my intelligence[1232] I understand them. With reverence[1233] I distinguish among them. With my intellect I comprehend them. With my wisdom I illuminate them.
I also distinctly remember their teachings, take them up mindfully, examine them in action, analyze them, follow them with discernment, and elucidate them with wisdom.
ma byon pa'i sangs rgyas gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa byams pa la sogs pa dag kyang mthong zhing shes te/ sems kyi skad cig gcig la sangs rgyas brgya'ang mthong ngo/ /
“I also see and know the future succession of buddhas, such as Maitreya. I see a hundred buddhas in one instant of mind.
“I also perceive the successive buddhas of the future, beginning with Maitreya, seeing a hundred buddhas in a single mental instant,

de'i 'og ma'i sems kyis sangs rgyas stong yang mthong ba nas/ de'i 'og ma'i sems kyis de bzhin gshegs pa sangs rgyas kyi zhing brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed dag kyang mthong ste/

In the next instant of mind I perceive a thousand buddhas, and so on, up to the instant of mind in which I see tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms in an inexpressible number of inexpressible numbers of buddha realms.
then a thousand, and so on, uninterruptedly seeing as many buddhas as atoms in untold buddha-lands.
de bzhin gshegs pa de dag gis thugs dang po bskyed pa'i tshogs gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa la'ang 'jug go /
“I also perceive the successive accumulations for the first development of the aspiration to enlightenment by those tathāgatas.
I also see the order of their aspiration and preparation and so on,
thugs dang po bskyed pas 'thob pa'i rnam par 'phrul pa la'ang 'jug go /
I perceive the miraculous powers they attain through their first development of the aspiration to enlightenment.
smon lam rnam pa tha dad pa mngon par bsgrubs pa rnam par dag pa la 'ang 'jug go /
I perceive their pure fulfillment of their different prayers.
spyod pa rnam par dag pa la'ang 'jug go /
I perceive their pure conduct.
pha rol tu phyin pa yongs su rdzogs par mdzad pa la'ang 'jug go
I perceive their complete accomplishment of the perfections.
byang chub sems dpa'i sa thams cad yongs su bsgrubs pa la 'ang 'jug go /
I perceive their attainment of all the bodhisattva bhūmis.
bzod pa brnyes pa rnam par dag pa la'ang 'jug go /
I perceive their pure attainment of patience.
bdud kyi dkrugs ma rnam par 'thor ba'i khyu mchog gi mthu phyung ba la'ang 'jug go /
I perceive their roaring[1234] that disperses the disturbances of the māras.
mngon par rdzogs par 'tshang rgya ba'i rnam par 'phrul pa'i rgyan la'ang 'jug go /
I perceive the display of the miracles of their complete buddhahood.
sangs rgyas kyi zhing rnam par dag par mdzad pa rnam pa tha dad pa la'ang 'jug go /
I perceive the purification of their different buddha realms.
sems can yongs su smin par mdzad pa rnam pa tha dad pa la'ang 'jug go /
I perceive their different ripening of beings.
'khor kun nas 'dus pa rnam pa tha dad pa la'ang 'jug go /
I perceive their different gatherings of followers.
'od kyi dkyil 'khor rnam pa tha dad pa la'ang 'jug go /
I perceive their different halos of light.
chos kyi 'khor lo bskor ba'i khyu mchog gi mthu phyung ba la'ang 'jug go /
I perceive their supremacy in turning the wheel of the Dharma.
sangs rgyas kyi rdzu 'phrul dang / rnam par 'phrul pa dang /_cho 'phrul la'ang 'jug go /
I perceive their attainment of the miraculous powers, miracles, and miraculous manifestations of buddhahood.

de bzhin gshegs pa de dag gis chos bstan pa yang shin tu gsal ba dang / ma 'dres pa rjes su dran te/ yang dag par 'dzin to/ / dran pas yongs su bcangs so/ / rig pas rab tu shes par byed do/ / blo gros kyis rnam par 'byed do/ / blos rtogs par byed do/ / shes rab kyis snang bar byed do/ /

“I remember and keep the Dharma teachings of these tathāgatas clearly and distinctly. Through my memory I possess them. With my intelligence[1235] I understand them. With reverence[1236] I distinguish among them. With my intellect I comprehend them. With my wisdom I illuminate them.
and distinctly remember their teachings, take them up mindfully, examine them, follow them, and elucidate them.

ji ltar 'jig rten gyi khams kyi rgyud 'di/ sngon gyi mtha' dang / phyi ma'i mthar gtogs pa'i sangs rgyas gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa mthong zhing shes pa de bzhin du phyogs bcu'i 'jig rten gyi khams kyi rgyud 'das pa dang / ma 'ongs pa sangs rgyas kyi zhing brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa snyed kyi de bzhin gshegs pa gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa/ thams cad kyang shes shing mthong ngo/ /

“Just as I see and know the succession of buddhas in the past and in the future in the lineage of this world realm, I see and know in the lineage of world realms in the ten directions as numerous as the atoms in an inexpressible number of inexpressible numbers of buddha realms the succession of tathāgatas in the past and in the future.

And just as I see the succession of past, future, and present buddhas in this world-system, so do I also comprehend the succession of all buddhas in as many past and future world-systems in the ten directions as atoms in untold buddha-lands.
de bzhin gshegs pa de dag gi thugs dang po bskyed pa'i tshogs gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa la'ang 'jug go /
“I also perceive the successive accumulations for the first development of the aspiration to enlightenment by those tathāgatas, and so on.
I also comprehend the order of the aspiration and preparations of those buddhas,

sangs rgyas gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa de la'ang rgyun mi 'chad pa dang / mi zad pa dang / dad pas shes par bya ba dang / byang chub sems dpa'i brtson 'grus dang / zhe non pas khong du chud par bya ba dang / byang chub sems dpa'i brtson 'grus kyi shugs rnam par 'phel bar byed pa dang / 'jig rten thams cad dang / nyan thos dang / rang sangs rgyas thams cad dang / de'i yul la ma zhugs pa'i byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyis mi 'phrogs par shes shing khong du chud par byed do/ /

“I know and comprehend the unbroken, unceasing succession of the buddhas. It is unequaled;[1237] it is known through faith, is known through the diligence and resolve of bodhisattvas, augments the power of the diligence of bodhisattvas, and cannot be overcome by the entire world, by all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, or by bodhisattvas who have not entered its scope.

and I comprehend the unbroken continuity of the successive incarnations of those buddhas, incomparable, accessible to faith and the vigorous resolution of enlightening beings, increasing the energy of enlightening beings, unsurpassed by any worldlings, individual illuminates, or enlightening beings who have not reached that sphere.
rnam par snang mdzad la sogs pa da ltar byung ba'i de bzhin gshegs pa phyogs bcu'i 'jig rten gyi khams na bzhugs pa/ gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa thams cad kyang mthong zhing shes te/
“I see and know the succession of the present tathāgatas that reside in world realms in the ten directions, such as Vairocana.
“I am also aware of the succession of buddhas of the present in all worlds in the ten directions, beginning with Vairocana,

sems kyi skad cig gcig la sangs rgyas brgya'ang mthong zhing shes so/ / de'i 'og ma'i sems kyis sangs rgyas stong yang mthong ba nas/ de'i 'og ma'i sems kyis/ de bzhin gshegs pa sangs rgyas kyi zhing brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi bar du'ang mthong ste/

“I see a hundred buddhas in one instant of mind. In the next instant of mind I perceive a thousand buddhas, and so on, up to the instant of mind in which I see tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms in an inexpressible number of inexpressible numbers of buddha realms.

In a single mental instant I see a hundred buddhas; in the next instant of awareness I see a thousand buddhas, continuing thus without interruption until I meet as many buddhas as atoms in untold buddha-lands.

nam de bzhin gshegs pa gang zhig gi zhal blta bar dga' ba de'i tshe'ang de bzhin du mthong ste/ sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das de dag gis bstan pa dang / bstan pa mdzad pa dang / bstan par 'gyur ba de dag thams cad kyang thos so/ / thos nas kyang 'dzin to/ /
“When I wish to see a certain tathāgata, I see him. I hear all that has been taught, is being taught, and will be taught by those buddhas, those bhagavats. When I have heard them, I retain them.
“I see whatever buddhas I wish, whenever I wish, and I hear all that has been, is being, and will be spoken by those buddhas I meet, and I take up what I hear,
dran pas yongs su bcangs so/ / rigs pas rab tu shes par byed do/ / blo gros kyis rnam par 'byed do/ / blos rtogs par byed de/ / shes rab kyis snang bar byed do/ /
Through my memory I possess them. With my intelligence[1238] I understand them. With reverence[1239] I distinguish among them. With my intellect I comprehend them. With my wisdom I illuminate them.
remember it, examine it in action, analyze it, follow it with discernment, and elucidate it with wisdom.

rigs kyi bu/ kho bos ni byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa yongs su mya ngan las mi 'da' ba'i mthar phyin pa 'di shes par zad na/ kho bos byang chub sems dpa' dus gsum skad cig gcig tu shes pa rab tu thob pa/ skad cig gi cha shas la ting nge 'dzin rnam par phye ba la spyod pa/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i nyi ma las byung ba/ rtog pa dang rnam par rtog pa thams cad mnyam pa nyid du khong du chud pa/ sangs rgyas thams cad dang mnyam pa'i ting nge 'dzin rjes su rtogs pa/ bdag dang / sems can dang / sangs rgyas mi gnyis par spyod pa/ rang bzhin gyis 'od gsal ba'i chos kyi rgyan gyi dkyil 'khor dang ldan pa/ ye shes kyi 'khrul 'khor gyis 'jig rten gyi dra ba 'gengs pa/ de bzhin gshegs pa rgya mtsho thams cad dang mi 'gal bar rnam par spyod pa/ chos kyi dbyings thams cad du rnam par rtogs par byed pa'i ye shes kyi yul dang ldan pa/ de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyis chos bstan pa rnam par rig par byed pa'i ye shes kyi yul can de dag gi spyod pa shes pa'am/ yon tan brjod par nus re skan/

“Noble one, I know this bodhisattva liberation called the attainment of the summit of inexhaustibility, but how could I know the conduct or describe the qualities of the bodhisattvas who know the three times in a single instant; who in one fraction of an instant of their practice dwell in an array of samādhis; who have entered into the sunlight of the tathāgatas;[1240] who understand the equality of all concepts and misconceptions; who have realized the samādhi that is equal to that of all the buddhas; who act in the nonduality of self, beings, and buddhas; who are in the domain of the display of the Dharma of natural luminosity; who have cut through the net of the world with the device of wisdom; who act without disturbing the seal[1241] of the Dharma of the tathāgatas; who have the scope of wisdom that understands the entire realm of phenomena; who have the scope of wisdom that understands the Dharma teaching of all the tathāgatas?

“I know this enlightening liberation of ultimate nonextinction; how can I know the practice or tell of the virtues of the enlightening beings who have attained instantaneous knowledge of past, present, and future, who dwell in all concentrations in the space of an instant, who are imbued with the light of those who realize Thusness, who realize the equality of all thoughts and imaginations, who are focused on the equality of all buddhas, who abide in the nonduality of self, sentient beings, and buddhas, whose realm is the manifestation of principles, whose nature is clarity, whose workings of knowledge pervade the network of worlds, who dwell unwavering on the seal of the teaching of all buddhas, who are in the range of knowledge making known all realms of reality, who are in the range of knowledge conveying the teachings of all buddhas?

song / rigs kyi bu/ lho phyogs kyi rgyud 'di nyid na/ ri gru 'dzin ces bya ba yod de/ de na byang chub sems dpa' spyan ras gzigs kyi dbang po zhes bya ba 'dug gi/ de'i gan du song la/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bya ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bya ba dris shig ces nas/

“Depart, noble one. In this southern region, there is the mountain named Potalaka. There dwells the bodhisattva by the name of Avalokiteśvara. Go to him and ask him, ‘How should a bodhisattva train in bodhisattva conduct? How should a bodhisattva practice it?’ ”
“South of here is a mountain called Potalaka, where an enlightening being named Avalokiteshvara lives. Go ask him how to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings.”
de'i tshe tshigs su bcad pa 'di gnyis smras so/ /
Then he spoke these two verses:
Then Veshthila said in verse,

song shig nor bzang dpal gyi chu rgyal dbus zhig na/ / mkhas pa rnams kyi ri rgyal gru 'dzin mdzes pa yod/ / rin chen rgyus byas shing dang nags tshal me tog mang / / bza' shing ra ba rdzing dang chu bran 'bab par ldan/ /

“Depart, Sudhana! In the center of the glorious king of the waters[1242] Is beautiful Potalaka, king of mountains, the residence of heroes. It has excellent trees made of jewels, is covered with flowers, And is endowed with parks, lotus ponds, and flowing streams. {1}
Go, Sudhana, to Mount Potalaka in the ocean, a pure abode of the valiant, Made of jewels, covered with trees, scattered with flowers, complete with gardens, ponds, and streams.

ri mchog de la brtan pa spyan ras gzigs kyi dbang / / 'gro ba rnams la phan pa'i don du rnam par spyod/ / de gan song dang nor bzang khyod la mgon po yis/ / yon tan rgya chen tshul la 'jug pa ston par byed/ /

“Wise Avalokiteśvara who benefits beings‍— That resolute one[1243] dwells on that supreme mountain. Go to him, Sudhana, and you will be taught The qualities of[1244] the Guides, the entry into the way of vast goodness.” {2}
On the mountain the steady, wise Avalokiteshvara dwells for the benefit of the world. Go ask him the virtues of the Guides—he will teach you great, wonderful means of attainment.

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis/ khyim bdag nan khugs kyi rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal nas/ khyim bdag nan khugs la lan brgya stong du mas g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas te/ yang dang yang bltas nas; khyim bdag nan khugs kyi drung nas song ngo// //

Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, bowed his head to the feet of the householder Veṣṭhila, circumambulated the householder Veṣṭhila many hundreds of thousands of times, keeping him to his right, and, looking back again and again, departed from the householder Veṣṭhila.
So Sudhana paid his respects to Veshthila and went on.

Chapter 30. Avalokiteśvara
Avalokiteshvara

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang / khyim bdag nan khugs kyi gdams ngag rjes su sems shing / byang chub sems dpa'i mos pa'i mdzod de ni shes par byed/ byang chub sems dpa'i rjes su dran pa'i stobs de ni rjes su dran par byed/ sangs rgyas kyi tshul gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa'i stobs ni yang dag par 'dzin/ sangs rgyas gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa'i mtshams ni khong du chud par byed/ rnas thos pa'i sangs rgyas kyi mtshan de dag gi ni rjes su 'brang / sangs rgyas kyi chos bstan pa'i tshul de dag ni mthun par byed/ sangs rgyas kyi yang dag par bsgrub pa'i rgyan de ni khong du chud par byed/ sangs rgyas mngon par rdzogs par 'tshang rgya ba'i khyu mchog gi mthu phyung ba de la ni yid ches par byed/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i 'phrin las bsam gyis mi khyab pa de ni mngon du byed cing /

Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, contemplating the instruction of the householder Veṣṭhila, knowing that treasury of bodhisattva aspiration, remembering that power of bodhisattva memory, keeping in his mind the power of that successive lineage of the way of the buddhas, comprehending the continuous succession of the lineage of the buddhas, remembering the names of the buddhas that he had heard,[1245] being in accord with the way of the Dharma taught by the buddhas, comprehending the array of attainments through the Dharma[1246] of the buddhas, having confidence in the proclamation[1247] of complete buddhahood by the buddhas, and focused on the inconceivable activity of the tathāgatas,

Reflecting on the teaching of Veshthila, entering the treasury of zealous application of enlightening beings, remembering the power of mindfulness of enlightening beings, remembering the power of the succession of enlightened guides, realizing the unbroken continuity of buddhas, remembering the progression of the hearing of the names of buddhas, following the principles of the teachings of the buddhas, entering into the array of collective practice of the buddha-teachings, intent on the the exclamation made by buddhas on becoming perfectly enlightened, focusing his attention on the inconceivable action of buddhas,
mthar gyis ri gru 'dzin gang na ba der song nas/ ri gru 'dzin gyi steng du phyin te/ byang chub sems dpa' spyan ras gzigs kyi dbang po yongs su rmed cing tshol tshol ba las/
eventually came to the Potalaka Mountain. He ascended the Potalaka Mountain and searched and searched for the bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
Sudhana made his way to Mount Potalaka. Climbing the mountain, he looked around for Avalokiteshvara

nub phyogs logs kyi ri'i sman ljongs mtsho dang / mtshe'u dang / 'bab chus mdzes par gyur pa/ bai DUr+ya sngon po'i dkyil 'khor ltar sngo zhing 'jam la gzhon pa'i spang nags tshal chen po'i mthongs na 'dug pa zhig na/ rin po che rdo rje'i rdo stegs shig la skyil mo krung bcas te 'dug cing / rin po che sna tshogs kyi rdo stegs la 'khod pa'i byang chub sems dpa'i tshogs dpag tu med pas kun nas bskor cing chos ston te/ chos kyi rnam grangs 'gro ba thams cad yongs su sdud pa'i yul byams pa chen po dang / snying rje chen po'i sgo gsal bar ston pa zhes bya ba yang dag par ston cing 'dug pa mthong ngo/ /

He saw Avalokiteśvara on the upper slope[1248] of the western side of the mountain. It was a fresh, gentle, verdant pasture like a circular area of blue beryl and was beautified by springs, waterfalls, and streams,[1249] an open grove within a great forest. He was teaching the Dharma, seated cross-legged upon a diamond rock encircled by a countless assembly of bodhisattvas seated upon rocks that were various jewels. He was giving the Dharma teaching called The Clear Teaching of the Gateway to Love and Compassion, which has as its scope the gathering of all beings into the Dharma.

and saw him on a plateau on the west side of the mountain, which was adorned with springs, ponds, and streams, sitting wakefully on a diamond boulder in a clearing in a large woods, surrounded by a group of enlightening beings seated on various jewel rocks, to whom he was expounding a doctrine called “light of the medium of great love and compassion,” which concerns the salvation of all sentient beings.

mthong nas kyang dga' rangs te/ mgu zhing nyams bde la tshim zhing yid bde ba skyes nas dga' bas rgyas shing mi 'dzum pa'i mig gis thal mo sbyar nas/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen la dad pa'i shugs dang ldan pas/ sems mi 'khrugs pa/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen mthong na sangs rgyas thams cad mthong bar 'dzin pa dge ba'i bshes gnyen las byung ba'i chos kyi sprin thams cad yang dag par gzung ba'i 'du shes dang ldan pa/ yon tan dang / nan tan thams cad dge ba'i bshes gnyen la rag lus pa'i 'du shes can/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen dang phrad pa shin tu dga' bar sems pa/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen las stobs bcu'i ye shes rin po che 'byung zhing 'thob par 'gyur pa'i 'du shes dang ldan pa/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen las ye shes snang ba mi zad pa 'byung ba'i 'du shes can/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi rten gyis bsod nams kyi rgyud rnam par 'phel bar 'gyur ba'i 'du shes dang ldan pa/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen ni thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi sgo yang dag par ston pa'i 'du shes dang ldan pa/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen ni ye shes kyi rgya mtsho chen po la 'jug pa yongs su ston par 'du shes pa/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen ni thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi tshogs yang dag par 'dus pa yongs su bskyed pa'i 'du shes dang ldan pa de/

On seeing him, Sudhana was filled with joy, delighted, elated, pleased, and happy. With increasing rapture, he kept his eyes wide open. He placed his hands together in homage. His mind was at peace through being endowed with the power of faith in kalyāṇamitras. He believed that to see kalyāṇamitras was to see all the buddhas. He believed that the acquisition of the entire cloud of Dharma originated from the kalyāṇamitras. He believed that all qualities and practices depended on the kalyāṇamitras. He believed that it was difficult to encounter kalyāṇamitras. He believed that the attainment of the precious wisdom of the ten strengths came from the kalyāṇamitras. He believed that the inexhaustible light of wisdom[1250] came from the kalyāṇamitras. He believed that the continuous increase of merit was dependent on the kalyāṇamitras. He believed that the gateway to omniscience was revealed by the kalyāṇamitras. He believed that entry into the great ocean of wisdom was taught by the kalyāṇamitras. He believed that the gathering of the accumulation of omniscience was born from the kalyāṇamitras.

Transported with joy on seeing Avalokiteshvara, his eyes fixed on him, his mind undistracted, full of the energy of faith in the spiritual benefactor, thinking of seeing spiritual benefactors as at once seeing buddhas, thinking of reception of the multitudes of all truths as originating in spiritual benefactors, thinking of the attainment of all virtues as deriving from spiritual benefactors, thinking of how hard it is to meet spiritual benefactors, thinking of spiritual benefactors as the source from which the jewels of knowledge of the ten powers are obtained, thinking of spiritual benefactors as the source of vision of inexhaustible knowledge, thinking that the growth of the sprouts of goodness depends on spiritual benefactors, thinking that the door of omniscience is revealed by spiritual benefactors, thinking that the way to enter the ocean of great knowledge is pointed out by spiritual benefactors, thinking that the accumulation of the store of omniscience is fostered by spiritual benefactors,

byang chub sems dpa' spyan ras gzigs kyi dbang po gang na ba der phyin te/ /de nas byang chub sems dpa' spyan ras gzigs kyi dbang pos/ tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang ring zhig nas tshur 'ong ba mthong nas smras pa/
He went toward the bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara. The bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara could see Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, coming in the distance and said,
Sudhana went up to Avalokiteshvara. The enlightening being Avalokiteshvara, seeing Sudhana approaching in the distance, said,
tshur shog/ dpe med pa'i theg pa chen po yangs shing / bsam gyis mi khyab pa la zhugs pa/
“Come here! You are welcome,[1251] you who have entered the inconceivable, vast Mahāyāna, which is beyond any analogy;
“Welcome, you who have set out on the incomparable, lofty, inconceivable Great Vehicle,
skye ba las byung ba'i sdug bsngal sna tshogs kyis gtses shing skyabs med par gyur pa'i 'gro ba thams cad yongs su bskyabs pa'i bsam pa dang ldan pa/
you who have the motivation to be a refuge for all beings who are tormented by various sufferings that arise through being born and who have no refuge;
intending to save all beings who are oppressed by various firmly rooted miseries and have no refuge,
sangs rgyas kyis chos thams cad mngon sum du gyur pa/ 'jig rten thams cad las 'das te/ dpe med tshad med pa la mngon par mos pa/
you who wish to witness all the Dharmas of the buddhas, which transcend the world, are beyond analogy, and are beyond measure;
seeking to directly experience all the teachings of buddhas, which are beyond all worlds, incomparable, and immeasurable;
snying rje chen pos byin gyis brlabs pas 'gro ba thams cad yongs su bskyabs pa'i blo gros can/
you who are filled with the power[1252] of great compassion and intend to liberate all beings;
you are filled with the energy of great compassion, determined to liberate all sentient beings,
blta na kun tu bzang po'i spyod pa la mngon du bltas pa/
you in whom the completely good conduct is evidently seen;
directed toward practice of the vision of universal good,
smon lam chen po'i dkyil 'khor yongs su sbyangs pa'i sems dang ldan pa/
you who aspire to make pure a domain of great prayers;
intent on purifying the sphere of great vows,
sangs rgyas thams cad kyi chos kyi sprin yongs su gzung bar mos pa/
you who wish to possess the clouds of Dharma of all the buddhas;
seeking to retain the multitudes of teachings of all buddhas;
dge ba'i rtsa ba bsags pas ngoms mi shes pa'i bsam pa dang ldan pa/
you whose motivation to accumulate roots of merit is never satisfied;
with the tireless will to build up roots of goodness,
dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi gdams ngag la yang dag par zhugs pa/
you who follow perfectly the instructions of kalyāṇamitras;
correctly proceeding on the instructions of spiritual benefactors,
'jam dpal gyi ye shes rgya mtsho las byung ba'i yon tan gyi 'byung gnas sangs rgyas kyi byin gyi rlabs thob par bya ba la mngon du bltas pa/
you who are the source of a lotus[1253] of good qualities, arising from the ocean of the wisdom of Mañjuśrī; you who are focused on attaining the blessing of the buddhas;
born of the ocean of knowledge of Manjushri, a mine of lotuses of virtue, fit to receive the empowerment of buddhas,
ting nge 'dzin gyi snang ba dang shugs rab tu thob pa;
you who have attained the light and power of samādhi;
imbued with the energy of the light of concentration,
sangs rgyas thams cad kyi chos kyi sprin gyi char yang dag par gzung ba la mngon par mos pa'i sems dang ldan pa/
you who aspire to obtain the rain[1254] from the clouds of Dharma of all the buddhas;
seeking to keep in mind the teachings of all buddhas,
sangs rgyas mthong bas dga' ba dang / mos pa'i shugs kyis yid rab tu bde bar gyur pa/
you whose mind is made happy by the power of faith and delight on seeing the buddhas;
thrilled with the joy of the vision of buddhas,
legs par spyod pa tshad med cing bsam gyis mi khyab pa'i shugs kyis mngon par brlan pa'i sems dang ldan pa/
you whose mind is moistened by the power of immeasurable, inconceivable conduct;
yon tan la nan tan du bya ba'i shugs kyis rnam par dag pa'i bsod nams dang ye shes kyi mdzod bdag la mngon du gyur pa/
you who have become the lord of a treasure of pure merit and wisdom through the power of the practice of good qualities;
your mind expanded by the incalculable energy of achievement of virtue,
thams cad mkhyen pa'i ye shes mthong ba'i lam gyi shugs gzhan la yongs su bstan pa'i bsam pa can/
you who are motivated to teach others the power of the path to seeing omniscient wisdom;
wishing to reveal to others the power of the measure of omniscience to which you have access through your own mystic knowledge,
snying rje chen po'i shugs ma nyams pa'i rtsa ba dang ldan pa/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i ye shes snang ba'i shugs yang dag par gzung ba'i blo gros can khyod 'ongs pa legs so/ /
you who possess the root that is the undiminishing power of great compassion; you who are intent on possessing the power of the light of the wisdom of the tathāgatas.”
determined to sustain the energy of light of knowledge of buddhas, firmly rooted in the power of great compassion.”

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang / byang chub sems dpa' spyan ras gzigs kyi dbang po gang na ba der song nas/ byang chub sems dpa' spyan ras gzigs kyi dbang po'i rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te/ byang chub sems dpa' spyan ras gzigs la lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas mdun du 'dug ste/ thal mo sbyar nas 'di skad ces smras so/ /

He circumambulated the bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara many hundreds of thousands of times, keeping him to his right. Then he stood before him and, with his hands placed together in homage, said,
Then Sudhana went up to Avalokiteshvara, paid his respects, and said,

'phags pa/ bdag gis bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed na; ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bgyi ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bgyi ba ma 'tshal te/
“Ārya, I have developed the aspiration for the highest, complete enlightenment, but I do not know how bodhisattvas should train in bodhisattva conduct and in what way they should practice it.
“Noble one, I have set my mind on supreme perfect enlightenment, but I do not know how to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings.

'phags pa ni/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams la gdams ngag dang / rjes su bstan pa mdzad do zhes bdag gis thos na/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bgyi ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bgyi ba 'phags pas bdag la bshad du gsol/
“Ārya, I have heard that you give instruction and teachings to bodhisattvas! Explain to me how bodhisattvas should train in bodhisattva conduct and how they should practice it!”
I hear you give enlightening beings instruction, and I ask you to tell me how to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings.”

de nas byang chub sems dpa' spyan ras gzigs kyi dbang pos/ mdog 'dzam bu chu klung gi gser gyi kha dog tu 'dug pa/ 'od kyi dra ba rnam pa sna tshogs tshad med pa 'phro ba'i rgyan gyi sprin rab tu 'gyed pa'i lag pa g.yas pa brkyang ste/ mtshan dang dpe byad bzang po las byung ba'i 'od zer sna tshogs dri ma med pa/ lus dang sems kyi bde ba tshad med pa rab tu skyed pa'i tshogs kyis shin tu rgyas pa'i lag pa/ tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gi spyi bo la bzhag ste

Then the bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara extended his right hand, which was the color of gold from the Jambu River and emanated a display of clouds of countless networks of lights of various colors, and upon Sudhana’s head he placed his hand, which had the multicolored light rays that shine from the signs and features of a great being and bring stainless, measureless physical and mental bliss.
'di skad ces smras so// rigs kyi bu/ de ltar khyod kyis bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed pa legs so/ / legs so/ /
The bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara said, “Noble one, it is excellent, excellent, that you have in that way developed the aspiration for the highest, complete enlightenment!
Avalokiteshvara said, “It is good that you aspire to supreme perfect enlightenment.
rigs kyi bu/ nga ni byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa'i sgo snying rje chen po'i sgo thogs pa med pa zhes bya ba shes te/
“Noble one, I know the gateway to bodhisattva activity called the unimpeded gateway to great compassion.
I know a way of enlightening practice called ‘undertaking great compassion without delay,’

rigs kyi bu/ nga ni byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa'i sgo snying rje chen po'i sgo thogs pa med pa de ni/ 'gro ba thams cad la dbye ba med par sems can yongs su smin par bya ba dang gdul ba la zhugs pa/ sgo kun nas thos shing rnam par rig par 'gyur bas/ sems can yongs su bsdu ba dang gdul ba la nye bar gnas pa ste/

“Noble one, my gateway to bodhisattva activity called the unimpeded gateway to great compassion ripens and guides beings without making any distinctions among all beings, and it gathers and guides beings through their completely hearing and knowing this gateway.
which sets about impartially guiding all sentient beings to perfection, dedicated to protecting and guiding sentient beings by communicating knowledge to them through all media.

rigs kyi bu/ de ltar byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa'i sgo snying rje chen po'i sgo thogs pa med pa la gnas pas/ de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi zhabs kyi drung nas kyang mi g.yo la/ sems can thams cad kyi dgos pa la'ang sta gon du gnas te/ sbyin pas kyang sems can yongs su sdud do/ / ngag snyan pa dang / don bya ba dang / don mthun pas kyang sems can yongs su sdud do/ /

“Noble one, in that way, being established in the gateway to bodhisattva activity called the unimpeded gateway to great compassion, though I never depart from being at the feet of all the tathāgatas, I remain focused on what should be done for all beings. I gather beings through generosity. I gather beings through pleasant words, through benefiting them, and through practicing what I teach.

Established in this method of enlightening practice undertaking great compassion without delay, I appear in the midst of the activities of all sentient beings without leaving the presence of all buddhas, and take care of them by means of generosity, kind speech, beneficial actions, and cooperation.

gzugs kyi lus rnam par bstan pas kyang sems can yongs su smin par byed do/ / kha dog dang / dbyibs dang / gzugs bsam gyis mi khyab pa bstan te/ rnam par dmigs par bya ba dang / 'od zer gyi dra ba dgye bas kyang / sems can rab tu sim par byed cing yongs su smin par byed do/ / bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du dbyangs brjod pa dang / ci la dga' ba'i spyod lam yongs su bstan pa dang / mos pa sna tshogs dang tshul mthun par chos bstan pa dang / rdzu 'phrul dang / rnam 'phrul ba rnam pa sna tshogs dang / dge ba'i chos bsags par bag mi byed pa'i sems can gyi sems yongs su bskul ba dang / bsam pa dang mthun par sprul pa sna tshogs tshad med pa yongs su bstan pa dang / rigs sna tshogs su skyes pa'i sems can rnam dang skal pa mthun pa'i gzugs yongs su bstan pa dang / gnas gcig tu 'grogs pas kyang / sems can yongs su bsdus shing yongs su smin par byed do/ /

“I also ripen beings through manifesting physical bodies. I gladden and ripen beings through manifesting countless pure[1255] colors, shapes, and forms and through radiating a net of light rays. I speak to them in accordance with their aspirations. I manifest whatever path of conduct they delight in. I teach them the Dharma in accordance with their various wishes. I manifest various forms of miracles so as to inspire beings who have not been attentive in accumulating virtuous qualities. I manifest a variety of countless emanations in accordance with their wishes. I gather and ripen beings by manifesting forms that accord with the states of the beings born in the various classes of existence and by living with them in the same place.

I also develop sentient beings by appearing in various forms: I gladden and develop them by purity of vision of inconceivable forms radiating auras of light, and I take care of them and develop them by speaking to them according to their mentalities, and by showing conduct according to their inclinations, and by magically producing various forms, and by teaching them doctrines commensurate with their various interests, and by inspiring them to begin to accumulate good qualities, by showing them projections according to their mentalities, by appearing to them as members of their own various races and conditions, and by living together with them.
rigs kyi bu/ de ltar ngas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa'i sgo snying rje chen po'i sgo thogs pa med pa 'di yongs su sbyangs pas/ 'gro ba thams cad rab tu rten pa'i smon lam bskyed de/
“Noble one, in that way I have purified the gateway to bodhisattva activity called the unimpeded gateway to great compassion and therefore prayed to be a support for all beings.
“Perfecting this practice of unhesitating compassion, I have vowed to be a refuge for all sentient beings,
'di ltar sems can thams cad kyi g.yang sa'i 'jigs pa dang /
I have accomplished the prayer to be a support for all beings in order that I end for all beings the fear of precipices,
to free them from fears of calamity,

sems can thams cad kyi rgyud kyi 'jigs pa zhi bar bya ba dang / sems can thams cad kyi mgo rmongs pa'i 'jigs pa rnam par bzlog pa dang / sems can thams cad kyis bcings pa'i 'jigs pa yongs su gcad pa dang / sems can thams cad kyi srog la bab par mi bde ba'i 'jigs pa rnam par bzlog pa dang /
