cause fears[1256] within all beings to cease, eliminate fear from confusion in all beings, eliminate in all beings the fear of being in bondage, dispel in all beings the fear of circumstances[1257] that cause loss of life,
threat, confusion, bondage, attacks on their lives,

sems can thams cad kyi yo byad kyis phongs pa'i 'jigs pa bsal ba dang / sems can thams cad kyi 'tsho ba med pa'i 'jigs pa zhi bar bya ba dang / sems can thams cad kyi grags pa med pa'i 'jigs pa las yongs su bzla ba dang / sems can thams cad kyi 'khor ba'i 'jigs pa rab tu zhi bar bya ba dang /

banish from all beings the fear of being deprived of material necessities, end in all beings the fear of being without a livelihood, dispel in all beings the fear of ill repute,[1258] dispel in all beings the fear of being in saṃsāra,
insufficiency of means to support life, inability to make a living, ill repute, the perils of life,

sems can thams cad kyi 'khor du bag tsha ba'i 'jigs pa med pa bya ba dang / / sems can thams cad 'chi ba'i 'jigs pa las rnam par bzla ba dang / sems can thams cad kyi ngan song gi 'jigs pa rnam par bzlog pa dang / sems can thams cad kyi lam mun pas nyam nga ba phyir mi ldog pa'i snang bas gsal bar bya ba dang /

cause the fear of timidity within an assembly to cease in all beings, cause all beings to transcend the fear of death, dispel in all beings the fear of the lower existences, shine the light of irreversibility upon those whose path has degenerated in great[1259] darkness,
intimidation by the crowd, death, miserable conditions, unknown hardships,

sems can thams cad kyi skal ba mi mnyam pa dang 'grogs pa'i 'jigs pa shin tu bsal ba dang / sems can thams cad kyi sdug pa dang bral ba'i 'jigs pa dgag par bya ba dang / sems can thams cad kyi mi sdug pa dang 'grogs pa'i 'jigs pa med par bya ba dang / sems can thams cad lus la mi bde ba'i 'jigs pa dang bral bar bya ba dang /

completely eliminate in all beings the fear of meeting misfortune, extinguish in all beings the fear of being apart from what is liked, eliminate in all beings the fear of having to be with what is disliked, separate all beings from the fear of physical torment,
servitude, separation from loved ones, living with the uncongenial, physical violence,
sems can thams cad sems la mi bde ba'i 'jigs pa las dgrol ba dang / sems can thams cad sdug bsngal ba dang / yid mi bde ba dang / 'khrug pa las yongs su bzla ba'i phyir/
free all beings from mental torment, and cause all beings to transcend suffering, unhappiness, and disturbances.
mental violence, sorrow, and depression.
'gro ba thams cad rab tu rten pa'i smon lam mngon par bsgrub pa 'di byas so/ /
[…see above…]
I have undertaken a vow to be a refuge for all beings from all these fears and perils.

sems can thams cad kyi 'jigs pa rnam par zhi bar bya ba'i phyir yang 'jig rten du rjes su dran pa'i sgo byin gyis brlabs so/ / sems can thams cad 'jigs pa dang bral bar bya ba'i phyir/ rang gi ming gi 'khor lo'ang 'jig rten du rnam par dmigs par byas so/ / dus ji lta ba bzhin du 'gro bas rnam par dmigs par bya ba'i phyir/ 'gro ba thams cad rnam pa'i bye brag mtha' yas pa dang mnyam par nga'i lus kyang byin gyis brlabs so/ /

“I manifest the gateway to mindfulness in all worlds in order to dispel fear in all beings. I have made the wheel of my name known in all worlds in order to free all beings from fear. I miraculously manifest my body to be the same[1260] as the distinct forms of all endless beings in order to be perceived by beings at the appropriate times.

I have also caused a way of remembrance to appear in all worlds, to extinguish the fears of all beings; I have caused my name to be known in all worlds to drive away the fears of all beings. I have caused the tranquillity of all beings, in endless forms, to appear in my body, to communicate to all beings individually according to the time.

rigs kyi bu/ de ltar nga ni thabs 'dis sems can thams cad 'jigs pa las yongs su bkrol zhing sangs rgyas kyi chos thams cad thob par bya ba'i phyir/ bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed cing phyir mi ldog par byed do/ /

“Noble one, through this method, I liberate all beings from fear and cause them to develop an irreversible aspiration for the highest, complete enlightenment so that they will attain all the Dharmas of the buddhas.
By this means I release beings from all fears, inspire them to seek supreme enlightenment, and cause them never to regress in the attainment of the qualities of buddhas.

rigs kyi bu/ ngas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa'i sgo snying rje chen po'i sgo thogs pa med pa 'di thob par zad na/ ngas byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po rnams sangs rgyas thams cad kyi smon lam gyi dkyil 'khor la rnam par dag pa/ byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po'i spyod pa khong du chud par rtogs pa/ dge ba'i chos mngon par 'du bya ba rgyun mi gcod pa'i rgyud dang ldan pa/ byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin thams cad kyi rgyud la rtag tu mnyam par gzhag pa/ bskal pa thams cad du gnas shing spyod pa las phyir mi ldog pa'i rgyud dang ldan pa/ dus gsum thams cad kyi tshul rjes su rtogs pa'i rgyud dang ldan pa/ 'jig rten gyi khams thams cad kyi klong yongs su 'khyil ba'i rgyud la mkhas pa/ sems can thams cad kyi mi dge ba'i sems rnam par zhi bar byed pa'i rgyud dang ldan pa/ sems can thams cad kyi dge ba'i sems yongs su 'phel ba'i rgyud dang ldan pa/ sems can thams cad 'khor ba'i rgyun las phyir ldog par byed pa'i rgyud dang ldan pa de dag gi spyod pa shes pa'am/ yon tan brjod par nus re skan/

“Noble one, I know this gateway to bodhisattva activity called the unimpeded gateway to great compassion, but how could I know the conduct or describe the qualities of the completely good bodhisattvas who have the pure domain of the prayers of all buddhas; who have realized the completely good conduct of bodhisattvas; who have an unbroken continuity of creating virtuous qualities; who are always resting in a continuity of the samādhi of all bodhisattvas; who have nonregressing conduct while residing in all kalpas; who have the continuous understanding of the ways of all three times; who are skilled in the continuity of the turning of the cycle of all world realms; who have the continuity of ending nonvirtuous mentalities in all beings; who have a continuity of increasing the virtuous mentalities of all beings; and who have the continuity of countering the continuity of saṃsāra for all beings?”

“I have only attained this way of enlightening practice through unhesitating great compassion. How can I know the practice or tell of the virtues of the universally good enlightening beings, who have perfected the vows of all enlightened ones, who have gone the way of the practice of the universally good enlightening being, who are uninterrupted streams of performance of good works, who are always focused on the perception of the concentrations of enlightening beings, who continue their practice without deviation or regression through all ages, who continuously adapt to the times everywhere, who are familiar with the changing currents in all worlds, who continuously work to extinguish all sentient beings’ bad thoughts and to increase their good thoughts, who continuously work to turn all sentient beings away from the repetitious circles of the mundane whirl?”
de la 'di skad ces bya'o/ /
Concerning this it is said:
Then this was said:

g.yas phyogs bskor ba byas te gus par bkur bstod nas/ / nor bzang shin tu dul ba lho phyogs rgyud du song / / spyan ras gzigs dbang drang srong snying rje rnam spyod pa/ / rin chen ri yi sul na gnas par des kyang mthong / /

Sudhana, who was self-disciplined, circumambulated, Praised reverently, and departed on the southern road‍— He saw, residing in a cleft in a precious mountain, Avalokiteśvara, a ṛṣi who abided in compassion. {1}
Having respectfully rendered honor and praise, Sudhana, well controlled, went south. On a cliff of a mountain he saw Avalokiteshvara, the seer who abides in compassion.

rin chen sna tshogs rdo rje'i ri yi sman ljongs na/ / pad+mo'i snying po'i seng ge'i khri la brtan pa 'dug/ lha dang lha min klu dang srin po mi'am ci/ / rgyal ba'i sras kyis bskor cing de la chos kyang ston/ /

The wise one was seated in the center of a lotus on a lion throne On the side[1261] of the diamond mountain with various precious jewels. He was teaching the Dharma to the devas, asuras, nāgas,[1262] Kinnaras, rākṣasas, and bodhisattvas who encircled him. {2}
On a diamond slope, adorned with jewels, Sitting on a lion seat in a lotus calyx, the Steadfast, Surrounded by various creatures and enlightening beings, Expounds the Teaching to them.

mthong nas nor bzang dga' ba tshad med skyes par gyur/ / bsnyen te yon tan rgya mtsho'i rkang la phyag 'tshal nas/ / ci nas bzang po'i spyod pa bdag gis thob 'gyur bar/ / 'phags pas thugs rje bskyed de gdams shing bslab par gsol/ /

When Sudhana saw him, he was filled with unequaled joy, Approached him, and bowed down to the feet of the ocean of qualities. He said, “Ārya, have compassion and teach to me the training So that I may attain good conduct.” {3}
Seeing this, Sudhana, his joy unequaled, Went and bowed to the feet of the Ocean of Virtue And said, “Teach me, noble one, with compassion, To attain this good conduct.”

bsod nams brgya bas brgyan pa'i dri med lag brkyang ste/ / 'od sprin dra ba rgya chen bzang po rab bton nas/ / nor bzang spyi bor bzhag ste sems can rnam dag pa/ / spyan ras gzigs kyi dbang po mkhas pas tshig 'di smras/ /

Extending his stainless hand, adorned by a hundred merits, Which emitted excellent, vast networks of clouds of light, And placing it upon Sudhana’s head, that pure being, The wise one Avalokiteśvara, spoke these words: {4}
Extending his undefiled arm of a hundredfold auspicious splendor, Radiating far-reaching pure light, Avalokiteshvara, the purified being, the sage, Laid his hand on Sudhana’s head and spoke:

sangs rgyas sras po da ni rnam thar gcig sgo shes/ / ye shes snying po rgyal ba kun gyi thugs rjes sdug / 'gro ba thams cad bskyab cing yongs su bsdu phyir byung / / kun tu bdag nyid rang la byams pa bzhin du rgyu/ /

“Son of the buddhas, I know one gateway to liberation, Which is the mass of compassion, the essence of wisdom of all the jinas, Which arises in order to gather and liberate all beings, And my love for them thus courses everywhere. {5}
“I know a gate of liberation, the embryo of knowledge Of clouds of compassion of all buddhas, Born of my own love and operating everywhere To protect and care for all beings.

'gro ba mang po thams cad sdug bsngal kun las skyob/ / gang rnams dam du bcings shing dgra lag phyin pa dang / / lus la gzer cing de bzhin btson rar btsud pa yang / / nga yi ming thos bcings shing bzung ba thar bar 'gyur/ /

“I protect all beings from every suffering. Those who are tightly bound, who are in the hands of enemies, Whose bodies are struck, and who are put into prisons On hearing my name are freed from bondage. {6}
“I protect all beings from many disasters; Those caught in the grip of enemies, Physically injured, and imprisoned Are freed from their bonds on hearing my name.

rgyal po dag la nyes pa'i g.yon byas gsad spangs pa/ / de tshe de dag nga yi ming yang dran 'gyur na/ / mda' 'phangs de yi lus la phog par mi 'gyur te/ / mtshon rnon btab kyang de dag mi 'dzug rgal bar 'gyur/ /
“Those who have broken the law will escape execution When at that time they remember my name. Arrows that are fired will not hit their bodies. Weapons that strike them will be not pierce them. {7}
“Arrows shot at the condemned do not wound them, Weapons break and swords are deflected If they remember my name.

dbang po'i 'khor du phyin dang gang rnams rtsod gyur pa/ / dgra rnams kun las rgyal 'gyur grags pa thob par 'gyur/ / grags dang grogs dang rigs dang nor rnams 'phel bar 'gyur/ / nga yi ming dran de dag thub pa med par 'gyur/ /

“Those who remember my name will be invincible. Though they enter the courts of lords, no matter who disputes with them, They will be victorious over all adversaries and attain excellence,[1263] And their fame, friends, families, and wealth will increase. {8}
“In disputes among kings, those who remember my name Defeat their adversaries and gain what is good, Increase in repute among friends and relatives, And their property becomes inviolable.

gang gis nga yi ming ni rjes su dran byas pa/ / de dag rkun pos 'jigs dogs dgras 'jigs nags phyin te/ / seng ge dom gzig gcan zan g.yag rgod sbrul gang yang / / dgra rnams kun las rgyal zhing 'jigs pa med par 'gyur/ /

“Anyone who remembers my name Entering forests fearful with thieves, fearful with enemies, With lions, bears, leopards, wild beasts, yaks, and snakes, Will be free of fear and victorious over enemies. {9}
“Any who remember my name Go without fear To forests infested with bandits and wild animals, Conquering all enemies.

gang rnams la las nga yi ming zhig dran byas na/ / sdang ba'i sems kyis rin chen ltongs su bor gyur tam/ / sol ma dag lce med rab tu 'bar bar bor gyur kyang / / me rnams pad+mos gang ba'i chu yi gter du 'gyur/ /

“When anyone who remembers my name Is malevolently thrown from the summit of a great mountain[1264] Or hurled into a blazing fire of coals, The fire will transform into a treasure of water filled with lotuses. {10}
“For those who are thrown from a mountain into burning coals By malefactors to harm them, The flames become lotus sprouts in a pond of water If they remember my name.

nga yi ming ni skad 'ga' yud tsam rjes dran na/ / rgya mtsho'i chur bor de yi nang du 'chir mi 'gyur/ / chu bos mi khyer me yi dbus su 'tshig mi 'gyur/ / don med kun tu mi 'gyur don rnams 'grub par 'gyur/ /

“Anyone who instantly remembers my name When thrown into the sea will not die there. They will not be swept away by rivers or burn in the midst of fire. In everything they will not fail but will be successful. {11}
“Thrown into the sea, they will not die, Nor will they be swept away by a river or burned in fire: No harm will come to them, but rather benefit instead, If they remember my name, even for a while.

shing sgrog dbyig chings lcags sgrog de bzhin ltung rnams dang / / brnyas shing khyad bsad de bzhin bring cing bslus pa dang / / spyos shing bsdigs te gshe dang sma phab rnam pa las/ / nga yi ming tsam dran par byas na thar pa thob/ /
“From fetters, chains, and beatings, Scorn, humiliation, and constraint, Abuse, whipping, threats, and scolding, Those who remember my name will gain release.

gang rnams shar gnyer sna tshogs glags lta ji snyed dang / / gang rnams rtag tu zhe sdang mi snyan brjod pa'i rnams/ / nga yi ming thos dran byas snyan par brjod par 'gyur/ / mthong ba tsam gyis mod la byams pa'i sems kyang skye/ /

“All those who are hostile and seek to harm, Who are always angry and speak unpleasant words, Will become friendly the moment they see Those who have heard and remember my name and will praise them. {13}
“The inimical, faultfinders, Those who always maliciously slander, Become friendly on sight When they hear my name remembered.
nga yi ming tsam la la gang gis dran byas na/ / gnod pa'i don du ro langs sngags dang byad byed pa'i/ / dgra rnams rtag tu de yi zil gyis non par 'gyur/ / ma lus dug gis de yi lus la mi tshugs so/ /
“Anyone who remembers my name Will always overpower those enemies Who, in order to harm, practice vetāla mantras and sorcery, And they will not be harmed by any poison. {14}

la la gang gis nga yi ming tsam dran byas na/ / klu dbang srin tshogs mkha' lding sha za thams cad dang / / grul bum srul po 'tshe byed gtum pa'i sems ldan dang / / mdangs 'phrog 'jigs byed rmi lam 'ong ba'ang zhi bar 'gyur/ /

“Those who have remembered my name will pacify All nāga lords, hordes of rākṣasas, garuḍas, piśācas, Kumbhāndas, and pūtanas who with wrathful minds cause harm, Who steal vitality, and who terrify in dreams. {15}

“Evil magicians trying to kill them are appeased, And no poison can injure those who remember my name. “Malicious spirits, fiends, demons, and goblins, life-sapping, dangerous, Are all quelled, even in dreams, once my name is recalled.

nga yi ming ni skad cig yud tsam dran byas kyang / / pha dang ma dang gnyen gshes mdza' ba kun dang yang / / 'bral bar mi 'gyur sdang dang 'grogs par de bzhin min/ / nor zad mi 'gyur phongs pa'i dngos su mi 'gyur ro/ /
“One will not be separated from family and friends Or be joined with the unfriendly Or become materially destitute, If one remembers my name, even for a while.
nga yi ming gi rjes su la la dran byed na/ / 'di nas shi 'phos mnar med sems dmyal mi 'gro ste/ / byol song skye gnas yi mi khom gnas su min/ / sems can dag pa lha dang mi yi gnas su skye/ /
“Anyone who remembers my name Will not go to the Avīci hell when they die But will be reborn as a good being, a deva or human, And not as an animal or a preta, or in an unfortunate existence. {17}
“Those who remember my name will not go to hell Or become animals or ghosts Or fall into other unfavorable states; They will be reborn as celestial or human, purified beings.

nga yi ming ni la la gang gis dran byas na/ / dmus long zhar ba 'on pa zha bor mi 'gyur te/ / theng po long bar mi 'gyur gsal smra blta sdug 'gyur/ / bskal ba bye ba mang por dbang po kun ldan 'gyur/ /

“Those who remember my name will become humans Who are not blind, one-eyed, deaf, unable to walk, Or with a limp, but who speak clearly and have a pleasant appearance, And they will possess all faculties for many millions of kalpas. {18}
“People remembering my name will not Be blind, deaf, or infirm; They will not be violent, but friendly And sound in mind and body for countless ages.
{19}[1265] those who make offerings of flowers, incense, and so on to me will be reborn in my buddha realm.
“Those who scatter a handful of flowers over me, Calling my name, go to my refuge of bliss; Those who give me offerings with a clear mind Will be worthy of receiving offerings in my buddha-land.

la la gang gis nga yi ming ni rjes dran na/ / sems can dag pa 'di nas shi 'phos phyogs bcu yi/ / 'jig rten khams su sangs rgyas mngon sum skye bar 'gyur/ / sangs rgyas mthong 'gyur de dag chos kyang thos par 'gyur/ /

“Anyone who remembers my name Will be a pure being who on passing away will be reborn In the presence of buddhas in world realms in the ten directions, Will see the buddhas, and will hear their Dharma. {20}
“Purified beings, passing away, are born here, Face to face with the buddhas of all worlds; Those who remember my name see the buddhas And hear their teaching.

'di dang de bzhin gzhan dag thabs mang ji snyed kyis/ / 'gro ba sems can nga 'dul gzhal dang zad mi nus/ / sangs rgyas sras po ngas ni rnam thar gcig bsgom ste/ / yon tan can gyi yon tan thams cad ngas mi shes/ /

“These and all my many other methods For guiding beings in worlds are endless and innumerable. Son of the buddhas, I meditate on this one liberation, But I do not know all the qualities of those with qualities.” {21}
“By this and infinite other means I guide sentient beings in the world; I have developed one liberation, And cannot know all the virtues of the virtuous.
Sudhana has tirelessly studied with kalyāṇamitras in worlds in the ten directions. {22}[1266]

“Sudhana has attended spiritual benefactors In the worlds of the ten directions And has not tired of hearing the teaching of the offspring of Buddha; Why would joy not arise while hearing the Teaching?”

de'i tshe byang chub sems dpa' gzhan du mi 'gro ba zhes bya ba/ shar phyogs nas nam mkha'i dbyings las 'ongs te mi mjed kyi 'jig rten gyi khams kyi khor yug gi rtse mor 'dug go/ byang chub sems dpa' gzhan du mi 'gro bas/ mi mjed kyi 'jig rten gyi khams khor yug gi rtse mo la rkang pa gnyis por ma thag tu/ mi mjed kyi 'jig rten gyi khams 'di rnam ba drug tu g.yos te/ rin po che du ma'i rang bzhin du kun nas gnas par gyur to/ /

At that time the bodhisattva Ananyagāmin came from the east through the sky and resided on a peak of the Cakravāla mountain range in the Sahā world realm. The moment that the bodhisattva Ananyagāmin’s feet landed on a peak of the Cakravāla mountain range in the Sahā world realm, the Sahā world realm shook in six ways and transformed into being composed of many jewels.

At that moment an enlightening being named Ananyagamin descended from the eastern sky and stood on the top of the mountain range surrounding this world. As soon as he set foot on the mountain, the whole world quaked and appeared to be made of jewels.

byang chub sems dpa' gzhan du mi 'gro ba des/ nyi ma dang / zla ba'i 'od thams cad zil gyis non pa dang / lha dang / klu dang / gnod sbyin dang / dri za dang / lha ma yin dang / nam mkha' lding dang / mi'am ci dang / lto 'phye chen po dang / brgya byin dang / tshangs pa dang / 'jig rten gyi mgon po dang / me dang / rin po che dang / glog dang / skar ma'i 'od kyang zil gyis non pa de lta bu'i 'od lus bkye ste/

The bodhisattva Ananyagāmin outshone the light of the sun and moon. The light from his body outshone devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, Śakra, Brahmā, the world guardians, fire, jewels, lightning, and starlight.
The body of that enlightening being gave off such a light that the sun and moon were overwhelmed, the lights of all realms of being, fire, jewels, and stars were obscured,

sems can dmyal ba chen po dag kyang snang bar byas/ byol song gi skye gnas dang / gshin rje'i 'jig rten gyi lam gyi rgyud thibs po thams cad kyang snang bar byas te/ ngan song gi sdug bsngal thams cad kyang de ma thag tu zhi'o/ / sems can thams cad kyi nyon mongs pa'ang nyams su mi gnod par gyur to/ / mya ngan gyi zug rngu dang / sdug bsngal sna tshogs kyang rtse zil bar gyur to/ / sangs rgyas kyi zhing sa thams cad du'ang rin po che'i sprin gyi char phab ste/ me tog dang / spos dang / bdug pa dang / phreng ba dang / byug pa dang / phye ma dang / na bza' dang / gdugs dang / rgyal mtshan dang / ba dan gyi rgyan thams cad dang ldan pa'i mchod pa sna tshogs kyi sprin gyi char yang mngon par phab ste/

He even illuminated the great hells. He illuminated all dark existences in the realm of animals and the world of Yama. He caused all the sufferings in the lower existences to instantly cease. All beings ceased to be tormented by the kleśas. Various kinds of misery, pain, and suffering were alleviated. Rain from clouds of jewels fell over all of this buddha realm, and there also fell rain from clouds of a variety of offerings, the entire display of flowers, perfumes, incense, garlands, ointments, powders, clothing, parasols, banners, and flags.

the great hells were lit up, the dark recesses of the realms of animals and ghosts were illumined, all ills and miseries were allayed, sentient beings were not bound by afflictions, and all sorrows ceased. He also appeared to go to the buddha, causing clouds of all kinds of offerings—jewels, flowers, perfumes, garlands, robes, parasols, banners—to rain all over the buddha-land,

bcom ldan 'das gang na ba der song ngo/ / de'i lus de'i gzugs brnyan ni/ sems can thams cad kyi gnas su snang ba ste/ bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du sim par byed pa la mngon par gzhol bas/ ri gru 'dzin de la byang chub sems dpa' spyan ras gzigs kyi dbang po'i drung du'ang phyin par snang ngo/ /

He then went to where the Bhagavat was, and the image of his body appeared in the residences of all beings, appearing so as to satisfy them in accordance with their wishes. He also appeared to come before the bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.

and he also appeared reflected in the abodes of all beings, appearing to them so as to please them according to their inclinations, and he also appeared to have come to the enlightening being Avalokiteshvara on the peak of Mount Potalaka.

de nas byang chub sems dpa' spyan ras gzigs kyi dbang pos/ tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la 'di skad ces smras so/ / rigs kyi bu khyod kyis byang chub sems dpa' gzhan du mi 'gro ba/ 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor 'dir phyin pa mthong ngam/ smras pa/ 'phags pa/ mthong ngo/ /
Then the bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara said to Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, “Noble one, did you see the bodhisattva Ananyagāmin coming to the gathering of this assembly?
Then Avalokiteshvara said to Sudhana, “Do you see the enlightening being Ananyagamin in this assembly?” Sudhana said, “Yes.”

smras pa/ rigs kyi bu/ byang chub sems dpa' gzhan du mi 'gro ba'i gan du song la/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bya ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bya ba dris shig/
“Depart, noble one. Go to the bodhisattva Ananyagāmin and ask him, ‘How should a bodhisattva train in bodhisattva conduct? How should a bodhisattva practice it?’ ”
Avalokiteshvara said, “Go to Ananyagamin and ask him how to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings.”

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis/ byang chub sems dpa' spyan ras gzigs kyi dbang po'i rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te/ byang chub sems dpa' spyan ras gzigs kyi dbang po la lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas/ byang chub sems dpa' spyan ras gzigs kyi dbang po'i drung nas song ngo/ /

Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, bowed his head to the feet of the bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, circumambulated the bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara many hundreds of thousands of times, keeping him to his right, and, looking back again and again, departed from the bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
So then Sudhana paid his respects to Avalokiteshvara and went.

d.crumb: [byang chub sems dpa' gzhan du mi 'gro ba]

f.d: [byang chub sems dpa' gzhan du mi 'gro ba]
Chapter 31. Ananyagāmin
Ananyagamin

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang / byang chub sems dpa' spyan ras gzigs kyi dbang po'i ye shes kyi gting ma rnyed pa'i sems kyis/ spyan ras gzigs kyi dbang po bltas pas kyang ma ngoms bzhin du bsgo ba dang mi 'gal bar byang chub sems dpa' gzhan du mi 'gro ba gang na ba der song ste/

Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, his mind having acquired Avalokiteśvara’s verses of wisdom,[1267] had not had enough of gazing on the bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, but so as not to disobey his instruction, Sudhana went to where the bodhisattva Ananyagāmin was.
Then Sudhana, with Avalokiteshvara’s verse of knowledge in mind, had not seen enough of Avalokiteshvara but obeyed his words and went to the enlightening being Ananyagamin.
byang chub sems dpa' gzhan du mi 'gro ba'i rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal nas/ mdun du 'dug ste thal mo sbyar nas 'di skad ces smras so/ /
He bowed his head to the feet of the bodhisattva Ananyagāmin. Then he stood before him and, with his hands placed together in homage, said,
Paying his respects, Sudhana said,

'phags pa/ bdag gis bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed na; ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bgyi ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bgyi ba ma 'tshal te/
“Ārya, I have developed the aspiration for the highest, complete enlightenment, but I do not know how bodhisattvas should train in bodhisattva conduct and in what way they should practice it.
“Noble one, I have set my mind on supreme perfect enlightenment, but I do not know how to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings.

'phags pa ni byang chub sems dpa' rnams la gdams ngag dang / rjes su bstan pa mdzad do zhes bdag gis thos na/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bgyi ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bgyi ba 'phags pas bdag la bshad du gsol/
“Ārya, I have heard that you give instruction and teachings to bodhisattvas! Explain to me how bodhisattvas should train in bodhisattva conduct and how they should practice it!”
I hear you give enlightening beings instruction, so please tell me how an enlightening being is to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings.”
des smras pa/ rigs kyi bu/ nga ni byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa'i sgo kun tu 'gro ba thob pa'o/ /
Then the bodhisattva Ananyagāmin said, “Noble one, I have attained the bodhisattva liberation called the arising of every gateway.”[1268]
Ananyagamin said, “I have attained an enlightening liberation ‘speeding forth in all directions.’”

smras pa/ 'phags pa khyod kyis de bzhin gshegs pa gang gi zhabs kyi drung nas/ byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa sgo kun tu 'gro ba zhes bgyi ba 'di brnyes/ / 'jig rten gyi khams de ni 'di nas ji srid cig na mchis/ 'jig rten gyi khams de nas bzhud nas ni ji srid cig lags/

Sudhana asked, “Ārya, at the feet of which tathāgata did you attain the bodhisattva liberation called the arising of every gateway? How far from here is that world realm? How long did it take to come from that world realm?”
Sudhana asked, “What buddha did you learn it from? How far away is that buddha’s world, and when did you leave that world?”

smras pa/ rigs kyi bu/ gnas 'di ni/ lha dang mi dang lha ma yin du bcas pa'i 'jig rten dang / dge sbyong dang bram zer bcas pa'i skye dgus kyang shes par dka' ste/ de ni byang chub sems dpa'i mthu dang / byang chub sems dpa'i brtson 'grus mi ldog pa dang / byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa mi 'phrog pa'i yul te/

The bodhisattva Ananyagāmin said, “Noble one, this is something that is difficult to comprehend for beings such as the śramaṇas and brahmins in this world with its devas, humans, and asuras. It is the power of the bodhisattvas, the irreversible diligence of the bodhisattvas, and the unsurpassable conduct of the bodhisattvas.

Ananyagamin said, “This point is hard for celestial, human, and titanic beings, for monks and priests, to know, being the power of an enlightening being, the unregressing energy of an enlightening being, the accomplishment of the energy of an enlightening being.

de ni rigs kyi bu/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyis yongs su ma zin pa/ sangs rgyas kyis ma dgongs pa/ dge ba'i rtsa ba ma bsags pa/ bsam pa yongs su ma dag pa/ byang chub sems dpa'i dbang po ma thob pa/ shes rab kyi mig dang mi ldan pa rnams kyis thos pa'am/ yongs su gzung ba'am/ yid ches pa'am/ khong du chud par bya bar mi nus so/ /

“Noble one, those who are not in the care of a kalyāṇamitra, who are not regarded by the buddhas, who have not accumulated the roots of merit, who do not have a pure motivation, who have not attained the faculties of a bodhisattva, and who do not have the eyes of wisdom will not be able to hear of it, grasp it, believe in it, or comprehend it.”

It cannot be heard or retained or believed in or comprehended by those who are not under the tutelage of spiritual benefactors, who are not under the attention of buddhas, who have no accumulated roots of goodness, who have not purified their intentions, who have not attained the faculties of enlightening beings, who do not have the eye of wisdom.”
smras pa/ sangs rgyas kyi mthu dang dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi gzungs kyis dad pa dang mos par bgyi na 'phags pas bdag la bka' mi stsal tam/
Sudhana said, “Tell it to me, for I am apprehended[1269] by the buddhas and in the care of kalyāṇamitras, and I have faith and aspiration!”
Sudhana said, “Please tell me, noble one—I will believe, I will have faith, by the empowerment of buddhas and the assistance of spiritual benefactors.”

des smras pa/ rigs kyi bu/ nga ni shar phyogs kyi 'jig rten gyi khams dpal gyi snying po dang ldan pa/ de bzhin gshegs pa dpal kun nas yang dag par 'byung ba'i sangs rgyas kyi zhing nas 'ongs te/ de bzhin gshegs pa dpal kun nas yang dag par 'byung ba'i zhabs kyi drung nas/ ngas byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar bsgo kun tu 'gro ba 'di thob bo/ /

The bodhisattva Ananyagāmin said, “Noble one, I have come from a world realm in the eastern direction that is called Śrīgarbhavatī, the buddha realm of the Tathāgata Samantaśrīsaṃbhava. I obtained the bodhisattva liberation called the arising of every gateway at the feet of the Tathāgata Samantaśrīsaṃbhava.

Ananyagamin said, “I come from the buddha-land of a buddha named Born of Universal Light in a world to the east called Full of Light. I attained the enlightening liberation ‘speeding forth in all directions’ at the feet of that buddha.

rigs kyi bu/ 'jig rten gyi khams dpal gyi snying po dang ldan pa de nas nga song nas ni/ bskal pa sangs rgyas kyi zhing brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed cig 'das te/
“Noble one, as many kalpas as there are atoms in an anabhilāpyānabhilāpya of buddha realms passed while I came from the world realm Śrīgarbhavatī.
As many eons as atoms in untold buddha-lands have passed since I left that world Full of Light.

sems bskyed pa re re zhing yang gom pa sangs rgyas kyi zhing brjod du med pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed cig por ro/ / gom pa re res kyang sangs rgyas kyi zhing brjod du med pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi sangs rgyas kyi zhing 'das te/ sangs rgyas kyi zhing de dag thams cad kyang / de bzhin gshegs pa dang ldan par shes te/ sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das de dag thams cad la'ang de bzhin gshegs pa'i mchod pa bla na med pa/ yid kyi rang bzhin chos nyid mngon par 'du bya ba med pa'i rgyas btab pa/ de bzhin gshegs pas gnang ba/ byang chub sems dpa'i dga' ba yongs su bskyed pas mthong ba byas so/ /

“With each development of an aspiration, I took as many steps as there are atoms in an anabhilāpyānabhilāpya of buddha realms. With each step, I passed as many buddha realms as there are atoms in an anabhilāpyānabhilāpya of buddha realms. There was a tathāgata in each of those buddha realms, and I perceived all those buddha bhagavats. To all those tathāgatas I made offerings that were authorized by the tathāgatas and were unsurpassable, composed of the mind, and sealed by the noncomposite nature of phenomena and gave rise to joy in bodhisattvas.

With each thought I take as many steps as atoms in untold buddha-lands, and with each step I pass as many buddha-lands as atoms in untold buddha-lands, in all of which are buddhas. I go to all those buddhas, and honor each buddha with the finest mentally produced offerings, stamped with the cosmic seal that has no formation, approved by the buddhas, pleasing to all enlightening beings.

'jig rten gyi khams de dag na/ sems can gyi khams rgya mtsho ji snyed pa de dag thams cad kyang mthong ste/ de dag thams cad kyi sems rgya mtsho'ang khong du chud do/ / de dag thams cad kyi dbang po'i 'khor lo yang yongs su shes shing bsam pa dang mos pa ji lta bzhin du gzugs kyi lus yongs su bstan to/ / chos kyi dbyings rab tu bsgrags so/ / 'od kyi dkyil 'khor yongs su bkye'o/ / yo byad sna tshogs phun sum tshogs pas kyang nye bar sdud do/ / rang gi lus kyang de dag la byin gyis brlabs te; de ni yongs su smin par bya ba dang / gdul ba'i sbyor ba rgyun mi 'chad pa'i phyir ro/ /

“I saw in those world realms an ocean of beings, and I perceived the ocean of all their minds. I knew the wheels of all their faculties, and I manifested physical bodies in accord with their aspirations, proclaimed the words of the Dharma, radiated a halo of light, brought them the gift of various necessities, and empowered my own body, so that I could continuously be engaged in ripening and guiding them.

I also observe the oceans of sentient beings in all the worlds, penetrate their minds, discern their faculties, and appear to them bodily in accord with their inclinations and interests, speak of the Teaching, radiate auras of light, and provide them with various material necessities. I adapt my form for them, ceaselessly striving to guide them to perfection.

shar phyogs nas ji ltar 'ongs pa de bzhin du lho phyogs dang / nub phyogs dang / byang phyogs dang / byang shar gyi phyogs mtshams dang / shar lho'i phyogs mtshams dang / lho nub kyi phyogs mtshams dang / nub byang gi phyogs mtshams dang / 'og dang / steng gi phyogs nas kyang de bzhin te/

“In the same way that I came from the east, I came from the south, from the west, from the north, from the northeast, from the southeast, from the southwest, from the northwest, from below, and from above.
And just as I proceed in the east, so do I also proceed in the south, west, north, northeast, southeast, southwest, northwest, the nadir and the zenith.

rigs kyi bu/ ngas ni byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa sgo kun tu 'gro ba zhes bya ba 'di shes par zad na/ ngas byang chub sems dpa' phyogs kun tu mngon par gzhol ba tha mi dad pa'i ye shes kyi yul dang ldan pa/ chos kyi dbyings thams cad du lus rnam par bkod pa/ sems can thams cad kyi bsam pa dang / mos pa ji lta ba bzhin du mthun par spyod pa/ zhing thams cad lus kyis rgyas par 'gengs pa/ chos thams cad kyi rgyud kyi rjes su song ba/ dus gsum gyi rgyud mnyam pa nyid du gyur pa/ chos kyi phyogs kyi rgyud dang mnyam pa nyid du gyur pa'i lus dang ldan pa/ 'gro ba'i rgyud thams cad du rnam par snang ba/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i rgyud thams cad la rnam par rtog pa med pa/ chags pa med pa'i rgyud thams cad khong du chud pa/ gnas med pa'i rgyud la rab tu gnas pa de dag gi spyod pa shes pa'am/ yon tan brjod par yang nus re skan/

“Noble one, I know only the bodhisattva liberation called the arising of every gateway. How could I know the conduct or describe the qualities of bodhisattvas who face in all directions; who have a scope of wisdom that is without division; who distribute their bodies throughout the realm of phenomena; who act in accord with the thoughts and aspirations of all beings; who pervade all realms with their bodies; who act in conformance with all phenomena; who have arrived at the equality of the three times; who have bodies that are equal to the range of phenomena in every direction; who illuminate every range of worlds of beings; who have no conceptualization of the range of tathāgatas; who enter all regions without impediment; and who dwell in the state that has no location?

“I only know this enlightening liberation speeding in all directions. How can I know the practice or tell of the virtue of the enlightening beings who go everywhere, who face in all directions, who are in the realm of unfragmented knowledge, whose bodies are distributed evenly throughout all universes, who adapt their action to all sentient beings according to the inclinations and interests of those beings, whose bodies pervade all lands, who act in accord with the way things really are, who have realized the equality of past, present, and future, who accord with the equality of all places, who illumine the paths of all beings, who do not have arbitrary notions of buddhahood, who go along all paths without attachment or obstruction, who stand on the path of nonreliance?

song / rigs kyi bu/ lho phyogs kyi rgyud 'di nyid na grong khyer sgo dang ldan pa zhes bya ba yod de/ de na lha lha chen po zhes bya ba 'dug gi /de'i gan du song la/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bya ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bya ba dris shig /

“Depart, noble one. In this southern region, there is a city named Dvāravatī. There dwells the deity by the name of Mahādeva. Go to him and ask him, ‘How should a bodhisattva train in bodhisattva conduct? How should a bodhisattva practice it?’ ”
“South of here is a city called Dvaravati, where the celestial Mahadeva lives. Go ask him how to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings.”

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis/ byang chub sems dpa' gzhan du mi 'gro ba'i rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te/ byang chub sems dpa' gzhan du mi 'gro ba la lan brgya stong du mar g.yas su bskor ba byas nas yang dang yang bltas te/ byang chub sems dpa' gzhan du mi 'gro ba'i drung nas song ngo/ /

Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, bowed his head to the feet of the bodhisattva Ananyagāmin, circumambulated the bodhisattva Ananyagāmin many hundreds of thousands of times, keeping him to his right, and, looking back again and again, departed from the bodhisattva Ananyagāmin.
So Sudhana paid his respects to the enlightening being Ananyagamin and went on.
[lha lha chen po]
Chapter 32. Mahādeva
Mahadeva

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa rgya chen po'i rjes su song ba'i sems dang ldan pa/ byang chub sems dpa' gzhan du mi 'gro ba'i ye shes kyi spyod yul 'dod pa'i ngang tshul can/ mngon par shes pa chen po/ mngon par bsgrubs pa'i yul la yon tan gyi khyad par du lta ba/ brtson 'grus brtan pa'i go cha rab tu dga' ba'i khyad par thob pa/ bsam gyis mi khyab pa'i rnam par thar pas rnam par rtse ba'i rjes su song ba'i bsam pa dang ldan pa de/ byang chub sems dpa'i yon tan gyi sa la ni nan tan du byed/ ting nge 'dzin gyi sa la ni rnam par dpyod/ gzungs kyi sa la ni rab tu gnas par byed/ smon lam gyi sa la ni 'jug par byed/ tha dad pa yang dag par shes pa'i sa la rjes su slob/ stobs kyis ni yongs su sgrub cing

Sudhana had a mind that followed the vast conduct of bodhisattvas. He had the nature of longing for the scope of the wisdom of the bodhisattva Ananyagāmin. He saw the special qualities of accomplishing great higher cognition. He had attained joy in the armor of stable diligence. He had the aspiration to follow the displays[1270] of inconceivable liberations. He practiced the qualities of the bodhisattva level. He analyzed on the level of samādhi. He was established on the level of the power of retention. He engaged in the level of prayer. He trained in the level of discernment. He was accomplishing the level of power.

His mind following the far-reaching practice of enlightening beings, eager to embody the sphere of knowledge of the enlightening being Ananyagamin, seeing the excellence of the qualities of the realm of exercise of great mystic knowledge, girding himself with the armor of steadfast vigor, full of joy, his mind on the freedom of inconceivable liberation, accomplishing the virtues of enlightening beings, practicing concentration, establishing mental command, entering into vows, learning powers of analysis and expression, bringing forth power,
mthar gyis grong khyer sgo dang ldan pa gang na ba der song ste/ lha lha chen po kun tu dris pa dang / de la 'gro ba mang pos bstan pa/
He eventually arrived at the city named Dvāravatī. He inquired about the deity Mahādeva, and many people declared to him,
Sudhana went to the city of Dvaravati and asked for Mahadeva. The people of the city told Sudhana,
rigs kyi bu/ 'di re/ lha lha chen po grong khyer gyi lam gyi bzhi mdo na/ bdag nyid shin tu che bas sems can rnams la chos ston cing 'dug go;
“Noble one, this[1271] deva Mahādeva is in the temple[1272] at the crossroads of the city, and with greatness of being he is teaching the Dharma to beings.”
“This Mahadeva is in a temple at a crossroads in the city expounding the Teaching in a giant body.”
de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang lha lha chen po gang na ba der song ste/ lha lha chen po'i rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te/ mdun du 'dug ste thal mo sbyar nas 'di skad ces smras so/ /
Then Sudhana went to where the deity Mahādeva was. He bowed his head to the feet of Mahādeva, stood before him with his hands together in homage, and said,
Sudhana then went to Mahadeva, paid his respects, and said,

'phags pa/ bdag gis bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed na/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bgyi ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bgyi ba ma 'tshal te/ 'phags pa ni/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams la gdams ngag dang / rjes su bstan pa mdzad do zhes bdag gis thos na/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bgyi ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bgyi ba 'phags pas bdag la bshad du gsol/

“Ārya, I have developed the aspiration for the highest, complete enlightenment. How does a bodhisattva train in bodhisattva conduct? In what way does a bodhisattva practice it? Ārya, I have heard that you teach and give instructions to bodhisattvas. Therefore, Ārya, teach me how bodhisattvas train in bodhisattva conduct and in what way they practice it!”

“Noble one, I have set my mind on supreme perfect enlightenment, but I do not know how to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings. I hear that you give enlightening beings instruction, and wish you would tell me how to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings.”

de nas lha lha chen pos lag pa bzhi phyogs bzhir brkyang ste/ rgya mtsho chen po bzhi las shin tu myur ba'i shugs kyis chu blangs te/ bdag gi gdong bkrus nas/ tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la gser gyi me tog gis gtor te 'di skad ces smras so/ /

The deity Mahādeva extended his four arms, and from the four great oceans and with the power of great speed he brought water and washed his mouth. He then scattered golden flowers on Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, and said,
Then the celestial Mahadeva extended four hands in four directions, brought water from the oceans with extreme speed and washed his face; he scattered golden flowers over Sudhana and said,

rigs kyi bu/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams ni mthong bar shin tu dka' ste/ thos par yang rab tu dka'o/ / skyes bu mchog gi me tog pun da ri ka ni 'jig rten gyi phul du bya ba yin par ngos tshar rmad du byung ba yin te/ 'jig rten gyi gnas su gyur pa'o/ / 'gro ba'i rten du gyur pa'o/ / sems can rnams la snang ba chen po 'byin pa'o/ / lam rmongs pa rnams la lam bde ba ston pa'o/ / chos kyi tshul du gzud pa la mgon du gyur pa'o/ / thams cad mkhyen pa'i grong khyer du phyin par bya ba la ded dpon chen po gyur pa ste/ de la kho bo 'di snyam du sems so/ /

“Noble one, it is very difficult to see the bodhisattvas. It is difficult to hear them. The appearance of the white lotuses that are supreme beings is a great marvel because of its greatness; they are a support for the world, a refuge for beings; they create a great light for beings; they teach the path of truth to those on the path of ignorance; they are guides for those who follow the way of the Dharma; they are great guides for going to the city of omniscience.

“Enlightening beings are hard to get to see, extremely hard to get to hear. They rarely appear in the world, being so exalted. They are supreme lotuses of humanity, saviors of the world, refuges for the world, reliances for the world. They are great suns, makers of light for sentient beings, the ones who show the path of safety and peace to those on the path of delusion. They are guides to the truth, leaders on the way to the citadel of omniscience.

byang chub sems dpa' sems dpa' chen po rnams kyi ming ni sems dri ma med pa rnams la rang gi lus kyi gzugs brnyan ston cing / lus rnam par dag pa rnams la mngon par snang ba dang / ngag gi nyes pa spangs pa rnams dbyangs kyi snang ba yongs su gdon par byed pa dang / bsam pa dag pa rnams la dus thams cad du mngon sum du gyur par gnas pas lta ba ngan pa 'joms pa yin par bsams so/ /

“Noble one,[1273] this is what I think: the bodhisattva mahāsattvas are called the destroyers of wrong views because, with stainless minds, they manifest the appearance of their pure bodies; they manifest the activities[1274] of their pure bodies; they shine the light of eloquence of their faultless speech; and with a pure motivation they remain manifest at all times.

I think ‘killer of wrong views’ is the name for enlightening beings, in that they manifest themselves to those whose minds are undefiled, they appear before those whose deeds are pure, they imbue those who are free from evils of speech with the light of eloquence, and at all times they stand before those whose intentions are purified.
rigs kyi bu/ kho bo ni byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa sprin gyi dra ba thob pa'o/ /
“Noble one, I have attained the bodhisattva liberation called the net of clouds.”
Son, I have attained an enlightening liberation called ‘cloud net.’”
smras pa/ 'phags pa/ byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa sprin gyi dra ba de'i yul ji lta bu zhig mchis/
Sudhana asked him, “What is the scope of the bodhisattva liberation called the net of clouds?”
Sudhana asked, “What is the sphere of this ‘cloud net’ liberation?”
de nas lha lha chen pos tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gi mdun du ri chen po tsam gyi gser gyi phung po dang / dngul gyi phung po dang / bai DUr+ya'i phung po dang / shel gyi phung po dang /
In every direction in front of Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, the deva Mahādeva manifested mountain-sized heaps of gold, heaps of silver, heaps of beryls, heaps of crystals,
At that moment the celestial Mahadeva manifested a heap of gold the size of a mountain before Sudhana, as well as a heap of silver, a heap of lapis lazuli, a heap of crystals,
mus ra gal pa'i phung po dang / asmra gar b+ha'i phung po dang / nor bu rin po che ngang gis snang ba'i phung po dang / nor bu rin po che dri ma med pa snying po'i phung po dang /
heaps of white corals, heaps of emeralds, heaps of precious asteria jewels, heaps of precious vimalagarbha jewels,
a heap of coral, a heap of emeralds, a heap of starry jewels, a heap of clear jewels,
nor bu rin po che rnam par snang ba'i phung po dang /
heaps of precious vairocana jewels,
a heap of radiant jewels,
nor bu rin po che phyogs kun tu mngon pa'i phung po dang /
a heap of jewels with facets facing in all directions,
gtsug gi nor bu rin po che dang / cod pan gyi phung po dang /
heaps of precious topknot jewels, heaps of crowns,
a heap of crown jewels, a heap of varicolored jewels,
nor bu rin po che sna tshogs kyi se mo do'i phung po dang /
heaps of necklaces made of various precious jewels,
a heap of necklaces,
dpung rgyan gyi phung po dang /
heaps of armlets,
rna cha'i rgyan gyi phung po dang / gdu bu'i phung po dang /
heaps of earrings, heaps of bracelets,
a heap of earrings, a heap of bracelets,
ska rags kyi phung po dang / rkang gdub kyi phung po dang / mu tig dmar po'i dra ba'i phung po dang / nor bu rin po che sna tshogs kyi phung po dang /
heaps of girdles, heaps of anklets, heaps of strings of red pearls,[1275] heaps of various precious jewels,
a heap of belts, a heap of anklets,
yan lag dang nying lag thams cad kyi rgyan gyi phung po dang / nor bu rin po che yid bzhin gyi rgyal po'i phung po dang /
heaps of adornment for the greater and smaller parts of the body, heaps of the kings of wish-fulfilling precious jewels,
me tog thams cad dang / spos thams cad dang /
all flowers, all perfumes,
a heap of various kinds of flowers, fragrances,
bdug pa thams cad dang / phreng ba thams cad dang / byug pa thams cad dang / phye ma thams cad dang /
all incenses, all garlands, all ointments, all powders,
incenses, garlands, unguents, aromatic powders,
gos thams cad dang / gdugs thams cad dang / rgyal mtshan thams cad dang / lha'i ba dan thams cad dang /
all cloths, all parasols, all banners, all flags,
robes, parasols, banners, pennants,
rol mo brdung ba thams cad dang / rol mo dkrol ba thams cad dang / 'dod pa'i yul thams cad dang / bu mo bye ba brgya stong grangs med pa dag kyang nye bar bstan nas/
all musical instruments, all percussion instruments, all that is desirable, and countless trillions of maidens.
musical instruments, and all objects of desire.
tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la 'di skad ces smras so/ /
Mahādeva said to Sudhana, the head merchant’s son,
He then said to Sudhana,

rigs kyi bu/ 'di dag las khyer la sbyin pa mang po ni byin cig/ bsod nams mang po ni gyis shig/ de bzhin gshegs pa rnams la ni mchod cig/ sems can mang po ni sbyin pas bsdu ba'i dngos pos yongs su bsdus te/ gtong ba'i pha rol tu phyin pa la khod cig/ 'jig rten na sbyin pa la slobs shig/ gtang bar dka' ba yongs su gtang ba ni ston cig /

“Noble one, take these, and with them perform acts of great generosity! Create much merit! Make offerings to the tathāgatas! Gather many beings through generosity as a method of gathering pupils! Practice the perfection of generosity! Teach the world through generosity![1276] Give that which is difficult to give![1277]

“Take of these and give gifts, do good works, make offerings to buddhas, take care of beings by generous giving, get them to practice transcendent relinquishment, teach the world by giving, show relinquishment, which is hard to do.

rigs kyi bu khyod la kho bos ji ltar yo byad kyi rnam pas bstud pa 'di bzhin du sbyin pa'i bsam pa dang ma bral ba'i sems can tshad med pa dag gis bsam pa'i rgyud kyang gtong bas yongs su bsgo ba byed do/ / sangs rgyas dang / chos dang / dge 'dun dang / byang chub sems dpa' dang / dge ba'i bshes gnyen rnams la'ang dge ba'i rtsa ba bskyed cing / bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu yang dag par bskul ba byed do/ /

“Noble one, I gather for you this manner of things, and in that same way I establish in generosity an incalculable number of beings whose minds have an unceasing motivation to give. I cause them to generate roots of merit in the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha and the bodhisattvas and kalyāṇamitras, and I inspire them toward the highest, complete enlightenment.

In the same way as I give you all these goods, so also do I make relinquishment habitual in countless sentient beings whose sense of generosity is not repressed. Having gotten them to plant roots of goodness with the Buddha, the Teaching, and the Community, and spiritual benefactors, I get them to aspire to supreme perfect enlightenment.
rigs kyi bu/ gzhan yang kho bo ni sems can 'dod pa'i dga' bas myos pa/ yul gyi longs spyod la yongs su chags pa rnams la yul de dag ni mi sdug par byin gyis rlob bo/ /
“Moreover, noble one, I bless with the ugliness of sensory objects those beings who are intoxicated by the joys of desire and have attachment to the enjoyment of sensory objects.
“Furthermore, to those who are intoxicated with the enjoyment of objects of desire, who are very greedy for the enjoyment of objects, I make objects appear impure.

khro bas non pa dang / nga rgyal can dang / rgyags shing dregs pa dang / rlom pa tshar gcod pas 'dul ba rnams la ni gtum zhing srin po ltar mi sdug la/ 'jigs pa'i lus sha za zhing khrag 'thung ba'i tshul dang ldan bar bstan te/ rlom pa dang snyems pas 'khrug pa de dag thams cad zhi bar byed do/ /

“I manifest terrifying wrathful bodies like rākṣasas, eating flesh and drinking blood, to those who are possessed by anger, who are proud, arrogant, conceited, and haughty, and who are to be guided through destruction, pacifying all who are agitated by pride and arrogance.[1278]

To those filled with anger, those who are arrogant, conceited, proud, and haughty, those who should be led away from strife, I show terrors like fiends and ghouls who feed on flesh and blood, and show them that it is all the vehemence of arrogance.

le lo can brtson 'grus bor ba'i sems can rnams la ni me dang / chu dang / rgyal po dang / rkun po dang / gnod pa'i 'jigs pa yongs su bstan cing skyo bar byas te/ brtson 'grus rtsom pa la 'god par byed do/ /
“I manifest the danger of being harmed by fire, water, kings, and thieves for beings who are lazy and abandon diligence, causing them to be distressed and become diligent.
To those who are lazy and negligent I show the dangers of fire, water, kings, and brigands, to stir them to vigor and diligence.

de ltar thabs de dang de dag gis pha rol tu phyin pa thams cad kyi phyogs dang mi mthun pa rab tu gzhom pa dang / pha rol tu phyin pa thams cad kyi tshogs bsags pa dang / sgrib pa'i ri'i g.yang sa'i lam thams cad las yang dag par bzla ba dang / sgrib pa med pa'i chos la gzud pa'i phyir mi dge ba thams cad las rnam par bzlog ste/ dge ba thams cad phun sum tshogs pa la yang dag par 'god pa byed do/ /

“In that way, through those methods, I turn them away from that which is not virtuous and establish them in a perfection of virtue so that they may defeat all that is adverse to the perfections, gather all the accumulations of the perfections, transcend all the paths of the mountain precipices of obscurations, and enter the unobscured Dharma.

Thus with various appropriate means I turn them away from bad conduct and get them to develop good qualities, to destroy all impediments to the transcendent ways, to make the necessary preparations for the transcendent ways, to cross over all the precipitous paths on the mountains of barriers to enlightenment, and to enter the unobstructed state.

rigs kyi bu/ kho bos ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa sprin gyi dra ba 'di shes par zad na/ kho bos byang chub sems dpa' dbang po ltar nyon mongs pa'i lha ma yin rab tu 'joms pa/ chu ltar 'gro ba thams cad kyi sdug bsngal gyi me'i phung po zhi bar byed pa/ me'i phung po ltar 'gro ba thams cad gyi srid pa'i chu skems pa/ rlung ltar 'dzin pa'i mngon par chags pa thams cad kyi ri rnam par 'thor ba/ rdo rje ltar bdag gis 'du shes sra ba'i brag rab tu rnyil ba de dag gi spyod pa shes pa'am/ yon tan brjod par nus re skan/

“Noble one, I know only the bodhisattva liberation called the net of clouds. How could I know the conduct or describe the qualities of bodhisattvas[1279] who are like Indra defeating the asuras of the kleśas, who are like water extinguishing the mass of fire of the suffering of all beings, who are like a mass of flames drying up the water of the cravings of all beings, who are like a wind scattering the mountain of all clinging to attachment, and who are like thunderbolts shattering the hard rock of the perception of a self?

“I only know this ‘cloud net’ enlightening liberation. How can I know the practice or tell of the virtues of the enlightening beings who are like the celestial chief Indra, crushing the titans of affliction, who are like water, extinguishing the fire of suffering of all beings, who are like heat, evaporating the water of craving of all beings, who are like wind, shattering the mountains of all attachments, who are like thunderbolts, rending asunder the mountain of the congealed notion of self?

song / rigs kyi bu/ 'dzam bu'i gling 'di nyid kyi yul ma ga d+ha'i snying po byang chub na/ sa'i lha mo brtan ma zhes bya ba 'dug gi /de'i gan du song la/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bya ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bya ba dris shig /

“Depart, noble one. In this Jambudvīpa, in the land of Magadha, at the bodhimaṇḍa, there is the goddess of the earth who is named Sthāvarā. Go to her and ask her, ‘How should a bodhisattva train in bodhisattva conduct? How should a bodhisattva practice it?’ ”
“South of here, at the site of enlightenment in the region of Magadha in Jambudvipa, lives an earth goddess named Sthavara. Go ask her how to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings.”

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis/ lha lha chen po'i rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te/ lha lha chen po la lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas yang dang yang du bltas te/ lha lha chen po'i drung nas song ngo/ /

Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, bowed his head to the feet of the deva Mahādeva, circumambulated the deva Mahādeva many hundreds of thousands of times, keeping him to his right, and, looking back again and again, departed from the deva Mahādeva.
So then Sudhana paid his respects to Mahadeva and went on.
[sa'i lha mo brtan ma]
Chapter 33. Sthāvarā
Sthavara

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang / mthar gyis yul ma ga d+ha'i snying po byang chub tu sa'i lha mo brtan ma gang na ba der song ba dang / de 'gro ba'i tshe sa'i lha mo brgya stong phrag bcu gcig la gcig 'di skad ces 'dzer to/ /

Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, eventually reached the goddess of the earth, Sthāvarā, in the land of Magadha’s bodhimaṇḍa. When he arrived there, one million earth goddesses proclaimed to one another,
Then Sudhana went to the earth goddess Sthavara at the site of enlightenment in Magadha. Ten hundred thousand earth goddesses said to one another,

sems can thams cad kyi rten du 'gyur ba zhig ni 'di nas tshur 'ong ngo/ / de bzhin gshegs pa'i snying po can/ sems can thams cad kyi ma rig pa'i sgo nga'i sbubs 'dral bar 'gyur ba zhig ni 'di nas tshur 'ong ngo/ / chos kyi rgyal po'i rigs su byung ba/ chags pa med cing dri ma med pa'i chos kyi rgyal po'i go 'phang dam pa 'thob par 'gyur ba zhig ni 'di nas tshur 'ong ngo/ / ye shes kyi mthu bo che rdo rje'i mtshon cha can dpa' bo phas kyi rgol ba'i 'khor thams cad rab tu 'dul ba zhig 'di nas tshur 'ong ngo zhes nas/

“Someone who will be a refuge for all beings is coming here! Someone who has the essence of the tathāgatas and who will break open the enclosing egg of ignorance of all beings is coming here! Someone who is in the family of the kings of Dharma and will attain the state of an unimpeded, stainless king of the Dharma is coming here! Someone who is a hero with the thunderbolt weapon that has the great power of wisdom and who will subdue the circle of opponents is coming here!”

“Someone comes who will be a refuge for all sentient beings; a vessel of enlightenment comes who will break the shell of ignorance of all sentient beings; one who springs from the family of spiritual sovereigns comes who will put on the turban of unattached supreme purity of a spiritual sovereign; a hero bearing the mighty thunderbolt of knowledge comes who will destroy the weapons of all false teachers.”

de'i mod la lha mo brtan ma la sogs pa sa'i lha mo brgya stong phrag bcus sa chen po rab tu bskyod de/ 'brug sgra zab mo lta bu'i sgra chen po grag par byas nas/ stong gsum gyi stong chen po'i 'jig rten gyi khams 'od chen pos snang bar byas te/ lus rin po che'i rgyan dang lhab lhub thams cad kyis shin tu brgyan nas/ glog gi phreng ba'i tshogs nam mkha'i dbyings las 'gyu zhing snang ba lta bu sha stag tu byas te/

At that moment, Sthāvarā and the other one million earth goddesses shook the great earth, caused a loud sound like deep thunder, and illuminated the world realm of a billion worlds with a vast light. Their bodies were adorned by all adornments and precious jewelry. They shone and moved in the sky like a mass of streaks of lightning.

Then those earth goddesses, led by Sthavara, caused the earth to tremble, made the ocean roar, illumined the whole universe with a glorious light, and with bodies adorned with all kinds of jewelry, like bundles of lightning bolts descending from the sky,

shing thams cad kyi myu gu ni skye bar byed/ me tog gi shing thams cad ni kha 'bu bar byed/ chu klung gi rgyun thams cad ni 'bab par byed/ mtsho dang / mtshe'u dang / lu ma thams cad ni rgyas par byed/ spos chu'i char pa ni rab tu 'bab par byed/ me tog gi sprin rab tu 'thor ba'i rlung chen po ni ldang bar byed/ sil snyan bye ba khrag khrig brgya stong ni rab tu sgra sgrog par byed/ lha rdzas kyi gzhal med khang dang / rgyan gyi tshogs mang po ni rab tu 'khrol bar bed/ ba lang dang / khyu mchog dang / glang po dang / stag dang / ri kyi dbang po ni rab tu sgra 'byin par byed/ lha dang / lha ma yin dang / klu dang / 'byung po'i dbang po rnams ni 'brug sgra 'byin par byed/ ri'i dbang po chen po rnams ni phan tshun thug par byed/ gter gyi tshogs bye ba brgya stong ni mngon du 'byung bar byed cing / sa'i 'og nas 'thon to/ /

They rose up out of the ground, causing the seedlings of all trees to sprout; causing all flowering trees to blossom; causing all rivers to flow; causing lakes, ponds, and reservoirs to rise; causing a great rain of scented water to fall; causing a great wind that scattered a cloud of flowers to blow; causing a quintillion musical instruments to sound; causing a multitude of divine aerial palaces and ornaments to spread; causing the lords of cows, bulls, elephants, tigers, and deer to make their cries; causing the leaders of devas, asuras, nāgas,[1280] and bhūtas to roar; causing the great lords of mountains to clash together; and causing trillions of masses of treasures to emerge.

emerged from the surface of the earth, with all tree sprouts growing, all flowering trees blooming, all rivers flowing, all lakes and ponds rising, fragrant rains showering, great winds bearing flowers, billions of musical instruments playing, celestial palaces, ornaments, and tiaras appearing, bulls, elephants, tigers, and lions roaring, the lords of the gods, titans, serpents and spirits thundering, mountains crashing together, and hundreds of billions of treasuries surfacing.

de nas sa'i lha mo brtan mas/ tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la 'di skad ces smras so/ / rigs kyi bu khyod 'dir 'ongs pa legs so/ / sa'i phyogs 'di ni sngon khyod kyi gnas su gyur te/ kho mo'i mngon sum du dge ba'i rtsa ba bskyed pa yin na/ de'i rnam par smin pa'i phyogs 'ga' tsam blta bar 'dod dam/

Then the earth goddess Sthāvarā said to Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, “Noble one, it is excellent that you have come here.[1281] This area is where in the past you dwelled and generated roots of merit, where I am the witness for that. Do you wish to see just a fraction of their ripening?”
Then the earth goddess said to Sudhana, “Welcome. This is a spot of ground where you have planted roots of goodness, which I have witnessed. Do you want to see the results in one place?”

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis/ sa'i lha mo brtan ma'i rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te/ sa'i lha mo brtan ma la lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas/ sa'i lha mo brtan ma'i mdun du 'dug ste/ thal mo sbyar nas 'di skad ces smras so/ / 'phags ma/ 'tshal lo/ /

Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, bowed his head to the feet of the earth goddess Sthāvarā. He circumambulated the earth goddess Sthāvarā many hundreds of thousands of times, keeping her to his right. Then he stood before her and, with his hands placed together in homage, said, “Āryā, I do wish it!”
Sudhana paid his respects to the goddess and said, “I do.”
de nas sa'i lha mo brtan mas rkang pa'i mthil gyis sa chen po la brdabs te/ rin po che'i gter bye ba brgya stong grangs med pas rab tu brgyan pa bstan nas 'di skad ces smras so/ /
Then the earth goddess Sthāvarā stamped on the ground with the sole of her foot and revealed an array of countless millions of millions of precious treasures and said,
Then the goddess, touching the earth with the sole of her foot, caused it to appear adorned with hundreds of billions of deposits of countless jewels, and said to Sudhana,

rigs kyi bu/ rin po che'i gter bye ba khrag khrig brgya stong 'di dag kyang / khyod kyi rjes su 'brang ba'o/ / khyod kyi sngon du 'gro ba'o/ / khyod kyis ci dgar spyad pa'o/ / khyod kyi bsod nams kyi rnam par smin pa las byung ba'o/ / khyod kyi bsod nams kyi stobs kyis bsrungs pa'o/ / 'di las long ste/ khyod kyis ci dgos pa de dag gyis shig/

“Noble one, these millions of millions of precious treasures follow you. They go before you. You can use them as you like. They come from the ripening of your merit. They are protected by the power of your merit. You can take from among them whatever you need.

“These billions of treasuries of jewels accompany you and are at your service, to be used as you wish; they have been produced as a result of your good works and are preserved by the power of your good works. Take of them and do whatever should be done.

rigs kyi bu/ gzhan yang kho mo ni byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa ye shes thub par dka' ba'i snying po can thob pa ste/ de ltar kho mo ni byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa 'di dang ldan pas/ de bzhin gshegs pa mar me mdzad tshun chad du byang chub sems dpa'i rjes su 'brang zhing / rtag tu srung ba la zhugs pa ste/

“Noble one, moreover, I have attained the bodhisattva liberation called the essence of invincible wisdom. Through my possessing this bodhisattva liberation, since the time of the Tathāgata Dīpaṅkara I have constantly followed bodhisattvas and always protected them.

“I have attained an enlightening liberation, ‘unassailable asylum of knowledge.’ Having attained this liberation, I have constantly stayed by and protected the enlightening being Vairocana since the time of Dipankara Buddha.

de tshun chad du/ rigs kyi bu/ kho mo ni byang chub sems dpa'i sems kyi spyod pa la rnam par spyod do/ / ye shes kyi yul la 'jug go/ smon lam gyi dkyil 'khor khong du chud par byed do/ / byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa rnam par dag pa rjes su rtogs par byed do/ / ting nge 'dzin thams cad kyi tshul gyi rjes su 'brang ngo/ /

Since that time, noble one, I have practiced the mental conduct of the bodhisattvas, been immersed within the scope of wisdom, entered the domain of prayer, realized pure bodhisattva conduct, followed the ways of all samādhis,

Since then I have observed the enlightening being’s mental activity, entered his sphere of knowledge and all his vows, followed his purification of enlightening practice, gone along into all concentrations,
byang chub sems dpa'i mngon par shes pa thams cad dang / sems rgya chen pos rgyas par 'gengs so; ;
permeated the vast motivations and higher cognitions of all bodhisattvas,
pervaded the vastness of the mind of the mystic knowledges of all enlightening beings,
byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi stobs kyis dbang bsgyur ba dang / zhing gi dra ba thams cad rgyas par dgang ba dang /
and realized, possessed, and acquired mastery of the powers of all bodhisattvas, the pervasion of the network of all realms,

and have comprehended, remembered, and taken in his mastery of the powers of all enlightening beings, his insuperability like that of all enlightening beings, his pervasion of the network of all lands,

de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyis lung bstan pa yang dag par mnod pa dang / dus thams cad du mngon par 'tshang rgya ba yang dag par bstan pa dang / chos kyi 'khor lo bskor ba'i tshul thams cad dang / mdo sde yang dag par brjod pa'i chos kyi sprin gyi tshul thams cad dang /

the acquisition of prophecies from all the tathāgatas, the sight at all times of the attainment of buddhahood, all the ways of turning the wheel of the Dharma, all the ways of the clouds of Dharma that elucidate the sūtras,

his reception of the prediction of enlightenment from all buddhas, his manifestation of attainment of enlightenment in all times, his way of activating all the cycles of the Teaching, the doctrines expounded in all the scriptures,

chos snang ba chen pos snang bar bya ba'i tshul dang / sems can thams cad yongs su smin par bya ba'i tshul dang / sangs rgyas kyi rnam par 'phrul pa thams cad yang dag par bstan pa'i tshul yang rjes su rtogs par byed do/ / yang dag par 'dzin to/ / yang dag par nod do/ /
the way of illumination by the great radiance of the Dharma, the way of completely ripening all beings, and the way of the display of all the miraculous manifestations of the buddhas.
his way of revealing the vista of the great Teaching, his way of knowing how to lead all sentient beings to perfection, and his way of manifesting all the miracles that buddhas perform.

rigs kyi bu/ byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa ye shes thub par dka' ba'i snying po can 'di yang bskal pa ri rab kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi pha rol de'i yang pha rol gcig tu/ 'jig rten gyi khams zla ba'i rgyal mtshan zhes bya bar bskal pa snang bas rnam par brgyan pa la/ de bzhin gshegs pa spyan bzang po las thob ste/

“Noble one, I received this bodhisattva liberation, the essence of invincible wisdom, far beyond and even more beyond as many past kalpas as there are atoms in Sumeru, during a kalpa called Avabhāsavyūha, in a world realm called Candradhvajā, from the Tathāgata Sunetra.

“I attained this ‘unassailable asylum of knowledge’ enlightening liberation from the buddha Skillful Guide in the world Moon Banner eons ago, more eons than the number of atoms in the polar mountain, in an eon called Supernal Manifestation of Light.

rigs kyi bu/ de ltar kho mo byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa ye shes thub par dka' ba'i snying po can 'di la yongs su dpyod dpyod/ rnam par dpyod dpyod/ shin tu dpyod dpyod/ yang dag par 'phel bar byed de/ shin tu rgyas par byed byed pas/ bskal pa bzang po la thug gi bar du de bzhin gshegs pa mthong ba dang ma bral lo/ /

“Noble one, in that way, until this Bhadra kalpa, while cultivating,[1282] practicing,[1283] increasing, and augmenting this bodhisattva liberation called the essence of invincible wisdom, I have never been deprived of the sight of the tathāgatas.
Going in and out of this ‘unassailable asylum of knowledge’ liberation and causing it to expand and broaden, I have always been seeing buddhas, continuing up to this eon of virtue in the present,

de srid kyi bar gyis kho mos de bzhin gshegs pa dgra bcom pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas/ sangs rgyas kyi zhing brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed cig bsnyen bkur to/ / de bzhin gshegs pa de dag thams cad snying po byang chub tu gshegs pa'i rnam par 'phrul pa yang mthong ste/ kho mo ni de bzhin gshegs pa de dag thams cad kyi dge ba'i rtsa ba mngon sum du mthong ba'o/ /

“During that time, I have propitiated as many tathāgata arhat samyaksaṃbuddhas as there are atoms in an anabhilāpyānabhilāpya of buddha realms. I have seen the miraculous manifestation of all those tathāgatas going to the bodhimaṇḍa. I have witnessed the roots of merit of all those tathāgatas.

and now I have propitiated as many buddhas as atoms in untold buddha-lands, and I have seen the spiritual transformations of all those buddhas when they came to the site of enlightenment, and I have witnessed all those buddhas’ roots of goodness.

rigs kyi bu/ kho mos byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa ye shes thub par dka' ba'i snying po can 'di shes par zad na/ kho mos byang chub sems dpa' de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi zham ring du 'brang ba/ sangs rgyas thams cad kyi gsung gi rjes su 'brang ba/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i ye shes 'jug par dka' ba la rab tu zhugs pa/ sems kyi skad cig gis chos kyi dbyings thams cad rgyas par 'gengs pa'i shugs dang ldan pa/ de bzhin gshegs pa dang mnyam pa nyid du gyur pa'i lus dang ldan pa/ sangs rgyas thams cad kyi dgongs pa dri ma med pa'i snying por gyur pa/ sangs rgyas byung ba thams cad du rtag tu mngon par bsgrubs pa/ sangs rgyas kyi 'phrin las tha mi dad pa'i pho nyar gyur pa/ de dag gi spyod pa shes pa'am/ yon tan brjod par nus re skan/

“Noble one, I know only the bodhisattva liberation called the essence of invincible wisdom. How could I know the conduct or describe the qualities of bodhisattvas who attend all tathāgatas, who follow the teaching of all buddhas, who enter into the impenetrable wisdom of the tathāgatas, who have the power to pervade the entire realm of phenomena in one instant of mind, who have bodies that are the same as those of the tathāgatas, who have the essence of the stainless intention of all the buddhas, who always realize all appearances of buddhas, and who are emissaries inseparable from the activity[1284] of the buddhas?

“I know only this enlightening liberation ‘unassailable asylum of knowledge.’ How can I know the practice or tell the virtues of the enlightening beings who attend all buddhas, who remember the tales of all the buddhas, who have entered the recondite knowledge of all buddhas, who speed throughout the cosmos in a moment of thought, who are physically equal to the buddhas, who are undefiled receptacles of the mind of all buddhas, who have always effected the birth of all buddhas, who are envoys physically indivisible from all buddhas?

song / rigs kyi bu/ 'dzam bu'i gling 'di nyid kyi yul ma ga d+ha zhes bya ba na/ grong khyer ser skya'i gnas zhes bya ba yod de/ de na mtshan mo'i lha mo dpyid dang ldan pa zhes bya ba 'dug gi /de'i gan du song la/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bya ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bya ba dris shig/

“Depart, noble one. In this Jambudvīpa, in the land of Magadha, in the city of Kapilavastu, is the goddess of the night named Vāsantī. Go to her and ask her, ‘How should a bodhisattva train in bodhisattva conduct? How should a bodhisattva practice it?’ ”
“In this country Magadha in Jambudvipa is a city called Kapilavastu, where a night goddess named Vasanti lives. Go ask her how to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings.”

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis/ sa'i lha mo brtan ma'i rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te/ sa'i lha mo brtan ma la lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas/ yang dang yang bltas te/ sa'i lha mo brtan ma'i drung nas song ngo/ /

Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, bowed his head to the feet of the earth goddess Sthāvarā, circumambulated the earth goddess Sthāvarā many hundreds of thousands of times, keeping her to his right, and, looking back again and again, departed from the earth goddess Sthāvarā.
So then Sudhana paid his respects to the earth goddess Sthavara and went on.

d.crumb: [mtshan mo'i lha mo dpyid dang ldan pa]

f.d: [mtshan mo'i lha mo dpyid dang ldan pa]
Chapter 34. Vāsantī
Vasanti

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang / sa'i lha mo brtan ma'i gdams ngag rjes su dran par byed cing / byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa ye shes thub par dka' ba'i snying po can de rjes su dran par bya ba dang / byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin bsgom pa de rab tu goms par bya ba dang / byang chub sems dpa'i chos kyi tshul de'i rjes su bsam pa dang / byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pas rnam par rtse ba de la rnam par dpyad pa dang / byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa'i ye shes shin tu phra ba de la rnam par blta ba dang / byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa'i ye shes rgya mtsho de la 'jug par bya ba dang / byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa'i ye shes tha dad pa de la yid ches par bya ba dang / byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa'i ye shes shin tu sbyangs pa de rjes su rtogs par bya ba dang / byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa'i ye shes rgya mtsho de la 'bab par bya ba byed cing / grong khyer chen po ser skya'i gnas gang na ba der phyin te/

Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, remembering the teaching of the earth goddess Sthāvarā, remembering the bodhisattva liberation called the essence of invincible wisdom, becoming adept in the meditation of bodhisattva samādhi, contemplating the way of the bodhisattva Dharma, analyzing the displays of bodhisattva liberation, viewing the very subtle wisdom of bodhisattva liberation, entering the ocean of the wisdom of bodhisattva liberation, with faith in the different wisdoms of bodhisattva liberation, realizing the mastery of the wisdom of bodhisattva liberation, and descending into the ocean of the wisdom of bodhisattva liberation, arrived at the location of the town of Kapilavastu.

Then Sudhana went to the great city Kapilavastu, remembering the teaching of the earth goddess Sthavara, remembering that enlightening liberation “unassailable asylum of knowledge,” extending the cultivation of that enlightening concentration, contemplating that enlightening doctrine, roaming in the freedom of that enlightening liberation, looking into the subtleties of knowledge of that enlightening liberation, entering into the ocean of knowledge of that enlightening liberation, focusing on the unity of the knowledge of that enlightening liberation, pursuing the accomplishment of the endless knowledge of that enlightening liberation, plunging into the ocean of knowledge of that enlightening liberation.
grong khyer chen po ser skya'i gnas la g.yas phyogs su bskor nas/ shar phyogs logs kyi grong khyer gyi sgo nas song ste/
He circumambulated the town of Kapilavastu, keeping it to his right, and entered the town through its eastern gate.
Going around the city from left to right, he went in by the eastern gate
