nyi ma nub nas ring po ma lon pa zhig tu grong khyer gyi lam gyi sum mdo'i dbus shig na/ byang chub sems dpa'i gdams ngag mthun par len pa de/ mtshan mo'i lha mo dpyid dang ldan pa mthong bar 'dod cing / dge ba'i bshes gnyen yod na sangs rgyas kyi ye shes 'thob par 'gyur bar nges pa'i blo gros dang ldan pa/ ye shes kyi mig kun tu lta ba'i yul gyi rang bzhin gyi byin gyi rlabs dang ldan pa/ phyogs thams cad du mngon par gzhol zhing / dge ba'i bshes gnyen blta ba'i sems kyis mos pa dang / ye shes chen po'i snying por gyur pa'i 'du shes kyi sems dang ldan pa/ dmigs pa thams cad la rab tu zhugs pa'i ye shes kyi mig dang ldan pa/ chos kyi dbyings kyi tshul thams cad du ye shes rgya mtsho 'byams klas pas rgyas par 'gengs pa dang ldan pa'i ting nge 'dzin gyi mig gis/ phyogs thams cad du shes bya'i rgya mtsho la rnam par blta ba/ ye shes chen po'i mig 'thob par bya ba la rab tu gzhol zhing bsam pa rtse gcig tu bzhag nas 'dug 'dug pa dang / mtshan mo'i lha mo dpyid dang ldan pa de/ grong khyer chen po ser skya'i gnas kyi steng gi nam mkha'i dbyings la/ nor bu rin po che sna tshogs dpe med pa'i khang pa brtsegs pa zhig na/ rin po che'i seng ge'i khri chen po spos zhim po thams cad kyi pad+mo'i snying po can zhig la/

He stayed at the town’s central junction of three streets, where, soon after sunset, wishing to see Vāsantī, the goddess of the night, while reverentially following the bodhisattva teaching, having the definite understanding that the wisdom of buddhahood is attained through kalyāṇamitras, having the blessing of the scope of the view of the eyes of wisdom, facing every direction with the aspiration to see the kalyāṇamitra, with a mind that perceives the essence of great wisdom, with eyes of wisdom that engage with all objects of perception, with eyes of samādhi that pervade the vast extent of the ocean of the wisdom of all the ways of the realm of phenomena, seeing the ocean of all that is to be known in all directions, with a single-pointed mind intent on attaining the eyes of wisdom resting with one-pointed thought, he saw Vāsantī, the goddess of the night, in the realm of space above the great town of Kapilavastu. She was in a kūṭāgāra of various precious jewels beyond compare. She was seated upon a lotus that had every excellent aroma, in the center of a great precious lion throne.

and stood in the middle of the crossroads of the city. Before long the sun set, and, skillfully grasping the instructions of spiritual benefactors, he longed to see the night goddess Vasanti, considering spiritual benefactors a sure source of attainment of enlightened knowledge, based concretely on the sphere of the eye of universal knowledge, turning in all directions, wishing to see the spiritual benefactor, thinking of her with great respect as the abode of knowledge, his eye of knowledge extending to all objects, looking over the ocean of all that is knowable with the eye of concentration reaching throughout the ocean of knowledge of principles of all reality realms, intent on extension of the eye of great knowledge. He saw the night goddess Vasanti in the sky over Kapilavastu, in a tower of brilliant, incomparable jewels, sitting on a great jewel lion throne in the calyx of a lotus of all the finest fragrances.

lus kyi mdog gser gyi kha dog tu 'dug pa/ skra 'jam zhing mang la mthon mthing du 'dug pa/ mig dkar nag 'byes pa/ gzugs bzang ba shin tu mdzes pa/ blta na sdug pa/ lus rgyan dang lhab lhub thams cad kyis klubs shing brgyan pa/ kha dog bsgyur ba'i gos bgos pa/ tshangs pa'i gtsug tor gyi cod pan zla ba'i dkyil 'khor gyis brgyan pa thogs pa/ lus la rgyu skar dang / gza' dang / skar chen dang / skar ma'i tshogs thams cad kyi gzugs brnyan snang bar gyur pa 'dug par mthong ngo; ;

Her body was the color of gold. Her hair was soft, abundant, and deep black. Her eyes were deep black.[1285] She was beautiful, attractive, and lovely to the sight. Her body was beautified by all jewelry and adornments. She was wearing dyed[1286] clothing. She possessed a sacred topknot adorned by the disk of the moon as a crest. The constellations, the planets, and all the stars appeared in her body.

She was beautiful, with a golden complexion, soft, rich black hair, and dark eyes. Her body was adorned with all kinds of ornaments, and she was wearing a red robe. She wore a sacred crest adorned with the orb of the moon, and her body showed reflections of all the stars and constellations.

des sems can gyi khams yangs par mi khom pa dang / ngan song dang / ngan 'gro dang / log par ltung ba nas/ sems can ji snyed cig yongs su dgrol ba de dag thams cad kyang / de'i ba spu'i sbubs su chud par mthong ngo/ /
He saw within her pores all the beings she had liberated who in the vast realm of beings had fallen into inopportune states, lower existences, and lower realms.
He also saw in her pores all the sentient beings who had been liberated by her from the calamities of unfavorable circumstances, evils, and miserable conditions.

ji snyed cig mtho ris kyi 'jig rten du bkod pa dang / ji snyed cig nyan thos dang / rang sangs rgyas kyi byang chub dang / thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du yongs su smin par bya ba de dag thams cad kyang de'i ba spu'i sbubs su chud par mthong ngo/ /
He saw within her pores all those she had brought to the higher realms, all those she had ripened for the enlightenment of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, and those she had ripened for omniscience.
He also saw in her pores all the sentient beings whom she had settled in heaven, and all whom she had perfected in the enlightenment of hearers and individual illuminates, and in omniscience.

lus mngon par bsgrub pa dang / gzugs mngon par bsgrub pa dang / kha dog mngon par bsgrub pa'i thabs sna tshogs kyis ji snyed cig yongs su smin par byas pa de dag kyang de'i ba spu'i sbubs su chud par mthong ngo/ /
He saw within her pores all her created bodies, created forms, and created colors that were her various methods that ripened beings.
He also saw in her pores all the various means, embodiments, and appearances she assumed to perfect them.

nga ro mngon par bsgrub pa dang / dbyangs kyi yan lag mngon par bsgrub pa dang / skad kyi tshul sna tshogs yongs su sbyar ba ji snyed cig gis yongs su smin par byas pa de dag kyang / de'i ba spu'i sgo nas rjes su brjod pa thos so/
He heard sounding from her pores the creation of sounds, the creation of the aspects of the voice, and their application to the various ways of speech[1287] through which she ripened beings.
He also heard coming from her pores the various utterances she used to teach and develop them.

dus mngon par bsgrub pa dang / bsam pa dang mos pa ji lta ba bzhin du sems can gyi rjes su 'brang bar bya ba dang / byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa dang / byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par gnon pa dang / byang chub sems dpa'i ting 'dzin gyis rnam par 'phrul ba'i sgo dang / byang chub sems dpa'i khyu mchog gi mthu phyung ba dang / byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par spyod pa dang / byang chub sems dpa'i yongs su lta ba dang / byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par lta ba dang / byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par 'phrul pa dang / byang chub sems dpa'i skyes bu seng ge chen po'i rnam par bsgyings pa dang / byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pas rnam par rtse ba ji snyed cig gis/ des sems can yongs su smin par byas pa de dag kyang / de'i ba spu'i sbubs su chud par mthong ngo; ;

He perceived within her pores her creation of times, her bodhisattva conduct, her bodhisattva prowess, her entrances to bodhisattva samādhis and transformations, her bodhisattva power of leadership, her bodhisattva states of being,[1288] her bodhisattva view, her bodhisattva observation, her bodhisattva emanations, her bodhisattva lion-like awesomeness of a great being, and her displays of bodhisattva liberation through which she ripened beings in accordance with their motivations and aspirations.

He also perceived in her pores the timing, the adaptation to sentient beings’ inclinations and interests, the enlightening practices, forceful means, ways of mystic transformation through concentration, powers, states, observations, contemplations, mystic projections, powerful expansions of the great person, and free masteries of liberation by which they were perfected.

des thabs sna tshogs dang ldan pa'i chos kyi tshul rgya mtsho de dag mthong zhing thos nas dga' rangs te/ mgu zhing nyams bde la/ tshim zhing yid bde ba skyes nas/ mtshan mo'i lha mo dpyid dang ldan pa de la lus thams cad kyis phab nas phyag 'tshal te/ langs nas mtshan mo'i lha mo dpyid dang ldan pa la lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas/ mtshan mo'i lha mo dpyid dang ldan pa'i mdun du 'dug ste/ thal mo sbyar nas 'di skad ces smras so/ /

He saw and heard an ocean of the ways of the Dharma that employed various methods, and he was satisfied, joyful, pleased, delighted, content, and happy. He prostrated to the night goddess Vāsantī with the full length of his body, got up, and circumambulated the night goddess Vāsantī, keeping her to his right, many hundreds of thousands of times. Then he stood before her and, with his hands placed together in homage, said,
Having seen and heard those oceans of teachings involving various means, Sudhana was transported with joy; he paid his respects to the night goddess Vasanti and said to her,

lha mo/ bdag gis bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed de/ de ltar bdag gis dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi byin gyi rlabs kyis/ sangs rgyas kyi yon tan thams cad 'byung bar yang dag par mthong bas dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi phyag tu bdag nyid por ba lags na/ lha mo shul gang la brten na/ byang chub sems dpa'i stobs bcu'i sar 'byung bar 'gyur ba'i thams cad mkhyen pa'i shul bdag la bshad du gsol/ de skad ces smras pa dang /

“Goddess, I have developed the aspiration for the highest, complete enlightenment. I have seen that all the qualities of buddhahood arise through the blessing of a kalyāṇamitra. I put myself in the hands of the kalyāṇamitra. Show me, goddess, the path to omniscience upon which a bodhisattva will bring forth the ten strengths.”

“Noble one, I have set my mind on supreme perfect enlightenment. Seeing all qualities of buddhahood as based on spiritual benefactors, I rely on spiritual benefactors. Please show me the way of omniscience whereon an enlightening being sets forth to the stage of the ten powers.”
mtshan mo'i lha mo dpyid dang ldan pas/ tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la 'di skad ces smras so/ /
The night goddess Vāsantī said to Sudhana, the head merchant’s son,
Vasanti answered Sudhana,

rigs kyi bu/ da ltar khyod dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi byin gyis non te/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi tshig mnyan par 'dod pa dang / dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi gdams ngag la nan tan du byed pa legs so/ /legs so; ;
“Noble one, it is excellent, excellent, that you are thus in awe of kalyāṇamitras and wish to hear a kalyāṇamitra’s words and practice the teaching of kalyāṇamitras.
“It is good that you are so devoted to spiritual benefactors and desire to hear the words of spiritual benefactors.
rigs kyi bu/ khyod ni de ltar dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi gdams ngag la nan tan du byed pas/ gdon mi za bar bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu nye bar 'gyur ro/ /
“Noble one, through thus practicing the teaching of the kalyāṇamitras, you will, without a doubt, approach the highest, complete enlightenment.
Carrying out the instructions of spiritual benefactors, you will surely arrive at supreme perfect enlightenment.

rigs kyi bu/ kho mo ni byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa sems can thams cad kyi mun pa rnam par sel ba'i chos kyi snang bas 'gro ba rnam par 'dul ba'i sgo thob pa ste; bsam pa mi mnyam pa dang ldan pa'i sems can rnams la byams pa'i sems dang ldan pa'o/ /

“Noble one, I have attained the bodhisattva liberation called the gateway to guiding beings through the radiance of the Dharma that eliminates the darkness of all beings. My mind has love for beings who have unstable minds.
I have attained an enlightening liberation, a means of guiding sentient beings by the light of truth, which dispels the darkness for all sentient beings. I am kind to the evil-minded,
mi dge ba'i las kyi lam la zhugs pa rnams la snying rje'i sems dang ldan pa'o/ /
My mind has compassion for beings who follow the path of nonvirtuous actions.
compassionate to evil-doers,
dge ba'i las kyi lam la zhugs pa rnams la dga' ba'i sems dang ldan pa'o/ /
My mind rejoices in those who follow the path of virtuous actions.
pleased with those who do good,
sems mnyam pa dang mi mnyam par ldan pa'i sems can rnams la mi gnyis pa'i sems dang ldan pa'o/ /
My mind does not discriminate between beings with stable and unstable minds.
impartial toward the good and the bad;
kun nas nyon mongs pa rnams la rnam par sbyang ba'i sems dang ldan pa'o/ /
My motivation is to purify those afflicted by the kleśas.
I am determined to purify the defiled,
nyam nga bar gyur pa rnams la yang dag par zhugs pa'i sems dang ldan pa'o/ /
My motivation is to bring the pitiful to perfection.
to set the misguided straight,
dma' ba la mos pa rnams la yangs pa la mos pa yongs su bskyed pa'i sems dang ldan pa'o/ /
My motivation is to generate a vast aspiration in those with inferior aspiration.
to inspire higher aspirations in those with low aspirations,
dbang po zhum pa rnams la brtson 'grus chen po'i shugs rnam par spel ba'i sems dang ldan pa'o/ /
My motivation is to develop great diligence in those with inferior power.[1289]
to increase the energy of those with inferior faculties,
'khor ba la mngon par mos pa rnams la 'khor ba'i rgyud kyi 'khor lo las rnam par bzlog pa'i sems dang ldan pa'o/ /
My motivation is to turn away from existences in the cycle of saṃsāra those whose aspiration is for saṃsāra.
to free those attached to the mundane whirl from its repetitious circles,
nyan thos dang / rang sangs rgyas kyi theg pa la mngon par mos pa'i sems can rnams la/ thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi lam la dgod pa'i sems dang ldan pa'o/ /
My motivation is to establish on the path to omniscience those beings whose aspiration is for the Śrāvakayāna and Pratyekabuddhayāna.
and to set those oriented toward the vehicles of individual salvation onto the path of omniscience.

rigs kyi bu/ de ltar kho mo de lta bu'i sems dang yid la bya bar ldan la/ byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa sems can thams cad kyi mun pa rnam par sel ba'i chos kyi snang bas 'gro ba rnam par 'dul ba'i sgo 'di dang yang ldan pas/

“Noble one, those are the motivations and intentions that I have. I possess the bodhisattva liberation called the gateway to guiding beings through the radiance of the Dharma that eliminates the darkness of all beings.
I am concentrating on these concerns and am imbued with the enlightening liberation through which I guide sentient beings with the light of truth that dispels the darkness for all sentient beings.

sems can gang ji snyed cig mun nag smag tu gyur pa'i nam la/ mi ni nyal bar gyur/ 'byung po'i tshogs ni rgyu bar gyur/ rkun chom mang pos ni rgyas par gyur/ sems can mi srun pa'i tshul can ni phyogs su rgyu bar gyur/ sprin stug po nag pos kun nas khebs par gyur/ dud pa dang / rdul gyi tshogs kyis ni kun nas 'grigs par gyur/ rdzi char mi bzad pas ni rab tu gtags par gyur/ zla skar gyi tshogs ni mi snang bar gyur/ mig gis bya ba'i mthu ni med par gyur pa'i mun pa la/

“When beings are in darkness, humans sleep, the hosts of spirits roam around, the numbers of thieves and robbers increase, dangerous beings are active in all directions, thick black clouds cover everything, there is a thick mass of smoke or dust, there is the assault of terrible wind and rain, the moon and stars are hidden, and the eyes are unable to see.

“Any people who travel on a dark night, where ghosts, thieves, and thugs lurk, when the sky is covered with black clouds, when it is misty, windy, and raining, when there is no moonlight or starlight, when there is no visibility,

sems can gang ji snyed cig rgya mtsho la spyod dam/ thang la spyod dam/ ri la spyod dam/ nags tshal gzhan na spyod dam/ yul gzhan na spyod dam/ grong gzhan na spyod dam/ phyogs gzhan na spyod dam/ phyogs mtshams gzhan na spyod dam/ lam gzhan na spyod kyang rung ste/ rgya mtsho la spyod spyod pa las gru bub par gyur pa'am/ thang la spyod spyod pa las nyam nyes pa'am/ ri la spyod spyod pa las g.yang sa chen por lhung bar gyur pa'am/ 'brog dgon pa la spyod spyod pa las kha zas kyis phongs par gyur pa'am/ nags tshal thibs por sba'i zang zing la thogs pa'am/ tshul ma yin pa'i nyam nyes shig tu gyur tam/ yul gzhan na spyod spyod pa las chom pos bcom pa'am/ grong gzhan na spyod spyod pa las mi srung pa'i tshul can gyis gtses pa'am; phyogs gzhan na spyod spyod pa las 'brog rmis pa'am/ phyogs mtshams gzhan na spyod spyod pa las mgo rmongs pa'am/ lam gzhan na spyod spyod pa las nye zhor gyur kyang rung ste/

“Noble one, through various methods I protect those beings in the darkness who are on the ocean, on a plain, on mountains, in a remote wilderness,[1290] in[1291] a forest, in the countryside, in a town, in a direction, in an intermediate direction, or on a road; those on the ocean whose ship is sinking; those who are in distress; those on the plains; those who are falling down precipices in the mountains; those who have no food or drink in remote wildernesses; those caught in thickets of bamboo in dense forests; those whom calamitous wrongdoing has befallen; those who are being slain by bandits in the countryside; those who perish from ruthless actions in towns; those who are bewildered in the directions; those who are confused in the intermediate directions; and those who encounter disaster on the road.

if they go on the sea, or on land, or in the mountains, or over deserts, or through forests, or through provinces or villages, or on the roads, if they are shipwrecked at sea or held up on land, or fall in the mountains or run out of provisions in the desert, or if they get stuck in the underbrush in the forest or run into trouble, or if they get scattered in the darkness, or if they get mugged in a town, or if they get lost or confused and cannot tell which direction they are going in, or if they run into disaster on the road,

rigs kyi bu/ kho mo ni sems can de dag la/ thabs sna tshogs kyi sgo nas skyabs su gyur par byed pa ste/ 'di ltar rgya mtsho chen po la spyod pa rnams kyi rlung sprin nag po gtor ba dang / chu'i rnyog pa dang ba dang / rlung mi bzad pa'i dkyil 'khor bzlog pa dang / rlabs kyi shugs chen po zhi bar bya ba dang / klong gi 'jigs pa las thar par bya ba dang / phyogs bstan pa dang / chu'i lam legs par dmigs pa dang / 'gram bstan pa dang / rin po che'i gling du phyin par bya ba'i phyir lam yongs su ston te/ yongs su sbud pa'i gzugs dang; ded dpon gyi gzugs dang / rta'i rgyal po rngog chen gyi gzugs dang / glang po'i rgyal po'i gzugs dang / rus sbal gyi rgyal po'i gzugs dang / lha ma yin gyi rgyal po'i gzugs dang; nam mkha' lding gi rgyal po'i gzugs dang / mi'am ci'i rgyal po'i gzugs dang / lto 'phye chen po'i rgyal po'i gzugs dang / rgya mtsho'i lha'i gzugs dang / mnyan pa'i gzugs kyis skyabs su gyur par byed do/ /

“I do so in this way: for those on the great ocean, I dispel the black winds and clouds, I make troubled waters clear, I dispel the circle of cruel winds, I calm the huge powerful waves, I bring freedom from the danger of lightning, I show the direction to go, I provide the correct course over the waters, I reveal the shore, and I show the way to reach the island of jewels. I protect them in the form of a gatherer of beings,[1292] the form of a merchant leader, the form of a great-maned king of horses, the form of a king of elephants, the form of a king of turtles, the form of a king of the asuras, the form of a king of the garuḍas, the form of a king of the kinnaras, the form of a king of the mahoragas, the form of a deity of the sea, and the form of a ferryman.[1293]

I rescue them by various means. For those traveling on the sea I quell hurricanes, get them past bad waters, stop unfavorable winds, quiet the raging billows, free them from the perils of whirlpools, clarify the directions, lead them on the right sea lanes, show them the channels, guide them to the isles of treasure, show them the way in the form of a navigator. Through various forms of being I act as a support and reliance.
dge ba'i rtsa ba de yang 'di ltar/ sems can thams cad sdug bsngal gyi phung po thams cad las yongs su bzlog pa'i phyir skyabs su gyur par shog cig ces yongs su bsngo'o/ /
“I dedicate those roots of merit in this way: ‘May I be a protector of all beings in order to free them from the entire mass of suffering!’
This root of goodness, furthermore, I dedicate in this way: ‘May I be a refuge for all sentient beings, to put an end to all suffering.’

thang la spyod pa'i sems can mun pa chen po shin tu gnag pa'i nam la/ sa gzhi 'od ma dang / tsher ma dang / gseg ma dang / gyo mos gang ba/ sbrul gdug pa gtum po shin tu mang ba/ thag thug dang mi bde ba'i lam can/ rdul dang phyag dar shin tu 'thul ba/ rdzi char drag pos gtags pa/ tsha ba dang / grang ba'i sdug bsngal yod pa/ sbrul dang gcan zan gyis bag tsha ba yod pa/ thong [*thod?] mi dang chom po rgyu bar gyur pa zhig la/ mgo 'khor bar gyur ba'i sems can rnams la nyi ma'i gzugs dang / zla ba'i gzugs dang / skya rengs 'char ba'i gzugs dang / skar mda' chen po'i gzugs dang / glog gi phreng ba 'byung ba'i gzugs dang / rin po che'i 'od kyi gzugs dang / gza'i 'khor gyi gzugs dang / rgyu skar dang / skar ma'i tshogs kyi gzhal med khang gi 'od kyi gzugs dang / lha'i gzugs dang / byang chub sems dpa'i gzugs kyis skyabs su gyur par byed do/ /

“When beings on the plains at night[1294] are in great darkness and the ground is covered with bamboo, thorns, pebbles, and potsherds; when there are numerous fierce poisonous snakes, uneven ground, and difficult paths, and when dust and dirt swirl thickly; when there is the assault of fierce wind and rain, being stricken with the suffering of heat and cold, and the fear of snakes and wild beasts; and when bands of murderers and bandits are prowling around, I protect those beings who are confused in the dark, in the form of the sun, in the form of the moon, in the form of the rising of dawn, in the form of great shooting stars, in the form of flashes of lightning, in the form of the light of jewels, in the form of the circle of the planets, in the form of light from the aerial palaces of the constellations and stars, in the form of a deva, and in the form of a bodhisattva.

“For those on land on a dark night, where there are thickets and brambles, gravel and grit, on uneven terrain, battered by vicious wind and rain, painfully cold or hot, where savage beasts lurk, where killers and bandits roam, I save those who have lost their way on the earth, by means of the forms of the sun, the risen moon, meteoric showers, planets, the light of the stars, celestial beings, and enlightening beings.
sems dge ba'i rtsa ba 'dis/ nyon mongs pa'i mun pa thams cad rnam par bsal ba'i phyir/ sems can thams cad kyi skyabs su shog cig par bskyed do/ /
“In my mind there arose this aspiration: ‘May I become a refuge for all beings through this root of merit, in order to dispel all the darkness of the kleśas.’
And I think: By this root of goodness may I become a savior of all sentient beings.

ri'i g.yang sa la spyod cing 'chi bas 'jigs skrag pa rnams kyi srog dbyung ba dang / grags pa 'dod pa'i dbang du gyur pa dang / snyan pa dang / sgra'i rgyal mtshan 'dod pa dang / longs spyod tshol ba dang / 'dod pa'i zil gyis non pa dang / yo byad yongs su btsal ba la brtson pa dang / 'jig rten gyi phun sum tshogs pa 'dod cing brtson pa dang / bu dang chung ma gtong mi phod pas thogs par gyur pa dang / lta ba'i thibs por 'khyams pa dang / sdug bsngal ba dang / 'jigs pa sna tshogs kyis gtses pa rnams la yang / thabs sna tshogs kyi sgo nas skyabs su gyur par byed de/

“I protect through various methods those on mountain precipices who are afraid of dying and who through clinging to life are under the power of the desire for fame, who desire the banner of words of renown, who have enjoyment as their goal, who are overpowered by desire, who are engaged in the pursuit of the prerequisites for life, who primarily yearn for worldly good fortune, who are tied by affection to children and wife,[1295] who are lost in the thicket of views, and who are oppressed by various kinds of suffering and fears.

“For those on precipitous mountain paths, in danger of death, so that they may live, and for those who are dominated by the desire for fame, those who wish for renown, those who seek enjoyment, those who are avaricious, those who strive to get material things, those whose foremost desire is worldly success, those who are wrapped up in affection for their families, those who are lost in the jungle of views, and those who are oppressed by various miseries and fears,

'di ltar ri'i phug dang / bya skyibs mngon par bsgrub pa dang / shing tog dang / rtsa ba bzar rung ba mngon par bsgrub pa dang / chu'i lam dang / chu mig mngon par bsgrub pa dang / tsha ba dang / grang ba'i gnyen po mngon par bsgrub pa dang / yang dag pa'i lam bstan pa dang / ka la ping+ka'i sgra skad bsgrag pa dang / rma bya'i rgyal po skad 'byin pa'i dbyangs dang / sman 'bar bas snang ba'i gzugs dang / ri'i lha'i 'od kyi gzugs dang /

“I do so in this way: by providing them with caves and shelters, by providing them with fruit and roots to eat, by providing them with streams and springs, by providing them with protection against heat and cold, by showing them correct pathways, by the sound of the song of the avadavat, by the sound of the cry of the king of peacocks, through the form of illumination from burning herbs, and through the form of light from the mountain deities.

I become a refuge by various means: for example, by producing caves in the mountains for shelter, by producing fruits and roots for food, by producing streams for drinking water, by producing shelter against cold and heat, by showing the right path, by the songs of birds, by the luster of medicinal plants, by the glow of mountain spirits.

ri'i phug dang / sul dang / ltongs su rlag ste sdug bsngal sna tshogs kyis gtses pa'i sems can rnams kyi mun pa'i rab rib rnam par bsal ba dang / sa'i gzhi mnyam par mngon par bsgrub pas skyabs su gyur par byed de/

“I become a protector of those in mountain caves, clefts, and chasms who are afflicted by various sufferings, by providing them with level ground, and to dispel the blinding darkness those beings are in.
I become a refuge for those in mountain caves and crevices, those oppressed by various pains, dispelling the darkness, producing level ground for them.

sems kyang ji ltar bdag gis sems can ri la spyod pa 'di dag yongs su bskyabs pa de bzhin du/ 'khor ba'i ri'i lam rgyud g.yang sa la gnas shing / rga shi'i gdon gyis zin pa de dag gi skyabs su yang bdag 'gyur bar shog cig par bskyed do/ /

“In my mind there arises this thought: ‘Just as I have protected these beings who are in the mountains, may I become a protector for those who have fallen into the chasms of the mountain of saṃsāra and have been seized by the demons of old age and death.’

And I resolve that just as I rescue these people in the mountains, so will I become a refuge for those fallen on the precipitous trails of the mountain of mundane existence, who are in the grip of old age and death.

nags tshal thibs po'i dra bas thogs pa'i sems can mtshan mo mun pa'i mun nag gis chod de/ shing dang shing phran 'dzings pa'i gseb shin tu nyam nga ba dang / chu dang / rtswa dang / sdong po dang / 'khri shing gis lam chod pa dang / shing dang / shing phran sna tshogs kyi nags tshal thibs po'i nang du phyin te/ stag gi sgra thos pas skrag pa'i snying can/ don ma grub pas sems 'khrugs par gyur pa dang / 'jigs pa dang / 'tshe ba dang / mi dga' ba sna tshogs kyis nyams mi bde ba/ nags tshal stug po nas 'byung ba'i phyogs mi shes pa rnams la/ kho mo ni bde bar 'gro ba'i lam yongs su ston par byed do/ /

“I become someone who shows the correct path to follow for those beings who are trapped in the net of a dense forest and blinded by the darkness of the night; who are in distress within a tangle of trees and shrubs;[1296] whose path is blocked by grass, rivers, thorns,[1297] trees,[1298] and vines; who have entered a dense forest of numerous trees and vines; who have fear in their hearts on hearing the roaring of tigers; who are distressed at being unable to accomplish their goals; who are afflicted by various dangers, misfortunes, and troubles; and who do not know the way out of a thick forest.

“For those stuck in the jungle on a dark night, confronted with a vast expanse of trees, on roads blocked by grass and water, reeds, trees, and vines, in thickets of various trees and creepers, frightened by tigers roaring, their minds filled with what they have to do, plagued with various perils and misfortunes, not knowing the way out of the forest, I show the right way to go.

sems kyang 'di ltar dge ba'i rtsa ba 'dis/ sems can lta ba thibs po sna tshogs la gnas pa/ sred pa'i dra bas 'khris par gyur pa/ 'khor ba'i sdug bsngal sna tshogs kyis gtses pa rnams sdug bsngal thams cad las yongs su 'grel par shog cig par bskyed do/ /

“In my mind there arises this thought: ‘Through this root of merit, may I free from all suffering those beings who are in the thicket of various views, who are caught in the net of craving, and who are oppressed by the various sufferings and dangers of saṃsāra.’

And I resolve that by this root of goodness I will free those in the thicket of views, caught in the web of craving, oppressed by the various pains and perils of the mundane whirl, liberating them from all miseries.

'brog dgon pa la spyod pa'i sems can mun pa'i nang na 'thoms pa rnams kyang thabs kyi sgo sna tshogs kyis bde ba yongs su bskyed cing lam bstan te/ de dag 'jigs pa med pa dang / bde ba la rab tu bkod nas /
“Through various methods I bring happiness to those beings who are confused in darkness in remote wildernesses. I show them the path and bring them to a safe and pleasant place.
“And as for those in the desert, in the darkness, by various means I comfort them, show them the way, and lead them to safety,

sems kyang dge ba'i rtsa ba 'dis/ sems can 'khor ba'i 'phrog dgon pa na 'thoms pa/ ngan song thams cad kyi lam du zhugs pa rnams/ sdug bsngal thams cad las yongs su bkrol te/ shin tu phun sum tshogs pas bde ba'i thams cad mkhyen pa'i lam la rab tu dgod par bya bar shog cig par bskyed do/ /

“In my mind there arises this thought: ‘Through this root of merit, may I free from all suffering and bring to the great good fortune of the path to happiness and omniscience those beings who are lost in the remote wilderness of saṃsāra and are following the path to all the lower realms.’

resolving that by this root of goodness I shall liberate those who are in the desert of the mundane whirl, who have fallen into evil ways, freeing them from all suffering and setting them on the road of omniscience, where there is eternal safety.

rigs kyi bu/ yul dang ljongs la chags pa'i sems can mngon par chags pa'i rgyu las byung ba'i sdug bsngal nyams su myong bar gyur pa rnams la yang kho mo ni skyo bar bya ba'i thabs sna tshogs kyis yul la mngon par chags pa de las gyen du bskyod pa byed de/
“Noble one, through various methods that bring disillusionment, I free from attachment to their homeland those beings in homelands who experience suffering caused by that attachment.
“As for those in inhabited areas who are experiencing the trouble of owning a home, I draw them away from their attachments to their abodes by various means

sems kyang 'di ltar dge ba'i rtsa pa 'dis sems can thams cad phung po la mngon par chags pa las gyen du bskyod de/ gnas med pa'i thams cad mkhyen pa'i ye shes la dgod par bya bar shog cig par bskyed do/ /
“In my mind there arises this aspiration: ‘Through this root of merit, may I free all beings from attachment to the skandhas and bring them to the wisdom of omniscience that has no location.’
and resolve by this root of goodness to remove all sentient beings from attachment to the elements of body and mind and establish them in nonreliant omniscience.

rigs kyi bu/ kho mo ni grong na spyod pa'i sems can khyim dang / gnas kyi 'ching pas glags pa rnams/ mtshan mo mun pa shin tu gnag pas chod pa'i nang na/ khyim gyi don sna tshogs nyams su gnod pas sdug bsngal bar gyur pa rnams kyang skyo bar 'gyur ba'i sgo sna tshogs kyis skyo bar byas te/ chags pa med pa'i sems yongs su bskyed nas/ chos kyi sbyin pas yongs su bzung ste/ tshim par byas nas rten pa med pa'i chos la bkod de/

“Noble one, the beings who dwell in villages, who are destroyed by their bondage to house and home, who are bewildered in the darkness of the night, and who suffer because of the various demands of their homes‍—through various ways of causing distress, I bring them to disillusionment. I cause them to develop a mind free of attachment. I care for them through the gift of the Dharma. I make them perfectly content and establish them in the Dharma that has no home.

“As for those in villages who are attached to their house and relatives, beset by various family troubles, their minds agitated by various anxieties, I take care of them by material gifts and please them in a proper manner, establish them in the state of nonattachment,

sems kyang 'di ltar dge ba'i rtsa ba 'dis/ sems can skye mched drug gi grong la gnas pa rnams 'khor ba'i lam gyi rgyud kyi spyod yul las gyen du bskyod de/ thams cad mkhyen pa'i ye shes kyi spyod yul la dgod par bya bar shog cig par bskyed do/ /

“In my mind there arises this thought: ‘Through this root of merit, may I free all beings dwelling in the town of their six āyatanas from the realm of activity that is existence in saṃsāra, and may I establish them in the realm of activity of the wisdom of omniscience.’
and resolve by this root of goodness to remove those who cling to the village of their senses from the sphere of mundane objects and set them in the sphere of omniscience.

rigs kyi bu/ gang yang mtshan mo mun pa shin tu gnag pa'i nang na/ shar phyogs la sogs pa'i phyogs dang / phyogs mtshams re rer phyogs bslad par gyur pa/ sa'i phyogs mnyam pa la mi mnyam pa'i g.yang sar 'du shes pa dang / sgang bu la gshong du 'du shes par gyur te/ phyogs kyi lam dang / sa tshod la mgo 'khor bar gyur pa de dag la'ang / kho mo ni thabs sna tshogs kyis snang bar byas te/ phyir 'byung ba rnams la ni sgo yongs su ston to/ / rgal bar 'dod pa rnams la ni mu stegs yongs su ston to/ / brkyal bar 'dod pa rnams la ni gru yongs su ston to/ / khyim du 'gro bar 'dod pa rnams la ni khyim yongs su ston to/ / rnam par blta bar 'dod pa rnams la ni phyogs yongs su ston to/ / sa'i gzhi mtho ba dang / dma' ba yongs su ston to/ / sa'i gzhi phyogs mnyam pa dang / mi mnyam pa dang / gzugs kyi rnam pa sna tshogs kyang yongs su ston to/ / lam gyis dub pa rnams la grong dang / grong khyer dang / ljongs dang / khams dang / rgyal po'i pho brang 'khor kyang yongs su ston to/ / tsha ba dang / skom pas mnar ba rnams la yang mtsho dang / mtshe'u dang / lu ma dang / rdzing dang / rdzing bu dang / chu klung dang / nags tshal dang / bza' shing gi ra ba dang / kun dga' yid du 'ong ba yongs su ston to/ /

“Noble one, through various methods I bring illumination to those beings who are bewildered in the darkness of night in the east and other directions and intermediate directions, who see level areas as being uneven with chasms, who perceive high ground as depressions and depressions as high ground,[1299] and who are bewildered as to the directions of paths and areas. I reveal a door to those who wish to exit. I reveal a path to those who wish to go upon it.[1300] I reveal a ford to those who wish to cross a river. I reveal a ship to those who wish to cross[1301] the sea.[1302] I reveal a house to those who wish to go inside. I reveal a region to those who wish to see it. I reveal the high ground and the low ground. I reveal the areas that are level, those that are not level, and their various forms. I reveal villages, towns, markets,[1303] kingdoms, and capitals to exhausted travelers. I reveal springs, ponds, lakes, reservoirs, lotus ponds, rivers, forests, orchards, and gardens to those afflicted by heat and thirst.

“As for those who lose their sense of direction on a dark night, who think level ground is uneven, who think high ground is low, who think low ground is high, I light the way for them by various means. To those who want to go out I show the door, to those who want to travel I show the road, to those who want to cross over I show the bridge, to those who want to go in I show the house, to those who want to look around I show the directions. I show the high and low ground, the smooth and rough terrain and its various formations. I show travelers the villages, cities, towns, provinces, and capitals. I show those who are hot and thirsty streams and ponds and groves and parks.

sdug pa dang bral zhing phrad par 'dod pa rnams la; pha dang / ma dang / bu dang / chung ma dang / mdza' bo dang / blon po dang / gnyen bshes dang / yid du 'ong ba'i gzugs kyi rnam pa sna tshogs yongs su ston te/
I reveal pleasant forms of various kinds such as father, mother, children, wives, friends, families,[1304] and relatives to those who wish to meet the beloved they are separated from.
To those grieving at separation from their loved ones I show their family and friends, advisers, acquaintances, and kin, and various pleasing forms.
sems kyang ji ltar bdag gis sems can mtshan mo mun pa mun gnag gis chod pa/ mig rab rib kyis nyams pa/ phyogs bslad pa/

“In my mind there arises this thought: ‘May I bring light and illumination, so that they will perceive the various forms around them, to those who are bewildered in the darkness of night, whose eyes are afflicted by blindness, and who are bewildered as to directions.
And I resolve that just as I light the way for those in the dark who cannot see and have lost their way,

lam 'khor ba rnams la/ gzugs kyi rnam pa sna tshogs rnam par dmigs par bya ba'i phyir snang ba bskyed de/ 'od byas pa de bzhin du/ bdag gis yun ring po nas 'khor ba'i mun ba na gnas pa'i sems can yang dag pa nyid kyi phyogs la bslad pa/ ma rig pa'i mun par 'thoms pa/ ye shes kyi mig mi shes pa'i ling tog gis chod pa/ 'du shes dang / sems dang / lta bas phyin ci log tu gyur pa/ mi rtag pa la rtag par 'du shes pa/ sdug bsngal ba la bde bar 'du shes pa/ bdag med pa la bdag tu 'du shes pa/ mi sdug pa la sdug par 'du shes pa/ bdag dang / sems can dang / srog dang / gso ba dang / gang zag tu 'dzin pa dam po la gnas pa/ phung po dang / khams dang / skye mched la gnas pa/ rgyu dang 'bras bu la mgo 'khor ba/ mi dge ba'i las kyi lam gyi phyogs su zhugs pa/

“ ‘Similarly, there are beings who have dwelled in the darkness of saṃsāra for a long time who are confused concerning the right direction; who are bewildered in the darkness of ignorance; whose eyes of wisdom are clouded by the cataracts of ignorance; who have incorrect perception, mind, and view; who perceive the impermanent as permanent; who perceive suffering as happiness; who perceive the absence of a self as a self; who perceive the unpleasant as pleasant; who believe in an enduring self, being, soul, person,[1305] or individual; who rely on the skandhas, dhātus, and āyatanas; who are confused about cause and result; who follow the path of nonvirtuous actions;

as I create light to make various forms manifest, in the same way I will use the light of great wisdom to destroy the darkness of ignorance of those in the long night of the mundane whirl, who have no sense of direction at all, who are in the darkness of ignorance, whose eye of knowledge is covered by the veil of nescience, who are perverted in concepts, thoughts, and views, who think the impermanent is permanent, who think the painful is painless, who think the selfless has self, who think the impure is pure, who cling to a definite self, being, life, soul, individuality, and personality, who are attached to sense faculties, sense consciousnesses, and sense data, who are confused about cause and effect, who do what is not good,

srog gcod pa/ ma byin par len pa/ 'dod pas log par g.yem pa/ brdzun du smra ba/ phra ma zer ba/ ngag rtsub po 'byin pa/ tshig kyal pa smra ba/ chags sems dang ldan pa/ gnod sems kyi sems dang ldan pa/ log par lta ba can/ phar mi shes pa/ mar mi shes pa/ dge sbyong dang bram zer mi shes pa/ dbang po mi shes pa/ skyes bu dam pa mi shes pa/

who kill; who steal; who engage in sexual misconduct; who lie; who slander; who speak harsh words; who speak meaninglessly; who are covetous; who are malicious; who hold wrong views; who do not respect their fathers; who do not respect their mothers; who do not respect śramaṇas and brahmins; who do not respect the powerful; who do not respect holy beings;

who take life, who steal, who abuse sexuality, who tell lies, who slander others, who speak harshly, who sow dissension, who are covetous, who are malicious, who hold erroneous views, who do not honor their parents or mendicants or priests,

chos ma yin pa la chags shing zhen pa/ mi tshul pa'i 'dod pas zil gyis non pa/ log pa'i chos kyis yongs su 'khris pa/ de bzhin gshegs pa la skur pa 'debs pa/ chos kyi 'khor lo nub par bya ba la zhugs pa/ bdud kyi rgyal mtshan 'dzin pa/

who have passion and devotion for what is not the Dharma; who are overcome by inappropriate desires; who are in the bondage of wrong views; who malign the tathāgatas; who engage in bringing the wheel of the Dharma to an end; who hold the banner of Māra;

who do not recognize the blameworthy or the good, who do not take pleasure in what is right, who are dominated by ill-gotten gain, who pervert what is right by erroneous views, who falsely impugn the enlightened, who try to suppress true teaching, who fly the banner of demons,

byang chub sems dpa' la gnod par byed pa/ theg pa chen po la zhe sdang ba/ byang chub kyi sems la mos pa spong bar byed pa/ byang chub sems dpa' la mi snyan du brjod pa/ snod ma bskams par snying ring ba/ gnod pa ma byas par dgrar len pa/ 'phags pa la skur pa 'debs pa/ skyes bu dam pa ma yin pas spyod pa'i chos kyi spyod yul can/ mchod rten dang dge 'dun gyi dngos po la 'khu ba/

who harm[1306] bodhisattvas; who have anger toward the Mahāyāna; who are engaged[1307] in reviling the aspiration to enlightenment; who criticize bodhisattvas; who harm or injure their mothers;[1308] who are[1309] harmful and hostile; who malign the āryas; who practice a religious conduct that is not that of[1310] good people; who damage that which belongs to stūpas and the saṅgha;

who injure or kill enlightening beings, who are hostile to the Great Vehicle, who cut off the aspiration for enlightenment, who defame enlightening beings, who injure or kill their mothers, who are hostile, who revile the wise, who consort with the corrupt and unjust, who damage the relics of saints and the goods of the religious community,
pha ma la log par sems pa/ mtshams med pa'i las byed pa/ g.yang sa chen po la mngon par bltas pa'i sems can rnams kyi ma rig pa'i mun pa/
who oppose their parents; who commit the acts with immediate result on death; and who are facing a great abyss.
who oppose their parents, who act in hellish ways, who are on the brink of disaster—

shes rab kyi snang ba chen pos bsal te/ bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu yang dag par bskul nas/ theg pa chen po kun tu bzang pos stobs bcu'i ye shes kyi sa'i lam yongs su ston par gyur cig /de bzhin gshegs pa'i sa dang / de bzhin gshegs pa'i yul dang / thams cad mkhyen pa'i ye shes kyi tshul rgya mtsho dang / sangs rgyas gyi ye shes kyi spyod yul dang / sangs rgyas kyi yul dang / stobs bcu yongs su grub pa dang / sangs rgyas kyi gzungs kyi stobs dang / sangs rgyas thams cad kyi sku mchog tu gyur pa yongs su ston par shog cig/ yongs su bstan nas kyang / sangs rgyas thams cad kyi mnyam pa nyid kyi gnas la rab tu dgod par shog cig par bskyed do/ /

“ ‘May I dispel the darkness of their ignorance with the great light of wisdom, inspire them toward the highest, complete enlightenment, and reveal to them, through the completely good Mahāyāna, the path to the level of the wisdom of the ten strengths, the level of the tathāgatas, the scope of the omniscient wisdom of the tathāgatas, the ocean of the ways of omniscient wisdom, the range of activity of the wisdom of the buddhas, the scope of the buddhas, the accomplishment of the ten strengths, and the strength of the power of retention of the buddhas and the single[1311] body of all the buddhas. Having revealed that, may I establish them in the knowledge[1312] of the equality of all the buddhas.’

having destroyed the darkness of their ignorance by the light of great wisdom and directed them toward supreme perfect enlightenment, by the Great Vehicle of universal good I shall show them the path to the stage of knowledge of the ten powers; I shall show them the stage of the enlightened, the realm of the enlightened, the ocean of wisdom of omniscience, the sphere of enlightened knowledge, the consummation of the ten powers, the power of mental command of buddhas, and the unity of all bud-dhas. Having shown them this, I will establish them in the knowledge of equality of all buddhas.

rigs kyi bu/ kho mo ni sems can yun ring po nas na zhing nad kyis yongs su skyo ba/ lus nyam chung ba dang / rgas pa/ rga ba'i zil gyis non pa dang / mgon med pa dang / phongs shing dbul pa dang / log par ltung ba dang / yul gzhan du phyin pa dang / phyogs log par zhugs pa dang / btson ra na 'dug pa dang / chad pas bcad pa dang / nyes pa byung ste rgyal pos gsad par bkri ba rnams kyang srog dang bral gyi 'jigs pa las yongs su bskyab pa'i phyir gnas so/ /

“Noble one, I am present to save those beings who are sick, who are depressed by being ill for a long time, whose bodies are weakened, who are old, who have been overpowered by old age, who have no protector, who are destitute, who are poor, who are ruined, who have gone astray into another land, who are going in the wrong direction, who are in prison, who are being punished, who are criminals, who are being led to execution, and who are afraid of losing their lives.

“As for those who are sick, who are worn out from long illness, whose bodies are weakened, who have wasted away, those who have grown old and are overcome by old age, those who are wretched and poor, those who have come to the end of their lives, those who are in bondage, those who are being tortured, and convicts who have been imprisoned, I stand by them to save them from the danger of injury to their lives.

rigs kyi bu/ de ltar kho mo ni sems can nad pa rnams kyi nad thams cad ni thabs thams cad kyis gso bar nan tan du byed do/ / rgas pa dang / rga ba'i zil gyis non pa rnams la ni/ bsnyen bkur ba dang / rim gro dang / yo byad kyis mi phongs par yongs su sdud par byed do/ / mgon med ba'i sems can rnams la mgon byed do/ / phongs shing dbul ba rnams ni nor dang gser gyi phung pos yongs su sdud do/ / log par ltung ba rnams ni don mthun pas yongs su sdud do; ; yul gzhan du phyin pa rnams ni rang gi yul du phyin par byed do/ / phyogs log par zhugs pa rnams ni phyogs ma nor bar 'dzud do; ; btson ra na 'dug pa rnams ni btson ra nas thar bar byed do/ / chad pas bcad pa ni chad pa'i sdug bsngal las grol bar byed do/ / nyes pa byung ste rgyal pos gsad par bkri ba rnams ni srog gi dbugs phyin pa thob par byed de/

“Noble one, I am dedicated to using every method to heal all the illnesses of sick beings. I serve and attend those who are old, who are overpowered by old age. I collect the necessities for life for those who are without them. I am a protector for beings who have no protector. I gather a mass of wealth and gold for those who are destitute and poor. I gather what is needed for those who are ruined. I lead those who have gone astray in other lands back to their homelands. I take into the correct direction those who follow the wrong direction. I free from prison those who are in prison. I free from the suffering of punishment those who are being punished. I save the lives of those who are criminals being led to execution.

I employ all means to remove the illnesses of those who are sick. Those who are wasted away and overcome by old age I take care of by constant attendance. I provide protection for the helpless, I enrich the poor, I take care of those who have fallen into misfortune by regarding their welfare as my own. Those abroad I lead to their own country, and those astray I lead in the right direction. Those in bondage I release from their bonds. Those who are being tortured I release from the pain of torture. I save the lives of convicts who have been handed over to the king for execution.

sems kyang bdag ji ltar sems can 'di dag 'jigs pa dang / gnod pa sna tshogs las yongs su skyob cing mgon byed pa de bzhin du/ bdag gis 'di rnams bla na med pa'i chos kyi yongs su bsdu bas yongs su bsdus te/ nyon mongs pa thams cad las yongs su dgrol bar bya'o/ / skye ba dang / rga ba dang / na ba dang / 'chi ba dang / mya ngan dang / smre sngags 'don pa dang / sdug bsngal ba dang / yid mi bde ba dang / 'khrugs pa las yang dag par bzla bar bya'o/ / ngan song dang / log par ltung ba'i 'jigs pa thams cad las yongs su dgrol bar bya'o/ / dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi gzugs la rab tu dgod par bya'o/ / chos rin po che sbyin pa'i yongs su bsdu bas yongs su bsdu bar bya'o/ / kha na mtho ba med pa'i las la rab tu dgod par bya'o/ / de bzhin gshegs pa'i sku rnam par dag pa yang dag par bskul bar bya'o/ / rga shi yongs su med pa'i dbyings shin tu rtogs pa las rab tu dgod bar bya bar bskyed do/ /

“In my mind there arises this thought: ‘May I protect and save these beings from these various kinds of fear and harm. Similarly, may I free them from all the kleśas through gathering a collection of the highest Dharmas. May I cause them to transcend birth, aging, illness, death, misery, wailing, suffering, unhappiness, and torment. May I liberate them from all fear of falling into the lower realms. May I bring them into the care of kalyāṇamitras. May I gather a collection of the gift of the precious Dharma. May I establish them in nontransgressive conduct. May I inspire them toward the pure body of the tathāgatas. May I establish them in the realization of the essence that is completely free of aging and death.’

I resolve that just as I am a refuge saving these beings from various perils and afflictions, so shall I take care of them with the supreme protection of the truth and liberate them from all mental afflictions. I shall enable them to transcend birth, old age, sickness, death, grief, lamentation, misery, depression, and mental disturbance. I shall free them from all fears of falling into bad conditions. I shall establish them in the care of spiritual benefactors. I shall take care of them by giving them jewels of true teaching. I shall get them to act impeccably. I shall direct them to the purity of the body of the enlightened. I shall establish them in the knowledge of the realm where there is ultimately no old age or death.

rigs kyi bu/ kho mo ni sems can log pa'i lam la zhugs pa/ lta ba'i rnam pa thibs po sna tshogs la mngon par zhen pa/ log par lta ba'i spyod yul can/ lus dang ngag dang yid kyi las nya ma nga bar 'gyur ba la yongs su spyod pa/ brtul zhugs dang dka' thub sna tshogs la gnas pa/ yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas ma yin yang / yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas su 'du shes pa/ lus gdung ba dang / yongs su gdung ba la rab tu brtson pa/ mtsho dang / mtshe'u dang / lu ma dang / rdzing bu dang / chu klung dang / ri'i gzar dang / phyogs dang / phyogs mtshams la 'dud cing phyag 'tshal ba la mos pa/ sdig pa'i grogs po'i dbang du gyur pa rnams la yang / thabs sna tshogs kyis mgon du gyur par byed de/

“Noble one, through various methods I become the protector of those beings who follow wrong paths; who are attached to various dark views; who have the range of activity of incorrect concepts;[1313] who engage in dreadful physical, vocal, and mental conduct; who follow various kinds of discipline and asceticism; who view that which is not complete buddhahood as complete buddhahood; who are engaged in paining and tormenting their bodies; who bow down to, pay homage to, and place their trust in lakes, ponds, springs, reservoirs, rivers, precipitous mountains, the directions, and the intermediate directions; and who are under the power of bad companions.

“As for those on wrong paths, those in the tangles of various views, those acting on erroneous conceptions, those doing evil in thought, word, and deed, those uncontrolled in action, those devoted to various pious observances and ascetic practices, those who think the unenlightened are enlightened, those who think the enlightened are unenlightened, those who practice self-torture, those who worship bodies of water, mountains, or particular places, and those who are under the control of bad companions, I become a refuge for them by various means

da dag sdig pa'i lta ba'i rnam pa dang / ngan song thams cad kyi g.yang sar ltung ba'i lam las rnam par bzlog go/ 'jig rten pa'i yang dag par lta ba la rab tu bkod cing / lha dang mi'i phun sum tshogs pa la yang yongs su 'god do/ /

“I turn them away from evil views and all paths that lead to falling into the abyss of the lower realms. I establish them in the correct worldly view. I establish them in the good fortune of humans and devas.
and thence turn them away from evil, from immersion in views, from all bad conditions. I establish them in right seeing in the world and place them in celestial and human states.

sems kyang ji ltar bdag gis sems can 'di dag nyam nga ba'i nan tan dang sdug bsngal las yongs su 'grol ba de bzhin du/ bdag gis sems can thams cad kyang 'phags pa 'jig rten las 'das pa'i pha rol tu phyin pa'i lam la bkod de/ thams cad mkhyen pa nyid las phyir mi ldog par byas la/ kun tu bzang po'i smom [*smon?] lam chen pos/ thams cad mkhyen pa nyid la dgod par bya'o/ / sems can gyi khams thams cad ma dul gyi bar du/ byang chub sems dpa'i sa las kyang mi g.yo bar bya bar bskyed do/ /

“In my mind there arises this thought: ‘May I liberate these beings from dreadful practices and suffering. Similarly, may I establish all beings in the noble, transcendent path of the perfections. May I cause them to progress irreversibly toward omniscience and through completely good great prayer bring them to omniscience. And may I never depart from the level of a bodhisattva until all realms of beings have been guided.’ ”[1314]

I resolve that just as I liberate these sentient beings from the miseries of such bad behavior, so shall I establish all sentient beings in the transmundane path of transcendence, make them irreversible in progress toward omniscience, and lead them to omniscience by the great vow of universal good; and I shall not fall from the stages of enlightening beings, while not turning away from the realm of all sentient beings.”

de nas mtshan mo'i lha mo dpyid dang ldan pas/ de'i tshe byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa'i phyogs sems can thams cad kyi mun pa rnam par sel ba'i chos kyi snang bas 'gro ba rnam par 'dul ba'i sgo 'di brnan te/ bstan par bya ba'i phyir/ sangs rgyas kyi byin gyi rlabs kyis phyogs bcur rnam par bltas te/ tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la/ tshigs su bcad pa 'di dag smras so/ /

At that time, Vāsantī, the goddess of the night, in order to teach further the bodhisattva liberation called the gateway to guiding beings through the radiance of the Dharma that eliminates the darkness of all beings, through the blessing of the buddhas looked into the ten directions and then recited these verses to Sudhana, the head merchant’s son:

At that point, further revealing the realm of the enlightening liberation which guides the world by the light of truth that dispels the darkness for all sentient beings, the goddess looked over the ten directions by the power of Buddha and spoke these verses to Sudhana:
gti mug ma rig mun nag bsal don du/ / sems can phan phyir kho mo chos ston te/ / dus la bsdad cing 'gro ba bde bar byas/ / 'di ni rnam thar tshul mchog zhi ba yin; ;

“I teach the Dharma so as to benefit beings,[1315] In order to dispel the darkness of ignorance and stupidity. I observe the time and bring happiness to beings. This is my supreme way of liberation, of peace. {1}
This peaceful liberation of mind guides the world To happiness in accord with the time By producing the light of truth To end the darkness of delusion and ignorance.
kho mos byams yangs shin tu sbyang ba byas/ / bskal ba mtha' yas sngon chad shin tu bsgoms/ / des ni 'jig rten rgyas bkang snang bar byed/ / nor bzang brtan pas tshul 'di shes par gyis/ /
“I have perfectly practiced vast love,[1316] Meditating throughout limitless kalpas in the past. In that way, I have filled the world with illumination. Sudhana, know this way well.[1317] {2}
My kindness is vast and pure, Developed over boundless eons past; Dispelling evil, I illumine the world— Realize this wisdom, O Sudhana, steadfast one.
kho mo'i snying rje rgya mtsho tshad med de/ / 'di las dus gsum rgyal ba 'jig rten 'byung / / de ni 'gro ba'i sdug bsngal zhi bar byed/ / nor bzang brtan pas tshul 'di shes par gyis/ /
“My ocean of compassion is measureless. Through it the jinas of the three times appear in the world. Through it the suffering of beings is quelled. Sudhana, know this way well. {3}
Measureless is my ocean of compassion for the world; Herein the buddhas of all times are born, Hereby the pains of the world are soothed— Realize this wisdom, O Sudhana, steadfast one.
'jig rten bde ba mngon par bsgrub pa dang / / ma byas 'phags pa'i bden pa mngon bsgrub cing / / des ni kho mo dga' mgur rangs par byed/ / rgyal sras khyod kyis tshul 'di shes par gyis/ /
“Creating worldly happiness And noncomposite, higher bliss Pleases, delights, and gladdens me. Jinaputra, understand this way of mine. {4}
Producing worldly happiness, both the joys Which are conditional and those of the sages, Thereby I am delighted, uplifted, pleased— Realize this wisdom, O son of Buddha.
sangs rgyas stobs rnams yongs su sbyong byed cing / / nyan thos ye shes rnam thar 'bras bu dang / / 'dus byas skyon las rtag tu phyir phyogs kyi/ / rgyal sras khyod kyis tshul 'di shes par gyis/ /
“Always turned away from composite faults And the wisdom, liberation, and results of the śrāvakas, I purify the strengths of the buddhas. Jinaputra, understand this way of mine. {5}
Forever turned away from the ills of the conditional, As well as the knowledge and liberation of individual salvation, Perfecting the power of buddhas— Realize this wisdom, O son of Buddha.
kho mo'i mig ni rgya che yongs su dag/ / des ni phyogs bcu'i zhing rnams mang po mthong / / zhing dbyings de dag kun gyi rang byung rnams/ / byang chub shing dbang drung na bzhugs pa mthong / /
“My eyesight is vast and completely pure. With it I see many realms in the ten directions. I see the self-originated ones in those realms Seated under the lords of Bodhi trees. {6}
Vast and pure is my eye, by which I see The lands of the ten directions— I see the buddhas in those lands Sitting under the enlightenment tree.
sangs rgyas sku ni mtshan gyis yongs brgyan cing / / 'od bzang rnam pa sna tshogs kun 'gyed de/ / ba sbu kun nas 'od zer mang 'gyed pa'i/ / sangs rgyas 'khor dang bcas pa kho mos mthong / /
“I see the buddhas and their assemblies, The buddhas’ bodies beautified by signs, Emanating multicolored beautiful light rays, A multitude of light rays emanating from all their pores. {7}
I see thousands of buddhas with their circles, The buddhas’ bodies adorned with marks of greatness, Emanating multifold glorious lights, Radiating oceans of light from their pores.
zhing dbyings de dag kun gyi sems can rnams/ / shi 'pho skye ba'i sgor yang kun mthong ste/ / byis pa de dag 'gro rgyud rgya mtsho na/ / 'khor zhing rang rang las kyang myong bar byed/ /

“I see the beings within those realms And their entrances into death and rebirth, Those foolish ones who in those oceans of existences Continue in saṃsāra and experience the results of their actions. {8}
I see the sentient beings in those lands, How they die and are born; I see the ignorant in the ocean of transmigration as they go Round in circles experiencing the results of their own deeds.
kho mo'i rna ba rgya mtsho rnam dag ste/ / der ni sgra rnams ma lus yongs su 'du/ / 'gro ba kun gyi sgra skrad [*skad?] rgya mtsho dag / kun kyang thos nas dran pas yongs su 'dzin/ /
“Completely pure is the ocean of my hearing In which are gathered all sounds without exception. I hear and hold in my memory The entire ocean of the languages in all worlds. {9}
My ocean of hearing is pure, And all sounds enter therein: Hearing the words of all sentient beings, I keep them in mind.
dbyangs kyi yan lag sgra skad thams cad kyis/ / dpe zla med pa'i gsung ni rab brgyan te/ / des ni rgyal ba 'khor lo rab tu bskor/ / de dag kho mos thos shing dran pas 'dzin/ /
“The speech beyond analogy or equal, Adorned by all aspects of speech and all sounds, The wheel that is turned by the jinas I hear and hold in my memory. {10}
The infinite expressions of the teachings of buddhas I also hear and remember.
kho mo'i sna'i mthu yongs su rnam dag ste/ / chos tshul rgya mtsho dag la thogs pa med/ / rnam thar gnas rnams kun tu rab 'jug pa'i/ / tshul ni rgyal sras khyod kyis shes par gyis/ /
“My power of smell also is completely pure. Jinaputra, understand this way that is The entrance to dwelling in all liberations, Without impediment, in the ocean of the ways of the Dharma. {11}
My sense of smell is far-reaching and pure, Unobstructed in the midst of all things, An entry into all states of liberation; You should realize this wisdom.
kho mo'i lce ni rgya che rab tu yangs/ / srab cing mdog dmar rin chen 'od du dag / sems can bsam pa ji bzhin des shes byed/ / rgyal sras khyod kyis tshul 'di shes par gyis/ /
“My tongue is vast and extensive, Subtle, red, and shining like a jewel. Jinaputra, understand this way through which I know the thoughts of beings. {12}
My tongue is broad and long, coppery red, Shiny like a jewel, pure; With it I communicate to beings according to their mentalities: You should realize this wisdom.
kho mo'i chos lus shin tu rnam dag ste/ / dus gsum kun tu 'od gsal rab tu gnas/ / gzugs lus sems can bsam pa ji bzhin te/ / de dag kun gyi dad pa'i dbang du mthong / /

“My Dharma body is completely pure. I remain in its brilliance[1318] throughout the three times, In a form of body in accordance with the wishes of beings, Which they all see through the power of their faith. {13}
My reality body is transcendentally pure, Omnipresent in all times; The physical body beings see according to their mentalities, By the power of their devotion.
kho mo'i sems ni chags med zag pa med/ / sgra dbyangs sprin gyi nga ro ji bzhin te/ / de yi khongs su mi mchog kun chud kyang / / de la kho mo rnam par rtog pa med/ /
“My mind is without attachment, undefiled. The sound of speech is like the roaring of the clouds. Though all lords of humans are contained in it, I have no conceptualization concerning that. {14}
My mind is free from attachment and taint, Resonant with thunderous sound; Therein are all buddhas assembled, Yet I have no discrimination.
zhing gi dbyings kyi sems can bsam mi khyab/ / de dag sems kyi rgya mtsho kho mos shes/ / de dag dbang po bsam pa rab shes kyang / / de la kho mo rnam par rtog pa med/ /
“I know the ocean of the minds Of the countless beings in the realms. I know their faculties and aspirations, But in this I have no conceptualization. {15}
Innumerable are the beings on the face of the earth; I know the oceans of their minds, I know their faculties and inclinations, But I have no discrimination.
kho mo'i rdzu 'phrul rab yangs shin tu grub/ / des ni bsam yas zhing yang rab tu bskyod/ / lus kyi 'od dang mthu yang de bzhin te/ / des ni sems can gdul dka' shin tu 'dul/ /
“My miracles are vast and perfectly performed. They are inconceivable and shake the realms. Similarly, the light and power of my body Subdue the beings who are difficult to subdue. {16}
My occult power is vast and consummate, I shake innumerable worlds And produce an aura of light Whereby I tame the intractable.
kho mo'i bsod nams rnam yangs yongs su dag / kun tu rgyan byed zad pa med pa'i mdzod/ / des ni rgyal ba rnams la mchod pa byed/ / 'gro ba thams cad nye bar 'tsho ba'ang yin/ /
“My merit is vast and completely pure, An inexhaustible treasure completely displayed, Through which offerings are made to the jinas And all beings are sustained. {17}
My virtue is vast and pure, An endless treasury, adorning everywhere; With it I make offerings to buddhas And sustain the life of all beings.
kho mo'i shes rab rnam yangs shin tu dag / des ni chos mang rgya mtsho rab tu shes/ / 'gro ba kun gyi the tshom yongs su gcod/ / rgyal sras khyod kyis tshul 'di shes par gyis/ /
“Vast and completely pure is my wisdom, Through which I know an ocean of Dharma And cut through the doubts of all beings. Jinaputra, understand this way of mine. {18}
I have entered the ocean of buddhas, Realizing the wisdom of all time, And I enter into their vows— This wisdom is peerless and perfect.
dus gsum kun la kho bo zhugs gyur pas/ / sangs rgyas rgya mtsho kun kyang mthong zhing shes/ / de dag smon lam la yang rab tu zhugs/ / tshul 'di dpag yas rab tu rdzogs pa yin/ /
“Comprehending all three times, I see and know an ocean of buddhas And comprehend their prayers. This way is measureless[1319] and perfect. {19}
rdul mang kun la zhing rnams rgya mtsho mthong / / de dag dus gsum 'jug pa'ang de bzhin te/ / de dag kun gyi sangs rgyas rgya mtsho mthong / / 'di ni kun tu gnas ba'i chu la byis/ /
“I see an ocean of realms within all atoms And their entry into the three times. I see within them an ocean of buddhas And the level[1320] of their way that is present everywhere. {20}
In every atom I see oceans of worlds Of past, present, and future; And I see oceans of buddhas therein, And their universal ground of wisdom.
rnam par snang mdzad byang chub sangs rgyas te/ / phyogs rnams kun gyi zhing rnams yongs bkang zhing / / rdul sbubs kun gyi byang chub shing drung na/ / zhi ba'i chos rnams gsung du sgrog pa ltos/ /
“See how the enlightenment, the buddhahood, of Vairocana Pervades the realms in all directions. Within every atom, at the foot of a Bodhi tree, He is speaking of the Dharma of peace.” {21}
See Vairocana, enlightened, Pervading all lands in the ten directions, Sitting at the foot of the enlightenment tree In each atom expounding the teaching of peace.

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis/ /mtshan mo'i lha mo dpyid dang ldan pa la 'di skad ces smras so/ / lha mo khyod bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu zhugs nas ji srid cig lags/ de ltar khyod tshul 'di lta bus/ sems can gyi don bgyi ba la sta gon du zhugs pa'i rnam par thar pa de ni khyod kyis brnyes nas ji srid cig lags/ de skad ces smras pa dang /

Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, asked Vāsantī, the goddess of the night, “Goddess, how long has it been since you have been established in the highest, complete enlightenment? How long has it been since you attained this liberation through which you have become established in accomplishing the benefit of beings in this way?”

Then Sudhana said to the night goddess Vasanti, “How long ago did you set out for supreme perfect enlightenment? How long ago did you attain this liberation, by the at tainment of which you have come to perform all beneficial actions in this way?”

mtshan mo'i lha mo dpyid dang ldan pas/ tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la 'di skad ces smras so/ / rigs kyi bu/ sngon 'das pa'i dus ri rab kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi bskal pa'i yang pha rol gcig tu bskal pa rab tu zhi ba'i 'od ces bya ba/ sangs rgyas bye ba phrag lnga brgya skyes pa byung ste/ de'i 'jig rten gyi khams ni rin chen dpal 'byung ba zhes bya bar gyur to/ / 'jig rten gyi khams de'i gling bzhi pa 'bring po rin chen zla ba sgron ma'i 'od ces bya ba de na/ rgyal po'i gnas pad+mo'i 'od ces bya ba yod de/ rgyal po'i gnas der/ rgyal po chos rab mu stegs zhes bya ba chos dang mthun pa'i rgyal po 'khor los bsgyur ba/ gling bzhi la dbang ba/ rin po che bdun dang ldan pa byung ste/ des sa chen po de yang ri dang rgya mtshor bcas pa'i mthas gtugs par chos kyis rgyas par byas nas/ bde bar gnas par byas so/ /

Vāsantī, the goddess of the night, answered, “Noble one, beyond and even more beyond as many past kalpas as there are atoms in Sumeru, during a kalpa called Praśantaprabha, there was a world realm called Ratnaśrīsaṃbhava in which there appeared five thousand million buddhas. Within that world realm there was a medium-sized four-continent world called Ratnacandrapradīpaprabhā, the capital of which was called Padmaprabhā. In that capital city there was King Sudharmatīrtha, who was a cakravartin Dharma king who ruled over the four continents and possessed the seven jewels. He spread the Dharma over the mountains and seas of that great world up to its edges and made it happy.

Vasanti replied, “As many eons ago as atoms in the polar mountain, there was an eon called Tranquil Light, in which five billion buddhas were born. There was then a world system called Born of the Light of Jewels, in which there was a central world of four continents called Jewel Moon Lamp Light, the capital city of which was called Lotus Light. In that capital city was a king named Bridge of Good Law, who was a just ruler, a sovereign with all the attributes of kingship. He had conquered that trouble-free earth by justice and ruled it righteously.

rgyal po chos rab mu stegs de'i btsun mo chos kyi blo gros zla ba zhes bya ba byung ste/ de srod la 'dod pas myos shing dga' bar rtse rtse bas dub nas nam gyi gung la btsun mo'i 'khor gyi gnas su phyin te nyal lo/ /
King Sudharmatīrtha had a queen named Dharmamaticandrā. At dusk, intoxicated by desire and exhausted by bliss, she returned to the harem at midnight and went to sleep.
“The king’s wife was named Moon of Understanding of Right. She enjoyed herself making love in the first part of the night, and in the middle of the night, when the love play had ceased, she slept.

de nas rgyal po'i gnas pad+mo'i 'od de'i shar phyogs kyi nags tshal chen po zhi ba'i dpal 'byung ba zhes bya bar rin po che'i rgyan thams cad kyi 'od dang ldan pa'i lhun can/ sangs rgyas thams cad kyi rnam par 'phrul pas byung ba'i byang chub kyi shing chen po'i drung du de bzhin gshegs pa chos thams cad rab tu sgrog pa'i rgyal po zhes bya ba/ bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu mngon par sangs rgyas nas/ de'i mthus 'jig rten gyi khams rin po che dpal 'byung ba thams cad ni 'od chen po kha dog du ma can gyis rgyas shing gang bar gyur to/ /

To the east of the capital city of Padmaprabhā there was a great forest called Śamathaśrīsambhava, in which appeared a tathāgata by the name of Sarvadharmanigarjitarāja, whose body shone with the light of all kings of jewels and was the miraculous manifestation of all the buddhas. At the foot of a Bodhi tree, he attained the highest, complete enlightenment of buddhahood. Through the power of that, a great light of many colors filled the world realm of Ratnaśrīsaṃbhava.

At that time, in a forest called Source of Radiance of Peace, to the east of the city of Lotus Light, a buddha named Supreme Thunder of All Truths attained supreme perfect enlightenment at a great enlightenment site made of the finest jewels, with the lights of all supernal manifestations, radiating the lights of the magical displays of all buddhas. That buddha lit up the whole world-system Born of the Light of Jewels clearly with a great multicolored light.

rgyal po'i gnas pad+mo'i 'od ces bya ba de na/ mtshan mo'i lha mo zla ba shin tu rnam par dag pa'i 'od ces bya ba 'dug 'dug ste/ de rgyal po'i btsun mo chos kyi blo gros zla ba'i gan du song nas; rgyan dkrol ba'i sgras sad par byas te/ 'di skad ces smras so/ / 'di ltar rgyal po'i btsun mo/ shes par gyis shig/ nags tshal chen po zhi ba'i dpal 'byung bar de bzhin gshegs pa; chos thams cad rab tu sgrog pa'i rgyal po zhes bya ba/ bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu mngon par sangs rgyas so/ / de nas des rgyal po'i btsun mo de'i mdun du/ sangs rgyas kyi yon tan bsngags pa dang / sangs rgyas kyi rnam par 'phrul pa dang / byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po'i spyod pa dang / smon lam rgya cher bshad do/ /

In the capital city of Padmaprabhā there was a goddess of the night called Suviśuddhacandrābhā. She approached Dharmamaticandrā, the king’s queen, woke her with the sound of rattling her jewelry, and said to her, ‘Know this, queen of the king! The Tathāgata Sarvadharmanigarjitarāja has attained the highest, complete enlightenment of buddhahood in the great forest Śamathaśrīsambhava.’ Then, in front of the king’s queen she praised the qualities of the buddha and described at length the miraculous manifestations of the buddhas and the completely good conduct and prayer of the bodhisattvas.

“Also in that capital city Lotus Light was a night goddess named Pure Moonlight. She went to the wife of the king, awakened her by the sound of her jewelry jingling, and said to her, ‘Know, O queen, that in the forest Source of Radiance of Peace, a buddha named Supreme Thunder of All Truths has attained supreme perfect enlightenment.’ And she gave the queen an extensive explanation of the virtuous qualities of the buddha, the spiritual transformation of the buddha, and the vow practices by universally good enlightening beings.

rigs kyi bu/ rgyal po'i btsun mo de yang / de bzhin gshegs pa'i 'od kyis snang bar gyur te/ bsam pa thag pas bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu yang dag par zhugs nas/ des de bzhin gshegs pa de dang / byang chub sems dpa' dang / nyan thos kyi dge 'dun du bcas pa la mchod pa dang / rim gro cher byas so/ /

“Noble one, the king’s queen was illuminated by the light from that tathāgata, and she sincerely entered into the path to the highest, complete enlightenment. She made offerings to that tathāgata and his saṅgha of bodhisattvas and śrāvakas.

The queen, illumined by the light of the buddha, set out for supreme perfect enlightenment with overpowering resolve. She made great offerings to that buddha and to his group of enlightening beings and disciples.

rigs kyi bu/ de la ji snyam du sems/ de'i tshe de'i dus kyi rgyal po'i btsun mo chos kyi blo gros zla ba zhes bya ba de/ gzhan zhig yin pa tsam du sems na ni de ltar mi blta ste/ kho mo ni de'i tshe de'i dus na/ rgyal po'i btsun mo chos kyi blo gros zla ba zhes bya bar gyur to/ /

“What do you think, noble one? At that time, in that time, who was that king’s queen, Dharmamaticandrā? Do not think that it was anyone else, for at that time, in that time, I was the king’s queen, Dharmamaticandrā.
“Do not suppose that queen was anyone other than me myself—I was that queen Moon of Understanding of Right in that time.

rigs kyi bu/ kho mo ni mos pa'i sems bskyed pa de dang / de bzhin gshegs pa la bskyed pa'i dge ba'i rtsa ba des/ bskal pa ri rab kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed tshun chad du nam yang ngan song ngan 'gro log par ltung bar ma skyes te/ sems can dmyal bar ma yin no/ / byol song gi skye gnas su ma yin no/ / yi su ma yin no/ / nam yang rigs dma' bar ma skyes so/ / nam yang dbang po dang mi ldan par ma gyur to/ / nam yang sdug bsngal bar ma gyur te/ de ltar kho mos rtag par lha'i nang du lha'i bdag nyid che ba nyid thob; mi'i nang du ni/ mi'i bdag nyid che ba nyid thob ste/ 'di ltar sangs rgyas dang / byang chub sems dpa'i dge ba'i bshes gnyen dang yang ma bral lo/ / dus ngan par yang ma skyes so; ;

“Noble one, under that tathāgata I developed the motivation of aspiration and created roots of merit so that for kalpas as numerous as the atoms in Sumeru I never fell into rebirth in the lower realms. I was never reborn as a denizen of hell, as an animal, or as a preta. I was never reborn in an inferior family. I was never reborn as someone without sensory faculties. I was never someone who suffered. I always attained the state of a great deity among deities, and a great human among humans. In this way, I was never apart from buddhas and bodhisattva kalyāṇamitras. I was never reborn in a bad time.

By virtue of that aspiration, and the roots of goodness I planted with that buddha, I was not born in any bad states for as many eons as atoms in the polar mountain, nor did I have defective faculties, nor did I suffer. I always attained celestial greatness among celestials, and human greatness among humans, and never was apart from spiritual benefactors—that is buddhas and enlightening beings. I never came upon bad times.

rigs kyi bu/ de ltar kho mos sangs rgyas gcig nas gcig tu dge ba'i rtsa ba bskyed de/ bskal pa ri rab kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed cig tu lam bde zhing mnyam pa nas nye zho med par phyin kyang / de tsam gyis kho mo'i byang chub sems dpa'i dbang po yongs su grub par ma gyur te/

“Noble one, in that way, I created roots of merit under one buddha after another, and for as many kalpas as there are atoms in Sumeru, I traveled on easy and level paths without any impediment, but I had not yet accomplished the powers of a bodhisattva.

So I passed as many eons as atoms in the polar mountain happily, peacefully, safely, and rightly, planting roots of goodness with the enlightened: yet after all that time my enlightening faculties were not yet perfectly developed.

ri rab kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi bskal pa de dag ni 'das/ bskal pa bzang po 'di'i snga rol gyi ni bskal pa chen po stong phrag bcu'i thog ma la bab pa de'i tshe/ 'jig rten gyi khams gzi brjid rdul gyi dri ma med pa zhes bya bar/ bskal pa mya ngan med cing rdul dang bral ba zhes bya ba byung ste/

When those kalpas as numerous as the atoms in Sumeru had passed, ten thousand great kalpas before this Bhadra kalpa, at the time of the first of those kalpas, which was called Aśokaviraja, there was a world realm called Rajovimalatejaḥśrī.
“After those eons had passed, ten thousand eons before this eon of Virtue, there was an eon called Sorrowless Dispassion, in a world called Blazing Light Undefiled by Passion.
rigs kyi bu/ 'jig rten gyi khams gzi brjid rdul gyi dri ma med pa'i dpal de ni/ kun nas nyon mongs pa rnam par dag par gyur te/ der sangs rgyas lnga brgya byung ngo/ /
“Noble one, that world realm Rajovimalatejaḥśrī was completely pure of the kleśas, and five hundred buddhas appeared within it.
That world was both defiled and pure. Five hundred buddhas were born there.

sangs rgyas lnga brgya po de dag gi thog ma la de bzhin gshegs pa mkhyen pa dang zhabs su ldan pa/ bde bar gshegs pa/ 'jig rten mkhyen pa/ bla na med par skyes bu 'dul ba'i kha lo sgyur ba; lha dang mi'i ston pa/ sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das ri rab rgyal mtshan spyan yangs shing zhi ba'i dpal zhes bya ba 'jig rten du byung ste/ de'i tshe kho mo yang tshong dpon snyan pa rnam par grags pa'i bu mo shes rab snang ba'i dpal zhes bya ba gzugs mdzes shing bzang la/ blta na sdug pa/ kha dog shin tu mdzes shing rgyas pa dang ldan pa zhig tu gyur te/

The first of those five hundred buddhas was a tathāgata, an arhat, a samyaksaṃbuddha, one with wisdom and conduct,[1321] a sugata, one who knows the world’s beings, an unsurpassable guide who tames beings, a teacher of devas and humans, a buddha, a bhagavat, who was named Sumerudhvajāyatanaśāntanetraśrī. At that time, I was Prajñāvabhāsaśrī, the daughter of the head merchant Vighuṣṭakīrti. I was beautiful and attractive, a delight to see, with a very beautiful, perfect complexion.
