The first of those five hundred buddhas was named Light of Tranquil Eyes with Senses Like the Polar Mountain, accomplished in knowledge and action, gone to felicity, supreme knower of the world, guide of tractable people, teacher of celestials and humans, enlightened, blessed. I was an outstanding girl named Light of Wisdom, daughter of an eminent man named Resounding Fame, and I was beautiful and robust.

mtshan mo'i lha mo zla ba shin tu rnam par dag pa'i 'od ces bya ba de yang smon lam gyi dbang gis/ gling bzhi pa'i 'jig rten gyi khams rdul dang bral ba'i rgyal po'i gnas rgyal mtshan sna tshogs su; mtshan mo'i lha mo mig rnam par dag pa zhes bya bar gyur te/ des kho mo mtshan mo mi nyal tsam zhig na/ pha ma nyal bar gyur pa dang / khyim de'ang yongs su bskyod de/ 'od chen po snang bar byas nas rang gi gzugs bstan te/ sangs rgyas kyi yon tan bsngags pa brjod nas/ de bzhin gshegs pa thog ma mngon par sangs rgyas nas zhag bdun lon te/ snying po byang chub la bzhugs pa de bstan to/ /

“The goddess of the night called Suviśuddhacandrābhā, through the power of her prayers, had become the goddess of the night called Viśuddhanetrābhā in Vicitradhvaja, the capital of the four-continent world realm named Virajovatī. At night, while I was not yet asleep and my parents were asleep, she shook our house, illuminated it with a great light, revealed her own form to me, and praised the qualities of the buddhas. She revealed the tathāgata residing at the bodhimaṇḍa seven days after he had attained buddhahood.

The night goddess Pure Moonlight, by the power of a vow, became a night goddess named Light of Purified Eyes. In the still of the night when my parents were in bed, she made our house tremble, showed her body to me with a great light, told me about the qualities of the buddha, and then showed me the buddha sitting at the enlightenment site in the first week after his enlightenment.
de nas kho mo pha ma dang / gnyen bshes kyi tshogs chen po dang 'grogs te/ mtshan mo'i lha mo shin tu rnam par dag pa'i zla ba'i 'od sngon du bdar nas/ de bzhin gshegs pa de'i spyan sngar phyin to/ /
“Then, accompanied by my parents and a great crowd of my family, and preceded by Viśuddhanetrābhā, the goddess of the night, I went into the presence of that tathāgata.
“I went with my parents and a large group of relatives to that buddha, led by the night goddess Pure Moonlight.

de nas kho mos de bzhin gshegs pa de la mchod pa rgya chen po byas te/ de bzhin gshegs pa de'i zhal mthong ma thag tu/ ting nge 'dzin 'gro ba 'dul zhing sangs rgyas mthong bar byed pa zhes bya ba dang / ting nge 'dzin dus gsum gyi dbyings ye shes kyi snang ba'i dkyil 'khor ces bya ba'ang thob par gyur to/ / de thob pas kyang kho mos bskal pa ri rab kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed po de dag kyang rjes su dran par gyur to/ / kho mo'i byang chub kyi sems de yang mngon du gyur te/

I then made vast offerings to the Tathāgata, and as soon as I saw the Tathāgata’s face, I attained the samādhi called guiding beings and seeing the Buddha’s face and the samādhi called the domain illuminated by the wisdom of the range of the three times. Through attaining them I remembered as many kalpas as there are atoms in Sumeru. My aspiration to enlightenment manifested.

I made great offerings to that buddha, and when I saw the buddha, I attained a concentration called ‘born of the world-guiding vision of Buddha,’ and I attained a concentration called ‘sphere of light of knowledge of the ground of past, present, and future,’ whereby I remembered those eons as many as atoms in the polar mountain; and my aspiration for enlightenment came to the fore.

de ltar kho mos de bzhin gshegs pa de las chos bstan pa thos te/ byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa sems can thams cad kyi mun pa rnam par sel ba'i chos kyi snang bas 'gro ba rnam par 'dul ba'i sgo 'di yang thob par gyur to/ / de thob pas kyang 'jig rten gyi khams sangs rgyas kyi zhing bcu'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed lus kyis rgyas par 'gengs te/ 'jig rten gyi khams de dag tu de bzhin gshegs pa ji snyed cig bzhugs pa de dag thams cad kyang kho mo'i mig lam du snang zhing / bdag nyid kyang de dag thams cad kyi zhabs kyi drung na 'dug par shes so/ / 'jig rten kyi khams de dag tu sems can ji snyed cig skyes pa de dag thams cad kyang / kho mo'i mig lam du snang ste/ de dag gi sgra skrad [*skad?] rnam pa tha dad pa'i brda yang rab tu shes so/ / sems dang / bsam pa dang / dbang po dang / mos pa yang rab tu shes so/ / sngon gyi mtha'i dge ba'i bshes gnyen rnams kyi drung du yongs su smin par gyur pa'ang rab tu shes so/ / de dag la bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du tshim par 'gyur ba'i lus kyang yongs su ston to/ /

In that way, I heard the Dharma from that tathāgata, and I attained the bodhisattva liberation called the gateway to guiding beings through the radiance of the Dharma that eliminates the darkness of all beings. Through attaining that, I pervaded with my body as many worlds as there are atoms in ten buddha realms, and there appeared to my sight all the buddhas who were present in those worlds, and I knew that I was present at the feet of all of them. All of the beings who had been born in those world realms appeared to my sight, and I knew all the symbols of their different languages. I knew their minds, thoughts, faculties, and aspirations. I knew the past kalyāṇamitras in whose presence they were ripened. I manifested to them the bodies that satisfied them according to their aspirations.

Having heard the Teaching from that buddha, I attained this enlightening liberation called ‘the means of guiding sentient beings by the light of truth which dispels the darkness for all sentient beings,’ by the attainment of which I physically pervade as many worlds as atoms in ten buddha-lands, and see the buddhas in those worlds, and perceive myself at the feet of those buddhas. I also see all the sentient beings in those worlds, and I know their vocal signals, and their thoughts, inclinations, faculties, and interests, and their previous development under the tutelage of spiritual benefactors; and I manifest a body to them which will please them according to their inclinations.

kho mo'i rnam par thar pa de yang sems kyi skad cig re re la rnam par 'phel te/ rnam par thar pa'i sems de'i 'og ma'i sems kyis/ sangs rgyas kyi zhing 'jig rten gyi khams brgya'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed lus kyis rgyas par 'gengs so/ / de'i 'og ma'i sems kyis sangs rgyas kyi zhing 'jig rten gyi khams stong gi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed lus kyis rgyas par 'gengs so/ / de'i 'og ma'i sems kyis sangs rgyas kyi zhing 'jig rten gyi khams brgya phrag stong gi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed lus kyis rgyas par 'gengs so/ / de bzhin du sems kyi skad cig re re zhing / sangs rgyas kyi zhing 'jig rten gyi khams brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi bar dag kyang lus kyis rgyas par 'gengs so/ / sangs rgyas kyi zhing de dag na/ de bzhin gshegs pa ji snyed cig bzhugs pa de dag thams cad kyang kho mo'i mig lam du snang ste/ bdag nyid kyang de dag gi zhabs kyi drung na 'dug par shes so/ / sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das de dag gis chos bstan pa de dag thams cad kyang len to; ; 'dzin to/ / yongs su 'dzin to/ / nye bar 'dzin to/ / de bzhin gshegs pa de dag gi sngon gyi tshul rgya mtsho dang / smon lam rgya mtsho la yang 'jug go/ de bzhin gshegs pa de dag gi sangs rgyas kyi zhing yongs su dag pa de dag thams cad kyang rang gi sangs rgyas kyi zhing yongs su dag par bya ba'i phyir mngon par sgrub bo/ / sems can ji snyed cig 'jig rten gyi khams rgya mtsho de dag tu skyes par gyur ba de dag thams cad kyang kho mo'i mig lam du snang ste/ sems can de dag gi bsam pa dang / dbang po dang / mos pa'i bye brag ji snyed pa de snyed kyi bre brag tu de dag yongs su smin par bya ba dang / gdul ba'i phyir lus byin gyis rlob ste/

That liberation of mine increased with each instant of the mind. Through the instant of mind that followed that instant of mind of liberation, my body pervaded as many buddha realms as there are atoms in a hundred world realms. Through the next instant of mind, my body pervaded as many buddha realms as there are atoms in a thousand world realms. Through the next instant of mind, my body pervaded as many buddha realms as there are atoms in a hundred thousand world realms, and so on, up to my body pervading, in each instant of mind, as many buddha realms as there are atoms in an anabhilāpyānabhilāpya of world realms. There appeared to my sight all the buddhas that were present in those worlds, and I knew that I was present at the feet of all of them. I obtained all the Dharma that was taught by those buddha bhagavats. I possessed it, kept it, preserved it. I comprehended the past ocean of ways and ocean of prayers of those tathāgatas. All those buddha realms purified by those tathāgatas were created in order to purify their own buddha realms. All of the beings who had been born in those world realms appeared to my sight. I blessed my body in order to ripen and guide all of their different minds, thoughts, faculties, and aspirations.

“Also, this liberation grows in each mental moment: in an unbroken succession of mental moments I pervade as many buddha-lands as atoms in a hundred worlds, as many buddha-lands as atoms in a thousand worlds, as many buddha-lands as atoms in a hundred thousand worlds; in each mental moment I go on like this to pervade up to as many buddha-lands as atoms in untold unspeakable numbers of worlds: and I see all the buddhas in those lands, and I perceive myself in their presence, and I hear, take in, remember, reflect on, and meditate on the teachings of those buddhas. I also enter into the oceans of past vows of those buddhas, and the purifications of the buddha-lands of those buddhas. I also undertake to purify a buddha-land. I also see the sentient beings in those oceans of worlds, and I transform my body to accord with the measures of the inclinations, faculties, and interests of those sentient beings, in order to develop and guide them.
de ltar kho mo'i rnam par thar pa de ni sems kyi skad cig re re la yang / chos kyi dbyings 'byams klas pa rgyas par 'gengs pa'i tshul gyis rnam par 'phel lo/ /
“Thus, the way in which my liberation pervaded the entire extent of the realm of phenomena increased with each instant of mind.
Thus this liberation expands in each mental moment, by working to expand it to pervade everywhere in the cosmos.

rigs kyi bu/ kho mos byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa sems can thams cad kyi mun pa rnam par sel ba'i chos kyi snang bas/ 'gro ba rnam par 'dul ba'i sgo 'di shes par zad na/ kho mos byang chub sems dpa' mtha' dang dbus med pa'i byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po'i spyod pa dang / smon lam gyis byung ba/ chos kyi dbyings rgya mtsho'i tshul 'byams klas pa 'dal ba la 'jug par dbang bsgyur ba/ byang chub sems dpas yang dag par bsgrub pa'i ting nge 'dzin ye shes rdo rje'i dpal gyis rnam par rtse ba dang / 'jig rten gyi khams thams cad du de bzhin gshegs pa'i rigs thams cad yang dag par gzung ba la smon lam chen pos byung ba/ 'jig rten gyi khams 'byams klas pa thams cad sems kyi skad cig gcig gis yongs su dag par bya ba'i bsod nams kyi rgya mtsho chen po yongs su grub pa/ sems kyi skad cig re re la sems can gyi khams thams cad yongs su smin par bya ba dang / gdul ba'i ye shes dbang bsgyur ba/ 'jig rten gyi khams thams cad du sems can thams cad kyi sgrib pa'i mun pa thams cad rnam par sel ba'i ye shes kyi nyi ma'i mig dang ldan pa/ sems can gyi khams thams cad la theg pa chen po rnam par dmigs par bya ba'i mthu dang ldan pa/ 'gro ba thams cad kyi the tshom dang / nem nur dang / yid gnyis kyi rab rib rnam par sel ba'i blo gros kyi zla ba dang ldan pa/ srid pa'i rgya mtsho thams cad la mngon par chags pa las gyen du bskyod pa'i sgra dbyangs kyi dkyil 'khor rnam par dag pa; chos kyi dbyings thams cad kyi rdul gyi cha shas la rnam par 'phrul pa yongs su ston pa la dbang bsgyur ba/ dus gsum gyi dbyings kyi dkyil 'khor la ye shes dbyer med pa de dag gi spyod pa shes pa'am/ yon tan brjod pa'am/ spyod yul la 'jug pa'am/ rnam par thar pas rnam par rtse ba yongs su bstan par nus re skan/

“Noble one, I know only this bodhisattva liberation called the gateway to guiding beings through the radiance of the Dharma that eliminates the darkness of all beings. How could I know the conduct or describe the qualities of bodhisattvas who have arisen from the completely good bodhisattva conduct and prayers that have no middle or edge; who have the power to enter the entire extent of the ways of the ocean of the realm of phenomena; who play in the samādhi called the glorious vajra of wisdom, which is attained by bodhisattvas[1322] who have arisen from the great prayers to be in the care of all the families of tathāgatas in all world realms; who have accomplished a great ocean of merit that purified in an instant of mind the vast extent of world realms; who in each instant of mind ripen all the realms of beings; who have the eyes of the sun of wisdom that dispels all the darkness of the obscurations of all beings in all the world realms that are under the power of their guiding wisdom; who have the power to communicate the Mahāyāna to all the realms of beings; who possess the moon of intelligence that dispels the darkness of doubt, uncertainty, and equivocation within all beings; who have the pure domain of speech that lifts beings from attachment to the entire ocean of existence; who have the power to manifest emanations in the atoms throughout the entire realm of phenomena; and who are inseparable from the domain of the knowledge of the entire range of the three times?

“I only know this enlightening liberation that is a method of guiding the world by the light of the truth which dispels the darkness of all sentient beings—how can I know the practice or tell of the virtues or comprehend the sphere or show the freedom of liberation of the enlightening beings who are completely versed in the infinite vow of enlightening practice of universal good, who command the power to enter into every principle in the ocean of the cosmos, who have mastered the adamantine concentration of knowledge realized by all enlightening beings, who have undertaken the vow to preserve the lineage of buddhas in all worlds, who have perfected great goodness purifying all worlds in each mental moment, who command the knowledge to develop and guide all universes in each mental moment, whose eyes are suns that dispel the darkness of all obstructions for all sentient beings in all worlds, who strive to inform all sentient beings about the Great Vehicle of universal liberation, who are moons of wisdom dispelling the darkness of doubt and confusion for all sentient beings, whose pure voices obliterate attachment to existence, who have the power to show miracles in each atom of all phenomena, who have unfragmented knowledge of the ground of past, present, and future?

song / rigs kyi bu/ yul ma ga d+ha 'di nyid kyi snying po byang chub la kho mo bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed bskyed pa/ yang dang yang bskul bskul ba'i mtshan mo'i lha mo kun tu zab pa'i dpal dri ma med pa'i 'od ces bya ba 'dug gi/ de'i gan du song la/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bya ba dang; ji ltar nan tan du bya ba dris shig/

“Depart, noble one. At the bodhimaṇḍa in this land of Magadha there is the goddess of the night called Samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhā, whom I have inspired again and again to develop the aspiration for the highest, complete enlightenment. Go to her and ask her, ‘How should a bodhisattva train in bodhisattva conduct? How should a bodhisattva practice it?’ ”

“In this very enlightenment site in Magadha lives a night goddess named Samantagambhirashrivimalaprabha, who inspired in me the determination for enlightenment and has encouraged me time and again. Go ask her how to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings.”
de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis/ mtshan mo'i lha mo dpyid dang ldan pa la/ tshigs su bcad pa 'di dag gis mngon par bstod do/ /
Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, praised the night goddess Vāsantī with these verses:
Then Sudhana praised the night goddess with these verses:
khyod sku shin tu rnam par dag pa mthong / / mtshan gyis rnam brgyan ri bo ji bzhin du/ / 'jig rten kun las mngon 'phags 'jig rten du/ / phun sum tshogs sku 'jam dpal bzhin du mdzes/ /
“I see the purity of your body Adorned by signs, like Meru, Superior to all worlds; within the world You have a perfect body as beautiful as Mañjuśrī’s. {22}
I see your body now, pure, with various characteristics, Like the polar mountain. Above the world, you illumine the world, With a body like Manjushri.
khyod kyi chos sku shin tu rnam dag ste/ / dus gsum kun tu mnyam zhing rnam mi rtog / der ni 'jig rten ma lus kun 'dus te/ / 'byung zhing rnam par 'jig kyang chags mi mnga'; ;
“Your Dharma body is completely pure, The same in all three times, without conceptualization. Every world without exception is contained within it Without creation, destruction, or abiding. {23}
Your reality body is transcendentally pure, Equal in all times, without distinction: Therein all worlds are gathered, And form and dissolve without obstruction.
lam rgyud 'byams klas thams cad kun tu yang / / khyod kyi sku ni gzugs brnyan rnam par phye/ / skar chen zla skar rgyu skar tshogs bzhin du/ / spu rtse kun la'ang khyod ni bdag gis mthong / /
“I see the image of your body dispersed Throughout the whole extent of existences, And I see within the pores of your body The constellations of stars with the moon and planets. {24}
I see your body in all realms, In a variety of manifestations: And in your pores I see The moon and stars.
khyod kyi thugs yangs shin tu rnam dag ste/ / phyogs rnams kun gyi nam mkha'i dbyings su rgyas/ / der ni mi mchog kun kyang yongs su 'du/ / khyod la ye shes mi rtog dam pa mnga'/ /
“Your mind also is completely pure, Pervading the realm of space in all directions. Even the supreme among humans are all included within it. You possess the supreme wisdom free of concepts. {25}
Your mind is broad and pure, pervading Like space in all directions; Therein are assembled all buddhas, Yet your knowledge is free from the taint of discrimination.

zhing gi rdul snyed rnam pa sna tshogs sprin/ / khyod kyi spu rtse kun nas mngon 'thon pa/ / rgyal mang sna tshogs char pa mngon 'bebs shing / / phyogs bcu'i sangs rgyas zhabs drung rgyas par 'gengs/ /
“Multicolored clouds as numerous as the atoms in a realm Arise out of all the pores of your body, Spread to the buddhas in the ten directions, And send down a rainfall of all adornments. {26}
Brilliant clouds, as many as atoms in lands, Issue from your pores; They reach the buddhas in the ten directions, Raining all kinds of ornaments.
'gro ba kun snyed lus rnams mtha' yas pa/ / khyod kyi spu rtse kun nas mngon 'thon cing / / phyogs bcu'i 'jig rten rgyas par yongs bkang nas/ / sna tshogs thabs kyis sems can rnam par spyod/ /

“The endless number of the bodies as numerous as beings Arise out of the pores of your body. They pervade and fill the worlds in the ten directions And purify[1323] beings through various methods. {27}
Infinite bodies, as many as living beings, Emerge from your pores; They fill all the worlds in the ten directions, And purify beings by various means.
spu rtse kun la bsam yas zhing gi rnams/ / sna tshogs rgyan ldan rnam pa tha dad mthong / / lam rgyud sems can khyod kyis rnam sbyangs pa/ / ji snyed de dag bsam bzhin kun kyang byung / /

“I see an inconceivable number of realms With various different displays in all your pores. They appear in accordance with all the aspirations Of those you purify in the various existences of beings. {28}
I see inconceivably many lands in your pores, Adorned in various ways, Which you have purified, Produced according to the minds of the beings.
gang zhig khyod kyi mtshan thos dga' gyur pa/ / de dag thob bya legs thob legs par 'tsho/ / sems can gang gis khyod kyi sku mthong ba/ / byang chub lam la mngon du bltas par 'gyur/ /
“Whoever rejoices on hearing your name Will easily attain their goals and live well. Whatever being sees your body Will be facing the path to enlightenment. {29}
Happy are those who hear your name, Great is their gain; And people who see you Are near the path of enlightenment.
de ltar thos nas rab tu sems dga' la/ / mthong ba tsam gyis nyon mongs zhi mdzad pas/ / bskal pa bsam yas ngan song gnas kyang rung / / khyod kyi zhal blta'i don du mos par bgyi/ /
“Merely seeing you causes the kleśas to cease In one who rejoices on hearing your name. I would endure countless kalpas in the lower realms So that I could see your face. {30}
One should endure inconceivable eons of misfortune In order to see you; For those who are happy to hear of you, You will extinguish their afflictions on sight.
zhing rnams stong gi rdul snyed lus byas te/ / de snyed bskal pa brgyud de khyod 'dra ba'i/ / spu gcig khyod kyi yon tan legs brjod kyang / / legs pa'i mthar phyin nam du'ang mi 'gyur ro/ /

“If I were to create as many bodies as there are atoms in a thousand realms, And for the duration of that same number of kalpas They were to describe the qualities of just one of your pores, They would never be able to reach the end of that description.” {31}
Even if one were to speak Of your qualities for as many eons As atoms in a thousand lands, There is no exhausting them.

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis/ mtshan mo'i lha mo dpyid dang ldan pa la tshigs su bcad pa de dag gis mngon par bstod nas/ mtshan mo'i lha mo dpyid dang ldan pa'i rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te/ mtshan mo'i lha mo dpyid dang ldan pa la/ lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas yang dang yang bltas te/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen la bsnyen bkur bya bas ma ngoms bzhin du/ mtshan mo'i lha mo dpyid dang ldan pa'i drung nas song ngo// //

Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, bowed his head to the feet of the night goddess Vāsantī, circumambulated the night goddess Vāsantī many hundreds of thousands of times, keeping her to his right, and, looking back again and again with unfulfilled longing, departed from the night goddess Vāsantī.
Having praised the night goddess Vasanti with these verses, Sudhana paid his respects to her, looking at her again and again, never tired of attending spiritual benefactors, and left her.
bam po dgu bcu rtsa dgu pa/

d.crumb: [mtshan mo'i lha mo kun tu zab pa'i dpal dri ma med pa'i 'od]

f.d: [mtshan mo'i lha mo kun tu zab pa'i dpal dri ma med pa'i 'od]
Chapter 35. Samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhā
Samantagambhirashrivimalaprabha

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang / mtshan mo'i lha mo dpyid dang ldan pa/ thog ma byang chub tu zhugs pa'i byang chub kyi sems kyi dkyil 'khor yongs su dag pa ni khong du chud par byed/ byang chub sems dpa'i snying po yang dag par byung ba la ni rjes su dpyod/ byang chub sems dpa'i smon lam rgya mtsho la ni yongs su 'jug/ byang chub sems dpa'i pha rol tu phyin pa'i lam ni yongs su sbyong / byang chub sems dpa'i sa'i dkyil 'khor ni yongs su gnon/ byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa'i dkyil 'khor ni rgya cher byed/ byang chub sems dpa'i 'byung ba rgya mtsho ni rjes su 'brang / thams cad mkhyen pa'i snang ba chen po rgya mtsho la ni rnam par blta/ 'gro ba thams cad yongs su bskyab pa la gzhol ba'i byang chub sems dpa'i snying rje chen po'i sprin ni rgya cher byed/ mtshan mo'i lha mo dpyid dang ldan pa'i byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po'i spyod pa dang / smon lam gyi dkyil 'khor ni/ zhing thams cad du phyi ma'i mthar byin gyis brlabs pas mngon par bsgrub cing / mtshan mo'i lha mo kun tu zab pa'i dpal dri ma med pa'i 'od gang na ba der song ste/ mtshan mo'i lha mo kun tu zab pa'i dpal dri ma med pa'i 'od kyi rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te/ mtshan mo'i lha mo kun tu zab pa'i dpal dri ma med pa'i 'od la/ lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas/ mtshan mo'i lha mo kun tu zab pa'i dpal dri ma med pa'i 'od kyi mdun du 'dug ste/ thal mo sbyar nas 'di skad ces smras so/ / 'phags ma/ bdag gis bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed na/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i sa la spyod pa dang / ji ltar 'byung ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bgyid pa ma 'tshal to/ /

Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, contemplating the night goddess Vāsantī’s first entry into the pure domain of aspiration to enlightenment, analyzing the arising of the essence of a bodhisattva, comprehending the ocean of bodhisattva prayer, purifying the bodhisattva path of perfections, overcoming the domain of the bodhisattva levels, augmenting the domain of bodhisattva conduct, following[1324] an ocean of the setting-forth of bodhisattvas, looking at the ocean of the great illumination of omniscience, increasing the bodhisattva clouds of great compassion intent on saving all beings, and attaining the blessing of the completely good bodhisattva conduct and prayer of the night goddess Vāsantī that extends to the limits of all realms, went to the location of the night goddess Samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhā. Having reached her, he bowed his head to the feet of the night goddess Samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhā, circumambulated the night goddess Samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhā many hundreds of thousands of times, keeping her to his right, and then stood before her and, with palms together, said, “Āryā, I have developed the aspiration for the highest, complete enlightenment. However, I do not know how a bodhisattva practices on the level of a bodhisattva, how a bodhisattva sets forth, how a bodhisattva accomplishes.”

Realizing the purity of the sphere of the night goddess Vasanti’s initial stage of determination to be an enlightening being, contemplating the origin of the embryo of enlightenment, entering into the ocean of vows of enlightening beings, purifying the path of transcendent ways of enlightening beings, going into the sphere of stages of enlightening beings, extending the sphere of practice of enlightening beings, remembering the ocean of ways of emancipation of enlightening beings, looking over the vast ocean of light of omniscience, extending the cloud of great compassion of enlightening beings intent on the salvation of all sentient beings, putting Vasanti’s vow of practice of universally good enlightening action into effect throughout all lands forever, Sudhana went to the night goddess Samantagambhirashrivimalaprabha, paid his respects to her, and said, “Noble goddess, I have set my mind on supreme perfect enlightenment, but I do not know how an enlightening being acts in the stage of enlightening practice, or how one proceeds, and how one perfects it.”

smras pa/ rigs kyi bu/ de ltar khyod bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed cing / byang chub sems dpa'i sa la spyod pa dang / 'byung ba dang / yongs su 'grub pa 'dri ba legs so/ /legs so/ /

She answered, “Noble one, it is excellent, excellent, that you have developed the aspiration for the highest, complete enlightenment and that you ask how to practice, set forth, and accomplish on the level of a bodhisattva.
She said, “It is good that, aspiring to enlightenment, you ask how to proceed and how to fully accomplish the stages of enlightening beings.
rigs kyi bu/ chos bcu dang ldan pa'i byang chub sems dpa' rnams/ byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la yongs su grub pa yin te/ bcu gang zhe na/
It is through possessing ten qualities that bodhisattvas accomplish bodhisattva conduct. What are these ten?
By the fulfillment of ten things is the practice of enlightening beings accomplished:
'di lta ste/ de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad mngon du gyur par mthong ba'i ting nge 'dzin thob pa rnam par dag pa dang /
They are (1) the pure attainment of the samādhi that directly perceives all the tathāgatas;
by purification of attainment of concentration in which all buddhas are seen face to face;
sangs rgyas thams cad kyi sku mtshan sna tshogs dang ldan pa rnam par blta ba'i mig rnam par dag pa dang /
(2) the pure eyesight that sees the bodies, endowed with the various signs, of all the buddhas;
by purification of the eye viewing the infinite body of all buddhas resplendent with marks of distinction;
de bzhin gshegs pa'i kha dog rgya mtsho mtha' dang dbus med pa rnam par dmigs par bya ba la 'jug pa dang /
(3) realizing the perception of the centerless, endless ocean of the colors of the tathāgatas;
by entering into the manifestation of the infinite ocean of qualities of buddhas;
sangs rgyas kyi chos snang ba'i dkyil 'khor rgya mtsho tshad med pa la chos kyi dbyings thams cad kyi tshad kyis 'jug pa dang /
(4) comprehending the extent of the entire realm of phenomena and the measureless ocean of the domain of the radiant qualities of the buddhas;
by realizing the cosmic dimensions of the ocean of spheres of the infinite manifestations of the teaching of buddhas;
de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi ba spu'i sgo nas 'od zer rgya mtsho sems can thams cad dang mnyam pa dang / sems can sna tshogs kyi don du bkye ba la 'jug pa dang /
(5) comprehending the ocean of light rays from the pores of all the tathāgatas that are as numerous as all beings and radiate to benefit the variety of beings;
by entering the emanation of multitudes of beams of light, as many as beings, from the pores of all buddhas, aiding sentient beings in various ways;
ba spu'i bu ga re re nas 'od 'phro ba rin po che thams cad kyi kha dog tu 'dug pa rgya mtsho ston pa dang /
(6) seeing an ocean of light rays, the colors of all jewels, coming from each pore;
by seeing oceans of flames the colors of all jewels coming from each pore;
sems kyi skad cig re re la sangs rgyas kyi sprul pa rgya mtshos chos kyi dbyings thams cad rgyas par bkang zhing / sems can 'dul ba'i byin gyi rlabs la 'jug pa dang /
(7) comprehending the ocean of emanations of the buddhas that in each instant of mind pervade the entire realm of phenomena and give the blessing that guides beings;
by penetrating the my stical manifestation of oceans of emanations of buddhas pervading all universes and guiding sentient beings in each mental moment;

de bzhin gshegs pa'i gsung sems can thams cad kyi dbyangs kyi yan lag dang ldan pas dus gsum du byung ba'i chos kyi 'khor lo'i sgra sgrogs pas/ mdo sde thams cad kyi sprin gyi 'brug sgra 'byin pa'i dkyil 'khor la 'jug pa dang /

(8) comprehending the domain of thunder from the clouds of all the sūtras through possessing the speech of the tathāgatas, which has the aspects of the voices of all beings, and the sound of the wheel of the Dharma appearing in the three times;
by penetrating the sounds of thunder of all the scriptures proclaimed in the past, present, and future cycles of teachings of the buddhas, using the myriad languages of all sentient beings;
sangs rgyas gyi mtshan rgya mtsho mtha' dang dbus med pa la 'jug pa dang /
(9) comprehending the centerless and endless ocean of the signs of the buddhas;
by entry into the infinite ocean of buddha-names;
sangs rgyas kyi rnam par 'phrul ba bsam gyis mi khyab pa yongs su bstan pas sems can 'dul ba la 'jug pa ste/
and (10) comprehending the guiding of beings through the manifestation of the inconceivable emanations of the buddhas.
by penetrating the guidance of sentient beings by manifestation of inconceivable miraculous transformations of buddhas.
rigs kyi bu/ chos bcu po 'di dag dang ldan pa'i byang chub sems dpa' rnams/ byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la yongs su grub pa yin no/ /
“Noble one, the bodhisattvas who possess these ten qualities accomplish bodhisattva conduct.
By attainment of these ten things, enlightening beings become fully accomplished in enlightening practice.
rigs kyi bu/ kho mo ni byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa bsam gtan zhi ba'i bde bas kun tu rnam par gnon pa thob pa ste/
“Noble one, I have attained the bodhisattva liberation called complete subjugation through the bliss of the peace of śamatha.
“I have attained the enlightening liberation ‘bliss of tranquil meditation boldly going everywhere.’

rigs kyi bu/ kho mo ni de'i mthus dus gsum du gshegs pa'i de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyang mthong ste/ de bzhin gshegs pa de dag gi sangs rgyas kyi zhing yongs su dag pa la'ang 'jug go / 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor rgya mtsho dang / ting nge 'dzin mtha' dang dbus med pa'i rnam par 'phrul pa rgya mtsho dang / sngon gyi tshul rgya mtsho dang / mtshan rgya mtsho la'ang 'jug go/ de bzhin gshegs pa de dag gi chos kyi 'khor lo rab tu 'khor ba rnam pa tha dad pa la'ang 'jug go/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i sku tshe tshad sna tshogs dang / dbyangs kyi yan lag rnam pa tha dad pa dang / de bzhin gshegs pa de dag gi chos kyi dbyings mtha' dang dbus med pa'i sku la'ang 'jug ste/

“Noble one, through its power I see all the tathāgatas who are in the three times, and I perceive the completely pure buddha realms of those tathāgatas. I perceive the ocean of their assemblies of followers, the ocean of their centerless and endless miraculous manifestations from samādhi, the ocean of their past practices, and the ocean of their names. I also perceive each separate turning of the wheel of the Dharma by those tathāgatas. I perceive the various lifespans and different aspects of voice of those tathāgatas and the bodies of those tathāgatas who have the nature of the centerless and limitless realm of phenomena.

By this I see the buddhas of past, present, and future, and enter into their oceanic congregations, their oceanic projections by concentration, their oceanic efforts in the past, and the oceans of their names. I also comprehend the differences of the teaching cycles of those buddhas, the variety of their life spans, the differences in their voices, and their embodiment of the infinite realm of reality.
de bzhin gshegs pa de dag la dngos por mngon par zhen pa yang med do/ /
“Those tathāgatas are not attached to things as being existent.
Yet I do not become attached to those buddhas in terms of state of being.
de ci'i phyir zhe na/ 'jig rten gyi khams thams cad du bzhud pa 'gags pa'i phyir/ de bzhin gshegs pa de dag ni bzhud pa med pa'o; ;
Why is that? Those tathāgatas do not go because of their cessation of going through all worlds.
Why? Because those buddhas do not go, having stopped all worldly courses of action;
rang bzhin gyis byung ba med pas na de bzhin gshegs pa de dag ni byon pa med pa'o/ /
Those tathāgatas do not arrive because their nature has no arising.
they do not come, because of the nonbecoming of intrinsic nature;
mi skye ba'i chos nyid dang mnyam pa'i sku mnga' ba'i phyir/ de bzhin gshegs pa de dag ni ma skyes pa'o/ /
Those tathāgatas are unborn because they have a body that is the same as the birthless true nature.
they are not present, being physically equal to the unoriginated nature of reality;
mi skye ba'i mtshan nyid dang ldan pa'i phyir/ de bzhin gshegs pa de dag ni ma 'gags pa'o/ /
Those tathāgatas are unceasing because they have the characteristic of birthlessness.
they are not extinct, being characterized by nonorigination;
sgyu ma'i rnam pa lta bur mthong zhing rnam par dmigs pa'i phyir/ de bzhin gshegs pa de dag ni bden pa ma yin pa'o/ /
Those tathāgatas are not true[1325] because of perceiving and seeing phenomena to be illusions.
they are not real, because they convey the vision of phenomena as in illusion;
'gro ba thams cad kyi don du byung ba'i phyir/ de bzhin gshegs pa de dag ni brdzun pa ma yin pa'o/ /
Those tathāgatas are not false because there arises benefit for all beings.
they are not false, because of accomplishing the welfare of all beings;
shi 'pho dang skye ba las rnam par 'das pa'i phyir/ de bzhin gshegs pa de dag ni 'pho ba med pa'o/ /
Those tathāgatas do not pass away because they have transcended death, passing, and birth.
they do not pass from one condition to another, because they are free from death and birth;
chos kyi rang bzhin gyis 'jigs pa med pa'i chos nyid yin pa'i phyir/ de bzhin gshegs pa de dag ni 'jig pa med pa'o/ /
Those tathāgatas are not destroyed because the indestructible true nature is the nature of phenomena.
they do not perish, because of the imperishable nature of things;
ngag gi lam thams cad las yongs su 'das pa'i phyir/ de bzhin gshegs pa de dag thams cad ni mtshan nyid gcig pa'o/ /
All those tathāgatas have a single characteristic because of their transcendence of all paths of speech.
they are uniform, because they are beyond all manner of speech;
chos kyi mtshan nyid kyi rang bzhin gyi mthar thug pas/ de bzhin gshegs pa de dag ni mtshan nyid mi mnga' ba'o/ /
Those tathāgatas do not have characteristics because they are the termination of the nature of the characteristics of phenomena.
they are formless, because of being done with the forms and natures of things.

rigs kyi bu/ kho mo ni de ltar de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad khong du chud par byed cing / byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa bsam gtan zhi ba'i bde bas kun tu rnam par gnon pa 'di/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i bsam gtan gyi dkyil 'khor snang bas shin tu rgya che bar byed do/ / shin tu yangs par byed do/ / khong du chud par byed do/ / rtogs par byed do/ / mnyam par byed do/ / mngon par bsgrub bo/ / gzhi snyoms par byed do/ / rab tu 'jug go/ rnam par 'phel bar byed do/ / nges par sems so/ / nye bar rtog go/ dran par byed do/ / spyod yul du byed do/ / brtan par byed do/ / snang bar byed do/ / rab tu brjod do/ / rnam par spyod do/ / rnam par 'byed do/ / tshogs su byed do/ / yid ches par byed do/ /

“Noble one, I perceive all tathāgatas in that way, and through the radiance of the tathāgatas’ domain of dhyāna, I increase this bodhisattva liberation called complete subjugation through the bliss of the peace of śamatha; I make it vast, perceive it, realize it, make it even, accomplish it, make it level, enter it, augment it, contemplate it, reflect upon it, am mindful of it, make it my field of practice, make it firm, illuminate it, explain it, divide it, categorize it, unite it, and have conviction in it.

“Furthermore, while thus understanding all buddhas, by the light of the sphere of meditation of buddhas I expand this enlightening liberation ‘bliss of tranquil meditation boldly going everywhere’; I extend it, enter into it, follow it, live up to it, accomplish it, make it consistent, delve into it, develop it, meditate on it, contemplate it, internalize it, make it my sphere of action, stabilize it, make it manifest, illumine it, order it, analyze it, fulfill its requirements, and effect it.

yongs su rtog pa thams cad rgyu ba med pa'i snying rje chen po de la gnas te/ sems can thams cad yongs su bskyab pa la yang dag par spyad par sems rtse gcig tu bya ba'i phyir bsam gtan dang po bsgom mo/ /
“I meditate on the first dhyāna in order to remain in that great compassion in which there is no movement of any thought and in order to have a single-pointed mind for engaging in saving all beings.
“Therein, based on great compassion without any false conceptions, to focus my mind solely on carrying out the salvation of all beings, I cultivate the first stage of meditation.

yid kyi las thams cad nye bar zhi bar bya ba dang / ye shes kyi stobs dang mthus sems can thams cad yongs su bsdu ba la dga' ba'i bde ba la sems rtse gcig tu bya ba'i phyir/ bsam gtan gnyis pa bsgom mo/ /
“I meditate on the second dhyāna in order to pacify all mental activity and, through the strength and power of wisdom, to have a one-pointed mind with joy of bliss in gathering all beings.
To cease all mental action and focus my mind solely on joy and happiness in taking care of all sentient beings with the power of knowledge, I cultivate the second stage of meditation.
'khor bar log par zhugs pa la btang snyoms su byas te/ sems can thams cad kyi rang bzhin nges par rtogs par bya ba'i phyir/ bsam gtan gsum pa bsgom mo/ /
“I meditate on the third dhyāna in order to have equanimity toward the distress of saṃsāra and to realize the nature[1326] of all beings.
To realize the purity of inherent nature of all beings with equanimity detached from the mundane world, I cultivate the third stage of meditation.
sems can thams cad kyi nyon mongs pa dang / sdug bsngal rab tu zhi bar bya ba'i phyir; bsam gtan bzhi pa bsgom mo/ /
“I meditate on the fourth dhyāna in order to bring an end to the kleśas and suffering of all beings.
To extinguish the burning of the pain of afflictions of all sentient beings I cultivate the fourth stage of meditation.

thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi smon lam gyi dkyil 'khor shin tu yangs par bya ba dang / ting nge 'dzin rgya mtsho thams cad mngon par bsgrub pa la mkhas par bya ba dang / byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa rgya mtsho thams cad kyi tshul la 'jug par bya ba dang / byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par rtse ba'i ye shes thams cad mngon par shes par bya ba dang / byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pas rnam par 'phrul ba thams cad mngon par bsgrub par bya ba'i phyir/ sgo kun nas chos kyi dbyings la 'jug pa'i ye shes kyi tshul yongs su spyod zhing / byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa bsam gtan zhi ba'i bde bas kun tu rnam par gnon pa 'di bsgom mo/ /

“I purify the way of the wisdom that enters the realm of phenomena through every gateway and thus meditate on this bodhisattva liberation called complete subjugation through the bliss of the peace of śamatha in order to increase[1327] the domain of aspiration for omniscience, to become skilled in the accomplishment of an ocean of samādhis, to realize the ways of the ocean of all bodhisattva liberations, and to have the higher cognition of all the wisdoms displayed by bodhisattvas.

To extend the sphere of the vow for omniscience, for skill in producing the ocean of all concentrations, to enter the means of access to the ocean of liberation of all enlightening beings, to know the science of occult powers of all enlightening beings, to effect the mystic projection of practices of all enlightening beings, I cultivate the enlightening liberation that goes everywhere through tranquil meditation, purifying the knowledge that enters into every realm of reality.

rigs kyi bu/ de ltar kho mo rnam par thar pa 'di sgom zhing thabs sna tshogs kyi sems can yongs su smin par byed de/ 'di ltar nub mo zhi bar gyur pa'i tshe/ dga' ba la mos par gyur pa'i sems can rnams kyi mi sdug pa'i 'du shes bskyed do/ / mi dga' ba'i 'du shes dang / yongs su skyo ba'i 'du shes dang / gegs su 'gyur ba'i 'du shes dang / 'ching ba'i 'du shes dang / srin mo'i 'du shes dang / mi rtag pa'i 'du shes dang / sdug bsngal ba'i 'du shes dang / bdag med pa'i 'du shes dang / rje med pa'i 'du shes dang / gzhan la rag las pa'i 'du shes dang / rga shi'i 'du shes dang / 'dod pa'i yul dang / longs spyod thams cad la dga' ba med pa'i 'du shes bskyed de/ sems can de dag kyang sems de la yongs su bsgoms pas/ 'dod pa'i dga' ba thams cad la mngon par dga' ba med pas chos la mos pa'i dga' ba la 'jug cing khyim nas khyim med par rab tu 'byung ngo/ / de dag dgon pa la gnas pa'i tshe 'di chos dang mthun pa'i dad pa yongs su bskyed do/ / sgra chen po 'jigs pa mi snyan pa'i sgra skad thams cad kyang zhi bar byed do/ / mtshan mo zhi bar gyur pa las sangs rgyas kyi chos zab mo yang yang dag par ston to/ /

“Noble one, in that way I meditate on this liberation and ripen beings through various methods: I instill in the beings who enjoy carnal pleasure in the peace of the night the perception of it as ugliness, the perception of it as lack of pleasure, the perception of it as wearying, the perception of it as an obstacle, the perception of it as bondage, the perception of it as a rākṣasī, the perception of impermanence, the perception of suffering, the perception of no self, the perception of no ownership, the perception of dependence on others,[1328] the perception of aging and death, and the perception of a lack of joy in all indulgence in desires. When those beings meditate on that state of mind, they will take no delight in any indulgence in carnal pleasure and will instead aspire to enjoy the delights of the Dharma and leave home for homelessness. When they dwell in solitude, I instill in them the faith that accords with the Dharma. I cause all loud, frightening, unpleasant sounds to cease, and in the peace of the night I teach the profound Dharma of the buddhas.

“Furthermore, as I cultivate this liberation, I develop sentient beings to maturity by a variety of means. In people engrossed in sex play in the still of the night I induce the thought of impurity, the thought of disappointment, the thought of weariness, the thought of trouble, the thought of bondage, the thought of bedevilment, the thought of impermanence, the thought of pain, the thought of selflessness, the thought of ownerlessness, the thought of offense, the thought of old age and death, and the thought of indifference to all objects of desire. And those people, developing this state of mind, indifferent to all pleasures, coming to enjoy spiritual pleasure, go forth from home to homelessness. When they have gone into the forest and are following spiritual principles, I foster faith in them. I cause a lull in all disturbing, frightening, loud sounds, and in the quiet of the night I reveal to them the profundity of the buddha-teaching.

spang ba dang mthun pa'i rkyen kyang nye bar ston to/ / khyim gyi sgo'ang rnam par 'byed do/ / lam yang yongs su ston to/ / snang bas kyang mngon par byed do/ / mun pas chod pa'ang rnam par sel to/ / 'jigs pa'ang med par byed do/ / rab tu byung ba la yang yang dag par bsngags par byed do/ / sangs rgyas kyi legs pa'ang brjod do/ / chos kyi legs pa dang / dge 'dun gyi legs pa dang / dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi legs pa'ang brjod do/ / dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi drung du 'gro ba la'ang bsngags pa byed do/ /

“I gather[1329] the conditions necessary for renunciation. I open the door of the house for their departure. I show them the path. I illuminate it. I dispel the darkness. I free them from fear. I praise departure from home. I describe the qualities of buddhahood. I explain the excellence of the Dharma, the excellence of the saṅgha, and the excellence of the kalyāṇamitra. I praise going to a kalyāṇamitra.

I provide them with circumstances conducive to effort, open the door of renunciation, show the path, provide light, dispel darkness, put a stop to fear, praise renunciation, speak of the qualities of the Buddha, the Teaching, and the Community, and of spiritual benefactors, and praise going to spiritual benefactors.

rigs kyi bu/ kho mo rnam par thar pa 'di la sgom zhing / sems can rnams kyi chos ma yin pa'i 'dod chags kyi zhen pa rnams kyi chos ma yin pa'i 'dod chags kyi yongs su rtog pa rnams kyang med par byed do/ /
“Noble one, meditating on this liberation, I eliminate in beings the passion and desire for what is not Dharma, and thoughts of desire for what is not Dharma.
“As I cultivate this liberation, I put a stop to sentient beings’ wrong passions and wrong feelings and thoughts.
tshul ma yin pa'i 'dod pas non pa rnams dang / log par yongs su rtog pa'i spyod yul can rnams kyi yongs su rtog pa de dag dang / yid la bya ba de dag kyang med par byed do/ /
I dispel the thoughts and notions of those overpowered by inappropriate desires, and those whose conduct comes from wrong thoughts.
I put a stop to the ideas and thoughts of those dominated by wrongful gain, those who act on false notions.
sdig to mi dge ba'i chos ma skyes pa rnams mi skye ba dang / sdig to'i yongs su rtog pa skyes par gyur pa rnams kyang med par 'gyur ba'i rkyen nye bar bsgrub bo/ /
“I create the conditions for those who have not developed evil thoughts and bad qualities to not develop them, and for those who think evil thoughts to eliminate them.
I see to it that evil does not arise in those in whom it has not yet arisen, and that the false conceptions of those in whom evil has arisen are stopped.

dge ba'i yongs su rtog pa'i pha rol tu phyin pa dang ldan pa dang / spyod pa dang ldan pa dang / thams cad mkhyen pa'i ye shes su 'byung ba'i smon lam mngon par bsgrub pa dang ldan pa dang / byams pa'i tshul dang ldan pa dang / sems can rnams la snying rje chen pos rgyas par 'gengs pa dang ldan pa dang / lha dang mi'i bde ba'i rnam pa sna tshogs yongs su bskyed pa dang ldan pa'i yongs su rtogs pa bskyed pa dang / skyes nas kyang tshul sna tshogs kyi rkyen nye bar sgrub pa byed pa nas/ thams cad mkhyen pa nyid dang mthun pa'i rkyen kyang nye bar sgrub pa byed de/

“I create in various ways the supporting conditions for those who have virtuous thoughts, who practice the perfections, who are engaged in good conduct, who are engaged in accomplishing prayers for the arising of omniscient wisdom, who are engaged in the ways of love, who are pervaded by great compassion for beings, who are engaged in creating the various kinds of happiness of devas and humans, and who have given rise to such thoughts, and I create the conditions that support omniscience.

For those in whom thoughts of roots of goodness have not yet arisen, I motivate thoughts of the ways of transcendence, spiritual practice, achievement of the aspiration for omniscience and release, the principle of kindness, suffusing all sentient beings with great compassion, and producing the various bases of celestial and human happiness. For those to whom such thoughts already occur, I provide various means of guidance. I motivate all the appropriate thoughts and intentions until they are in accord with the way to omniscience.

rigs kyi bu/ kho mos byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa bsam gtan zhi ba'i bde bas kun tu rnam par gnon pa 'di shes par zad na/ kho mos byang chub sems dpa'i kun tu bzang po'i spyod pa dang / smon lam gyis byung ba'i byang chub sems dpa' rnams mtha' yas pa'i chos kyi dbyings kyi ye shes rab tu thob pa/ dge ba'i rtsa ba thams cad kyis rnam par spel ba'i sems dang ldan pa/ de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi ye shes kyi mthus sems kyi snang ba rab tu thob pa/ de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi yul la gnas pa'i sems dang ldan pa/ gnas thams cad du sgrib pa med pa'i sems dang ldan pa; thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi smon lam yongs su rdzogs pa'i sems dang ldan pa/ zhing rgya mtsho thams cad du zhugs pa'i sems dang ldan pa/ sangs rgyas rgya mtsho thams cad mthong bar bya ba la zhugs pa'i sems dang ldan pa/ de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi chos kyi sprin gyi char yang dag par gzung ba'i sems dang ldan pa/ sems can thams cad kyi ma rig pa'i mun pa rnam par sel ba/ 'khor ba'i bde ba la dga' zhing sred pa zad cing mthar phyin par 'gyur ba'i lam gyis thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du snang ba skyed pa'i sems dang ldan pa de dag gi spyod pa shes pa'am/ yon tan brjod par nus de skan/

“Noble one, I know only the bodhisattva liberation called complete subjugation through the bliss of the peace of śamatha. How could I know the conduct or describe the qualities of bodhisattvas who have arisen through completely good bodhisattva conduct and prayers, who have attained the wisdom of the infinite realm of phenomena, who have minds that increase all roots of merit, who have attained illumination of their minds through the power of the wisdom of all the tathāgatas, who have minds that maintain the same scope as that of all the tathāgatas, whose minds are unobscured in all situations, whose minds have perfected the aspiration for omniscience, whose minds perceive the entire ocean of realms, whose minds are focused on the vision of the entire ocean of buddhas, whose minds have received the clouds of the Dharma of all the tathāgatas, who dispel the darkness of ignorance of all beings, and who have minds that have given rise to the illumination of omniscience through the path of the final cessation of delight in and craving for saṃsāra?

“I know only this enlightening liberation of the bliss of tranquil meditation boldly going everywhere. How can I know the practice or tell of the virtues of the enlightening beings who are completely conversant with the vows of practice of universally good enlightening beings, who have attained knowledge of the cosmos with its endless forms, in whose minds all roots of goodness are developed, who have attained awareness of the knowledge and powers of all buddhas, whose minds abide in the sphere of all buddhas, whose minds are unhindered wherever they may be, who have fulfilled the resolve for omniscience, whose minds have entered the ocean of all lands, whose minds see all buddhas and take in the teachings of all buddhas, who dispel the darkness of all ignorance, whose minds generate the light of omniscience as the way to effect the final destruction of craving for repetitious mundane enjoyment?

song /rigs kyi bu/ 'di nyid nang dang yang rgyang mi ring ste/ rnam par snang mdzad kyi snying po byang chub kyi g.yas rol gcig nas mtshan mo'i lha mo rab tu dga' ba'i mig 'gro bar rnam par snang ba zhes bya ba 'dug go/ de'i gan du song la/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i lam la brtson par bya ba dris shig;

“Depart, noble one. Here, not far from me, to the south of Vairocana’s bodhimaṇḍa, there is the goddess of the night named Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā. Go to her and ask her, ‘How should a bodhisattva train in bodhisattva conduct? How should a bodhisattva practice it?’ ”

“Right by me, on the right side of the site of enlightenment of Vairocana, there lives a night goddess named Pramuditanayanajagadvirocana. Go ask her how an enlightening being should work on the deeds of enlightening beings.”

de nas mtshan mo'i lha mo kun tu zab pa'i dpal dri ma med pa'i 'od kyis/ de'i tshe byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa bsam gtan zhi ba'i bde bas kun tu rnam par gnon pa 'di nyid brnan te bstan par bya ba'i phyir/ tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la tshigs su bcad de smras pa/

Then at that time, the night goddess Samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhā, in order to emphasize and teach this bodhisattva liberation called complete subjugation through the bliss of the peace of śamatha, recited these verses to Sudhana, the head merchant’s son:
Then the night goddess Samantagambhirashrivimalaprabha spoke these verses to Sudhana, further revealing the enlightening liberation of the bliss of tranquil meditation boldly going everywhere:
dus rnams kun tu byung ba'i bde gshegs rnams; ; mngon du bya bar mos pa'i sems ldan pa/ / de dag mig yangs rnam par dag par 'gyur/ / des ni sangs rgyas rgya mtsho mthong bar 'ong / /
“Those with a mind that aspires to be in the presence Of the sugatas[1330] that appear in the three times Will have a vast and pure eyesight And will see an ocean of the buddhas. {1}
The buddhas, supreme in all times, Appear to those with faith. Their eye is vast and pure; Thereby they enter the oceans of buddhas.
rgyal ba'i sku gsal dri ma med la ltos/ / mtshan gyis yongs su brgyan pas shin tu mdzes/ / rgyal ba'i rnam par 'phrul pa chos dbyings rnams/ / skad cig re res rgyas 'gengs de la'ang ltos/ /
“See the bright, stainless body of the Jina Beautifully adorned by the signs of a great being! See the Jina’s miraculous manifestations That in an instant fill the realm of phenomena! {2}
See the undefiled body of Buddha, Beautifully adorned with distinctive marks; And see the miracle of the Buddha Pervading the cosmos in every moment.
byang chub shing drung sangs rgyas gdan rab la/ / bde gshegs rnam par snang mdzad mngon sangs rgyas/ / chos dbyings yangs pa rgyas pa khyab mdzad cing / / 'gro ba'i bsam pa ji bzhin 'khor lo bskor/ /
“The Sugata, the perfect Buddha, Vairocana Is upon the buddha throne under the Bodhi tree. He pervades the vast realm of phenomena, Turning the wheel in accordance with the aspirations of beings. {3}
The felicitous one Vairocana has become enlightened Sitting at this enlightenment tree; Throughout the vast cosmos, He teaches according to mentality.
rgyal bas chos nyid lus med rab zhi ba/ / gnyis med rang bzhin med pa thugs chud nas/ / gzugs sku bzang po mtshan gyis brgyan pa yis/ / 'gro ba ma lus bkang zhing ston pa mdzad/ /

“The Jina has realized the true nature, which is bodiless, Complete peace, nondual, with no own nature. His physical body, beautiful and adorned by signs, Pervades and teaches in every world without exception. {4}
The Buddha has realized true nature As bodiless, utterly quiet, nondual; His physical body, adorned with marks of distinction, He manifests throughout the world.
sangs rgyas sku ni rgya che bsam mi khyab/ / chos kyi dbyings kun yongs su rgyas bkang zhing / / de ni kun tu mnyam par snang ba ste/ / rgyal ba thams cad kun tu ston pa mdzad/ /
“The Buddha’s body is inconceivably vast. It fills the entirety of the realm of phenomena. It appears equally everywhere, Revealing all the jinas everywhere. {5}
The body of Buddha is vast, inconceivable, Filling the entire cosmos: It is seen everywhere equally, Showing all the buddhas everywhere.
zhing rnams kun gyi rdul rab phra ba snyed/ / 'od kyi dkyil 'khor mnga' ba'i sangs rgyas sku/ / kha dog bzang po gzhan dang gzhan snang bas/ / chos dbyings rgyas par skad cig re res 'gengs/ /
“Bodies of the Buddha, with halos of light, As numerous as the atoms in all realms, Their beautiful color appearing here and there, Fill the realm of phenomena in every instant. {6}
The Buddha’s auras of light, Numerous as atoms in all lands, Reflecting each other’s radiant colors, Pervade the cosmos every moment.
rgyal ba'i ba spu'i sgo nas 'od zer sprin/ / rgya che bsam yas mi zad mngon 'byung ba/ / de dag 'gro ba ma lus 'gengs byed cing / / srog chags rnams kyi nyon mongs gdung ba sel/ /
“Clouds of light rays appear from the Jina’s pores. They are vast, inconceivable, and unending. They fill every world without exception And dispel the torment of the kleśas in beings. {7}
Inconceivable, vast clouds of light Stream endlessly from the Buddha’s pores; They pervade all worlds and extinguish The heat of afflictions of all beings.
sangs rgyas sprul pa rgya mtsho mi zad pa/ / rgyal ba'i spu yi 'khor nas yongs bton cing / / chos dbyings yangs pa rgyas par kun bkang ste/ / srog chags rnams kyi sdug bsngal ngan song sel/ /

“The Buddha’s inexhaustible ocean of emanations Appear from the circles of the Jina’s pores And spread and fill the vast realm of phenomena, Dispelling the suffering of beings in the lower realms. {8}
Infinite oceans of emanations of Buddha, Emerging from Buddha’s pores, Go throughout the cosmos and stop the suffering Of all miserable states of being.
sangs rgyas gsung snyan rab tu sgrog mdzad pa/ / dbyangs kyi yan lag rgya mtsho sgra 'od can/ / chos char chen po rab tu 'bebs pa mdzad/ / srog chags byang chub bsam pa yongs su skyed/ /
“The sound of the Buddha’s voice resounds With the light of an ocean of aspects of speech, Sending down a great rain of the Dharma, Causing the aspiration to enlightenment to grow in beings. {9}
Buddha’s voice thunders pleasantly, And the light of the ocean of good sayings Showers the widespread rain of truth And produces the will for enlightenment in sentient beings.
bskal pa rgya mtshor spyad pa spyod pa'i tshe/ / 'dis ni sngon chad yongs su gzung mdzad pa/ / de dag kun gyis rgyal ba rnam snang mdzad/ / zhing rnams kun tu gzugs brnyan mtshan nyid mthong / /

“He has in the past taken care of those Practicing bodhisattva conduct during an ocean of kalpas. They have all seen in all the worlds The characteristics of the visual form of the Jina Vairocana. {10}
Those who have been guided by him in the past And practiced the ways of enlightenment for eons See Vairocana Buddha’s features Reflected in all lands.
de bzhin gshegs pa 'jig rten kun tu byung / / sems can re re kun la'ang mngon par bzhugs/ / mos pa'i tshul bzhin spyod yul gzhan dang gzhan/ / de dag kho mos kun tu shes mi nus/ /
“The Tathāgata has appeared in all worlds In the presence of each and every being With this and that conduct according to their aspirations, And those are beyond my ability to know. {11}
The Buddha, appearing in all worlds, Stands before all beings: I cannot know all Their various realms of attention.
rgyal sras dam pa thams cad ma lus par/ / bde bar gshegs pa'i spu gcig rtse las 'byung / / rnam par de la gang rnams bsam yas pa/ / de dag thams cad kho mos shes mi nus/ /
“All the perfect bodhisattvas without exception Have appeared from a single pore of the Sugata. That liberation is inconceivable And is beyond my ability to know. {12}
All the exalted enlightening beings Are together in one pore of Buddha: That way of liberation, which is inconceivable, I cannot know in full.
kho mo'i 'dab na gnas pa'i lha mo 'di/ / 'jig rten mgon la mngon 'gyur rab tu dga'/ / ming du snang ba 'od 'phro mig ces bya/ / de la byang chub spyod pa ci 'dra dris/ /
“This goddess who is nearby to me Delights in the presence of the Lord of the World. Her name is Jyotirarcinayanā. Ask her, what is the practice for enlightenment!” {13}
My neighbor goddess Stands rapt before the Buddha, Her eyes like starry fire— Go ask her how to practice enlightenment.

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis/ mtshan mo'i lha mo kun tu zab pa'i dpal dri ma med pa'i 'od kyi rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te/ mtshan mo'i lha mo kun tu zab pa'i dpal dri ma med pa'i 'od la/ lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas/ /yang dang yang bltas te mtshan mo'i lha mo kun tu zab pa'i dpal dri ma med pa'i 'od kyi drung nas song ngo/ /

Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, bowed his head to the feet of the night goddess Samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhā, circumambulated the night goddess Samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhā many hundreds of thousands of times, keeping her to his right, and, looking back again and again, departed from the night goddess Samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhā.
Then Sudhana paid his respects to the night goddess Samantagambhirashrivimalaprabha and took leave of her.

Chapter 36. Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā
Pramuditanayanajagadvirocana

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi gdams ngag gi byin gyis brlabs pa/ dge pa'i bshes gnyen gyi tshig la nan tan du bya ba'i sems yang dag par skyes pa/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi sman pa la nad pa lta bu'i 'du shes kyis yongs su spyad pa'i sems dang ldan pa/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen mthong ba yid la byed pa ma 'khrugs pa'i sems dang ldan pa/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen blta ba la sgrib pa'i ri thams cad rnam par gtor ba'i glags rnyed pa'i sems dang ldan pa/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen mthong ba la sems can gyi khams thams cad yongs su bskyab pa'i snying rje chen po'i tshul rgya mtsho la 'jug pa thob pa'i sems dang ldan pa/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen mthong ba la chos kyi dbyings kyi tshul rgya mtsho'i ye shes snang ba rab tu thob pa'i sems dang ldan pa de/ mtshan mo'i lha mo rab tu dga' ba'i mig 'gro bar rnam par snang ba gang na ba der song ngo/ /

Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, was blessed by the instruction of the kalyāṇamitra; his mind practiced the words of the kalyāṇamitra; his mind had the perception of the kalyāṇamitra as a physician and himself as a patient; his mind was contented by focusing on the vision of the kalyāṇamitra; his mind had obtained the opportunity to disperse the mountain of obscurations to the vision of the kalyāṇamitra; his mind had attained, through seeing the kalyāṇamitra, entry into the ocean of the ways of the great compassion that saves all the realms of beings; his mind had attained, through seeing the kalyāṇamitra, the illumination by wisdom of the ocean of the ways of the realm of phenomena. Thus, he approached the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā.

Immersed in the teachings of the spiritual benefactors, with practice of the words of the spiritual benefactors in mind, desirous of the sciences of spiritual benefactors, his attention focused without distraction by seeing spiritual benefactors, his mind illumined through seeing spiritual benefactors with a light that destroys all obstructions, his mind immersed, through seeing spiritual benefactors, in the ocean of great compassion that saves all beings, his mind illumined, through seeing spiritual benefactors, by the light of knowledge of the ocean of principles of the cosmos, Sudhana went to the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocana.

de nas mtshan mo'i lha mo rab tu dga' ba'i mig 'gro bar rnam par snang bas/ tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang / de bas kyang dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi drung du 'gro ba/ dge ba'i rtsa ba'i tshogs las byung bas yongs su smin par bya ba'i phyir/
The night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā, in order to further increase the ripening of his accumulation of the roots of merit through approaching a kalyāṇamitra,
The goddess, in order to further mature the development of Sudhana’s roots of goodness based on visiting spiritual benefactors,
dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi drung du 'gro ba tshogs chen po las byung bar byin gyis brlabs so/ /
blessed approaching a kalyāṇamitra as arising from a great accumulation,
showed him visiting spiritual benefactors as made possible by great provisions of virtue and knowledge,
dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi drung du 'gro ba rnam par gnon pa chen por byin gyis brlabs so; ;
blessed going to a kalyāṇamitra as great prowess,
as great heroic effort,
dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi drung du 'gro ba brtson 'grus kyi las 'jug par dka' bar byin gyis brlabs so/ /
blessed approaching a kalyāṇamitra as diligence in actions that is difficult to realize,
as energy that is hard to attain,
dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi drung du 'gro ba bsdad cing shin tu legs par byin gyis brlabs so/ /
blessed approaching a kalyāṇamitra as reliance[1331] throughout a long time,
as longterm perseverance,
dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi drung du 'gro ba phyogs mtha' dang dbus med pa la 'jug par byin gyis brlabs so/ /
blessed approaching a kalyāṇamitra as going into centerless and limitless directions,
as entry into infinite realms,
dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi drung du 'gro ba yun ring por gnas pas byung bar byin gyis brlabs so/ /
blessed approaching a kalyāṇamitra as the source for dwelling together for a long time,
as connected with long association,
dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi drung du 'gro ba don mtha' yas pa yongs su rdzogs pa'i rnam par dmigs pa 'byung bar byin gyis brlabs so/ /
blessed approaching a kalyāṇamitra as the source of perceiving infinite tasks being completed,
as connected with manifestation of fulfillment of endless tasks,
dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi drung du 'gro ba lam gyi rgyan mtha' dang dbus med pa'i tshogs kyis yongs su gnon par byin gyis brlabs so/ /
blessed approaching a kalyāṇamitra as the prowess of an accumulation of centerless and limitless displays of the path,
as undertaking the provision of the endless equipment of the path,
dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi drung du 'gro ba sgo kun nas rnam par gnon bas byung bar byin gyis brlabs so/ /
blessed approaching a kalyāṇamitra as prowess through every gateway,
as made possible by indomitably going everywhere,
dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi drung du 'gro ba g.yo ba med par 'ong pas rnam par gnon par byin gyis brlabs so/ /
and blessed approaching a kalyāṇamitra as the prowess of undeviating arrival.
as coming and going without departure.
de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang / thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi tshogs kyi brtson 'grus la rab tu brtson pas/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi drung du 'gro ba dang /
Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, approached the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā in this way: approaching a kalyāṇamitra with diligent dedication in the accumulation of omniscience;
Then Sudhana went to the night goddess in the manner of one going to a spiritual benefactor energetically proceeding to provide for omniscience,
smon lam chen po rgya mtsho mngon par bsgrub pa'i rnam par gnon pas dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi drung du 'gro ba dang /
approaching a kalyāṇamitra with the prowess of accomplishing an ocean of great prayers;
striving to carry out the ocean of great vows,
sems can gcig gi don du phyi ma'i mtha'i bskal pa'i mur thug par sdug bsngal nyams su blangs pa'i zhe non pas/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi drung du 'gro ba dang /
approaching a kalyāṇamitra with the resolve to undergo suffering for the sake of a single being until the conclusion of the last future kalpa;
determined to endure endless suffering for the sake of even one single sentient being,

rdul shin tu phra ba gcig la chos kyi dbyings thams cad du sgra sgrog cing / yun ring por gnas pa'i rnam par gnon pa dang / brtson 'grus chen po'i go bgos pas/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi drung du 'gro ba dang /

approaching a kalyāṇamitra with the prowess of remaining for a long time[1332] within a single atom, emitting sound[1333] throughout the entire realm of phenomena while wearing the armor of diligence;
proceeding with perseverance to traverse the cosmos in a single atom wearing the armor of great energy,
phyogs rgya mtsho 'byams klas pa thams cad du shugs kyis 'gro bas dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi drung du 'gro ba dang /
approaching a kalyāṇamitra while moving at great speed through the entire extent of the ocean of directions;
speeding everywhere in all directions,
ba spu'i sbubs gcig tu phyi ma'i mtha'i bskal par byang chub sems dpa'i spyad pa spyod pa la gnas pas/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi drung du 'gro ba dang /
approaching a kalyāṇamitra while maintaining all bodhisattva conduct of future kalpas in a single pore of the body;
associating with the practice of enlightening beings of endless eons at a single point,
byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la gnas nas kyang / sems kyi skad cig re re la thams cad mkhyen pa'i ye shes 'gengs pa la gnas par bya bas/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi drung du 'gro ba dang /
approaching a kalyāṇamitra with the attainment of bodhisattva conduct and in each instant of mind dwelling in omniscient wisdom;
every moment of thought in enlightening practice entirely based on omniscience,
dus gsum du gshegs pa'i de bzhin gshegs pa'i rnam par 'phrul pa'i rgyan dang / lam yongs su gnon par zhe non pas/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi drung du 'gro ba dang /
approaching a kalyāṇamitra while intent on following the path and the display of miracles of the tathāgatas of the three times;
determined to tread the path mystically projected by the buddhas of all times,
chos kyi dbyings kyi tshul gyi rgyun du zhugs pa'i lam yongs su gnas pas/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi drung du 'gro ba dang /
approaching a kalyāṇamitra while following the path of entering the stream of all the ways of the realm of phenomena;
treading the path flowing through all spheres of reality,
chos kyi dbyings kyi tshul thams cad la dmigs pa las ma g.yos par chos kyi dbyings kun tu rgyas par 'gengs pas/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi drung du 'gro bas/
and approaching a kalyāṇamitra without deviating from being focused on all the ways of the realm of phenomena and pervading the entire realm of phenomena.
keeping the attention on the principles of all realms of reality, pervading the whole cosmos of reality.

mtshan mo'i lha mo rab tu dga' ba'i mig 'gro bar rnam par snang ba gang nas ba der phyin pa dang / des mtshan mo'i lha mo rab tu dga' ba'i mig 'gro bar rnam par snang ba/ bcom ldan 'das kyi 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor la/ seng+ge'i khri me tog gi snying po can la 'dug cing / byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin kun tu bzang po'i dga' ba yangs shing dri ma med pa'i shugs kyi rgyal mtshan la mnyam par bzhag pa mthong ngo/ /

He saw the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā seated on a flower in the center of a lion throne within the circle of the assembly of the Bhagavat, resting in the bodhisattva samādhi called the banner of the power of vast, stainless, completely good joy.
He saw the night goddess sitting in a lion seat in a flower calyx in the circle of the Buddha, in an enlightening concentration characterized by the vast, pure energy of the joy of universal good.

de'i ba spu'i bu ga thams cad nas/ sbyin pa la sogs pa'i pha rol tu phyin pa'i spyod pa mngon par ston pa'i sprin sems can thams cad mngon par dga' ba/ sems can thams cad kyi yid du 'ong ba /sems can thams cad kyis blta na nyams su bde ba/ sems can thams cad kyis blta na sdug pa/ rnam pa sna tshogs 'byung ba'ang mthong ste/

He saw emanating from all her pores clouds of manifestations of the practice of the perfections, such as generosity, which delighted all beings, which brought pleasure to all beings, and which were various kinds of beauty for all beings.

He also saw emerging from all her pores multitudes of emanations illumining all sentient beings, making all sentient beings happy, showing the practices of the transcendent ways according to the vision of all sentient beings, pleasing to the sight of all sentient beings.

'di ltar sems can thams cad la phan gdags shing rtsod pa med par bya ba dang / dngos po thams cad la phangs par rtsi ba med par bya ba dang / sems can thams cad la sbyor ba mtshungs pas yongs su gtang bar bya ba dang / sems can thams cad la mnyam pa'i sems su bya ba dang / sems can thams cad la brnyas pa med par yongs su gtang ba dang / nang dang phyi'i dngos po thams cad yongs su gtang ba dang / dka' ba chen po yongs su gtang bar bstan pa dang / 'jig rten thams cad du sems can gyi bsam pa ji bzhin gyi sbyin pa'i spyod pa yongs su bstan par bya ba'i phyir/ sems can thams cad kyi bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du rnam par dmigs pa dang mthun pa'i sgras/

They were like this: he saw clouds of manifestations of the practice of generosity in accord with the aspirations, perceptions, and languages of all beings, in order to benefit beings without causing discord, in order for there to be no concern for all material things, in order to give equally to all beings, in order for there to be impartiality toward all beings, in order to give respectfully to all beings, in order to give all inner and outer things, in order to manifest the generosity that is difficult,[1334] and in order to manifest in all worlds the practice of generosity according to the wishes of beings.

He saw multitudes of emanations showing the practice of giving in accord with the mentalities of all sentient beings, using their own languages to communicate with them, to detach all sentient beings from their attachments, by indifference to material things, giving impartially to all sentient beings without neglecting any, impartial toward all sentient beings, not disrespecting or disregarding any sentient beings, relinquishing all things internal and external, showing the relinquishment of that which is very hard to give up, showing the practice of giving to sentient beings in all worlds according to their mentalities.

sbyin pa'i spyod pa yongs su ston pa'i sprin dang / dus gsum du byung ba'i byang chub sems dpa' rnams gtang bar dka' ba yongs su gtong ba'i sprul pa bsam gyis mi khyab pa'i sprin 'thon nas/ phyogs bcu'i 'jig rten gyi khams 'byams klas par gtogs pa'i sems can thams cad kyis rnam par dmigs par gyur pa mthong ngo/ /

He saw clouds of manifestations of the countless difficult acts of generosity by the bodhisattvas that appear in the three times, which being emanated were perceived by all beings within the vast extent of the worlds in the ten directions.

He saw multitudes of emanations projecting the difficult act of relinquishment practiced by the enlightening beings of past, present, and future emerge and appear to all sentient beings in all worlds in the ten directions, by attainment of the inconceivable mystic power of enlightening beings.

'di lta ste/ byang chub sems dpa'i khyu mchog gi mthu phyung ba dang / rnam par 'phrul pa bsam gyis mi khyab pa thob pas /ba spu'i bu ga thams cad nas sems can thams cad dang mnyam pa'i skye ba sna tshogs su sprul pa'i lus kyi sprin mngon par 'thon te/ 'jig rten gyi khams thams cad du gtogs pa'i sems can thams cad la rgyas par khyab par byas nas/ mngon sum du brtul zhugs thams cad kyi yi dam las mi g.yo bar yongs su ston pa dang /

It was like this: because of her attainment of the inconceivable miraculous powers of the might of bodhisattvas, he saw, issuing forth from all her pores, clouds of emanated bodies of various beings, equal in number to that of all beings, which spread throughout all beings within all world realms, demonstrating directly to them the unwavering commitment to vows of discipline;

He saw multitudes of projected bodies in the forms of all sentient beings emerge from every pore of the goddess, appearing before all sentient beings in all worlds, showing them unshakability in all aspects of self-control,
sems can gyi khams dang mnyam pa'i dka' thub dang / brtul zhugs kyi dkyil 'khor sna tshogs rab tu ston pa dang /
demonstrating throughout the realms of beings the field of the various vows of discipline of[1335] asceticism;
illustrating as many forms of austerity as there are living beings,
'jig rten thams cad du gnas pa med pa dang / yul thams cad la ltos pa med pa dang / 'khor ba thams cad du gnas pa las phyir phyogs pa dang /
demonstrating nondependence on all worlds, no concern for all fields of perception, and the rejection of all locations in saṃsāra;
showing independence from all worlds, disregard of all objects, indifference to all mundane abodes,
lha dang mi'i phun sum tshogs pa rgud pa'i sgor gzhol ba yongs su ston pa dang /
demonstrating entering the gateway to the decline of the good fortune of devas and humans;[1336]
showing that celestial and human prosperity and decline,
mi sdug pa'i dkyil 'khor rab tu ston pa dang /
demonstrating the field of unattractiveness;
happiness and suffering, are all inextricably intertwined,
'jig rten gyi sdug pa'i 'du shes kyi phyin ci log rnam par bzlog pa dang /
dispelling the incorrect perception of attractiveness in the world;
showing impurity and putting an end to the false notion of purity in the world,
mi rtag pa dang g.yo ba dang 'jig pa dang / 'gyur ba'i chos nyid yongs su ston pa dang /
revealing the nature of phenomena to be impermanence, instability, destruction, and change;
revealing the nature of things as impermanent, unstable, and changing,
'du byed thams cad kyi chos nyid sdug bsngal zhing / bdag med pa yongs su ston pa dang /
showing the true nature of all that is composite to be suffering and the absence of a self;
showing the nature of all conditioned states as painful and selfless,
de bzhin gshegs pa'i yul la gnas pa dang mi 'bral bar mos par byed pa dang /
yearning to dwell inseparably within the field of activity of the tathāgatas;
promoting the appeal of living constantly in the realm of the enlightened,
de bzhin gshegs pa'i tshul khrims shin tu dag par bya ba'i phyir/ sems can thams cad la yang dag par bskul ba dang /
inspiring beings toward the perfectly stainless conduct of the tathāgatas;
directing sentient beings to the ultimate purity of the way of life of the enlightened,
sems can thams cad kyi bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin gyi sgras/ tshul khrims kyi spyod pa yongs su ston pa dang /
teaching to beings, in accordance with their aspirations and languages, the practice of correct conduct;
teaching the practice of discipline using expressions adapted to the mentalities of all sentient beings,
sems can thams cad yongs su tshim par byed pa'i tshul khrims kyi dri zhim po yongs su ston par byed cing /
manifesting the lovely scent of correct conduct that brings satisfaction to beings;
showing the grace of ethical conduct pleasing all sentient beings,
sems can thams cad yongs su smin par byed pa mthong ngo/ /
and ripening all beings.
developing all sentient beings to maturity.
