lha mo khyod bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu zhugs nas ji srid cig lags/ lha mo khyod kyis byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa kun tu bzang po'i dga' ba shin tu yangs shing dri ma med pa'i shugs kyi rgyal mtshan 'di thob nas ni; ji srid cig lags/

“Goddess, how long has it been since you entered into attaining the highest, complete enlightenment? Goddess, how long has it been since you attained the bodhisattva liberation called the banner of the power of vast, stainless, completely good joy?”
“How long have you been devoted to supreme perfect enlightenment, and how long ago did you attain this enlightening liberation characterized by the immense pure energy of the joy of universal good?”
de nas mtshan mo'i lha mo rab tu dga' ba'i mig 'gro bar rnam par snang bas/ tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la tshigs su bcad de smras pa/
The night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā recited these verses to Sudhana, the head merchant’s son:
The goddess answered him,
dran pa bskal pa mang 'das pa/ / zhing gi rdul snyed de yi snga rol na/ / zhing ni rin chen mdog bde byung / / de yi bskal pa zhi ba'i dbyangs zhes bya/ /
“I remember, in the past, as many kalpas ago As there are atoms in a realm, There was the realm Maṇiprabhasukhābha In a kalpa called Praśantaghoṣa. {11}
“I remember, many eons ago, past as many eons as atoms in the world, the land Blissful Light of Jewel Radiance, in the eon Silent Sound,
gling bzhi bye ba khrag khrig ste/ / brgya stong phrag bcu rnams kyis yongs su gang / / tshad med rin chen ri bo 'dra/ / gling bzhi'i bar ma bzang po rnam par bkram/ /
“It was filled with ten thousand quintillion[1379] Four-continent world realms. The central four-continent world, beautifully formed, Resembled a measureless mountain of jewels. {12}
filled with a hundred duodecillion sets of four continents, in the center of which were four beautiful continents, extending as far as the light of a mountain of jewels,
rgyal po'i pho brang bye ba brgya/ / stong phrag bcu rnams yongs su tshang ba ste/ / rgyal po'i pho brang mdangs dga' ba/ / dbus na gnas pa spos kyi rgyal mtshan 'od/ /
“It was filled by the king’s cities Numbering ten thousand quintillion.[1380] The beautiful central royal city, Gandhadhvajā, shone with jewels.[1381] {13}
filled with a hundred duodecillion royal cities, in the center of which was a delightful city Fragrant Banner, radiant with jewels:
der ni phyogs kyi dbang po sa yi bdag / 'khor los bsgyur ba mngon par gzugs bzang byung / / mtshan rab sum cu gnyis dang ldan/ / de yi lus kyang dpe byad bzang pos brgyan/ /

“There a lord of the directions, sovereign of the land, A cakravartin with a handsome body, appeared. He had the thirty-two signs of a great being, And the features of a great being also adorned his body. {14}
therein lived a wise king named Lord of the People, a world ruler, adorned with the thirty-two marks and eighty embellishments of great people,
pad+mo'i sbubs nas rdzus te byung / / gser gyi mdog bzang 'od 'byung lus dang ldan/ / 'dzam bu'i rgyal mtshan thams cad du/ / mkha' las 'gro zhing 'od kyis de 'gengs so/ /
“He was miraculously born from inside a lotus. His body was golden and shone with light. He moved through the sky and filled with light The entirety of Jambudhvaja. {15}
born spontaneously from a lotus calyx, his body shining gold, his light filling the continent all at once, spreading through the sky.
de yi bu ni stong tshang ste/ / kun kyang yan lag dam pa'i gzugs dang ldan/ / blon po mkhas shing gsal ba dang / / mdzangs shing yid gzhungs bye ba shin tu mang / /
“He had a full thousand sons, All of whom had bodies with excellent limbs. He had many millions of ministers Who were wise, intelligent, learned, and honest. {16}
He had a thousand sons, all with the constitution of heroes, ten million ministers, learned, intelligent, wise,
btsun mo bye ba phrag bcu tshang / / lha mo ji bzhin dga' ba'i tshul la mkhas/ / de dag phan sems bde sems kyis/ / rgyal po de la nye ba'i yid du gnas/ /
“He had a full hundred million queens Who resembled apsarases, were skilled in the art of pleasure, And with loving minds, caring minds,[1382] Affectionately attended that king. {17}
and ten million concubines, beautiful as goddesses, expert in the arts of love, affectionate, altruistic, kind, attentive to the king.
rgyal po de ni sa chen de/ / ri dang khor yug kun gyi mthas klas pa'i/ / gling bzhi phun sum tshogs pa dag / kun kyang chos kyi stobs kyis gnas par byed; ;
“That king, through the power of the Dharma, Caused that great land, the entirety of the four continents As far as the Cakravāla mountain range,[1383] To remain in a state of good fortune. {18}
That king ruled the whole four continents and enriched them by the power of justice.
kho mo 'khor los bsgyur ba yi/ / btsun mo tshangs pa'i sgra skad rin chen lus/ / gser gyi mdog 'chang dri med 'od/ / dpag tshad stong du 'od kyis rgyas par 'gengs/ /
“I was that cakravartin’s principal[1384] queen. I had the voice of Brahmā and a bejeweled[1385] body, With a bright halo the color of gold That illuminated for a thousand yojanas. {19}
nyi ma nub par gyur nas kyang / / rgyal po sras dang 'khor bcas gzims gyur nas/ / rol mo'i dbyangs kyang zhir gyur te/ / kho mo mal na bde bar nyal nyal na/ /
“After the sun had set And the king and his sons were asleep And the sound of music had ceased, I slept comfortably on my bed. {20}
One night as the king, his sons, and his retinue slept, the sounds of singing ended, and as I was peacefully asleep in bed,
nam gyi phyed tsam gung zhig la/ / sangs rgyas dpal gyi rgya mtsho byung bar gyur/ / de tshe rgyal bas rnam 'phrul ba/ / phyogs bcu rgyas par bkang ste bstan pa mdzad/ /
“In the middle of the night, The Buddha Śrisamudra appeared. The Jina manifested limitless[1386] miracles That spread throughout the ten directions. {21}
in the middle of the night a buddha appeared in the world and filled the ten directions with infinite mystic projections,
rgyal ba'i 'od zer rgya mtsho des/ / zhing gi rdul snyed 'jig rten khyab par gyur/ / rnam 'phrul sku rnams sna tshogs kyis/ / phyogs bcu thams cad ma lus rgyas par bkang / /
“That ocean of the Jina’s light Spread through worlds as numerous a realm’s atoms. Various kinds of emanated bodies Filled all ten directions without exception. {22}
pervading everywhere with various magical bodies imbued with glorious oceans of light, as many as atoms in all lands.
sa rnams ri dang bcas par g.yos/ / rgyal ba byung zhes sgra yang yongs su brjod/ / lha dang lha min mi dang klu/ / kun kyang rgyal ba byung bas rab tu dga'/ /
“The earth and its mountains shook, And a voice proclaimed, ‘A jina has come!’ Devas, asuras, humans, and nāgas Were all delighted that a buddha had appeared. {23}
The earth, including the mountains, quaked, announcing the appearance of the buddha; gods, titans, humans and spirits, were all thrilled at the emergence of the buddha.
sangs rgyas ba spu'i sgo kun nas/ / sprul pa'i rgya mtsho mang po mngon par byung / / des ni phyogs bcu rgyas bkang nas/ / 'jig rten bsam pa bzhin du chos kyang bstan/ /
“Many oceans of emanations appeared From all the pores of the Buddha. They spread throughout the ten directions And taught the Dharma in accordance with the aspirations of beings. {24}
rnam 'phrul mtha' yas de dag kyang / / rgyal bas thams cad bdag gi rmi lam bstan/ / zab mo'i 'brug sgra thos gyur nas/ / khong du chud pas kho mo dga' yid gyur/ /
“The Jina revealed to me in a dream All those limitless miraculous manifestations. When I heard the profound thunderous sound, I understood its meaning and was delighted. {25}
The buddha showed me all those infinite manifestations in a dream: hearing those profound teachings, I was joyful while dreaming.
mtshan mo'i lha mo stong snyed kyang / / kho mo'i steng gi bar snang mkhar gnas shing / / rgyal ba'i legs pa brjod byas nas/ / kho mo sad par smra zhing brjod/ /
“Ten[1387] thousand night goddesses Residing in the sky above me Spoke to me, waking me from sleep, Praising the excellence of the Jina. {26}
Ten thousand night goddesses stood in the sky above me, describing the buddha in celestial tones and telling me to wake:
lha yi blo gros btsun mo longs/ / khyod kyi rgyal po'i khams su rgyal ba skyes/ / bskal pa rgya mtsho brgya dag tu/ / de 'dra'i phun sum tshogs pa rnam dag dkon/ /
“ ‘Arise, wise queen of His Majesty, A jina has appeared in your kingdom. This kind of good fortune is difficult to find[1388] Even in a hundred oceans of kalpas.’ {27}
‘Arise, O queen, a buddha has appeared in your realm, hard to meet in a hundred oceans of eons; those who behold him are happy and purified.’
kho mo dgar gyur sad par gyur/ / 'od gsal dri med rnam dag mthong / / 'od bzang de ni ga las blta blta na; ; byang chub shing rgyal drung gi rgyal ba mthong / /
“I awoke with happiness And saw the clear, pure light. I looked to see where this good light came from And saw the Jina at the foot of the Bodhi tree. {28}
I became joyful, and on awakening I saw an immaculate light. Seeing this light, immediately I beheld the buddha at the enlightenment tree,
mtshan nyid sum cu gnyis kyis brgyan/ / ba spu kun nas 'od zer rgya mtsho bkye/ / ri rab ji bzhin mngon par 'phags/ / rgyal ba g.yas g.yos kun tu'ang de bzhin no/ /

“He was adorned by the thirty-two signs of a great being, And an ocean of light rays shone from all his pores. Just like Sumeru he was above all, And the Jina was the same on the right and the left. {29}

“When I saw him I was overjoyed, And in my mind rose the aspiration to be like him. Having seen the manifestations of the Buddha, I made a very vast prayer. {30}

“I requested the king to arise, And his court and his wives also got up. When they saw the vast light from the Buddha, They all experienced physical pleasure. {31}

“I proceeded to the presence of the Jina Together with the king and his armed forces And accompanied by ten million carriages[1389] And many quintillions[1390] of beings. {32}
I went to the buddha with my husband, accompanied by millions of people and troops.

“For twenty thousand years I made offerings to the Jina. I presented him[1391] with the seven jewels And the earth and its oceans. {33}
I made offerings to the buddhas for twenty thousand years, giving precious substances, the earth, and its seas.

“The clouds of the qualities of an ocean of sūtras, Which were a display arisen from an ocean of prayers, Had all appeared from the Tathāgata And were taught to beings according to their dispositions. {34}
The buddha expounded myriad scriptures, multitudes of virtues, an ocean of vows, and the adornments thus produced, explaining the origins of all buddhas according to mentalities in this world.

“Those night goddesses,[1392] wishing to benefit[1393] me, With compassion woke me at that time.[1394] There arose an aspiration in me toward them:[1395] ‘May I become like them, awakening the intoxicated.’[1396] {35}
That night goddess awakened me for my benefit, and then I was inspired with compassion, eager to become like this and then awaken the heedless.
kho mo'i smon lam de 'dra'i sems/ / thog ma byang chub mchog tu skyes par gyur/ / 'khor ba'i rgya mtsho gnas pa'i tshe/ / srid pa'i rgya mtshos de ni zhig ma gyur/ /

“That was the prayer that I made in my mind, My first development of the aspiration for the highest enlightenment, Which my residing in the ocean of saṃsāra, The ocean of existences, has not destroyed. {36}
This was my first aspiration to supreme enlightenment, and while coming and going in the oceans of being, I have never lost this resolve.
sangs rgyas bye ba khrag khrig la/ / kho mos dad pa bskyed de mchod pa byas/ / 'khor ba'i lha dang mi dbus su/ / yul gyi dga' dang bde la mngon par smon/ /
“I had faith in and offered to Ten[1397] million trillion buddhas. While in the midst of saṃsāra’s devas and humans, I desired the scope of pleasure and bliss. {37}
“I served ten decillion buddhas with faith while desiring celestial and human enjoyments in the mundane.
rgyal ba'i dang po dpal gyi mtsho/ / de yi 'og ma yon tan sgron ma ste/ / rgyal ba gsum pa rin chen dpal/ / sangs rgyas bzhi pa nam mkha'i shes rab bo; ;
“The first was Śrīsamudra. After him came Guṇapradīpa. The third was the Jina Ratnaketu. The fourth was the Buddha Gaganaprajña. {38}
The first buddha was Ocean of Glory, next was Lamp of Virtue, third was Jewel Brightness, fourth was Spacelike Wisdom,

“The fifth jina was Kusumagarbha. The sixth jina was Asaṅgamaticandra. The seventh jina was Dharmacandraprabhurāja. The eighth was Jñānamaṇḍalaprabhāsa. {39}
fifth was Flower Calyx, sixth was Moon of Unattached Intellect, seventh was Power King of the Moon of Truth, eighth was Light of the Sphere of Knowledge;

“I made offerings to those ten And all the other lords of humans. But I did not at that time attain The vision of entering the ocean of ways. {41}
I served all the buddhas, beginning with these, but had not yet attained the eye to enter this ocean of wisdom.

“The first was Śaśimaṇḍala. The second born was Bhāskarapradīpa. The third buddha was Jyotidhvaja, And after him there were Maṇisumeru, {43}
The first buddha was Light of the Lunar Sphere, second was Solar Lamp, third was Star Banner, fourth was Jewel Mountain,

“Kusumārcisāgarapradīpa, Jvalanaśrīśa, Devaśrīgarbha, Avabhāsarāja, and Prabhaketu. The tenth was Samantajñānaprabharāja. {44}

fifth was Flower Flame Ocean Lamp, sixth was Blazing Glory, seventh was Filled with Heavenly Glory, eighth was Shining King, ninth was Radiant Clarity, and tenth was King of Light of Universal Knowledge.

“I made offerings to those ten And all the rest of those lords of humans. But I delighted[1399] in being located in the body. I had a mind dwelling in the Dharma that has no location. {45}

the buddhas in that world were numberless, and I served them and their retinues, and reverently heard the teachings of all those buddhas.
rgyal ba'i dang po rin chen ri/ / de yi 'og ma yon tan rgya mtsho ste/ / rgyal ba chos dbyings dbyangs kyi dpal; ; chos rab rgya mtsho sgrog pa bzhi pa'o/ /

The first buddha was Jewel Mountain, second was Ocean of Virtues, third was Clarity of the Cosmic Voice, fourth was Roar of the Ocean of Truth,

fifth was Banner of Truth, sixth was Energy of Mystic Spells, seventh was Light of the Power of Truth, eighth was Spacelike Awareness, ninth was Light of the Peak of the Polar Mountain of Flames of Truth, and tenth was Massive Radiance;
bcu po de la sogs pa dag / mi yi dam pa de dag kun mchod de/ / rgyal ba'i rgya mtsho 'dir zhugs pa'i/ / chos nyid de ni dag ma gyur/ /

“The first after him[1406] was Gandharvarāja, Second was the Buddha Drumarāja, The third jina was Guṇasumeru, And after him were Ratnanetra, {53}
First was King of Celestial Musicians, second was Tree King, third was Polar Mountain of Virtue, fourth was Jewel Eye,
rnam par snang mdzad 'od kyi rgyan/ / chos kyi rgya mtsho sangs rgyas gzi brjid dpal/ / 'jig rten dbang po 'od bzang dpal/ / kun gyi tha ma chos 'od rgyal po'o/ /

fifth was Array of Shining Lights, sixth was Radiance of the Ocean of Truth, seventh was Lord of the World, eighth was Blazing Glory, ninth was Virtuous, and tenth was King of Light of All Laws;

beginning with these ten, I served all those buddhas, yet still did not attain the knowledge to enter the ocean of truth.

“After that, there was a perfectly pure realm Called Vajramāṇyabhedyadṛḍhatejas,[1408] In which there were constant clouds of light And the presence of numerous beautiful displays. {56}

therein were many purified beings, mostly healthy, with few afflictions. In the age Energy of the Tranquil Mind, a thousand buddhas came forth:

fifth was Energy of Compassion, sixth was Ocean of Vows, seventh was Lamp of the Sphere of Patience, eighth was Light of the Sphere of Truth,

ninth was Array of Oceans of Light, tenth was King of Tranquil Light. Beginning with these ten, I served all those buddhas,

yet I did not awaken to the real nature which is spacelike, inherently pure, based on which I could carry on spiritual practices in all lands.

“The first jina was Vipulakīrti, Then there were Dharmasamudravegaśrīrāja, Dharmendrarāja, Guṇaghoṣa, Dharmaśrī, and Devamakuṭa; {64}

in the age Luminous there, five hundred buddhas emerged. I honored all those buddhas, seeking this liberation:

“The first jina was Kusumarāśi, Then there were Sāgaragarbha, Saṃbhavagiri, Devendracūḍa, Maṇigarbha, Kāñcanaparvata, Ratnaraśi, {74}

“The first was Samantaguṇamegha. Then there were the Buddha Gaganacitta, The Buddha Susaṃbhavavyūha, Garjitadharmasāgaranirghoṣa, {81}
first was Mass of All Virtues, then Spacelike Mind, Array of Good Capacities, Thunder of the Ocean of Truths,
rgyal ba chos dbyings gsung dbyangs dang / / sprul pa'i sprin sgra snyan pa'i dpal mnga' dang / / sangs rgyas phyogs kun gzi brjid dang / / chos kyi rgya mtsho yongs byung sgra dbyangs dang / /
“The Jina Dharmadhātusvaraghoṣa, Nirmitameghasusvaraśrī, The Buddha Samantadiśatejas, And Dharmasamudrasaṃbhavaruta, {82}
Voice of the Cosmos, Blissful Light of Myriad Emanations, Universal Energy, Sound Born of the Ocean of Truths,
yon tan rgya mtsho dpal gyi sgron/ / rgyal ba'i nyi ma dgu pa byung bar gyur/ / de dag kun gyi tha ma ste/ / rin chen dpal sgron yon tan dpal mchod do/ /
“Then there was the ninth of the jina suns, Guṇasāgaraśrīpradīpa.[1418] Following those there came Ratnaśrīpradīpaguṇaketu. {83}
Mountainous Lamp in an Ocean of Virtues; and the last of them I propitiated was Paragon of Virtue Radiant As a Jewel.
rin chen dpal sgron yon tan dpal/ / rkang gnyis dam pa byung bar gyur pa'i tshe/ / kho mo lha mo zla bzhin te/ / mi yi dam pa byung tshe mchod pa byas/ /
“When Ratnaśrīpradīpaguṇaketu, The lord of two-legged beings, set forth, I was the goddess Śaśivakra, And I made offerings to the lord of humans as he set forth. {84}
When that buddha emerged in the world, I was a queen, Moonlike Face, going to honor the buddha.
rgyal ba des ni kho mo la/ / mdo sde smon lam rgya mtsho 'byung ba'i rgyan/ / gnas med rgyan kyang rab tu bshad/ / thos nas kho mos dran pa'i stobs kyis bzung / /
“That jina[1419] proclaimed[1420] to me Sūtras that were displays without location, Displays that arose from an ocean of prayers, Which I heard and retained through the power of memory. {85}
He expounded a scripture on the supernal manifestations originating in an ocean of independent vows, which I listened to and remembered.
kho mos mig yangs der thob ste/ / ting 'dzin zhi dang gzungs kyi stobs kyang thob/ / skad cig re rer zhing brgyud pa'i/ / rgyal ba rgya mtsho mang po'ang kho mos mthong / /
“I attained at that time vast vision, Samādhis, and the power of retention. In each instant I saw oceans of jinas And a succession of realms. {86}
I attained tranquil concentration of broad vision, and the power of mental command. I see oceans of buddhas in one land after another, from moment to moment.
byams tshul kun tu snang ba'i sprin/ / byang chub sems rab mkha' dang mnyam pa ste/ / snying rje'i snying pos brgyan pa yang / / sangs rgyas stobs kyi tshad du yangs par skyes/ /

“There arose in me the essence of compassion, The completely illuminating clouds of the way of kindness, The aspiration to enlightenment, as vast as space, And the vast beauty of the immeasurable buddha strengths.[1421] {87}
I have borne a cloud of universal light from the womb of compassion by means of kindness, a will for enlightenment as vast as space, with the measureless light of the powers of buddhas.
'gro ba phyin ci log gyur te/ / rtag dang bde dang gtsang dang bdag zhen pa/ / gti mug ldongs gyur ma rig bsgribs/ / nyon mongs 'khrugs shing log par 'du shes pa/ /

“I saw beings who were in a state of delusion, Attached to permanence, happiness, purity, and self,[1422] Blinded[1423] by stupidity, obscured by ignorance, Disturbed by the kleśas, and having misperceptions. {88}
“Seeing the world in error, engrossed in the glitter of permanence and pleasure, shrouded in the darkness of delusion and ignorance, filled with afflictions, thinking falsely,
lta ba'i rnam par stug la spyod/ / lam gyi 'gro rgyud nyam ngar sred dbang gyur/ / rnam pa sna tshogs bye brag tu/ / las kyis rnam par bris pas kun byung ba/ /
“They performed actions in a thicket of wrong views, Following frightening paths[1424] under the power of craving. Many various forms appearing Were painted[1425] by karma. {89}
given to views, wandering in obscurity, controlled by craving and evildoing, accumulating a variety of deeds in mundane conditions,
'gro rgyud kun gyi shi 'pho'i sgor/ / skye bar 'gyur bas kun tu skyer gyur cing / / skye dang rga shi gnod pa rnams/ / lus dang sems kyi nyams su myong gyur pa/ /
“Those who appeared through being born Through the gateways to rebirth in all existences Had bodies and minds that experienced The torments of birth, aging, and death. {90}
going from one state to another, suffering the physical and mental pains of birth, old age, and death,
mthong nas de dag phan bde'i phyir/ / zhing rnams 'byams klas thams cad kyi/ / stobs bcu gang las byung ba yi/ / bla na med pa'i sems kyang kho mos bskyed/ /
“Seeing that, in order to bring them benefit and happiness I developed the supreme motivation Wherever those with the ten strengths appeared, Anywhere throughout the vast extent of realms. {91}
I have therefore wished above all for their welfare and happiness: in all places where there were buddhas,
de las smon lam sprin byung ba/ / 'gro ba kun la bde bar gzhol ba'i mchog / tshogs rnams dbyung ba mtha' yas dang / / lam tshul rgya mtsho rtogs pa'ang de nas byung / /
“From that arose clouds of prayers, Perfect dedication to the happiness of beings, The arising of limitless accumulations, And the understanding of the ways of an ocean of paths. {92}
'jug pa'i sprin yangs thob gyur pa/ / lam rgyud kun tu sgo gsal shugs ldan te/ / pha rol phyin gyi sprin yangs pa'ang / / chos dbyings 'byams klas kun tu rnam par 'byed/ /
“I obtained vast clouds of practices, The power of clear gateways to all paths, Vast clouds of the perfections, And the opening of the entire extent of the realm of Dharma. {93}
and I emanated vast multitudes of projections of the transcendent ways throughout the cosmos, speeding to gladden the beings in all paths of existence.
sa gnon shugs drag yangs ldan dang / / dus gsum rgya mtsho'i tshul gyi sa rnams la/ / chags pa med par spyod par gyur/ / skad cig gcig gis rgyal ba kun drung 'gro /
“With the vast power to ascend the bhūmis, Practicing without attachment on the bhūmis, In the ways of the ocean of the three times, In each instant I came into the presence of all jinas. {94}
gzhan yang rgyal sras kho mos ni/ / spyod pa kun tu bzang po yongs su gnon/ / chos dbyings bye brag bcu rnams kyi/ / rgya mtsho'i tshul yang kho mos rtogs par 'jug /
“What is more, I also mastered The completely good jinaputra[1426] conduct, And I realized the ways of the ocean Of the ten aspects of the realm of the Dharma. {95}
and having entered the practice of universal good, I realized the myriad principles of the differentiations of the ten universes.

rigs kyi bu de la ji snyam du sems/ de'i tshe de'i dus na/ rgyal po 'khor los bsgyur ba sangs rgyas kyi rigs kyi rgyun mi gcod pa la zhugs pa mi'i bdag po zhes bya ba byung ba de/ gzhan zhig yin pa snyam du sems na ni/ rigs kyi bu/ de ltar mi blta ste/ 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pa ni/ de'i tshe de'i dus na/ rgyal po mi'i bdag po zhes bya ba 'khor los bsgyur ba/ sangs rgyas kyi rigs rgyun mi gcod pa la zhugs pa'o/ / kho mo sad par byed pa'i mtshan mo'i lha mo de ni/ byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang pos sprul pa'o/ /

“Noble one, do you think that the cakravartin king, that sovereign, who at that time, in that time, was established in the unbroken lineage of the family of the buddhas is anyone else? Noble one, do not see him in that way. Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta was at that time, in that time, that king, that sovereign, who was the cakravartin, established in the unbroken lineage of the family of the buddhas. The night goddess who awoke me was an emanation of the bodhisattva Samantabhadra.

“That king named Lord of the People, the world ruler who was determined to prevent the dying out of the lineage of buddhas, was none other than Manjushri, who had become a king, successful in perpetuating the family of buddhas. The night goddess by whom I was awakened was emanated by the enlightening being Universally Good.

rigs kyi bu/ de la ji snyam du sems/ de'i tshe de'i dus na/ 'khor los bsgyur ba'i btsun mo bud med rin po che bzang po'i blo gros ma zhes bya ba byung ba de/ gzhan zhig yin pa snyam du sems na ni/ de ltar mi blta ste/ kho mo ni de'i tshe de'i dus na/ 'khor los bsgyur ba'i btsun mo bud med rin po che bzang po'i blo gros ma zhes bya bar gyur te/ kho mo mtshan mo'i lha mo des sad par byas nas/ sangs rgyas blta ba la yang dag par bskul to/ /

“Noble one, what do you think? If you think that Bhadramati, the precious woman who was the queen of the cakravartin in that time, at that time, was anyone else, do not see her in that way. At that time, in that time, I was Bhadramati, the precious woman who was the queen of the cakravartin. I was awoken by that night goddess and inspired by her to go see the Buddha.
The wife of the king was me. When I was awakened by the night goddess, I was caused to see Buddha;

rigs kyi bu/ kho mos ni/ bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems de srid cig nas bskyed de/ de ltar kho mo sems bskyed pa de'i mthus/ bskal pa sangs rgyas kyi zhing gi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed du nam yang ngan song log par ltung bar ma skyes te/ rtag tu rgyun mi 'chad par lha dang mi'i 'gro ba'i rgyud la rten cing / thams cad du'ang de bzhin gshegs pa blta ba dang ldan par gyur to/ /

“Noble one, I developed in that one existence the aspiration for the highest, complete enlightenment. In that way, through the power of that development of aspiration, I have, throughout kalpas as numerous as the atoms in a buddha realm, never fallen into rebirth in the lower realms but have always continuously depended on existence as a human or deva, and in all those existences I have seen tathāgatas.

this was when I first aspired to enlightenment. Ever since that inspiration, for as many eons as atoms in a buddha-land, I have never fallen into bad states but have always wound up in celestial and human states. Wherever I have been, I have never been apart from the sight of buddhas;

tha mar kho mos bcom ldan 'das de bzhin gshegs pa dgra bcom pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas rin chen dpal gyi sgron ma yon tan rgyal mtshan mthong ba tsam gyis byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa kun tu bzang po'i dga' ba shin tu yangs shing dri ma med pa'i shugs kyi rgyal mtshan zhes bya ba 'di thob ste/ de thob pas kho mo sems can yongs su smin par bya ba dang / gdul ba'i don du rnam pa 'di lta bus sta gon du gnas pa yin no/ /

Finally, through just seeing the Bhagavat Arhat Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnaśrīpradīpaguṇaketu,[1427] I attained the bodhisattva liberation called the banner of the power[1428] of vast, stainless, completely good joy. When I had attained it, I took on this kind of form in order to ripen and guide beings.

then when I saw the buddha Paragon of Virtue Radiant As a Jewel, I attained this enlightening liberation characterized by the immense pure energy of the joy of universal good, by the attainment of which I have come to develop and guide all sentient beings in this way.
rigs kyi bu/ kho mos byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa kun tu bzang po'i dga' ba rgya chen po'i shugs kyi rgyal mtshan 'di shes par zad na/
“Noble one, I know only this bodhisattva liberation called the banner of the power[1429] of vast, stainless, completely good joy.
“I just know this enlightening liberation characterized by the immense pure energy of the joy of universal good.

kho mos byang chub sems dpa' de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi zhabs kyi drung na 'khod cing / sems kyi skad cig re re la thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du 'jug pa'i shugs drag po rgya mtsho chen po rab tu thob pa/

How could I know the conduct or describe the qualities of bodhisattvas who, at the feet of all the tathāgatas in each instant of mind, attain a great ocean of the power for setting out upon omniscience;
How can I know the virtues or tell of the practice of the enlightening beings who have attained the ocean of great speed setting out for omniscience in the presence of all buddhas in each instant,
'jug pa'i sgo thams cad la sems kyi skad cig re re zhing smon lam chen po rgya mtshos 'jug pa rab tu thob pa/
who, in each instant of mind, have completed the attainment of an ocean of great prayers within all the entrances for setting out upon omniscience;
who enter unceasingly into the ocean of great vows at every moment in the beginning of all undertakings,
sems kyi skad cig re re zhing smon lam rgya mtsho thams cad kyi tshul la phyi ma'i mtha'i bskal par spyad pa'i dkyil 'khor mngon par bsgrub pa la mkhas pa/
who, in each instant of mind, are skilled, through the ways of making an ocean of prayers, in accomplishing a domain of conduct in future kalpas;
who are skilled in carrying out a multitude of practices in every moment of thought over endless eons in the ways shown by the ocean of all vows,
spyod pa re re la yang lus sangs rgyas kyi zhing thams cad kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed mngon par bsgrub pa la mkhas pa/
who are skilled in accomplishing, within each conduct, as many bodies as there are atoms in all buddha realms;
and who are skilled in producing in each practice as many bodies as atoms in all buddha-lands,
lus re res kyang chos kyi dbyings kyi tshul rgya mtsho thams cad rgyas par 'gengs pa la mkhas pa/
who are skilled in pervading, with each body, the entire ocean of different ways in the realm of phenomena;
and who pervade the systems of all universes with each body,
chos kyi dbyings kyi tshul rgya mtsho re re la'ang sangs rgyas kyi zhing thams cad du sems can rnams kyi bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du lus rnam par dmigs pa'i spyod pa yongs su ston pa la mkhas pa/

who are skilled in manifesting, in each ocean of different ways in the realm of phenomena, a perceivable conduct of the body that accords with the dispositions of beings throughout all the buddha realms;
and who are skilled in demonstrating practices according to the mentality of sentient beings in each universe,
zhing thams cad du'ang zhing gi rdul shin tu phra ba thams cad la de bzhin gshegs pa rgya mtsho mtha' dang dbus med pa la 'jug par mkhas pa/
who are skilled in comprehending, in each ocean of different ways in the realm of phenomena, an ocean of tathāgatas, without limit or center, within all the atoms of a realm in all realms;
de bzhin gshegs pa re re zhing yang chos kyi dbyings kyis klas par rgyas par 'gengs pa'i de bzhin gshegs pa'i rnam par 'phrul pa la 'jug par mkhas pa/
who are skilled in comprehending each tathāgata’s miraculous tathāgata manifestations that pervade the entire extent of the realm of phenomena;
de bzhin gshegs pa re re'i sngon gyi mtha'i bskal pa la byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa'i tshogs yongs su bsgrub pa yang dag par bsdus pa la 'jug par mkhas pa/
who are skilled in comprehending each tathāgata’s accomplishment of gathering the accumulation of bodhisattva conduct in past kalpas;
de bzhin gshegs pa re re'i chos kyi 'khor lo shin tu yangs pa yang dag par blang ba dang / yongs su gzung ba la mkhas pa/
who are skilled in obtaining and possessing each tathāgata’s vast[1430] wheel of the Dharma;
dus gsum thams cad kyi de bzhin gshegs pa'i rnam par 'phrul pa'i tshul rgya mtsho la 'jug par mkhas pa de dag gi spyod pa shes pa'am/ yon tan brjod par nus re skan/
and who are skilled in comprehending the ocean of the different ways of miraculous manifestations by the tathāgatas in the three times?
and skilled in comprehending the ocean of ways of transformation of all buddhas of past, present, and future?

song / rigs kyi bu/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor 'di nyid na/ kho mo dang rgyang mi ring ba zhig na mtshan mo'i lha mo sems can kun tu skyong ba'i gzi brjid dpal zhes bya ba 'dug gi /de'i gan du song la/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa'i dkyil 'khor la 'jug par bya ba dang / ji ltar yongs su sbyang bar bya ba dris shig /

“Depart, noble one. In this circle of the Tathāgata’s assembly, not far from me, there is the goddess of the night named Samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśrī. Go to her and ask her, ‘How should a bodhisattva train in bodhisattva conduct? How should a bodhisattva practice it?’ ”

“There is a night goddess named Samantasattvatranojahshri who lives right here in the Buddha’s circle. Go ask her how an enlightening being is to enter and purify the sphere of practice of enlightening beings.”

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis/ mtshan mo'i lha mo rab tu dga' ba'i mig 'gro bar rnam par snang ba'i rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te/ mtshan mo'i lha mo rab tu dga' ba'i mig 'gro bar rnam par snang ba la/ lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas yang dang yang bltas te/ mtshan mo'i lha mo rab tu dga' ba'i mig 'gro bar rnam par snang ba'i drung nas song ngo// //

Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, bowed his head to the feet of the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā, circumambulated the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā many hundreds of thousands of times, keeping her to his right, and, looking back again and again, departed from the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā.
So then Sudhana paid his respects to the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocana and left her.
bam po brgya tham pa;

d.crumb: [mtshan mo'i lha mo sems can kun tu skyong ba'i gzi brjid dpal]

f.d: [mtshan mo'i lha mo sems can kun tu skyong ba'i gzi brjid dpal]
Chapter 37. Samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśrī
Samantasattvatranojahshri

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang / mtshan mo'i lha mo rab tu dga' ba'i mig 'gro bar rnam par snang ba'i byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa kun tu bzang po'i dga' ba shin tu yangs shing / dri ma med pa'i shugs kyi rgyal mtshan de la mos par bya ba dang /

Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, aspiring to the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā’s samādhi of the bodhisattva liberation called the banner of the power[1431] of vast, stainless, completely good joy,
Entering with intense absorption into the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocana’s liberation of immense pure energy of the joy of universal good,

khong du chud par bya ba dang / rtogs par bya ba dang / shes par bya ba dang / yid ches par bya ba dang / rab tu gzhol bar bya ba dang / rgyas par dgang bar bya ba dang / rjes su shes par bya ba dang / rjes su dran par bya ba dang / rjes su gzhol bar bya ba dang / sgom pa byed cing / dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi gdams ngag la nan tan du bya ba dang / gdams ngag rjes su bstan pa la bar chad med par bya ba'i phyir/ mtshan mo'i lha mo rab tu dga' ba'i mig 'gro bar rnam par snang bas 'gro khar gdams pa rjes su dran pa byed cing /

comprehending it, understanding it, knowing it, believing in it, undertaking it, pervading it, recollecting it, remembering it, and meditating on it,[1432] practicing the instruction of the kalyāṇamitra and memorizing the instruction given by the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā in order to maintain the continuity of the teaching of instruction,

understanding it, plunging into it, penetrating it, following it throughout its full range, going along with it, cultivating it, accomplishing it, encompassing it, carrying out the instructions of the spiritual benefactors, recollecting the teachings projected by the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocana for the continuity of teaching and instruction,

dge ba'i bshes gnyen blta ba'i rjes su sems pa'i dbang po'i dkyil 'khor dang / dge ba'i bshes gnyen mthong ba thob par bya ba la yang dag par spyod pa phyogs kun tu mngon par bltas pa dang / dge ba'i bshes gnyen btsal bar yid la bya ba dang / nga rgyal thams cad dang bral ba dang / dge ba'i bshes gnyen bsnyen bkur ba'i mthu tshogs chen po yongs su bsgrub par zhe non pa dang / dge ba'i bshes gnyen dang rgyud kyi tshul gcig tu gyur pa'i dge ba'i rtsa bas dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi thabs mkhas pa'i spyod pa thams cad la bsam pa mi phyed pas zhugs pa/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen la brten pa yongs su 'phel bar bya ba la brtson 'grus kyi shugs chen po rgya mtsho yongs su skyes pa/ bskal pa thams cad du dge ba'i bshes gnyen mnyam pa nyid khong du chud pas gnas par bya ba'i smon lam dang ldan pa de/ mtshan mo'i lha mo sems can kun tu skyong ba'i gzi brjid dpal gyi drung du song ngo/ /

approached the night goddess Samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśrī. Through contemplating[1433] seeing a kalyāṇamitra, through the domain of all his faculties,[1434] by going from place to place[1435] to obtain the sight of a kalyāṇamitra, through looking in all directions, through being intent on searching for a kalyāṇamitra, through being free from all pride, through the prowess[1436] of pleasing a kalyāṇamitra, through being resolved to create a great accumulation of merit, through having become single-mindedly intent upon a kalyāṇamitra,[1437] and through all his roots of merit,[1438] he had gained the unwavering motivation for a kalyāṇamitra’s conduct of skillful methods, had developed an ocean of the power of diligence for increasing reliance on a kalyāṇamitra, and had prayed to dwell with and follow kalyāṇamitras equally in all kalpas.

with all faculties turned in all directions following the sight of spiritual benefactors, with the intention to get to see spiritual benefactors, free from all conceits, with attention focused on seeking spiritual benefactors, with determination to develop the great provisions of virtue and knowledge, with vigorous initiative to harmonize with spiritual benefactors, with all roots of goodness one with those of spiritual benefactors, firmly intent on the practice of all skill in means of spiritual benefactors, having generated an ocean of energy fostered by spiritual benefactors, Sudhana went to the night goddess Samantasattvatranojahshri.

de de ltar 'gro ba'i tshe/ mtshan mo'i lha mo sems can kun tu skyong ba'i gzi brjid dpal gyis; byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa 'jig rten thams cad mngon du gyur pas/ 'gro ba rnam par 'dul ba ston pa'i khyu mchog gi mthu phyung ba yongs su bstan pa'i phyir; mtshan dang dpe byad bzang pos yongs su grub pa'i lus bstan te/ mdzod spu nas 'od zer ye shes kyi 'od kun tu snang ba dri ma med pa'i mdangs kyi rgyal mtshan zhes bya ba 'od zer gyi mtha' dang dbus med pa dang ldan par bkye'o/ /

As he approached her, the night goddess Samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśrī, in order to demonstrate the supreme might of the limitless bodhisattva liberation called the manifestations that guide beings that appear in all worlds, revealed her body, which had the complete beautiful signs and features of a great being. She then radiated from her ūrṇā hair a ray of light called the banner of stainless light that is a lamp of the complete radiance of wisdom, accompanied by light rays without end or center.

When Sudhana came to her, the night goddess, in order to show him the majesty of the endless enlightening liberation manifesting guidance for sentient beings in all works, showed him a body replete with beautiful features and embellishments, and emanated a light from the circle of hair between her brows called “emblem of pure stars of the lamp of flames of universal knowledge,” with infinite light beams;
des 'jig rten thams cad snang bar byas nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gi spyi bor 'dus te/ lus thams cad du khyab par gyur to/ /
They illuminated all worlds and then descended into the crown of the head of Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, and spread throughout his entire body.
the light illumined the whole world, then descended into Sudhana and pervaded his entire body.
tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la 'od zer des reg par gyur ma thag tu de nyid kyi mod la ting nge 'dzin shin tu rdul dang bral ba zhes bya ba'i dkyil 'khor thob par gyur to/ /
As soon as Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, was touched by those light rays, he instantly attained the samādhi called the area that is completely free of particles.[1439]
As soon as Sudhana was touched by the light, he attained a concentration called “sphere of ultimate dispassion,”

de thob pas mtshan mo'i lha mo rab tu dga' ba'i mig'gor bar rnam par snang ba dang / mtshan mo'i lha mo sems can kun tu skyong ba'i gzi brjid kyi dpal gnyis kyi bar gyi lam na sa'i dkyil 'khor yod pa de la me'i rdul shin tu phra ba'am/ chu'i rdul shin tu phra ba'am/ sa'i rdul shin tu phra ba'am/ rdo rje'i rdul shin tu phra ba'am/ nor bu rin po che'i rgyal po dam pa sna tshogs kyi rdul shin tu phra ba'am/ me tog dang / spos dang / phye ma'i rdul shin tu phra ba'am/ rgyan thams kyi rdul shin tu phra ba'am/ dmigs pa thams cad kyi rdul shin tu phra ba ji snyed cig yod pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba de dag thams cad la rdul phra mo re re zhing yang 'jig rten gyi khams sangs rgyas kyi zhing gi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed

Because he had attained that, he saw the area of ground that was the route between the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā and the night goddess Samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśrī as being made of atoms of fire; or atoms of water; or atoms of earth; or atoms of diamond; or atoms of various great kings of precious jewels; or atoms of flowers, incense, and powders; or atoms of all precious arrays; or atoms of all locations. In each atom there were world realms as numerous as the atoms in a buddha realm.

whereby he saw as many worlds as atoms in a buddha-land forming and dissolving in each particle of fire, water, earth, diamond, various jewels, flowers, perfumes, incenses, arrays of gems, and all objects in between the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocana and the night goddess Samantasattvatranojahshri.
chu'i phung po dang bcas/
He saw that they had aggregations of water,
He also saw clusters of water,
me'i phung po dang bcas/
had aggregations of fire,
fire,
rlung gi phung po dang bcas/
had aggregations of air,
air,
sa'i phung po dang bcas/
had aggregations of earth,
and earth,
'jig rten gyi khams kyi mtshams dang bcas/
had world-realm boundaries,[1440]
and the sentient beings in all the worlds,
gzhi dang bcas/ rten dang bcas pa dbyibs sna tshogs can/ sa'i gzhi rnam pa tha dad pa sna tshogs dang ldan pa/
had bases, had foundations, had different shapes, had surfaces of various kinds of different forms,
with the various abodes they dwell in and the various arrays of the lands—
ri'i 'khor sna tshogs can/
had different kinds of encircling mountains,
various mountain ranges,
chu klung dang / mtsho sna tshogs kyis brgyan pa/
rivers, lakes,
rgya mtsho sna tshogs kyis kun nas 'khor ba/
had various kinds of encircling oceans,
oceans,
lha rdzas kyis khyim sna tshogs kyi rgyan dang ldan pa/ /
had arrays of various kinds of buildings made of divine materials,
heavens,
shing sna tshogs kyis yongs su gang ba/
had various kinds of trees,
trees,
nam mkha'i dbyings kyi rgyan sna tshogs can/
had various adornments in the sky,
adornments of the skies,
lha'i grong khyer gyi khyim gyi rgyan dang bcas pa/
had the adornment of the buildings of the cities of devas,
adornments of the habitations of all kinds of beings,
klu'i grong khyer gyi khyim gyi rgyan dang bcas pa/
had the adornment of the buildings of the cities of nāgas,
gnod sbyin gyi grong khyer gyi khyim gyi rgyan dang bcas pa/
had the adornment of the buildings of the cities of yakṣas,
dri za'i grong khyer gyi khyim gyi rgyan dang bcas pa/
had the adornment of the buildings of the cities of gandharvas,
lha ma yin gyi grong khyer gyi khyim gyi rgyan dang bcas pa/
had the adornment of the buildings of the cities of the asuras,
nam mkha' lding gi grong khyer gyi khyim gyi brgyan dang bcas pa/
had the adornment of the buildings of the cities of garuḍas,
mi'am ci'i grong khyer gyi khyim gyi rgyan dang bcas pa/
had the adornment of the buildings of the cities of kinnaras,
lto 'phye chen po'i grong khyer gyi khyim gyi rgyan dang bcas pa/
had the adornment of the buildings of the cities of mahoragas,
mi'i grong khyer gyi khyim gyi rgyan dang bcas pa/
had the adornment of the buildings of the cities of humans,
phyogs dang phyogs mtshams thams cad na rnam par gnas pa'i sems can thams cad kyi grong khyer gyi khyim gyi gnas dang /
had the adornment of the buildings of the cities of all beings in the main and intermediate directions,
sems can dmyal ba'i 'jig rten gyi yul dang /
had the realm of the world of hells,
the realms of hells,
byol song gi skye gnas kyi 'jig rten gyi yul dang /
had the realm of the world of animals,
animals,
gshin rje'i 'jig rten gyi yul dang /
had the realm of the world of Yama,
ghosts,
mi dang mi ma yin pa'i lam gyi rgyud kyi shi 'pho dang skye ba'i yul dang bcas pa/
had the realm of the death and rebirth of humans and nonhumans,[1441]
the realms of death and birth among humans,
skye ba sna tshogs kyis ma 'dres pa'i rgyud mtha' yas pa'i bye brag la yongs su gzhol ba rnams 'du zhing 'jig par gyur pa mthong ngo/ /
had various kinds of births, and had the accumulation and destruction of various kinds of existences.
all the various conditions of existence being interconnected, infinite different courses of being interrelated.
'jig rten gyi khams de dag kyang rnam pa sna tshogs su mthong ste/
He saw various kinds of differences between those worlds:
He also saw the difference in those worlds—
'jig rten gyi khams la la ni kun nas nyon mongs par mthong ngo/ /
he saw some worlds that were defiled,
he saw some worlds to be defiled,
la la ni yongs su dag par mthong ngo/ /
some that were pure,
some pure,
la la ni shin tu kun nas nyon mongs par mthong ngo/ /
some that were completely defiled,
some wholly defiled,
la la ni lam gyi rgyud yongs su dag pa mthong ngo/ /
some that were purified of ordinary existences,
some with purified states of being,
la la ni kun nas nyon mongs pa la yongs su dag par mthong ngo/ /
some that were purified of defilements,
some with purity in the midst of defilement,
la la ni rnam par dag pa la kun nas nyon mongs par mthong ngo/ /
some that were both pure and defiled,
some with defilement in the midst of purity,
la la ni shin tu yongs su dag par mthong ngo/ /
some that were completely pure,
some wholly pure,
la la ni gzhi mnyam par mthong ngo/ /
some that were a flat surface,
some level,
la la ni spyi'u tshugs su gnas par mthong ngo/ /
some that were upside-down,
some inverted,
la la ni snrel zhir 'dug par mthong ngo/ /
and some that were disordered,
some askew.

'jig rten gyi khams de dag gi sems can gyi lam gyi rgyud dang / sems can gyi skye gnas thams cad na/ mtshan mo'i lha mo sems can kun tu skyong ba'i gzi brjid dpal/ sems can so so nas 'dul ba'i rkyen bzhin du 'jig rten thams cad la ma 'dres par yongs su bstan pa'i phyir/ sems can thams cad la mngon du gyur par gnas par mthong ngo/ /

and he saw how in all the existences of beings, in all the births of beings in those world realms, the night goddess Samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśrī became present for all those beings in order to guide them according to their circumstances.
He saw the night goddess Samantasattvatranojahshri in all realms of being in those worlds, facing every sentient being capable of being guided; by seeing all worlds together at once,

sems can tshe'i tshad rnam pa ji lta bu dang ldan pa dang / mos pa'i spyod yul rnam pa sna tshogs can dang / lus rnam pa ji lta bu dang ldan pa dang / ngag rnam par phye ba dang / nges pa'i tshig gi 'du byed kyi tha snyad rnam pa ji lta bu dang ldan pa dang / sbyor ba'i rnam pa ji lta bu dang ldan pa dang / dbang gi rnam pa ji lta bu dang ldan pa rnams yongs su smin par bya ba dang / gdul ba'i don du sems can thams cad la ma 'dres par mngon sum du gnas par mthong ngo/ /

He saw her becoming present separately for every being in order to ripen and guide them in accordance with their lifespans; the various scopes of their aspirations; the forms of their bodies; their languages, terminology, and established definitions; the forms of their practices; and their dominance.

he saw her standing, without division, before all sentient beings, adapting to their life spans, their various spheres of belief, their physical forms, their conventions of verbal communication, and their mastery, in order to guide them to full development.
de yang 'di lta ste/ sems can dmyal ba'i lam gyi rgyud du gtogs pa'i sems can rnams kyi sems can dmyal ba'i sdug bsngal dang / 'jigs pa rnam par bzlog pa dang /
This means that he saw her becoming present separately for every being in order to dispel the fear of the various sufferings of hell for the beings who were in hell existences;
That is to say, he saw her standing before all sentient beings without division to free beings in hells from the pains and fears of hell,
byol song gi skye gnas sna tshogs su skyes pa'i sems can rnams kyi gcig la gcig za ba'i 'jigs pa rnam par bzlog pa dang /
in order to dispel in beings among the various animals the fear of being eaten by one another;
to free beings in brutish states from the perils of mutual predation,
gshin rje'i 'jig rten gyi lam gyi rgyud du gtogs pa'i sems can rnams kyi bkres pa dang / skom pa la sogs pa'i sdug bsngal gyi 'jigs pa rnam par bzlog pa dang /
in order to dispel the fear of the suffering of hunger, thirst, and so on for beings within Yama’s realm;
to free beings in the realm of ghosts from the pains and perils of hunger and thirst,
klu'i 'jig rten gyi lam gyi rgyud du gtogs pa'i sems can rnams kyi klu'i sdug bsngal dang / 'jigs pa thams cad rnam par bzlog pa dang /
in order to dispel all fear of the suffering of nāgas for those in nāga existences;
to free beings in the realm of dragons from all the pains and perils of the dragon realm,
'dod pa'i khams su gtogs pa'i sems can thams cad kyi 'dod pa'i khams kyi sdug bsngal dang / 'jigs pa rnam par bzlog pa dang /
in order to dispel all fear of the sufferings of the desire realm for all beings within the desire realms;
to free all beings in the realm of desire from all the pains and perils of the realm of desire,
mi'i 'jig rten gyi lam gyi rgyud du gtogs pa'i sems can rnams kyi mtshan mo mun pa mun nag gis chod pa'i mun pa'i 'jigs pa thams cad rnam par bzlog pa dang /
in order to dispel in those who existed in the human world all fear of being bewildered in the darkness of night;
to free all beings in the human realm from all the fears and perils of darkness,

mi snyan pa dang / bsngags pa ma yin pa dang / grags pa ma yin pa'i sgra dang / tshigs su bcad pa la mngon par zhen pa'i sems can rnams kyi grags pa ma yin pa dang / bsngags pa ma yin pa'i 'jigs pa rnam par bzlog pa dang /
in order to dispel the fear of blame and infamy for those who were preoccupied with criticism, blame, and infamy;
to free beings from all fear of ill repute,
'khor gyi 'jigs par lhung ba'i sems can rnams kyi 'khor du bag tsha ba'i 'jigs pa rnam par bzlog pa dang /
in order to dispel the fear of anxiety before an assembly for those beings who had the fear of anxiety before an assembly;
to free beings from intimidation by groups,
'chi bas 'jigs shing dngangs pa'i sems can rnams kyi 'chi ba'i 'jigs pa rnam par bzlog pa dang /
in order to dispel the fear of death in those beings who were frightened and terrified of death;
to free beings from fear of death,
ngan song gi g.yang sas 'jigs shing dngangs pa'i sems can rnams kyi ngan song gi g.yang sas 'jigs pa rnam par bzlog pa dang /
in order to dispel the fear of the abyss of the lower existences for those beings who were frightened and terrified of the abyss of the lower realms;
to free beings from fear of falling into states of misery,
'tsho ba med pas 'jigs shing skrag pa'i sems can rnams kyi 'tsho ba med pa'i 'jigs pa rnam par bzlog pa dang /
in order to dispel the fear of having no livelihood for those beings who were frightened and terrified of having no livelihood;
to free beings from fear of not being able to make a living,
dge ba'i rtsa ba chud zos kyis 'jigs shing / bag tsha ba'i sems can rnams kyi dge ba'i rtsa ba chud zos kyis 'jigs pa rnam par bzlog pa dang /
in order to dispel the fear of the loss of their roots of merit for those beings who were frightened of losing their roots of merit;
to free beings from fear of loss of virtue,
byang chub kyi sems nyams kyis 'jigs shing bag tsha ba'i sems can rnams kyi byang chub kyi sems nyams kyis 'jigs pa rnam par bzlog pa dang /
in order to dispel the fear of a diminution of the aspiration for enlightenment for those beings who were afraid of a diminution of their aspiration for enlightenment;
to free beings from fear of loss of the determination for enlightenment,
sdig to'i grogs po dang phrad kyis 'jigs shing bag tsha ba'i sems can rnams kyi sdig to'i grogs po dang phrad pa'i 'jigs pa rnam par bzlog pa dang /
in order to dispel the fear of meeting bad companions for those beings who were frightened of meeting bad companions;
to free beings from the danger of association with bad companions,
dge ba'i bshes gnyen dang bral gyis dogs shing / bag tsha ba'i sems can rnams kyi dge ba'i bshes gnyen dang bral ba'i 'jigs pa rnam par bzlog pa dang /
in order to dispel the fear of separation from kalyāṇamitras in those beings who were frightened of separation from kalyāṇamitras;
to free beings from fear of separation from spiritual benefactors,
nyan thos dang / rang sangs rgyas kyi sar lhung gis 'jigs shing bag tsha ba'i sems can rnams kyi nyan thos dang / rang sangs rgyas kyi sar lhung ba'i 'jigs pa rnam par bzlog pa dang /
in order to dispel the fear of falling to the level of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas in those beings who were frightened of falling to the level of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas;
to free beings from fear of falling into the stages of individual salvation,
'khor ba'i gnas sna tshogs kyi sdug bsngal gyis 'jigs shing skrag pa rnams kyi 'khor ba'i gnas sna tshogs kyi sdug bsngal gyi 'jigs pa rnam par bzlog pa dang /
in order to dispel the fear of the various kinds of suffering in saṃsāra for those beings who were afraid of the various kinds of suffering in saṃsāra;
to free beings from fear of suffering the pains of the various mundane states,
sems can skal pa mi mnyam pa dang phrad kyis 'jigs shing bag tsha ba rnams kyi sems can skal pa mi mnyam pa dang phrad pa'i 'jigs pa rnam par bzlog pa dang /
in order to dispel the fear of meeting contrary beings for those beings who were frightened and afraid of meeting contrary beings;
to free beings from fear of all association with the uncongenial,
dus mi bzad par skyes kyis 'jigs shing bag tsha ba rnams kyi dus mi bzad par skye ba'i 'jigs pa rnam par bzlog pa dang /
in order to dispel the fear of unfortunate times in those beings who were frightened and afraid of unfortunate times;
to free beings from fear of coming on bad times,
rigs ngan par skyes kyis 'jigs shing bag tsha ba rnams kyi rigs ngan par skye ba'i 'jigs pa rnam par bzlog pa dang /
in order to dispel the fear of rebirth into unfortunate families in those beings who were frightened and afraid of rebirth into unfortunate families;
to free beings from fear of being born among bad people,
sdig to'i las byas kyis 'jigs shing bag tsha ba rnams kyi sdig to'i las byed pa'i 'jigs pa rnam par bzlog pa dang /
in order to dispel the fear of committing bad actions for those beings who were frightened and afraid of committing bad actions;
to free beings from fear of doing evil,
las dang nyon mongs pa'i sgrib pas 'jigs shing dngangs pa rnams kyis las dang / nyon mongs pa'i sgrib pa'i 'jigs pa rnam par bzlog pa dang /
in order to dispel the fear of the obscurations of karma and kleśas for those beings who were frightened and afraid of the obscurations of karma and kleśas;
to free beings from fear of obstruction by deeds,

'du shes kyi rnam pa sna tshogs kyi gnas dang / 'ching bas 'jigs shing dngangs pa rnams kyi 'du shes kyi rnam pa sna tshogs kyi gnas dang / 'ching ba'i 'jigs pa rnam par bzlog pa dang / sems can thams cad la so sor mngon du gyur par gnas par mthong ngo/ /
and in order to dispel the fear of the bondage of remaining fixed in a variety of conceptions for those beings who were frightened and afraid of remaining fixed in a variety of conceptions.
to free beings from fear of bondage by attachment to various notions.

'di lta ste/ sgo nga las skyes pa'i sems can dang / mngal nas skyes pa dang / drod gsher las skyes pa dang / rdzus te skyes pa dang / gzugs yod pa dang / gzugs med pa dang / 'du shes yod pa dang / 'du shes med pa dang / 'du shes yod pa'ang ma yin/ 'du shes med pa'ang ma yin pa'i sems can thams cad yongs su bskyabs pa'i smon lam gyi stobs mngon par sgrub pa dang /

This means he saw her, being present in and purifying all realms, through possessing the supremacy of the vast miraculous powers of bodhisattva liberation and through the accomplishment of the power of the prayer to protect all beings: beings born from eggs, born from wombs, born from warm moisture, born spontaneously, and with form, without form, with perception, without perception, and neither with perception nor without perception;[1442]

That is to say, he saw her confronting the purification of all lands by undertaking the vow to save all beings, whether corporeal or incorporeal, thinking, nonthinking, and neither thinking nor nonthinking,

byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin gyi shugs drag po dang / rnam par gnon pa shin tu yangs pa'i stobs dang / byang chub sems dpa'i mngon par shes pa chen po stobs dang / mthu dang / byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po'i spyod pa dang / smon lam mngon par bsgrubs pa'i stobs kyis snying rje chen po'i tshul rgya mtsho'i shugs drag po shin tu skyes pa'i phyir;

through the vast prowess of the power of bodhisattva samādhi; through the power of the great higher cognitions of a bodhisattva; through the power of attaining the completely good conduct and prayer of a bodhisattva; and through developing the power of an ocean of the ways of compassion;

by the immense power of the vigorous exercise of the energy of concentration of enlightening beings, by exertion of the power of the great mystic knowledges of enlightening beings, by the power of execution of the vow to practice the conduct of universally good enlightening beings, by having generated the energy of the ocean of means of great compassion,

'gro ba thams cad du thogs pa med pa'i byams pa chen pos rgyas par dgang ba dang / sems can thams cad kyi bde ba yongs su bsgrubs pa dang / dga' ba'i shugs rnam par 'phel bar bya ba dang / sems can thams cad yongs su bsdu ba'i ye shes rab tu bsgrub pa'i phyir/ byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa rgya chen po'i rnam par 'phrul pa dang / khyu mchog gi mthu phyung ba dang ldan pas zhing thams cad yongs su dag par bya ba la mngon du gyur pa gnas par mthong ngo/ /

in order to spread everywhere the great love for all beings that is free of attachment; in order to create happiness for all beings and increase the power of their joy; and so that all beings will accomplish the accumulation of wisdom.

to suffuse all beings with desireless universal love, to increase the energy of joy, which is the origin of happiness for all beings, to apply the knowledge of how to take care of all beings, by embodiment of the vast spiritual power of enlightening liberation.

chos cad kyi rgyus shes par bya ba la mngon du gyur pa dang / sangs rgyas thams cad mchod cing rim gror bya ba la mngon du gyur pa dang / de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi bstan pa yongs su gzung ba la mngon du gyur pa dang / dge ba'i rtsa ba thams cad bsags pa la mngon du gyur pa dang / byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa thams cad rnam par 'phel bar bya ba la mngon du gyur pa dang / sems can thams cad kyi sems la sgrib pa med par mngon du gyur par gnas pa dang / sems can thams cad kyi dbang po yongs su smin par bya ba la mngon du gyur par gnas pa dang / sems can thams cad kyi mos pa rgya mtsho rnam par sbyang ba la mngon du gyur pa dang / sems can thams cad kyi sgrib pa'i chos rnam par bzlog pa la mngon du gyur pa dang / sems can thams cad kyi mi shes pa'i mun pa rnam par bsal ba la mngon du gyur cing / thams cad mkhyen pa'i ye shes snang ba yongs su bskyed pa'i don du gnas pa mthong ngo/ /

He saw her focused on knowing the knowledge of all Dharmas; being present there focused on making offerings and honoring all buddhas; focused on holding the teachings of all the tathāgatas; focused on the accumulation of all roots of merit; focused on the increase of all bodhisattva conduct; focused on the minds of all beings being free of obscurations; focused on ripening the faculties of all beings; focused on purifying the ocean of the aspirations of all beings; focused on dispelling obscuring qualities in all beings; focused on dispersing the darkness of ignorance in all beings;[1443] and focused on creating the light of omniscient wisdom.

He saw her confronting realization of knowledge of all things, attendance of all buddhas, preservation of the teachings of all buddhas, accumulation of all roots of goodness, development of all enlightening practices, unhindered penetration of the minds of all beings, maturation of the faculties of all beings, purification of the ocean of interests of all beings, removal of obstructing elements for all beings, dispersal of the darkness of nescience of all beings, and the implementation of all good, to generate the light of omniscience.

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis/ mtshan mo'i lha mo sems can kun tu skyong ba'i gzi brjid dpal gyi byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa'i khyu mchog gi mthu phyung ba dang / rnam par 'phrul pa 'jig rten thams cad la mngon par gnas shing / 'gro ba rnam par 'dul ba ston pa bsam gyis mi khyab pa de lta bu mthong nas rab tu dga' ba skyes te/ spro ba chen po'i shugs drag po rgya mtsho rab tu thob nas/

When Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, had seen this miraculous prowess of the night goddess Samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśrī’s inconceivable bodhisattva liberation called the manifestations that guide beings that appear in all worlds, he was overjoyed and acquired an ocean of the power of great delight.
Then Sudhana, having seen this inconceivable manifestation of the night goddess’s enlightening liberation showing guidance for beings in all worlds,
mtshan mo'i lha mo sems can kun tu skyong ba'i gzi brjid dpal la lus thams cad kyis phab ste; phyag byas nas ngor gyen du bltas so/ /
He prostrated with his entire body before the night goddess Samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśrī and then stood and gazed upon[1444] her.
prostrated himself before her, enraptured.

de nas mtshan mo'i lha mo sems can kun skyong ba'i gzi brjid dpal gyis byang chub sems dpa'i gzugs dang / mtshan rnam par dag pa de mi snang bar byas te/ mtshan mo'i lha mo'i gzugs su byas nas/ rnam par 'phrul pa thams cad 'byin cing 'dug par gnas so/ /

Then the night goddess Samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśrī made her appearance in the pure form and physical signs of a bodhisattva vanish, and she remained in the form of a night goddess emanating all miraculous manifestations.
At that point the night goddess stopped assuming the adornments of the forms of enlightening beings and continued to produce all the mystical manifestations by means of the form of a night goddess.
de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis/ mtshan mo'i lha mo sems can kun tu skyong ba'i gzi brjid dpal gyi mdun du 'dug ste thal mo sbyar nas/ de'i tshe tshigs su bcad pa 'di dag smras so/ /
At that time, Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, standing with hands together in homage before the night goddess Samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśrī, recited these verses to her:
Then Sudhana stood respectfully before her and spoke these verses to her:
khyod kyi sku yangs mtshan rab rgyan gyis brgyan/ / shin tu bzang zhing mdzes pa bdag gis mthong / / nam mkha' skar ma'i tshogs kyis brgyan pa bzhin/ / dpe byad bzang pos rnam par bris pa mthong / /
“I have seen your vast[1445] body Adorned by the excellent, beautiful signs[1446] And the wonderful special features, Like the sky adorned by stars. {1}
I have seen your immense body, Of excellent appearance, adorned with jewels, Variously beautified by embellishments As the sky is by the stars.
'od kyi 'khor can sku bzang dam pa'i mchog / mtha' yas zhing gi rdul khams mang po snyed/ / kha dog sna tshogs rnam pa'i dpe tshul du/ / phyogs rnams kun gyi dbyings su khyab par gang / /

“Your perfect, beautiful body’s halo of light rays As numerous as the atoms in infinite realms, With its multicolored, incomparable[1447] radiance, Spreads throughout the extent of every direction. {2}
Your aura of light, the sublime radiance of your body, Is equal to the atoms in endless lands; Like various kinds of matchless colors, It pervades everywhere endlessly.
'od zer dra ba mang po 'gro sems mnyam/ / khyod ni ba spu'i sgo nas 'gyed pa mdzad/ / 'od zer sgo la pad+mo yid 'ong gnas/ / khyod kyi sprul pa 'gro ba'i sdug bsngal sel/ /

“From the pores of your body shine As many networks of light rays as there are minds of beings. At the tip of each light ray an emanation of yours, Seated upon a beautiful lotus, eliminates the sufferings of beings. {3}
From every pore you radiate nets of light, As many as minds of beings; On a beautiful lotus in each ray of light Stands an emanation of you, extinguishing pain in the world.
spos kyi na bun sprin du chags pa'i 'gyed/ / 'gro ba'i gzugs su gnas te kun nas mdzes/ / me tog sgo rnams kun nas dgye mdzad pas/ / chos dbyings bzhugs pa'i rgyal ba kun tu khyab/ /
“Clouds of incense mists are emitted, Taking on the forms of beautiful beings. Flowers spread out everywhere To all the jinas in the realm of phenomena. {4}
You emit fragrant clouds of light In the forms of all beings, all pure, Showering flowers everywhere, On all the buddhas in the cosmos.
khyod kyi phrag pa'i lhun yangs 'phags pa ni/ / rin chen 'od 'phro ri bo ri rab 'dra/ / dri med de ni 'gro ba kun tu gsal/ / gti mug mun nag rnam par bzlog pa mdzad; ;
“The vast, sublime mass of your shoulders[1448] Shines with stainless jewel light, the size of Mount Meru, With which you illuminate all beings, Dispelling the darkness of ignorance. {5}
Your multitude of lights, vast and pure, Is like a mountain radiant with jewels; With it you illumine all worlds And remove the darkness of delusion.
khyod kyi dri med zhal mdog bzang po las/ / na bun sprin dang nyi ma yangs pa 'byung / / khyod kyi nyi ma'i 'khor 'dra 'od bzang ba/ / rnam par snang mdzad spyod yul yangs pa 'byin/ /

“Vast masses of clouds of suns[1449] are emanated From your beautifully colored, stainless[1450] face. Your wonderful light, which is like the disk of the sun, Is emanated throughout Vairocana’s vast field of activity. {6}
Myriad pure suns emerge From your mouth; Your sunlight shines throughout The vast realm of Vairocana.
khyod kyi spyan nas zla skar 'od 'byung ba/ / rtag tu dri med sprin ltar mang ba ste/ / de dag phyogs bcur bkang zhing 'gro ba rnams/ / rab tu snang byed 'jig rten rab rib sel/ /

“Clouds of the stainless light of the moon and the stars Are constantly emanated from your eyes. They spread throughout the ten directions, Illuminating beings and eliminating the world’s blindness. {7}
Pure moon and star lights Radiate from your eyes in great numbers And pervade the ten directions, Illumining the world and destroying darkness.
khyod kyi mtshan las 'gro ba'i lus mnyam pa'i/ / sprul pa rgya mtsho phyogs su khyab par 'phro/ / de dag chos dbyings yangs pa rgyas 'gengs shing / / sems can tshad med tshogs rnams yongs su 'dul/ /

“An ocean of emanations as numerous as the bodies of beings Is emanated into all directions from your physical signs of a great being. They spread throughout the vast realm of phenomena And guide[1451] the immeasurable multitudes of beings. {8}
From your features come myriad emanations In the forms of all beings; They go throughout the cosmos Developing the countless masses.
khyod kyi sku ni 'byams klas phyogs su snang / / 'gro ba kun la mngon gyur dga' ba bskyed/ / rgyal po me dang rkun po chus bskyed pa'i/ / 'jigs pa thams cad rnam sel zhi bar mdzad/ /
“Your body appears throughout the extent of the directions, Appearing to all beings and bringing them happiness, Dispelling and alleviating all fears Created by kings, fire, thieves, and water. {9}
Your body appears before all beings Everywhere, creating joy; You put an end to measureless dangers— From kings, brigands, fire, and floods—guiding beings.
gang tshe khyod kyi spyan sngar bdag btang nas/ / yon tan rnam par sems shing nyer phyin pa/ / de tshe 'od zer dri med 'khor bzang po/ / khyod kyi zhal gyi smin mtshams gseb nas 'thon/ /
“When I was sent into your presence, I approached you contemplating good qualities. At that time a beautiful, stainless mass of light rays Radiated from between your eyebrows. {10}
As directed, I have come to you, Observing your qualities; A pure aura of light beams Emanated from between your brows,
phyogs rnams rgya mtsho brgya mang snang mdzad nas/ / 'jig rten snang ba rgya che yongs bskyed de/ / rnam 'phrul rnam pa mang po rnams bstan nas; ; de tshe bdag gi lus kyi gseb tu zhi/ /
“They illuminated hundreds of oceans of directions And created a vast radiance in the world. They revealed many miraculous manifestations, And at that time they entered into my body. {11}
Illuminating all places, Producing great light in the world; Having shown many various wonders, It descended into my body.
gang tshe 'od kyi 'khor gyis bdag reg pa/ / de tshe bde ba rmad byung yangs pa myong / / gzungs dang ting 'dzin brgya mang yongs su non/ / phyogs bcu'i rgyal ba dpag yas mthong bar gyur/ /
“When that mass of light touched me, At that time I experienced a marvelous bliss. I gained mastery of many hundreds of dhāraṇīs and samādhis, And I saw limitless jinas in the ten directions. {12}
When the light descended on me, I experienced a marvelous, supreme happiness; I was imbued with mental command, a hundred concentrations, And I saw the infinite buddhas everywhere.
gom pa rnam por gyen du bteg pa la'ang / / rdul phran grangs snyed tshul ni bdag gis rig / rdul phran shin tu phra ba gcig la yang / / zhing gi rdul snyed zhing rnams mthong bar gyur/ /
“Wherever I stepped with my feet I could perceive the number of atoms there, And I saw in every single atom Realms as numerous as a realm’s atoms. {13}
I knew the number of atoms In the ground where I walked, And saw in each atom As many lands as atoms in lands.
rdul la gnas kyang rnam pa tha dgu ste/ / zhing mang brgya ni shin tu nyon yang mongs/ / de yi 'gro ba sdug bsngal nyams su myong / / cho nger ngu zhing smre sngags yongs su 'don/ /
“There were many hundreds of defiled realms Of many different kinds, located in atoms In which beings experienced suffering, Crying out with the sounds of lamentation and wailing. {14}
In an atom are hundreds Of various mixed-up, defiled lands, Where the beings suffer pains And weep and wail.
zhing mang la la kun nas nyon mongs dag / de na sdug bsngal mang zhing bde ba chung / / rgyal ba thugs rje can yang der skye ste/ / rgyal ba'i nyan thos rang rgyal de bzhin no/ /

“There were also many realms both defiled and pure, In which there was much suffering and little happiness, In which the compassionate jinas took birth, As did the jinas’ śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.[1452] {15}
There are also many lands with purity amid defilement, Where the happiness is little and the suffering much, Where the compassionate buddhas, Their disciples, and the self-enlightened gather.
zhing tshul la la yongs dag nyon mongs te/ / byang chub sems dpa'i gnas bzang mang pos brgyan/ / skyes pa bud med yongs brgyan blta na sdug / skyon med rgyal ba'i gdung yang rgyun mi 'chad/ /

“There were some realms, purified of defilements, That were ornamented by the presence of many bodhisattvas And adorned by beautiful men and women, And the brilliant family of the jinas resided there. {16}
There are also lands with defilement amid purity, Where many enlightening beings are assembled, Beautiful lands graced with men and women, Where the family of buddhas abides.
zhing rnams rgya mtsho yangs shing dri med pa/ / rdul la gnas shing mnyam pa'i gzhi dang ldan/ / de dag bskal pa brgya mang sngon gyi tshe/ / rnam par snang mdzad spyod mdzad yongs su sbyangs/ /
“There were vast, stainless oceans of realms, With level surfaces, that were located in atoms, Where for many hundreds of kalpas Vairocana purified his conduct in the past. {17}
Oceans of lands, vast and pure, Are in an atom, or an even plane, Purified over long eons past By the action of Vairocana.
zhing rnams 'byams klas kun na rgyal ba dag / shing dbang dam pa'i drung du gshegs pa ston/ / rnam par 'phrul zhing byang chub 'tshang yang rgya/ / chos kyi 'khor lo bskor cing 'dul ba ston/ /
“Within that entire vast extent of realms, Jinas were revealed going to the lord of trees, Attaining enlightenment, manifesting miracles, Turning the wheel of the Dharma, and guiding beings. {18}
In every land buddhas appear At the enlightenment tree; Having attained enlightenment, They teach and guide the world.
rnam par snang mdzad spyod yul yangs pa la/ / khyod kyang kun tu rjes su bzhud par mthong / / mchod pa stong phrag tshad med khrag khrig gis/ / rgyal ba kun la mngon par mchod mdzad mthong / /
“And I saw you also following In the vast scope of Vairocana’s activity And making offerings equally to all the jinas With countless millions of billions of offerings.” {19}
I see you in the vast realm of Vairocana, Honoring all the infinite buddhas.
de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis tshigs su bcad pa de dag smras nas/ mtshan mo'i lha mo sems can kun tu skyong ba'i gzi brjid dpal la 'di skad ces smras so/ /
When Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, had recited those verses, he said to the night goddess Samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśrī,
Then Sudhana said to the night goddess,

lha mo/ byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa de/ de lta bur zab pa ni ngo mtshar chen/ rnam par thar pa de'i ming ni ci zhes bgyi/ de khyod kyis brnyes nas yun ni ji srid cig lags/ byang chub sems dpas ji ltar nan tan du bgyis na rnam par thar pa de yongs su dag par 'gyur/

“Goddess, that profound bodhisattva liberation is a great wonder. What is the name of that liberation? How long ago did you attain it? How does a bodhisattva practice in order to purify that bodhisattva liberation?”
“It is wonderful how deep your enlightening liberation is. What is this liberation called? How long ago did you attain it? How does an enlightening being practice so as to purify this liberation?”

smras pa/ rigs kyi bu/ gnas 'di ni lha dang bcas pa'i 'jigs rten dang / nyan thos dang / rang sangs rgyas su bcas pas yid ches par dka' ba ste; de ci'i phyir zhe na/ 'di ni byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po'i spyod pa dang / smon lam khong du chud pa rnams kyi spyod yul te/ 'di ni byang chub sems dpa' snying rje chen po lhur len pa/ 'gro ba thams cad yongs su bskyab pa la zhugs pa/

The night goddess Samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśrī said, “Noble one, this subject is difficult to believe in for the world and its devas, as well as for the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas. Why is that? Because it is the field of practice of those bodhisattvas who follow the completely good conduct and prayer of the bodhisattvas; who are dedicated to the essence of compassion; who are engaged in saving all beings;

She replied, “This state is hard for celestials, Buddhist disciples, and individual illuminates to arrive at. Why? Because this is the realm of enlightening beings who follow the commitment to the practice of universally good enlightening beings; it is the sphere of enlightening beings imbued with great compassion who have undertaken the salvation of all sentient beings,

mi khom pa dang / ngan song dang / ngan 'gro'i lam thams cad rnam par bzlog pa la zhugs pa/ sangs rgyas kyi zhing khams thams cad sangs rgyas kyi zhing yongs su dag pa bla na med par bya ba la zhugs pa/ sangs rgyas kyi zhing thams cad na bzhugs pa'i de bzhin gshegs pa'i rigs rgyun mi gcod pa la zhugs pa/ sangs rgyas thams cad kyi bstan pa yongs su bzung ba la zhugs pa/ bskal pa thams cad du byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la gnas pas gnas par bya ba'i smon lam chen po rgya mtsho la zhugs pa/

who purify the paths that lead to all unfortunate and lower realms; who purify all realms to become the highest buddha realms; who create the unbroken continuity of the Buddha’s family in all buddha realms; who hold the teachings of all the buddhas; who have oceans of great prayers for remaining in the practice of bodhisattva conduct throughout all kalpas;

who have undertaken the purgation of all unfavorable and unhappy states, who have undertaken the perpetuation of the lineage of buddhas in all buddha-lands, who have undertaken to preserve the teachings of all buddhas, who have plunged into the ocean of great vows to continue enlightening practice through all ages,

chos rgya mtsho thams cad la bsgribs pa med pa'i ye shes snang ba rnam par sbyang ba la zhugs pa/ skad cig re re zhing dus gsum gyi tshul rgya mtsho thams cad du ye shes snang bas rnam par gnas pa rab tu thob pa rnams kyi yul te/ 'on kyang de bzhin gshegs pa'i byin gyi rlabs kyis bstan par bya'o/ /

and who create the pure light of wisdom, free of darkness, for all the oceans of Dharma; and those bodhisattvas who in each instant have attained the state of remaining in the light of wisdom of the entire ocean of the ways of the three times. However, through the blessing of the Tathāgata, I will teach it.

who have undertaken to clarify the light of unobscured knowledge of the ocean of all phenomena, who have attained the state of the light of instantaneous knowledge of the ocean of wisdom of past, present, and future. “Now, then, by the empowerment of Buddha I will tell you:

rigs kyi bu/ sngon 'das pa'i dus bskal pa sangs rgyas kyi zhing gi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed cig gi pha rol tu/ 'jig rten gyi khams rnam par snang mdzad gzi brjid dpal zhes bya bar/ bskal pa rdul dang bral ba'i dkyil 'khor ces bya ba byung ste/ bskal pa de la sangs rgyas ri rab kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed byung bar gyur to/ /

“Noble one, in the past beyond kalpas as numerous as the atoms in a buddha realm, there was a world realm called Vairocanatejaḥśrī during a kalpa called Virajomaṇḍala. In that kalpa there appeared as many buddhas as there are atoms in Sumeru.

in the past, as many eons ago as atoms in a buddha-land, there was an age called Sphere of Dispassion in a world called Sunny Brilliance; as many buddhas as atoms in the polar mountain arose in that age.

'jig rten gyi khams rnam par snang mdzad gzi brjid dpal zhes bya ba de ni/ rin po che thams cad kyi sprin gyi rgyan gyis brgyan pa ste/ rdo rje las byas pa'i gzhal med khang dang / gnas kyis yongs su mdzes par byas pa'o/ /
In that world realm called Vairocanatejaḥśrī there was an array of clouds of all jewels, and it was beautified by aerial palaces made of diamonds.
That world, furthermore, was arrayed with multitudes of all kinds of jewels and adorned with palaces and mansions made of diamond.
