'jig rten gyi khams de'i gzhi ni rin po che'i rgyal po dri ma med pa'i 'od kyi rgya mtsho las blangs pa ste/ lhun dang lus ni nor bu rin po che spos thams cad kyi rgyal po las gyur pa'o/ / de ni dbyibs kun tu zlum pa ste/ rnam par dag cing kun nas nyon mongs pa/ lhab lhub thams cad kyi sprin gyi bla res kun nas khyab pa/ rin po che'i khor yug rgyan thams cad dang ldan pa rim pa stong gis yongs su bskor ba/ gling bzhi pa bye ba khrag khrig brgya stong gis shin tu rgyas par brgyan pa ste/ de la gling bzhi pa la la ni kun nas nyon mongs pa ste/ sems can kun nas nyon mongs pa'i las dang ldan pa rnams kyi gnas so/ / la la ni kun nas nyon mongs shing rnam par dag pa ste/ sems can las 'dren ma dang ldan pa rnams kyi gnas so/ / la la ni rnam par dag cing kun nas nyon mongs pa ste/ sems can yongs su dag cing kun nas nyon mongs pa/ dge ba'i rtsa ba sbyangs pa/ kha na ma tho ba nyung ba rnams kyi gnas so/ / la la ni shin tu yongs su dag pa ste/ byang chub sems dpa' dag pa rnams kyi gnas so/ /

“That world realm was situated on a foundation of an ocean of the kings of jewels possessing stainless light. Its solid body[1453] was formed from precious jewels possessing all the kings of perfumes. It was completely round in shape. It was both pure and defiled. It was covered by a canopy of clouds of every adornment. It had the array of a thousand precious Cakravāla mountains. It was adorned by a quintillion four-continent worlds. Some four-continent worlds were defiled and were the dwelling places of beings who had defiled karma. Some were the dwelling places of beings who had a mixture[1454] of both defiled and pure karma. Some were the dwelling places of beings who were pure and also defiled, who had pure good actions and few blameworthy actions. Some were the dwelling places of pure bodhisattvas.

Now, that world rested on an ocean of all kinds of jewels of pure light and was itself made of all kinds of fragrant jewels. It was perfectly round and pure, with some defilement. It was covered with canopies of all kinds of ornaments, and surrounded by a thousand peripheral mountain ranges, circles of jewels in all arrays. It had millions of sets of four continents, some of which were inhabited by beings whose actions were defiled and beings whose actions were undefiled, some of which were inhabited by beings whose actions were a mixture of defilement and purity, some of which were inhabited by beings who were mostly pure with some defilement, beings of refined virtues, beings with little in them that is blameworthy; and some were inhabited by wholly pure enlightening beings.

'jig rten gyi khams rnam par snang mdzad gzi brjid dpal zhes bya ba de'i shar phyogs logs kyi khor yug gi mtshams na/ gling bzhi pa rin po che me tog sgron ma'i rgyal mtshan zhes bya ba rnam par dag cing kun nas nyon mongs pa/ ma rmos/ ma skyes pa'i 'bras la yongs su spyod pa sngon gyi las kyi rnam par smin pas mngon par grub pa'i khang pa brtsegs pa'i gnas dang / gzhal med khang la yongs su spyod pa/ 'khor kun nas yid bzhin gyi shing gis 'khor ba/ spos kyi shing sna tshogs kyi lhun las spos kyi sprin rgyun mi 'chad par 'byung ba/ phreng ba sna tshogs kyi shing las phreng ba'i sprin rgyun mi 'chad par 'byung ba/ me tog sna tshogs kyi shing las me tog kha dog dang dri bsam gyis mi khyab pa'i sprin gyi char rgyun mi 'chad par 'bab pa/ phye ma kha dog sna tshogs kyi shing gi lhun las spos rin po che'i rgyal po thams cad kyi phye ma'i char rgyun mi 'chad par 'bab pa/ rin po che'i shing sna tshogs las rin po che'i 'bru mang po 'brul ba'i kha dog snang bas shin tu snang bar byas pa/ lha rdzas kyi rol mo sna tshogs kyi shing las sil snyan sna tshogs kyi sprin rlung gis bskyod cing / nam mkha'i dbyings las sgra dbyangs snyan pa 'byung ba/ nyin mtshan gyi bde ba nyi ma dang / zla bas 'byung ba/ nor bu rin po che kun tu snang bas gzhi byas pa'i sa rab tu mnyam par gyur pa ste/

“To the east of the world realm Vairocanatejaḥśrī, next to the Cakravāla mountains, there was a four-continent world called Ratnakusumapradīpadhvajā. It was pure but defiled. There beings enjoyed the unplowed harvests. They lived in kūṭāgāras and aerial palaces that were created by the ripening of their past karma. It was encircled by wish-fulfilling trees. There were various kinds of aromatic trees that continually released clouds of perfume. There were various kinds of garland trees that continually released clouds of garlands. There were various kinds of flowering trees from which fell a continuous rain of clouds of flowers with inconceivable colors and scents. There were various kinds of colored-powder trees from which fell a continuous rain of the powders of all the kings of precious scents. There were various kinds of jewel trees from which fell many jewel seed-pods[1455] that shone with various colors. There were trees of various kinds of divine music from which were emanated clouds of the sound of music. From the sky came melodious sounds. Day and night, there was the pleasant light of the sun and moon. The ground, which shone with all precious jewels, was level.

“In the eastern part of that world, at the border of the peripheral mountains, was a set of four continents called Jewel Flower Lamp Banner. The land was pure, with some defilement. There was an abundance of food without plowing or sowing, and there were dwelling places resulting from the maturation of past deeds. There were wish-fulfilling trees everywhere, trees of various fragrances always emitting clouds of perfume, various garland trees constantly showering garlands, various flower trees raining multitudes of flowers of inconceivable colors and scents, trees of aromatic powders of various qualities continually giving forth a rain of powder of fragrant jewels, various jewel trees shining with light from their jewel buds, and trees of various celestial instruments that filled the air with beautiful sounds produced when stirred by the breeze. The sun and moon shined pleasantly day and night, and jewels shone everywhere.

gling bzhi pa der rgyal po'i pho brang bye ba khrag khrig brgya stong byung bar gyur te; rgyal po'i pho brang de dag re re zhing yang chu klung stong gis yongs su bskor ba'o/ / chu klung de dag thams cad kyang lha rdzas kyi me tog sil mas gang ba'o; ; lha rdzas kyi rol mo dang / glu'i sgra skad snyan cing yid du 'ong ba 'byin pa'o/ / chu 'gram rin po che'i shing yid du 'ong bas rnam par brgyan pa'o/ / rin po che sna tshogs kyis shin tu brgyan pa'i gru phan tshun du rgyu ba'o/ / bde ba sna tshogs ci dga' bar yongs su spyad du yod pa'o/ / chu klung gi mtshams kyi gzhi re re dag na yang grong khyer bye ba khrag khrig brgya stong phrag bcu kun nas gnas pa ste/ grong khyer de dag re re zhing yang grong rdal bye ba khrag khrig brgya phrag stong gi 'khor gyis yongs su bskor ba'o/ / grong dang grong khyer dang grong rdal de dag thams cad kyang lha rdzas kyi bza' shing gi ra ba dang / gzhal med khang dang / khang pa bye ba khrag khrig brgya phrag stong gi 'khor gyis yongs su bskor ba'o; ;

“In those four continents there were a quintillion royal cities. Each of those royal cities was encircled by a thousand rivers. All those rivers were filled with the petals of divine flowers. They emitted the melodious, beautiful sounds of divine music and song. Their banks were adorned by beautiful precious trees. Boats adorned by various jewels crossed back and forth. Every kind of happiness that could be delighted in was enjoyed there. In between each river a quintillion towns had been established. Each of those towns was encircled by a quintillion markets. All those villages, cities, and markets were encircled by a quintillion divine parks, aerial palaces, and mansions.

“At that time there were millions of capital cities on those four continents, each of which was surrounded by a thousand rivers. Each of those rivers carried various celestial flowers and produced celestial music; the banks were lined with trees of various jewels, and those who traveled by boat on the rivers enjoyed various delights to their hearts’ content. Between the river were built millions of cities, each surrounded by millions of towns. In all the cities and towns were many heavenly parks, palaces, and mansions.
gling bzhi pa de'i 'dzam bu'i gling gi dbus na/ rgyal po'i pho brang dbu ma rin po che'i me tog sgron ma zhes bya ba yod par gyur te/
In the center of the Jambudvīpa of that four-continent world was the central royal city, which was called Ratnakusumapradīpā.
“In the middle of the southernmost of those four continents was a central capital city called Jewel Flower Lamp Banner,

de ni skyid cing longs spyod phun sum tshogs pa dang ldan la/ rtag tu lo legs shing bde ba'i rnam pa thams cad dang ldan pa'o/ / lha dang mi mang pos yongs su gang ba'o/ / sems can dge ba bcu'i las kyi lam dang ldan pa rnams kyi gnas su gyur pa ste/

“This was a place that was prosperous and wealthy, with an abundance of food;[1456] it had every kind of happiness and was filled with many devas and humans, and the beings there followed the path of the ten good actions.
which was prosperous and peaceful, with a large population of virtuous people.

rgyal po'i pho brang rin po che'i me tog sgron ma zhes bya ba de na/ rgyal po rnam par snang ba rin chen pad+mo dpal gyi gtsug phud snying po zhes bya ba 'khor los bsgyur ba gling bzhi la dbang ba/ pad+mo'i snying po la rdzus te byung ba/ mi chen po'i mtshan sum cu rtsa gnyis kyis lus shin tu brgyan pa/ chos dang ldan pa/ chos kyi rgyal po rin po che bdun dang ldan pa gnas par gyur to/ /

“Here dwelled King Vairocanaratnapadmagarbhaśrīcūḍa, a cakravartin who was sovereign over the four continents. He had been spontaneously born from the center of a lotus flower, was adorned by the thirty-two signs of a great being, was a follower of the Dharma, a Dharma king, and possessed the seven jewels of a cakravartin.
The king in that city ruled the four continents; spontaneously born in the calyx of a lotus, he had the thirty-two marks of a great man and was a just ruler.
de'i bu dpa' zhing rtul phod la yan lag dam pa'i gzugs dang ldan pa/ gzhan gyi 'khor rab tu 'joms pa/ rnam pa thams cad yongs su tshang ba'i yan lag dam pa dang ldan pa stong tshang bar byung ngo/ /
“He had a full thousand sons who were courageous and heroic,[1457] who had perfectly formed bodies, who crushed the armies of enemies[1458] and had perfect bodies fully formed in all aspects.
He had a thousand sons, valiant, strong, destroyers of enemy armies.

de'i btsun mo'i 'khor gyi bud med kyang bye ba khrag khrig brgya stong phrag bcu yod par gyur te/ de dag kun kyang 'khor los bsgyur ba'i skal ba dang mnyam pa'i dge ba'i rtsa ba las byung ba mthun par spyod pa/ rin po che'i rgyan rang 'khrungs su byung ba/ dge ba'i sems dang ldan pa/ lha'i bu mo dang khyad par med par 'dra ba'i gzugs can/ dzam+bu chu klung gi gser gyi kha dog lta bu'i mdog dang ldan pa'i lus can/ lus kyi ba spu las lha rdzas kyi spos sna tshogs 'byung ba/ lus las lha rdzas kyi 'od dri zhim po dri ma med pa rab tu 'gyed pa sha stag go /

“In his harem there were a quintillion women, all of whom had originated from roots of merit that corresponded to those of the cakravartin, who had the same conduct as he had, were born adorned with jewels,[1459] had virtuous minds, and had bodies that were no different from those of goddesses, bodies that were the color of Jambu River gold, that emitted various divine scents from the pores of their bodies, and that shone with a pure, aromatic, divine light.

He also had millions of concubines who were products of the same virtues as was the king, carried out the same practices, and were noble-minded. They were as beautiful as goddesses, with golden complexions, celestial fragrances and auras of pure light emanating from their bodies.
de'i blon po bye ba phrag bcu byung ste/ blon po rin po che la sogs pa dag go /
“He had millions of ministers such as the precious prime minister.[1460]
He also had millions of ministers, superlative advisers.

'khor los bsgyur ba'i rgyal po rnam par snang ba rin chen pad+mo dpal gyi gtsug phud snying po de'i btsun mo dam pa/ bud med rin po che dpal gyi bzhin yongs su rgyas pa zhes bya ba/ gzugs mdzes shing sdug pa/ blta na yid du 'ong ba/ kha dog bzang po shin tu rgyas pa'i dam pa dang ldan pa/ skra mthon mthing du 'dug pa/ mig dkar nag 'byes pa/ mdog gser gyi kha dog tu 'dug pa/ tshangs pa'i dbyangs dang ldan pa/ lus las 'od rtag tu 'byung ba/ 'khor kun tu dpag tshad stong gi tshad du 'od kha dog du ma dang ldan pa; lha rdzas kyi dri zhim po can 'gyed pa byung ngo/ /

“The cakravartin king Vairocanaratnapadmagarbhaśrīcūḍa’s queen named Saṃpūrṇaśrīvakrā was the precious woman. She was beautiful, attractive, and lovely to look at. She possessed an excellent, magnificent, perfect color. Her hair was deep black. She had deep black eyes.[1461] She had golden skin. She had the voice of Brahmā. Light continually shone from her body. She spread lights of various colors and divine aromas for a thousand yojanas around her.
“The king also had a beautiful wife, whose aura constantly suffused a thousand leagues all around her with multicolored light of celestial fragrance.

rgyal po'i btsun mo dpal gyi bzhin yongs su rgyas pa zhes bya ba de las/ bu mo pad+mo bzang mo mig yid du 'ong ba'i dpal gyi zla ba zhes bya ba/ yan lag thams cad tshang ba/ gzugs mdzes shing sdug pa/ blta na yid du 'ong ba/ 'jig rten thams cad kyis blta na mi ngoms pa byung bar gyur te/ rigs kyi bu/ 'di lta ste/ dper na/ 'khor los bsgyur ba'i rgyal po la blta na su yang ngoms par mi 'gyur ba de bzhin du/ 'khor los bsgyur ba'i bu mo pad+mo bzang mo mig yid du 'ong ba'i dpal de la blta bas kyang / su yang ngoms par mi 'gyur te/ shes rab kyis yongs su ngoms par 'gyur ba ni ma gtogs so/ /

“Saṃpūrṇaśrīvakrā, the king’s queen, had the cakravartin’s daughter named Padmabhadrābhirāmanetraśrīcandrā.[1462] She had a completely perfect body. She was beautiful, attractive, and lovely to look at. The whole world never had enough of looking at her. For example, noble one, just as no one was ever satisfied that they had seen enough of the cakravartin, in the same way no one was ever satisfied that they had seen enough of the cakravartin’s daughter Padmabhadrābhirāmanetraśrī, except for those who had gained the satisfaction of wisdom.

That queen had a daughter by the king who was so beautiful that no one ever tired of looking at her. Just as no one was ever tired of the sight of the sovereign, in the same way no one was ever sated with the sight of the princess, except those sated with wisdom.
de'i tshe de'i dus na sems can rnams kyang tshe dpag tu med par gyur te/ tshe la gcig tu nges pa med pas bar ma dor 'chi ba ni yod do/ /
“At that time, in that time, beings had an immeasurable lifespan. There was no definite lifespan, so death occurred during it.[1463]
“At that time the life span of the beings in that world was measureless—there were none with fixed life spans and no untimely deaths.

de'i dus na sems can rnams kyi dbyibs sna tshogs dang / kha dog sna tshogs dang / dbyangs sna tshogs dang / ming sna tshogs dang / rigs sna tshogs dang / tshe'i tshad sna tshogs dang / chu zheng rnam pa tha dad pa dang / mos pa dang / stobs dang / brtson 'grus dang / mthu rnam pa tha dad pa dang / yid du 'ong ba dang / yid du mi 'ong ba rnam pa tha dad pa dang / yangs pa dang / dma' ba la mos pa sna tshogs kyang yod par gyur te/

At that time, beings had various shapes, various colors, various voices, various names, various families, various lifespans, and different sizes; different aspirations, strengths, diligences, and powers; different beautiful and ugly appearances; and various higher and lower aspirations.

Also at that time the variety of forms of sentient beings was known, as was the variety of their colors, voices, names, families, life spans, physical sizes, abilities and strengths, agreeable and unpleasant affairs, and higher and lower inclinations.

de la sems can ji snyed cig kha dog bzang ba dang / yangs pa la mos pa dang / yan lag tshang ba dang / blta na sdug cing yid du 'ong bar gyur pa de dag ni 'di skad ces 'dzer to/ / kye/ mi dag /nga ni khyed pas kha dog ches bzang ngo zhes zer ro/ /
“Those beings who had good color, high aspirations, and perfect bodies and were beautiful and lovely to look at said, ‘Oh! We have a much better color than you!’
There, those with better appearances and more confidence, who were physically perfect and good-looking, proclaimed their superiority to others;

de bzhin du sems can ji snyed cig lus kyi dbyibs legs pa dang ldan par gyur pa de dag kyang / sems can lus kyi dbyibs mi sdug par gyur pa rnams la rlom zhing khyad du gsod do/ / de dag de ltar gcig la gcig khyad du gsod pa las byung ba'i mi dge ba'i rtsa bas tshe'i tshad las kyang yongs su bri bar gyur to/ / kha dog dang stobs dang bde ba las kyang yongs su bri bar gyur to/ /

“In the same way, those beings who had an excellent body shape were dismissive and arrogant toward those beings who had ugly body shapes. In that way, they did not care about each other, so that through the roots of demerit, their lifespans diminished. Even their color, strength, and happiness diminished.

and those with well-formed bodies looked down on all those with ill-formed bodies. Then, because of the evil of mutual contempt, they lost their span of life, physical appearance, strength, and happiness—all was lost.

rgyal po'i pho brang rin po che'i me tog sgron ma de'i byang phyogs logs na/ snying po byang chub kyi shing kun du grag pa'i chos kyi sprin sgra'i rgyal mtshan zhes bya ba/ de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi snying po byang chub kyi rgyan skad cig re re la yongs su ston pa/ rtsa ba rin po che'i rgyal po rdo rje ltar sra zhing mi 'jig pa/ nor bu rin po che thams cad las grub pas/ lhun shin tu yangs shing rgyas pa/ sdong po dang / yal ga dang / lo ma dang / 'dab ma dang / me tog dang / 'bras bu rin po che thams cad kyi rgyu las grub pa/ kun tu cha mnyam par rnam par bkod cing kun tu khyab pa'i yal ga dang ldan pa/ rgyan kun tu rgyas par 'gengs shing mi zad pa dang ldan pa/ rin po che sna tshogs kyi 'od 'phro ba dang / 'od zer kun tu snang bar 'gyed pa/ de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi yul gyi rnam par 'phrul ba'i dbyangs rjes su sgrog pa yod de/

“To the north of the royal capital Ratnakusumapradīpā there was the bodhimaṇḍa tree called Samantāvabhāsanadharmameghanirghoṣadhvaja that manifested in each instant the display of the bodhimaṇḍas of all tathāgatas. Its roots were as hard and indestructible as diamond, the king of jewels. Its bulk was made from all precious jewels and was vast and huge. Its trunk, branches, leaves, flowers, and fruit were made from all jewels. It was perfectly symmetrical. It had branches that spread everywhere. It was a spreading, unceasing display. It shone with the lights of various jewels, its light rays shining everywhere. It resounded with descriptions of the miraculous manifestations that were the scope of all the tathāgatas.

“There was an enlightenment tree north of the city called Sound of Clouds of Teachings Illumining All. Its strong roots were made of indestructible diamonds that showed the arrays of the enlightenment sites of all buddhas in every moment; its trunk was a mass of all kinds of jewels, high and wide; its foliage, flowers, and fruits were made of all kinds of jewels. It was perfectly formed, well proportioned everywhere, its foliage equally distributed, with endless adornments throughout, flashing with all kinds of jewel lights radiating in all directions, producing sounds of magical displays of the spheres of all buddhas.

snying po byang chub de'i mdun rol na/ spos chu'i mtsho rin po che'i me tog dang / glog dang / chos kyi 'brug sgra'i sprin gyi dbyangs zhes bya ba yod de/ de ni rin po che'i shing bye ba khrag khrig brgya stong phrag bcus kun nas bskor ba ste/ rin po che'i shing de dag thams cad kyang byang chub kyi shing gi dbyibs su 'khod pa sha stag go /

“In front of that bodhimaṇḍa there was a lake of scented water called Ratnakusumavidyuddharmanigarjitameghaghoṣa. It was encircled by a quintillion precious trees, and all those precious trees had the same form as the Bodhi tree.

“In front of that enlightenment site there was a pond of fragrant water called Sound of Clouds Thundering Teachings with Jewel Flower Lightning, surrounded by millions of jewel trees. Each of those trees was formed like the enlightenment tree.

spos chu'i mtsho chen po rin po che'i me tog dang / glog dang / chos kyi 'brug sgra'i sprin gyi dbyangs zhes bya ba de'i 'gram thams cad kyang / nor bu rin po che thams cad bkram zhing rnam par bkod pa ste/ rin po che thams cad kyi phreng ba sna tshogs su dkrigs pa'o/ /

“All the banks of that great lake of scented water called Ratnakusumavidyuddharmanigarjitameghaghoṣa were covered with a splendid array of all precious jewels, decorated by various strings of all jewels,
The banks of the pond were made of well-distributed collections of all kinds of gems, hung with strings of all kinds of jewels,
rin po che rnam par dag pa las byas pa'i khang pa sna tshogs kyi rgyan gyis yongs su brgyan pa'o/ / rgyan rnam par dag pa sna tshogs kyi rgyan gyis shin tu brgyan pa'o/ /
adorned by an array of mansions made of pure jewels, and beautified by an array of all pure adornments.
graced with arrays of mansions made of pure jewels, adorned with pure arrays of all kinds of ornaments.
snying po byang chub de'i 'khor thams cad kyang nor bu rin po che'i khang pa brtsegs pa chen po rgyan bsam gyis mi khyab pa dang ldan pa/ pad+mo'i snying po can sha stag gis yongs su 'khor ba ste/
“All around the bodhimaṇḍa were countless kūṭāgāras made of precious jewels, with lotuses in their centers.
The whole enlightenment site was also surrounded by countless jewel towers in lotus calyxes with inconceivable adornments.

spos chu'i mtsho chen po rin po che'i me tog dang / glog dang / chos kyi 'brug sgra'i sprin gyi dbyangs zhes bya ba de'i dbus nas/ pad+mo'i rgyal po chen po lo ma'i mtshams nas dus gsum gyi de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi yul rnam par ston pa'i 'od zer gyi sprin gyi rgyan ces bya ba byung bar 'gyur te/ pad+mo chen po de la de bzhin gshegs pa ri rab kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed de dag gi nang nas bskal pa'i thog ma pa/ de bzhin gshegs pa ye shes rin po che'i 'od kun tu 'phro ba'i dpal yon tan dpal gyi rgyal po zhes bya ba byung bar gyur te/ de ni bskal pa de la thams cad kyi thog mar bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu mngon par rdzogs par sangs rgyas te/

“In the center of the great lake of scented water called Ratnakusumavidyuddharmanigarjitameghaghoṣa there was a great king of lotuses[1464] called Sarvatryadhvatathāgataviṣayapatrasaṃdhividyotitameghavyūha. On that great lotus appeared a tathāgata named Samantajñānaratnārciśrīguṇaketurāja,[1465] who was the very first[1466] from among tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms in Sumeru. He would be the first of all of them to attain the highest, complete enlightenment in that kalpa.

In the middle of the pond appeared a great ruby lotus called Array of Clouds of Light Rays Flashing Lightning from Between the Leaves Illumining the Sphere of the Buddhas of Past, Present, and Future.“In that lotus appeared a buddha named Paragon of Virtue Radiant with the Light of Universal Knowledge, who was the first of as many buddhas as atoms in the polar mountain to attain supreme perfect enlightenment in that eon.

des lo stong phrag du ma zhig tu chos bstan pas sems can yongs su smin par mdzad nas/ lo stong phrag bcur 'od zer snang ba'i rnam par 'phrul pas yongs su smin par mdzad do/ / de bzhin gshegs pa de lo stong phrag bcu na 'byung bar 'gyur ro zhes bya ba'i tshe/

Having ripened beings by teaching the Dharma for many thousands of years, he was ripening beings for ten thousand years through the miraculous manifestation of the radiance of light rays, and then after ten thousand years that tathāgata would appear there.

Having developed sentient beings for thousands of years by hearing the Teaching, he prepared them by manifestation of lights for ten thousand years for the appearance of the buddha in ten thousand years:

pad+mo'i rgyal po chen po lo ma'i mtshams nas dus gsum gyi de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi yul rnam par ston pa'i 'od zer gyi sprin gyi rgyan ces bya ba de las/ sems can thams cad rdul dang 'byed pa'i sgron ma zhes bya ba'i 'od zer byung bar gyur te/ 'od des phog pa'i sems can rnams kyis kyang lo stong phrag bcu na de bzhin gshegs pa 'byung bar 'gyur ro zhes bya bar shes so/ /

“At that time, the great king of lotuses, Sarvatryadhvatathāgataviṣayapatrasaṃdhividyotitameghavyūha, radiated a ray of light called Sarvasattvavirajaḥpradīpa. The beings who were touched by that ray of light knew that in ten thousand years a tathāgata would come.
there emanated from that great lotus a light called ‘spotless lamp of all beings,’ and the beings touched by that light became aware that the buddha would emerge in ten thousand years.

lo stong phrag dgu na de bzhin gshegs pa de 'byung bar 'gyur ro zhes bya ba'i tshe/ byang chub kyi shing de las rdul dang bral ba'i dpal gyi snying po zhes bya ba'i 'od zer byung ste/ 'od zer des phog pa'i sems can de dag gis kyang gzugs thams cad shin tu phra ba mthong bar gyur to/ /

“At the time when the tathāgata would come in nine thousand years, the Bodhi tree shined a ray of light called Virajovatīśrīgarbhā. The beings who were touched by that ray of light saw all subtle forms.

They realized that the buddha would emerge in nine thousand years as a light called ‘full of undefiled radiance’ emanated from the enlightenment tree, and the beings touched by the light perceived all subtle forms.

lo stong phrag brgyad na de bzhin gshegs pa 'byung ngo zhes bya ba'i tshe/ byang chub kyi shing chen po de nyid las 'od zer sems can thams cad kyi las rnam par smin pa'i dbyangs zhes bya ba byung ste; des phog pa'i sems can de dag thams cad kyis kyang rang rang gi las rgya mtsho khong du chud par gyur te/ las dran pa'i ye shes kyang thob par gyur to/ /

“At the time when the tathāgata would come in eight thousand years, the great Bodhi tree shined a ray of light called Sarvasattvakarmavipākanirghoṣa. The beings who were touched by that ray of light comprehended the ocean of their own karma and attained the wisdom that remembers karma.

Realizing that the buddha would emerge in eight thousand years as a light called ‘voice of the results of the deeds of all beings’ emanated from the enlightenment tree, the beings touched by the light comprehended the oceans of their own doings and gained recollection and knowledge of their deeds.

lo stong phrag bdun na de bzhin gshegs pa de 'byung bar 'gyur ro zhes bya ba'i tshe/ byang chub kyi shing de nyid las 'od zer dge ba'i rtsa ba thams cad yang dag par 'byung ba'i dbyangs zhes bya ba byung ste; 'od zer des sems can de dag la phog nas/ dbang po nyams pa med cing yongs su tshang bar gyur to/ /

“At the time when the tathāgata would come in seven thousand years, the great Bodhi tree shined a ray of light called Sarvakuśalamūlasaṃbhavanirghoṣā. The beings who were touched by that ray of light gained unimpaired complete faculties.

Realizing that the buddha would emerge in seven thousand years as a light called ‘voice produced by all roots of goodness’ emanated from the enlightenment tree, the beings touched by the light gained completeness of all their faculties.

lo stong phrag drug na de bzhin gshegs pa de 'byung bar 'gyur ro zhes bya ba'i tshe/ byang chub kyi shing chen po de nyid las 'od zer sangs rgyas kyi yul bsam gyis mi khyab pa'i dbyangs zhes bya ba byung ste/ des sems can de dag la phog nas bsam pa rgya chen pos rnam par 'phrul par gyur to/ /

“At the time when the tathāgata would come in six thousand years, the great Bodhi tree shined a ray of light called Acintyabuddhaviṣayanidarśananirghoṣā. The beings who were touched by that ray of light made emanations with a vast motivation.

Realizing that the buddha would emerge in six thousand years as a light called ‘sound of revelation of the inconceivable sphere of buddhas’ emanated from the enlightenment tree, the beings touched by the light were transformed into higher states.

lo stong phrag lnga na de bzhin gshegs pa de 'byung bar 'gyur ro zhes bya ba'i tshe/ byang chub kyi shing chen po de nyid las 'od zer sangs rgyas kyi zhing thams cad yongs su dag par sgra 'byin pa'i gzugs brnyan rnam par dmigs pa zhes bya ba byung ste/ des sems can de dag la phog nas/ sangs rgyas kyi zhing rnam pa thams cad du yongs su dag par mthong bar gyur to/ /

“At the time when the tathāgata would come in five thousand years, the great Bodhi tree shined a ray of light called Sarvabuddhakṣetrapariśuddhinigarjitapratibhāsavijñāpanā. The beings who were touched by that ray of light saw with complete purity all buddha realms.

Realizing that the buddha would emerge in five thousand years as a light called ‘conveying the dramatic mental impression of the purity of all buddha-lands’ emanated from the enlightenment tree, the beings touched by the light saw all aspects of the purity of buddha-lands.

lo stong phrag bzhin de bzhin gshegs pa de 'byung bar 'gyur ro zhes bya ba'i tshe/ byang chub kyi shing chen po de nyid las 'od zer de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi yul tha mi dad pa'i sgron ma zhes bya ba byung ste/ des sems can de dag la phog nas de bzhin gshegs pa de'i rnam par 'phrul pa thams cad du song ba la zhugs par gyur to/ /

“At the time when the tathāgata would come in four thousand years, the great Bodhi tree shined a ray of light called Sarvatathāgataviṣayāsaṃbhedapradīpā. The beings who were touched by that ray of light comprehended the all-pervading miraculous manifestations of the tathāgatas.

Realizing the buddha would emerge in four thousand years as a light called ‘lamp of the unity of the realm of buddhas’ emanated from the enlightenment tree, the beings touched by the light comprehended the omnipresent miracle of the buddha.

lo stong phrag gsum na de bzhin gshegs pa de 'byung bar 'gyur ro zhes bya ba'i tshe; byang chub kyi shing chen po de las 'od zer 'gro ba thams cad la mngon du gyur pa'i sgron ma zhes bya ba byung ste/ des sems can de dag la phog nas de bzhin gshegs pa de yang mngon du mos pas mthong bar gyur to/ /

“At the time when the tathāgata would come in three thousand years, the great Bodhi tree shined a ray of light called Sarvajagadabhimukhapradīpā. The beings who were touched by that ray of light directly saw, through their aspiration, the tathāgatas.

Realizing the buddha would emerge in three thousand years as a light called ‘lamp in the presence of all beings’ emanated from the enlightenment tree, the beings touched by the light were engrossed in the sight of the buddha right before them.

lo stong phrag gnyis na de bzhin gshegs pa de 'byung bar 'gyur ro zhes bya ba'i tshe/ byang chub kyi shing chen po de las 'od zer dus gsum gyi ye shes kyi glog gi sgron ma zhes bya ba de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi sngon gyi tshul rab tu sgrog pa byung ste/ des sems can de dag la reg nas de bzhin gshegs pa de'i sngon gyi tshul rgya mtsho la rtog cing 'jug par gyur to/ /

“At the time when the tathāgata would come in two thousand years, the great Bodhi tree shined a ray of light called Tryadhvajñānavidyutpradīpā. The beings who were touched by that ray of light realized and comprehended the ocean of the past ways of the tathāgatas.

Realizing the buddha would emerge in two thousand years as a light called ‘lamp of lightning of knowledge of past, present, and future’ emanated from the tree of enlightenment along with the voice of the past efforts of the buddha, the beings touched by the light put faith in and entered into the oceans of past efforts of the buddha.

lo stong na de bzhin gshegs pa de 'byung bar 'gyur ro zhes bya ba'i tshe/ byang chub kyi shing chen po de las 'od zer ye shes rab ri ba med pa de bzhin gshegs pa'i sgron ma zhes bya ba byung ste/ des sems can de dag la phog nas/ de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi rnam par 'phrul pa dang / zhing thams cad dang / sems can thams cad mthong bar 'gyur ba'i mig kun tu lta ba thob par gyur to/ /

“At the time when the tathāgata would come in a thousand years, the great Bodhi tree shined a ray of light called Vitimirajñānatathāgatapradīpā. The beings who were touched by that ray of light attained the all-seeing view of the vision that sees all the manifestations of the tathāgatas, all realms, and all beings.

Realizing the buddha would emerge in a thousand years as a light called ‘lamp of realization of suchness of unobscured knowledge’ emanated from the enlightenment tree, the beings touched by the light gained the power of the universal eye to see the miracles of all buddhas, the buddha-lands, and all sentient beings.

de bzhin gshegs pa de lo brgya na 'byung bar 'gyur ro zhes bya ba'i tshe/ byang chub kyi shing chen po de nyid las 'od zer 'gro ba thams cad kyis sangs rgyas mthong ba rnam par smin pa'i dge ba'i rtsa ba las byung ba zhes bya ba byung ste/ des sems can de dag la phog nas/ de bzhin gshegs pa skye ba'i 'du shes thob par gyur to/ /

“At the time when the tathāgata would come in a hundred years, the great Bodhi tree shined a ray of light called Sarvajagadbuddhadarśanavipākakuśalamūlasaṃbhavā. The beings who were touched by that ray of light attained the perception of the arising of the tathāgatas.

Realizing the buddha would emerge in a hundred years as a light called ‘product of virtues of all beings resulting from seeing buddhas’ emanated from the enlightenment tree, the beings touched by the light got an impression of the emergence of Buddha.

de bzhin gshegs pa de zhag bdun na skye bar 'gyur ro zhes bya ba'i tshe/ byang chub kyi shing chen po de nyid las 'od zer sems can thams cad rab tu dga' ba dang / spro ba dang / mos pa yongs su 'byung ba'i dbyangs zhes bya ba byung ste/ des sems can de dag la phog nas/ sangs rgyas mthong bar 'gyur ba'i dga' ba'i shugs chen po skyes par gyur to/ /

“At the time when the tathāgata would come in seven days, the great Bodhi tree shined a ray of light called Sarvasattvapraharṣaprītiprāmodyasamudayanirghoṣā. The beings who were touched by that ray of light developed the great power of the joy of seeing the tathāgatas.

Realizing the buddha would appear in seven days as a light called ‘sound producing happiness and joy in all sentient beings’ emanated from the enlightenment tree, the beings touched by the light developed the energy of the great joy of seeing Buddha.

rigs kyi bu/ de ltar 'od zer gyis yongs su smin par bya ba'i tshul tshad med pa rnam pa de lta bus/ lo stong du sems can rnams yongs su smin par mdzad nas zhag bdun pa la thug pa dang / 'jig rten gyi khams de thams cad yongs su bskyod pa'i tshul tshad med pas yongs su bskyod nas shin tu dag par byin gyis brlabs so/ / phyogs bcu'i de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi sangs rgyas kyi zhing yongs su dag pa ji snyed pa rgyan bsam gyis mi khyab pa rnam pa sna tshogs dang ldan pa de dag thams cad kyang / sangs rgyas kyi zhing der sems kyi skad cig re re la yongs su bstan par gyur to/ /

“Noble one, he ripened beings through that kind of immeasurable method of ripening through light rays for a thousand years. Then, on reaching the seventh day, he blessed the entire world realm as completely pure by shaking it through an immeasurable method for shaking it. In each instant of mind, all the pure buddha realms of all the tathāgatas in the ten directions with their various inconceivable displays appeared in that buddha realm.

“Having thus developed beings for ten thousand years by means of such measureless lights, when the seven days were up he shook that whole world with infinite means of shaking it and made it completely pure, as the buddha-lands of all buddhas in the ten directions are pure—and in each moment of thought he showed the various inconceivable arrays of all those buddha-lands.

de nas zhag bdun pa tha ma la bab pa dang / 'jig rten gyi khams de na sems can sangs rgyas mthong bar 'gyur bar yongs su smin pa de dag thams cad snying po byang chub tu mngon par gzhol bar gyur to/ /
“On the last, seventh, day, the beings in that world realm had been ripened by the sight of the buddhas, and they all came to face the bodhimaṇḍa.
And in those final seven days all the beings in that world who were ripe for the sight of Buddha stood facing the site of enlightenment.

de nas 'jig rten gyi khams de'i khor yug thams cad dang / ri rab thams cad dang / ri thams cad dang / chu klung thams cad dang / rgya mtsho thams cad dang / shing thams cad dang / sa'i gzhi thams cad dang / grong khyer thams cad dang / ra ba thams cad dang / gnas thams cad dang / gzhal med khang thams cad dang / gos dang / rgyan dang / longs spyod thams cad dang / rol mo'i shing thams cad dang / rol mo brdung ba'i dbyangs thams cad dang / sprul pa'i rgyan thams cad kyi dmigs pa re re las kyang de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi yul dang / mthu'i sgra rab tu sgrog pa'i spros dang /

“Then, from all that world realm’s Cakravāla mountains, from all the Sumeru mountains, from all mountains, from all rivers, from all oceans, from all trees, from all the surface of the ground, from all towns, from all walls, from all dwellings, from all aerial palaces, from all clothes, jewelry, and enjoyments, from all musical trees, from all sounds of musical instruments, from all emanated displays, from each perceived thing, there came the description of the range of activity and the power of all tathāgatas,

“Then the supremacy of the realm of all buddhas was proclaimed from every single object in that world—from all the peripheral mountains, all the polar mountains, all the other mountains, all the rivers, all the seas, all the trees, all the land masses, all the cities, all the walls, all the buildings, all the clothing, ornaments, and paraphernalia, all the music and song, and all the created adornments—
bdug spos thams cad kyi sprin mngon par 'thon te/
and there issued forth clouds of all incenses and perfumes;
emanating clouds of all kinds of fragrant smoke,
rin po che 'od 'phro ba'i sprin dang /
clouds of lights shining from jewels;
clouds of lusters of all jewels,
spos dang / bdug spos thams cad kyi 'od 'phro dam pa dang /
clouds of lights shining from all perfumes and incenses;
spos rin po che thams cad kyi gzugs kyi sprin dang /
clouds in the form of all perfume and jewels;[1467]
gos rin po che dang / rgyan rin po che thams cad kyi sprin dang /
clouds of all clothing, jewels, and precious jewelry;
clouds of all kinds of precious clothing and jewelry,
rin po che'i me tog sna tshogs kyi ri rab kyi sprin dang /
clouds of Sumerus of various precious flowers;
clouds of mountains of all kinds of jewel flowers,
phye ma sna tshogs kyi sprin mang po
many clouds of various powders;
clouds of all kinds of aromatic powders,
de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi 'od zer gyi sprin rnam par ston pa/
and clouds of the light rays of all the tathāgatas.
clouds of light rays of all buddhas flashing,
de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi 'od kyi dkyil 'khor gyi sprin rab tu 'gyed pa/
The Cakravāla mountains and so forth emitted clouds of the halos of light of all the tathāgatas.
clouds of auras of all buddhas,
rol mo brdung ba dang dkrol ba thams cad kyi sprin yongs su 'khrol zhing brdung ba/
They resounded with clouds of the music of all instruments and drums.
de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi smon lam gyi sgra skad kyi sprin rab tu 'byin pa/
They emitted clouds of the sound of the prayers of all the tathāgatas.
de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi dbyangs kyi yan lag dang / gsung rgya mtsho'i sprin rab tu sgrog pa/
They resounded with clouds of the aspects of voice and the oceans of speech of all the tathāgatas.
clouds of oceans of sayings of all buddhas,
de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi mtshan dang / dpe byad bzang po'i gzugs brnyan sna tshogs kyi sprin rab tu ston pa byed cing /
They manifested clouds of various images of the signs and features of a great being possessed by all the tathāgatas.
clouds of glorious manifestations of the marks and embellishments of all buddhas,
de bzhin gshegs pa 'byung ba'i ltas sngon du byung ba bsam gyis mi khyab pa yongs su bstan te/
They revealed countless omens of the coming of a tathāgata.
manifesting the signs that a buddha is about to appear in the world.

rin po che'i rgyal po'i pad+mo chen po lo ma'i mtshams nas/ dus gsum gyi de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi yul rnam par ston pa'i 'od zer gyi rgyan de'i pad+mo'i 'khor rin po che'i rgyal po las byas pa chen po sha stag tu byas te 'khod do/ /
“The lotus Sarvatryadhvatathāgataviṣayapatrasaṃdhividyotitameghavyūha had a retinue of great lotuses that were all made of the kings of jewels.
Around the great ruby lotus Array of Clouds of Light Rays Flashing Lightning from Between the Leaves Illumining the Sphere of the Buddhas of Past, Present, and Future,

rin po che'i rgyal po'i pad+mo chen po'i 'khor gyi rin po che'i pad+mo chen po de dag gi ze ba dang / snying po la seng+ge'i khri rin po che'i pad+mo chen po'i snying po can/ sangs rgyas kyi zhing bcu'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed dag byung bar gyur te/ rin po che'i snying po can gyi khri de dag la'ang byang chub sems dpa' sangs rgyas kyi zhing bcu'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed skyil mo krung bcas te 'khod par gyur to/ /

On the filaments and pericarps of the great lotuses that were the retinue of the great lotus made of the kings of jewels, there were precious lion thrones with great lotuses in their centers. They were as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha realms. As many bodhisattvas as there are atoms in ten buddha realms were seated cross-legged around those thrones with a precious center.
there stood as many ruby lotuses as atoms in ten buddha-lands, on which appeared as many jewel lion seats, on which appeared as many enlightening beings sitting cross-legged.

bcom ldan 'das ye shes rin po che'i 'od kun tu 'phro ba'i dpal yon tan dpal gyi rgyal po de bzhin gshegs pa de/ bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu mngon par sangs rgyas ma thag tu de'i mod la phyogs bcu'i 'jig rten gyi khams su de bzhin gshegs pa mang po dag kyang bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu mngon par sangs rgyas te/ sems can rnams kyi bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du mngon sum du chos kyi 'khor lo bskor bar gyur to/ /

“The moment that tathāgata, the Bhagavat Samantajñānaratnārciśrīguṇaketurāja, attained the highest, complete enlightenment of buddhahood, many tathāgatas in world realms in the ten directions also attained the highest, complete enlightenment of buddhahood and, in accordance with the dispositions of beings, turned the wheel of the Dharma.

“As soon as that buddha, Paragon of Virtue Radiant with the Light of Universal Knowledge, had realized supreme perfect enlightenment, the buddhas in all worlds in the ten directions attained supreme perfect enlightenment and set in motion the wheel of teaching for sentient beings in accordance with their mentalities:
des kyang 'jig rten gyi khams de dag gi sems can tshad med pa rnams ngan song dang log par ltung ba thams cad las rnam par bzlog go /
“The countless beings in those world realms were turned away from all lower realms and downfalls.
thereby innumerable sentient beings in that world were thenceforth freed from the calamities of all states of misery,
sems can tshad med pa ni mtho ris su skye ba la rab tu bkod do/ /
Countless beings were brought to rebirth in the higher realms.
innumerable sentient beings were led to heaven,
sems can tshad med pa ni nyan thos kyi sa la rab tu bkod do/ /
Countless beings were established on the level of the śrāvakas.
innumerable beings were led to the stage of saints,
sems can tshad med pa ni rang sangs rgyas kyi byang chub tu yongs su smin par byas so/ /
Countless beings were ripened for the enlightenment of the pratyekabuddhas.
innumerable beings were led to the stage of individual enlightenment,
sems can tshad med pa ni shugs drag po 'od kyis 'byung ba'i byang chub tu yongs su smin par byas so/ /
Countless beings were ripened for the enlightenment that arises in the light of power.
innumerable beings were developed to the point of enlightenment in which emancipation is realized by way of intense illumination,
sems can tshad med pa ni brtson 'grus dri ma med pa'i rgyal mtshan gyi byang chub tu yongs su smin par byas so/ /
Countless beings were ripened for enlightenment in the banner of stainless diligence.
innumerable sentient beings were developed to the point of enlightenment characterized by pure exertion,
sems can tshad med pa ni chos rab tu bsgom pa'i gnas su 'byung ba'i byang chub la rab tu bkod do/ /
Countless beings were established in the enlightenment that arises in dwelling in meditation on the Dharma.
sems can tshad med pa ni dbang po yongs su dag pa rab tu bsgom pas 'byung ba'i byang chub tu yongs su smin par byas so/ /
Countless beings were ripened for the enlightenment that arises in meditation on the purification of the faculties.
innumerable sentient beings were developed to the point of enlightenment in which emancipation is realized through the efficacy of purification of the senses,
sems can tshad med pa ni stobs mnyam pa nyid la yang dag par spyod pa khong du chud pas 'byung ba'i byang chub tu yongs su smin par byas so/ /
Countless beings were ripened for the enlightenment that arises in comprehending the practice of the equanimity of strength.
innumerable sentient beings were developed to the point of enlightenment in which emancipation is realized through pursuing conduct consonant with the powers of knowledge,
sems can tshad med pa ni chos grong khyer mngon du 'gyur ba'i yul gyi theg pa skye bas 'byung ba'i byang chub la rab tu bkod do/ /
Countless beings were established in the enlightenment that arises in the emergence of the yāna with its field of attention turned toward the city of the Dharma.
innumerable sentient beings were led to enlightenment in which emancipation is made possible by conveyance to the precincts of the citadel of truth,
sems can tshad med pa ni thams cad du rjes su song ba'i rdzu 'phrul tha mi dad pa'i tshul gyi theg pas 'byung ba'i byang chub la rab tu bkod do/ /
Countless beings were established in the enlightenment that arises in the yāna of the ways of various miraculous manifestations that pervade everywhere.
sems can tshad med pa ni spyod pa'i sbyor ba la yang dag par gzhol ba'i tshul gyis 'byung ba'i byang chub la rab tu bkod do/ /
Countless beings were established in the enlightenment that arises in the way of being dedicated to practice.
innumerable sentient beings were led to enlightenment in which emancipation is realized by means of integration of efforts in practice,
sems can tshad med pa ni ting nge 'dzin gyis 'jug pa'i tshul gyis 'byung ba'i byang chub la rab tu bkod do; ;
Countless beings were established in the enlightenment that arises in the ways of entering samādhi.
innumerable sentient beings were led to enlightenment in which emancipation is realized through methods of concentration,
sems can tshad med pa ni dmigs pa'i yul thams cad yongs su dag pa'i dkyil 'khor gyi tshul gyi 'byung ba'i byang chub la rab tu bkod do/ /
innumerable sentient beings were led to enlightenment in which emancipation is realized through means of purifying all objects,
sems can tshad med pa ni byang chub sems dpa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed do/ /
Countless beings developed the aspiration for the enlightenment of the bodhisattvas.
innumerable sentient beings were inspired to the enlightenment of enlightening beings,
sems can tshad med pa ni byang chub sems dpa'i lam la rab tu bkod do/ /
Countless beings were established on the bodhisattva path.
innumerable sentient beings were set in the path of enlightening beings,
sems can tshad med pa ni pha rol tu phyin pa'i lam rnam par dag pa la rab tu bkod do/ /
Countless beings were established on the pure path of the perfections.
innumerable sentient beings were led to the purification of the path of transcendent ways,
sems can tshad med pa ni byang chub sems dpa'i sa dang po la rab tu bkod do/ /
Countless beings were established on the first bodhisattva bhūmi.[1468]
innumerable sentient beings were led to the first stage of enlightening beings;
sems can tshad med pa ni byang chub sems dpa'i sa gnyis pa dang / gsum pa dang / bzhi pa dang / lnga pa dang / drug pa dang / bdun pa dang / brgyad pa dang / dgu pa la rab tu bkod do/ /
Countless beings were established on the second, third, fourth, fifth, sixth, seventh, eighth, and ninth bodhisattva bhūmis.

in the same way, as the buddha turned the wheel of teaching by his inconceivable spiritual power, in each moment of consciousness innumerable sentient beings were led to the second, third, fourth, fifth, sixth, seventh, eighth, ninth,
sems can tshad med pa ni byang chub sems dpa'i sa bcu pa la rab tu bkod do/ /
Countless beings were established on the tenth bhūmi.
and tenth stages;
sems can tshad med pa ni byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa smon lam gyi khyad par can la btsud do/ /
Countless beings were brought into the preeminent conduct and prayers of the bodhisattvas.
innumerable sentient beings were introduced to the practice of enlightening beings based on the most excellent vows;
sems can tshad med pa ni byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po'i spyod pa dang / smon lam rnam par dag pa la rab tu bkod do/ /
Countless beings were established in the completely good conduct and prayers of the bodhisattvas.
innumerable sentient beings were led to the purification of commitment to the conduct of universally good enlightening beings.

de ltar de bzhin gshegs pa des sangs rgyas kyi khyu mchog gi mthu phyung ba dang / rnam par 'phrul pa bsam gyis mi khyab pas chos kyi 'khor lo bskor bas/ sems kyi skad cig re re la sems can gyi khams mtha' dang dbus med pa rnam par dul bar gyur to/ /

“In that way, the Tathāgata turned the wheel of the Dharma through the inconceivable miraculous manifestations and the power of the preeminence of a buddha, so that in each instant of mind he guided realms of beings without end or center.
Thus, as the buddha turned the wheel of teaching by his inconceivable spiritual power, he succeeded in guiding innumerable sentient beings in each moment of consciousness,
'jig rten gyi khams de'i sems can thams cad kyis kyang de bzhin gshegs pa de'i sku sna tshogs dang / thabs mkhas pa sna tshogs kyis bsgrubs pa'i chos bstan pa yongs su shes par gyur to/ /
“All the beings of that world realm understood the Dharma taught by that tathāgata through various bodies and the accomplishment of various skillful methods.
and all the sentient beings in that world, according to their mentalities, perceived the Teaching through various bodies expediently projected by the buddha.

rgyal po'i pho brang rin po che'i me tog sgron ma'i sems can du gzugs dang / kha dog dang / yul dang / longs spyod kyis rgyags shing dregs te/ gcig la gcig khyad du gsod pa de rnams gdul ba'i don du/ byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang pos kha dog dang gzugs mchog tu byon par mngon par sprul te/ rgyal po'i pho brang der phyin to/ /

“In order to guide those beings in the royal capital Ratnakusumapradīpā, who were proud and arrogant because of their form, color, scope, and enjoyments and had no care for one another, the bodhisattva Samantabhadra manifested a supreme color and form and went to the royal capital. His halo was so vast that it illuminated the entire royal capital.[1469]

“At that time, furthermore, in order to discipline the beings in the city who were intoxicated with enjoyment of forms and colors and who were contemptuous of each other, the enlightening being Universally Good magically assumed a body of superlative appearance and went to the city.

de'i 'od shin tu yangs pas rgyal po'i gnas de dag thams cad yongs su snang bar gyur te/ rgyal po'i gnas de'i 'od dang / 'khor los bsgyur ba'i rgyal po rnam par snang ba'i rin chen pad+mo dpal gyi gtsug phud snying po'i lus las byung ba'i 'od dang / bud med rin po che'i 'od dang / rin po che'i shing gi 'od dang / nor bu rin po che chen po'i 'od dang / nyi zla dang / gza' skar dang / rgyu skar gyi 'od dang / dzam+bu'i gling na 'od ji snyed cig yod pa de dag thams cad kyang mi snang bar gyur te/

“The light of the royal capital, the light from the body of the cakravartin king Vairocanaratnapadmagarbhaśrīcūḍa, the light from the precious queen, the light from the precious trees, the light from the precious jewels, the light from the sun, moon, planets, and stars, and whatever lights there were in Jambudvīpa all ceased to shine.

His glorious light illumined the city so that the lights of the king and queen, the lights of the jewel trees and the precious stones, even the lights of the sun, moon, planets, and stars, and all the lights of the whole continent, could not be perceived.

dper na/ nyi ma shar te mun pa dang ba dang / zla ba dang / gza' skar dang / rgyu skar gyi 'od kyang mi snang la/ me dang nor bu'i 'od kyang mi snang ngo/ / de bzhin du byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po'i zil gyis non nas/ dzam+bu'i gling de na 'od yod pa thams cad kyang mi snang bar gyur to/ /

“For example, when the sun shines, darkness and the light of the moon, planets, stars, and constellations vanish, and the light from fire and jewels vanishes. In the same way, through being outshined by the bodhisattva Samantabhadra, all the lights in Jambudvīpa vanished.

Just as when the sun rises the darkness disappears and the moon, planets, and stars cannot be seen, in the same way all the lights of the continent, overwhelmed by the light of Universal Good, could not be seen.

'di lta ste/ dper na; dzam+bu chu klung gi gser gyi sa le sbram gyi drung du snag tsha'i gzugs bzhag na mdzes par mi rung / lhag ger mi rung / lham mer mi rung / lhang nger mi rung ngo/ / de bzhin du byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po'i mdun du sems can de dag gi gzugs kyi lus kyang mdzes par mi rung / lhag ger mi rung / lha ma mer mi rung / lhang nger mi rung ngo/ /

“It is just as if, for example, you were to place some lampblack[1470] in front of a lump of Jambu River gold, it would not be beautiful, would not be bright, would not glow, and would not shine. In the same way, when the physical forms of those beings were in front of the bodhisattva Samantabhadra, they were not beautiful, were not bright, were not glowing, and were not shining.

Just as a mass of carbon black does not look beautiful or shine or seem bright or lustrous in the presence of pure gold, in the same way the bodies of those beings did not look beautiful or shine or seem bright or lustrous in the presence of the universally good enlightening being Samantabhadra.

de nas de dag 'di snyam du gyur te; de lta su zhig /de ltar de'i drung du bdag cag gi lus sam/ 'od dam/ kha dog gam /gzi brjid kyis kyang mdzes par mi rung / lhag ger mi rung / lham mer mi rung / lhang nger mi rung ba de lta lha'am/ tshangs pa'am/ ci zhig /de'i mtshan ma ni gzung bar mi nus so snyam mo/ /

“They thought, ‘In front of him our bodies, light, color, and brilliance are not beautiful, not bright, not glowing, and they do not shine. Is this a deva or Brahmā whose attributes we are unable to comprehend?’
They thought, ‘Who might this be, a god, or Brahma, before whom we do not appear beautiful, do not shine, do not glow, have no radiance or luster? We cannot grasp his appearance.’

de nas byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang pos/ rgyal po'i gnas rin po che'i me tog sgron ma'i dbus 'khor los bsgyur ba'i rgyal po rnam par snang ba rin po chen pad+mo dpal gyi gtsug phud snying po'i gzhal med khang gi steng gi bar snang la 'dug ste/ 'khor los bsgyur ba'i rgyal po rnam par snang ba rin chen pad+mo dpal gyi gtsug phud snying po la 'di skad ces smras so/ /

“Then the bodhisattva Samantabhadra stood in the sky above the aerial palace of the cakravartin king Vairocanaratnapadmagarbhaśrīcūḍa, which was in the center of the royal capital Ratnakusumapradīpā. He said to the cakravartin king Vairocanaratnapadmagarbhaśrīcūḍa,
“Then Universally Good stood in the sky above the palace of the king in the middle of the city and said to the king,

rgyal po chen po/ shes par gyis shig /de bzhin gshegs pa dgra bcom pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas 'jig rten du byung ste/ khyod kyi khams 'di nyid kyi snying po byang chub chos kun tu snang ba'i chos kyi sprin gyi sgra dbyangs rgyal mtshan 'di nyid na rnam par spyod do zhes pa dang /
‘Great king, know this! A tathāgata arhat samyaksaṃbuddha has appeared in this world. He is dwelling in your land, at the bodhimaṇḍa called Samantāvabhāsanadharmameghanirghoṣadhvaja.’[1471]

‘Know, O king, that a buddha, a perfectly enlightened one, has arisen in the world. He is in this very realm of yours, at the enlightenment site Emblem of the Sound of Clouds of Teaching Revealing Universal Truth.’

rgyal po'i bu mo ye shes kyi 'od kun tu 'phro ba/ pad+mo bzang mo mig yid du 'ong ba'i dpal gyi zla bas byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po'i gzugs kyi lus dang / 'od dang / rnam par 'phrul pa dang / rgyan mthong ste/ dbyangs thos nas/ dga' ba dang mos pa'i shugs chen po skyes te/

“When the king’s daughter, Samantajñānārcipadmabhadrābhirāmanetraśrīcandrā, saw the bodhisattva Samantabhadra’s body, light, miracles, and adornments and heard his voice,[1472] she experienced a powerful happiness and delight.[1473]

“Now, the daughter of the king, seeing the form-body and the supernal manifestation of light of the enlightening being Universally Good, and hearing the sound of his ornaments, was enraptured and was inspired

de'i tshe sems 'di snyam du bskyed do/ / bdag gis dge ba'i rtsa ba gang ci bsags pa des/ bdag kyang lus 'di 'dra ba thob par shog cig /rgyan 'di 'dra ba dang / mtshan 'di 'dra ba dang / spyod lam 'di 'dra ba dang / rdzu 'phrul 'di 'dra bar shog cig /ji ltar 'dis mtshan mo mun nag gi nang na sems can rnams la snang ba chen po bskyed de/ sangs rgyas skye ba yongs su brjod pa de bzhin du/ bdag gis kyang sems can rnams kyi mi shes pa'i mun pa bsal te/ ye shes chen po'i snang ba bskyed par bya'o/ / gang dang gang du skyes pa thams cad du'ang / dge ba'i bshes gnyen 'di dang mi 'bral bar shog cig /

“At that time, she thought, ‘May I, through whatever roots of merit I accumulate, attain a body like that! May I have that kind of jewelry, those kinds of characteristics, that kind of conduct, and those kinds of miraculous powers! Just as he has brought a great light for beings in the darkness of night and told them of the birth of a buddha, so may I dispel the darkness of ignorance in beings and bring them the light of great wisdom! Wherever I am reborn, may I never in all those lives be separated from this kalyāṇamitra!’

with this thought: ‘Whatever basic goodness I have accumulated, may I thereby attain such a body, such adornment, such features, such deportment, such mystic power. Just as he generates light in the dark night of sentient beings and announces the emergence of a buddha, in the same way may I also dispel the darkness of nescience in sentient beings and produce the light of great knowledge. Wherever I may be born, may I never be apart from this spiritual benefactor.’

de nas/ rigs kyi bu/ 'khor los bsgyur ba'i rgyal po rnam par snang ba rin chen pad+mo dpal gyi gtsug phud snying po yan lag bzhi'i dpung gi tshogs dang lhan cig /rin po che bdun dang lhan cig /bud med kyi tshogs kyi 'khor dang lhan cig /bu dang / blon po dang / ljongs kyi mi dang lhan cig tu rgyal bo'i rdzu 'phrul chen po dang / rgyal po'i mthu chen pos/ rgyal po'i gnas rin po che'i me tog sgron ma de nas 'phags te/ gyen du nam mkha' la dpag tshad gcig tsam du mngon par 'phags nas/ dzam+bu'i gling thams cad dang / gling bzhi pa'i 'jig rten gyi khams thams cad snang ba chen pos rgyas par bkang ste/ sems can thams cad sangs rgyas blta ba la yongs su bskul ba'i don du/ rin po che'i ri thams cad la gzugs brnyan mngon par bstan cing / gling bzhi pa'i 'jig rten gyi khams su gtogs pa'i sems can rnams la mngon sum du gnas te/ sangs rgyas blta ba de tshigs su bcad de glu'i dbyangs kyis bsngags pa/

“Then, noble one, the cakravartin king Vairocanaratnapadmagarbhaśrīcūḍa, with the four divisions of his army,[1474] with his seven jewels, with his retinue of women, and with his ministers and the people of his land, through the king’s miraculous powers, through the great might of the king, rose up into the sky above the royal capital Ratnakusumapradīpā to a height of one yojana. He filled the whole of Jambudvīpa and the entire four-continent world with a great light. In order to encourage all beings to come and see the Buddha, he manifested his image on all the precious mountains and became present before all beings in the four-continent world realm and sang a song of verses that praised seeing the Buddha:

“Then the king, along with his armies, his concubines, his sons, his ministers, and the inhabitants of the city, left the city and rose a league in the air by the magic power of the king, who filled the four continents with a great light, and who, in order to get all sentient beings to see the buddha, manifested his reflection in all the jewel mountains, stood before all the sentient beings in the four continents, and praised the sight of buddha in verse:
lus can thams cad skyabs mdzad pa'i/ / sangs rgyas 'jig rten byung bar gyur/ / 'jig rten gtso bo de blta bar/ / kun kyang longs te 'dong bar gyis/ /
“ ‘Into the world has come a buddha Who will be a savior for all who have bodies. Everyone should rise and set forth In order to see that lord of the world! {20}
Buddha has appeared in the world, Savior of all living beings; All should get up and go To see the guide of the world.
lus can kun la phan don du/ / chos rab ston pa gang mdzad pa'i/ / de bzhin gshegs pa 'byung ba ni; ; bskal pa bye ba'i brgya lam na'o/ /
“ ‘The appearance of a tathāgata, Someone who teaches the Dharma In order to benefit all who have bodies, May occur only once in a billion[1475] kalpas. {21}
Buddhas appear once In millions of eons And teach the truth For the benefit of all beings.
'jig rten phyin cir log gyur cing / / mi shes sgrib pas bsgribs gyur te/ / 'khor ba'i sdug bsngal myong ba rnams/ / gzigs shing thugs rje che bskyed nas/ /
“ ‘He developed compassion on seeing The world having gone astray, Obscured by the darkness of ignorance And experiencing the suffering of saṃsāra. {22}
Seeing the world in error, Shrouded by the darkness of nescience, And oppressed by the pains of life and death, Buddhas conceive great compassion.
sdug bsngal thams cad gzhil don du/ / sems can yongs su smin bya'i phyir/ / bskal pa bye ba grangs med du/ / byang chub spyod pa spyad pa mdzad/ /
“ ‘In order to ripen beings So as to extinguish all suffering, He practiced enlightened conduct For countless millions of kalpas. {23}
For countless millions of eons They have practiced enlightenment To perfect sentient beings And extinguish all suffering.
bskal pa mtha' yas mu med par/ / sangs rgyas byang chub mchog don du/ / zhabs dang phyag kyang yongs su btang / / spyan dang snyan dang dbu yang btang / /
“ ‘For limitless, endless kalpas, For the sake of the supreme enlightenment of buddhahood, He gave away his legs and his arms, And he also gave away his eyes, ears, and head. {24}
They have given up Their hands and feet, ears, noses, and heads For endless eons, to attain The immortality of enlightenment.
mthong zhing bsnyen bkur byas pa dang / / thos pa don yod 'gyur ba yin/ / 'jig rten mgon po 'jig rten du/ / 'byung ba bskal pa bye bar dkon/ /
“ ‘To see him, honor him, And hear him will be beneficial. It is rare even in ten million kalpas For a lord of the world to appear in the world. {25}
It is hard to find a guide of the world, Even in millions of eons; To listen to them, meet them, and associate with them Cannot but be fruitful.
de ni byang chub gdan la bzhugs/ / gsung ba'i dam pa bltar yang yod/ / bdud rnams sde dang bcas btul te/ / byang chub mchog tu rnam sangs rgyas/ /
“ ‘He is dwelling at the seat of enlightenment. He is there like a supreme secret. He has subjugated Māra and his armies And attained the supreme enlightenment of buddhahood. {26}
This supreme teacher is to be seen Sitting on the seat of enlightenment, Having conquered the demon armies And realized the highest awakening.
'od zer dkyil 'khor mtha' yas pa/ / sangs rgyas sku las mngon bkye zhing / / 'gro ba tshim par mdzad pa yi/ / kha dog sna tshogs 'di la ltos/ /
“ ‘There is an infinite aura of light That radiates from the Buddha’s body. Come see its various colors That bring satisfaction to beings. {27}
Behold the body of Buddha, With an endless array of lights, Emanating various glows Which soothe the world.
'od zer sprin mang grangs med pa/ / sangs rgyas sku las 'thon pa rnams/ / de ni sems can snang gyur na/ / bde ba dpe med thob par 'gyur; /
“ ‘There are countless clouds of light rays That come from the Buddha’s body. Those beings upon whom they shine Attain an unparalleled happiness. {28}
Countless multitudes of light beams Emanate from the Buddha’s pores; Those on whom they shine Feel incomparable joy.
brtson 'grus chen po rab rtsom ste/ / rang dang rang gi bsam pa yis/ / mgon po de la mchod pa gyis/ / tshur shog de yi gan du 'dong / /
“ ‘Develop great diligence. And each according to your wishes, Make offerings to that protector. Come! And go into his presence!’ {29}
Honor the guide of your own will— Muster great energy and go to him.
de nas rgyal po rnam par snang ba rin chen pad+mo dpal gyi gtsug phud snying pos/ tshigs su bcad pa de dag gis bdag gi khams na gnas pa'i sems can thams cad yongs su bskul te/
“After King Vairocanaratnapadmagarbhaśrīcūḍa had thus encouraged all the beings in his realm with those verses,
“Then the king, having exhorted the inhabitants of his domain with these verses,

mchod pa'i sprin sna tshogs brgya stong phrag bcu 'khor los bsgyur ba'i dge ba'i rtsa bas yongs su grub pa'i char pa/ snying po byang chub kun nas snang ba'i chos kyi sprin gyi dbyangs kyi rgyal mtshan gyi 'khor kun tu mngon par 'bebs shing /
the cakravartin’s roots of merit created a rain of a million clouds of various offerings that descended onto the bodhimaṇḍa Samantāvabhāsanadharmameghanirghoṣadhvaja.[1476]
showering the whole enlightenment site with offerings from ten thousand clouds of offerings developed from the roots of goodness of the ruler, went to the buddha,
rin po che'i gdugs kyi sprin gyis nam mkha' kun nas yog par bya ba dang /
Clouds of precious parasols covered the entire sky.
covering the sky with clouds of parasols of all jewels
me tog thams cad kyi bla re'i sprin gyis nam mkha' bla nas khebs par bya ba dang /
Clouds of canopies of all flowers were spread above.
and canopies of clouds of all kinds of flowers,
na bza' sna tshogs kyi sprin gyis nam mkha' kun nas yog cing brgyan par bya ba dang /
*? Clouds of all kinds of food covered and adorned the sky.
adorning the sky with cloud covers of all kinds of robes,
rin po che sna tshogs kyi dril bu'i dra ba'i sprin gyis nam mkha'i dbyings brgyan par bya ba dang /
Clouds of nets of bells of various jewels adorned the expanse of the sky.
clouds of nets of jewel bells,
spos sna tshogs rgya mtshos dri zhim par byas pa'i spos kyi 'od zer gyi sprin gyi rgyan nam mkha'i dbyings la byin gyis brlab par bya ba dang /
The adornment of clouds of light rays of perfume that had been perfumed by an ocean of various perfumes was present[1477] throughout the expanse of the sky.
clouds of fragrant flames given off by an ocean of all kinds of scents,
rin po che thams cad kyi khri la rin po che'i gdan 'phel bar gting ba'i sprin gyi rgyan nam mkha'i dbyings la byin gyis brlab pa dang /
The adornment of clouds of thrones made of all jewels with seats that were precious cushions was present throughout the expanse of the sky.
clouds of chairs made of all kinds of jewels,
rin po che thams cad kyi rgyal mtshan gyi sprin mngon par bsgreng ba'i rgyan nam mkha'i dbyings la byin gyis brlab pa dang /
The adornment of clouds of upright banners, made of all jewels, was present throughout the expanse of the sky.
magically adorning the sky with clouds raining all kinds of presents.
khang pa dang / gzhal med khang thams cad kyi sprin gyis kun nas yog pa'i rgyan nam mkha'i dbyings la byin gyis brlab pa dang /
The all-covering adornment of clouds of mansions and aerial palaces was present throughout the sky.
me tog sna tshogs kyi sprin gyis kun nas yog pa'i rgyan nam mkha'i dbyings la byin gyis brlab pa dang /
The all-covering adornment of clouds of various flowers was present throughout the sky.
mchod pa'i rgyan thams cad kyi sprin gyi char rab tu 'bab pa'i rgyan nam mkha'i dbyings la byin gyis brlab pa byed cing /
The adornment of rain from clouds of every display of offerings was present throughout the sky.

bcom ldan 'das de bzhin gshegs pa ye shes rin po che'i 'od kun tu 'phro ba'i dpal yon tan dpal gyi rgyal po gang na ba der dong ste phyin nas/ bcom ldan 'das de bzhin gshegs pa ye shes rin po che'i 'od kun tu 'phro ba'i dpal yon tan dpal gyi rgyal bo'i zhabs gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te/ bcom ldan 'das la lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas/

“The king approached the location of the Bhagavat Samantajñānaratnārciśrīguṇaketurāja. Having arrived, he bowed his head to the feet of the Bhagavat Samantajñānaratnārciśrīguṇaketurāja. Then with the Bhagavat to his right, he circumambulated him many hundreds of thousands of times.
Having gone to the buddha and paid his respects,
bcom ldan 'das kyi spyan sngar/ stan nor bu rin po che chen po phyogs kun tu rnam par snang ba'i pad+mo'i snying po can la 'dug go /
He then sat before the Bhagavat upon a seat that had as its center a great lotus of precious jewels that shined light into the ten directions.
the king sat before the buddha in a throne of great jewels flashing light in all directions.

de nas 'khor los bsgyur ba'i bu mo ye shes rin po che'i 'od kun tu 'phro ba'i pad+mo bzang mo mig yid du 'ong ba'i dpal gyi zla bas/ rang gi rgyan rnams lus las bkrol te/ bcom ldan 'das de bzhin gshegs pa ye shes kyi 'od kun tu 'phro ba'i dpal yon tan dpal gyi rgyal po la gtor to/ /mngon par gtor to/ /
“Then the cakravartin’s daughter, Padmabhadrābhirāmanetraśrīcandrā, removed the jewelry from her body and scattered it over the Bhagavat Samantajñānaratnārciśrīguṇaketurāja.
“At that point the daughter of the king took off all her jewelry and scattered it over the buddha;

de nas rgyan de dag/ bcom ldan 'das de'i dbu'i gtsug gi steng gi bar snang la/ nor bu rin po che'i rgyan gyi gdugs chen po nor bu rin po che sna tshogs kyi dra bas yongs su bskor ba/ klu'i dbang po'i lus kyis bzung ba/ rgyan thams cad kyi lus kyi dbyibs shin tu legs par kun nas bskor ba/ rgyan gyi gdugs kyi dkyil 'khor bcus yongs su bskor ba/ shin tu dag pa/ khang pa brtsegs pa'i dbyibs sna tshogs kyis brgyan pa/ rin po che thams cad kyi lhab lhub kyi sprin gyis kun nas yog pa/ nor bu rin po che'i rgyal po thams cad kyi shing gi rgyan gyis kun nas khebs pa/ nor bu rin po che'i rgyal po spos thams cad kyi rgya mtshos yongs su brgyan bar 'dug par gyur te/

“She saw that the jewelry became a great parasol of jewelry made of precious jewels that was situated in the air above the crown of the Bhagavat’s head. Around its border hung a net of various jewels, it was held by a lord of the nāgas, its round form was composed of all the jewelry, and it was surrounded by a circle of ten parasols made of jewelry. There was also a beautiful display of a completely pure variety of kūṭāgāras. There was a covering of clouds of every jewel adornment. There was a covering of an array of trees made of all king jewels. There was the adornment of all the king jewels of an ocean of perfume.

the jewelry formed a parasol over the buddha’s head and stayed there, covered all around with nets of various jewels, held by the chief water spirits, the whole body of jewelry forming a perfect circle surrounded by ten jewel parasols, all completely pure, in the shape of a tower, variously arrayed, covered by clouds of all kinds of jewel ornaments, covered by arrays of diamond trees, adorned with the finest pearls from all the fragrant seas.

de'i dbus na byang chub kyi shing chen po chos kyi dbyings las byung ba'i rin po che thams cad kyi yal ga dang lhun du ldan pa zhes bya ba/ rgyan brjod na mtha' dang dbus med pa/ skad cig re re zhing rgyan sna tshogs yongs su ston pa yod par mthong bar gyur to/ /

In their center there was a great Bodhi tree called Dharmadhātuprabhavasarvaratnamaṇiśākhāpralamba. This was a display with no end or center to its description, a variety of displays that were revealed with each instant.

In the middle of that she saw a great enlightenment tree called ‘draped with foliage of all jewels produced by the cosmos of realities,’ with infinitely various adornments, displaying various auspicious supernal manifestations.

de'i drung na de bzhin gshegs pa rnam par snang mdzad ces bya ba/ byang chub sems dpa' sangs rgyas kyi zhing brjod du med pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kun kyang / byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po'i spyod pa dang / smon lam gyis byung ba/ byang chub sems dpa'i rgyan sna tshogs tha mi dad cing bsam gyis mi khyab pa la rnam par spyod pa sha stag gis bskor cing mdun du byas pa dang /

“She saw at the foot of that tree the tathāgata named Vairocana. “She saw bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in countless buddha realms, who had all arisen through the completely good bodhisattva conduct and prayer and practiced many countless various different bodhisattva displays surrounding him and in front of him.

There she saw a buddha named Vairocana surrounded by as many enlightening beings as atoms in untold buddha-lands, all of whom had undertaken the vows of practice of universally good enlightening beings and dwelt in the inconceivably various total unity of all enlightening beings.
'jig rten gyi dbang po thams cad kyang de la mngon du gyur par mthong ngo/ /
“She also saw all the lords of the world present there.
She also saw the leaders of all worlds in the presence of the buddha.
bcom ldan 'das rnam par snang mdzad de'i sangs rgyas kyi rnam par 'phrul pa mtha' dang dbus med pa yang mthong bar gyur to/ /
“She saw the Bhagavat Vairocana’s buddha miracles that were without end or center.
She saw the infinitely various projections of Vairocana Buddha and perceived the successive ages of his past enlightening practice.

sngon gyi byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa bskal pa gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa la'ang zhugs par gyur to/ / 'jig rten gyi khams de'i 'du ba dang / 'jig pa'i bskal pa la yang zhugs par gyur to/ / 'jig rten gyi khams der 'das pa'i sangs rgyas kyi rgyud gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa la yang zhugs par gyur to/ /

“She comprehended his past bodhisattva conduct through a succession of kalpas. She comprehended that world realm’s kalpas of formation and destruction. She comprehended the succession of past buddhas in that world realm.
She also perceived that world’s ages of formation and disintegration, and the succession of past buddhas in that world.
'jig rten gyi khams de na byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po/ de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi zhabs kyi drung na sangs rgyas mchod pa la brtson par gnas pa yang mthong ngo/ /
“She saw the bodhisattva Samantabhadra diligently making offerings at the feet of all the tathāgatas.
She also saw the universally good enlightening being Samantabhadra in that world, and saw him in the presence of all buddhas, honoring the buddhas
sems can thams cad yongs su smin par bya ba dang / gdul bar bya ba la mngon du gyur par yang mthong ngo/ /
She saw his ripening and guiding of all beings.
and guiding all sentient beings to full development.

byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyang byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po'i lus la gzugs brnyan du gyur par 'khod cing / bdag nyid kyang de'i rjes su 'brang bar mthong ngo/ / de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi zhabs kyi drung dang / byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi drung dang / sems can thams cad kyi gnas dang / 'jig rten gyi khams de dang de dag thams cad na'ang / byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po'i gzugs brnyan kun tu byung ste/

“She saw all bodhisattvas becoming images within the body of the bodhisattva Samantabhadra, and that she herself followed them there. “She saw the image of the bodhisattva Samantabhadra appearing everywhere‍—at the feet of all the tathāgatas, in the dwelling places of all beings, and in every one of the world realms.

She also saw all the enlightening beings reflected in the body of Universal Good, and saw herself there too in the presence of all the buddhas, in the presence of all the enlightening beings reflected in the body of Universal Good, in the abodes of all sentient beings.

'jig rten gyi khams de dag re re na'ang / sangs rgyas kyi zhing rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi 'jig rten gyi khams mtshams kyi rgyan dang bcas pa dang / gzhi dang bcas pa dang / dbyibs dang bcas pa dang / lhun dang bcas pa dang / rgyan sna tshogs yongs su dag pa dang bcas pa/ rgyan sna tshogs kyi sprin gyis kun nas khebs pa rnam par bkod pa dang / ming dang grangs rnam pa sna tshogs dang ldan pa dang / de bzhin gshegs pa'i rgyud sna tshogs las brjod pa/ dus gsum gyi tshul sna tshogs su gtogs pa/ phyogs 'byams klas pa sna tshogs su 'du ba/ chos kyi dbyings 'byams klas pa sna tshogs kyi khongs su gtogs pa/ chos kyi dbyings kyi gzhi sna tshogs su 'dus pa/ nam mkha'i dbyings sna tshogs la rnam par gnas pa; snying po byang chub sna tshogs kyis brgyan pa/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i rnam par 'phrul pa sna tshogs kyis byung ba/ sangs rgyas kyi seng+ge'i gdan sna tshogs kyis brgyan pa/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor rgya mtsho sna tshogs dang ldan pa/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor gyi rgyud sna tshogs can/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i thabs mkhas pa sna tshogs yongs su brjod pa/ dang ldan pa/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i chos kyi 'khor lo 'khor ba'i tshul sna tshogs can/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i dbyangs kyi yan lag dang gsung gi nga ro sna tshogs rab tu 'byung ba/ skad sna tshogs rgya mtsho shin tu bstan pa dang ldan pa/ mdo sde'i sprin sna tshogs rjes su sgrog pa can dag kyang mthong bar gyur to/ /

“She saw that in each of those world realms there were as many worlds as there are atoms in a buddha realm, with the extent of their arrays and with their foundations, their shapes, their forms, their various pure arrays, their being covered by clouds of various displays, their various names and numbers, the descriptions of their various buddha lineages and their various appearances within the three times, their pervasion throughout the extent of the directions, their various presences throughout the extent of the realm of phenomena, their appearance within the various areas of the realm of phenomena, their various locations within areas in space, their displays of various bodhimaṇḍas,[1478] the arising of the various miracles of the tathāgatas, the display of the various lion thrones of the buddhas, the various oceans of the assemblies of followers of the tathāgatas, the various activities of the followers of the tathāgatas, the revelation of the skillful methods of the tathāgatas, the various ways of the turning of the Dharma wheels of the tathāgatas, the arising of the various aspects of speech and the sound of the voices of the tathāgatas, the teaching through an ocean of various languages, and the roar of clouds of various sūtras.
