In each of those worlds she also saw as many worlds as atoms in a buddha-land, with their boundaries, bases, forms, masses, and various purities of adornment, covered by clouds of various supernal manifestations, with various names and numbers of ages, various lineages of buddhas appearing, various temporal locations, various spatial locations, belonging to various phenomenal realms within various planes of the cosmos, situated in various planes of space, with various arrays of enlightenment sites, various lights projected by buddhas, various buddhas’ lion thrones, various oceanic audiences of buddhas, various circulations of the audiences of buddhas, various clarifications by the skill in means of buddhas, various buddhas’ ways of turning the wheel of teaching, various sayings of buddhas, various indications of oceans of ways of expressing thought, and enunciations of multitudes of various scriptures.

mthong nas de bas kyang dga' ba dang mos pa'i shugs chen po thob par gyur te/ de de ltar dga' ba'i shugs chen po skyes par gyur pa la/ bcom ldan 'das ye shes rin po che'i 'od kun tu 'phro ba'i dpal yon tan dpal gyi rgyal po de bzhin gshegs pa des/ de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi chos kyi 'khor lo rab tu bsgrags pa zhes bya ba'i mdo sde/ 'khor gyi mdo sde sangs rgyas kyi zhing bcu'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed dang bcas pa yang dag par bstan te/ des mdo sde de thos par gyur nas/

“When she saw that, she attained a powerful happiness and delight.[1479] After she had given rise to powerful happiness, that tathāgata, the Bhagavat Samantajñānaratnārciśrīguṇaketurāja, taught the sūtra called The Resounding of the Dharma Wheels of All the Tathāgatas and as many accompanying sūtras as there are atoms in ten buddha realms.

“Seeing all these, she was all the more enraptured. The buddha expounded to her in her rapture a scripture called Voice of the Cycles of Teaching of All Buddhas, along with as many accompanying scriptures as atoms in ten buddha-lands.
ting nge 'dzin gyi sgo stong phrag bcu shin tu phra zhing reg na bde ba thob par gyur te/ de ni/ dper na/ ma'i mngal du rnam par shes pa zhugs par gyur ma thag pa lta bu dang /
When she heard that sūtra, she attained the bliss of reaching ten thousand subtle gateways to samādhi. This was like the day[1480] a consciousness enters the mother’s womb, to give an analogy.
When she had heard these scriptures, ten hundred thousand kinds of concentration entered into her, subtle and pleasant, like the consciousness of an embryo on the first day in the mother’s womb,
'di lta ste/ dper na/ sems can rnams kyi las mngon par bsgrubs pa lta bu dang /
This was like the completed karma of beings.
like the commencement of activity in beings,
'di lta ste/ dper na/ zhing bzang po dam pa'i sa bon btab nas ring po ma lon yang myu gu skye ba'i rgyur gyur pa lta bu ste/
This was like a day[1481] in which a seed or seedling that is the cause of an excellent sal[1482] tree[1483] is planted.[1484]
like the impulse of the sprout in the seed of a tree on the day it is planted—
de bzhin du ting nge 'dzin de dag kyang 'jam zhing yid du 'ong ba ste/
“She attained these gentle and pleasant samādhis:
this is how subtle and full of potential those concentrations were. Ten hundred thousand concentrations descended into her, beginning with
'di ltar de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad mngon du rnam par dmigs pa zhes bya ba'i ting nge 'dzin dang /
the samādhi called directly perceiving all tathāgatas,
such concentrations as one called ‘face-to-face communication with all buddhas,’
zhing 'byams klas pa thams cad du snang ba rjes su song ba zhes bya ba'i ting nge 'dzin dang /
the samādhi called the radiance that goes through the entire extent of all the realms,
one called ‘illumination of all lands,’
dus gsum gyi tshul thams cad la 'jug pa khong du chud pa zhes bya ba'i ting nge 'dzin dang /
the samādhi called entry into comprehending all the ways of the three times,
one called ‘penetrating the principles of all pasts, presents, and futures,’
de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi chos kyi 'khor lo sgrog pa zhes bya ba'i ting nge 'dzin dang /
the samādhi called the resounding of the Dharma wheels of all the tathāgatas,
one called ‘voice of the teaching activity of all buddhas,’
sangs rgyas thams cad kyi smon lam rgya mtsho rnam par dmigs pa zhes bya ba'i ting nge 'dzin dang /
the samādhi called perceiving the ocean of prayers by all the buddhas,
one called ‘communicating the ocean of vows of all buddhas,’
'khor ba thams cad kyi sdug bsngal gyis gzir ba'i sems can 'byung ba'i nga ro rab tu bsgrags pas rnam par dmigs par byed pa zhes bya ba'i ting nge 'dzin dang /
the samādhi called the perception of the resounding of the roaring that saves beings afflicted by the suffering of saṃsāra,
one called ‘communicating the voice of all means of emancipation from all suffering and torture of the mundane whirl,’
sems can thams cad kyi mun nag rnam par sel ba'i smon lam gyi rgyan ces bya ba'i ting nge 'dzin dang /
the samādhi called the array of prayers to dispel the darkness of all beings,
one called ‘manifestation of the vow to dispel the darkness of all sentient beings,’
sems can thams cad sdug bsngal dang dbral ba'i smon lam gyis rnam par dmigs pa zhes bya ba'i ting nge 'dzin dang /
the samādhi called the perception of the prayers for all beings to be free from suffering,
one called ‘determination to release all sentient beings from suffering’,
sems can thams cad kyi bde ba 'grub pa yongs su 'byin pa zhes bya ba'i ting nge 'dzin dang /
the samādhi called the origin of the attainment of happiness by all beings,
one called ‘source of achievement of happiness for all sentient beings,’
sems can thams cad yongs su smin par bya ba dang / gdul bas mi skyo ba'i snying po zhes bya ba'i ting nge 'dzin dang /
the samādhi called the essence of never wearying in ripening and guiding all beings,
one called ‘source of tireless developmental guidance for all sentient beings,’
byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi lam la 'jug pa'i rgyal mtshan zhes bya ba'i ting nge 'dzin dang /
the samādhi called the banner of entering the path of all bodhisattvas,
one called ‘characterized by entry into the path of all enlightening beings,’
byang chub sems dpa'i sa thams cad yongs su gnon par sgrub pa'i rgyan ces bya ba'i ting nge 'dzin dang /
the samādhi of the display of reaching all the bhūmis of the bodhisattvas,
and one called ‘supernal manifestation produced by entry into the stages of all enlightening beings.’
de dag la sogs pa ting nge 'dzin gyi sgo stong phrag bcu rnams des thob par gyur to/ /
and the other ten thousand gateways to samādhi.
[…see above]

de phra ba la mnyam par bzhag pa'i sems dang / mi g.yo ba'i sems dang / rab tu dga' ba'i sems dang / dbugs phyin pa'i sems dang / dpag tu med pa'i sems dang / dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi rjes su 'brang ba'i sems dang /

“She had a mind that rested in subtle equanimity, a mind that was unwavering, a mind that was filled with joy, a mind that was relieved, a mind that was immeasurable, a mind that followed the kalyāṇamitras,
“With her mind subtly concentrated, unwavering, joyful, refreshed, unpreoccupied, in harmony with the wise,

thams cad mkhyen pa nyid shin tu zab pa la dmigs pa'i sems dang / byams pa'i rjes su 'gro ba'i tshul rgya mtsho la zhugs pa'i sems dang / mngon par zhen pa thams cad las gyen du 'phags pa'i sems dang / 'jig rten gyi yul thams cad la mi gnas pa'i sems dang / de bzhin gshegs pa'i yul la 'jug pa'i sems dang / sangs rgyas thams cad kyi gzugs dang / kha dog rgya mtshos snang bar gyur pa'i sems dang /

a mind that was focused on profound omniscience, a mind that had entered an ocean of the ways of kindness, a mind that had risen above all attachments, a mind that did not dwell within the scope of the world, a mind that had entered the scope of the tathāgatas, a mind that was illuminated by the forms and colors of all the buddhas,

focused on profound omniscience, swelling with oceanic love, free from all attachments, not dwelling on any worldly objects, entering the sphere of those who arrive at Thusness, aware of the appearances of all buddhas,

'khrug pa med pa'i sems dang / g.yo ba med pa'i sems dang / khong khro ba med pa'i sems dang / mthon dman med pa'i sems dang / mi skyo ba'i sems dang / mi zlog pa'i sems dang / zhum pa med pa'i sems dang / chos thams cad kyi rang bzhin nges par rtogs pa'i sems dang / chos thams cad kyi tshul rgya mtsho'i rjes su song ba'i sems dang / chos thams cad rab tu 'byed pa'i tshul gyi rjes su song ba'i sems dang /

a mind that was undisturbed, a mind that was immovable,[1485] a mind that was without anger,[1486] a mind that was without instability,[1487] a mind that was without weariness, a mind that was without regression, a mind that was without dejection,[1488] a mind that understood the nature of all phenomena, a mind that had the understanding of the analysis of all phenomena,

unperturbed, unagitated, unobstructed, unfragmented, neither excited nor depressed, tireless, unretreating, undiscouraged, meditating on the inherent nature of all things, realizing the ocean of principles based on the inherent nature of all things, following the principles of investigation of all things,

sems can rgya mtsho thams cad la 'jug pa'i sems dang / 'gro ba thams cad yongs su bskyab pa'i sems dang / sangs rgyas rgya mtsho mang po'i snang ba yongs su skyes pa'i sems dang / de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi smon lam rgya mtsho la 'jug pa'i sems dang / sgrib pa thams cad kyi ri rnam par 'thor ba'i sems dang / bsod nams kyi tshogs rgya chen po yang dag par sgrub pa'i sems dang / de bzhin gshegs pa'i stobs bcu la spobs pa mngon sum du gyur pa'i sems dang /

a mind that comprehended the ocean of all beings, a mind that wished to save all beings, a mind that gave rise to the illumination of the ocean of multitudes of buddhas, a mind that comprehended the ocean of prayers of all the tathāgatas, a mind that shattered the mountain of all obscurations, a mind that accomplished a vast accumulation of merit, a mind that was directed toward attaining[1489] the ten strengths of the tathāgatas,

plunging into the ocean of all sentient beings, determined to save all worldlings, illumined by the vast ocean of buddhas, plunging into the ocean of vows of all buddhas, breaking through all obstructions to enlightenment, gathering great stores of virtue, on the verge of attainment of the ten powers of buddhas,
byang chub sems dpa'i yul thams cad la snang ba thob pa'i sems dang /
a mind that had attained the illumination of the range of all bodhisattvas,
aware of the realms of all enlightening beings,
byang chub sems dpa'i tshogs thams cad 'phel bar byed pa'i sems dang /
a mind that increased the accumulations of all bodhisattvas,
amassing the provisions of all enlightening beings for the path of enlightenment,
phyogs rgya mtsho thams cad rgyas par 'gengs pa'i sems dang ldan pas/
and a mind that pervaded throughout all directions.
her mind reaching everywhere to take up the great vow of universal good,

kun tu bzang po'i smon lam chen po la lhag par dmigs par bya bas/ smon lam rgya mtsho sangs rgyas kyi zhing bcu'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyis/ de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi sngon gyi smon lam rang gi sangs rgyas kyi zhing yongs su dag par bya ba'i don du mngon par bsgrub ste/

“With an ocean of prayers as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha realms, she made the past prayers of all tathāgatas, so that she could acquire[1490] completely good great prayers and purify her own buddha realm.
by as many oceans of vows as atoms in ten buddha-lands she undertook the past vow of all buddhas for the purification of their own buddha-lands.
'di ltar sems can gyi khams thams cad yongs su smin par bya ba dang / gdul bar bya ba dang /
“They included prayers to ripen and guide all realms of beings,
That is, by guiding all sentient beings to perfection,
chos kyi dbyings 'byams klas pa yongs su shes par bya ba dang /
to know the entire extent of the realm of phenomena,
to know all ways to the realm of reality,
chos kyi dbyings kyi tshul rgya mtsho la 'jug par bya ba dang /
to comprehend the ocean of the ways of the realm of phenomena,
to enter the ocean of all ways to the realm of reality,
sangs rgyas kyi zhing thams cad du phyi ma'i bskal par byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa spyad par bya ba dang /
to practice bodhisattva conduct in all buddha realms throughout future kalpas,
to enter enlightening practice in all buddha-lands forever,
byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa'i dkyil 'khor thams cad la phyi ma'i mtha'i bskal par gnas par bya ba dang /
to remain in the domain of bodhisattva conduct throughout all future kalpas,
to live in the sphere of the practices of all enlightening beings forever,
de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi drung du 'gro bar bya ba dang /
to go into the presence of all tathāgatas,
to visit all buddhas,
dge ba'i bshes gnyen thams cad bsnyen bkur ba dang /
to please all kalyāṇamitras,
to associate with all spiritual benefactors,
de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad la mchod cing rim gror bya ba yongs su rdzogs par bya ba dang /
to perfectly make offerings to and be an attendant for all tathāgatas,
to fully honor and serve all buddhas,
sems kyi skad cig re re la thams cad mkhyen pa'i ye shes rnam par bsgrub pa dang / rnam par 'tshang rgya bar bya bas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa rgyun mi gcod par bya ba'i phyir/
to attain omniscient wisdom in every instant, and to have continuous bodhisattva conduct in order to attain buddhahood.
to continue with each moment of consciousness the practice of enlightening beings which increasingly becomes aware of omniscient knowledge.

de dag la sogs pa smon lam mngon par bsgrub pa'i sgo rgya mtsho sangs rgyas kyi zhing bcu'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyis/ byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po'i spyod pa la smon lam mngon par sgrub par gyur to/ /
“Through accomplishing an ocean of gateways to prayers, as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha realms, she was making the prayer for completely good bodhisattva conduct.
She undertook the vow of universally good enlightening practice by means of as many oceans of ways of undertaking vows as atoms in ten buddha-lands, beginning with such vows as these.

de'i byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po'i spyod pa dang / smon lam mngon par bsgrub pa'i phyir/ bcom ldan 'das de bzhin gshegs pa ye shes rin po che'i 'od kun tu 'phro ba'i dpal yon tan dpal gyi rgyal pos/ sngon gyi dge ba'i rtsa ba yongs su bskul ba mdzad do/ /

“In order for her to accomplish the completely good bodhisattva conduct and prayer, the Bhagavat Samantajñānaratnārciśrīguṇaketurāja encouraged her and inspired her with past roots of virtue that he taught,
“Then the buddha Paragon of Virtue Radiant with the Light of Universal Knowledge made her aware of his past roots of goodness and inspired her to achieve them—
rab tu bstan pa mdzad do/ / yongs su bstan pa mdzad do/ /
revealed, explained,
he made them clear to her, revealed them,
rnam par dbye ba mdzad do/ / rnam par dgrol bar mdzad do/ /
analyzed them, described them,
yang dag par bstan par mdzad do/ /
displayed,
and explained them;
chud za bar mi 'gyur bar bya ba'i phyir rab tu brtan par mdzad do/ /
made stable so they would not be lost,
he strengthened them to endure without perishing,
rgya chen por khyab par bya ba'i phyir shin tu yangs par mdzad do/ /
increased so that they would spread greatly,
extended them to great range,
thams cad mkhyen pa nyid lhur len par bya ba'i phyir rab tu gnas par mdzad do/ /
and caused to remain so that there would be dedication to omniscience.
and firmly established them so as to make them equal to the measure of omniscience,
de ni 'di lta ste/ thog ma sems bskyed pa nas nye bar bzung ba phyin chad/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i sngon gyi smon lam rgya mtsho grangs med pa rab tu thob par bya ba'i phyir ro/ /
“This concerned the first development of her aspiration to enlightenment and her acquiring an ocean of the countless prayers of past tathāgatas.

rigs kyi bu/ sngon 'das pa'i dus/ de'i yang pha rol gyi bskal pa bcu pa la/ 'jig rten gyi khams rin chen nyi ma'i 'khor lo rnam par snang ba'i 'od ces bya bar/ de bzhin gshegs pa zla ba'i rgyal mtshan dpal gyi gsung rab la/ bu mo ye shes kyi 'od kun tu 'phro ba pad+mo bzang mo mig yid du 'ong ba'i dpal gyi zla ba des/ byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang pos yongs su bskul te/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i sku gzugs pad+mo la bzhugs pa zhig bcos so/ /

“Noble one, in a past time, ten kalpas before that, the daughter Samantajñānārcipadmabhadrābhirāmanetraśrīcandrā was following the teaching of the Tathāgata Candradhvajaśrīketu in a world realm called Maṇisūryacandravidyotitaprabhā. The bodhisattva Samantabhadra instigated her to repair a broken statue of the Tathāgata seated upon a lotus.

“Ten eons before that, in the world Light Shining from a Jewel Sun and Moon, in which the teaching of the buddha Moonlike Brilliance was preserved, that same woman, instructed by the enlightening being Universally Good, repaired a ruined image of the Buddha seated on a lotus,

bcos nas kyang ri mo bris so/ / ri mo bris nas kyang rin po ches shin tu brgyan to/ / dge ba'i bshes gnyen byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po la brten te/ bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu'ang sems bskyed do/ /

When she had repaired it, she painted it. When she had painted it, she adorned it with jewels. Through following the bodhisattva Samantabhadra she developed the aspiration for the highest, complete enlightenment.
painted it, and adorned it, having gone to Universally Good with the aspiration for enlightenment.

de dge ba'i rtsa ba des log par mi ltung ba'i chos can du gyur te/ rtag tu lha'i dbang po'i rigs dang / mi'i dbang po'i rigs su skyes par gyur to/ / thams cad du yang gzugs mdzes shing sdug la blta na yid du 'ong ba dang / kha dog bzang po shin tu rgyas pa dam pa dang ldan par gyur te/ rtag tu de bzhin gshegs pa mthong ba dang / byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po dang yang bral bar ma gyur to/ / dge ba'i bshes gnyen de nyid kyis tshe rabs de dang / de dag tu yongs su smin par byas so/ / dran par byas so/ / nga yang des byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po yongs su bsnyen bkur te/ yid byung bar ma byas so; ;

“As a result of that root of merit, she became a Dharma follower free of downfalls. She was always born into a family of lords of devas or a family of lords of humans. In all her lives she had a body that was attractive and lovely to look at and had an excellent, beautiful color. She always saw tathāgatas and was never separated from the bodhisattva Samantabhadra. That bodhisattva ripened her in every lifetime and made her remember. She always honored the bodhisattva Samantabhadra and was always devoted to him.

Because of that root of goodness, she never fell into misfortune and always was born in celestial or human families and was always beautiful. She always saw buddhas and associated with the enlightening being Universally Good, and in every life was developed, inspired, and caused to be mindful by that spiritual benefactor. At this time, furthermore, Universally Good was thoroughly pleased with her.

rigs kyi bu/ de la ji snyam du sems/ de'i tshe de'i du sa na 'khor los bsgyur ba'i rgyal po rnam par snang ba rin chen pad+mo dpal gyi gtsug phud snying po zhes bya ba byung ba de gzhan zhig yin pa snyam du sems na ni/ rigs kyi bu khyod kyis de ltar mi blta ste/ byang chub sems dpa' byams pa ni/ de'i tshe de'i dus na/ 'khor los bsgyur ba'i rgyal po rnam par snang ba rin chen pad+mo dpal gyi gtsug phud snying po zhes bya bar gyur to/ /

“Noble one, who do you think was the cakravartin king Vairocanaratnapadmagarbhaśrīcūḍa at that time, in that time? Do not think that it was anyone else. It was the bodhisattva Maitreya who was Vairocanaratnapadmagarbhaśrīcūḍa at that time, in that time.
“Who do you think the king of that time was? It was none other than the enlightening being Manjushri, the Glorious One, who was the king.

rigs kyi bu/ de'i tshe de'i dus na/ rgyal po'i btsun mo dpal gyi gzhir yongs su rgyas pa zhes bya ba byung ba de/ gzhan zhig yin pa snyam du sems na yang de ltar mi blta ste/ mtshan mo'i lha mo kho mo'i drung na 'dug pa sgra rgya mtsho rab tu zhi ba dang ldan pa 'di yin no/ /

“Noble one, who do you think was the king’s queen, Saṃpūrṇaśrīvakrā, at that time, in that time? Do not think that it was anyone else. It was this night goddess, Praśantarutasāgaravatī, who is before me.
And do not suppose that it was anyone else but the night goddess Prashantarutasagaravati, who is seated here near me, who was the queen.

rigs kyi bu/ de la ji snyam du sems/ de'i tshe de'i dus na/ rgyal po'i bu mo ye shes kyi 'od kun tu 'phro ba pad+mo bzang mo mig yid du 'ong ba'i dpal gyi zla ba zhes bya ba byung ba de/ gzhan zhig yin pa snyam du sems na ni de ltar mi blta ste/ kho mo ni de'i tshe de'i dus na/ rgyal po'i bu mo ye shes kyi 'od kun tu 'phro ba pad+mo bzang mo mig yid du 'ong ba'i dpal gyi zla ba zhes bya bar gyur to/ / kho mo bu mo gzhon nur gyur te/ de bzhin gshegs pa dbang po'i rgyal mtshan dpal gyi gsung rab la/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i sku pad+mo la bzhugs pa bcos pa de ni/ kho mo'i bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub kyi rgyur gyur to/ / de'i tshe byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang pos kho mo bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu yongs su bskul ba de ni kho mos byang chub tu sems dang po bskyed pa yin no/ /

“Noble one, who do you think was the king’s daughter, Samantajñānārcipadmabhadrābhirāmanetraśrīcandrā, at that time, in that time? Do not think that it was anyone else. I was at that time, in that time, the king’s daughter, Samantajñānārcipadmabhadrābhirāmanetraśrīcandrā. When I was a young girl in the time of the teaching of the Tathāgata Candradhvajaśrīketu and repaired the statue of the Tathāgata seated upon a lotus, that was the cause for my highest, complete enlightenment. At that time, the bodhisattva Samantabhadra inspired me toward the highest, complete enlightenment, and that was my first development of that aspiration.

And do not think it was anyone but I who was the daughter of the king and queen, who in the time of the teaching left by the buddha Moonlike Brilliance repaired a ruined image of the Buddha on a lotus. That became a determining factor for me all the way to supreme enlightenment. And when I was directed by the enlightening being Universally Good toward supreme perfect enlightenment, I first aroused the determination for enlightenment.

kho mos bcom ldan 'das de bzhin gshegs pa ye shes rin po che'i 'od kun tu 'phro ba'i dpal gyi yon tan dpal gyi rgyal po'i drung du phyin te/ rgyan gyis gtor nas/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i rnam par 'phrul pa dang / cho 'phrul mthong bar gyur te/ kho mos bcom ldan 'das de'i drung nas chos thos par gyur pa de'i tshe/ kho mos byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa 'jig rten thams cad mngon du gyur pas 'gro ba rnam par 'dul ba ston pa 'di thob bo/ /

“I went into the presence of the Bhagavat Samantajñānaratnārciśrīguṇaketurāja and scattered my jewelry over him and then saw the Tathāgata’s miraculous manifestations. Then when I heard the Dharma from that bhagavat, I attained this bodhisattva liberation called the manifestations that guide beings that appear in all worlds.

Then, when I went to the buddha Paragon of Virtue Radiant with the Light of Universal Knowledge and cast my jewelry over him, saw the buddha’s miraculous power, and heard the Teaching from him, I attained this enlightening liberation showing guidance to all sentient beings.

de bzhin gshegs pa ri rab kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed de dag thams cad kyang bsnyen bkur te/ yo byad dang mchod cing rim gror bya ba thams cad kyis kyang bkur stir byas so/ / de bzhin gshegs pa de dag gi chos bstan pa de dag thams cad kyang kho mos thos te/ de bzhin gshegs pa de dag gi gdams ngag dang / rjes su bstan pa la'ang zhugs par gyur to/ / de bzhin gshegs pa de dag la kho mos rim gro cher byas te/ rim gro de'i rnam pas sems kyi skad cig gcig la de bzhin gshegs pa de dag thams cad dang / byang chub sems dpa'i 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor de dag dang / sangs rgyas kyi zhing de dag thams cad kyang mthong ste/

“I have honored tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms in Sumeru. I have honored them by all the activities of offering them necessary articles and attending upon them. I have heard all the Dharma that those tathāgatas have taught, and I have followed the instructions and teachings of those tathāgatas. I have greatly venerated those tathāgatas so that through that veneration I have seen in an instant of mind all tathāgatas, their assemblies of bodhisattvas, and all their buddha realms.

And I propitiated all those buddhas, numerous as atoms in the polar mountain, and honored them with all kinds of offerings. And I listened to all their teachings, and put their instructions into practice; and I gained such intense respect for those buddhas that in a single moment of thought I would see all those buddhas, their circles of enlightening beings, and their buddha-lands.

'jig rten gyi khams rnam par snang ba'i khams de ni 'das par gyur/ bskal pa rdul dang bral ba'i dkyil 'khor de ni mthar phyin par gyur nas/ de'i rjes la 'jig rten gyi khams ni/ rin chen 'khor lo sna tshogs kyis klubs shing brgyan pa zhes bya/ bskal pa ni 'od chen po zhes bya ba zhig byung ste/ de la sangs rgyas lnga brgya byung bar gyur to/ / de dag thams cad kyang kho mos bsnyen bkur te/ bskal pa 'od chen po la de bzhin gshegs pa thugs rje chen po sprin gyi rgyal mtshan zhes bya ba bskal pa'i dang po la byung ste/ de mngon par 'byung ba'i tshe/ kho mo mtshan mo'i lha mor gyur pas mchod pa byas so/ /

“The world realm Vairocanatejaḥśrī[1491] passed away, and the kalpa called Virajomaṇḍala came to an end. They were followed by the world realm called Maṇicakravicitrapratimaṇḍitavyūhā and the kalpa called Mahāprabha, in which appeared five hundred buddhas, and I honored all of them. The very first of them in the Mahāprabha kalpa was the tathāgata whose name was Mahākaruṇameghadhvaja. When he set forth into homelessness, I was a night goddess who made offerings to him.

“When that world Radiant Brilliance had passed away and the age Sphere of Dispassion was over, there followed a world called Magnificent Array Brilliantly Adorned with Jewel Discs, and an age called Great Light; five hundred buddhas emerged therein, and I propitiated them all. The first buddha in that age was named Representative of Great Compassion; when he was leaving home, I, who had become a night goddess, made offerings to him.

de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa rdo rje mthu bo che'i dpal zhes bya ba byung ste/ de la kho mos 'khor lo bsgyur bar gyur pas mchod pa byas so/ / de bzhin gshegs pa des kho mo la mdo sde sangs rgyas thams cad skye zhing 'byung ba zhes bya ba/ mdo sde sangs rgyas kyi zhing bcu'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi 'khor dang bcas pa yang dag par bstan te/ de yang kho mos thos nas yongs su bzung ngo/ /

“After that, there was the tathāgata whose name was Vajranārāyaṇaketu. I was a cakravartin who made offerings to him. That tathāgata taught me the sūtra called The Birth and Arising of All Buddhas, together with accompanying sūtras as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha realms. I heard it and retained it.

After him, a buddha named Adamantine Paragon of Man arose; I, at that time a ruler, made offerings to him, and he expounded to me a scripture called Source of All Buddhas, accompanied by as many scriptures as atoms in ten buddha-lands, which I listened to and took up.

de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa me'i 'od 'phro ri'i dpal gyis rnam par brgyan pa zhes bya ba byung ste/ de la kho mo tshong dpon gyi bu mor gyur pas mchod pa byas so/ / de bzhin gshegs pa des kho mo la mdo sde/ dus gsum snang ba'i snying po zhes bya ba/ mdo sde dzam+bu'i gling gi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi 'khor dang bcas pa yang dag par bstan te/ de yang kho mos thos nas yongs su bzung ngo/ /

“After that, there was the tathāgata whose name was Jvalanārciḥparvataśrīvyūha. I was a head merchant’s daughter and made offerings to him. That tathāgata taught me the sūtra called The Essence of the Light of the Three Times, together with accompanying sūtras as numerous as the atoms in Jambudvīpa. I heard it and retained it.

After that a buddha named Magnificent Array of Lights of a Mountain of Blazing Fire appeared; at that time the daughter of a grandee, I made offerings to him, and he expounded to me a scripture called Containing the Manifestations of Past, Present, and Future, accompanied by as many scriptures as atoms in the continent, which I listened to and took up.
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa chos rgya mtsho thams cad kyis mngon par 'phags pa'i shugs kyi rgyal po zhes bya ba byung ste/ de la kho mo lha'i rgyal por gyur bas mchod pa byas so/ /
“After that, there was the tathāgata whose name was Sarvadharmasamudrābhyudgatavegarāja. I was a king of devas and made offerings to him.
After that a buddha named King of Energy Risen Above the Ocean of All Phenomena appeared in the world; at that time a titan chieftain, I made offerings to him,

de bzhin gshegs pa des kho mo la mdo sde chos kyi dbyings kyi gzhi thams cad shes pa'i bye brag ces bya ba mdo sde lnga brgya'i 'khor dang bcas pa yang dag par bstan te/ de'ang kho mos thos nas yongs su bzung ngo/ /
That tathāgata taught me the sūtra called The Categories of the Knowledge of All the Bases of the Realm of Phenomena, together with five hundred accompanying sūtras. I heard it and retained it.
and he expounded to me a scripture called Analysis of Knowledge of the Planes of All Reality Realms, accompanied by five hundred scriptures, which I listened to and took up.

de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa chos zab mo'i dpal rgya mtshos yang dag par 'byung ba'i 'od ces bya ba byung ste/ de la kho mo klu'i dbang po'i bu mor gyur pas/ nor bu rin po che yid bzhin gyi rgyal po'i sprin gyi char mngon par phab ste/ mchod pa byas so/ /

“After that, there was the tathāgata whose name was Gambhīradharmaśrīsamudraprabha. I was the daughter of a lord of the nāgas and made an offering to him of the rain from a cloud of kings of precious wish-fulfilling jewels.
After that a buddha named Light of the Ocean of Splendor of the Profound Doctrine appeared; at that time the daughter of a chief water spirit, I honored him with a shower of wish-fulfilling jewels,

de bzhin gshegs pa des kho mo la mdo sde dga' ba rgya mtsho rnam par 'phel ba shugs zhes bya ba/ mdo sde bye ba brgya stong phrag bcu'i 'khor dang bcas pa yang dag par bstan te/ de'ang kho mos thos nas yongs su bzung ngo/ /
That tathāgata taught me the sūtra called The Power of an Increasing Ocean of Delight, together with a million accompanying sūtras. I heard it and retained it.
and he expounded to me a scripture called Light of Reason in the Ocean of Reality Realms, accompanied by as many scriptures as atoms in ten buddha-lands, which I listened to, took up, and memorized.

de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa rin chen ri bo'i spo'i 'od zer sgron ma zhes bya ba byung ste/ de la kho mo rgya mtsho'i lha mor gyur pas/ rin po che'i pad+mo'i sprin gyi char gyis nye bar bsnyen te mchod pa byas so/ /
“After that, there was the tathāgata whose name was Ratnaśikharārciḥparvatapradīpa. I was an ocean goddess who approached him and made an offering of the rain from a cloud of precious lotuses.

de bzhin gshegs pa des kho mo la mdo sde chos kyi dbyings rgya mtsho'i tshul zhes bya ba mdo sde sangs rgyas kyi zhing rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi 'khor dang bcas pa yang dag par bstan te/ de'ang kho mos thos nas yongs su blangs so/ /dran pas yang dag par bzung ngo/ /

That tathāgata taught me the sūtra called Ways of the Ocean of Phenomena, together with accompanying sūtras as numerous as the atoms in a buddha realm. I heard it and retained it, memorized it, and kept it.

de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa yon tan rgya mtsho snang ba'i dkyil 'khor gyi dpal zhes bya ba byung ste/ de la kho mo drang srong mngon par shes pa lnga dang ldan par gyur pa/ drang srong stong phrag drug cus kun nas bskor bas/ rdzu 'phrul chen po'i rnam par 'phrul pas nye bar bsnyen te/ spos kyi me tog ri bo tsam gyi sprin gyi char mngon par phab nas mchod pa byas so/ /

“After that, there was the tathāgata whose name was Guṇasamudrāvabhāsamaṇḍalaśrī. I was a ṛṣi with the five higher cognitions who was encircled by sixty thousand ṛṣis and manifested great miracles. I approached him and made an offering of the rain from a mountain-sized cloud of perfumed lotuses.

After that a buddha named Splendor of the Multitude of Manifestations of the Ocean of Virtue appeared; at that time a seer with five kinds of occult knowledge, I went to him by magical power with a company of six thousand seers and honored him with incense and flowers.
de bzhin gshegs pa kho mo la mdo sde chos gnas med pa'i sgron ma zhes bya ba mdo sde stong phrag drug cu'i 'khor dang bcas pa yang dag par bstan te/ de'ang kho mos thos nas yongs su bzung ngo/ /
That tathāgata taught me the sūtra called The Lamp of Phenomena Being without Location, together with ten thousand accompanying sūtras. I heard it and retained it.
He expounded to me a scripture called Lamp of Independence, accompanied by six thousand scriptures, which I listened to and took up.

de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa rnam par snang mdzad dpal gyi snying po zhes bya ba byung ste/ kho mo yang mnyam pa nyid kyi don 'byung ba zhes bya ba'i sa'i lha mo zhig tu gyur nas kho mo sa'i lha mo'i 'khor grangs med pa dang bcas pas/ rin po che'i shing thams cad kyi lhun las/ rin po che'i me tog gi sprin gyi char mngon par phab ste/ rin po che'i phreng ba'i sprin gyi char yang rab tu phab nas/ de bzhin gshegs pa de la mchod pa bya ba'i phyir spyan sngar phyin to/ /

“After that, there was the tathāgata whose name was Vairocanaśrīgarbha. I was an earth goddess named Samatārthasaṃbhavā. Together with a countless retinue of earth goddesses, I approached him to make an offering of the rain falling from a cloud of precious flowers and a cloud of strings of jewels that had arisen from the trunks of trees made of all jewels.

After that a buddha named Imbued with Sunny Radiance appeared. At that time I was an earth goddess named Source of Common Weal; accompanied by countless earth goddesses, I went to that buddha showering jewel flowers and garlands from trees of all jewels as tokens of honor.

de bzhin gshegs pa des/ kho mo la mdo sde de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad yang dag par 'byung ba'i gnas kyi snying po zhes bya ba/ mdo sde grangs med pa'i 'khor dang bcas pa yang dag par bstan te/ de'ang kho mos thos nas bzung ste/ chud zos par ma byas so/ /

That tathāgata taught me the sūtra called The Essence of the Source of the Wisdom[1492] That Is the Origin of All the Tathāgatas, together with countless accompanying sūtras. I heard it, retained it, and did not lose it.
He expounded a scripture called Womb of Knowledge from Which All Buddhas Are Born, along with countless scriptures, which I listened to and remembered permanently.

rigs kyi bu/ de bzhin gshegs pa lnga brgya po de dag thams cad kyi tha mar/ de bzhin gshegs pa chos kyi dbyings nam mkha' mdzod spus yongs su rgyas pa'i rtse mo dpal gyi sgron ma zhes bya ba 'jig rten du byung ste/ de'i tshe kho mo yang gar mkhan gyi bu mo bzhin mngon par mdzes pa'i dpal zhes bya ba zhig tu gyur te/ de bzhin gshegs pa de grong khyer du gshegs nas/ gar mkhan gyi tshogs kyis rol mo byas pa'i tshe/ kho mos sangs rgyas kyi byin gyis steng gi nam mkha'i dbyings las tshigs su bcad pa stong gis/ de bzhin gshegs pa de la mngon par bstod de spyan sngar phyin to/ /

“Noble one, the last of all those five hundred tathāgatas was the tathāgata Dharmadhātugaganapūrṇaratnaśikharaśrīpradīpa who appeared in the world. At that time, I was the daughter of a dancer and had the name Abhirāmaśrīvakrā. The tathāgata came to the city, and when the dancers were playing music, through the power of the Buddha I rose up into the air and praised the tathāgata with a thousand verses. Then I went to him.

“The last of those five hundred buddhas was named Lamp Radiant As a Mountain Peak of Jewels Filling the Space of the Cosmos. At that time I was a dancing girl named Radiantly Beautiful Face. When the buddha came into the city, I began to dance and by the power of the buddha rose into the air and went to the buddha, praising him with a thousand verses.

de bzhin gshegs pa des mdzod spu nas 'od zer chos dbyings rnam par snang ba'i rgyan ces bya ba bkye ste/ kho mo'i lus thams cad kyang snang bar mdzad do; ; 'od zer des kho mo la phog ma thag tu/ rnam par thar pa chos kyi dbyings kyi tshul yongs su 'khyil ba'i snying po zhes bya ba thob par gyur cing /

From the tathāgata’s ūrṇā hair shined a ray of light called the display of the radiance of the realm of the Dharma, which illuminated my entire body. The instant that light touched my body, I obtained the liberation called the concentrated essence of the way of the realm of Dharma.

He illumined my whole body with a light called Array of Cosmic Lightning, which emanated from the circle of hair between his brows; and as soon as that light touched me I attained a liberation called ‘offspring of contemplation of the principles of the reality realm.’

rigs kyi bu/ de ltar de bzhin gshegs pa de dag la sogs pa/ bskal pa 'od chen po la 'jig rten gyi khams rin chen 'khor lo sna tshogs kyis klubs shing brgyan par sangs rgyas lnga brgya byung bar gyur pa de dag thams cad kyang mnyes par byas te/ de bzhin gshegs pa de dag la kho mos mchod pa yang byas so/ /

“Noble one, in that way I pleased and made offerings to all those tathāgatas, the five hundred buddhas that appeared in the world realm called Maṇicakravicitrapratimaṇḍitavyūhā during the kalpa called Mahāprabha. Those tathāgatas taught me the Dharma, and I remembered it all. I did not forget a single letter or a single word of those ways of the Dharma.
“Thus I associated with and honored all the five hundred buddhas of that age in that world, and I remember everything they taught me, forgetting nothing, not even a line or letter.
de bzhin gshegs pa de dag gis kho mo la chos bstan pa de dag thams cad kyang dran te/ chos kyi tshul de dag las yi ge 'ga'am/ tshig 'ga' yang brjed par ma gyur to/ /
“When I went before each of those tathāgatas, I recited the Buddha’s Dharma, and in that way I benefited countless beings.
Also, as I went to each buddha, I benefited innumerable beings by describing the ways of buddhas.

de bzhin gshegs pa de dag re re'i drung du 'gro ba'i tshe yang / sangs rgyas kyi chos yongs su brjod par bya bas sems can tshad med pa'i don byas so/ / de bzhin gshegs pa de dag re re la'ang kho mos chos kyi dbyings kyi rang bzhin rgya mtsho dus gsum gyi ye shes kyi snying po/ chos kyi dbyings shin tu yangs pa zhes bya ba'i thams cad mkhyen pa'i glog mngon par snang ba/ kun tu bzang po'i spyod pa thams cad la gnas par yang dag par gzhol ba thob par gyur te/

“From each of those tathāgatas I obtained an ocean of the contents of the realm of the Dharma, an illumination from the lightning of omniscience, which was called The Extensive Realm of the Dharma That Is the Essence of the Knowledge of the Three Times, and I followed and continued all the completely good conduct.

Also, from each buddha I obtained illumination by the lightning of omniscience, called ‘womb of knowledge of past, present, and future, extensive as the cosmos,’ which is the oceanic body of the reality realm, containing at once all the practices of universal good.

rigs kyi bu/ kho mo la ni da ltar yang sems kyi skad cig re re la de bzhin gshegs pa mtha' dang dbus med pa yongs su snang ste/ de bzhin gshegs pa de dag kho mos mthong bar gyur pas thams cad mkhyen pa'i glog mngon par snang ba sngan chad ma thob pa/ sngan chad ma mthong ba dag kyang kho mo'i sems kyi rgyud la gnas par gyur te/ 'on kyang byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po'i spyod pa las g.yo ba med do/ /

“In that way, noble one, in each instant of mind there appear tathāgatas without outer limit or center. When I see those tathāgatas, there is the illumination of the lightning of omniscience, and that which I had not previously attained, which I had not previously seen, becomes present within the continuum of my mind, without ever deviating from the completely good conduct of the bodhisattva.

Now I perceive infinite buddhas in each mental moment, and from seeing those buddhas, flashes of light of omniscience which I have not previously apprehended or seen enter into my mind, and I do not fall away from the practice of universally good enlightening beings.
de ci'i phyir zhe na/ thams cad mkhyen pa'i glog mngon par snang ba thob pa 'di ni mtha' dang dbus med par bstan pa'o/ /
“Why is that? This attainment of the illumination from the lightning of omniscience is a teaching that has no outer limit or center.”
Why? Because apprehending these flashes of light of omniscience is endlessly and infinitely revealing and instructive.”

de nas mtshan mo'i lha mo sems can kun tu skyong ba'i gzi brjid dpal gyis/ de'i tshe byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa 'jig rten thams cad mngon du gyur pas 'gro ba rnam par 'dul ba zhes bya ba 'di brnan te bstan pa dang / rnam par dbye bar bya ba'i phyir/ sangs rgyas kyi byin gyi rlabs kyis tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la tshigs su bcad de smras pa/

At that time, the night goddess Samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśrī, in order to teach further and classify the bodhisattva liberation called the manifestations that guide beings that appear in all worlds, through the blessing of the Buddha recited these verses to Sudhana, the head merchant’s son:
Then the night goddess Samantasattvatranojahshri spoke these verses to Sudhana, further elucidating the enlightening liberation showing guidance for beings in all worlds:
zab mo blta dka' khong du chud dka' ste/ / dus gsum dbyings kun tha dad tshul ldan la/ / chos 'od dkyil 'khor kun tu 'od 'byung ba'i/ / kho mo'i tshig 'di nor bzang mnyan par gyis/ /

“The profound view is difficult; it is difficult to comprehend The different ways of the extents of the three times And the completely shining domain of Dharma light. Listen to these words of mine, Sudhana. {30}
Listen, Sudhana, as I tell Of what is deep, hard to see, hard to fathom: Means of distinction of the planes of all times, Total illumination of the appearances of things.
sangs rgyas yon tan 'dod pas byang chub tu/ / kho mos thog ma ji ltar sems bskyed dang / / ji ltar kho mos rnam thar 'di thob pa/ / de dag rnam par phye ba'i tshul 'di nyon/ /
“Listen to me as I reveal the way, Wishing for the qualities of buddhahood, I first developed the aspiration for enlightenment And how it was I attained this liberation. {31}
Listen to me explain how I first aspired to enlightenment In quest of the qualities of buddhas, And how I attained This liberation of awareness.
'di nas sangs rgyas zhing gi rdul snyed kyi/ / bskal pa gcig nas gcig brgyud pha rol tu/ / 'jig rten khams yangs dri ma'i skyon med pa/ / rnam snang rgyal mtshan sgron ma'i dpal byung ste/ /
“In the past, beyond kalpa after kalpa, As many as there are atoms in a buddha realm, There was a vast, stainless, faultless world realm Called Vairocanadhvajapradīpaśrī. {32}
More eons ago than atoms in a buddha-land, There was a land called Radiant Brilliance, vast and pure,
bskal pa rdul dang bral ba'i dkyil 'khor byung / / de la sangs rgyas rigs ni rgyun ma chad/ / de tshe ri rab rdul phran rab snyed kyi/ / stobs bcu skyon med mang po byung bar gyur/ /
“There had arisen the kalpa Virajomaṇḍala, In which there was a succession of buddhas. At that time those with the faultless ten strengths Appeared as numerous as the atoms in Sumeru. {33}
Where there was an age called Sphere of Dispassion, During which there was an unbroken succession of buddhas. As many buddhas as atoms in the polar mountain, free from evil, appeared:
de la bde gshegs thog mar rin chen 'od/ / kun tu 'phro dpal yon tan dpal rgyal byung / / rgyal ba chos kyi rgyal mtshan ri rab dpal/ / yon tan seng+ge'i dbang po rgyal ba bzhi/ /
“The first of those sugatas was Samantajñānaratnārciśrīguṇaketurāja, Then there was the Jina Dharmadhvaja, then Śrīsumeru, And the fourth jina was Guṇakeśarīśvara. {34}
The first was Paragon of Virtue Radiant with the Light of Universal Knowledge; Then Banner of Truth, Polar Mountain of Light, and Lion of Virtue;
rgyal ba bzhi pa'i rgyal po skye bcil dang / / grags pa'i ri bo yon tan ri rab dpal/ / rgyal ba nyi ma zla zhal bcom ldan 'das/ / bcu po 'di dag tshul 'di thog ma'o/ /
“Then there were the Jina Śāntirāja, Samitāyus, Yaśaḥparvata, Guṇasumeruśrī, The Jina Abhāskara, and the Bhagavat Śaśimukha, And those were, in that way, the first ten. {35}
King of Peace, Continual Life, Lofty Renown, Glory of Supreme Virtue, Light Maker, Moon Face—these were the first ten buddhas there.
rgyal ba nam mkha'i gzhi dang kun nas 'od/ / phyogs su yongs byung dran pa rgya mtsho'i sgo/ / rgyal ba mngon 'phags 'od mnga' ri rab dpal/ / bde gshegs chos kyi 'od 'phro ri bo dpal/ /
“Then there were the Jina Gaganālaya, and Samataprabha, Diśasaṃbhava, Smṛtisamudramukha, The Jina Abhyudgata, Sumeruśrī, And the Sugata Dharmārciparvataśrī, {36}
Vault of the Sky, Universal Light, Omnipresent, Source of the Sea of Mindfulness, Exalted, Summit of Glory, Light of Lofty Flames of Truth,
thugs rje che mnga' dgu pa pad+mos 'phags/ / sangs rgyas bcu pa chos dbyings me tog ste; / sangs rgyas rgya mtsho yongs su brjod pa las/ / tshul 'di bcu pa gnyis pa 'di yin no/ /
“Then Kāruṇika, and ninth was Padmodgata.[1493] The tenth buddha was Dharmadhātukusuma. In that way, these were the second ten From the description of the ocean of buddhas. {37}
Lotus Born, The Compassionate, and Flower of the Cosmos— These were the second ten, lighting the ocean of buddhas.
'od dpal rgyal po ye shes blo gros dang / / sna tshogs don dbang dpal gyi blo gros lha; ; rgyal ba shugs kyi rgyal blo ye shes dpal/ / snang ba'i rgyal po 'od kyi rgyal mtshan dpal/ /
“Then there were Prabhaketurājamati,[1494] Jñānamati, Citrārthendra, Śrīdevamati, Jina Vegarājamati, Jñānaśrī, And Avabhāsarāja, and Prabhaketuśrī, {38}
Mind of Foremost Light, Mind of Knowledge, Manifold Benefits, Glory of Indra, Celestial Intellect, Mind of Supreme Energy, Splendor of Knowledge,
rgyal ba rnam par gnon pa'i lha stabs dang / / de bzhin chos dbyings pad+mo bcu pa ste; ; rgya chen yongs su bstan las tshul 'di ni/ / tshul 'dir bcu pa gsum pa bstan pa'o/ /
“Then the Jina Vikrāntadevagati, And likewise Dharmadhātupadma. In that way, those were the third ten Within the way of this vast teaching. {39}
Brilliance of the Best of Lights, Mighty Celestial Stride, Lotus of the Cosmos— These were the third ten buddhas, revealing this vast teaching.
rin chen 'od 'phro ri dpal bcom ldan 'das/ / de yi 'og ma yon tan rgya mtsho dpal/ / chos kyi 'od dang pad+mo snying po dpal/ / 'gro ba'i zla ba spyan tshul bde bar gshegs/ /
“Then there was the Bhagavat Ratnārciparvataśrī, And following him were Guṇasamudraśrī, Dharmaprabha, Padmagarbhaśrī, And the Sugata Gaticandranetranayana, {40}
Splendor of a Mountain of Jewel Lights, then Radiant Ocean of Virtues, Light of Truth, Lotus-Born Glory, Moonlike Eye of the World, Fragrant Light,
spos kyi 'od dang rin chen ri rab dpal/ / rgyal ba dri za lus 'od rgyal po dang / / rin chen snying po rgyal dpal gzi brjid ldan/ / rgyal ba bcu pa zhi ba'i gzugs rtsi stabs/ /
“Then Gandhaprabha, Maṇisumeruśrī, Gandharvakāyaprabharāja, and Maṇigarbharājaśritejavatin, And the tenth jina was Praśamarūpagati. {41}
Brilliant As a Mountain of Jewels, Radiant King in the Form of a Celestial Musician, Full of Glorious Light of the Finest of Jewels, and tenth was Physically Calm.
de yi 'og ma rgyal ba rgya chen blo/ / rin chen 'od dang nam mkha'i sprin gyi dpal/ / rgyal ba dam pa'i mtshan gyi dpal gyur dang / / brtul zhugs dkyil 'khor rang gi lus kyi 'od/ /
“Following them were the Jina Vipulabuddhi, Ratnaprabha, and Gaganameghaśrī. Then there were the Jina Varalakṣaṇaśrī, Vratamaṇḍala, and Svaśarīraprabha, {42}
After that were Vast Awareness, Jewel Luster, Splendor of Clouds in the Sky, Superb Appearance, magnificent, and Sphere of Holy Practices, radiant,
mthu chen brtul zhugs ri rab dpal mnga' dang / / rgyal ba yon tan khor yug dpal gyi rgyal/ / bcom ldan mi pham brtul zhugs rgyal mtshan dang / / shing gi ri bo rgyal ba de dag bcu/ /
“Then Nārāyaṇavratasumeruśrī, The Jina Guṇacakravālaśrirāja, The Bhagavat Aparājitavratadhvaja, And Drumaparvata, the tenth of those jinas. {43}
Living Like Primeval Man, Splendid As the Polar Mountain, King Resplendent with Virtue, Paragon of Invincible Resolve, and Lofty Tree the tenth of them.
rgyal ba sA la'i rgyal po dpal gyi mchog / 'jig rten dbang po'i lus ni snang ba'i 'od/ / mngon par 'phags 'od dpal gyi bcom ldan 'das/ / rdo rje 'od dang sa yi gzi brjid dpal/ /
“Then there were the Jina Sālendrarājaśrigarbha, Lokendrakāyapratibhāsaprabha, The Bhagavat Abhyudgataprabhaśrī, Vajraprabha,[1495] and Dharaṇitejaśrī, {44}
Imbued with the Splendor of the King of Trees, Reflection of the Bodies of the Leaders of the Worlds, Superlative Radiance, Spotless Light, Brilliance of the Energy of Earth,
rgyal ba zab chos 'od kyi rgyal po dpal/ / chos kyi rgya mtsho dbyangs kyi blo gros dang / / ri rab rgyal mtshan dpal dang blo gros snang / / rgyal ba bcu pa rin chen rgyal po dpal/ /
“Then the Jina Gambhīradharmaguṇarājaśrī, Dharmasāgaranirghoṣamati, Merudhvajaśri, Prabhāsamati, And the tenth jina, Ratnarājaśri. {45}
Glory of the Supreme Virtues of the Profound Teaching, Knowledge of the Sound of the Ocean of Truths, Pole of the World, Radiant Mind, Diamond Light.
tshangs pa'i 'od dang rgyal ba nam mkha'i dbyings/ / de bzhin chos kyi dbyings ni gzugs brnyan dpal/ / snang ba'i dkyil 'khor 'od kyi bcom ldan 'das/ / tha dad phyogs mkhyen ye shes blo gros dang / /
“Then there were Brahmaprabha, the Jina Gaganaghoṣa, Dharmadhātupratibhāsaśri, The Bhagavat Ālokamaṇḍalaprabha, And Diśabhedajñānaprabhaketumati, {46}
Light of Brahma, Sound of Space, Splendor of Reflection of the Cosmos, Sphere Of Lights, Brilliant Mind with the Ten Powers of Knowledge,
nam mkha'i sgron ma mngon par dga' ba'i dpal/ / rnam par snang mdzad 'od dpal bde bar gshegs/ / bsod nams rab tu snang dpal zhi ba'i dpal/ / bcu pa snying rje chen po sprin gyi dpal/ /
“Then Gaganapradīpa, Abhirāmaśrī, The Sugata Vairocanaprabhaśrī, and Puṇyaprabhāsaśriśāntaśrī, And the tenth was Mahākaruṇameghaśrī. {47}
Lamp of Space, Beautiful Splendor, Glory of Sunlight, Light of Virtue, Tranquil Radiance, and Beauty of Clouds of Compassion, were the next ten buddhas.
de bzhin nyi 'od stobs snang blo gros/ dang / / rgyal ba 'gro ba thams cad mngon gzugs dang / / de tshe rgyal ba mngon 'phags 'od mnga' 'byung / / de yi 'og ma zhi ba'i sku yi 'od/ /
Mindful of the Light of Power Born of Thusness, Appearing to All Beings, Exalted Light, Embodiment of Impartiality,
chos 'phags bde gshegs de bzhin byung bar gyur/ / de yi 'og ma rlung gi drag shul dpal/ / dpa' ba'i rgyal mtshan rin chen lus kyi dpal/ / dus gsum snang ba'i 'od ni bcu pa'o/ /
“In the same way, there was the Sugata Dharmodgata, And after him came Anilavegaśrī, Śūradhvaja, and Ratnagātraśrī, And the tenth was Tryadhvapratibhāsaprabha. {49}
Born of Truth, Swift As the Wind, Paragon of Heroism, Jewel Body Luster, Light Appearing in All Times— These were the next ten buddhas.
smon lam rgya mtsho rab tu snang dpal dang / / gnyis pa dgongs pa rdo rje ri bo dpal/ / rgyal ba gsum pa seng+ge ri rab dpal/ / dran pa'i rgyal mtshan rgyal po chos dpal blo/ /
“Then there was Praṇidhānasāgaraprabhāsaśrī, The second was Vajrāśayagiriśrī, The third jina was Harisumeruśrī, And then there were Smṛtiketurājaśri and Dharmamati, {50}
Shining Light of the Ocean of Vows, Splendor of the Mountain of Adamantine Will, Exalted Brilliance, Paragon of Mindfulness,
shes rab sgron ma 'od kyi rgyal mtshan dpal/ / de yi 'og ma rgyal ba rgya chen blo/ / rgyal ba chos dbyings tshul gyi ye shes stabs/ / chos kyi rgya mtsho blo gros ye shes dpal/ /
“Then Prajñāpradīpa, Prabhaketuśrī, And after them the Jina Vipulabuddhi, The Jina Dharmadhātunayajñānagati, And Dharmasamudramatijñānaśri. {51}

Aware of Truth, Lamp of Wisdom, Radiance of the Most Excellent Light, then Vast Intellect, Following the Course of Knowledge of the Principles of the Cosmos, and Light of Knowledge of Oceanic Awareness.
chos 'dzin pa dang rin chen sbyin dpal dang / / rgyal ba yon tan khor yug dpal gyi sprin/ / bzod pa'i sgron ma dpal dang gzi brjid ldan/ / shugs 'ong zhi gnas dbyangs kyi rgyal ba dang / /
“Then there were Dharmadhara, Ratnadānaśri, The Jina Guṇacakravālaśrimegha, Kṣāntipradīpaśrī, and Tejovat,[1496] And the Jina Vegaprabhaśamathaghoṣa, {52}
Sublime Giver of Jewels of Truth, Clouds of Glory of Mountains of Virtue, Light of the Lamp of Peace, Light of Fiery Energy, Voice of Cessation, Paragon of Tranquillity,
zhi ba'i rgyal mtshan 'gro ba'i sgron ma dpal/ / sangs rgyas smon lam chen po shugs kyi dpal/ / bcom ldan gzhan gyis mi thub rgyal mtshan stobs/ / rgyal ba ye shes 'od 'phro rgya mtsho dpal/ /
“Then Śāntidhvajajagatpradīpaśrī, The Buddha Mahāpraṇidhivegaśrī, The Bhagavat Aparājitadhvajabala, And the Jina Jñānārcisāgaraśrī. {53}
Radiant Lamp of the World, Energy of Great Vows, Invincible Power, Radiant Sea of Lights of Knowledge.
rgyal ba chos dbang blo gros chags pa med/ / 'gro skad rgya mtsho dbyangs kyi blo gros dang / / thams cad dbyangs kyi yan lag sgra skad dpal/ / dbang sgyur mchod sbyin grags pa'i mchod sdong blo/ /
“Then there were the Jina Dharmeśvara, Asaṅgamati, Jagamantrasāgara, Nirghoṣamati, Sarvasvarāṅgarutaghoṣaśrī, Vaśavartiyajñayaśayaṣṭimati, {54}
Spiritual Master, Unattached Mind, Understanding the Speech of All Beings, Articulate in All Languages, Resolved to Sacrifice Willingly,
phyogs yul 'gro ba mngon sum bcom ldan 'das/ / sems can bsam par mnyam pa sku yi dpal/ / gzhan yang sangs rgyas gnas dang bcas pa'i dpal/ / rgyal ba rang bzhin lus dpal bzang po dang / /
“The Bhagavat Diśadeśāmukhajaga, Sattvāśayasamaśarīriśri, The Buddha Parārthasavihāraśrī, And the Jina Prakṛtīśarīraśrībhadra. {55}
der ni rgyal ba de la sogs pa byung / / de dag byung nas 'gro ba'i sgron ma mdzad/ / bskal pa ri rab shin tu phra rdul snyed/ / bdag gis rgyal ba rgya mtsho de dag mchod/ /
“Those jinas and the others appeared there. When they appeared, they were lamps for the world. I made offerings to that ocean of jinas For as many kalpas as there are atoms in Sumeru. {56}
Beginning with these, I served as many buddhas, light-makers, As atoms in the polar mountain.
bskal pa sangs rgyas zhing gi rdul snyed po/ / de dag tu ni rgyal ba gang byung ba/ / bde gshegs de dag thams cad bdag gis mchod/ / rnam par thar ba'i tshul ni 'di la zhugs/ /
“Whatever jinas have appeared in kalpas As numerous as the atoms in a buddha realm, I have made offerings to all those sugatas And followed this way of liberation. {57}
And I served all the buddhas who appeared In as many eons as atoms in the buddha-lands, And entered this ocean of liberation.
rnam par thar pa'i tshul 'di sgom byed cing / / bskal pa mtha' yas bdag gis sngon spyad kyi/ / khyod kyis thos nas nan tan myur gyis shig / tshul 'di ring po mi thogs thob par 'gyur/ /
“I have practiced throughout endless past kalpas, Meditating on this way of liberation. Having heard it, practice it quickly, And you will attain this way before long. {58}

rigs kyi bu/ kho mos byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa 'jig rten thams cad mngon du gyur pas 'gro ba rnam par 'dul ba ston pa 'di shes par zad na/ /kho mos byang chub sems dpa' mtha' dang dbus med pa'i byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa rgya mtsho la mos pa sna tshogs kyis yang dag par gnas pa/ bsam pa sna tshogs kyi lus dang ldan pa/ dbang po rgya mtsho sna tshogs yongs su grub pa/ byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa dang / smon lam sna tshogs shin tu rtogs pa de dag gi spyod pa shes pa'am/ yon tan brjod par nus re skan/

“Noble one, I know only this bodhisattva liberation called the manifestations that guide beings that appear in all worlds. How could I know the conduct or describe the qualities of bodhisattvas who remain in the aspiration to an ocean of bodhisattva conduct that has no outer limit or center, who have bodies in accordance with the various dispositions of beings, who accomplish an ocean of various faculties, and who have the realization of the various kinds of bodhisattva conduct and prayers?

“I know only this enlightening liberation showing guidance to beings in all worlds. How can I know the practice on tell the virtues of the enlightening beings who live by various resolutions in the infinitely varied ocean of enlightening practices, who manifest various minds and bodies, who have perfected oceans of various faculties, who have carried through the various vows of enlightening beings?

song / rigs kyi bu/ snying po byang chub 'di nyid na/ kho mo dang rgyang mi ring ba zhig na mtshan mo'i lha mo sgra rgya mtsho rab tu zhi ba dang ldan pa zhes bya ba/ pad+mo'i khri rin po che'i rgyal po snang ba'i rgyal mtshan gyis rab tu brgyan pa zhig la 'dug cing / mtshan mo'i lha mo grangs med pa brgya stong phrag bcu'i 'khor gyis bskor ba 'dug gi /de'i gan du song la/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bya ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bya ba dris shig /

“Depart, noble one. Here in the bodhimaṇḍa, there is the goddess of the night named Praśantarutasāgaravatī. “She is seated on a lotus throne with the adornment of shining banners of kings of jewels in its center, and with an entourage of countless millions of night goddesses. Go to her and ask her, ‘How should a bodhisattva train in bodhisattva conduct? How should a bodhisattva practice it?’ ”

“In this same enlightenment site is a night goddess named Prashantarutasagaravati, who sits next to me on a lotus seat, in a calyx adorned with starry diamonds, surrounded by countless tens of hundreds of thousands of night goddesses—go ask her how to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings.”

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis/ mtshan mo'i lha mo sems can kun tu skyong ba'i gzi brjid dpal gyi rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te/ mtshan mo'i lha mo sems can kun tu skyong ba'i gzi brjid dpal la/ lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas/ yang dang yang bltas te/ mtshan mo'i lha mo sems can kun tu skyong ba'i gzi brjid dpal gyi drung nas song ngo// //

Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, bowed his head to the feet of the night goddess Samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśrī, circumambulated the night goddess Samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśrī many hundreds of thousands of times, keeping her to his right, and, looking back again and again, departed from the night goddess Samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśrī.
So Sudhana paid his respects to the night goddess Samantasattvatranojahshri and left her.
shin tu rgyas pa chen po'i mdo/ sangs rgyas phal po che las/ sdong pos brgyan pa'i le'u ste/ bam po brgya gcig pa/

d.crumb: [sgra rgya mtsho rab tu zhi ba dang ldan pa]

f.d: [sgra rgya mtsho rab tu zhi ba dang ldan pa]
Chapter 38. Praśantarutasāgaravatī
Prashantarutasagaravati

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang mtshan mo'i lha mo sems can kun tu skyong ba'i gzi brjid dpal gyi byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa'i 'jig rten thams cad mngon du gyur pas 'gro ba rnam par 'dul ba de la yongs su bsgom zhing khong du chud par bya ba dang / yid ches par bya ba dang / 'jug par bya ba dang / shin tu rgyas par bya ba dang / yongs su khyab par bya ba dang / rab tu mchod par bya ba dang / dbang du bya ba dang / snang bar bya ba dang / yang dag par gzhol bar bya ba byed cing / mtshan mo'i lha mo sgra rgya mtsho rab tu zhi ba dang ldan pa gang na ba der phyin te/

Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, meditating on the night goddess Samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśrī’s bodhisattva liberation called the manifestations that guide beings that appear in all worlds, and contemplating it, having faith in it, engaging in it, increasing it, expanding it, augmenting it,[1497] gaining power over it, illuminating it, and being absorbed in it, approached the night goddess Praśantarutasāgaravatī.

Then Sudhana, cultivating that enlightening liberation of the night goddess Samantasattvatranojahshri, showing guidance to beings in all worlds, entering into it, becoming absorbed in it, plunging into it, expanding it, spreading it, extending it, mastering it, making it manifest, attaining it, went to the night goddess Prashantarutasagaravati.

mtshan mo'i lha mo sgra rgya mtsho rab tu zhi ba dang ldan pa'i rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te mtshan mo'i lha mo sgra rgya mtsho rab tu zhi ba dang ldan pa la lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas mtshan mo'i lha mo sgra rgya mtsho rab tu zhi ba dang ldan pa'i mdun du 'dug ste/

He bowed his head to the night goddess Praśantarutasāgaravatī’s feet, circumambulated the night goddess Praśantarutasāgaravatī many hundreds of thousands of times, and then stood before the night goddess Praśantarutasāgaravatī.
He paid his respects to her
thal mo sbyar nas 'di skad ces smras so/ /
With his hands placed together in homage, he said,
and said,

'phags ma lha mo/ bdag ni/ bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub du yang dag par zhugs pa ste/ bdag ni/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi rten gyis byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la slob cing byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la zhugs te byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la nan tan du bgyi ba dang / byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la rab tu gnas pas thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du 'byung bar 'tshal na/ 'phags ma lha mo/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bgyi ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bgyi ba bdag la bshad du gsol/

“Āryā, I have entered upon the highest, complete enlightenment, and through relying on kalyāṇamitras I am training in bodhisattva conduct. I have entered into bodhisattva conduct, and I am practicing bodhisattva conduct. I wish to bring forth omniscience through being established in bodhisattva conduct. Therefore, Āryā, goddess, I pray that you explain to me how bodhisattvas should train in bodhisattva conduct and how they should practice it!”

“With the help of spiritual benefactors I am learning the practice of enlightening beings, entering into the practice of enlightening beings, carrying out the practice of enlightening beings; having undertaken the practice of enlightening beings, I want to become thoroughly familiar with omniscience. So please tell me, noble goddess, how an enlightening being is to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings.”
de nas mtshan mo'i lha mo sgra rgya mtsho rab tu zhi ba dang ldan pas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la 'di skad ces smras so/ /
The night goddess Praśantarutasāgaravatī said to Sudhana, the head merchant’s son,
The goddess said,
rigs kyi bu/ de ltar khyod dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi rten gyis byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa yongs su tshol ba legs so/ / legs so/ /
“Noble one, it is excellent, excellent, that in this way you seek bodhisattva conduct by relying on kalyāṇamitras.
“It is good that you seek the ocean of practices of enlightening beings by relying on spiritual benefactors.
rigs kyi bu/ kho mo ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa dga' ba yangs pa'i shugs 'byung bas sems kyi skad cig rnam par brgyan pa thob pa'o/ /
Noble one, I have attained the bodhisattva liberation called the display in each instant of mind of the arising of the power of vast delight.”
I have attained an enlightening liberation of supernal manifestations of a moment of consciousness producing floods of immense joy.”

nor bzang gis smras pa/ 'phags ma/ khyod ni/ 'phrin las ci mdzad/ yul gang dang ldan/ sbyor ba gang dang ldan/ ci la rnam par dpyod/ byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa dga' ba yangs pa'i shugs 'byung bas sems kyi skad cig rnam par brgyan pa de'i yul ni/ ji lta bu zhig mchis/

Sudhana asked, “Āryā, what kind of activity do you accomplish? What kind of range do you have? What is your practice? What do you contemplate? What is the range of the bodhisattva liberation called the display in each instant of mind of the arising of the power of vast delight?”
Sudhana said, “What is your activity, your sphere of action, your means of practice, your contemplation? What is the scope of this liberation?”

des smras pa/ rigs kyi bu/ kho mo ni/ sems dang bsam pa rgya mtsho yongs su dag pa'i mnyam pa nyid du zhugs pa ste/ 'jig rten gyi rdul dang dri ma thams cad rnam par bsal ba'i mi phyed pas brgyan pa'i bsam pa la zhugs pa'o/ / brtsams pa las mi ldog /mi ldog pa'i sems dang ldan pa'o/ / rin po che'i ri bo ltar yon tan gyis brgyan pa'i sems mi sgul ba dang ldan pa'o/ / mi gnas mi rten pa'i sems dang ldan pa'o/ / 'gro ba thams cad yongs su bskyab pa la mngon par phyogs pa'i sems can dang ldan pa'o/ / sangs rgyas rgya mtsho thams cad mthong bas mi ngoms pa'i sems dang ldan pa'o/ /

She replied, “Noble one, I have entered the equanimity of the purification of the ocean of mind and thought. I have attained the aspiration for an inviolable display that is clear of all worldly dust and dirt. I have a mind that will not regress or turn back from this undertaking. I have a mind that is like an unshakable jewel mountain adorned by qualities. I have a mind that is not stationed anywhere, not located anywhere. I have a mind that is focused on saving all beings. I have a mind that never tires of seeing the ocean of all the buddhas.

She said, “I have attained equanimity through purification of the ocean of mind. I have attained indestructible adornment undefiled by the taint of all worldly passion. My mind is unregressing and unswerving from its object. My mind is unshakable, adorned with virtues like a mountain of jewels. My mind is not fixed on anything, not dependent on anything. My mind is intent on serving all beings. My mind is tireless in seeing all buddhas.

byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi stobs kyi bsam pa rnam par dag pa'i sems dang ldan pa'o/ / dran pa'i rgya mtsho ye shes kyi snang ba chen pos brgyan pa la yang dag par gnas pa'i sems dang ldan pa'o/ / sems can thams cad mya ngan gyi dgon pa las yang dag par bzla ba la zhugs pa'o/ / sems can thams cad sdug bsngal dang / yid mi bde ba las rnam par zlog pa la mngon par brtson pa'o/ / sems can thams cad kyi yid du mi 'ong ba'i gzugs dang / sgra dang / dri dang / ro dang / reg yongs su rgyu ba rnam par zlog pa la zhugs pa'o/ / sems can thams cad kyi sdug pa dang mi sdug pa dang bral zhing phrad pa'i sdug bsngal rab tu zhi bar bya ba la zhugs pa'o/ / sems can thams cad kyi yul gyi rkyen las byung bas mgo rmongs pa'i sdug bsngal rnam par zlog pa la rab tu brtson pa'o/ / log par ltung ba'i sems can thams cad kyi rten du gyur pa'o/ / sems can thams cad 'khor ba'i gnas kyi sdug bsngal las 'byung ba yang dag par ston pa la mngon par brtson pa'o/ /

I have a mind that has a pure motivation. I have a mind that has the strength of all the bodhisattvas. I have a mind that dwells in an ocean of the awareness of the display of the light of great wisdom. I am engaged in leading all beings out of the wilderness of misery. I am dedicated to dispelling the sufferings and unhappiness of all beings. I am engaged in turning beings away from involvement with unpleasant[1498] form, sound, smell, taste, and touch. I am engaged in ending the suffering of being separated from what is liked and encountering what is disliked. I am dedicated to dispelling the suffering of ignorance that arises in relation to the scope of perception. I am a support for all beings who fall. I am dedicated to revealing to all beings the way out of the suffering of being in saṃsāra.

My desire for the powers of all enlightening beings is pure. My mind dwells in the ocean of mindfulness of the manifestations of great knowledge. I have set out to overcome the sorrows of all beings and am devoted to removing the suffering and sadness of all beings. I have undertaken to stop all beings’ preoccupation with objects of sense. I have undertaken to extinguish beings’ suffering caused by separation from loved ones and contact with the uncongenial. I am intent on stopping all the sufferings of beings that come from delusion arising from their relations to objects. I am a refuge for all fallen beings and am engaged in showing all beings means of emancipation from the miseries of the mundane whirl.
sems can thams cad kyi rga shi dang / mya ngan dang / smre sngags 'don pa dang / sdug bsngal ba dang / yid mi bde ba dang / 'khrug pa rnam par zlog pa la zhugs pa'o/ /
I am engaged in eliminating the aging, death, misery, lamentation, suffering, unhappiness, and tribulations of all beings.
I have undertaken to stop all sentient beings’ sadness, lamentation, suffering, depression, and mental disturbance occasioned by birth, old age, and death.

sems can thams cad la de bzhin gshegs pa'i bde ba bla na med pa yongs su sgrub par zhugs pa ste/ grong dang / grong khyer dang / ljongs dang / yul dang / khams dang / rgyal po'i gnas na 'khod pa'i sems can thams cad bde bar rim gror bya bas nyams dga' bar 'gyur zhing / de dag la chos dang mthun par bsrung ba dang / bskyab pa dang / rim gro bya ba yang legs par byed de/

I am engaged in causing all beings to attain the supreme happiness of the tathāgatas. I gain satisfaction through bringing to happiness all beings in villages, towns,[1499] countrysides, kingdoms, realms,[1500] and capital cities, and in ways that accord with the Dharma I guard them, protect them, and help them.

I have undertaken to produce the supreme felicity of the enlightened in all beings. I find satisfaction in presenting my services for the happiness of beings in all abodes, and I see to their spiritual protection,
de dag rim pas thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du yongs su smin par byed do/ /
“I gradually ripen them for omniscience in this way:
and I gradually develop them to omniscience.

I develop nonattachment within beings who dwell in mansions and aerial palaces. I dispel their unhappiness. I bring an end to all attachments. I teach them the Dharma so that they will know the nature of all phenomena.

That is to say, I produce detachment in beings who live in great palaces and mansions, and I remove their various melancholies, and in order to put an end to all attachments, I teach them to realize the intrinsic nature of all things.

pha ma dang / phu nu dang / sring mo dang / gnyen bshes dang / 'grogs pa'i sems can yun ring po nas bshes shing mdza' bar gyur pa dag las sangs rgyas dang byang chub sems dpa' dang 'phrad par bya ba'i phyir chos ston to/ /
I teach the Dharma to those who for a long time have been close and affectionate with fathers, mothers, brothers, sisters, relatives, and friends, so that they will meet buddhas and bodhisattvas.
I teach those who have long-standing ties of affection with their families and relatives in such a way that they may get to meet and associate with buddhas and enlightening beings.

bu smad dang 'grogs pa'i sems can rnams la 'khor ba'i sred pa thams cad rab tu spang ba dang / sems can thams cad la mnyam pa nyid kyi sems su bya ba dang / snying rje chen po rab tu thob par bya ba'i phyir chos ston to/ /
I teach the Dharma so that beings who spend time with their wives[1501] will forsake all craving for saṃsāra, view all beings equally, and attain great compassion.

Those who are involved with their spouses and children I teach in such a way as to extinguish their craving for mundane enjoyments and so that they will become impartial toward all and will come to have great compassion.
tshong 'dus kyi dbus na 'khod pa'i sems can rnams la 'phags pa'i dge 'dun dang / de bzhin gshegs pa mthong bar bya ba la yang dag par gzhol bar bya ba'i phyir chos ston to/ /
I teach the Dharma so that those who are in the middle of markets will become engaged in seeing the noble saṅgha and the tathāgatas.
Those in the marketplaces I teach in such a way that they will enter into association with the community of sages and get to meet enlightened people.
longs spyod kyi dregs pas myos pa'i sems can rnams la bzod pa'i pha rol tu phyin pa yongs su rdzogs par bya ba'i phyir chos ston to/ /
I teach the Dharma so that beings who are intoxicated by pride in their pleasure will complete the perfection of patience.
Those who are obsessed with consumer goods I teach in such a way that they acquire transcendent forbearance.
glu dang / gar dang / rol mo la mngon par dga' ba'i sems can rnams la chos kyi dga' ba la mos par bya ba'i phyir chos ston to/ /
I teach the Dharma so that those beings who delight in songs, dance, and music will aspire to delight in the Dharma.
Those who take pleasure in music, song, and dance, I teach the way to enjoy spiritual pleasures.
yul gyi dga' ba la chags pa'i sems can rnams la de bzhin gshegs pa'i yul la yang dag par gzhol bar bya ba'i phyir chos ston to/ /
I teach the Dharma so that beings who are attached to the delights of the perceptions of their senses will become engaged in the perception of the tathāgatas.
Those eagerly desirous of enjoyment of sense objects I teach in such a way that they may arrive at the realm of the enlightened.
khro bas yongs su non pa'i sems can rnams la bzod pa'i pha rol tu phyin pa la rab tu dgod par bya ba'i phyir chos ston to; ;
I teach the Dharma so that beings oppressed by anger will become established in the perfection of patience.
Those who are filled with anger I teach in such a way as to lead them to transcendent tolerance.

sems can le lo can rnams la brtson 'grus kyi pha rol tu phyin pa yongs su dag par bya ba'i phyir chos ston to/ / sems rnam par myos pa'i sems can rnams la de bzhin gshegs pa'i bsam gtan gyi pha rol tu phyin pa rab tu thob par bya ba'i phyir chos ston to/ / lta ba'i rnam pa thibs por zhugs pa'i sems can ma rig pa'i mun nag tu 'thom pa rnams la lta ba'i rnam pa thibs po dang / ma rig pa'i mun pa rnam par bsal ba'i phyir chos ston to/ / shes rab 'chal ba can gyi sems can rnams la shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa rab tu thob par bya ba'i phyir chos ston to/ / khams gsum pa la mngon par zhen pa'i sems can rnams la 'khor ba las 'byung bar bya ba'i phyir chos ston to/ /

I teach the Dharma so that beings who are lazy will have the pure perfection of diligence. I teach the Dharma so that beings who are deranged will attain the perfection of the meditation of the tathāgatas. I teach the Dharma so that beings who are in the thicket of wrong views and blinded by the darkness of ignorance will eliminate the thicket of wrong views and the darkness of ignorance. I teach the Dharma so that beings who are stupid will attain the perfection of wisdom. I teach the Dharma so that beings who are attached to the three realms will depart from saṃsāra.

Those who are lazy I teach in such a way as to purify transcendent vigor. Those whose minds are confused I teach to attain the transcendent meditation of those who arrive at Thusness. Those lost in a tangle of views, fallen into the darkness of ignorance, I teach in such a way as to lead them out of the tangle of views and the darkness of ignorance. Those who are stupid I teach in such a way that they may acquire transcendent wisdom. Those attached to the realms of desire, form, or formlessness, I teach in such a way that they may escape from the sufferings of the mundane whirl.
dman pa la mos pa'i sems can rnams la de bzhin gshegs pa'i byang chub tu smon lam yongs su rdzogs par bya ba'i phyir chos ston to/ /
I teach the Dharma so that beings who are attracted to what is inferior will have the complete aspiration for the enlightenment of the tathāgatas.
Those with low aspirations I teach in such a way that they may fulfill the vow of enlightenment.
bdag la phan par brtson pa'i sems can rnams la sems can thams cad la phan par bya ba'i smon lam yongs su rdzogs par 'gyur bar bya ba'i phyir chos ston to/ /
I teach the Dharma so that beings who are dedicated to benefiting themselves will have the complete aspiration to benefit all beings.
Those intent on their own benefit I teach in such a way that they may fulfill the vow to bring benefit to all beings.
bsam pa nyam chung ba'i sems can rnams la byang chub sems dpa'i stobs kyi pha rol tu phyin pa rnam par dag par bya ba'i phyir chos ston to/ /
I teach the Dharma so that beings who have weak motivation will have the pure perfection of the strength of the bodhisattvas.
Those with weak wills I teach in such a way that they may perfect the transcendent power of enlightening beings.
ma rig pa'i mun pas sems blong ba'i sems can rnams la byang chub sems dpa'i ye shes kyi pha rol tu phyin pa rnam par dag par bya ba'i phyir chos ston to/ /
I teach the Dharma so that beings whose minds are dimmed by the darkness of ignorance will have the pure perfection of knowledge of the bodhisattvas.
gzugs mi sdug pa dang ldan pa'i sems can rnams la de bzhin gshegs pa'i gzugs kyi sku rnam par dag par bya ba'i phyir chos ston to/ /
I teach the Dharma so that beings with ugly bodies will have the form body of a tathāgata.
lus kyi dbyibs mi mdzes pa dang ldan pa'i sems can rnams la chos kyi sku bla na med pa rnam par dag par bya ba'i phyir chos ston to/ /
I teach the Dharma so that beings with misshapen bodies will have the supreme Dharma body.

kha dog mi sdug pa dang ldan pa'i sems can rnams la de bzhin gshegs pa'i sku mdog gser gyi kha dog lta bu dang / shin tu 'jam zhing ka tsa lin+da ka ltar reg na bde ba'i lus rnam par dag par bya ba'i phyir chos ston to/ /
I teach the Dharma so that beings with an ugly color will have a body that is golden like the body of the tathāgatas and is as soft as down and pleasant to the touch.
sdug bsngal ba'i sems can rnams la de bzhin gshegs pa'i bde ba dam pa rab tu thob par bya ba'i phyir chos ston to/ /
I teach the Dharma so that beings who are suffering will attain the ultimate happiness of the tathāgatas.
Those in misery I teach in such a way as to enable them to attain the felicity of omniscience.
bde ba'i sems can rnams la thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi bde ba rab tu thob par bya ba'i phyir chos ston to/ /
I teach the Dharma so that beings who have happiness will attain the happiness of omniscience.
nad pa na ba'i sems can rnams la byang chub sems dpa'i lus gzugs brnyan lta bu yongs su grub par bya ba'i phyir chos ston to/ /
I teach the Dharma so that beings who are ill will attain the body of a bodhisattva that is like a reflection.
Those who are sick I teach in such a way that they may develop the reflectionlike bodies characteristic of enlightening beings.
dga' ba sna tshogs la brtson pa'i sems can rnams la byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa'i dga' ba rab tu thob par bya ba'i phyir chos ston to/ /
I teach the Dharma so that beings who are dedicated to various delights will attain delight in bodhisattva conduct.
Those attached to various pleasures I teach in such a way that they may acquire delight in the practices of enlightening beings.
phongs pa'i sems can rnams la byang chub sems dpa'i chos kyi gter dang mdzod rab tu thob par bya ba'i phyir chos ston to/ /
I teach the Dharma so that beings who are destitute will obtain the store of treasures of the bodhisattva Dharma.
Those who are destitute I teach in such a way that they may obtain the spiritual treasury of enlightening beings.
bza' shing gi ra ba na gnas pa'i sems can rnams la sangs rgyas kyi chos yongs su btsal ba la mngon par brtson pa'i rgyu thob par bya ba'i phyir chos ston to/ /
I teach the Dharma so that beings who go to parks will obtain the cause for dedication to seeking the Buddha’s Dharma.
Those who resort to parks and gardens I teach in such a way that they are motivated to seek the way to enlightenment.
lam du zhugs pa'i sems can rnams la thams cad mkhyen pa'i lam du 'jug par bya ba'i phyir chos ston to/ /
I teach the Dharma so that beings who are on the road will follow the road to omniscience.
Those who are on the road I teach in such a way that they set out on the road to omniscience.
