through perceiving the immeasurable repeated presence of the tathāgatas, when they were bodhisattvas, in an ocean of kalpas, and seeing the entire ocean of all the buddhas in the past;
by concentration on attainment of the scope of knowledge of infinite buddhas’ productions of bodies going throughout all lands in the past when they were enlightening beings,
de bzhin gshegs pa sngon byang chub sems dpar gyur pas zhing rgya mtsho ma lus pa rgyas par dgang ba'i sku mngon par sgrub pa tshad med pa'i ye shes snang ba rab tu thob par bya ba'i tshul dang /
through having attained the illuminating knowledge of the tathāgatas as bodhisattvas having the immeasurable accomplishment of their bodies pervading the entire ocean of realms;
de bzhin gshegs pa'i sngon gyi byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa tshad med pas chos kyi dbyings ma lus pa rgyas par dga' ba'i tshul dang /
through the immeasurable, vast bodhisattva conduct of the tathāgatas pervading the entire realm of phenomena;
by concentration on infinite buddhas’ extension of their past enlightening practices throughout all universes,

de bzhin gshegs pa'i sngon gyi byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa thabs sna tshogs kyi sgo dang ldan pas sems can thams cad yongs su smin par mdzad pa dang / rnam par gdul bar mdzad pa tshad med pa yongs su bstan pa'i tshul dang /
through the vision of the past immeasurable bodhisattva conduct by the tathāgatas of ripening and guiding all beings through various methods;[1521]
by concentration on the manifestation of infinite buddhas’ past practices as enlightening beings using various methods to develop and guide all sentient beings,
de bzhin gshegs pa'i 'od phyogs rgya mtsho ma lus pa thams cad du rab tu 'phro ba tshad med pas rgyas par dgang bar bya ba'i tshul dang /
through the immeasurable radiating light of the tathāgatas pervading the entire ocean of directions;
by concentration of infinite buddhas’ pervasion of all realms with their light,
de bzhin gshegs pa sems can thams cad la mngon du gyur pa rnam par 'phrul pa tshad med pa yongs su bstan pa'i tshul dang /
through the tathāgatas’ immeasurable display of miraculous manifestations directly to beings;
by concentration on infinite buddhas’ demonstration of miracles to sentient beings,
de bzhin gshegs pa'i ye shes kyi sa tshad med pa yongs su gnon pa'i ye shes snang ba rab tu thob par bya ba'i tshul dang /
through having attained[1522] the illuminating knowledge of the ascent to the immeasurable level of the knowledge[1523] of the tathāgatas;
by concentration on the scope of knowledge of infinite buddhas’ ascent through the stages of enlightenment,
de bzhin gshegs pa'i mngon par rdzogs par byang chub pa'i rnam par 'phrul pa tshad med pa'i ye shes snang ba rab tu thob par bya ba'i tshul dang /
through having attained the illuminating knowledge of the immeasurable miraculous manifestation of the attainment of buddhahood by the tathāgatas;
by concentration on attainment of the scope of knowledge of the miracle of perfect enlightenment of infinite buddhas,
de bzhin gshegs pa'i chos kyi 'khor lo rab tu 'khor ba dang / chos kyi sprin tshad med pa thams cad ma lus par yang dag par blangs shing yongs su bzung ba'i tshul dang /
through having obtained and possessed the entirety of all the immeasurable clouds of Dharma from the turnings of the wheel of the Dharma by the tathāgatas;
by concentration on receiving and holding all the doctrines preached by infinite buddhas,
de bzhin gshegs pa'i mtshan rgya mtsho tshad med pa rnam par dmigs pa'i ye shes snang ba rab tu thob par bya ba'i tshul dang /
through having attained the illuminating knowledge that perceives the immeasurable ocean of the characteristics of the tathāgatas;
by concentration on attainment of knowledge of the oceans of marks of distinction manifested by infinite buddhas,
de bzhin gshegs pa'i sku rgya mtsho'i rgyud tshad med pa rnam par dmigs pa'i snang ba rab tu thob par bya ba'i tshul dang /
through having attained the illuminating knowledge that perceives the immeasurable ocean of the activities[1524] of the bodies of the tathāgatas;
by concentration on awareness of infinite buddhas’ oceans of embodiments representing practices,
de bzhin gshegs pa'i yul shin tu yangs pa'i ye shes snang ba rab tu thob par bya ba'i tshul gyis
and through having attained the illuminating knowledge of the immeasurable,[1525] vast scope of the tathāgatas.
by concentration on attaining the scope of knowledge of the vast realm of infinite buddhas,
de bzhin gshegs pa de dag gi thog ma thugs bskyed pa nas dam pa'i chos nub par ma gyur pa'i bar de dag thams cad la'ang 'jug cing khong du chud par byed do/ /
[…see above]
in every moment of thought I comprehend everything about those buddhas from their first determination to the cessation of their true teaching.

de skad du khyod kyis byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa dga' ba yangs pa'i shugs 'byung bas sems kyi skad cig rnam par brgyan pa 'di thob nas ji srid cig lon zhes zer ba ni/ de ltar kho mos bskal pa sangs rgyas kyi zhing gnyis kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi pha rol gyi 'jig rten gyi khams gser ltar dri ma med pa'i 'od du byang chub kyi shing gi lha mo bsod nams sgron ma phun sum tshogs pa kun nas dpal gyi 'od ces bya bar gyur te/ de bzhin gshegs pa phyir mi ldog pa'i chos kyi dbyings kyis chos bstan pa thos nas bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed de/ bskal pa sangs rgyas kyi zhing gnyis kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed po de dag tu byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa spyad nas mi mjed kyi 'jig rten gyi khams 'dir skyes te/ log par dad sel la sogs pa tha ma shAkya thub pa'i bar gyi de bzhin gshegs pa bskal pa bzang po pa dag kyang bsnyen bkur te/ ma byon pa'i sangs rgyas rnams kyang bsnyen bkur ro/ /

“You ask me how long it has been since I attained this bodhisattva liberation called the display in each instant of mind of the arising of the power of vast delight? It was like this: As many kalpas ago as there are atoms in two buddha realms, in the world realm called Kanakavimalaprabhā, I was a Bodhi-tree goddess by the name of Puṇyapradīpasaṃpatsamantaketuprabhā. When I heard the Dharma taught by the Tathāgata Avivartyadharmadhātunirghoṣa, I developed that aspiration to attain the highest, complete enlightenment. I practiced bodhisattva conduct for as many kalpas as there are atoms in two buddha realms and was then reborn in this world realm called Sahā. I venerated the tathāgatas of the Bhadra kalpa, from Krakucchanda to Śākyamuni, and I will also venerate its future buddhas.

“If you ask also how long ago I attained this enlightening liberation of supernal manifestations in a moment of thought producing great floods of joy, when I was an enlightenment tree goddess named Exemplary Light Serving As a Beacon of Good in the world Pure Golden Radiance as many eons ago as atoms in a buddha-land, I first aspired to enlightenment on hearing the teaching of the buddha Unremitting Voice of the Reality Realm, and after having carried out the practice of enlightening beings for as many eons as atoms in a buddha-land, I was born in this world and propitiated the buddhas of the eon of Virtue from Krakucchanda to Shakyamuni. And I will propitiate and honor all the buddhas yet to come,
'jig rten gyi khams 'dir ji lta ba de bzhin du 'jig rten gyi khams thams cad du'ang sangs rgyas kyi rgyud ma byon pa rnams yongs su bsnyen cing bkur ro/ / mchod do/ /
And just as in this world realm, I will venerate and make offerings to the future succession of buddhas in all world realms.
in this world and in all worlds.
rigs kyi bu/ da dung du'ang 'jig rten gyi khams gser ltar dri ma med pa'i 'od de yang yod la/ sangs rgyas kyi rigs kyang rgyun ma chad kyi/ de bas na/
“Noble one, there continues even now to be a succession of buddhas in the world realm Kanakavimalaprabhā.
Even now that world of Pure Golden Radiance still exists, and the lineage of the buddhas there is unbroken.
rigs kyi bu/ tshul 'di la byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par gnon pa chen pos brtson par gyis shig /
“Therefore, noble one, you should dedicate yourself to this way with the fortitude of the bodhisattva.”
So you should apply yourself to this doctrine with the great strength of enlightening being.”

de nas mtshan mo'i lha mo sgra rgya mtsho rab tu zhi ba dang ldan pas de'i tshe byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa dga' ba yangs pa'i shugs 'byung bas sems kyi skad cig rnam par brgyan pa 'di nyid brnan te bstan par bya ba'i phyir tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la tshigs su bcad de smras pa;

At that time, the night goddess Praśantarutasāgaravatī, in order to teach further the bodhisattva liberation called the display in each instant of mind of the arising of the power of vast delight, recited these verses to Sudhana, the head merchant’s son:
Then the goddess further explained her liberation to Sudhana in verse:
rnam thar dge 'di ji ltar thob gyur pa/ / kho mo'i tshig 'di nor bzang khyod nyon cig / thos nas dga' ba'i stobs kyang yongs bskyed de/ / rnam thar tshul 'di la ni 'jug par gyis/ /
“Listen, Sudhana, to these words of mine About how I obtained this good liberation. Hearing them will give rise to great delight, And you must comprehend this liberation. {1}
Listen to me tell, O Sudhana, How I attained this pure liberation. Hearing this and generating the power of joy, Enter this way of liberation.
bdag gi sems dang bsam pa yongs sbyong zhing / / mos pa'i shugs yangs yongs su bskyed byas te/ / thams cad mkhyen pa'i ye shes grong 'dun pas; ; bskal pa rgya mtsho mang por sngon spyad do/ /
“I purified my mind and my thoughts, And I developed a vast, powerful aspiration. Intent on the city of omniscient wisdom, I practiced for many oceans of past kalpas. {2}
I practiced for many eons past And purified my mind; Generating great momentum of zealous application, I came into the presence of the citadel of omniscience.
bde gshegs dus gsum byung ba thos nas kyang / / de dag kun la mos pa yangs bskyed do/ / bskal pa brgya phrag mang por sgo kun tu/ / de dag 'khor dang bcas par kho mos bkur/ /
“I listened to the sugatas in the three times And developed an aspiration toward them all. Through the passage of many hundreds of kalpas, I attended on them and their assemblies. {3}
Hearing of the buddhas, supreme in all times, And developing great faith in them, I served them and their retinues for hundreds of eons With all that is pleasing.
sngon gyi bde gshegs kho mos mthong gyur nas/ / 'gro la phan phyir yun ring mchod byas te/ / spro ba'i stobs ni rnam yangs yongs bskyed nas/ / bdag gis gdung ba med pa'i chos kyang thos/ /

“I saw the sugatas of the past and made offerings to them Over a long time, so as to bring benefit to beings. Having developed a powerful enthusiasm, I listened to their Dharma without weariness.[1526] {4}
Seeing the buddhas of the past, I honored them for the benefit of all beings; And I heard their incomparable teaching, Generating immense power of joy.
rnam par thar pa 'di la 'jug pa na/ / pha dang ma dang bla ma'i skye bo la/ / de tshe bdag gis phan bdes bsti stang byas/ / bsnyen bkur sri zhur gnas pa kun kyang byas/ /
“On following the way of this liberation, I continually and respectfully attended Those who were my father, mother, and guru, Venerating them and bringing them happiness and benefit. {5}
I always paid respect to my parents and elders, Taking pleasure in their welfare; I served them and honored them, While entering this liberation.
rgas pa nad pa nor med mi rnams dang / / dbang po ma tshang sdug bsngal mgon med pa/ / mang po bdag gis byams sems bde bkod nas/ / tshe rabs brgyar yang nor phyug mgon yod byas/ /

“Through hundreds of lifetimes and with a loving mind, I was a wealthy protector who brought happiness To many people who were old, who were sick, and who were poor, Who had impaired faculties, were in suffering, and had no protector. {6}
Many people who were old, infirm, poor, Handicapped, suffering, helpless, I made happy, rich, and protected, Over hundreds of lifetimes.
rgyal po me dang rkun chom rkyen gyur dang / / seng+ge glang po pha rol dgras 'jigs dang / / srid pa'i rgya mtsho'i 'jigs dngos sna tshogs las/ / sngon tshe spyod pa'i dus na bdag gis bskyabs/ /
“During my bodhisattva conduct in past lives, I saved beings from an ocean of various dangers Caused by kings, fire, and bandits[1527] And by lions, elephants, and enemies. {7}
In my past practice I rescued those In the sea of existence from various perils— From the perils of kings and robbers, Fire and water, wild beasts and enemies.
rtag tu srid gsum nyon mongs gdungs gyur te/ / las kyis rab gdungs de bzhin mi dge bas/ / 'khor ba'i ri gzar g.yang du lhung ba yi/ / skye bo 'gro ba'i rgyud du bdag gis bskyabs/ /
“During my bodhisattva conduct in past lives, I saved beings afflicted by kleśas in the three realms From the various terrors of the ocean of existence That arise through their bad actions. {8}
I saved those always burning with afflictions in the world, Made that way by impure deeds, In dangerous straits in the mundane whirl, Born in the paths of existence.
sdug bsngal ngan song g.yang sas 'jigs pa dag / rtag tu mi bde shin tu mi bzad dang / / skye rga na zhing 'chi ba'i 'jigs mang kun/ / bdag gis 'jig rten spyod tshe zhi bar byas/ /

“I protected those classes of beings Who have fallen into the abyss of saṃsāra, Terrified by the sufferings of the lower realms, Which are always overwhelmingly dreadful. As I practiced bodhisattva conduct in the world, I ended the terrors of birth, old age, sickness, and death.[1528] {9}
The terrors of the calamities in the woeful states of misery Are harsh and violent, continuous and manifold; The terrors of birth, old age, death and sickness in the world I put an end to entirely.
'khor ba'i sdug bsngal zhi bar bya ba dang / / sems can kun gyi bde ba yongs bskyed cing / / sangs rgyas bde ba dam pa bskyed pa ni/ / bskal pa phyi mar kho mo'i smon lam mo; ;
Stilling the intense pains of the mundane world, Producing all happiness in sentient beings, Producing the ultimate bliss of the enlightened, For endless eons—this is my vow.

rigs kyi bu/ kho mos byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa dga' ba yangs pa'i shugs 'byung bas sems kyi skad cig rnam par brgyan pa 'di shes par zad na; kho mos byang chub sems dpa' chos kyi dbyings kyi tshul rgya mtsho thams cad la zhugs pa/ phyi nang gi sdug bsngal ma lus pa las rnam par grol ba/ bskal pa'i ming du bya ba thams cad shes par gyur pa/ 'jig rten gyi khams rgya mtsho thams cad 'byung ba dang / 'jig pa'i rgyus la mkhas pa de dag gi spyod pa shes pa'am/ yon tan brjod par nus re skan/

“Noble one, I know only this bodhisattva liberation called the display in each instant of mind of the arising of the power of vast delight. How could I know the conduct or describe the qualities of bodhisattvas who have comprehend the entire realm of phenomena, who are liberated from every outer and inner suffering, who know the names of all kalpas, who are wise in the creation of the ocean of all worlds and their destruction?

“I only know this enlightening liberation of supernal manifestations in a moment of thought producing vast floods of joy—how can I know the practice or tell the virtues of the enlightening beings who have plunged into the ocean of all principles of the cosmos of reality, who are freed from all internal and external suffering, who know all eons are in the thoughts, who are versed in the knowledge of the becoming and dissolution of all worlds?

song rigs kyi bu/ snying po byang chub 'di nyid na bcom ldan 'das rnam par snang mdzad kyi 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor na mtshan mo'i lha mo grong khyer thams cad srung ba 'byung ba'i gzi brjid dpal zhes bya ba 'dug gi /de'i gan du song la ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bya ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bya ba dris shig /

“Depart, noble one. Here in this very bodhimaṇḍa, within the assembly of the Bhagavat Vairocana, there is the goddess of the night who has the name Sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśrī. Go to her and ask her, ‘How should a bodhisattva train in bodhisattva conduct? How should a bodhisattva practice it?’ ”

“At this same enlightenment site, in the circle of Vairocana Buddha, is a night goddess named Sarvanagararakshasambhavatejahshri—go ask her how an enlightening being is to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings.”
de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis mtshan mo'i lha mo sgra rgya mtsho rab tu zhi ba dang ldan pa la tshul dang 'dra pa'i tshigs su bcad pa 'di dag smras so/ /
Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, recited these appropriate verses to the night goddess Praśantarutasāgaravatī:
Then Sudhana spoke these verses to the night goddess Prashantarutasagaravati:
dge ba'i bshes kyis ma nor mthun bstan pas/ / lha mo khyod kyi drung du nye bar mchis/ / mtha' dang dbus mi mnga' ba'i sku tshul du; ; khyod ni gdan la bzhugs pa bdag gis mthong / /
“The kalyāṇamitra instructed me correctly, And therefore I came into your presence, goddess. I saw you seated upon your throne With a body that knows no limit or center. {11}
Instructed by a spiritual benefactor, I came to you, O goddess; I see you sitting on your seat Of infinite height.
kha dog dbyibs dang mtshan ma'i spyod yul ba/ / srid la gnas dang dngos por 'du shes dang / / 'du shes dma' dang log par lta ba yis/ / khyod kyi spyod yul 'tshal bar mi nus so/ /

“Those who rely on existence and believe things to be real, Whose fields of perception are colors, shapes, and characteristics, Inferior beings who hold wrong views, Cannot know this field of activity of yours. {12}
Those whose minds are on appearances, Who cling to existence or conceptualize being, And the low-minded with false views, Cannot know this realm of yours.
khyod kyi sku gzugs blta na mtha' yas pas/ / khyod kyi sku gzugs mdog gi mtshan min/ / bskal pa mtha' yas dag tu yongs brtags kyang / / lha dang 'jig rten bcas pas shes mi nus/ /
“The vision of your body is infinite. The world and its devas could not know The characteristics of your form and color Even by examining them for endless kalpas. {13}
No worldly or celestial beings can know The features of your appearance and form, Even if they look for endless eons— So endless is the sight of your form.
lha mo khyod ni phung po'i gnas las 'phags/ / skye mched rnams la'ang de bzhin mi gnas te/ / 'jig rten rnam par 'das pas the tshom bral/ / 'jig rten dag tu rnam par 'phrul ba mdzad/ /
“Goddess, you are above the basis of the skandhas. You are not located within the āyatanas. There is no doubt that you have transcended the world And manifest miracles within the world. {14}
You are free from dependence on the body-mind clusters, And you do not rest on the sense media either; Gone beyond the world and transcended desire, You appear in the world, transforming.
g.yo ba mi mnga' skyon bral chags pa med/ / khyod kyis ye shes spyan ni rnam sbyangs pas/ / rdul gyi go la thams cad rdul tshad du/ / sangs rgyas rnam par 'phrul pa mang po gzigs/ /
“You are unshakable, without fault, without impediment. You have purified your eyes of wisdom. You see in an atom as many buddhas As there are atoms, performing miracles. {15}
You have attained immovability, faultless and unattached, You have clarified the eye of higher knowledge; In every atom you see as many buddhas as all atoms Magically transforming.
khyod kyi sku ni chos sku'i snying po can; ; khyod kyi thugs kyang ye shes chags pa med/ / khyod ni kun tu 'od kyis snang mdzad pas/ / 'jig rten skye bo rnams la mtha' yas snang / /
“Your body has the essence of the Dharma body. Your mind consists of unobstructed wisdom. You shine with the radiance of all-pervading light, Illuminating the endless beings in the world. {16}
Your body contains the body of truth, Your mind is made of knowledge, unhindered. Illumined by universal light, You produce endless light in the world.
sems las mtha' yas las rnams yongs su 'byung / / 'jig rten thams cad las kyis rnam par bris/ / 'gro ba sems kyi dngos su mkhyen gyur pas/ / rang gi sku yang 'gro ba snyed du bstan; ;
“Endless karma arises from the mind. All the worlds are paintings by karma. You know directly the minds of beings, And the manifestations of your body are as numerous as beings. {17}
You produce endless deeds from the mind, So all worlds are adorned by your deeds; Knowing that worlds are mental in nature, Your manifest yourself in bodies Equal to beings.
'jig rten du ni rmi lam 'drar mkhyen nas/ / sangs rgyas kun kyang gzugs brnyan lta bu dang / / ma lus chos rnams sgra brnyan 'drar mkhyen pas/ / chags pa mi mnga' 'gro ba kun tu spyod/ /
“You know this world to be like a dream And that all the buddhas are like reflections, That every single Dharma is like an echo, And without impediment you act within all worlds. {18}
Knowing this world is like a dream And all buddhas are like reflections And all phenomena like echoes, You live in the world without clinging to anything.
dus gsum gnas pa'i 'gro ba thams cad la/ / skad cig re rer rang gi sku ston kyang / / khyod kyi thugs la gnyis su mi rgyu ste/ / phyogs rnams kun tu chos kyang rab tu bstan/ /
“You manifest your body in each instant To all the beings dwelling in the three times. With no duality in your mind, You teach the Dharma throughout all directions. {19}
In each moment you show yourself To the beings of past, present, and future, Yet there is no inclination to dualism in your mind, And thus do you expound the Teaching in all realms.
rdul la 'gro ba rgya mtsho mtha' yas dang / / de bzhin sems can mtsho chen dpag yas dang / / mtha' dbus med pa'i bde gshegs gang chen mtsho/ / kun kyang khyod kyi rnam thar dam pa'i yul/ /
“The ocean of atoms is without end, And the ocean of beings is also measureless. The ocean of the buddhas has no edge or center, And they are all within the scope of your liberation.” {20}
The oceans of beings are as infinite As the endless oceans of atoms, And infinite too are the oceans of Buddha— All are the sphere of your practice of liberation.

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis mtshan mo'i lha mo sgra rgya mtsho rab tu zhi ba dang ldan pa la tshul dang 'dra ba'i tshigs su bcad pa de dag gis mngon par bstod de lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas yang dang yang bltas te mtshan mo'i lha mo sgra rgya mtsho rab tu zhi ba dang ldan pa'i drung nas song ngo/ /

Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, having praised the night goddess Praśantarutasāgaravatī with these appropriate verses, circumambulated the night goddess Praśantarutasāgaravatī many hundreds of thousands of times, keeping her to his right, and, looking back again and again, departed from the night goddess Praśantarutasāgaravatī.
Then Sudhana paid his respects to the night goddess and left her.
shin tu rgyas pa chen po'i mdo/ sangs rgyas phal po che zhes bya ba las/ sdong pos brgyan pa'i le'u ste// ` // bam po brgya gnyis pa/

d.crumb: [mtshan mo'i lha mo grong khyer thams cad srung ba 'byung ba'i gzi brjid dpal]

f.d: [mtshan mo'i lha mo grong khyer thams cad srung ba 'byung ba'i gzi brjid dpal]
Chapter 39. Sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśrī
Sarvanagararakshasambhavatejahshri

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa dga' ba yangs pa'i shugs 'byung bas sems kyi skad cig rnam par brgyan pa de ni; sgom pa dang / rjes su sgom pa dang / yang dag par sgom pa dang / mtshan mo'i lha mo sgra rgya mtsho rab tu zhi ba dang ldan pa'i gdams ngag rjes su bstan pa la ni/ rjes su 'brang bar bya ba dang / rjes su dran par bya ba dang / khong du chud par byed/ tshig dang yi ge re re la ni/ tshul du ma dang bsam pa tshad med pas chos nyid kyi tshul shes pa rjes su dran par byed cing / dren pas rjes su 'brang bar bya ba dang / blo gros kyis rnam par dbye ba dang / rigs pas khong du chud par bya ba dang / blos shin tu yangs par bya ba dang / lus kyis reg par byas te rnam par spyad pa dang / rjes su 'jug pa byed cing /

Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, was meditating on, familiarizing himself with,[1529] and cultivating the bodhisattva liberation called the display in each instant of mind of the arising of the power of vast delight. He was following, remembering, and comprehending the instruction and teachings of the night goddess Praśantarutasāgaravatī, remembering each word and letter, the numerous countless aspects, the knowledge of the aspects of the nature of phenomena, and he was relying on it through his memory, analyzing it with his intelligence, comprehending it with his understanding,[1530] increasing it with his intellect, feeling it with his body, practicing it, and engaging in it,

Then, contemplating that enlightening liberation of supernal manifestations in a moment of thought producing floods of joy, fostering it and making it manifest, remembering the instruction of the night goddess Prashantarutasagaravati, absorbing it, keeping in mind knowledge of the principles inherent in it, a measureless repository of many principles to be found in each statement, fixing it in memory, examining it intellectually, putting it into practice, consciously extending it, physically feeling and dwelling in it, entering into it,
mthar gyis mtshan mo'i lha mo grong khyer thams cad srung ba 'byung ba'i gzi brjid dpal gang na ba der phyin pa dang /
and eventually he arrived where the night goddess Sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśrī was.
Sudhana made his way to the night goddess Sarvanagararakshasambhavatejahshri.

mtshan mo'i lha mo grong khyer thams cad srung ba 'byung ba'i gzi brjid dpal pad+mo'i khri chen po nor bu rin po che'i rgyal po grong khyer dang / gnas thams cad rab tu snang bar byed pa'i snying po can la phyogs thams cad dang / 'gro ba thams cad la mngon du gyur pa'i lus dang / 'gro ba thams cad kyi gzugs dang mnyam pa'i lus dang / sems can thams cad la mngon du gyur pa'i lus dang / 'gro ba thams cad kyis ma gos pa'i lus dang / 'gro ba thams cad dang rang bzhin mnyam pa'i lus dang / 'gro ba thams cad las mngon par 'phags pa'i lus dang / 'gro ba thams cad yongs su smin par bya ba dang / gdul ba la mthun pa'i lus dang / 'gro ba thams cad du sgra rab tu sgrog pa'i lus dang / 'gro ba thams cad du 'pho ba med pa'i lus dang / sgrib pa thams cad shin tu bcom pa'i lus dang / de bzhin nyid kyi rang bzhin gyi lus dang / 'gro ba thams cad gdul ba mthar phyin par byed pa'i lus su 'dug cing / mtshan mo'i lha mo brjod du med pa'i 'khor gyis bskor te 'dug pa

He saw the night goddess Sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśrī seated upon a great lotus throne containing the kings of precious jewels that illuminate towns and dwellings, with an entourage of countless night goddesses, with a body that appeared in all directions to all beings, with a body that had the forms of those of all beings, with a body that appeared before all beings, with a body that was unstained by all beings, with a body that had the same nature as that of all beings, with a body that was superior to those of all beings, with a body of the kind that could ripen and guide all beings, with a body through which she spoke to all beings, with a body that did not pass away among all beings, with a body that had vanquished all obscurations, with a body that had the nature of the ultimate nature of things,[1531] with a body that had reached the conclusion of guiding all beings.

He saw the night goddess sitting on a great lotus seat full of diamonds illumining the dwelling places in all cities, accompanied by untold numbers of night goddesses, with a body appearing to the beings in all realms, with a body equal in form to all beings, with a body appearing to all beings, with a body unstained by all worlds, with a body equal to all beings in number of manifestations, with a body transcending all worlds, with a body adapted to developing and guiding all beings, with a body proclaiming the truth in all realms, with a body reaching everywhere, with a body ultimately freed from obstructions, with a body of the essence of those who arrive at Thusness, with a body guiding all beings to ultimate perfection.

mthong nas dga' rangs te mgu zhing nyams bde la tshim zhing yid bde ba skyes nas mtshan mo'i lha mo grong khyer thams cad srung ba 'byung ba'i rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te mtshan mo'i lha mo grong khyer thams cad srung ba 'byung ba'i gzi brjid dpal la lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas mtshan mo'i lha mo grong khyer thams cad srung ba 'byung ba'i gzi brjid dpal gyi mdun du 'dug ste

When Sudhana saw her, he was filled with joy, delighted, elated, pleased, and happy. He bowed his head to the night goddess Sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśrī’s feet, circumambulated the night goddess Sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśrī many hundreds of thousands of times, and then stood before the night goddess Sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśrī.
Sudhana, enraptured upon seeing the night goddess, paid his respects to her
thal mo sbyar nas 'di skad ces smras so/ /
With his hands placed together in homage, he said,
and said,

lha mo/ /bdag bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu yang dag par zhugs na/ lha mo/ / ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la rjes su bslab na sems can la sman par 'gyur ba lags/ ji ltar na/ sems can bla na med pa yongs su bsdu bas yongs su sdud par 'gyur/ ji ltar na/ byang chub sems dpa' de bzhin gshegs pas gnang ba'i byang chub sems dpa'i las la brtson pa lags/ ji ltar brtson par bgyis na/ byang chub sems dpa' chos kyi rgyal por nye bar 'gyur ba bdag la bshad du gsol/ de skad ces smras pa dang /

“Goddess! I have entered upon the highest, complete enlightenment. Goddess, I pray that you explain to me how bodhisattvas should train in bodhisattva conduct so that they will be a medicine[1532] for beings. How do bodhisattvas gather beings into the highest gathering? How do bodhisattvas, authorized by the tathāgatas, dedicate themselves to bodhisattva conduct so that, having become dedicated, they become kings of the Dharma.

“O goddess, I have set out for supreme perfect enlightenment; please tell me how an enlightening being is to be a benefactor to others while carrying out enlightening practice, and how an enlightening being is to take care of sentient beings with the highest protection and care, and how an enlightening being, engaged in the work of enlightening beings by the assent of the enlightened, is to approach the seat of a spiritual sovereign?”
mtshan mo'i lha mo grong khyer thams cad srung ba 'byung ba'i gzi brjid dpal gyis tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la 'di skad ces smras so/ /
The night goddess Sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśrī said to Sudhana, the head merchant’s son,
The night goddess replied,

rigs kyi bu/ khyod de ltar 'gro ba thams cad yongs su smin par bya ba dang / rnam par gdul ba'i mthar phyin par bya ba dang / de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi rigs yang dag par bzung ba'i sbyor ba mthar phyin par bya ba dang / phyogs 'byams klas pa thams cad rgyas par dgang ba'i ye shes rab tu sbyar ba dang / chos kyi dbyings kyi tshul rgya mtsho thams cad la 'jug pa mngon du 'gyur ba dang / shes bya nam mkha'i dbyings dang mnyam pa mtha' yas pa rgyas par dgang ba dang / de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi chos kyi 'khor lo rab tu blang zhing yongs su gzung ba'i phyir 'gro ba rgya mtsho thams cad kyi bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du chos kyi sprin gyi char mngon par dbab pa'i spyod pa'i tshul yongs su 'dri ba legs so/ /legs so/ /

“Noble one, it is excellent, excellent, that you ask about conduct that is a rain from clouds of Dharma that accords with the aspiration of the entire ocean of beings, so as to reach the conclusion of ripening and guiding all beings; so as to reach the conclusion of joining and maintaining the family of the tathāgatas; so as to conjoin with the wisdom that pervades throughout the extent of the directions; so as to focus on comprehending the entire ocean of the ways of the realm of the Dharma; so as to pervade the infinity of all that can be known, which is as vast as the extent of space; and so as to obtain and possess the wheels of Dharma of all the tathāgatas.

“It is very good that you ask about the way of practice of distributing teachings to sentient beings according to their mentalities, to attain the goal of guiding all sentient beings to perfection, to attain the goal of the effort to preserve the family of all buddhas, to apply all-pervasive knowledge, to confront entry into the ocean of means leading to all realms of reality, to penetrate all knowables by knowledge boundless as space, to receive and hold the teachings of all buddhas.
rigs kyi bu/ kho mo ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa sgra yid du 'ong ba dang / rnam par 'grul ba zab mo la 'jug pa thob pa ste/
“Noble one, I have attained the bodhisattva liberation called the entry into beautiful sounds and profound manifestations.
“I have attained an enlightening liberation, ‘entry into the profound miracle of pleasing sound.’
de ltar kho mo rnam par thar pa de dang ldan pas chos smra ba chen po'i go 'phang thogs pa med pa la dmigs pa'i sbyor ba dang ldan pa/
“Noble one, through this liberation I undertake being on the unimpeded level of a dharmabhāṇaka.
Having attained this liberation, engaged in preaching the great Teaching, free from attachment,
de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi chos kyi mdzod yongs su btang ba'i smon lam dang ldan pa/
I have the aspiration to make a gift of the Dharma treasure of all the tathāgatas.
dedicated to dissemination of the treasury of teachings of all buddhas,
snying rje chen po dang ldan pa/ byams pa chen po'i stobs rab tu thob pa/
I have attained the power of great love and compassion.
imbued with the power of great compassion and goodwill,
sems can thams cad byang chub kyi sems la dgod pa'i phyir sems can thams cad kyi don bya ba la zhugs pa;
I am dedicated to activities that benefit all beings in order to bring all beings to the aspiration for enlightenment.
set on working for the welfare of all sentient beings to inspire them to seek enlightenment,
byang chub kyi sems kyi dge ba'i rtsa ba dang / tshogs rab tu bsags pa rgyun mi gcad pa'i phyir 'gro ba thams cad kha lo sgyur ba'i sa la yang dag par gnas pa/
I remain on the level of a guide for beings so that they will continuously gather the accumulation of the roots of merit of the aspiration for enlightenment.
set out to become a leader of all sentient beings to ceaselessly accumulate stores of virtues in determination for enlightenment,
sems can thams cad thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi lam la rab tu dgod pa'i phyir 'jig rten gyi chos kyi sprin thams cad las chos kyi nyi ma yongs su dbyung ba'i sbyor ba dang ldan pa/
In order to bring all beings onto the path to omniscience, I engage in causing the sun of the Dharma to appear out of the clouds of the Dharma in the world.
engaged in producing clouds of teaching and suns of teaching in all worlds to guide all sentient beings on the path of omniscience,
dge ba'i rtsa ba tshad med pa bskyed pas 'jig rten thams cad snang bar bya ba'i phyir 'gro ba thams cad la mnyam pa'i sems su 'jug pa rgyun mi 'chad pa/
I continuously engage in a motivation that regards all beings as equal in order to illuminate all worlds with countless roots of merit.
ceaselessly reaching out impartially to all sentient beings to illumine all worlds so as to produce infinite roots of goodness,
'gro ba thams cad kyi dge ba'i rtsa ba mngon par 'du bya ba yongs su sgrub pa'i sbyor ba shes par bya ba'i phyir sems rnam par dag pa'i sbyor ba dang ldan pa/
I am conjoined with a pure motivation so that all beings will know the accomplishment of accumulating roots of merit.
applying a purified mind to practical knowledge of sustaining the performance of good works of all sentient beings,
dge ba'i las kyi lam thams cad mthun par sgrub pas sems can thams cad kyi ded dpon du zhugs pa/
I engage in being a leader of the caravan of all beings so that they will appropriately accomplish all the paths of good actions;
set out to lead all sentient beings to accord with all paths of good action,
mi dge ba'i las kyi lam thams cad rab tu spangs pa/ sems can thams cad dge ba'i chos la rab tu dgod pa'i sbyor ba dang ldan pa/
I am engaged in the activity of causing all beings to reject all paths of bad actions and be established in the Dharma of good actions.
engaged in the work of directing all sentient beings in good ways,
sems can thams cad la lam bde ba yongs su ston pa'i sbyor ba dang ldan pa/
I am engaged in teaching the path to happiness to all beings.
engaged in showing all sentient beings the way to peace and security,
sems can thams cad kyi theg pa'i rgyan gyi thog mar 'dren pa la zhugs pa/
I bring all beings to the beginning of the array of the yānas.
set out to lead all sentient beings to emancipation,
dge ba'i chos kyi spyod pa thams cad la sems can thams cad rab tu dgod pa'i sbyor ba dang ldan pa/
I am engaged in establishing all beings in all virtuous Dharma practices.
engaged in directing all sentient beings to all good practices,
dge ba'i bshes gnyen thams cad la mi phyed par bsnyen bkur dang rim gro byed pa la zhugs pa/
I am engaged in providing unceasing service and veneration to all kalyāṇamitras.
set out to serve all spiritual friends uninterruptedly,
sems can thams cad de bzhin gshegs pa'i bstan pa la rab tu dgod pa'i sbyor ba dang ldan pa/
I am engaged in establishing all beings in the teaching of the tathāgatas.
engaged in directing all sentient beings to the teaching of the enlightened,
chos kyi sbyin pa'i sngon 'den cing chos dkar po thams cad yang dag par brtsams pa'i sbyor ba dang ldan pa/
I am engaged in causing all beings to commence upon good qualities through receiving the very first gift of the Dharma.
engaged in undertaking all pure and good practices such as giving,
thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi sems bskyed pas mngon par byung bas bsam pa brten zhing mi shigs pa/
I cause the arising of an aspiration for omniscience that is enduring and indestructible.
firmly resolved to realize omniscience,
rdo rje mthu bo che ltar brtan zhing sra bas sangs rgyas kyi stobs la dmigs pa'i sems rgya chen po'i dkyil 'khor dang ldan par dge ba'i bshes gnyen la brten cing rnam par spyod de/
I have the vast domain of the aspiration focused on the strengths of the Buddha, which is as enduring and solid as the most powerful vajra, and I practice by relying on a kalyāṇamitra.
with a broad mental sphere firmly focused on the powers of buddhas, I stay by the spiritual benefactor,

kho mo ni/ nyon mongs pa dang / las kyi sgrib pa thams cad kyi ri rnam par gtor ba'i sems dang ldan pa'o/ / thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi tshogs yang dag par rtsom pa'o/ / dkar po'i chos thams cad yang dag par sgrub pa'i sbyor ba dang ldan pa'o/ / thams cad mkhyen pa nyid mtha' dang dbus med pa la mngon par 'dun cing dmigs pa'i sems kyi sbyor ba la brtson pa'o/ /

“I have a mind that shatters the mountain of all the obscurations from karma and kleśas. I am dedicated to the accumulation of omniscience. I am engaged in accomplishing all good qualities. I am dedicated to being engaged in a mind that is focused on and aspires for omniscience that has no end or center.

determined to shatter the mountains of afflictions and obstructions to enlightenment caused by actions, undertaking the preparations for omniscience, engaged in developing all good qualities, engaged in application of thought to the infinite variety of objects confronting omniscience.
rigs kyi bu/ de ltar kho mo chos snang ba'i sgo sems can thams cad la yongs su ston pa rnam pa de lta bu yongs su sbyong zhing dge pa'i rtsa ba bsags pa'i tshogs la sta gon du gnas pas
“Noble one, in that way, I am purifying the revelation to all beings of the gateway to the light of the Dharma, and I am establishing them in gathering the accumulation of roots of merit.
“Furthermore, as I purify this medium of light of the Teaching, communicating to all sentient beings, accumulating roots of goodness,
rnam pa bcus chos kyi dbyings la rnam par lta zhing khong du chud pa dang / rjes su gzhal bar byed do/ /
“I look upon, comprehend, and fathom the realm of phenomena in ten ways.
I observe, approach, and proceed through the reality realm in terms of ten aspects.
bcu gang zhe na/ 'di lta ste/
What are those ten?
What are the ten?
ye shes snang ba shin tu yangs pa thob pas chos kyi dbyings ni/ tshad med pa khong du chung par byed do/ /
(1) I comprehend the realm of phenomena because I have attained the vast light of wisdom.
I realize that the reality realm is immeasurable, by gaining vast vision of knowledge.
de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi rnam par 'phrul ba rnam par dmigs par bya ba'i phyir chos kyi dbyings ni/ mtha' dang dbus med par khong du chud par byed do/ /
(2) I comprehend the realm of phenomena as having no end and no center in order to perceive the miraculous manifestations of all the tathāgatas.
I realize that the reality realm is infinitely various, so as to perceive the miracles of all buddhas.
sangs rgyas kyi zhing thams cad yongs su gnan pa dang / de bzhin gshegs pa mchod cing rim gror bya ba'i phyir chos kyi dbyings ni/ mu med par khong du chud par byed do/ /
(3) I comprehend the realm of phenomena as limitless in order to reach all buddha realms and to make offerings and show veneration to the tathāgatas.
I realize that the reality realm is endless, so as to fulfill travel to all buddha-lands and service of buddhas.
'jig rten gyi khams rgya mtsho thams cad du byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa yongs su bstan pa'i phyir chos kyi dbyings ni/ sa mtshams med par khong du chud par byed do/ /
(4) I comprehend the realm of phenomena as having no boundary in order to have the vision of bodhisattva activities within the ocean of all worlds.
I realize that the reality realm is boundless, so as to show the practice of enlightening beings in all oceans of worlds.
de bzhin gshegs pa'i ye shes kyi dkyil 'khor tha mi dad pa la 'jug par bya ba'i phyir chos kyi dbyings ni/ ris tshad med par khong du chud par byed do/ /
(5) I comprehend the realm of phenomena as being without division in order to enter the undivided domain of wisdom of the tathāgatas.
I realize that the reality realm is uninterrupted, so as to enter the sphere of unfragmented knowledge of those who arrive at Thusness.

bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du sems can thams cad kyis rnam par dmigs pa'i de bzhin gshegs pa'i gsung gi dkyil 'khor la 'jug par bya ba'i phyir chos kyi dbyings ni/ rgyud kyi tshul gcig tu gyur par khong du chud par byed do/ /
(6) I comprehend the realm of phenomena as singleness in order to enter the domain of speech of the tathāgatas, which is perceived by all beings in accordance with their aspirations.
I realize that the reality realm is one, so as to enter the sphere of the voice of those who realize Thusness, which communicates to all sentient beings according to their mentalities.

'gro ba thams cad rnam par gdul ba'i mthar phyin pas de bzhin gshegs pa'i sngon gyi smon lam gyi mtha thug pa la 'jug par bya ba'i phyir chos kyi dbyings ni/ rang bzhin gyis rgya che bar khong du chud par byed do/ /

(7) I comprehend the realm of phenomena as having a nature of vastness[1533] in order to realize the ultimate conclusion of the past prayers of the tathāgatas to reach the conclusion of guiding all beings.
I realize that the reality realm is inherently pure, so as to realize the ultimate end of the past vow to guide all sentient beings to perfection.
byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po'i spyod pa 'byams klas pa la 'jug par bya ba'i phyir chos kyi dbyings ni/ 'gro ba thams cad la mnyam pa nyid du gyur par khong du chud par byed do/ /
(8) I comprehend the realm of phenomena as having the equality of all beings in order to realize the vast extent of completely good bodhisattva conduct.
I realize that the reality realm is equal in all worlds, so as to enter the range of the practice of universal good.
kun tu bzang po'i spyod pa'i rnam par 'phrul pa'i rgyan la 'jug par bya ba'i phyir chos kyi dbyings ni/ rgyan gcig tu gyur par khong du chud par byed do/ /
(9) I comprehend the realm of phenomena as a single adornment in order to comprehend the adornment of the miraculous manifestations of completely good conduct.
I realize that all realms of reality are adorned with one adornment, so as to comprehend the adornment of the miracle of the universally good enlightening being.
dge ba thams cad kyis chos kyi dbyings rgyas par dgang zhing rnam par dag par bya ba chud mi za ba'i chos can du bya ba'i phyir chos kyi dbyings ni/ thug pa med par khong du chud par byed do/ /
(10) I comprehend the realm of phenomena as being indestructible[1534] in order for the pure pervasion of the realm of phenomena by all good actions to have the nature of indestructibility.
I realize that the reality realm is imperishable, because of the imperishable nature of the purity of all good pervading the reality realm.

rigs kyi bu/ de ltar kho mo rnam pa bcu po de dag gis dge ba'i rtsa ba dang / tshogs thams cad yongs su bsags pa dang / sangs rgyas kyi bdag nyid che ba nyid la 'jug par bya ba dang / sangs rgyas kyi yul bsam gyis mi khyab pa rjes su rtogs par bya ba'i phyir chos kyi dbyings thams cad la rnam par blta'o/ /khong du chud pa dang / rjes su gzhol bar byed do; ;

“Noble one, I look upon, comprehend, and fathom the entire realm of phenomena in those ten ways in order to gather all the accumulations of good karma, in order to comprehend the greatness of the buddhas, and in order to realize the inconceivable scope of the buddhas.

Thus do I observe, approach, and proceed through the whole reality realm in terms of ten aspects, to accumulate all roots of goodness, to realize the greatness of buddhas, to arrive at the inconceivable sphere of buddhas.

rigs kyi bu/ gzhan yang kho mo de ltar de bzhin gshegs pa'i bdag nyid che ba nyid kyi rjes su 'brang ba'i yid la bya ba dang ldan pas gzungs kyi dkyil 'khor gyi rgyud stong phrag bcus sems can rnams la chos ston te/
“Moreover, noble one, I teach the Dharma to beings with my mind fixed upon the greatness of the tathāgatas and through ten-thousandfold domains of the activity of mental retention.

“Furthermore, I expound the Teaching to sentient beings by means of the operation of ten thousand spheres of mental command, with the attention on the greatness of Buddha in this way. I expound the Teaching to sentient beings by means of the operation of ten thousand spheres of mental command,
bcu gang zhe na/ 'di ltar
What are those ten? They are
beginning with,
chos rgya mtsho thams cad yang dag par 'du ba zhes bya ba'i gzungs kyi dkyil 'khor dang /
(1) the domain of mental retention called the gathering of the entire ocean of the Dharma,
the sphere of mental command called absorption in the ocean of all truths,
chos thams cad byin gyis rlob pa'i gzungs kyi dkyil 'khor dang /
(2) the domain of mental retention called the blessing of all dharmas,
chos kyi sprin thams cad yongs su 'dzin pa'i gzungs kyi dkyil 'khor dang /
(3) the domain of mental retention called the holding of all dharmas,
de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi dgongs pa sgron ma'i gzungs kyi dkyil 'khor dang /
(4) the domain of mental retention called the lamp of the intention of all the tathāgatas,
the sphere of mental command of light of remembrance of all buddhas,
sems can thams cad kyi las rgya mtsho rab tu snang bar byed pa'i snying po'i gzungs kyi dkyil 'khor dang /
(5) the domain of mental retention called the essence that illuminates the ocean of the karma of all beings,
the sphere of mental command containing light illumining the ocean of deeds of all sentient beings,
theg pa'i tshul rgya mtsho dri ma med pa thams cad la yang dag par gzhol ba'i gzungs kyi dkyil 'khor dang /
(6) the domain of mental retention called the fathoming of the entire stainless ocean of the ways of the yānas,[1535]
the sphere of pure mental command of absorption in the ocean of all means of liberation,
sangs rgyas rgya mtsho thams cad kyi sgron ma'i snying po'i gzungs kyi dkyil 'khor dang /
de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi mtshan gyi 'khor lo'i glong rab tu sgrog pa'i gzungs kyi dkyil 'khor dang /
(7) the domain of mental retention called the proclamation of the turning[1536] of the wheel of the names of all the buddhas,
the sphere of mental command uttering the names of all buddhas,
dus gsum gyi sangs rgyas kyi sngon gyi smon lam rgya mtsho bstan pa la yang dag par gzhol ba'i gzungs kyi dkyil 'khor dang /
(8) the domain of mental retention called the fathoming of the teaching of the ocean of the past prayers of the buddhas in the three times,
the sphere of mental command of absorption in manifestation of the ocean of past vows of all buddhas,
chos thams cad la mngon par 'khyil ba'i shugs drag po'i gzungs kyi dkyil 'khor dang /
(9) the domain of mental retention called the intense power of the gathering of all dharmas, and
the sphere of mental command of swift turning of the attention to all truths,
thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi shugs rab tu 'byung ba zhes bya ba'i gzungs kyi dkyil 'khor dang /
(10) the domain of mental retention called the arising of the power of omniscience.
and the sphere of mental command called light of absorption in omniscience.
rigs kyi bu/ gzungs kyi dkyil 'khor bcu po de dag la sogs pa gzungs kyi dkyil 'khor gyi rgyud stong phrag bcus sems can rnams la chos ston to/ /
“Noble one, I teach the Dharma to beings through these ten domains of mental retention and the rest of the ten thousand domains of mental retention.
rigs kyi bu/ gzhan yang kho mo ni/ thos pa'i shes rab kyis sems can rnams la chos ston to/ / bsam pa'i shes rab dang / bsgoms pa'i shes rab kyis sems can rnams la chos ston te/

“Moreover, noble one, I teach the Dharma to beings through the wisdom that comes from hearing the Dharma. I teach the Dharma to beings through the wisdom from contemplation and the wisdom from meditation.
“Moreover, I teach sentient beings with wisdom consisting of learning, wisdom consisting of thinking, and wisdom consisting of practice.
srid pa'i rgyud gcig las kyang brtsams shing sems can rnams la chos ston to/ / srid pa'i rgyud rgya mtsho thams cad las kyang brtsams shing sems can rnams la chos ston to/ /
“I teach the Dharma to beings beginning with one existence. I teach the Dharma to beings beginning with all existences.
I teach sentient beings about the process of one existence, and I teach sentient beings about the processes of all existences.

de bzhin gshegs pa gcig gi mtshan gyi 'khor lo rgya mtsho las kyang brtsams shing chos ston to/ / de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi mtshan gyi 'khor lo rgya mtsho las kyang brtsams shing chos ston to; ;
“I teach the Dharma to beings beginning with the ocean of the wheel of names of one tathāgata. I teach the Dharma to beings beginning with the ocean of the wheel of names of all tathāgatas.
I teach about the ocean of names of one buddha, I teach about the oceans of names of all buddhas.
'jig rten gyi khams rgya mtsho gcig las kyang brtsams shing chos ston to/ / 'jig rten gyi khams rgya mtsho thams cad las kyang brtsams shing chos ston to/ /
“I teach the Dharma to beings beginning with one ocean of world realms. I teach the Dharma to beings beginning with all oceans of world realms.
I teach about one ocean of worlds, I teach about all oceans of worlds.
sangs rgyas gcig gis lung bstan pa las kyang brtsams shing chos ston to/ / de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyis lung bstan pa rgya mtsho las kyang brtsams shing chos ston to; ;
“I teach the Dharma to beings beginning with the ocean of prophecies of one buddha. I teach the Dharma to beings beginning with the ocean of prophecies of all tathāgatas.
I teach about the ocean of predictions of enlightenment of one buddha, I teach about the oceans of predictions of enlightenment of all buddhas.

de bzhin gshegs pa gcig gi 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor rgya mtsho las kyang brtsams shing chos ston to/ / de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor rgya mtsho las kyang brtsams shing chos ston to/ /

“I teach the Dharma to beings beginning with the ocean of the community of the followers of one tathāgata. I teach the Dharma to beings beginning with the ocean of the communities of the followers of all tathāgatas.
I teach about the ocean of audiences of one buddha, I teach about the oceans of audiences of all buddhas.
de bzhin gshegs pa gcig gi chos kyi 'khor lo las kyang brtsams shing chos ston to/ / de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi chos kyi 'khor lo rgya mtsho las kyang brtsams shing chos ston to/ /
“I teach the Dharma to beings beginning with the Dharma wheel of one tathāgata. I teach the Dharma to beings beginning with the ocean of the Dharma wheels of all tathāgatas.
I teach about the cycle of teachings of one buddha, I teach about the oceans of cycles of teachings of all buddhas.
mdo sde gcig las kyang brtsams shing chos ston to/ / de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi chos kyi 'khor lo la yang dag par gzhol ba'i mdo sde las kyang brtsams shing chos ston to/ /
“I teach the Dharma to beings beginning with one sūtra. I teach the Dharma to beings beginning with the sūtras that are present within the Dharma wheels of all tathāgatas.
I teach about one scripture, I teach about the scriptures containing the cycles of teachings of all buddhas.

de bzhin gshegs pa gcig gi 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor kun nas 'dus pa las kyang brtsams shing chos ston to/ / de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor kun nas 'dus pa rgya mtsho las kyang brtsams shing chos ston to/ /

“I teach the Dharma to beings beginning with the gathering of the community of followers of one tathāgata. I teach the Dharma to beings beginning with the ocean of the gatherings of the communities of followers of all tathāgatas.
I teach about one gathering of an audience of a buddha, I teach about the oceans of audiences of all buddhas.
thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi sems gcig las kyang brtsams shing chos ston to/ / byang chub kyi sems kyi yan lag rgya mtsho thams cad las kyang brtsams shing chos ston to/ /
“I teach the Dharma to beings beginning with one aspiration to omniscience. I teach the Dharma to beings beginning with the entire ocean of the aspects of the aspiration to enlightenment.
I teach about one thought of omniscience, I teach about the oceans of all elements of determination for enlightenment.
theg pa gcig las kyang brtsams shing chos ston to/ / theg pa thams cad kyi 'byung ba rgya mtsho las kyang brtsams shing chos ston to/ /
“I teach the Dharma to beings beginning with one yāna. I teach the Dharma to beings beginning with the ocean of the arising of all yānas.
I teach about one vehicle of emancipation, I teach about the oceans of all vehicles of emancipation.

rigs kyi bu/ de ltar kho mos bstan pa'i tshul mngon par sgrub pa brjod du med pas sems can rnams la chos ston te/ rigs kyi bu/ de ltar kho mo chos kyi dbyings kyi tshul tha mi dad pa'i de bzhin gshegs pa rgya mtsho la 'jug cing sems can thams cad la chos ston pas bla na med pa'i yongs su bsdu ba byed cing / byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po'i spyod pa la phyi ma'i mtha'i mur thug pa'i bskal pa rgya mtshor gnas par bya bas byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa sgra yid du 'ong ba dang / rnam par 'phrul pa zab mo la 'jug pa 'di la sems kyi skad cig re re zhing rnam par 'phel ba'i rnam par thar pa'i yul sgom pa'i tshul gyis yongs su sgom ste/ rnam par thar pa'i yul sgom pa'i tshul re res kyang sems kyi skad cig re re la chos kyi dbyings thams cad du rgyas par 'gengs so/ /

“Noble one, in that way, I teach the Dharma to beings through comprehending that in the way of the realm of the Dharma there is no differentiation in the ocean of the tathāgatas. Thereby I create an unsurpassable accumulation of the Dharma, continue with the bodhisattva’s completely good conduct throughout all future kalpas, and meditate on this bodhisattva liberation called the entry into beautiful sounds and profound manifestations, expanding with each instant of mind the way of meditation on the vista of this liberation, with each instant of mind expanding throughout the entire realm of phenomena the way of meditation on the vista of this liberation.”

I teach sentient beings in untold ways such as these. “Entry into the oceans of those who arrive at Thusness, identical to the structures of the reality realm, taking care of sentient beings in the highest spiritual way of expounding the Teaching to them, living by the practice of universally good enlightening beings for endless eons, I cultivate this enlightening liberation of entry into the profound miracle of pleasing sound, by expanding it in every moment of consciousness, by the means of actualizing the sphere of liberation; and I pervade all realms of reality in every moment of thought with each means of actualizing the sphere of liberation.”
nor bzang gis smras pa/ lha mo/ byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa de de ltar zab pa ngo mtshar chen/ 'phags ma/ khyod kyis byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa 'di brnyes nas ji srid cig lags/
Sudhana said, “Goddess, it is wonderful that this bodhisattva liberation is so profound. Āryā, how long has it been since you attained this bodhisattva liberation?”
Sudhana said, “This enlightening liberation is marvelous. How long ago did you attain it?”

smras pa/ rigs kyi bu/ sngon 'das pa'i dus bskal ba 'jig rten gyi rgyud kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed 'das pa'i pha rol cig tu 'jig rten gyi khams chos kyi 'od 'phro ba'i grong khyer dpal gyi sprin ces bya ba rin po che'i spos thams cad dang ldan pa/ gling bzhi pa'i 'jig rten gyi khams rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi sprin la blangs pa/ de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi sngon gyi smon lam dbyangs su sgrog pa'i pad+mos mtshams rnam par brgyan pa/ lhun sems can thams cad kyi las rgya mtshos byung ba'i nor bu rin po che'i rgyal po rgya mtsho las grub pa/ pad+mo chen po'i dbyibs su 'dug pa/ rnam par dag cing kun nas nyon mongs pa/ me tog gi khor yug ri rab kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyis kun nas bskor ba/ spos kyi rin po che ri rab kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi rgyan ri rab ltar mngon par 'phags pa dang ldan pa/ gling bzhi pa chen po ri rab kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi rgyan dang ldan pa/ gling bzhi pa re re zhing yang grong rdal bye ba khrag khrig brgya stong brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa dang ldan pa byung ngo/ /

She replied, “Noble one, in the past, in time gone by, beyond as many kalpas as there are atoms in a world realm, there was a world realm called Dharmārcinagarameghā, which had as many clouds of perfumed jewels as there are atoms in a four-continent world realm. It was bordered with lotuses that had been proclaimed in the past prayers of all the tathāgatas. Its body was formed from the ocean as the king of precious jewels, having arisen from the ocean of the karma of all beings. It had the shape of a great lotus. It was both pure and defiled.[1537] It had as many encircling Cakravāla mountain ranges of lotuses as there are atoms in Sumeru. It was adorned by as many risen Sumerus of perfumed jewels as there are atoms in Sumeru. It was adorned by as many great four-continent worlds as there are atoms in Sumeru. In each four-continent world there was an anabhilāpyānabhilāpya of quintillions of cities.

The goddess said, “Many eons ago there was world called Multitude of Cities of Spiritual Lights, set on a network of lofty fragrant jewel mountains, as many as atoms in four continents, arrayed with lotus flowers intoning the past vows of all buddhas, composed of multitudes of jewels produced by the deeds of all sentient beings, shaped like a huge lotus, pure with some defilement, encircled by as many masses of flowers as atoms in a mountain, adorned by lofty polar mountains of fragrant jewels, as many as atoms in a polar mountain, and with as many sets of four continents as atoms in a polar mountain. On each continent were untold trillions of cities.

rigs kyi bu/ 'jig rten gyi khams de'i bskal pa mdog dri ma med pa'i 'od ces bya ba byung ste/ bskal pa de la de bzhin gshegs pa ri rab kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed byung ngo/ / 'jig rten gyi khams chos kyi 'od 'phro ba'i grong khyer dpal gyi sprin gyi gling bzhi pa dbu ma rgyal mtshan sna tshogs zhes bya ba byung ste/ de'i dbus na rgyal po'i gnas rin chan me tog kun tu snang ba zhes bya ba yod par gyur te/

“Noble one, there was in that world realm a kalpa called Vimalābha.[1538] During that kalpa there appeared as many tathāgatas as there are atoms in Sumeru. In the center of that world realm called Dharmārcinagarameghā there was a four-continent world called Vicitradhvaja, in the center of which was the royal capital called Samantaratnakusumaprabhā.

“In that world there was an age called Pure Light, in which there arose as many buddhas as atoms in a polar mountain. In the middle of the world was a set of four continents called Resplendent Banner, in the middle of which was a metropolis called Omnipresent Jewel Flower Light,

rgyal po'i gnas de dang ha cang yang mi ring ba zhig na snying po byang chub chos kyi rgyal po'i pho brang rab tu snang ba zhes bya ba yod de/ snying po byang chub de la de bzhin gshegs pa ri rab kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed po de dag gi bskal pa'i dang po la de bzhin gshegs pa chos rgya mtsho thams cad kyi dbyangs 'od kyi rgyal po zhes bya ba byung ste/

“Not far from that royal capital was a bodhimaṇḍa called Dharmarājabhavanapratibhāsa. At that bodhimaṇḍa there appeared the Tathāgata Sarvadharmasāgaranirghoṣaprabharāja, the first of the tathāgatas of that kalpa, who were as numerous as the atoms in Sumeru.

not too far from which was an enlightenment site called Image of the Abode of a Spiritual Sovereign. At that site a buddha named Illuminating King Voicing the Ocean of All Truths arose, the first of the buddhas of that age.

de'i tshe 'khor los bsgyur ba'i rgyal po nyi ma ltar bzhin mdog dri ma med pa zhes bya ba byung nas des bcom ldan 'das de bzhin gshegs pa chos rgya mtsho thams cad kyi dbyangs 'od kyi rgyal po las mdo sde chos thams cad kyi glong rgya mtsho zhes bya ba yongs su bzung ste/ bzung nas kyang chos kyi 'khor lo rjes su bskor to/ / yongs su mya ngan las 'das nas kyang rab tu byung ste bstan pa yongs su bzung ngo/ /

“At that time there was a cakravartin king by the name of Vimalavakrabhānuprabha, who received from the Tathāgata Sarvadharmasāgaranirghoṣaprabharāja the sūtra called The Ocean of All Dharmas. After he had received it, after the Dharma wheel was turned, and after the passing into nirvāṇa, the king entered homelessness and possessed all the teaching.

At that time there was a monarch named Radiantly Pure Countenance, who received from that buddha a scripture called Ocean of All Truths and followed it. “After that buddha passed away, the king left home and preserved the buddha’s teachings.

bstan pa nub tu cha ste/ bstan pa yang stong du gyes/ chos bstan pa shin tu bstan pa'i tshul ni/ brgya phrag bcur gyur/ rnyog pa'i bskal pa bar ma ni/ nye bar gnas par gyur pa'i che sems can las dang nyon mongs pa'i sgrib pas bsgribs pa/ 'thab mo dang / rtsod pa dang / dkrugs ma la zhugs par gyur pa dang / dge slong sangs rgyas kyi bstan pa'i yon tan don du mi gnyer cing yul gyi dga' ba lhur len par gyur pa/ rgyal po dang rkun po'i gtam la zhugs pa/ bud med dang / yul dang / rgya mtsho'i gtam la mos pa/ 'jig rten rgyang pan pa'i tshig la zhugs pa rnams yongs su skyo ba bskyed pa'i phyir kye ma'o; ;

“At the time when the teaching was reaching its end, it divided into a thousand teachings, and in each teaching there was a division into a thousand ways of teaching. During the intermediate kalpa of deterioration, beings were obscured by the obscurations of karma and kleśas, and they were engaged in fighting, quarreling, and disruption. Bhikṣus were not concerned with the good qualities of the Buddha’s teachings but were dedicated to delighting in the objects of the senses, engaged in conversations about kings and thieves, were interested in stories about women and countries and oceans, and used the words of the Lokāyatas.

At the time of the ending of the teaching, when it was divided into a thousand sects, with a thousand different explanations of the doctrine, and uninterrupted degeneracy of the age was imminent, in order to shake up the people shrouded by the barriers of afflictions and contentious quarrelsome mendicants, who were not seeking the virtues taught by the buddha but were wholly devoted to enjoyment of sense objects, addicted to talk of kings and thieves, addicted to talk of women, lands, and seas, addicted to materialistic thought and conversation,

bskal pa du mar yongs su bsgrubs pa'i chos kyi sgron ma chen po ni/ nub par gyur ma khad do/ / zhes chos dang ldan pa'i 'o dod bos te yongs su skyo bar 'gyur ba'i gtam byas nas de steng gi nam mkha'i dbyings su ta la bdun tsam du mngon par 'phags nas 'od 'phro ba kha dog mtha' yas pa'i sprin rab tu bkye ste/ 'od zer gyi dra ba'i rgyan chen po kha dog sna tshogs dang ldan pa bkye nas 'od kha dog du ma dang ldan pas 'jig rten gyi nyon mongs pa'i gdung ba zhi bar byas te sems can mtha' dang dbus med pa dag kyang byang chub la rab tu bkod do/ / de bzhin gshegs pa'i bstan pa de yang phyir gsal bar byas te lo stong phrag drug cur gnas par gyur to/ /

“The follower of the Dharma cried out, ‘Oh! The great lamp of the Dharma, which has been established for many kalpas, is close to being extinguished!’ Having said these sad words, he rose into the air to the height of seven palm trees and emanated clouds of light of infinite colors. When he had emanated that great display of a net of light rays of various colors, those multicolored lights pacified the torment of the kleśas in the world and established beings without end or center in enlightenment, which revived the teachings of the tathāgata so that it remained for a further sixty thousand years.

the renunciant king, a true follower of the religion, warned them, ‘Alas! The torch of the great teaching, which was developed over many eons, is going to die out.’ Then he rose into the sky to the height of seven palm trees, emanated clouds of flames of infinite colors, produced great networks of multicolored lights from his body, extinguished the burning of afflictions in the world with multicolored light, and directed infinitely many sentient beings toward enlightenment. The buddha’s teaching was thereby rekindled and remained in the world for another sixty thousand years.

de'i tshe 'khor los bsgyur ba'i rgyal po nyi ma ltar bzhin mdog dri ma med pa de nyid kyi bu mo dge slong ma chos kyi 'khor los sprul pa'i 'od ces bya ba dge slong ma brgya phrag stong gi 'khor dang ldan pa byung ste/ des yongs su skyo bar 'gyur ba'i sgra de thos nas cho 'phrul chen po de mthong ste/ 'khor dang bcas pas byang chub tu sems bskyed nas dge slong ma brgya phrag stong po de dag kyang bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub las phyir mi ldog par byas te/ de bzhin gshegs pa mngon du 'gyur ba la yang dag par gzhol ba zhes bya ba'i ting nge 'dzin kyang rab tu thob par gyur te/ /de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi chos kyi 'khor los sprul pa'i 'od ces bya ba'i gzungs kyang rab tu thob bo/ / chos rgya mtsho'i tshul thams cad la 'jug pa zhes bya ba'i shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa yang rab tu thob par gyur to/ / dge slong mchos kyi 'khor los sprul pa'i 'od kyis kyang de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi bstan pa las byung ba'i 'od kyi sgron ma zhes bya ba'i ting nge 'dzin dang / byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa sgra yid du 'ong ba dang / rnam par 'phrul pa zab mo la 'jug pa 'di yang shin tu phra zhing 'jam pa'i tshul du rab tu thob par gyur te/ de thob pas de la de bzhin gshegs pa chos rgya mtsho thams cad kyi dbyangs 'od kyi rgyal po'i rnam par 'phrul pa de dag thams cad kyang mngon du gyur to/ /

“At that time, the cakravartin king Vimalavakrabhānuprabha’s daughter, a bhikṣuṇī by the name of Dharmacakranirmāṇaprabhā, had an entourage of a hundred thousand bhikṣuṇīs. When she heard those sad words and saw that miraculous manifestation, she and her entourage developed the aspiration for enlightenment, and the hundred thousand bhikṣuṇīs became irreversible on the path to the highest, complete enlightenment and attained the samādhi called the manifest presence of the tathāgatas. They also obtained the power of mental retention called the light emanated from the Dharma wheel of all the tathāgatas. They also attained the perfection of wisdom called the entry into all the ways of the ocean of the Dharma. The bhikṣuṇī Dharmacakranirmāṇaprabhā attained the samādhi called the lamp of the light that arises from the teachings of all the tathāgatas, and she attained in a subtle and gentle way this bodhisattva liberation called the entry into beautiful sounds and profound manifestations. When she had attained that, she directly perceived all the miraculous manifestations of the Tathāgata Sarvadharmasāgaranirghoṣaprabharāja.

“At that time there was also a nun named Light of Projections of the Wheel of the Teaching. She was the daughter of that king Radiantly Pure Countenance, and she had a retinue of a hundred thousand nuns. Hearing that rousing speech and seeing that great miraculous performance, she and her retinue had been inspired to seek enlightenment. Furthermore, those hundred thousand nuns became irreversible in progress toward supreme perfect enlightenment: they attained a concentration called ‘coming into existence in the presence of those who have arrived at Thusness,’ and they attained a mental command called ‘adamantine light of the teachings of all buddhas,’ and a perfection of wisdom called ‘entry into the principles of the ocean of all truths.’ The nun Light of Projections of the Wheel of the Teaching attained a concentration called ‘lamp illumining the source of the teachings of all buddhas,’ as well as this subtle, gentle enlightening liberation ‘entry into the profound miracle of pleasing sound,’ after which all the miracles of the buddha Illuminating King Voicing the Ocean of All Truths became visible to her.

rigs kyi bu/ de la ji snyam du sems/ de'i tshe de'i dus na 'khor los bsgyur ba'i rgyal po nyi ma ltar bzhin mdog dri ma med pa zhes bya ba de bzhin gshegs pa chos rgya mtsho thams cad kyi dbyangs 'od kyi rgyal po'i bstan pa la rab tu byung ste chos kyi 'khor lo rjes su bskor ba dang / yongs su mya ngan las 'das nas kyang bstan pa nub tu cha ba'i che dang dus na bstan pa yongs su 'dzin cing chos kyi sgron ma chen po 'bar bar byed pa de gzhan zhig yin pa snyam du sems na ni/ rigs kyi bu/ khyod kyis de lta mi blta ste/ byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po ni/ de'i tshe de'i dus na 'khor los bsgyur ba'i rgyal po nyi ma ltar bzhin mdog dri ma med pa zhes bya bar gyur to/ /

“Noble one, what do you think? At that time, in that time, who do you think was the cakravartin king Vimalavakrabhānuprabha, who entered homelessness in the teaching of the Tathāgata Sarvadharmasāgaranirghoṣaprabharāja and, after the turning of the wheel of the Dharma and the passing into nirvāṇa, when the teachings were coming to an end, lit the Dharma lamp of holding the teaching? Noble one, do not think that he was anyone else; at that time, in that time, the bodhisattva Samantabhadra was the cakravartin king Vimalavakrabhānuprabha.

“What do you think—was the king of that time, who went forth into the teaching of the buddha Illuminating King Voicing the Ocean of All Truths, followed the buddha’s teaching, sustained the teaching after the buddha’s demise when it was dying out, and kindled the torch of the teaching, anyone else? You should not see it this way. It was none other than Samantabhadra, the universally good enlightening being, who was that king Radiantly Pure Countenance.

rigs kyi bu/ de la ji snyam du sems/ de'i tshe de'i dus na 'khor los bsgyur ba'i rgyal po nyi ma ltar bzhin mdog dri ma med pa'i bu mo dge slong ma chos kyi 'khor lo sprul pa'i 'od ces bya ba/ dge slong ma brgya phrag stong gi 'khor dang ldan pa byung ba de gzhan zhig yin pa snyam du sems na ni; de ltar mi blta ste/ kho mo ni/ de'i tshe de'i dus na/ dge slong ma chos kyi 'khor los sprul pa'i 'od ces bya bar gyur te/ de ltar kho mos de bzhin gshegs pa chos rgya mtsho thams cad kyi dbyangs 'od kyi rgyal po'i bstan pa'ang yongs su bzung ngo/ / dge slong ma brgya phrag stong po de dag kyang bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub las phyir mi ldog par byas te/ de bzhin gshegs pa mngon du gyur pa la yang dag par gzhol ba'i ting nge 'dzin la'ang rab tu bkod do/ / de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi 'khor los sprul pa'i 'od kyi gzungs dang / chos rgya mtsho'i tshul thams cad la 'jug pa'i shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa la'ang rab tu bkod do/ /

“Noble one, what do you think? At that time, in that time, who do you think was the bhikṣuṇī Dharmacakranirmāṇaprabhā, the daughter of the cakravartin king Vimalavakrabhānuprabha, who had an entourage of a hundred thousand bhikṣuṇīs? Noble one, do not think that she was anyone else; at that time, in that time, I was the bhikṣuṇī Dharmacakranirmāṇaprabhā. In that way, I held the teaching of the Tathāgata Sarvadharmasāgaranirghoṣaprabharāja. I caused those hundred thousand bhikṣuṇīs to progress irreversibly toward the highest, complete enlightenment. I established them in the samādhi called the manifest presence of the tathāgatas. I also established them in the power of mental retention called the light emanated from the Dharma wheel of all tathāgatas and the perfection of wisdom called the entry into all the ways of the ocean of the Dharma.

And do you think the king’s daughter, who became a nun, accompanied by a hundred thousand nuns, was anyone else? Do not see it that way. It was I myself who was that nun at that time. I preserved the teaching of that buddha, and I made those hundred thousand nuns irreversible in their progress toward supreme perfect enlightenment, I established them in the concentration ‘coming into existence in the presence of those who have arrived at Thusness,’ I established them in the mental command ‘adamantine light of the teachings of all buddhas’ and the perfection of wisdom ‘entry into the principles of the ocean of all truths.’
de bzhin gshegs pa de'i 'og tu kho mos de bzhin gshegs pa chos dri ma med pa'i ri bo ye shes kyi rtse mo'i 'od cas bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“After that tathāgata, I venerated the Tathāgata Vimaladharmaparvatajñānaśikharābha.
“After that I learned from a buddha named Light of the Peak of Knowledge of the Mountain of the Undefiled Teaching,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa chos kyi dkyil 'khor gyi 'od rab tu snang ba'i gtsug phud ces bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
After him, I venerated the Tathāgata Dharmamaṇḍalāvabhāsaprabhacūḍa.[1539]
then Crest of Light,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa chos kyi nyi ma dpal gyi sprin ces bya ba bsnyen bkur to; ;

then Multitudes of Lights of the Sun of the Teaching,
