After him, I venerated the Tathāgata Sarvadharmasamādhiprabhaghoṣa.
then Light and Sound of Concentration on All Truths,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa chos kyi sgo'i dbyangs mang po'i mdzod ces bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
After him, I venerated the Tathāgata Dvārasvaraprabhūtakośa.
then Mine of Initiatory Sounds,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa chos 'bar ba'i 'od 'phro rgya mtsho'i dbyangs zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
After him, I venerated the Tathāgata Dharmajvalanārciḥsāgaraghoṣa.
then Sound of the Ocean of Blazing Flames of the Teaching,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa dus gsum gyi mtshan rab tu snang ba'i gzi brjid ces bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
After him, I venerated the Tathāgata Tryadhvalakṣaṇapratibhāsatejas.
then Light of Reflections of the Appearances of Past, Present, and Future,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa chos kyi dkyil 'khor dpal gyi ri bo snang ba'i 'od ces bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
After him, I venerated the Tathāgata Dharmamaṇḍalaśrīśikharābhaprabha.
then Shining Light of the Highest Splendor of the Sphere of the Teaching,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa chos kyi dbyings kyi seng+ge'i 'od ces bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
After him, I venerated the Tathāgata Dharmadhātusiṃhaprabha.
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa rnam par snang mdzad dpal gyi ri rab ces bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
After him, I venerated the Tathāgata Vairocanaśrīsumeru.[1540]
then Powerful Light in the Realm of Reality,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa ting nge 'dzin rgya mtsho thams cad snang bar mdzad pa'i seng+ge zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
After him, I venerated the Tathāgata Sarvasamādhisāgarāvabhāsasiṃha.
then Lion Manifesting the Ocean of All Concentrations,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa ye shes kyi 'od kun tu snang ba zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
After him, I venerated the Tathāgata Samantajñānaprabhāsa.
then Light of Total Knowledge,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa shes rab kyi 'od kun tu gsal ba chos kyi grong khyer rab tu snang ba zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
After him, I venerated the Tathāgata Samantaprajñābhadharmanagarapradīpa.
then Lamp of the City of Reality with the Light of Universal Wisdom.
de ltar rigs kyi bu / sangs rgyas brgya po 'di dag la sogs pa bskal pa mdog dri ma med pa'i 'od ces bya ba la de bzhin gshegs pa ri rab kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed cig byung ste/
“In that way, noble one, there were these hundred buddhas and the other tathāgatas, as numerous as the atoms in Sumeru, who appeared in the kalpa called Vimalābha.
“In that age Pure Light, as many buddhas as atoms in the polar mountain appeared, beginning with these.

rigs kyi bu/ de bzhin gshegs pa ri rab kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed po de dag thams cad kyi tha mar de bzhin gshegs pa chos kyi dbyings kyi grong khyer ye shes kyi 'od kyis rab tu snang ba'i rgyal po zhes bya ba byung bar gyur te/
“Noble one, the last of those tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms in Sumeru was a tathāgata by the name of Dharmadhātunagarābhajñānapradīparāja.
The last of them was a buddha named Supreme Lamp of Knowledge Lighting the City of the Reality Realm.

de ltar rigs kyi bu; kho mos de bzhin gshegs pa ri rab kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed po de dag las chos kyi rgya mtsho thams cad kyi dbyings kyi 'od kyi rgyal po zhes bya ba la sogs pa tha ma chos kyi dbyings kyi grong khyer ye shes kyis rab tu snang ba'i bar de dag thams cad kho mos mchod do/ / de bzhin gshegs pa de dag thams cad la kho mos rim gror byas so/ / thams cad kyi chos bstan pa yang thos so/ / de bzhin gshegs pa de dag thams cad kyi bstan pa la yang kho mo rab tu byung ngo/ / de bzhin gshegs pa de dag thams cad kyi bstan pa yang kho mos yongs su bzung ngo/ / byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa sgra yid du 'ong ba dang / rnam par 'phrul pa zab mo la 'jug pa 'di yang de bzhin gshegs pa de dag thams cad las thob pa'i tshul rnam pa sna tshogs kyis rab tu thob bo/ de bzhin gshegs pa de dag thams cad kyi zhabs kyi drung du'ang kho mos sems can rgya mtsho mtha' dang dbus med pa yongs su smin par byas so/ /

“In that way, noble one, I made offerings to those tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms in Sumeru, beginning with Sarvadharmasāgaranirghoṣaprabharāja and ending with Dharmadhātunagarābhajñānapradīparāja. I attended to all those tathāgatas. I heard the Dharma taught by them all. I entered homelessness in the teachings of all those tathāgatas. I possessed the teachings of all those tathāgatas. I obtained the bodhisattva liberation called the entry into beautiful sounds and profound manifestations from all those tathāgatas, obtaining it in various ways. At the feet of all those tathāgatas I ripened an ocean of beings without edge or center.

I served all those buddhas, from the first to the last, and I listened to their teachings, and left society to delve into all their teachings. I kept all their instructions in mind, and from all of them I attained this enlightening liberation of entry into the profound miracle of pleasing sound, by various methods of attainment, and I matured infinitely many sentient beings in the presence of all those buddhas.
de tshun chad du bskal pa sangs rgyas kyi zhing gi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed la de bzhin gshegs pa ji snyed cig byung bar gyur pa de dag thams cad ni/ kho mos chos kyi nan tan gyis mchod pa byas te/
“Since then, in practicing the Dharma I have made offerings to as many buddhas as have appeared throughout as many kalpas as there are atoms in a buddha realm.
Since then I served all the buddhas that have emerged in as many eons as atoms in a buddha-land by putting their teachings into practice.

rigs kyi bu/ de phyin chad du kho mos sems can 'khor ba'i mun pa na 'khod cing mi shes pa'i gnyid kyis log pa rnams kyi mel tshe byas so/ / de dag gi sems kyi grong khyer yang yongs su bsrungs so/ / de dag khams gsum gyi grong khyer nas gyen du bskyod cing thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi grong rdal du'ang rab tu bkod do/ /

“Noble one, during that time, I have watched over beings as they slept in ignorance in the darkness of saṃsāra. I have guarded the cities of their minds. I have brought them up out of the city of the three realms and brought them into the city of omniscience.

Thenceforth I have been awake in the midst of beings asleep in the slumber of nescience during the night of mundane routines; I have guarded the city of their minds, removed them from the city of the triple world, and settled them in the city of the way of omniscience.

rigs kyi bu/ kho mos byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa sgra yid du 'ong ba dang / rnam par 'phrul pa zab mo la 'jug pa 'jig rten gyi tshig kyal ba rnam par zlog pa/ gnyis su smra ba med pa la rab tu 'god pa/ bden pa la rab tu gzhog pa'i mthar phyin pa 'di shes par zad na/ kho mos byang chub sems dpa' dag gi lam gyi rang bzhin thams cad thogs pa med par shes pa/ sems kyi skad cig re re la chos thams cad mngon par 'tshang rgya bar dbang bsgyur ba/ sems can thams cad kyi sgra skad dang tshig rgya mtsho la zhugs pa/ skad rgya mtsho thams cad mngon par 'du bya ba la mkhas pa/ chos thams cad kyi grangs dang / ming rgya mtsho'i tshul dang chog la mkhas pa/ chos thams cad la yang dag par gzhol ba'i gzungs rgya mtsho la dbang bsgyur ba/ sems can thams cad kyi bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du chos kyi sprin mngon par sgrub pa la mkhas pa/ sems can thams cad yongs su smin par bya ba dang gdul bar spyod pa'i mthar phyin par byed pa de dag gi spyod pa shes pa'am/ yon tan brjod pa'am/ sems can thams cad yongs su sdud pa'i nan tan shes par bya ba'am/ byang chub sems dpa'i lam bla na med par brtsams pa'i sbyor ba'am/ byang chub sems dpa'i ye shes shin tu phra ba khong du chud pa'am/ byang chub sems dpa'i chos kyi gter dang / mdzod rnam par 'byed pa'i khyu mchog gi mthu'am/ byang chub sems dpa'i chos kyi gtam la seng+ge'i khri yongs su gnan par bya ba shes par nus re ska na/

“Noble one, I know only this bodhisattva liberation called the entry into beautiful sounds and profound manifestations, which prevents meaningless worldly talk, establishes speech that is not dishonest, and concludes with it being firmly established in truth. How could I know the conduct or describe the qualities of bodhisattvas who know without impediment all languages,[1541] who understand all Dharma in each instant of mind, who comprehend all the words and languages of all beings, who are skilled in accumulating the entire ocean of languages, who are skilled in the ways and practices of an ocean of numbers and terms in all Dharmas, who have the power of an ocean of mental retention that engages with all the Dharma, who are skilled in creating clouds of Dharma that accord with the dispositions of all beings, and who have fully attained ripening and guiding all beings? How could I know their practice of gathering all beings, their application to undertaking supreme bodhisattva activity,[1542] their comprehension of very subtle bodhisattva knowledge, their power of supremacy in opening the treasures and treasuries of bodhisattva Dharma, or their ascending the lion throne for teaching the bodhisattva Dharma?

“I just know this enlightening liberation of entry into the miracle of pleasing sound, which stops mixed-up worldly talk and does not use duplicitous speech, ultimately leading to truth. How can I know the practice or tell of the virtues of the enlightening beings who have unobstructed knowledge of the essential nature of all speech, who command awareness of all realities in each moment of thought, who comprehend the utterances of all beings, who are familiar with the patterns of thought of all beings, who know the ways of classification and naming of all things, who are masters of the ocean of mental command of all truths, who are skilled in producing teachings adapted to the mentalities of all beings, who endeavor to guide all beings to perfection—how can I know their accomplishment in taking care of all beings, or know their efforts applied to undertaking the supreme works of enlightening beings, their attainment of subtle knowledge of enlightening beings, their multifaceted powers of the mine of practice of enlightening beings, or their accession to the lion throne of those who tell of the deeds of enlightening beings?
de ci'i phyir zhe na/ skyes bu dam pa de dag ni/ chos thams cad kyi sa'i dkyil 'khor gyi gzungs yongs su gnon pa sha stag go /
“Why is that? It is because those excellent beings have all attained the retention of the domain of the level of the entire Dharma.
Why do I say this? They are people of truth who have entered mental command of all stages of the Teaching.

song rigs kyi bu/ bcom ldan 'das rnam par snang mdzad kyi zhabs kyi drung 'di nyid du mtshan mo'i lha mo shing thams cad kyi me tog rgyas pas bde bar gnas pa zhes bya ba 'dug ste/ kho mo dang rgyang mi ring ba zhig na 'dug gi /de'i gan du song la ji ltar byang chub sems dpa' rnams thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du slob pa dang / ji ltar nan tan du byed cing / sems can thams cad thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du 'god par byed pa dris shig /

“Depart, noble one. Here at the feet of the Bhagavat Vairocana, there is the goddess of the night who has the name Sarvavṛkṣpraphullanasukhasaṃvāsā. She is not far from me, so go to her and ask her, ‘How should bodhisattvas[1543] train in omniscience? How should they practice it so as to bring all beings to omniscience?’ ”

“Right here in the presence of Vairocana Buddha there is a night goddess named Sarvavrikshapraphullanasukhasamvasa, who is sitting next to me. Ask her how an enlightening being is to learn omniscience and how one is to practice so as to lead all sentient beings to omniscience.”

de nas mtshan mo'i lha mo grong khyer thams cad srung ba 'byung ba'i gzi brjid dpal gyis de'i tshe byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa sgra yid du 'ong ba dang / rnam par 'phrul ba zab mo la 'jug pa 'di nyid brnan te bstan pa'i phyir tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la tshigs su bcad de smras pa/

Then at that time, the night goddess Sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśrī, in order to teach further the bodhisattva liberation called the entry into beautiful sounds and profound manifestations, recited these verses to Sudhana, the head merchant’s son:
Then the night goddess Sarvanagararakshasambhavatejahshri spoke these verses to Sudhana, further illustrating the enlightening liberation entering into profound miracles of pleasing sound:

rnam thar gang gis dus gsum rgyal ba ma lus dang / / chos dbyings kun tu 'byams klas mtha' dang dbus med pa/ / shes byed mtshan nyid kun gyi gzhir thug rtogs pa yi/ / rgyal sras rnams kyi rnam thar zab cing blta bar dka'/ /

“Profound and difficult to see is the bodhisattvas’ liberation By which they know every jina in the three times, The entire realm of phenomena without edge or center, And the complete extent of the characteristics of all cognition.[1544] {1}
Profound and hard to see is the liberation of enlightening beings, Like space, entering everywhere; They see the buddhas of all times, Infinite, throughout the cosmos.

tshogs las byung ba'i rnam thar tshul ni mtha' yas te/ / chos nyid thob pas tshad med bsam du med pa yin/ / yongs su 'phel zhing kun tu chags med shugs drag par/ / dus gsum byams pa'i tshul gyi lam la 'jug par gyis/ /

“The ways of the liberation that arise from the accumulations are infinite. They are inconceivable and immeasurable, for they attain[1545] the true nature. You should enter into the paths of the ways of love in the three times That completely increase power that is unimpeded. {2}

They attain endless liberations born of virtue and knowledge, Of inconceivable nature, immeasurable: Increasing unimpeded momentum in all directions, They plunge into the paths of benevolence in all times.

'di ltar sangs rgyas zhing rgyud rdul phran rab snyed kyi/ / bskal pa 'das pa'i snga rol sngon gyi zhing byung ba/ / 'jig rten khams ni chos 'od sprin gyi grong khyer dpal/ / bskal pa byung ba dri med mdog tu 'od chen no/ /
Many eons ago there was a world Called Cities of Spiritual Lights: In that glorious world Was a brilliant age called Pure Light.

bskal pa de gcig rgyal ba'i gdung ni rgyud ma chad/ / sangs rgyas ri rab rdul phran rab snyed byung bar gyur/ / bde gshegs chos kyi rgya mtsho 'od dbyangs rgyal po ni/ / thog mar byung ste de dag bskal pa dang po pa; ;

“In that one kalpa there appeared an unbroken succession of jinas, As many buddhas as there are atoms in Sumeru. First to appear, the first in that kalpa, Was the Sugata Dharmasamudraprabhagarjitarāja. {4}
In that age was an unbroken succession of buddhas, As many as atoms in the polar mountain. Illuminating King Voicing the Ocean of All Truths Was the first buddha of the age,

rgyal ba chos sprin grong khyer 'od snang rgyal po ni/ / bde gshegs de dag kun gyi tha mar 'jig rten byung / / de dag kun gyi spyan sngar phyin te kho mos mchod/ / de dag kun las chos kyang dga' ba chen pos thos/ /

“The last of those tathāgatas to appear in the world Was the Jina Dharmameghanagarābhapradīparāja. I came before them all and made offerings to them. From them all I heard the Dharma with great joy. {5}
Supreme Lamp of Knowledge Lighting the City of the Reality Realm Was the last of those buddhas: I visited and served them all, And joyfully heard their teachings.

kho mos thog mar mthong ba gser mdog 'od mnga' ba/ / rgya mtsho'i chos 'od sgrog pa'i gsung gi rgyal po ste/ / mtshan rab sum cu gnyis kyis yongs brgyan ri bo 'dra/ / mthong nas bdag ni bde gshegs 'gyur snyam blo gros gyur/ /
“First I saw, having a golden light, Dharmasamudraprabhagarjitarāja, Adorned with the thirty-two signs and resembling Meru, And seeing him I thought, ‘I shall become a sugata!’ {6}

I saw the golden light of the first buddha, Illuminating King Voicing the Ocean of All Truths, Like the polar mountain resplendent with the thirty-two marks, And seeing him I determined to become a buddha.

de bzhin gshegs pa de ni kho mos mthong mod la/ / thams cad mkhyen nyid 'byams klas 'byung ba'i rgyu rkyen gyis/ / mkha' dbyings rnam yangs de bzhin nyid kyi rang bzhin can/ / rgyal ba'i sems kyi dang po stobs ldan rab tu skyes/ /

“The very moment I saw that tathāgata, There arose the powerful first aspiration to become a jina Who had the character of the true nature, as vast[1547] as space, Because of the all-pervading arising of omniscience. {7}
As soon as I saw that buddha there arose My first aspiration to buddhahood, full of power, By means arising from the progress of omniscience, As pure as space, of the nature of Thusness.

snying rje bdud rtsi rgya mtsho che las byung ba des/ / dus gsum gshegs pa'i bde bar gshegs pa thams cad kun/ / rgyal sras rgya mtshos bskor ba ma lus thams cad dang / / sems can rgya mtshor bcas pa'i rgya mtsho'i zhing yang rgyas/ /

“All of the sugatas within the three times, Encircled by oceans of all the bodhisattvas, The extensive ocean of realms with their oceans of beings, Have arisen from the great ocean of the amrita of compassion. {8}

Thenceforth seeing all the buddhas throughout all times, And all the multitudes of enlightening beings, And all the myriad worlds and sentient beings there, I produced an ocean of ambrosia of goodwill.

lus kyis zhing rnams thams cad ma lus khyab bya dang / / 'gro ba kun gyi bsam pa bzhin du lus bstan phyir/ / zhing rnams ma lus bskyod cing snang bar bya ba dang / / 'gro ba smin bya'i don du bdag gis sems kyang bskyed/ /

“I also aspired that in order to ripen beings I would pervade every single realm with my body, Manifest a body to beings in accordance with their aspirations, And illuminate and shake every single realm. {9}
I determined to pervade all lands, Showing my body differently to sentient beings according to their mentalities, To illumine and stir all the lands And develop the beings to maturity.

rgyal ba gnyis pa'i spyan sngar kho mo phyin nas kyang / / zhing rnams rgya mtsho bcu bzhugs rgyal ba'i dbang po mthong / / rgyal ba tha ma mthong nas zhing gi rgya mtsho rnams/ / rgya mtsho'i zhing gi rdul phran rab snyed bzhugs pa mthong / /
“I also came before the second buddha And saw jina lords in ten oceans of realms. I saw the last jina within an ocean of realms As numerous as the atoms in an ocean of realms. {10}
I went and saw the second buddha, And the buddhas in the oceans of lands in the ten directions, In as many lands as atoms in an ocean of lands, And finally saw the last buddha of that age.

de yi tshu rol bskal pa zhing rgyud rdul snyed du/ / rgyal ba 'gro ba'i sgron ma ji snyed skyes gyur pa/ / de dag thams cad spyan sngar kho mo phyin gyur te/ / rnam thar rgya mtsho'i tshul 'di sbyong tshe mchod pa byas//

“Since then, during kalpas as numerous as a realm’s atoms, I have gone before and made offerings to All of the jinas, the lamps of the world, who appeared And purified an ocean of ways of liberation.” {11}
I went and served all the buddhas, Lamps of the world, that appeared In as many ages as atoms in all worlds, That I might purify this liberation.

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa sgra yid du 'ong ba dang / rnam par 'phrul pa zab mo la 'jug pa thob pa/ ting nge 'dzin gyi sgo rgya mtsho mtha' dang dbus med pa la zhugs pa/ gzungs kyi sgo rgya mtsho rgya chen po las byung ba'i sems dang ldan pa/ byang chub sems dpa'i mngon par shes pa'i snang ba chen po rab tu thob pa/ tha dad pa yang dag par shes pa chen po rgya mtsho la zhugs pa/ dga' ba'i shugs rgya mtsho shin tu yangs pa rnam par 'phel ba'i sems dang ldan pa

Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, attained this bodhisattva liberation called the entry into beautiful sounds and profound manifestations, attained an endless, centerless ocean of samādhis, gained an understanding that arose from a vast ocean of gateways to retention, attained the great illumination of a bodhisattva’s higher cognitions, and entered an ocean of great discernment,[1548] and in his mind spread a vast ocean of powerful delight.

Then, having attained this enlightening liberation of entry into the profound miracle of pleasing sound, having entered an ocean of infinitely various media of concentration, his mind having developed an immense ocean of means of sustained attention, illumined with the great mystic knowledge of enlightening beings, having entered an ocean of great joyful intelligence, his mind expanded with a vast ocean of ecstasy,
nges mtshan mo'i lha mo grong khyer thams cad srung ba 'byung ba'i gzi brjid dpal la tshul dang mthun pa'i tshigs su bcad pa 'di dag gis mngon par bstod do/ /
He then praised the night goddess Sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśrī by reciting these appropriate verses:
Sudhana praised the night goddess with these verses:

khyod kyi shes rab chos yangs rgya mtsho kun la spyod/ / srid pa'i rgya mtsho mtha' dbus med par khyod kyis spyad/ / ye shes lus mchog snying po tshe ring snyun bral ba/ / lha mo khyod ni 'khor 'dir byon cing rnam par mdzes; ;

“Your wisdom is active in a vast ocean of the Dharma. You practice in the centerless, endless ocean of existences. The essence of your perfect wisdom body lives long without illness. Goddess, you have come and beautified this assembly. {12}

Vast is your wisdom, coursing in the ocean of truth, And you have traversed the infinite sea of existences. Long-lived, without affliction, an embodiment of beneficent knowledge, Your presence illumines this assembly, O goddess.

chos kyi rang bzhin nam mkha' lta bur thugs chud de/ / dus gsum kun gyi tshul yang chags med thugs chud mdzad/ / thugs kyi skad cig gcig la tshad med bsam yas pa'i/ / dmigs pa thams cad rtog pa mi mngar 'jal ba mdzad/ /

“You have realized the nature of phenomena to be like space. You realize without impediment the ways of all three times. In each instant of mind there are inconceivable, countless Perceptions, all of which are without conceptualization. {13}
Aware of the nature of things, like the sky, You enter unhindered into all times; In an instant of consciousness without discriminatory thought You assess all objects, inconceivable as they are.

ye shes spyan mnga' chos nyid sems can med gzigs kyang / / sems can rgya mtsho mtha' yas thugs rjes gzigs pa mdzad/ / thugs kyi rnam thar shin tu yangs la 'jug mdzad cing / / sems can tshad med 'dul zhing yongs su smin par mdzad/ /

“With your wisdom eyes you see the true nature in which there are no beings, Yet you perceive with compassion the infinite ocean of beings. You enter the very vast[1549] liberation of your mind, And you guide and ripen countless beings. {14}

With the eye of knowledge you see into the beingless nature, While by compassion you enter infinite oceans of beings. Deliberately plunging into most profound liberation, You guide and develop innumerable beings.

khyod ni chos kyi dkyil 'khor rnam dpyad tshul mkhyen te/ / chos kyi rang bzhin shes bya'i tshul la rnam sangs rgyas/ / 'phags lam dri ma med pa thams cad yongs bsgoms te/ / 'gro ba ma lus rnam par sbyong zhing yongs su 'byung / /

“You know through analyzing the field of phenomena. You have realized the way of knowing the nature of phenomena. You meditate on all the stainless paths of the āryas. You purify all beings without exception and liberate them. {15}
You know how to analyze all states of being, And are aware of the way to penetrate the essence of things: You practice the undefiled path of all sages; You will liberate all beings, purifying them.

thams cad mkhyen pa'i ye shes dri med rtogs mdzad pas/ / khyod ni sems can rgya mtsho'i mchog las mngon par skyes/ / khyod ni chos dbyings khong chud sems can kun khyab par/ / chos rab bstan cing 'jig rten 'jigs pa zhi bar mdzad/ /

“You have realized the stainless wisdom of omniscience. Goddess, you have become the supreme guide[1550] of beings. You pervade all beings within the realm of phenomena And teach them the Dharma and end all fear in the world. {16}
You are an unexcelled leader of beings, O goddess, As you acquire omniscient knowledge throughout the universe, You expound the Teaching to all beings therein, And extinguish all fears in the world.

khyod ni rnam par snang mdzad smon lam lam tshul gyis/ / yang dag bzhud cing chags med blo yangs dri med ldan/ / thams cad bgod pa'i rgyal ba'i stobs ni thugs chud cing / / zhing rnams kun gyi rgyal ba rnam par 'phrul pa gzigs/ /

“Goddess, through the way of the prayers of Vairocana, You have a vast,[1551] stainless, unimpeded, exact understanding. You have understood the power[1552] of the omnipresent jinas, And you see the miraculous manifestation of the jinas in all realms. {17}
You go by way of the path of Vairocana’s vows, With unhindered, vast, undefiled understanding; Everywhere practicing the powers of the enlightened, You witness the miracles of buddhas in all lands.

khyod kyi thugs ni mkha' 'dra thub par dka' ba ste/ / nyon mongs kun gyi dri mas ma gos snga nas dag / der ni dus gsum byung ba'i zhing rnams thams cad dang / / sangs rgyas sras dang bcas pa sems can kun bcas 'dus/ /

“Your mind is as invincible as space. You are primordially pure, unstained by the stains of the kleśas. Within it appear all the realms of the three times And the assemblies of all buddhas and bodhisattvas. {18}
Hard to accomplish is a skylike mind such as yours, Free from the taints of the afflictions; Therein are all lands in all times, All buddhas, enlightening beings, and all living creatures.

skad cig gcig gis nyin mtshan yud du zla ba dang / / skad cig yud tsam lo dang 'du 'jig bskal pa dang / / bskal pa rgya mtsho ming grangs rgya mtshor bcas pa dang / / 'gro ba rnams kyi 'du shes rgya mtsho'ang thugs su chud/ /

“Within each instant there are days and nights and months, In each moment years and the creation and destruction of kalpas. You know an ocean of kalpas, their ocean of names and numbers, And the ocean of the perceptions of beings, within each instant. {19}

Day and night, instants and moments, seasons, fortnights, months, And years, along with their passing away and imagined discriminations, And the waves of eons, with their enumerations of myriad names, The oceans of concepts of sentient beings, all you see in an instant.

phyogs rnams kun gyi sems can skye 'chi ji snyed dang / / gzugs yod pa dang gzugs med 'du shes yod med kyi/ / rnam spyod bden pa'i tshul ni thugs su chud mdzad cing / / de dag lam bstan byang chub mchog tu 'god pa mdzad/ /

“You know the births and deaths of beings in all directions, Those with and without form, with and without perception, Those who follow the way of belief in reality. You show them the path and bring them to supreme enlightenment. {20}

The deaths and births of beings in the ten directions, With form or without, thinking and thoughtless, You comprehend according to their conventional truth, And show them the way to supreme enlightenment.

rnam par snang mdzad smon lam dra ba'i rigs las byung / / bde gshegs kun gyi sku gcig tshul las yang dag 'khrungs/ / khyod ni chos sku yongs dag thugs la chags mi mnga'/ / 'jig rten kun tu sku gzugs yid bzhin ston pa mdzad/ /

“Manifesting from the family of Vairocana’s net[1553] of prayers, Born from the single body of all the sugatas, Your unimpeded mind is the pure Dharma body, And you manifest your form body in all worlds according to aspirations.” {21}
Born of the family of the network of Vairocana’s vows, Having become one with all buddhas, Your spiritual body pure, your mind unobstructed, You appear to beings according to their minds.

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis mtshan mo'i lha mo grong khyer thams cad srung ba 'byung ba'i gzi brjid dpal la tshul dang 'dra ba'i tshigs su bcad pa de dag gis mngon par bstod de/ mtshan mo'i lha mo grong khyer thams cad srung ba 'byung ba'i gzi brjid dpal gyi rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal nas mtshan mo'i lha mo grong khyer thams cad srung ba 'byung ba'i gzi brjid dpal la lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas te/ yang dang yang bltas nas mtshan mo'i lha mo grong khyer thams cad srung ba 'byung ba'i gzi brjid dpal gyi drung nas song ngo/ /

Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, having praised the night goddess Sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśrī with these appropriate verses, bowed his head to the feet of the night goddess Sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśrī, circumambulated the night goddess Sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśrī many hundreds of thousands of times, keeping her to his right, and, looking back again and again, departed from the night goddess Sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśrī.
Having eulogized the goddess with these verses, Sudhana paid his respects and went on.
shin tu rgyas pa chen po'i mdo/ sangs rgyas phal po che zhes bya ba las; sdong pos brgyan pa'i le'u ste/ bam po brgya gsum pa/

Chapter 40. Sarvavṛkṣpraphullanasukhasaṃvāsā
Sarvavrikshapraphullanasukhasamvasa

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa sgra yid du 'ong ba dang / rnam par 'phrul pa zab mo la 'jug pa de/ de bas kyang rgya cher sgom pa dang / yid ches par bya ba dang / shin tu rgyas par byed cing / mtshan mo'i lha mo shing thams cad kyi me tog rgyas pas bde bar gnas pa gang na ba der phyin nas

Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, further meditating on, believing in,[1554] and increasing the bodhisattva liberation called the entry into beautiful sounds and profound manifestations, went to where the night goddess Sarvavṛkṣpraphullanasukhasaṃvāsā was.

Then Sudhana, further cultivating, fostering, and expanding the enlightening liberation of entry into the profound miracle of pleasing sound, went to the night goddess Sarvavrikshapraphullanasukhasamvasa.

mtshan mo'i lha mo shing thams cad kyi me tog rgyas pas bde bar gnas pa spos rin po che thams cad kyi shing gi yal ga'i khang pa brtsegs pa zhig na seng+ge'i khri rin po che'i shing gi myu gu'i snying po can zhig la 'dug ste/ mtshan mo'i lha mo stong phrag bcus kun nas bskor cing 'dug pa mthong ngo/ /

He saw the night goddess Sarvavṛkṣpraphullanasukhasaṃvāsā seated upon a lion throne consisting of the saplings of precious trees, inside a kūṭāgāra made from the branches of all perfumed precious trees and encircled by an entourage of ten thousand night goddesses.
He saw her sitting on a lion throne of jewel tree shoots inside a tower of branches of jewel trees of all fragrances, surrounded by ten thousand night goddesses.

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis mtshan mo'i lha mo shing thams cad kyi me tog rgyas pas bde bar gnas pa'i rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te mdun du 'dug nas thal mo sbyar te 'di skad ces smras so/ / lha mo/ bdag gis bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed na/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpa' rnams byang chub sems dpa'i spyad pa spyod pa dang / ji ltar slob pa dang / ji ltar spyod ji ltar slob cing thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du 'byung ba bdag la bshad du gsol/ de skad ces smras pa dang /

Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, bowed his head to the feet of the night goddess Sarvavṛkṣpraphullanasukhasaṃvāsā and then stood before her. With his hands placed together in homage, he said, “Goddess, I have developed the aspiration for the highest, complete enlightenment, and so I pray that you explain how bodhisattvas should practice bodhisattva conduct, how they should train in it, and how, having practiced and trained in it, they proceed toward omniscience!”

He went up to her, paid his respects, and said, “Noble goddess, I have set my mind on supreme perfect enlightenment, but I do not know how an enlightening being is to carry out and learn the practice of enlightening beings. Please tell me how to perform and learn the practice of enlightening beings, and how to act and learn so as to arrive at omniscience.”
mtshan mo'i lha mo shing thams cad kyi me tog rgyas pas bde bar gnas pas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la 'di skad ces smras so/ /
The night goddess Sarvavṛkṣpraphullanasukhasaṃvāsā said to Sudhana, the head merchant’s son,
The goddess said to Sudhana,

rigs kyi bu/ kho mo'i mthus ni/ mi mjed kyi 'jig rten gyi khams na nyi ma nub tu cha ba'i tshe pad+mo shin tu rgyas pa rnams kyang rnam par 'dzum par 'gyur ro/ / skyes pa dang bud med bza' shing gi ra ba na gnas shing dga' bar rtse ba la brtson pa dag kyang khyim du 'dong pa'i blo skyed do/ /

“Noble one, through my power, when the sun sets in the Sahā world realm, the lotus blossoms close,[1555] the men and women who are dedicated to delighting in pleasures in parks have the wish to return to their homes,
“By my power, when the sun goes down, the blooming lotuses become highly fragrant; all the men and women sporting in the parks decide to go home;
lam dang srang na rgyu ba'i sems can rnams kyang zhag gi gnas sems shing tshol te/ 'gro ba'i gnas thams cad du mngon par gzhol bar 'gyur ro/ /
the beings who travel along roads and narrow paths think of finding somewhere to stay for the night, and they turn their attention to all the safe dwellings for beings.
the highly conscious beings on the roads and paths in the night head for the protection of all beings:
nags tshal dang / gseb dang / phug la brten pa'i sems can rnams kyang nags tshal dang / gseb dang / phug tu 'dong ngo/ /
Those who dwell in forests, in mountain clefts, and in caves enter their forests, clefts, and caves.
those who live in mountain caves go into the mountain caves,
shing la gnas pa'i sems can rnams kyang shing gi gnas la brten par mngon par gzhol lo/ /
Those beings who dwell in trees think of returning to their homes in the trees.
those who lie in trees head for the trees,
khung na gnas pa'i sems can rnams kyang khung du 'dong ngo/ /
Those beings who dwell in holes return to their holes.
those who live in caves go into their caves,
grong dang / grong khyer dang / ljongs dang / yul la gnas pa'i sems can rnams kyang grong dang / grong khyer dang / ljongs dang / yul du 'dong ngo/ /
Those beings who dwell in villages, towns, districts, and lands return to their villages, towns, districts, and lands.
those who live in villages, cities, or towns go into their villages, cities, and towns,
chu na gnas pa'i sems can rnams kyang chur 'dong ngo/ /
Those beings who dwell in water enter the water.
those who live in water go down in the water,
phyogs gzhan gyi yul du phyin pa'i sems can rnams kyang nub mo bde zhing dga' bar gnas pa'i don du rang rang gi yul gyi phyogs kyi bsam pa skyed do/ /
Those beings who have gone to lands in other directions begin to think of the directions of their own lands in order to remain in a feeling of happiness during the night.
those who live in other abodes go to their respective dwelling places, to spend the night comfortably.

rigs kyi bu/ gzhan yang kho mo ni/ skyes pa dang / bud med gzhon nu dar la bab pa/ dar ba'i nyams drod kyis myos pa dang / glu dang / gar dang / rol mo'i dga' bas myos pa dang / 'dod pa'i yon tan la dga' zhing brtson pa rnams la skye ba dang / rga shi dang / gti mug gi mun pa chen pos 'jigs pa'i gnyen por dag ba'i rtsa ba yongs su bskyed pa'i phyir brtson 'grus kyi legs pa'i bsngags pa byed do/ / sems can ser sna dang ldan pa rnams ni/ sbyin pa la rab tu sbyor ro/ / sems can tshul khrims ngan pa can rnams ni/ tshul khrims la rab tu 'god do/ / ngan sems dang ldan pa'i sems can rnams la ni/ byams pa'i legs pa rjod par byed do/ / sems 'khrugs pa'i sems can rnams ni/ bzod pa la rab tu 'god do/ / le lo can gyi sems can rnams ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i brtson 'grus brtsam pa la rab tu 'god do/ / sems rnam par myos pa'i sems can rnams ni/ bsam gtan la rab tu 'god do/ / shes rab 'chal ba can gyi sems can rnams ni/ shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa la yongs su sbyor ro/ / theg pa dma' ba la mos pa'i sems can rnams ni/ theg pa chen po la rab tu 'god do/ / khams gsum la mngon par zhen pa'i sems can rnams ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i smon lam gyi pha rol tu phyin pa srid pa'i lam gyi rgyud mthar phyin pa'i dkyil 'khor la spyod pa la rab tu 'god do/ / dmigs pa'i dbang du gyur pa'i sems can las dang nyon mongs pas rab tu mnar ba/ bsod nams dang ye shes kyi stobs med pa rnams ni; byang chub sems dpa'i stobs kyi pha rol tu phyin pa la rab tu 'god do/ / mi shes pa'i mun nag gis khebs pa'i sems can bdag tu bya ba dang / bdag gir bya bas ma rig pa'i mun nag tu 'thom pa rnams ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i ye shes kyi pha rol tu phyin pa la rab tu 'god do/ /

“Moreover, noble one, to the young men and women in the prime of life who are intoxicated by youthfulness, intoxicated by the delights of singing, dancing, and music, who are dedicated to delighting in sensory pleasures, to them I praise dedication to creating roots of merit as a remedy for the fear of birth, old age, death, and the great darkness of ignorance. I bring beings who are miserly to the practice of generosity. I bring beings who have bad conduct to the practice of correct conduct. I praise love to beings who have malicious minds. I establish beings with disturbed minds in the practice of patience. I establish beings who are lazy in the practice of undertaking bodhisattva diligence. I establish beings who have intoxicated minds in the practice of dhyāna. I bring beings with poor wisdom to the practice of the perfection of wisdom. I establish beings who aspire to the lower yānas in the practice of the Mahāyāna. I establish beings who have attachment to the three realms in the bodhisattva perfection of prayer, the field of the ultimate conclusion of the paths of existence. I establish in the perfection of bodhisattva strength those beings who are overpowered by their objects of perception,[1556] are tormented by karma and kleśas, and have weak merit and wisdom. I establish in the perfection of bodhisattva knowledge those beings who are overwhelmed by the darkness of ignorance and enveloped in the darkness of believing in a self and possessions.

“Furthermore, to the young men and women intoxicated with the joy of youth, reveling in music and song and intent on sensual pleasures, I praise the effort to produce roots of goodness as an antidote to the fears of the darkness of birth, old age, and death. I enjoin giving on those who are greedy and lead the ill-behaved to discipline. To those who are hostile I praise kindness, and I lead those agitated in mind to patience. I lead the lazy to undertake the vigorous effort of enlightening beings. Those whose minds wander I establish in meditation. I furnish the stupid with transcendent wisdom. Those who are interested in the Lesser Vehicle I establish in the Great Vehicle. Those who are attached to the world, who act within the sphere of attachment to the conditions of existence, I lead to the transcendent commitment of enlightening beings. Those who are overcome by obstructions, tormented by afflictions in their actions, lacking in the power of virtue and knowledge, I lead to the transcendent power of enlightening beings. Those bound up in the darkness of nescience, in the darkness of the ignorance characterized by egoism and possessiveness, I lead to the transcendent knowledge of enlightening beings.
rigs kyi bu/ gzhan yang kho mo ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa dga' ba'i 'od spro ba yangs pa yang dag par 'byung ba thob pa'o/ /
“Moreover, noble one, I have attained the bodhisattva liberation called the arising of the vast radiating light of joy.”
“Furthermore, I have attained the enlightening liberation ‘manifestation of contentment with the treasure produced from great joy.’”
nor bzang gis smras pa/ lha mo/ byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa dga' ba'i 'od spro ba yangs pa yang dag par 'byung ba de'i yul ji lta bu zhig mchis/
Sudhana asked, “Goddess, what is this bodhisattva liberation called the arising of the vast radiating light of joy like?”
Sudhana said, “What is the sphere of this liberation?”
smras pa/ rigs kyi bu/ rnam par thar pa de ni/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i bsod nams kyis sems can yongs su sdud pa'i ye shes dang thabs snang ba dang ldan pa ste/ de ci'i phyir zhe na/
She answered, “Noble one, this bodhisattva liberation has the radiance of the knowledge and methods of gathering beings through the merit of the tathāgatas. Why is that?
The goddess said, “The scope of this liberation is the knowledge and means to take care of sentient beings by the goodness of those who arrive at Thusness. How is that?

rigs kyi bu/ sems can rnams kyi bde ba nyams su myong ba ji snyed cig yod pa de dag thams cad ni/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i bsod nams kyi mthus byung ba'o/ / de bzhin gshegs pa'i gdams ngag gi tshul gyis byung ba'o/ / de bzhin gshegs pa'i gsung la nan tan du byas pas byung ba'o/ / de bzhin gshegs pa'i rjes su bslab pas byung ba'o/ / de bzhin gshegs pa'i byin gyi rlabs kyis byung ba'o/ / de bzhin gshegs pas bstan pa'i lam la nan tan du byas pas byung ba'o/ / de bzhin gshegs pa dang tshul 'dra ba'i dge ba'i rtsa ba bskyed pas byung ba'o/ / de bzhin gshegs pas chos bstan pa'i mthun pa'i rgyus byung ba'o/ / de bzhin gshegs pa'i ye shes kyi nyi ma snang bas byung ba'o/ /

“Noble one, it is because all happiness that beings experience occurs through the power of the merit of the tathāgatas, through the path of instruction of the tathāgatas, through practicing the words of the tathāgatas, through following the example of the tathāgatas, through the blessing of the tathāgatas, through practicing the path taught by the tathāgatas,[1557] through creating roots of merit in the same way the tathāgatas have, through the power of the natural result of the Dharma that is taught by the tathāgatas, and through illumination from the sun of the wisdom of the tathāgatas.

Whatever well-being sentient beings experience is all due to the power of the goodness of the enlightened, due to the path of the teaching of the enlightened, due to putting the word of the enlightened into practice, due to learning from the enlightened, due to the support of the enlightened, due to practicing the path of knowledge of the enlightened, due to planting roots of goodness like the enlightened, due to the true teaching of the enlightened, due to the illumination of the sun of knowledge of the enlightened.
rigs kyi bu/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i rigs kyi chos dkar po'i dkyil 'khor gyi snang bas ni/ sems can rnams kyi bde ba yongs su 'byung ste/ de ci'i phyir zhe na/
“Noble one, the happiness of beings arises from the light of the disk of good qualities[1558] of the family of the tathāgatas. Why is that?
“Indeed, the happiness of beings comes from the light of the sphere of pure deeds of the family of the enlightened. How do I know?

'di ltar rigs kyi bu/ kho mos byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa dga' ba'i 'od spro ba yangs pa yang dag par 'byung ba 'di la 'jug pa'i tshe bcom ldan 'das de bzhin gshegs pa dgra bcom pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas rnam par snang mdzad kyi sngon gyi byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa rgya mtsho rjes su dran par byed cing / 'jug pa dang khong du chud par byed pa'i tshe

“Noble one, it is like this: I realized this bodhisattva liberation called the arising of the vast radiating light of joy when I remembered, comprehended, and understood the ocean of the past bodhisattva conduct of the Bhagavat Tathāgata Arhat Samyaksaṃbuddha Vairocana.

As I enter into this enlightening liberation of the manifestation of contentment with the treasure produced from great joy, and recall and plunge into the ocean of Vairocana Buddha’s past practices as an enlightening being, thus do I know and understand—

'di ltar bcom ldan 'das sngon byang chub sems dpa'i sa la bzhugs pas sems can bdag tu bya ba dang / bdag gir bya ba la mngon par zhen pa/ ma rig pa'i mun pas 'thom pa/ lta ba thibs po'i lta bas dgon par 'khyams pa/ sred pa'i dbang du gyur pa/ 'dod chags kyi bcings pas glags pa/ zhe sdang gis khong khro ba'i sems dang ldan pa/ gti mug gis sems kyi rgyud 'khrugs par gyur pa/ phrag dog dang ser sna kun nas 'khor ba/ nyon mongs pas rab tu dkrugs pa'i sems dang ldan pa; 'khor ba'i sdug bsngal chen po nyams su myong bar gyur pa/ 'khor ba na phongs pa'i sdug bsngal gyis rab tu gzir ba/ sangs rgyas blta ba las phyir phyogs par gyur pa thams cad gzigs nas thugs rje chen po'i thugs skyes par gyur to/ /

“When, in the past, the Bhagavat was on the bodhisattva bhūmis, he developed a motivation of great compassion on seeing beings with the belief in a self, with the belief in possessions, enveloped in the darkness of ignorance, wandering in the wilderness of thickets of wrong views, under the power of craving,[1559] imprisoned within the bondage of desire, having thoughts of hatred caused by anger, with their minds disturbed by ignorance, ensnared by jealousy and greed, with their minds disturbed by kleśas, experiencing great suffering in saṃsāra, afflicted by the suffering of poverty in saṃsāra, and having turned away from the sight of a buddha.

as the Buddha was concentrating on the stages of enlightenment in the past, seeing sentient beings caught up in egoism and possessiveness, in the darkness of ignorance, gone into a tangle of views, dominated by craving, bound by the fetters of desire, hostile and malevolent, continuously pursuing delusions, wrapped up in envy and jealousy, their minds crowded with afflictions, experiencing the great misery of the mundane whirl, tormented by the pains of poverty in the mundane whirl, deprived of the sight of the enlightened, there appeared in the Buddha a mind of great compassion,

sems can thams cad kyi don du 'gro ba thams cad la yo byad dang rin po ches yongs su bsdu zhing yongs su sdud pa'i thugs dang / sems can thams cad kyi 'khor ba'i yo byad yongs su sgrub pa'i thugs dang / dngos po thams cad la chags pa mi mnga' ba'i thugs dang / yul thams cad la ye rngam pa mi mnga' ba'i thugs dang / dga' ba thams cad la chags pa mi mnga' ba'i thugs dang / longs spyod thams cad la yongs su ma zhen pa'i thugs dang / sbyin pa thams cad la rnam par smin pa la re ba med pa'i thugs dang / 'jig rten gyi phun sum tshogs pa thams cad la bzhed pa mi mnga' ba'i thugs dang / rgyu dang rkyen la ma rmongs pa'i thugs dang / legs par btsal ba'i chos la yang dag pa ji lta ba bzhin du mkhyen pa'i thugs dang / sems can thams cad kyi don la gzhol bar bya ba mngon par sgrub pa'i thugs yang dag par skyes par gyur to/ /

“He developed a motivation to benefit all beings through the accumulation and possession of precious requisites in the world, a motivation to produce necessary requisites for all beings, a motivation that was without attachment to anything, a motivation that had no yearning for anything in the entire field of perceptions, a motivation that had no clinging to any pleasure, a motivation that had no longing for any enjoyment, a motivation that had no wish for results ripening from generosity, a motivation that had no longing for any worldly prosperity, a motivation that was not[1560] oblivious of causes and conditions, a motivation that had the understanding of the Dharma that was being sought, and a motivation that had attained dedication to the benefit of all beings.

a mind to take care of all sentient beings materially for their benefit, a mind to produce means of worldly support for all sentient beings, a mind free from attachment to all things, a mind without acquisitiveness for any objects, a mind not dwelling on any pleasures, a mind free from grasping for any material goods, a mind not seeking rewards for giving, a mind not eager for existence in any world, a mind not confused about causal relations, a mind contemplating the truth after thorough investigation, a mind to provide refuge for the welfare of all living beings.
de de ltar chos thams cad kyi rang bzhin la yang dag par zhugs pa'i thugs dang ldan pa/ sems can gyi khams thams cad du byams pa chen pos snyoms par zhugs pa/
“In that way, he had a mind that understood the nature of all phenomena, the realization of the impartiality of great love toward all realms of beings.
“Having comprehended the essence of all things as it really is, having impartial goodwill toward all sentient beings,
'gro ba thams cad thugs rje chen po'i sprin gyis rgyas par dgang ba'i sbyor ba mnga' ba/
He had the activity of spreading clouds of great compassion over all worlds of beings.
working to fill all worlds with great compassion,
sems can gyi 'jig rten thams cad kun nas khebs pa'i chos kyi gdugs chen po'i dkyil 'khor mnga' ba/
He possessed a great round parasol of the Dharma that sheltered all worlds of beings.
covering all worlds with the canopy of the great Teaching,
sems can thams cad kyi nyon mongs pa'i ri rnam par 'joms pa'i ye shes rdo rje'i mtshon cha mnga' ba/
He possessed the thunderbolt weapon of great wisdom that destroys the mountains of obscurations of all beings.
holding the thunderbolt of great knowledge,
'gro ba thams cad kyi bde ba yongs su sgrub pas dgyes pa'i shugs rnam par 'phel ba'i thugs mnga' ba/
His mind had the increasing power of contentment through bringing happiness to all beings.
which shatters the mountain of afflictions of all sentient beings,
sems can thams cad la bde ba phul du phyin par mngon par sgrub pa'i smon lam gyi thugs mnga' ba/
His mind prayed that all beings would attain the ultimate happiness;
his mind growing in satisfaction through the welfare of all sentient beings,
bsam pa dang smon pa ji lta ba bzhin du sems can thams cad la nor gyi char rab tu dbab pa'i thugs mnga' ba/
he intended to send down a rain of wealth on all beings in accordance with their wishes and aspirations.
determined to effect the ultimate happiness of all sentient beings, wishing to provide all sentient beings with everything they need,
sems can thams cad yongs su mi gtong zhing snyoms par sbyor ba'i thugs mnga' ba/
His mind never abandoned beings but was focused on them all equally.
working impartially without abandoning any sentient beings,
'phags pa'i nor gyis sems can thams cad tshim par mdzad pa'i thugs mnga' ba/
He intended to satisfy all beings with the wealth of the āryas.
wishing to satisfy all sentient beings with the wealth of sages,
stobs bcu'i ye shes rin po che phul du dri ma med pa thob par mdzad pa'i thugs mnga' ba/
He intended that they attain the supreme, stainless, precious knowledge of the ten strengths.
determined to attain the jewel of knowledge of the supreme ten powers,
byang chub sems dpa'i mngon par shes pa chen po'i stobs dang shugs rab tu brnyes pa de/
He had attained the strength of the higher cognitions of a bodhisattva.
empowered with the mystic knowledges of enlightening beings,
byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par 'phrul pa sna tshogs kyi sprin chen pos sems can gyi khams chos kyi dbyings kyis klas pa/ nam mkha'i mthas gtugs pa thams cad rgyas par bkang ste
He filled the entirety of the realms of beings and the vast realm of phenomena, as far as space extends, with great clouds of various miraculous bodhisattva manifestations.
pervading all worlds throughout the space of the entire cosmos with a multitude of various enlightening manifestations,
sems can thams cad la mngon par gyur par bzhugs shing sbyin pa'i dmigs pa thams cad kyi sprin gyi char chen po rnam pa thams cad du dbab pa dang /
He manifested his presence before all beings and sent down a gift of great rain from a cloud of every form and every kind of object of perception.
appearing before all sentient beings, swirling a great cloud of all manner of objects
rin po che'i rgyan thams cad kyi sprin chen po'i char mngon par 'bebs pa mdzad de/
He sent down rain from a great cloud of every kind of precious jewelry.
and showering a rain of all kinds of precious ornaments,
'di ltar sems can thams cad so so'i tshul dang ji ltar mthun pas longs spyod par bya ba'i phyir dngos po rnam pa tha dad pa mtha' yas pa dang /
“In that way, so that all beings could have enjoyment according to their own kind, he accomplished giving infinite, different kinds of things,
he undertook to give infinite various articles to all sentient beings for their use as appropriate,
yo byad rnam pa tha dad pa tshad med pa la spyad par bya ba dang /
practiced countless different kinds of assistance,
to perform innumerable services,
sbyin pa rnam pa sna tshogs thams cad kyis yongs su bsdu ba'i tshul dang /
engaged in accumulating all the many various kinds of gifts,
to strive to provide care by all sorts of charity,
dngos po yongs su gtang ba rnam pa du ma la yongs su spyad pa dang /
practiced the conduct of giving away a numerous variety of things,
giving away many kinds of things,
yo byad kyi rnam pa dang / rgyan gyi 'du byed brjod du med pa dang /
produced an indescribable array of different kinds of requisites,
to construct arrangements of myriad benefits, services, and useful articles,

sbyin pa'i tshogs rnam pa sna tshogs mtshan nyid sna tshogs dang ldan pa/ sems can rnams bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du yongs su tshim par bya ba'i sbyin pa'i tshul mtha' yas pa thugs su chud pas sems can gyi bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du yongs su tshim par bya ba/
and realized the way of infinite generosity that satisfies beings according to their aspirations with an accumulation of various gifts with various characteristics.

mngon par bsgrubs pa'i dngos po thams cad gtang ba dang / yongs su gtang ba dang / sbyin pa bya ba dang / 'gro ba thams cad kyi 'du byed kyi sdug bsngal rgyun mi 'chad pa las yongs su bskyab pa'i tshul du bya ba rnams sems can thams cad la lan la re ba mi mnga' ba dang / 'gro ba thams cad la mnyam pa nyid du 'byung ba'i thugs mnga' bas 'gro ba thams cad kyi sems rin po che yongs su sbyong ba mdzad cing / sangs rgyas thams cad kyi dge ba'i rtsa ba rgya mtsho gcig tu gyur pa las byung ba'i yongs su bsdu ba'i tshul 'gro ba thams cad kyi bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du yo byad kyi char dbab pa/ 'gro ba thams cad la thams cad mkhyen pa'i bsod nams rgya mtsho'i shugs rnam par 'phel bar mdzad pas

“Thus he gave, conferred, and bestowed all the things that would bring contentment to beings according to their aspirations. He engaged in saving all beings from continuous composite suffering. He had no wish for any being to repay his kindness. He possessed the realization of the equality of all beings, so that he purified the precious minds of all beings, and through the methods of gathering beings that have arisen from the roots of merit of all buddhas as a single ocean, he sent down a rain of requisites in accordance with the wishes of all beings, and he increased the power of the ocean of the merit of omniscience for all beings.

to practice various forms of giving, satisfying sentient beings according to their mentalities by endless giving, to make uninterrupted effort to save all beings from the miseries of the mundane world, without desiring the gratitude of anyone, impartial toward all beings, purifying the mind-jewel of all beings, increasing the flood of the ocean of wealth of all-knowledge for all beings produced from the ocean of roots of goodness at one with those of all buddhas, engaged in taking care of all beings by providing for their needs,
thugs kyi skad cig re re la sems can ma lus pa thams cad yongs su smin par bya ba dang / gdul ba gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa rnam par dag par bya ba'i phyir mngon par sgrub pa mdzad pa dang /
“He accomplished this in order to purify the successive ripening and guiding of all beings without exception in each instant of mind;
undertaking all this continuously, from moment to moment, to develop and guide all sentient beings and gradually purify them.

thugs kyi skad cig re re zhing gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa ma lus pa thams cad sangs rgyas kyi zhing nye bar nyon mongs pa med cing bla na med pa'i rgyan rnam par dag pas rnam par klubs shing rab tu brgyan pa yongs su rdzogs par bya ba dang /
in order in each instant of mind to cover and adorn the succession of all realms without exception with the pure adornments of the highest, undefiled buddha realms;
“He undertook to adorn every land as a supreme pure buddha-land in every moment of thought,
thugs kyi skad cig re re la chos kyi tshul rgya mtsho ma lus pa thams cad rgyas par dgang bar rnam par dag par bya ba dang /
in order in each instant of mind to pervade and purify the ocean of the ways of all phenomena without exception;
to purify the practice of the ocean of methods of the Teaching in every moment of thought,
thugs kyi skad cig re re la nam mkha'i dbyings kyi gtos ma lus pa thams cad rgyas par dgang ba'i ye shes kyi tshul yongs su rdzogs par bya ba dang /
in order in each instant of mind to complete the way of wisdom that pervades the entire extent of space without exception;
to fulfill the means of knowledge pervading all of space in every moment of thought,
thugs kyi skad cig re re la sems can dang dus ma lus pa thams cad la 'jug pa'i ye shes kyi tshul rnam par dag par bya ba dang /
in order in each instant of mind to purify the way of the wisdom that comprehends all beings and times without exception;
to purify the means of knowledge of how to tame all sentient beings in every moment of thought,
thugs kyi skad cig re re la 'gro ba ma lus pa thams cad rnam par 'dul ba'i ye shes kyi tshul snang ba rab tu thob par bya ba dang /
in order in each instant of mind to attain the illumination of the way of the wisdom that guides all beings without exception;
to bring to light the knowledge of how to guide all worldlings in every moment of thought,
thugs kyi skad cig re re la dus ma lus pa thams cad du chos kyi 'khor lo bskor ba las phyir mi ldog par bya ba dang /
in order in each instant of mind to irreversibly[1561] turn the wheel of the Dharma in all times without exception;
to always teach in a manner appropriate to the time in every moment of thought,
thugs kyi skad cig re re la thams cad mkhyen pa'i ye shes kyi byin gyi rlabs la mkhas pa ma lus par yongs su bstan pas 'gro ba thams cad la phan thogs par bya ba dang /
and in order in each instant of mind to benefit all beings through revealing all skills, without exception, that are the blessing of omniscient wisdom.
to be a benefactor to all beings by showing the skillfulness to support all knowledge in each moment of thought,
thugs kyi skad cig re re la 'jig rten gyi khams ma lus pa'i grangs su bya ba'i rgyud dang ldan pa/
“He performed bodhisattva conduct in each instant of mind in all the numbers of world realms without exception;
carrying out the practice of enlightening beings in each moment of thought
'jig rten gyi khams rgya mtsho thams cad mngon par bstan pa/
in the arisen[1562] ocean of all world realms;
in all kinds of worlds,
'jig rten gyi khams rgya mtsho thams cad yongs su 'du ba/
in the congregation of the ocean of all world realms;
'jig rten gyi khams 'byams klas pa sna tshogs brjod du yod pa/
in the vast extent of world realms of various descriptions;
'jig rten gyi khams kyi rgyud rnam par gnas pa sna tshogs kyis mtshams rnam par 'dul ba/
within the array of the boundaries of various differentiated families[1563] of world realms with boundaries;
gzhi sna tshogs dang / lhun du mar brjod du yod pa/
with descriptions of various bases and masses;
rnam par phye ba sna tshogs kyi bskal pa rnam pa tha dad pa bstan du yod pa/
in world realms with descriptions of various divisions into kalpas;

kun nas nyon mongs shing rnam par dag pa dang / rnam par dag cing kun nas nyon mongs pa dang / gcig tu yongs su dag pa dang / gcig tu kun nas nyon mongs pa dang / che ba dang / yangs pa dang / tshad med pa dang / dog pa dang / phra ba dang / rgya che ba dang / gzhi mnyam pa dang snrel zhi dang / spyi'u tshugs dang / phyogs dang phyogs mtshams su mngon par bltas pa dang / phyogs rgya mtsho sna tshogs su yongs su gzhol ba/

in world realms that were defiled but also pure, pure but also defiled, entirely pure, and entirely defiled, that were immense, vast, measureless, narrow, minute, and huge, high, level, sideways, upside-down, facing the principal directions and the intermediate directions, and located in the ocean of various directions;

sgo sna tshogs nas bstan cing sgo mtha' yas pa'i dbyibs rnam pa sna tshogs su 'dug pa'i rnam par phye ba sna tshogs dang ldan pa'i 'jig rten gyi khams rgya mtsho thams cad du byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa spyod de/
and in an array of various shapes and entrances described in various ways.
in various forms, by various means, having entered the way of enlightening beings,

byang chub sems dpa'i skyon med pa yongs su mnan nas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa dang / rnam par 'phrul pas rgyas par dgang bar bya ba dang / thugs kyi skad cig re re la dus gsum gyi sangs rgyas kyi 'phrin las ma lus pa thams cad sems can pha rol gyi sems dang bsam pas rnam par dmigs par bya ba'i phyir 'gro ba thams cad la thams cad mkhyen pa'i bsod nams rgya mtsho'i shugs rnam par 'phel bar mdzad de/ mngon par sgrub pa mdzad par gyur pas mngon par shes so/ / rjes su dran no/ /

“He entered a bodhisattva’s faultlessness in order to spread widely his bodhisattva conduct and miraculous manifestations, in order that in each instant of mind other beings would perceive in their minds and thoughts all the activity[1564] of the buddhas of the three times without exception, so that all beings would accomplish increasing the ocean of merit of omniscience. I know and I remember his accomplishment.[1565]

to suffuse the worlds with various manifestations of the practice of enlightening beings, to show the bodies of all the buddhas of past, present, and future to other beings according to their mentalities in each moment of thought, increasing the flood of the ocean of wealth of all-knowledge for all beings.
rigs kyi bu/ de ltar bcom ldan 'das de bzhin gshegs pa rnam par snang mdzad sngon byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa mdzad pa'i tshe
“Noble one, in that way, when the Bhagavat Vairocana was previously practicing bodhisattva conduct,
“Thus as Vairocana Buddha was carrying out the practice of enlightening beings in the past,
'jig rten gnas pa bsod nams dang ye shes kyi tshogs dang bral ba/
he had compassion for those dwelling in the world, who were devoid of the accumulations of merit and wisdom,
he aroused great compassion for those without virtue or knowledge, those attached to the world,
sems can byas pa drin du mi gzo bas yongs su gang ba/
who were filled with ingratitude toward other beings,
ungrateful,
mi shes pa'i mun pas chod pa;
who were enveloped by the darkness of ignorance,
wrapped up in the darkness of nescience,
bdag tu bya ba dang / bdag gir bya ba la mngon par zhen pa/
who were attached to belief in a self and belief in possessions,
egotistical and possessive,
ma rig pa'i mun pa rab rib kyis bsgribs pa/
who were obscured by the darkness and blindness of ignorance,
shrouded by the darkness of ignorance,
tshul bzhin ma yin par rnam par rtog pa la zhugs pa;
who had inappropriate thoughts,
immersed in unreasonable thought,
lta ba thibs po bas dgon par mgo brlags pa/
who were deep[1566] in the wilderness of thickets of wrong views,
lost in the wilderness of views,
rgyu dang 'bras bu la mgo rmongs pa/
who were ignorant of cause and results,
heedless of cause and effect,
nyon mongs pa dang las kyi dbang du gyur pa/
who were under the power of kleśas and karma,
dominated by afflictions in action,
'khor ba'i mya ngam chen po'i sdug bsngal gyi sa'i 'og tu lhung ba/
who had fallen into the underground world of the great suffering of saṃsāra’s wilderness
fallen into a pit of suffering in the wasteland of the mundane whirl,
phongs pa'i sdug bsngal sna tshogs nyams su myong bar gyur pa rnams la thugs rje chen po bskyed de/
and were experiencing the various[1567] sufferings of poverty.
experiencing the misery of various kinds of want;

pha rol tu phyin pa sbyang ba'i sprin chen po mngon par bsgrubs te dge ba'i rtsa ba la brten par gnas pa/ yongs su bsngags pa dang sems can thams cad kyi 'khor ba'i phongs pa'i sdug bsngal rnam par bzlog pa dang / bsod nams dang ye shes kyi tshogs chen po la mngon par mos par bya ba dang / rgyu'i dkyil 'khor gyi phyogs mngon par bstan pa dang / las dang chos su mi 'gal ba'i phyogs rab tu brjod pa dang / sangs rgyas kyi chos kyi dkyil 'khor yongs su bsdu ba'i phyogs snang bar bya ba dang / sems can thams cad kyi mos pa'i phyogs rab tu brjod par bya ba dang / sems can thams cad kyi zhing yongs su sgrub pa'i phyogs legs par bstan pa dang / de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi rigs mi gcad pa'i phyogs kyi rjes su 'brang bar bya ba dang / sangs rgyas thams cad kyi bstan pa'i phyogs yongs su gzung ba dang / mi dge ba'i chos thams cad kyi phyogs rnam par bzlog pa dang / thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi tshogs kyi phyogs yongs su brjod pa mdzad de/ pha rol tu phyin pa'i sprin chen pos sems can gyi khams thams cad rgyas par bkang ste mngon par bsgrubs nas bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du sems can tshim par 'gyur bar chos kyis shin tu bsdu ba la sems can rab tu dgod par mdzad do/ / thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi tshogs la yang dag par bskul to/ / byang chub sems dpa'i pha rol tu phyin pa chen po la rab tu btsud do/ / 'phags pa'i nor thams cad rab tu thob par bya bas nye bar bstan to/ / thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du 'dun pa'i shugs kyis sems can rnams dge ba'i rtsa ba rgya mtsho rnam par 'phags par mdzad do/ /

“Having compassion for them, he praised establishing strong roots of merit through a vast cloud of the practice of the perfections, dispelled saṃsāra’s suffering of poverty in all beings, inspired them toward a great accumulation of merit and wisdom, elucidated the aspect of the field of causes, explained the aspect of actions that are in accord with the Dharma, illuminated the aspect of understanding[1568] the domain of the Buddhadharma, elucidated the aspect of the aspirations of beings, taught the aspect of the creation of the realms of beings, followed the aspect of the uninterrupted family of all the buddhas, held the aspect of the teaching of all the buddhas, dispelled the aspect of all bad qualities, described the aspect of the accumulation of omniscience, and filled all the realms of beings with the great cloud of the perfections. Having accomplished that, he satisfied beings in accordance with their aspirations, establishing beings in the compilation of the Dharma; he inspired them toward the accumulation of omniscience; he brought them to the great perfections of a bodhisattva; he increased the ocean of the roots of merit of beings; he strengthened them through the attainment of the wealth of the āryas; and he increased the ocean of the roots of merit of beings through the power of their aspiration for omniscience.

producing vast multitudes of practices of the ways of transcendence, praising the firm foundation of roots of goodness, removing the pain of mundane want from all sentient beings, fostering the growth of great stores of virtue and knowledge, clarifying the realm of causes, enlightening them on the consistency of deeds and states, showing the origin of all beings and lands, involving them in the continuation of the family of buddhas, getting them to remember the teachings of all buddhas, turning them away from all evil, describing the preparations for omniscience, producing a great multitude of transcendent practices filling all realms of beings, he established sentient beings in the care of the ultimate Teaching, satisfying them according to their mentalities. He directed them in preparation for omniscience, he introduced them to the great transcendent ways of enlightening beings, he got them to support themselves on the wealth of sages, he got them to increase their roots of goodness by the momentum of the joy of omniscience.

de bzhin gshegs pa rnam par 'phrul pa'i sgor yang de dag rab tu btsud de/ phung po shin tu zhi ba'i bde bas yongs su bsdu ba bsdus te/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i bdag nyid che ba la mngon du mos par byas nas byang chub sems dpas yongs su bzung ba'i ye shes la rab tu bkod do/ /

“He brought them to enter the gateways to the miraculous manifestations of the tathāgatas, gathered them through possessing the bliss of the pacification of the skandhas, made them aspire to the greatness that is the nature of the tathāgatas, and established them in the wisdom possessed by the bodhisattvas.”

Introducing them to the miracles of all buddhas, taking them into ultimate unattached bliss, showing them the greatness of the enlightened, he led them to enlightening beings’ knowledge of means of salvation.”
nor bzang gis smras pa/ 'phags ma khyod bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu yang dag par zhugs nas ji srid cig lags/
Sudhana asked, “Āryā, how long has it been since you entered upon the highest, complete enlightenment?”
Sudhana said, “How long ago did you set out for supreme perfect enlightenment?”

smras pa/ rigs kyi bu/ gnas 'di ni/ yid ches par dka' ba ste/ shes par dka' ba'o/ / mos par dka' ba'o/ / 'jug par dka' ba'o/ / brjod par dka' ba'o/ / khong du chud par dka' ba ste/ lha dang bcas pa'i 'jig rten dang / nyan thos dang rang sangs rgyas thams cad kyis kyang khong du chud par mi nus so/ /

She answered, “Noble one, this is a subject that is difficult to believe in,[1569] difficult to know, difficult to aspire to, difficult to comprehend, difficult to describe, and difficult to understand; the world and its devas and the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas are unable to comprehend it.

The goddess said, “This is hard to reach, hard to know, hard to believe, hard to penetrate, hard to say, hard to understand. Neither celestial nor human beings can comprehend it, nor can any listeners or individual illuminates comprehend it,
gzhan du na de bzhin gshegs pa'i byin gyi rlabs dang /
However, through the blessing of the tathāgatas,
except those who, by the empowerment of Buddha,
dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyis yongs su bzung ba ma gtogs te/
through being in the care of a kalyāṇamitra,[1570]
by the help of spiritual benefactors,
gnas 'di ni/ sems can 'khor ba'i bde ba thams cad la mngon par 'dod pa med pa/
those beings who have no yearning for any bliss in saṃsāra,
thus do not seek any mundane pleasures,
de bzhin gshegs pa'i bde ba la lhag par dmigs pa/
who are focused on the bliss of the tathāgatas,
are focused on the pleasure of the enlightened,
sems can thams cad kyi sdug bsngal dang yid mi bde ba rab tu zhi bar bya ba la zhugs pa/
who are engaged in ending the suffering and unhappiness of all beings,
have undertaken to put an end to the suffering and misery of all beings,
de bzhin gshegs pa'i yon tan rgya mtsho la 'jug pa'i nan tan la mngon par mos pa/
who aspire to the knowledge[1571] that comprehends the ocean of the qualities of the tathāgatas,
are headed into the ocean of virtues of the enlightened,
chos thams cad kyi rang bzhin nges par rtogs pa/ nam mkha'i spyod yul dang ldan pa/
who have realized the nature of all phenomena and have space as their field of activity,
are in the realm of the space of meditation on the intrinsic nature of things,
mos pa yangs pa'i lam gyis rnam par dag pa/
who are purified by the path of a vast aspiration,
have purified the path of higher aspirations,
'khor ba'i rgyun las phyir phyogs pa/
who have turned away from the course of saṃsāra,
have turned away from the flow of the mundane whirl,
de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi ye shes rgya mtsho la mngon par mos pa/
who aspire to the ocean of wisdom of all the tathāgatas,
are turned toward the ocean of knowledge of the enlightened,
chos kyi grong khyer du 'gro bar gcig tu chad pa/
who are determined to go to the city of the Dharma,[1572]
are certain to arrive at the citadel of omniscience,
de bzhin gshegs pa'i yul yongs su gnon pa'i brtson 'grus can/
who have the diligence to attain the field of activity of the tathāgatas,
proceed energetically into the sphere of those who arrive at Thusness,
sangs rgyas kyi sa'i rgyud rnam par gnon pa/
who have the prowess to reach the level of the buddhas,
advance boldly toward buddhahood,
thams cad mkhyen pa'i stobs yongs su rdzogs par bya ba la mngon par mos pa/
who aspire to the perfection of the power of omniscience,
are headed toward complete fulfillment of the powers of omniscience,
stobs bcu rab tu thob par bya ba'i mthar thug pa rnams kyis bsod nams dang /
and who have fully attained the ten strengths,
and will ultimately attain the ten powers—
ye shes kyi tshogs yangs pas nye bar bsten pa'i sems dang /
with a mind supported by a vast accumulation of merit and wisdom,
by the mind being stabilized on great stores of virtue and knowledge,
bsam pa rnam par dag pa dang
with a pure motivation,
by purity of intention,
ma zhum pa/
with a mind that is not disheartened,
by the mind being buoyant,
nyon mongs pa med pa dang
is not defiled,
undisturbed,
ma yo ba dang /
is not insincere,
straightforward,
ma nyams pa dang /
is unimpaired,
unimpaired,
ma 'chums pa dang /
has not narrowed,
open,
mun pa med pa'i sems dang /
and is not in darkness,
unobscured,
ye shes kyi snang ba kun tu snang bas snang bar gyur pa'i sems dang /
with a mind that is illuminated by the light of completely illuminating wisdom,
by the mind being illumined by the light of universal knowledge,
sems can thams cad la phan pa dang bde bar bya bar shin tu 'dun pa'i sems dang /
with a mind intent on bringing happiness and benefit to all beings,
by the mind being dedicated to the welfare and happiness of all beings,
bdud kyi 'khor dang nyon mongs pa thams cad kyis mi thub pa'i sems dang /
with a mind that cannot be defeated by the kleśas and all Māra’s entourage,
by the mind being invulnerable to the afflictions of all demons,
thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi ye shes thob par bya bar skabs phye ba'i sems kyis kyang
and with a mind that has the opportunity to attain omniscient wisdom,
by the mind being within range of attainment of omniscience, — such people
khong du chud pa dang /
are able to understand,
can penetrate,
'jug pa dang /
comprehend,
yid ches par bya ba dang /
believe in,
believe in,
gzung ba dang /
grasp,
grasp,
rjes su 'brang bar bya ba'am/ shes par bya ba mi nus so/ /
follow, and know this subject.
follow, and know this matter.

de ci'i phyir zhe na/ rigs kyi bu/ gnas 'di ni/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i ye shes kyi yul te/ byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyis yongs su ma non na/ sems can gzhan thams cad kyis lta ci zhig smos/ 'on kyang sems can cang shes rnams kyi bsam pa phun sum tshogs pa rnam par dag par bya ba dang / dge ba'i rtsa ba la spyod pa'i sems can rnams kyi lhag pa'i bsam pa dbang du 'gyur bar bya ba dang / khyod kyis bsam pa thag pa nas yongs su dris pa'i lung bstan pa'i chos nyid rab tu 'byung ba thob par bya ba'i phyir de bzhin gshegs pa'i byin gyis bstan to/ /

“Why is that? Noble one, this subject is the field of the knowledge of the tathāgatas. All bodhisattvas, let alone all other beings, cannot reach it. Nevertheless, through the blessing of the tathāgatas, I teach it so that noble beings will have a perfectly pure motivation, so that beings with a conduct of roots of virtue will have a superior motivation, and so that you will obtain the arising of the true answer to your sincere[1573] question.”

Why? Because this matter is the sphere of buddhas—not even enlightening beings can reach it, much less others. Now, with the support of the Buddha I will tell you, for the sake of the correct purification of the minds of those capable of learning, so that those who practice good can master their minds, and so that you may have an explanation of what is on your mind.”

de nas mtshan mo'i lha mo shing thams cad kyi me tog rgyas pas bde bar gnas pas de'i tshe don de nyid brnan te bstan pa'i phyir dus gsum du byung ba'i de bzhin gshegs pa'i yul la rnam par bltas te tshigs su bcad pa 'di dag smras so/ /

Then, at that time, the night goddess Sarvavṛkṣpraphullanasukhasaṃvāsā, in order to teach this meaning further, looking into the field of knowledge of the tathāgatas of the three times, recited these verses:
Then the goddess, further elucidating what she meant, looked over the realm of the buddhas of past, present, and future and spoke these verses:
sangs rgyas sras po khyod kyis gang dris pa/ / de ni bsam yas zab mo sangs rgyas yul/ / bsam yas zhing gi rdul phran rab snyed kyi/ / bskal pa mang pos de kun brjod mi nus/ /

“The profound, inconceivable field of knowledge of the buddhas About which you, son of the buddhas, have asked a question Cannot be entirely explained, even in as many kalpas As there are atoms in countless realms. {1}
Profound, infinite, is the sphere of buddhas, Of which you now ask, O child of Buddha. Even in eons as many as atoms in inconceivable lands It could not be fully told.
sems can 'dod pa'i sems ldan sdang ba dang / / de bzhin gti mug mun pas bsgribs pa dang / / 'chab dang dregs pas bsam pa nyams gyur pas/ / rgyal ba'i chos nyid zhi ba shes mi nus/ /

“Beings who have desiring minds and those with angry minds, And similarly those obscured by the darkness of ignorance And those who are afflicted by hypocrisy and arrogance, Are unable to know the peace of the true nature of the jinas. {2}
The peaceful nature of the buddhas cannot be known By the covetous or the malevolent, Or by those shrouded in the darkness of delusion, Or those whose minds are defiled by hypocrisy and conceit.
phrag dog 'jungs pa'i dbang gi rjes 'brang dang / / g.yo sgyus bsam pa rnyog par gyur pa dang / / nyon mongs las kyi sgrib pas bsgribs pa yis/ / sangs rgyas yul 'di shes par mi nus so/ /

“Those who are overpowered by and follow envy and jealousy, Those who are polluted by thoughts of deception and deceit, And those who are obscured by the obscuration of kleśas and karma Are unable to know this field of the buddhas. {3}
This sphere of buddhas cannot be known By those ruled by envy and jealousy, Or those whose minds are polluted by guile and deceit, Or those enshrouded by barriers of action based on afflictions.
phung po khams dang skye mched gnas pa dang / / 'jig tshogs mang la gnas par gyur pa dang / / lta sems 'du shes phyin ci log gyur pas/ / zhi ba'i sa 'di shes par mi nus so/ /

“Those who are established in the skandhas, dhātus, and āyatanas, Those who are dependent on the destructible accumulation, And those whose minds and views are aberrant Are unable to know this level of the buddhas. {4}
Buddhahood cannot be known By those who depend on mental or material elements, Or those attached to the body as real, Or those with false views and ideas.
rgyal ba'i yul ni shes dka' zhi ba ste/ / rang bzhin dri med rnam par rtog pa med/ / srid par brten cing 'khor la chags pa yis/ / chos 'di yang dag shes par mi nus so/ /

“The field of the jinas is a peace that is difficult to comprehend. Its nature is stainless, and it is without conceptualization. Those who are dependent on existence and cling to saṃsāra Are not able to know this Dharma. {5}
Hard to know is the tranquil realm of buddhas, Which is inherently pure and nonconceptual— This reality cannot be truly known By those attached to life and being.
sangs rgyas rigs su rigs ldan gang skyes pa/ / de bzhin gshegs pa kun gyis byin brlabs shing / / chos kyi rgyal po'i gdung rabs yongs 'dzin pa/ / drang srong de dag yul ni 'di yin no/ /
“This is the field for those ṛṣis Of the family and born in the family[1574] of the buddhas, Who have been consecrated by all the tathāgatas And are holders of the lineage of the Dharma king. {6}
Those who are born in the family of buddhas, Who are empowered by all the buddhas, Who preserve the lineage of the enlightened, Are the knowers of this sphere.
dkar chos rgya mtshos mi ngoms sems ldan zhing / / gang rnams dge ba'i bshes kyis yongs bzung ste/ / thub pa'i stobs la dmigs pa'i sems sprin can/ / de dag 'di thos bzod pa thob par 'gyur/ /

“Those who are never satisfied by an ocean of good qualities, Who have been taken into the care of kalyāṇamitras, And who have a cloud of aspiration focused on the strengths of the munis Attain peace when they hear this. {7}
Those who are tireless in good practices And are helped by spiritual benefactors, With their minds focused on the powers of sages, They attain peace on perceiving this.
gang rnams bsam pa dri med rnams rtog med/ / bar snang mkha' bzhin phyogs dang phyogs mtshams su/ / mun pa rnam bsal blo gros sgron ma'i sprin/ / dri med de dag spyod yul 'di yin no/ /
