“Those who have stainless, nonconceptual motivation, Whose understanding is like a cloud of lamps ending darkness‍— Those stainless ones have this field of activity Throughout the main and intermediate directions, to the extent of space. {8}
This is the sphere of the undefiled Whose minds are pure, without false ideas, Like the sky in all directions, Lamps of wisdom who have dispelled darkness.
snying rje'i bsam pas 'gro ba rgya mtsho rnams/ / dus gsum byung ba gang rnams rgyas byed cing / / sems can ma lus rjes 'brang byams pa can/ / de dag rgyal ba'i tshul 'dir 'jug par 'gyur/ /
“They who have a motivation of compassion for the ocean of beings‍— Their presence pervades the entire three times. They follow every single being with love, Entering this way of the jinas. {9}
Those who pervade all worlds Of all times with compassion And are benevolent to all beings Enter the way of the buddhas.
gang rnams 'dzin med dga' ba'i sems ldan zhing / / rtag par bdog pa thams cad sbyin brtson la/ / sems can kun la mnyam par zhugs gyur pa/ / chags med de dag spyod yul sa 'di yin/ /

“Those who have a rapturous mind that is free of grasping Are constantly dedicated to giving away everything. They engage in activity with all beings equally And have no attachment to this level of conduct. {10}
This is the stage of those without grasping, The happy ones without attachment Who always gladly give all there is Impartially to all beings.
nyon mongs med sems bskyod med spyod ldan zhing / / gang rnams 'gyod pa rnams bsal la sems ldan te/ / sangs rgyas gdams ngag nan tan byed ldan pa/ / dri med de dag spyod yul 'di yin no; ;

“Those who are without defilements, with conduct free of transgressions, Who are dedicated to practicing the teaching of the buddhas And whose minds have repentance of wrongdoing[1575]‍— Those stainless ones have this field of activity. {11}
This is the sphere of the undefiled, Whose minds are unafflicted and conduct impeccable, Whose minds are ultimately free from regret, Who apply themselves to practice of Buddha’s teaching.
gang rnams mi sgul sems ldan mi bskyod sems/ / chos kyi rang bzhin rtogs pa'i sems ldan zhing / / las kyi rgya mtshor mi 'gal sems ldan pa/ / mi bzad de dag rnam thar 'di yin no/ /
“Those who have unshakable, steadfast minds, Whose minds have realized the nature of phenomena, Who have minds unhindered by an ocean of karma‍— For them this liberation is inexhaustible. {12}
This is the liberation of the inexhaustible Whose minds are unshakable, imperturbable, Whose minds are focused on the essence of things, Whose minds are unhindered by the oceans of actions.
gang rnams mi skyo'i sems dang mi ldog sems/ / brtson 'grus mthu dang rtsal du ldan pa rnams/ / thams cad mkhyen tshogs brtson 'grus mtha' yas pa/ / brtul zhugs bzang ldan de dag yul 'di yin/ /

“For those with minds that are never disheartened,[1576] never turn back, Those who have strong and powerful diligence, With endless diligence for the accumulation of omniscience‍— For those with excellent discipline, there is this field of activity. {13}
This is the sphere of the disciplined, With indefatigable and nonregressing minds, With strength, vigor, and control, With endless energy in preparing for omniscience.
zhi ba'i sems ldan mnyam par bzhag pa gang / / shin tu zhir gyur rim dang bral ba rnams/ / kun mkhyen bsam gtan yan lag mchor spyod pa/ / rab tu zhi ba de dag tshul 'di yin/ /
“Those with minds of peace, minds at rest, Who are in complete peace, unfevered, Practicing an ocean of omniscient dhyāna‍— For those who have become peaceful, there is this way. {14}
This is known to those gone to peace, With tranquil minds, concentrated, Ultimately calm and cool, Practitioners of all the branches of meditation.
gang rnams chags pa kun las sems grol zhing / / chos kyi rang bzhin khong du chud sems can/ / rgyal ba'i chos dbyings rtogs par khong chud pa/ / shes rab sgron ma de dag tshul 'di yin/ /

“Those whose minds are freed from all attachment, Whose minds have understood the nature of phenomena, Who have realized the Dharma realm of the jinas‍— For those who are lamps of wisdom, there is this way. {15}
This is known to the lamps of wisdom, Whose minds are liberated from all attachments And have penetrated the essence of things, Who have gone the way into the reality realm of the enlightened.
sems can rang bzhin rtogs sems ldan gyur cing / / gang rnams srid pa'i mtsho la chags med sems/ / sems can sems la gzugs brnyan zla 'char ba/ / lam mkhan de dag rnam thar 'di yin no; ;

“Those whose minds have realized the nature of beings, Whose minds have no attachment to the ocean of existence, Who appear to the minds of beings like the reflections of the moon‍— For those who are wise in the path, there is this liberation. {16}

This is the liberation of those who know the path, Whose minds have penetrated the essence of beings, Whose minds are not imprisoned in the sea of existence, Who are moons reflected in the minds of beings.
dus gsum byung ba'i rgyal ba rgya mtsho rnams/ / smon lam gang chen mtsho rgyud skyes pa yi/ / zhing rnams kun tu phyi ma'i mthar spyod pa/ / kun tu bzang po de dag tshul 'di yin/ /

“Those who practice in all future realms That arise from the ocean of the family of prayers Of the ocean of jinas who are in the three times‍— For those who are completely good, there is this way. {17}
This is known to the universally good, Who are born from the ocean of vows Of the buddhas past, present, and future, And carry them out forever in all lands.
gang rnams chos dbyings tshul rnams rgya mtsho yis/ / 'gro ba rgya mtsho 'du dang 'jig pa yi/ / bskal par bcas pa khong du chud pa rnams/ / rtog med de dag rnam thar 'di yin no/ /

“Those who through an ocean of the ways of the realm of Dharma Enter into the entire ocean of worlds In all the kalpas of creation and destruction‍— For those who are free of conceptualization, there is this liberation. {18}
This is the liberation of those who penetrate all oceans of worlds By means of the oceans of principles of the reality realm And see their ages of becoming and decay without discrimination.
zhing rnams kun gyi rdul phran thams cad la/ / sangs rgyas grangs med shing rgyal drung bzhugs shing / / byang chub 'tshang rgya 'gro 'dul mthong ba yi/ / chags med dmigs can de dag tshul 'di yin/ /

“Those who see, in the atoms of the realms in all directions, Countless buddhas at the foot of the kings of trees Attaining enlightenment and guiding beings‍— For those with vision free of attachment, there is this way. {19}
This is known to those of unobstructed vision Who see the buddhas under the enlightenment trees, As many as atoms in all lands, Teaching after having realized enlightenment.
khyod ni bskal pa rgya mtsho rgya chen du/ / dge ba'i bshes gnyen mang po bsnyen bkur te/ / chos 'dod chos tshol mi skyo 'dir phyin pas/ / thos nas de ni yongs su gzung bar nus/ /
“You have served kalyāṇamitras Through a great ocean of kalpas And so have come here, unwearyingly seeking the Dharma. You are able to hold this when you have heard it. {20}
You have come after many eons Of serving spiritual benefactors In quest of the Teaching, seeking tirelessly; Having heard it, you can remember it.
khyod kyi bsam pa yongs su sbyang ba'i phyir/ / bde gshegs byin rlabs bsam gyis mi khyab pas/ / rnam par snang mdzad tshad med yul 'di yang / / kho mo'i tshig las chags pa med par 'byung / /
“In order to purify your motivation, Through the inconceivable blessing of the sugatas[1577] This immeasurable field of Vairocana Will arise without impediment from my words. {21}
To purify your mind I will tell you freely Of the infinite realm of Vairocana By the inconceivable power of Buddha.

rigs kyi bu/ sngon byung ba'i dus bskal pa 'jig rten gyi khams kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi pha rol de'i yang pha snga zhig tu 'jig rten gyi khams rgya mtsho gser rin po che'i ri spos rnam par snang ba zhes bya ba byung ste/
“Noble one, in a time in the past even beyond as many kalpas as there are atoms in a world realm, there was an ocean of world realms called Maṇikanakaparvataśikharavairocana.
The goddess continued, “Long ago, past eons as many as atoms in an ocean of worlds, there was an ocean of worlds called Sun on the Summit of a Mountain of Gold and Jewels.

rigs kyi bu/ 'jig rten gyi khams rgya mtsho gser rin po che'i ri spos rnam par snang ba der de bzhin gshegs pa ye shes ri bo'i 'od chos kyi dbyings su snang ba'i gzi brjid rgyal po zhes bya ba byung ste/ de bzhin gshegs pa ye shes kyi ri bo'i 'od chos kyi dbyings su snang ba'i gzi brjid rgyal po de/ sngon byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa mdzad pa'i tshe 'jig rten gyi khams rgya mtsho gser rin po che'i ri spos rnam par snang ba zhes bya ba/

“Noble one, in that ocean of world realms called Maṇikanakaparvataśikharavairocana there was a tathāgata by the name of Jñānaparvatadharmadhātudikpratapanatejorāja. The Tathāgata Jñānaparvatadharmadhātudikpratapanatejorāja, through his previous bodhisattva conduct, had purified the ocean of world realms called Maṇikanakaparvataśikharavairocana.[1578]

Therein, furthermore, was a buddha called Supreme Light Illumining the Realm of Truth at the Summit of Knowledge, who purified that ocean of worlds while carrying out the practice of enlightening beings in the past.

'jig rten gyi khams rgya mtsho'i sa dang ri rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi 'jig rten gyi khams 'byams klas pa bstan du yod pa dang ldan pa/ 'jig rten gyi khams kyi rgyud re re zhing yang bskal pa'i grangs shin tu bstan pa 'jig rten gyi khams kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed dang ldan pa; bskal pa re re zhing yang bskal pa bar ma shin tu bstan pa du ma dang ldan pa/ bskal pa bar ma re re zhing yang 'jig rten gyi khams rnam pa tha dad du bya ba bstan pa du ma dang ldan pa/ de bzhin gshegs pa 'byung ba dang / rdzu 'phrul sna tshogs bstan du yod pa/ de bzhin gshegs pa byung ba re re zhing yang mdo sde yang dag par bstan pa 'jig rten gyi khams kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed brjod du yod pa/ mdo sde re re la yang byang chub sems dpa'i lung bstan pa 'jig rten gyi khams brjod du med pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed bstan du yod pa/ sems can 'dul ba mtha' dang dbus med pa shin tu bstan pa tha dad pa'i tshul gyis bsgrubs pa/ sangs rgyas kyi rnam par 'phrul pa dang / cho 'phrul sna tshogs kyis rnam par 'dul ba dang ldan pa yongs su sbyangs te/

“In that ocean of world realms called Maṇikanakaparvataśikharavairocana appeared as many ranges of world realms as there are atoms in the earth and the mountains. In each range of world realms appeared as many groups of world realms as there are atoms in a multitude of world realms. In each world realm[1579] appeared as many kalpas as there are atoms in a world realm. In each kalpa appeared numerous intermediate kalpas. In each intermediate kalpa appeared numerous world realms with different appearances. In those appeared various occurrences of tathāgatas and their miraculous manifestations. During each appearance of a buddha appeared as many sūtras as there are atoms in a world realm. Within each sūtra appeared as many prophecies to bodhisattvas as there are atoms in a world realm. There appeared a vast extent of guided beings, without edge or center, accomplishment through the ways of various yānas, and guidance through various miraculous manifestations.

In that ocean of worlds were as many world systems as atoms in all the mountains on earth, each system containing as many worlds as atoms in a galaxy. In each world there were as many sets of eons as atoms in a world, each containing many eons, in each of which there were many events, including buddhas appearing in the world and displaying miracles. Each buddha that appeared expounded as many scriptures as atoms in a world, in each of which scriptures were outlined as many instructions for enlightening beings as atoms in the world, with infinitely various indications of how to guide sentient beings, operated by the principles of various vehicles of liberation, guided by the buddhas’ various mystic powers of perception and prescription.

rigs kyi bu/ 'jig rten gyi khams rgya mtsho gser rin po che'i ri spos rnam par snang ba der 'jig rten gyi khams bar ma'i rgyud phyogs kun tu mngon par bltas pa'i sgo rgyal mtshan gyis rnam par brgyan pa zhes bya ba byung ste;
“Noble one, in that ocean of world realms called Maṇikanakaparvataśikharavairocana there was a central group of world realms called Samantadigabhimukhadvāradhvajavyūha.
“Within that ocean of worlds was a central world-system called Array of Markers of Doors Facing All Directions,

rigs kyi bu/ 'jig rten gyi khams bar ma'i rgyud phyogs kun tu sgo mngon par bltas pa rgyal mtshan gyis rnam par brgyan pa der 'jig rten gyi khams rin po che thams cad kyi mdog kun tu snang ba'i dpal yon bya ba 'jig rten gyi khams kyi gzhi dang /
“Noble one, in that central group of world realms called Samantadigabhimukhadvāradhvajavyūha there was the world realm called Sarvaratnavarṇasamantaprabhāsaśrī.
in which there was a world called Ubiquitous Light the Color of All Jewels.

mtshams kyi rgyan rin po che'i rgyal po de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi snying po byang chub rab tu snang ba las byas pa/ rin po che sna tshogs kyi me tog rgya mtsho la gnas pa/ lhun rin po che'i rgyal po de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi sprul pa'i gzugs brnyan rab tu ston pa las bsgrubs pa/ lha'i grong khyer gyi dbyibs su 'dug pa/ rnam par dag cing kun nas nyon mongs pa byang bar gyur te/

“It had a display of basis and borders of world realms. It had the shining bodhimaṇḍas of all the tathāgatas that were made of kings of jewels.[1580] It resided upon an ocean of flowers of various jewels. Its main mass was made of kings of precious jewels in which appeared the images of the emanations of all the tathāgatas. It had the form of a city of devas. It was both pure and defiled.

The borders of that world were arrayed with jewels reflecting images of the enlightenment sites of all buddhas; it rested on an ocean of flowers made of all kinds of jewels, it was composed of jewels showing the appearances of emanations of all buddhas, it was shaped like a celestial palace, and it was pure with an admixture of defilement.

'jig rten gyi khams der gling bzhi pa'i 'jig rten gyi khams ri rab kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed byung bar gyur to/ / gling bzhi pa'i ri rab kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed po de dag gi gling bzhi pa dbu ma rin po che sna tshogs kyi rtse mo'i rgyal mtshan zhes bya ba byung ste/ gling bzhi pa'i 'jig rten gyi khams rin po che sna tshogs kyi rtse mo'i rgyal mtshan der gling mchu zhang du dpag tshad brgya phrag stong yod pa bzhi byung nas gling re re la yang grong khyer chen po stong phrag re re byung ngo/ / gling bzhi pa de'i gling gi dbus su rgyal po'i gnas rin po che'i gnas rin po che'i sa las rnam par brgyan pa sprin gyi sgron ma zhes bya ba grong khyer stong phrag bcu'i 'khor dang ldan par byung ngo/ /

“In that world realm there were as many four-continent world realms as there are atoms in Sumeru. The central four continents among those four continents that were as numerous as the atoms in Sumeru was called Sarvaratnaśikharadhvaja. In that four-continent world called Sarvaratnaśikharadhvaja, each of the four continents was a hundred thousand yojanas wide. In each of those continents there were a thousand great cities. In the center of the Jambudvīpa of that four-continent world there was a royal capital called Ratnasālavyūhameghapradīpā, which was encircled by ten thousand cities.

Furthermore, in that world there were as many world-regions with four continents as atoms in the polar mountain; at the center was a set of four continents called Mountain Peak of All Jewels, whose four continents were innumerable hundreds of thousands of leagues in extent. On each continent were ten thousand great cities. In the middle of the southern continent was a great metropolis called the Light of Myriad Arrays of Jewel Trees, surrounded by ten thousand cities.

de'i tshe 'dzam bu'i gling de'i mi rnams kyang tshe'i tshad lo stong phrag bcu thub par gyur to/ / rgyal po'i gnas rin po che'i sa las rnam par brgyan pa sprin gyi sgron ma der 'khor los bsgyur ba'i rgyal po chos thams cad kyi nga ro'i gdugs kyi dkyil 'khor rab tu sgrog pa zhes bya ba byung ste/ 'khor los bsgyur ba'i rgyal po chos thams cad kyi nga ro'i gdugs kyi dkyil 'khor rab tu sgrog pa de'i blon po ni/ lnga brgya byung ngo/ / btsun mo ni/ stong phrag drug byung ngo/ / sras ni/ kun kyang dpa' ba/ rtul phod pa/ yan lag dam pa'i gzugs dang ldan pa; blta na sdug pa/ gzi brjid che ba/ stobs che ba brgya phrag bdun byung ngo/ /

“At that time, the people of that Jambudvīpa had a lifespan of ten thousand years. In the royal capital called Ratnasālavyūhameghapradīpā there was a cakravartin king by the name of Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa. The cakravartin king Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa had five hundred ministers. He had sixty thousand queens. He had seven hundred sons who were all courageous and heroic, with perfectly formed bodies, handsome and magnificent, and very strong.

On that continent, furthermore, the life span of the people was ten thousand years. The king in that metropolis was named Encompassing Sound of the Proclamation of All Laws, a sovereign ruler. The king had five hundred ministers, six thousand concubines, and seven hundred sons all of whom were brave and manly, well built and handsome, dignified and strong.

rgyal po chos thams cad kyi nga ro'i gdugs kyi dkyil 'khor rab tu sgrog pa de'i tshe la dzam+bu'i gling thams cad kyang gdugs gcig gis bskyangs par gyur te pha rol gyi 'khor dang dgra thams cad kyang shin tu chom par gyur to/ /
“During the time of King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa, he protected all of Jambudvīpa under one parasol and vanquished all enemies and opponents.
The whole continent was under the protection of that king, and he had no enemies or opponents.

de'i tshe 'jig rten gyi khams der bskal pa bar ma ni/ zad du cha/ rnyog pa lnga 'jig rten du byung / dge ba bcu'i las kyi lam ni/ nub par gyur nas sems can mi dge ba bcu'i lam la spyod pa phal cher ngan song du yang 'dong bar gyur to/ /

During that time, in that world realm, as the intermediate kalpa was ending, the five degenerations appeared, the path of the ten good actions vanished, beings practiced the path of the ten bad actions, and most went to the lower realms.

“At that time the end of the eon was approaching in that world; the five corruptions were in evidence, people had stopped acting virtuously and had taken to bad ways, most of them were headed for misery.

de dag mi dge ba bcu'i las kyi lam yongs su 'dzin pa'i rgyus tshe thung ba dang / longs spyod chung ba dang / gzugs ma legs pa dang / kha dog mi sdug pa dang / lus ma legs pa dang / bde ba'i rnam pa nyung ba dang / sdug bsngal nyams su myong ba'i rnam pa mang ba dang / phan tshun slu zhing 'drid pa'i rang bzhin can dang / phan tshun dbye ba la zhugs pa dang / zhe gcod pa'i tshig la spyod pa dang / 'chal ba'i tshig tu smra ba dang / 'dod pa mi bzad pas zil gyis non pa dang / zhe sdang ba'i yid kyi rtog pa dang ldan pa/ lta ba'i thibs po sna tshogs kyi mya ngan du 'khyams par gyur nas de dag chos ma yin pa'i 'dod chags la zhen cing 'dod pa mi bzad pas zil gyis non la/ log pa'i chos kyis kun nas 'khor bas

Their following the path of bad actions became the cause for lifespans to become short, pleasures to be few, and bodies to be ugly, have a bad color, and be misshapen. There was little happiness and the experience of many kinds of suffering. They deceived and betrayed one another. They caused divisions between one another. They engaged in harsh speech. They spoke incoherently. They were overcome by overpowering desires. They had the thoughts of angry minds. They wandered in a wilderness of various thickets of wrong views. They clung to desires that were contrary to the Dharma, and they were overcome by those overpowering desires. They were encompassed by false Dharma.

Because of their wrongdoings their lives were short, they had scanty means of subsistence, they were ugly, they experienced little pleasure and much pain, they were in the habit of argument and dissent, they were given to foul and incoherent speech, they were overcome by acquisitiveness, they were corrupt in mind and thought, they were lost in the jungle of various views. As they were obsessed with unreasonable desires and dominated by unwholesome acquisitiveness,

sa la shing rtsi dang / lo zas skye bar 'gyur ba'i char yang dus su mi 'bab par 'gyur te/ sems can de dag kyang dang / gel ba dang / sman dang / nags tshal dang / bza' shing gi ra ba dang / sdong po dag kyang bskams par gyur nas nad sna tshogs kyis thebs shing phyogs dang phyogs mtshams su skyabs med pas phan tshun khod mi myong zhing g.yen spyo bar gyur te/

Therefore, trees, plants, and harvests of food did not grow from the ground. The rain did not come on time. For those beings, the grass, herbs, shrubs, forests, orchards, and trees withered. They were afflicted by various illnesses. Throughout the main and intermediate directions they had no protector, and so they disrespected and were in contention with one another.

the rain that would cause the crops to grow did not fall in the proper season. For that reason, furthermore, with all the vegetation withered, the people suffered from various diseases and scattered to the eight directions, without resort.

de dag kun kyang gcig tu 'dus nas rgyal ba'i gnas rin po che'i sa las rnam par brgyan pa sprin gyi sgron ma gang na ba der dong ste kun tu bskor nas la la ni/ lag pa gyen tu bsgreng / la la ni/ thal mo sbyor/ la la ni/ lus shin tu 'dar/ la la ni/ gyed/ la la ni/ bub/ la la ni/ lus thams cad kyis phab cing phyag 'tshal/ la la ni/ pus mo sa la 'dzugs/ la la ni/ lag pa nam mkha'i dbyings su g.yo ba/ la la ni/ gos med cing sgren mor 'khod/ la la ni/ kha mig mi sdug par gyur cing rgyal po chos thams cad kyi nga ro'i gdugs kyi dkyil 'khor rab tu sgrog pa la mngon du bltas shing / snying rje rje skad du 'o dod chen po 'bod de/

“They all gathered together and went to the royal capital Ratnasālavyūhameghapradīpā. They surrounded it, some with their arms upraised, some with hands clasped together, some with their bodies trembling, some collapsing,[1581] some falling with their heads on the ground, some with their bodies stretched out on the ground prostrate, some kneeling, some waving their arms in the air, some naked without clothes, some with an ugly expression of the face and eyes. They stared at King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa and cried out in a great piteous clamor,
They all went to the capital city Light of Myriad Arrays of Jewel Trees, surrounded it, and with various gestures of supplication raised a great outcry to the king—

lha chen po/ bdag cag ni/ nyam thag go / bkres pa dang skom pa'i sdug bsngal gyis rab tu gzir to/ / 'jigs pa sna tshogs kyis g.yen spyo'o/ / bdag cag la skyabs su yang ma mchis so/ / bdag cag la mgon dang dpung gnyen ma mchis so/ / sdug bsngal gyi shing thags kyis 'khor to/ / srog chad la thug go / 'chi bar gyur ma khad do/ / zhes te/

‘Your Majesty! We are in distress! The suffering of hunger and thirst pains us! We are afflicted by various fears! We have no refuge! We have no protector or last resort! We are walled around by suffering! We are losing our lives! We are facing death!’

‘We are oppressed, abandoned, tormented by hunger and thirst, dismayed and distressed, without any savior, without refuge or resort, in a cage of suffering; our livelihood is threatened, and we are on the brink of death.’

smre sngags sna tshogs su bla zhing dbyangs kyi rnam pa sna tshogs dang / tshig sna tshogs kyis kha gdong mi sdug par gyur par 'du shes dang / tshig sna tshogs kyi tha snyad dang / cho 'brang dang / skad kyi gdangs don sna tshogs rjod pa'i tshig dang / ngag gis 'o dod bos so/ /

“In that way they wailed in various ways, crying out with various kinds of voices, with various words, various unpleasant facial expressions, various verbal expressions,[1582] terms of speech, and words from various dialects and in various accents.
rgyal po'i gnas de'i skyes pa dang / bud med dang / khye'u dang / bu mo bkres pa dang / skom pas mnar ba/
“All the men and women, boys and girls of that royal capital, who were tormented by hunger and thirst,
The people in the city who were suffering from hunger and thirst,
lus la rgyan med pa/ sgren mo gos med pa/
whose bodies were devoid of jewelry, who had no clothes and were naked,
who were naked and homeless,
kha dog mi sdug pa/ lus gas shing rtsub pa/
who were unsightly and discolored, whose skin was cracked and rough,
also were sick
sdug bsngal zhing yid mi bde la mi dga' ba
and who were suffering and unhappy, were in distress,
who were in misery, despondent,
de dag thams cad kyang bde ba ni/ mngon par 'dod/ sdug bsngal gyi 'jigs pas ni/ brla khyer nas
yearning for happiness, and afraid of suffering.
and depressed, and tired of suffering.

rgyal po shes pa'i skyes bu chen po chos thams cad kyi nga ro'i gdugs kyi dkyil 'khor rab tu sgrog pa de la bde ba thams cad thob par bya ba'i 'du shes dang / sdug bsngal thams cad dang mi 'grogs par bya ba'i 'du shes dang /

Therefore, they sought protection from the great wise being King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa as a refuge, perceiving him to be someone through whom they could obtain happiness, perceiving him to be someone through whom they could become free of suffering,[1583]
They betook themselves to the king as a man of great knowledge and a protector, thinking they had found a source of comfort, happiness,
'tsho ba'i bsam pa dang ldan zhing gter thob par bya ba'i 'du shes dang /
perceiving him to be someone through whom they could gain sustenance and obtain treasure,
and livelihood,
mu stegs mthong bar bya ba'i 'du shes dang /
perceiving him to be like the sight of a ford,
lam chen po la nan tan du bya ba'i 'du shes dang /
a guide to the way out,
gru chen po'i 'du shes dang /
perceiving him to be a ship,
a great ship,
ye shes kyi gling chen po'i 'du shes dang /
perceiving him to be a great island of wisdom,[1584]
an island of jewels of knowledge,
don chen po rab tu thob par bya ba'i 'du shes dang /
perceiving him to be someone through whom they could attain a great benefit,
a great benefit,
mtho ris kyi dga' ba dang / bde ba thams cad rab tu thob par bya ba'i 'du shes kyis mgon dang skyabs tshol bar gyur to/ /
and perceiving him to be someone through whom they could obtain all the joys and happiness of higher existences.
thinking they had found all the delights of heaven.

rgyal po chos thams cad kyi nga ro'i gdugs kyi dkyil 'khor rab tu sgrog pas 'khor kun nas slong ba mang po snying rje rje skad du 'bod pa'i 'o dod chen po de thos nas de snying rje chen po'i sgo brgya stong grangs med pa phrag bcu la zhugs par gyur to/ / de snying rje chen po'i tshul yid la bab pa'i sems su gyur nas yud tsam zhig rtse gcig tu bsam ste snying rje chen po dang ldan pa'i tshig bcu brjod do/ / bcu gang zhe na/

“When King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa heard the great clamor of the wailing of numerous piteous cries from all around him, he entered countless millions of gateways into great compassion. His mind resting in the mental state that is the way of great compassion, he contemplated one-pointedly for a moment and then spoke ten sentences of great compassion. What were those ten? They were:

“The king, hearing their outcry, was filled with countless tens of hundreds of thousands of facets of great compassion. Meditating on the principle of great compassion, in a moment he became single-minded and uttered ten statements of great compassion:

kyi hud kye sems can 'di dag ni/ 'khor ba'i g.yang sa chen por lhung yang skyabs med pa lta na/ bdag nam zhig 'khor ba'i g.yang sa chen por lhung ba'i sems can rnams de bzhin gshegs pa'i sa la 'god pas gnas su 'gyur/

“ ‘Oh! Alas! I see these beings have fallen into the abyss of saṃsāra and are without a support. When can I become a refuge for these beings, who have fallen into the great abyss of saṃsāra, and bring them to the level of the tathāgatas?
‘Alas, these people, without support, have fallen into the great pitfall of the mundane whirl—how can I be a refuge for them, leading them to the state of repose of the enlightened?

kyi hud kyi sems can 'di dag ni/ nyon mongs pa'i gnod pas gtses shing skyabs med pa lta na/ nam zhig bdag sems can nyon mongs pa sna tshogs kyi 'jigs pa dang gnod pas gtses te skyabs med pa rnams kha na ma tho ba med pa'i las kyi mtha' la 'god pas skyabs su 'gyur/

“ ‘Oh! Alas! I see these beings are oppressed by the torment of the kleśas and have no refuge. When can I become a refuge for these beings, who are frightened by various kleśas, without a refuge, and oppressed by the torment of the kleśas, and establish them in irreproachable actions?
Alas, these people have no savior and are oppressed by all kinds of afflictions—how can I become their savior, leading them to impeccable behavior?

kyi hud kye sems can 'di dag ni/ 'jig rten na rga shi'i 'jigs pas tshar chod cing mgon med pa lta na/ nam zhig bdag sems can mgon med pa rnams kyi 'khor ba'i 'jigs pa thams cad rnam par sel bas mgon du 'gyur/

“ ‘Oh! Alas! I see these beings are overcome by the fear of old age and death in this world and have no refuge. When can I become a refuge for these beings, who have no refuge, and dispel all their fear of saṃsāra?
Alas, these people have no refuge in the world and are terrorized by old age and death—how can I become a refuge for them, removing all their fears of life and death?

kyi hud kye sems can 'di dag ni/ 'jig rten gyi 'jigs pa sna tshogs kyis gtses te rten med pa lta na/ nam zhig bdag sems can 'jig rten gyi 'jigs pa sna tshogs kyis gtses pa rnams shin tu bde zhing skyon med pa'i thams cad mkhyen pa'i lam la dgod pas rten du 'gyur/

“ ‘Oh! Alas! I see these beings are tormented by the various fears in this world and have no recourse. When can I become a recourse for these beings, who are tormented by the various fears in the world, and establish them on the very happy and faultless path to omniscience?
Alas, these people have no resort and are oppressed by various kinds of worldly distress—how can I become a resort for them, leading them to ultimate safety on the path of omniscience?

kyi hud kye sems can 'di dag ni/ ma rig pa'i mun par 'thom ste the tshom dang / yid gnyis kyi rab rib kyis bsgribs pa lta na/ nam zhig bdag sems can thams cad kyi ma rig pa'i mun pa rnam par sel bas sgron mar 'gyur/

“ ‘Oh! Alas! I see these beings are enveloped in the darkness of ignorance in the world, and their sight is obscured by doubts and uncertainty. When can I become a lamp for these beings who have no refuge and dispel all the darkness of their ignorance?
Alas, everyone is in the darkness of ignorance, shrouded in the darkness of uncertainty and doubt—how can I become a light, dispelling the darkness of ignorance for them?
kyi hud kye sems can 'di dag ni/ snang ba dang bral ba lta na/ nam zhig bdag ye shes kyi sgo rab rib med pa yongs su ston pas ye shes chen po'i snang ba 'byin par 'gyur/
“ ‘Oh! Alas! I see these beings who are deprived of light. When can I provide them with the light of great wisdom by revealing to them the undarkened gateway to wisdom?
Alas, these people are without illumination—how can I spread the light of great knowledge, showing them all the way into unobscured knowledge?

kyi hud kye sems can 'di dag ni/ phrag dog dang / 'jungs ba dang / g.yo dang / sgyu'i rnyog pas bsam pa rnyog pa can du gyur te ye shes kyi mdog gsal ba med pa lta na/ nam zhig bdag sems can thams cad shin tu dag pa la rab tu gsal bar byed par 'gyur/

“ ‘Oh! Alas! I see beings, deprived of the brilliant light of wisdom, who are polluted by envy and jealousy, deception and deceit. When can I establish all beings in perfect purity and illuminate them with the brilliant light of the highest wisdom?

Alas, the world of these people lacks the light of knowledge, and their minds are polluted by envy, jealousy, guile, and deceit—how can I produce the light of supreme knowledge, leading them all to cultivate purity?

kyi hud kye sems can 'di dag ni/ 'khor ba rgya mtsho'i yul gyi rgyud du zhugs shing 'dren pa med pa lta na/ nam zhig bdag sems can chos thams cad chos rgya mtsho'i tshul la 'dzud par gyur cing 'dren par 'ong /
“ ‘Oh! Alas! I see the world of beings, who are without guidance, without a guide. When can I bring all beings into the ways of the ocean of the Dharma and become their guide?
Alas, the world is without a guide and has plunged into a dangerous current in the ocean of the mundane whirl—how can I become a guide, to show them what to do?

kyi hud kye sems can 'di dag ni/ ma dul zhing rnam par 'dren pa med pa lta na/ nam zhig bdag sems can thams cad rnam pa thams cad du yongs su smin par bya ba dang / rnam par gdul ba la de bzhin gshegs pa'i byin gyi rlabs kyis dus las mi 'da' zhing rnam par 'dren par 'ong /

“ ‘Oh! Alas! I see the world of beings, within the current of the ocean of saṃsāra, who are without a guide. When can I ripen and guide all beings in every way, without missing the time for the blessing of the tathāgatas, and become their guide?
Alas, everyone lacks a teacher, all are misguided—how can I become a teacher for everyone, with the proper timing commanded by a buddha to guide people to complete maturity in all qualities?

kyi hud kye sems can 'di dag ni/ dmus long du gyur te yongs su 'dren pa med pa lta na/ nam zhig bdag sems can thams cad sgrib pa med pa'i thams cad mkhyen pa'i ye shes kyi tshul la 'dzud cing yongs su 'dren par 'gyur/
“ ‘Oh! Alas! I see the world of beings is blind and without a guide. When can I bring all beings into the way of unobscured omniscient wisdom and become their guide?’
Alas, everyone lacks a leader, all are as though blind—how can I become a leader, to lead everyone on the way to unobstructed omniscience?’

de skad du des snying rje chen po dang ldan pa'i tshig rnam pa bcu brjod nas rgyal po'i gnas der dril chen po brdungs te gtong ba chen po'i rnga bo che'ang yongs su brdungs nas su ci 'dod pa de la de sbyin gyi/ 'gro ba thams cad kyang yongs su tshim par bya'o; ;zhes sgra brjod nas

“After he had spoken these ten sentences of great compassion, the great bell of the royal capital was rung, and the great drum of the great gift-giving was beaten. He declared, ‘I shall give whatever anyone desires, and I shall bring satisfaction to all beings.’
“Having made these expressions of compassion, the king announced that he would undertake a great sacrifice, that he would satisfy everyone, giving them whatever they needed.

des 'dzam bu'i gling thams cad kyi rgyal po'i gnas thams cad dang / grong dang / grong khyer dang / ljongs dang / yul dang / grong rdal thams cad du yo byad thams cad kyi mdzod phye ste/ lam gyi mdo dang / lam gyi sum mdo dang / srang thams cad du'ang yo byad sna tshogs kyi rnam pa mang po bkod de/ 'gro ba thams cad nye bar 'tsho bar bstabs so/ /

“In all the royal capitals throughout Jambudvīpa, and in all the villages, towns, market towns, districts, countries, and cities, all the stores of requisites were opened, and many different kinds of requisites were arranged at all crossroads, at the junctions of three roads, and in streets, and all beings were provided with the necessities of life.
With that the storehouses in every city and town on the continent were opened and all kinds of goods were placed on the streets, all the necessities of life were set out,
mdzod dang bang ba thams cad kyang phye ste/ rin po che'i gter chen po dang / tshogs kyang yongs su bstan to/ /
“All treasure houses and treasuries were opened, and a great accumulation of a treasure of jewels was displayed.
all treasuries were opened, all stores of valuables were displayed;
rin po che rnam pa sna tshogs kyi phung po du ma yang spungs so/ /
Many piles of various jewels were heaped up.
zas dang / skom dang / gos dang / bzhen pa dang / me tog dang / phreng ba dang / bdug pa dang / byug pa dang / phye ma dang / gos rin po che kha dog sna tshogs kyi mdzod phye nas
“Storehouses of food and drink, clothes, vehicles, flowers, garlands, incense and perfume, powders, jewelry, and precious clothes of various colors were opened.

khang pa dang / gzhal med khang dang / khyim mang po mal cha dang / stan dang / gos kyis yongs su brgyan te nor dang dbyig thams cad phun sum tshogs par byas nas nor bu rin po che'i rgyal po snang ba'i gzi brjid rnam par bkod pas mun pa rnam par sel ba bshams nas

“There were mansions, divine palaces, and houses, adorned by beds, seats, and clothing, with a perfection of all wealth and treasure, and a display of kings of jewels that dispelled darkness with their brilliant[1585] radiance.
des sems can de dag ci 'dod pa'i bsam pa thams cad yongs su rdzogs par bya ba'i phyir khyim de dag re rer yang rang gi lus dang 'dra ba'i sprul pa'i lus mngon par sprul te kun tu bkod do/ /
“He emanated and displayed in each of those houses an emanation that resembled his body, so that he could fulfill all the wishes and desires of those beings.
and the king projected a likeness of himself to every house to fulfill their wishes.
sems can thams cad kyi nad thams cad gso ba'i phyir sman pa dang / sman dang / rim gro pa dang / 'tsho ba'i yo byad sna tshogs kyi rkyen phun sum tshogs pa yongs su bshams so/ /
“In order to heal all the illnesses of all beings, he arranged the perfect conditions of medicines, doctors, treatments, and the various requisites for sustaining life.
[…see below…]
“He also set out containers of different shapes, made of various precious materials, that contained every kind of the variety of requisites:

rin po che sna tshogs kyi snod rnam pa tha dad pa yo byad sna tshogs kyis ci rigs su bkang pa dag kyang nye bar bkod de/ 'di ltar rin po che rdo rje'i snod ni/ spos kyi nor bu rin po che sna tshogs kyis yongs su bkang / spos kyi nor bu rin po che sna tshogs kyi snod ni/ gos kha dog dam pa sna tshogs kyis yongs su bkang ngo/ /

There were containers made of diamond jewels that were filled with various kinds of perfumed precious jewels. There were containers made of various perfumed precious jewels that were filled with clothes of various excellent colors.

shing rta mang po dbyibs dang mdog sna tshogs su 'dug pa/ rin po che sna tshogs kyis rab tu brgyan pa/ rta dang glang po dang ba lang cang shes la bcas pa/ rin po che'i shing rta sna tshogs rgyal po'i rkyen du rung ba/ rin po che thams cad kyi rgyan gyi longs spyod dang ldan pa/ stan sna tshogs bting ba/ rin po che sna tshogs kyis rnam par brgyan pa/ bla re sna tshogs bres pa/ rin po che'i dril bu'i dra ba bres pa/ gdugs dang / rgyal mtshan dang / ba dan bsgreng bas brgyan pa dag gis kyang yul gyi phyogs gang bar bkod do/ /

There were many chariots, set out throughout all the regions of the land, that were of various shapes and colors and adorned with various jewels, that had thoroughbred horses,[1586] oxen, and elephants[1587]‍—various precious chariots that were worthy of a king, made enjoyable with all adornments and jewels, set with various kinds of cushions, adorned with various jewels, covered with various canopies, hung with strings of precious bells, and adorned with upright parasols, banners, and flags.
grong dang / grong khyer dang / ljongs dang / yul thams cad sbyin par yang 'o dod kyis bsgo'o/ /
He commanded that villages, towns, countrysides, and regions were to be given away.

bza' shing gi ra ba dang / kun dga'i ra ba dang / dka' thub kyi nags tshal sna tshogs yongs su gtang ba dang / khyim dang / chung ma dang; bu dang / bu mo thams cad yongs su gtang ba dang / rin po che rin thang med pa thams cad yongs su gtang ba dang / rang gi snying dang / rkang dang / rgyu ma dang / mkhal ma dang; tshil dang / sha dang / khrag dang / pags pa dang / rkang lag dang / rna ba dang / mig dang / sna dang / so dang / mchu dang / mgo yongs su gtang ba nas phyi nang gi dngos po thams cad rnam pa thams cad du yongs su gtang bar yang 'o dod kyis bsgo'o/ /

“He gave away various orchards, parks, and forests for ascetics. He gave away all his homes, wives, sons, and daughters. He gave away all his priceless jewels. He gave away his own heart, marrow, intestines, kidneys, fat, flesh, blood, skin, arms, legs, nose, eyes, ears, tongue, teeth, lips, and head. He commanded that every kind of every outer and inner thing was to be given away.
des yo byad de lta bu yongs su gtang ba'i rnam pa mang po bshams te bsags nas
He had assembled and set out the many kinds of such gifts of requisites.
“Having arranged this act of giving things away,

rgyal po'i gnas rin po che'i sa las rnam par brgyan pa'i sprin gyi sgron ma de'i shar phyogs logs na grong khyer rin chen rtse mo'i gzi brjid ces bya ba'i mdun rol nas gzhi mnyam pa'i phyogs yangs pa mchu zheng du rgya che zhing mnyam pa/ mthon dman med pa/
To the east of the royal capital Ratnasālavyūhameghapradīpā, in front of the city called Maṇiśikharatejas, there was a vast level area of immense breadth, without any rise or fall.

he had a great place of sacrifice prepared east of the city, in front of the city gate called Jewel Mountain Light. That place was equal in length and width, covering a most extensive area. It was level and clean, without potholes,
rnam par dag cing gzhi mnyam pa/ ngam grog dang / g.yang sa dang / sdong dum dang; tsher ma dang / gseg ma dang / gyo mo thams cad med pa/
It was pure and level ground free of ravines, crevasses, tree stumps, thorns, pebbles, and gravel.
clear of brambles, dust, and gravel.

rin po che thams cad kyi khams las grub pa/ gzhi rin po che thams cad las byas shing rin po che'i rgyal po thams cad bkram pa; nor bu rin po che'i rgyan rnam pa du mas brgyan pa/ rin po che'i me tog sna tshogs kyis gang ba/

It consisted of a realm of all jewels. The ground was made from all jewels. All kings of jewels were strewn over it. It was adorned by many adornments of precious jewels. It was filled with various jewel flowers.
It was made of all precious elements, and the surface was spread with jewels. It was adorned with many arrays of jewels and strewn with flowers of various jewels.

phye ma sna tshogs dri shin tu zhim pa'i rdul ldang ba/ bdug spos sna tshogs kyis bdugs pa/ rin po che'i sgron ma dpal gyi gzi brjid can rab tu 'bar ba/ spos dang bdug spos thams cad kyi na bun dang / sprin gyis nam mkha' kun tu khebs pa'i rgyan dang ldan pa; rin po che sna tshogs kyi shing gi phreng ba legs par bkye bas mdzes par brgyan pa/ khang pa dang / gzhal med khang dang / khang pa brtsegs pa sna tshogs kyis yongs su brgyan pa/

Various extremely aromatic powders rose up from it as dust. There was a mist of perfumes and incense, and clouds of them formed an adornment that covered the entire sky. It was beautifully adorned by perfectly arranged lines of trees made of various precious materials. It was adorned by a variety of mansions, divine palaces, and kūṭāgāras.

There was an abundance of all the finest aromatic powders, and it was perfumed with all kinds of scents. There were lamps giving off jewel lights, and the sky was covered with radiant clouds of incense. The place was adorned with orderly rows of trees of all kinds of jewels as well as various mansions, palaces, and towers.

gdugs dang / rgyal mtshan dang / ba dan bsgreng ba/ rin po che'i snam bu lding ba/ rnam par snang ba/ rin po che sna tshogs kyi me tog gi dra bas kun nas khebs pa/ rin po che spos thams cad kyi rgyal po'i dra ba'i gdugs kyi dkyil 'khor can/

The cloth of precious parasols, banners, and flags fluttered. It was covered with a network of shining flowers of various jewels. It had a network of the circular shapes of parasols made of the kings of all precious incenses.

Overhead were parasols, banners, and pennants, flashing with trailing strings of various jewels. It was covered with nets of various jewel flowers, encircled with parasols made of webs of fragrant jewels.

gser gyi dra ba las rin po che'i dril bu 'khrol ba dang ldan pa/ bla re rin po che sna tshogs kyis rnam par mdzes par byas pas khebs par bres pa/ spos kyi rgyal po sna tshogs kyi phye ma rnam par bkram pa/ rin po che sna tshogs kyi me tog sil mas dga' dga' ltar gang ba/

It had jingling golden strings of precious bells. It was canopied over and beautified by various precious canopies. It was strewn with powders of the various kings of incenses. It was delightfully filled with the petals of jewels made of various jewels.

Jewel bells on nets of gold rang. It was shaded by canopies shining with various jewels, spread with aromatic powders of all the finest fragrances, and beautifully strewn with flowers made of all kinds of jewels,

rol mo brdung ba dang dkrol ba bye ba khrag khrig brgya stong gi sgra skad yid du 'ong ba 'byung ba/ rin po che thams cad kyi rgyan sna tshogs rnam par dag pas rnam par brgyan pa/ byang chub sems dpa'i las rnam par smin pas mngon par grub pa zhig yod pa

It emitted the beautiful sound of a quintillion musical instruments being played and beaten. It was adorned by a pure variety of adornments made of all jewels. It had been created through the ripening karma of bodhisattvas.
while pleasant music sounded from innumerable instruments. It was purified with arrays of various ornaments of all kinds of jewels, produced as a result of the deeds of enlightening beings.

de'i dbus su seng+ge'i khri chen po rin po che sna bcu las grub pa'i sa'i gzhi sna tshogs la gnas pas rin po che'i khri 'phang sna tshogs bcu'i 'khor gyis rnam par mdzes par byas pa/ rin po che'i shing yal ga can bcus stegs bu'i mtshams rnam par klubs pa'i rgyan mdzes pa dang ldan pa/ rdo rje'i 'khor lo'i sa'i gzhi mi shigs pa la rkang pa rab tu brten pa/

“In its center there was a great lion throne situated on a multicolored ground made of ten precious materials. It was magnificent in the center of a pavilion made of ten precious materials. It had the beautiful display of a well-arranged balustrade made from the branches of trees made of the ten jewels. It was set upon the surface of a circular platform of indestructible diamond.

“In the middle was a great lion throne, standing on a surface made of a variegated collection of ten kinds of jewels, surrounded by shining railings made of ten kinds of jewels, beautified with trees of ten kinds of jewels arrayed evenly between the railings, its feet firmly set on unbreakable diamond.

rin po che thams cad kyi gzugs dang mdog yongs su 'dzin pa'i stan gyi 'khor lo can/ rin po che du ma las byas pa'i bog re'i rgyan brgya phrag du mas brgyan pa/ rin po che sna tshogs kyi tshom bu rnam pa tha dad pa'i rgyan gyis shin tu brgyan pa/ rin po che'i rgyal mtshan kun nas rnam par phye ste 'phel ba bsgreng ba/ rin po che sna tshogs kyi ba dan dbyangs pa/ rnam pa tha dad pa'i rgyan dang ldan pa/ rin po che'i dril bu'i dra bas brgyan pa'i lha rdzas kyi rin po che sna tshogs dang / gser gyi dra ba sna tshogs rnam par bres pa/ rin po che sna tshogs kyi me tog gi dra ba dang / rin po che'i rgyal po chen po'i dra ba dang / gos rin po che sna tshogs dang / rin po che'i dra ba ci rigs su kun nas bkab cing mdzes par byas pa'i rgyan dang ldan pa/

It had a circular cushion with a form and color made of all precious materials. It was adorned by hundreds of crest adornments made of various precious materials. It was decorated by an array of inlays of different kinds made of many precious materials. Well-arranged precious banners had been erected all around it. It was hung[1588] with flags made of various precious materials. It was decorated with various kinds of decorations.[1589] It was adorned with nets of precious little bells.[1590] It was decorated with various divine jewels on strings of gold. It was covered with all kinds of beautifying arrays of nets of flowers made of various jewels, nets of great kings of jewels, nets of precious cloth, and nets of jewels.[1591]

The throne was set with jewel figurines and was adorned with hundreds of jewel protuberances. It was embellished with variegated arrays of jewels, jewel banners and streamers were raised all around it, and it was covered with nets of jewel bells, nets of celestial jewels, and nets of jewel flowers.

spos rin po che rnam pa tha dad pa'i tshogs las snyim pas bcus shing sprin mngon par gtor ba/ rin po che'i rgyal po kha dog dang dri bsam gyis mi khyab pa las byung ba'i dbyibs yid du 'ong ba sna tshogs dang / spos thams cad kyi na bun dang sprin 'byung ba/ gam yo nas lha rdzas kyi spos dang bdug spos sna tshogs kyis rab tu bdugs pa/ lha rdzas las kyang 'das pa'i stan reg na bde ba kha dog bzang po du ma can legs par bting ba/

Handfuls of precious aromatic substances were scattered as clouds of perfume. Kings of jewels with inconceivable colors and aromas formed various beautiful shapes[1592] and emitted mists and clouds of all perfumes. It was perfumed by various present[1593] divine aromatic substances and incenses. The well-arranged seat of many excellent colors was pleasant to the touch, more so than those of the devas.
It gave off clouds of fragrance and was arrayed with many-colored cloths of pleasant texture, finer than those of the heavens.
lha rdzas kyi rol mo dang glu snyan pa yid du 'ong pa brgya stong du ma'i sgra kun nas 'byung ba/
There arose all around the sound of the music of many hundreds of thousands of divine musical instruments and beautiful melodious songs.
Sweet music and song were heard all around.

rin po che sna tshogs kyi them skas kyi phreng ba gdan gyis rnam par klubs pas rab tu brgyan pa'i rgyan dang ldan pa/ rin po che'i 'bru'i gzugs rin po che sna tshogs kyis spras pa/ rnam par 'phrul pa sna tshogs kyis rnam par snang bar byed pa'i 'od dang ldan pa mngon par grub ste/

It had the display of being adorned by a stairway of various precious materials covered with flags. It was beautified by various precious stones. It shone with various miraculous lights. It was decorated with various precious forms composed of precious stones. It shone with light produced by various manifestations.[1594]
There were stairs of various jewels, arrayed with banners and railings, and shining jewel statues depicting various spiritual transfigurations.
de la rgyal po chos thams cad kyi nga ro'i gdugs kyi dkyil 'khor rab tu sgrog pa
“Seated upon it was King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa.
Here the king sat,
gzugs bzang pa/ shin tu mdzes pa/ blta na sdug pa;
He was very handsome, with an excellent body, and delightful to look at.
handsome,
kha dog bzang po dam pa rgyas pa dang ldan pa/
He possessed a completely excellent, beautiful color.
serene,
mi chen po'i mtshan rnam par dag pa rab tu thob pa/
He had attained the pure signs of a great being.
endowed with the pure marks of a great man,
rin po che rnam par snang ba'i cod pan can/
He wore a crown that shone with jewels.
rdo rje mthu bo che ltar mkhregs shing mi shigs pa'i lus dang ldan pa/
His body was as solid and indestructible as a powerful thunderbolt.
strong,
rtsib ma'i mtshams thags bzang zhing brtan par 'brel ba/
His well-aligned ribs were strongly connected.
robust,
yan lag dang nying lag thams cad yongs su bzang ba/ kun nas bzang ba/ kun nas mdzes pa/ kun nas sdug pa/
The larger and smaller parts of his body were perfectly formed, completely excellent, completely beautiful, and completely splendid.
good, kind, and virtuous in all ways,
rnam pa'i mchog thams cad dang ldan pa/
He had obtained every perfect physical feature.
endowed with all the best qualities,
chos kyi rgyal po chen po'i rigs su byung ba/
He had been born into a great family of Dharma kings.
born of a line of great rulers,
yo byad thams cad la dbang rab tu thob pa/
He had obtained power over all requisites.
in command of all goods,
chos kyi dbang shin tu rnam par dag pas
He had the completely pure power of the Dharma.
pure in control of the law,
rang gi sems la dbang bsgyur ba/
He had power over his own mind.
master of his own mind,
tshig gi dkyil 'khor kha ma bab pa/
He had an unimpeded range of speech.
eloquent,
mi 'khrugs pa'i ye shes dang ldan pa/
He had unshakable knowledge.
endowed with unshakable knowledge,
chos kyi sbyor ba ma nor ba shin tu brtan par byas pa/
He had perfectly established, unmistaken practice of the Dharma.
correctly applying well-constructed laws,
yon tan dang legs pa mtha' yas par brjod du yod pa de 'dug par gyur to/ /
He revealed[1595] endless qualities and excellencies.
showing endless virtues.

rgyal po chos thams cad kyi nga ro'i gdugs kyi dkyil 'khor rab tu sgrog pa de seng+ge'i khri chen po la 'dug pa dang steng gi spyi bo'i thad ka'i bar snang la gdugs kyi dkyil 'khor chen po rin po che sna tshogs rnam par 'brel ba'i yu ba can/ nor bu rin po che dam pa'i mdzod kyi snying po dang ldan pa/ rin po che sna tshogs kyi shar bu brgya stong legs par bres pa/ rin po che du ma'i 'od 'phro ba dpal gyi gzi brjid rab tu 'bar bas rnam par brgyan pa/ 'dzam bu chu klung gi gser 'od 'tsher zhing gsal la rnam par dag pas bla nas bkab pa/ rin po che sna tshogs spa bar spel bas spras pa'i gser gyi dra bas nang shun gyi rgyan byas pa/ mu tig sna tshogs kyi se mo do mngon par dpyangs pa/ rin po che sna tshogs kyi dra bas kun nas bkab pa/ rin po che'i dril bu'i dra ba las gser rin po che'i dril chen rin po che'i chun po'i lda ldi la brgyus pa mngon par dpyangs pa/ nor bu rin po che dam pa'i phreng ba kun nas mngon par dpyangs pa'i rgyan dang ldan pa/ lha rdzas kyi sgra yid du 'ong ba'i gdangs grags par 'byung ba/ sems can thams cad dag pa'i las kyi lam la skul ba'i dril gyi sgra rnam par grags pa byung bar gyur te/

“King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa was seated upon the great lion throne and shaded, in the air directly above his head, by a great round parasol with a handle made of a blend of various precious materials and a treasure of excellent precious jewels in its center. It was adorned by a hundred thousand spokes[1596] of various jewels. It displayed shining, brilliant splendor, radiating the lights of many jewels. It was pure and bright, shining with Jambu River gold. It was adorned by an inner layer of lines of various jewels on a network of gold strings. It was hung with strings of various pearls. It was covered with a net of various jewels. It had a net of precious little bells and large precious golden bells strung along strings in clusters. It was adorned by being hung with strings of excellent, precious jewels. It emitted divine, beautiful sounds, and the sounds of the ringing bells inspired all beings to the path of good actions.

“Furthermore, as the king sat there, in the sky above him there appeared a great parasol, on a long, brilliant jewel pole, its hundred thousand ribs made of all kinds of jewels, brilliantly adorned with blazing lights, covered with lustrous gold, arrayed with nets of jewels, hung with bells of gold and jewels on strings of jewels, adorned with garlands of jewels twirling all around, producing sweet heavenly sounds, the ringing of the bells urging all beings to act virtuously.

rgyal po chos thams cad kyi nga ro'i gdugs kyi dkyil 'khor rab tu sgrog pa de/ rin po che'i rdul yab kyis mngon par g.yab cing lha'i dbang po brgya byin bas kyang lhag par gzi brjid rab tu 'bar bas shin tu mdzes so/ /
“King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa was being fanned with precious yak-tail fans. He was beautiful, shining with a majesty that surpassed that of Śakra, the lord of the devas.
The king, moreover, fanned with jewel wisp fans, shone with a splendor surpassing that of the king of gods.
de seng+ge'i khri de la 'dug ma thag tu 'gro ba mang po de dag thams cad mngon du gyur te thal mo sbyar nas rgyal po de la phyag 'tshal lo/ /
“As soon as he was seated upon the lion throne, many beings stood before him with palms together in homage.
As soon as the king sat on this throne, all the people stood before him with their palms joined and paid their respects.

de nas rgyal po chos thams cad kyi nga ro'i gdugs kyi dkyil 'khor rab tu sgrog pa de'i drung du slong ba'i srog chags bye ba khrag khrig brgya stong sna tshogs dngos po sna tshogs yongs su len pa/ yo byad sna tshogs la mos pa/ rigs sna tshogs dang ldan pa/ 'gro ba'i rgyun sna tshogs su gtogs pa/ 'dod pa sna tshogs kyi sems dang ldan pa/

“The quintillion beings standing before King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa wished to obtain various necessities and various things. They came from various families, they were various kinds of beings, they had minds with various desires,
“Then, seeing the assembly of countless petitioners, with various needs and desires,
smon pa dang bsam pa sna tshogs can/
they had various aspirations and wishes,

phyogs sna tshogs nas 'dus pa/ yul gyi spyod pa sna tshogs la gnas pa; longs spyod sna tshogs la mngon par smon pa'i sems dang ldan pa/ bsam pa dang yongs su rtog pa sna tshogs can/ mi'i ris sna tshogs su gtogs pa/ rigs kyi skye gnas sna tshogs su skyes pa/ yul sna tshogs nas 'ongs pa/

they had gathered from various regions, they were accustomed to various ranges of enjoyments, they had minds that aspired for various kinds of enjoyment, they had various kinds of intentions and ideas, they were from various classes of humans, they had been born into various families, they had come from various lands,
from various places,
sgra skad dang tshig gi 'du byed sna tshogs dang ldan pa/ dbyings kyi dkyil 'khor sna tshogs 'byin pa/ dngos po sna tshogs kyi don du gsol ba 'debs pa/ tshig dang ngag sna tshogs brjod pa/
they spoke various languages and with various vocabularies, they gave rise to various fields of speech, they supplicated for various things, and they spoke in various words and voices.
speaking various languages,
bsod nams kyi ri rab chen po de 'ba' zhig gi gdong du lta ba/ 'di 'ba' zhig shes pa'i skyes bu chen po yin zhes nges par sems ba/
“They all thought with certainty, ‘This great Sumeru of merit that we are looking at‍—he alone is a great man of wisdom.’
all looking up to the king as the pole of prosperity, each thinking of him as a man of great knowledge,
bsod nams chen pos brtan pa'o/ / skyes bu chen po'i zla ba'o/ / gtong ba chen po'i bsam pa dang ldan pa'o/ / zhes bya bar 'dun pa'i sems kyis rtog pa/
“In expectation they thought, ‘He is supported by great merit, he is a moon that is a great man, and he intends to perform a great act of generosity.’
looking up to him as a great man of goodness and charity,

byang chub sems dpa'i smon lam gyi sems kyis 'dug pa/ byang chub sems dpa'i smon lam gyi sems kyis sprul pa'i slong mo pa'i tshogs chen po de mthong nas slong mo ba de dag la sems dga' ba dang / sems mos pa dang / sems spro ba dang / dge ba'i bshes gnyen mthong ba'i 'du shes su gyur to; ; snying rje chen po'i shugs drag po shin tu yangs pa yang byung bar gyur to/ / phyi ma'i mtha'i bskal par slong mo ba thams cad yongs su tshim par bya ba las phyir mi ldog pa'i brtson 'grus kyi shugs drag po yang skyes par gyur to/ / 'gro ba thams cad du snyoms pa'i sbyor bas yongs su gtang ba'i sems kyis rgyas par dgang ba'i sprin kyang mngon par byung bar gyur te/

“When he saw the great gathering of supplicants who had been gathered by a mind with the aspiration of a bodhisattva, who had been manifested by a mind with the aspiration of a bodhisattva, he felt in his mind affection, delight, and benevolence[1597] toward them. He perceived them to be his kalyāṇamitras. There arose in him a vast and powerful great compassion. He also developed the powerful diligence that would never turn back from satisfying all supplicants throughout future kalpas. There also arose all-pervading clouds of the aspiration to be equally engaged in generosity toward all beings.

considering him to have undertaken the vows of enlightening beings, the king felt as if he were seeing good friends and was flooded with immense compassion. There arose in him the dauntless energy to satisfy all petitioners forever and the all-pervasive will to give to everyone impartially.

rgyal po chos thams cad kyi nga ro'i gdugs kyi dkyil 'khor rab tu sgrog pa des slong mo ba de dag mthong ba'i mod la de'i rgyus ches dga' bar gyur gyi; bskal pas mtshams med pa'i mthas klas par stong gsum gyi 'khor los bsgyur ba'i rgyal po thob pas ni/ ma yin no/ / bskal pa bye ba khrag khrig brgya stong mang po'i mthas klas par brgya byin gyi dbang la gnas pas ni/ ma yin no/ / bskal pa bye ba khrag khrig brgya stong mang po'i mthas klas par rab mtshe ma'i lha'i rgyal po'i dbang la gnas ba thob pas ni/ ma yin no/ / bskal pa bye ba khrag khrig brgya stong mang po'i mthas klas par rab dga' ldan gyi lha'i rgyal po'i dbang la gnas pas ni/ ma yin no/ / bskal pa tshad med pa'i mthas klas par rab 'phrul dga'i lha'i rgyal po'i dbang phyug gi dbang la gnas pa thob pas ni/ ma yin no/ / bskal pa bsam gyis mi khyab pa'i mthas klas par dbang sgyur gyi lha'i rgyal po'i dbang rab tu thob ste lha'i bu mo bzhin bzang mo yid du 'ong bas bsnyen bkur bas ni/ ma yin no/ / bskal pa brjod du med pa'i mthas klas par tshangs pa'i gnas kyi bde bas tshangs pa'i thabs la gnas pa thob pas ni/ ma yin no/ / bskal pa mtha' yas pa'i mthas klas par gya nom snang ba'i lha'i bde ba thob pas ni/ ma yin no/ / bskal pa dpag tu med cing mi zad par dge rgyas kyi lha'i bde ba thob pas ni/ ma yin no/ / bskal pa mu med pa'i mthas klas par gnas gtsang ma'i lha'i rnam par thar pa zhi ba'i bde ba la rnam par spyod pa thob pas ni/ ma yin no/ /

“As soon as King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa saw those supplicants, it caused him to experience a joy greater than attaining the sovereignty of a cakravartin king of a billion-world universe for endless kalpas; a joy greater than attaining the throne of the sovereignty of Śakra for many quintillions of kalpas; a joy greater than attaining the throne of the sovereignty of the lord of devas, Suyāma, for many quintillions of kalpas; a joy greater than attaining the throne of the sovereignty of the lord of devas, Saṃtuṣita, for many quintillions of kalpas; a joy greater than attaining the throne of the sovereignty of the lord of devas, Sunirmita, for endless kalpas; a joy greater than attaining the throne of the sovereignty of the lord of devas, Vaśavartin, and being honored by beautiful, delightful apsarases for countless kalpas; a joy greater than attaining the throne of Brahmā and enjoying the bliss of dwelling in the Brahmā paradise for endless kalpas; a joy greater than attaining the bliss of the Ābhāsvara devas for endless kalpas; a joy greater than attaining the bliss of the Śubhakṛtsna devas for an unceasing, unequaled number of kalpas; and a joy greater than attaining the bliss of peaceful liberation of the Śuddhāvāsa devas for kalpas without end.

“Furthermore, when the king saw all those petitioners, he became happier than if he had acquired rule over the galaxy for boundless eons, more than if he had acquired the throne of lordship over the gods for countless eons.

rigs kyi bu/ 'di lta ste/ dper na/ skyes bu sred pa la spyod pa pha ma dang / phu nu dang / bu sring dang / mdza' bo dang / blon po dang / gnyen bshes dang / bu dang / bu mo dang / chung ma dang / yun ring mo zhig tu bral la/ 'brog dgon par 'khyams te/ de dag mthong bar 'dod 'dod pa las de dag dang phrad na/ de dag mthong bas mi ngoms shing dga' ba dang / chags pa chen po skye bar 'gyur ro/ /

“Noble one, it was like a solitary[1598] man, filled with longing, who has been separated for a long time from his father, mother, brothers, sisters, friends, relatives,[1599] sons, daughters, and wife and is wandering in a wilderness. He longs and longs to see them, and when he meets them he never has enough of looking at them, and a great joy and affection arises within him.
His joy upon seeing those petitioners was as that of someone in the wilderness, long separated from family and friends, upon being united with them.

rigs kyi bu/ de bzhin du rgyal po chos thams cad kyi nga ro'i gdugs kyi dkyil 'khor rab tu sgrog pas slong mo ba de dag mthong par gyur pa'i mod la dga' ba'i shugs chen po skyes so/ / sems kyi dga' ba'i ro ba de ba dang ldan par gyur to/ / sems spro ba'i shugs rab tu byung ngo/ / rab tu dga' ba chen po'i shugs yongs su skyes so/ / sangs rgyas kyi byang chub tu dad pa dang mos pa'i shugs kyi stobs rgya chen po 'phel to/ / thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du rtsa ba brtan pa'i dad pa rnam par 'phel to/ / sangs rgyas thams cad kyi chos la lhag pa'i bsam pa rnam par dag pa'i stobs mngon par 'phel to/ / byang chub sems dpa'i dbang po las su rung ba yongs su byung ngo/ sems dga' bas rgyas pas mos pa'i shugs chen po skyes par gyur to/ / sems spro ba'i shugs yangs pas dge ba'i bshes gnyen la dbang po dang bsam pa shin tu gus par gyur to/ /

“Noble one, in the same way, the instant King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa saw those supplicants, a great powerful joy arose in him. His mind was overpowered[1600] by bliss and happiness. He experienced an intensely powerful delight. The power of a great joy arose in him. The great strength of the power of faith in and aspiration for the enlightenment of buddhahood increased. The heartfelt faith in omniscience increased. The strength of his pure, superior aspiration for the Dharma of all the buddhas increased. He became capable of attaining the powers of a bodhisattva. There arose the great power of aspiration through his mind being pervaded with joy. Through the vast power of his rapture, he became deeply reverential in faculties and thoughts toward kalyāṇamitras.[1601]

His mind was filled with happiness, he was uplifted with joy and flooded with delight. The power of his faith in the enlightenment of buddhas increased, his budding faith in omniscience grew, the power of his purity of determination for all the qualities of buddhahood swelled, his faculties as an enlightening being became fit for use, he was flooded with a feeling of contentment and well-being, and by the force of great joy his senses and will as a benefactor became flexible.
de ci'i phyir zhe na/ rgyal po chos thams cad kyi nga ro'i gdugs kyi dkyil 'khor rab tu sgrog pa thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du dmigs pa la brtson pa/
“Why was that? Because King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa was engaged in undertaking attaining omniscience;
Why? Because the king, who was intent on omniscience,
thams cad mkhyen pa nyid la rab tu gzhol ba/
he had set out for omniscience;
had betaken himself to the nature of omniscience,
thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi lam dang sgo la mngon du bltas pa/
he was turned toward the gateway to omniscience;
stood before the door to the path of omniscience,
'gro ba thams cad shin tu tshim par bya ba'i yid la bya ba la brtson pa/
he was engaged in focusing on bringing satisfaction to all beings;
had engaged his attention on the satisfaction of all living beings,
sangs rgyas thams cad kyi yon tan rgya mtsho la 'jug pa'i nan tan la 'dun pa/
he was intent on practicing entry into the ocean of the qualities of all the buddhas;
was on the verge of entry into the ocean of all enlightened virtues,
bdud dang las dang nyon mongs pa'i sgrib pa thams cad kyi ri rnam par 'thor ba la brtson pa/
he was dedicated to destroying the mountain of all the obscurations from māras, karma, and kleśas;[1602]
was intent on shattering the mountains of obstructions caused by demons, actions, and afflictions,
de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi gdams ngag mthun par blang ba la sta gon du gnas pa/
he was prepared to respectfully obtain the teachings of all the tathāgatas;
was absorbed in properly taking up the instructions of all buddhas,
dge ba'i rtsa ba rgya mtsho sgra kun nas yongs su bsdu ba la brtson pa'i snying po can/
from his heart he was dedicated to accumulating completely and totally an ocean of the roots of merit;
was endeavoring to embody all roots of goodness,
mngon par zhen pa thams cad las gyen du 'phags pa'i rgyud dang ldan pa/
the continuum of his mind had transcended all attachment;
was free from all attachments,
'jig rten gyi yul thams cad la mngon par zhen pa med pa/
he had no attachment to any sensory object in the world;
was unattached to any objects in the world,
chos kyi rang bzhin nam mkha'i spyod yul can des slong mo pa de dag la bu gcig pa'i 'du shes bskyed pa'i phyir ro/ /
his field of activity was space, which is the nature of phenomena;
and realized that all things are in essence like space,
pha dang ma'i 'du shes dang /
thought of all those petitioners as like an only son, as like his parents,
sbyin pa'i gnas kyi 'du shes dang /
he perceived them to be worthy of offerings;
as worthy of gifts,
dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi 'du shes dang /
he perceived them to be kalyāṇamitras;
as spiritual benefactors,
dkon pa'i 'du shes dang /
he perceived them to be rare;
as precious,
dka' ba byed pa'i 'du shes dang /
he perceived them to be those who do what is difficult;
as doers of what is difficult,
mang po byas pa'i 'du shes dang /
he perceived them to be those who do much;
as useful in many ways,
phan 'dogs pa dam pa'i 'du shes dang /
he perceived them to be of the highest benefit;
as supreme benefactors,
byang chub kyi lam nye bar ston pa'i 'du shes dang /
he perceived them to be teachers of the path to enlightenment;
as supporting the path of enlightenment,
mkhan po'i 'du shes dang /
he perceived them to be ācāryas;
as guides
ston pa'i 'du shes bskyed pa'i phyir te/
and he perceived them to be teachers.
and teachers.

de ltar des slong mo pha de dag don ci la 'ongs pa dang / don ci la phyin pa dang / dus ci tsam na 'dus pa dang / yul gang dang gang na gnas pa dang / dngos po ci dang ci slong ba dang / rnam pa gang 'dod pa dang / bsam pa ci 'dra ba dang / ci dang ci la smon pa dang / ci dang ci 'dod pa dang / dngos po gang dang gang tshol ba de dag thams cad tshul bzhin du mi dga' ba med pa'i byams pa chen po'i dkyil 'khor dang / slong mo pa'i 'gro ba las phyin phyogs su ma bltas pa'i gtong ba chen po'i 'od zer dang / sems can thams cad la snyoms par sbyor ba'i gtong ba'i sgos yongs su tshim par byas so/ /

“In that way, wherever they came from,[1603] for whatever reason,[1604] whenever they had assembled, however long they had been present, whatever the things they were asking for, whatever their longings, whatever they wished for, whatever they yearned for, whatever they desired, whatever the things they sought, he satisfied those supplicants through the gateway of generosity that was without any disapproval, that had a great range of love, that was not dependent on what the supplicants would do with what they received, that had the light rays of great generosity, and that was united with the equality of all beings.
“The king then fulfilled the needs and wishes of all the petitioners with unmitigated kindness, without turning his back on anyone, giving impartially to everyone, according to their needs.

des zas 'dod pa la ni; zas byin no/ / skom 'dod pa la ni/ skom byin no/ / gos 'dod pa la ni/ gos byin no/ / me tog 'dod pa la ni/ me tog byin no/ / de bzhin du spos dang / bdug spos dang / phreng ba dang / byug pa dang / phye ma dang / gos dang / gdugs dang / rgyal mtshan dang / ba dan dang / rin po che dang / rgyan dang / stan dang / mal dang / khyim dang / gzhal med khang dang / gtsug lag khang dang / bza' shing gi ra ba dang / kun dga'i ra ba dang / dka' thub kyi nags tshal dang / rta dang / glang po dang / shing rta dang / rkang thang dang / dgal ba dang / khyogs dang / bzhon pa dang / gser dang / dbyig dang / nor bu dang / mu tig dang / dung dang / man shel dang / byi ru dang / sa le sbram dang / dngul dag kyang byin par gyur to/ /

“He gave food to those who wanted food. He gave drink to those who wanted drink. He gave clothes to those who wanted clothes. He gave flowers to those who wanted flowers. In the same way, he gave perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes,[1605] parasols, banners, flags, precious materials, jewelry, seats, beds, houses, divine palaces, temples, orchards, parks, forests for ascetics, cavalry, elephants, chariots, infantry, carriages, palanquins, steeds, gold, treasures, jewels, pearls, conches, crystals, corals, gold nuggets, and silver.
He gave away whatever he had to whoever required it, impartial toward all living beings.
rang gi khyim dang / gzhal med khang dang / btsun mo'i 'khor dang / g.yog 'khor dang / rgyal po'i mdzod thams cad kyang phye ste bgos nas rab tu btang bar gyur to/ /
“He opened, shared, and gave away all his own dwellings, divine palaces, harem, court, and royal treasures.

su ci 'dod pa de dag de khyer cig ces nas yul 'dod pa dag kyang yul byin no/ / grong 'dod pa dag kyang grong byin no/ / grong khyer 'dod pa dag kyang gron khyer byin to/ / sems can thams cad la snyoms par zhugs pa des slong mo pa de dag thams cad la ci bdog pa yongs su btang ste/ dngos po thams cad yongs su btang bas mngon par bstod do/ /

He said, ‘Take whatever you want!’ If they wanted a land, he gave them a land; if they wanted a city, he gave them a city; if they wanted a town, he gave them a town. Treating all beings equally, he gave away everything he owned to those supplicants, and in giving away everything presented[1606] it to them.
shin tu rgyas pa chen po'i mdo/ sangs rgyas phal po che zhes bya ba las/ sdong pos brgyan pa'i le'u ste/ bam po brgya bzhi pa/
de'i tshe tshong dpon gyi bu mo rin cen 'od ces bya ba bu mo drug cu'i 'khor dang ldan pa/
“At that time, there was a head merchant’s daughter by the name of Ratnaprabhā, who had an entourage of sixty girls and had arrived at the site of the great offering.
“At that time, in that gathering at the sacrificial ground, there was a grandee’s daughter, named Jewel Light, with a retinue of sixty girls.

gzugs bzang zhing mdzes la blta na sdug pa/ kha dog bzang po'i dam pa rgyas pa dang ldan pa/ mdog gser gyi kha dog lta bu dang ldan pa/ skra mthon mthing du 'dug pa/ mig dkar nag 'byes pa/ dri zhim po yid du 'ong ba dang ldan pa; tshangs pa'i dbyangs dang ldan pa/
She was beautiful, with a clear, healthy complexion, dark hair and eyes, a pleasant scent, and a clear voice.
gos bzang ba/ rgyan gyis legs par brgyan pa/
she wore excellent clothing; she was perfectly adorned in jewelry;
She was well dressed and wore fine ornaments.
dran pa dang / blo gros dang / rig pa dang / khrel yod pa dang / dga' ba dang / ngo tsha shes pa dang / spyod pa dang / cha lugs phun sum tshogs pa/
She was alert and intelligent, modest, stable, and well behaved.
bla ma la sri zhu dang ldan pa/ shes bzhin gyi dam pas spyod pa/ byed rgu zab pa/ chos blang ba dang / gzung ba dang / khong du chud par bya ba la yid gzhungs pa dang ldan pa/
She was respectful to the worthy, most circumspect and clear-headed in conduct, profound in action, endowed with wisdom.
sngon dge ba'i rtsa ba legs par byas pa/ chos kyis mngon par brlan pa'i sems kyi rgyud rab tu dang ba; dge ba'i bsam pa rnam par dag pa/
She had already accomplished basic skills involved in grasping, practicing, and realizing enlightening teachings,

mos pa yangs pa/ nam mkha'i spyod yul can/ gzhan la phan par dga' ba'i sems dang ldan pa/ sangs rgyas blta ba'i phyogs la rnam par bltas pa/ thams cad mkhyen pa'i ye shes la mngon par 'dun pa zhig mchod sbyin gyi rab chen po der 'ongs te

and she had attained clarity and serenity through the teachings. Her intentions were pure and good, and she was dedicated to the welfare of others. She was aiming for the vision of Buddha and was seeking omniscient knowledge.

tshong dpon gyi bu mo rin cen 'od ces bya ba de rgyal po chos thams cad kyi nga ro'i gdugs kyi dkyil 'khor rab tu sgrog pa'i seng+ge'i khri chen po'i g.yas rol ha cang mi ring ba zhig na 'dug 'dug ste/ rgyal po de la phyag 'tshal nas phar ci la'ang len pa med do/ / de phyogs gcig na 'dug cing sems 'di ltar bskyed par gyur te/ bdag gis dge ba'i bshes gnyen 'di lta bu mthong zhing 'grogs su yod pa ni/ bdag gis thob par bya ba legs par thob bo/ /snyam ste/

“Ratnaprabhā, the head merchant’s daughter, was standing with palms together in homage, not far away, on the right-hand side of the lion throne of King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa. She bowed down to the king but did not take anything from him. Then she went to one side and thought, ‘That I have been able to see and to be with this kind of kalyāṇamitra is an excellent attainment.’

She stood near the king’s throne in an attitude of respect, but she did not take anything from among the goods the king was distributing. Just standing there, she thought, ‘I have gained a true boon in getting to see such a spiritual friend as this.’

des rgyal po chos thams cad kyi nga ro'i gdugs kyi dkyil 'khor rab tu sgrog pa de la dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi 'du shes dang / ston pa'i 'du shes dang / snying brtse bar byed pa'i 'du shes dang / phan 'dogs pa'i 'du shes dang / sangs rgyas kyi 'du shes bskyed de

“She perceived King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa to be a kalyāṇamitra, perceived him to be a teacher, perceived him to be compassionate, perceived him to be someone who benefits others, and perceived him to be a buddha.
Thinking of the king as a spiritual friend, a sympathizer, a protector, and an enlightened one,

g.yo sgyu med pa'i sems kyis dga' ba dang / mos pa dang / spro ba'i shugs rab tu yangs pa thob pas rang gi rgyan rnams lus las bkrol te/ rgyal po chos thams cad kyi nga ro'i gdugs kyi dkyil 'khor rab tu sgrog pa gang na ba der mngon par bltas te gtor ba dang / de dag de'i seng+ge'i khri'i 'og /

“She attained the power of joy, aspiration, and enthusiasm, and with a mind that was free of dissimulation, she removed her jewelry and, gazing at King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa, threw it toward him, scattering it on the platform at the foot of the lion throne.

with a mind free from deceit or guile, flooded with supreme joy and happiness, she took off her jewelry and tossed it before the king, so that it lay on the ground between the railings around the throne.

khri'i 'phang gi sa'i steng du bkram par 'gyur to/ / de rgyan de dag de ltar gtor nas smon lam btab pa/ ji ltar rgyal po chos thams cad kyi nga ro'i gdugs kyi dkyil 'khor rab tu sgrog pa 'di sems can mgon med cing mun pa'i nang na 'thom pa rnams kyi mgon skyabs su gyur pa de ltar bdag kyang ma 'ongs pa'i dus na 'gyur bar shog cig /'di chos gang shes pa de dag kyang bdag gis kyang shes par shog cig /'di theg pa gang gis 'byung ba des bdag kyang 'byung bar shog cig /'di lam gang na zhugs pa de nas bdag kyang 'jug par shog cig /ji ltar 'di gzugs blta na btang mi bral zad mi shes pa'i longs spyod dang ldan te/ g.yog 'khor mtha' yas la gzhan gyis mi thub cing thub par dka' ste thub pa med pa de bzhin bdag kyang shog cig / 'di gang dang gang du skye bar 'gyur ba de dang der bdag kyang skye bar 'gyur bar shog cig / snyam pa dang /

When she had in that way scattered her jewelry, she made this prayer: ‘May I in the future become the same as King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa, who is a refuge for beings who have no protector and are enveloped in darkness. May I know whatever Dharma he knows. May I set forth through whatever yāna he has set forth. May I follow whatever path he has followed; may I become just like him whose body gives unending pleasure when gazed upon, who has a limitless entourage and is undefeatable, invincible, and unconquerable. Wherever he is born, may I also be reborn there.’

Having scattered her jewelry, she made these vows: ‘Just as the king Encompassing Sound of the Proclamation of All Laws is a refuge for leaderless people in the dark, so may I also become one such in the future. The reality he knows, may I also know. By the means through which he attains emancipation, may I also be emancipated. The path he practices, may I also practice. Just as he is fair to behold, has endless wealth and assistants, and is invulnerable and invincible, may I also become like this. Wherever he is born, may I also be born.’
