de de ltar sems shing yid la byed pa la brtson pa rgyal po chos thams cad kyi nga ro'i gdugs kyi dkyil 'khor rab tu sgrog pas shes nas de la bltas te 'di skad ces smras so/ /
“King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa knew what her mind was focused on and engaged with, and he said to her,
“Perceiving her involved in such thoughts, the king looked at her and said,
bu mo/ khyod la ci dgos pa khyer cig / bu mo/ nga ni/ bdog pa thams cad yongs su gtong ba ste/ sems can thams cad yongs su tshim par bya ba la zhugs pa'o/ /de skad ces byas pa dang /
‘Girl, take whatever you need! Girl, I am giving away all my possessions. I am engaged in satisfying all beings.’
‘Take what you need. I am giving away all I have to satisfy everyone.’

“She thought, ‘King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa has understood me,’ and gained an even greater faith in him. With that faith in him, giving rise to the power of immense vast roots of merit, she recited these verses to King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa:
Made this offer by the king, she gained even more faith; with a serene mind, energized by lofty, far-reaching virtue, she spoke these verses to the king:
sngon chad sa las rnam brgyan sprin 'di ni/ / rgyal po seng+ge khyod 'khrungs ma gyur tshe/ / mdangs dgar ma gyur gzi brjid ma mchis te/ / yi 'jigs pa'i gnas dang ci mi 'dra/ /
“ ‘In the past, in Sālavyūhamegha, Before you, the lion king, were born, There was no delight,[1607] no magnificence. It was like the dreadful land of the pretas. {22}
Before you were here in this city, great king, It was joyless, lifeless, horrible as the realm of ghosts.
mi rnams kun kyang srog gcod mos par gyur/ / ma byin len la tshul dang sbyor ma mchis/ / brdzun du smra zhing brlang ba'i tshig kyang brjod/ / phra ma kyal ba'i tshig kyang rab tu smra/ /
“ ‘All the people wished to kill. They stole and acted inappropriately. They told lies and spoke harshly And spoke slanderous and meaningless words. {23}
People were murderous, thieving, unrestrained, Deceitful, harsh, and foul in speech.
gzhan gyi nor la chags pa'i sems dang ldan/ / gang zag gzhan la kun kyang ngan du sems/ / lta ba'i rnam gnas sdig to'i spyod yul can/ / log pa'i sbyor bas ngan pa'i 'gro bar ltung / /

“ ‘They had minds that craved the wealth of others. They thought maliciously of all other people. They had wrong views and a field of sinful activity. Through misleading practices they fell into the lower existences. {24}
They were covetous, malicious, and opinionated; By their wrongdoing they fell into states of woe.
chos ngan chos la spyod pa'i mi yi rnams; ; ma rig gti mug mun pas bsgribs pa dag / lta ba log zhugs phyin ci log mthong bas/ / dgung lo mang por dgung char bab ma gyur/ /

“ ‘The people practiced what was not Dharma, Obscured by the darkness of ignorance and stupidity, Following wrong views, and having heretical viewpoints, And therefore for many years the rains did not fall. {25}
Because of the ills of the views of these unjust, ignorant people, For many years there was no rain.
dgung char ma bab sa bon chab 'tshal te/ / lo tog mi 'khrungs zhugs shing 'khrungs ma gyur/ / mtsho dang lu ma chu bran rgyud kyang bskams/ / nags tshal rtsi shing kun kyang de bzhin te/ /
“ ‘When the rains did not fall, seeds died,[1608] The harvests did not grow, trees did not grow, Lakes, ponds, and streams dried up, And it was the same for all the forests and plants. {26}
Because of drought the seeds died, crops and trees did not grow: Lakes and streams dried up, plants and forests withered.
rnam dag spyan khyod 'khrungs par ma gyur bas/ / chab klung kun kyang ma lus bskams par gyur/ / bza' shing ra ba kun kyang ri dgon 'dra/ / rus pa dkar pos dogs bltams par gyur/ /
“ ‘When you, who have pure eyes, had not been born, Every river, without exception, had dried up. All orchards resembled desolate mountains, And the ground was covered with white bones. {27}
The rivers all went dry, the parks were like deserts; Before you appeared, clear-eyed, the earth was strewn with bleached bones.
gang tshe khyod la slong ba mang 'dus te/ / slong ba thams cad yongs su tshim mdzad pas/ / phyogs bzhi kun nas sprin chen 'dus par gyur; ; thang dang gshong rnams kun kyang ngoms par bgyis/ /

“ ‘When you gathered together a multitude of supplicants And brought satisfaction to all those supplicants, Great clouds gathered from all four directions, Bringing satisfaction to all plains and lowlands. {28}
Now you have joined with the needy, and all are satisfied— Coming forth, you shower gifts on the four quarters, fulfilling all, low and high.
slan chad rkun chom g.yon can chad par gyur/ / dgum pa ma mchis su yang gzung ma mchis/ / mgon med gang yang 'gum par mi 'gyur te/ / khyod ni 'gro ba mngon med kun gyi skyabs/ /

“ ‘Since then there has been no thieving, robbery, or fraud. There has been no murder and no executions.[1609] No one has died because they had no protector. You have become the protector for all beings who have none. {29}
There are no more thieves, mercenaries, or frauds—no one is killed or injured; None go hopelessly to death, the world is leaderless no more.
srog gcod pa la mngon par mos pa'i mi/ / gzhan rnams bkum zhing de yi khrag 'tshal la; ; gcig la gcig gi sha 'tshal gyur ba dag / khyod kyi sbyin pa chen pos byams sems gyur/ /
“ ‘Those humans who delighted in killing, Who slew others and then drank their blood, And those who ate one another’s flesh, Through your great generosity now have benevolent minds. {30}
People who like to kill used to drink the blood of their victims— Those who used to eat each other’s flesh have become kindly due to your charities.
brgya stong grangs su bgrang bar gyur pa las/ / de tshe 'ga' zhig rad pa 'tshal gyur gyi/ / gzhan ni dang lo ma rad pa 'tshal/ / de tshe kun kyang yi bkres mnar bzhin/ /

“ ‘At that time, those who possessed clothes Numbered no more than one hundred thousand. The others covered their bodies with clothing of straw and leaves, And at that time, all were tormented by hunger as pretas are. {31}
People used to wear rags and leaves, And were hungry and homeless.
'gro ba mgon med mgon du khyod 'khrungs nas/ / sa bon ma btab ma rmos 'bras kyang byung / / dpag bsam shing las mdzod rnams rnam par thon/ / skyes pa bud med mkhas pa gda' bar gyur/ /

“ ‘You were born as a protector for those without a protector. Now even rice grows without being planted, without plowing. Treasures are obtained from wish-fulfilling trees, And men and women have become learned. {32}
With you here, the grains grow by themselves and the trees give forth their bounty; Wise women and men appear too, now that you have been born, leader of the world.
zla ba zla phyed don du sngon chad ni/ / lam nor gnas pa gsog cing sri zhu ra bgyid/ / deng sang rad pa rab 'tshal rgyan mang ldan/ / dga' ba'i gnas na rtse ba'i lha yang 'dra/ /

“ ‘In the past, for a month or half a month they would Follow bad ways, working to accumulate to no avail.[1610] But nowadays they have much jewelry and excellent clothing And are always happy, like devas amusing themselves. {33}
Those who were formerly all on wrong paths Are now well adorned and dressed, sporting like gods in paradise.
sngon chad log pa rnams la mi bzad zhugs/ / chos ngan 'dod chags mi rnams zhen cing chags/ / na chung gzhon nu gzhan gyis bsrungs pa rnams/ / nan gyis 'phrog rlom chab 'tshal ma rung bgyis/ /

“ ‘Previously, passionate men, with dreadful[1611] wrong conduct, Because of their desires and contrary to the Dharma, Would forcefully take away and rape young maidens Who were under the protection of others. {34}
Men were wrongly obsessed with desires, delighting in unruly passion, Given to raping women and girls in their own care and the care of others.
lha mo bzang mo'i kha dog gzugs ldan pa; ; gos bzang rgyan ldan deng sang mthong 'gyur te/ / gzhan gyi bud med spos dri gda' mchis kyang / / dga' ldan ji bzhin mchis brang rgyan gyis 'tshal/ /

“ ‘Today, just on seeing the perfumed[1612] wives of others, With the bodies and complexions of beautiful apsarases, Wearing splendid clothes and adorned in jewelry, They become satisfied[1613] as if by their own wives in Tuṣita. {35}
Now, though others’ wives be like goddesses, well dressed, adorned, and perfumed, When men see them they are satisfied with their own wives, as in the heaven of content.
sho be brlang pa phra ma rkyal ba rnams/ / sngon chad g.yo sgyu'i dbang gis ngag tu brjod/ / deng yang tshig gi nongs pa bzhi spangs shing / / lta ba ngan spangs chos la kun kyang spyod/ /

“ ‘In the past, people spoke for the purpose of deception. They lied, spoke harshly, slandered, and spoke meaninglessly. Nowadays they have abandoned those four faults of speech, Have abandoned wrong views, and completely practice the Dharma. {36}
People used to be deceitful, cruel, coarse, and dishonest in speech; Having given this up, now they act justly, freed from wrong views.
tshangs dbyangs ka la ping+ka'i sgra byung ba'i/ / khyod kyi gsung mchog 'di yi cha shas la'ang / / rol mo'i sgra dbyangs shin tu snyan pa dang / / lha rdzas glu dbyangs 'di dag nyer mi 'gyur/ /
“ ‘Even the most melodious music And this divine singing do not come close To a fraction of your supreme speech, Which emerges as the sound of Brahmā’s voice or of the avadavat. {37}
No music or celestial song, nor even the voice of Brahma or the singing of birds Can match your voice, O leader.
khyod kyi spyi gtsug dbu steng gdugs lding ba/ / rin chen brgyus bgyis gser gyi dra bas bkab/ / dpal gyi snying mdzod yu ba bai DUr+ya/ / kun nas rin chen mchog gi dril gyis 'khor/ /

“ ‘Above the crown of your head floats a parasol Made of precious materials and covered by a net of gold, With a glorious center of treasure and a handle of beryl And encircled by completely precious, excellent bells. {38}
Above you stands a jewel parasol with webs of gold, On a jewel cane, radiant, with nets of jewelry all around.
dril las byung ba'i sgras kyang ma lus pa'i/ / 'jig rten sgra dbyangs ma lus zil mnan cing / / sangs rgyas gsung gi yan lag 'dra bar 'khrol/ / dam pa'i chos kyi sgra dbyangs zhi ba sgrog /
“ ‘All the sounds that come from those bells Outshine all the music in this world. They emit sounds like the aspects of the Buddha’s speech, Resounding with the peaceful sounds of the Dharma. {39}
The notes of its bells surpass all sounds in the world: Like the tones of Buddha’s voice, they intone the tranquil sound of truth.
de thos sems can nyon mongs zhi bar bgyid/ / ma lus phyogs kyi zhing rnams brgyud pa yi/ / bskal pa rgya mtsho'i bde gshegs rgya mtsho dang / / blo ldan rgya mtsho'i mtshan gyi 'khor lo rnams/ /

“ ‘The kleśas cease in all beings who hear The wheels of the names of the ocean of wise ones, Of the ocean of sugatas in the ocean of successive kalpas In the realms in all directions, without exception. {40}
Those in all lands who hear this put an end to afflictions, Hearing the names of the buddhas over the ages and the oceans of the wise.
sngon mtha'i zhing rnams gcig nas gcig brgyud du/ / gang mtshan gang dang gang lags rim bzhin dang / / ma lus phyogs su dam chos 'khor lo yang / / khyod kyi byin gyis dril rnams rab tu sgrog /

“ ‘Through your blessing, the bells sound out In correct sequence whatever the names Of those who have appeared in the past, in one realm after another, And turned the wheel of the Dharma in all directions without exception. {41}
By your power the bells bespeak the successive lands since the past, The names of the lands, and the cycles of true teaching everywhere.
khyod kyi dril sgra thogs pa ma mchis par/ / tshangs dbang lha dbang 'gro ba'i bdag po rnams/ / rang rang las kyi tshul ni kun rjod cing / / 'dzam bu'i rgyal mtshan khyab par kun tu sgrog /

“ ‘For as long as your bells continue to ring, They will resound throughout Jambudhvaja, Describing the nature of the karma of each one Of the lords of Brahmās, the lords of devas, and the lords of humans. {42}
The sound of the bells, liquid, free-flowing, rings throughout the continent, Telling of the manners of action of the gods and the lords of the worlds.
dril gyi sgra las lha dang mi rnams kyis/ / rang rang las kyi tshul rgyud thos gyur nas/ / sdig to rnam spangs dge ba spyod par gyur/ / sangs rgyas byang chub mchog la kun kyang gnas/ /

“ ‘From the sound of the bells, each deva and human Hears the nature of their individual karma, So they give up bad actions, adopt good conduct, And are all directed to the supreme enlightenment of buddhahood. {43}
Hearing the bells tell of the accumulations of their deeds, gods and people Give up evil, practice good, and rely on the enlightenment of the buddhas.
khyod kyi yab ni mi bdag skar ma'i 'od/ / de yi btsun mo pad+mo khyod kyi yum/ / rnyog pa lnga rnams shin tu rgyas gyur du/ / chos 'grib rgyal srid des ni bzhes par gyur/ /
“ ‘Your father was the sovereign over humans, Jyotiṣprabha, And his Queen, Padmaprabhā, was your mother. In the time when the five deteriorations spread, He had inherited the Dharma kingdom. {44}
Your father was Starlight, the king, your mother queen Lotus Light; You were born in a corrupt age and acquired the rulership.
de yi bza' shing ra ba yangs byung ba/ / me tog rgyas brgyan rin chen sgron ma ste/ / shing mang brgyas bskor rdzing bu lnga brgya yis/ / de ni shin tu brgyan pa byung bar gyur/ /
“ ‘His royal gardens were vast, Arrayed with blossoming flowers and precious lamps, Beautified by five hundred lotus ponds, Encircled by many hundreds of trees. {45}
There was a large park, arrayed with flowers and precious lamps, Adorned with five hundred lotus ponds, and surrounded with hundreds of trees.
de dag so so re re'i dogs su yang / / ka ba stong ldan gzhal med khang bzang byung / / stegs bu bzang po sna tshogs stong gis brgyan/ / zla gam dra bas kun nas mdzes par bgyis/ /
“ ‘And each of them had on every side A palace with a thousand pillars, A variegated array of a thousand balconies, And beautifying[1614] nets of crescents everywhere. {46}
On the bank of each pond was a villa, with a thousand pillars, Resplendent with a thousand balustrades, with radiant nets and crescents all around.
chos ngan stobs ni rab tu 'phel gyur bas/ / dgung lo mang por dgung char bab ma gyur/ / rdzing bu kun gyi chab dang zhugs shing rnams/ / de tshe lo ma mdog dang bcas te bskams/ /
“ ‘The power of bad qualities became widespread, So that for many years the rain did not fall. At that time, the water in all the lotus ponds, And the trees with all their leaves, dried up. {47}
When it had not rained for years, with lawlessness prevailing everywhere, The water in the ponds evaporated and the trees withered.
dgung bdun na ni khyod bltams 'gyur ba'i tshe; ; de tshe ngo mtshar rmad byung ltas byung ste/ / de dag mthong nas sems can nges rtogs par/ / bdag cag skyob pa nges par 'byung zhes mchi/ /
“ ‘For seven nights before you were born, There were marvelous, wonderful omens. When beings saw them, they said with certainty, “Our savior has definitely arrived.” {48}
Seven nights before your birth there were innumerable wonders, Convincing all who saw them that a savior was surely to be born.
dgung gi gung la bab nas rnam drug tu; ; khams kyi dogs yongs su g.yos par gyur/ / ma smad shin tu bzang ba'i rdzing de yi/ / dbus su gdugs dang mnyam pa'i 'od cig byung / /
“ ‘At the midnights of those nights, The entire surface of the world shook in six ways. In the center of the supreme lotus pond, There appeared a light as bright as the sun.[1615] {49}
In the middle of the night the earth quaked, And a light like the sun appeared in the pond called Impeccable.
chab bzang yan lag brgyad ldan rgyas par gyur/ / rdzing bu lnga brgya kun kyang de bzhin te/ / zhugs shing kun kyang lo ma 'khrungs par gyur/ / me tog 'bras bu kha dog mdog dang ldan/ /
“ ‘All five hundred lotus ponds were filled With excellent water that had the eight qualities. On the branches of the trees grew leaves And magnificent flowers and fruits. {50}
Thereupon the five hundred ponds were filled with pure water, The trees flourished, and flowers and fruits were filled with life.
rdzing bu de rnams chab kyis bltams gyur pas/ / nags tshal ma lus de dag ngoms par bgyis/ / chab chen de las byung ba'i rgyud 'phros pas/ / 'dzam bu'i rgyal mtshan chab kyis bltams par gyur/ /
“ ‘Those lotus ponds filled with water Satisfied entire forests without exception. The great rivers that flowed from them Filled Jambudhvaja with their water. {51}
The ponds, filled with water, refreshed the whole grove; By the streams flowing from them the whole continent was replenished with moisture.
zhugs shing sman dang lo tog ldum bu yang / / 'khrungs gyur zhugs shing me tog 'bras bu rgyas/ / dog sa'i steng na mchis rgu'i sa bon rnams/ / kun kyang chab kyis brlan pas rnam par 'khrungs/ /
“ ‘The trees, herbs, crops, and plants grew. Trees were covered with flowers and fruits. The many kinds of seeds on the surface of the world Were all moistened by the water and sprouted. {52}
The herbs, crops, and greenery growing, the trees flowered and fruited; All the seeds in the earth sprouted, moistened by the water.
chab kyis bangs gyur dog sa'i phyogs rnams kyang / / de tshe thams cad rab tu mnyam par gyur/ / sgang gshong dog sa'i phyogs rnams ji snyed pa/ / de dag kun kyang de tshe mnyam par gyur/ /
“ ‘The surface of the earth was saturated with water, So at that time it became completely level. All the upland and downland in all directions On the world’s surface became level. {53}
Every place on earth was equally watered then, And all places low and high became level.
g.yang sa grog po mi bde'i phyogs kyi rnams/ / de tshe yud kyis kun kyang mnyam par gyur; ; tsher ma gseg ma la sogs ma mchis gyur/ / rin chen bzang po'i 'byung gnas yongs su thon/ /
“ ‘At that time, chasms, precipices, and rugged places All became level, everywhere in an instant. Thorns and pebbles and so on ceased to exist, And sources of excellent jewels appeared. {54}
Ravines and rugged terrain then became instantly level; Brambles, gravel, and the like disappeared, replaced by beautiful jewels.
skyes pa bud med tshogs rnams dga' bar gyur/ / skom pas gdungs pa kun kyang chab la 'tshal/ / kye ma de ring bde na su mthu zhes/ / snyan par brjod pa de skad chad du brjod/ /

“ ‘Crowds of men and women were rapturous, And all who were afflicted by thirst had plenty of water. With happy voices they cried out in joy, “Ah! Through whose power has today’s happiness come?” {55}
All the people exulted, like the thirsty drinking water, And celebrated this park, saying, “By whose power is this felicity?”
ngog sa'i mnga' bdag skar 'od sras dang bcas/ / sras mo blon po'i tshogs bcas de yi tshe/ / skye bo bye ba stong gis yongs bskor te/ / bza' shing ra bar dgyes par gshegs pa mdzad/ /

“ ‘At that time, the ruler of the earth, Jyotiḥprabha, and his son, Together with his daughters and a crowd of his ministers And encircled by a thousand million people, Proceeded to the gardens with delight. {56}
Then the king Starlight, with his wife, son, and ministers, Surrounded by millions of people, went to enjoy the park.
mdangs dga' rdzing chen yongs su ma smad pa/ / spos chus bltams pa dbus na mchis gyur ba'i/ / de yi dbus su chos stegs bzang po yi/ / pho brang steng gshegs btsun mo bcas pas bzhugs/ /
“ ‘Together with his queen he came up onto The terrace of the staircase of righteousness[1616] Of the charming, preeminent, central Lotus pond filled with scented water. {57}
In the middle was the pond Impeccable, filled with fragrant water; There the king stood, up in its villa, a temple of truth.
dgung bdun lon par gyur nas de yi chab/ / dgung gi gung la gyen du lud par gyur/ / ri dang gzhal med khang gi phreng bcas pa'i/ / dog sa'ang de'i tshe yongs su g.yos par gyur/ /
“ ‘For the duration of seven nights, Each night the water rose upward, And at that time the entire surface of the earth, With its mountains and garlands of palaces, was shaken. {58}
It had been seven nights since the water had appeared; Again the whole earth trembled, with all its mountains and abodes.
yongs su ma smad de yi dbus nas kyang / / pad+mo chen po lo ma stong ldan 'khrungs/ / gdugs stong mdor gsal sprin gyi dra ba can/ / ri rab rtse mo man chad 'od kyis 'gengs/ /
“ ‘In the center of the preeminent pond Appeared a great lotus with a thousand petals And a net of clouds of the light of a thousand suns Spreading upward as far as Sumeru’s summit. {59}
In the middle of the pond a thousand-petaled lotus appeared, Shining like a thousand suns, suffusing the peak of the polar mountain with light.
chu ba rdo rje nang rim dri bda' ste/ / rin chen dbang po'i lo ma rnam dag yangs/ / 'dzam bu chu klung gser bzang snying po can/ / ze ba spos rab 'bar ba phun sum tshogs/ /

“ ‘It had a diamond stem and an aromatic center. Its multitude of pure petals were lords of jewels. Its pericarp was splendid Jambu River gold. It had a perfection of bright stamens with an excellent aroma. {60}
Its stem was diamond, its calyx the essence of beauty, its clean broad leaves Diamond, its pericarp of finest gold, its filaments radiant, with superb fragrance.
mgon po khyod ni de yi snying po las/ / skyil mo krung bcas sku ni byung bar gyur/ / mtshan gyis rnam brgyan yan lag shin tu mdzes/ / lha mang brgyas kyang mngon par mchod pa bgyis/ /
“ ‘You, lord, were born upon that pericarp. You appeared[1617] sitting cross-legged, Your beautiful body adorned by the signs of a great being, With hundreds of devas making offerings to you. {61}
On that pericarp the Guide was born, sitting up straight, cross-legged; You shone, your body resplendent with the marks of greatness, attended by celestial beings.
rgyal po pho brang steng nas shod gshegs te/ / phyag gnyis brkyangs te legs par khyod blangs nas/ / btsun mo'i mgo la bzhag ste 'di skad gsungs/ / khyod kyi bu 'di yin gyi dgar gyis shig /

“ ‘The king descended from the terrace’s platform.[1618] He reached out with his arms and lifted you up, Gave you to the supreme[1619] queen, and said these words: “This is your son! Be of happy mind!” {62}
Descending from the temple, the king took you in his arms, delighted, And handed you to the queen, saying “This is your son—be of good cheer.”
'jig rten mgon khyod de ltar bltams gyur tshe/ / bye ba'i gter rnams rab tu thon par gyur/ / zhugs shing kun kyang mngon par kha 'bus te/ / steng gi mkha' las rol mo'i sgra yang byung / /
“ ‘When you, protector of the world, were thus born, Ten million treasures appeared, The buds of all trees opened, And the sound of music came from the sky. {63}
Millions of hidden treasuries appeared, the trees of plenty released Their goods, and the air was filled with music as you were born, leader of the world.
'dzam bu rgyal mtshan sems can thams cad kyang / / khyod la mngon lta 'dud cing phyag kyang 'tshal/ / thal mo sbyar cing kye ma mgon med pa'i/ / mgon zhig byung zhes dga' ba'i tshig kyang brjod/ /
“ ‘All the beings in Jambudhvaja Gazed upon you, bowed, and paid homage. With palms together they said with joy, “Oh! You have come as a protector for the helpless!” {64}
All those living on the continent looked up to you, trusting— Respectfully they said, “This is the leader of the leaderless.”
khyod kyi sku las 'od zer mang 'byung bas/ / dog sa kun tu rab tu snang bar gyur; ; 'gro ba'i mun pa kun kyang rnam bsal nas/ / nad mang ma lus rab tu zhi bar gyur/ /
“ ‘From your body you radiated light rays That illuminated the entire world, Eliminating all the darkness in beings And bringing to an end every kind of illness. {65}
The light emanating from your body illumined the whole earth; Dispelling the darkness of the world, it put an end to all ailments.
gnod sbyin grul bum sha za mang po'i tshogs/ / rnam par 'tshe ba de dag bsal bar gyur/ / shin tu gdug pas sems can 'gums pa yi/ / sbrul gdug kun kyang de tshe yong mi rgyu/ /
“ ‘Those gatherings of yakṣas, kumbhāṇḍas, and piśācas Who were causing harm were dispelled. All poisonous snakes, who with malicious intent Killed beings, were rendered immobile. {66}
All malevolent creatures, the venomous and harmful, Became inactive then.
thob med sman pa mi snyan sdug bsngal dang / / nad rlangs nad mang gnod par 'tshe ba dag / mdor bsdus kun kyang zhi zhing ma mchis gyur/ / 'jig rten kun tu rab dga' byung bar gyur/ /

“ ‘The suffering of misfortune and disgrace, Being afflicted by illness, harmed by many illnesses All these were, in brief, brought to an end, ceased to exist, And there was great happiness throughout the entire world. {67}
Frustration, censure, ill-fame, pain, misfortunes, illness, accidents— These all ended, fortune came, and everyone became joyful.
phan tshun ma dang 'dra ba'i 'du shes kyis; ; khong nas byams pa de tshe 'gro kun gyur/ / shar gnyer sems bral 'tshe ba ma mchis te/ / thams cad mkhyen lam nan tan ldan par gyur/ /
“ ‘At that time, all beings had loving minds, Perceiving one another as being like their mother. Without aggression and without violence, They practiced the path to omniscience. {68}
Everyone loved one another, and all became kind; Free from animosity, nonviolent, they set out on the path of knowledge.
ngan song rgyud rnams rnam par rab tu bzlog / mtho ris lam chen kun kyang btod par gyur/ / thams cad mkhyen pa'i lam yang shin tu bstan/ / de ltar khyod kyis 'gro don yangs pa mdzad/ /
“ ‘They were turned away from the lower existences, Turned toward the great path to higher existences, And shown the path toward omniscience. In that way you created a vast benefit for beings. {69}
The righteous king shut off the evil ways, opened the way to heaven, And showed the way to omniscience—you have done a great service to the world.
rgya mtsho che 'dra yongs su gtong mdzad pa/ / khyod mthong bdag ni thob pa dam pa thob/ / yun ring 'khyams pa'i 'gro ba mgon bral du/ / khyod ni rmad du byung ba'i mgon zhig gshegs/ /

“ ‘Your generosity has been as vast as an ocean. I[1620] have attained the excellent attainment of seeing you. You have come to be a marvelous guide For those who have been helplessly lost for a long time.’ {70}
We benefit further from seeing you, oceanic giver; after long absence, A leader of the helpless is born in the world—you are a rare guide.

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu mo rin chen 'od kyis rgyal po chos thams cad kyi nga ro'i gdugs kyi dkyil 'khor rab tu sgrog pa la tshigs su bcad pa de dag gis mngon par bstod de snyan par bkur nas rab tu bsngags te lan brgya phrag stong du g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas te phyag 'tshal nas phyogs gcig tu gus pa'i tshul gyis 'dug go /

“The head merchant’s daughter, Ratnaprabhā, praised King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa with those verses. Having honored and praised him, she circumambulated him, keeping him to her right, a hundred thousand times. Having paid homage, she reverently went to sit to one side.
“Having thus eulogized the king, the girl Jewel Light then paid her respects to him and stood there reverently.

de nas rgyal po chos thams cad kyi nga ro'i gdugs kyi dkyil 'khor rab tu sgrog pas tshong dpon gyi bu mo rin chen 'od la bltas te 'di skad ces smras so/ / bu mo/ de ltar khyod sems can pha rol gyi yon tan gyi khyad par shes pa'i mngon par shes pa la zhugs pa legs so/ /legs so/ /

“King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa looked at the merchant’s daughter Ratnaprabhā and said these words: ‘Girl, it is excellent, excellent, that you have thus set out for the higher knowledge that knows the special qualities of other beings.
Looking at her, the king said,
bu mo/ 'jig rten thams cad na'ang sems can gang sems can pha rol gyi yon tan la mos pa de lta bu ni/ dkon te/
“ ‘Girl, beings who aspire for the good qualities in other beings are rare in all worlds.
‘Rare are those who appreciate the virtues of others.

bu mo/ sems can mun pas bsgribs pa/ phan gdags pa la drin du mi gzo ba/ blo phyin ci log la zhugs pa/ sems 'khrugs par gyur pa/ rgyud 'dzings par gyur pa/ mun pa'i sems dang ldan pa/ bsam pa ngang gis log pa/ nan tan dang mi ldan pa/ sems can pha rol gyi yon tan gyi khyad par mngon par mi shes pa rnams kyis ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i yon tan la 'jug par bya ba'am/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i yon tan la brtag par bya ba'am/ yon tan thams cad shes pa'i khyad par mngon par shes pa thob par bya bar mi nus so/ /

“ ‘Girl, beings who are obscured by darkness, who are ungrateful, who have wrong judgment, who have disturbed minds, whose trains of thought are in disorder, whose minds are in darkness, whose thoughts are naturally ruinous, who do not practice, and who do not know the special qualities of other beings are unable to comprehend the qualities of bodhisattvas, to conceive the qualities of the tathāgatas, or to attain the higher cognition that is the unique knowledge of all qualities.

For the ignorant, the ungrateful, the undiscerning, the agitated, the disturbed, the muddled thinkers, the deranged, the backsliders, those who do not realize the excellence of others’ virtues, it is impossible to comprehend or even conceive of the virtues of the enlightened, or to realize the excellence of knowledge of all virtues.
bu mo/ de ltar khyod sems can chen po mngon par shes pas byang chub sems dpa'i yon tan gyi rnam pa de lta bu la 'jug pa ni/ gdon mi za bar byang chub tu yang dag par zhugs pa'o/ /
“ ‘Therefore, girl, as you comprehend the qualities of the bodhisattvas through a higher cognition of great beings, you are, without doubt, established in the way to enlightenment.
Without a doubt you have set out for enlightenment, since you have understood such virtues of enlightening beings.
de ltar nga'i khams su khyod lta bu ye shes de 'dra ba dang ldan pa skyes pa ni/ dzam+bu'i gling du ngas sems can yongs su bsdus pa'i mthu don yod do/ /
“ ‘My prowess in gathering together the beings of Jambudvīpa has proved meaningful because someone like you, with your kind of knowledge, has been born in my realm.’
Our efforts for the care of beings have not been fruitless, as you, endowed with such knowledge, have appeared in our kingdom, by virtue of the higher knowledge of superior people.’

de nas rgyal po chos thams cad kyi nga ro'i gdugs kyi dkyil 'khor rab tu sgrog pas nor bu rin po che chen po rin thang med pa dang / nor bu rin po che skar ma'i 'od sna tshogs dang / gos rin po che rin thang med pa bdag gis lag bdar te blangs nas tshong dpon gyi bu mo rin chen 'od la byin no/ / de'i 'khor gyi bu mo thams cad kyang gos rin po che sna tshogs kyis khyad par byin nas 'di skad ces smras so/ /

“Then King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa picked up with his own hands a great, priceless, precious jewel, a multicolored precious jewel that contained the lights of the stars, and priceless, precious clothing, and gave them to the head merchant’s daughter Ratnaprabhā. He gave various precious clothing to each of the girls in Ratnaprabhā’s entourage. He said,
“Then with his own hand the king gave her a priceless robe, radiant with sparkling jewels, and also gave a precious robe to each of her companions. He said,
bu mo/ gos rin po che 'di khyer la bdag gis yongs su spyad pa gyis shig /
‘Girl, take this precious clothing, keep it, and wear it yourself!’
‘Take this and put it on.’

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu mo rin chen 'od 'khor dang bcas pas pus mo gnyis sa la phab ste gos rin po che dag lag pa gnyis kyis blangs nas spyi bo la blangs te phyir byung nas rin po che de dag bgos so/ / de'i 'khor gyi bu mo thams cad kyis kyang so so nas rang rang gi gos rin po che de dag bgos nas des gos rin po che de dag bgos pa'i 'og tu rgyal po chos thams cad kyi nga ro'i gdugs kyi dkyil 'khor rab tu sgrog pa la bdag gi 'khor bu mo de dag dang bcas pas g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas so/ / de dag thams cad kyi gos rin po che de dag la rgyu skar dang / skar ma thams cad kyi gzugs brnyan snang bar gyur te/ de dag mthong nas 'gro ba'i tshogs mang po 'di skad ces 'dzer te/

“Then the head merchant’s daughter, Ratnaprabhā, accompanied by her entourage, knelt with both knees on the ground, took up the precious clothing with both hands, placed it on her head, withdrew, and put on that precious clothing. All the girls in the entourage also each put on their own precious clothing. When she had put on that precious clothing, accompanied by her entourage of girls, she circumambulated King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa, keeping him to her right. The images of all constellations and stars appeared on those precious clothes. When the gathering of people saw her, they said,

Jewel Light then knelt on the ground, picked up the robe in both hands, lifted it to her head, and put it on. Her companions likewise each put on their robes. Having put on the robes, the girl and her companions circled the king in respect, with the reflections of all the stars glittering in their robes. Seeing this, the people said,
bu mo/ khyod kyi 'khor bu mo 'di dag ni/ mtshan mo'i lha mo skar ma'i tshogs kyis brgyan pa ltar shin tu mdzes pa ste/ khyod de dag gis bskor bas gya nom par mdzes so/ /
‘Girl, your entourage of girls is as beautiful as a night goddess adorned by the stars. You, encircled by them, are even more beautiful.’ ”
‘You are beautiful, young lady, with your companions, adorned with stars like a night goddess; surrounded by them, you sparkle most brightly.’”

de nas mtshan mo'i lha mo shing thams cad kyi me tog rgyas pas bde bar gnas pas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la 'di skad ces smras so/ / rigs kyi bu/ de la ji snyam du sems/ de'i tshe de'i dus na rgyal po chos thams cad kyi nga ro'i gdugs kyi dkyil 'khor rab tu sgrog pa zhes bya ba byung ba de gzhan zhig yin pa snyam du sems na ni/ de ltar mi blta ste/ bcom ldan 'das de bzhin gshegs pa dgra bcom pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas rnam par snang mdzad 'di ni/ de'i tshe rgyal po chos thams cad kyi nga ro'i gdugs kyi dkyil 'khor rab tu sgrog pa zhes bya bar gyur to/ /

Then the night goddess Sarvavṛkṣpraphullanasukhasaṃvāsā said to Sudhana, “Noble one, what do you think? At that time, in that time, who was King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa? Do not think that it was anyone else, for at that time, in that time, it was this bhagavat tathāgata arhat samyaksaṃbuddha Vairocana who was King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa.

Then the night goddess Sarvavrikshapraphullanasukhasamvasa said to Sudhana, “You should realize that it was none other than the buddha Vairocana, who at that time was the king Encompassing Sound of the Proclamation of All Laws,

rigs kyi bu/ de'i tshe de'i dus na rgyal po skar ma'i 'od kyi btsun ma pad+mo'i 'od ces bya ba/ rgyal po chos thams cad kyi nga ro'i gdugs kyi dkyil 'khor rab tu sgrog pa'i yum du gyur pa de gzhan zhig yin pa snyam du sems na yang de ltar mi blta ste/ lha mo sgyu ma 'di ni/ de'i tshe rgyal po'i btsun mo pad+mo'i 'od ces bya bar gyur te/ rdzus te byung ba'i gzhon nu thu par len len pa'o/ /

“What do you think, noble one? At that time, in that time, who was Padmaprabhā, the queen of King Jyotiṣprabha and the mother of King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa? Do not think that it was anyone else, for at that time, in that time, Māyādevī was Padmaprabhā, the king’s queen who took the miraculously born prince onto her lap.[1621]

and the queen Lotus Light, wife of the king Starlight and mother of the king Encompassing Sound of the Proclamation of All Laws, was none other than Queen Maya; Maya was the queen Lotus Light at that time, by whom the spontaneously born child was carried at the hip.

yang rigs kyi bu/ khyod de'i tshe de'i dus na rgyal po skar ma'i 'od ces bya ba; rgyal po chos thams cad kyi nga ro'i gdugs kyi dkyil 'khor rab tu sgrog pa'i yab tu gyur pa byung ba de gzhan zhig yin pa snyam du sems na'ang de ltar mi blta ste/ rgyal po zas gtsang ma ni/ de'i tshe de'i dus na rgyal po skar ma'i 'od ces bya bar gyur to/ /

“Also, what do you think, noble one? At that time, in that time, who was Jyotiṣprabha, the father of King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa? Do not think that it was anyone else, for at that time, in that time, Śuddhodana was the king named Jyotiṣprabha.
And the king father, the elder king Starlight, was none other than King Shuddhodana.

yang rigs kyi bu/ khyod de'i tshe de'i dus na tshong dpon gyi bu mo rin chen 'od ces bya ba byung ba de gzhan zhig yin pa snyam du sems na'ang de ltar mi blta ste/ kho mo ni/ de'i tshe de'i dus na tshong dpon gyi bu mo rin chen 'od ces bya bar gyur to/ /

“Also, what do you think, noble one? At that time, in that time, who was Ratnaprabhā, the head merchant’s daughter? Do not think that it was anyone else, for at that time, in that time, I was Ratnaprabhā, the head merchant’s daughter.
And you may think the girl Jewel Light of that time was someone else, but you should realize that she was none other than I—I myself was that girl Jewel Light in that time.

yang rigs kyi bu; khyod de'i dus na sems can dzam+bu'i gling der skyes shing rgyal po chos thams cad kyi nga ro'i gdugs kyi dkyil 'khor rab tu sgrog pas bsdu ba'i dngos po bzhis yongs su bsdus pa de dag gzhan dag cig yin pa snyam du sems na ni/ de ltar mi blta ste/ bcom ldan 'das kyi 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor 'di nyid du 'dus te bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub las phyir mi ldog pa'i byang chub sems dpa'i sa la bkod de/ la la ni/ sa dang po la bkod/ la la ni/ sa gnyis pa la/ la la ni/ sa gsum pa/ la la ni/ sa bzhi pa/ la la ni/ sa lnga pa/ la la ni/ sa drug pa/ la la ni/ sa bdun pa/ la la ni/ sa brgyad pa/ la la ni/ sa dgu pa/ la la ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i sa bcu pa la bkod par gyur pa'i

“Also, what do you think, noble one? At that time, in that time, who were the beings who had been born in Jambudvīpa and whom King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa had gathered together through the four methods of gathering pupils? Do not think that it was anyone else, for they are those who are gathered in this assembly of the followers of the Bhagavat, have been established on the bodhisattva path, and are progressing irreversibly toward the highest, complete enlightenment. Some are established on the first bhūmi, some on the second bhūmi, some on the third bhūmi, some on the fourth bhūmi, some on the fifth bhūmi, some on the sixth bhūmi, some on the seventh bhūmi, some on the eighth bhūmi, some on the ninth bhūmi, and some are established on the tenth bodhisattva bhūmi.

As for the people of that time who were taken care of by the king Encompassing Sound of the Proclamation of All Laws by means of generosity, kindness, charitable works, and sympathy, you might think they were other people, but you should not see it that way—they are now the enlightening beings gathered here in the audience of the Buddha, standing on the ground of enlightening beings, irreversibly determined to reach supreme perfect enlightenment, some in the first stage, some in the second, some in the third, some in the fourth, some in the fifth, some in the sixth, some in the seventh, some in the eighth, some in the ninth, some in the tenth stage,
byang chub sems dpa' smon lam sna tshogs rnam pa tha dad pa dang /
“They are bodhisattvas who have their attainments through various kinds of prayers,
who have attained by various different vows,
thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du 'jug pa sna tshogs dang /
various ways of setting out toward omniscience,
various approaches to omniscience,
tshogs sna tshogs dang /
various accumulations,
various preparations,
yang dag par sgrub pa sna tshogs dang /
various accomplishments,[1622]
various accomplishments,
spyod pa sna tshogs dang /
various conducts,[1623]
various ways of emancipation,
'byung ba sna tshogs dang /
various setting forths,
lam gyi rgyan rnam par dag pa sna tshogs dang /
various pure displays of the path,
various purifications of manifestations of the path,
rnam par 'phrul ba dang / khyu mchog gi mthu phyung ba sna tshogs dang /
various supremacies in miraculous manifestations,
various mystic powers,
lam gyi rgyan rnam pa sna tshogs kyis yongs su byung ste
and different kinds of displays of the path.
and various manifestations of the path,
rnam par thar pa la rnam par spyod pa sna tshogs kyis 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor 'di ni; chos kyi gzhal med khang sna tshogs na rnam par spyod pas 'khod cing rnam par spyod pa 'di dag yin no/ /
“They are these practitioners who are dwelling and practicing within various divine palaces of the Dharma in this assembly of followers through their practice of various kinds of liberations.”
and, by various states of liberation, abide in various spiritual abodes in this assembly.”

de nas mtshan mo'i lha mo shing thams cad kyi me tog rgyas pas bde bar gnas pas de'i tshe byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa dga' ba'i 'od spro ba yangs pa yang dag par 'byung ba 'di nyid brnan te bstan pa'i phyir tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la tshigs su bcad de smras pa/

The night goddess Sarvavṛkṣpraphullanasukhasaṃvāsā, in order to teach further the bodhisattva liberation called the arising of the vast radiating light of joy, recited these verses to Sudhana, the head merchant’s son:
Then the night goddess spoke these verses to Sudhana, further revealing the enlightening liberation of manifestation of satisfaction by treasure produced from great joy:
rgyal ba'i sras po kho mo'i mig yangs te/ / phyogs kun zhing mang rgya mtsho sna tshogs kyi/ / sems can rgya chen gang chen mtsho yi rnams/ / 'khor bar gyur tshe kun la rnam par lta/ /
“Son of the jinas, with my vast sight I am looking into all directions At the vast ocean of realms of various kinds And also the ocean of beings in saṃsāra. {71}
Broad is my vision, with which I observe everywhere, vast oceans Of lands of many kings, and oceans of beings in a whirl.
'byams klas zhing rnams kun na bzhugs pa yi/ / rgyal ba byang chub shing gi drung bzhugs pa; ; rdul med kun kyang phyogs bcu rgyas bkang ste/ / chos sgrog rtag par 'gro 'dul mthong bar byed/ /
“I see the spotless jinas in the vast extent of all realms Present everywhere throughout the ten directions Seated at the feet of Bodhi trees, Teaching the Dharma and guiding beings. {72}
In all lands buddhas sit at enlightenment trees, dispassionate, Pervading everywhere by mystic powers and always teaching and guiding beings.
kho mo'i rna ba rgya mtsho yongs su dag / sgra rnams ma lus thams cad des thos te/ / bde bar gshegs pas chos gsungs ma lus par/ / thams cad dga' bas yang dang yang du thos/ /
“With the pure ocean of my hearing, I hear all sounds without exception. All the Dharma that is taught by the sugatas I hear with delight again and again. {73}
My hearing is perfectly clear, and I hear all sounds thereby; I hear all the teachings of the buddhas and am extremely joyful.
kho mo'i ye shes gnyis med chags pa med/ / sems can gzhan gyi sems kyi yul la 'jug / 'gro ba'i sems kyi rgya mtsho yangs pa rnams/ / ma lus kun la mtshan nyid dngos kyis 'jug /
“My nondual, unimpeded knowledge Enters the field of the minds of other beings. I comprehend the entirety of the characteristics[1624] Of the vast ocean of the minds of other beings. {74}
My knowledge, nondualistic, unhindered, penetrates the spheres of others’ minds; The vast ocean of minds of the world I comprehend in an instant.
sngon gyi mtha' dran ting nge 'dzin stobs kyis/ / bskal pa rgya mtsho tshad med kho mos shes/ / tshe rabs rgyud mang gang chen mtsho dag kyang / / pha rol dag dang bdag gi'ang de bzhin shes/ /
“Through the power of memory and samādhi I know the ocean of countless kalpas in the past. And similarly I know the ocean of the successions Of the many lifetimes of myself and of others. {75}
I remember the past by the power of recollection and concentration, Know oceans of eons, the many hundreds of oceans of lives of myself and others.
rgya mtsho'i zhing gcig rdul phran rab snyed kyi/ / bskal pa skad cig gcig gis ma lus shes/ / sems can 'gro rgyud dag na 'khor ba dang / / sangs rgyas rnam 'phrul tshogs bcas de bzhin no; ;
“I know in a single instant kalpas As numerous as the atoms in an ocean of realms, The existences of beings within saṃsāra, And the buddhas and their hosts of miraculous manifestations. {76}
I know in an instant as many eons as atoms in an ocean of lands, The beings transmigrating, the buddhas and their projections.
de dag thog ma'i smon lam ci 'dra dang / / yang dag sgrub tshul 'jug tshul rnam yangs dang / / spyod la brten pas tshogs rnams yongs sgrub pa/ / 'jig rten mkhyen pa rnams kyang kho mos dran/ /
“I also remember the first aspirations Made by the knowers of the world, Their vast ways of attainment and engagement, And how through conduct they accomplished the accumulations. {77}
I also remember the initial vow of the buddhas, and those who attained, Having accomplished their practice, by many means appropriate to their undertaking.
mnyam med tshad med tshogs gyur yon tan mtsho mnga' ba'i/ / dbang bskur sar byon ji snyed de dag dang / / byang chub 'tshang rgya'i tshul ni rnam yangs la/ / sems kyi skad cig gcig gis kho mo 'jug /

“In a single instant of mind I comprehend The vast ways of enlightenment and buddhahood Of all those who have reached the level of empowerment Of having an ocean of unequaled, immeasurable qualities. {78}
The attainments to the stage of coronation of the oceans of lofty virtue, And their many ways of awakening, I comprehend in an instant.
thabs kyi rnam pa gang dang gang dag gis/ / bde gshegs 'khor lo dam pa 'gror bskor dang / / mya ngan 'das pa yon tan tshad med dang / / chos rnams gnas pa'i dus kyang kho mos shes/ /
“I know how the sugatas, through various methods, Turn the supreme wheel for beings, The measureless qualities of their nirvāṇas, And the length of time their Dharma remains. {79}
I know the methods by which they taught in the world, their measureless virtues In nirvana, and how long their teachings remained.
dri med theg pa rgya mtsho'i tshul rnams dang / / sems can rnams 'dul rnam yangs ji snyed dang / / 'gro bar de dag gis ni gang bstan pa/ / so so kun la sna tshogs tshul gyis 'jug /
“I comprehend individually, through various ways, The ocean of the ways of their stainless yānas, All their vast guidance for beings, And the teachings they give to beings. {80}
The pure principles of their myriad vehicles and extensive guidance of beings Shown in the world, I know in particular, in countless various ways.
dga' ba'i gter dang mos pa'i dbyig gi rnams/ / kun tu snang ba rnam thar tshul 'di yin/ / kho mos bskal pa brgya mang rgya cher bsgoms/ / de tshul de la khyod kyang myur 'jug gyis/ /

“I have meditated for many hundreds of kalpas On the way of this liberation of the illumination Of the treasure of delight and the wealth of aspiration.[1625] You too should quickly comprehend this way. {81}
This way of liberation, witnessing the wealth of satisfaction produced from the treasury of joy, I have cultivated over many hundreds of eons, and you too should enter this way.

rigs kyi bu/ kho mos byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa dga' ba'i 'od spro ba yangs pa yang dag par 'byung ba 'di shes par zad na/ kho mos byang chub sems dpa' de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi zhabs kyi drung du thams cad mkhyen pa nyid la 'jug pa'i smon lam rgya mtsho la zhugs pa/ de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi sngon gyi smon lam rgya mtsho mngon par sgrub pa'i smon lam yongs su rdzogs pa'i byang chub sems dpa'i sa gcig non pas byang chub sems dpa'i sa rgya mtsho thams cad yongs su gnon pa'i stabs la mkhas pa/ byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa rgya mtsho thams cad spyod pa re rer yang dag par 'du ba'i smon lam dang spyod pa yongs su dag pa/ byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa re re la byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa rgya mtsho thams cad yongs su 'du bar rnam par spyad pa la dbang bsgyur ba de dag gi spyod pa shes pa'am/ yon tan brjod par nus re skan/

“Noble one, I know only this bodhisattva liberation called the arising of the vast radiating light of joy. How could I know the conduct or describe the qualities of bodhisattvas who at the feet of all the tathāgatas engage in an ocean of prayers to enter omniscience; who complete the fulfillment of the ocean of the past prayers by the tathāgatas; who are skilled in reaching the ocean of all bodhisattva bhūmis through reaching one bodhisattva bhūmi; who have pure prayer and conduct in which there is an ocean of all bodhisattva conducts included within each conduct; who have the power of practice of the entire ocean of bodhisattva liberations being included within each bodhisattva liberation?

I know only this enlightening liberation of manifestation of satisfaction by treasure produced from great joy. How can I know the practice or tell of the virtues of the enlightening beings in the presence of all buddhas who have plunged into the ocean of commitment to omniscience, who have fulfilled the vow to accomplish the myriad past vows of all buddhas, who have the mighty knowledge to enter all stages of enlightening upon entering one stage of enlightening, who have purified the practice of the vow to comprehend all practices of enlightening beings in one practice, who are masters of the state of comprehension of the whole ocean of all enlightening liberations in each enlightening liberation?

song rigs kyi bu/ snying po byang chub 'di nyid na mtshan mo'i lha mo 'gro ba thams cad srung ba'i smon lam la brtson pa'i 'od ces bya ba zhig /bcom ldan 'das kyi spyan sngar phyin cing 'dug gi /de'i gan du song la ji ltar byang chub sems dpas bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems can yongs su smin par bya ba dang / ji ltar sangs rgyas kyi zhing thams cad yongs su sbyang bar bya ba dang / ji ltar de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad shin tu mnyes par bya bas bsnyen bkur zhing rim gror bya ba dang / ji ltar byang chub sems dpas sangs rgyas kyi chos thams cad la brtson par bya ba dris shig /

“Depart, noble one. The goddess of the night who has the name Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā has come to this bodhimaṇḍa and is in the presence of the Bhagavat. Go to her and ask her, ‘How should a bodhisattva ripen beings for the highest, complete enlightenment? How should a bodhisattva purify all buddha realms? How should a bodhisattva honor and serve all tathāgatas so as to please them? How should a bodhisattva be dedicated to the Dharma[1626] of all the buddhas?’ ”

“In this same enlightenment site there is a night goddess named Sarvajagadrakshapranidhanaviryaprabha, in the presence of the Buddha; go ask her how an enlightening being is to develop sentient beings to supreme perfect enlightenment, purify all buddha-lands, serve all buddhas, and practice all buddhas’ teachings.”

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis mtshan mo'i lha mo shing thams cad kyi me tog rgyas pas bde bar gnas pa'i rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te mtshan mo'i lha mo shing thams cad kyi me tog rgyas pas bde bar gnas pa la lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas yang dang yang du bltas te mtshan mo'i lha mo shing thams cad kyi me tog rgyas pas bde bar gnas pa'i drung nas song ngo/ /

Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, bowed his head to the feet of the night goddess Sarvavṛkṣpraphullanasukhasaṃvāsā, circumambulated the night goddess Sarvavṛkṣpraphullanasukhasaṃvāsā many hundreds of thousands of times, keeping her to his right, and, looking back again and again, departed from the night goddess Sarvavṛkṣpraphullanasukhasaṃvāsā.
Then Sudhana paid his respects to the night goddess Sarvavrikshapraphullanasukhasamvasa and went on.

d.crumb: [mtshan mo'i lha mo 'gro ba thams cad srung ba'i smon lam la brtson pa'i 'od]

f.d: [mtshan mo'i lha mo 'gro ba thams cad srung ba'i smon lam la brtson pa'i 'od]
Chapter 41. Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā
Sarvajagadrakshapranidhanaviryaprabha

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang mtshan mo'i lha mo 'gro ba thams cad srung ba'i smon lam la brtson pa'i 'od gang na ba der song song nas mtshan mo'i lha mo 'gro ba thams cad srung ba'i smon lam la brtson pa'i 'od 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor de nyid na chos kyi dbyings kyi tshul rab tu snang ba'i rin po che'i dra bas kun nas yog pa'i lus dang ldan pa/

Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, went to where the night goddess Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā was. He saw the night goddess Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā in the center of her entourage, seated upon a throne that contained kings of jewels that illuminated the dwellings of all beings. She had a body covered completely in a net of jewels that illuminated the ways of the realm of phenomena.

Then Sudhana went to the night goddess Sarvajagadrakshapranidhanaviryaprabha and saw her sitting, in that same assembly, on a seat of jewels reflecting the abodes of all beings; her body was covered with a net of jewels reflecting the principles of the cosmos.

nyi zla dang / gza' skar dang / rgyu skar thams cad kyi gzugs brnyan yongs su ston pa'i lus dang ldan pa/ bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du sems can gyis rnam par dmigs par ston pa'i lus dang ldan pa/ sems can thams cad kyi lus kyi dbyibs dang 'dra bar rang gi lus rnam par dmigs par byed pa'i lus dang ldan pa/ kha dog rgya mtsho yangs pa mtha' dang dbus med pa rnam par dmigs par ston pa'i lus dang ldan pa/ spyod lam thams cad la rnam par spyod pa'i tshul yongs su ston pa'i lus dang ldan pa/ sgo kun tu mngon par bltas par rnam par dmigs par byed pa'i lus dang ldan pa/ chos kyi sprin gyi 'brug sgra kun tu sgrog cing rnam par 'phrul pa sna tshogs kyis phyogs thams cad rgyas par bkang ste 'gro ba thams cad la mngon du gnas pa'i lus dang ldan pa/ dus thams cad du 'gro ba thams cad kyi don la mngon du bltas par nam mkha'i dbyings kyis glo ba'i lus dang ldan pa/

Her body revealed the images of the sun, the moon, and all the planets, stars, and constellations. She had a body that manifested to the perception of beings in accordance with their wishes. She had a body such that her own body was perceived by all beings as having the same form as their bodies. She had a body that manifested perceptions of a vast, centerless, edgeless ocean of skin colors. She had a body that manifested practicing all paths of the practice of conduct. She had a body that could be perceived from every kind of orientation.[1627] She had a body that was present in all worlds, filling all directions with the sound of thunder from the cloud of the Dharma and with various miraculous manifestations. She had a body that reached throughout the realm of space, at all times looking at how to benefit all beings.

Her body showed reflections of all moons, suns, stars, and planets; she appeared to sentient beings according to their mentalities, she manifested her own body in forms like those of all beings; her body manifested infinitely various appearances; her body manifested the principles of the states of all modes of bearing; her body appeared to be present everywhere; her body appeared to sentient beings everywhere to mature them; her body appeared to all beings, pervading everywhere with various projections proclaiming the truth; her body descended from the sky to meet the needs of beings at all times;

de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi zhabs la 'dud cing phyag 'tshal ba'i lus dang ldan pa/ sems can thams cad kyi dge ba'i rtsa ba bsags pa la gces shing sngon du 'gro ba'i lus dang ldan pa/ de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad las mngon du chos kyi sprin yang dag par len cing yongs su 'dzin pa'i smon lam grub cing yongs su rdzogs par bya ba'i sems las phyir phyogs su ma gyur cing dran pas yongs su 'dzin pa'i lus dang ldan pa/ mtha' dang dbus med pa'i 'od kyis phyogs dang phyogs mtshams thams cad rgyas par 'gengs pa'i lus dang ldan pa/ 'gro ba thams cad kyi mun pa rnam par sel ba'i chos kyi sgron ma'i 'od kun tu 'gyed cing snang ba yongs su ston pa'i lus dang ldan pa/

She had a body that paid homage and bowed down at the feet of all tathāgatas. She had a body that came before all beings, aiding them in the accumulation of roots of merit. She had a body that possessed the mindfulness of keeping and never deviating from the motivation to accomplish and fulfill the prayer to receive and possess clouds of Dharma directly from all the tathāgatas. She had a body that filled all principal and intermediate directions with light that had no edge or center. She had a body that manifested the illumination and the spreading light of the lamp of Dharma, dispelling the darkness in all beings.

her body was bowing at the feet of all buddhas; her body was leading all sentient beings in accumulating roots of goodness; her body was facing all buddhas, receiving their teachings and remembering them, heedfully minding and retaining them in fulfillment of her vows; her body was filling all directions with infinite various manifestations; her body was radiating the light of the lamp of truth dispelling darkness for all beings;

chos sgyu ma'i rnam pa lta bu'i ye shes kyi lus dri ma med pa rab tu ston pa'i lus dang ldan pa/ chos kyi lus mun pa dang rdul du bral ba rab tu ston pa'i lus dang ldan pa/ chos nyid sgyu ma lta bu las byung ba'i lus dang ldan pa/ chos nyid rab tu rtogs pas mun pa med pa'i sems dang ldan pa/ ye shes kyi snang ba sgo kun tu gsal ba rab tu thob pa shin tu nad med cing gdung ba med pa'i yid kyi lus dang ldan pa/ chos kyi sku mi shigs shing brtan pa dang ldan pa'i dbyings las byung ba/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i byin gyi rlabs gnas med pa'i rang bzhin kun nas nyon mongs pa med pa'i dang / dri ma med pa'i chos nyid kyi lus rnam par dag pa'i lus dang ldan pa de rin po che'i rgyal po 'gro ba thams cad kyi gnas rab tu snang ba'i snying po can gyi bstan la 'dug pa mthong ngo/ /

She had a body that manifested as a stainless body of the wisdom that phenomena are like illusions. She had a body that manifested as a Dharma body free of darkness and dust. She had a body that appeared with the nature of being an illusion. She had a mind free of darkness that had realized the true nature. She had attained the illumination in all aspects of the light of wisdom. She had a mental body that was completely free of illness and had no pain. She had appeared from the realm of the enduring and indestructible Dharma body. She had a body that was the pure body of the stainless true nature, the state completely without kleśas, and which had the nature of the unlocated blessing of the tathāgatas.

her body showed the embodiment of pure knowledge of the illusoriness of things; her body showed the embodiment of spirituality free from ignorance and passion; her body was born of the magical nature of reality; her mind was aware of the nature of reality; she was illumined with the light of impartial knowledge; her mind and body were ultimately free from irritation and inflammation; she had come from the indestructible realm of the body of reality; her body was a pure embodiment of the nature of things, inherently undefiled, naturally unafflicted, empowered by the realization of Thusness, not fixed or dependent.

des de mthong nas spyi bos btud de mthong bar bya ba'i tshul sangs rgyas kyi zhing gi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed rjes su dran par byas nas sa'i gzhi las btud de rgyang bcad pa zhig tu mngon par btud do/ / de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang sa'i gzhi de las langs te thal mo sbyar nas mtshan mo'i lha mo 'gro ba thams cad srung ba'i smon lam la brtson pa'i 'od de'i lus la bltas pa dang / 'du shes rnam par dag pa bcu thob par gyur te/ de dag thob pas dge ba'i bshes gnyen thams cad dang skal pa mnyam pa rab tu thob par gyur to/ /

When he had seen her, he bowed his head, and, remembering the ways of seeing her, which were as numerous as the atoms in a buddha realm, he bowed down to the ground, prostrating himself for a long time.[1628] Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, then stood up from the ground, placed his palms together, and, looking at the body of the night goddess Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā, he gained ten pure perceptions, and through gaining them he gained commonality with all kalyāṇamitras.[1629]

Sudhana, seeing her, bowed his head; remembering as many ways of seeing her as atoms in a buddha-land, he prostrated himself on the ground for a long time. Finally rising from the ground, in a reverential attitude Sudhana gazed at the body of the night goddess, and as he did so he attained ten purities of thought, whereby he gained communality with all spiritual friends.

bcu gang zhe na/ 'di lta ste/ thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du brtsams pa'i brtson 'grus la dmigs pa thams cad du gnas par bya ba'i phyir dge ba'i bshes gnyen rnams la rang gi sems kyi 'du shes rab tu thob par gyur to/ /
What were those ten? (1) He gained the perception of his own mind being among the kalyāṇamitras in order to have all the diligence for undertaking the attainment of omniscience.
What were those ten? He thought of spiritual friends as his own mind, to associate with them in all situations in the effort to attain omniscience.
dge ba'i bshes gnyen bsnyen bkur zhing dge ba'i rtsa ba yangs pa yongs su sgrub pa grub par bya ba'i phyir rang gi las kyi rnam par smin pa rnam par dag pa'i rang bzhin gyi 'du shes rab tu thob bo/ /
(2) He gained the perception of the pure nature of the ripening of his own karma so as to attain the accomplishment of vast roots of merit from honoring kalyāṇamitras.
He thought of them as the pure essence of the development of his own actions, to accomplish the attainment of extensive roots of goodness to please spiritual friends.
smon lam thams cad kyis brgyan pa'i spyod pa la yang dag par gnas par bya ba'i phyir byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa'i rgyan gyi 'du shes rab tu thob bo/ /
(3) He gained the perception of the adornment of bodhisattva conduct so as to remain in the conduct that is the adornment of all prayers.
He thought of them as adorning the practice of enlightening beings, to associate with them in carrying out adornment by all spiritual vows.
dge ba'i bshes gnyen thams cad kyi gdams ngag gi lam la nan tan du bya ba'i phyir sangs rgyas kyi chos thams cad rab tu sgrub pa'i 'du shes rab tu thob bo/ /
(4) He gained the perception of the accomplishment of all the Dharmas of the buddhas so as to practice the path of the instructions of all the tathāgatas.
He thought of them as bringing him to all aspects of buddhahood, to practice the paths taught by all spiritual friends.
sangs rgyas thams cad kyi yul du gyur pa'i chos bla na med pa la rnam par spyod pa'i snang ba yongs su mthong bar bya ba'i phyir nyams su myong ba ba skyed pa'i 'du shes rab tu thob bo/ /
(5) He gained the perception of the arising of sensations so as to see the radiance of practicing the unsurpassable Dharma that is the field of all buddhas.
He thought of them as the state of comfort, to manifest the abode of the supreme state of the realm of all buddhas.
kun tu bzang po'i spyod pas 'byung ba'i smon lam dang / spyod pa rnam par dag par bya ba'i phyir 'byung ba gcig gi 'du shes rab tu thob par gyur to/ /
(6) He gained the perception of a single setting forth so as to have the pure conduct and prayer of setting forth through the completely good conduct.[1630]
He thought of them as the one way of emancipation, to purify the practice of the commitment of emancipation by the vehicle of universal good.
dge ba'i chos yongs su bsags pa thams cad rnam par 'phel bar bya ba'i phyir thams cad mkhyen pa'i bsod nams rgya mtsho'i 'byung gnas kyi 'du shes rab tu thob bo/ /
(7) He gained the perception of the origin of the ocean of the merit of omniscience so as to increase the accumulation of all good qualities.
He thought of them as oceans of virtues of omniscience, to increase the production of all good qualities.

sangs rgyas kyi byang chub tu thams cad mkhyen pa'i ye shes la brtson 'grus kyi shugs yongs su 'phel bar bya ba'i phyir dge ba'i chos yongs su ma rdzogs pa yongs su rdzogs par byed pa dang / yang dag par 'phel bar byed pa dang / yongs su skyong ba'i 'du shes rab tu thob par gyur to/ /
(8) He gained the perception of protecting, increasing, and completing incomplete[1631] good qualities so as to increase the power of diligence for omniscience in the enlightenment of buddhahood.
He thought of them as fulfilling, increasing, and preserving all consummate good, to increase the force of energetic effort for total knowledge of complete enlightenment.
sems can thams cad kyi bsam pa thams cad yongs su rdzogs par bya ba'i phyir dge ba'i rtsa ba thams cad yongs su rdzogs pa'i 'du shes rab tu thob par gyur to/ /
(9) He gained the perception of the completion of all roots of merit so as to fulfill the wishes of all beings.
He thought of them as fulfilling all roots of goodness, to fulfill the aspirations of all beings.
byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi chos la dbang bsgyur bar rab tu gnas par bya ba'i phyir dge ba'i bshes gnyen rnams la don thams cad yongs su sgrub pa'i 'du shes rab tu thob ste/
(10) He gained the perception of the accomplishment of all goals among kalyāṇamitras so as to be established in having the power of the qualities[1632] of all bodhisattvas.
He thought of spiritual friends as fulfillers of all aims, to establish the mastery of all acts of enlightening beings.

'du shes rnam par dag pa bcu po de dag rab tu thob par gyur to/ / de dag thob pas mtshan mo'i lha mo 'gro ba thams cad srung ba'i smon lam la brtson pa'i 'od snang ba las byang chub sems dpa' dang skal pa mthun pa sangs rgyas kyi zhing gi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed thob par gyur te/

Those are the ten pure perceptions he gained. Having gained them, he gained from the night goddess Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā commonalities with bodhisattvas that were as numerous as the atoms in a buddha realm.
He attained these ten purities of thought, whereby he attained communality with the night goddess and enlightening beings as numerous as atoms in a buddha-land.
'di ltar phyogs bcu'i de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi dus gsum rjes su dran pa'i tshul la dran pa'i skal ba mnyam pa dang /
These were the commonality of memory in the way of remembering the three times of all the tathāgatas in the ten directions;
That is, he attained communality of recollection, in remembering all buddhas of all times and places;
chos rgya mtsho'i tshul thams cad tha ma dad par khong du chud par bya ba la blo gros kyi skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of understanding in comprehending the different[1633] ways of the ocean of all Dharmas;
communality of intellect, in unconfused ascertainment of the principles of the ocean of all truths;
de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi chos kyi 'khor lo'i dkyil 'khor rigs pas rjes su shes par bya ba'i bye brag dang / tshul tha dad par mkhas pa la rig pa'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of knowledge in the skill of the different, particular ways of having knowledge of the range of the wheel of the Dharma of all the tathāgatas;
communality of course, in familiarity with the principles of clear distinction following the courses of the teachings of all buddhas;
blo nam mkha' dang mnyam pas dus gsum thams cad kyi tshul rgya mtsho snang ba rab tu thob par bya ba'i phyir blo'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of understanding for attaining, through an understanding as extensive as space, the illumination of the ocean of ways in the three times;
communality of enlightenment, so as to realize the ocean of all principles of all times by spacelike awareness;
byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi dbang po rgya mtsho shes pa'i snang ba rab tu thob par bya ba'i phyir dbang po rnam par dag pa'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of pure faculties for attaining the illumination of the knowledge of an ocean of the faculties of all bodhisattvas;
communality of purity of faculties, so as to realize the knowledge of the ocean of faculties of all enlightening beings;

rnam pa thams cad du sems can yongs su bsdu ba'i rgyan gyis rnam par brgyan pa'i byang chub sems dpa'i lam gyi yon tan la nan tan du bya ba'i rgyan gyis lam khong du chud par bya ba'i phyir sems rnam par dag pa'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of pure mind for realizing the path adorned by the acquisition of the qualities of the bodhisattva path with its display of gathering beings in every way;
communality of mental purity, so as to accomplish the path of adornment achieving the virtues of the path of enlightening beings adorned by the protection and care of living beings in all ways;
de bzhin gshegs pa'i ye shes kyi spyod yul snang ba rab tu thob par bya ba'i phyir spyod yul gyi skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of a pure field of activity for attaining the illumination of the field of activity of the wisdom of the tathāgatas;
communality of sphere, so as to attain the scope of the sphere of knowledge of those who have arrived at Thusness;
thams cad mkhyen pa'i tshul rgya mtsho la 'jug pa'i lam snang ba rnam pa thams cad rab tu thob par bya ba'i phyir tshul gyi rjes su 'brang ba'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of following a way for attaining all aspects of the illumination of the path for entering an ocean of the ways of omniscience;
communality of following principles, so as to gain the light of the path of entry into the ocean of principles of complete omniscience;
chos thams cad kyi rang bzhin shes shing khong du chud pa rab tu thob par bya ba'i phyir don khong du chud pa'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of the comprehension of meaning for attaining the comprehension of the nature of all phenomena;
communality of comprehension of meaning, so as to attain comprehension of knowledge of the nature of all things;
chos kyi tshul rgya mtsho thams cad la chos la rnam par spyod pa'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
sgrib pa thams cad kyi ri rnam par gtor ba'i phyir mi 'jigs pa'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of Dharma practice for the destruction of the mountain of all obscurations;[1634]
communality of spiritual abode, so as to shatter the mountains of all obstructions;

bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du 'gro ba rnams la rnam pa tha dad par yongs su bstan pa'i mtshan dang dpe byad bzang pos rnam par bris pa'i lus rnam par dag pa rab tu thob par bya ba'i phyir gzugs kyi lus rnam par dag pa'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of a pure form body for attaining a pure body adorned by signs and features of a great being that are manifested separately to beings according to their wishes;

communality of purity of the physical body, so as to attain physical purity resplendent with the marks and embellishments of greatness, appearing to sentient beings variously according to their dispositions;
byang chub sems dpa'i stobs yongs su rdzogs pas thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du dmigs pa rnam par 'phel bar bya ba'i phyir stobs kyi skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of strength for the increase of focusing on omniscience through perfecting the strength of a bodhisattva;
communality of power, so as to increase focus on omniscience in which all powers of enlightening beings are consummated;
sems dang bsam pa'i nam mkha' yongs su dag par bya ba'i phyir mi 'jigs pa'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of fearlessness for the purification of the space of mind and thoughts;
communality in expertise in all spiritual methods, so as to make the mind clear as space;
bskal pa thams cad du byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la gnas pas mi skyo ba rab tu thob par bya ba'i phyir btson 'grus kyi skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of diligence for attaining the unwearying continuation of bodhisattva conduct throughout all kalpas;
communality of energy, so as to be capable of tireless perseverance in enlightening practices through all ages;
chos thams cad la sgrib pa med pa'i ye shes snang ba rab tu thob par bya ba'i phyir spobs pa'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of eloquence for attaining the illumination of the unobscured knowledge of all Dharma;
communality of eloquence, so as to illumine unobstructed knowledge of all things;
'gro ba thams cad las mngon par 'phags pa'i lus yongs su dag par bya ba'i phyir zil gyis mi non pa'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of being unsurpassable for the purification of a body superior to all beings;
communality of insuperability, so as to purify the body beyond all worldlings;
'khor gyi dkyil 'khor thams cad mngon par dga' bar bya ba'i tshigs yongs su dag par bya ba'i phyir ma zhum mi dma' ba'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of undaunted, intrepid speech[1635] for the purification of words that bring joy to all circles of followers;
communality of noble-minded, nondepressive, intrepid speech, for purity of good relations with all groups;
chos kyi tshul rgya mtsho thams cad kyi sgra rab tu bsgrag pa'i phyir dbyangs kyi skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of sound for expressing the ocean of sound of the ways of all the Dharma;
communality of voice, for enunciation of all truths;
'gro ba thams cad kyi tshig rnam par dmigs pa'i tha snyad dang / tshul rgya mtsho la dbyangs kyi yan lag rnam par dag pa'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of the pure aspects of the voice in the ocean of the ways and terms used in the words of all beings;
communality of purity of articulation, in respect to the myriad principles of conventions of expression of the languages of all beings;
de bzhin gshegs pa'i gdams ngag gi yon tan khong du chud pa rnam par dag par bya ba la yon tan rnam par dag pa'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of the pure qualities in the pure realization of the qualities of the teaching of the tathāgatas;
communality of purity of virtue, in respect to purities of accomplishment of virtues taught by the buddhas;
kha na ma tho ba med pa'i las rnam par smin pa yongs su dag par bya ba'i phyir chos dang las kyi rgyud du mi 'gal ba'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of not being in contradiction with the lineage of Dharma and karma for the pure ripening of karma without transgressions;
communality of harmonizing with the tradition of principles and actions of buddhas, for purity of consequences of blameless action;
sangs rgyas byung ba thams cad kyi chos kyi 'khor lo rab tu bskor ba'i phyir mchod sbyin gyi chos bzang po la rab tu gnas pa'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of being established on the level of good Dharma through Dharma generosity for the turning of the Dharma wheel of all buddhas that have appeared;
communality of devotion to truth, so as to turn the wheels of teaching of all buddhas who appear in the world;
de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi yul dang ye shes la yang dag par gnas par bya ba'i phyir tshangs pa'i spyod pa rnams par dag pa'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of pure celibacy for remaining in the knowledge and field of all the tathāgatas;
communality of religious practice, so as to dwell in the knowledge of the realm of all buddhas;
byams pa'i tshul sna tshogs kyis skad cig re re la sems can rgya mtsho thams cad du rgyas par dgang bar bya ba'i phyir byams pa chen po'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of great kindness for spreading in each instant, through various ways of kindness, throughout the ocean of all beings;
communality of great kindness, so as to pervade the ocean of all beings in every moment with the various aspects of kindness;
sems can gyi khams thams cad yongs su skyob pa'i chos kyi sprin gyi char mngon par dbab pa'i phyir snying rje chen po'i tshul rgya mtsho la 'jug pa'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of entering the ocean of the ways of great compassion of sending down a rain of the Dharma that protects all realms of beings;
communality of entry into the ocean of great compassion, so as to rain teachings for the salvation of all beings;
sems can thams cad yongs su smin par byed pa'i thabs kyi rgyud du skal pa mnyam par bya ba'i phyir lus kyi las kyi skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of activity of the body for having the same existence as all beings as a method for ripening them;
communality of physical action, for equality in application of means to perfect all beings;
chos thams cad brjod cing smos pa la ngag gi las rnam par dag pa'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of activity of the speech for speaking and communicating the Dharma;
communality of purity in verbal action, in respect to seeking modes of expression of all truths;
sems can thams cad kyi sems la thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du dmigs pa nye bar bsgrub pa'i phyir yid kyi las kyi skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of activity of the mind for instilling a focus on omniscience in the minds of all beings;
communality of mental action, for production of focus on omniscience in the minds of all beings;
sangs rgyas kyi zhing thams cad la rgyan rnam pa sna tshogs thams cad kyis rab tu brgyan pa'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of the beautification of all various displays within all buddha realms for approaching the presence of all tathāgatas;
communality of adornment of all kinds, to approach all buddhas in all buddha-lands;
sangs rgyas 'byung brgya mtsho thams cad du de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi spyan sngar 'gro ba'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of approaching their presence within the ocean of all buddhas that have appeared;
communality of visitation of all buddhas appearing in the world;
de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad la chos kyi 'khor lo bskor bar gsol ba gdab pa'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of requesting all tathāgatas to turn the wheel of the Dharma;
communality of seeking the teachings of all buddhas;
de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad la dus ma lus par mchod pa thams cad kyis rim gro bya ba'i phyir mchod pas rim gror bya ba'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of serving through offerings all tathāgatas throughout all times without exception;
communality of service, to serve all buddhas at all times;
sems can gyi khams thams cad du sems can yongs su smin par bya ba dang gdul ba'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of the guidance that ripens all beings within all realms of beings;
communality of leading beings to full development, in all realms of beings;
chos kyi tshul thams cad la snang ba rab tu thob pa'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of attaining the illumination of all the ways of the Dharma;
communality of attainment of illumination of all methods of teaching sentient beings;
ting nge 'dzin gyi tshul rgya mtsho thams cad la ting nge 'dzin rab tu thob pa'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of attaining samādhi in the entire ocean of the ways of samādhi;
communality of attainment of concentration, in all methods of concentration;
sangs rgyas kyi zhing rgya mtsho thams cad du byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa dang rnam par 'phrul pas rgyas par dgang ba'i phyir kun tu rgyas par dgang ba'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of pervasion for pervading the entire ocean of buddha realms with all the miraculous manifestations and conduct of bodhisattvas;
communality of universal pervasion, so as to pervade all buddha-lands with projections of practices of enlightening beings;
byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi rnam par 'phrul pa'i tshul rgya mtsho la byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par spyod pa'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of bodhisattva conduct within the ocean of all the miraculous manifestations of bodhisattvas;
communality of states of enlightening beings, in the oceans of means of miracles of all enlightening beings;
byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la gnas pa la 'khor gyi skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of followers in the maintenance of all bodhisattva conduct;
communality of associates, associating with all enlightening beings in practice;
'jig rten gyi khams thams cad shin tu phra bar 'jug pa la 'jug pa'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of entry in entering all the most subtle world realms;
communality of entry, entering the most suitable aspects of all worlds;
sangs rgyas kyi zhing shin tu yangs pa thams cad du sems rnam par phye ba'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of distinctions of motivation in the vastness of all buddha realms;
communality of mental distinction of the extent of all buddha-lands;
sangs rgyas kyi zhing rgya mtsho thams cad la 'jug pa rnam pa tha dad pa khong du chud par bya ba la khong du chud pa rnam pa tha dad pa'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
