the commonality of the different kinds of approaching[1636] in approaching the various kinds of entry into the ocean of all buddha realms;
communality of differences in approach, according to differences in entering the ocean of all buddha-lands;
sangs rgyas kyi zhing thams cad rnam par phye ba ye shes mtha' yas pas rnam par dmigs par bya ba la tshul 'byams klas pas kun tu rgyas par dgang ba'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of pervading the extent of every kind of way in the perception of the infinite knowledge of the categories of all buddha realms;
communality of thorough penetration of the entire range of reason, in representations of endless knowledge of differentiations of all buddha-lands;
sangs rgyas kyi zhing thams cad du mngon par 'byung ba'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of arising in all buddha realms;
communality of emergence in all buddha-lands;
phyogs thams cad rgyas par dgang bar yang dag par gzhol ba thogs pa med cing phyir mi ldog par bya ba'i phyir mi ldog pa'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of irreversibility for irreversibly and without impediment spreading throughout and remaining in all directions;
communality of nonregression, never to regress in penetrating and comprehending all realms;
sangs rgyas thams cad kyi snying po byang chub tu rnam par 'tshang rgya ba'i ye shes kyi dkyil 'khor snang ba rab tu thob par bya ba'i phyir mun pa rnam par sel ba'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of eliminating darkness for attaining the illumination of the domain of wisdom of the enlightenment at the bodhimaṇḍas of all buddhas;
communality of dispelling darkness, so as to illumine the sphere of knowledge of all buddhas awakening at the site of enlightenment;
sangs rgyas thams cad kyi 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor rgya mtshor rjes su phyin pa'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of following in the ocean of the circles of followers of all buddhas;
communality of arrival in the oceans of audiences of all buddhas;
sangs rgyas kyi zhing brjod du med pa'i de bzhin gshegs pa mchod cing rim gro bya ba'i sbyor ba la sangs rgyas kyi zhing thams cad lus kyi dra bas rgyas par dgang ba'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of a spreading network of bodies in all the buddha realms in dedication to offering and service to tathāgatas in countless buddha realms;
communality of pervasion of the network of all buddha-lands, in efforts to serve the buddhas in untold buddha-lands;
chos kyi tshul rgya mtsho rjes su rgyu ba de dang de dag la ye shes mngon sum gyi skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of direct knowledge in constant engagement with the ocean of the ways of the Dharma;
communality of direct knowledge of the connections of all principles of the Teachings;
rjes su mthun pa'i chos kyi tshul thams cad mngon du bya ba'i sbyor ba la nan tan gyi skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of practice in appropriate engagement with all the ways of the Dharma;
communality of application, in undertaking all the principles of the Teaching in order;
chos kyi mos pa shin tu shas che ba'i brtsams pa rnam par dag par bya ba'i phyir btsal ba'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of seeking the purification of undertakings made with an intense aspiration for the Dharma;
communality of seeking, to purify intensive seeking for truth;
lus dang ngag dang yid kyi las kyis sangs rgyas kyi yon tan gyi rgyan yongs su sgrub pa la rnam par dag pa'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of purity in accomplishing the adornment of the qualities of buddhahood through the activities of body, speech, and mind;
communality of purity, in accumulating the adornments of enlightened virtues of physical, verbal, and mental action;
nyam nga ba'i rtog pa med pa'i sems kyi dkyil 'khor gyis chos thams cad kyi ye shes kyi dkyil 'khor yongs su dag par bya ba'i phyir yid kyi skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of mind for the purification of the domain of the knowledge of all Dharmas by the domain of mind that is free of fearful thoughts;
communality of goodness of mind, to purify the sphere of knowledge of all things and the sphere of mind without evil thoughts;
dge ba'i rtsa ba thams cad kyi tshogs yang dag par brtsams pa mthar phyin par bya ba'i sbyor ba la brtson 'grus brtsams pa'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of diligent undertakings in engagement in bringing to its conclusion the undertaking of the accumulation of all roots of merit;
communality of vigor, in efforts to fulfill the undertaking of collection of all roots of goodness;
byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa thams cad yongs su rdzogs par bya ba la spyod pa'i rgyan gyi skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of the display of conduct in the practice of all bodhisattva conduct;
communality of arrays of practices, in accomplishments of all enlightening practices;
chos thams cad kyi mtshan ma khong du chud par bya ba la chags pa med par rnam par spyad pa'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of practice without impediment in the comprehension of the attributes of all Dharmas;
communality of unhindered state, in understanding the characteristics of all things;
chos la rnam par spyod pa'i ye shes kyis rnam par 'phrul pa de dang de dag tu thabs mkhas pa'i tshul gyi skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of the way of skillful methods in the miraculous manifestations here and there through the knowledge of the practice of the Dharma;
communality of skill in means, in mystical displays of the knowledge of each spiritual state;
bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du sems can rnams la yul bstan pas yang dag par bskul ba'i phyir skye mched rnam par dag pa'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of pure āyatanas in[1637] manifesting a field of sensory perception in accordance with the wishes of beings;
communality of purification of senses, in assumptions of suitable appearances according to the mentalities of sentient beings;
chos thams cad sgom pa dang / rnam par sgom pa rab tu thob par bya ba'i phyir byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin gyi sgo rab tu thob par bya ba'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of the attainment of the gateways to bodhisattva samādhi within the attainment of meditation on and cultivation of all Dharmas;
communality of attainment of the concentration methods of enlightening beings, in cultivation of all enlightening teachings;
de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi byin gyi rlabs kyi skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of empowerment in the abodes of all the tathāgatas;[1638]
communality of base, in the abodes of all buddhas;
sangs rgyas dang / byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyis rab tu thob par bya ba las yongs su gnan pa'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of reaching the bhūmis[1639] on attaining all the bhūmis[1640] of the buddhas and bodhisattvas;
communality of accession to the stages of enlightenment, in attainments of all stages of buddhas and enlightening beings;
byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par dgod pa thams cad la rab tu gnas pa'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of abode in the establishment of all bodhisattvas;
communality of standpoint, in all states of enlightening beings;
sangs rgyas thams cad kyis lung bstan pa la yongs su bstan pa'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of revelation in the prophecies of all the buddhas;
communality of instruction, in receiving the instructions of all buddhas;
skad cig gcig gi ting nge 'dzin rgya mtsho'i tshul thams cad la ting nge 'dzin gyi skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of samādhi in an ocean of samādhis in each instant;
communality of concentration, entering the ocean of all concentrations at once;
sangs rgyas kyi 'phrin las mtshan nyid sna tshogs la ting nge 'dzin rnam par dgod pa'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of being established in samādhi within the various characteristics of the activities of the buddhas;
communality of differentiation of concentrations, in the context of various buddha-works;
rjes su dran pa'i dmigs pa'i tshul rgya mtsho thams cad la rjes su dran pa'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of mindfulness in the ocean of all the ways of being focused on mindfulness;
communality of mindfulness, of all points to remember;
byang chub sems dpa'i bya ba la phyi ma'i mtha'i bskal pa'i mur thug par zhe non pa la byang chub sems dpas spyad pa'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of bodhisattva conduct in being dedicated to bodhisattva activities until the last of future kalpas;
communality of conduct of enlightening beings, continuing to perform the tasks of enlightening beings through all times;
sangs rgyas kyi ye shes tshad med pa la mos shing dga' ba'i shugs rgya mtsho rnam par 'phel bar bya ba'i phyir mos pa'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of aspiration for increasing the ocean of the power of delight in aspiring to the immeasurable knowledge of buddhahood;
communality of pure faith, to expand the ocean of energy of joy of devotion to infinite enlightened knowledge;
sgrib pa'i ri thams cad la rnam par zlog pa'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of repelling the mountain of all obscurations;
communality of destruction of all obstructions to enlightenment;
sangs rgyas kyi ye shes kyi tshogs mtha' yas pa yongs su bsgrub pa'i phyir phyir mi zlog pa'i ye shes kyi skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of irreversible knowledge that accomplishes the infinite accumulation of the knowledge of the buddhas;
communality of nonregressing knowledge, to produce endless stores of enlightened knowledge;
sems can thams cad yongs su sbyin par bya ba dang / gdul ba'i dus su skye ba'i skal pa dang mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of taking birth in the times for ripening and guiding all beings;
communality of emergence at appropriate times to guide all sentient beings to full development;
thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi tshul gyi sgo la rnam par spyod pa'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of practice in the gateways to the ways of omniscience;
communality of abode on the ways to omniscience;
chos kyi dbyings kyi tshul gyis khyu mchog gi mthu phyung ba'i yul la rab tu 'jug par bya ba'i phyir yul gyi skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of scope in entering the scope of supremacy in the ways of the realm of the Dharma;
communality of sphere, entering the sphere of the majesty of the design of the cosmos;
gzhi thams cad yongs su chom pa'i sems su bya ba'i phyir gzhi med pa'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of being unbased in order to have a mind that has eradicated all bases;
communality of independence, so as to be mentally free of all dependence;
chos mnyam pa nyid kyi ye shes la 'jug par bya ba'i phyir chos bstan pa'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of the teaching of the Dharma for entering into the knowledge of the equality of all phenomena;
communality of teaching of all truths, realizing knowledge of the equality of all things;
sangs rgyas thams cad kyi byin gyi rlabs rang gi lus kyis yang dag par gnon pa'i phyir brtson pa'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of application for the body acquiring the empowerment of all the buddhas;
communality of exertion, so as to embody the power of all buddhas;
'jig rten thams cad kyis khong du chud par bya ba'i phyir nan tan gyi tshul la mngon par shes pa'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of higher cognition in the ways of practicing gaining knowledge of all worlds;
communality of higher knowledge of means of accomplishing communication with all beings;
phyogs thams cad kyi zhing rgya mtshor 'jug par bya ba la mngon par 'du bya ba med pa'i rdzu 'phrul rab tu thob pa'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of attaining miraculous powers without karmic accumulation in entering the ocean of realms in all directions;
communality of attainment of uncontrived mystic powers, entering the oceans of lands in all directions;
gzungs rgya mtsho thams cad kyi snang ba rab tu thob par bya ba la gzungs kyi sa'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of the level of mental retention for attaining the illumination of an ocean of all retentions;
communality of the stage of mental command, so as to gain the illumination of the ocean of all concentration spells;
mdo sde'i chos kyi rnam grangs thams cad la sangs rgyas thams cad kyi chos kyi 'khor lo'i dgongs pa khong du chud par bya ba'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of comprehending the intention of the Dharma wheels of the buddhas within the transmission of the sūtras;
communality of penetration of the secrets of all the buddhas’ teachings in the doctrines of all the scriptures;
nam mkha'i dbyings lta bu'i chos kyi tshul thams cad khong du chud par bya ba'i phyir chos zab mo la 'jug pa'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of comprehending the profound Dharma in comprehending the ways of the Dharma that are as vast as space;
communality of entry into profundity, in realizations of the principle of all things being like space;
'jig rten gyi khams 'byams klas pa thams cad du snang bar bya ba'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of illumination in the extent of all world realms;
communality of range, coursing through all worlds;
bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du 'gro bas rnam par dmigs par bstan pa la mngon par gsal ba'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of brilliance in manifesting to the perception of beings in accordance with their aspirations;
communality of splendor, appearing to beings according to their mentalities;
zhing gi byin gyi rlabs dang / rnam par 'phrul pa sems can yongs su bstan pa'i phyir rab tu bskyod pa'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
the commonality of shaking in manifesting to beings blessings and miraculous manifestations in the worlds;
communality of shaking, showing beings changes in the basis of the world;
mthong ba dang / thos pa dang / rjes su dran pas sems can gdul ba'i phyir don yod par spyad pa'i skal pa mnyam pa dang /
and the commonality of meaningful conduct in guiding beings through being seen, heard, or remembered;
communality of fruitful action, edifying all who see, hear, or remember them;
smon lam rgya mtsho'i tshul thams cad yongs su rdzogs pas stobs bcu'i ye shes rjes su 'tshang rgya bar bya ba'i phyir 'byung ba'i skal pa mnyam pa yang rab tu thob par gyur to/ /
and he attained the commonality of setting forth for the awakening of the knowledge of the ten strengths, which fulfills all the ways of an ocean of prayers.
communality of emancipation, so as to awaken to the knowledge of the ten powers, to fulfill all vows.

de ltar tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang shin tu dga' ba'i sems su gyur te/ mtshan mo'i lha mo 'gro ba thams cad srung ba'i smon lam la brtson pa'i 'od la bltas pas 'du shes rnam par dag pa de dag thob par gyur te/ 'di dag la sogs pa mtshan mo'i lha mo 'gro ba thams cad srung ba'i smon lam la brtson pa'i 'od las skal pa mnyam pa'i tshul sangs rgyas kyi zhing gi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyang thob par gyur to/ /

In that way, Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, gained a state of delight. He attained those pure perceptions through looking at the night goddess Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā. He attained these and other commonalities, as numerous as the atoms in a buddha realm, from the night goddess Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā.
Thus did Sudhana, by attainment of ten purities of thought while gazing at the night goddess, gain communality with the night goddess in as many such ways as atoms in a buddha-land.

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang mtshan mo'i lha mo 'gro ba thams cad srung ba'i smon lam la brtson pa'i 'od la blta ba'i tshul sangs rgyas kyi zhing rdul shin tu phra ba snyed la zhugs pa; dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi 'du shes rnam par dag pa mtha' dang dbus med pa rab tu thob pa/ skal pa mnyam pa'i tshul sangs rgyas kyi zhing gi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed la zhugs pas

Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, because of the night goddess Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā, entered ways of seeing that were as numerous as the atoms in a buddha realm; he attained pure perceptions, without end or center, of the kalyāṇamitras; and he entered ways of commonality that were as numerous as the atoms in a buddha realm.

Then, having seen the night goddess in as many ways as atoms in a buddha-land, having attained an infinite variety of purity of perception of spiritual friends and entered into as many aspects of communality with them as atoms in a buddha-land,
bla gos phrag pa gcig tu gzar te mtshan mo'i lha mo 'gro ba thams cad srung ba'i smon lam la brtson pa'i 'od gang na ba der thal mo sbyar te btud nas de'i tshe tshigs su bcad pa 'di dag smras so/ /
With his upper robe removed from one shoulder and with his palms together, he bowed in the direction of the night goddess Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā and recited these verses:
Sudhana bared one shoulder, bowed to the goddess, and spoke these verses:
de ni bdag gi sems la bdag dgongs te/ / byang chub mos pa mi ldog shin tu brtan/ / khyod kyi thugs la'ang bdag ni de bzhin du/ / bdag gi bzhin du de ring brtan par skyes/ /
“I regard my own mind and my aspiration To enlightenment to be firm and irreversible. As it is in your mind, so it is in mine. And that which is mine has today become firm. {1}
As the power in my own mind, my will For enlightenment is firm and unbending; As in your mind, O goddess, so in mine This determination now spontaneously arises.
sdig to ma lus rnam par byang bar gyur/ / dge ba'i rnam smin mi nya ma rab tu thob/ / bdag gis blta na mdzes pa khyod mthong bas/ / chos dkar mi bas bdag gis yongs su bsags/ /
All evils are cleared away, And resplendent good is developed: From witnessing your beauty Endless goodness is born in me.
bdag gi sems ni yon tan chu bos brgyan/ / sems can phan brtson rnam pa tha dad pas/ / brgyan 'gyur des ni phyi mtha'i bskal par yang / / zhing rnams kun tu spyod pa spyad par bgyi/ /
“My mind is adorned by a river of qualities. Through dedication to benefiting beings in various ways, I practice a conduct that is thus adorned Within all realms until the last of future kalpas. {3}
My mind is adorned with myriad virtues, Each to the benefit of living beings; Adorned thereby, I carry on practice In all lands for all time.
'phags mas bdag la thugs brtse mdzad slad du; ; chos rnams thams cad grub pa khyod kyis bstan/ / bdag la sman slad rjes su gzung dgongs te/ / chos kyi gdams ngag dam pa stsal du gsol/ /

“Āryā, in order to show your kindness to me, You have revealed the accomplishment of all Dharmas. I pray that for my benefit[1643] you will decide to care for me And bestow on me the highest teaching of the Dharma. {4}
You have taught me the consummation Of all the teachings to aid me: For my benefit, thinking to assist me, You present supreme spiritual instruction.
ngan 'gror ltung ba'i lam ni rnam par bzlog / mtho ris shul gtsang dam pa yongs su bstan/ / bde gshegs ma lus bzhud cing rjes bzhud pa'i/ / thams cad mkhyen pa'i shul kyang khyod kyis bstan/ /

“You have repelled the path of falling into lower existences. You have shown the pure path to the higher existences. You have taught the path[1644] to omniscience, Which is the way followed by every sugata. {5}
You have blocked the path to woe and calamity And shown the way to felicity; You have also shown the way to omniscience, Followed by all enlightened ones.
dpe med rmad du byung mang khyod la bdag / 'byung ba'i 'du shes dam pa nye bar skyes/ / nam mkha' lta bur dri med tshad med pa'i/ / thams cad mkhyen nyid chos sgo rnam par dag /

“Incomparable, marvelous one, I have in your presence[1645] Developed the supreme conception of setting forth. The pure entranceway to the Dharma of omniscience Is immeasurable and stainless, like space. {6}
I think of you as a vehicle Of emancipation, incomparable, rare; Like space, undefiled, infinite, Pure is the door to omniscience.
kun mkhyen tshad med 'byung gnas bzang po yi/ / 'du shes de ring tshad med khyod la skyes/ / bsod nams rgya mtsho mkha' ltar tshad med pa'i/ / sems las byung ba skad cig re rer 'byung / /
“Today I have developed the immeasurable perception of you As the excellent source of immeasurable omniscience. An ocean of merit as immeasurable as space Arises in the mind with every instant. {7}
I think of you as a pure, Immeasurable mine of omniscience; Oceans of virtues, vast as the sky, Arise in my mind every moment.
'phags ma pha rol phyin pas bdag bkur gsol/ / bsam yas bsod nams kyis kyang rnam spel gsol/ / yon tan dge ba thams cad yongs 'phel nas/ / thams cad mkhyen pa'i go 'phang myur thob mdzod/ /
“Āryā, I pray you empower me with the perfections. I pray that you augment inconceivable merit. Having augmented all goodness and qualities, Cause me to quickly attain the level of omniscience. {8}
Guide me by the transcendent ways And nourish me with inconceivable virtues; Fully developed by pure virtues, before long I will gain the turban of omniscience.
dge ba'i bshes gnyen rnams la rtag par bdag / thams cad mkhyen lam rab rdzogs 'du shes te/ / de yi slad du bdag gi chos dkar rnams/ / myur du rdzogs par 'gyur zhes tshim par gyur; ;
“I constantly perceive the kalyāṇamitras As the complete path to omniscience. Therefore they will be made content By my quickly perfecting all good qualities.[1646] {9}
I always think of spiritual friends As fulfillers of the path of omniscience; Therefore I think by serving them all, Good can be quickly developed.
de slad 'di las don kun rab tu 'byung / / dge ba'i yon tan ldan pa grub par gyur/ / brjod pa mtha' yas thams cad mkhyen pa'i lam/ / 'di ni yongs su bsgrubs shing 'gro la brjod/ /
“Therefore, from this come all benefits And the accomplishment of good qualities. I shall accomplish this path to omniscience And proclaim it to beings through infinite praises. {10}
All advantages come from that, And achievement of good qualities; Having honored this infinite group, I will tell the world of the path of all knowledge.
yon tan tshad med khyod ni slob dpon gyur/ / thams cad mkhyen gyi chos la bdag 'dren pa/ / bskal pa bye ba khrag khrig grangs med pas; ; 'phags ma khyod la bdag gis lan mi lon/ /
“You are my teacher of immeasurable qualities. You are my guide toward the qualities of omniscience. Āryā, even in countless quintillions of kalpas I will not be able to repay your kindness.” {11}
You are my mentor, of measureless virtue, My guide on the way of omniscience; Even in countless millions of eons I could never thank you enough, O sage.
de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis tshigs su bcad pa de dag smras nas mtshan mo'i lha mo 'gro ba thams cad srung ba'i smon lam la brtson pa'i 'od la 'di skad ces smras so/ /
Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, having recited those verses, said to the night goddess Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā,
Having spoken these verses, Sudhana said to the night goddess,

lha mo/ khyod kyis bdag la byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa'i lus bsam gyis mi khyab pa 'di ni; bstan ni/ lha mo/ rnam par thar pa 'di'i ming ni/ ci zhes bgyi/ lha mo/ khyod ni/ ci srid cig nas bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu zhugs/ ci srid cig na ni/ khyod bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu mngon par 'tshang rgya bar 'gyur/ de skad ces smras pa dang /

“Goddess, if you teach me this inconceivable scope of your bodhisattva liberation, then, goddess, what is the name of this liberation? Goddess, how long has it been since you entered upon attaining the highest, complete enlightenment? How long will it be before you attain the highest, complete enlightenment of buddhahood?”

“You have shown me the sphere of this inconceivable enlightening liberation; tell me, what is this liberation called? How long ago did you set out for supreme perfect enlightenment? When will you realize supreme perfect enlightenment?”
mtshan mo'i lha mo 'gro ba thams cad srung ba'i smon lam la brtson pa'i 'od kyis tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la 'di skad ces smras so/ /
The night goddess Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā said to Sudhana, the head merchant’s son,
The goddess replied,
rigs kyi bu/ rnam par thar pa 'di ni/ sems can thams cad yongs su smin par bya ba la yang dag par skul ba'i dge ba'i rtsa ba yongs su 'byung ba zhes bya ba ste/
“Noble one, this liberation is called the origin of the roots of merit that inspire the ripening of all beings.
“This liberation is called ‘made of roots of goodness fostering the development of all beings.’

rigs kyi bu/ kho mo rnam par thar pa 'di dang ldan pas chos thams cad kyi rang bzhin mnyam pa nyid khong du chud do/ / chos thams cad kyi ngo bo nyid la zhugs nas gnas med pa'i chos la brten te 'jig rten thams cad las 'phags par gyur to; ;

Noble one, through possessing this liberation, having realized the equal nature of all phenomena, having comprehended the nature of all phenomena, and having relied on the Dharma that has no location, I have risen above all worlds,
Imbued with this liberation, realizing the equality of the essence of all things, comprehending the nature of all things, going to refuge in the independent state, passing away from all worlds,
chos rnams kyi gzugs shin tu rnam par phye ba la zhugs te
understood the differentiation of the forms of all phenomena, and,
comprehending the differentiations in forms of things
mi 'dra ba med pa'i kha dog dang / sna tshogs med pa'i kha dog dang / rnam pa tha dad pa med pa'i kha dog dang / mi rtog pa'i kha dog dang /
understanding the true nature that has no distinct color, no variation of color, no separate aspect of color, no concept of color,
yet realizing the nature of things is without difference, without variation or distinction in appearance,
mi sngo ba'i kha dog dang / mi ser ba'i kha dog dang / mi dmar ba'i kha dog dang / mi dkar ba'i kha dog dang /
no blue color, no yellow color, no red color, no white color,
not blue, yellow, red, or white,
mi mthun pa med pa dang / sna tshogs med pa dang / rnam pa tha dad pa med pa dang / rtog pa med pa dang /
no dissimilarities, no variety, no different aspects, no concepts,
I manifest different bodies, of many appearances— of varying appearance, of nonvarying, undifferentiated appearance,
mi sngo ba dang / mi ser ba dang / mi dmar ba dang / mi dkar ba'i kha dog gi chos nyid la zhugs nas
no blue, no yellow, no red, and no white colors,[1647]
neither colored nor colorless,
kha dog rnam par phye ba du ma'i gzugs kyi lus sna tshogs kyi kha dog can/ kha dog du ma dang / kha dog tshad med pa dang /
of many appearances, infinite appearances,
kha dog rnam par dag pa dang / rgyan thams cad 'byin pa'i kha dog dang / kun tu snang ba'i kha dog dang / 'gro ba thams cad dang 'dra ba'i kha dog dang /
pure appearance, appearing to emanate all sorts of supernal manifestations, appearing to be visible everywhere, appearing to be the same as all beings,

'jig rten thams cad la mngon du gyur cing lhag pa'i kha dog dang / gzugs brnyan kun tu snang ba'i kha dog dang / mi mthun pa med pa'i kha dog dang / mtshan dang dpe byad bzang pos rnam par sbyangs pa'i kha dog dang /
transcendent appearance manifest to all beings, appearance of light reflected everywhere, nonoffensive appearance, appearance beautified with the marks and embellishments of greatness,

kha na ma tho ba med par spyod pa'i 'od dang ldan pa'i kha dog dang / stobs chen pos rnam par gnon pa yongs su ston pa'i kha dog dang / zab mo thob par dka' ba'i kha dog dang / 'jig rten thams cad kyis mi thub pa'i kha dog dang /
appearance resplendent with impeccable behavior, appearance manifesting the exertion of great power, appearance of unapproachable profundity,

'gro ba thams cad kyi tshig gis mi zad pa'i kha dog dang / skad cig re re la sna tshogs su 'gyur ba'i kha dog dang / kha dog gi sprin sna tshogs yongs su ston pa'i kha dog dang / gzugs dang dbyibs sna tshogs kyi kha dog dang /
appearance unsurpassed in all worlds, appearance varying from moment to moment, appearance manifesting multitudes of different forms, appearance of various physical forms,

rnam par 'phrul pa tshad med pa ston pa'i kha dog dang / shin tu yid du 'ong zhing rnam par snang ba'i kha dog dang / bzang po dang mdzes pa thams cad 'bel ba'i kha dog dang / sems can thams cad yongs su smin par bya ba dang mthun pa'i kha dog dang /
appearance manifesting infinite miraculous displays, appearance as an eloquent speaker, appearance of all beautiful forms, appearance adapted to development of all beings,

bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du 'dul ba la mngon du 'gyur ba'i dge ba'i kha dog dang / thogs pa med par kun tu snang ba'i kha dog dang / dang zhing rnyog pa med la rnam par gsal te 'od dang ba'i kha dog dang /
appearance of consummate good manifest to those who are teachable according to their mentalities, appearance reflected everywhere without obstruction, pure, untainted, serene, radiant appearance,
mi shigs pa'i lus kyis bsgrubs pas mdzes par gyur pa'i kha dog dang /
healthy, beautiful appearance of an indestructible body,
chos kyi tshul bsam gyis mi khyab pa rab tu ston pa'i kha dog dang /
colors that manifest countless ways of the Dharma;
appearance of cultivation of inconceivable spiritual methods,
zil gyis ma non la zil gyis gnon pas thams cad zil du rlag par byed pa'i kha dog dang /
unsurpassable colors that surpass and overwhelm all;
superlative appearance overwhelming all,
mun pa dang rab rib med pa'i kha dog dang /
colors that have no darkness or dimness;
appearance without darkness or obscurity,
mun pa thams cad rnam par sel ba'i kha dog dang /
appearance dispelling all darkness,

dkar po thams cad shin tu bsgrubs pa'i kha dog dang / bdag nyid che ba'i yon tan rgya mtsho'i kha dog dang / sngon bla ma la rim gror byas pas shin tu bsgrubs pa'i kha dog dang / lhag pa'i bsam pa nam mkha' yongs su dag par byed pa'i kha dog dang /

appearance imbued with all good qualities, appearance of an ocean of virtues of a great soul, appearance attained by honoring the worthy in the past, appearance of supreme vastness of a mind clear as the sky,
mchog dam pa phul du byung bar shin tu yangs pa'i kha dog dang /
colors that are perfect, sublime, wonderful, and vast;[1649]
mi 'phrog mi zad pa'i yon tan rgya mtsho rab tu ston pa'i kha dog dang /
colors that manifest an ocean of insuperable, inexhaustible qualities;
appearance revealing an ocean of indestructible, inexhaustible virtues,
'jig rten thams cad la mi gnas shing ma 'dres pa'i kha dog dang /
colors that do not dwell in and are not mixed in with the world;
appearance free from all worldly attachments,
thogs pa med par phyogs thams cad rgyas par 'gengs pa'i kha dog dang /
colors that pervade all directions without impediment;
appearance freely pervading everywhere,
sems kyi skad cig 'byams klas pa la zhing rgya mtsho brjod du med par kha dog sna tshogs rnam pa du ma yongs su ston pa'i kha dog dang /
colors that manifest the numerous varieties of the colors of the vast extent of countless realms in each instant;
appearance instantly manifesting a multitude of different appearances in untold myriads of realms,
sems can thams cad kyi dga' ba'i shugs chen po rnam par 'phel bar byed pa'i kha dog dang /
colors that increase the great power of joy in all beings;
appearance increasing floods of great joy in all sentient beings,

sems can rgya mtsho thams cad yongs su sdud pa'i kha dog dang / ba spu'i sgo thams cad na sangs rgyas kyi yon tan rgya mtsho ma lus pa'i sprin gyi sgra sgrog pa'i kha dog dang / sems can thams cad kyi bsam pa dang mos pa rgya mtsho rnam par sbyong ba'i kha dog dang / chos thams cad kyi don rnam par gdon mi za ba yongs su ston pa'i kha dog dang /

appearance to protect all beings, appearance emanating multitudes of manifestations of all virtues of buddhahood from every pore, appearance purifying the wills and aspirations of all sentient beings, appearance showing determination of the meanings of all spiritual teachings,

'od zer gyi dra ba'i dkyil 'khor kha dog sna tshogs su snang ba'i kha dog dang / nam mkha' ltar dri ma med par snang ba'i kha dog dang / rin po che'i rgyal po rnam par dag pa ltar rdul gyi dri ma med pa'i 'od la gnas pa'i kha dog dang / chos nyid dri ma med pa'i 'od kyi kha dog dang /

appearance radiating a network of varicolored lights, appearance of pure light as vast as the sky, appearance contained in the light of the untainted essence of pure jewels, appearance reflecting the undefiled real nature of things,

kha dog dpag tu med pa'i tshul rgya mtsho rnam pa tha dad pa yongs su ston pa'i kha dog dang / phyogs kun tu snang bar byed pa'i kha dog dang / dus la gang du bab par 'gro ba yongs su ston pa ma 'dres pa'i kha dog dang / zhi ba dang dul ba'i phyogs las byung ba'i kha dog dang /

incomparable appearance, appearance reflecting the variety of the ocean of means of liberation, appearance of ubiquitous light, appearance manifest to the world according to the time without fragmentation, appearance originating in the realm of tranquillity and restraint,

nyon mongs pa thams cad rab tu zhi bar byed pa'i kha dog dang / 'gro ba bsod nams kyi zhing thams cad la rab tu ston pa'i kha dog dang / 'jigs pa thams cad rab tu sel ba'i kha dog dang / don yod par 'gro ba rgyas par 'gengs pa'i kha dog dang /
appearance quelling all afflictions, appearance revealing a field of blessing for all sentient beings, appearance producing calm by all means, appearance fruitfully manifest throughout the world,

ye shes kyi rnam par gnon pa chen po rab tu brjod pa'i kha dog dang / chags pa med pa'i lus kyis kun tu rgyas par 'gengs pa'i kha dog dang / lus dam pa'i sprin gyi dbyangs kyis 'gro ba kun tu ston par byed pa'i kha dog dang / byams pa'i rgya mtsho chen po yongs su sdud pa'i kha dog dang /

appearance revealing the exertion of great knowledge, appearance of an unobstructed all-pervasive body, appearance of a universally supreme body manifest in ways beneficial to all beings, appearance embodying an ocean of great love,

bsod nams kyi ri rab chen po yongs su sgrub pa'i kha dog dang / 'gro ba thams cad du mi gnas kyang 'jig rten gyi rgyud thams cad du gzugs brnyan 'byung ba'i kha dog dang / ye shes kyi stobs chen po rnam par sbyong ba'i kha dog dang / 'jig rten thams cad kyi rjes su dran pa dang 'grogs pa'i kha dog dang /

appearance embodying a mountain of great virtue, appearance reflected in all states of being while independent of all worlds, appearance purifying the power of great knowledge, appearance coexisting with the memory of all worlds and beings,

rin po che thams cad lta bu'i kha dog dang / rnam par snang ba'i snying po ltar yongs su ston pa'i kha dog dang / 'gro ba thams cad kyi mos pa'i tshul dang mthun pa'i kha dog dang / thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi rnam pa la mngon du gyur pa'i kha dog dang /
appearance of light of all jewels, appearance showing the matrix of the source of light, appearance corresponding to the faith of all beings, appearance actualizing expression of all knowledge,

mig 'dzum gyis rgyas pas 'gro ba mos par byed pa'i kha dog dang / rin po che'i rgyan dam pa'i 'od kyi kha dog dang / 'gro ba thams cad du thogs pa med pa la phyir phyogs pa med pa'i kha dog dang / nges pa med cing mngon par zhen pa med pa'i kha dog dang /

appearance with laughing eyes cheering the world, appearance of light of the finest arrays of all jewels, appearance without grasping yet not turning away from sentient beings, unfixed, uninvolved appearance,
byin gyi rlabs kyis rnam par 'phrul pa'i khyu mchog gi mthu 'byin pa yongs su ston pa'i kha dog dang /
colors that manifest the rising of the power of the supremacy of manifestations through blessings;
appearance manifesting mystical powers,

rdzu 'phrul thams cad kyis rnam par 'phrul ba'i khyu mchog gi mthu phyung ba yongs su ston pa'i kha dog dang / de bzhin gshegs pa'i dge ba'i rtsa ba snang bar byed pa'i kha dog dang / chos kyi dbyings kha na ma tho ba med pa'i tshul rgya mtsho la rab tu zhugs pa'i kha dog dang / sangs rgyas thams cad kyi 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor du phyin pa'i gzugs brnyan 'byung ba'i kha dog dang /

appearance showing all kinds of miracles, appearance of revealing the roots of goodness of the enlightened, impeccable appearance arising from the ocean of principles of all realms of reality, appearance as reflections going to the assemblies of all buddhas,

kha dog sna tshogs rab tu sgrub pa'i kha dog dang / legs par spyad pa dang / rgyu mthun pa bzang pos byung ba'i kha dog dang / 'dul ba ji lta ba bzhin du nye bar sgrub pa'i kha dog dang / 'jig rten thams cad kyis blta na mi ngoms pa'i kha dog dang /
appearance perfecting all kinds of forms, appearance resulting from good action, appearance adapted to guide those to be taught, appearance that all beings never tire of seeing,
'od dang ba rnam pa sna tshogs kyi 'od du snang ba'i kha dog dang /
colors that shine with pure light in the form of lights of many colors;
appearance radiating multicolored lights,

dus gsum gyi kha dog rgya mtsho thams cad yongs su ston pa'i kha dog dang / 'od zer kha dog thams cad dang ldan pa rgya mtsho rab tu 'gyed pa'i kha dog dang / 'od kyi dkyil 'khor rgya mtsho kha dog brjod du med pa sna tshogs rnam pa tha dad pa yongs su ston pa'i kha dog dang / spos thams cad kyi 'od 'phro ba kun las 'das pa'i kha dog dang /

appearance showing the ocean of forms of past, present, and future, appearance radiating lights of all colors, inexpressible appearance, appearance showing a variety of meanings in halos of light, appearance transcending all worlds,
ba spu'i sgo re re nas sangs rgyas kyi zhing brjod du med pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi nyi ma'i dkyil 'khor gyi sprin yongs su ston pa'i kha dog dang /
colors from each pore that manifest clouds of sun disks that are as numerous as the atoms in countless buddha realms;
appearance manifesting as many suns as atoms in untold buddha-lands in each pore,
zla ba'i dkyil 'khor gyi gzugs dri ma med cing yangs pa'i sprin gyi byin gyi rlabs kyi kha dog dang /
colors that have the blessing of vast clouds of the stainless forms of the disks of the moon;
appearance magically producing multitudes of forms like the clear moon,
me tog yid du 'ong ba'i ri rab kyi sprin mtha' yas pa rab tu 'gyed pa'i kha dog dang /
colors that spread infinite clouds of Sumerus of beautiful flowers;
appearance emanating multitudes of mountains of flowers of infinite colors,
phreng ba sna tshogs mngon par sgrub pa'i shing gi sprin phreng ba/ thams cad kyi char rab tu 'bebs pa'i kha dog dang /
colors that send down rain from cloud banks of trees created from various garlands;
appearance emanating garlands of all kinds of adornments,
rin po che thams cad kyi pad+mo'i sprin yongs su ston pa'i kha dog dang /
colors that manifest clouds of lotuses made of all jewels;
appearance manifesting multitudes of lotuses of all jewels,
spos dang bdug spos thams cad kyi na bun gyi gzugs kyi sprin gyis chos kyi dbyings thams cad rgyas par 'grengs pa'i kha dog tu
and colors that spread clouds formed from the mist of all perfumes and incenses throughout the entire realm of phenomena,
appearance filling all universes with clouds of incense of all fragrances;

sems kyi skad cig re re la phye ma'i mdzod kyi sprin thams cad byin gyis brlabs shing phyogs bcur chos kyi dbyings kyi tshul rgya mtsho thams cad rgyas par bkang nas mthong bas 'dul ba'i sems can rnams dang /

[1654] which in each instant of mind are blessed as clouds of all treasures of powders and pervade throughout the ten directions of the ocean of the ways of the entire realm of phenomena, and through having acquired the blessing of the tathāgatas I manifest to beings who are guided through seeing,

in each moment of consciousness producing clouds of treasuries of all kinds of fragrant powders and pervading all universes in the ten directions, I show all this to sentient beings who can be guided by seeing,
thos pas 'dul ba dang / rjes su dran pas 'dul ba dang / chos kyi 'khor lo sprul pa mngon par sgrub pas 'dul ba dang / yongs su smin par 'gyur ba'i dus la bab pas 'dul bar 'gyur ba dang /
who are guided through hearing, who are guided through remembering, who are guided through creating emanations of Dharma wheels, who are guided through the time having come for their ripening,
those who can be guided by hearing, those who can be guided by remembering, those who can be guided by production of emanations of teaching cycles, those who can be guided when the time is ripe,
gzugs kyi lus yongs su bstan pas 'dul ba dang / bsnyen bkur bya bas 'dul ba dang / khong du chud par bya bas 'dul ba dang / rnam par 'phrul ba dang /

who are guided through the manifestation of form bodies, who are guided through acts of veneration, who are guided through realization, who are guided through manifesting various miracles and emanations,

those who can be guided by seeing physical bodies, those who can be guided by service, those who can be guided by comprehension, those who can be guided by manifestation of various miraculous effects,

chos 'phrul sna tshogs yongs su bstan pas 'dul ba dang / rnam par 'phrul pa dang / chos 'phrul bsam gyis mi khyab pa rnam par dmigs pa yongs su bstan pas 'dul ba'i sems can rnams kyi bsam pa'i dbang dang / dus kyi dbang dang / mi dge ba'i las las rnam par bzlog pa'i dbang dang /

and who are guided through manifesting the perception of countless miracles and emanations, through the power of their aspirations, the power of the time, the power of turning them away from bad actions,
those who can be guided by manifestation of inconceivable miraculous effects, by mastery of minds, by mastery of timing, by mastery of prevention of evil deeds,

dge ba'i las yongs su sgrub pa la so sor dgod pa'i dbang dang / sngon smon lam chen po mngon par bsgrubs pa'i dbang dang / thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi shugs kyi dbang dang / byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa rgya chen po'i rnam par 'phrul pa rab tu thob pa'i chos kyi dbang dang /

the power of establishing them in the accomplishment of good actions, the power of accomplishing the karma of great prayers of the past, the power of the might of omniscience, the power of the qualities of attaining the miraculous manifestations of vast bodhisattva liberations,

by mastery of promotion of good deeds, by mastery of accomplishment of past great vows, by mastery of momentum toward omniscience, by mastery of the means of attainment of the immense miracles of the liberations of enlightening beings,
'gro ba thams cad yongs su bskyab pa shin tu sgrub pa'i snying rje chen po'i stobs yongs su 'byung ba'i dbang dang /
the power of the arising of the strength of great compassion that creates a refuge for all beings,
by mastery of the source of power of great compassion accomplishing the salvation of all beings,
byams pa chen po'i rgya mtsho rnam par dag pa yongs su skyed pa'i bsam pa'i dbang gis de bzhin gshegs pa'i byin gyi rlabs yang dag par blang ba'i phyir rab tu 'jug go /
and the power of the aspiration that creates a pure ocean of great love.
by mastery of the will producing purity of the ocean of great love, empowered by the enlightened.

rigs kyi bu/ de ltar kho mos byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa sems can thams cad yongs su smin par bya bas bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du dge ba'i rtsa ba la yang dag par bskul ba la rab tu gnas te/ rnam par dbye ba med pa'i chos la zhugs nas mtha' dang dbus med pa'i lus kyi kha dog dang dbyibs yongs su bstan te/ spyod pa'i lus re re las mtha' dang dbus med pa'i kha dog rgya mtsho 'jig rten du rnam par dmigs par byas te spyod pa'i kha dog re re las mtha' dang dbus med pa'i 'od zer gyi spring yongs su bkye zhing / 'od zer re re las kyang sangs rgyas kyi zhing gi gzugs brnyan mtha' dang dbus med pa yongs su bstan nas sangs rgyas kyi zhing re rer yang de bzhin gshegs pa 'byung ba mtha' dang dbus med pa yongs su bstan te/ de bzhin gshegs pa re re zhing yang sangs rgyas kyi rnam par 'phrul pa mtha' dang dbus med pa yongs su ston pa byed cing / sngon gyi dge ba'i rtsa ba yang dag par skul ba byed do/ / dge ba'i rtsa ba ma bskyed pa rnams kyang yongs su skyed do/ / bskyed pa rnams kyang yangs par byed do/ / dge ba'i rtsa ba yangs par byas pa rnams ni/ rnam par 'phel bar byed de/

“Noble one, in that way I am established in this bodhisattva liberation called the origin of the roots of merit that inspire the ripening of all beings, and comprehending the true nature of phenomena[1655] to be without division, I manifest the shapes and colors of bodies without limit or center, and from each manifested body come the perceptions within worlds of an endless and centerless ocean of colors, and from each manifested color clouds of light rays without limit or center are radiated, and from each light ray the images of buddha realms without limit or center are manifested, and in each buddha realm tathāgatas without limit or center are manifested, and each tathāgata manifests buddha miracles without limit or center, and thus I inspire those who have[1656] past roots of merit, and I cause those who have not generated roots of merit to generate them, those who have generated them to increase them, and those who have increased them to make them vast.

“Thus, based on this enlightening liberation, fostering roots of goodness according to sentient beings’ mentalities for their development, realizing the undifferentiated essence of reality, manifesting an infinite variety of physical forms, projecting visions of an infinite variety of multitudes of appearances from each body representing practices, radiating an infinite variety of multitudes of light beams from each appearance of action, showing reflections of buddha-lands, showing infinite buddhas emerging from each beam of light in each buddha-land, showing the infinite variety of projections of each buddha, I vivify past roots of goodness, develop new roots of goodness, increase existing roots of goodness, and enhance developed roots of goodness;
kho mo ni/ sems kyi skad cig re re la yang sems can gyi khams mtha' dang dbus med pa bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub las phyir mi ldog pa'i sa la rab tu dgod par byed do/ /
“In each instant of mind, I establish realms of beings without limit or center on the level of irreversible progress toward the highest, complete enlightenment.
and in each mental moment I establish infinite beings in the stage of nonregression, where they will not retreat, advancing toward supreme perfect enlightenment.
shin tu rgyas par chen po'i mdo; sangs rgyas pa po che zhes bya ba las/ sdong pos brgyan pa'i le'u ste/ ` bam po brgya lnga pa/

rigs kyi bu/ gzhan yang khyod kyis 'di skad du smras te/ khyod bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu zhugs nas ni/ ji srid cig lon/ bskal pa brgya phrag ji snyed cig nas ni/ byang chub kyi spyod pa la spyod ces zer ba de'i don kyang sangs rgyas kyi byin gyi rlabs kyis bstan par bya'o/ /

“Moreover, noble one, you asked, ‘How long has it been since you entered upon attaining the highest, complete enlightenment? For how many hundreds of kalpas have you been practicing bodhisattva conduct?’ Through the blessing of the buddhas I will teach you the answer.
“Also, you ask how long ago I set out for supreme perfect enlightenment, and how many eons I have been carrying out enlightening practice. I will tell you this, too, by the power of Buddha.

rigs kyi bu/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi ye shes kyi dkyil 'khor ni/ rtog pa dang rnam par rtog pa'i yul dang ldan pa ste/ de la 'khor ba ring ba'am/ 'khor ba thung bar rnam par dgod cing brjod par bya ba med do/ / bskal pa kun nas nyon mongs pa'am/ bskal pa rnam par dag pa'am/ bskal pa chung ba'am/ bskal pa che ba'am/ bskal pa mang ba'am/ bskal pa tha dad pa'am/ bskal pa rnam pa sna tshogs su bya ba'am/ bskal pa rnam pa tha dad par bya bar yang rnam par dgod pa dang / brjod par bya ba med do/ /

“Noble one, the domain of wisdom of the bodhisattvas is a field of perception without thoughts, concepts, or assumptions.[1657] There is no[1658] establishment or description of saṃsāra as being long or being short. There is no establishment or description of defiled kalpas, pure kalpas, short kalpas, great kalpas, numerous kalpas, differing kalpas, a variety of kalpas, or irregular[1659] kalpas.

“The sphere of knowledge of enlightening beings is not in the realm of thought, conception, or imagination. It cannot be known in terms of length or brevity of life, or in terms of defilement or purity of ages, or in terms of brevity or length of ages, or in terms of multitude or variety of ages, or in terms of variation or differentiation of ages.

de ci'i phyir zhe na/ rigs kyi bu/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi ye shes kyi dkyil 'khor ni/ rang bzhin gyi ngo bo nyid kyis yongs su dag pa ste/ 'du shes kyi dra ba thams cad dang bral bar sgrib pa'i ri thams cad las yang dag par 'das pa'i bsam pa la yongs su 'char te/ de'ang sems can thams cad yongs su smin par bya ba'i dus su 'dul ba ji lta ba bzhin du snang bar byed do/ /

“Why is that? Noble one, the domain of wisdom of the bodhisattvas naturally has a completely pure nature, is free of all nets of conceptualization, has transcended all the mountains of obscurations, and, arising in their aspirations, illuminates all beings whom it is time to ripen and guide accordingly.

Why? Because the sphere of knowledge of enlightening beings is utterly pure in its essential nature, it is outside the net of all conceptions, it is beyond the mountains of all obstructions. It appears in the mind and sheds light on beings who can be guided, according to their mentalities, when the time is ripe for their development.

rigs kyi bu/ 'di lta ste/ nyi ma'i dkyil 'khor la nyin mtshan gyi grangs su bya ba med de mi srid kyang nyi ma'i dkyil 'khor nub na ni/ nub mor snang ngo/ / nyi ma'i dkyil 'khor shar na ni/ nyin par du snang zhing brjod pa yod do/ /

“Noble one, it is like this: the disk of the sun itself has no enumeration of and does not exist as days and nights, but when it sets, that is perceived as sunset,[1660] and when the disk of the sun rises, that is said to be daytime.
“It is like the sun: there is no reckoning of day and night on the sun, but when the sun has gone down that is known as the night, and when it has come up that is known as the day.

rigs kyi bu; de bzhin du byang chub sems dpa'i ye shes kyi dkyil 'khor rnam par rtog pa med pa la rtog pa dang / yongs su rtog pa thams cad med de/ 'khor ba na gnas pa'i 'du shes kyi rnam pa thams cad dang dus su bya ba thams cad kyang med mod kyi/ 'on kyang byang chub sems dpa'i bsam pa las byung ba'i ye shes kyi dkyil 'khor rnam par rtog pa med pa ni/ sems can thams cad yongs su smin par bya ba'i dus kyi dbang gis bskal par gnas pa dang / 'khor ba'i 'du shes kyi rnam par bgrang ba'i grangs su bgrang ba yin te/ ye shes kyi dkyil 'khor rnam par rtog pa med pa la sngon gyi mtha' dang / phyi ma'i bskal par gnas pa'i 'du shes kyi rnam par bgrang ba yod do/ /

“Noble one, in that way, in the domain of wisdom of the bodhisattvas there are no thoughts, concepts, or assumptions; there are also no perceptions of residing in saṃsāra and no division into times. However, through the power of the time for ripening all beings, that domain of wisdom without concepts that arises from the aspiration of the bodhisattvas has the enumeration of numbers concerning the duration of kalpas and the perceptions of saṃsāra. There is the enumeration of the duration of past and future kalpas in the conceptless domain of wisdom.

In the same way, in the nonconceptual sphere of knowledge of enlightening beings there are no thoughts or conceptions of imaginations, or notions of cycle or duration or time frames: but when the will of enlightening beings arises, then by the light of the sphere of nonconceptual knowledge, and by mastery of timing in development of all sentient beings, conceptual calculations of ages, duration, and cycles are distinguished; in the sphere of nonconceptual knowledge, conceptual calculations of passage of time in past and future ages are distinguished.

rigs kyi bu/ 'di lta ste; dper na/ nyi ma'i dkyil 'khor ni/ nam mkha'i dbyings la 'dug kyang rin po che'i ri thams cad dang / rin po che'i shing thams cad dang / rin po che'i snod thams cad dang / rin po che'i 'byung gnas thams cad dang / rgya mtsho thams cad dang / mtsho dang mtshe'u thams cad dang / chu dang ba'i snod thams cad dang / 'gro ba thams cad kyi sems la gzugs brnyan rnam par dmigs pa snang ste/ sems can thams cad la mngon du gyur bar snang ngo/ / rin po che thams cad kyi rdul shin tu phra ba rnams la nyi ma'i dkyil 'khor gyi gzugs brnyan byung bar snang yang nyi ma'i dkyil 'khor de ni/ rin po che'i ri rnams la yang gnas pa med do/ / rin po che'i shing nas rin po che'i rdul shin tu phra ba rnams kyi bar du'ang zhugs pa med/ rin po che'i 'bru rnams kyi khongs su chud pa'ang ma yin/ rin po che'i 'byung gnas rnams kyi rjes su song ba'ang ma yin/ rgya mtsho rnams kyi nang du song ba'ang ma yin/ chu'i snod thams cad kyi nang du zhugs pa'ang ma yin mod kyi/ thams cad kyi khongs na 'dug par yang snang ngo/ /

“Noble one, it is like the analogy of the disk of the sun in the realm of space, which appears as a perceived image on all jewel mountains, all jewel trees, all jewel vessels, all jewel quarries, all oceans, all lakes and ponds, in all bowls of water, and to all beings. It appears as a direct perception for all beings. The image of the disk of the sun appears in the atoms of all jewels, but the disk of the sun is not present in the mountains of jewels, does not enter the jewel trees, and so on, up to atoms of jewels, is not contained within precious stones, does not come to jewel quarries, does not enter oceans, and does not go into bowls of water, yet it appears within them.

“It is like the orb of the sun in the sky: it is perceived reflected in all jewel mountains, in all jewel trees, in all jewels, in all jewel treasuries, in all oceans, in all springs and streams, in all vessels of clear water, and in the minds of all beings; it appears to all beings, and is seen reflected in each particle of all the jewels—the sun does not originate in the jewel mountains, does not enter the jewel trees or particles, is not in the crystals, does not come to the jewel treasuries, does not enter the oceans, does not enter any bodies of water—yet it is seen within them all.

rigs kyi bu/ de bzhin du byang chub sems dpa' sems dpa' chen po yang 'khor ba'i rgya mtsho las ni/ gyen du 'phags/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i chos kyi dbyings kyi nam mkha' la ni/ mngon par byung / chos kyi rang bzhin nam mkha'i rgyud la ni/ rgyu zhing spyod/ zhi ba'i nam mkha'i dbyings la ni/ gnas par gyur mod kyi/ srid pa'i lam gyi rgyud dang / skye gnas thams cad du'ang sems can thams cad yongs su smin par bya ba dang gdul ba'i don du sems can thams cad dang 'dra ba'i lus su skye bar snang ste/ 'khor ba'i nyes pas gos par mi 'gyur ro/ / skyed dang shi 'pho ba'i sdug bsngal gyis nye bar gdung ba med do/ / rtog pa dang rnam par rtog pa dag dang 'grogs pa med do/ / bskal pa la'ang ring ba'i 'du shes sam thung ba'i 'du shes su 'gyur ba med do/ /

“Noble one, in that same way, bodhisattva mahāsattvas have risen high above the ocean of saṃsāra and are in the sky of the realm of Dharma of the tathāgatas, active within the field of activity that is the sky of the nature of phenomena, and dwell in the realm of the sky of peace. However, in order to ripen and guide all beings in all the paths of existence and births, they appear in bodies that are the same as those of all beings, but without being stained by the faults of saṃsāra, without being accompanied by thoughts and concepts, without the perception of a kalpa being long, and without the perception of a kalpa being short.

In the same way a great enlightening being, leaving the ocean of existence, risen into the sky of the reality realm of the enlightened, dwelling in the realm of the sky of the essence of things, abiding in the sky of peace, is seen in all realms of existence in forms similar to all sentient beings, for the development and civilization of sentient beings: yet the enlightening being is not stained by the ills of the mundane whirl, is not burnt by the suffering of death and birth, does not live by concepts and imaginations, and has no notion of length or brevity of the age.

de ci'i phyir zhe na; de ni/ byang chub sems dpa' phyin ci log las shin tu 'das pa dang / 'du shes dang / sems dang / lta ba'i phyin ci log las yongs su 'das pa dang / rmi lam lta bu'i 'jig rten thams cad yang dag pa ji lta ba bzhin du ye shes kyis khong du chud pa dang / sgyu ma lta bu'i 'jig rten thams cad rab tu rtogs pa dang / sems can med pa'i ye shes kyi dbyings rab tu thob pa dang / yang dag pa ji lta ba bzhin du chos rab tu mthong bas snying rje'i dkyil 'khor shin tu yangs pa dang / smon lam chen po'i stobs kyis sems can thams cad yongs su smin par bya ba dang / gdul ba'i don du sems can thams cad la mngon du gyur par snang ngo/ /

“Why is that? Because bodhisattvas have transcended error, have transcended erroneous perception, mentation, and views, have comprehend all worlds to be like dreams, realize all worlds to be like magical conjurations, have attained the realm of the wisdom that there are no beings, view all phenomena exactly as they truly are, and, through the power of the vast domain of compassion and of great prayers, appear to all beings in order to ripen and guide all beings.

Why? The enlightening being is ultimately beyond all errors of mistaken conceptions, thoughts, and views, sees with accurate knowledge of all worlds as dreamlike, realizes all worlds are like magic, has attained knowledge of the realm devoid of beings, sees things as they are, and yet by control of great vows of the sphere of vast compassion appears to all sentient beings to guide them to perfection.

rigs kyi bu/ 'di lta ste/ dper na/ chu klung chen po la sogs pa la gru ni/ rtag tu rgyun mi 'chad par sems can yongs su bsgral ba la brtson pa ste/ nam ma zhig gi bar du rgyun gcod pa med kyang de la pha rol gyi ngogs la mngon par chags pa med/ tshu rol gyi ngogs la'ang chags pa med/ chu'i dbus na'ang gnas pa med do/ /

“Noble one, it is like the analogy of a ship on a great river, and so on, which is continuously engaged in ferrying beings across. It does not stay at the opposite shore, it does not stay at the near shore, and it does not remain in between.
“Just as a boatman is always at work on the rivers to ferry people over, never ceasing, all his life never dwelling on the near shore or on the farther shore, and not remaining in midstream either,

rigs kyi bu/ de bzhin du byang chub sems dpa' yang pha rol tu phyin pa chen po'i gru'i mthus 'khor ba'i chu klung gi rgyud las sems can thams cad yongs su bsgral ba la zhugs pa yin te/ de la tshu rol gyi mus 'jigs pa med do/ pha rol gyi mur bde bar 'gyur ba'i 'du shes med do/ / 'on kyang rtag tu rgyun mi 'chad pa'i byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bskal pa dpag tu med pa thams cad du gnas par bya bar zhe non pas sems can thams cad yongs su bsgral bar bya ba la zhugs pa yin te/ bskal pa'i rnam pa tha dad pa la mngon par zhen pa med do/ / bskal pa 'da' bar bya ba la ring ba'i 'du shes su gyur cing byang chub sems dpa'i spyad pa la spyod pa ma yin no/ /

“Noble one, in the same way, bodhisattvas, through the power of the ship of the great perfections, are engaged in ferrying beings across the flow of the river of saṃsāra, doing so without fear of the near shore and without a conception of the bliss of the far shore. Yet they are continuously engaged in the practice of bringing all beings to liberation while maintaining bodhisattva conduct throughout countless kalpas without attachment to the different kinds of kalpas. They do not practice bodhisattva conduct with the perception that the passing of a kalpa is a long time.

in the same way the enlightening being undertakes to save sentient beings from the current of the mundane whirl by the power of the boat of the transcendent ways; the enlightening being does not fear the near shore, does not think of the farther shore as safety, and yet is always engaged in ferrying sentient beings over. Though the enlightening being enters the variety of ages by persisting in enlightening practice through all ages, beyond measure, yet the enlightening being does not carry on enlightening practice within notions of passage and length of ages.

rigs kyi bu/ 'di lta ste/ dper na/ chos kyi dbyings ltar yangs pa'i nam mkha'i dbyings nam mkha'i gzhi'i dkyil 'khor na 'jig rten gyi khams thams cad 'du 'am/ 'jig gam/ 'das par gyur kyang rnam par rtog pa med cing rang bzhin gyis rnam par dag pa la kun nas nyon mongs pa med de/ 'khrug pa med cing bsgribs pa med la phyi ma'i mtha'i dus su zhing thams cad 'dzin kyang yongs su skyo ba med do/ /

“Noble one, it is like the analogy of the realm of space that is the domain of the sky, the vast realm of phenomena, which though it includes the creation, destruction, and passing of all world realms is without thought and is naturally pure and completely undefiled, undisturbed, unobscured, and unwearied by possessing all realms throughout all future time.

“Just as space, extensive as the cosmos, is without discrimination whether worlds become, decay, or disappear, is by nature pure, undefiled, neither turning back nor tiring, not long or short, eternally supporting all lands,

rigs kyi bu/ de bzhin du byang chub sems dpa'i bsam pa ye shes nam mkha'i dkyil 'khor kyang smon lam chen po'i rlung gi dkyil 'khor gyis kun nas bskor cing ngan song gi g.yang sa thams cad las sems can yongs su 'dzin kyang yongs su skyo ba med do/ / bde ba'i lam la 'god pa byed kyang yongs su sgyid lug pa med do/ / thams cad mkhyen pa'i lam la 'god kyang zhum par byed pa med do/ / nyon mongs pa thams cad kyis kyang 'khrug pa med do/ / 'khor ba'i nyes pa thams cad kyis kyang yongs su gdung ba med do/ /

“Noble one, in the same way, the domain of the space of the wisdom of bodhisattvas’ aspiration, with the revolving of the circle of the wind of great prayers, holds back beings from all the abysses of the lower existences without ever wearying; it brings them onto the path to happiness without being disheartened, brings them onto the path to omniscience without becoming despondent, is undisturbed by any kleśas, and is not afflicted by any of the harms of saṃsāra.

in the same way the space of the will and knowledge of the enlightening being, with the whirlwind of great vows, never tires in keeping sentient beings from falling into all states of misery, has no fear in leading them to the paths of felicity, is not exhausted in setting them on the ways to omniscience, does not follow afflictions, and is not stained by the ills of the mundane whirl.

rigs kyi bu/ 'di lta ste/ dper na/ sgyu ma'i rnam pa las grub pa'i mi yan lag dang nying lag shin tu tshang ba la lus la gnas pa'i chos bcu med de/ bcu gang zhe na; 'di lta ste/ dbugs nang du rgyu ba'am/ dbugs phyir rgyu ba'am/ grang ba'am/ dro ba'am/ bkres pa'am/ skom pa'am/ dga' ba'am/ mi dga' ba'am/ skye ba dang / rga ba dang / na ba dang / 'chi ba'am/ gnod par 'gyur ba med do/ /

“Noble one, it is like the analogy of a man, with all the larger and smaller parts of the body complete, who is a magical conjuration and in whose body ten qualities are absent. What are those ten? They are (1) inhalation, (2) exhalation, (3) cold, (4) warmth, (5) hunger, (6) thirst, (7) happiness, (8) unhappiness, (9) birth, aging, sickness, and death,[1661] and (10) injury.

“Just as a magically produced man has all his limbs and body parts but lacks ten physical elements—inhalation and exhalation, coolness and warmth, hunger and thirst, joy and sorrow, the pains of birth, old age, sickness, and death—

rigs kyi bu/ de bzhin du byang chub sems dpa' ye shes kyi sgyu ma'i rnam pa las byung ba'i gzugs dang ldan pa/ chos kyi dbyings tha mi dad pa'i lus dang ldan pa/ srid pa'i lam gyi rgyud thams cad du sems can yongs su smin par byed pa'i don du skyes te

“Noble one, in the same way, bodhisattvas have forms that emerge as the magical conjuration of wisdom; they have bodies that are not separate from the realm of the Dharma, and which are born in order to ripen all beings in the classes of existence within saṃsāra.[1662]
in the same way, in the enlightening being whose form is born of the magic of knowledge, whose body is one with the cosmos, who appears in all states of existence to perfect sentient beings,

bskal pa thams cad du gnas pa la'ang chos bcu med de/ bcu gang zhe na/ 'di ltar 'khor ba la mngon par dga' ba'am/ 'khor ba srid pa'i lam gyi rgyud du skye bas skyo bar 'gyur ba'am/ yul gyi dga' ba la 'dun pa'am/ khong khro ba'i sems sam/ longs spyad par 'dod pa'am/ nyon mongs pa thams cad kyis yongs su gdung ba'am/ sdug bsngal gyi tshor ba nyams su myong ba'am/ lam nyam nga bar skye bas 'jigs pa'am/ srid par mngon par 'dun pa'am/ mngon par chags pa med do/ /

“Although they are present in all kalpas, there are ten qualities that they do not have. “What are those ten? They are (1) delight in saṃsāra, (2) sadness on being reborn within a class of existence within saṃsāra, (3) dedication to the pleasures of the senses, (4) an angry mind, (5) desire for enjoyments, (6) being afflicted by all the kleśas, (7) experiencing the sensation of suffering, (8) fear through being born in frightening existences, (9) yearning for an existence, and (10) clinging to an existence.

who lives through all ages, ten things are not to be found: desire for the mundane world, rejection of life in the mundane, currying of enjoyment of objects, malevolence, desire for enjoyment, the burning of afflictions, experiences of painful feelings, fear of difficult situations, desire for existence, and attachment.

'on kyang rigs kyi bu/ sangs rgyas kyi byin gyi rlabs kyis ma 'ongs pa'i byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi byang chub sems dpa'i smon lam rgya chen po'i stobs rnam par 'phel bar bya ba'i phyir bstan par bya'o/ /
“However, noble one, I shall also teach, through the blessing of the buddhas, in order to increase the power of the vast bodhisattva prayers of future bodhisattvas.
“I will tell you more, by the power of Buddha, to increase the power of vows of enlightening beings of the future.

rigs kyi bu/ sngon 'das pa'i dus bskal pa 'jig rten gyi khams rgya mtsho'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi pha rol de'i yang pha snga 'das par gyur pa de'i tshe de'i dus na 'jig rten gyi khams rin po che'i 'od ces bya ba zhig byung ste/

“Noble one, in the past, in times gone by, beyond as many kalpas as there are atoms in an ocean of world realms, and even further beyond, there was at that time, in that time, a world realm called Ratnaprabhā.
“In the very remote past there was a world called Jewel Light.
rigs kyi bu/ 'jig rten gyi khams rin po che'i 'od de la bskal pa ni/ 'od bzang po zhes bya ba byung ngo/ / bskal pa 'od bzang po zhes bya ba de la ni/ sangs rgyas stong phrag bcu byung bar gyur te/
“Noble one, in that world realm called Ratnaprabhā there was kalpa called Suprabha. In that kalpa called Suprabha there appeared ten thousand buddhas.
In that world was an age called Beautiful Light. In that age ten thousand buddhas appeared.

rigs kyi bu/ sangs rgyas stong phrag bcu po de dag las bskal pa'i dang po la de bzhin gshegs pa dgra bcom pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas chos kyi 'khor lo'i sgra nam mkha'i sprin gyi sgron ma rgyal po zhes bya ba mkhyen pa dang zhabs su ldan pa/ bde bar gshegs pa/ 'jig rten mkhyen pa/ bla na med pa/ skyes bu 'dul ba'i kha lo sgyur ba/ lha dang mi'i ston pa sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das 'jig rten du byung ste/ de thams cad kyi thog ma la bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu mngon par sangs rgyas so/ /

“Noble one, the first of those ten thousand buddhas in that kalpa who appeared in that world was the Tathāgata Arhat Samyaksaṃbuddha Dharmacakranirghoṣagaganameghapradīparāja, who was one with wisdom and conduct,[1663] a sugata, one who knows the world’s beings, an unsurpassable guide who tames beings, a teacher of devas and humans, a buddha, and a bhagavat. He was the first of them all to attain the highest, complete enlightenment of buddhahood.

The first of those buddhas was one called King Illumining Space with the Voice of Truth, who was one of those who has arrived at Thusness, perfectly enlightened, consummate in knowledge and action, arrived at felicity, supreme knower of the world, tamer of humans, teacher of humans and gods, a blessed buddha.

rigs kyi bu/ de bzhin gshegs pa de gling bzhi pa'i dbus na rgyal po'i gnas dga' bas brgyan pa zhes bya ba yod pa dang tshad du'ang rgyang mi ring ba zhig tu byung ste/ rgyal po'i gnas dga' bas brgyan pa de'i shar phyogs logs na nags tshal 'od bzang po zhes bya ba zhig yod de/ nags tshal 'od bzang po der snying po byang chub rin po che'i me tog gi sprin ces bya ba byung ngo/ / snying po byang chub rin po che'i sprin ces bya ba der gdan seng+ge'i khri rin po che rnam par snang ba'i snying po can byung ste/ de la bcom ldan 'das de bzhin gshegs pa chos kyi 'khor lo'i sgra nam mkha'i sprin gyi sgron ma rgyal po bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu mngon par sangs rgyas so/ /

“Noble one, that tathāgata appeared not far from the royal capital named Rativyūhā in the central four-continent world. To the east of the royal capital Rativyūhā, there was a forest called Suprabha. In Suprabha Forest there was a bodhimaṇḍa called Ratnakusumamegha. At that bodhimaṇḍa called Ratnakusumamegha there appeared a lion throne on which there was a shining jewel lotus.[1664] It was upon this that the Tathāgata Arhat Samyaksaṃbuddha Dharmacakranirghoṣagaganameghapradīparāja attained the highest, complete enlightenment of buddhahood.

“That buddha appeared not far from a capital city called Array of Delights, in the middle of the four continents of the world. East of that city was a forest called Beautiful Light, in which there was an enlightenment site called Cloud of Jewel Flowers. At that site a lion throne in the calyx of a lotus of radiant jewels appeared, and this is where that buddha realized supreme perfect enlightenment.

de'i tshe mi'i tshe'i tshad lo stong phrag bcu thub pa las 'jig rten du sems can srog gcod pa dang / ma byin par len pa dang / 'dod pas log par g.yem pa dang / brdzun du smra ba dang / phra ma zer ba dang / zhe gcod pa'i tshig smra ba dang / tshig kyal ba zer ba dang / chags sems dang ldan pa dang / gnod sems yod pa dang / log par lta ba can byung ste/ de ltar mi dge ba'i las kyi lam bcu rnam par rgyas par gyur nas rab tu brtan par gyur te/

“At that time, in that time, the lifespan of humans was ten thousand years, but there occurred killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, lying, slander, harsh speech, meaningless talk, avariciousness, maliciousness, and wrong views, and in that way the path of the ten bad actions became widespread and enduring.

“At that time the human life span was ten thousand years. Now, there being many who were set in evil ways—killing, stealing, raping, lying, foul and harsh in speaking, divisive, covetous, malicious, and deluded—

bcom ldan 'das de bzhin gshegs pa chos kyi 'khor lo'i sgra nam mkha'i sprin gyi sgron ma rgyal po des 'jig rten gyi dbang po sngon gyi rgyal ba la bya ba byas pa rnams dang / 'dzam bu'i gling gi mi rnams kyi dge ba'i rtsa ba yongs su smin par bya ba'i phyir snying po byang chub mchog tu gshegs te byang chub sems dpa' rnams la chos bstan to/ /

“The Bhagavat Dharmacakranirghoṣagaganameghapradīparāja remained[1665] at the bodhimaṇḍa, teaching the Dharma to bodhisattvas,[1666] in order to ripen the roots of merit of the lords of the world and Jambudvīpa humans who had served past jinas.

the buddha sat at the site of enlightenment for a full thousand years and taught enlightening beings, world leaders, and people who had served past buddhas, in order to mature people’s existing roots of good.

de'i tshe rgyal po'i gnas dga' bas brgyan pa de na rgyal po rgyal ba'i 'od ces bya ba 'dug 'dug ste/ des mi ma byin par len pa/ rku ba/ sdig to byed pa/ srog gcod pa/ 'dod pas log par g.yem pa/ rdzun zer ba/ phra ma smra ba/ zhe gcod pa'i tshig dang ldan pa/ tshig kyal pa smra ba/ chags sems can/ gnod sems yod pa/ log par lta ba/ chos ma yin pa'i 'dod chags la zhen pa/ 'dod pa mi bzad pas mngon par non pa/ log pa'i chos kyi kun nas 'khor ba/ sdig to byed byed pa/ khro gtum byed byed pa/ bsod nams ma byas pa/ 'jigs pas bag tsha ba med pa/ mar mi shes pa/ phar mi shes pa/ dge sbyong du bya ba med pa/ bram zer bya ba med pa/ tshul mi shes pa/ g.yo dang ldan pa brgya stong du ma rab tu gdul bar bya ba'i phyir btson rar btsud par gyur to; ;

“At that time, in that time, in the royal capital Rativyūhā, there lived King Jayaprabha, who in order to subdue them imprisoned many hundreds of thousands of people who had stolen, robbed, performed criminal acts, killed, performed sexual misconduct, lied, slandered, spoken harshly, and talked meaninglessly, who were avaricious, were malicious, held wrong views, were attached to desires contrary to the Dharma, were overwhelmed by irresistible desires, were encompassed by wrong Dharma, and who committed sinful actions, acted wrathfully, did not create merit, did not save[1667] those who were in fear, did not respect their mothers, did not respect their fathers, were not reverential to mendicants, were not reverential to brahmins, were not respectful of āryas,[1668] and committed transgressions.

“At that time there was a king called Victorious Light in that capital city Array of Delights. He had thrown many hundreds of thousands of criminals and evildoers into prison to discipline them—thieves, killers, rapists, liars, abusive and violent people, troublemakers, greedy people, malicious people, people obsessed with aberrant ideas, people addicted to unlawful pleasures, people overcome by desire for ill-gotten gains, people involved in false cults, evildoers, people who had committed violence, people who had done no good, people who had neglected to come to the aid of those in danger and fear, people without respect for their parents or for mendicants, priests, and holy people.

rgyal po rgyal ba'i 'od de la bu gzugs bzang ba/ shin tu mdzes pa/ blta na sdug pa/ kha dog bzang po dam pa rgyas pa dang ldan pa/ mi chen po'i mtshan nyi shu rtsa brgyad dang ldan pa rnam par rgyal ba zhes bya ba zhig yod pa de khang pa glu snyan pa'i dbyangs zhes bya ba'i steng du phyin te bud med kyi 'khor mang pos yongs su bskor cing 'dug 'dug pa las btson ra na 'khod pa'i sems can mtshon cha sna tshogs kyis dmad du glags pa de dag gi sgra 'jigs 'jigs skad du 'bod pa thos par gyur to/ / thos nas mi dga' zhing shin tu nyams mi bde ba'i sems su gyur te/ snying rje chen po skyes nas khang steng de nas shod du babs te/ btson ra der phyin nas btson ra dam po na 'khod pa'i sems can shing sgrog dang / lcags sgrog dang / khong sgril dang / ltung dang mdo rtod kyis sgrog shing brtod de gcig gi lus dang gcig tu sbrel nas mun pa mun nag tu btsud de dud pa'i rab rib kyis 'grigs shing rlung nad nyams su mi bde bas nyam thag par gyur pa/ dbugs shin tu mi bde bar rgyu ba/ bkres pa dang skom pas mnar ba/ sgren mo gos med pa/ lus thams cad phyag dar dang rdul gyi nang na 'gre ba/ lus rang gi skras yog pa/ brla sgril gyis dam du bcings pa/ nyon mongs pa sna tshogs kyis mtho brtsams pa/ sdug bsngal gyi tshor bas zil gyis mnan cing sdug bsngal nyams su myong bar gyur te/ mi bzad pa sna tshogs kyi smre sngags bla zhing 'o dod 'bod pa

“King Jayaprabha had a son whose name was Vijitāvin. He was handsome, attractive, a delight to see, and he had a very beautiful, perfect, magnificent complexion. He had twenty-eight of the signs of a great being. He went up on the roof of the palace called Sarasvatisaṃgīti, where he stayed, encircled by an entourage of many women. He heard the terrified cries of the beings who had been put into prison and were tightly bound by various instruments. On hearing them he became unhappy, and his mind was not at ease. Great compassion arose in him, and he descended from the roof of the palace. He entered the prison and inside that strict prison saw the beings who in darkness were imprisoned, bound in wooden stocks, chains, manacles, and fetters and chained one to another. It was thick with blinding smoke, and they were stricken by unpleasant sickening air, breathing with difficulty, tormented by hunger and thirst, and naked, without clothes, their bodies entirely covered in dirt and dust, their bodies covered by their own hair, their thighs tightly bound together; they were overwhelmed by a sensation of the suffering of a series of various torments, and in their suffering they cried out with unendurable wailing and screams.

“The king had a son named Conqueror, who had twenty-eight of the marks of a great man, and lived in the palace surrounded by many graceful women. He heard the frightful cries of those who were bound up in prison; agitated and upset by these cries, moved with compassion, he left the palace and went into the prison, where he saw those people cast into the dungeons, bound by all sorts of fetters and shackles, chained together and thrown into the darkness, shrouded in smoke, exposed to unhealthy drafts, emaciated, hungry and thirsty, naked and homeless, filthy and unkempt, being subjected to various tortures, screaming in pain.

de dag mthong nas snying rje chen po skyes te/ snying rje'i bsam pa rgya chen po byung nas gzhan la phan par bya ba'i sems skyes te btson ra thibs po na 'khod pa'i sems can rnams btson ra nas thar par bya'o/ /zhes dbugs bton nas des sems can de dag la mi 'jigs pa byin te

“When he saw this, a great compassion arose in him along with a motivation to help others. He reassured them, saying, ‘I will free from prison all those who have been placed in the darkness of this prison,’ thus giving them the gift of freedom from fear.

“Seeing the prisoners, the prince was inspired with great compassion and an unprecedented determination to help others. He comforted the prisoners, intending to deliver them from their bonds. Giving them assurance,

rgyal po rgyal ba'i 'od gang na ba der song ste 'di skad ces gsol to/ / lha'i zhal snga nas mkhyen pa mdzad du gsol/ btson ra mi bde ba na mchis pa'i sems can rnams la glo ba rje nas bdag gis mi 'jigs pa stsal na/ de dag dgye bar ci gnang zhes nas

“He went to King Jayaprabha and said to him, ‘Your Majesty, I request your attention. Taking pity on those beings who are in the unhappiness of being imprisoned, I have given them the assurance of freedom from fear. Please release them.’
he went to the king and said, ‘Know, O king, that I have given assurance to the people in prison. Please set them free.’
de nas rgyal po rgyal ba'i 'od kyis blon po lnga brgya po bsags nas khyed ji snyam du sems zhes smras pa dang /
“King Jayaprabha gathered together his five hundred ministers and asked them, ‘What do you think?’ [1669]
“The king called his five hundred ministers together and asked them what they thought about this.

de dag gis smras pa/ btson 'di rnams ni/ rgyal po'i phyag mdzod rku ba/ rgyal po'i sku la dar ba/ btsun mo'i 'khor du zhugs pa las bzung ba sha stag ste/ de dag ni/ mi 'gum du'ang mi rung / de dag gi chad pa ni/ 'gum pas 'bra bar bas ste/ ma lags na'ang btson rar gum na/ chad pa 'bra lags grang / de dag gi mgon su bgyid pa de'ang rgyal po'i zhal sngar glo ba ring ngo/ /

“They said, ‘All these prisoners have stolen from the king’s treasuries, have attempted to harm the king, have trespassed into your harem, and so on. They should be executed. Their punishment should be execution or to die in chains. Someone who undertakes to help them is committing a crime against the king.’[1670]

They said, ‘These people are plunderers of the royal treasuries, attackers of the king, arrested entering the royal palace; they should be executed. Furthermore, anyone who wants to save them is also guilty of crime against the king.’
