de nas rgyal po'i bu rnam par rgyal ba'i snying rje chen pos mi bzod ches nas blon po de dag la smras pa/ khyed kyis ji skad du smra ba de ltar yang rung ste/ ngas khong ta 'di dag gi don du sdug bsngal nyams su blang ba thams cad kyang bzod par bya na/ de dag la khyed kyis ci bya ba de nga la gyis te nyes pa can de dag khye zhig /ngas de rnams btson ra nas dgrol ba'i don du mi bde ba thams cad nyams su blang ste lus dang / srog yongs su dor bar bya'o/ /

“Prince Vijitāvin, giving rise[1671] to an overwhelming compassion, said to those ministers, ‘Let it be as you have just said. I will endure all their experiences of suffering for their sake. Do to me whatever you would do to them and set them free! I will undergo every kind of unhappiness in order to free them from prison. I will even give up my body and life.

“The prince, overwhelmed with great compassion, said to those ministers, ‘Let it be as you say. Just release these convicts—I can endure all pains for their sake. Whatever you would do to them, do to me. To free them from bondage I will undergo all kinds of torture and give up my body and life.

de ci'i phyir zhe na/ gal te ngas sems can 'di rnams tsam zhig kyang btson ra nas dgrol bar ma nus na/ khams gsum pa'i btson ra na 'khod pa'i sems can sred pa'i zhags pas glags pa/ ma rig pa'i thibs po na 'khod pa/ gti mug gi mun par btsud pa/ phongs pa'i sdug bsngal gyis mnar ba/ ngan song gi rgyud zabs su ring zhing 'byung bar dka' bar chud pa/ dbyibs mi sdug la mdog mi sdug pa dang ldan pa/ dbang po'i sbyor ba thams cad dang bral ba/ nor ba'i yid dang ldan pa/ 'byung ba mi mthong ba/ snang ba med pa/ khams gsum pa la mngon par zhen pa/ bsod nams dang ye shes kyi tshogs med pa/ ye shes kyi skye mched dang skol ba/ nyon mongs pa sna tshogs kyis sems dri ma can du gyur pa/ sdug bsngal gyi shing thags kyis 'khor ba/ bdud kyi dbang du gyur pa/ skye ba dang / rga ba dang / na ba dang / 'chi ba dang / mya ngan dang / smre sngags 'don pa dang / sdug bsngal ba dang / yid mi bde ba dang / 'khrug pas mnar ba rnams kyang ji ltar khrol bar bya zhes nas

Why is that? If I am unable to free even these beings from prison, how would I be able to liberate beings who are imprisoned in the three realms, who are bound by the noose of craving, who are within the darkness of ignorance, who have been cast into the darkness of stupidity, who are tormented by the suffering of poverty, who are distressed in the deep abyss of the lower existences, whose bodies have unpleasant shapes and ugly color, who are lacking in the functioning of the senses, who have bewildered minds, who do not see a way out of saṃsāra, who are devoid of light, who cling to the three realms, who lack the accumulations of merit and wisdom, who are deprived of a basis for wisdom, whose minds are stained by various kleśas, who are trapped in an enclosure of suffering, who are under the power of Māra, and who are tormented by birth, aging, sickness, death, misery, wailing, suffering, unhappiness, and tribulation?’

Why? If I cannot liberate these people from bondage, how can I liberate those who are bound to the world, who are tied up by the ropes of craving, who are in the abyss of ignorance, who are cast into the darkness of delusion, who suffer the pains of poverty, who have fallen into the depths of evil ways, who act senselessly, whose minds are confused, who see no way to emancipation, who are without illumination, who are attached to the world, who lack virtue and knowledge, who have lost their faculties of knowledge, whose minds are tainted with various afflictions, who are flung in the mud of suffering, who are under the control of demons, who are tormented by birth, old age, death, grief, lamentation, misery, depression, and sorrow?’

rgyal po gzhon nu rnam par rgyal bas btson ra na 'khod pa'i sems can de dag bdag nyid yongs su gtang ba dang / rnam pa thams cad du yongs su gtang bas g.yog 'khor thams cad dang / nor gyi phung po thams cad kyis blus te btson ra de dag nas yongs su bkye nas sems can de dag gi sdug bsngal nyams su blangs te phyir ldog pa med par gyur to/ /

“Prince Vijitāvin could not be dissuaded from freeing those imprisoned beings by offering up himself, by offering everything, and by ransoming them with his entourage and all his accumulation of wealth, and then taking on the suffering of those beings.
“Then the prince released all those prisoners from their bonds, by giving up himself, his whole retinue, and all his wealth. Freeing them, he removed all that was torturing them once and for all.

de nas blon po lnga brgya po de dag gis lag pa gyen du bsgreng ste 'o dod bos nas rgyal po rgyal ba'i 'od kyi gan du dong ste 'di skad ces smras so/ / rgyal po'i zhal snga nas mkhyen par mdzad du gsol/ gzhon nu rnam par rgyal ba'i mchid thabs su bgyis pas rgyal po'i chab srid kyang stor bar 'gyur/ bdag cag rnams kyang srog la 'bab par the tshom 'tshal te/ lha'i zhal snga nas rgyal po gzhon nu rnam par rgyal ba la bka' nan ma mdzad na ni/ ring po'ang mi thogs par lha'i zhal sngar sku la dar bar 'gyur ro/ / zhes pa dang /

“Then the five hundred ministers, wailing with their arms upraised, went to King Jayaprabha and said to him, ‘Your Majesty, we request attention. Prince Vijitāvin’s plans will destroy the kingdom![1672] We are even concerned for our own lives! If Your Majesty does not restrain the prince, before long Your Majesty’s life will be taken from you!’

At that point the five hundred ministers, up in arms, went to the king and said, ‘Know that the law of the king has been broken by the will of the prince, and all of our lives are uncertain. If you do not punish the prince, your own life will not last long.’
de nas rgyal po rgyal ba'i 'od shin tu khros nas rgyal po'i bu rnam par rgyal ba dang / g.yon dang ldan pa'i mi de dag tu bcas te gsad par byas so/ /
“Then King Jayaprabha became angry and condemned to death Prince Vijitāvin and all those people who were criminals.
“The king, enraged, set out to kill his son and those convicts as well.

de nas de'i ma skyed skyed pas thos nas mi dga' ste/ bud med kyi 'khor stong dang bcas te skra ni/ bshig /lus kyi rgyan ni/ bor/ rang gi bzhin ni/ dral/ brang ni/ rdung / mgo ni/ phyag dar gyis gang bar snying rje rje skad kyi nga ror du zhing rgyal po'i drung du phyin nas 'khor dang bcas pas rkang pa gnyis la phyag byas te 'di skad du gsol ba btab bo/ / lha'i zhal snga nas thugs ci dgongs/ rgyal po gzhon nu rnam par rgyal ba gtang du gsol/ rgyal po gzhon nu rnam par rgyal ba'i srog stsal du gsol zhes nas

“When his birth mother heard this, she was distressed and, with her entourage of a thousand women with their hair in disarray, their jewelry cast aside, and their faces scratched, beating their breasts, with their heads covered with dirt, and wailing with piteous cries, came into the presence of the king, and she and her entourage bowed down at his feet and made this supplication: ‘Your Majesty, listen to our plea! Free Prince Vijitāvin! Spare the life of Prince Vijitāvin!’

The queen, hearing of this, was very upset: her hair undone, her jewelry and makeup removed, she went to the king with a thousand of her ladies, beating her breast and throwing dust on her head, weeping and wailing; she said to him, ‘Let the prince go free, let him live.’

de nas rgyal pos rgyal po gzhon nu rnam par rgyal ba mdun du bzhag ste 'di skad ces smras so/ / gzhon nu/ g.yon dang ldan pa'i mi 'di rnams thong / de ste mi gtong zhing de rnams kyi le lan du shi bar gyur ta re zhes pa dang /
“Then the king had Prince Vijitāvin brought before him and said to him, ‘Prince, abandon those people who are criminals! If you do not abandon them, you will be executed in their stead!’
The king turned to the prince and said, ‘Give up on these criminals. If you do not, you will die for their sake.’
des zhum pa med pa'i sems ma 'khums pa/ thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du dmigs par brtson pa/ gzhan la phan par gzhol ba/ snying rje chen po sngon du 'gro bas 'chi bar khas blangs pa dang /

“The prince was not disheartened or discouraged but was engaged in attaining the goal of omniscience, was dedicated to benefiting others, was led in all his actions by compassion, and accepted his death.
“The prince, facing death, was not fazed, being focused on omniscience, dedicated to the welfare of others, guided by great compassion.

de'i mas rgyal po rgyal ba'i 'od la zla ba phyed cig tu phrad par gsol ba btab pa/ dgung zla phyed cig tu gzhon nu 'di sbyin pa stsol du ci gnang / de slan chad ni; su ci dgyes pa de'ang mdzad par gsol zhes pa dang / de de ltar gyis shig /ces rgyal pos gnang ngo/ /

“His mother requested King Jayaprabha to give him half a month, saying, ‘I request that this prince be allowed to perform acts of charity for half a month, and after that you may do as you wish.’ “The king gave his permission, saying, ‘Let it be so!’

The queen, his mother, asked the king to allow a fortnight for observation: ‘Let the prince give people whatever they need for half a month; then do whatever you want with him.’ The king agreed to this.

de nas rgyal po'i gnas dga' bas brgyan pa de'i byang phyogs logs shig na sngon mchod sbyin gyi gnas su bya ba'i bza' shing gi ra ba chen po nyi ma'i 'od ces bya ba der gzhon nu de song nas su ci 'dod pa de la de byin te/ des gtan pa med pa'i mchod sbyin byas nas zla ba phyed du sbyin pa rnam pa sna tshogs byin no/ / zas 'dod pa la ni/ zas byin/ skom 'dod pa la ni/ skom byin/ bzhon pa dang / gos dang / me tog dang / byug pa dang / phye ma dang / chos gos dang / gdugs dang / rgyal mtshan dang / ba dan dang / rin po che'i rgyan dang / yo byad thams cad dang / lhab lhub thams cad dang / yo byad kyi rnam pa thams cad kyang de dag 'dod pa la yongs su btang ste/

“The prince went to the great park called Sūryaprabha, which was to the north of Rativyūhā, the royal capital, and was the traditional location for offerings and acts of charity. There the prince gave anyone whatever they wanted, making unconditional offerings and gifts of every kind for half a month. He gave food to those who wanted food, gave drink to those who wanted drink, and likewise gave steeds, clothes, flowers, powders, ointments, Dharma robes, parasols, banners, flags, precious jewelry,[1673] all ornaments, and every kind of necessity that was wished for.

“North of the city there was a large park called Sunlight that had been made in the past as a sacrificial ground. The prince went there and gave to anyone who asked whatever they needed. Thus for half a month he freely gave away various goods—food, clothing, utensils, and so on—to whoever needed them.

de nas nyi ma tha ma la bab par gyur pa dang 'gro ba mang po'i tshogs kun nas 'dus te/ rgyal po'i blon po dang / bud med kyi tshogs dang / tshong dpon dang / khyim bdag dang / ljongs dang yul gyi mi dang zhags pa thub pa thams cad kyang kun nas 'dus/

“When the last day arrived, an assembly of many[1674] beings gathered. The king’s ministers, the group of queens, the head merchants, the householders, the people of the land, and the Jains assembled.
“Then, on the last day of the fortnight, the whole population gathered—

bcom ldan 'das chos kyi 'khor lo'i sgra nam mkha'i sprin gyi sgron ma rgyal po de bzhin gshegs pa de yang sems can yongs su smin par bya ba dang / gdul ba'i dus thugs su chud nas mchod sbyin gyi gnas der gshegs te lha'i dbang po'i tshogs kyis ni/ yongs su bskor; klu'i dbang pos ni/ yang dag par mchod/ gnod sbyin gyi dbang pos ni/ lus mngon par btud/ dri za'i dbang pos ni/ mngon par bstod/ lha ma yin gyi dbang pos ni/ lus shin tu btud/ nam mkha' lding gi dbang po gtsug gi rin po ches rnam par brgyan pas ni/ sems dang ba'i mchod pa'i rnam pas rab tu bkang / mi'am ci'i dbang po rnams kyis ni/ dga' bas yongs su mchod de bstod pa'i glu dbyangs kyis yongs su bskul/ lto 'phye chen po'i dbang po rnams kyis ni/ kun nas bskor cing zhal du blta ba de

“The Bhagavat, the Tathāgata Dharmacakranirghoṣagaganameghapradīparāja, knowing it was the time to guide and ripen beings, also went to the site of the distribution of gifts. A gathering of lords of the devas was his entourage; lords of the nāgas made offerings to him; lords of the yakṣas were bowing to him; lords of the gandharvas were praising him; lords of the asuras were bowing down to him; lords of the garuḍas, who were adorned by crest jewels, were with delight strewing offerings; lords of the kinnaras made offerings with joy and sang inspirational songs of praise; and lords of the mahoragas encircled him, gazing at his face.

the king, his ministers, his women, the grandees, the landlords, the townspeople, and all the religious impostors. Now the buddha-king Illumining Space with the Voice of Truth, realizing it was an opportune time to teach people, went to that sacrificial ground, respectfully surrounded by celestial and spiritual beings.

'gro ba'i tshogs chen po de dang / rgyal po gzhon nu rnam par rgyal bas bcom ldan 'das de bzhin gshegs pa dgra bcom pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas chos kyi 'khor lo'i sgra nam mkha'i sprin gyi sgron ma rgyal po shin tu mdzes pa/ blta na sdug pa/ dbang po zhi ba/ thugs zhi ba; shin tu dben par dbang po las rgyal ba/ glang po ltar shin tu dul ba/ mtsho ltar rab tu shing gsal la rnyog pa med pa/ sangs rgyas kyi rnam par 'phrul pa dang; cho 'phrul chen po dang / sangs rgyas kyi khyu mchog gi mthu phyung ba chen pos ni/ rnam par mdzes/ sangs rgyas kyi bdag nyid che bas ni/ rab tu 'bar/ sangs rgyas kyi mtshan dang / dpe byad bzang po'i rgyan gyis ni/ sku mdzes par brgyan/ 'jig rten thams cad ni/ sangs rgyas kyi 'od kyi dkyil 'khor snang bas rgyas par 'gengs shing sangs rgyas kyi 'od zer gyis rab tu snang bar mdzad/ sku'i ba spu'i bu ga thams cad nas ni/ spos rin po che'i ngad 'phro ba'i 'khor lo rab tu 'gyed/ sangs rgyas kyi zhing rab tu bskyod pa'i tshul du ni/ 'jig rten gyi khams thams cad yongs su skyob pa mdzad cing rgyan thams cad kyi sprin gyi char rab tu 'bebs pa'i sangs rgyas kyi rnam par gnon pa dang / sems can thams cad kyi nyon mongs pa spong ba'i sangs rgyas kyi spyod lam dang / sems can thams cad kyi dga' ba'i shugs rnam par 'phel bar mdzad pa'i sangs rgyas kyi zhal blta ba'i byin gyis pha zad cig nas tshur gshegs pa mthong nas de bzhin gshegs pa la sems mngon par mos par gyur to/ /

“That great gathering of beings and Prince Vijitāvin saw, approaching from afar, the Bhagavat, the Tathāgata Arhat Samyaksaṃbuddha Dharmacakranirghoṣagaganameghapradīparāja, who was handsome and delightful to look at, with pacified senses and a pacified mind, withdrawn,[1675] victorious over the senses, as tame as an elephant, as pure, clear, and unpolluted as a lake, beautified by buddhahood’s emanations and great miraculous manifestations and by the powerful supremacy of buddhahood, and shining with the greatness of buddhahood. His body was beautifully adorned by the adornments of the physical signs and features of a buddha, and he was filling all worlds with the illumination of a buddha’s halo of light, illuminating with a buddha’s light rays, emanating a field of the spreading aroma of precious perfumes from all his body’s pores, and shaking all world realms in the manner of shaking buddha realms. He was approaching while sending down a rain from a cloud of all adornments, with the prowess of buddhahood, with the conduct of buddhahood that eliminates kleśas within all beings, and through the sight of the buddha’s face increasing the power of joy in all beings, who on seeing the tathāgata gained faith in their minds in the tathāgata.

The crowd of people, and the prince, saw the buddha coming from afar, serene, pleasant to see, senses calm, mind quiet, self-controlled, master of his faculties, tranquil as an elephant, clear as a pool of water, purified, undefiled, miraculously radiating light by the great power of a buddha, overpowering with the mastery of a buddha, shining with the magnificence of a buddha, adorned with the marks and embellishments of a buddha, pervading all worlds with the light of his aura, illuminating them with rays of light, emanating orbs of fragrant jewel fire from every pore, causing all worlds to quake with the quaking of a buddha-land, destroying all beings’ afflictions, coming forth as a buddha raining multitudes of all kinds of supernal manifestations, bearing himself as a buddha, increasing the flow of joy in all beings, conveying the power of the sight of a buddha. Seeing the buddha thus, everyone’s mind became clear and serene.

de nas rgyal po gzhon nu rnam par rgyal ba dang / 'gro ba'i tshogs chen po de dag gis bcom ldan 'das de bzhin gshegs pa chos kyi 'khor lo'i sgra nam mkha'i sprin gyi sgron ma rgyal po de pha zad du bsu nas mos pa'i sems kyis lus thams cad kyis phab ste phyag 'tshal nas zhabs gnyis la spyi bos gtugs te mchod pa rnam pa sna tshogs kyis yang dag par mchod nas tshig 'di skad du brjod do/ / bcom ldan 'das tshur gshegs su gsol/ bde bar gshegs pa tshur gshegs su gsol/ de bzhin gshegs pas bdag cag dgongs so/ / bde bar gshegs pas bdag cag yongs su bzung ngo/ /

“Then Prince Vijitāvin and the great gathering of beings went to greet in the distance the Bhagavat Dharmacakranirghoṣagaganameghapradīparāja, and with faith in him they prostrated with their whole bodies, touching the tops of their heads to his feet. They offered various kinds of offerings to him and said, ‘Come, Bhagavat! Come, Sugata! Tathāgata, pay heed to us! Tathāgata, take us into your care!’

“Then the prince and the people, going out to meet the buddha, their minds clear, prostrated themselves before the buddha, made offerings of many kinds, and said, ‘Welcome, welcome, Blessed One; the Buddha has turned his attention to us, the Buddha has bestowed his favor on us.’
de nas rgyal po gzhon nu rnam par rgyal bas bcom ldan 'das la gdan dam pas bstabs te 'di skad ces gsol to/ / bcom ldan 'das gdan bting ba 'di la bzhugs su gsol zhes nas
“Then Prince Vijitāvin prepared an excellent seat for the Bhagavat and said to him, ‘Bhagavat, I request that you be seated upon this seat that has been arranged for you.’
Then the prince pointed out a seat of honor to the buddha and said, ‘Please sit down, O Blessed One—this seat has been prepared.’

bcom ldan 'das der gshegs pa dang / gdan de yang gtsang sbra lhur len pa'i lus kyi ris su gtogs pa'i lha rnams kyis sangs rgyas kyi byin gyis rin po che spos kyi rgyal po'i pad+mo'i snying po can du byin gyis brlabs nas

“The Bhagavat approached it, and, through the blessing of the buddha, the types of devas who were devoted to cleanliness of the body transformed the seat so that it had in its center a lotus of the king of precious perfumes.
Then, as the buddha approached, the gods of purity, by the power of the buddha, changed it into a calyx of a lotus of fragrant diamonds.

gdan de la bcom ldan 'das chos kyi 'khor lo'i sgra nam mkha'i sprin gyi sgron ma rgyal po de bzhin gshegs pa bzhugs so/ / 'khor gyi stan de dag la byang chub sems dpa' rnams 'khod de/ de'i zhal mthong ma thag tu 'khor de'i sems can thams cad kyang sgrib pa thams cad dang bral te/ nad thams cad kyang zhi bar gyur nas 'phags pa'i chos kyi snod du gyur to/ /

“The Bhagavat, the Tathāgata Dharmacakranirghoṣagaganameghapradīparāja, sat upon that seat, and bodhisattvas sat upon the surrounding seats. The beings of that assembly, as soon as they saw his face, became freed from all obscurations; all their illnesses ceased, and they became vessels for the Dharma of the āryas.

The buddha sat on it, and enlightening beings sat on surrounding seats. As soon as they saw the buddha, everyone in the assembly was relieved of afflictions and obstruction and disturbance, and became fit vessels for the holy teachings.

de nas bcom ldan 'das de bzhin gshegs pa chos kyi 'khor lo'i sgra nam mkha'i sprin gyi sgron ma rgyal pos sems can de dag snod du gyur par thugs su chud nas bstan pa rim pas bka' stsal te/ 'di ltar rgyu'i dkyil 'khor rab tu snang ba zhes bya ba'i mdo sde yang dag par bstan nas zhal gyi sgo nas 'gro ba thams cad kyi skad rgya mtsho dang / des pa'i tshig dang ngag gi dbyangs su brjod pa'i gsung dbyangs kyi yan lag stong dang ldan pa/ chos kyi yan lag thams cad dang ldan pa rab tu bsgrags pa dang;

“Then the Bhagavat, the Tathāgata Dharmacakranirghoṣagaganameghapradīparāja, knowing that those beings had become ready vessels, gave the teachings in stages. He taught the sūtra called The Illumination of the Field of Causes. He spoke through the entire ocean of the languages of beings, definitions, and sounds of the voice, speaking with the thousands of aspects of speech and possessing the thousands of aspects of the Dharma.

“Then the buddha, knowing that those people had become capable of receiving the Teaching, gave them a systematic talk. He expounded to them a scripture called Illumination of the Multitude of Causes, including all elements of the Teaching, which he spoke in the languages of all people.

de'i mod la 'khor de nas srog chags bye ba phrag brgyad cu ni/ rdul dang bral te dri ma med par gyur nas chos la chos kyi mig skyes par gyur to/ / srog chags bye ba mang zhig gis ni/ mi slob pa'i sa thob par gyur to/ / srog chags stong phrag bcu ni/ theg pa chen po la rnam par dul bar gyur te/ 'di ltar byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa kun tu bzang po dang / smon lam chen po yongs su rdzogs pa'i tshul la zhugs par gyur to/ /

“At that moment, eight hundred million beings within that assembly became free of impurities, became stainless, and developed the Dharma vision of the Dharma; many millions of beings attained the state beyond training; and ten thousand beings were guided into the Mahāyāna. Thus they entered into the way of completely good bodhisattva conduct and accomplished great prayers.

At that, eighty million people in that crowd attained dispassionate, pure, objective vision of things. Many millions reached the stage beyond learning. Ten thousand were led to the Great Vehicle, introduced to the way of fulfillment of the great vows of universally good enlightening action.

“When the Bhagavat this time turned the wheel of the Dharma through the great miraculous powers of buddhahood, beings in the ten directions, as numerous as the atoms in a hundred thousand buddha realms, were guided into the Mahāyāna; beings without end or middle throughout the extent of the various worlds and buddha realms were turned away from the lower existences, and beings beyond number were brought onto the path to rebirth in the higher existences.

Thus as the buddha turned the wheel of teaching by the great miraculous power of buddhas, as many beings as atoms in a hundred thousand buddha-lands in the ten directions came to the guidance of the Great Vehicle. An infinite variety of beings in the interrelated buddha-lands in the worlds of the ten directions put an end to evil. Countless beings were established in the way to paradise.

rgyal po gzhon nu rnam par rgyal bas kyang byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa sems can thams cad yongs su smin par bya bas bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du dge ba'i rtsa ba la yang dag par skul ba 'di thob par gyur to/ /
“Prince Vijitāvin also attained this bodhisattva liberation called the origin of the roots of merit that inspire, in accordance with their dispositions, the ripening of all beings.[1676]
And as for the prince, he attained this enlightening liberation made of roots of goodness fostering the perfection of all beings according to their mentalities.

rigs kyi bu/ de la de'i tshe de'i dus na rgyal po gzhon nu rnam par rgyal ba zhes bya ba byung ste/ rang gi lus dang srog yongs su btang nas nor gyi tshogs dang / 'khor thams cad dang / mi'i 'jig rten na 'tsho ba'i bde ba yongs su spangs nas btson ra na 'khod pa'i sems can de dag thar par byas pa/ mchod sbyin chen po gtan pa med pa'i mchod sbyin byed byed pa/ bcom ldan 'das de bzhin gshegs pa dgra bcom pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas chos kyi 'khor lo'i sgra nam mkha'i sprin gyi sgron ma rgyal po de la bsnyen bkur byed byed pa/ de bzhin gshegs pa de'i zhal mthong ba'i mod la bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed de/ byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa sems can thams cad yongs su smin par bya bas bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du dge ba'i rtsa ba la yang dag par skul ba yang thob par gyur pa de gzhan zhig yin pa snyam du sems na ni/ rigs kyi bu/ khyod kyis de ltar mi blta ste kho mo ni/ de'i tshe de'i dus na rgyal po gzhon nu rnam par rgyal ba zhes bya bar gyur to/ /

“Noble one, at that time, in that time, there was the prince named Vijitāvin who gave up his own body and life, his accumulation of wealth, his entire entourage, and the happiness of living in the human world and freed those beings who were in prison, made an unrestricted great distribution of gifts and offerings, honored the Bhagavat, the Tathāgata Arhat Samyaksaṃbuddha Dharmacakranirghoṣagaganameghapradīparāja, and, when he saw the face of that tathāgata, developed the aspiration for the highest complete enlightenment and attained this bodhisattva liberation called the origin of the roots of merit that inspire, in accordance with their dispositions, the ripening of all beings. If you think he was anyone else, noble one, do not see him in that way. At that time, in that time, I was the prince named Vijitāvin.

“Now then, you may think that the prince in that time, who gave up his body and life, his wealth and retinue, and all human pleasures, in order to liberate those people from bondage, was somebody else. Who was it who made that great sacrifice without reservations, who won the favor of the buddha of that time, who resolved to attain perfect enlightenment when he saw the buddha, who attained this enlightening liberation made of roots of goodness fostering the development of all beings according to their mentalities? It was none other than I myself who was that prince in that time.

de ltar kho mo rgyal po gzhon nu rnam par rgyal ba zhes bya par gyur te/ snying rje chen pos rab tu mi dga' zhing 'gro ba thams cad la phan par zhugs te/ khams gsum la mi gnas pa dang / rnam par smin pa'i lan la re ba med pa dang / grags pa dang / snyan pa dang / ming smos pa la mngon par dga' ba med pa dang / bdag la bstod pa med pa dang / gzhan la smod pa med pa dang / dngos po thams cad la mngon par zhen pa med pa dang / sred pa'i 'du shes las gyen du 'phags pa dang / khams gsum pa la mngon par dga' ba med pa dang / 'jig rten gyi yul gyi bde ba las phyir phyogs pa dang / de bzhin gshegs pa'i yul la mngon du gyur pa dang / byang chub sems dpa'i bsam pa rnam par dag pa dang / lhag pa'i bsam pa rdo rje yongs su grub pa dang / 'gro ba thams cad la byams pa chen pos nan tan du byed pa dang / 'gro ba thams cad la snying brtse bas sdug bsngal rnam par zhi bar bya ba la brtson pa dang / de bzhin gshegs pa'i stobs la bsam pa thag pa nas lhag par dmigs pa dang / byang chub sems dpa'i lam yongs su sbyang ba dang / theg pa chen po'i rgyan gyis 'byung ba'i lam rab tu brgyan par bya ba dang / thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi sgo mngon par blta bar bya ba'i tshul gyis de dag de lta bur dka' ba dag kyang byas par gyur to/ /

In that way, I was the prince named Vijitāvin, who became saddened because of great compassion and who engaged in benefiting all beings without any hope of not remaining in the three realms or of having a karmic result in return; without any delight in fame, renown, or a great name; without praise for oneself; without criticizing others; without attachment to anything; having risen above the perceptions of existence; without delighting in the three realms; while turning away from the pleasures of the sensory field of the world, perceiving the field of the tathāgatas, having the pure motivation of the bodhisattvas, having created the thunderbolt of the superior motivation, and dedicated with great love to all beings; through compassion[1677] for all beings undertaking the ending of suffering; with a sincere focus on the strengths of the tathāgatas; and while training in the path of the bodhisattvas, adorning the path that brings forth the displays of the Mahāyāna, and gazing upon the gateway[1678] into omniscience, in that way accomplishing actions that are difficult[1679] to do.

As that prince, overwhelmed by great compassion, set on the welfare of all beings, unattached to the things of the world, desiring only perfection, with no wish for glory, fame, or repute, not elevating myself, not degrading others, unattached to things, without any notion of existents, without desire for anything in the world, material or immaterial, indifferent to the pleasures of the world, attentive to the sphere of the enlightened, purely intent on enlightenment, having developed an indomitable will, benevolent toward all living beings, compassionately resolved to quell the suffering of all beings, intent on the power of the enlightened, purifying the path of enlightenment, preparing the paths of emancipation of the Great Vehicle, contemplating the path to omniscience, I did these difficult deeds.

rigs kyi bu/ kho mos ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa sems can thams cad yongs su smin par bya bas bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du dge ba'i rtsa ba la yang dag par skul ba 'di yun de srid du ring ba zhig nas thob par gyur to/ /

“Noble one, that is how long it has been since I attained this bodhisattva liberation called the origin of the roots of merit that inspire, in accordance with their dispositions, the ripening of all beings.
This is how long ago I attained this liberation.

rigs kyi bu/ de la ji snyam du sems/ de'i tshe de'i dus ni rgyal po rgyal ba'i 'od la log par gsol ba 'debs shing kho mo gsad pa'i phyir gros su gsol ba'i blon po lnga brgya po de rnams gzhan dag cig yin pa snyam du sems na ni/ de ltar mi blta ste/ lhas byin gyis bcom ldan 'das dgrongs pa'i phyir skyes bu lnga brgya bkye ba de dag yin te/

“Noble one, what do you think? If you think that anyone else was at that time, in that time, the five hundred ministers who made a perverse request to King Jayaprabha and gave their counsel so that I would be executed, do not see them in that way. They were the five hundred men sent by Devadatta to assassinate the Bhagavat.
“And who do you think those five hundred ministers were, who unjustly incited the king to execute me? They were none other than five hundred people whom Devadatta incited to kill the Buddha.

de dag kyang bcom ldan 'das kyis ma 'ongs pa'i dus bskal pa ri rab kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed na bskal pa 'od bzang po zhes bya ba zhig la sangs rgyas lnga brgya sangs rgyas kyi zhing gi yon tan dang rgyan sna tshogs dang ldan pa/ rigs dang rgyud sna tshogs su skyes pa/ pha dang ma sna tshogs su smos pa/ skye ba'i rnam par 'phrul ba sna tshogs yongs su ston pa/ mngon par 'byung ba'i rnam par 'phrul pa sna tshogs dang ldan pa/ byang chub kyi shing gi 'od sna tshogs yongs su ston pa/ snying po byang chub sna tshogs su nye bar 'dong ba'i sgo sna tshogs dang ldan pa/ bdud pham pa sna tshogs yongs su ston pa/ mngon par 'tshang rgya ba'i rnam par 'phrul pa sna tshogs yongs su ston pa/ chos kyi 'khor lo rab tu bskor ba'i tshul dang / ming dang / nges pa'i tshig sna tshogs dang ldan pa/ mdo sde'i tshul shin tu bstan pa sna tshogs dang ldan pa/ tshig gi lam dang skad sna tshogs rab tu ston pa/ 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor gyi rgyan sna tshogs dang ldan pa/ 'od kyi dkyil 'khor gyi mthu dang rgyan sna tshogs rab tu 'gyed pa/ tshe'i tshad sna tshogs dang ldan pa/ bstan pa'i byin gyi rlabs sna tshogs dang ldan pa/ bstan pa rnam par dmigs pa sna tshogs dang ldan pa; ming sna tshogs dang ldan pa/ snying rje chen po'i lus su gyur pa sha stag tu 'gyur te/

“The Bhagavat has prophesied that they too will attain the highest, complete enlightenment in a future time, after as many kalpas as there are atoms in Sumeru, in a kalpa called Suprabha, as five hundred buddhas with various qualities and displays of a buddha realm, born into various clans and castes; with mothers and fathers with various names; manifesting various miraculous births; with various miraculous settings forth into homelessness; manifesting various lights from Bodhi trees; having various gateways into going toward bodhimaṇḍas; manifesting various defeats of Māra; manifesting various miraculous attainments of buddhahood; having various ways of turning the Dharma wheel, of terms, and of definitions; teaching various ways of the sūtras; teaching with various kinds of speech and voice; having an array of various assemblies of followers; radiating the various displays and powers[1680] of their halos of light; having various lifespans; having various blessings from their teachings; their teachings having various objectives; having various names; and all having bodies of great compassion.

The Buddha subsequently guided them and foretold their enlightenment, predicting that in the future, after as many eons as atoms in a polar mountain, in an age called Good Light, there would be five hundred buddhas, with buddha-lands of various qualities, born of various races, tribes, and families, showing various miracles at birth, undergoing various spiritual transmutations on leaving society, manifesting various lights at the tree of enlightenment, approaching the pinnacle of enlightenment in various ways, showing various ways of destroying demons, showing various miracles on attainment of enlightenment, articulating various terms for the principles of their teachings, expounding various scriptures, speaking various languages, surrounded by various audiences, emanating various auras of light, having various life spans, their teachings to remain for various lengths of time, their teachings variously circulating, and their names to be various, all embodiments of great compassion.

de dag gi bskal pa'i dang po la de bzhin gshegs pa thugs rje chen po mnga' ba zhes bya ba 'jig rten gyi khams rin chen 'od du bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu mngon par 'tshang rgya'o/ / de'i rjes la 'jig rten gyi khams de nyid du de bzhin gshegs pa gnyis pa 'gro ba thams cad la phan pa'i smon lam zla ba zhes bya ba 'byung ngo/ / de bzhin gshegs pa gsum pa thugs rje chen po'i seng+ge zhes bya ba 'byung ngo/ / de bzhin gshegs pa bzhi pa 'jig rten thams cad la phan pa mdzad pa zhes bya ba 'byung ba nas thams cad kyi tha mar de bzhin gshegs pa sman pa'i rgyal po zhes bya ba 'byung bar 'gyur ro/ /zhes bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu lung bstan to/ /

“The first in that kalpa will be a tathāgata by the name of Mahākāruṇika, who will attain the highest, complete enlightenment of buddhahood in a world realm called Ratnaprabhā. After him, in that same world, there will be the second tathāgata called Sarvajagaddhitapraṇidhānacandra. The third tathāgata will be called Mahākaruṇāsiṃha. The fourth tathāgata will be called Sarvalokahitaiṣin. The last of them all will be a tathāgata called Vaidyarāja.

The first buddha of the age to attain supreme enlightenment in the world Jewel Light would be one named Great Compassionate One, the second would be named Moon of Commitment to the Welfare of All Beings, the third would be Lion of Great Compassion, the fourth would be Desirous of the Welfare of All Beings, and the last one would be Supreme Healer.

rigs kyi bu/ de la ji snyam du sems/ de'i tshe de'i dus na g.yon dang ldan pa'i mi'i rgyal po la snying ring bar gyur te/ kho mos gsod ma mi'i lag tu phyin pa las rang gi lus dang srog yongs su btang ste btson ra de dag nas bkye ba de rnams gzhan dag cig yin pa snyam du sems na ni/ de ltar mi blta ste/ de bzhin gshegs pa log par dad sel la sogs pa bskal pa bzang po pa'i de bzhin gshegs pa rnams dang / de ma yin pa'i byang chub sems dpa' grangs med pa brgya stong phrag bcu dag ste/ bcom ldan 'das de bzhin gshegs pa stobs mtha' yas grags par brjod pa'i dpal yang dag par 'byung ba'i blo gros mthong bar gyur ma thag tu bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed nas da ltar phyogs bcu na byang chub sems dpa'i spyad pa spyod cing byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa sems can thams cad yongs su smin par bya bas bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du dge ba'i rtsa ba la yang dag par bskul ba 'di yang sgom zhing shin tu rgyas par byed pa dag go /

“Noble one, as for the men who were criminals at that time, in that time, who had committed offenses against the king, and whom I freed from imprisonment by going to the executioners and giving up my life and body, if you think that they were anyone else, do not see them in that way. They were the tathāgatas of the Bhadra kalpa, beginning with Krakucchanda, and also countless millions[1681] of bodhisattvas, who upon seeing the Bhagavat, the Tathāgata Anantabalavighuṣṭanirnāditaśrīsaṃbhavamati, developed the aspiration for the highest, complete enlightenment and are now practicing bodhisattva conduct in the ten directions and meditating and increasing this bodhisattva liberation called the origin of the roots of merit that inspire, in accordance with their dispositions, the ripening of all beings.

“Who do you think those criminals of that time were, doomed to die, whom I released from bondage by sacrificing my life? They were none other than the buddhas of the present age, Virtue, beginning with Krakucchanda, and countless millions of other enlightening beings who were inspired to seek enlightenment by seeing the buddha Resolution Born of the Glory of the Proclamation of Endless Power, and are now carrying out enlightenment practice throughout the universe, and are cultivating and extending this enlightening liberation born of roots of goodness aiding the development of all beings according to their mentalities.

rigs kyi bu/ de la ji snyam du sems/ de'i tshe de'i dus na rgyal po rgyal ba'i 'od ces bya ba byung ba de gzhan zhig yin pa snyam du sems na ni/ de ltar mi blta ste/ smra ba chen po bden pa can ni; de'i tshe de'i dus na rgyal po rgyal ba'i 'od ces bya bar gyur to/ /

“Noble one, what do you think? If you think that King Jayaprabha at that time, in that time, was anyone else, do not see him in that way. The great teacher Satyaka was at that time, in that time, King Jayaprabha.
“Who do you think the Victorious Light of that time was? It was none other than the great debater Satyaka.

rigs kyi bu/ de la ji snyam du sems/ de'i dus na rgyal po'i 'khor du gyur pa btsun mo'i 'khor dang / btsun mo'i gnas kyi sgo ba'am/ 'khor na gnas pa'am/ rjes su 'brang ba de dag kyang gzhan dag cig yin pa snyam du sems na ni/ de ltar mi blta ste; zhags pa thub pa stong phrag drug cu po smra ba chen po bden pa can gyi smra ba'i rgyal mtshan yongs su gzung ba'i don du bcom ldan 'das la rgol du 'gro ba'i tshe bcom ldan 'das kyi sbyan sngar blags nas kun kyang zhing sna tshogs kyi rgyan dang / bskal pa sna tshogs dang / ming sna tshogs kyi de bzhin gshegs par 'jig rten du 'byung bar 'gyur ro/ / zhes bcom ldan 'das kyis bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu lung bstan pa dag go /

“Noble one, what do you think? If you think that King Jayaprabha’s retinue of queens in the harem, the sentinels at the harem entrance, and his court and attendants at that time, in that time, were anyone else, do not see them in that way. They were these six thousand Jains whom Satyaka brought before the Bhagavat, who came to debate against the Bhagavat so as to possess the victory banner of teaching, and when they came, the Bhagavat prophesied their attainment of the highest, complete enlightenment, telling them that they would come into a world as tathāgatas with the arrays of various realms, in various kalpas, and with various names.

And who do you think were the retinue and servants of the king, but the sixty thousand philosophers whom Satyaka brought to the buddha to debate and whom the buddha predicted would become enlightened and appear in the world as buddhas, with variously arrayed buddha-lands, in various ages, with various names.

rigs kyi bu/ rgyal po gzhon nu rnam par rgyal ba de pha dang mas gnang nas sems can brtson ra ba de dag yongs su bkrol ba'i 'og tu srid shin tu bde ba dang / nor dang / dbyig rin po che phun sum tshogs ba dag kyang por/ bu dang chung ma dag kyang spangs nas bcom ldan 'das de bzhin gshegs pa chos kyi 'khor lo'i sgra nam mkha'i sprin gyi sgron ma rgyal po'i zham 'bring du rab tu byung ngo/ / rab tu byung nas kyang lo stong phrag lngar tshangs par spyod pa spyad de/

“Noble one, Prince Vijitāvin’s father and mother gave him permission, so that after he freed those beings from prison, he cast aside the pleasure of existence, the good fortune of wealth and precious treasuries, abandoned children and wives, and entered mendicancy under the Bhagavat, the Tathāgata Dharmacakranirghoṣagaganameghapradīparāja. After entering mendicancy he maintained celibacy for five thousand years.

“To continue, the prince, Conqueror, given permission by his parents, after having released the prisoners, gave up his great wealth and family and went to the buddha. For five thousand years thereafter he cultivated spiritual practice,

de'i bar skabs su ting nge 'dzin gyi sgo stong phrag bcu yongs su bsgrubs so/ / gzungs kyi sgo stong phrag bcu'ang rab tu thob bo/ / mngon par shes pa'i tshul stong phrag bcu la'ang rab tu zhugs so/ / byang chub sems dpa'i gter stong phrag bcu'ang rab tu thob bo; ; thams cad mkhyen pa'i shugs stong phrag bcu'ang yongs su skyes so/ / bzod pa'i sgo stong phrag bcu'ang yongs su sbyangs so/ / sems nges par gzhag pa stong phrag bcu'ang mngon par bsgrubs so/ / byang chub sems dpa'i stobs kyi lus stong phrag bcu'ang yongs su spel to/ / byang chub sems dpa'i ye shes kyi sgo stong phrag bcur yang rab tu zhugs so/ / shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa'i tshul stong phrag bcu yang yongs su skyes so/ / sangs rgyas blta ba'i phyogs kyi sgo stong phrag bcu yang mngon du gyur to/ / byang chub sems dpa'i smon lam stong phrag bcu'ang mngon par bsgrubs so/ /

“During that time he accomplished ten thousand gateways into samādhi, he attained ten thousand gateways into the power of mental retention, he entered ten thousand ways of higher cognition, he attained ten thousand bodhisattva treasures,[1682] he developed ten thousand powers of omniscience, he purified ten thousand gateways into patience, he accomplished ten thousand realizations through contemplation, he multiplied ten thousand bodies with the strengths of a bodhisattva, he entered ten thousand gateways into the knowledge of a bodhisattva, he developed ten thousand ways of the perfection of wisdom, he perceived ten thousand gateways for looking at the buddhas in the directions, and he accomplished ten thousand bodhisattva prayers.

during which time he perfected ten thousand concentration methods, attained ten thousand ways of mental command, entered into ten thousand channels of mystic knowledge, attained ten thousand great treasuries of enlightening beings, produced ten thousand currents of momentum toward omniscience, purified ten thousand facets of tolerance, carried out ten thousand contemplations, developed ten thousand bodies of power of enlightening beings, entered ten thousand doors of knowledge of enlightening beings, produced ten thousand ways to transcendent wisdom, became aware of ten thousand channels of conscious vision of thousands of buddhas, and accomplished ten thousand vows of enlightening beings.

de de lta bu'i chos dang ldan pas sems kyi skad cig re re la phyogs bcur sangs rgyas kyi zhing stong phrag bcu yongs su gnon to/ / 'jig rten gyi khams re re zhing yang sems kyi skad cig re re la sangs rgyas stong phrag bcu sngon gyi mtha' dang phyi ma'i mthar rjes su dran no/ / de bzhin gshegs pa de dag gi sangs rgyas kyi sprul pa rgya mtsho stong phrag bcu phyogs bcur gshegs pa de dag kyang mthong zhing shes so/ /

“Possessing such qualities in each instant of mind, he could arrive in ten thousand buddha realms. In each world realm, in each instant of mind, he could remember ten thousand past and future buddhas. He could see and know ten thousand oceans of emanations from each of those buddhas going into the ten directions.

With these realizations, in each mental moment he went to ten thousand buddha-lands in the ten directions, and in each moment of thought remembered ten thousand buddhas past and future in each world; and he perceived ten thousand multitudes of emanations of those buddhas radiating throughout the ten directions.

sems kyi skad cig re re la yang sangs rgyas kyi zhing stong phrag bcur gtogs pa'i sems can 'gro ba'i rgyud sna tshogs su skyes pa shi 'pho zhing skye bar gyur pa mtho ba dang / dma' ba dang / bde 'gro'i lam du phyin pa dang / ngan song gi lam du phyin pa dang / kha dog sdug pa dang / kha dog mi sdug pa las ci bzhin du skyes par gyur pa thams cad kyang mthong bar gyur to/ /

“In each instant of mind, he could see all the beings within those ten thousand buddha realms. He knew their birth into various existences, their passing away and their rebirths, their decline, their ascent, their going on the path to happy existences, their going on the path to lower existences, their having a beautiful color, and their having a bad color,[1683] exactly as they were born.

In each moment of thought he saw all the beings in ten thousand buddha-lands, passing away and coming to life in various states, undeveloped and developed, felicitous and miserable, of good and bad appearance, following their desires;

sems can de dag gi shi 'pho dang skye ba yang khong du chud cing mthong ste/ sems kyi rgyud dang / sems kyi spyod pa dang / sems kyi 'dab 'brel ba dang / bsam pa sna tshogs dang / dbang po rgya mtsho dang / sbyor ba 'byams klas pa dang / las mthar thug pa dang / yongs su smin par bya ba dang / rnam par gdul ba'i dus kyang khong du chud cing mthong ngo/ /

“He saw the passing away and the rebirth of all those beings, and he saw and knew their movements of mind, the conduct of their minds, the continuation of their minds, their various thoughts, their ocean of faculties, the vast extent of their activities, the conclusion of their karma, and the times for ripening and guiding them.

and he understood the passing away and coming to life of those beings, as well as the revolving of their minds, the conduct of their minds, the continuity of their thoughts, the variety of their inclinations, the multitude of their faculties, the courses of their endeavors, their habits of action, and the proper timing to develop and guide them.

rigs kyi bu/ rgyal po gzhon nu de de nas shi 'phos nas kyang 'dzam bu'i gling de nyid du rgyal po'i gnas dga' ba dang ldan par rgyal po de nyid kyi rigs su skyes nas 'khor los bsgyur ba'i rgyal srid thob par gyur to/ / de 'khor los bsgyur ba'i rgyal por gyur pas bcom ldan 'das de bzhin gshegs pa chos kyi 'khor lo'i sgra nam mkha'i sprin gyi sgron ma rgyal po yongs su mya ngan las 'das pa'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa chos kyi nam mkha' la dpal shin tu 'phags pa'i rgyal po bsnyen bkur to/ /

“Noble one, when that prince passed away, he was reborn in the family of that king in the royal capital, Rativyūhā, in that Jambudvīpa, and he succeeded to the sovereignty of a cakravartin king. When he had become a cakravartin king, following the parinirvāṇa of the Bhagavat, the Tathāgata Dharmacakranirghoṣagaganameghapradīparāja, he honored the Tathāgata by the name of Dharmagaganābhyudgataśrīrāja.

“Subsequently the prince passed away from there and was reborn in the same city Array of Delights, in the same royal family, and attained sovereign rulership. As the king, following the demise of the buddha-king Illumining Space with the Voice of Truth, he propitiated a buddha named Glorious King Risen in the Sky of Truth.
de'i 'og tu snying po byang chub de nyid du brgya byin du gyur te/ de bzhin gshegs pa lha dbang snying po zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“After that, he became a Śakra who at the bodhimaṇḍa honored the Tathāgata by the name of Devendragarbha.
After that, at that same enlightenment site, having become a chief god, he propitiated a buddha named Sanctuary of Celestial Rulers.
de'i 'og tu 'jig rten gyi khams de nyid du rab mtshe ma'i lha'i rgyal por gyur te/ de bzhin gshegs pa sa'i dpal ri bo'i gzi brjid ces bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“After that, in that world realm he became a Suyāma king of devas who honored the Tathāgata by the name of Dharaṇīśrīparvatatejas.
After that, in the same world, having become a celestial chief of the heaven of timely portion, he propitiated a buddha named Fiery Energy of the Radiant Mountain of Mental Command.
de'i 'og tu 'jig rten gyi khams de nyid du rab dga' ldan gyi lha'i rgyal por gyur te/ de bzhin gshegs pa chos kyi 'khor lo'i 'od rab tu bsgrags pa'i rgyal po zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“After that, in that world realm he became a Saṃtuṣita king of devas who honored the Tathāgata by the name of Dharmacakraprabhanirghoṣarāja.
After that, having become a celestial chief of the heaven of satisfaction in the same world, he propitiated a buddha named King Proclaiming the Light of the Wheel of the Teaching.
de'i 'og tu 'jig rten gyi khams de nyid du rab 'phrul dga'i lha'i rgyal por gyur te/ de bzhin gshegs pa nam mkha' mdzes pa'i rgyal po zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“After that, in that world realm he became a Sunirmita king of devas who honored the Tathāgata by the name of Gaganakāntarāja.
After that, having become a celestial chief of the heaven of good emanation in the same world, he propitiated a buddha named King Like the Moon in the Sky.
de'i 'og tu 'jig rten gyi khams de nyid du dbang bsgyur gyi lha'i rgyal por gyur te/ de bzhin gshegs pa stobs la thug pa med pa'i dpal zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“After that, in that world realm he became a Vaśavartin king of devas who honored the Tathāgata by the name of Anavamardabalaketu.
After that, having become a celestial chief of the heaven of command of others’ emanations in the same world, he propitiated a buddha named Paragon of Indestructible Power.
de'i 'og tu 'jig rten gyi khams de nyid du lha ma yin gyi dbang por gyur te/ de bzhin gshegs pa chos thams cad kyi 'brug sgra bsgrags pa'i rgyal po zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“After that, in that world realm he became an asura lord who honored the Tathāgata by the name of Sarvadharmanigarjitarāja.
de'i 'og tu 'jig rten gyi khams de nyid du tshangs pa'i dbang por gyur te/ de bzhin gshegs pa chos kyi 'khor lo sprul pa kun tu snang ba'i dbyangs zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“After that, in that world realm he became a Brahmā lord who honored the Tathāgata by the name of Dharmacakranirmāṇasamantapratibhāsanirghoṣa.
After that, having become a chief Brahma god in the same world, he propitiated a buddha called Sound of Projections of the Wheel of Teaching Reflected Everywhere.

rigs kyi bu/ 'jig rten gyi khams rin chen 'od de nyid du bskal ba 'od bzang po de nyid la de bzhin gshegs pa de dag la sogs pa sangs rgyas stong phrag bcu byung ste/ de bzhin gshegs pa de dag thams cad kyang rgyal po gzhon nu rnam par rgyal bas bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Noble one, there were those and the rest of the ten thousand buddhas who appeared in that world realm of Ratnaprabhā during the Suprabha kalpa. Prince Vijitāvin honored all those tathāgatas.
Beginning with these, ten thousand buddhas emerged in the age Beautiful Light in the world Jewel Light, all of whom were propitiated by the prince Conqueror.
rigs kyi bu/ bskal pa 'od bzang po de'i 'og tu bskal pa 'od zer bzang po zhes bya ba byung ste; bskal pa 'od zer bzang po de la yang sangs rgyas stong phrag bcu byung ngo/ /
“Noble one, following that Suprabha kalpa arose the kalpa[1684] called Suraśmi. During that Suraśmi kalpa there were ten thousand buddhas.
“Following that age Beautiful Light was an age called Subtle Light;
kho mo yang bskal pa de la rgyal po blo gros chen po zhes bya ba zhig tu gyur te/ de'i tshe kho mo rgyal por gyur pas de bzhin gshegs pa mtshan gyi dpal ri bo zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“In that kalpa, I became Mahāmati. During the time when I was King Mahāmati, I honored the Tathāgata by the name of Lakṣaṇaśrīparvata.
in that age I was a king called Great Wisdom. As a king, I propitiated a buddha named Glorious Mountain of Marks of Greatness.
de'i 'og tu bskal pa de nyid la khyim bdag cig tu gyur te/ de bzhin gshegs pa phung po yongs su grub pa zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Following that, in that same kalpa, I was a householder and I honored the Tathāgata by the name of Saṃvṛtaskandha.
Next, in the same age, as a householder I propitiated a Buddha named Restrained in Body and Mind.
de'i 'og tu bskal pa de nyid la blon po zhig tu gyur te/ de bzhin gshegs pa dri ma med pa'i sras zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Following that, in that same kalpa, I was a minister and I honored the Tathāgata by the name of Vimalavatsa.
Next, in the same age, as a government minister, I propitiated a buddha named Undefiled Child.
de'i 'og tu bskal pa de nyid la lha ma yin gyi dbang po zhig tu gyur te/ de bzhin gshegs pa shugs mnga' ba zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Following that, in that same kalpa, I was an asura lord and I honored the Tathāgata by the name of Veśadhārin.
Next, in the same age, as a titan chief, I propitiated a buddha named Holder of Energy.
de'i 'og tu bskal pa de nyid la shing gi lha mo zhig tu gyur te/ de bzhin gshegs pa mtshan nyid ri rab ces bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Following that, in that same kalpa, I was a tree goddess and I honored the Tathāgata by the name of Lakṣaṇasumeru.
Next, in the same age, as a tree spirit, I propitiated a buddha named Polar Mountain of Marks of Greatness.
de'i 'og tu bskal pa de gnyis la ded dpon cig tu gyur te /de bzhin gshegs pa phyag dri ma med pa zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Following that, in that same kalpa, I was a caravan leader and I honored the Tathāgata by the name of Vimalabāhu.
Next, in the same age, as a caravan leader, I propitiated a buddha named Undefiled Arms.
de'i 'og tu bskal pa de nyid la grong khyer gyi lha mo zhig tu gyur te/ de bzhin gshegs pa seng+ge rnam par gnon pas bzhud pa zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Following that, in that same kalpa, I was a city goddess and I honored the Tathāgata by the name of Siṃhavikrāntagāmin.
Next, in the same age, as a city spirit, I propitiated a buddha named Walking Boldly As a Lion.
de'i 'og tu bskal pa de nyid la ngal bso bo zhig tu gyur te/ de bzhin gshegs pa lha dbang gtsug phud ces bya ba bsnyen bkur to; ;
“Following that, in that same kalpa, I was a Vaiśravaṇa and I honored the Tathāgata by the name of Devendracūḍa.
Next, in the same age, as a god of riches, I propitiated a buddha named Crown of the Lord of Gods.
de'i 'og tu bskal pa de nyid la dri za'i rgyal po zhig tu gyur te/ de bzhin gshegs pa grags pa chos kyis 'phags pa zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Following that, in that same kalpa, I was a gandharva king and I honored the Tathāgata by the name of Dharmodgatakīrti.
Next, in the same age, as a celestial musician, I propitiated a buddha named Spiritual Renown.
de'i 'og tu bskal pa de nyid la grul bum gyi dbang po zhig tu gyur te/ de bzhin gshegs pa snang ba'i cod pa na zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Following that, in that same kalpa, I was a kumbhāṇḍa lord and I honored the Tathāgata by the name of Avabhāsamakuṭin.
Next, in the same age, as a goblin chief, I propitiated a buddha named Crown of Light.

rigs kyi bu de ltar kho mos de bzhin gshegs pa bcu po de dag la sogs pa bskal pa 'od zer bzang po de la skye ba'i rigs sna tshogs su skyes nas de bzhin gshegs pa bye ba phrag drug cu bsnyen bkur te/ kho mos de bzhin gshegs pa de dag thams cad la mchod pa byas so/ / de bzhin gshegs pa re re'i sbyan sngar 'gro ba'i tshe yang sems can gyi khams mtha' dang dbus med pa/ bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu yongs su smin par byas so/ /

“Noble one, in that way, I honored those ten tathāgatas and all the others. I was reborn in various existences in the Suprabha kalpa and honored six hundred million tathāgatas and made offerings to all those tathāgatas. Whenever I came before each of those tathāgatas, I ripened realms of beings without end or middle for the highest, complete enlightenment.

“In this way, I propitiated sixty million buddhas in the age of subtle light, beginning with these ten. I honored and served those buddhas in various forms of existence, and as I went to each buddha I matured countless beings for supreme perfect enlightenment.

de bzhin gshegs pa re re'i sbyan sngar 'gro ba'i tshe yang ting nge 'dzin gyi sgo sna tshogs rab tu thob par gyur to/ / gzungs kyi sgo sna tshogs dang / mngon par sgrub pa'i tshul sna tshogs dang / tha dad pa yang dag par shes pa mngon par sgrub pa'i tshul sna tshogs dang / thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi tshul rjes su rtogs par bya ba sna tshogs dang / chos snang ba'i sgo thob par bya ba'i tshul sna tshogs dang / ye shes kyi tshul khong du chud par dpyad pa rnams pa sna tshogs dang / phyogs rgya mtsho la 'jug pa'i snang ba sna tshogs dang / zhing rgya mtsho sna tshogs la 'jug cing khong du chud par bya ba'i snang ba sna tshogs dang / de bzhin gshegs pa rgya mtsho mthong bar bya ba rnam par dmigs pa'i snang ba sna tshogs kyang rab tu thob pa/ /

Whenever I came before each of those tathāgatas, I attained various entrances into samādhis, various entrances into powers of mental retention, various ways of accomplishments, various ways of accomplishing discernments, various realizations of the ways of omniscience, various ways of attaining the entrances to the illumination of the Dharma, various aspects of the analysis that comprehends the ways of knowledge, various illuminations of entering into the ocean of directions, and various illuminations of entering and comprehending the various oceans of realms, and I attained various illuminations of the perception that sees the ocean of tathāgatas.

And as I went to each buddha I attained various concentrations, various mental commands, various accomplishments, various types of specialized knowledge, various perspectives on truth, various operations of knowledge, various perceptions of the totality of realms, various awarenesses of the totality of lands, various perceptions of the totality of visions of Buddha;
yongs su non to/ / rnam par dag go / yongs su rdzogs so/ / yongs su gnas par gyur to/ / skyes so/ / byung ngo/ / rnam par 'phel to/ / yongs su 'phel to/ / rab tu byung ngo/ / rnam par byung ngo/ /
I overcame them, purified them, perfected them, and remained in them. They were born, they arose, they were increased, they were magnified, they arose perfectly, and they arose completely.
all these I entered into, purified, enlarged, and devoted my attention to from start to finish.

bskal pa 'od zer bzang po de la de bzhin gshegs pa rnams ji ltar rim gror byas pa de bzhin du bskal pa 'jig rten gyi khams rgya mtsho thams cad kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed du de bzhin gshegs pa ji snyed cig byung bar gyur pa dang / de bzhin gshegs pa ji snyed cig 'jig rten gyi khams gzhan nas de dag tu byon te chos bstan par gyur pa'i de bzhin gshegs pa de dag thams cad las kyang kho mos chos bstan pa thos te/ thos nas kyang yongs su bzung ngo/ / de bzhin gshegs pa de dag thams cad kyang kho mos bsnyen bkur to/ / rim gror byas so/ / sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das de dag gi bstan pa yang kho mos yongs su bzung ngo/ / de bzhin gshegs pa de dag thams cad las kyang kho mos byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa sems can thams cad yongs su smin par bya bas bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du dge ba'i rtsa ba la yang dag par skul ba 'di thob par bya ba'i tshul sna tshogs dang / rnam par thar pa'i tshul gyi sgo sna tshogs kyis thob par gyur to/ /

“Just as I attended the tathāgatas in that Suprabha kalpa, during kalpas as numerous as the atoms in all the ocean of world realms, however many tathāgatas appeared, however many tathāgatas came from other world realms, from all those tathāgatas who taught the Dharma, I heard the Dharma that they taught, and having heard it, I possessed it. I honored all those tathāgatas and served them. I held the teaching of all those buddha bhagavats. I obtained from all those tathāgatas various ways for the attainment of this bodhisattva liberation called the origin of the roots of merit that inspire, in accordance with their dispositions, the ripening of all beings, and I obtained various entrances into ways of liberation.”

“And just as I propitiated the buddhas in the age of Subtle Light, so did I propitiate all the buddhas who arose in as many eons as atoms in all oceans of worlds and came from other worlds and taught, and I listened to their teaching and remembered it. I have retained all their teachings, and from all of those buddhas I got this enlightening liberation born of roots of goodness aiding the development of all beings according to their mentalities, by various means of attainment and by various ways of liberation.”

de nas mtshan mo'i lha mo 'gro ba thams cad srung ba'i smon lam la brtson pa'i 'od kyis de'i tshe rnam par thar pa'i tshul 'di nyid yongs su brjod pa dang / yongs su bstan pa'i phyir tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la tshigs su bcad de smras pa/
Then at that time, the night goddess Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā, in order to describe and teach this liberation, recited these verses to Sudhana, the head merchant’s son.
Then the night goddess spoke these verses to Sudhana elucidating this liberation:
bsam gyis mi khyab rnam thar dam pa 'di/ / grags pa khyod kyis bdag la gang dris pa/ / bde bar gshegs pa'i byin gyis de bstan gyi/ / ma lus yang dag ji bzhin bdag la nyon/ /
“You, friend,[1685] have asked me about This inconceivable supreme liberation. I shall teach it through the blessing of the Sugata. Listen to me properly and entirely. {12}
This supreme liberation is inconceivable; Resolute, you ask me about it. Listen as I tell you all, By the power of the Buddha.
bskal pa bsam yas yangs pa mtha' yas pa/ / rgya mtsho'i zhing gi rdul dang grangs mnyam pa/ / de kun 'das pa'i snga rol mdangs dga' ba'i/ / 'jig rten khams shig byung ba rin chen 'od/ /
“There was the beautiful world realm Ratnaprabhā in the past beyond Inconceivable, vast, endless kalpas As numerous as the atoms in an ocean of buddha realms. {13}
Endless, vast, inconceivable eons ago, Countless worlds away, There was a pleasant world Called Jewel Light.
de tshe bskal pa bzang po'i 'od kyang byung / / de la rgyal ba dpag tu med pa skyes/ / thub pa'i dbang po de dag kho mo yis/ / rnam thar 'di la sgom zhing bsnyen bkur to/ /
“In that time, there arose the kalpa Suprabha In which countless jinas appeared. I honored those lords of munis And meditated on this liberation. {14}
There was an age called Beautiful Light In which numberless buddhas emerged; I propitiated those supreme sages As I cultivated this liberation.
rgyal po'i gnas rab yangs shing bzang byung ba/ / de yi ming ni dga' bas brgyan pa ste/ / de tshe sems can rnam par ma dag sems/ / mi bzang ngan du spyod pa der byung gyur/ /
“There was a vast, excellent royal capital, And its name was Rativyūhā. At that time, the minds of beings were impure, And they had dreadfully bad conduct. {15}
There was a great and glorious metropolis there Called Array of Delights In which there lived both Pure-minded people and evildoers.
der ni rgyal po rgyal ba'i 'od byung ste/ / sems can de dag chos kyis bskyang ba byas/ / de yi bu ni rnam par rgyal ba ste/ / mdzes shing mtshan gyis yan lag brgyan pa po/ /
“In that time, there was King Jayaprabha, Who governed those beings according to the Dharma.[1686] His son, named Vijitāvin, was handsome And adorned by the signs of a great being. {16}
The king there was Victorious Light, Who ruled his people justly; His son was called Conqueror, A fine man with the marks of greatness.
g.yon ldan stong phrag mang po de dag kyang / / de tshe rgyal pos gsad par byas mthong nas/ / bzhon nu snying brtse mi dga' kun nas 'khor/ / myur du dgye bar rgyal po de la gsol/ /
“At that time, seeing that the king was executing Those many thousands of criminals, The prince was filled with compassion and sadness, And he quickly beseeched the king to release them. {17}
Thousands of offenders had been Condemned to death by the king; Seeing them, the prince was seized with compassion And asked the king to release them.
rgyal pos thos nas de tshe blon po rnams/ / ma lus kun bsdus de la bka' stsal nas/ / kun gyis de la phyag byas phyir gsol pa/ / de ni rgyal po khyod dgrongs thabs cig lags/ /
“When the king had heard him, he gathered together All his ministers and spoke to them. They all bowed down to him and said to him, ‘This is a plan to assassinate you, Your Majesty!’ {18}
Hearing this, the king called his ministers And told them all about it: They all said, bowing to the king, “He is out to destroy you.”
rgyal po de ltar log par thugs bcug nas/ / sras de gsad par de tshe byas gyur kyang / / bdag srog phangs par ma brtsis ngo zum med/ / rgyal po'i sras kyis gsad par byas ma btang / /
“The king, having this misunderstanding, At that time ordered the execution of his son. The prince was indifferent to the loss of his own life, And he did not free himself from being executed. {19}
Incited by the ministers, the king Hastened to kill the prince. Undismayed, indifferent to his own death, The prince did not abandon the convicts.
gsad par byas pa de yi mas thos nas/ / rgyal po de la 'khor bcas gsol ba 'debs/ / dgung zla phyed cig sbyin pa ma lus par/ / 'jig rten stsol du gzhon nu gtang bar gnong / /

“When his mother heard that he was to be executed, With her entourage she supplicated the king, Asking for permission for the prince to give to the world All that he possessed for the duration of half a month. {20}
Grieved to hear the prince was condemned, The queen and the palace ladies asked the king To free the prince for a fortnight To give all kinds of gifts to the people.
rgyal po des kyang de ltar gnang gyur nas/ / des ni ci 'dod sbyin pa yongs su btang / / zla ba phyed du nyin mtshan sbyin byas nas/ / nyi ma'i tha mar tshogs par gyur pa yi/ /

“The king gave his permission for that to be done, And the prince gave away whatever was wanted For half a month, day and night, practicing generosity. And on the last day, to a gathering of Jains {21}
Granted permission by the king, the prince Made gifts of all that was asked for, Day and night, for half a month, Giving charity to all who came.
zhags pa thub pa gang rnams ci 'dod pa/ / de la de byin 'chi bar sta gon gnas/ / rgyal po'i gnas der 'gro ba mang po dag / cho der du zhing kun kyang 'dus par gyur/ /
“He gave whatever they desired, And having given to them he prepared for death. A multitude of beings wailing and weeping Gathered together at the royal capital. {22}
Whatever the needy required, That he gave them, prepared for death; The whole population of the city came out, Lamenting the fate of the prince.
byang chub shing drung bde gshegs de yi tshe/ / dam chos dbyangs mchog sgron ma'i rgyal zhugs pas/ / 'gro ba'i dbang po smin par thugs chud nas/ / mchod sbyin ra bar thugs rje chen pos byon; ;

“At that time, there sat at the foot of a Bodhi tree The Sugata Saddharmaghoṣāmbaradīparāja. That lord of beings knew it was time to ripen them, And with great compassion he came to the place where gifts were given. {23}
Then the buddha at the enlightenment tree, Illumining Space with the Voice of Truth, Realizing people’s faculties were ripe, Went to that sacrificial ground out of compassion.
de bzhin gshegs pa'i rnam 'phrul rnam phye bas/ / de yi 'khor du bde gshegs byon gyur nas/ / chos kyi sgron ma'i sprin gyi sgra sgrog pa'i/ / mdo sde rgyal po bde bar gshegs pas bshad/ /
“The Tathāgata came to that gathering Through his miraculous powers, And the Sugata taught the king of sūtras, The sound of the Dharma as a cloud of lamps of the Dharma. {24}
Going there, the buddha Produced a miraculous display And expounded a scripture, The voice of the Teaching as myriad lamps of truth.
'gro ba mtha' dang dbus med rnam btul nas/ / de tshe byang chub mchog tu lung yang bstan/ / rgyal ba'i sras po rnam par rgyal ba yang / / shin tu dga' bas byang chub mchog tu zhugs/ /
“He guided beings without end or middle And at that time gave prophecies of enlightenment. The son of the king, Vijitāvin, was overjoyed And entered upon attaining the supreme enlightenment. {25}
Countless people were edified, And the buddha foretold their enlightenment; The prince Conqueror, enraptured, Set out for supreme enlightenment.
bde gshegs bsnyen bkur mchod pa rnam yangs pas/ / de la mchod byas dga' bar smras pa ni/ / 'gro ba rnam 'dul skyabs su bdag 'gyur bgyi/ / mgon dang gnas dang dpung du'ang de bzhin zhes/ /
“He offered to the Sugata vast honors and offerings, And with joy he said these words: ‘May I become for beings a sanctuary, a guide, A protector, a refuge, and a defender.’ {26}
The prince gave the buddha Many offerings and joyfully said, “May I become a guide, savior, refuge, And resort for the people of the land.”
rgyal ba de yi zham ring thar par zhugs/ / yang dag byang chub lam ni yongs tshol zhing / / chos kyi rang bzhin rab tu brtag bya bas/ / der gnas bskal pa brgya phrag mang du spyad/ /
“He became a mendicant under that muni And sought the path to enlightenment. He examined the nature of phenomena, Remaining practicing in that way for a hundred kalpas. {27}
He left home to join the buddha, Seeking the path of perfect enlightenment; He spent hundreds of eons Thoroughly investigating the essence of thing.
sdug bsngal rgya mtshor lhung zhing ldongs gyur pa'i/ / 'gro ba mgon med kun la snying brtse bas/ / yang dag byang chub lam la yongs bsgoms nas/ / de tshe de yis rnam thar 'di thob bo/ /
“He had compassion for beings with no protector Who were falling into an ocean of suffering, And, meditating on the path to true enlightenment, He attained at that time this liberation. {28}
Pitying all the helpless ones Fallen into the sea of suffering, Having cultivated the path of enlightenment, He attained this liberation.
bskal pa de la bde gshegs gang byung ba/ / de dag kun la'ang dga' bas bsnyen bkur nas/ / de dag kun la mchod pa chen po byas/ / chos kyi 'khor lo yongs su bzung bar gyur/ /
“He joyfully honored every one Of the sugatas who appeared in that kalpa, Making great offerings to all of them And possessing their wheels of the Dharma. {29}
All the buddhas in that age He propitiated with pure faith; He made great offerings to them And kept their teachings in mind.
de yi 'og tu bskal pa rgya mtsho rnams; ; zhing mang rgya mtsho'i rdul snyed kun la yang / / rgyal ba ji snyed skyes par gyur pa dag / rab tu mchod cing de dag bsnyen bkur byas/ /
“After that, during an ocean of kalpas As numerous as the atoms in a sea of realms, He made offerings, and he honored However many jinas appeared. {30}
After that, for eons numerous As atoms in oceans of lands, He propitiated and made offerings to All the buddhas that arose.
rnam par rgyal zhes bya ba kho mo yin/ / nyam nga btson rar gnas pa'i btson mthong nas/ / de dag dgrol phyir lus kyang yongs su btang / / rnam thar 'di yang de tshe thob par gyur/ /
“I was the one named Vijitāvin, Who saw the prisoners in the dreadful prison, Offered up his body in order to free them, And at that time attained this liberation, {31}
I was the prince Conqueror, Who, seeing people imprisoned, Gave up my body to free them And thus attained this liberation.
zhing rnams rgya mtsho'i rdul phran rab bgrangs pa'i/ / bskal pa rgya mtsho mang po bsgoms par byas/ / tshul mang mtha' dang dbus med mnyam med pas/ / skad cig re re dag tu rnam par spel; ;
“Who meditated during a great ocean of kalpas As numerous as the atoms in an ocean of realms, And who, in each instant, multiplied the ways That were unequaled and vast, without end or middle. {32}
I cultivated it for eons as many As atoms in oceans of lands, Expanding it moment by moment Through endless incomparable means.
thub pa'i bdag po ji snyed mthong gyur pa/ / de dag spyan sngar sngon chad 'di thob ste/ / sgo tshul rnam pa gzhan dang gzhan dag gis/ / de dag gis ni rnam thar 'di yang bstan/ /
From all the buddhas I saw I gained some realization And was shown this liberation By a succession of means.
de dag rnam thar ma nor bsam yas la/ / bskal pa bye ba mang por kho mos bslab/ / de la rgyal bas bkod cing grol gyur pa/ / de dag dam chos sprin las gcig car 'thung / /

“I trained for many millions of kalpas In this unmistaken, inconceivable liberation I received from them. Established in it by the jinas, I was liberated. I simultaneously drank from their clouds of Dharma. {34}
From them I learned the inconceivable Reality of liberation over countless eons, Imbibing all at once the multitude of teaching Projected by the buddhas when established therein.
phyogs bcu kun gyi zhing rnams thams cad du/ / thogs pa med par lus kyis rgyas par 'gengs/ / skad cig re rer zhing rgyud bsam yas pa'i/ / dus gsum rgyud rnams kun la'ang rab tu 'jug /
“My bodies pervaded without impediment All the realms in all the ten directions. In each instant, I entered countless realms And entered the divisions of the three times. {35}
Those established therein Go everywhere without attachment, Instantly comprehending the countless Names and groups of past, present, and future.
dus gsum rgyal ba rgya mtsho ma lus pa/ / re re kun la'ang mngon du rab tu lta/ / de dag lus kyi gzugs brnyan rgyal ba la/ / sprin du gyur pa rnams kyang spyan sngar 'grim/ /
“They gaze upon each and every one without exception In the ocean of the jinas in the three times. They wander in the presence of the clouds Of the visual images of their bodies. {36}
They appear before all the multitudes Of buddhas of all times, Manifesting themselves in the presence Of those buddhas as reflected images.
phyogs rnams kun tu nye bar phyin 'dong zhing / / rgyal ba'i spyan sngar 'dong bas shin tu mdzes/ / rgyan rnams ma lus mngon par char 'bebs shing / / rgyal ba rnams la de dag mchod pa byed/ /
“They go in every direction, Going into the presence of the jinas. They send down a rain of every beautiful display, And they offer it to those jinas. {37}
They go everywhere and appear Before all the buddhas, Showering all kinds of ornaments As offerings to the buddhas.
sangs rgyas rgya mtsho che la rnam yangs pa'i/ / zhu ba mtha' yas kun kyang zhu ba byed/ / rgyal ba'i chos sprin mngon par char 'bab pa/ / kun kyang ma lus yongs su 'dzin pa byed/ /
“They ask an endless number of all questions To the immense, vast ocean of buddhas. And they possess all, without exception, of the rain That falls from the clouds of the Dharma of the jinas. {38}
Then they ask the myriads of buddhas Multitudes of questions And remember the infinite teachings Poured forth by the buddhas.
phyogs bcu ma lus kun tu de dag 'dong / / rgyal ba'i dkyil 'khor kun gyi spyan sngar 'bab/ / gzugs mang rnam pa sna tshogs bstan gnas shing / / rnam 'phrul sna tshogs nye bar ston par byed/ /
“They go into every direction without exception, Arriving in the presence of the fields of the jinas. They manifest a variety of a multitude of forms, And they manifest a variety of miracles. {39}
They go to the circles of buddhas everywhere, As far as they can see, Sitting on seats of many forms, Manifesting various miracles.
kha dog mtha' yas rang gi lus gzugs kyis/ / phyogs rnams thams cad rnam pa stong du 'gengs/ / de dag lus gcig las kyang gzugs kyi rnams/ / mtha' dang dbus med rnam par ston par byed/ /

“They fill all directions with thousands of forms With their physical bodies that have infinite colors. They can manifest from the form of a single body Infinite aspects, vast without end or middle. {40}
With bodies of infinite appearances, They fill all realms, by the thousands; They show an endless, endless variety of forms, And all those forms in one.
ba spu re re'i sgo nas grangs med pa'i/ / 'od zer mang po rgya mtsho de dag 'gyed/ / skye rgu'i nyon mongs me yi gdung pa dag / sna tshogs thabs kyis rab tu zhi bar byed/ /
“They radiate an ocean of innumerable Light rays from each and every pore, And through a variety of methods they extinguish The pain from the fire of the kleśas within beings. {41}
From each pore they emanate countless Multitudes of light rays And extinguish the fire of afflictions Of all beings by various means.
'di la gnas pa lus sprul sprin mang ba/ / ba spu re re'i sgo nas 'gyed byed cing / / ngo mtshar rmad kyis phyogs kun rgyas bkang nas/ / chos chu'i char gyis sems can rnam par 'dul/ /

“While they remain in one place, clouds of emanated bodies Are radiated from each and every pore, Filling all directions with marvelous wonders And guiding beings with the rain of the water of the Dharma. {42}
In this state, emanating myriad projected bodies From each and every pore, They pervade all realms with them And guide beings with rain from the ocean of truth.
tshul 'jug 'di ni bsam gyis mi khyab gzugs/ / rgyal sras kun gyi gnas su gyur pa ste/ / de la gnas shing phyi mtha'i bskal par yang / / zhing rnams kun tu spyad pa rab tu spyod/ /

“This way of entering is that of inconceivable form. It is the support for all the progeny of the jinas. Remaining in this, they practice the conduct Within all realms until the last of future kalpas. {43}
This way of enlightenment, with inconceivable forms, Is the resort of all enlightening beings; Based on this they carry out practices In all lands for all time.
bsam pa ji bzhin chos rnams ston byed cing / / de dag lta ba'i dra ba rnam par zlog / mtho ris mya ngan 'das la sems can 'god/ / thams cad mkhyen pa'i sa yang rnam par ston/ /

“They teach the Dharma in accordance with aspirations, And they repel the nets that are wrong views. They establish beings in the higher existences and nirvāṇa, And they teach the level of omniscience. {44}
Expounding the Teaching according to mentalities, They remove the web of views; Dwelling in ultimate felicity, They show people the stage of omniscience.
'jig rten skye gnas thams cad ma lus par/ / kha dog mtha' yas lus mang bsam yas pa; ; bsam pa bzhin du chos rnams rjod byed de/ / de dag sems can kun gyi gzugs brnyan gzugs/ /

“They teach the Dharma according to aspirations With endless colors and countless bodies, With all kinds of birth and worlds without exception, With bodies that are the images of the bodies of all beings. {45}
With inconceivably many bodies of endless forms In all states of existence, They teach according to mentality, Their forms reflections of all beings.
'di dang gzhan dag tshad las 'das pa yi/ / yon tan rgya mtsho zhing mang rgya mtsho yi/ / rdul phran rab snyed bsam gyis mi khyab pa/ / rnam thar zhi ba 'di ldan thob par gyur/ /
“These and also a measureless ocean of other qualities, As numerous as the atoms in an ocean of realms And beyond conception, are attained By those who have this liberation, this peace. {46}
So many and infinitely more, As inconceivably many as atoms in all lands, Are the oceans of manifestations of the fearless ones When they have attained this peaceful liberation.
