rigs kyi bu/ kho mos byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa sems can thams cad yongs su smin par bya bas bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du dge ba'i rtsa ba la yang dag par skul ba 'di shes par zad na/ kho mos byang chub sems dpa' 'jig rten thams cad kyi lam gyi rgyud las 'das pa/ 'jig rten gyi skye gnas thams cad du gzugs brnyan rab tu 'byung ba/ 'jig rten gyi shes pa thams cad las yang dag par 'das pa/ shes bya'i sgrib pa thams cad kyi ri rnam par 'thor ba la brtson pa/ chos thams cad kyi rang bzhin dang mtshan nyid rab tu rtogs pa/ nyon mongs pa'i sgrib pa dang / mun pa thams cad rnam par sel ba la brtson pa/ chos thams cad rab tu dpyad pas mngon par sgrub pa la mkhas pa/ bdag med pa'i chos mngon du gyur pa/ sems can thams cad yongs su smin par bya ba dang / gdul ba rgyun mi gcod pa / chos kyi dbyings kyi tshul gnyis su med par rab tu rtogs pa dag gi lam gyi tshul rgya mtsho thams cad kyi rjes su 'brang ba'i blo dang ldan pa de dag gi spyod pa shes pa'am/ yon tan rgya mtsho la 'jug pa'am/ ye shes kyis rnam par gnon pa yongs su shes par bya ba'am/ sems kyi gnas khong du chud par bya ba'am/ ting nge 'dzin la dbang sgyur ba rtogs par bya ba'am/ rnam par thar pas rnam par 'phrul pa yongs su shes par bya bar nus re skan/

“Noble one, I know only this bodhisattva liberation called the origin of the roots of merit that inspire, in accordance with their dispositions, the ripening of all beings. How could I know the conduct, or comprehend the ocean of qualities, or understand the prowess of the knowledge, or ascertain the states of mind, or realize the power of samādhi, or know completely the miraculous manifestation of the liberations of bodhisattvas who have transcended all the existences in worlds, who appear in the visual form of all births in worlds, who have transcended all worldly knowledge, who are dedicated to destroying the mountain of all obscurations of knowledge, who have discerned the nature and characteristics of all phenomena, who are dedicated to eliminating all the obscurations and darkness of the kleśas, who are skilled in the accomplishment of the analysis of all phenomena, who have the direct perception of the Dharma of there being no self, who are continuously ripening and guiding beings, who have realized the way of nonduality of the realm of the Dharma, and who have the intelligence to follow the ocean of all the ways within the scope of speech?[1687]

The goddess continued, “I know only this enlightening liberation born of roots of goodness fostering the development of all beings according to their mentalities. How can I know the practice, or comprehend the oceans of virtues, or completely know the power of knowledge, or know the realm of thought, or understand the mastery of concentration, or recognize the miracle of liberation, of the enlightening beings who have transcended all worldly courses, who appear as reflections in all states of being, who are intent on shattering the mountains of barriers to omniscience, who know the nature and characteristics of all things, who are engaged in dispelling the darkness of all barriers caused by afflictions, who are skilled in carrying out a thorough investigation of all things, who actually realize the knowledge of selflessness, who ceaselessly develop and guide all sentient beings, who really know the principle of the nondual reality realm, whose intellects encompass the ocean of all manners of verbal expression?

song rigs kyi bu/ 'dzam bu'i gling 'di nyid kyi lum+bi ni'i nags tshal na lum+bi ni'i nags tshal gyi lha mo gzi brjid kyi dkyil 'khor bzang pos dga' ba'i dpal zhes bya ba 'dug gi /de'i gan du song la ji ltar na/ byang chub sems dpa' de bzhin gshegs pa'i rigs su byung ba yin pa dang / ji ltar na/ 'jig rten rnams la snang ba byed par 'gyur ba dang / ji ltar na/ phyi ma'i mtha'i bskal pa'i mur thug par byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa spyad pas mi skyo bar 'gyur ba dris shig /

“Depart, noble one. In the forest of Lumbinī in this Jambudvīpa, there is the goddess of the Lumbinī Forest called Sutejomaṇḍalaratiśrī. Go to her and ask her, ‘How are bodhisattvas born into the family of the tathāgatas? How do bodhisattvas appear in the world? How do they unwearyingly practice bodhisattva conduct until the last of all future kalpas?’ ”

“In the Lumbini grove, here on Jambudvipa, there lives a goddess of the Lumbini grove named Sutejomandalaratishri. Go ask her how enlightening beings are born in the family of buddhas, how they become light-makers for the world, and how they carry on the practice of enlightening beings forever without wearying.”

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis mtshan mo'i lha mo 'gro ba thams cad srung ba'i smon lam la brtson pa'i 'od kyi rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te mtshan mo'i lha mo 'gro ba thams cad srung ba'i smon lam la brtson pa'i 'od la lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas thal mo sbyar te phyir lta zhing mtshan mo'i lha mo 'gro ba thams cad srung ba'i smon lam la brtson pa'i 'od kyi drung nas song ngo/ /

Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, bowed his head to the two feet of the night goddess Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā, circumambulated the night goddess Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā many hundreds of thousands of times, keeping her to his right, and, with palms together, looking back at her, departed from the night goddess Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā.
Then Sudhana paid his respects to the night goddess Sarvajagadrak-shapranidhanaviryaprabha and left.
shin tu rgyas pa chen po'i mdo/ / sangs rgyas phal po che zhes bya ba las/ sdong pos brgyan pa'i le'u ste/ bam po brgya drug pa/

d.crumb: [lum+bi ni'i nags tshal gyi lha mo gzi brjid kyi dkyil 'khor bzang pos dga' ba'i dpal]

f.d: [lum+bi ni'i nags tshal gyi lha mo gzi brjid kyi dkyil 'khor bzang pos dga' ba'i dpal]
Chapter 42. Sutejomaṇḍalaratiśrī
Sutejomandalaratishri

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang mtshan mo'i lha mo 'gro ba thams cad srung ba'i smon lam la brtson pa'i 'od kyi gdams ngag de rjes su dran par byed cing / byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa sems can thams cad yongs su smin par bya bas bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du dge ba'i rtsa ba la yang dag par skul ba de la yongs su sgom pa dang / khong du chud par bya ba dang / rgya cher byed cing mthar gyis lum+bi ni'i nags tshal gang na ba der phyin te

Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, remembering the instruction of the night goddess Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā and meditating on, comprehending, and augmenting the bodhisattva liberation called the origin of the roots of merit that inspire the ripening of all beings, eventually arrived at the Lumbinī Forest.

Remembering the instruction of the night goddess Sarvajagadrak-shapranidhanaviryaprabha, cultivating and extending the enlightening liberation born of roots of goodness fostering the development of all beings according to their mentalities, Sudhana made his way to the Lumbini grove. When he got to the Lumbini grove
lum+bi ni'i nags tshal la g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas lum+bi ni'i nags tshal gyi lha mo gzi brjid kyi dkyil 'khor bzang pos dga' ba'i dpal yongs su tshol tshol ba las/
He circumambulated the Lumbinī Forest, keeping it to his right, and then searched for Sutejomaṇḍalaratiśrī, the Lumbinī Forest goddess.
he circled it, looking for the goddess Sutejomandalaratishri.

lum+bi ni'i nags tshal gyi lha mo gzi brjid kyi dkyil 'khor bzang pos dga' ba'i dpal lum+bi ni'i nags tshal na rin po che'i shing gi yal ga thams cad kyi dkyil 'khor gyi khyim brtsegs pa zhig na seng+ge'i khri rin po che'i pad+mo'i snying po can zhig la 'dug cing nags tshal gyi lha mo khrag khrig brgya stong phrag nyi shu'i 'khor gyis kun nas bskor te mdun du byas nas chos ston te/ byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi skye ba rgya mtsho shin tu bstan pa zhes bya ba'i mdo sde yongs su ston cing / de bzhin gshegs pa'i rigs kyi rgyud du rigs dang ldan par skyes pa'i byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi yon tan rgya mtsho'i shugs rnam par 'phel bar byed cing 'dug pa mthong nas

He saw Sutejomaṇḍalaratiśrī, the Lumbinī Forest goddess, in the Lumbinī Forest inside a kūṭāgāra made by the encircling of all branches of trees made of all precious materials. She was seated upon a precious lion throne with a lotus in its center and accompanied by an assembly of two hundred thousand trillion forest goddesses, seated before her and to whom she taught the Dharma. She was teaching them a sūtra called The Teaching of the Ocean of Lifetimes of All Bodhisattvas. She was increasing the power of the ocean of qualities of bodhisattvas who had been born into the family of the tathāgatas.

Finally he saw her sitting on a jewel lotus calyx lion seat in a tower made of encircling branches of trees of all jewels in the Lumbini grove, surrounded by twenty million billion wood goddesses, teaching them, expounding to them a scripture called Exposition of the Ocean of Lives of All Enlightening Beings, born in the family of buddhas, increasing the flood of the ocean of virtues of enlightening beings.

lum+bi ni'i nags tshal gyi lha mo gzi brjid kyi dkyil 'khor bzang pos dga' ba'i dpal gang na ba der song ste phyin nas lum+bi ni'i nags tshal gyi lha mo gzi brjid kyi dkyil 'khor bzang pos dga' ba'i dpal gyi rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal nas mdun du 'dug ste thal mo sbyar nas 'di skad ces smras so/ / 'phags ma/ bdag gis bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed na/ ji ltar na/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams de bzhin gshegs pa'i rigs su byung ba lags pa'ang ma 'tshal/ ji ltar na/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams spyod pa la spyod cing sems can rnams la snang ba 'byin par 'gyur ba'ang ma 'tshal to/ / de skad ces smras pa dang /

He approached the Lumbinī Forest goddess Sutejomaṇḍalaratiśrī, bowed down to the feet of the Lumbinī Forest goddess Sutejomaṇḍalaratiśrī, and, standing before her with palms together, said, “Āryā, I have developed the aspiration for the highest, complete enlightenment, but I do not know how bodhisattvas are born into the tathāgata family and how in practicing bodhisattva conduct they bring light to beings.”

Seeing the goddess, Sudhana went up to her, paid his respects, and said, “I have set my mind on supreme perfect enlightenment, but I do not know how enlightening beings get to be born in the family of buddhas, or how, carrying out the practice of enlightening beings, they become light-makers for sentient beings.”

lum+bi ni'i nags tshal gyi lha mo gzi brjid kyi dkyil 'khor bzang pos dga' ba'i dpal gyis tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la 'di skad ces smras so/ / rigs kyi bu/ bcu po 'di dag ni/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi skye ba ste/ de dag dang ldan na/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams de bzhin gshegs pa'i rigs su skyes pa yin no/ / de dag las byung na; byang chub sems dpa' rnams sems kyi skad cig re re la'ang byang chub sems dpa'i dge ba'i rtsa bas rnam par 'phel bar 'gyur te/ thogs pa med pa dang / zhum pa med pa dang / phyir ldog pa med pa dang / rgyun gcod pa med pa dang / yongs su skyo ba med pa dang / sgyid lug par 'gyur ba med pa dang / nyams par 'gyur ba med pa dang / nyams dma' bar 'gyur ba med pa dang / yongs su yi chad par 'gyur ba med pa dang / chud za bar 'gyur ba med pa dang / thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi phyogs kyi rjes su 'brang bar 'gyur ba dang / chos kyi dbyings kyi tshul la yongs su gzhol bar 'gyur ba dang / sangs rgyas kyi byang chub tu yongs su smin pa thob par 'gyur ba dang / byang chub sems dpa' sems bskyed pa shin tu yangs par 'gyur ba dang / pha rol tu phyin pa thams cad kyis rnam par 'phel bar 'gyur ba dang / 'jig rten gyi lam rgyud thams cad las rnam par ldog par 'gyur ba dang / de bzhin gshegs pa'i sar yongs su grub par 'gyur ba dang / ye shes kyis mngon par shes pa shin tu byang bar 'gyur ba dang / sangs rgyas kyi chos mngon du 'gyur pa dang / thams cad mkhyen pa'i yul gyi don dang ldan par 'gyur ba'o/ /

The Lumbinī Forest goddess Sutejomaṇḍalaratiśrī said, “Noble one, if the bodhisattvas possess these ten kinds of birth, they are born into the family of the tathāgatas. The bodhisattvas who originate from them in every instant of mind increase the roots of merit of a bodhisattva, are unimpeded, are not disheartened, do not regress, are not interrupted, are not dismayed, are not discouraged, do not deteriorate, do not become confused, do not become downcast, and do not come to ruin. They follow the direction of omniscience, they are dedicated[1688] to the ways of the realm of the Dharma, they attain ripening for the enlightenment of buddhahood, they have a vast development of the bodhisattva’s aspiration for enlightenment, they increase all the perfections, they turn away from all worldly existences, they accomplish the level of the tathāgatas, they purify the higher cognition of[1689] knowledge, they directly perceive the qualities of buddhahood, and they possess the meaning of the range of omniscience.

The goddess replied, “There are ten kinds of birth by which enlightening beings become born in the family of buddhas. Enlightening beings who have accomplished these develop correctly by means of the skills of enlightening beings, without stopping, without becoming exhausted, without regressing, without giving up, without wearying, without becoming discouraged, without becoming confused, without tarrying, without becoming afraid, without waning away. They follow the way to omniscience and remember the principle of the realm of reality; they become ripe for the enlightenment of buddhas and broaden the determination for enlightenment. They grow by means of all the transcendent ways, they withdraw from all worldly ways, and progress into the stage of those who realize Thusness. They refine mystic knowledge, become aware of all principles of enlightenment, and accord with the realm of omniscience.
bcu gang zhe na/ 'di lta ste/ sangs rgyas thams cad la bsnyen bkur ba'i smon lam gyi sbyor ba'i snying po zhes bya ba ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i skye ba dang po'o/ /
“What are these ten? The first birth of a bodhisattva is called the essence of dedication to the prayer to serve all buddhas.
What are these ten kinds of birth of enlightening beings? The first is called the birth of enlightening beings as offspring of the undertaking of the vow to serve all buddhas.
byang chub kyi sems kyi yan lag yongs su grub par 'gyur ba 'byung ba'i snying po zhes bya ba ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i skye ba gnyis pa'o/ /
“The second birth of a bodhisattva is called the essence of the origin of the attainment of the aspects of the aspiration to enlightenment.
The second is the birth of enlightening beings as offspring of consummation of all elements of the determination for enlightenment.
chos kyi tshul la nges par rtogs par gzhag pa'i sbyor ba'i tshul mngon du gyur pa 'byung ba'i snying po zhes bya ba ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i skye ba gsum pa'o; ;
“The third birth of a bodhisattva is called the essence of the origin of the perception that is established in certainty in the ways of the Dharma.
The third is the birth of enlightening beings as offspring of meditation on the principles of the Teaching.
dus gsum snang bar bya ba'i lhag pa'i bsam pa rnam par dag pa'i snying po zhes bya ba ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i skye ba bzhi pa'o/ /
“The fourth birth of a bodhisattva is called the essence of the pure, superior motivation that illuminates the three times.
The fourth is the birth of enlightening beings as offspring of purification of the intent in viewing past, present, and future.
kun nas snang ba'i 'od kyi snying po zhes bya ba ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i skye ba lnga pa'o/ /
“The fifth birth of a bodhisattva is called the essence of all-illuminating light.
The fifth is the birth of enlightening beings as offspring of the light of universal awareness.
de bzhin gshegs pa'i rigs kyi rgyud du 'byung ba'i snying po zhes bya ba ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i skye ba drug pa'o/ /
“The sixth birth of a bodhisattva is called the essence of the origin of the lineage of the tathāgata family.
The sixth is the birth as enlightening beings as offspring of the family of all buddhas.
de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi stobs kyi 'od snang ba'i rgyan gyi snying po zhes bya ba ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i skye ba bdun pa'o/ /
“The seventh birth of a bodhisattva is called the essence of the adorning light that illuminates the strengths of the buddhas.
The seventh is the birth of enlightening beings as offspring of the array of lights of the manifestation of powers of buddhas.
ye shes kyi sgo kun nas rnam par spyad pas yongs su 'grub pa 'byung ba'i snying po zhes bya ba ni; byang chub sems dpa'i skye ba brgyad pa'o/ /
“The eighth birth of a bodhisattva is called the essence of the origin of the accomplishment through the complete analysis of the entrances into knowledge.
The eighth is the birth of enlightening beings as offspring of consummation of contemplation of the way to omniscience.
chos kyi dbyings sprul pas brgyan pa bye ba'i snying po zhes bya ba ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i skye ba dgu pa'o/ /
“The ninth birth of a bodhisattva is called the essence of the display of emanations throughout the realm of phenomena.
The ninth is the birth of enlightening beings as offspring of manifestation of emanations throughout the cosmos.
de bzhin gshegs pa'i sa yongs su gnon pa'i shugs drag po'i snying po zhes bya ba ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i skye ba bcu pa'o/ /
“The tenth birth of a bodhisattva is called the essence of the power of ascending to the level of the tathāgatas.
The tenth is the birth of enlightening beings as offspring of momentum going into the stage of the enlightened.

rigs kyi bu/ de la byang chub sems dpa'i skye ba dang po sangs rgyas thams cad la bsnyen bkur ba'i smon lam gyi sbyor ba'i snying po zhes bya ba gang zhe na/ rigs kyi bu/ 'di la byang chub sems dpa' thog mar sangs rgyas mchod cing rim gror bya ba la 'jug ste/ de sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das rnams la rim gro dang / bkur sti dang / bsti stang dang / mchod pa byed cing bsnyen bkur byed de dgyes par byed la thugs byung bar mi byed pas de bzhin gshegs pa'i zhal blta bas mi doms pa/ sangs rgyas la rim gro bya bar brtson pa/ sangs rgyas la dga' ba'i shugs kyis rnam par spel ba'i shugs dang ldan pa; de bzhin gshegs pa mthong bas mos pa'i shugs drag po yongs su skyes pa de phyir mi ldog pa'i dad pas bsod nams yongs su sdud pa'i tshe de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad la mchod pa'i tshogs yongs su bsdu ba la brtson zhing sbyor ba rgyun mi gcod pa yin te/

“Noble one, what is the first birth of a bodhisattva, called the essence of dedication to the prayer to serve all buddhas? It is when the bodhisattva first engages in serving and making offerings to the buddhas; venerating, worshiping, honoring, offering, serving, pleasing, and never displeasing the buddha bhagavats; never having enough of gazing upon the face of a tathāgata; being dedicated to venerating the buddhas; having increasing power through the power of delight in the buddhas; giving rise to a powerful adoration on seeing the tathāgatas; and while accumulating merit with irreversible faith, uninterruptedly dedicating to completing an accumulation of offerings to all the tathāgatas.

“What is the first birth of enlightening beings, as offspring of the undertaking of the vow to serve all buddhas? Here the enlightening beings, honoring, respecting, serving, attending, and pleasing all buddhas just as when they first made offerings in service of a buddha, never tire of seeing the enlightened; their minds expanded by floods of joy from the buddhas they honor, they are flooded with well-being by the sight of buddhas. Gaining virtue with unwavering faith, tireless, they ceaselessly work to bring offerings to all buddhas.

rigs kyi bu/ de ni/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi skye ba dang po sangs rgyas thams cad la bsnyen bkur ba'i smon lam gyi sbyor ba'i snying po zhes bya ba ste/ thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi tshogs dge ba'i rtsa ba yongs su 'grub par yang dag par sdud par 'gyur ba'o/ /
“Noble one, that is the first birth of a bodhisattva, called the essence of dedication to the prayer to serve all buddhas, which acquires the accumulation of the roots of merit for omniscience.

This is enlightening beings’ first kind of birth, as offspring of the undertaking of the vow to serve all buddhas, which is conducive to the production and acquisition of roots of goodness in preparation for omniscience.
rigs kyi bu/ de la byang chub sems dpa'i skye ba gnyis pa byang chub kyi yan lag yongs su grub par 'gyur ba 'byung ba'i snying po zhes bya ba gang zhe na/
“Noble one, what is the second birth of a bodhisattva, called the essence of the origin of the attainment of the aspects of the aspiration to enlightenment?
“What is enlightening beings’ birth as offspring of consummation of all elements of the determination for enlightenment?

rigs kyi bu/ 'di la byang chub sems dpa' bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed de/ 'di ltar sems can thams cad yongs su bskyab pa'i phyir snying rje chen po'i sems dang / shin tu dgyes par bya ba'i phyir sangs rgyas thams cad bsnyen bkur ba'i sems dang / dngos po thams cad la phangs par mi brtsi ba'i phyir sangs rgyas kyi chos thams cad yongs su btsal ba'i sems dang / thams cad mkhyen pa nyid mngon du 'gyur bar bya ba'i phyir bshams pa chen po'i sems dang / 'gro ba thams cad yongs su bsdu ba'i sbyor bas rgyas par dgang ba'i phyir byams pa chen po'i sems dang / thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi go cha bstan par bya ba'i phyir 'gro ba thams cad yongs su mi gtong ba'i sems dang / yang dag pa ji lta ba bzhin du shes pa'i snang ba rab tu thob par bya ba'i phyir g.yo dang sgyu med pa'i sems dang / byang chub sems dpa'i lam lan nan tan du bya ba'i phyir kha 'og tu lus khrus pa'i sems dang / de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi smon lam dang mi 'gal bar bya ba'i phyir sangs rgyas thams cad la sku bslu ba med pa'i sems dang / phyi ma'i mtha'i mur thug par sems can thams cad yongs su smin par bya ba dang gdul ba rgyun mi gcad pa'i phyir thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du smon lam chen po 'debs pa'i sems dang /

“Noble one, it is when the bodhisattva develops the aspiration for the highest, complete enlightenment and in that way has the motivation of great compassion for protecting all beings, has the motivation to serve all the buddhas in order to please them, has the motivation to seek for all the Dharmas of the buddhas in order to be indifferent toward all things, has the motivation of the great setting forth[1690] in order to perceive omniscience, has the motivation of great love in order to increase application to gathering all beings, has the motivation to never abandon all beings in order to have the strong armor of omniscience, has a motivation free of deception and dissimulation in order to attain the illumination of genuine knowledge, has the motivation to act in accord with what one teaches[1691] in order to practice the path of the bodhisattvas, has the motivation to never break one’s word[1692] to all the buddhas in order not to run counter[1693] to the prayers of all the tathāgatas, and has the motivation to make the great prayer for omniscience in order to continuously ripen and guide all beings until the end of future time.

Here enlightening beings arouse the will for supreme perfect enlightenment: that involves the will of great compassion to save all beings; the will to please all buddhas ultimately; the will to seek all ways of enlightenment, to be equanimous toward all things; the will for the greatest of undertakings, to head for omniscience; the will of great kindness, to treat all beings with care; the will not to abandon any beings, to be firmly equipped for omniscience; the will to avoid deceit and falsehood, to attain the light of truthful knowledge; the will to act in accord with one’s speech, to carry out the path of enlightening beings; the will not to disappoint the buddhas, to keep the vows of all buddhas; the will for the great undertaking of omniscience, to ceaselessly guide and perfect all beings that will ever be.

de dag la sogs pa byang chub sems kyi yan lag gi tshogs sangs rgyas kyi zhing gi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyis yongs su rdzogs pa'i byang chub sems dpa' ni/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i rigs su skyes pa yin te/

“Through completing the accumulation of these and other aspects of the aspiration to enlightenment, which are as numerous as the atoms in a buddha realm, a bodhisattva is born into the family of the tathāgatas.
When enlightening beings have fulfilled as many such elements of the determination for enlightenment as atoms in a buddha-land, then they are born in the family of buddhas.
rigs kyi bu/ de ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i skye ba gnyis pa byang chub kyi sems kyi yan lag yongs su grub par 'gyur ba 'byung ba'i snying po zhes bya ba'o/ /
“Noble one, that is the second birth of a bodhisattva, called the essence of the origin of the attainment of the aspects of the aspiration to enlightenment.

rigs kyi bu/ de la byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi byang chub sems dpa'i skye ba gsum pa chos kyi tshul la nges par gzhag pa'i sbyor ba'i tshul mngon du gyur pa 'byung ba'i snying po zhes bya ba gang zhe na/
“Noble one, what is the third birth of bodhisattvas, called the essence of the origin of the perception that is established in certainty in the ways of the Dharma?
“What is enlightening beings’ birth as offspring of meditation on the principles of the Teaching?

rigs kyi bu/ 'di la byang chub sems dpa' chos thams cad kyi tshul rgya mtsho yod do cog nges par rtogs pas mngon du bya ba'i sems dang ldan pa/ thams cad mkhyen pa'i lam gyi rnam pa yongs su rdzogs par bya bas mngon du bya bar gcig tu sems pa'i sems dang ldan pa; kha na ma tho ba med pa'i las la yang dag par spyad par sems pa'i sems dang ldan pa/ byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin gyi tshul rgya mtsho thams cad yongs su dag par bya bas mngon du bya ba'i sems dang ldan pa/ byang chub sems dpa'i yon tan thams cad la nan tan du bya bas yongs su grub par bya ba'i sems dang ldan pa/ byang chub sems dpa'i lam gyi rgyan thams cad mngon par sgrub pa'i sems dang ldan pa/ thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du dmigs pa'i tshogs rgya chen po yongs su sgrub pa bskal pa'i me 'bar bas kyang rgyun mi gcad par brtson par bya ba'i sems dang ldan pa/ 'gro ba thams cad yongs su smin par bya ba dang / gdul ba la rab tu zhugs pa/ byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa kun tu bzang po mngon par sgrub pa'i sems dang ldan pa/ yongs su spyad pa'i tshul thams cad la rab tu zhugs pa ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i yon tan yongs su rdzogs par bya ba la dngos po thams cad rnam par sgom pas dngos po med pa'i tshul la zhugs pa'i sems dang ldan pa yin te/

“Noble one, it is when a bodhisattva has a mind focused on understanding the entire ocean of the ways of the Dharma; has a mind single-pointedly focused on fulfilling the aspects of the path to omniscience; has a mind with the intention to accomplish actions that are without fault; has a mind focused on purifying the entire ocean of the ways of bodhisattva samādhis; has a mind that completes the attainment of bodhisattva qualities; has a mind that attains the display of all the aspects[1694] of the bodhisattva path; has a mind that has continuous[1695] diligence, like the fire that burns at the end of a kalpa, in attaining the vast accumulation[1696] focused on omniscience; has a mind that accomplishes the completely good[1697] bodhisattva conduct that is engaged in ripening and guiding all beings; and has a mind that enters into the ways of the nonexistence of things through meditation on all things in completing the qualities of a bodhisattva and engaging in all the ways of conduct.

Here the enlightening beings’ minds are turned to meditation according all the principles of the teaching, dedicated to fulfilling all aspects of the path of omniscience, intent on practicing impeccable actions, bent on purification of the ocean of all concentration methods of enlightening beings, determined to practice and perfect all qualities of enlightening beings, intent on accomplishing all elements of the path of enlightening beings, energetically striving for omniscience, like the fire that burns ceaselessly through an eon of destruction, determined to accomplish the infinite variety of practices of enlightening beings aimed at guiding all sentient beings to perfection; in terms of all practical techniques and accomplishments of perfect qualities of enlightening beings they enter into the means of realization of all methods of cultivation and meditation.
rigs kyi bu/ 'di ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i skye ba gsum pa chos kyi tshul la nges par rtogs pas gzhag pa'i sbyor ba'i tshul mngon du gyur pa 'byung ba'i snying po zhes bya ba'o/ /
“Noble one, that is the third birth of bodhisattvas, called the essence of the origin of the perception that is established in certainty in the ways of the Dharma.
rigs kyi bu/ de la byang chub sems dpa'i skye ba bzhi pa dus gsum snang bar bya ba'i lhag pa'i bsam pa rnam par dag pa'i snying po zhes bya ba gang zhe na/
“Noble one, what is the fourth birth of a bodhisattva, called the essence of the pure, superior motivation that illuminates the three times?
“What is enlightening beings’ birth as offspring of purification of the intent in viewing past, present, and future?

rigs kyi bu/ 'di la byang chub sems dpa' lhag pa'i bsam pa'i dbyings las gya nom par yongs su dag pa yin/ sangs rgyas kyi byang chub la snang ba rab tu thob pa yin/ byang chub sems dpa'i tshul rgya mtsho la rab tu zhugs pa yin/ bsam pa brtan pa rdo rje'i khams lta bus yongs su zin pa'i sems dang ldan pas shin tu brtan pa yin/ srid pa'i lam gyi rgyud du skye ba las phyin phyogs su phyogs pa yin/ de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi rnam par 'phrul pa yongs su grub par bya ba la mngon du gyur pa yin/ byang chub sems dpa'i dbang po rnam par spel ba la khyad par du 'bogs pa rab tu thob pa yin/ lhag pa'i bsam pa shin tu 'od gsal bar bya ba'i phyir/ sems shin tu dge ba yin/ smon lam brtan zhing rgya che ba rnam par 'phel bar bya ba la mi g.yo ba yin/ sgrib pa thams cad kyi ri rnam par gtor ba'i phyir de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyis yang dag par dgongs pa yin/ 'gro ba thams cad nye bar 'tsho bas mgon du gyur pa yin te/

“Noble one, it is when a bodhisattva has purified the element of excellent, superior motivation; has attained the illumination of the enlightenment of buddhahood, has entered the ocean of the ways of a bodhisattva, has stability through having a mind that possesses the vajra element of a stable motivation, has turned away[1698] from rebirth in all states of existence, has turned toward the accomplishment of the miraculous manifestations of all the tathāgatas, has gained the special attainment for the increase of the faculties[1699] of a bodhisattva, has a virtuous mind in order to illuminate the superior motivation, is unshakable in increasing firm, vast prayers; is focused on[1700] all the tathāgatas in order to destroy the mountain of all kleśas, and is a protector through taking care of all beings.

Here enlightening beings become pure in the element of intent; they come into the range of the enlightenment of buddhas; they enter the ocean of methods of enlightening beings; their minds are firm, governed by an intent as strong as steel; they are aloof from all forms of existence; they are attentive to the accomplishments of miracles of all buddhas; they gain higher direction so as to increase the keenness of awakening faculties; they become noble-minded, so that their will becomes clear; they become unshakable, so that they develop their firm great vows; they are kept in mind by the buddhas, so that they break through all barriers; they become refuges relied upon by all sentient beings.
rigs kyi bu/ 'di ni/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi byang chub sems dpa'i skye ba bzhi pa dus gsum snang bar bya ba'i lhag pa'i bsam pa rnam par dag pa'i snying po zhes bya ba'o/ /
“Noble one, that is the fourth birth of a bodhisattva, called the essence of the pure, superior motivation that illuminates the three times.
rigs kyi bu/ de la byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi byang chub sems dpa'i skye ba lnga pa kun nas snang ba'i 'od kyi snying po zhes bya ba gang zhe na/
“Noble one, what is the fifth birth of a bodhisattva, called the essence of all-illuminating light?
“What is enlightening beings’ birth as offspring of the light of universal awareness?

rigs kyi bu/ 'di la byang chub sems dpa' 'gro ba thams cad yongs su smin par bya ba dang / gdul ba la rab tu zhugs pas sbyor ba phun sum tshogs pa yin/ sbyin pa lhug par gtong bas dngos po'i 'du shes thams cad las gyen du 'phags pa yin/ tshul khrims mtha' yas pas mtha' las rgal bar rnam par dag pa yin/ sangs rgyas kyi chos thams cad la bzod pa'i snang ba rab tu thob pas de bzhin gshegs pa'i yul la gnas pa'i bzod pa dang ldan pa yin/ thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du yangs par 'byung ba la zhugs pas brtson 'grus chen po dang ldan pa yin/ sgo kun tu lta ba'i ting nge 'dzin gyi dkyil 'khor rnam par dag pas bsam gtan la rab tu brtson pa yin/ chos snang ba thams cad rab tu thob pas shes rab kyi mthu'i 'od dang ldan pa yin/ sangs rgyas blta ba rgya mtsho rnam par dmigs par bya ba la zhugs pas thogs pa med pa'i mig dang ldan pa yin/ 'jig rten thams cad yongs su tshim par byed pas chos thams cad kyi de kho na nyid la dbang sgyur bas smos pa yin/ chos kyi tshul yang dag pa ji lta ba bzhin du thob par bya ba la rab tu brtson pa yin te/

“Noble one, it is when a bodhisattva has perfect application because of engaging in ripening and guiding all beings, has unlimited generosity because of transcending all conceptions of things, has endless purity because of limitless correct conduct, has the patience that is from within the scope of the tathāgatas because of attaining the illumination of the patience toward phenomena of all the buddhas, has great diligence because of engaging in the arising of omniscience,[1701] has dedication to dhyāna because of purifying the domain of knowledge of every entrance to samādhi, has the light of diligence in wisdom because of attaining the illumination of all Dharmas, has unimpeded vision because of engaging in the perception of the ocean of visions of the buddhas, has power over the nature of all phenomena because of bringing satisfaction to all worlds, and has perfect application because of correct attainment of the way of the Dharma.

Here the enlightening beings become fully engaged in the effort to guide all sentient beings to perfection. They become free from any notion of things, having let go and relinquished all. They become perfectly pure and self-controlled, dwelling in the sphere of those who arrive at Thusness. They become tolerant, having attained the light of acceptance of all teachings of buddhas. They become greatly energetic, accomplishing right emancipation everywhere. They become released through meditation, having purified the sphere of knowledge of all-sided concentration. They become radiant with the energy of transcendent wisdom, having attained awareness of all truths. They become unimpeded in vision, perceiving the manifestations of the ocean of vision of buddhas. They manifest the total potential of the reality of all things, satisfying all beings. They become engrossed in the attainment of truth.
rigs kyi bu/ 'di ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i rnams kyi byang chub sems dpa'i skye ba lnga pa kun nas snang ba'i 'od kyi snying po zhes bya ba'o/ /
“Noble one, that is the fifth birth of a bodhisattva, called the essence of all-illuminating light.
rigs kyi bu/ de la byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi byang chub sems dpa'i skye ba drug pa de bzhin gshegs pa'i rigs kyi rgyud du 'byung ba'i snying po zhes bya ba gang zhe na/
“Noble one, what is the sixth birth of a bodhisattva, called the essence of the origin of the lineage of the tathāgata family?
“What is enlightening beings’ birth as offspring of the family of all buddhas?

rigs kyi bu/ 'di la byang chub sems dpa' de bzhin gshegs pa'i rigs su byung ba yin/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i rgyud du skyes pa yin/ tshul gyi sgo thams cad la shin tu grub pa yin/ 'das pa dang / ma byon pa dang / da ltar byung ba'i de bzhin gshegs pa rnams kyi smon lam chen po la rnam par dag pa yin/ de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi dge ba'i rtsa ba la rang bzhin gcig pa'i dge ba'i rtsa bar gyur pa yin/ sangs rgyas thams cad dang lus gcig tu gyur pa yin/ chos dkar pos 'jig rten gzhan du 'gro ba yin/ sangs rgyas kyi byin gyi rlabs yongs su bstan pa'i ting nge 'dzin la bdag nyid che ba'i chos kyis rnam par spyod pa yin/ dus la ji ltar 'bab pa bzhin du sems can rnam par dag par bya ba'i chos la zhugs pa yin/ sangs rgyas kyi chos yongs su dris pa la spobs pa rgyun mi 'chad pa yin te/

“Noble one, it is when a bodhisattva is born into the family of the tathāgatas; is born into the lineage of the tathāgatas; accomplishes every entranceway into the Dharma of the buddhas;[1702] becomes purified in the great prayers of all past, future, and present tathāgatas; has roots of merit that have the same nature as the roots of merit of all tathāgatas; has the same body as all buddhas; goes to other worlds through having good qualities; practices the greatness of the Dharma in the samādhi that has the vision of the blessing of the buddhas; and when the time comes engages in the Dharma that purifies beings with uninterrupted eloquence that asks Dharma questions.

Here the enlightening beings are born in the family of buddhas, born into the lineage of buddhas. They become accomplished in the methods of all buddha teaching and pure in the great vows of the buddhas of past, present, and future. Their roots of goodness become one with the roots of goodness of all buddhas, and they become one body with all buddhas. They go beyond the world by pure qualities. They come to abide in the state of a great being, in absorption in the sight of the power of buddhas. They carry out the means of purifying beings according to the time and are tireless in answering questions about the ways of enlightenment.
rigs kyi bu/ 'di ni/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi byang chub sems dpa'i skye ba drug pa de bzhin gshegs pa'i rigs kyi rgyud du 'byung ba'i snying po zhes bya ba'o/ /
“Noble one, that is the sixth birth of a bodhisattva, called the essence of the origin of the lineage of the tathāgata family.
rigs kyi bu/ de la byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi byang chub sems dpa'i skye ba bdun pa de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi stobs kyi 'od snang ba'i rgyan gyi snying po zhes bya ba gang zhe na/
“Noble one, what is the seventh birth of a bodhisattva, called the essence of the adorning light that illuminates the strengths of the buddhas?
“What is enlightening beings’ birth as offspring of the array of lights of the manifestation of powers of buddhas?

rigs kyi bu/ 'di la byang chub sems dpa' sangs rgyas kyi stobs la 'jug pa'i snang bas sangs rgyas kyi zhing du 'gro ba las phyir mi ldog go / byang chub sems dpa'i yon tan rgya mtsho las phyir mi 'gyur ro/ / chos thams cad sgyu ma'i rnam pa ltar yang dag pa ji lta ba bzhin du shes par bya ba la gnas pas yongs su yi chad par mi 'gyur ro/ / 'jig rten thams cad rmi lam lta bur rab tu rtogs par byed do/ / gzugs su rnam par dmigs pa'i gnas thams cad gzugs brnyan lta bur mngon par sgrub bo/ / mngon par shes pas rnam par 'phrul pa sprul pa lta bu la dbang rab tu thob par byed do/ / srid pa thams cad du skye ba grib ma lta bur gdod rab tu ston to/ / de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi chos kyi 'khor lo sgra brnyan lta bur rab tu shes so/ / thabs kyi tshul don sna tshogs dang ldan pa la rab tu brtson pas chos kyi dbyings kyi tshul rab tu bstan pa la pha rol tu phyin pa'i dam pa thob pa yin te/

“Noble one, it is when a bodhisattva goes irreversibly to buddha realms because of the radiance of entering the strengths of buddhahood, is irreversible from the ocean of the qualities of a bodhisattva, is never disheartened because of correctly knowing the illusory nature of all phenomena, realizes that all worlds are like dreams, attains the state of perceiving forms as being like reflections, gains the power over miracles through higher cognitions that are like illusory manifestations, teaches that the gateways into rebirths in all existence are like shadows, knows that the wheels of Dharma of all tathāgatas are like echoes, and attains the supreme perfection of teaching the ways of the Dharma through dedication to the ways[1703] of methods and various meanings.

Here enlightening beings, within range of entry into the powers of buddhas, do not regress in their travels to buddha-lands, and do not backslide in their approach to the ocean of various virtues of enlightening beings. They are not frightened by the knowledge that all things are really illusory, and they know all worlds are like dreams. They effect the magical manifestation of all forms, like reflections, and they attain mastery of the miraculous effects of mystic knowledge, like emanations. They show their faces like shadows or reflected images in all states of being. They know all buddhas’ teachings are like echoes, and they attain supreme perfection of explanation of the principles of the reality realm, teaching through the use of various meanings and methods.
rigs kyi bu/ 'di ni/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi byang chub sems dpa'i skye ba bdun pa de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi stobs kyi 'od snang ba'i rgyan gyi snying po zhes bya'o/ /
“Noble one, that is the seventh birth of a bodhisattva, called the essence of the adorning light that illuminates the strengths of the buddhas.
rigs kyi bu/ de la byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi byang chub sems dpa'i skye ba brgyad pa ye shes kyi sgo kun nas rnam par dpyad pas yongs su 'grub par 'byung ba'i snying po zhes bya ba gang zhe na/
“Noble one, what is the eighth birth of a bodhisattva, called the essence of the origin of the accomplishment through the complete analysis of the entrances into knowledge?
“What is enlightening beings’ birth as offspring of consummation of contemplation of the ways to omniscience?

rigs kyi bu/ 'di la byang chub sems dpa' gzhon nur gyur cing byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par dgod pa la rnam par gnas pa yin te/ de la gnas nas thams cad mkhyen pa nyid ye shes kyi tshul la rnam par dpyod do/ / ye shes kyi tshul gyi sgo re re la yang byang chub sems dpa'i spyod yul tshad med par yongs su ston pas bskal pa tshad med par zad par 'gyur ro/ / byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin thams cad la'ang pha rol tu phyin pa'i dam pas dbang du 'gyur te/ sems kyi skad cig re re zhing sems kyi skad cig thams cad la yang phyogs bcu'i sangs rgyas kyi zhing brjod du med pa dag na bzhugs pa'i de bzhin gshegs pa rnams kyi zhabs kyi drung du skyes te/ dmigs pa tha mi dad pas tha mi dad pa'i ting nge 'dzin la snyoms par 'jug go / tha mi dad pa'i chos rnams la tha dad pa'i ye shes kyi dbang yongs su ston to/ / dmigs pa brjod du med pa dag kyang bsgribs pa med pa'i dbyings yongs su non par byed do; ; dmigs pa chung dus kyang mtha' yas pas brtan pa'i sa la yongs su 'jug go / chos nyid tshad med pa yang chung ba'am/ che bar khong du chud par byed do/ / 'jig rten thams cad kyang rnam par dmigs pa dang / mnyam par rab tu rtogs par byed do/ / chos kyi dmigs pa thams cad dang / rnam par shes pa'i rgyud thams cad kyang sgom pas khong du chud par byed do;

“Noble one, it is when a bodhisattva becomes a youth and maintains the appearance of a bodhisattva and, remaining in that way, analyzes the ways of omniscient knowledge; manifests measureless fields of bodhisattva activity throughout countless kalpas within each gateway to the ways of knowledge; attains the ultimate perfection of power over all bodhisattva samādhis; in each instant of mind, in all instants of mind, is born in the presence of the tathāgatas who reside in countless buddha realms in the ten directions; rests in undifferentiated samādhi with undifferentiated foci; manifests the power of undifferentiated knowledge in undifferentiated[1704] phenomena; has arrived at the state without obscuration[1705] even though there are infinite objects of perception; has entered the level of infinite manifestations through the smallest objects of perception; discerns endless small and great natures; comprehends all worlds as being the same as mentations; and comprehends, through meditation, all perceived phenomena and all the continuums of mentations.

Here the enlightening beings, like children, become established in the state of enlightening beings, where they contemplate the way to omniscience. In each medium of the way of knowledge they will travel for measureless eons defining the infinite realm of enlightening beings, and they become masters of all concentrations of enlightening beings, attaining supreme perfection. In each and every moment of awareness they appear in the presence of the buddhas in untold buddha-lands in the ten directions. They attain holistic concentration on differentiated objects, and show mastery of distinct knowledge of inseparable things. They enter the realm of no object in boundless objects. They enter the stage of endless definition of minute objects, and they know the immeasurable nature of things as small or large. They realize all worlds are equally definitions of consciousness, and they understand all objects and all modes of making them known, by means of meditation.
rigs kyi bu/ 'di ni/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi byang chub sems dpa'i skye ba brgyad pa ye shes kyi sgo kun nas rnam par dpyad pas yongs su 'grub pa 'byung ba'i snying po zhes bya ba'o/ /
“Noble one, that is the eighth birth of a bodhisattva, called the essence of the origin of the accomplishment through the complete analysis of the entrances into knowledge.
rigs kyi bu/ de la byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi byang chub sems dpa'i skye ba dgu pa chos kyi dbyings sprul pas brgyan par byed pa'i snying po zhes bya ba gang zhe na/
“Noble one, what is the ninth birth of a bodhisattva, called the essence of the display of emanations throughout the realm of phenomena?
“What is enlightening beings’ birth as offspring of manifestation of emanations throughout the universe?

rigs kyi bu/ 'di la byang chub sems dpa' sems kyi skad cig thams cad la rgyan sna tshogs dang / rgyan du mar ldan pa'i sangs rgyas kyi zhing byin gyis rlob ste/ sprul pa thams cad la mi 'jigs pa'i pha rol tu phyin pa'i dam pa thob pa yin/ sangs rgyas kyi sprul pa thams cad la shin tu mkhas par gyur pa yin/ chos kyi sprul pa la mi 'jigs pa rnam par dag pa yin/ chos kyi dbyings dam pa chags pa med pa'i spyod yul dang ldan pa yin/ bsam pa ji bzhin du sems can gyi lus rnam par dmigs par bya ba'i byin gyi rlabs la mkhas pa yin/ sems can gdul ba mkhas pa bsam gyis mi khyab pa dang ldan pa yin/ spyod pa sna tshogs kyis mngon par 'tshang rgya ba yongs su ston pa yin/ thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi lam sgrib pa med pa mngon par sgrub pa la mkhas pa yin/ de'i rgyud kyi chos kyi 'khor lo bskor ba la mkhas pa yongs su ston pa yin/ sems can mtha' dang dbus med pa gdul ba'i thabs mngon par sgrub pa la mkhas pa yin/ rnam par snang mdzad kyi ye shes dbyig tu bya ba'i mdzod dang ldan pas sems can gdul ba'i dus la bab na rtag tu sta gon du gnas pa yin te/

“Noble one, it is when a bodhisattva in each instant of mind consecrates buddha realms with various displays and many displays, attains the ultimate perfection of fearlessness in all[1706] manifestations, is skilled in the manifestations of buddhas, has pure fearlessness in the manifestations of the Dharma, possesses an unimpeded field of activity in the realm of the Dharma, is skilled in the empowerment of perceived bodies of beings[1707] in accordance with the aspirations of others, has inconceivable skill in guiding beings; manifests buddhahood through various kinds of conduct, is skilled in accomplishing the unobscured path to omniscience and thereupon manifests skill in turning the wheel of the Dharma, is skilled in accomplishing methods for guiding a vast extent of beings without end or middle, and is always prepared for guiding beings when the time has come through the treasure of a wealth of illuminating wisdom.

Here the enlightening beings set up variously arrayed buddha-lands everywhere in an instant of thought. They become perfectly expert in creating emanational beings, skilled in producing emanational buddhas, and expert in creating projections of the Teaching. Their sphere of action is the unobstructed cosmos of realities; they become able to produce manifestations of all kinds of bodies according to the mentalities of those they are dealing with, and arrive at the skill to guide unthinkable numbers of sentient beings. They show enlightenment through various practices, are skilled in accomplishing the unobstructed path of omniscience, and thereupon demonstrate the ability to turn the wheel of the Teaching. They become skilled in accomplishing an infinite variety of means of guiding sentient beings; they are able to guide sentient beings with proper timing, and are always absorbed in the mother lode of illuminating knowledge.
rigs kyi bu/ 'di ni/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi byang chub sems dpa'i skye ba dgu pa chos kyi sprul pas brgyan par byed pa'i snying po zhes bya ba'o; ;
“Noble one, that is the ninth birth of a bodhisattva, called the essence of the display of emanations throughout the realm of phenomena.
rigs kyi bu/ de la byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi byang chub sems dpa'i skye ba bcu pa de bzhin gshegs pa'i sa yongs su gnon pa'i shugs drag po'i snying po zhes bya ba gang zhe na/
“Noble one, what is the tenth birth of a bodhisattva, called the essence of the power of ascending to the level of the tathāgatas?
“What is enlightening beings’ birth as offspring of momentum going into the stage of the enlightened?

'di la byang chub sems dpa' dus gsum gyi de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad dang rang bzhin gcig pa'i yul la dbang bskur ba yin te/ 'jig rten gyi khams thams cad 'dab chags pa'i yul la rab tu 'jug pa yin/ sems can thams cad kyi sngon gyi mtha' dang / phyi ma'i mtha'i shi 'pho ba dang / skye ba'i sems rgyun chags par 'byung ba'ang rab tu shes so/ / byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi ye shes 'dab chags pa'i yul yang rab tu shes so/ / 'das pa dang / ma byon pa dang / da ltar byung ba'i sangs rgyas thams cad kyi mngon par rdzogs par 'tshang rgya ba 'dab chags pa yang rab tu shes so/ / chos thams cad kyi rgyud 'dab chags pa la mkhas par bya ba yang rab tu shes so; ; bskal pa 'jig pa dang 'du ba thams cad kyi sngon gyi mtha' dang / phyi ma'i mtha' dang / da ltar byung ba rnams kyang ming dang bcas/ sa tshigs dang bcas par 'dab chags par rab tu shes so/ / sems can tshul ji lta bur yongs su smin par byas pa dang / dus la gang du 'bab pa rnams la mngon par rdzogs par 'tshang rgya ba'i rgyan dang / rnam par 'tshang rgya bas gdul bar bya ba yongs su bstan pa'i phyin gyi rlabs kyi ye shes kyang mngon par sgrub bo/ / sangs rgyas byung ba thams cad mngon par 'tshang rgya ba'i drung du nye bar 'gro zhing chos kyi 'khor lo bskor ba la mkhas pa'i tshul 'dab chags pa yang sems can gyi khams mtha' dang dbus med pa gdul ba'i thabs mngon par sgrub pa la mkhas pas yongs su ston te/

“Noble one, it is when a bodhisattva is established in the field that is the single nature of all the tathāgatas in the three times; comprehends the field of the succession of all world realms; knows the successive arising of the minds of all beings in their deaths and rebirths in the past and in the future; knows the fields of the successive conduct[1708] and knowledge of all bodhisattvas; knows the successive attainment of buddhahood of all the buddhas in the past, future, and present; knows the successive skillfulness in the presentation of all the Dharma; knows the successive destruction and formation of all kalpas in the past, future, and present, together with their names and their details; attains the knowledge of the blessing that manifests the field of the display and enlightenment of buddhahood when the appropriate time has come for ripening beings in the appropriate way; and manifests the successive ways of the skill in turning the wheel of the Dharma on approaching the appearance and enlightenment of all buddhas through skill in accomplishing the methods for guiding a vast extent of realms of beings without end or middle.

Here enlightening beings are initiated into the realm of oneness of all buddhas of all times, and they enter into the perspective of continuity of all worlds. They know the continuous generation of mind of all beings in their past and future goings and comings. They know the continuum of action and knowledge of all enlightening beings, they know the continuum of enlightenment of all past, future, and present buddhas, and they know the continuum of skill in use of all the teachings. They know the continuum of all past, future, and present ages of formation and disintegration, as well as their names and features. They effect the knowledge underlying showing sentient beings the realm of awakening to the manifestation of enlightenment according to their development, at the appropriate times, and they show the continuity of the means of turning the wheel of teaching leading to realization of enlightenment applied by all buddhas who appear in the world, by skill in carrying out techniques of guiding endless numbers of beings.
rigs kyi bu/ 'di ni; byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi byang chub sems dpa'i skye ba bcu pa de bzhin gshegs pa'i sa yongs su gnon pa'i shugs drag po'i snying po zhes bya ba'o/ /
“Noble one, that is the tenth birth of a bodhisattva, called the essence of the power of ascending to the level of the tathāgatas.[1709]

rigs kyi bu/ de dag ni; byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi byang chub sems dpa'i skye ba bcu rnams te/ de dag gis byang chub sems dpa' rnams skye bar 'gyur ba'o/ / 'byung bar 'gyur ba'o/ / yang dag par sgrub bar byed pa'o/ / yang dag par 'phel bar byed pa'o/ / rab tu rdzogs par byed pa'o/ / yongs su grub par byed pa'o/ / zhing ma lus pa thams cad khong du chud par bya ba'i phyir rgyan gcig gi lhab lhub la rgyan dang lhab lhub kyi rgyud rnam pa sna tshogs byin gyis rlob pa'o/ / sems can gyi khams gdul ba rgyun mi gcad pa'i phyir phyi ma'i mtha'i bskal pa'i mur thug par byin gyis rlabs kyis rgyun chad pa med par byed pa'o/ / chos rgya mtsho thams cad kyi dmigs pa sna tshogs dang / shin tu bstan pa gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa sna tshogs du ma rnam pa tha dad pa dang / chos mtha' yas pa gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa'i rgyun mngon par 'tshang rgya bar byed pa'o/ /

“Noble one, those are the ten births of the bodhisattvas, through which the bodhisattvas are born, appear, attain, increase, complete, and accomplish.[1710] They manifest various adornments, an array of adornments through a single display so as to be comprehended in all realms without exception. They create manifestations continuously in order to continuously guide the realm of beings until the end of all future kalpas. They are realized concerning the various perceptions of an ocean of all the Dharmas, the many various different lineages of the teachings, and the successive transmission of endless Dharmas.

“These are enlightening beings’ ten births as enlightening beings, in which they are born, come into existence, form and develop, are fulfilled and completed; they magically produce offerings of adornments in a single array for awakening in all lands; they produce magical powers for endless eons to guide sentient beings ceaselessly; they awaken to the stream of the endless succession of teachings in the multifaceted succession of particularizations of the various objects of sense in the ocean of all actualities;

sangs rgyas kyi khyu mchog gi mthu phyung ba bsam gyis mi khyab pa chos kyi dbyings kyis klas pa/ nam mkha'i dbyings kyi mtha' gtugs pa yongs su ston pa'o/ / sems can tshad med pa spyod pa rgya mtsho sna tshogs dang ldan pa yongs su smin par bya ba dang / gdul bas yongs su 'dus pa rnams la chos kyi 'khor lo bskor ba yongs su ston pa'o/ / sems can gyi khams thams cad sangs rgyas 'byung ba dang mi 'bral bar byin gyis rlob pa'o/ / chos thams cad kyi sprin dbyangs kyi yan lag rgya mtsho brjod du med pas rnam par dag pa dmigs pa thams cad las rab tu 'byung ba rnam par dmigs par byed pa'o/ / tshad med par rnam par spyad pa la sgrib pa med par rtogs pas khong du chud pa rnams chos yid du 'ong ba'i rgyan thams cad dang ldan pa'i byang chub sems dpa'i dkyil 'khor bsam pa dang / mos pa gang dang ldan pa'i tshul bzhin du sems can rnams la yongs su ston pa'o/ / sangs rgyas kyi sa tshad med pa'i rjes su song ba rnams 'jig rten thams cad yongs su bsgrub pa'i don du chos kyi mdzod mtha' dang dbus med pa rab tu ston pa'o/ /

They manifest the inconceivable supremacy of buddhahood throughout the realm of phenomena and to the ends of space. They manifest turning the wheel of the Dharma in ripening, guiding, and caring for an immeasurable ocean of beings with various conducts. They manifest the appearance of buddhas in all the realms of beings. They perceive the arising within all perceptions of the purity of an indescribable ocean of the aspects of speech of the clouds of all Dharmas. They have realized measureless, unobscured activities and manifest[1711] the bodhisattva field that has the display of the entire, beautiful Dharma. They teach[1712] beings in accordance with their aspirations and wishes. They teach vast Dharma without end or middle so that all worlds may accomplish the approach to measureless buddhahood.”

they show the inconceivable majesty of buddhas throughout the space of the cosmos; they show the operation of the Teaching in the context of the immeasurable oceans of varieties of actions of sentient beings, to develop and guide and care for them; they cause all worlds never to be deprived of the presence of a buddha; they convey the multitudes of all teachings, the purity of the ocean of their innumerable utterances, in all objects of sense; having reached the state of unobstructed infinitude, they produce spheres of enlightening beings beautifully arrayed with all realities; they expound the infinitely various treasury of the Teaching, pursuant to infinite buddhahood, for the purpose of perfecting all beings, expounding it to all beings in accord with their mentalities.”

de nas lum+bi ni'i nags tshal kyi lha mo gzi brjid kyi dkyil 'khor bzang pos dga' ba'i dpal gyis de'i tshe byang chub sems dpa'i chos kyi don 'di nyid gsal bar brjod pa'i phyir sangs rgyas kyi byin gyi rlabs kyis phyogs bcur rnam par bltas te tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la tshigs su bcad de smras pa/

Then at that time, the Lumbinī Forest goddess Sutejomaṇḍalaratiśrī, in order to elucidate the meaning of this bodhisattva Dharma, through the blessing of the Buddha gazed into the ten directions and then recited these verses to Sudhana, the head merchant’s son:

Then Sutejomandalaratishri, goddess of the Lumbini grove, looking over the ten directions by the empowerment of Buddha, spoke these verses to Sudhana, shedding light on the meaning of the ten kinds of birth of enlightening beings:

lhag pa'i bsam pa dri med rnyog pa med pa yis/ / gang rnams rgyal ba blta bas nam yang mi ngoms shing / / rgyal ba kun gyi phyi ma'i mtha' yi rgyan sprin la/ / smon pa'i mkhas pa de dag skye ba'i thog ma gnas/ /

“Those who, with stainless, unalloyed higher motivation, Never have enough of gazing upon the jinas, The wise ones who pray for all-pervading clouds Of displays for all the jinas, are in their first birth.[1713] {1}
Those who behold the buddhas With pure, untainted minds never weary: Undertaking endless offerings to all buddhas, They are established in the first birth, wise.

dus gsum byung ba'i 'jig rten ma lus kun bkang ste/ / zhing dang sems can de bzhin chos dang sangs rgyas rnams/ / sems can dgrol phyir smon lam 'debs pas brgyan pa'i sems/ / de ni bsam gyis mi khyab rnams kyi skye ba gnyis/ /

“Those who pervade, without exception, all worlds, realms, Beings,[1714] and also the Dharma and buddhas in the three times, Whose minds are adorned by the prayer to liberate beings‍— They are in their inconceivable second birth. {2}
Extending to all lands in all times, All things, and all buddhas, Minds equipped with the vow to liberate beings, This is called the second birth of the inconceivable.

gang rnams chos kyi sprin 'thung nam yang mi ngoms shing / / ngoms par rtogs pa'i yid kyis dus gsum chags med lus/ / mkha' dbyings dri med mnyam med sems kyi lus ldan pa/ / mtshungs pa med pa de ni de dag skye ba gsum/ /

“Those who never have enough of drinking the clouds of the Dharma, Who have unimpeded bodies in the three times, and minds with definitive realization, Who have mental bodies that are as stainless as the realm of space‍— They are in this third birth that is unequaled. {3}
Those who tirelessly imbibe the Teaching, Contemplative and unattached, Equanimous in mind and body, pure as space, Attain the third peerless birth.

lhag pa'i bsam pa ri rab brdo rje mtshungs brtan pas/ / thams cad mkhyen tshul rgya mtshor rnam par 'jug byed cing / / gang rnams snying rje chen po'i gang chen mtshor 'jug pa/ / de ni skyes bu khyu mchog rnams kyi skye ba bzhi/ /

“Those who with a higher motivation, like Sumeru, as firm[1715] as a vajra, Are entering the ocean of the ways of omniscience, Who enter into the ocean of great compassion‍— They, supreme among humans, are in their fourth birth. {4}
Those who enter the ocean of great compassion With wills as firm as a diamond mountain, Plunging into the ocean of means of omniscience, Theirs is the fourth birth of the best of people.

gang rnams byams pas phyogs bcu rgyas par yongs bkang zhing / / pha rol phyin pa dri med rgya mtsho mngon bsgrubs te/ / chos kyi 'od 'gyed 'gro ba yongs su smin byed pa/ / de ni skyes bu chen po de dag skye ba lnga/ /

“They who pervade the ten directions[1716] with love, Who accomplish an ocean of stainless perfections, Who radiate the light of the Dharma and ripen beings‍— They are in the fifth birth of great beings. {5}
Those who carry out the oceans of pure transcendent ways, Suffusing all worlds with love, Developing beings by the lights of truth, Theirs is the fifth birth of great people.

chos kyi rang bzhin rab tu rtogs pas chags med sems/ / dus gsum dpe zla med pa'i sangs rgyas rigs byung zhing / / gang rnams chos dbyings rgya mtsho'i tshul la 'jug byed pa/ / de ni mkhas pa de dag skye ba yangs pa drug /

“They who having realized the nature of phenomena have unimpeded minds, Who are born into the family of the buddhas unequaled in the three times, Who enter into the ocean of the ways of the realm of the Dharma‍— They are in this sixth birth of those who have wisdom. {6}
Knowing the nature of things, unhindered in mind, Born in the family of the peerless buddhas of all times, Those who enter the ocean of the reality realm Attain the sixth great birth of sages.

gang rnams chos lus yongs su chags pa med pa'i sems/ / zhing rnams ma lus rang gi lus kyis dgang byas shing / / sangs rgyas stobs rnams ma lus khong du chud rtogs pa/ / de ni mkhas pa rnams kyi skye ba bsam yas bdun/ /

“Those who have a completely pure Dharma body and an unimpeded mind, Who with their own bodies pervade all realms without exception, Who have gained the realization of all the strengths, without exception, of the buddhas‍— They are in the inconceivable seventh birth of the wise ones. {7}
Those whose spiritual body is pure and mind unattached, Who pervade all lands with their own bodies, And enter into all powers of buddhas, Attain the seventh inconceivable birth of the enlightened.

gang rnams ye shes rgya mtsho'i tshul la dbang ldan zhing / / thams cad mkhyen pa'i sgo tshul rnam par dpyod byed la/ / ting nge 'dzin kun tshul gang chen mtsho la yongs 'jug pa/ / de ni de bzhin nyid rten rnams kyi skye ba brgyad/ /

“Those who have dominion over the ways of an ocean of knowledge, Who analyze the ways of the entrances into omniscience, Who enter into an ocean of the ways of all samādhis‍— They are in the eighth birth of those who rely on the true nature. {8}
Those who have mastered the ocean of knowledge, Contemplate the way to omniscience, And enter the ocean of all ways of concentration Attain the eighth birth of those abiding in Thusness.

gang rnams zhing kun 'byams klas yongs su sbyong byed cing / / sems can thams cad yongs smin byed 'dul rab brtson la/ / sangs rgyas rnam par 'phrul pa'i rgyan rnams rnam ston pa; ; de ni grangs pa chen po rnams kyi skye ba dgu/ /

“Those who purify the vast extent of all realms, Who are dedicated to ripening and guiding all beings And manifest the display of the miracles of the buddhas‍— They are in the ninth birth of those with vast fame. {9}
Those who purify spiritual realms, Engaged in perfection of all beings, And show the miraculous effects of buddhas, Attain the ninth birth of the great-minded.

gang rnams rgyal ba'i stobs rnams ji bzhin rab zhugs te/ / thams cad mkhyen pa'i shugs drag yangs pa rnam spel cing / / gang rnams chos dbyings gzhi tshul tha dad chags med pa/ / de ni rgyal sras rnams kyi skye ba bcu yin no/ /

“Those who have entered the strengths of the jinas, Who increase the vast powers of omniscience, Who are unattached to the various ways within the realm of phenomena‍— They are in the tenth birth of the sons of the jinas. {10}

Those who enter the power of the conquerors, Developing the immense force of omniscience, With unhindered knowledge of the differentiation of the cosmos, Attain the tenth birth of the offspring of buddhas.
rigs kyi bu/ skye ba bcu po de dag gis byang chub sems dpa' rnams de bzhin gshegs pa'i rigs su skye'o/ / de ltar na/ 'jig rten thams cad la snang ba byed pa yin no/ /
“Noble one, a bodhisattva is born into the family of the tathāgatas through those ten births. In that way, the bodhisattva illuminates all worlds.
“By these ten births enlightening beings are born in the family of buddhas and become light-makers for sentient beings.
rigs kyi bu/ kho mo ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa bskal pa tshad med par dmigs pa thams cad du byang chub sems dpa'i skye bas rnam par 'phrul ba yongs su ston pa thob pa'o/ /
“Noble one, I have attained the bodhisattva liberation called the miraculous manifestations at the birth of bodhisattvas throughout all the perceptions of countless kalpas.”
“Also, I have attained an enlightening liberation of vision of the birth of enlightening beings in all objects for incalculable eons.”

smras pa/ 'phags ma/ byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa bskal pa tshad med par dmigs pa thams cad du byang chub sems dpa'i skye bas rnam par 'phrul ba yongs su ston pa 'di'i yul ji lta bu zhig mchis/
Sudhana said, “Āryā, what is the scope of this bodhisattva liberation called the miraculous manifestations at the birth of bodhisattvas throughout all the perceptions of countless kalpas?”
Sudhana asked, “What is the scope of this liberation?”
smras pa/ rigs kyi bu/ kho mo ni/ byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi skye ba yongs su lta zhing nye bar 'gro ba'i smon lam yongs su grub pa ste/
She answered, “Noble one, I fulfilled the prayer to see and approach the births of all bodhisattvas.
The goddess said, “I have perfected a vow to go to see all manifestations of birth of enlightening beings. Indeed,

rigs kyi bu/ de ltar kho mo ni/ bcom ldan 'das rnam par snang mdzad kyi skye ba rgya mtsho shin tu yangs pa la 'jug cing khong du chud pa ste/ 'di ltar stong gsum gyi stong chen po'i 'jig rten gyi khams 'di'i byang chub sems dpa'i skye ba khong du chud par byed cing / gling bzhi pa skal pa dang ldan pa'i dzam+bu'i gling 'di'i lum+bi ni'i nags tshal du byang chub sems dpa' 'byung ba yongs su blta ba'i don du sngon gyi smon lam gyis skyes te/ da ltar kho mo 'di ni; byang chub sems dpa' 'byung ba'i rjes su dran pa sgom zhing rnam par spyod do/ / de ltar kho mo 'di na gnas gnas te/ de phan chad lo brgya na bcom ldan 'das dga' ldan gyi pho brang nas 'pho bar 'gyur ro/ / zhes bya ba'i tshe lum+bi ni'i nags tshal 'dir sngon gyi ltas bcu byung bar gyur te/

“Noble one, I have comprehended the vast ocean of births of the Bhagavat Vairocana. Thus, I have observed his births as bodhisattvas in this world realm of a thousand million worlds. Because of my past prayer, I have been born in the Lumbinī Forest of Jambudvīpa, one of the four continents, in order to see the appearance of bodhisattvas. Now I am dwelling here, remembering and meditating on the births of bodhisattvas. In that way, I remain here. After I had been dwelling here for a hundred years, the Bhagavat transmigrated from Tuṣita. At that time, there were ten omens that appeared in the Lumbinī Forest.

I have entered the immense ocean of births of the blessed Vairocana—perceiving the births of the enlightening being in this billion-world universe, when the Blessed One was to manifest birth here in the Lumbini grove, I appeared here by my past vow and stayed here cultivating recollection of the enlightening being’s births, and as I did so I realized that the Blessed One would descend to earth from the heaven of happiness in one hundred years. “Then ten omens appeared in this Lumbini grove.
bcu gang zhe na/ 'di ltar lum+bi ni'i nags tshal 'di thams cad mthon dman med la ngam grog dang ga yang sa med cing mnyam par gnas par gyur pa 'di ni/ sngon gyi ltas dang po byung ba'o/ /
What were those ten? The first omen was that in this Lumbinī Forest everywhere became level without ravines or cliffs or high ground and low ground.
What ten? The whole grove became level, without uneven terrain, without any pitfalls; this was the first omen to appear.

yang lum+bi ni'i nags tshal 'di thams cad gseg ma dang gyo mo med la/ sdong dum dang tsher ma dang bral te sa'i gzhi rdo rje las grub par gyur nas rin po che mang pos yongs su gang bar gnas par gyur pa 'di ni/ sngon gyi ltas gnyis pa byung ba'o/ /
The second omen was that throughout this Lumbinī Forest the ground became made of diamond, was free of pebbles, gravel, pieces of wood, and thorns, and was filled with many jewels.
Then the whole grove became clear of gravel and brambles, and the ground became diamond, strewn with jewels; this was the second omen to appear.

yang lum+bi ni'i nags tshal 'di thams cad rin po che thams cad kyi shing dang / sA la dang / ta la'i phreng bas rnam par 'khrigs pas yongs su brgyan par kun nas gnas par gyur pa 'di ni/ sngon gyi ltas gsum pa byung ba'o/ /
The third omen was that this entire Lumbinī Forest became a place thick with rows of precious trees, sal trees, and palm trees.
Then the whole grove was adorned with rows of trees of all kinds of jewels; this was the third omen to appear.

yang lum+bi ni'i nags tshal 'di thams cad lha rdzas las kyang 'das pa'i spos kyi myu gu kun nas thon pa dang / phye ma thams cad kyi mdzod kun nas thon pa dang / rgyal mtshan thams cad kyi sprin dang na bun yongs su byung ba dang / spos kyi rin po che'i gzugs kyi shing drung kun nas 'khor te rgyan yongs su sbyangs par kun nas gnas par gyur pa 'di ni/ sngon gyi ltas bzhi pa byung ba'o/ /

The fourth omen was that this entire Lumbinī Forest became a place in which grew aromatic seedlings that were superior to divine matter, in which appeared a treasure of all powders, in which arose clouds and mists of all banners, and which was adorned on every side by tree trunks formed of aromatic precious materials.

Then the whole grove was arrayed with adornments set on tree roots made of figurines of fragrant jewels, sending forth sprouts more fragrant than celestial perfumes, growing from mines of aromatic powders, producing multitudes of all kinds of banners and pennants; this was the fourth omen to appear.

yang lum+bi ni'i nags tshal 'di thams cad lha rdzas kyi me tog dang / phreng ba dang / lhab lhub sna tshogs kyi mdzod rnam pa thams cad yongs su rgyas pa dang ldan par kun nas gnas par gyur pa 'di ni/ sngon gyi ltas lnga pa byung ba'o/ /
The fifth omen was that this entire Lumbinī Forest became a place where there appeared, spreading everywhere, a treasury of[1717] various flowers, garlands, and ornaments made of divine materials.
Then the whole grove was filled with all kinds of arrays of garlands of various celestial flowers; this was the fifth omen to appear.
yang lum+bi ni'i nags tshal 'di thams cad kyi shing thams cad la nor bu rin po che dam pa'i mdzod mngon par grub par gyur pa 'di ni/ sngon gyi ltas drug pa byung ba'o/ /
The sixth omen was that throughout this Lumbinī Forest all the trees became treasures of excellent precious jewels.
Then great treasuries of jewels opened up in all the trees in this grove; this was the sixth omen to appear.

yang lum+bi ni'i nags tshal 'di thams cad kyi pad+mo'i tshal thams cad du chu las skyes pa'i me tog thams cad kyang kha 'bus te sa'i gzhi las thon nas chu las mngon par 'phags par gnas pa 'di ni/ sngon gyi ltas bdun pa byung ba'o//
The seventh omen was that in all the lotus beds throughout this Lumbinī Forest, all the flowers that grew from water blossomed, rose up out of the ground, and floated above the water.
Then in all the lotus ponds in the grove, all kinds of jewel lotuses sprang up from the earth in bud and emerged on the surface of the water; this was the seventh omen to appear.

yang 'jig rten gyi khams 'di'i 'dod pa la spyod pa dang / gzugs la spyod pa'i lha'i bu rnams dang / klu dang / gnod sbyin dang / dri za dang / lha ma yin dang / mi'am ci dang / lto 'phye chen po dang / 'jig rten gyi dbang po'am/ 'gro ba'i dbang po ji snyed cig yod pa de dag thams cad kyang lum+bi ni'i nags tshal 'di na thal mo sbyar cing 'khod par gyur te/ 'di ni/ sngon gyi ltas brgyad pa byung ba'o/ /

The eighth omen was that all the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, lords of the world, and lords of beings in this world’s desire realms and form realm gathered with their palms together in homage in this Lumbinī Forest.
Then the various beings of the realms of desire and the realm of form in this world all stood reverently here in this grove; this was the eighth omen to appear.

yang 'dzam bu'i gling gi 'jig rten gyi khams 'di'i lha'i bu mo'am/ klu'i bu mo'am/ gnod sbyin dang / dri za dang / lha ma yin dang / nam mkha'i lding dang / mi'am ci dang / lto 'phye chen po'i bu mo ji snyed cig yod pa de dag thams cad kyang rab tu dga' ba'i yid kyis mchod pa'i rnam pa thams cad lag na thogs shing blag sha'i yal ga la mngon du lta ste 'dud cing phyag 'tshal bar 'khod par gyur pa 'di ni/ sngon gyi ltas dgu pa byung ba'o/ /

The ninth omen was that all the female devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas in this world realm of Jambudvīpa[1718] gathered in this Lumbinī Forest joyfully, holding every kind of offering in their hands, gazing at the branches of the pippala tree, bowing down, and paying homage.
Then the females of all the various kinds of beings came here joyfully with all kinds of offerings and bowed before the holy fig tree; this was the ninth omen to appear.

yang phyogs bcu'i de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi sku lte ba'i dkyil dag nas byang chub sems dpa'i skye bas rnam par 'phrul ba'i sgron ma zhes bya ba'i 'od zer mang po thon te/ lum+bi ni'i nags tshal 'di thams cad snang bar byas nas gnas par gyur te/ 'od zer gyi sgo'i dkyil 'khor de dag thams cad la'ang de bzhin gshegs pa de dag thams cad kyi skye bas rnam par 'phrul ba gzugs brnyan du gyur par snang ba dang / thog ma bltams pa'i rnam par 'phrul ba dang bcas par byang chub sems dpa'i yon tan thams cad kyang sangs rgyas kyi gsung gi dbyangs dang ldan par 'od zer gyi sgo'i dkyil 'khor de dag las sgrar thon cing grags par gyur pa 'di ni/ sngon gyi ltas bcu pa byung ba'o/ /

The tenth omen was that many light rays called the lamps of the miraculous birth of the bodhisattva shone from the circle of the navels on the bodies of all the tathāgatas in the ten directions, and they illuminated and remained in this Lumbinī Forest. And all the qualities of the bodhisattvas, including their miraculous births, were heard emanating, with the sound of a buddha’s speech, from the circular tips of those light rays.”

Then lights called “lamp of the magical manifestations of birth of enlightening beings” emanating from the navels of all the buddhas of the ten directions appeared in this grove; and in all the beams of light, reflections of the magical manifestations of births of all the buddhas were seen, and the sounds of the voices of buddhas telling of the virtues of enlightening beings magically born were heard emanating from the light beams. This was the tenth omen to appear.

byang chub sems dpa' skye ba'i dus la bab pa'i tshe sngon gyi ltas bcu po de dag byung bar gyur te/ de byung bas 'jig rten gyi dbang po thams cad kyis kyang byang chub sems dpa' 'byung bar 'gyur ro/ /zhes bya bar shes so/ /
“Those are the ten omens that appeared when the time came for the birth of the bodhisattvas. When they appeared, all the lords of the world knew, ‘a bodhisattva is going to be born.’

These ten omens appeared when the time of the enlightening being Vairocana’s birth was near, and because of the appearance of these omens the thought occurred to all world leaders that the enlightening being would be born.
rigs kyi bu / de ltar kho mo sngon gyi ltas bcu po 'di dag mthong bas kyang dga' ba'i shugs bsam gyis mi khyab pa rab tu thob bo/ /
“Noble one, in that way they gained an inconceivably powerful joy on seeing those ten omens.
And I, for my part, was flooded with inconceivable joy from seeing those omens.

rigs kyi bu/ gzhan yang lha mo sgyu ma grong khyer chen po ser skya'i gnas nas byung ba'i tshe lum+bi ni'i nags tshal 'dir sngon gyi ltas snang ba chen po bcu byung bar gyur to/ / de dag byung bas sems can tshad med pa rnams thams cad mkhyen pa'i chos kyi snang bas dga' ba'i shugs rnam par 'phel bar gyur to/ /

“Moreover, noble one, when Māyādevī came from the great city of Kapilavastu, ten great illuminating omens appeared in this Lumbinī Forest. When they appeared, they increased within countless beings the power of joy in the light of the Dharma of omniscience.

“Then, as Lady Maya (mother of Vairocana-Shakyamuni Buddha) went out of the city of Kapilavastu, ten omens of great light appeared in this Lumbini grove, by the appearance of which the fervor of joy of vision of the teaching of omniscience grew in countless beings.
bcu gang zhe na/ 'di lta ste/ sa'i steng na gnas pa'i rin po che'i khang pa brtsegs pa thams cad du snang ba rab tu byung ngo/ /
“What were those ten? (1) All of the precious kūṭāgāras upon the surface of the earth shone.
What were the ten? Light appeared in the chambers of all the jewel towers on the ground level;
(2) All the classes of aromatic flowers shone.[1719]
light appeared in the buds of all the fragrant flowers;
rin po che'i pad+mo kha ma bye ba kha bye bar gyur pa'i 'dab ma thams cad las snang ba rab tu byung ste bltams pa legs par bltams so/ /zhes bya ba'i sgra snyan pa yang de dag bas byung bar gyur to/ /
(3) Light shone from all the petals of blossomed precious lotuses, and they emitted the sweet-sounding words: ‘The excellent birth has come to be.’
light appeared in the blossoming buds of all the jewel lotuses, coming from all the petals, and sweet, agreeable sound flowed from them.
phyogs bcu'i byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyis thog ma sems bskyed pa'i snang ba ji snyed cig yod pa de dag kyang lum+bi ni'i nags tshal 'dir snang bar byas te mngon par shar to/ /
(4) The illumination from all the first aspirations to enlightenment by bodhisattvas in the ten directions appeared in and illuminated this Lumbinī Forest.
Also, the light of the first inspiration of the enlightening beings of the ten directions appeared, illumining this Lumbini grove.
phyogs bcu'i byang chub sems dpa' rnams byang chub sems dpa'i sa thams cad yongs su gnon pa'i snang ba'i rnam par 'phrul ba ji snyed cig yod pa de dag kyang lum+bi ni'i nags tshal 'dir byung ngo/ /
(5) The miraculous manifestation of illumination from the bodhisattvas ascending all the bhūmis appeared in and illuminated this Lumbinī Forest.
