Also, the mystical manifestation of light of the enlightening beings of the ten directions entering all the stages of enlightening beings appeared in this grove.

phyogs bcu'i byang chub sems dpa' rnams pha rol tu phyin pa thams cad yongs su sgrub cing ye shes khong du chud pa'i snang ba'i 'od ji snyed cig yod pa de dag kyang lum+bi ni'i nags tshal 'dir byung bar gyur to/ /

(6) All the illumination from the light of the accomplishment of all the perfections and the realization of knowledge by the bodhisattvas in the ten directions appeared in and illuminated this Lumbinī Forest.
Also, the light of the attainment of knowledge on consummation of all the transcendent ways by the enlightening beings of the ten directions appeared in this grove.
phyogs bcu'i byang chub sems dpa' rnams smon lam thams cad la dbang sgyur ba'i ye shes snang ba'i 'od ji snyed cig yod pa de dag kyang lum+bi ni'i nags tshal 'dir byung bar gyur to/ /
(7) All the illumination from the knowledge of the bodhisattvas in the ten directions that has power over all prayers appeared in this Lumbinī Forest.
Also the light of knowledge controlling all vows of the enlightening beings of the ten directions appeared in this grove.
phyogs bcu'i byang chub sems dpa' rnams smon lam rgya chen po mngon par sgrub pa'i ye shes snang ba'i 'od ji snyed cig yod pa de dag kyang lum+bi ni'i nags tshal 'dir byung bar gyur to/ /
(8) All the illumination from the knowledge of the bodhisattvas in the ten directions that accomplishes their vast prayers appeared in this Lumbinī Forest.

phyogs bcu'i byang chub sems dpa' rnams sems can yongs su smin par bya ba dang / gdul bar byed pa'i ye shes snang ba'i 'od ji snyed cig yod pa de dag kyang lum+bi ni'i nags tshal 'dir byung bar gyur to/ /
(9) All the illumination from the knowledge of the bodhisattvas in the ten directions that ripens and guides beings appeared in this Lumbinī Forest.
Also the light of all enlightening beings’ knowledge of developmental disciplines appeared in this grove.
phyogs bcu'i byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyis chos kyi dbyings kyi tshul gyi ye shes khong du chud pa'i snang ba ji snyed cig yod pa de dag kyang lum+bi ni'i nags tshal 'dir byung bar gyur to/ /
Also the light of all enlightening beings’ attainment of knowledge of the principles of the reality realm appeared in this grove.

phyogs bcu'i byang chub sems dpa' thams cad sangs rgyas thams cad kyi rnam par 'phrul ba dang / skye ba dang / mngon par byung ba dang / byang chub tu rnam par 'tshang rgya ba dang / ye shes thugs su chud par mdzad pa'i snang ba'i 'od ji snyed cig yod pa de dag kyang lum+bi ni'i nags tshal 'dir byung bar gyur to/ /

(10) All the illumination from the knowledge of the bodhisattvas in the ten directions that comprehends the miracles of all the buddhas, their setting forth, and their enlightenment at buddhahood appeared in this Lumbinī Forest.
Also the light of all enlightening beings’ attainment of knowledge of buddhas’ projected birth, leaving society, and realization of enlightenment appeared in this grove.
sngon gyi ltas snang ba chen po bcu po de dag rab tu byung bar gyur te/ de dag gis sems can mtha' dang dbus med pa'i sems dang bsam pa'i mun pa thibs po thams cad kyang rab tu snang bar byas so/ /
Those ten great illuminating omens appeared. They illuminated the darkness of mind and thoughts in a vast number of beings without end or middle.
These ten omens of light appeared, by which the darkness of the recesses of the minds of infinite enlightening beings were lit up.

rigs kyi bu/ de la lha mo sgyur ma shing blag sha'i gnas su phyin pa'i tshe 'jig rten gyi dbang po 'dus pa thams cad dang / 'dod pa'i khams kyi lha'i bu lha'i bu'i tshogs dang / lha'i bu mo'i 'khor dang bcas te 'dus pa thams cad dang / gzugs la spyod pa'i lha'i bu dri nga ba med pa thams cad dang / klu dang / gnod sbyin dang / dri za dang / lha ma yin dang / nam mkha' lding dang / mi'am ci dang / lto 'phye chen po'i 'khor dang bcas te tshogs pa/ byang chub sems dpa' la mchod par brtson pa thams cad kyi lus dang / mchod pa'i tshogs thams cad kyang lha mo sgyu ma'i gzi brjid dang / dpal dang / kha dog dang / gzugs kyis rab tu snang bar byas so/ /

“Noble one, when Māyādevī came to the pippala tree, all the gathered assemblies of the lords of the world, the devas of the desire realms with groups of apsarases and retinues of deva maidens, all the assembled devas of the form realms, who were free of odors, and the gatherings of nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, and their retinues who were engaged in making offerings to the bodhisattvas had their bodies and their assembled offerings illuminated by Māyādevī’s brilliance, splendor, color, and form.

“Then, as Lady Maya leaned against the holy fig tree, all the world rulers, the gods and goddesses of the realm of desire, the gods and goddesses of the realm of form, and all the other beings who had gathered there to make offerings to the enlightening being were bathed in the glorious radiance of Maya’s body, and their arrays of offerings were also illumined thereby;
stong gsum gyi stong chen po'i 'jig rten gyi khams 'di na 'od gang ji snyed cig yod pa de dag thams cad kyang zil du brlags par gyur te zil gyis mnan to/ /
All the lights that were in this world realm of a thousand million worlds were outshone and eclipsed.
and all the lights in the billion-world universe were eclipsed by Maya’s light.

lha mo sgyu ma'i ba spu'i sgo thams cad nas byung ba'i 'od dang snang ba dag ni/ 'od gzhan gyis nyams par gyur pa med/ bsgribs par gyur pa med/ chod par gyur pa med/ thogs par gyur pa med de/ phyogs thams cad rgyas par bkang nas sems can dmyal ba'i sdug bsngal thams cad dang / byol song gi skye gnas kyi sdug bsngal thams cad dang / gshin rje'i 'jig rten gyi sdug bsngal thams cad dang / srid pa'i lam gyi rgyud du gtogs pa'i sems can thams cad kyi sdug bsngal thams cad dang / nyon mongs pa thams cad rab tu zhi bar byas te lhag ge/ lham me/ lhang nger gnas par gyur to/ /

No other lights could affect, obscure, prevent, or impede the light and radiance that was emitted from all Māyādevī’s pores. They filled all the directions and ended all the suffering of beings in the hells, all the suffering of beings in birth as an animal, all the suffering in the world of Yama, and all the suffering and kleśas of all beings within the various states of existence, and they remained illuminating, shining, and brilliant.

The lights emanating from all her pores, not repelled by other lights, unobscured, unobstructed, pervaded everywhere, extinguished all the pains of the hells, the animal realms, the ghost realms, and the pains and afflictions of the beings in all states of existence, then remained, shining, illuminating.
rigs kyi bu/ 'di ni/ byang chub sems dpa' skye ba'i rnam par 'phrul pa lum+bi ni'i nags tshal du byung ba dang po'o/ /
“Noble one, that was the first miraculous manifestation at the birth of the bodhisattva that appeared in the Lumbinī Forest.
This was the first miracle attending the birth of the enlightening being in the Lumbini grove.

rigs kyi bu; gzhan yang gang gi tshe lha mo sgyu ma'i lus su stong gsum gyi stong chen po'i 'jig rten gyi khams 'di chud cing gzugs brnyan byung bar snang bar gyur pa de'i stong gsum gyi stong chen po'i 'jig rten gyi khams kyi gling bzhi pa'i 'jig rten gyi khams bye ba phrag brgya'i 'dzam bu'i gling thams cad kyi rgyal po'i gnas ming sna tshogs dang ldan pa sha stag dang / nags tshal gyi mid sna tshogs dang ldan pa sha stag dang / shing drung rnam pa tha dad pa sha stag tu'ang lha mo sgyu ma phyin cing 'jig rten gyi dbang po thams cad kyis yongs su bskor te byang chub sems dpa'i skye ba la stag gon du sdod cing / byang chub sems dpa'i yum gyi ye shes kyi rnam par 'phrul ba bsam gyis mi khyab pas rnam pa 'di bzhin du snang bar gyur te/

“Moreover, noble one, at that time, there appeared situated within Māyādevī’s body[1720] the visual images of this world realm of a thousand million worlds. Within that world realm of a thousand million worlds, in all the Jambudvīpas in its thousand million four-continent worlds, in kingdoms with various names, in forests with various names, Māyādevī went to the foot of various kinds of trees, where she was encircled by all the lords of the worlds, waiting in preparation for the birth of the bodhisattva. This was through the inconceivable miraculous manifestation of the wisdom of the bodhisattva’s mother.

“Then everything in this universe was seen reflected in the abdomen of Lady Maya, and in all the worlds in the universe, at the foot of trees in groves in the capitals of the southern continents Lady Maya appeared just as she did in the Lumbini grove, surrounded by all the world leaders as she was about to give birth to the enlightening being, by the miracle of knowledge which gives birth to enlightening beings.
rigs kyi bu/ 'di ni/ byang chub sems dpa' skye ba'i rnam par 'phrul pa lum+bi ni'i nags chel du byung ba gnyis pa'o/ /
“Noble one, that was the second miraculous manifestation at the birth of the bodhisattva that appeared in the Lumbinī Forest.
This was the second miracle attending the birth of the enlightening being in the Lumbini grove.

rigs kyi bu/ gzhan yang lha mo sgyu ma'i ba spu'i bu ga thams cad kyi ba spu'i sgo re re la yang sngon byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa mdzad pa'i tshe bcom ldan 'das kyis de bzhin gshegs pa ji snyed cig bsnyen bkur te/ rim gror mdzad pa dang / bsti stang dang / bkur stir mdzad de mchod pa de dag thams cad kyang yongs su snang bar gyur to/ / de bzhin gshegs pa de dag gis chos ji snyed cig bstan pa de dag thams cad kyang ba spu'i bu ga de dag nas sangs rgyas kyi gsung gi yan lag dang ldan par ma lus par grags par gyur te/ dper na/ chu'i phor bu chung ngu'am/ gser gyi rdul phra mo'am/ me long gi dkyil 'khor shin tu gsal ba'am/ chu shin tu dang ba la nam mkha'i dkyil 'khor nyi zla dang gza' skar gyi tshogs kyis rab tu brgyan pa dang / sprin gyi tshogs 'brug sgra zab mo 'byin pa can yang gzugs brnyan du gyur par snang ngo/ /

“Moreover, noble one, there appeared within each opening of all Māyādevī’s pores all the tathāgatas that in the past were honored, worshiped, venerated, and offered to by the Bhagavat during his practice of bodhisattva conduct. All the Dharma that those tathāgatas were teaching could be heard sounding from each pore with the aspects of a buddha’s speech. It was like how the reflection of the display in the domain of the sky of the sun, moon, planets, and stars, and of clouds emitting the deep sound of thunder, appear in a small bowl of water, or a particle of gold, or the bright surface of a mirror, or on very clear water.

“Then, from every one of Lady Maya’s pores came visions of how the Blessed One had served buddhas as he carried out enlightening practice in the past, and the teachings expounded by those buddhas were also heard in the buddhas’ voices coming from her pores. Just as the sun, moon, stars, planets, and thunderclouds are seen reflected in a lake, in a piece of gold, in a mirror, or in crystal-clear water,

rigs kyi bu/ de bzhin du lha mo sgyu ma'i ba sbu'i sgo'i dkyil 'khor thams cad la'ang sngon gyi de bzhin gshegs pa'i rnam par 'phrul pa rnams kyang yongs su snang / chos bstan pa'i sgra thams cad kyang yongs su grags par gyur te/
“Noble one, in that way, the miraculous manifestations of the past tathāgatas appeared and the sound of all their Dharma teachings sounded within the openings of all Māyādevī’s pores.
in the same way the past emanations of the buddhas, thundering with exposition of all the teachings, were seen in the pores of Lady Maya.
rigs kyi bu/ 'di ni/ byang chub sems dpa' skye ba'i rnam par 'phrul pa lum+bi ni'i nags tshal du byung ba gsum pa'o/ /
“Noble one, that was the third miraculous manifestation at the birth of the bodhisattva that appeared in the Lumbinī Forest.
This was the third miracle attending the birth of the enlightening being in the Lumbini grove.

rigs kyi bu/ gzhan yang lha mo sgyu ma'i lus thams cad dang / ba spu'i sgo'i dkyil 'khor thams cad las ba spu'i sgo re ra nas kyang zhing ji snyed cig dang / 'jig rten gyi khams rgya mtsho ji snyed cig dang / 'jig rten gyi khams 'byams klas pa ji snyed cig dang / 'jig rten gyi khams kyi rgyud ji snyed cig dang / 'jig rten gyi khams kyi ming du bya ba ji snyed cig tu bcom ldan 'das kyis sngon byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa mdzad de/

“Moreover, noble one, from Māyādevī’s entire body and from each opening of all her pores appeared all the realms, the entire ocean of world realms, the entire vast extent of world realms, the entire multitude of world realms, and all that are called world realms in which the Bhagavat practiced bodhisattva conduct in the past.
“Then, from each of Maya’s pores appeared visions of all the universes, all the worlds, all the lands, and all the places the Blessed One had carried on enlightening practices,
zhing gi gzhi ji lta bu zhig dang ldan par gyur pa dang /
There appeared the surface of the realms;
all the features of the lands,
dbyibs ni/ ci 'dra ba dang /
their shapes;
rgyan ni/ ji lta bu zhig dang ldan par gyur pa dang /
their arrangement;
lhun ni/ ji lta bu zhig dang ldan par gyur pa dang /
their bulks;
ri'i rgyan ni / ji lta bu dag cig yod par gyur pa dang /
their adorning mountains;
grong dang / grong khyer dang / yul dang / grong rdal gyi rgyan ni/ ji lta bu dag cig gnas gnas pa dang /
their adorning villages, towns, regions, lands, and cities;
bza' shing gi ra ba dang / mtsho dang / lu ma dang / rgya mtsho'i rgyan ni/ ji lta bu zhig dang ldan par gyur pa dang /
their adorning parks, rivers,[1721] lakes, ponds, and seas;
nam mkha' dang / sprin gyi rgyan ni/ ji lta bu zhig dang ldan par gyur pa dang /
their adorning skies and clouds;
sems can gyi gnas ni/ ji lta bu zhig yod par gyur pa dang /
their abodes of beings;
theg pa bstan pa ni/ gang dang ldan par gyur pa dang /
the yānas that were taught there;
the means of salvation being taught,
bskal pa'i mid dang grangs ni/ ji snyed cig ces bya bar gyur ba dang /
the numbers and names of their kalpas;
the names and numbers of the ages,
sangs rgyas skye ba ni; ji snyed cig byung bar gyur pa dang /
their births of buddhas;
the buddhas there,
rnam par dag pa ni/ gang du 'du bar gyur pa dang /
their perfect purities;
the pinnacles of purification,
sems can gyi tshe'i tshad ni/ ji tsam zhig dang ldan par gyur pa dang /
the lifespans of beings;
the life span of the beings of those ages,
'jig rten gyi skye gnas ni/ gang du skyes par gyur pa dang /
their rebirths into worlds;
the enlightening being’s births in the worlds,
sems can ni/ ji lta bu zhig dang 'grogs 'grogs pa dang /
the communities of beings;
the people he associated with,
dge ba'i bshes gnyen ni/ ji lta bu zhig la brten brten pa dang /
the dependence on kalyāṇamitras;
the spiritual benefactors he followed,
dge ba'i chos ni/ ji lta bu zhig la brtson par spyod spyod pa dang /
the dedication to virtuous qualities;
the good practices he applied himself to,
chos kyi nan tan ni/ ji lta bu zhig la brtson par byas te/
the engagement in the practice of the Dharma;
the principles he put into action,
byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa spyod spyod pa'i sangs rgyas kyi zhing de dag thams cad kyang yongs su snang bar gyur/
and the practice of bodhisattva conduct in buddha realms.
the buddha-lands in which he carried out enlightening practice,

bcom ldan 'das kyis phyir mi ldog pa'i gnas brnyes nas sngon sku ni/ ji snyed cig rnam par spyod pa ji lta bu zhig / cha byad ni/ ji lta bu zhig / longs spyod ni/ ci dang ldan/ bde ba dang sdug bsngal ni/ ji lta bu zhig sku nyams su bzhes/ sku tshe'i rgyud ni/ ji lta bu zhig dang ldan par gyur te/ sngon byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa spyad par gyur pa de dag thams cad kyang ba spu'i sgo thams cad nas yongs su snang bar gyur to/ /

In all the pores there appeared all the Bhagavat’s attainment of the state of irreversibility, his previous bodies, his conduct, his appearance, what possessions he had, what happiness and unhappiness he experienced, and his lifespans.

the bodies in which he performed enlightening practice and attained nonregression, and what his appearance, surroundings, and pleasant and painful experiences were in his successive lifetimes—all was seen in each of Maya’s pores.

sangs rgyas kyi zhing de dag thams cad kyi skye gnas de dag tu lha mo sgyu ma byang chub sems dpa'i yum du gyur pa dang / byang chub sems dpa'i sku de dag thams cad kyang lha mo sgyu ma'i ba spu'i sgo thams cad du rnam par 'phrul pa'i gzugs brnyan byung bar gyur te;
There appeared in all the pores of Māyādevī’s body images of the various births in all those buddha realms, Māyādevī as the mothers of the bodhisattvas, and all those bodies of the bodhisattvas.
And in each of those lifetimes, Lady Maya was the mother of the enlightening beings. And all the bodies of the enlightening being were seen as a magical reflection in the pores of Lady Maya.
rigs kyi bu/ 'di ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i skye ba'i rnam par 'phrul pa lum+bi ni'i nags tshal du byung ba bzhi pa'o/ /
“Noble one, that was the fourth miraculous manifestation at the birth of the bodhisattva that appeared in the Lumbinī Forest.
This was the fourth miracle attending the birth of the enlightening being in the Lumbini grove.

rigs kyi bu/ gzhan yang bcom ldan 'das kyi sngon sku ni/ ji snyed cig gis byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa spyad pa dang / kha dog ni/ ji lta bu zhig/ dbyibs ni/ ci 'dra ba zhig /cha byad ni/ ji lta bu zhig /da rod ni/ ji lta bu zhig longs spyod ni/ ci dang ldan/ bde ba dang sdug bsngal ni/ ji lta bu zhig sku nyams su bzhes/ sku tshe'i rgyud ni/ ji lta bu zhig dang ldan par gyur pa de dag thams cad kyang lha mo sgyu ma'i lus kyi ba spu'i sgo thams cad la gzugs brnyan du snang bar gyur te/

“Moreover, noble one, there appeared in all the pores of Māyādevī’s body images of the past bodies in which the Bhagavat practiced bodhisattva conduct, their colors, their shapes, their appearances, their forms, their possessions, their happiness and sufferings, and their lifespans.

“Then the physical forms, the means of subsistence, the pleasures and pains, and the life cycles through which the Blessed One performed enlightening practice in the past were all seen reflected in all the pores of Lady Maya’s body.
rigs kyi bu/ 'di ni/ byang chub sems dpa' skye ba'i rnam par 'phrul pa lum+bi ni'i nags tshal du byung ba lnga pa'o/ /
“Noble one, that was the fifth miraculous manifestation at the birth of the bodhisattva that appeared in the Lumbinī Forest.
This was the fifth miracle attending the birth of the enlightening being in the Lumbini grove.

rigs kyi bu/ gzhan yang bcom ldan 'das sngon byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa mdzad pa'i tshe gtang bar dka' ba yongs su btang ste/ zhabs dang phyag yongs su btang ba'am/ snyan dang shangs yongs su btang ba'am/ ljags dang tshems yongs su btang ba'am/ spyan dang / dbu yongs su btang ba'am/ sha dang khrag yongs su btang ba'am/ rus pa dang rkang yongs su btang ba'am/ mkhal ma dang thugs yongs su btang ba'am/ pags pa dang phri yongs su btang ba'am/ phyi nang gi dngos po yongs su btang ba'am/ sras po dang / sras mo dang / btsun mo yongs su btang ba'am/ sku yongs su btang ba'am/ longs spyod rin po che yongs su btang ba'am/ grong dang / grong khyer dang / ljongs dang / yul dang / khams dang / rgyal po'i gnas yongs su btang ba'am/ nor dang / 'bru dang / mdzod dang / bang ba yongs su btang ba'am/ nor bu dang / mu tig dang / be DUr+ya dang / dung dang / man shel dang / byi ru dang / gser dang / dngul yongs su btang ba'am/ rin po che'i rgyan sna tshogs yongs su btang ba'am/ ma la cha yongs su btang ba'am/ khang pa dang gzhal med yongs su btang ba'am/ yo byad yongs su btang ba de ltar gtong ba'i byang chub sems dpa'i sku gzugs dang / rnam pa ji lta bur yongs su btang bar gyur pa dang / len pa de dag kyang rnam pa ji lta bus len par gyur pa dang / sbyin pa'i dngos po rnam pa ji lta bu dag yongs su btang bar gyur pa dang / yul gyi phyogs gang dag tu yongs su btang bar gyur pa dang / de'i ste byang chub sems dpa'i 'khor du gyur pa de dag thams cad kyang lha mo sgyu ma'i ba sbu'i sgo thams cad las gzugs brnyan du snang bar gyur to/ / slong mo ba'i sgra de dag kyang grags par gyur te/

“Moreover, noble one, there appeared in all the pores of Māyādevī’s body images of when the Bhagavat was practicing bodhisattva conduct in the past and gave away that which was difficult to give. He gave away his legs and arms. He gave away his ears and nose. He gave away his tongue and teeth. He gave away his eyes and head. He gave away his flesh and blood. He gave away his bones and marrow. He gave away his kidneys and heart. He gave away his skin and subcutaneous tissue. He gave away all his outer and inner things. He gave away his sons, daughters, and wives. He gave away his body. He gave away his precious possessions. He gave away his villages and towns. He gave away his regions and realms. He gave away his royal capital. He gave away his wealth, grain, treasures, and storehouses. He gave away his jewels, pearls, beryls, conches, crystals, corals, gold, and silver. He gave away his various precious adornments. He gave away his beds and seats. He gave away his houses and palaces. He gave away all his possessions. There appeared the physical forms of the bodhisattva and the way in which he gave, the appearance of those who acquired what he gave away, the appearance of the things that he gave away, the places where he gave them away, and all who were at that time in the entourage of the bodhisattva.

“Then the difficult sacrifices the Blessed One made in the course of his past enlightening practice, relinquishing everything inside and outside himself, the appearances of the enlightening being as a donor, the appearances of those who received his gifts, the gifts themselves, the circumstances of the giving, and the company of the enlightening being, were all seen reflected in the pores of Lady Maya.
rigs kyi bu/ 'di ni/ byang chub sems dpa' skye ba'i rnam par 'phrul ba lum+bi ni'i nags tshal du byung ba drug pa'o/ /
“Noble one, that was the sixth miraculous manifestation at the birth of the bodhisattva that appeared in the Lumbinī Forest.
This was the sixth miracle attending the birth of the enlightening being in the Lumbini grove.

rigs kyi bu/ gzhan yang sngon gyi mtha'i rgyud du byung ba'i de bzhin gshegs pa rnams yum gyi sku nas bltams par gyur pa'i tshe sangs rgyas kyi zhing gi rgyan dang lhab lhub ji snyed cig byung bar gyur pa dang / sems can gyi rgyan rnam par phye ba dang / bza' shing gi rgyan rnam par phye ba dang / me tog dang / bdug ba dang / spos dang / phreng ba dang / byug pa dang / phye ma dang / na bza' dang gdugs dang / rgyal mtshan dang / ba dan gyi rgyan rnam par phye ba dang / rin po che'i rgyal po thams cad rnam par 'phrul pa'i rgyan rnam par phye ba dang / rol mo dang / glu dang / bstod pa dang / sil snyan gyi sgra ji snyed cig byung bar gyur pa de dag thams cad kyang lha mo sgyu ma lum+bi ni'i nags tshal du phyin pa'i tshe lum+bi ni'i nags tshal 'dir yongs su byung bar gyur to/ / mngon par skyes so/ / 'gro bas rnam par dmigs su yod par byung bar gyur te/

“Moreover, noble one, when it was time for the succession of tathāgatas in the past to be born from their mother’s body, there appeared all the arrays and adornments of buddha realms; the arrays of adorning beings; the arrays of adorning trees; the arrays of flowers, perfumes, incenses, garlands, ointments, powders, clothing, banners, and flags; the various miraculous manifestations of arrays of all precious jewels; and music, song, praises, and the sound of musical instruments. When Māyādevī came to the Lumbinī Forest, all of those arose, appeared, and were perceived by beings in the Lumbinī Forest.

“Then manifestations of the lands, the groves, the raiment, the flowers and garlands, perfumes and incenses, banners, pennants, and parasols, all the precious adornments, and the sublime sounds of the music and singing of the times when all the buddhas of the past descended into their mother’s womb, appeared in this grove for all to see and hear.
rigs kyi bu/ 'di ni/ byang chub sems dpa' skye ba'i rnam par 'phrul ba lum+bi ni'i nags tshal du byung ba bdun pa'o/ /
“Noble one, that was the seventh miraculous manifestation at the birth of the bodhisattva that appeared in the Lumbinī Forest.
This was the seventh miracle attending the birth of the enlightening being in the Lumbini grove.

rigs kyi bu/ gzhan yang byang chub sems dpa'i longs spyod lha'i dbang po thams cad kyi gnas kyi rgyan gyi longs spyod las yongs su 'das pa dang / klu dang / gnod sbyin dang / dri za dang / lha ma yin dang / nam mkha' lding dang / mi'am ci dang / lto 'phye chen po dang / mi'i dbang po thams cad kyi gnas kyi rgyan gyi longs spyod las 'das pa 'di lta ste/ rin po che'i rgyal po thams cad kyi khang pa brtsegs pa'i longs spyod dam/ rin po che'i rgyal po'i gzhal med khang gi longs spyod dam/ rin po che'i rgyal po'i dra ba'i longs spyod dam/ rin po che'i rgyal po'i 'bru'i longs spyod dam/ rin po che'i rgyal po'i gzugs kyi longs spyod dam/ rin po che'i rgyan thams cad kyi longs spyod dam/ spos kyi rgyal po thams cad kyi longs spyod dam/ dmigs pa thams cad bzang zhing mthun pa'i longs spyod kyang rung ste/ de dag thams cad lha mo sgyu ma'i rum nas ma 'dres par thon te lum+bi ni'i nags tshal 'di yongs su brgyan cing kun nas gnas par gyur te/

“Moreover, noble one, all that is enjoyed by bodhisattvas, which are the enjoyment of kūṭāgāras made of all kings of jewels, the enjoyment of divine palaces made of kings of jewels, the enjoyment of nets of kings of jewels, the enjoyment of objects made of kings of jewels, the enjoyment of statues made of kings of jewels, the enjoyment of displays of kings of jewels, the enjoyment of all adornments,[1722] the enjoyment of all kings of perfume, the enjoyment of all perceptions that are beautiful and pleasing, which transcend the enjoyment of the displays in the residences of all lords of devas and transcend the enjoyment of the displays in the residences of all nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, and lords of humans, were all emanated, unmixed with one another, from the womb of Māyādevī and were present and arrayed everywhere in the Lumbinī Forest.

“Then all the furnishings of the enlightening being, surpassing those arraying the abodes of the celestial chiefs and the abodes of the chiefs of all other realms of being—diamond towers, diamond mansions, diamond nets, diamond statues, diamond ornaments, all the finest fragrances, and all kinds of beautiful objects—emerged from Lady Maya’s abdomen and arrayed this Lumbini grove.
rigs kyi bu/ 'di ni/ byang chub sems dpa' skye ba rnam par 'phrul pa lum+bi ni'i nags tshal du byung ba brgyad pa'o/ /
“Noble one, that was the eighth miraculous manifestation at the birth of the bodhisattva that appeared in the Lumbinī Forest.
This was the eighth miracle attending the birth of the enlightening being in the Lumbini grove.

rigs kyi bu/ gzhan yang lha mo sgyu ma'i lus las byang chub sems dpa' sangs rgyas kyi zhing brjod du med pa bye ba khrag khrig brgya phrag stong gi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed bcom ldan 'das rnam par snang mdzad dang / sku gzugs dang / sku mdog dang / dbyibs 'dra ba/ mtshan dang / dpe byad bzang po'i rgyan gyis 'dra bar brgyan pa/ 'od 'dra ba dang / 'od zer 'dra ba rab tu 'gyed pa/ tshul dang 'gros stabs 'dra ba/ rtsal dang mthu 'dra ba/ rnam par snang ba'i rnam par 'phrul pa mthun pa/ 'khor 'dra ba; rgyan mtshungs pa mang po yang bcom ldan 'das rnam par snang mdzad kyi legs pa rgya mtsho yongs su brjod cing thon par gyur te/

“Moreover, noble one, from the body of Māyādevī emanated bodhisattvas, as numerous as the atoms in countless quintillions of buddha realms, who had the same body, color, and shape as the Bhagavat Vairocana, the same adornment of the signs and features of a great being, the same aura, the same radiating of light rays, the same way of moving, the same prowess, the same illuminating miraculous manifestations, the same following, and the same displays, and they praised and resembled the ocean of Bhagavat Vairocana’s excellences.

“Then as many enlightening beings as atoms in untold millions of buddha-lands, all of the same appearance as the blessed Vairocana, adorned with similar marks and embellishments of greatness, with similar auras, emanating similar lights, with similar deportment, projecting similar radiance, with similar retinues, and similar adornments, emerged from Lady Maya’s abdomen first, extolling the myriad qualities of the Blessed One.
rigs kyi bu/ 'di ni/ byang chub sems dpa' skye ba'i rnam par 'phrul ba lum+bi ni'i nags tshal du byung ba dgu pa'o/ /
“Noble one, that was the ninth miraculous manifestation at the birth of the bodhisattva that appeared in the Lumbinī Forest.
This was the ninth miracle attending the birth of the enlightening being in the Lumbini grove.

rigs kyi bu/ gzhan yang byang chub sems dpa' bltams par gyur pa'i dus la bab pa dang / lha mo sgyu ma'i mdun du 'og gi rdo rje'i gzhi las sa chen po mngon par brtol te/ rin po che'i rgyal po'i pad+mo chen po rin po che thams cad kyi rgyan gyi dam pa zhes bya ba/ chu ba rin po che'i rgyal po gzhan gyis mi thub pa'i rdo rje chen po las grub pa/ rin po che'i rgyal po 'gro ba rgya mtsho'i nang rim dang ldan pa/ ze ba'i rtse mo rin po che'i rgyal po thams cad kyis brgyan pa/ 'dab ma'i phreng ba sangs rgyas kyi zhing bcu'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyis brgyan cing shin tu rnam par phye ba/ lo ma'i dkyil 'khor rin po che'i rgyal po sna tshogs kyis byas pa; snying po mdzes pa rin po che yid bzhin gyis rnam par dag pa dang ldan pa/ ze ba'i phreng ba rnam par phye ba dang / rin po che thams cad kyi kha dog tshad med pa dang ldan pa/ rin po che'i rgyal po grangs med pa'i dra ba'i rgyan dang ldan pas yongs su yog pa/ rin po che'i rgyal po rdo rje mthu bo ches mi shigs pas lhun kun nas bkab pa/

“Moreover, noble one, the time having come for the birth of the bodhisattva, in front of Māyādevī there rose up from the vajra ground below, breaking through the great earth, a great lotus made of the kings of jewels called an essence that is a display of all jewels. Its essence[1723] comprised the king of jewels, the great indestructible vajra.[1724] All kings of jewels adorned the tips of its filaments.[1725] It was adorned by rows of circles of petals as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha realms. Its surrounding leaves were made of various kings of jewels. Its beautiful[1726] pericarp was composed of pure wish-fulfilling[1727] jewels. It had an array of circles of filaments that had the countless colors of all jewels. An adorning net of countless precious kings of jewels enveloped it. It was covered by a mass of indestructible, powerful, vajra kings of jewels.

“Then, when the time for the birth of the enlightening being had come, the diamond ground in front of Lady Maya split and a great jewel lotus called Calyx Arrayed with All Jewels emerged. Its calyx was unsurpassed diamond, surrounded by all the finest jewels in a dazzling array. It had as many petals as atoms in ten buddha-lands, all evenly arrayed, made of various jewels fringed with pure wish-fulfilling gems, lined with innumerable filaments the colors of all jewels, draped with nets of countless jewels, covered with heaps of indestructible diamonds,

lha'i ris thams cad kyis kun nas bskor ba/ klu'i dbang po thams cad kyis spos chu'i sprin gyi char mngon par dbab pa/ gnod sbyin gyi dbang po thams cad kyis kun nas bskor cing lha rdzas kyi me tog snyim pa nas gtor ba/ dri za'i dbang po thams cad kyis sngon gyi sangs rgyas la rim gror byas pa'i klu'i dbyangs snyan cing yid du 'ong ba'i da ro dang sbyar te bstod pa'i sprin gyis mngon par bstod pa/ lha ma yin gyi dbang po thams cad kyis nga rgyal dang / rlom pa dang / dregs pa thams cad btang zhing shin tu btud de phyag bya ba/ nam mkha' lding gi dbang po thams cad kyis rin po che'i snam bu kun tu spyangs te nam mkha' kun nas brgyan par bya ba/ mi'am ci'i dbang po thams cad kyis byang chub sems dpa'i yon tan yongs su brjod cing rol mo dang / glu'i dbyangs la brtson pa dang / nyams su rab tu bde bas kun nas blta ba/ lto 'phye chen po'i dbang po thams cad kyis shin tu dga' ba dang mos pa skyes pas yongs su blta zhing sgra snyan pa byung ste rgyan gyi sprin thams cad kyi char mngon par dbab pa byung bar gyur te/

“All the lords[1728] of the devas encircled it. All the lords of the nāgas sent down rain from clouds of scented water. All the lords of the yakṣas encircling it cast down handfuls of divine flowers. All the lords of the gandharvas sang clouds of praises to it that had a beautiful sound of melodious songs that had honored the buddhas of the past. All the lords of asuras, forsaking all pride, arrogance, and haughtiness, bowed down and paid homage. All the lords of the garuḍas hung[1729] precious cloths that adorned the entire sky.[1730] All the lords of the kinnaras gazed upon it while engaged in describing with delight the qualities of bodhisattvas with song and music. All the lords of the mahoragas, gazing upon it with great joy and faith, were engaged in emitting beautiful sounds and sending down rain from clouds of every kind of display.

surrounded by celestial chiefs, sprinkled by showers from fragrant clouds by the water spirits, surrounded by the chief demigods clasping celestial flowers in their hands, with the chief celestial musicians appearing singing eulogies of the enlightening being’s past service of buddhas, the chief titans prostrating themselves in respect, freed of arrogance, pride, and conceit, the chief birds trailing jewel streamers, adorning the sky, the chief celestial choristers looking on joyfully singing songs encouraging the enlightening beings, the chief serpents showering adornments, proclaiming their joy.
rigs kyi bu/ 'di ni/ byang chub sems dpa' skye ba'i rnam par 'phrul ba lum+bi ni'i nags tshal du byung ba bcu pa'o/ /
“Noble one, that was the tenth miraculous manifestation at the birth of the bodhisattva that appeared in the Lumbinī Forest.
This was the tenth miracle attending the birth of the enlightening being in the Lumbini grove.
rigs kyi bu/ byang chub sems dpa' skye ba'i rnam par 'phrul pa bcu po de dag lum+bi ni'i nags tshal du byung bar gyur nas
“Noble one, those ten miraculous manifestations at the time of the bodhisattva’s birth occurred in the Lumbinī Forest.
“After these ten miracles had appeared,

de'i rjes la byang chub sems dpa' 'od tshad med bsam gyis mi khyab pa mnga' ba/ blta na btang mi bra ba zhig lha mo sgyu ma'i rum nas bltams te nam mkha'i dbyings rum nas nyi ma'i dkyil 'khor shar ba lta; sprin gyi tshogs rum nas glog gi phreng ba 'gyur ba lta/ ri chen po'i spo rum nas nyi ma shar kha'i sprin go lta/ mun pa stug rum nas sgron ma chen po byung ba lta ste/ mngon par bltams par gyur to/ /

“After that, the bodhisattva, who possessed inconceivable, measureless light that could not be looked at, was born from Māyādevī’s womb, like the disk of the sun from the surface of the sky, like lightning flashing from clouds, like the dawn clouds rising from behind a mountain peak, like a great lamp from a deep darkness.

the enlightening being, manifesting an effusion of inconceivable, measureless light, emerged from Lady Maya’s abdomen, like the sun from the horizon, like lightning from the clouds, like the diffusion of the dawn from the mountains, like a great torch from the darkness.

de ltar byang chub sems dpa' lha mo sgyu ma'i lus las gzugs brnyan ltar bstan pa'i chos nyid dang / rmi lam ltar bstan pa'i chos nyid dang / sgyu ma'i rnam pa'i gzugs rnam par dmigs pa ltar bstan pa'i chos nyid dang / 'gro ba dang 'ong ba med pa'i chos nyid dang / skye ba dang 'gag pa med pa'i 'od rnam par dmigs pa yongs su bstan pa'i chos nyid kyis mngon par 'byung ba yongs su bstan to/ /

“In that way, the bodhisattva emerged from the body of Māyādevī, manifesting in the nature of reflection, manifesting in the nature of a dream, manifesting in the nature of perceiving a form that is a conjured illusion, having the nature of being without coming or going, having the nature of a manifestation of the perception of a light that has no birth or cessation.

Thus did the enlightening being manifest emergence from the abdomen of Lady Maya, by the nature of manifestation of illusory form, by the nature of noncoming, by the nature of manifestation of appearance to the world without origin or extinction.
rigs kyi bu/ de ltar kho mo ni/ lum+bi ni'i nags tshal 'di na gnas shing / bcom ldan 'das rnam par snang mdzad kyi sku tshe'i rnam par 'phrul pa rgya mtsho la lta zhing khong du chud par byed de/
“Noble one, in that way, while residing in this Lumbinī Forest, I see and comprehend the ocean of the miraculous manifestations at the birth[1731] of the Bhagavat Vairocana.
“Thus did I perceive the oceans of miracles attending the birth of the Blessed Vairocana as I sojourned here in the Lumbini grove.
rigs kyi bu/ kho mo gling bzhi bskal pa dang ldan pa 'di na bcom ldan 'das rnam par snang mdzad kyi sku tshe'i rnam par 'phrul ba la lta zhing khong du chud par bya bar gnas pa
“And, noble one, just as I see and comprehend the ocean of the miraculous manifestations at the birth[1732] of the Bhagavat Vairocana in this four-continent world,
And just as I perceived the oceans of miracles attending the birth of this Vairocana in this world,

de bzhin du stong gsum gyi stong chen po'i 'jig rten gyi khams thams cad kyi gling bzhi pa thams cad kyi 'dzam bu'i gling bye ba phrag brgya thams cad na'ang bcom ldan 'das rnam par snang mdzad kyi sku tshe'i rnam par 'phrul ba bye ba phrag brgya la lta zhing khong du chud par byed do/ /

in that same way I see and comprehend a thousand million miraculous manifestations at the birth of the Bhagavat Vairocana in the thousand million Jambudvīpas in all the four-continent worlds in this world realm of a thousand million worlds.
in the same way I perceived the oceans of miracles attending the birth of Vairocana Buddha in all worlds in this universe.

“Just as I see and comprehend the miraculous manifestations of the birth of the Bhagavat Vairocana in a thousand million Jambudvīpas in all the four-continent worlds in this world realm of a thousand million worlds,
And just as I perceived the billions of miracles attending the birth of Vairocana Buddha in all worlds in this universe,

stong gsum gyi stong chen po'i 'jig rten gyi khams thams cad du 'dus pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba'i khongs su chud pa'i sangs rgyas kyi zhing thams cad rdul shin tu phra ba la 'jug pa'i ye shes kyis khong du chud pa dag tu yang sems kyi skad cig re re la sems kyis khong du chud par bya ba re res bcom ldan 'das rnam par snang mdzad kyi sku tshe'i rnam par 'phrul ba sangs rgyas kyi zhing gi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed la lta zhing khong du chud par byed do/ /

in the same way, I comprehend the miraculous manifestations at the birth of the Bhagavat Vairocana that are as numerous as the atoms in a buddha realm with each instant of mind, with the penetration of the mind, in all the atoms contained within an entire world realm of a thousand million worlds, known by the knowledge that enters into the atoms of all buddha realms.

so also did I perceive, in each mental moment, with each penetration of consciousness, as many miracles attending the birth of Vairocana Buddha as atoms in a buddha-world, in the worlds within all the atoms in all universes accessible to knowledge penetrating the atoms in all buddha-lands.

de'i 'og ma'i sems kyis sangs rgyas kyi zhing rdul shin tu phra ba rnams kyi khong du chud pa'i sangs rgyas kyi zhing de dag las sangs rgyas kyi zhing re rer yang de dang mnyam pa'i byang chub sems dpa' skye ba'i rnam par 'phrul pa la lta zhing khong du chud par byed de/
“In the next mentation, I see and comprehend equally the miraculous manifestations at the birth of bodhisattvas within each of the buddha realms contained within the atoms of a buddha realm.
In the next moment I perceived, in each of the buddha-lands in the atoms of a thousand buddha-lands, an equal number of miracles attending the birth of the enlightening being.

tshul de lta bus sangs rgyas kyi zhing thams cad kyi rdul shin tu phra ba'i khongs su chud pa'i sangs rgyas kyi zhing re re dag tu yang byang chub sems dpa' skye ba'i rnam par 'phrul pa thams cad la lta zhing khong du chud par byed kyang rdul shin tu phra ba thams cad kyi rdul re re la zhing gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa'i mtha' rnyed par mi rung ngo/ / zhing thams cad kyi zhing re rer byang chub sems dpa' skye ba gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa'i yang mu rnyed par mi rung ngo/ /

“In that way, although I see and comprehend the miraculous manifestations at the births of bodhisattvas in each of the buddha realms contained within the atoms of all buddha realms, there is no knowable end to the succession of realms in each one of all the atoms, and there is no knowable end to the succession of births of bodhisattvas in each one of all the realms.

In this way, in each of the buddha-lands in the atoms of each buddha-land, I perceived all the miracles attending the birth of the enlightening being, without reaching their end. I did not reach the end of the succession of buddha-lands in each and every atom, or of the miracles attending the birth of the enlightening being in each and every one of those buddha-lands.

ji ltar kho mo 'jig rten gyi khams 'di'i byang chub sems dpa'i skye ba rnam par 'phrul pa thams cad la lta zhing khong du chud par byed pa de bzhin du phyogs bcu'i 'jig rten gyi khams mtha' dang dbus med pa dang / rdul shin tu phra ba thams cad la'ang sems kyi skad cig re re'i sems kyis khong du chud par bya ba re re la byin gyi rlabs rgyun mi 'chad pa'i tshul gyis byang chub sems dpa' skye ba'i rnam par 'phrul ba thams cad la lta zhing khong du chud par byed do/ / de skad ces smras pa dang /

“Just as I see and comprehend all the miraculous manifestations at the birth of bodhisattvas in this world realm, in the same way, in each instant of mind, with the penetration of the mind, through continuous spiritual power, I see and comprehend all the miraculous manifestations at the births of bodhisattvas in all the vast extent of world realms, without end or middle, in the ten directions and in all atoms.”

And just as I perceived all the miracles attending the birth of the enlightening being in this world, so also did I perceive, in each moment of consciousness, all aspects of all the miracles attending the birth of the enlightening being in infinitely many worlds in the ten directions, by application of unceasing power.”

tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis lum+bi ni'i nags tshal gyis lha mo gzi brjid kyi dkyil 'khor bzang pos dga' ba'i dpal la 'di skad ces smras so/ / 'phags ma/ khyod kyis byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa bskal pa tshad med par dmigs pa thams cad du byang chub sems dpa'i skye ba rnam par 'phrul ba yongs su ston pa 'di rnyed nas yun ji srid cig lags/

Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, asked Sutejomaṇḍalaratiśrī, the Lumbinī Forest goddess, “Āryā, how long has it been since you attained this bodhisattva liberation called the miraculous manifestations at the birth of bodhisattvas throughout all the perceptions of countless kalpas?”
Then Sudhana asked the goddess, “How long ago did you attain this enlightening liberation of vision of the miracle of birth of enlightening beings in all objects over incalculable eons?”

smras pa/ rigs kyi bu/ sngon 'das pa'i dus bskal pa sangs rgyas kyi zhing bye ba'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed 'das pa'i pha rol de'i yang pha snga zhig tu 'jig rten gyi khams kun nas rin po che zhes bya bar bskal ba mnyam par bzhag pa zhes bya ba sangs rgyas bye ba khrag khrig brgyad cu byung ba la de bzhin gshegs pa dgra bcom pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas dbang phyug gi yon tan gzhan gyis mi thub pa'i rgyal mtshan zhes bya ba/ mkhyen pa dang zhabs su ldan pa/ bde bar gshegs pa/ 'jig rten mkhyen pa/ bla na med pa/ skyes bu 'dul ba'i kha lo sgyur ba/ lha dang mi rnams kyi ston pa sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das 'jig rtan du byung ngo/ /

She answered, “Noble one, in the past, in times gone by, beyond as many kalpas as there are atoms in ten million buddha realms, and even further beyond, there was a world realm called Samantaratnā in a kalpa called Samāpadyata in which appeared eighty quintillion buddhas. There appeared in that world the Tathāgata Arhat Samyaksaṃbuddha Īśvaraguṇāparājitadhvaja, who was one with wisdom and conduct,[1733] a sugata, one who knows the world’s beings, an unsurpassable guide who tames beings, a teacher of devas and humans, a buddha, and a bhagavat.

She replied, “In the past, as many eons ago as atoms in ten million buddha-lands and even more, there was a buddha named Invincible Paragon of Virtue who emerged in a world called Ubiquitous Jewels in an age in which eighty decillion buddhas appeared.

rigs kyi bu/ 'jig rten gyi khams kun nas rin po che zhes bya ba der gling bzhi pa dbu ma rgyan sna tshogs kyi 'od ces bya ba byung ste/ gling bzhi pa de'i 'dzam bu'i gling gi dbus su rgyal po'i gnas ri rab rnam par dag pa'i rgyan gyi rgyal mtshan zhes bya ba byung ste/ rgyal po'i gnas der rgyal po rin po che 'od 'phro ba'i mig gi 'od ces bya ba byung ngo/ / rgyal po rin po che 'od 'phro ba'i mig gi 'od de la btsun mo rab tu dga' ba'i 'od la dbang sgyur ba zhes bya ba mnga'o/ /

“Noble one, at the center of the world realm called Samantaratnā, there was a four-continent world called Vicitravyūhaprabhā. In the middle of the Jambudvīpa of that four-continent world there was a royal capital called Meruviśuddhavyūhadhvajā. In that royal capital there was King Ratnārcinetraprabha. King Ratnārcinetraprabha had a queen called Suharṣitaprabheśvarā.

In that world there was a central group of four continents called Dazzling Array of Lights, in the southern continent of which was a capital city called Lofty Banner of Pure Adornments, where there was a king named Jewel Flame Eye Light, whose wife was named Queen of Joyous Light.

rigs kyi bu/ dper na/ gling bzhi pa skal pa dang ldan pa 'di'i 'dzam bu'i gling du lha mo sgyu ma bcom ldan 'das rnam par snang mdzad kyi yum du gyur pa de bzhin du de'i tshe de'i dus na gling bzhi pa rgyan sna tshogs kyi 'od kyi 'dzam bu gling du yang rab tu dga' ba'i 'od la dbang sgyur ba zhes bya ba yang bcom ldan 'das de bzhin gshegs pa dbang phyug gi yon tan gzhan gyis mi thub pa'i rgyal mtshan gyi yum du gyur te/ sangs rgyas bye ba khrag khrig phrag brgyad cu bskal pa'i dang po la byung ste/ thog mar byung ba'i bcom ldan 'das de bzhin gshegs pa dbang phyug gi yon tan gzhan gyis mi thub pa'i rgyal mtshan gyi yum du gyur te/

“Noble one, just as Māyādevī became the mother of the Bhagavat Vairocana in this four-continent world, at that time, in that time, Queen Suharṣitaprabheśvarā became the mother of the Bhagavat, the Tathāgata Īśvaraguṇāparājitadhvaja, in the four-continent world called Vicitravyūhaprabhā. He was the first of the eighty quintillion buddhas. She was the mother of the first bhagavat to appear, the Tathāgata Īśvaraguṇāparājitadhvaja.

Just as Maya is the mother of the Buddha Vairocana here, that queen was the mother of that buddha Invincible Paragon of Virtue in that world at that time, the first of the eighty decillion buddhas of the age.

rigs kyi bu/ lha mo rab tu dga' ba'i 'od la dbang sgyur ba de byang chub sems dpa' skye ba'i dus la bab pa dang / bud med khrag khrig brgya stong phrag nyi shu dang lhan cig tu bza' shing gi ra ba chen po 'od kyi dkyil 'khor gser gyi me tog ces bya ba der phyin te/ dbang phyug gi yon tan gzhan gyis mi thub pa'i rgyal mtshan gzhon nu de yang byang chub sems dpa' skye ba'i rnam par 'phrul ba bsam gyis mi khyab pas der bltams so/ /

“Noble one, when the time had come for the birth of the bodhisattva, Queen[1734] Suharṣitaprabheśvarā, together with two hundred thousand trillion women, went to the great park called Suvarṇapuṣpābhamaṇḍala. Prince Īśvaraguṇāparājitadhvaja was born there with the inconceivable miraculous manifestations that occur at the birth of a bodhisattva.

When the time for the birth of the enlightening being came, the queen went to a park called Circle of Lights of Golden Flowers, accompanied by twenty decillion women, and there gave birth to the child Invincible Paragon of Virtue, by the inconceivable miracle of the birth of an enlightening being.

de'i tshe bza' shing gi ra ba chen po 'od kyi dkyil 'khor gser gyi me tog ces bya ba de'i dbus su pho brang brtsegs pa rin po che sna tshogs bzang po las brtsegs pa zhes bya ba byung ste/ pho brang brtsegs pa de'i nang du shing 'dod pa thams cad 'byin pa'i yal ga la 'ju ste lha mo rab tu dga' ba'i 'od la dbang sgyur ba las/ bcom ldan 'das de bzhin gshegs pa dbang phyug gi yon tan gzhan gyis mi thub pa'i rgyal mtshan bltams so/ /

“At that time, there appeared in the center of the great park called Suvarṇapuṣpābhamaṇḍala a kūṭāgāra called Subharatnavicitrakūṭa. The Bhagavat, the Tathāgata Īśvaraguṇāparājitadhvaja was born from Queen Suharṣitaprabheśvarā as she held on to a branch of a wish-fulfilling tree inside that kūṭāgāra.
In the middle of that park was a tower called Brilliant Heap of Pure Jewels, and this was where that queen gave birth to that buddha, holding on to the limb of a wish-fulfilling tree.

de'i tshe bcom ldan 'das de bltams khar ma ma dri ma med pa skyed pa'i 'od ces bya ba sta gon du gnas gnas te/ byang chub sems dpa' de bltams par gyur ma thag tu 'jig rten gyi dbang po rnams kyis spos dri shin tu zhim pa'i spos chu'i bum pa me tog dri zhim zhing yid du 'ong ba sna tshogs mngon par 'thor bas sku bsil te/ de la tshul dang mthun pa'i mchod pa bsam gyis mi khyab la grangs med pa mchog tu bya bas mchod nas ma ma dri ma med pa skyed pa'i 'od kyi bar du bzhag go / ma ma des byang chub sems dpa' pang du blangs ma thag tu de'i mod la ma ma de dga' ba dang / mos ba'i shugs chen po thob par gyur nas byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin yul kun tu lta ba zhes bya ba thob par gyur to/ / de thob par gyur ma thag tu des phyogs bcu'i 'jig rten gyi khams na bzhugs pa'i de bzhin gshegs pa tshad med pa de dag thams cad kyang mthong bar gyur to/ / byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa bskal pa tshad med pa dmigs pa thams cad du byang chub sems dpa'i skye bas rnam par 'phrul pa yongs su ston pa 'di la 'ang shin tu phra ba'i tshul gyis zhugs par gyur te/ de ni/ dper na/ ma'i mngal du zhugs ma thag pa'i rnam par shes pa lta bu'o/ / rnam par thar pa de thos par gyur pas kyang des de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad skye ba'i rnam par 'brul pa yang dag par lta ba'i smon lam chen po yang mngon par bsgrubs so/ /

“At that time, when the Bhagavat was born, the nurse Vimalasaṃbhavaprabhā was in attendance. As soon as the bodhisattva was born, the lords of the world sprinkled him with a vase of scented water that was wonderfully aromatic and with a variety of beautiful flowers so as to cool his body. They made countless inconceivable, supreme appropriate offerings to him and placed him on the nurse Vimalasaṃbhavaprabhā’s lap. The instant that she took the bodhisattva onto her lap, the nurse attained great powerful joy and faith and attained the bodhisattva samādhi called all-seeing. As soon as she attained that, she saw the countless tathāgatas present within the world realms in the ten directions. She entered in a subtle way this bodhisattva liberation called the miraculous manifestations at the birth of bodhisattvas throughout all the perceptions of countless kalpas. This was like the moment when a consciousness enters a womb. Through attaining that liberation, she made the great prayer to see the miraculous manifestations at the births of all tathāgatas.

“At the time of the buddha’s birth there was a wet nurse named Light of Purity standing by, and as soon as the buddha was born, the world leaders bathed him with fragrant water, presented countless suitable offerings of the finest quality, then handed him over to the nurse Light of Purity. As soon as she took him into her hands, the nurse was flooded with great joy and attained an enlightening concentration called ‘sphere of the universal eye,’ by the attainment of which she saw countless buddhas in various worlds in the ten directions, and this enlightening liberation of vision of the miracle of birth of enlightening beings in all objects over countless ages subtly entered into her, just as the consciousness of the embryo enters the abdomen of the mother on the day of conception. By attaining this liberation, she accomplished the great vow to see the miracle of birth of all buddhas.

rigs kyi bu/ de la ji snyam du sems/ de'i tshe de'i dus na byang chub sems dpa'i ma ma dri ma med pa skyed pa'i 'od ces bya ba byung bar gyur pa de gzhan zhig yin pa snyam du sems na ni/ khyod kyis de ltar mi blta ste/ kho mo ni/ de'i tshe de'i dus na byang chub sems dpa'i ma ma dri ma med pa skyed pa'i 'od ces bya bar gyur to/ /

“Noble one, what do you think? If you think that the bodhisattva’s nurse, Vimalasaṃbhavaprabhā, at that time, in that time, was anyone else, do not see her in that way. I was at that time, in that time, the bodhisattva’s nurse, Vimalasaṃbhavaprabhā.
“Now, who do you think the enlightening being’s nurse Light of Purity at that time was? It was none other than I myself who was the nurse Light of Purity.

rigs kyi bu/ de la ji snyam du sems de'i tshe de'i dus na bud med khrag khrig brgya stong phrag nyi shu byung bar gyur pa de dag gzhan dag cig yin pa snyam du sems na yang de ltar mi lta ste/ lha mo khrag khrig brgya stong phrag nyi shu po lum+bi ni'i nags tshal na gnas pa kho mo'i 'khor du gyur pa 'di dag yin no/ /

“Noble one, what do you think? If you think that the two hundred thousand trillion women at that time, in that time, were anyone else, do not see them in that way. They are these two hundred thousand trillion goddesses who now dwell in the Lumbinī Forest and are my entourage.
And who do you think the twenty decillion women were? They were none other than the twenty decillion goddesses who live here in the Lumbini grove, my companions.

rigs kyi bu/ de la ji snyam du sems/ de'i tshe de'i dus na dbang phyug gi yon tan gzhan gyis mi thub pa'i rgyal mtshan gzhon nu'i yum rab tu dga' ba'i 'od la dbang sgyur ba zhes bya ba byung ba de gzhan zhig yin pa snyam du sems na'ang de ltar mi blta ste/ lha mo sgyu ma 'di ni/ de'i tshe de'i dus na rab tu dga' ba'i 'od la dbang sgyur ba zhes bya ba'i lha mor gyur to/ /

“Noble one, what do you think? If you think that Queen Suharṣitaprabheśvarā, the mother of the Tathāgata Īśvaraguṇāparājitadhvaja, at that time, in that time, was anyone else, do not see her in that way. This Māyādevī was at that time, in that time, the queen named Suharṣitaprabheśvarā.
And who do you think was Queen of Joyous Light, mother of the child Invincible Paragon of Virtue? It was none other than Lady Maya here.

rigs kyi bu/ de la ji snyam du sems/ de'i tshe de'i dus na rgyal po rin po che 'od 'phro ba'i mig gi 'od ces bya ba byung ba de gzhan zhig yin pa snyam na'ang de ltar mi blta ste/ rgyal po zas gtsang ma 'di ni/ de'i dus na rgyal po rin po che 'od 'phro ba'i mig gi 'od ces bya bar gyur to/ /

“Noble one, what do you think? If you think that King Ratnārcinetraprabha at that time, in that time, was anyone else, do not see him in that way. King Śuddhodana was at that time, in that time, the king named Ratnārcinetraprabha.
And who was the king Jewel Flame Eye Light? It was none other than this king Shuddhodana.

rigs kyi bu/ de ltar kho mo ni/ de phyin chad du bcom ldan 'das rnam par snang mdzad kyi byang chub sems dpa'i skye ba'i rnam par 'phrul pa rgya mtsho la lta zhing khong du chud par byed pa dang / sems can rnam par 'dul ba'i khyu mchog gi mthus rnam par 'phrul ba rgya mtsho la lta zhing khong du chud par byed pa dang / skad cig thams cad du bral bar ma gyur to/ /

“Noble one, since that time, in every instant I have never been apart from seeing and comprehending the ocean of miraculous manifestations at the bodhisattva births of the Bhagavat Vairocana or from seeing and comprehending the ocean of the miraculous manifestations of his supremacy in guiding beings.

From that time on I was never separated from the Blessed Vairocana, by entry into the ocean of miracles of his births as an enlightening being, and entry into the ocean of miraculous manifestations of his power to guide sentient beings, in every moment of awareness.

rigs kyi bu/ kho mo mi mjed kyi 'jig rten gyi khams 'di na bcom ldan 'das rnam par snang mdzad kyi smon lam rgya mtsho 'byams klas pa las byung ba'i de bzhin gshegs pa rnams kyi sangs rgyas kyi zhing rgya mtsho rdul shin tu phra ba thams cad na yod pa la sems kyi skad cig thams cad du rdul shin tu phra ba thams cad la yongs su 'dul ba'i ye shes kyi mig gis lta zhing khong du chud par byed de/ sangs rgyas kyi zhing de dag tu de bzhin gshegs pa byung brgya mtsho dag kyang lta zhing khong du chud par byed la; de bzhin gshegs pa de dag gi byang chub sems dpa' skye ba'i rnam par 'phrul pa rgya mtsho chen po dag la lta zhing khong du chud par byed pa

“Noble one, in every moment of mind, with eyes of knowledge that encompass all atoms, I see and comprehend within all atoms in this world realm of Sahā an ocean of the buddha realms of the tathāgatas, which have appeared from the vast extent of the ocean of prayers made by the Bhagavat Vairocana. I see and comprehend the ocean of the tathāgatas that are in those buddha realms. I also see and comprehend the great ocean of the miraculous manifestations at the bodhisattva births of those tathāgatas.

“Furthermore, just as in this world I perceived the oceans of lands of Vairocana and the buddhas born of the ocean of the totality of great vows in every moment of thought in all atoms by the eye of knowledge penetrating all atoms, and perceived the ocean of manifestations of buddhas in those lands, and perceived the ocean of miracles of births of those buddhas as enlightening beings,

de bzhin du phyogs bcu'i de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi byang chub sems dpa' skye ba'i rnam par 'phrul brgya mtsho dang / sems can rnam par 'dul ba'i khyu mchog gi mthu phyung bas rnam par 'phrul ba rgya mtsho thams cad la'ang sems kyi skad cig thams cad du lta zhing khong du chud par byed do/ /

“In the same way, in every instant of mind I see and comprehend the entire ocean of the miraculous manifestations of the supremacy of guiding beings and the ocean of the miraculous manifestations at the bodhisattva births of all tathāgatas in the ten directions.
in the same way, in every mental moment I perceived the oceans of miracles of births as enlightening beings of infinite buddhas in the ten directions.

ji ltar stong gsum gyi stong chen po'i 'jig rten gyi khams 'dir rdul shin tu phra ba 'byams klas pa thams cad gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa la 'jug pas byang chub sems dpa' skye ba ma nor par mngon du gyur te/ sangs rgyas kyi yon tan la zhugs par gyur pa

“I perceive without error the births of bodhisattvas through comprehending the succession of the entire vast extent of atoms in this world realm of a thousand million worlds, and I comprehend the qualities of the buddhas.
And just as in this universe, by successive penetration of all atoms, I perceived the buddha-qualities of complete perfect buddhas as they were being born as enlightening beings,

de bzhin du phyogs bcu'i 'jig rten gyi khams sangs rgyas kyi zhing brjod du med pa bye ba khrag khrig brgya stong phrag bcu'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi rdul shin tu phra ba 'byams klas pa thams cad kyi khongs su chud pa'i zhing rgya mtsho thams cad la'ang sangs rgyas 'jug ste/ de dag tu'ang sangs rgyas rgya mtsho shin tu yangs pa la 'jug go / sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das de dag byang chub sems dpar gyur pa'i byang chub sems dpa' 'byung ba'i rnam par 'phrul pa rnams kyang mngon du gyur par blta'o/ / de bzhin gshegs par gyur nas mchod par byed do/ / de bzhin gshegs pa de dag las kyang chos bstan pa nyan to/ / chos la yang gnyer ba'i chos kyis nan tan byed do/ /

In the same way, I comprehend the entire ocean of realms contained within the entire vast extent of the atoms in countless tens of thousands of quintillions of buddha realms in the ten directions, and I comprehend the vast ocean of buddhas within them. I also see the perception of the miraculous manifestations at the bodhisattva births of those buddha bhagavats. I make offerings to them when they become tathāgatas. I hear the teachings that those tathāgatas give. I practice the correct Dharma of their Dharma.”

in the same way I perceived oceans of lands in the atoms of untold decillions of buddha-lands in the ten directions, and perceived the vast oceans of buddhas therein, saw those buddhas as they were miraculously being born as enlightening beings, paid reverence to them as buddhas, listened to those buddhas’ teachings, and practice in accord with their teaching.”

de nas lum+bi ni'i nags tshal gyi lha mo gzi brjid kyi dkyil 'khor bzang pos dga' ba'i dpal gyis de'i tshe byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa bskal pa tshad med par dmigs pa thams cad du byang chub sems dpa'i skye bas rnam par 'phrul pa yongs su ston pa 'di gsal bar bstan pa'i phyir sangs rgyas kyi byin gyi rlabs kyis phyogs bcur rnam par bltas te tshigs su bcad pa 'di dag smras so/ /

Then at that time, Sutejomaṇḍalaratiśrī, the goddess of the Lumbinī Forest, in order to teach clearly the bodhisattva liberation called the miraculous manifestations at the birth of bodhisattvas throughout all the perceptions of countless kalpas, through the blessing of the Buddha, gazed into the ten directions and recited these verses:

Then Sutejomandalaratishri, goddess of the Lumbini grove, elucidating this enlightening liberation of vision of the miracle of birth of enlightening beings over countless eons, looked over the ten directions by the power of Buddha and spoke these verses:
rim gro bskyed cing nga la gang 'dri ba [?]/ / de dag bdag las rgyal ba'i sras nyon cig / rgyal ba'i spyod yul blta dga' zhi ba ste/ / rgyu dang rkyen gyis tshul gyis rnam par bstan/ /

“Son of the jinas,[1735] you have shown respect And have asked a question, so listen to what I have to say. The field of activity of the jinas is a peace that is hard to see And which is manifested through the ways of causes and conditions. {1}
Son of Buddha, listen respectfully To what I say to your question: The realm of buddhas, silent and hard to see, I explain in terms of cause.
zhing rnams bye ba'i rdul phran rab snyed kyi/ / sngon gyi bskal pa bsam gyis mi khyab dran/ / bskal pa'i ming ni snga phyi mnyam zhes bya/ / de la rgyal ba bye ba brgyad cu byung / /
“I remember as many countless kalpas ago As there are atoms in ten million realms, There was a kalpa that had the name Samāpadyata,[1736] In which there were eight hundred million[1737] jinas. {2}
I remember unthinkable eons ago, past as many eons As atoms in a hundred million lands, An age in which there were Eight decillion buddhas.
bskal pa'i dang por de bzhin gshegs byung ba/ / dbang phyug yon tan mi thub rgyal mtshan no/ / nags tshal dam pa gser mdog me tog tu/ / mgon po de 'khrungs bdag gis mthong bar gyur/ /
“The first of the kalpa’s tathāgatas to appear Was Īśvarājitaguṇadhvaja. I saw the birth of that lord of beings In the supreme forest Svarṇapuṣpaprabhava. {3}
Invincible Paragon of Virtue Was the first of those buddhas; I saw him being born In the wonderful park of golden flowers.
ming du dri med skyed pa'i 'od ces bya/ / de yi ma ma mkhas par bdag gyur te/ / bltams ma thag tu gser mdog dam pa'i 'od/ / 'jig rten dbang pos bdag gis pang du bzhag /
“I was his wise nurse, Vimalasaṃbhavaprabhā. As soon as he was born, there was a supreme golden light, And the lords of the world placed him on my lap. {4}
I was then his wet nurse, By the name of Light of Purity, wise; The world guardians put him in my arms When he was born, shining with golden light.
gang zag dam pa pang du bzhag tshe yang / / de yi spyi gtsug blta bar mi nus te/ / bsam yas de la g.yas dang g.yon du yang / / bltas shing mtha' rnyed mthong bar ma gyur to/ /
“When the supreme individual was placed on my lap, I could not see the top of his inconceivable head. Though I looked from the right and the left, I was not able to see where it ended. {5}
Taking that supreme person in my arms, I could not see the top of his head; Looking at his inconceivable body, I could not see any bounds.
mtshan rab bzang pos de ni yongs su brgyan/ / dri med de sku blta na rab sdug ste/ / rin chen gzugs 'dra bdag gis mthong gyur nas/ / dga' ba'i shugs drag mtshungs med rnam par 'phel/ /
“He was adorned with the excellent physical signs, And his body was stainless and beautiful. He was as if made of jewels, and when I saw him An unparalleled powerful joy increased within me. {6}
Adorned by marks of greatness, pure, His body was beautiful to behold; Seeing him, like a jewel figurine, Incomparable joy welled up in me.
de yi yon tan dpag yas sems sems nas/ / kho mo'i bsod nams rgya mtsho dpag med 'phel/ / de yi rnam 'phrul rgya mtsho mthong gyur nas/ / rgya chen byang chub sems kyang skyes par gyur/ /
“As I contemplated his measureless qualities, The ocean of my merit increased. When I saw the ocean of his miraculous manifestations, A vast aspiration for enlightenment arose within me. {7}
Thinking of his measureless virtues, An infinite sea of felicity grew in me; And seeing his ocean of miracles, I was inspired to seek enlightenment.
rgyal ba'i legs pa rgya mtsho dga' smon nas/ / smon lam rgya mtsho bdag gis rab tu bskyed/ / 'byams klas zhing rnams thams cad rnam par sbyangs/ / dan song lam rnam kun kyang rnam par bzlog /
“With joy and faith in the Jina’s ocean of excellences, I gave rise to an ocean of prayers. The vast extent of all realms was purified, And all paths to lower existences were averted. {8}
Seeking the oceans of qualities of buddhas, My ocean of vows grew; All lands were purified, And all paths of miserable states were closed.
zhing rnams 'byams klas kun gyi bde gshegs rnams/ / ma byon bsam gyis mi khyab mchod pa dang / / sems can sdug bsngal rnam par dgrol ba'i phyir/ / smon lam rgya mtsho kho mos btab par gyur/ /
“I made an ocean of prayers that I would make Countless offerings to future sugatas Throughout the vast extent of realms And liberate beings from suffering. {9}
To serve the inconceivable buddhas To come in all lands, And to liberate suffering beings, My ocean of vows emerged.
mgon po de las bdag gis chos thos nas/ / rnam thar dam pa'i dkyil 'khor 'di yang thob/ / bskal pa zhing rnams bye ba'i rdul snyed du/ / spyad pa spyad de de yang rnam par sbyangs/ /
“I heard the Dharma from that lord And attained the field of this liberation. For kalpas as numerous as atoms in ten million realms, I practiced and purified bodhisattva conduct. {10}
Hearing the teachings of those saviors, I attained this excellent sphere of liberation, Having carried out practice to purify enlightenment For as many eons as atoms in a hundred million lands.
de la mgon po ji snyed byung gyur pa; ; de dag ma lus bdag gis kun kyang mchod/ / rnam thar rgya mtsho 'di ni sbyong byed cing / / de dag bstan pa kho mos yongs su bzung / /
“I have made offerings to however many lords Have appeared without exception. I became a holder of their teachings, And I purified the ocean of this liberation. {11}
I served all the buddhas Who appeared over the ages, And remembered their teachings, Purifying this ocean of liberation.
zhing rnams bye ba'i rdul phran rab snyed kyi/ / stobs bcu mnga' ba ji snyed 'das byung ba/ / de dag chos kyi 'khor lo kho mos bzung / / rnam thar dkyil 'khor 'di yang rab tu bsgoms/ /
“I became a holder of the Dharma wheel Of all the past possessors of the ten strengths, As numerous as the atoms in ten million realms, And I have meditated on the field of this liberation. {12}
There were as many buddhas in the past As atoms in a hundred million lands; Remembering their cycles of teaching, I developed this sphere of liberation.
sangs rgyas zhing gi rdul phran ji snyed pa; ; rdul rtse 'byams klas kun la rnam par mthong / / rdul phran re re la yang rgya mtsho'i zhing / / sngon chad rgyal bas sbyangs pa rab tu mthong / /
“I see all the vast extent of the surfaces of atoms, As many atoms as there are in the buddha realms. In each atom I see the ocean of realms That have been purified in the past by the jinas. {13}
Seeing all atoms In a buddha-land, In every atom I see oceans of lands Purified by the Buddha.
zhing rnams 'byams klas de dag kun tu yang / / mgon po thugs rgyud gcig la bsam yas pa'i/ / rlam 'phrul yangs pa yongs su ston mdzad cing / / nags tshal mchog tu 'khrungs gyur bdag gis mthong / /
“In all that vast extent of realms, The lords from their one mind Manifest countless miracles, And I see their births in supreme forests. {14}
In those lands I see Guides Being born in the best of groves, In an instant manifesting Inconceivable vast miracles.
rgyal ba la la zhing rnams la la na/ / byang chub 'dam par 'tshang rgya thugs dgongs shing / / dga' ldan 'jig rten gnas na bzhugs pa yang / / zhing rnams bye ba bsam gyis mi khyab po/ /
“There are certain jinas in certain realms Intending to attain supreme enlightenment, Who though they are residing in the world of Tuṣita Manifest within an ocean of realms. {15}
I see the leaders, in whatever land, Seeking supreme enlightenment, Living in heaven, or appearing to be born, In inconceivable decillions of lands.

zhing rnams rgya mtsho'i dbyings su rnam 'phrul ba/ / shin tu yangs pa skye pa'ang bdag gis mthong / / na chung dam pa'i tshogs kyi dbus bzhugs shing / / mgon po chos rnams ston pa'ang de bzhin mthong / /
“In countless tens of millions of realms, I see this vast extent of their births. I see the lords teaching the Dharma While in the center of an assembly of youths. {16}
I see them being born with great miracles, In hundreds of oceans of lands, Attended by the best of women, Expounding the Teaching.
zhing rnams bye ba'i rdul phyan rang snyed kyis/ / dpa' bo sems kyi skad cig re re la/ / mngon par byung zhing shing rgyal drung gshegs dang / / sangs rgyas spyod yul yangs pa ston pa mthong / /

“I see in each instant of mind those heroes Who are as numerous as the atoms in ten million realms Leaving home and going to the foot of the king of trees And manifesting the vast field of activity of a buddha.[1738] {17}
zhing gcig rdul la bsam gyis mi khyab bar/ / yul rnams gzhan dang gzhan dag ston mdzad pas/ / 'gro rgyud sems can sdug bsngal 'grol mdzad cing / / mi gtso rnam par 'tshang rgya bdag gis mthong / /

“They manifest inconceivable numbers of this and that realm, Which are as numerous as the atoms in a realm. I see the supreme humans attaining buddhahood And liberating beings in various existences from suffering.[1739]
rdul phran re re'i rtse la mi zad pa'i/ / rang byung 'khor lo rab tu bskor mdzad cing / / dbyangs rnams rgya mtsho mi zad sgrog mdzad pas/ / chos sprin rgya chen char 'bebs mdzad pa mthong / /
“They turn the unceasing, self-originated, Supreme wheel of the surface of each atom. Their voices have an unceasing ocean of speech. I see them sending down rain from clouds of Dharma.[1740]
'gro pa kun la rnam pa du mar yang / / skad cig re rer mya ngan 'das ston pa/ / zhing rnams bye ba'i rdul phran rab snyed kyi/ / sangs rgyas zhing gcig rdul la bdag gis mthong / /
“In each instant they manifest passing into nirvāṇa In many different forms for all beings. I see, in[1741] a single atom of a realm, buddhas As numerous as the atoms in ten million realms.[1742]
I see as many buddhas as atoms in a hundred million In one moment of consciousness, Showing the world in many ways Tranquillity in an instant.
rdul gcig bltas kyang zhing rnams rgya mtsho dang / / rgyal ba 'byung ba ji snyed kun kyang mthong / / tshe rabs kun tu lus mang khrag khrig gis / de dag mchod pa'i don du nye bar phyin/ /
“Looking at one atom, I see an ocean of realms And all the jinas who appear in them. In many hundred billion[1743] bodies in my lifetimes, I have gone to make offerings to them. {18}
I see all the births of buddhas, Looking into the oceans of lands in an atom; In life after life, in millions of bodies, I arrive at compassion in their service.
zhing tshul rgya mtsho bsam gyis mi khyab pa'i/ / 'gro rgyud mi bzad ji snyed yod pa yi/ / 'gro ba kun la mngon du kho mo ni/ / chos sprin yangs pa'i char yang rab tu 'bebs/ /
“There are all the endless existences of beings In the inconceivable ways of the ocean of realms. I come before them all and send down A rain from the vast clouds of the Dharma. {19}
In inconceivable oceans of lands, In the endless realms where they appeared, In all those worlds I appear before them And make the clouds of Teaching rain.
rgyal sras kho mos bsam gyis mi khyab pa'i/ / rnam thar dkyil 'khor dam pa 'di shes kyi/ / bskal pa bye ba khrag khrig bsam yas su/ / thams cad bstan par kho mos nus re skan/ /
“Son of the jinas, I know this inconceivable Supreme field of liberation, But I could not teach it all In countless quintillions of kalpas. {20}
Child of Buddha, I know This inconceivable, exalted liberation, Which could not be all seen Even in inconceivable decillions of eons.

rigs kyi bu/ kho mos byang chub sems dpa' rnam par thar pa bskal pa tshad med par dmigs pa thams cad du byang chub sems dpa'i skye bas rnam par 'phrul ba yongs su ston pa 'di shes par zad na/ kho mo byang chub sems dpa' sems kyi skad cig re re la bskal pa thams cad du zhugs pa'i mngal nas yongs su byung ba'i sems dang ldan pa/ chos kyi tshul thams cad nges par rtogs pa'i skye ba rab tu ston pa/ de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad mchod pa'i smon lam gyis bsam pa yongs su skyed pa; sangs rgyas kyi chos thams cad mngon par rdzogs par 'tshang rgya bar bya ba la rab tu gzhol ba/ sems can thams cad kyi rigs dang / rgyud kyi lam yongs su bstan pa la gzugs brnyan lta bur gyur pa/ de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi zhabs kyi drung du pad+mo'i nang nas skye ba/ 'gro ba thams cad yongs su smin par bya ba'i dus la mkhas pa/ sems can thams cad gdul ba la mngon par mos shing cher skye bas rnam par 'phrul pa yongs su ston pa/ zhing 'byams klas pa thams cad du rnam par 'phrul ba'i sprin yongs su ston pa/ 'gro ba thams cad kyi rgyud du skye ba dang / rigs su gzugs brnyan byung bar gyur pa de dag gi spyod pa shes pa'am/ yon tan brjod par nus re skan/

“Noble one, I know only this bodhisattva liberation called the miraculous manifestations at the birth of bodhisattvas throughout all the perceptions of countless kalpas. How could I describe the qualities or know the conduct of bodhisattvas who in each instant of mind have the motivation to appear in all kalpas from the wombs they have entered; who manifest births that have the definitive understanding of all the ways of the Dharma; who have the aspiration that gives rise to prayers to make offerings to all the tathāgatas; who are dedicated to attaining the complete realization of all the Dharma of the buddhas; who manifest like reflections within the classes and existences of all beings; who are born from lotuses at the feet of all the tathāgatas; who are skilled in knowing when the time has come to ripen all beings; who manifest the miracle of taking rebirth with the intention to guide all beings; who manifest clouds of miracles throughout the entire vast extent of realms; and who appear as reflections in all the classes of births and existences of all beings?

“I just know this enlightening liberation of vision of the miracles of birth of enlightening beings in all objects over countless ages—how can I know the practice or tell the virtues of the enlightening beings whose minds are the sources of all eons from moment to moment of consciousness, who manifest birth by meditation on all the principles of the Teaching, who are determined to serve all buddhas, who are intent on realizing all buddha-teachings, who are like reflections appearing to be born in all races, who are born spontaneously in lotus calyxes in the presence of all buddhas, who have higher knowledge of proper timing in developing all beings, who manifest miracles of birth oriented toward guiding all beings, who show multitudes of miracles in all lands, who are reflected in all conditions and classes and families of beings?

song rigs kyi bu/ grong khyer chen po ser skya'i gnas 'di na shAkya'i bu mo go pa zhes bya ba 'dug gi /de'i gan du song la ji ltar byang chub sems dpa' sems can yongs su smin par bya ba'i phyir 'khor ba'i 'khor bar bya ba dris shig /
“Depart, noble one. In the great city of Kapilavastu there is the Śākya maiden called Gopā. Go to her and ask her, ‘How should a bodhisattva continue in saṃsāra in order to ripen beings?’ ”
“In the city of Kapilavastu lives a girl of the Shakya clan named Gopa. Go ask her how an enlightening being should live in the world for enlightening development.”

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis lum+bi ni'i nags tshal gyis lha mo gzi brjid kyi dkyil 'khor bzang pos dga' ba'i dpal gyi rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te lum+bi ni'i nags tshal gyi lha mo gzi brjid kyi dkyil 'khor bzang pos dga' ba'i dpal la lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas yang dang yang bltas te lum+bi ni'i nags tshal gyi lha mo gzi brjid kyi dkyil 'khor bzang pos dga' ba'i dpal gyi drung nas song ngo/ /

Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, bowed his head to the two feet of Sutejomaṇḍalaratiśrī, the Lumbinī Forest goddess, circumambulated Sutejomaṇḍalaratiśrī, the Lumbinī Forest goddess, many hundreds of thousands of times, keeping her to his right, and, with palms together, looking back at her, departed from Sutejomaṇḍalaratiśrī, the Lumbinī Forest goddess.
Then Sudhana paid his respects and left the goddess of the Lumbini grove.
shin tu rgyas pa chen po'i mdo/ sangs rgyas phal bo che zhes bya ba las/ sdong pos brgyan po'i le'u ste/ bam po brgya bdun pa/
[shAkya'i bu mo go pa ]
Chapter 43. Gopā
Gopa

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang lum+bi ni'i nags tshal gyi lha mo gzi brjid kyi dkyil 'khor bzang pos dga' ba'i dpal gyi drung nas song ste grong khyer chen po ser skya'i gnas gang na ba der phyin nas
Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, left the presence of Sutejomaṇḍalaratiśrī, the Lumbinī Forest goddess, and went to the location of the great city of Kapilavastu.
Then Sudhana left the Lumbini goddess and went to the city of Kapilavastu;

byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa bskal pa tshad med par dmigs pa thams cad du byang chub sems dpa'i skye bas rnam par 'phrul pa yongs su ston pa de nyid sgom pa dang / khong du chud par bya ba dang / rgya cher bya ba dang / nan tan du bya ba dang / shin tu sbyangs pa dang / yongs su bsam pa dang / rnam par dbye ba byed cing / byang chub sems dpa' yang dag par 'gro ba'i khang pa chos kyi dbyings rab tu snang ba'i 'od gang na ba der song ngo; /

While meditating on, comprehending, increasing, practicing, purifying,[1744] contemplating, and examining the bodhisattva liberation called the miraculous manifestations at the birth of bodhisattvas throughout all the perceptions of countless kalpas, he came to the assembly hall of the bodhisattvas called the Illuminating Light of the Realm of the Dharma.

cultivating that enlightening liberation of vision of miracles of birth of enlightening beings in all objects over countless ages, entering into it, expanding it, practicing it, purifying it, mastering it, contemplating it, examining it, he made his way to the meeting hall of enlightening beings reflecting the cosmos.

der 'gro ba'i tshe byang chub sems dpa' yongs su 'gro ba'i khang pa'i lha mo mya ngan med pa'i dpal zhes bya ba khyim gyi lha mo stong phrag bcu dang bcas pas bsu nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la 'di skad ces smras so/ /
When he arrived there, he was greeted by Aśokaśrī, the goddess of the assembly hall of the bodhisattvas, together with ten thousand house goddesses.
