When he went there, a goddess of the enlightening beings’ meeting hall named Sorrowless, together with ten thousand house goddesses, appeared before Sudhana and said to him,

skyes bu chen po shes rab dang ye shes chen pos rnam par gnon pa/ byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa bsam gyis mi khyab pa sgom pa la lhag par dmigs pa'i smon lam gyi sems dang ldan pa/ chos yangs pa'i gzhal med khang gi spyod yul la spyod pa/ chos kyi grong khyer du mngon par gzhol ba/ byang chub sems dpa'i thabs kyi tshul mtha' yas pas sems can gdul ba la 'jug pa rgyun mi gcod pa/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i yon tan rgya mtsho snang ba rab tu thob pa/ 'gro ba thams cad rnam par gdul ba la rab tu snang ba'i spobs pa dang ye shes mngon du gyur pa/ sems can thams cad kyi spyod pa shes pa'i lus kyis 'gro zhing rjes su 'brang bar bya ba'i spyod pa la mngon du gyur pa'i sems dang ldan pa/ 'gro ba thams cad kyi sems kyi dga' ba rgya mtsho'i shugs rnam par 'phel bar bya ba'i smon lam dang ldan pa/ de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi chos khong du chud par bya ba'i lam du zhugs pa khyod byon pa legs so/ /

She said to Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, “We welcome you, great being who has the prowess of great wisdom and knowledge; whose mind has attained the meditation of inconceivable bodhisattva liberation; whose field of activity is the vast divine palace of the Dharma; who enters the city of the Dharma; who is continuously engaged in guiding beings through infinite bodhisattva methods; who has attained the illumination of the ocean of qualities of the tathāgatas; who has the manifest knowledge and illuminating eloquence for guiding all beings; who has the motivation to manifest the conduct of[1745] a corresponding body and language[1746] that knows the conduct of all beings; who prays to increase the power of an ocean of joy in the minds of all beings; and who follows the path to the comprehension of the Dharma of all the tathāgatas.

“Welcome is the great person with wisdom, knowledge, and courage, who roams the grounds of the vast palace of reality intent on cultivating the inconceivable liberations of enlightening beings, in the presence of the city of truth, ceaselessly entering into the endless methods of enlightening beings, attaining manifestation of the ocean of virtues of those who realize Thusness, aiming for the knowledge of how to act and speak so as to mature all people, acting and speaking according to knowledge of the behavior of all people, mind oriented toward spiritual practice, committed to increasing the flood of the ocean of joy in the feelings of all beings, on the path of knowledge of the Teaching of all those who arrive at thusness.

mig phyir glan pa med pas spyod pa dang spyod lam zab cing rnam par dag pa'i spyod yul can khyod la bltas na/ khyod ni/ ring po mi thogs par de bzhin gshegs pa'i sku dang / gsung dang / thugs kyi rgyan rnam par dag pa bla na med pa rab tu thob ste mtshan dang dpe byad bzang pos rab tu brgyan pa'i lus dang / stobs bcu'i ye shes snang bas brgyan pa'i sems kyis 'jig rten du rnam par spyod par 'gyur ro/ /

“I see that you have the field of activity of profound behavior with a steady[1747] gaze, and that therefore you are someone who will soon attain the unsurpassable pure adornments of the body, speech, and mind of the tathāgatas and will act in this world with a body adorned by the signs and features of a great being and with a mind adorned by the light of knowledge of the ten strengths.

As I see you, with steady gaze on the pure realm of conduct of profound spiritual practice, before long you will attain perfection of the supreme ornaments of body, speech, and mind of the enlightened, and will act in the world with a body adorned with the marks and embellishments of greatness and a mind adorned with the light of knowledge of the ten powers.

khyod kyi brtson 'grus dang / rnam par gnon pa la bltas na/ khyod ni/ ring po mi thogs par dus gsum gyi de bzhin gshegs pa mngon du gyur par mthong ba dang ldan zhing de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi chos kyi sprin yongs su 'dzin pa dang / byang chub sems dpa'i bsam gtan dang / rnam par thar pa dang / ting nge 'dzin dang / snyoms par 'jug pa'i chos zhi ba dang ldan pa'i gzhal med khang gi dga' ba myong ba dang / sangs rgyas kyi rnam par thar pa zab mor chud par 'gyur ro/ /

“I see that you have diligence and prowess, and that therefore you are someone who soon will have the vision of the tathāgatas of the three times; will hold the clouds of Dharmas of all the tathāgatas; will experience the joy of the divine palace of the four qualities of bodhisattva dhyānas, liberations, samādhis, and samāpattis; and will enter the profound liberation of the buddhas.

As I see your steadfast, energetic exertion, before long you will be furnished with all the requisites for manifesting your being in the presence of all buddhas of past, present, and future; receiving their teachings, experiencing the delight of the tranquil palace of spirituality, with all the meditations, liberations, concentrations, and attainments of enlightening beings, you will see into the profound liberation of buddhas.

de yang de ltar khyod dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi drung du 'gro ba dang / blta ba dang / bsnyen bkur ba dang / gdams ngag ma nor bar blang ba dang / de'i yon tan la nan tan du bya ba'i tshul la brtson par byed pas yongs su mi skyo/ phyir mi ldog /sgyid lug par mi 'gyur te/ khyod la bgegs sam; bar du gcod pa'am/ sgrib pa gang gis kyang mi tshugs te/ bdud dam bdud kyi ris su gtogs pa'i lha rnams kyang mdun na gnas pa med pa de'i phyir khyod ni/ ring po mi thogs par sems can thams cad dga' bar byed par 'gyur ro/ / de skad ces smras pa dang /

“In that way, you go before kalyāṇamitras, gaze upon them, honor them, receive their teaching without error, and are dedicated to the practice of its qualities that is unwearied, irreversible, and never disheartened. You are unaffected by any hindrance, obstacle, or obscuration whatsoever. Neither Māra nor the māra class of deities are present before you, and therefore you will soon bring happiness to all beings.”

That is because you do not tire, do not regress, do not feel pain in going to spiritual benefactors, meeting them, associating with them, receiving instructions, and applying the ways to virtue; and you are not overcome by any interference or barrier or obstacle, or by any demon or deity. Therefore you will soon become a source of joy for all beings.”

tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis byang chub sems dpa' yongs su 'gro ba'i khang pa'i lha mo mya ngan med pa'i dpal la 'di skad ces smras so/ / lha mo/ khyod kyis ji skad du smras pa de ltar 'gyur ro/ / lha mo/ kho bo ni/ sems can thams cad kyi nyon mongs pa'i gdung ba rnam par zhi bas dga' bar 'gyur ro/ / sems can thams cad kyi las nyam nga ba'i rnam par smin pa phyir log pa dang / sems can thams cad kyi bde ba 'grub pa dang / sems can thams cad kha na ma tho ba med pa'i las la nan tan du byed pas dga' ba dam pa nyams su myong bar 'gyur ro/ / nam sems can de dag las dang nyon mongs pa rnam pa sna tshogs mi bde ba'i sbyor bas sems rnam par 'khrugs shing ngan song du ltung bar gyur pa'am/ bde ba'i rgyud na gnas kyang lus dang sems kyi sdug bsngal dang / yid mi bde ba sna tshogs nyams su myong bar gyur cing mi dga' bar gnas pa de'i tshe byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyang shin tu ying mi bde bar 'gyur ro/ /

The head merchant’s son, Sudhana, said to Aśokaśrī, the goddess of the assembly hall of the bodhisattvas, “Goddess, I gain the highest delight in ending the torment of the kleśas for all beings. I gain the highest delight in repelling dreadful[1748] karma for all beings, in bringing happiness to all beings, and in making all beings practice faultless actions. Bodhisattvas become very unhappy when beings engage in the unhappiness of various kinds of karma and kleśas, which disturbs their minds and causes them to fall into the lower existences. Even if those beings remain in happier existences, they experience physical and mental sufferings and various kinds of unhappiness and remain in a state of sorrow.

Then Sudhana said to the goddess Sorrowless, “May it be as you say—I would find supreme joy in extinguishing the burning of all beings’ afflictions, in stopping the development of their evil deeds, in making them all happy, in getting them to act impeccably. Whenever sentient beings are involved in evil deeds and afflictions, with scattered minds, fall into painful or pleasurable states, and experience various forms of physical and mental distress, enlightening beings become most unhappy at that.

lha mo/ 'di lta ste/ dper na/ mi shin tu ngang gis byams pa zhig la bu gcig pa sdug cing yid du 'ong ba zhig bdog par gyur la/ de'i yan lag dang nying lag bcad pa zhig mthong na/ shin tu ngang gis byams pa'i phyir rab tu yid mi bde zhing mi dga' bar 'gyur ro; ;

“Goddess, it is like if a very loving father who has a beloved, beautiful son sees the limbs and smaller parts of his son’s body being cut off. Because he is so loving, he becomes extremely unhappy and sorrowful.
Just as a doting parent would love its only child and would be most distressed at seeing the child be dismembered,

lha mo/ de bzhin du byang chub sems dpa' byang chub sems dpa'i spyad pa spyod pa'i tshe yang sems can rnams las dang nyon mongs pa'i dbang gis ngan song gsum gyi rgyud du ltung ba zhig mthong na/ rab tu mi dga' la shin tu nyams mi bde bar 'gyur ro/ /

“Goddess, in the same way, when a bodhisattva who is engaged in bodhisattva conduct sees beings falling into the three lower existences through the power of their karma and kleśas, the bodhisattva becomes extremely unhappy and sorrowful.
in the same way a practicing enlightening being is most unhappy to see people fallen into miserable states because of compulsion by afflictions in action.

gang gi tshe sems can rnams lus dang / ngag dang / yid kyis legs par spyad pa yang dag par len pa'i rgyus lus zhig nas bde ba'i rgyus mtho ris kyi 'jig rten du skye bar gyur tam/ lha dang mi'i lam gyi rgyud du lus dang sems kyi bde ba nyams su myong ba zhig tu gyur na/ de'i tshe byang chub sems dpa' shin tu bde ba dang ldan zhing nyams bde ba dang / yid dga' ba dang / rab tu spro ba dang / dga' ba'i yid nyams su bde ba dang ldan par 'gyur ro/ /

“The bodhisattvas are happy, glad, joyful, delighted, and pleased when beings are reborn into happy existences when their bodies are destroyed, or when they experience physical and mental happiness in a divine or human existence as the result of their having adopted good physical, vocal, and mental conduct.

Whenever sentient beings live in felicity because of good thoughts, words, and deeds, and experience physical and mental pleasures in celestial and human realms, enlightening beings are delighted and become happy and joyful.

lha mo/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams ni/ bdag gi don gyi phyir thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du smon cing don du gnyer ba ma yin te/ 'khor ba'i dga' ba dang / bde ba sna tshogs nyams su myong bar bya ba'i phyir ma yin/ 'dod pa'i khams su gtogs pa'i dga' ba rnam pa tha dad pa sna tshogs don du gnyer bas ma yin/ 'du shes dang / sems dang / lta ba phyin ci log tu gyur pa'i dbang gis ma yin/ kun tu sbyor ba dang / 'ching ba dang / bag la nyal ba dang / kun nas 'khor ba'i dbang du gyur pas ma yin/ srid pa dang / lta ba'i dbang du gyur pas ma yin/ sems can sna tshogs dang 'du zhing 'dzi ba'i dga' ba'i 'du shes kyi sems rnam par 'phel bas ma yin/ bsam gtan gyi dga' ba dang / bde ba myong ba la yongs su chags pas ma yin/ sgrib pa sna tshogs kyis bsgribs shing 'khor ba'i rgyud na 'dre ldog pa ma yin gyi/

“Goddess, the bodhisattvas do not aspire to and are not dedicated to omniscience for their own sake or in order to experience the various joys and pleasures of saṃsāra. It is not from dedication to the various different kinds of joys within the desire realm. It is not through the power of mistaken perception, motivation, or views. It is not through the power of involvement, bondage, predispositions, or being overwhelmed. It is not through the power of the view of craving. It is not through the increase of a mind that conceives of the joys of crowds and the gatherings of various beings. It is not through attachment to the experiences of the joy and bliss of dhyāna. It is not going around and around in the continuity of saṃsāra while being obscured by various obscurations.

“Furthermore, enlightening beings do not seek omniscience for their own sake, nor to produce mundane enjoyments and pleasures, nor in search of the various enjoyments of the realm of desire, nor under the compulsion of errors of conception, thought, and view. They live and work in the world without being controlled by fetters, bonds, propensities, or obsessions, without being controlled by craving or views, without their minds being bound up in ideas of mundane enjoyments, without being taken with the taste of pleasure of meditation, without being blocked by mental barriers.

lha mo/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams ni/ sems can 'khor ba'i rgya mtsho na 'khod cing sdug bsngal dpag tu med pas shin tu mnar ba rnams la snying rje chen po bskyed cing 'gro ba thams cad yongs su bsdu ba'i smon lam chen po mngon par sgrub ste/ de dag ni/ snying rje chen pos smon lam mngon par sgrub pa'i shugs kyis sems can yongs su smin par bya ba dang / gdul ba la brtson zhing / 'khor ba na byang chub sems dpa'i spyad pa spyod par snang ngo/ /

“Goddess, the bodhisattvas have great compassion for beings who are in the ocean of saṃsāra and who are tormented by immeasurable sufferings. They make great prayers to gather to themselves all beings. Through the power of having made those prayers with great compassion, they are dedicated to ripening and guiding beings, and they appear carrying out bodhisattva conduct in saṃsāra.

“Furthermore, enlightening beings, giving rise to great compassion for sentient beings suffering immeasurable miseries in the ocean of existence, undertake a great vow to care for all beings. They appear carrying out the practice of enlightening beings in the mundane whirl, engaged in the development and guidance of sentient beings, by the force of the power of carrying out the vow of great compassion.

de dag ni/ sems can thams cad kyi sgrib pa thams cad rnam par bzlog pa'i don du thams cad mkhyen pa'i ye shes sgrib pa med pa yongs su tshol zhing / de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad mchod pa dang / bsnyen bkur ba'i smon lam mngon par sgrub bo/ /
In order to eliminate all the obscurations of beings, they seek the unobscured wisdom of omniscience and make prayers to serve and make offerings to all the tathāgatas.
They undertake a vow to serve all buddhas in quest of thoroughly unobstructed omniscience for all sentient beings.

de dag de bzhin gshegs pa mchod cing rim gror bya ba'i smon lam gyi dbang gis byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pas yongs su skyo ba med de/ de dag byang chub sems dpa'i spyad pa la spyod pa'i tshe kun nas nyon mongs pa'i zhing mthong na/ sangs rgyas kyi zhing thams cad yongs su dag par bya ba'i smon lam mngon par sgrub bo/ /

Through the power of their prayers to serve and make offerings to all the tathāgatas, they are never disheartened in their practice of bodhisattva conduct. When they are practicing bodhisattva conduct and see a realm that is completely defiled, they make the prayer to purify all buddha realms.
By mastery of the vow to serve buddhas, they do not tire in enlightening practice. While they carry on enlightening practice, seeing defiled lands they undertake a vow to purify all buddha-lands.

kun nas nyon mongs pa'i zhing yongs su sbyong zhing sems can thams cad kyi skye mched sna tshogs mthong bar gyur pa'i tshe chos kyi sku tha dad pa med cing bla na med pa yongs su dag par bya ba'i phyir smon lam mngon par sgrub bo/ /
When they are purifying defiled realms and see the various āyatanas of all beings, they make the prayer to purify the Dharma body that is undifferentiated and unsurpassable.
While purifying oceans of lands, observing the variety of beings’ states, they undertake a vow to purify the undifferentiated supreme reality body.

sems can rnams kyi lus dang / ngag dang / sems kun nas nyon mongs pa dang ldan pa mthong na/ sems can thams cad kyi lus dang / ngag dang / sems kyi rgyan yongs su dag par bya ba'i phyir smon lam mngon par sgrub bo/ /
When they see the defiled bodies, speech, and minds of beings, they make the prayer to purify the bodies, speech, and minds that adorn all beings.
Seeing sentient beings’ acts, words, and thoughts defiled, they undertake a vow to purify sentient beings’ acts, words, and thoughts.

sems can skye mched ma tshang ba dang / sems yongs su ma dag pa mthong na/ sems can thams cad kyi sems dang / spyod pa yongs su sbyong zhing / byang chub sems dpa'i spyad pa la spyod pas yongs su skyo ba med do/ /
When they see the incomplete āyatanas and impure minds of beings, they purify the minds and conduct of all beings and are never disheartened in carrying out bodhisattva conduct.
Seeing sentient beings with incompletely purified senses and minds, they carry on enlightening practice tirelessly, completely purifying the mental behavior of all sentient beings.
lha mo/ de ltar byang chub sems dpa' rnams ni/ yongs su skyo ba med pa'i sems kyis byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa mtha' dang dbus med pa la spyod do/ /
“Goddess, in that way, with minds that are never disheartened, the bodhisattvas carry out vast bodhisattva conduct without end or middle.
“Thus enlightening beings are indefatigable in carrying out the infinitely various practice of enlightening beings.

de ltar spyod pa ni/ lha dang mi'i phun sum tshogs pa yongs su skyed pas lha dang bcas pa'i 'jig rten gyi rgyan du gyur pa yin/ byang chub tu sems bskyed pa la rab tu 'god pa'i phyir pha dang mar gyur pa yin/ byang chub sems dpa'i lam du 'dzud pas ma ma lta bur gyur pa yin/ ngan song gi g.yang sa'i 'jigs pa las srung ba'i phyir lhan cig skyes pa'i lha rtag tu phyi bzhin 'brang blta bur gyur pa yin/ 'khor ba'i rgya mtsho las sgrol ba'i phyir mnyan pa chen po lta bur gyur pa yin/

With that kind of conduct they are adornments of the world because they create the good fortune of devas and humans. They are like parents because they establish beings in the aspiration for enlightenment. They are like nurses because they bring beings onto the bodhisattva path. They are like connate deities, who are deities that always accompany a being because they protect beings from the terror of the abyss of the lower existences. They are like great ferrymen because they free beings from the ocean of saṃsāra.

Practicing in this way, they become ornaments of heaven and earth, by producing human and celestial welfare. They become parents, because they bring enlightening beings into existence. They become nurses, leading into the path of enlightening beings. They become guardian spirits, giving protection from the danger of falling into bad ways. They become great mariners, ferrying beings across the ocean of the mundane whirl.

bdud dang nyon mongs pa'i 'jigs pa thams cad rnam par zlog pa'i phyir skyabs su gyur pa yin/ shin tu bsil ba'i rang bzhin nye bar stob pas gnas su gyur pa yin/ sangs rgyas rgya mtsho thams cad du 'jug par byed pas mu stegs su gyur pa yin/ chos rin po che'i gling du skyel bas mgon byed par gyur pa yin/

They are refuges because they repel all the terrors of the māras and kleśas. They are shelters because they bring beings to a state of complete tranquility.[1749] They are bathing places because they bring beings into the ocean of all buddhas. They are protectors because they escort beings to the island of the jewels of the Dharma.

They become refuges, eliminating the dangers of all demons and afflictions. They become resorts, leading to the ultimate state of coolness. They become landings leading into the ocean of enlightenment. They become guides, leading to the island of spiritual jewels.

sangs rgyas kyi yon tan thams cad kyi me tog gis sems yongs su rgyas par byed pas me tog tu gyur pa yin/ bsod nams dang ye shes kyi 'od yangs pa rab tu 'gyed pas rgyan du gyur pa yin/ kun nas mdzes pas dga' ba dang bde ba dam pa yin/ kha na ma tho ba med pa'i las la nan tan du byed pas phrad na legs pa yin/ yan lag dam pa rnam pa thams cad du yongs su tshang ba'i lus dang ldan pas kun tu bzang ba yin/ blta na mi mthun pa med pas btang mi bra ba'i gzugs dang ldan pa yin/ ye shes kyi 'od zer rab tu 'gyed pa'i phyir 'od byed pa yin/ chos kyi sgron ma 'dzin pa'i phyir snang ba byed pa yin/

They are flowers because their minds have blossomed with all the qualities of buddhahood. They are adornments because they radiate the light of merit and wisdom. They bring the highest delight and happiness because they are beautiful. They are excellent to meet because they are dedicated to faultless actions. They are completely good because they possess bodies that are complete in having all aspects of excellent limbs. They have charming forms because the sight of them is without anything disagreeable. They bring light because they radiate the light rays of wisdom. They bring illumination because they hold the torch of the Dharma.

They become flowers, their minds blooming with the virtues of all buddhas. They become adornments, radiating the light of great virtue and knowledge. They become sources of supreme joy, pleasing in all ways. They become worth visiting, because they act impeccably. They become universally good, perfecting themselves in all respects. They become an ever-welcome sight, never appearing disagreeable. They become light-makers, emanating light beams of knowledge. They become illuminators, holding the lamp of truth.

byang chub kyi bsam pa yongs su dag par byed pa'i phyir gsal bar byed pa yin/ bdud kyi las rnam par zlog pa'i phyir dmag dpon du gyur pa yin/ shes rab kyi 'od zer gyi dra ba rab tu snang ba 'gyed pa'i phyir nyi mar gyur pa yin/ chos kyi nam mkha' la blo'i zla ba 'char bar byed pas zla bar gyur pa yin/ 'gro ba thams cad du chos kyi sprin chen po'i char 'bebs pas sprin du gyur pa yin te;

They bring clarity because they purify the motivation for enlightenment. They are generals because they repel the activities of the māras. They are suns because they radiate a net of the light rays of wisdom. They are moons because they rise as moons of realization in the sky of the Dharma.[1750] They are clouds because they send down rain from great clouds of Dharma onto all beings.

They become radiant, purifying the will for enlightenment. They become warrior chiefs, stopping the acts of demons. They become suns, radiating webs of light rays of wisdom. They become moons, the moon of awareness rising in the sky. They become clouds, showering the Teaching on all beings.
lha mo/ de ltar nan tan du byed pa'i byang chub sems dpa' rnams ni/ sems can thams cad kyi yid du 'ong ba yin no/ /
“Goddess, the bodhisattvas who practice in that way are a delight for all beings.”
Thus do enlightening beings become a joy to all living creatures as they carry out enlightening practice.”

de nas byang chub sems dpa' yongs su 'gro ba'i khang pa'i lha mo mya ngan med pa'i dpal khyim gyi lha mo stong phrag bcu dang bcas pas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la lha rdzas las kyang 'das pa'i me tog dang / phreng ba dang / bdug spos dang / phye ma dang / byug pa dang / phye ma rin po che'i rgyan gyi char yid kyi rang bzhin mngon par phab ste kun nas bskor cing rjes su 'brangs nas byang chub sems dpa'i khang par 'gro ba'i tshe tshigs su bcad pa 'di dag gis mngon par bstod do/ /

Then Aśokaśrī, the goddess of the assembly hall of the bodhisattvas, together with ten thousand goddesses of the home, sent down onto Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, a rain of flowers, garlands, incense, powders, ointments, and precious jewelry that transcended divine materials. Encircling him and following him as he entered the assembly hall of the bodhisattvas, they praised him with these verses:

Then Sorrowless, goddess of the hall of assembly of enlightening beings, with those ten thousand house goddesses, showered Sudhana with a rain of mentally created flower garlands, aromatic powders, perfumes, and jewelry, all superior to those in the heavens; then, surrounding him, they sang these verses in his praise as he entered the abode of enlightening beings:
byang chub rdzogs par thugs bskyed cing / / sems can kun la thugs brtse bas/ / rgyal ba ye shes nyi ma rnams/ / bar 'ga' zhig na 'jig rten 'byung / /
“Having developed the aspiration for enlightenment Out of love for all beings, The jinas, the suns of wisdom, Sometimes appear in the world. {1}
Buddhas emerge in the world at times, Producing the light of knowledge, Resolved on perfect enlightenment Out of compassion for the world.
bskal pa bye ba mang pos kyang / / khyod kyi zhal mthong shin tu dka'/ / 'jig rten ma rig ldongs pa la/ / khyod kyi ye shes nyi chen yin/ /
“Even in many millions[1751] of kalpas It is difficult to see your face. Your wisdom is a great sun In the world blinded by ignorance. {2}
Hard to get to see Even in millions of eons, You are a sun of knowledge For the world in the darkness of ignorance.
mi shes rab rib sgrib pa yi/ / 'jig rten phyin ci log gzigs nas/ / thugs rje chen po rab bskyed de/ / khyod ni rang byung nyid du zhugs/ /
“Great compassion arose in you When you saw the world in error, Obscured by the darkness of unknowing, And you spontaneously appeared in it and remained. {3}
Seeing the world in error, Shrouded in the darkness of nescience, Conceiving great compassion You’ve set out for independence.
khyod ni dgongs pa rnam dag pas/ / sangs rgyas byang chub don du brtson/ / dge bshes bsnyen bkur bstan mdzad cing / / lus srog phangs par mdzad mi mnga'/ /
“With your pure motivation, you are dedicated To attaining the enlightenment of buddhahood. You serve and depend on kalyāṇamitras Without regard for your own body and life. {4}
With pure intention you seek The enlightenment of buddhas; You serve spiritual benefactors Without concern for yourself.
khyod ni 'jig rten brten mi mnga'/ / 'du 'dzi mi mnga' gnas mi mnga'/ / 'dren pa ma mchis mi brten pas/ / dgongs pa thogs med nam mkha' bzhin/ /
“You have no reliance on this world. You have no location and no preoccupations. You have no entanglements and no abode. Your motivation is like space, without impediment. {5}
You are not attached to the world, You are independent and aloof; You do not dwell in the defilement of the world, Your mind is free as the sky.
byang chub sems dpa'i spyod mdzad cing / / bsod nams dkyil 'khor 'od bzang bas/ / ye shes sgron ma rab 'gyed pas/ / 'jig rten tshad med kun tu 'char/ /
“As you practice bodhisattva conduct With the brilliant light of a field of merit, Your radiant torch of wisdom Shines within countless worlds. {6}
You practice lofty deeds of enlightenment, Beautiful light of virtues; You appear in the world Radiating lights of knowledge.
'jig rten nas kyang 'phags mi mdzad/ / 'jig rten chos kyis yongs mi 'go / chags pa med par 'jig rten spyod/ / mkha' la ser bu ji bzhin no/ /
“You are not above the world, But you are unstained by worldly qualities. You act in the world without impediment, Like the breezes moving through the sky. {7}
You do not leave the world, Nor are you stained by worldly things; You traverse the world unattached, Like the wind through the sky.
bskal pa'i me 'bar me bzhin du/ / rtag tu 'bar bas rab tu brtson/ / me lta bu yi brtson 'grus kyis/ / byang chub spyad pa spyod pa mdzad/ /
“You are dedicated to constantly blazing Like the burning at the kalpa’s end. You practice the bodhisattva conduct With the ardor of the fire that ends a kalpa. {8}
Just as the holocaust Burns constantly, With energy like fire You carry on enlightening practice.
seng+ge bzhin du shin tu dpa'/ / brtson 'grus rnam par gnon pa brtan/ / ye shes rnam par gnon dang ldan/ / gzhan gyis thub pa med par spyod/ /
“You have great courage, like a lion. With strong, diligent prowess You have attained the prowess of wisdom With a practice that is invincible. {9}
Lionlike, great hero, Progressing boldly with steadfast vigor, Imbued with the power of knowledge, You practice undaunted.
chos dbyings rgya mtsho 'di dag ni; ; rgya mtsho'i tshul rnams ji snyed pa/ / der yang dge bshes bsnyen bkur pas/ / dpa' bo khyod ni 'jug par 'gyur/ /
“Through honoring the kalyāṇamitras, You, here, have entered into The ocean of all the different ways Within the ocean of the realm of the Dharma.” {10}
All the oceans Of principles in the cosmos You will enter, O Hero, By serving true benefactors.

de nas byang chub sems dpa' yongs su 'gro ba'i khang pa'i lha mo mya ngan med pa'i dpal gyis tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la tshigs su bcad pa de dag gis mngon par bstod de/ de 'gro ba'i phyi bzhin chos 'dod pa'i don du 'brang bar gyur to/ /
In that way, Aśokaśrī, the goddess of the assembly hall of the bodhisattvas, praised in verse Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, while following him out of a yearning for the Dharma.
Then the goddess Sorrowless, having eulogized Sudhana, followed him as he went on, bound to him by love for truth.

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang byang chub sems dpa' yang dag par 'gro ba'i khang pa chos kyi dbyings rab tu snang ba'i 'od du phyin te/ nang du song nas shAkya'i bu mo go pa mthong bar 'dod de kun tu bltas na/

Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, went into the assembly hall of the bodhisattvas called the Illuminating Light of the Realm of the Dharma. When he had entered, wishing to find the Śākya maiden Gopā, he looked everywhere.
Sudhana went into the meeting hall of enlightening beings which shone with reflections of the cosmos and looked around, desirous of seeing the Shakyan girl Gopa.

shAkya'i bu mo go pa byang chub sems dpa' yang dag par 'gro ba'i khang pa chos kyi dbyings rab tu snang ba'i 'od kyi dbus na stan rin po che byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi gnas snang bar byed pa/ gzugs brnyan gyi pad+mo'i snying po can zhig la bud med rgyal po'i rigs su byung ba/ sngon byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la dge ba'i rtsa ba'i skal ba mnyam pa/ sngon sbyin pa'i yongs su bsdu bas shin tu bsdus pa/ tshig snyan cing 'jam par smra ba'i ngang tshul dang ldan pa/ thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du don mngon du bya bas shin tu bsdus pa/ sangs rgyas dang byang chub sems dpa'i yang dag par sgrub pa la don mthun pas shin tu bzung ba/ snying rje chen po sngon du 'gro bas bu dang bu mo yongs su gzung ba'i tshul bcangs pa/ byams pa chen po dang ldan pa'i rang gi khyim thab kyi rjes su 'brang ba yongs su dag par byas pa/ sngon byang chub sems dpa'i thabs mkhas pa bsam gyis mi khyab pas yongs su smin par byas pa/ stong phrag brgyad cu rtsa bzhi'i 'khor gyis kun nas bskor cing 'dug pa mthong ngo/ /

He saw the Śākya maiden Gopā in the center of the assembly hall of the bodhisattvas called the Illuminating Light of the Realm of the Dharma. She was seated upon a precious throne that had in its center a lotus with a form that illuminated all the abodes of bodhisattvas, and she was encircled by an entourage of eighty-four thousand women of royal families, who all had equally the roots of merit from the past practice of bodhisattva conduct; who in the past had attracted gatherings of beings through acts of generosity; who had a way of speaking with pleasant and gentle words; who cared for beings through causing them to focus on the goal of omniscience; who cared for beings in accord with the realizations of the buddhas and the bodhisattvas; who with all actions inspired by great compassion cared for beings as if they were their sons and daughters; who with great love followed and purified their spouses; and who in the past ripened beings through the inconceivable skillful methods of bodhisattvas.

He saw her in the middle of the hall sitting on a seat of jewels which reflected the abodes of all enlightening beings, surrounded by eighty-four thousand maidens, all of royal lineage, who had equally established good foundations of the practice of enlightening beings, who had been won over by her generosity in the past, who practiced gentle, pleasing speech, who were taken with the happiness of approaching the goal of omniscience, who were thoroughly absorbed in the common purpose of complete knowledge of buddhas and enlightening beings, who were sustained by the loving care guided by great compassion, who had purified great kindness, who had already developed the inconceivable skill in means of enlightening beings.

bud med stong phrag brgyad cu rtsa bzhi po de dag kyang bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub las phyir mi ldog pa; byang chub sems dpa'i pha rol tu phyin pa tshul la shin tu zhugs pa/ byang chub sems dpa'i bslab pa la gzhan gyi dring mi 'jog pa/ chags pa thams cad dang bral ba'i sems dang ldan pa/ 'khor ba'i dga' ba thams cad kyis skyo ba'i yid dang ldan pa/ chos kyi dbyings kyi tshul chags pa med pas yongs su dag pa/ thams cad mkhyen pa nyid mngon du bya ba'i sems kyi shugs dang ldan pa/ sgrib pa dang bar du gcod pa'i dra ba dang bral ba/ chags pa'i lam thams cad las shin tu 'das pa/ chos kyi sku la legs par sprul bas rnam par spyod pa; 'jig rten thams cad yongs su smin par bya ba dang / gdul ba la mngon par phyogs pa/ bsod nams rgya mtsho dri ma med pas yongs su byung ba'i sems dang ldan pa/ byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po'i spyod pa dang smin lam gyis shin tu byung ba/ byang chub sems dpa'i stobs kyi shugs yangs pas ye shes kyi nyi ma'i dkyil 'khor gyis sems rab tu snang ba yang dag par bskyed pa sha stag go /

Those eighty-four thousand women followed the way of the perfections of bodhisattvas who were progressing irreversibly toward the highest, complete enlightenment. They followed the bodhisattva training without expectation of reward from others. They had minds free from all attachment. They were disillusioned by all the delights of saṃsāra. They had purified without impediment all the ways in the realm of the Dharma. They had the power of the motivation directed toward omniscience. They were free from the net of obscurations and obstacles. They had transcended all the paths of attachment. They were active through emanations of their Dharma bodies. They were focused on ripening and guiding all worlds. They had minds in which a stainless ocean of merit had arisen. They had become what they were because of their completely good bodhisattva prayers and conduct. They had increased the vast power of the strengths of bodhisattvas. And their minds had become illuminating like the disk of the sun.

All of those eighty-four thousand women were irreversible in progress toward supreme perfect enlightenment; they had comprehended enlightening beings’ means of transcendence, and needed no one’s guidance in the studies of enlightening beings. Their minds were free from all attachments and aloof of all mundane pleasures. They had cleared the way to the unobstructed cosmos and their minds were rapidly approaching omniscience. They were free from the web of all obstacles and barriers, and transcended all attachments. They acted as positive emanations of the body of reality, dedicated to leading all beings to perfection. Their minds sprang from a vast ocean of virtue, and they carried out the vow of the practice of universal good. They had developed tremendous energy in powers of enlightening beings, and the light of their minds was as a sun of knowledge.

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang shAkya'i bu mo go pa gang na ba der phyin nas shAkya'i bu mo go ba'i rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te langs nas mdun du 'dug ste thal mo sbyar nas 'di skad ces smras so/ /
Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, bowed his head to the feet of the Śākya maiden and then stood before her, his hands placed together in homage, and said,
Then Sudhana went up to Gopa, paid his respects, and said,

'phags ma/ bdag gis bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub sems bskyed na/ ji ltar na/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams 'khor ba na yongs su 'khor yang 'khor ba'i skyon gyis mi gos pa dang / chos thams cad mnyam pa nyid kyi rang bzhin yang khong du chud la nyan thos dang rang sangs rgyas kyi sa la'ang mi gnas pa dang / sangs rgyas kyi chos snang ba'ang rab tu thob la byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa yang rgyun mi gcod pa dang / byang chub sems dpa'i sa la'ang rab tu gnas la de bzhin gshegs pa'i yul yang yongs su ston pa dang / 'jig rten gyi lam gyi rgyud thams cad las kyang yongs su 'das la 'jig rten gyi lam gyi rgyud thams cad du yang nye bar spyod pa dang / chos kyi lus yongs su grub pa dang ldan yang gzugs kyi lus kha dog mtha' yas pa'ang mngon par sgrub pa dang / mtshan ma med pa'i chos kyi sku la yang rab tu gzhol la 'gro ba thams cad kyi kha dog dang dbyibs kyi lus kyang yongs su ston pa dang / chos thams cad brjod du ma mchis par yang rab tu rtogs la dag gi lam dang / nges pa'i tshig thams cad brjod pas kyang sems can rnams la chos ston pa dang / sems can thams cad sems can med par yang rab tu shes la sems can gyi khams gdul ba'i tshul las kyang phyir mi ldog pa dang / chos thams cad ma skyes pa dang ma 'gag par yang khong du chud la de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad la mchod cing rim gror bya ba'i sbyor ba las kyang phyir mi ldog pa dang / chos thams cad la las dang rnam par smin pa ma mchis par yang rtogs la dge ba'i las mngon par 'du bya ba'i sbyor ba las kyang phyir mi ldog pa ma 'tshal to/ / de skad ces smras pa dang /

“Āryā, I have developed the aspiration for the highest, complete enlightenment, but I do not know how bodhisattvas continue within saṃsāra without being stained by saṃsāra; how they realize the equal nature of all phenomena but do not dwell on the level of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; how they attain the illumination of the Dharma of the buddhas and yet continue with their bodhisattva conduct; how they dwell on the level of a bodhisattva but teach the scope of knowledge of the tathāgatas; how they transcend all worldly existences but are active within all worldly existences; how they accomplish a body of the Dharma but also accomplish form bodies of infinite colors; how they attain the Dharma body that has no characteristics but manifest bodies with the colors and shapes of all beings; and how they realize that all Dharmas cannot be described but teach the Dharma to all beings, describing them with all ways of speaking and definitions. They know that all beings[1752] are without existence, but they do not turn away from the ways of guiding the realm of beings; they comprehend that all phenomena are unborn and unceasing, but they do not abandon engaging in making offerings to and venerating all the tathāgatas; and they realize that there is no karma and ripening within all phenomena, but they do not turn away from engagement in accomplishing good actions.”

“I have set my mind on supreme perfect enlightenment, but I do not know how enlightening beings act in the midst of the mundane whirl without being stained by its ills; how they realize the equal essence of all phenomena without staying in the stage of personal liberation alone; how they manifest the qualities of buddhas without stopping the practice of enlightening beings; how they remain in the stage of enlightening beings yet show the sphere of all buddhas; how they transcend all worldly states yet act in the midst of worldly states; how they achieve the reality-body yet produce endless physical manifestations; how they resort to the formless reality-body yet manifest bodies like all beings; how they comprehend all the inexpressible truths, yet expound the truths to sentient beings in all languages; how they know there are no beings in the elements of existence, yet do not give up efforts to guide all beings; how they realize all phenomena are unoriginated and unperishing, yet do not give up the effort to serve all buddhas; how they realize there are no results of action in phenomena, yet do not give up the effort to perform good deeds.”

shAkya'i bu mo go bas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la 'di skad ces smras so/ / rigs kyi bu/ de ltar khyod byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa'i chos nyid rnam pa de lta bu dri bar sems pa lags so/ /legs so/ / dri ba brjod pa de dag kyang kun tu bzang po'i smon lam dang spyod pa la mngon du gyur pa'i tshig go /

Gopā, the Śākya maiden, said to Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, “Noble one, it is excellent, excellent, that you intended to ask in that way about the nature of bodhisattva conduct. Those questions are also the words of the completely good prayer and conduct.

Gopa said to Sudhana, “It is very good that you think it fit to ask about the nature of this kind of practice of enlightening beings, as this is the question of one who is set on practicing the vow of universal good.
rigs kyi bu/ de bas na/ legs par nyon la shin tu yid la zungs shig dang / sangs rgyas kyi byin gyis bstan par bya'o/ /
“Therefore, noble one, listen carefully and remember, for I shall teach through the blessing of the Buddha.
So listen well and think carefully, for I will tell you, by the power of Buddha.

rigs kyi bu/ chos bcu dang ldan pa'i byang chub sems dpa' rnams ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa rnam pa 'di lta bu mig 'phrul gyi gzhi'i dpe dang 'dra ba/ ye shes kyi 'od kun tu 'byung ba yongs su rdzogs par byed do/ /
“Noble one, the bodhisattvas who have ten qualities such as these fulfill the bodhisattva conduct that is like the appearance of magical illusions and gives rise to the light of wisdom.
“There are ten things by which enlightening beings fulfill this kind of enlightening practice, the light of total knowledge, like the cosmic net of interrelation of all things.

bcu gang zhe na/ 'di lta ste/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen rlabs po che la brten pa dang / mos pa rgya chem po rab tu thob pa dang / dge ba'i bsam pa rlabs po che rnam par dag pa dang / bsod nams dang ye shes rgya mtsho yangs pas rab tu brtan pa'i sems dang / sangs rgyas skye ba 'byung pa'i chos bstan pa chen po thos pa rab tu thob pa dang / dus gsum gyi de bzhin gshegs pa la mos pa'i sems kyis gnas pa dang / byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa'i dkyil 'khor thams cad mnyam pa nyid du khong du chud pa dang / de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi byin gyi rlabs rab tu thob pa dang / rang bzhin gyis snying rje chen po'i lhag pa'i bsam pa rnam par dag pa dang / 'khor ba'i 'khor lo thams cad rab tu gcad pa'i sems kyi stobs shugs drag po dang ldan pa rab tu thob pa ste/

“What are these ten? They are (1) reliance on sublime kalyāṇamitras, (2) the attainment of a vast aspiration, (3) a pure, sublime virtuous motivation, (4) a mind supported by a vast ocean of merit and wisdom, (5) being able to hear great teachings of the Dharma that has originated and arisen from the buddhas, (6) the attainment of aspiration toward the tathāgatas of the three times, (7) the comprehension of the equality of all the fields of bodhisattva conduct, (8) the attainment of the blessing of all the tathāgatas, (9) the natural, pure, higher motivation of great compassion, and (10) that attainment of the strong power of the motivation to end the continuation of all the cycles of saṃsāra.

What are the ten? Association with superior spiritual friends; attainment of enormous devotion; purity of lofty good will; a state of mind founded on oceanic virtue and knowledge; listening to the great teaching of buddhas; associating with thought devoted to the buddhas of past, present, and future; equally following the practices of all enlightening beings; gaining the empowerment of all buddhas; purity of intent, greatly compassionate in nature; attainment of the basic power of mind to stop all vicious circles.

rigs kyi bu/ chos bcu po de dag dang ldan pa'i byang chub sems dpa' rnams byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa rnam pa 'di lta bu mig 'phrul gyi gzhi'i dpe dang 'dra ba/ 'od kun tu 'byung ba yongs su rdzogs par byed do/ /
“Noble one, the bodhisattvas who have those ten qualities fulfill the bodhisattva conduct that is like the appearance of magical illusions and gives rise to the light of wisdom.[1753]
Having attained these ten things, enlightening beings fulfill this kind of enlightening practice, like the cosmic net of interrelation of all things, radiating total knowledge.

rigs kyi bu/ de brtson 'grus phyir mi ldog pa dang ldan pa'i byang chub sems dpa' rnams ni/ chos de dag thob par gyur nas kyang mi zad pa'i tshul du mngon par sgrub cing /sgom pa dang / shin tu rgya che bar bya ba'i phyir dge ba'i bshes gnyen bsnyen bkur cing rnam pa bcus mngon par dga' bar byed do/ /

“Noble one, the bodhisattvas with nonregressing diligence who have obtained those ten qualities, in order to accomplish an inexhaustible way and practice an extremely vast meditation, serve the kalyāṇamitras and please them in ten ways.

“Then enlightening beings with unrelenting vigor, having attained these things, developing and expanding them by putting them into practice in endless ways, propitiate spiritual benefactors in ten ways:

bcu gang zhe na/ 'di lta ste/ lus dang srog la phangs par mi rtsi ba dang / 'khor ba'i yo byad don du mi gnyer ba dang / chos thams cad kyi rang bzhin mnyam pa nyid du khong du chud pa dang / thams cad mkhyen pa'i smon lam las phyir mi ldog pa dang / chos kyi dbyings kyi tshul thams cad la rnam par lta ba dang / srid pa'i rgya mtsho thams cad las gyen du 'phags pa'i yid dang / gnas med pa'i chos kyi nam mkha' la mi gnas mi rten pa dang / byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi smon lam la bsgribs pa med pa dang / zhing rgya mtsho thams cad du rab tu 'dal ba dang / byang chub sems dpa'i ye shes kyi dkyil 'khor bsgribs pa med pa shin tu sbyangs pa ste/

“What are those ten ways? They are (1) having no concern for one’s own life and body, (2) having no interest in the requisites of saṃsāra, (3) having the comprehension of the equality of all phenomena, (4) having an irrevocable prayer for omniscience, (5) observing all the ways of the realm of the Dharma, (6) having a mind that rises above the entire ocean of existences, (7) having no dependence or location within the space of the locationless Dharma, (8) having all the unobscured prayers of a bodhisattva, (9) pervading the entire ocean of realms, and (10) having the purified unobscured field of the knowledge of a bodhisattva.

by indifference to themselves, by not seeking worldly goods, by realizing the equality of essence of all things, by not turning back from the commitment to omniscience, by observing all the principles of the cosmos, by being mentally free of all existents, by independence in the space of truth where there is nothing to depend on, by freedom from obstruction in the undertaking of all enlightening beings, by entering all lands, by perfect clarification and purification of the unobstructed sphere of knowledge of enlightening beings.”
rigs kyi bu/ chos bcu po de dag dang ldan pa'i byang chub sems dpa' rnams dge ba'i bshes gnyen bsnyen bkur cing mngon par dga' bar byed do/ /
“Noble one, the bodhisattvas who have those ten qualities serve and please the kalyāṇamitras.”
de nas shAkya'i bu mo go bas don de nyid yongs su bstan pa'i phyir sangs rgyas kyi byin gyis phyogs bcur bltas te de'i tshe tshigs su bcad pa 'di dag smras so/ /
Then the Śākya maiden Gopā, in order to teach the meaning of that, through the blessing of the buddhas looked into the ten directions and recited these verses:
Then, by the empowerment of Buddha, looking over the ten directions, Gopa uttered these verses illustrating what she meant:

rlabs chen dri med blo ldan gzhan gyi don zhugs shing / / dge bshes dam pa bsnyen brtson g.yo dang sgyu med pa/ / ston pa'i 'du shes thob cing skyo med brtson 'grus can/ / de dag spyod pa 'jig rten mig 'phrul 'dra 'di yin/ /

“Those sublime, stainless, wise ones engaged in benefiting others, Dedicated without deceit or deception to serving excellent friends, Recognizing them as teachers and having unflagging diligence‍— They carry out in the world this conduct that is like a magical apparition. {11}
Those who set out for vast pure wisdom for the welfare of others And serve true benefactors honestly With tireless vigor, seeing them as teachers, Carry out practice in the world like the cosmic net.

gang rnams mos pa rlabs chen mkha' dang 'dra ldan zhing / / de yi khongs su dus gsum 'jig rten chud pa dang / / zhing dang sems can chos dang sangs rgyas de bzhin pa/ / ye shes 'od byed de dag spyod pa 'di yin no/ /

“There are those who have sublime motivation as vast as space Within whom is contained the worlds of the three times, Realms, beings, phenomena, and likewise the buddhas. This is the conduct of those who shine with wisdom. {12}
Those whose devotion is vast as the sky, Embracing all worlds of past, present, and future, All lands, beings, phenomena, and buddhas— Theirs is this practice, producers of the light of knowledge.

gang rnams bsam pa mkha' 'dra mtha' dang dbus med la/ / kun nas nyon mongs dri mas mgos rab dag cing / / de bzhin gshegs pa kun gyi yon tan 'byung gyur pa/ / de dag spyod pa mig 'phrul gzhi yi rnam pa 'dra/ /

“There are those whose motivation is like space, without end or middle, Who are completely pure, unstained by the kleśas, And who give rise to the qualities of all the tathāgatas. Their conduct is like the appearance of magical apparitions. {13}
When the will is infinite as the sky, Supremely pure, free from the taint of afflictions, Therein arise the virtues of all buddhas, Concentrating the whole variety of the cosmic net of practice.

kun mkhyen ye shes rnam yangs tshad med bsam yas dag / yon tan rgya mtshos yid bsal ldan pa nyer brten pa/ / de dag bsod nams rgya mtsho'i lus ngag snying po ste/ / 'jig rten spyod kyang 'jig rten dri mas gos mi 'gyur/ /

“There are those who have clear minds and an ocean of qualities And are established in vast, limitless, inconceivable, omniscient wisdom. They have bodies that have an ocean of merit and a pure essence That is unstained by worldly impurities even though they act within the world. {14}
The wise who rest on great oceans of virtue, Inconceivable, infinite, vast as omniscience, As pure offspring of the body of all virtues They act in the world unstained by the filth of the world.

rgyal ba'i gsung gi yan lag sgra skad tshul kun gyis/ / chos kyi 'brug sgra nyan kyang gang rnams mi ngoms shing / / chos tshul rjes su snyegs pa'i shes rab 'od kyi sgron/ / de dag 'gro bar 'od gsal byed pa'i spyod 'di yin/ /

“There are those who never have enough of listening to the thunder of the Dharma That has the aspects of the speech of the jinas and all the ways of languages And who are lamps of the light of wisdom, which follow the way of the Dharma. This is the conduct of those who bring illumination to beings. {15}
Those who listen to the teaching of buddhas And tirelessly catch every nuance Are lamps shining with wisdom in accord with truth; Theirs is this practice which lights the world.

gang rnams phyogs bcu'i de bzhin gshegs pa tshad med pa/ / gzhan dang gzhan dag sems kyi skad cig kun sems shing / / bde gshegs rgya mtsho thams cad lta zhing shes byed pa/ / sangs rgyas sems ldan de dag spyod yul 'di yin no/ /

“There are those who comprehend in each instant of the mind Each one of the countless tathāgatas in the ten directions, And they see and know the entire ocean of sugatas. This is the conduct of those who keep the buddhas in mind. {16}
Those who perceive in an instant of awareness The infinite buddhas everywhere, interrelated, Contemplate the ocean of all buddhas; This is the way into the mind of the enlightened.

rgyal ba rnams kyi rnam par yangs pa'i 'khor mthong zhing / / de dag ting nge 'dzin tshul rgya mtsho mang bo dang / / smon lam rgya mtsho mtha' dang dbus med tshul 'jug pa/ / mig 'phrul lta bu de dag spyod pa 'di yin no; ;

“There are those who see the vast assemblies of followers of the jinas And who comprehend the ocean of their ways of samādhi And the ways of their vast ocean of prayers with no end or middle. This conduct of theirs is like the appearance of illusions. {17}
Those who see the vast audiences of the buddhas Enter the ocean of their meditations And their infinite ocean of vows; This is the practice of those like the cosmic net.

phyogs bcu'i rgyal ba ma lus kun gyis byin brlabs te/ / phyi mtha'i bskal par spyod byed kun tu bzang po'i rnams/ / zhing rnams 'byams klas kun tu gzugs brnyan byung gyur pa/ / chos 'od byed pa de dag spyod pa 'di yin no/ /

“There are those who have been blessed by every jina in the ten directions, Who have the completely good conduct till the final kalpa, And whose images appear throughout the vast extent of the realms. This is the conduct of those who bring the light of the Dharma. {18}
Those empowered by all the buddhas Practice universal good for endless ages, Reflected in all lands; This is the practice of the lights of truth.

gang rnams ye shes nyi ma snying rje'i dkyil 'khor can/ / 'gro ba nyams nyes mthong zhing chos kyi 'od snang bas/ / 'gro ba'i mun pa bsal cing brtan pa 'char 'byung ba/ / nyi ma lta bus de dag spyod pa 'di yin no/ /

“There are those who have the disk of the sun of compassion, Who, seeing beings in distress, illuminate them with the Dharma’s light, Clear away the darkness of beings, and cause the teachings to shine. This is the conduct of those who are like the sun. {19}
The suns of compassion and knowledge emerge, steadfast, Seeing the misfortune of the world, And disperse the darkness of delusion with the light of truth; This is the practice of those like the sun.

skye rgu srid pa'i rgyud na 'dre ldog mthong gyur nas/ / yid gsal 'khor ba'i rgyud rnams phyir zlog rab gnas shing / / chos kyi 'khor lo kun nas yongs su sgrub byed pa/ / spyod pa kun bzang dam pa'i blo can rab tu spyod/ /

“There are those who see beings circling through existences, And those clear-minded ones remain, countering saṃsāra’s flow, And everywhere they bring about the wheel of the Dharma. They are practicing the wise, supreme, completely good conduct. {20}

Seeing people revolve in the rut of existence, The wise stand opposed to the flow of the mundane whirl; Developing the measureless wheel of true teaching, They practice universal higher goodness and wisdom.

tshul 'di bslab pa de dag mtha' dang dbus med pa'i/ / lus rnams bsam pa ji bzhin 'gro bar nyer bstan te/ / gzugs brnyan mig yor 'dra ba'i rang lus tshad med pas/ / srid pa'i rgya mtsho dag na 'gro mang yongs smin byed/ /

“There are those who, training in this, manifest to beings, In accord with aspirations, bodies without limit or middle, Their countless bodies being like reflections or mirages, And they ripen many beings within the ocean of existences. {21}
Those who learn these infinite principles, Appearing in the world according to people’s mentalities, With their own bodies like reflected images, Develop people in the oceans of being.

byams tshul shin tu yangs pas 'gro mang rgyas bkang ste/ / mos pa sna tshogs 'gro la rnam par spyod bstan nas/ / 'gro bar bsam pa ji bzhin chos kyi char 'bebs shing / / brtan pa byang chub don du sems can khrag khrig 'dul/ /

“There are those who are spreading among beings through the vast ways of love, Manifesting conducts to beings with various dispositions, And sending down a rain of Dharma in accordance with the aspirations of beings. Those resolute ones guide billions of beings toward enlightenment.” {22}

Suffusing the world with myriad expressions of love, Showing spiritual practice to people of various interests, Teaching them according to their mentalities, The steadfast lead billions to enlightenment.

de nas shAkya'i bu mo go pas tshigs su bcad pa de dag smras nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la 'di skad ces smras so; ; rigs kyi bu/ kho mos ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin rgya mtsho'i tshul thams cad la rnam par lta ba'i yul thob pa'o/ /

Those are the verses that Gopā, the Śākya maiden, recited. She then said to Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, “Noble one, I have attained the bodhisattva liberation called the range of the view of all the ways of the ocean of the samādhis of the bodhisattvas.”
Then Gopa said to Sudhana, “I have attained an enlightening liberation whose sphere is observation of the ocean of concentrations of all enlightening beings.”
nor bzang gis smras pa; 'phags ma/ byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin rgya mtsho'i tshul la rnam par lta ba'i yul de'i yul ji lta bu zhig mchis/
Sudhana asked, “Āryā, what is this bodhisattva liberation called the range of the view of all the ways of the ocean of the samādhis of the bodhisattvas like?”
Sudhana asked, “What is the scope of this liberation?”

smras pa/ rigs kyi bu; kho mo byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa 'di la snyoms par zhugs na/ 'jig rten gyi khams 'di'i bskal pa sangs rgyas kyi zhing brjod du med pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba rnyed mthong zhing khong du chud do/ / bskal pa de dag gi sems can lam gyi rgyud thams cad du gtogs pa ji snyed cig yod pa de dag kyang rab tu shes so/ /

Gopā answered, “Noble one, when I rest within this bodhisattva liberation, I see and comprehend as many kalpas in this world realm as there are atoms in countless buddha realms. I know all the existences of beings who are within that kalpa.
Gopa replied, “Having attained this liberation, I penetrate as many ages in this world as atoms in untold buddha-lands, and I know all the beings in all conditions of existence therein,

sems can de dag gi shi 'pho dang / skye ba'i sgo ji snyed cig yod pa de bzhin du rab tu shes so/ / mngon par 'grub pa'i sgo ji snyed cig yod pa dang / las mngon par 'du byed pa yongs su sgrub pa ji snyed cig yod pa dang / las rnam par smin pa sna tshogs ji snyed cig yod pa de dag kyang rab tu shes so/ / de dag gi las yongs su blangs pa dge ba yang rab tu shes so/ /

I also know all the gateways into death and rebirth of those beings. I know all their entrances into becoming, all their acquisition of created karma, and all the various ripenings of their karma. I know all the karma acquired through good actions.
and I know all the deaths and births of those beings, their developments, their accomplishments, the variety of results of their actions; I know their undertakings—good,
mi dge ba dang / 'byung ba dang / mi 'byung ba dang / nges pa dang / ma nges pa dang /
I know all the karma that is bad, that brings emancipation, that does not bring emancipation, that is definite, and that is indefinite;
bad, liberative, nonliberative, certain, uncertain,
log par nges pa dang / bag la nyal ba dang bcas pa dang / bag la nyal ba med pa dang /
I know the definitely false, the latent, the nonlatent,
wrongly fixated, compulsive, noncompulsive,
dge ba'i rtsa ba phun sum tshogs pa dang / dge ba'i rtsa ba rgud par gyur pa dang / dge ba'i rtsa ba yongs su zin pa dang / mi dge ba'i rtsa ba yongs su zin pa dang /
the perfection of roots of merit, the loss of roots of merit, the retention of roots of merit, the retention of roots of demerit,
based on good, not based on good, fostered by good, fostered by evil,
dge ba dang mi dge ba yongs su zin pa dang / de dag gi dge ba'i chos yongs su 'dus pa dang / sdig to'i chos yongs su 'dus pa'i las yongs su blangs pa yang rab tu shes so/ /
the retention of roots of merit and demerit, the acquisition of good qualities, and the acquisition of bad qualities.
fostered by good and evil, good by development, bad through neglect.

bskal pa sangs rgyas kyi zhing brjod du med pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed po de dag la sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das ji snyed cig byung ba de dag gi mtshan rgya mtsho yang shes shing khong du chud do/ /
“I know and comprehend all the buddha bhagavats that appear in those kalpas as numerous as the atoms in countless buddha realms. I know and comprehend the ocean of their names.
“I know the oceans of names of all the buddhas in those ages as numerous as atoms in untold buddha-lands;
sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das de dag gis thugs dang po bskyed pa rgya mtsho yang rab tu shes so; ;
I know the ocean of the first developments of the aspiration to enlightenment by those buddha bhagavats.
I know the oceans of initial inspirations of those buddhas,

thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du zhugs pa'i tshul rgya mtsho yang rab tu shes so/ / smon lam rgya mtsho thams cad mngon par bsgrubs pa yang rab tu shes so/ / sngon gyi sangs rgyas byung ba rnams kyi drung du gshegs pa rgya mtsho yang rab tu shes so/ / sngon gyi sangs rgyas la mchod cing rim gror mdzad pa'i sbyor ba rgya mtsho yang rab tu shes so/ / sngon byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa yongs su rdzogs par mdzad pa rgya mtsho yang rab tu shes so/ / 'byung ba'i rgyan rgya mtsho yang rab tu shes so/ /

I know the ocean of their ways of undertaking the attainment of omniscience. I know the creation of their entire ocean of prayers. I know the ocean of their going into the presence of past buddhas. I know the ocean of their engagements in offering to and serving past buddhas. I know the ocean of their perfecting bodhisattva conduct in the past. I know the ocean of their displays of setting forth.

the ways they set out for omniscience, their undertakings of the oceans of all vows, their heading for previous buddhas, their oceans of efforts in the service of previous buddhas, their oceans of fulfillment of past enlightening practices, their oceans of arrangements of means of emancipation.

sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das de dag gis sems can yongs su smin par mdzad pa dang gdul ba rgya mtsho yang rab tu shes so/ / mngon par 'tshang rgya ba mdzad pa rgya mtsho yang rab tu shes so/ / chos kyi 'khor lo bskor ba'i khyu mchog gi mthu dang rnam par 'phrul pa yang rab tu shes so/ / sangs rgyas kyi rnam par 'phrul pa rgya mtsho thams cad kyang rab tu shes so/ / sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das de dag gi 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor rnam par phye ba dag kyang rab tu shes so/ /

I know the ocean of the ripening and guiding of beings by those buddha bhagavats. I know the ocean of their attainment of buddhahood. I know miraculous manifestation and supremacy in turning the wheel of the Dharma. I know the entire ocean of the miracles of those buddhas.

I also know the oceans of those buddhas’ development and guidance of sentient beings, and I know their oceans of attainment of enlightenment, their majestic displays of mystic power in turning the wheel of the teaching, and their oceans of miraculous displays of all buddhas.

'khor gyi dkyil 'khor de dag na nyan thos ji snyed cig 'khod pa de dag gi 'byung ba'i tshul yang rab tu shes so/ / sngon kyi dge ba'i rtsa ba yang rab tu shes so; ; lam bsgoms pa sna tshogs kyang rab tu shes so/ / ye shes thob par bya ba phun sum tshogs shing rnam par dag pa'i bye brag kyang rab tu shes so/ /

I know the categories of the assemblies of followers of those buddha bhagavats. I know all the śrāvakas present among those followers and their ways of setting forth. I know their past roots of merit. I know their various meditations on the path. I know the categories of their pure, perfect attainment of wisdom.

I also know the differences in the audiences of those buddhas, and I know the methods of emancipation of the listeners in those audiences, as well as their past roots of goodness, the variety of their cultivation of the path, and the difference in the purity of their attainment of knowledge.

de bzhin gshegs pa de dag gis sems can ji snyed cig rang sangs rgyas kyi byang chub la bkod pa de dag kyang rab tu shes so/ / rang sangs rgyas de dag gi sngon gyi dge ba'i rtsa ba ji snyed cig yod pa de dag kyang rab tu shes so; ; rang sangs rgyas de dag gis rang sangs rgyas kyi byang chub khong du chung ba ji snyed cig yod pa de dag kyang rab tu shes so/ / rang sangs rgyas de dag gi zhi ba'i rnam par spyod pa la rnam par rtse ba'i rnam par thar ba'i sgo ji snyed cig yod pa de dag kyang rab tu shes so/ / rang sangs rgyas de dag gi rdzu 'phrul gyi rnam par 'phrul ba ji snyed cig yod pa de dag kyang rab tu shes so/ / rang sangs rgyas de dag gis sems can ji snyed cig yongs su smin par byas pa de dag kyang rab tu shes so/ / rang sangs rgyas de dag gis chos bstan pa ji snyed cig brjod pa de dag kyang rab tu shes so/ / rang sangs rgyas de dag ting nge 'dzin mtha' yas pa la rnam par spyod cing rnam par thar pa rnam pa sna tshogs kyis rnam par rtse ba ji snyed cig yod pa de dag kyang rab tu shes so/ /

I know all the beings that those tathāgatas established in the enlightenment of the pratyekabuddhas. I know all the past roots of merit of those pratyekabuddhas. I know all the realization of pratyekabuddha enlightenment by those pratyekabuddhas. I know all the entrances to the liberation of the play of the peaceful conduct of those pratyekabuddhas. I know all the various miraculous manifestations of those pratyekabuddhas. I know all the beings that are ripened by those pratyekabuddhas. I know all the Dharma teachings that are taught by those pratyekabuddhas. I know all the infinite samādhis of the pratyekabuddhas that they practice and the various entrances to liberations that they play in.

I also know the sentient beings who have been led to individual enlightenment by those buddhas, and I know the past roots of goodness of those individual illuminates, as well as their attainments of individual enlightenment, the doors of liberation mystically developing in their peaceful states, their various spiritual transformations, their development of others, their teachings, and the various freedoms of liberation in their infinite states of concentration.
sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das de dag gi yongs su mya ngan las 'da' ba ji snyed pa de dag kyang rab tu shes so/ /
I know all the parinirvāṇas of those buddha bhagavats.
I also know the ultimate extinction of those buddhas.
sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das de dag gi byang chub sems dpa'i 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor rgya mtsho ji snyed pa de dag kyang rab tu shes so/ /
I know the entire ocean of the assemblies of bodhisattva followers of those buddha bhagavats.
“I also know the oceans of enlightening beings surrounding those buddhas,
byang chub sems dpa' de dag gis thog ma dge ba'i rtsa ba bskyed bdag kyang rab tu shes so; ;
I know the first development of roots of merit by those bodhisattvas.
and I know those enlightening beings’ first cultivation of roots of goodness,
thog ma sems pa skyed pa'i smon lam dag kyang rab tu shes so/ /
I know their first development of the aspiration to enlightenment.
their first inspirations and vows,
smon lam rnam par dag pa tha dad pa dag kyang rab tu shes so/ /
I know their different prayers.
the variety of their vows,
byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pas 'byung ba'i rgyan thams cad mngon par sgrub pa rnam pa tha dad pa yang rab tu shes so/ /
I know the different forms of their accomplishment of the displays of setting forth through bodhisattva conduct.
the variety of their production of arrangements of vehicles of emancipation by all the practices of enlightening beings,
pha rol tu phyin pa'i lam gyi yan lag gi tshogs rnam par dag par bya ba rnam pa tha dad pa yang rab tu shes so/ /
I know the different forms of their pure accumulation of the aspect of the path of the perfections.
the variety of their perfection of provisions for the path of transcendence,
byang chub sems dpa'i lam la nan tan du bya ba'i rgyan rnam pa tha dad pa yang rab tu shes so/ /
I know the different forms of their display of practicing the bodhisattva path.
the variety of the manifestations of their practices of the path of enlightening beings,
byang chub sems dpa'i sa yongs su gnon pa'i tshogs rnam pa tha dad pa yang rab tu shes so/ /
I know the different forms of their accumulations of ascending the bodhisattva bhūmis.
the variety of their provisions for advancing through the states of enlightening beings,
byang chub sems dpa'i sa yongs su gnon pa'i shugs drag po rnam pa tha dad pa yang rab tu shes so/ /
I know the different forms of the strong powers of ascending the bodhisattva bhūmis.
the variety of the speed of their advance through the states of enlightening beings,
byang chub sems dpa'i sa la bzem pa'i mthu dang ldan pa'i ting nge 'dzin gyi dkyil 'khor rnam pa tha dad pa yang rab tu shes so/ /
I know the different forms of the fields of samādhis that have the power to cause one to progress[1754] through the bodhisattva bhūmis.
the variety of their spheres of concentration in the stages of enlightening beings,
byang chub sems dpa'i sa la yongs su gnon pas rnam par rtse ba dag kyang rab tu shes so/ /
I know the miraculous displays on ascending the bodhisattva bhūmis.
the spiritual manifestations of their advance through the states of enlightening beings,
byang chub sems dpa'i sa yongs su gnon pa'i rnam par spyod pa dag kyang rab tu shes so/ /
I know the conduct on ascending the bodhisattva bhūmis.
their spiritual states during their progress through the states of enlightening beings,
byang chub sems dpa'i sa la rab tu gnas pa dag kyang rab tu shes so/ /
I know being established on the bodhisattva bhūmis.
their footholds in the stages of enlightening beings,
byang chub sems dpa'i sa sgom pa'i rgyud dag kyang rab tu shes so/ /
I know the continuous meditation on the bodhisattva bhūmis.
their practices cultivating the states of enlightening beings,
byang chub sems dpa'i sa yongs su sbyangs pa'i tshul dag kyang rab tu shes so/ /
I know the ways of purification on the bodhisattva bhūmis.
their methods of purifying the stages of enlightening beings,
byang chub sems dpa'i sa la yang dag par gnas par bya ba dag kyang rab tu shes so/ /
I know dwelling on the bodhisattva bhūmis.
their abodes in the stages of enlightening beings,
byang chub sems dpa'i sa'i mtshan ma dag kyang rab tu shes so/ /
I know the characteristics of the bodhisattva bhūmis.
their characteristics in the stages of enlightening beings,
byang chub sems dpa'i sa'i dbang dag kyang rab tu shes so/ /
I know the powers of the bodhisattva bhūmis.
their mastery of the stages of enlightening beings,
byang chub sems dpa'i sa nas sar 'phar pa'i ye shes dag kyang rab tu shes so/ /
I know the wisdoms that cause ascent through the bodhisattva bhūmis.
their science of entry into the stages of enlightening beings,
byang chub sems dpa'i sa yongs su bsdu ba'i ye shes dag kyang rab tu shes so/ /
I know the wisdom that gathers together the bodhisattva bhūmis.[1755]
the enlightening beings’ science of salvation,
byang chub sems dpa'i sa yongs su smin par bya ba'i ye shes dag kyang rab tu shes so/ /
I know the wisdom that ripens the bodhisattva bhūmis.[1756]
the enlightening beings’ science of development,
byang chub sems dpa' rnam par dgod pa la yang dag par gnas par bya ba yang rab tu shes so/ /
I know the established states of bodhisattvas.
the different states of enlightening beings,
byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa'i dkyil 'khor gyi rgya yang rab tu shes so/ /
I know the vast field of conduct of bodhisattvas.
the mystic projections of enlightening beings’ practices,
byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la rnam par rtse ba dag kyang rab tu shes so/ /
I know the miraculous displays[1757] of the conduct of bodhisattvas.
byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin rgya mtsho dag kyang rab tu shes so/ /
I know the oceans of the samādhis of bodhisattvas.
the oceans of concentrations of enlightening beings,
byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa'i chul rgya mtsho dag kyang rab tu shes so/ /
I know the oceans of the liberations of bodhisattvas.
the oceans of methods of liberation of enlightening beings.
byang chub sems dpa' de dag sems kyi skad cig re re la ting nge 'dzin rgya mtsho sna tshogs thob par byed pa dag kyang rab tu shes so/ /
I know the attainment by bodhisattvas of various samādhis in each instant of mind.
I also know those enlightening beings’ attainments of oceans of various concentrations in each moment of consciousness,
thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi snang ba'i tshul thob par byed pa dag kyang rab tu shes so/ /
I know their attainments of the ways of the illumination of omniscience.
their discoveries of the range of omniscience,
thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi glog gi snang ba'i sprin dag kyang rab tu shes so/ /
I know the clouds of light from the lightning of omniscience.
their tremendous flashes of omniscience,
byang chub sems dpa'i bzod pa thob pa'i tshul dag kyang rab tu shes so/ /
I know the ways of the attainment of the patience of bodhisattvas.
their means of attainment of the forbearance of enlightening beings,
thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du 'jug pa'i ye shes kyi rnam par gnon pa dag kyang rab tu shes so; ;
I know the prowess of immersion in omniscience.
their plunges into omniscience. I also know those enlightening beings’ travels to oceans of lands,
byang chub sems dpa' rnams zhing rgya mtshor rjes su bgrod par byed pa dag kyang rab tu shes so/ /
I know the proceeding to oceans of realms by bodhisattvas.
their penetrations of the principles of oceans of phenomena,
chos rgya mtsho'i tshul la 'jug pa dag kyang rab tu shes so/ /
I know their entry into an ocean of the ways of the Dharma.
sems can rgya mtsho'i mtshan nyid tha dad pa dag kyang rab tu shes so/ /
I know the different characteristics of an ocean of beings.
the variety of characteristics of all things,
byang chub sems dpa'i dam par spyod pa'i tshul thams cad kyi rnam par 'phrul pa dag kyang rab tu shes so/ /
I know the miraculous manifestations of all the ways of the conduct[1758] of bodhisattvas.
the mystic projection of the designs of all states of enlightening beings,
smon lam gyi tshul sna tshogs rgya mtsho dag kyang rab tu shes so/ /
I know the oceans of the various ways of their prayers.
the oceans of principles of various vows,
rdzu 'phrul gyi rnam par 'phrul pa sna tshogs rgya mtsho rnam pa tha dad pa dag kyang rab tu shes so/ /
I know the different forms of the ocean of their various miraculous manifestations.
and the variety of oceans of miracles.

rigs kyi bu/ kho mo ji ltar mi mjed kyi 'jig rten gyi khams 'di'i 'das pa dang da ltar byung ba'i bskal pa sna tshogs rgya mtsho la zhugs te khong du chud pa de bzhin du phyi ma'i mtha' gcig nas gcig tu brgyud de rgyun mi 'chad pa'i ma 'ongs pa'i bskal pa rgya mtsho dag kyang rab tu shes so/ /

“Noble one, in the same way that I know and comprehend the ocean of various kalpas in this Sahā realm in the past and in the present, I also know the ocean of the continuous succession of future kalpas.
“Just as I penetrate the various oceans of ages past in this world, in the same way I know the endless unbroken succession of ages of the future;

mi mjed kyi 'jig rten gyi khams kyi bskal pa rgya mtsho ji ltar shes pa de bzhin du mi mjed kyi 'jig rten gyi khams su gtogs pa'i 'jig rten gyi khams gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa thams cad kyi bskal pa rgya mtsho dag kyang rab tu shes so/ /
and just as I know all this in this world, so do I know it in all the worlds within this world.

mi mjed kyi 'jig rten gyi khams su gtogs pa'i 'jig rten gyi khams gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa thams cad kyi bskal pa rgya mtsho ji ltar shes pa de bzhin du mi mjed kyi 'jig rten gyi khams kyi rdul shin tu phra ba'i khongs su chud pa'i 'jig rten gyi khams gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa thams cad kyi bskal pa rgya mtsho dag kyang rab tu shes so/ /

“In the same way that I know the ocean of kalpas of the entire succession of world realms that are contained within the Sahā world realm, I also know the ocean of kalpas of the entire succession of world realms contained within the atoms of the Sahā world realm.
And just as I know this in all the worlds within this world, so do I know it in all the worlds in the atoms of this world.

mi mjed kyi 'jig rten gyi khams kyi rdul shin tu phra ba'i khongs su chud pa'i 'jig rten gyi khams gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa thams cad kyi bskal pa rgya mtsho rnams ji ltar shes pa de bzhin du mi mjed kyi 'jig rten gyi khams phyogs bcur 'dab chags su gnas pa'i 'jig rten gyi khams thams cad kyi bskal pa rgya mtsho dag kyang rab tu shes so/ /

“In the same way that I know the ocean of kalpas of the entire succession of world realms contained within the atoms of the Sahā world realm, I also know the ocean of kalpas of all the world realms that surround the Sahā world realm in the ten directions.
And just as I know it in all the worlds in the atoms of this world, so do I know it in the worlds in the ten directions contiguous with this world.

mi mjed kyi 'jig rten gyi khams phyogs bcur 'dab chags su gnas pa'i 'jig rten gyi khams thams cad kyi bskal pa rgya mtsho rnams ji ltar shes pa de bzhin du mi mjed kyi 'jig rten gyi khams phyogs bcur 'dab chags su gnas pa gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa dag na gnas pa'i 'jig rten gyi khams thams cad kyi bskal pa rgya mtsho dag kyang rab tu shes so/ /

“In the same way that I know the ocean of kalpas of all the world realms that surround the Sahā world realm in the ten directions, I also know the ocean of kalpas of all the successive world realms present in all the world realms that surround the Sahā world realm in the ten directions.
And just as I know it in the worlds in the ten directions contiguous with this world, so do I know it in all the worlds in the ten directions surrounding this world.

mi mjed kyi 'jig rten gyi khams phyogs bcur 'dab chags su gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa dag na gnas pa'i 'jig rten gyi khams thams cad kyi bskal pa rgya mtsho rnams ji ltar shes pa de bzhin du phyogs bcu kun tu 'od rnam par snang ba'i 'jig rten gyi khams kyi rgyud du gtogs pa'i 'jig rten gyi khams thams cad kyi bskal pa rgya mtsho dag kyang rab tu shes so/ /

“In the same way that I know the ocean of kalpas of all the successive world realms present in the world realms that surround the Sahā world realm in the ten directions, I also know the ocean of kalpas of all the world realms contained within the family of the Prabhāsavairocana world realms in all the ten directions.[1759]
And just as I know it in all the worlds in the ten directions surrounding this world, so do I know it in all the worlds in the radiant world system of Vairocana.

phyogs bcu kun tu 'od rnam par snang ba'i 'jig rten gyi khams kyi rgyud du gtogs pa'i 'jig rten gyi khams thams cad kyi bskal pa rgya mtsho ji ltar shes pa de bzhin du/ phyogs bcu kun tu 'od rnam par snang ba'i 'jig rten gyi khams kyi rgyud phyogs bcur 'dab chags su gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa dag la gnas pa'i 'jig rten gyi khams kyi rgyud gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa rnams kyi bskal pa rgya mtsho dag kyang rab tu shes so/ /

“In the same way that I know the ocean of kalpas of all the world realms contained within the family of the Prabhāsavairocana world realms in all the ten directions, I also know the ocean of kalpas of all the successive world realms present in all the world realms that surround in the ten directions the family of the Prabhāsavairocana world realms.
And just as I know it in all the worlds in the radiant world system of Vairocana, I know it in all the worlds surrounding the radiant world system of Vairocana.

phyogs bcu kun tu 'od rnam par snang ba'i 'jig rten gyi khams kyi rgyud phyogs bcur 'dab chags su gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa dag la gnas pa'i 'jig rten gyi khams thams cad kyi bskal ba rgya mtsho rnams rab tu shes pa de bzhin du gzhi dang snying po me tog gi rgyan gyis brgyan pa'i 'jig rten gyi khams rgya mtsho 'dir gtogs pa'i 'jig rten gyi khams 'byams klas pa rnams kyi bskal pa rgya mtsho dag kyang rab tu shes so/ /

“In the same way that I know the ocean of kalpas of all the successive world realms present in all the world realms that surround in the ten directions the family of the Prabhāsavairocana world realms, I also know the ocean of kalpas in the vast extent of the world realms contained in this ocean of world realms, Kusumatalagarbhavyūhālaṃkāra.

And just as I know it in all the worlds surrounding the radiant world system of Vairocana, I know it in all the places in the worlds in the oceans of worlds in the masses of worlds in this whole flower treasury universe, and in all the structures and features of the worlds.
