de bzhin du 'jig rten gyi khams tshul du bya ba rnams dang / 'jig rten gyi khams kyi 'khor lo rnams dang / 'jig rten gyi khams kyi dkyil 'khor rnams dang / 'jig rten gyi khams kyi bye brag rnams dang / 'jig rten gyi khams kyi chu klung rnams dang / 'jig rten gyi khams kyi klong rnams dang / 'jig rten gyi khams yongs su 'khyil pa dang / 'jig rten gyi khams ri rab dang / 'jig rten gyi khams yongs su 'byung ba dang / 'jig rten gyi khams pad+mo dang / 'jig rten gyi khams sdong po dang / 'jig rten gyi khams rta babs dang / 'jig rten gyi khams ming du bya ba rnams kyi bskal pa rgya mtsho dag kyang rab tu shes so/ /

“In the same way, I know the ocean of kalpas in the ways of the world realms, in the circles of the world realms, in the field of the world realms, in the categories of the world realms, in the rivers of the world realms, in the vortexes of the world realms, in the revolving of the world realms, in the Sumerus of the world realms, in the arising of the world realms, in the lotuses of the world realms, in the trees of the world realms, in the toraṇas[1760] of the world realms, and in the naming of the world realms.

'jig rten gyi khams rgya mtsho gzhi dang snying po me tog gi rgyan gyis brgyan pa 'di ji ltar shes par gyur pa de bzhin du phyogs bcu mtha' yas mu med pa'i 'jig rten gyi khams rgya mtsho chos kyi dbyings kyis klas pa/ nam mkha'i mthas gtugs pa dag gi bcom ldan 'das rnam par snang mdzad kyi sngon gyi smon lam rgya mtsho dag kyang rab tu shes so/ /rjes su dran no/ /

“In the same way that I know the Kusumatalagarbhavyūhālaṃkāra ocean of world realms, I also know and remember the ocean of prayers made in the past by the Bhagavat Vairocana in the endless, limitless ocean of world realms in the ten directions throughout the extent of the realm of phenomena, up to the ends of space.
“And as in this flower treasury universe, so also in all universes in the endless cosmos, throughout space, I know, comprehend, and recall the oceans of past vows of Vairocana,
sngon gyi sbyor ba rgya mtsho dag la'ang shes shing khong du chud do/ /
I also know and comprehend the oceans of his past activities.
his oceans of past efforts,
sngon yongs su bsgrubs pa'i tshul rgya mtsho dag la yang shes shing khong du chud do/ /
I know and comprehend the oceans of his past accomplishments.
oceans of past attainments,
bskal pa mtha' dang dbus med par byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la yang dag par bzhugs pa mdzad pa dag kyang shes shing khong du chud do/ /
I also know and comprehend his continuing in bodhisattva conduct during kalpas without end or middle.
persistence in enlightening practice through infinite ages,
zhing yongs su dag par mdzad pa'i tshul dag kyang shes shing khong du chud do/ /
I also know and comprehend his ways of purifying realms.
methods of purifying lands,
sems can yongs su smin par mdzad pa'i thabs kyi tshul dag kyang shes shing khong du chud do/ /
I also know and comprehend the ways of his methods for ripening beings.
sngon gyi de bzhin gshegs pa rnams la bsnyen bkur mdzad cing gshegs pa'i rnam par 'phrul ba dag kyang shes shing khong du chud do/ /
I also know and comprehend his miraculous manifestations of going to the past tathāgatas and serving them.
means of serving past buddhas,
sngon gyi de bzhin gshegs pa la mchod cing rim gror mdzad pa'i sbyor ba'i tshul dag kyang shes shing khong du chud do/ /
I also know and comprehend his engagement in venerating and making offerings to the past tathāgatas.
sngon gyi de bzhin gshegs pa dag gis chos bstan pa yongs su bzung ba'i tshul dag kyang shes shing khong du chud do/ /
I also know and comprehend his ways of obtaining the Dharma teachings of the past tathāgatas.
ways of receiving the teachings of past buddhas,
sngon gyi byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin rab tu brnyes pa'i tshul dag kyang shes shing khong du chud do/ /
I also know and comprehend the ways of his attainment of bodhisattva samādhis.
methods of attaining enlightening concentrations in the past,
yo byad la dbang sgyur ba rab tu brnyes pa'i tshul dag kyang shes shing khong du chud do/ /
means of attaining control over utensils,
sngon gyi de bzhin gshegs pa'i yon tan rgya mtsho la nan tan du mdzad pa'i tshul dag kyang shes shing khong du chud do/ /
I also know and comprehend the ways of his practicing the ocean of the qualities of the past tathāgatas.
ways of practicing the oceans of virtues of past buddhas,
sbyin pa'i pha rol tu phyin pa'i tshul rgya mtsho dag kyang shes shing khong du chud do/ /
I also know and comprehend the oceans of his ways of the perfection of generosity.
oceans of ways of perfecting giving,
byang chub sems dpa'i tshul khrims dang brtul zhugs kyi dkyil 'khor yongs su dag pa mngon par sgrub pa mdzad pa'i tshul dag kyang shes shing khong du chud do/ /
I also know and comprehend the ways of his accomplishment of the pure field of disciplines and the correct conduct of bodhisattvas.
methods of effecting the purification of the conduct of an enlightening being,
byang chub sems dpa'i bzod pa brnyes pa'i tshul dag kyang shes shing khong du chud do/ /
I also know and comprehend the ways of his attainment of bodhisattva patience.
means of attaining the forbearance of an enlightening being,
byang chub sems dpa'i brtson 'grus kyi shugs drag po rgya mtsho dag kyang shes shing khong du chud do/ /
I also know and comprehend the ocean of his powerful bodhisattva diligence.
oceans of force of the vigor of an enlightening being,
bsam gtan gyi yan lag thams cad yongs su rdzogs par mdzad pa'i tshul rgya mtsho dag kyang shes shing khong du chud do/ /
I also know and comprehend the ocean of his perfecting the aspects of dhyāna.
oceans of methods of fulfilling all elements of meditation,
shes rab kyi dkyil 'khor yongs su dag par mdzad pa'i tshul rgya mtsho dag kyang shes shing khong du chud do/ /
I also know and comprehend the ocean of his ways of purifying the field of wisdom.
oceans of ways of purification of the sphere of wisdom,
'jig rten gyi khams kyi skye gnas thams cad du sku'i gzugs brnyan yongs su bstan pa mdzad pa'i thabs kyi tshul dag kyang shes shing khong du chud do/ /
I also know and comprehend his ways of methods in manifesting the images of his body through births in all the world realms.
means of manifesting reflections of life in all worlds,
kun tu bzang po'i spyod pa dang smon lam gyi dkyil 'khor yongs su dag par mdzad pa'i tshul dag kyang shes shing khong du chud do/ /
I also know and comprehend his ways of purifying the field of the completely good conduct and prayer.
ways of purification of the sphere of vows of practice of universal good,
zhing rgya mtsho thams cad yongs su rgyas par mdzad pa dag kyang shes shing khong du chud do/ /
I also know and comprehend his spreading through the ocean of realms.
pervasion of all worlds,
sangs rgyas kyi zhing thams cad yongs su dag par mdzad pa'i tshul rgya mtsho dag kyang shes shing khong du chud do/ /
I also know and comprehend the ocean of his ways of purifying all buddha realms.
oceans of means of purification of all lands,
de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad las ye shes snang bar gyur pa rgya mtsho dag kyang shes shing khong du chud do/ /
I also know and comprehend the ocean of the illumination of wisdom from all the tathāgatas.
oceans of light of knowledge of all buddhas,
sangs rgyas kyi zhing thams cad kyi byang chub yongs su gnas pa mdzad pa'i rnam par 'phrul pa rgya mtsho dag kyang shes shing khong du chud do/ /
I also know and comprehend the ocean of the miraculous manifestations of reaching[1761] the enlightenment of all buddhas.
oceans of spiritual manifestations of accession to the enlightenment of all buddhas,
de bzhin gshegs pa'i ye shes snang ba rab tu brnyes pa'i tshul dag kyang shes shing khong du chud do/ /
I also know and comprehend his ways of attaining the illumination of the wisdom of all the tathāgatas.
means of attainment of the range of knowledge of all buddhas,
thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du zhugs te thugs su chud pa'i tshul rgya mtsho dag kyang shes shing khong du chud do/ /
I also know and comprehend the ocean of his ways of comprehending the realization of omniscience.
mngon par rdzogs par 'tshang rgya ba'i rnam par 'phrul pa rgya mtsho dag kyang shes shing khong du chud do/ /
I also know and comprehend the ocean of the miraculous manifestation of the attainment of complete buddhahood.
oceans of mystic manifestations of attainment of enlightenment,
chos kyi 'khor lo bskor ba'i khyu mchog gi mthu dang rnam par rol pa'i tshul rgya mtsho dag kyang shes shing khong du chud do/ /
I also know and comprehend the ways of displaying and the power of supremacy in turning the wheel of the Dharma.
oceans of ways of free exercise of the majestic power of turning the wheel of teaching,
'khor gyi dkyil 'khor rgya mtsho dag kyang shes shing khong du chud do/ /
I also know and comprehend the ocean of the field of saṃsāra.
oceans of various audiences,
'khor gyi dkyil 'khor de dag gi byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi sngon gyi dge ba'i rtsa ba rgya mtsho dag kyang shes shing khong du chud do/ /
I also know and comprehend the ocean of the past roots of merit of all bodhisattvas in the field of saṃsāra.
the past roots of goodness of all the enlightening beings in all those audiences,
thog ma'i smon lam gyi tshul rgya mtsho dag kyang shes shing khong du chud do/ /
I also know and comprehend the ocean of the ways of initial prayers.
their oceans of initial vows,
sems can yongs su smin par byed pa dang 'dul ba'i thabs kyi tshul rgya mtsho dag kyang shes shing khong du chud do/ /
I also know and comprehend the ocean of the ways of the methods for ripening and guiding beings.
their oceans of methods of developing and guiding sentient beings,
bcom ldan 'das kyis sngon byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa mdzad pa'i tshe sems can rgya mtsho yongs su smin par mdzad pa de dag kyang shes shing khong du chud do/ /
I also know and comprehend the Bhagavat’s ripening of an ocean of beings when he was practicing bodhisattva conduct in the past.
the oceans of sentient beings matured by the Buddha as he carried out enlightening practice in the past,
sems can de dag gi sems kyi skad cig re re'i dge ba'i rtsa ba rnam par 'phrul pa'i thabs kyi tshul rgya mtsho dag kyang shes shing khong du chud do/ /
I also know and comprehend the ocean of the ways of methods that increase the roots of merit of those beings in each instant of their minds.
those enlightening beings’ oceans of means of causing roots of goodness to grow in every moment of consciousness,
ting nge 'dzin rab tu thob pa'i tshul rgya mtsho dag kyang shes shing khong du chud do/ /
I also know and comprehend the ocean of the ways of the attainment of samādhi.
their oceans of ways of attaining concentration,
gzungs kyi sgo rab tu thob pa'i tshul rgya mtsho dag kyang shes shing khong du chud do/ /
I also know and comprehend the ocean of the ways of the attainment of the power of mental retention.
oceans of means of attaining total mental command,
spobs pa'i ye shes kyi dkyil 'khor rnam par dag pa'i tshul rgya mtsho dag kyang shes shing khong du chud do/ /
I also know and comprehend the ocean of the ways of the pure field of the wisdom of eloquence.
oceans of means of purification of the sphere of expository knowledge,
byang chub sems dpa'i sa thams cad yongs su gnon pa'i rnam par 'phrul pa'i tshul rgya mtsho dag kyang shes shing khong du chud do/ /
I also know and comprehend the ocean of the ways of the miraculous manifestations of ascending all the bodhisattva bhūmis.
oceans of mystic manifestations of accession to all stages of enlightenment,
spyod pa'i dra ba mngon par sgrub pa'i tshul rgya mtsho dag kyang shes shing khong du chud do/ /
I also know and comprehend the ocean of the ways of accomplishing the net of conduct.
oceans of means of effecting the network of practice,
mthar gyis yongs su sgrub pa'i phyogs la 'jug pa'i ye shes kyi tshul rgya mtsho dag kyang shes shing khong du chud do/ /
I also know and comprehend the ocean of the ways of the wisdom that enters the direction of final accomplishment.
oceans of gradual refinement, oceans of knowledge of gradual attainment entering all worlds,

de dag gi dbang po dang / stobs dang / byang chub kyi yan lag dang / bsam gtan dang / rnam par thar pa dang / ting nge 'dzin dang / snyoms par 'jug pa'i rnam par 'phrul pa rgya mtsho dag kyang shes shing khong du chud do/ /
I also know and comprehend the ocean of his miraculous manifestations of the powers, strengths, aspects of enlightenment, dhyānas, liberations, samādhis, and samāpattis.
and oceans of all faculties, powers, elements of enlightenment, meditations, liberations, concentrations, attainments, and spiritual transformations.

ji ltar bcom ldan 'das rnam par snang mdzad kyi sangs rgyas dang byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa rgya mtsho chos kyi dbyings thams cad du byung ba shes shing khong du chud do/ / mngon par sgrub pa de bzhin du de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi sangs rgyas dang byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa rgya mtsho dang / ye shes kyi sgyu ma'i dra ba mtha' yas pa la 'jug pa chos kyi dbyings mtha' yas pa rgyas par 'gengs pa/ sgo mtha' yas pa nas shin tu bstan par bya ba/ phyi ma'i mtha' bskal par gnas pa la 'jug pas bstan par bya ba/ phyogs bcu'i 'jig rten gyi khams rgya mtsho chos kyi dbyings kyis klas pa/ nam mkha'i mthas gtugs par byung ba thams cad kyang ma 'dres par shes shing khong du chud do/ / mngon par sgrub bo/ /

“In the same way that I realize, know, and comprehend the ocean of the Bhagavat Vairocana’s buddha and bodhisattva conduct throughout the entire realm of phenomena, I also realize, know, and comprehend the ocean of buddha and bodhisattva conduct of all the tathāgatas and their entry into the infinite illusory net of wisdom, their pervasion of the infinite realm of phenomena, their teaching of infinite entrances, and their teaching through entering into remaining until the last of future kalpas, which appear distinctly within the ocean of the world realms of the ten directions, throughout the realm of phenomena up to the ends of space.

“And just as I comprehend, know, and realize the oceans of enlightening practice of Vairocana Buddha in this whole cosmos, so also do I comprehend, know, and realize the indivisible oceans of enlightening practice of all buddhas in all oceans of worlds throughout the cosmoses throughout all space. In this way I comprehend the entry into the indivisible totality of all enlightening beings’ practices, entry into the infinite web of illusion, infinite cosmic pervasion, infinite instruction, and indication of entry into the basis of endless eons, of all buddhas in all oceans of worlds throughout the cosmos, to the furthest reaches of space.

de ci'i phyir zhe na/ rigs kyi bu/ byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin gyi tshul rgya mtsho thams cad la rnam par lta ba'i yul gyi yul ni; de lta bu ste/ de'i phyir de la snyoms par zhugs na/ sems can thams cad kyi sems dang spyod pa'i tshul rab tu shes so/ /

“Why is that? Noble one, it is because this purview is that of the bodhisattva liberation called the range of the view of all the ways of the ocean of the samādhis of the bodhisattvas. When I am resting in that, I know the minds and conduct of all beings.

Why? Because this is the scope of the enlightening liberation whose sphere is observation of the ocean of concentrations of all enlightening beings; having attained this, I know the patterns of mental behavior of all beings,

sems can thams cad kyi dge ba'i tshogs kyang rab tu shes so/ / sems can thams cad kyi kun nas nyon mongs pa dang / rnam par byang ba'i ye shes kyi tshul rnams kyang rab tu shes so/ / sems can thams cad kyi las sna tshogs kyang rab tu shes so/ / nyan thos thams cad kyi ting nge 'dzin gyi sgo rnams kyang rab tu shes so/ / nyan thos thams cad kyi ting nge 'dzin gyi sa yang rab tu shes so/ / rang sangs rgyas thams cad kyi rnam par thar pa zhi bas rnam par 'phrul pa yang shes shing khong du chud do/ / byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi ting nge 'dzin rgya mtsho'i tshul dag kyang rab tu shes so/ / byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi rnam par thar pa rgya mtsho la 'jug pa yang rab tu shes so/ / de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi rnam par thar pa'i tshul rgya mtsho la 'jug pa yang rab tu shes so/ /

“I know the accumulation of good actions of all beings. I know the defilement and the purification of all beings. I know the various kinds of karma of all beings. I know the entrances to samādhi of all śrāvakas. I know the levels of samādhi of all śrāvakas. I know and comprehend the miraculous manifestation through the peace of the liberations of all pratyekabuddhas. I know the ways of the ocean of samādhis of all bodhisattvas. I know the ways of the ocean of the liberations of all bodhisattvas. I know the entry into the ocean of the liberations of all the tathāgatas.”

the accumulations of goodness of all beings, the means of purgation of defilements of all beings, the variety of deeds of all beings, the doors of concentration of all buddhas’ disciples, the stage of concentration of all buddhas’ disciples, the tranquillity, liberation, and mystic transformation of all individual illuminates, the methods of the oceans of concentrations of all enlightening beings, the ocean of ways of liberation of all enlightening beings, and the ocean of ways of liberation of all buddhas.”

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis shAkya'i bu mo go pa la 'di skad ces smras so/ / 'phags ma/ khyod kyis byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin gyi chul rgya mtsho thams cad la rnam par lta ba'i yul 'di brnyes nas ji srid cig lags/

Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, asked the Śākya maiden Gopā, “Āryā, how long has it been since you attained this bodhisattva liberation called the range of the view of all the ways of the ocean of the samādhis of the bodhisattvas?”
Then Sudhana asked Gopa, “How long ago did you attain this liberation?”

smras pa/ rigs kyi bu/ sngon 'das pa'i dus sangs rgyas kyi zhing brgya'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi bskal pa 'das pa'i pha rol gcig tu 'jig rten gyi khams mi 'jigs pa byed pa zhes bya ba byung ste/ 'jig rten gyi khams de'i bskal pa 'gro ba'i mchog ces bya bar gyur to/ /

She answered, “Noble one, in the past, in times gone by, beyond as many kalpas as there are atoms in a hundred buddha realms, there was a world realm called Abhayaṃkarā. In that world there was a kalpa called Gatipravara.
She replied, “As many eons ago as atoms in a hundred buddha-lands, there was a world called Producing Fearlessness. In that world was an age called Superior Conduct.

'jig rten gyi khams de'i dbus su gling bzhi pa bde ba yod pa zhes bya ba byung ste/ gling bzhi pa de'i 'dzam bu'i gling gi dbus su rgyal po'i gnas sdong po ri bo'i dpal zhes bya ba grong rdal stong phrag brgyad cu rtsa bzhi'i phul du bya ba byung ste/ rgyal po'i gnas sdong po ri bo'i dpal de dang / grong rdal stong phrag brgyad cu rtsa bzhi po de dag kyang so so nas sa'i gzhi bai DUr+ya sngon po las grub pa la gnas rin po che bdun las byas pa'i ra bas kun nas bskor ba/ 'obs spos chus yongs su gang ba/ gzhi gser gyi bye ma bdal ba; utpal dang / pad+mo dang / ku mu da dang / me tog puN+Da rI ka shing rta'i 'khor lo tsam kha dog dang 'od kyi dra ba sna tshogs shing dri zhim pas kun nas khyab pa bdun gyis yongs su bskor ba/ rin po che las byas pa'i stegs bu'i khri 'phang bdun las ta la'i phreng ba rim pa bdun gyis kun nas dkrigs pa/ rin po che sna bdun gyi shing gi nags tshal gyi phreng ba dkrigs pas kun nas bskor ba/

In the center of that world realm there was a four-continent world called Kṣemāvatī. In the center of the Jambudvīpa of that four-continent world there was the royal capital called Drumameruśrī, the principal city from among eighty-four thousand[1762] cities. In the royal capital Drumameruśrī and each of the eighty-four thousand towns, the ground was made of blue beryl. Walls made of the seven precious materials encircled them. And they were each encircled by seven moats that were filled with scented water and had bottoms covered in gold dust and surfaces covered with blue lotuses, red lotuses, night lotuses, and white lotuses that were the size of wagon wheels, shone with light rays of various colors, and had all-pervading lovely aromas. There were rows of seven promenades made of the seven precious materials and seven rows of palm trees. They were encircled by seven successive planted forests of trees made of the seven precious materials.

In the middle of that world was a set of four continents called Safe. On the southern continent was a metropolis called Magnificent Trees, the greatest of eighty-four billion cities. Each of the cities was built on a ground of blue lapis lazuli and was surrounded by walls made of seven precious substances and seven moats of fragrant water with gold sand on the bottom, covered with red, white, and blue lotuses as big as cartwheels radiating brilliant webs of light and beautiful scents. They were also surrounded by seven networks of railings made of jewels and seven rings of palm trees, and abounded in groves of trees made of seven precious substances.

steng nas gser gyi dra ba bres pa rin po che sna tshogs kyis rnam par phye ba'i mig mang ris mdzes par rnam par bres pas sa'i gzhi shin tu spa bar gyur pa/ dngos grub can gyi tshogs rnam par rgyu ba/ bya btsun pa'i khyus sgra skad yid du 'ong ba'i dbyangs snyan pa phyung ba/

Above there was a canopy of a net of gold.[1763] The ground was beautifully adorned by various jewels arranged in checkerboard patterns.[1764] Groups of siddhas wandered around. From flocks of noble birds came the beautiful sound of their melodious songs.

Above, they were covered with networks of clouds. The grounds of the cities were like jeweled checkerboards, the plots evenly divided by arrays of various jewels. Groups of mystic adepts lived and roamed there, and birds filled the air with pleasing song.

bza' shing gi rab bye ba brgya phrag stong gis mdzes par byas pa/ shin tu skyid cing phun sum tshogs par gnas pa/ skyes pa dang bud med brgya stong rab tu dga' bas gang ba/ ser bu bde zhing yid du 'ong bas bskyod de me tog gi char mang po rgyun mi 'chad par rab tu 'brul ba/ sa'i bdag po dam pa brgya phrag stong gi gnas su gyur pa dag ste/ grong rdal chen po de dag gi rin po che'i shing thams cad dang / gser gyi dra ba'i rgyan la sogs pa rlung gis bskyod de rol mo mang po'i sgra dang / snyan pa'i sgra skad byung ba dag las yid du 'ong ba'i tshig 'di skad byung ngo/ /

The towns were beautified by a trillion parks. They had abundant good fortune, and they were filled with crowds of hundreds of thousands of joyful men and women. Pleasant, delightful breezes blew, and rains of many flowers continuously fell. A hundred thousand kings dwelled among them. When all the precious trees, adornments of gold, and so on in the great towns were moved by the wind, there came from them the many sounds of music, and harmonious[1765] voices arose saying these happy words:

The cities were adorned with millions of parks, and they were prosperous and wealthy. Hundred of thousands of happy men and women populated them. There were constant showers of beautiful flowers, stirred by the wind. Hundreds of thousands of earth spirits lived in them. Furthermore, from the golden nets of wind chimes adorning all the trees came happy voices saying,
gsol cig /mnobs shig /chos la spyod cig /byang chub tu sems skyed cig /phyir mi ldog pa'i sa la mnga' thob mdzod cig /khyed rnams bde bar gyur cig /ces zer ro/ /
‘Bathe! Drink! Eat! Practice the Dharma! Develop the aspiration for enlightenment! Attain the power of the level of irreversibility! Be happy!’
‘Bathe, drink, eat, practice the Teaching, arouse the determination for enlightenment, realize mastery of the stage of nonregression; happiness to you!’

rgyal po'i gnas sdong po ri bo'i dpal der khams kyi rgyal po nor gyi bdag po zhes bya ba byung ste/ de la btsun mo'i 'khor bud med stong phrag brgyad cu rtsa bzhi yod do/ / blon po brgya phrag lnga yod par gyur te/ rgyal po nor gyi bdag po de la bu lnga brgya yod pa de thams cad kyang dpa' ba/ rtul phod pa/ yan lag dam pa'i gzugs dang ldan pa/ gzhan gyi sde rab tu 'joms pa/ shin tu mdzes pa/ blta na sdug pa/ kha dog bzang po'i mchog shin tu rgyas pa dang ldan pa sha stag go /

“In the royal city of Drumameruśrī there was the king of the realm whose name was Dhanapati. He had a harem of eighty-four thousand queens and five hundred ministers. King Dhanapati had five hundred sons, and they were all courageous and heroic, with perfect bodies, victorious over opponents, handsome, attractive, and with a magnificent, supreme, beautiful color.

“At that time, in the capital city Magnificent Trees, there was a king named Lord of Wealth, ruler of the region. He had eighty-four thousand women in his palace. He also had five hundred ministers, and also five hundred sons, all of whom were brave, powerful warriors, handsome and well built.

rgyal po nor gyi bdag po de'i btsun mo dam pa ni/ pad+mo'i dpal dam pa 'byung ba zhes bya ba ste/ bud med stong phrag brgyad cu rtsa bzhi po de dag gi nang nas gtso mor bya ba'o/ / de'i bu gzi brjid kyi dbang po zhes bya ba gzugs bzang ba/ shin tu mdzes pa/ blta na sdug pa/ mi chen po'i mtshan sum cu rtsa gnyis kyis rab tu brgyan pa'i lus dang ldan pa zhig yod par gyur te/ de la mi chen po'i mtshan sum cu rtsa gnyis po 'di dag yod par gyur to/ /

“King Dhanapati’s principal queen was Padmaśrīgarbhasaṃbhavā, who was the foremost among the eighty-four thousand wives. Her son was Tejodhipati. He had an excellent body and was handsome and attractive. He was beautified by the thirty-two physical signs of a great being in the following way:

His queen, the foremost of the eighty-four thousand women, was named Lotus Born. She had a son named Lord of Glory, who was very handsome and bore the thirty-two marks of a great man, pleasing to the sight of all.

de'ang 'di ltar rgyal bu gzhon nu gzi brjid kyi bdag po de rkang pa'i mthil shin tu gnas pa dang ldan te/ sa chen po la rkang pa'i mthil 'dor na mnyam par 'dor la/ 'deg na mnyam par 'deg ste/ gzhog na rkang pa'i mthil kun gyis sa chen po la mnyam par reg go /

1. “The soles of Prince Tejodhipati’s feet were well placed. When he took steps on the great earth, he stepped evenly. When he raised a foot, it was raised evenly, and when he placed his foot down, the entire sole of the foot touched the great earth evenly.

de'i rkang pa'i mthil gnyis la 'khor lo rtsibs stong dang ldan pa/ lte ba dang bcas pa/ mu khyud dang bcas pa/ rnam pa thams cad du shin tu tshang ba/ shin tu mdzes pa/ blta na sdug pa dag kyang byung bar gyur to/ /
2. “On the soles of his feet and the palms of his hands there was a thousand-spoked wheel, with hubs and rims, complete in all aspects, beautiful, and attractive.
de'i rkang pa'i bol gnyis kyang shin tu rgyas par gyur to/ /rkang pa'i steng gi mdog shin tu gsal la shin tu mdzes te/ me tog dam pa bas kyang lhag par mdog bzang zhing gsal bar gyur to/ /
3. “The upper part of both his feet[1766] was very prominent: the upper surface of his feet had a clear and very beautiful color, a color better and brighter than excellent flowers.
de'i rkang lag gi sor mo dra bar 'brel bar gyur te shin tu mdzes pas rnam par bye ba; bu ga med pas zag pa med pa ni/ dper na/ ngang pa'i rgyal po gnas srung lta bur gyur to/ /
4. “His toes and fingers were connected by a web: they were very beautiful, distinct, and with no holes or suppurations, like those of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the king of geese.
de rkang pa'i rting pa yangs pa/ shin tu dag la shin tu gsal ba/ rin po che thams cad kyi 'od rab tu 'gyed par grub pa dang ldan par gyur to/ /
5. His heels were wide: they were pure, bright, and shining with the lights of all jewels.
de'i sor mo rnams kyang ring zhing zlum la tshigs bar mnyam zhing yangs pa dang ldan par gyur te/ de dag mnyam par sa la 'jog go / mnyam par sa las 'deg go /
6. His toes and fingers were long: they were rounded, with evenly spaced joints and wide, and the toes came down evenly onto the ground and lifted off evenly from the ground.

de'i rkang pa dang lag pa'i mthil yang ka tsa lin+da bas kyang lhag par reg na bde bar gyur te/ des skyes pa'am/ bud med dam/ khye'u dang bu mo gang la reg kyang rung ste/ de dag thams cad bde ba dang / yid dga' ba'i dam pas tshim zhing yid shin tu bde bar 'gyur ro/ /

7. The soles of his feet and the palms of his hands were more pleasant to the touch than down. Whether it was a man or a woman, a boy or a girl who touched them, they were delighted and were made content and happy by perfect bliss.

de'i byin pa ri e na ya'i byin pa ltar 'dug par gyur te/ rim gyis gzhol ba dang / shin tu mdzes pa dang / legs par grub par gyur pas/ ri kyi rgyal po e na ye ltar de la sus kyang bsnyegs pa'am sleb par mi nus te/ 'gro bas ngal zhing dub par mi 'gyur ro/ /

8. “His calves were like those of the female blackbuck, gradually tapering, very beautiful and well formed. Like the female blackbuck, monarch among deer, no one could run after him and catch him, and he never became tired and fatigued when running.

rgyal bu gzhon nu gzi brjid kyi dbang po de bdun shin tu mtho ba dang yang ldan par gyur te/ de'i rkang pa gnyis la shin tu mtho ba zlum la shin tu legs pa dang / shin tu rgyas pa dang / tshigs mi snang ba dang / shin tu yid du 'ong ba dang / blta na sdug pa gnyis grub par gyur to; ; lag pa la gnyis/ thal gong gi lhun la gnyis/ ltag pa la gcig ste/ de ltar bdun no/ /

9. “The young prince Tejodhipati had the seven prominences. These seven were his two feet, which were prominent, rounded, excellent, wide, with joints not visible, beautiful, and attractive, and similarly his two hands, his two shoulders, and the nape of his neck.

de'i mtshan gsang ba'i sbubs na 'dug pa grub par gyur te/ de'i gsang pa'i gnas sbubs na 'dug pa shin tu mi mngon la nang du nub cing kun nas yog par 'dug pa ste/ dper na/ glang po cang shes sam/ rta cang shes ltar 'dug pas de gos ma gyon par 'dug kyang bud med dam/ skyes pa'am/ khye'u'am/ bu mo'am/ rgan pa'am/ dar la bab pa'am/ bla ma'am/ bla mar bya ba rnams kyis kyang mi mthong ste/ gzhan du na bdag longs par spyod pa'am/ ched du bstan par bya ste/ 'dod pas spyad pa ni/ ma gtogs so/ /

10. “His penis was retracted into his body: As his penis was retracted into his body, it was not visible but completely hidden and obscured, like that of an elephant or a stallion. Therefore, it was unstained and could not be seen by a woman or a man, a boy or a girl, someone who was old, middle-aged, or young,[1767] or a guru or a guru’s disciple,[1768] unless he was using it or wished to show it or was having sexual intercourse.

rgyal bu gzhon nu gzi brjid kyi bdag po de ro stong seng+ge ltar 'dug pa dang ldan par gyur te/ lus rim pas rgyas la ro stod shin tu yangs shing rdzogs pas/ ri kyi rgyal po bas kyang mdzes par dbyibs shin tu legs pa'i ro stod dang ldan par gyur to/ /

11. “The young prince Tejodhipati’s torso was like that of a lion: his body gradually widened so that his torso was broad and perfect, more beautiful and excellently shaped than that of the king of the animals.

de'i thal gong rgyas shing lus shin tu rgyas pa/ lus rnam par phye ba/ lus kyi cha thams cad rkyen du 'bab par mnyam pa/ lus la dma' ba med pa/ lus la mtho ba med pa/ lus la zhum pa med pa/ lus la dgu pa med pa; lus rin po che'i gtan pa shin tu phyis pa bas kyang lhag par gsal bar gyur to/ /

12. “He had wide shoulders: he had a very broad body, a perfectly proportional body, a perfectly symmetrical body, a body that was not too bulky, a body that was not too thin, a body that was not feeble,[1769] a body that was not stooped, and a body that shone brighter than a polished slab of jewels.
de dpung mgo shin tu zlum zhing sha rgyas la shin tu mdzes par gang ba dang ldan par gyur to/ /
13. “He had large shoulders: his shoulders were muscular, and his arms[1770] beautifully filled out.
des mi chen po'i mtshan lag pa shin tu ring ba thob par gyur pa/ des lus ma btud de lus drang por 'dug kyang pus mo'i lha nga gnyis la nyug cing reg go /
14. “He had also attained the sign of a great being of his arms being very long: even without bending, while standing up straight, his hands could touch and rub his kneecaps.

des mi chen po'i mtshan lus che zhing drang ba'ang thob par gyur te/ rnam pa thams cad du mchog tu gyur pa dang ldan la/ lus tshul dang 'dra bar mnyam pa dang / lus rab tu mnyen pa dang / lus shen tu lci ba dang / lus rab tu gsal ba dang / lus shin tu sim par byed pa dang ldan par gyur te/

15. “He had also attained the sign of a great being of his body being tall and straight. It was perfect in all its aspects and was properly formed. His body was supple.[1771] His body was very heavy. His body was very bright. His body was very pleasing to the eyes.

des mi chen po'i mtshan mgul dung lta bu yang thob par gyur te/ mi dma'i mgul dang / de'i mgul gyi 'khor thams cad dang / bzhin gyi 'khor thams cad na rtsa ji snyed cig yod pa de dag thams cad kyang shin tu mnyam par gyur te/ kun kyang rab tu tshang bar gyur to/ /

16. “He had also attained the sign of a great being’s conch-like throat. His neck was not short. All the channels of taste[1772] in the area of the throat and the area of the mouth were balanced and complete.

mi chen po'i mtshan seng+ge'i 'gram pa lta bu yang thob par gyur te/ za 'gram shin tu mkhregs pa dang / bzhin gyi dkyil 'khor shin tu rgyas pa dang / bzhin gyi dkyil 'khor shin tu legs shing yongs su dag pa dang / kha'i sgo shin tu yangs pa dang ldan par gyur to/ /
17. “He had also attained the sign of a great being’s lion-like cheeks and jaws. His jaws were very firm. His face was very wide, his face was excellent and pure, and his mouth was wide.

mi chen po'i mtshan so mnyam pa bzhi bcu dang yang ldan par gyur te/ so ma tshang ba med pa la zas shig za na yang lan gcig bldad pas chung du na 'bras can gyi 'bru 'ga' yang ma zhig par za ba med do/ /

18. “He also possessed the sign of a great being’s forty even teeth. There were no missing teeth. When he ate food, with one chew there was no food that remained unmasticated, not even a single grain of rice.

so thags bzang zhing mnyam pa rab tu thob ste/ mtshams chu sgo med pa dang / shin tu mnyam pa dang / rkyen rkyen du shin tu mdzes pa ste/ de kha zas shig za na yang 'go ba dang / 'chags pa dang / zhen pa dang / ljan ljin du 'gyur ba'am; thogs par 'gyur ba'am/ gseb 'gang bar 'gyur ba med do/ /

19. “He had attained even, gapless rows of teeth: there were no gaps, and they remained perfectly even and constantly beautiful, whatever occurred. The food he ate would not discolor his teeth,[1773] stick to his teeth, adhere to his teeth, cause his teeth to rot, cause abscesses,[1774] or get stuck between his teeth.[1775]

mi chen po'i mtshan so mnyam pa rab tu thob par gyur te/ so mnyam zhing rnga rngo med pa dang / so lhag med pa dang / so zhum pa med pa dang / so gyes pa med pa dang / so thog drung mnyam pa dang / so rngo ba med par gyur to/ /

20. “He had also attained the great being’s sign of even teeth: his teeth were even and not irregular, there was no deficiency in teeth, no extra teeth, no taller teeth, no smaller teeth, and no compacted teeth; the teeth were equal in height and breadth, and there were no broken teeth.
gzhon nu de'i mche ba shin tu dkar bar gyur te/ mche ba skyon med pa/ mche ba shin tu gsal ba/ mche ba shin tu dag pa/ mche ba shin tu brtan par gyur to/ /
21. “The youth’s eyeteeth were very white: his eyeteeth were without defects, his eyeteeth were bright, his eyeteeth were pure, and his eyeteeth were strong.

mi chen po'i mtshan lce shin tu yangs pa yang rab tu thob par gyur te/ de'i lce ni/ shin tu yangs la srab cing mnyen te/ shin tu 'jam pa dang / las su rung ba dang / yid du 'ong ba dang / bsgyur na bde ba dang / gdong gi dkyil 'khor kun 'gebs pa dang / bden zhing phan par 'gyur ba'i don dang / yi ge dang / ngag dang / nges pa'i tshig thogs pa med par rjod par gyur to/ /

22. “He had also attained the great being’s sign of a wide tongue: his tongue was wide, fine, very smooth, flexible, beautiful, versatile, could cover his entire face, and spoke without impediment true and beneficial meanings, consonants, words, and definitions.

gzhon nu de tshangs pa'i dbyangs dang ldan par gyur te/ dbyangs yid du 'ong ba dang / rol mo'i sgra dang / klu'i nga ro dang / sil snyan gyi dbyangs dang / sgra skad dang / brjod cing smra ba'i tshig gi las yid du 'ong ba brjod pas/ ngag gi lam mngon par dga' ba bskyed pa/ 'jig rten thams cad mngon par 'dun par 'gyur bar tshangs pa las kyang lhag pa'i dbyangs kyis ngag rjod de/ 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor las kyang gud du mi 'da' bar thams cad kyi yid dang mthun par byed pa dang ldan par gyur to/ /

23. “The prince had the voice of Brahmā: he had a beautiful voice that spoke with an activity of speech that had all the beautiful sounds of drumming, songs, musical instruments, speech, and conversation, which brought joy and inspired the world. He had a voice that was superior even to Brahmā’s, yet it was not beyond and inaccessible to his circle of followers but harmonized with everyone’s minds.

gzhon nu de ni/ mig dkar nag 'byes par gyur te/ mig shin tu dang ba dang / mig yongs su dag pa dang / mig la 'od chags pa dang / mig rnam par gsal ba dang / mig mngon par mdzes pa dang / mig blta na sdug pa dang / mig yid du 'ong ba dang / mig 'dzum pa dang ldan par gyur to/ /
24. “The prince had distinctly deep black[1776] eyes: he had clear eyes, pure eyes, bright eyes, serene[1777] eyes, beautiful eyes, delightful eyes, attractive eyes, and smiling eyes.

gzhon nu de ni/ rdzi ma ba'i rdzi ma lta bu dang ldan par gyur to/ /mig gi skye mched rin po che pad+ma rA ga ltar shin tu dag pa/ mig gi sprin mnyam pa/ mig gi sprin mtshungs pa/ mig gi sprin legs pa/ mig gi sprin yangs pa/ mig gi sprin rdzogs pa/ mig gi sprin shin tu brtan par gyur to/ /

25. “The prince had eyelashes like a cow’s eyelashes: he had sensory faculties of the eyes that were like pure ruby jewels, sameness of the whites of the eyes, identical whites of the eyes, excellent whites of the eyes, wide whites of the eyes, complete whites of the eyes, and constant whites of the eyes.

de'i smin mtshams su mdzod spu skyes par gyur te/ 'jam pa/ las su rung ba/ shin tu mnyen pa; shing bal ltar reg na bde ba/ dang ba/ gsal ba/ 'od yod pa/ chab rom lta bu kha ba'i kha dog ltar 'dug pa/ 'od zer dkar po'i dkyil 'khor gyi 'od rab tu snang ba dang ldan par gyur to; ;

26. “In between his eyebrows an ūrṇā hair had grown: it was soft and pliable, delicate, as pleasant to the touch as cotton wool, clear, bright, the color of snow, and like ice, and it had the shining light of a halo of white light rays.

de'i spyi bo la gtsug tor mngon par grub par gyur te shin tu legs pa/ kun nas zlum pa/ dbus su bab pa/ skra'i rgyan du gyur pa/ rin po che'i pad+mo 'dab ma bye ba brgya phrag stong dang ldan pa ltar snang ba/ kun nas cha mnyam par gnas pa/ rin thang gdab tu tshad med pas gces pa'i gtsug tu gyur pa dang ldan par gyur to/ /

27. “There was an uṣṇīṣa formed on the crown of his head: it was well formed, perfectly round, central, an adornment of the hair, resembling a precious lotus with a trillion petals, perfectly symmetrical, and cherished as a priceless crest adornment.

gzhon nu de pags pa shin tu 'jam pa dang ldan par gyur te/ de'i lus la rdul tam/ dri ma'am/ rdul tam/ ser ka'am/ gnyer ma'am/ lhod pa'am/ 'khums pa'am/ 'phyang ba'am/ slod bag tu gnas pa med par gyur to/ /
28. “The prince had very smooth skin: his body was free of dust, stains, sweat, cracks, wrinkles, flabbiness, shriveling, sagging, and looseness.[1778]

gzhon nu de ni/ mdog gser gyi kha dog lta bu dang ldan par gyur te/ 'dzam bu chu klung gi gser gyi mdog lta bu dang ldan zhing 'od kun tu 'dom gang ba dang / gser ltar gcig tu 'bar ba'i 'od kyi dkyil 'khor gyis mdzes par brgyan pa dang /
29. “The prince was golden in color: he was the color of Jambu River gold, had a halo a fathom wide, and was beautifully adorned by a halo of light that shone like gold.
ba spu'i bu ga thams cad nas dri zhim po'i 'od zer 'byung bas lus kyi rgyan rab rib med cing 'od gsal ba dang ldan par gyur to/ / gzhon nu de ni/ ba spu re re'i byung ba dang ldan par gyur te/
30. “That youth had arising from each pore a darkness-dispelling brightness of aromatic light rays that arose from all his pores and adorned his body:

ba spu'i bu ga re re nas ba spu re re skyes par gyur pa/ bai DUr+ya sngon po'i kha dog lta bu/ g.yas phyogs su 'khyil ba/ legs par skyes pa/ mthang la zhi bar 'dug pa/ shin tu legs par gnas pa dang ldan par gyur to/ / gzhon nu de'i spu yan lag gyen du 'khyil bar gyur te/ phyir mi ldog pa'i spu dang / mi ldog pa'i spu dang / ma 'dres pa'i spu dang ldan par gyur to/ /

from each pore grew perfectly a body hair that was the color of blue beryl and curled to the right, peacefully present on the body, perfectly arranged, perfectly present, perfectly established. The youth’s body hairs curled upward; his body hairs did not turn downward, his body hairs were irreversible, and his body hairs were unmixed.

gzhon nu de mi chen po'i mtshan skra mthon mthing du 'dug pa thob par gyur te/ de'i skra nor bu rin po che rnam par snang ba'i mdog ltar mthon mthing du 'dug pa/ 'jam pa/ snum pa/ legs par 'khyil ba/ g.yas phyogs su 'khyil ba; drung shin tu ran pa/ zad zed med pa/ 'jam 'jam ltar 'dug pa/ mi 'dzings pa/ dbyibs mnyam zhing mthun par gnas pa dang ldan par gyur to/ /

31. “The youth had attained the great being’s sign of having hair the color of blue sapphire:[1779] his hair was deep blue like the color of a shining blue[1780] precious jewel. It was soft, shiny, perfectly curving, curling to the right, and with good roots; it did not stand up, never tangled, was never in disarray, and always remained with the same even appearance.

rgyal bu gzhon nu de shing gro d+ha ltar mchu zheng gab pa'i mi chen po'i mtshan rab tu thob par gyur te/ kun nas rkyen du ran pa dang / kun tu bzang ba dang / kun tu mdzes pa dang ldan par gyur te/ de ni/ mdun nas bltas na'ang ngoms mi shes shing / blta na yid du 'ong ba/ rgyab dang / g.yas g.yon dang / 'gro ba dang / 'dug pa dang / 'greng ba dang / nyal ba dang / smra ba dang / mi smra bar 'dug pa la bltas na'ang ngoms mi shes shing yid du 'ong la blta na sdug par gyur te/

32. “The young prince had attained the great being’s sign of being like the overspreading width of a banyan tree: he was perfectly upright, completely good, and utterly beautiful. He was a lovely sight, and one could never have enough of gazing upon him. Whether from the back, the left, or the right; whether he was walking, sitting, standing, or lying down; whether he was talking or silent, he was a lovely sight, and one could never have enough of gazing upon him.
rigs kyi bu/ rgyal bu gzhon nu gzi brjid kyi bdag po de mi chen po'i mtshan sum cu rtsa gnyis po de dag gis yongs su brgyan pa'i lus dang ldan par gyur te/
“Noble one, Prince Tejodhipati had a body completely adorned by these thirty-two signs of a great being.

sems can thams cad kyis blta na yid du mi 'ong ba'i bag med pa/ blta na bsam pa thams cad yongs su rdzogs par byed pa/ blta na sems can thams cad kyi dga' ba yongs su 'byung ba de lta bu zhig skyes par gyur te/
“Noble one, he was a sight that was comforting to all beings, he was a sight that fulfilled all intentions, and he was a sight that brought delight to all beings. This was how he had been born.

rigs kyi bu/ de nas lan gcig cig rgyal bu gzhon nu gzi brjid kyi bdag po de yab kyis gnang nas rgyal po'i gnas sdong po ri bo'i dpal gyi bza' shing gi ra ba spos kyi myu gu'i rtse mo las 'od kyi sprin 'byung ba zhes bya ba der sa bzang po blta ba'i phyir bu mo stong phrag nyi shu dang lhan cig tu bsod nams kyi gzi brjid dang dpal gyi bskal ba bzang po'i rnam par 'phrul pa'i rgyan gyis byung nas skyes pa dang bud med kyi tshogs kyis kun nas dga' bar bya zhing /

“Noble one, at one time,[1781] Prince Tejodhipati, having obtained permission from his father, was going, accompanied by twenty thousand maidens, to the park of the royal capital of Drumameruśrī, which was called Gandhāṅkuraprabhamegha, in order to see that good place. He delighted a crowd of men and women with the display of the miraculous manifestations from the splendor of his merit and his glorious good fortune.

“Once, as a youth, this prince went, with the permission of his father and mother, to go see one of the parks of the city, called Clouds of Light on a Mountain of Fragrant Plants. He went together with twenty thousand girls, projecting a great aura of felicity, glory, energy, splendor, and beauty, admired by men and women all around.

dzam+bu chu klung gi gser gyi shing rta rdo rje rin po che'i 'khor lo chen po bzhi dang ldan pa/ rdo rje mthu bo che'i srog shing sra ba/ tsan+dan dam pa las bsgrubs pa'i yu ba bzang po dang ldan pa/ rin po che'i rgyal po spos sna tshogs kyi shing thags rnam par bkye ba/ rin po che thams cad kyi me tog sna tshogs kyis rab tu mdzes par byas pa/ rin po che thams cad kyi dra bas kun nas yog pa'i rgyan dang ldan pa/ seng+ge'i khri rin po che dam pa'i dra ba'i rgyan gyi snying po can dbus su bshams pa/ bu mo lnga brgyas rin po che'i srad bu'i lnga ldi nas yongs su bzung ba/ nam mkha' la chags pa med pa'i rlung ltar mgyogs pa'i rta cang shes stong dang bcas pa la zhon nas

“He mounted a chariot made of Jambu River gold. It had four great wheels of precious diamonds. It had an axle that was a powerful vajra. Its excellent shafts were made from the best sandalwood. It had well-arranged poles made of a variety of perfumed kings of jewels. It was decorated by a variety of flowers made from all jewels. It was covered by nets of strings of all jewels. In its center was a precious lion throne on which was a display of a network[1782] of sublime jewels. Five hundred maidens held its tasseled cords. Yoked to the carriage were a thousand thoroughbred stallions that could run as fast as the wind moves freely through the air.

They got into a golden vehicle with four huge diamond wheels and unbreakable diamond axles set in the finest sandalwood. It was ribbed with well-arranged diamonds of all fragrances, splendidly adorned with flowers of all jewels, draped with nets of all jewels, with a lion seat set in the middle of the interior, arrayed with great jewels. The reins, strings of jewels, were held by five hundred girls, and it was drawn by a thousand thoroughbred horses fleet as the wind.

gdugs chen po rim gyis gzhol zhing blta na sdug pa/ steng g.yogs rin po che'i rgyal po bai DUr+ya dkar po las byas pa/ 'od dri ma med pa tshad med pa 'byung ba/ rin po che bsam gyis mi khyab pa rmad du byung ba sna tshogs thams cad kyis spa bar spras te rnam pa thams cad du mdzes par brgyan pa/ yub rin po che'i rgyal po bai DUr+ya sngon po las bsgrengs pas ni/ bskyabs/ srog chags brgya stong mang pos ni/ yongs su bskor/ rol mo brgya stong mang po lha rdzas kyi dbyangs yid du 'ong ba snyan pa dang ldan pa dag ni/ rab tu blangs/ me tog gi char chen po ni/ mngon par 'bab/ lha rdzas kyi spos dri zhim pa'i bdug spos kyi snod bye ba khrag khrig brgya stong gis ni/ rab tu bdug cing 'gro bar gyur to/ /

It had a succession of beautiful great parasols.[1783] It had an awning made from white beryl kings of jewels. It shone with pure immeasurable light. It was beautified by the adornment of the entire variety of inconceivable, wonderful jewels. It was adorned with every kind of beauty. It had a great precious parasol[1784] that was held aloft by a pole of blue beryls, the kings of jewels. It was encircled by many hundreds of thousands of beings. The beautiful, melodious sound of music arose from hundreds of thousands of musical instruments. A great rain of flowers fell. A divine, beautiful aroma spread from a quintillion censers. That was the way he went to the park.

Overhead was a beautiful sloping canopy made of white lapis lazuli, with a flawless, immeasurable luster, supported by tall poles of blue lapis lazuli, adorned with all kinds of arrays of rare jewels, held by hundreds of thousands of people surrounding the vehicle, singing and playing music, scattering flowers and burning incense.

de de ltar 'gro ba'i tshe lam yang rgyud brgyad dang ldan par gyur te/ mthon dman med pa dang / gseg ma dang gyo mo med pa dang / gser dngul dang rin po che'i rgyal po sna tshogs kyi khams kyis sa'i gzhi rab tu bsgrubs pa dang / gser gyi phye ma bkram pa dang / rin po che sna tshogs kyi me tog sil mas chal bar gang ba dang / g.yas g.yon nas rin po che'i shing gi phreng bas dkrigs pa dang / rin po che sna tshogs kyi kha ran bkye ba dang / steng nas rin po che'i dra ba bres pa dang / rin po che'i gnam yol sna tshogs kyis bkab pa dang / rin po che'i rgyal mtshan dang / ba dan dang / snam bu brgya stong rab tu brgyan pa du ma bsgrengs shing dpyangs pas mdzes par brgyan pa dang /

“As he proceeded, at that time, the road became eight vehicles wide, without any unevenness, and without pebbles or gravel. The ground was made from the elements of gold, silver, and the various kinds of jewels. It was bestrewn with gold dust. It was covered with the scattered petals of flowers made of every kind of jewel. On both sides were rows of jewel trees on bases made of all kinds of jewels. Above there was a network of strings of precious bells and jingle bells. It was covered by a variety of precious canopies. It was perfectly adorned by a beautiful display of countless hundreds of thousands of erected precious banners, flags, and hanging streamers.

The eight-lane road was level and free of gravel, set on a bed of all precious substances, spread with gold sand, decorated with flowers of various jewels, lined on both sides with rows of jewel trees and railings of various gems. Above, it was covered with nets of golden bells, adorned with canopies of various jewels, and arrayed with many thousands of jeweled banners, pennants, and streamers.
g.yas g.yon nas rin po che'i stegs bu'i phreng ba rnam par bkod pas rnam par brgyan pa ste/
“On both sides, it was adorned by an arrangement of rows of precious platforms.
Rows of jewel buildings were arrayed on either side.
rin po che stegs bu la la la ni/ slong mo pa'i tshogs la yongs su bstab pa'i don du rin po che'i snod sna tshogs rin po che sna tshogs kyis yongs su bkang ba bkod;
“On some platforms, a variety of precious bowls filled with a variety of jewels had been arranged for the crowds of petitioners.
“In some of those buildings were precious vessels filled with various jewels, to be given to those in need.
stegs bu la la la ni/ rgyan 'dod pa'i slong mo pa rnams brgyan pa'i don du rin po che thams cad kyi rgyan gyi rnam pa yongs su bkod/
“On some platforms, all kinds of precious adornments had been placed for those who requested adornments.
In some buildings were all kinds of precious ornaments, for those in need of ornaments.
stegs bu la la la ni/ sems can thams cad kyi bsam pa yongs su rdzogs par bya ba'i phyir yid bzhin gyi nor bu rin po che bkod/
“On some platforms, wish-fulfilling jewels had been set out in order to fulfill the wishes of all beings.
In some buildings were wish-fulfilling jewels, to fulfill the wishes of all beings.
stegs bu la la la ni/ su ci 'dod pa de dag la de sbyin pa'i don du kha zas dang / btung ba dang / bro ba sna tshogs kyis yongs su bkang ba'i snod mang po bkod/
“On some platforms, many vessels containing food and drink with flavors of various kinds had been set out so as to provide whatever was desired.
In some buildings were vessels filled with all kinds of food and drink, to be given to whoever needed them.
stegs bu la la la ni/ rnam pa thams cad du mchog tu zhim pa'i ro dang / kha dag dang / dri dang / bro ba dang / reg bya yid du 'ong ba dang ldan pa'i lha rdzas kyi kha zas kyi rnam pa bkod/
“On some platforms, divine food with the most perfect flavors, colors, aromas, tastes, and pleasant textures had been provided.
In some buildings were celestial foods of all the most pleasant appearances, fragrances, savors, and textures.
stegs bu la la la ni/ ro bro ba sna tshogs dang ldan pa'i lha rdzas kyi shing thog sna tshogs thams cad spungs/
“On some platforms, divine fruits of every kind with a variety of flavors had been heaped up.
In some buildings were various delicious celestial fruits.

stegs bu la la la ni/ gos 'dod pa rnams yid bzhin du spyod du gzud pa'i phyir lha rdzas kyi gos rin po che kha dog sna tshogs dang ldan pa/ mdog bzang po rnam pa sna tshogs dag dang / ri mo sna tshogs shin tu spa bar rnam par phye ba/ shin tu btsun pa la 'os pa/ shin tu phra ba/ rab tu 'jam pa/ thags su ma btags pa bye ba brgya phrag stong snyed yongs su bkod par gyur to/ /

“On some platforms were set out trillions of divine, precious clothes for those who desired clothes to enjoy in accordance with their wishes. They were not woven on a loom, had various kinds of beauty and all kinds of excellent colors, were adorned with various designs, and were very noble, worthy, fine, and perfectly smooth.
In some buildings were millions of fine celestial garments, for those in need of clothing to use as they wished.

stegs bu la la la ni/ byug pa 'dod pa'i sems can rnams bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du yongs su spyod du gzud pa'i phyir lha rdzas kyi spos kyi rnam pa kha dog dang / dri rnam pa sna tshogs thams cad dang ldan pa dag bkod par gyur to/ /
“On some platforms were arranged all kinds of divine aromatic substances, with various colors and aromas, for those who wished to perfume themselves to enjoy in accordance with their wishes.
In some buildings were all kinds of the finest celestial fragrances, for those who wanted perfume, to use at will.
stegs bu la la la ni/ sems can rnams bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du yongs su spyod du gzud pa'i phyir yo byad thams cad kyi phung po dag bkod par gyur to/ /
“On some platforms, heaps of various artifacts had been arranged for beings to enjoy in accordance with their wishes.
In some buildings were all kinds of utensils for people to use as they wished.

stegs bu la la la ni/ na chung gzugs bzang ba/ rab tu mdzes pa/ shin tu sdug pa/ cha lug sdug gu sna tshogs dang ldan pa/ yid du 'ong ba'i gos sna tshogs dang ldan pa/ yid du 'ong ba'i gos sna tshogs gyon pa rgyan thams cad kyis mdzes par brgyan pa/ byug pa sna tshogs kyis tshul sdug gur brgyan cing mdzes par byas pa'i lus dang ldan pa/ bud med kyi bzo dang / sgyu dang / shes nyen gyi tshul la mkhas pa dag bkod par gyur to/ /

“On some platforms were arranged beautiful, charming, attractive women with a variety of pleasing appearances, their bodies beautified by being dressed in a variety of beautiful clothes, beautifully adorned by every kind of jewelry, perfumed by a variety of scents, and skilled in the female crafts and arts.

de'i tshe rgyal po'i gnas sdong po ri bo'i dpal de nyid na sbrul tshong ma'i dam pa rgyal po'i longs spyod du 'os pa/ blta na mdzes pa zhes bya ba zhig yod pa de'i bu mo dga' ba'i 'od kyi dpal shin tu sbyangs pa zhes bya ba gzugs bzang ba/ shin tu mdzes pa/ blta na sdug pa/ ha cang yang mi ring / ha cang yang mi thung / ha cang yang mi sbom/ ha cang yang mi phra/ ha cang yang mi dkar/ ha cang yang mi sngo ba/ skra mthon mthing du 'dug pa/ mig dkar nag 'byes pa/ bzhin yid du 'ong pa/ tshangs pa'i dbyangs dang ldan pa/ 'jam zhing snyan par smra ba/ shes rab dang ldan pa/ shes nyen gyi tshul thams cad la mkhas pa/ gtsug lag thams cad la shes pa/ brtson pa/ le lo med pa/ rim gro yod pa/ mos pa dang ldan pa/ byams pa'i sems bdog pa/ khong khro ba mi mnga' ba/ blta na mi ngoms shing yid du 'ong ba/ 'dod chags dang / zhe sdang dang / gti mug chung ba/ ngo tsha shes shing khrel yod pa/ drang zhing mnyen pa/ g.yo dang sgyu med pa zhig yod de/

“At that time, in the royal capital Drumameruśrī, there was the preeminent courtesan[1785] called Sudarśanā, who was worthy to be enjoyed by the king. She had a daughter named Sucalitaratiprabhāsaśrī, who was beautiful, with a lovely body, attractive, not too tall and not too short, not too plump and not too thin, not too white and not too dark, and with deep black hair, deep black eyes, a beautiful face, and a voice like Brahmā’s; who spoke gently and pleasantly, was wise, and was skilled in all the arts; and who knew all treatises, was diligent, was not lazy, was respectful, was gracious, had a kind mind, was not aggressive, was so attractive that one never tired of gazing upon her, had little desire, anger, or ignorance, had a sense of decorum and modesty, was honest and gentle, and had no deceit or trickery.

“At that time there was a courtesan named Beautiful in that metropolis, with whom the king consorted. She had a lovely daughter named Splendor of Delight in Virtuous Conduct, who was neither too tall nor too short, neither too stout nor too lean, neither too heavy nor too light. She had black hair and eyes, a pleasant face, and a clear voice. She spoke sweetly and kindly, she was wise, versed in all arts and sciences, clever and diligent, dignified and serene, kind-hearted and gentle, always pleasant to be with. She had scarcely any desire, aversion, or folly; she was modest and conscientious, soft and sincere, free from guile and deceit, self-controlled.

de ma dang lhan cig tu bu mo du ma zhig gis bskor te rin po che'i shing rta la zhon nas rgyal po'i gnas sdong po ri bo'i dpal nas byung ste rgyal pos bka' stsal nas rgyal bu gzhon nu gzi brjid kyi bdag po'i mdun nas phar rgyal bu gzhon nu de la glu len cing 'dong 'dong ba las/

“She mounted a precious carriage with her mother and accompanied by many girls, and they came out from Drumameruśrī. At the king’s command, they sought out the young prince Tejodhipati so as to sing before him.
She and her mother, accompanied by many girls, got in a jeweled chariot and rode out of the city before the prince Lord of Glory. Looking for the prince, going according to the king’s directions,

rgyal bu gzhon nu gzi brjid kyi bdag po mthong nas 'dod chags kyi sems shin tu mi bzad pa zhig g.yos te/ rgyal bu gzhon nu gzi brjid kyi bdag po shin tu yid du 'ong ches nas rjes su 'brang zhing sems la rang dbang med pas/ blta na sdug pa la
“When Sucalitaratiprabhāsaśrī saw Prince Tejodhipati, her mind was shaken by overwhelming desire. The beauty of Prince Tejodhipati was so great she helplessly followed him.
when she saw the prince she became greatly enamored of him. Bound by the excessive affection she conceived for the prince, unable to control herself,
'di skad ces smras so/ /ma 'di ltar mkhyen par mdzod cig /gal te bdag rgyal bu gzhon nu gzi brjid kyi bdag po la ma btang na ni/ 'gum pa'am/ srog la 'bab pa'i sdug bsngal gcig tu 'gyur ro/ /
“She said to her mother Sudarśanā, ‘Mother, know this: I will die if I am not given to this Prince Tejodhipati! The suffering will bring me to death!’
she said to her mother, ‘If you do not give me to the prince Lord of Glory, I will die or suffer torment equal to death.’

des smras pa/ bu mo/ de lta bu'i sems ma skyed cig/ gzhon nu 'di ni/ 'khor los bsgyur ba'i mtshan dang ldan pa ste/ de'i yab nor gyi bdag po mi bzhugs par 'gyur na/ 'khor los bsgyur ba'i rgyal srid la gnas par 'gyur ba'i gnas yod de/ de 'khor los bsgyur ba'i rgyal por 'gyur bas de'i bud med rin po che nam mkha' la 'gro ba 'byung bar 'gyur la/ bu mo bdag cag kyang sbrul tshong ma dag cig ste/ 'jig rten thams cad dga' bar byed pa yin gyi/ yu bus sems can 'ga' zhig la nam 'tsho'i bar du bsnyen bkur mi byar mi rung ba'ang med de/ yu bu ni; rgyal po nor gyi bdag po'i bkas rgyal bu gzhon nu gzi brjid kyi bdag po'i rim gror 'dong 'dong bar zad kyi/ de lta bu'i sems brtan par ma byed cig /gnas de ni/ thob par yang shin tu dka'o/ /

Sudarśanā replied, ‘My daughter, don’t have such an aspiration! This youth has the signs of a cakravartin. When his father Dhanapati is no longer with us, he will rule a cakravartin’s kingdom. When he has become a cakravartin, he will have a precious queen who will come flying through the air. My daughter, we are courtesans who bring pleasure to the entire world. We do not and cannot remain throughout our lifetime serving only one being. King Dhanapati commanded us to come before the young prince Tejodhipati only to show our respect! That kind of status would be too difficult to attain.’

Her mother said, ‘Do not think this way. This prince has the marks of a supreme ruler, and it is obvious that after his father passes away he will succeed to the throne and become king. At that time a special woman will appear from the sky. Furthermore, we prostitutes give pleasure to everyone; we do not serve one person all our lives as a rule. We have set out to attend the prince Lord of Glory at the command of the king Lord of Wealth. Do not hold fast to this wish of yours, for it is unattainable.’

de'i tshe de bzhin gshegs pa dgra bcom pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas sku nyi ma dam pa zhes bya ba mkhyen pa dang zhabs su ldan pa/ bde bar gshegs pa; 'jig rten mkhyen pa/ bla na med pa/ skyes bu 'dul ba'i kha lo sgyur ba/ lha dang mi rnams kyi ston pa sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das 'jig rten du byung ste/

“At that time, in that world there appeared a tathāgata, an arhat, a samyaksaṃbuddha, one with wisdom and conduct,[1786] a sugata, one who knows the world’s beings, an unsurpassable guide who tames beings, a teacher of devas and humans, a buddha, a bhagavat, who was named Sūryagātrapravara.

“Now, at that time a buddha named Supreme Sun was appearing in the world, a saint, perfectly enlightened, complete in knowledge and conduct, gone to felicity, supreme knower of the world, tamer of humans, teacher of celestials and humans, awake, blessed.

de'i snying po byang chub chos kyi sprin shin tu sdug pa'i 'od ces bya ba yang bza' shing gi ra ba spos kyi myu gu'i rtse mo las 'od kyi sprin 'byung ba zhes bya ba de'i nang du byung ste/ der bcom ldan 'das de bzhin gshegs pa sku nyi ma dam pa thog ma mngon par rdzogs par sangs rgyas nas zhag bdun lon pa

“His bodhimaṇḍa, called Dharmameghodgataprabhā, was near to the Gandhāṅkuraprabhamegha Park. It had been seven days since the Bhagavat, the Tathāgata Sūryagātrapravara had attained complete buddhahood there.

He was at an enlightenment site called Light Emerging from the Cloud of Teaching in the park Cloud of Light on a Mountain of Fragrant Plants, where he enjoyed his first seven days since attaining enlightenment.

de bu mo shing rta la zhon bzhin du yur zhing 'chog 'chog pa'i rmi lam du mthong nas sad par gyur pa dang sngon gnyen bshes su gyur pa'i lha mo zhig gis bstan pa/ bu mo/ de bzhin gshegs pa sku nyi ma dam pa de snying po byang chub chos kyi sprin shin tu sdug pa'i 'od ces bya ba rnam par spyod cing thog ma mngon par rdzogs par sangs rgyas nas zhag bdun lon te byang chub sems dpa'i tshogs kyis yongs su bskor cing / lha dang / klu dang / gnod sbyin dang / dri za dang / lha ma yin dang / nam mkha' lding dang / mi'am ci dang / lto 'phye chen po dang / tshangs pa dang / gya nom snang ba dang / 'og min gyi lha'i tshogs kyis mdun du byas shing bzhugs te/ der sa'i lha mo thams cad kyang kun nas 'dus/ chu'i lha mo dang / me'i lha mo dang / rlung gi lha mo dang / rgya mtsho'i lha mo dang / chu'i klung gi lha mo dang / ri'i lha mo dang / mtshan mo'i lha mo dang / skya rengs 'char ba'i lha mo dang / nags tshal gyi lha mo dang / shing gi lha mo dang / sman gyi lha mo dang / lo tog gi lha mo dang / grong khyer gyi lha mo dang / rkang gis 'gro ba'i lha mo dang / snying po byang chub kyi lha mo dang / lus kyi 'od zer gyi lha mo dang / sems can gyi ris kyi lha mo dang / nam mkha'i lha mo dang / phyogs thams cad kyi lha mo dag kyang bcom ldan 'das sku nyi ma dam pa'i zhal blta ba'i phyir kun nas 'dus so/ / zhes nas

The girl, while in her carriage, nodded off to sleep and saw him in a dream. When she woke up, a goddess, who in past times had been a relative, declared to her, ‘Girl, the Tathāgata Sūryagātrapravara is present in the Dharmameghodgataprabhā bodhimaṇḍa, after his first seven days since attaining complete buddhahood. He is encircled by an assembly of bodhisattvas, and before him are gathered assemblies of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, Brahmakāyika deities, Ābhāsvara deities, and Akaniṣṭha deities. Also gathered there to gaze upon the Tathāgata Sūryagātrapravara are all goddesses of the earth, goddesses of water, goddesses of fire, goddesses of the air, goddesses of the oceans, goddesses of the rivers, goddesses of the mountains, goddesses of the night, goddesses of the dawn, goddesses of the forests, goddesses of the trees, goddesses of herbs, goddesses of harvests, goddesses of towns, goddesses of footpaths, goddesses of the bodhimaṇḍas, goddesses of the body’s light rays, goddesses of classes of beings, goddesses of the sky, and goddesses from all directions.’

“The girl, who was reclining in the chariot, saw that buddha in a dream. When she awoke, a goddess who had been a relative in a past life told her that the buddha was in the park, in his first week of enlightenment, surrounded by a group of enlightening beings, before a crowd of all kinds of spirits, and that all the deities of earth, space, water, fire, wind, oceans, rivers, mountains, night, dawn, forests, trees, plants, grain, cities, foot tracks, sanctuaries, bodies of light, habitations, the sky, and all directions had gathered to see the buddha Supreme Sun.

de ltar des de bzhin gshegs pa mthong ba dang de bzhin gshegs pa'i yon tan thos pas bag tsha med pa thob par gyur te skabs su bab nas rgyal bu gzhon nu gzi brjid kyi bdag po'i mdun du de'i tshe tshigs su bcad pa 'di dag smras so/ /

“When Sucalitaratiprabhāsaśrī had seen the Tathāgata and heard of the qualities of the Tathāgata, she attained a state of serenity. When the opportunity came, she recited these verses before Prince Tejodhipati:
“Emboldened by seeing the buddha and hearing of the buddha’s virtues, finding a favorable opportunity, the girl then spoke these verses before the prince:
gzugs kyi mchog gis 'jig rten khyad par 'phags/ / yon tan rnams kyis thams cad phyogs su grags/ / shes rab stobs kyi bdag dang 'dra ma mchis/ / sgyu rtsal dga' ba sgyu ma'i tshul kun 'tshal/ /

“ ‘I am preeminent in this world because of my excellent body. My qualities are renowned in all directions. Because of the power of my wisdom, there is no one like me. I am learned in all the arts and skills of pleasure. {1}
I am known in the world for beauty, Renowned everywhere for virtues. None compares to me in the power of knowledge; I know all arts, amusements, and magic.
srog chags mang po stong 'phrag du ma yis/ / 'dod chags dbang gis bdag la rab bltas kyang / / gzhon nu bdag ni 'jig rten gang la yang / / glo ba chags par gyur pa gcig ma mchis/ /
“ ‘There are many thousands of beings Who gaze upon me with desire. Prince, I have had no desire within me For anyone in this world. {2}
Hundreds, thousands of men Look on me with lust, But I have no desire For people of the world.
sems can gang la'ang zhen par gyur pa'am/ / gang la'ang khong khror bdag gi sems ma gyur/ / gang la'ang dgra mi bgyid de zhe mi sdang / / bdag ni sems can sman par dga' ba lags/ /
“ ‘I have no attachment toward any being. In my mind there is no anger toward anyone. No one is my enemy, and I have no hatred. In my mind there is only delight in benefiting[1787] beings. {3}
I have no ill-will, Neither am I pleased by anyone. I have neither anger nor hatred; I delight in the welfare of all.
sku gzhon sku mchog yon tan rab mnga' khyod/ / gang tshe bdag gis gsal bar mthong gyur pa/ / de tshe dbang po kun kyang nyams su bde/ / rgya che yangs par shin tu dga' bar gyur/ /
“ ‘When, Prince,[1788] I clearly saw You who have a supreme body with excellent qualities, All my senses experienced bliss. There arose within me a vast, great bliss. {4}
When I saw you, young man, excellent In form and strength, endowed with virtue, All my senses were delighted, And immense joy arose in me.
khyod kyi dbu bzang lcang lor 'khyil ba 'am/ / rin chen rnam snang mdog tu mthon mthing gsal/ / zhal gyi smin sdug 'phral ba shangs su mdzes/ / khyod kyi zhal sngar lus 'di bdag 'bul lo/ /
“ ‘Your coiled hair upon your excellent head Is deep blue like the color of a shining jewel. You have lovely eyebrows and a beautiful nose. In your presence I offer you my body. {5}
Your complexion is like a pure shining jewel, Your hair is black and curly, You have a fine brow and nose; I offer myself to you.
mtshan gyi rab 'chang gzi brjid che mnga' ba/ / sku gzugs gser gyi ri bo bzang po 'dra/ / khyod kyi spyan sngar bdag lta mi mdzes te/ / zil du rlog pas snag tsha'i gzugs kyang 'dra/ /
You have excellent features. Resplendent, you are like a mountain of gold. In your presence I do not shine; I am like a pile of charcoal.
spyan gsal ring la dkar nag 'byes pas mdzes/ / shin tu zhal rgyas seng+ge'i za 'gram can/ / khyod kyi gsung ni thogs pa ma mchis na/ / gsung mchog mnga' bas bdag ni gzung du gsol/ /

“ ‘Your clear eyes are long, with contrasting white and black. You have a wide face and the cheeks and jaws of a lion. Your speech is free of any impediment. I pray that you, who have the supreme speech, take me. {7}
Your eyes are large and dark, Your jaw is like a lion’s, your face like the full moon. The fine sound of your voice is irresistible; Please take me in.
khyod kyi zhal na ljags yangs mnga' ba ni/ / mdog dmar yangs pa rin chen mchog gi 'od/ / tshangs dbyangs yan lag mchog gi gsung mnga' bas/ / gsung zhing 'gro ba rab tu dga' ba mdzad/ /

“ ‘You have a wide tongue within your mouth. It is wide and red, with the excellent light of a jewel. You possess speech with the supreme aspects of Brahmā’s voice. When you speak, you bring delight to beings. {8}
Your tongue is long and broad, Coppery red, soft, shining like a jewel; With your superb, clear voice You delight people when you speak.
khyod kyi zhal na thags bzang tshems mnga' ba/ / dung ltar dri med shin tu rnam par gsal/ / 'dzum zhing bzhad pa rnam par ston mdzad kyang / / skyes bu dpa' khyod 'gro ba dga' bar mdzad/ /
“ ‘You have even rows of teeth in your mouth, Very bright and stainless, like conches. When you show them in smiling or talking, You, glorious man, bring joy to beings. {9}
Your teeth are even, shining white, Clean and well spaced; When you show them as you smile, You delight people, O hero.
khyod kyi sku la mtshan rab mdzes pa rnams/ / sum cu rtsa gnyis dag cing 'od kyang gsal/ / sku gzugs bzang po yongs su des brgyan pas/ / mi yi dbang po 'khor los bsgyur ba byon; ;
“ ‘Your body is beautified by the thirty-two Supreme signs, and it shines brightly. As your body is adorned by those signs, Lord of humans, you will be a cakravartin.’[1789] {10}
Your body has the thirty-two marks Of greatness, brilliantly shining, pure. Adorned with them, you will become A sovereign ruler of men.
shin tu rgyas pa chen po'i mdo/ / sangs rgyas phal po che zhes bya ba las/ sdong pos brgyan pa'i le'u ste/ bam po brgya brgyad pa/

de nas rgyal bu gzhon nu gzi brjid kyi bdag pos bu mo dga' ba'i 'od kyi dpal shin tu sbyangs pa la 'di skad ces smras so/ / bu mo/ / khyod su'i/ khyod la yongs su srung ba ni/ gang zhig yod/ bu mo/ / nga la ni/ gzhan gyis yongs su bzung ba'i bud med bdag gir byar mi rung ngo/ / zhes nas de'i tshe tshigs su bcad pa 'di dag kyang smras so/ /
“Then Prince Tejodhipati asked Sucalitaratiprabhāsaśrī, ‘Girl, who are you? Who is your guardian? I cannot take as my own a woman who belongs to another.’ Then at that time he recited these verses:
“Then the prince Lord of Glory said to the maid Splendor of Delight in Virtuous Conduct, ‘Whose daughter are you, whose ward? I cannot make another’s ward my own.’ Then he spoke these verses:
blta sdug gzugs kyi yon tan legs ldan pa/ / mtshan bzang bsod nams rnam par dag pa'i lus/ / khyod la dri ba'i don 'di nga la smros/ / lus mchog khyod ni su yis yongs su bzung / /

“ ‘You who are beautiful with excellent physical qualities, Who have a pure body of merit with excellent signs, Give your answer to these questions I ask you: To whom do you, who have a perfect body, belong? {11}
O lovely one, endowed with beauty of form, With fine features and a pure body, I ask you to tell me this— Whose ward are you?
khyod la pha dang ma ni yod dam med/ / khyim thab med dam khyod ni su zhig dbang / / gzugs mdzes khyod la sems can gzhan nam gcig / bdag gi yin par 'du shes byed med dam/ /

“ ‘Do you have a father and mother or not? Are you unmarried, or who has authority over you? You who have a beautiful body, should I perceive you As belonging to some other being or see you as mine? {12}
Have you father or mother, Brother, husband, or master, Or someone else who thinks of you As his, treating you kindly?
khyod kyi yid ni gsod la mi dga' grang / / gzhan las ma byin 'phrog par mi byed dam/ / 'dod pas log par g.yem la mi dga' grang / / rdzun du brjod smrar yid ni mi smros sam/ /
“ ‘In your mind you do not delight in killing? You do not take from others what is not given? You do not delight in sexual misconduct? You do not wish in your mind to speak lies? {13}
I hope you are not vicious, Do not steal, Are not promiscuous, And do not lie.
khyod kyi blo gros mdza' dbyen mi 'jug gam/ / tshig brlang gzhan la gnod par mi smra grang / / gzhan gyi nor la chags par sems med dam/ / 'gro ba rnams la gnod par mi sems grang / /

“ ‘You do not use your intelligence to separate friends? You do not speak harmful words out of anger? You do not have a mind that craves the wealth of others? You do not intend to cause harm to others? {14}
I hope you do not cause discord, Do not slander others, Do not covet others’ goods, And are not hostile toward anyone.
lta ba'i 'brog dgon lam du ma zhugs grang / / las kyi rgyud la ye rngam sems med dam/ / g.yo mdog sgyu yi dbang du mi 'gro 'am/ / mi 'thad 'jig rten gnod par mi byed grang / /

“ ‘You do not enter the pathways into the wilderness of wrong views? You are not without restraint[1790] in terms of the different kinds of karma? Do you not fall under the power of deceit and trickery? Do you not cause wicked harm in the world? {15}
pha ma gnyen dang mdza' bshes bla ma la; ; sri zhu rim gro bya ba'i tshul 'chang ngam/ / phongs par gyur pa yongs su bsdu don du/ / khyod kyi yid la sbyin pa'i sems yod dam/ /
“ ‘Are you affectionate and respectful To father, mother, relatives, friends, and gurus? Do you have in your mind the intention to give To gatherings of those who have become destitute? {16}
Do you love and respect your parents, Relatives, friends, and elders? Does your heart reach out To give to the poor to help them?
chos dang mthun par dus su 'doms byed cing / / lus dang sems yid yongs su dag byed la/ / yang dag las su rung ba skyed byed pa'i/ / dge bshes rnams la dga' ba'i sems yod dam/ /

“ ‘Do you have the intention to please the good friends[1791] Who give you timely advice in accord with the Dharma, Who make the body and the mind tractable So that they may be completely purified?[1792] {17}
Are you well disposed toward spiritual benefactors Who tell you about religion at the appropriate time? Are you truly healthy and capable In body and mind?
sangs rgyas rnams la rim gror byed ldan nam/ / sangs rgyas sras la dga' mchog yod dam med/ / gang las bde gshegs sras rnams skyer 'gyur ba'i/ / chos kyi dam pa de ni shes mi shes/ /
“ ‘Do you honor the buddhas? Do you have great delight in the bodhisattvas? Do you or do you not know the supreme Dharma From which are born the sons of the sugatas? {18}
Do you respect the buddhas And love the enlightening beings? Do you know the supreme Teaching From which the enlightening beings are born?
chos yid mchog la gnas par khyod byed grang / / chos min spyad pa'i blo gros med grang ngo/ / legs pa mtha' yas yon tan rgya mtsho la/ / gus pa'i sri zhu dga' sems mchog yod dam/ /

“ ‘Do you dwell in a supreme Dharma mind? Do you not have a mind that acts contrary to the Dharma? Do you have a perfect mind that respectfully delights In the ocean of the qualities of infinite excellence? {19}
Can you abide by the supreme religion And not do any wrong? Do you have higher love and respect For the infinite ocean of virtues?
skye bo mgon med phongs par gyur pa yi/ / 'bren pa rnams la byams pa'i yid yod dam/ / ngan song 'gro ba'i lam la zhugs pa yi/ / shin tu nyam thag snying rjes sems grang ngo/ /

“ ‘Do you have a kind mind toward those beings Who have no protector, are destitute, and have no guide?[1793] Do you have compassion in your mind for those unfortunate ones Who have entered the path that leads to the lower existences? {20}
Are you kind To the helpless and lost? Are you really compassionate Toward evildoers?
gzhan gyi phun sum tshogs pa mthong gyur na/ / khyod ni dga' ba mchog dang ldan 'gyur ram/ / skye bo nyon mongs rnams kyis 'khol gyur la/ / shes rab mthu bskyed btang snyoms byed mi byed/ /
“ ‘Do you have perfect rejoicing When you see the good fortune of others? When beings are enslaved by their kleśas, Do you have equanimity through the power of wisdom, or not? {21}
Are you most happy To see the success of others? Are you indifferent, by the power of wisdom, To those who annoy you for no reason?
mi shes gnyid log skye bo mang mthong na/ / byang chub dam par smon lam 'debs byed grang / / bskal pa mtha' yas spyad pa spyod pa na/ / smon lam dam pas skyo bar mi 'gyur grang / /

“ ‘When you see many beings in the sleep of ignorance, Do you pray that they will attain perfect enlightenment? Are you not disheartened by the supreme prayer To practice bodhisattva conduct for endless kalpas?’ {22}
Seeing people in the slumber of ignorance, Do you firmly seek supreme enlightenment? Would you not weary of endless ages Of spiritual practice?

de nas bu mo dga' ba'i 'od kyi dpal shin tu sbyangs pa'i ma sbrul tshod ma'i gtso mo blta na sdug pas/ rgyal bu gzhon nu gzi brjid kyi bdag po la 'di skad ces smras so/ / gzhon nu/ bdag gi bu mo 'di ni/ rdzus te byung ba pad+mo'i nang nas skyes pa ste/ sngon chad khyim gyi nang nas phyi rol tu ma byung ngo/ / zhes nas de'i tshe tshigs su bcad pa 'di dag kyang smras so/ /

“Then Sudarśanā, the preeminent courtesan, who was the mother of the girl Sucalitaratiprabhāsaśrī, said to the young prince Tejodhipati, ‘Prince, this daughter of mine had a miraculous birth; she was born from inside a lotus. She has not until now been outside of her home.’ Then at that time she recited these verses:

“Then the supreme courtesan Beautiful, mother of the maid Splendor of Delight in Virtuous Conduct, said to the prince Lord of Glory, ‘This daughter of mine, who was spontaneously born from within a lotus, has never before gone out of the house.’ Then she spoke these verses:
bu mo 'di la khyod kyis gang smras pa; ; de ni bdag gis rim pas khyod la brjod/ / ji ltar bu mo 'di skyes bskyed bskyed pa/ / bdag gis khyod la gsol gyi gsan du gsol/ /
“ ‘I will give you, in order, the answers To the questions you have asked this girl. I request you to listen, for I shall relate to you The way in which the birth of this girl occurred. {23}
Listen to what I say, O prince, About my daughter, of whom you ask. I will tell you of her birth And how she grew up.
gang tshe dgung sangs khyod ni bltams gyur pa/ / de tshe bdag gi bu mo 'di skyes te/ / rdzus te dri med pad+mo'i sbubs nas byung / / yan lag kun tshang mig yangs 'di yang skyes/ /

“ ‘At the end of the night[1794] when you were born, At that same time this daughter of mine was born. She appeared miraculously from within a stainless lotus, Born with all her limbs complete, with lovely wide eyes. {24}
On the very same morn as your birth, My daughter too was born, Generated spontaneously in the calyx of an undefiled lotus, All her limbs complete, with nice big eyes.
dus kyi nang na sos ka dus mchog la/ / sman dang lo tog myu gu thon pa'i tshe/ / sA la'i ra ba bza' shing rab mchog tu/ / bdag ni rtse dga' de khrod mchi mchi ste/ /
