“ ‘During the best of seasons, the time of spring, When herbs, harvests, and sprouts emerge, I was wandering happily[1795] In a perfect park of sal trees. {25}
In springtime, the best of seasons, When the crops and herbs are growing, In my beautiful grove of sal trees I utterly forgot myself.
sna tshogs yal ga'i lo ma rgyas gyur cing / / zhugs shing me tog sdug rgyas sprin gyi mdog / bya bran sna tshogs sgra snyan zhugs shing nang / / nags khrod mya ngan ma mchis dgar mchis mchis/ /

“ ‘Variegated leaves were growing on the branches. The masses[1796] of blossoming trees were like clouds. Various birds were singing in the trees. I was happy, joyful, and carefree in the forest. {26}
The branches were blooming with most beautiful flowers, The fruiting trees were like dense clouds; Amid the trees with singing birds I roamed, joyful, free from care.
rgyan dang ldan zhing shin tu yid 'ong la/ / rin chen rat+na sna tshogs 'tshal ba rnams/ / rol mo glu la shin tu bslab pa yi/ / bu mo brgya phrag brgyad dang bdag kyang ldan/ /
“ ‘I was accompanied by eight hundred girls Who were adorned and very beautiful, Wearing all kinds of jewels And trained well in music and song. {27}
I was with eight hundred girls, Adorned with garlands of flowers, Wearing various precious cloths, Well versed in song and speech.
spos mchog ldan pa'i puN+Da rI ka dang / / rdzing 'gram me tog sil mas gtams pa yis/ / sa phyogs de na bud med mang po dang / / bdag cag de na dga' bar mchis mchis na/ /
“ ‘I, together with the many women, Proceeded joyfully to an area Where there were white lotuses with supreme scents And a pond with banks covered in petals. {28}
I sat on the bank of a pond Filled with lotuses of various scents; The area around, strewn with flowers, Was filled by those well-cultivated girls.
chab dbus de nas rin chen pad+mo'i mchog / 'dab ma stong dang ldan pa byung bar gyur/ / lo ma rin chen yu ba bai DUr+ya/ / snying po 'dzam bu chu klung gser las bgyis/ /
“ ‘In the middle of the water there appeared A perfect, precious thousand-petaled lotus. Its leaves were jewels and its stem was beryl, And its pericarp was made of Jambu River gold. {29}
In the middle of the water appeared A supremely fine lotus with a thousand petals; Its stem was lapis lazuli, its petals were diamond, Its pericarp was pure gold.
spos mchog rin chen dam pa'i ze ba can/ / 'od chen dzam+bu'i rgyal mtshan kun tu 'phro/ / de tshe dgung la gdugs shig shar tam zhes/ / skye bo kun kyang yid gnyis 'tshal bar gyur/ /

“ ‘It had filaments of aromatic supreme jewels And radiated a great light throughout Jambudhvaja. At that time, all beings were bewildered, wondering, “Has a sun arisen in the middle of the night?” {29}
It had a multitude of stamens of the finest fragrant jewels And had a brilliant golden sheen: The people were confused— How could the sun rise at night?
dgung sangs rgyur nas pad+mo chen po de/ / gdugs kyi 'od kyis rab tu rgyas bgyis nas/ / snang ba de dang sgra snyan rab kyang bkye/ / 'di 'byung de ni sngon gyi ltas su byung / /
“ ‘When the night came to an end, that great lotus And the light of the great[1797] sun dawned. Together with the light, it emitted melodious sounds. And these were omens of her birth. {31}
Then, the night ended, from the rising sun, Stimulating with its glow, There emanated light and sweet sounds, Foretelling the birth of this girl.
bud med rin chen 'di 'dra 'jig rten du/ / tshul khrims dam pa rnam par dag pas byung / / sug las bgyis pa chab 'tshal mi 'gyur bas/ / 'di ni sngon chad legs par spyad pa'i 'bras/ /

“ ‘A precious girl such as this was going to appear In this world because of pure, perfect conduct. The karma of one’s previous actions is never lost, And this was the result of her past excellent conduct. {32}
Then this precious girl appeared in the human world, Pure in the best of conduct. No deed is lost to the doer; she was the fruition Of good actions in the past.
skra ni mthon mthing mig yangs ut+pa la/ / tshangs pa'i dbyangs ldan kha dog rnam dag ldan/ / phreng ba rgyan mchog cha lugs dbyibs su shis/ / dpal ltar dri med pad+mo'i mchog las skyes/ /
With dark hair, lotus-blue eyes, A clear voice and golden complexion, Finely clad in garlands, she emerged From the lotus, resplendent as pure light.
lus ni rnam dag yan lag rkyen du mnyam/ / lus kyi dbyibs legs yan lag yongs su tshang / / gser gyi gzugs la nor bus phyis pa 'dra/ / phyogs kun 'od kyis rnam par gda' bar gsal/ /

“ ‘Her body was pure, all parts in proportion.[1798] Her body was perfectly shaped, her limbs fully formed. She was like a golden statue adorned with jewels. She was shining, illuminating all directions. {34}
Her limbs are bright, her body evenly balanced; Her limbs are complete, her body well proportioned: She shines like a golden statue adorned with jewels, Illumining all directions.
lus las tsan+dan rgyal po'i spos kyi dri/ / phyogs su rgyas par 'di yi lus las 'byung / / sgra snyan lha rdzas yid du 'ong brjod tshe/ / kha nas ut+pa la yi ngad kyang ldan/ /

“ ‘From her body came the aroma of sandalwood, the supreme perfume, Which coming from her body spread in all directions. When she spoke, there were beautiful and divine sounds. From her mouth came the scent of the blue lotus. {35}
The finest fragrance of sandalwood wafts from her body, Filling the air around her; As she speaks, with celestial sweetness, A scent like blue lotus comes from her mouth.
'di ni gang tshe 'dzum zhing dgod pa'i tshe/ / rol mo'i sgra snyan de tshe 'byung bar 'gyur/ / bud med rin chen 'jig rten 'dir byung ste/ / tha ma la kun gyi dbang du 'gyur ma lags/ /
“ ‘Whenever she smiled or whenever she laughed, There arose the melodious sound of music. A precious female had appeared in this world Who would never be under the power of anyone ordinary. {36}
Whenever she smiles, Heavenly music plays; This treasure of a woman should not be abandoned To the control of the vulgar.
khyod ma gtogs par mi yi 'jig rten na/ / 'di yi bdag po gzhan ni gcig ma mchis/ / mtshan rab brgyan pa'i sku gzugs mdzes mnga' ba/ / khyod kyi zhal sngar bu mo 'di bzhes gsol/ /
“ ‘There is no one else in this world Apart from yourself who could be her master. You who possess a beautiful body adorned by the signs, I pray you accept this girl who is before you. {37}
In the world of men no one can be found Who is worthy to be her husband, except you, A resplendent figure with the marks of greatness— Therefore, please accept this girl.
'di ni ha cang mi ring mi thung ste/ / ha cang mi spo ma ha cang phra ma lags; ; lto ni gzhu 'dra nu ma shas kyang rgyas/ / yan lag skyon bral 'di ni khyod la 'os/ /
“ ‘She is not too tall and not too short. She is not too plump and not too thin. Her waist is like a bow,[1799] and her breasts are large. Her limbs are faultless, and she is worthy of you. {38}
For she is not short or too tall, Not stout or too thin; She is slender at the waist, full-breasted, Suitable for you, with an impeccable body.
grangs dang yi ge shes bgyi tshul rnams dang / / lag brda'i tshul dang gtsug lag tshul la mkhas/ / 'jig rten kun na bzo rnams ji snyed pa/ / ma lus de la 'di ni pha rol phyin/ /
“ ‘She is skilled in hand gestures and treatises And likewise in the ways of counting and writing. She has perfected, without exception, All the arts there are in the world. {39}
She has perfect knowledge of calculation, Writing, symbology, and technical literature; She has mastered all the arts and crafts In the whole world.
mda' gzhu'i tshul la'ang rnam pa brgyas su mkhas/ / 'phong gi cho ga rnam pa rangs par rtogs; ; dgra yid bzho zhing dbab pa kun la yang / / 'di ni mchog tu pha rol phyin par gyur/ /

“ ‘She has complete knowledge of bows and arrows, And she has definitively mastered the art of archery. She has attained supreme perfection in the ways Of attracting enemies and calming their minds.[1800] {40}
She is expert in archery And always hits her mark; Pacifying opponents by her power of attraction, She is ultimately successful everywhere.
lus rnams kun nas rin chen rnam dag pa'i/ / 'od mchog 'khor gyis shin tu mdzes pa ste/ / sngon gyi legs pas shin tu sdug par brgyan/ / 'di ni khyod kyi phyag rjed khyod la 'os/ /
“ ‘Her entire body is perfectly adorned By a halo of a pure jewel’s supreme light. She is beautifully adorned through her past good actions. She is worthy to be at your service. {41}
All her limbs are like pure jewels; She radiates an aura of light. Adorned by the virtues she has accomplished, She is fit to be your companion.
mi yi 'jig rten gnas rnams ji snyed pa/ / de dag gso ba'i tshul gyi cho ga 'tshal; ; de dag ma lus thams cad zhir bgyi na'ang / / ma nor sman gyi cho gas gso la mkhas/ /
“ ‘She knows through the art of medicine how to heal All the illnesses[1801] in the human world. She eliminates them without exception Through the correct practice of medicine. {42}
She knows the cause of all illnesses That afflict living beings, And she is able to cure them By correct use of medicines.
dzam+bu'i rgyal mtshan skad rnams thams cad dang / / skye bo'i nges tshig ma lus bye brag dang / / 'jig rten tha snyad brjod pa'i mtshams sbyar ba/ / sna tshogs kun la'ang 'di ni pha rol phyin/ /
“ ‘She has also attained perfection in the various Languages throughout Jambudhvaja, Every specific definition of beings without exception, And the application of terminologies in the world. {43}
She has mastered all the different languages Of the people on the continent And the variety of customary usages Of society everywhere.
dbyangs kyi yan lag mngon par sgrub pa'i tshul/ / de dag bye brag tshul la'ang rab tu zhugs/ / 'jig rten glu gar rnam pa ji snyed pa/ / ma lus de rnams kun gyi tshul yang 'tshal/ /

“ ‘She has comprehended the ways of the categories Of accomplishing the different aspects of the voice. She knows the ways of all singing and dancing Without exception that are to be found in this world. {44}
She knows the articulation of sounds And the means of differentiation among them, And she is expert in all The songs and dances in the world.
rol mo sil snyan dag gi thabs rnams dang / / bzhad gad rol mo'i tshul la rnam par mkhas; ; chags dang ma chags mi rnams mngon 'tshal kyang / / khong khro chags par 'gyur ba ma mchis so/ /

“ ‘She comprehends the methods of drumming and music And of comedic and dramatic performances. Though she knows men who are passionate and those who are not, She herself has neither desire nor anger toward them. {45}
'jig rten bud med sgra rnams ji snyed pa/ / khyad par nang du de la ma lus 'tshal; ; bud med skye bo'i skyon du bgyi ba rnams/ / grangs med de dag 'di la gcig ma mchis/ /
“ ‘She knows without exception all the different Uses of the voice by women in the world. She does not have even a single one Of the countless faults of women. {49}
thil gyis blta dang zur gyis blta ba dang / / yan lag bstabs dang yan lag rnams bstan dang / / shes nyen kun la mkhas pa'i mthar phyin te/ / khyod kyi dgongs pa yongs su rdzogs par bgyid/ /
“ ‘She has fully mastered the skill in all the arts Of the direct gaze, the sideways gaze, Giving her body, and revealing her body. She will completely fulfill your heart’s desires. {47}
'di ni phrag dog ser sna ma mchis te/ / 'dod pa zhe dug mi ldang sdig mi bgyid/ / bzod cing drang la mnyen zhing des pa ste/ / mi khro mi brlang shin tu mkhas pa lags/ /

“ ‘She is not jealous; she is not greedy. She does not indulge in desires or commit bad actions. She is patient, honest, gentle, and tender. She is not angry, she is not harsh, and she is very wise. {48}
She is not jealous or envious, She is not lustful or ill-tempered; She is taciturn, honest, and gentle, Free from anger and harshness, very intelligent.
ldang ba'i ngang tshul yid du'ong ba'i ngag / rtag tu bla ma'i thugs dang sbyor ba ste/ / sku nyams gar bde lta zhing sri zhu che/ / khyod kyi spyod mthun rjes su snyegs tshul dang mthun/ /
“ ‘She is ever ready and speaks agreeably. She is always obedient to her gurus. Her behavior is always pleasant and very respectful. She will appropriately be in harmony with your conduct. {49}
She is diligent, well behaved, not argumentative, Always obedient to the worthy; She is respectful, seeking to do whatever is good. She will do as you ask.
rgyas shing gtugs dang nad dang ldan pa dang / / phongs pa shin tu sdug bsngal gyur pa dang / / mig dang bral zhing mgon skyabs ma mchis la/ / 'di ni snying brtse rtag tu skyed pa lags/ /
“ ‘She always has compassion for those Who have become aged and who are ill, Who are destitute and who are suffering, Who are blind and have no one to care for them. {50}
She is always compassionate toward the elderly, Toward the sick and the poor, Toward the suffering, the blind, And toward the helpless.
'di ni rtag tu gzhan don sems la brtson/ / bdag la sman pa sems par bgyid ma mchis/ / 'jig rten kun la sman par dga' ba ste/ / rlabs chen sems kyi yon tan kun gyis brgyan/ /

“ ‘Her mind is always dedicated to benefiting others. She never thinks of benefits[1802] for herself. She rejoices in benefiting[1803] the entire world. She is adorned with vast qualities of the mind. {51}
She is always thinking of the welfare of others, And never thinks of benefit for herself; Seeking the welfare of the whole world, She is adorned with superior virtues of mind.
mchis sam nyal lam mchi 'am 'greng yang rung / / smra'am mi smra 'dzum zhing dgod kyang rung / / rtag tu bag mchis dran pa shes bzhin te/ / 'di ni 'jig rten kun gyis rtag tu bsngags/ /

“ ‘She is always attentive, mindful, and circumspect, Whether standing, sitting, lying down, or walking, Whether speaking or silent, smiling or laughing, And she is always praised by the whole world. {52}
She is never careless, always mindful and aware, Whether standing, sitting, reclining, or walking, Whether silent or speaking; She is always remembered and honored.
bsod nams ldan pas kun tu rnam par snang / / 'gro ba kun kyang rtag tu dga' ba ste/ / 'di la lta bas 'jig rten ngoms mi 'gyur/ / 'di ni gang la'ang chags par 'gyur ma mchis/ /
“ ‘She always appears to be meritorious, She is always beloved by all people, Who never have enough of gazing upon her, And she has no attachment to anything in the world. {53}
This virtuous one shines in all ways, And is always loved by people; None would tire of looking at her, But she has no attachment to the world.
dge ba shes rnams la sri zhu 'di che ste/ / de dag mthong bar rtag par rab tu dga'/ / rjes su ci 'byung lta zhing skyon med tshul/ / sems bdag brtan pa ri rab ri dang 'dra/ /
“ ‘She is respectful to kalyāṇamitras, And she is always happy to see them. She looks far ahead, and her intentions are faultless. Her pure[1804] mind is as stable as Sumeru. {54}
Respectful of spiritual friends, She wants always to see you; This far-seeing, uncorrupted lady has a pure mind, Stable as the polar mountain.
'di ni bsod nams mchog gis rtag tu brgyan/ / mi mdza' dgrar len 'di la yong ma mchis/ / 'di yi shes 'dra bud med gcig ma mchis/ / rgyal sras khyod la 'di ni tshul dang mthun/ /
“ ‘She is always adorned by her excellent merit. She does not see anyone as being her enemy. There is no woman who has her kind of wisdom. Prince, she would be a suitable match for you.’ {55}
Ever-adorned with her own virtues, She has no enemies at all; She has no peer in knowledge. She is fit to be your bride, O prince.

de nas rgyal bu gzi brjid kyi bdag po bza' shing gi ra ba spos kyi myu gu'i rtse mo las 'od kyi sprin 'byung bar phyin te/ bu mo dga' ba'i 'od kyi dpal shin tu sbyangs pa'i ma sprul tshong ma'i gtso mo blta na sdug ba'i mdun du bu mo dga' ba'i 'od kyi dpal shin tu sbyangs pa la 'di skad ces smras so/ /

“Then Prince Tejodhipati came to Gandhāṅkuraprabhamegha, and, in the presence of Sudarśanā, the preeminent courtesan, who was the mother of Sucalitaratiprabhāsaśrī, he said to Sucalitaratiprabhāsaśrī,
“Then the prince, having entered the park, said to the maid in the presence of her mother,

bu mo/ nga ni/ bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu zhugs pa yin te/ de bas na/ ngas thams cad mkhyen pa'i tshogs ni/ tshad med pa zhig bsag par bya dgos/ bskal ba mtha' dang dbus med pa zhig tu byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa spyad de pha rol tu phyin pa thams cad ni/ yongs su rdzogs par bya dgos/ phyi ma'i mtha'i bskal ba'i mur thug par ni/ de bzhin gshegs pa rnams la mchod par bya dgos te/ sangs rgyas thams cad kyi bstan pa ni/ yongs su gzung bar bya/ sangs rgyas kyi zhing thams cad ni/ yongs su sbyang bar bya/ de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi rigs ni; mi gcad par bya/ sems can gyi rgyud thams cad ni/ yongs su smin par bya/ sems can thams cad kyi 'khor ba'i sdug bsngal ni/ rnam par bzlog par bya/ mtha' las rgal bar bde ba la ni/ sems can rab tu dgod par bya/ sems can thams cad kyi ye shes kyi mig ni/ yongs su dag par bya/ byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyis bsgrub pa la ni; brtson par bya/ byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi mnyam pa nyid la ni/ gnas par bya/ byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyis ni/ yongs su bsgrub par bya/ sems can gyi khams thams cad ni/ yongs su sbyang bar bya/ sems can thams cad kyi phongs pa yongs su gcad pa'i phyir bdag gi nor thams cad ni/ gtang bar bya/

‘Girl, I have undertaken to attain the highest, complete enlightenment. Therefore, I have to gather an immeasurable accumulation of omniscience. Throughout kalpas with no end or middle I must practice bodhisattva conduct and complete all the perfections. I must make offerings to the tathāgatas until the very last of future kalpas. I shall obtain the teachings of all the buddhas. I shall purify all buddha realms. I shall not be separated from the families of all tathāgatas. I shall ripen all the families[1805] of beings. I shall dispel the suffering of saṃsāra for all beings. I shall bring beings to a bliss that is beyond all limits. I shall purify the eyes of wisdom of all beings. I shall be dedicated to the accomplishments of all bodhisattvas. I shall rest in the equanimity of all bodhisattvas. I shall accomplish the bhūmis of all bodhisattvas. I shall purify the realms of all beings. I shall give away all my wealth so as to eliminate the poverty of all beings.

‘I have set out for supreme perfect enlightenment, whereby I may gather the infinite stores of omniscience, cultivate the practice of enlightening beings for infinite eons and perfect all the transcendent ways, serve the buddhas for endless eons, uphold the teaching of all buddhas, purify all buddha-lands, perpetuate the lineages of all buddhas, develop all groups of sentient beings to maturity, stop the pains of the mundane whirl for all sentient beings, lead sentient beings to ultimate bliss, clarify the eye of knowledge in all sentient beings, strive for the attainments of all buddhas and enlightening beings, abide in the equanimity of all enlightening beings, accomplish all the stages of enlightening beings, purify all sentient beings, cultivate total giving to put an end to poverty for all sentient beings,

phyi ma'i mtha'i mur thug pa'i bskal par spyin pa'i pha rol tu phyin pa la spyod pa'i tshe kha zas dang btung ba'i spyin pas ni/ sems can yongs su tshim par bya/ yo byad kyi dngos po thams cad yongs su btang bas ni/ slong ba'i tshogs thams cad yongs su tshim par bya dgos te/

“ ‘While I am practicing the perfection of generosity until the last future kalpa, I shall satisfy beings with the gift of food and drink, and through the gift of all kinds of artifacts I must bring satisfaction to all assemblies of supplicants.
practice transcendent giving for endless eons and satisfy all sentient beings with gifts of food and drink, and satisfy all beggars by giving away all goods.

de ltar bdog pa thams cad yongs su gtong ba la nan tan nyams su len pa'i tshe phyi nang gi dngos po gang ci yang rung ste/ yongs su mi gtang ba de lta bu med pas de ltar ngas bu dang / bu mo dang / chung ma yang sbyin par bya dgos/ /mig dang / mgo dang / rkang lag dang / yan lag dang / nying lag thams cad kyang yongs su gtang dgos na/ de'i tshe khyod gzhan la byin na/ /

“ ‘While I am in that way practicing the dedication to giving away everything, there will be nothing internal or external that I will not give away. Therefore, I will have to give away even my sons, daughters, and wives. I will have to give away my eyes, head, legs, arms, and the greater and smaller parts of my body.
As I practice total relinquishment, everything internal and external is to be given away—I am to give away my sons, daughters, wife; I am to relinquish my eyes, head, hands and feet, all my limbs.

nga'i sbyin pa'i bgegs su 'gyur ro/ / bu yid du 'ong ba yongs su btang na/ yid mi dga' bar 'gyur ro/ / lus dang sems kyi sdug bsngal yang mang po zhig nyams su myong bar 'gyur ro/ / nga la bdog pa thams cad yongs su btang bar byas na/ ser sna'i sems su 'gyur ro/ / nga'i yan lag dang / nying lag gtubs shing slong mo ba rnams la gtong ba'i tshe yid mi dga' bar yang 'gyur ro/ / nam zhig na ngas khyod bor te/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i bstan pa la rab tu 'byung bar 'gyur ba de lta bu'i dus kyang yod de/ de'i tshe'ang khyod yid mi dga' bar 'gyur ro/ /zhes nas

“ ‘At that time, you would become an obstacle to my generosity of giving to others. You would become unhappy when I give away our beautiful sons. You would experience much physical and mental suffering. When I give away everything, you would become miserly. When I cut off the greater and smaller parts of my body and give them to supplicants, you would become unhappy. There will also come a time when I would abandon you and enter homelessness within the teaching of a tathāgata. At that time you would become unhappy.’

You will hinder my giving, you will become unhappy at the relinquishment of beloved children, you will feel much physical and mental pain, you will resent my determination to give up everything. When I cut off my limbs to give them to beggars, you will be pained and grieved. And there will come a time when I leave you to go forth into the tutelage of a buddha; at that time you will be unhappy.’
rgyal bu gzi brjid bdag pos de'i tshe bu mo dga' ba'i 'od kyi dpal shin tu sbyangs pa la tshigs su bcad de smras pa/
“Then, at that time, Prince Tejodhipati recited these verses to the girl Sucalitaratiprabhāsaśrī:
Then the prince spoke these verses to the maid:
ngas ni 'gro kun snying rje rab bskyed de/ / yun ring mchog nas byang chub rab zhugs pas/ / yang dag byang chub tshogs chen rgya mtsho rnams/ / tshad med thams cad yongs su rdzogs bya dgos/ /
“ ‘I have developed compassion for all beings. For a long time I have been set on enlightenment. I must complete all the limitless oceans Of the great accumulations for true enlightenment. {56}
I am going to fulfill the immeasurable ocean Of provisions for perfect enlightenment; Therefore, with compassion for all, I have set forth forever for enlightenment.
bskal pa rgya mtsho mtha' dang dbus med par/ / mkha' ltar tshad med smon lam rnam sbyang zhing / / de bzhin gshegs pa bzhugs pa'i sa yi rnams/ / bskal pa mtha' yas yongs su sbyang yang dgos/ /

“ ‘For an ocean of kalpas that has no edge or middle, As measureless as space, I have purified my prayers. I must completely purify throughout endless kalpas The bhūmis on which the tathāgatas reside. {57}
For infinite eons, measureless as air, I will purify my vow; For endless eons I will perform the preparations Of the initial stage of the buddhas.
rgyal ba dus gsum 'byung ba thams cad kyi/ / pha rol phyin pa'i lam la ngas bslab ste/ / ye shes bla na med pa'i tshul chen gyis/ / byang chub lam mchog rnam par sbyang yang dgos/ /
“ ‘I will train in the path of the perfections Of all the jinas who appear in the three times. I must purify the supreme path to enlightenment Through the great way of the highest wisdom. {58}
I will learn the paths of transcendence From the buddhas of past, present, and future And perfect the path of supreme enlightenment By the great means of unexcelled knowledge.
phyogs rnams kun gyi zhing rnams thams cad kyang / / kun nas nyon mongs rnam par sbyang bar bya/ / 'jig rten kun gyi mi khom thams cad dang / / ngan song kun kyang rnam par bzlog dgos so/ /
“ ‘I will completely purify of defilements All the realms that are in every direction. I must dispel all unfortunate states in worlds And even all the lower existences. {59}
I will purify all Defiled lands everywhere; I will remove all difficulties And evil ways from all worlds.
nyon mongs bsgribs shing gti mug mun 'thoms pa'i/ / sems can kun kyang ma lus rnam sbyang dgos/ / sna tshogs thabs kyis yongs su sbyangs byas te/ / thams cad mkhyen lam tshul la dgod kyang dgos/ /

“ ‘I must purify every being, without exception, Enveloped in the darkness of ignorance and obscured by kleśas. I must purify them through various methods And bring them into the way of the path to omniscience. {60}
I will purify all beings Who are wrapped up in afflictions, blind with delusion; Developing them by various means, I will bring them into the path of omniscience.
chags med sa rnams kun kyang ngas sbyangs te/ / bskal ba rgya mtshor rgyal ba mchod par bya/ / 'gro ba ma lus kun la byams bskyed de/ / 'jig rten dag tu ma lus sbyin gtang dgos/ /

“ ‘I shall purify all the levels of nonattachment And make offerings to the jinas for an ocean of kalpas. I had developed love for all beings without exception, And I must give away everything in the world. {61}
I will accomplish the unobstructed stages And serve the buddhas for myriad eons; Generating kindness toward the world, I will give all gifts.
slong ba kun nas 'dus shing 'ongs mthong nas/ / thams cad gtang bar rtag tu brtson gyur na/ / de'i tshe khyod ni nga sems mi mthun te/ / zhum zhing dma' la 'jungs par mi 'gyur ram/ /
“ ‘When I see supplicants gathering and coming, I will dedicate myself to giving away everything. At that time won’t you be in disagreement with me And become saddened and be downcast? {62}
As I am engaged in giving all To beggars who come, Do not become depressed Or sad or unsympathetic.
nga yi mgo 'dod 'ongs par ngas mthong ste/ / byang chub sems dpa'i spyad pa spyod gyur na/ / de tshe khyod ni sdug bsngal gdungs 'gyur gyi/ / 'di 'dra'i don thos rab tu brtan par gyis/ /
“ ‘When I see someone come who wants my head, And if I then practice bodhisattva conduct, You will at that time be tormented by suffering. Listen to what I tell you and be resolute.[1806] {63}
Seeing benefit for one who wants my head, A wise person would delight in lofty conduct; You would be tormented, So hear my purpose and become firm.
nga yi rkang lag gtubs pa mthong gyur na/ / khyod ni mi dga' de tshe slong ba la/ / bud med ngang gis tshig drag mi bzod smra/ / don 'di thos shing sems la yongs su soms/ /
“ ‘When you see my legs and arms cut off, At that time you will be distressed. And you the woman will hear dreadful, harsh things. Listen to what I say and consider it. {64}
You would be grieved at my giving My severed hands and feet to beggars And speak bitterly, faint and distressed; So hear my purpose and think about it.
phangs pa'i dngos dang de bzhin bu rnams dang / / khyod kyang slong ba'i tshogs la sbyin dgos kyi/ / don 'di thos te mi dga' med na lta/ / khyod dga' thams cad de bzhin bya la rag /

“ ‘I will have to give away the highest material things, and similarly My children and even you, to the crowds of supplicants. On hearing this, see if it does not sadden you. All that you wish for depends on that.’ {65}
I will give away my prized possessions, Even my children, yet I want you; Hear my aim and if you do not despair, All shall be as you wish.
de skad ces smras pa dang / bu mo dga' ba'i 'od kyi dpal shin tu sbyangs pas rgyal bu gzi brjid kyi bdag po la 'di skad ces smras so/ /
“Then the girl Sucalitaratiprabhāsaśrī said to Prince Tejodhipati,
“The maid replied to the prince,

gzhon nu ji skad gsung ba de ltar bgyi'o/ / bdag ni/ khyod ci dgyes pa dang / ci bzhed par longs spyod pa dang / gang du dgyes par mchi ba dang / thams cad du yang slad nam las pas rjes su 'brang ba dang / rtag tu zham ring sleb pa dang / don thams cad la brtson pa dang / thugs dang mthun par spyad pa dang / med par nyams su blang ba dang / mi mthun pa ma mchis par nan tan du bgyi ba'i tshul la spyad par bgyi'o/ /zhes nas

‘Prince, may it be just as you have said, and I will do whatever you want. I will enjoy whatever you wish. Wherever you wish to go, I will follow you everywhere.[1807] I will always be in your presence, I will be dedicated to your goals, I will act in harmony with you, and I will practice sincerely; my conduct will be engaged in practicing that which accords with you.’

‘Let it be as you say. I will do as you wish. I am at your service and will accompany you wherever you want to go. I will always stay with you and be diligent in all tasks. I will behave as you wish. I will exert myself properly and act in harmony with you.”
bu mo dga' ba'i 'od kyi dpal shin tu sbyangs pas rgyal po'i sras gzi brjid kyi bdag po la tshigs su bcad de smras pa/
“Then the girl Sucalitaratiprabhāsaśrī recited these verses to Prince Tejodhipati:
Then she spoke these verses to the prince:
bdag gi lus 'di sems can dmyal ba yi/ / zhugs kyis yongs gdungs zhu bar gyur kyang rung / / khyod spyod skal ba mnyam pa'i phyag rjed du/ / tshe rabs rgya mtshor bdag gis spro bar bgyi/ /
“ ‘Even though my body is destroyed[1808] By being incinerated in the fires[1809] of hell, I will have the fortitude to assist you In our common practice during an ocean of lifetimes. {66}
Even if my body should be burnt to death In the fires of hell, I would endure it for myriad lifetimes As your companion in practice.
tshe rabs mtha' yas skyes pa re re zhing / / bdag gi lus ni shin tu gtubs gshags kyang / / brtan dam sems kyis rab tu spro bar bgyi/ / ngang dge khyod kyis bdag gis khyim thab mdzod/ /
“ ‘Even though my body is chopped up In each rebirth in endless lifetimes, I will be resolute in my fortitude To have you, virtuous one, as my husband. {67}
Even if life after life for endless lives My body were cut asunder, I would endure it with a steadfast mind If you were my husband.
khor yug ri yis bskal ba mtha' yas su/ / bdag gi mgo ni yongs su btags gyur kyang / / sems la mi bde ma mchis dad par bgyi/ / khyod kyis rtag par bdag gi khyim thab mdzod/ /
“ ‘Even though, for endless kalpas, my head Is crushed[1810] by the Cakravāla mountains, I would not be unhappy but would have faith in you, And you would always be my spouse. {68}
Even if the mountains should crush My head for endless ages, I would endure it unfazed If you became my husband.
khyod kyis tshe rabs grangs med thams cad du/ / bdag la thugs brtan thugs kyis mnga' mdzad de/ / yan lag sha gtubs gzhan la stsal ba mdzod/ / khyod kyi chos la bdag kyang brtan gzhag gsol/ /
“ ‘Within all our countless lifetimes, Give me mental stability and control over my own mind, And cut off my limbs and give them to others: I pray that you establish me firmly in your Dharma. {69}
In infinite lifetimes you may cut off Your own limbs and give them to others; Lead me to control of my thoughts And make me firm in my duty.
bdag gi lus ni slad na ma las par/ / skyes bu lha yi sras po khyod la dbul/ / bskal pa rgya mtshor spyod pa mdzad pa'i tshe/ / skye bo slong ba rnams la dgyes par stsol/ /
“ ‘All my successive bodies, without exception,[1811] I offer to you, a divine man. When you practice the conduct in an ocean of kalpas, I pray you use it to please the supplicants. {70}
I give you my body completely, O prince of men; Performing spiritual practice for myriad ages, Give me to whoever wants me, and I will be happy.
sems can kun la thugs rje mtha' yas pa/ / bskyed de sems can rgya mtsho bsdu slad du/ / byang chub dam pa mchog tu khyod zhugs pas/ / de slad bdag kyang thugs rjes bzung ba mdzod/ /

“ ‘You developed endless compassion for all beings In order to gather together an ocean of beings. You are set on attaining supreme, perfect enlightenment, So from now on hold me too in your compassion. {71}
You have set out for supreme enlightenment, With infinite compassion for beings; Having taken all beings into your care, Take me in too with compassion.
longs spyod don dang nor gyi don ma lags/ / 'dod spyod dga' ba bskyed pa'i don slad du/ / sems can mchog khyod khyor 'tshal ma lags kyi/ / khyod dang spyod pa mthun par spyad slad du'o/ /

“ ‘I desire you, the supreme being, as a husband, Not for the sake of possessions, not for the sake of wealth, And not for the sake of enjoying sensual pleasures But in order to practice the same conduct as you. {72}
It is not for enjoyment Or wealth or sensual pleasure That I want you, best of men, for my husband, But to share the same spiritual practice.
spyan gsal mdzes shing byams pa'i thugs mnga' ba/ / khyod ni 'jig rten gzigs pa ci tshul lags/ / thugs rje che yi 'dod chags thugs mi mnga'/ / de las thub dbang 'gyur ba gdon mi 'tshal; ;
“ ‘The way in which you look upon the world Is with clear, beautiful eyes and a mind of love, With great compassion and a mind free of passion: Lord of sages, I have no doubt in you. {73}
You look upon all beings With clear eyes and kind heart; Being compassionate with undefiled mind, You will surely become a king of sages.
khyod kyi zhabs kyis bcags pa'i sa rnams kyang / / dri med rin chen 'od du gnas pa las/ / khams gsum kun tu 'khor los bsgyur bar yang / / mtshan rab yongs kyis brgyan byon gdon mi 'tshal/ /

“ ‘The ground upon which you have trod Has become stainless with the light of jewels. You are adorned with the signs, and there is no doubt That you will be a cakravartin in all three realms.[1812] {74}
As you walk along, a jewellike glow From your footsteps remains on the earth, pure; Endowed with the marks of greatness, You will surely become a sovereign king in the human world.
bdag gis g.yar lam mthong ba dgung zhig la/ / chos bzang sprin 'od byang chub snying po yi/ / shing dbang drung na de bzhin gshegs pa bzhugs/ / sangs rgyas sras mang du mas mdun du bdar/ /
“ ‘I have seen in a dream A tathāgata[1813] at the foot of the lord of trees At the bodhimaṇḍa Sudharmameghaprabhā, With many sons of the buddhas before him. {75}
In a dream I saw the enlightenment site Illumined by clouds of true teaching in this kingdom; With the buddha sitting at the foot of the best of trees, In the company of many enlightening beings.
rgyal ba'i dbang po sku mchog nyi ma de/ / dzam+bu chu klung rin chen 'tsher ba 'dra/ / g.yar lam mthong bar phyag gis bdag mgo byugs/ / de nas sad nas glo ba rab tu dga'/ /
“ ‘Sūryagātrapravara, lord of jinas, Shining like precious Jambu River gold‍— I saw him in a dream stroking my head, And so today was filled with joy. {76}
That exalted buddha Supreme Sun Is like a mountain of finest rose gold; In my dream he patted my head, And I awoke then, full of joy.
dga' ba'i 'od ces bgyi ba rnam dag lus/ / sngon chad gnyen bshes gyur pa'i lha mo yis/ / bdag la bstan pa bde gshegs de nyid ni/ / snying po yang dag byang chub yongs la zhugs/ /
“ ‘A goddess with a pure body Named Ratiprabhā, a relative in the past, Proclaimed to me that this tathāgata Was present at the bodhimaṇḍa. {77}
A pure-bodied goddess named Light of Delight, Who had been a companion in the past, Told me the buddha was here, Staying at the supreme site of enlightenment.
sngon yang gzhon nu gzi brjid khyod blta zhes/ / bdag gi sems bskyed de ltar bsam par gyur/ / mdang sum dgung la lha mo dge ba yis/ / gzhon nu de ni mthong bar 'gyur zhes bstan/ /
“ ‘Before that I developed the aspiration Of thinking I shall see you, Prince Tejodhipati. The goddess proclaimed to me, “You will see that prince today!”[1814] {78}
I had been thinking before that I wanted To see the prince Lord of Glory, And I was told by the goddess I would see the prince soon.
bdag gis bde gshegs g.yar lam rmis pas mthong / / yongs su dag pa'i sems can khyod kyang mthong / / yid bzhin bsam 'grub khyod dang bdag bcas pas/ / de ring rgyal ba de la mchod par bgyi/ /
“ ‘I dreamed of seeing the sugata, And I also saw you, a pure being. You, a wish-fulfilling jewel, and I Will today make offerings to that jina.’[1815] {79}

de nas rgyal po'i bu gzi brjid kyi bdag pos de bzhin gshegs pa sku nyi ma dam pa'i mtshan thos te/ sangs rgyas blta ba'i skabs byung nas dga' ba dang mos pa'i shugs chen po skyes te bu mo dga' ba'i 'od kyi dpal shin tu sbyangs pa la nor bu rin po che lnga brgyas mngon par gtor nas gtsug gi rin po che dpal gyi 'od 'bar ba zhes bya ba'ang de la byin no/ / me'i mdog ltar 'dug pa'i nor bu rin po che dam pas brgyan pa'i gos rin po ches kyang de bkab bo/ /

“Then Prince Tejodhipati, on hearing the name of the Tathāgata Sūryagātrapravara, developed a powerful great aspiration and joy on having gained the opportunity to see that buddha. He scattered five hundred jewels on the girl Sucalitaratiprabhāsaśrī, gave her his crest jewel called glorious shining light,[1816] and covered her with precious clothing the color of fire and adorned her with excellent precious jewels.

“Then the prince, having heard the name of the buddha Supreme Sun and having thus gotten the opportunity to see the buddha, became very joyful; he showered the maid Splendor of Delight in Virtuous Conduct with five hundred jewels, gave her a shining crown of jewels, and covered her with a precious robe the color of fire blazing with jewels.

de de ltar rim gro byas kyang dga' bar gyur pa'am/ nyams bde bar gyur pa lta bu'ang med la/ dga' ba dang mos par ma gyur gyi/ gzhan du na thal mo sbyar cing mig mi 'gebs par gzhon nu gzi brjid bdag gi gdong la lta zhing gnas par gyur to/ /

“Though she was honored in that way, she did not delight or rejoice in it or become overjoyed, but with her hands together in homage remained gazing with her eyes fixed upon the face of Prince Tejodhipati.
And she, thus honored, neither rejoiced nor wept, nor did anything but gaze steadily at the prince with palms joined in respect.
de nas sprul tshong ma'i gtso mo blta na sdug pas rgyal bu gzhon nu gzi brjid kyi bdag po la tshigs su bcad de smras pa/
“Then Sudarśanā, the preeminent courtesan, recited these verses to Prince Tejodhipati:
“Then the prominent courtesan Beautiful spoke these verses to the prince:
bu mo 'di ni khyod gsal bgyi snyam nas/ / yun ring snga nas bdag gis bsam bsam ste/ / gzugs mdzes de yang de ring khyod la phul/ / bsod nams legs brgyan yon tan rab dang ldan/ /

“ ‘I have, for a long time, been thinking That I will give[1817] you this daughter of mine. Today I give you this one who has a beautiful body Adorned by excellent merits and possessing excellent qualities. {80}
For a long dark time I have wished To give this girl to you; Now this beautiful maiden Of virtue and quality is yours.
tshul khrims blo dang yon tan gzhan gyis kyang / / bu mo dam pa 'di dang 'dra ba ni/ / mi yi 'jig rten gang na'ang ma mchis te/ / 'jig rten kun gyi bud med nang na mchog /
“ ‘You will not find in the human world Another excellent girl who is like this. She has a mind of good conduct and other qualities. She is the best woman in all the world. {81}
There is no girl in the world Equal to her, much less superior; By virtue of her conduct, intellect, and other qualities, She is the best of women in the world.
pad+mo'i sbubs nas skyes pas rigs smos su/ / skyon gyi dri mas ma gos 'thad ma lags/ / ma lus skyon gyis ma gos sems dang ldan/ / rtag par khyod kyi spyod tshul mthun par 'gyur/ /
“ ‘Her birth was emergence from within a lotus. She is worthy, unstained by vices. Her mind is unblemished by any fault. Her conduct will always be in harmony with you. {82}
reg na bde la kun nas 'phags pas na/ / 'di yi lus ni shin tu 'jam pa ste/ / bro 'tshal nad pa gang la reg gyur kyang / / de yi mod la bro dang bral bar 'gyur/ /
“ ‘To touch her is blissful, superior to all. Her body[1818] has a perfect smoothness. Sick people who touch her Instantly become healthy. {83}
Her limbs are extremely soft, Conveying the finest pleasures of touch; The sick are instantly cured By her touch.
'di yi lus las spos kyi ngad 'byung ba/ / spos mchog gzhan rnams mngon par zil gyis gnon/ / de yi dri zhim tshor na rnam dag pa'i/ / tshul khrims gnas par mi rnams kun kyang 'gyur/ /
“ ‘Her body exudes the aroma of perfume So perfect it overshadows all other perfumes. All people who smell her lovely aroma Are established in pure, correct conduct. {84}
The pure fragrance of her body Excels all the finest perfumes; All men who smell it Become pure in conduct.
'di yi lus ni gser gyi mdog 'dra ste/ / pad+mo'i mchog ltar rnam par rab tu gsal/ / khros pas bltas na byams pa'i sems ldan par/ / sems can ma lus kun kyang rab tu 'gyur/ /
“ ‘Her body is like the color of gold And shines like the best[1819] of lotuses. All angry beings without exception Become loving on seeing her. {85}
Her body shines like gold, Undefiled like a lotus; Angry and cruel people Become kind when they have seen her.
'di yi tshig snyan yid du 'ong ba ste/ / nyams su bde bas 'gro ba nyan par dga'/ / thos na de rgyus skyon gyi mun pa dang / / mi dge'i sug las bgyid par mos mi 'gyur/ /
“ ‘Her speech is sweet, beautiful, and charming So that it is a delight for beings to listen to. Hearing it dispels the darkness of faults And causes there to be no wish to do bad actions. {86}
She speaks kindly, sweetly, pleasantly, A delight to people who hear; When they have heard her, the darkness of evil disperses, And none wants to do anything bad.
'di ni bsam bdag yid la dri med de/ / 'di la kun tu g.yo dang sgyu ma mchis/ / ci smra de dag yid la'ang de bzhin te/ / tshig dbyangs des ni 'gro ba tshim par bgyid/ /
“ ‘She has pure motivation and a stainless mind. She never has any deception or trickery. Whatever she says, that is what is in her mind, And with her words she brings contentment to beings. {87}
Her mind is pure, her heart untainted; There is no guile at all in her. What she says is just what she thinks, And thus she makes people happy.
sgyu yis sems can 'drid par mi bgyid de/ / nor gyi don du 'gro ba yongs mi slu/ / yid bsdams khrel gyis 'dzem dang ldan pa ste/ / rgan nam gzhon la'ang rtag tu sri zhu spyod; ;

“ ‘She does not deceive beings through trickery. She does not deceive beings for the sake of wealth. She has a sense of decorum and controls her mind, And she is always respectful to the young and the old. {88}
She does not fool anyone by deceit, Nor does she lead people on for gain; She is modest and discreet, Always respectful to old and young.
rigs rgyud gzugs kyis dregs pa ma mchis te/ / 'di ni 'khor gyis dregs pa'ang yongs ma mchis/ / nga rgyal rlom sems yongs dang bral ba ste/ / 'gro ba rnams la rtag tu gus par 'dud/ /
“ ‘She is not haughty because of birth, class, or body. She is not haughty because of her entourage. She is free of pride and arrogance And always bows respectfully to beings.’[1820] {89}
She is not fascinated by class Or looks or followers. She has no conceit or arrogance; She is always humble toward all.

de nas rgyal po'i bu gzi brjid kyi bdag po bu mo dga' ba'i 'od kyi dpal shin tu sbyangs pa 'khor dang bcas pa dang / bu mo stong phrag nyi shu dang / 'khor thams cad dang bcas par bza' shing gi ra ba spos kyi myu gu'i rtse mo nas 'od kyi sprin 'byung ba de nas byung ste snying po byang chub chos kyis 'phags pa'i 'od gang na ba der bcom ldan 'das de bzhin gshegs pa sku nyi ma dam pa gang na ba der bcom ldan 'das de bzhin gshegs pa sku nyi ma dam pa'i zhal blta ba dang / de la phyag 'tshal ba dang / mchod pa dang / bsnyen bkur ba'i phyir dong ste/

“Then Prince Tejodhipati, accompanied by the girl Sucalitaratiprabhāsaśrī and her entourage, and by his entourage of twenty thousand maidens, left Gandhāṅkuraśikharaprabhameghā Park and went to the Dharmodgataprabhāsa bodhimaṇḍa, where the Bhagavat, the Tathāgata Sūryagātrapravara, was, in order to gaze upon the Bhagavat, the Tathāgata Sūryagātrapravara, bow down to him, make offerings to him, and honor him.

“Then the prince and the maid, with her retinue of twenty thousand girls, left the park and went to the site of enlightenment where the buddha was, to see, pay respects to, make offerings to, and attend the buddha.
de rta babs sa'i bar du bzhon pas song nas babs te rkang pas bcom ldan 'das de bzhin gshegs pa sku nyi ma dam pa'i drung du song ngo/ /
“They rode as far as the gateway and then proceeded on foot to come into the presence of the Bhagavat, the Tathāgata Sūryagātrapravara.
Going by vehicle as far as the vehicle would go, the prince got off the vehicle and approached the buddha on foot;

de nas rgyal po gzhon nu gzi brjid kyi bdag pos rgyang ring po nas bcom ldan 'das de bzhin gshegs pa dgra bcom pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas rab tu bzang ba/ blta na sdug pa/ dbang po zhi ba/ thugs zhi ba; dbang po bsdams pa/ glang po ltar shin tu dul ba/ mtsho ltar shing rnyog pa med la rnam par gsal ba mthong ngo/ /

“Prince Tejodhipati saw from afar that the Tathāgata Arhat Samyaksaṃbuddha Sūryagātrapravara was attractive, handsome, with pacified senses, with a pacified mind, with restrained senses, as tamed as an elephant, and as clear, undefiled, and serene[1821] as a lake.
even at a distance he saw that the buddha was serene, a sight to behold, senses tranquil, mind quiet, senses under control, like a tame elephant, his heart like a clear, still pond.

de ltar mthong nas de'i sems mngon par mos par gyur to/ / de ltar sems mngon par mos par gyur nas sangs rgyas mthong ba'i dga' ba dang / mos pa'i shugs chen po rnam par spel te dga' ba dang / mos pa dang / spro ba chen pos yongs su rgyas pa'i sems kyis bcom ldan 'das de la lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas

“On seeing him in that way, Prince Tejodhipati was attracted to him, and with his mind attracted to him, there increased within him the power of great faith and joy on seeing the Buddha. With that increasing joy, faith, and attraction, he circumambulated the Bhagavat, keeping him to his right, many hundreds of thousands of times.

When he saw the buddha, the prince’s mind became settled, and with a clear mind he developed great joy, well-being, and energy that derives from seeing a buddha. With his mind full of great joy, energy, serenity, and rapture, he paid his respects to the buddha,

bu mo dga' ba'i 'od kyi dpal shin tu sbyangs pa la sogs pa 'khor thams cad dang bcas pas bcom ldan 'das de'i zhabs la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te rin po che dam pa'i pad+mo stong phrag lnga brgyas bcom ldan 'das de la mngon par gtor te/ bcom ldan 'das de'i gtsug lag khang lnga brgya nor bu rin po che'i rgyal po spos sna tshogs las byas pa/ rin po che'i rgyal po sna tshogs kyis rab tu brgyan pa lnga brgya brtsigs so/ / gtsug lag khang re re zhing yang nor bu rin po che'i rgyal po stong phrag lnga brgyas rab tu brgyan to/ /

“The girl Sucalitaratiprabhāsaśrī and the rest of the entourages bowed their heads to the Bhagavat’s feet and scattered five hundred thousand lotuses made of excellent jewels over the Bhagavat. They built for the Bhagavat five hundred vihāras made from various aromatic materials and kings of jewels and adorned by various kings of jewels. Each vihāra was adorned by five thousand kings of precious jewels.

and together with his whole company, including the young woman, covered the buddha with five hundred thousand great jewel lotuses, and made five hundred sanctuaries of jewels for the buddha and adorned each one with five hundred thousand diamonds.
de nas bcom ldan de bzhin de bzhin gshegs pa sku nyi ma dam pas gzhon nu gzi brjid kyi bdag po'i bsam pa thugs su chud nas mdo sde sgo kun tu lta ba'i sgron ma zhes bya ba yang dag par bstan to/ /
“Then the Bhagavat, the Tathāgata Sūryagātrapravara, knowing the thoughts of Prince Tejodhipati, taught the sūtra called The Lamp for Seeing All Entrances.
“Then the buddha, knowing the prince’s strong determination, expounded a scripture called Lamp at the Door of the Universal Eye,
des de thos nas chos thams cad kyi tshul la ting nge 'dzin gyi sgo rgya mtsho phrag bcu thob par gyur te/ 'di ltar
“When Prince Tejodhipati heard that, he attained ten oceans of samādhis of the ways of all Dharmas. They were like this:
upon hearing which the prince attained ten oceans of concentrations absorbed in all principles of the Teaching:
de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi smon lam rgya mtsho yang dag par 'byung ba zhes bya ba'i ting nge 'dzin gyi sgo rab tu thob bo/ /
“He attained the gateway of the samādhi called the arising of an ocean of prayers of all the tathāgatas.
he attained ways of concentration such as those called ‘light produced from the oceans of vows of all buddhas,’
dus gsum snang ba'i snying po zhes bya ba'i ting nge 'dzin gyi sgo rab tu thob bo/ /
“He attained the gateway of the samādhi called the essence of the appearances of the three times.
‘path of illumination of past, present, and future,’
sangs rgyas thams cad kyi dkyil 'khor mngon du gyur par 'byung ba zhes bya ba'i ting nge 'dzin gyi sgo rab tu thob bo/ /
“He attained the gateway of the samādhi called the arising of the manifestation of the fields of all the buddhas.
‘going forth into the circle of all buddhas,’
sems can 'byams klas pa thams cad rab tu snang bar bya ba la 'jug pa zhes bya ba'i ting nge 'dzin gyi sgo rab tu thob bo/ /
“He attained the gateway of the samādhi called entering the illumination of the entire vast extent of being.
‘entry into the highest range of awareness of all beings,’
'jig rten thams cad du 'byung ba'i ye shes kyi snang ba la zhugs pa zhes bya ba'i ting nge 'dzin gyi sgo rab tu thob bo/ /
“He attained the gateway of the samādhi called entering the illumination of wisdom that arises in all worlds.
‘attainment of the scope of knowledge of the causes that produce all worlds,’
sems can thams cad kyi dbang po rgya mtsho la 'jug pa snang ba'i sgron ma zhes bya ba'i ting nge 'dzin gyi sgo rab tu thob bo/ /
“He attained the gateway of the samādhi called the lamp that illuminates the entry into the ocean of the faculties of all beings.
‘lamp illumining the oceans of faculties of all beings,’
'gro ba thams cad yongs su skyob pa'i ye shes kyi sprin ces bya ba'i ting nge 'dzin gyi sgo rab tu thob bo/ /
“He attained the gateway of the samādhi called the cloud of wisdom that protects all beings.
‘cloud of knowledge to save all beings,’
'gro ba thams cad yongs su smin par bya ba dang / gdul ba la mngon du gyur pa'i sgron ma zhes bya ba'i ting nge 'dzin gyi sgo rab tu thob bo/ /
“He attained the gateway of the samādhi called the lamp that manifests the ripening and guiding of all beings.
‘lamp leading to the development and emancipation of all beings,’
de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi chos kyi 'khor lo'i sgra rnams dmigs par byed pa zhes bya ba'i ting nge 'dzin gyi sgo rab tu thob bo/ /
“He attained the gateway of the samādhi called the perception of the words of the Dharma wheels of all tathāgatas.
‘communicating the cycles of teaching of all buddhas,’
kun tu bzang po'i spyod pa'i dkyil 'khor yongs su dag par byed pa'i smon lam gyi sprin ces bya ba'i ting nge 'dzin gyi sgo rab tu thob ste/
“He attained the gateway of the samādhi called the cloud of the prayers that purify the field of completely good conduct.
and ‘multitude of undertakings to purify the practices of universal good.’
ting nge 'dzin gyi sgo bcu po 'di dag la sogs pa chos kyi tshul thams cad la ting nge 'dzin gyi sgo rgya mtsho phrag bcu rab tu thob par gyur to/ /
“He attained those ten samādhi gateways and so on, a further ten oceans of gateways to samādhis in all the ways of the Dharma.
Beginning with these, the prince attained ten oceans of concentrations absorbed in all the principles of the Teaching.

bu mo dga' ba'i 'od kyi dpal shin tu sbyangs pas kyang ye shes thub par dka' ba rgya mtsho'i snying po zhes bya ba'i sems nges par gzhag pa rab tu thob par gyur te/ bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub las kyang phyir mi ldog par gyur to/ /

“Also, the girl Sucalitaratiprabhāsaśrī attained the realization called the essence of the ocean of the wisdom that is difficult to accomplish and became irreversible in her progress to the highest, complete enlightenment.
The young woman attained a meditation called ‘filled with an ocean of invincible knowledge’ and became irreversible in progress toward supreme perfect enlightenment.

de nas rgyal po'i bu gzi brjid kyi bdag pos bcom ldan 'das de bzhin gshegs pa sku nyi ma dam pa'i zhabs gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te/ bcom ldan 'das la lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas bu mo dga' ba'i 'od kyi dpal shin tu sbyangs pa dang / 'khor thams cad dang bcas te bcom ldan 'das de'i spyan snga nas dong ngo/ /

“Then Prince Tejodhipati bowed his head to the feet of the Bhagavat, the Tathāgata Sūryagātrapravara and circumambulated the Bhagavat many hundreds of thousands of times, keeping him to his right, and then, together with the girl Sucalitaratiprabhāsaśrī and his entourage, he departed from the presence of the Bhagavat.
“Then the prince, paying respects to the buddha, left the presence of the buddha with the young woman and the rest of the company

de nas rgyal po'i gnas sdong po ri bo'i dpal gang na ba dang / rgyal po yab nor gyi bdag po gang na ba der dong ste drung du phyin nas rgyal po yab nor gyi bdag po'i rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te don 'di brjod do/ / lha'i zhal snga nas mkhyen par mdzad du gsol/ / de bzhin gshegs pa dgra bcom pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas sku nyi ma dam pa zhes bgyi ba/ mkhyen pa dang zhabs su ldan pa/ bde bar gshegs pa; 'jig rten mkhyen pa/ bla na med pa/ skyes bu 'dul ba'i kha lo sgyur ba/ lha dang mi rnams kyi ston pa sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das 'jig rten du byung ste/ khyod kyi khams 'di de nyid kyi snying po byang chub chos kyi sprin shin tu stug po'i 'od na rnam par spyod de/ mngon par rdzogs par sangs rgyas nas ring po ma lags so/ /

“He went to the royal capital Drumameruśrī and to his father King Dhanapati. He came into his presence, bowed his head to the feet of King Dhanapati, and said, ‘Your Majesty, I request that you heed me. There has appeared in the world a tathāgata, an arhat, a samyaksaṃbuddha, one with wisdom and conduct,[1822] a sugata, one who knows the world’s beings, an unsurpassable guide who tames beings, a teacher of devas and humans, a buddha, a bhagavat, named Sūryagātrapravara. He is dwelling in your realm’s bodhimaṇḍa called Dharmameghodgataprabhā. It is not long since he attained complete buddhahood.’

and went to his father, the king, in the city. Greeting the king respectfully, he informed him that the buddha Supreme Sun had appeared in the world and was staying in the king’s realm, having recently attained enlightenment.

de nas rgyal po nor gyi bdag pos gzhon nu gzi brjid kyi bdag po la 'di skad ces smras so/ / gzhon nu khyod la don 'di lha'am/ mi'am/ su zhig gis sbran/ des smras pa/ bdag la bu mo dga' ba'i 'od kyi dpal shin tu sbyangs pas sbran to; ;
“Then King Dhanapati said to Prince Tejodhipati, ‘Prince, did a deity or a human tell you about this?’ “He replied, ‘A girl named Sucalitaratiprabhāsaśrī told me.’
The king then asked the prince who had told him so, and he replied that it had been the young woman Splendor of Delight in Virtuous Conduct.

de nas rgyal po nor gyi bdag pos sangs rgyas byung bar thos nas sangs rgyas skye ba la ni/ gter rab tu thob pa tsam du sems/ sangs rgyas rin po che dang phrad par ni/ dga' bar sems/ de bzhin gshegs pa mthong bas ni/ ngan song gi g.yang sa'i 'jigs pa thams cad kyang rnam par ldog par sems/ nyon mongs pa'i nad chen po rab tu zhi bar bya ba la ni/ sman pa'i rgyal po chen po dang phrad pa tsam du sems/ 'khor ba'i sdug bsngal thams cad las ni/ yongs su 'grel ba yin par sems/ shin tu bde zhing ldan pa la ni; rab tu gzhog par sems/ rab rib med pa'i ye shes kyi snang ba ni/ yang dag par ston par sems/ ma rig pa'i mun pa bsal ba la ni/ sgron ma chen po byung ba tsam du sems/ 'jig rten mgon med pa las ni/ chos kyi tshul gyi mgon dang phrad par sems/ 'jig rten 'dren pa med pa las ni/ thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi theg pas 'dren pa skyes par sems shing / sangs rgyas byung bar thos pas mos pa dang / spro ba chen po skyes nas

“Then King Dhanapati, having heard that a buddha had appeared, thought how he had obtained the treasure of the birth of a buddha. He thought how it was difficult to meet a precious buddha. He thought how seeing a tathāgata dispels the danger of the abyss of the lower existences. He thought how it was like encountering a great king of medicines that cures the great illness of the kleśas. He thought how this liberates[1823] from all the sufferings of saṃsāra. He thought how this establishes one in perfect happiness. He thought how this is a great lamp that eliminates the darkness of ignorance. He thought how this is like obtaining a protector in the way of the Dharma for a world that has no protector. He thought how this is the appearance of a guide through the yāna of omniscience for a world that has no guide. On hearing that a buddha had appeared, he felt great joy and faith.

“Then the king, hearing of the emergence of the buddha, felt that he had gained a great treasure, felt that he had found the rare jewel of Buddha; he considered the sight of a buddha to be the end of the danger of falling into evil ways; he felt he had found a great physician who could heal all afflictions. He thought of the buddha as a liberator from all the sufferings of the mundane whirl, as one who leads to ultimate peace and felicity, as one who reveals the unobscured light of knowledge. He thought of the buddha as the appearance of a great torch dispelling the darkness of ignorance, and felt that he had found a spiritual guide for a world with no guide, thinking of the buddha as a leader to omniscience for the leaderless. “Hearing of the emergence of the buddha with great joy,

rgyal rigs dang / bram ze dang / ljongs kyi mi dang / yul mi dang / blon po dang / zham ring ba dang / gzhon nu dang / rgyal phran dang / khams kyi bdag po dang / 'khor thams cad kyang kun nas bsdus nas sangs rgyas byung bar sgra snyan pa sgrog pa'i gzhon nu gzi brjid kyi bdag po la rgyal po'i srid de yang chos kyi dga' bar byin no/ /

“He gathered together all the kṣatriyas, the brahmins, the townspeople,[1824] the country people, the ministers, the court priests, the princes, the local governors, the guardians, and the court. He bestowed the kingdom and the protection of the Dharma on Prince Tejodhipati, who had announced the appearance of the buddha.

the king Lord of Wealth gathered together all the warriors, priests, townspeople, ministers, family priests, princes, and governors, as well as the gatekeepers and courtiers, and abdicated the throne in favor of his son Lord of Glory, who had brought the joyous news of the appearance of the buddha.

de ltar gzhon nu de rgyal srid la dbang bskur nas srog chags stong phrag bcu dang lhan cig tu bcom ldan 'das de bzhin gshegs pa sku nyi ma dam pa gang na ba der song ste spyan sngar phyin nas bcom ldan 'das de'i zhabs gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te/ bcom ldan 'das de la lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas bcom ldan 'das de'i spyan sngar rang gi 'khor dang bcas te 'khod do/ /

“Having anointed him as the sovereign, he went together with two thousand people to where the Bhagavat, the Tathāgata Sūryagātrapravara was. Having come into his presence, he bowed his head to the Bhagavat’s feet, circumambulated the Bhagavat, keeping him to his right, many hundreds of thousands of times, and then sat with his entourage before the Bhagavat.
Then, having crowned the prince as king, he went together with ten thousand people to the buddha, paid his respects, and sat with his retinue before the buddha.

de nas bcom ldan 'das de bzhin gshegs pa sku nyi ma dam pas rgyal po nor gyi bdag po dang / 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor thams cad la gzigs nas de'i tshe mdzod spu nas 'od zer 'gro ba thams cad kyi sems kyi sgron ma zhes bya ba rab tu bkye'o/ / de phyogs bcu'i 'jig rten gyi khams snang bar byas te/ 'jig rten gyi dbang po thams cad mngon sum du bkod nas sangs rgyas kyi rnam par 'phrul ba bsam gyis mi khyab pa yongs su bstan to/ / sangs rgyas kyis 'dul ba'i sems can rnams kyi bsam pa dang / lhag pa'i bsam pa rnam par sbyangs nas

“The Bhagavat Sūryagātrapravara looked at King Dhanapati and all his entourage. At that time his ūrṇā hair radiated a light ray called a lamp for the minds of all beings. It illuminated the world realms in the ten directions and came before all the lords of the worlds, manifested countless buddha miracles, and purified the thoughts and higher motivations of the beings who were being guided by the buddhas.

“Then the buddha, looking at the king and the whole assembly, emitted a light from the curl of hair between his brows, a light called ‘lamp of the minds of all beings,’ which illumined all worlds in the ten directions, then stopped in front of all the world leaders, displayed inconceivable buddha-projections, clarified the minds of those beings who could be taught by the buddha,

de'i tshe sangs rgyas kyi byin gyi rlabs bsam gyis mi khyab pa'i mthus sangs rgyas kyi sku 'jig rten thams cad las mngon par 'phags pa dang / sangs rgyas kyi gsung dbyangs kyi yan lag rgya mtsho thams cad dang ldan pas gzungs kyi sgo chos thams cad la rab rib med pa'i don gyi sgron ma zhes bya ba gzungs kyi sgo sangs rgyas kyi zhing gi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed dang bcas par yang dag par bstan to/ /

“At that time, through the inconceivable blessing of the buddha, and through possessing a buddha’s body higher than all worlds, and through the entire ocean of the aspects of the voice of a buddha, he taught the dhāraṇī gateway called the lamp of the meaning of all the Dharmas freed from darkness, together with dhāraṇī gateways as numerous as the atoms in a buddha realm.

and then, by the inconceivable mastery of Buddha, by means of embodiment of Buddha appearing in all worlds, speaking all languages in the voice of Buddha, expounded a medium of mental command called ‘unshaded lamp of meaning of all things,’ which was accompanied by as many media of mental command as atoms in a buddha-land.
de nas rgyal po nor gyi bdag pos gzungs kyi sgo de thos nas chos thams cad la chos kyi snang ba chen po skyes par gyur to/ /
“Then King Dhanapati, having heard that dhāraṇī gateway, generated a great Dharma illumination of all Dharmas.
The king Lord of Wealth, hearing of this medium of mental command, gained an immense spiritual perspective on all things.

'khor de'i byang chub sems dpa' 'dzam bu'i gling gi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyis kyang chos thams cad la rab rib med pa'i don gyi sgron ma'i gzungs rab tu thob par gyur to/ / khrag khrig drug cus ni/ nye bar len pa med par zag pa las sems rnam par grol lo; ; srog chags stong phrag bcus ni/ chos rnams la chos kyi mig rdul dang bral zhing dri ma med pa rnam par dag par gyur to/ / sems can grangs med pa zhig gis ni/ sngon bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed pa yongs su bskyed do/ / phyogs bcur yang sangs rgyas kyi rnam par 'phrul pa bsam gyis mi khyab pa yongs su bstan pa des sems can gyi khams mtha' dang dbus med pa theg pa gsum gyis dul bar gyur to/ /

“The bodhisattvas in that assembly, who were as numerous as the atoms in Jambudvīpa, also attained the dhāraṇī gateway called the lamp of the meaning of all the Dharmas freed from darkness. Sixty hundred thousand million beings had their minds liberated from defilements, without grasping. Ten thousand beings gained a stainless, pure, unclouded Dharma vision of all Dharmas. Countless beings who had not[1825] previously developed the aspiration for the highest, complete enlightenment developed that aspiration. Also, the manifestation of inconceivable buddha miracles in the ten directions guided a vast extent of beings, without end or middle, by means of the three yānas.

As many enlightening beings there as atoms in the continent attained the mental command of the unshaded lamp of meaning of all things. Sixty million people, freed from contaminations, were mentally liberated. Ten thousand people became dispassionate and untainted, and their objective vision of things was clarified. An immense number aspired to supreme perfect enlightenment for the first time. Infinitely many beings in the ten directions, by seeing the inconceivable mystic displays projected by the buddha, reached liberation by way of the Three Vehicles.

de nas rgyal po nor gyi bdag po chos kyi snang ba rab tu thob pa de'i yid la 'di snyam ste/ khyim na gnas pas ni/ rnam pa 'di lta bu'i chos kyang khong du chud par mi nus la/ ye shes rnam pa 'di lta bu yang sgrub par mi nus kyi/ bdag ni/ bcom ldan 'das kyi zham ring du rab tu 'byung ngo/ / snyam nas

“Then King Dhanapati, who had attained the illumination of the Dharma, thought, ‘Living in a home, I will not be able to comprehend such a Dharma as this and will not be able to accomplish this kind of wisdom. I will enter homelessness as a servant of this bhagavat.’

“The king Lord of Wealth, having gained great illumination from the Teaching, thought, ‘I cannot apply myself assiduously to such a teaching or accomplish such knowledge while living at home; let me leave home to be with the buddha.’

rgyal po nor gyi bdag pos bcom ldan 'das de la 'di skad ces gsol to/ / bcom ldan 'das/ bdag bcom ldan 'das kyi zham ring du rab tu byung zhing bsnyen par rdzogs pa'i dge slong gi tshul la mchis par ci gnang zhes nas bcom ldan 'das des bka' stsal pa/ rgyal po chen po/ de'i dus la bab par shes na rung ngo/ /

“King Dhanapati said to the Bhagavat, ‘Bhagavat, I wish to enter homelessness in the presence of the Bhagavat and enter the way of a complete bhikṣu.’ “The Bhagavat said, ‘Great king, you may consider that the time for that has come.’
Then he told the buddha he wanted to receive the precepts from the buddha and leave home to become a mendicant. The buddha assented to this.

de nas rgyal po nor gyi bdag po srog chags stong phrag bcu dang lhan cig tu de bzhin gshegs pa sku nyi ma dam pa'i zham ring du rab tu byung ngo/ / de ltar rab tu byung nas ring po ma lon par gzungs kyi sgo chos thams cad la rab rib med pa'i don gyi sgron ma zhes bya ba 'khor dang bcas par yongs su bsgrubs so/ /bsgoms so/ /shin tu bsgoms so/ / de snyed kyi ting nge 'dzin kyi sgo yang rab tu thob par gyur to/ / byang chub sems dpa'i mngon par shes pa bcu yang rab tu thob bo/ / tha dad pa yang dag par shes pa'i tshul rgya mtsho la'ang yang dag par zhugs par gyur to/ / phyogs bcu'i de bzhin gshegs pa'i drung du 'gro bar thogs pa med pa'i spyod yul zhes bya ba'i lus yongs su dag pa yang rab tu thob ste/ de nas bcom ldan 'das de'i chos kyi 'khor lo yang dag par blangs so/ / yongs su bzung ngo/ / gtam gyi skyes bu yang byas so/ / chos smra ba chen po yang byas so/ / bstan pa yongs su bzung ba yang byas so/ /

“Then King Dhanapati, together with ten thousand beings, entered homelessness in the presence of the Tathāgata Sūryagātrapravara. Not long after entering homelessness, he accomplished the dhāraṇī gateway called the lamp of the meaning of all the Dharmas freed from darkness and its accompanying dhāraṇī gateways, meditated on them, and meditated on them well. He also attained many samādhi gateways. He also attained the ten higher cognitions of a bodhisattva. He also entered an ocean of the ways of discernment. He also attained a pure body called the unimpeded field of activity, through which he went without impediment into the presence of the tathāgatas in the ten directions. He obtained and held the Dharma wheels of that bhagavat and spoke about them with people, and he became a great dharmabhāṇaka and was a holder of the teaching.

“So then the king and ten thousand of his people left home to follow the buddha. Not long after leaving home, he accomplished the mental command of the unshaded lamp of meaning of all things, along with its subsidiaries, and attained that many concentrations. He also attained ten mystic knowledges of enlightening beings and plunged into infinite oceans of analytic knowledge. He also attained a purity of body called ‘unhindered sphere of action’ in going to see the buddhas of the ten directions. He received the teaching of the buddha, preserved it, and preached it, having become a great spiritual preacher and a practitioner of the teaching.

mngon par shes pa thob pa'i stobs kyis kyang 'jig rten gyi khams thams cad rgyas par bkang ste bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du sems can rnams la lus yongs su bstan nas sangs rgyas byung ba de rab tu brjod pa dang / sngon gyi de bzhin gshegs pas yongs su bsgrubs pa'i chos nyid mngon par brjod pa dang / sngon gyi sbyor ba phun sum tshogs pa de dag yongs su brjod pa dang / sangs rgyas kyi rnam par 'phrul pa'i mthu de dag yongs su brjod par bya bas bstan pa yongs su bzung pa byas so/ /

Through the power of attaining the higher cognitions, he spread throughout all world realms and manifested bodies to beings in accordance with their aspirations. He told them about this appearance of a buddha, told them about the nature of the accomplishments of the past tathāgatas, told them about the perfection of their past applications, described the power of the miraculous manifestations of the buddhas, and in that way was a holder of the teaching.

By the power of attainment of mystic knowledge, he pervaded the whole world, appearing to people according to their mentalities, telling them of the emergence of the buddha, illuminating the nature that produces all buddhas, explaining the accomplishment of the past practices of the buddha, praising the miraculous power of the buddha, supporting the buddha’s teaching.

rgyal po'i sras gzi brjid kyi bdag pos kyang de'i nyin par zla ba nya ste rgyas pa'i tshe rin po che bdun rab tu thob par gyur te/ de khang pa'i steng na bud med kyi tshogs kyis bskor cing 'dug ba'i mdun du 'khor lo rin po che chen po shugs la thogs pa med pa zhes bya brtsibs stong phrag brgya dang ldan pa/ rin po che thams cad kyis brgyan pa/ lha rdzas kyi dzam+bu chu klung gi gser las grub pa/ 'od kun tu 'byung ba/ rnam pa'i mchog thams cad dang ldan pa byung bar gyur to/ / glang po rin po che sna chen po rdo rje rin po che'i ri'i gzi brjid ces bya ba byung bar gyur to/ / rta rin po che ri sngo rlung gi shugs zhes bya ba byung bar gyur to/ / nor bu rin po che chen po nyi ma'i snying po 'od sprin rgyal po zhes bya ba byung bar gyur to/ / bu mo dga' ba'i 'od kyi dpal shin tu sbyangs pa de yang bud med rin po cher byung bar gyur to/ / khyim bdag rin po che nor gyi phung po mang po zhes bya bya ba byung bar gyur to/ / blon po rin po che mig dri ma med pa zhes bya ba yang byung bar gyur te/ de ltar bdun no/ /

“Prince Tejodhipati attained the seven precious possessions of a cakravartin on that very day, when the moon became full. When he was on the palace roof encircled by a gathering of women, there appeared before him a great precious wheel called Pratihatavega, which had a hundred thousand spokes, was adorned by all jewels, was made from divine Jambu River gold, was shining, and possessed every supreme feature. A great precious elephant called Vajraratnagiritejas appeared. A precious horse called Nīlagiryanilavega appeared. A great precious jewel called Ādityagarbhaprabhamegharāja appeared. The girl Sucalitaratiprabhāsaśrī appeared as the precious queen. A precious householder called Prabhūtaghanaskandha appeared. And seventh, a precious minister called Vimalanetra appeared.

“As for the new king, the son of Lord of Wealth, on that very day, the time of the full moon, he obtained the seven treasures of kingship. As he was sitting in the upper palace surrounded by a group of women, there appeared a great disc called ‘unobstructed momentum,’ adorned with a hundred thousand jewels, made of gold, shining all over, perfectly formed. There also appeared a great elephant named Diamond Mountain Blaze. There also appeared a horse named Swift As the Wind in the Mountains. There also appeared a great jewel called ‘supreme cluster of sunlight.’ There also appeared the young woman Splendor of Delight in Virtuous Conduct, to be his treasure of a wife. There also appeared a treasurer named Mass of Abundant Wealth. There also appeared a military leader, the seventh treasure, called Untainted Eye.

de de ltar rin po che bdun dang ldan pa'i rgyal po 'khor los bsgyur ba/ gling bzhi la dbang ba/ chos dang ldan pa/ chos kyi rgyal po rnam par rgyal ba dang ldan pa/ yul gyi mthu dang brtson 'grus su ldan par gyur to/ /

“In that way, he became a cakravartin king, a possessor of the seven jewels, a sovereign over the four continents, a follower of the Dharma, a Dharma king, and a victor, endowed with the power and vigor of an empire.
Endowed with these seven treasures, he became king, sovereign, ruler of the four continents, just, commander of the law, victorious, with the power and vigor of the people.
de la bu dpa' ba rtul phod cing yan lag dam pa'i gzugs dang ldan pa/ pha rol gyi sde rab tu 'joms pa stong yod par gyur te/
“He had a thousand sons who were courageous and heroic, with perfectly formed bodies, who could crush the armies of enemies.
He also had a full thousand sons, strong and valiant, destroyers of enemy armies.

des sa chen po 'di skyon med pa dang / dgra med pa dang / gnod pa med pa dang / 'tshe ba med pa dang / skyid pa dang / phun sum tshogs pa dang / bde ba dang / lo legs pa dang / mdangs dga' ba dang / skye bo dang mi mang pos yongs su gang ba yang ri dang rgya mtsho'i mthas klas par chos kyis mngon par rgyal te gnas par byas so/ /

“He ruled the great land to the ends of the mountains and oceans, adorning it with the Dharma, and it was free of problems, without enemies, free of harm, without violence, thriving, prosperous, peaceful, with excellent harvests, joyful, and filled with many beings.
Under his just rule the earth was free from war, free from evil, free from calamity, prosperous, peaceful, pleasant, and well populated.

des 'dzam bu'i gling de'i rgyal po'i gnas stong phrag brgyad cu rtsa bzhi dag tu yang rgyal po'i gnas re rer gtsug lag khang lnga brgya lnga brgya byed du btsud de/ thams cad kyang rnam pa'i mchog thams cad dang ldan pa sha stag go / longs spyod dang yo byad kyi rnam pa thams cad phun sum tshogs pa sha stag go / bza' shing gi ra ba dang / khang pa dang / 'chags dang / dus thams cad du bde bar spyad pa'i nags tshal gyi phreng bas rnam par brgyan pa sha stag go /

“There were eighty-four thousand royal capitals in that Jambudvīpa, and in each royal city five hundred vihāras were established, and all of them had all the best features. They all had a perfection of all kinds of requisites and pleasures. They all had gardens, buildings, and walkways and were adorned by rows of forests that could be enjoyed at all times.

“In each of the eighty-four thousand main cities on the continent, he had five hundred sanctuaries built, complete with all the finest features, equipped with all utensils, supplies, and facilities, adorned with gardens, buildings, promenades, and delightful groves.

gtsug lag khang re re zhing yang de bzhin gshegs pa'i mchod rten brtsigs pa ni/ lhun gyi rgya shin tu che bar byas pa ste/ nang rin po che rnam pa mang pos brgyan pa/ rin po che'i rgyal po sna tshogs kyis rnam par spras pa sha stag ste/
“In each vihāra was erected a caitya of the Tathāgata as large as a mountain and adorned on the inside with many jewels and beautified by various kings of jewels.
In each sanctuary he also had buddha-memorials built, high and wide, adorned with many arrays of jewels.
rgyal po'i gnas de thams cad du'ang bcom ldan 'das de bzhin gshegs pa sku nyi ma dam pa 'khor dang bcas pa grong khyer du gshegs par bya ba'i phyir spyan drangs so/ /
“The Tathāgata Sūryagātrapravara and his followers were invited to come to all those royal cities.
And he invited the buddha Supreme Sun to all those cities,
rgyal po'i gnas de dag kun tu yang de bzhin gshegs pa de la de bzhin gshegs pa'i mchod pa rnam pa thams cad du bsam gyis mi khyab pas mchod de/
In all those royal cities, inconceivable offerings of every kind worthy of a tathāgata were made to that tathāgata.
where he presented the buddha with inconceivable offerings of all kinds.
sangs rgyas grong khyer du gshegs pa'i cho 'phrul dang / rnam par 'phrul pas sems can tshad med pa'i dge ba'i rtsa ba yongs su bskyed pa'i phyir gshegs su gsol to/ /
He was asked to come because the miraculous manifestations of a buddha’s entry into a town generated roots of merit in beings.
The miracle of the entry of the buddha into the cities fostered virtue in innumerable people,
der yang sems can ma dad pa'i sems dang ldan pa rnams ni/ dad pa thob par gyur to/ /
Beings there who had no faith attained faith.
and all those with disturbed minds attained tranquillity,
dad pa dang ldan pa'i sems can rnams ni/ sangs rgyas mthong bas dga' ba'i shugs rnam par 'phel bar gyur to/ /
Beings who had faith had an increased power of joy on seeing the buddha.
while those with calm minds developed the intense joy of seeing the buddha;
dga' ba'i shugs rnam par 'phel ba'i sems can rnams ni/ byang chub kyi bsam pa rnam par dag pa thob par gyur to/ /
Beings who had an increased power of joy attained the pure aspiration to enlightenment.
those who were full of joy attained purity of will for enlightenment,
byang chub kyi bsam pa rnam par dag pa'i sems can rnams ni/ snying rje chen po'i sems bskyed par gyur to/ /
Beings who had the pure aspiration to enlightenment developed the motivation of great compassion.
while those whose will for enlightenment was pure developed great compassion;
sems can la phan par zhugs pa'i sems can rnams ni/ sangs rgyas kyi chos thams cad yongs su btsal ba la brtson par gyur to/ /
Beings who were engaged in benefiting beings became dedicated to seeking all the Dharma of the buddhas.
those of goodwill became involved in the quest for all buddha-teachings,
sangs rgyas kyi chos kyi tshul gyi rnam pa la mkhas pa'i sems can rnams ni/ chos thams cad kyi rang bzhin nges par khong du chud par bya ba'i phyir sems mngon par gzhol bar gyur to/ /
Beings who were learned in the ways of the Dharma of the buddhas focused their minds on realizing the nature of all phenomena.
while those who knew the principles of the buddha-teaching set their minds to meditation on the intrinsic nature of all things;
chos mnyam pa nyid la zhugs pa'i sems can rnams ni/ dus gsum mnyam pa nyid la 'jug pa'i phyir sems mngon par gzhol bar gyur to/ /
Beings who had realized the equality of all phenomena focused their minds on realizing the equality of the three times.
those who had realized the equality of things set their minds on realizing the equality of past, present, and future;
dus gsum gyi ye shes snang ba thob pa'i sems can rnams ni/ sangs rgyas gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa rnam par dmigs par bya ba'i don du ye shes snang ba la zhugs par gyur to/ /
Beings who had attained the illumination of the knowledge of the three times entered the light of wisdom in order to perceive the succession of buddhas.
those who had attained the scope of knowledge of past, present, and future entered into the light of knowledge of the succession of all buddhas,
de bzhin gshegs pa sna tshogs rnam par dmigs par bya ba la zhugs pa'i sems can rnams ni/ 'gro ba thams cad yongs su bsdu ba'i don du sems mngon par gzhol bar gyur to/ /
The beings who had realized the perception of the various tathāgatas focused their minds on gathering all beings.
while those who had entered the knowledge of various manifestations of buddhas set their minds on the salvation of all sentient beings;
'gro ba thams cad yongs su bsdu ba la brtson pa'i sems can rnams ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i lam rnam par dag par bya ba'i phyir smon lam bskyed par gyur to/ /
The beings who were dedicated to gathering beings generated prayers to purify the bodhisattva path.
those engaged in the salvation of all beings vowed to complete the path of enlightening beings,
