lam gyi mnyam pa nyid la zhugs pa'i sems can rnams ni/ de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi chos kyi 'khor lo mngon par bsgrub pa'i phyir ye shes snang ba bskyed par gyur to/ /
Beings who had realized the equality of the path gave rise to the light of wisdom in order to attain the Dharma wheels of all the buddhas.
while those who had realized the equanimity of the path generated the light of knowledge to bring forth the cycles of teaching of all buddhas;
chos rgya mtsho rnam par dbye ba la mngon par mos pa'i sems can rnams ni/ zhing gi dra ba thams cad rang gi lus kyis rgyas par dgang ba'i don du sems mngon par gzhol bar gyur to/ /
The beings who had turned toward the aspects[1826] of the ocean of the Dharma focused their minds on pervading the entire net of realms with their own bodies.
those who were ready for the guidance of the ocean of teachings set their minds on pervading the network of all lands with their own bodies,
zhing mnyam pa nyid la zhugs pa'i sems can rnams ni/ sems can thams cad kyi dbang po rgya mtsho yongs su shes par bya ba'i phyir smon lam 'debs par gyur to; ;
The beings who had realized the equality of the realms prayed to know the ocean of the capabilities of beings.
while those who realized the equality of lands undertook to know the faculties of all sentient beings,

'gro ba thams cad kyi dbang po dang mos pa ji lta ba bzhin du rnam par dpyad pa la brtson pa'i sems can rnams ni/ thams cad mkhyen pa nyid khong du chud par bya ba'i phyir bsam pa rnam par dag par gyur to/ /
The beings who were dedicated to analyzing exactly the aspirations and capabilities of beings purified the motivation to realize omniscience.
and those engaged in consideration of the faculties of all sentient beings in accord with their inclinations purified the determination to reach omniscience.

sems can rnam pa de lta bu dag gi don rnam pa de lta bu de dag 'grub par 'gyur ba mthong nas rgyal po gzi brjid kyi bdag pos sangs rgyas kyi rnam par 'phrul pa dang / chos 'phrul bsam gyis mi khyab pa bstan pas sems can de dag yongs su smin par bya ba dang / gdul ba'i don du rgyal po'i gnas de dag thams cad du de bzhin gshegs pa sku nyi ma dam pa gshegs su gsol to/ /

“King Tejodhipati, seeing that beings gained that kind of accomplishment of those kinds of goals, requested the Tathāgata Sūryagātrapravara to come to all those royal cities in order to ripen and guide those beings through his inconceivable manifestations and miracles.

Entering into the fulfillment of such benefits for such people, the king Lord of Glory had the buddha Supreme Sun enter all the cities, to develop and guide those people by the inconceivable vision of the miracles of the Buddha.

rigs kyi bu/ de la ji snyam du sems/ de'i tshe de'i dus na rgyal po'i bu gzhi brjid kyi bdag po zhes bya bar gyur pa de gzhan zhig yin pa snyam du sems na ni/ khyod kyis de ltar mi blta ste/ bcom ldan 'das de bzhin gshegs pa shAkya thub pa 'di ni/ de'i tshe de'i dus na rgyal po'i bu gzi brjid kyi bdag po zhes bya ba 'khor los bsgyur ba'i rgyal srid la dbang ba/ de bzhin gshegs pa sku nyi ma dam pa la bsnyen bkur byed byed pa de yin no/ /

“What do you think, noble one? At that time, in that time, who was Prince Tejodhipati? Do not think that it was anyone else, for at that time, in that time, the Bhagavat, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni was the Prince Tejodhipati who became the sovereign of a cakravartin’s kingdom and honored the Tathāgata Sūryagātrapravara.

“Now, who do you think that prince Lord of Glory was? You should see him as none other than this buddha Shakyamuni, who at that time was a prince named Lord of Glory, who attained kingship, and was on good terms with the buddha Supreme Sun.

rigs kyi bu; de la ji snyam du sems/ de'i tshe de'i dus na rgyal po nor gyi bdag po gzhon nu gzi brjid kyi bdag po'i yab tu gyur pa de gzhan zhig yin pa snyam du sems na ni/ de ltar mi blta ste; de bzhin gshegs pa rin po che'i me tog gi 'od ces bya ba ni/ de'i tshe de'i dus na rgyal po nor gyi bdag po zhes bya bar gyur pa ste/ da ltar shar phyogs su 'jig rten gyi khams rgya mtsho'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi 'jig rten gyi khams rgya mtsho'i pha rol gyi 'jig rten gyi khams rgya mtsho chos kyi dbyings nam mkha'i gzugs brnyan gyi sprin ces bya ba na 'jig rten gyi khams kyi rgyud dbu ma dus gsum rab tu snang ba'i rin po che'i rgyal po yongs su 'byung ba'i dbyings zhes bya ba'i 'jig rten gyi khams sangs rgyas kyi 'od kyi dkyil 'khor dpal gyi sgron ma zhes bya ba na snying po byang chub thams cad la dbang ba'i lus rab tu snang ba zhes bya bar bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu mngon par sangs rgyas te; sangs rgyas kyi zhing brjod du med pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi byang chub sems dpa'i 'khor gyis bskor cing chos ston to/ /

“What do you think, noble one? At that time, in that time, who was King Dhanapati, the father of Prince Tejodhipati? Do not think that it was anyone else, for at that time, in that time, the Tathāgata Ratnakusumaprabha was King Dhanapati. He is now at a bodhimaṇḍa called Sarvavaśitakāyapratibhāsa[1827] in a world realm called Buddhaprabhāmaṇḍalaśrīpradīpā, which is in a central group of world realms called Tryadhvapratibhāsamaṇirājasaṃbhavā, in an ocean of world realms called Dharmadhātugaganapratibhāsamegha, which is to the east beyond an ocean of world realms as numerous as the atoms in an ocean of world realms. There he has attained the highest, complete enlightenment of buddhahood and is teaching the Dharma encircled by an assembly of bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in countless buddha realms.

And who do you think the king Lord of Wealth, father of Lord of Glory, was? You should see him as none other than the buddha Jewel Flower Light, who at that time was a king named Lord of Wealth, who attained supreme perfect enlightenment at an enlightenment site symbolized by reflection of the moon and expounded the Teaching surrounded by as many enlightening beings as atoms in untold buddha-lands in a world called Shining Lamp of the Aura of Buddha in a world system called Family Born of a Diamond Reflecting Past, Present, and Future in the center of an ocean of worlds called Multitude of Reflections in the Space of the Cosmos of Realities, which was to the east past as many oceans of worlds as atoms in a world.

bcom ldan 'das de bzhin gshegs pa rin po che'i 'od ces bya ba des sngon byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa mdzad pa'i tshe 'jig rten gyi khams rgya mtsho chos kyi dbyings nam mkha'i gzugs brnyan du snang ba'i sprin yongs su dag par mdzad de/ 'jig rten gyi khams rgya mtsho der de bzhin gshegs pa ji snyed cig byung bar gyur pa dang / 'byung ba dang / 'byung bar 'gyur ba de dag thams cad kyang bcom ldan 'das de bzhin gshegs pa rin po che'i me tog gi 'od des sngon byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa mdzad pa'i tshe bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu smin phar mdzad pa sha stag go /

“When the Bhagavat, the Tathāgata Ratnakusumaprabha,[1828] was previously practicing bodhisattva conduct, he purified the ocean of world realms called Dharmadhātugaganapratibhāsamegha. All the tathāgatas who have appeared, are appearing, and will appear in that ocean of world realms were all ripened for the highest, complete enlightenment by the Bhagavat, the Tathāgata Ratnakusumaprabha, during his past practice of bodhisattva conduct.

Furthermore, that ocean of worlds, Multitude of Reflections in the Space of the Cosmos of Realities was purified by that buddha Jewel Flower Light in the course of his past practice as an enlightening being, and all the past, present, and future buddhas in that ocean of worlds were ripened for supreme perfect enlightenment by that buddha Jewel Flower Light as he carried out the practice of enlightening beings.

rigs kyi bu/ de la ji snyam du sems/ de'i tshe de'i dus na rgyal po'i btsun mo pad+mo dpal gyi snying po 'byung ba zhes bya ba byung ste/ gzhon nu gzi brjid kyi bdag po'i yum du gyur pa/ bud med stong phrag brgyad cu rtsa bzhi'i gtso mor gyur pa de gzhan zhig yin pa snyam du sems na ni/ de ltar mi blta ste/ rigs kyi bu; bcom ldan 'das kyi yum lha mo sgyu ma byang chub sems dpa' skyed skyed pa/ rnam par thar pa kun tu snang zhing sgrib pa med pa la rab tu gnas pa/ sngon de bzhin gshegs pas yongs su bsgrubs pa mngon du gyur pa/ byang chub sems dpa'i skye ba thams cad yongs su bstan pa'i tshul la mkhas pa 'di ni/ de'i tshe de'i dus na rgyal po nor gyi bdag po'i btsun mo dam pa pad+mo dpal gyi snying po 'byung ba zhes bya bar gyur to/ /

“What do you think, noble one? At that time, in that time, who was the king’s queen Padmaśrīgarbhasaṃbhavā, the mother of Prince Tejodhipati, preeminent among the eighty-four thousand wives? Do not think that it was anyone else, noble one, for at that time, in that time, Māyādevī, the mother of the Bhagavat, who gave birth to the bodhisattva, who is established in the liberation of unobscured, complete illumination, who has directly perceived the accomplishments of tathāgatas in the past, who knows the visions of the births of all bodhisattvas, was King Dhanapati’s preeminent queen, Padmaśrīgarbhasaṃbhavā.

“Now then, who do you think was the queen Lotus Born in that time, mother of the prince Lord of Glory, foremost of the eighty-four thousand women? You should see her as none other than Lady Maya, mother of the Blessed Buddha, progenetrix of the enlightening being Vairocana, established in unobstructed liberation of universal light, direct witness to the appearance of the countless multitude of all buddhas, who knows the manner of manifestation of birth of all enlightening beings.

rigs kyi bu/ de la ji snyam du sems/ de'i tshe de'i dus na sbrul tshong ma'i gtso mo blta na sdug pa zhes bya ba byung ba de gzhan zhig yin pa snyam du sems na ni/ de ltar mi blta ste/ shAkya lag na 'khar ba'i chung ma kho mo'i ma mig mdzes zhes bya ba 'di ni/ de'i tshe de'i dus na sbrul tshong ma'i gtso mo blta na sdug pa zhes bya bar gyur to/ /

“What do you think, noble one? At that time, in that time, who was Sudarśanā, the preeminent courtesan? Do not think that it was anyone else, noble one, for at that time, in that time, my mother, Sunetrā, the wife of the Śākya Daṇḍapāṇi, was Sudarśanā, the preeminent courtesan.
And who do you think was the great courtesan Beautiful? You should see her as Sunetra, wife of Dandapani of the Shakya clan, who is my mother.

rigs kyi bu/ de la ji snyam du sems/ de'i tshe de'i dus na bu mo dga' ba'i 'od shin tu sbyangs pa zhes bya bar gyur pa de gzhan zhig yin pa snyam du sems na ni/ de ltar mi blta ste/ kho mo ni/ de'i tshe de'i dus na sbrul tshong ma'i bu mo dga' ba'i 'od kyi dpal shin tu sbyangs pa zhes bya bar gyur to/ /

“What do you think, noble one? At that time, in that time, who was the girl Sucalitaratiprabhāsaśrī? Do not think that it was anyone else, noble one, for at that time, in that time, I was Sucalitaratiprabhāsaśrī, the daughter of the courtesan.
And who was her daughter, Splendor of Delight in Virtuous Conduct? You should see her as me.

rigs kyi bu/ de la ji snyam du sems/ de'i tshe de'i dus na rgyal pa gzi brjid kyi bdag po'i 'khor du gyur pa de rnams gzhan zhig yin pa snyam du sems na ni/ rigs kyi bu/ de ni/ de ltar mi blta ste; bcom ldan 'das kyis byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po'i spyod pa dang / smon lam yongs su rdzogs par bya ba la dgod dgod pa'i byang chub sems dpa'i 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor 'di nyid na 'khod cing / 'jig rten gyi khams thams cad du gzugs brnyan rab tu byung ba'i lus dang / byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin thams cad la rnam par spyod pa las ma nyams pa'i sems dang / de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi zhal mngon du mthong bar rnam par dmigs pa'i mig dang / de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi gsung gi yan lag gi sprin nam mkha' dang mnyam pa'i 'khor lo rab tu bsgrags pa'i dbyangs rnam par dmigs pa'i rna ba dang / chos thams cad la rnam par spyad par dbang sgyur ba'i dbugs phyi nang du rgyu ba dang / sangs rgyas kyi zhing thams cad du rjes su grags pa'i ming gi sgra dang / de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor du nye bar 'gro ba rgyun mi gcod pa'i byang chub sems dpa'i lus dang / sems can thams cad la bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du mngon par ston pa'i lus yongs su smin par bya ba dang / gdul ba la rjes su mthun pa mngon par bsgrubs pa dang / byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po'i spyod pa dang / smon lam yongs su rdzogs par bya ba dang / yang dag par sgrub pa phyogs kyi dra ba ma lus pa thams cad du 'dal te/ ma 'ongs pa'i bskal pa thams cad du rgyun mi 'chad pa dang ldan pa sha stag bcom ldan 'das kyi 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor na 'khod pa 'di dag yin no/ /

“What do you think, noble one? At that time, in that time, who were the entourage of King Tejodhipati? Do not think that they were anyone else, noble one, for they are now those who are established in this very assembly of followers who are bodhisattvas established by the Bhagavat in the perfection of the completely good conduct and prayer of bodhisattvas; whose bodies appeared as images in all world realms; whose minds never lapse from the practice of all bodhisattva samādhis; whose eyes have the perception of directly seeing the faces of all tathāgatas; whose ears perceive the voices of the clouds of the aspects of the speech, as vast as space, of all the tathāgatas that resound with the wheel of the Dharma; whose inhalations and exhalations have power over the practice of all Dharmas; the sound of whose names resound throughout all the buddha realms;[1829] whose bodhisattva bodies go without interruption to the circles of the assemblies of all the tathāgatas; who create bodies that manifest to all beings, in accordance with their aspirations, in ways that are favorable for ripening and guidance; and who, spreading throughout the entirety of the net of the directions, accomplish and perfect the completely good conduct and prayer continuously throughout all future kalpas and are present in the circle of the assembly of the Bhagavat.

“Who do you think were the retinue of the king Lord of Wealth? They were these enlightening beings seated here in this assembly, guided by the Buddha to the fulfillment of the vows of universally good action, with a body reflected in all worlds, mind unadulterated and unfragmented in all concentration states of enlightening beings, eyes seeing the being and countenance of all buddhas, ears hearing the utterances of all buddhas, breath in control of all spiritual stations, voice going to all buddha-lands, the body of an enlightening being ceaselessly going to the audiences of all buddhas, entering the network of all places by production of embodiments suitable to develop and guide according to the mentalities of those to whom the enlightening beings appear, arriving at fulfillment of the vows of practice of universal good unbroken throughout the ages.

rigs kyi bu/ de bzhin gshegs pa sku nyi ma dam pa de ni/ 'khor los bsgyur ba gzi brjid kyi bdag po dang / kho mos nam bzhugs kyi bar du na bza' dang / bshos dang / gzims cha dang / snyun gyi rkyen sman dang / yo byad kyis bsnyen bkur to/ /

“Noble one, the cakravartin Tejodhipati and I served the Tathāgata Sūryagātrapravara for as long as he lived, with clothing, food, alms, bedding, medicine during times of illness, and necessary articles.
“The king Lord of Glory and I, furthermore, attended the buddha Supreme Sun as long as he lived, providing him with the necessities of life.

rigs kyi bu/ de bzhin gshegs pa sku nyi ma dam pa yongs su mya ngan las 'das pa'i 'og tu 'jig rten gyi khams de nyid du de bzhin gshegs pa sku shin tu dang ba zhes bya ba 'jig rten du byung ste; de yang kho mo cag gis bsnyen bkur to/ / rim gror byas so/ / bsti stang du byas so/ / phu dud du byas so/ / mchod do/ /

“Noble one, after the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata Sūryagātrapravara, in that world realm there appeared in the world the tathāgata named Prasannagātra. We also served him, showed him respect, honored him, venerated him, and made offerings to him.
After that buddha passed away entirely, a buddha named Pure Body emerged, in that same world, and we honored and served him.
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa sku thams cad la ye shes kyi gzugs brnyan gyi zla ba snang ba zhes bya ba 'jig rten du byung ste/ de yang kho mo cag gis lha'i dbang por gyur te bsnyen bkur to/ /
After that we served, in succession, buddhas named Moon Reflecting Knowledge in All Limbs,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa 'dzam bu chu klung gi gzi brjid kyi rgyal po zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Subsequently, we served the tathāgata named Jāmbūnadatejorāja who appeared in the world.
King of Golden Light,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa sku mtshan gyis rnam par brgyan pa zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Subsequently, we served the tathāgata named Lakṣaṇabhūṣitagātra who appeared in the world.
Adorned with Marks of Greatness,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa 'od zer sna tshogs 'bar ba'i zla ba zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Subsequently, we served the tathāgata named Vicitraraśmijvalanacandra who appeared in the world.
Moon Blazing with a Web of Brilliant Light Beams,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa shin tu rnam par gzigs pa'i ye shes dpal zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Subsequently, we served the tathāgata named Suvilokitajñānaketu who appeared in the world.
Paragon of Observant Knowledge,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa ye shes chen po'i 'od zer shin tu yangs pa'i rgyal po zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Subsequently, we served the tathāgata named Vipulamahājñānaraśmirāja who appeared in the world.
King Illumined with Great Knowledge,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa rdo rje mthu bo che'i brtson 'grus zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Subsequently, we served the tathāgata named Nārāyaṇavajravīrya who appeared in the world.
Adamantine Energy,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa ye shes gzhan gyis mi thub pa'i mthu zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Subsequently, we served the tathāgata named Aparājitajñānasthāma who appeared in the world.
Invincible Power of Knowledge,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa kun tu rnam par gzigs pa'i ye shes zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Subsequently, we served the tathāgata named Samantavilokitajñāna who appeared in the world.
All-Observing Knowledge,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa ye shes dri ma med pa phun sum tshogs pa'i sprin zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Subsequently, we served the tathāgata named Vimalaśrīmegha who appeared in the world.
Cloud of Pure Light,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa seng+ge rnam par bsgyings pa'i 'od ces bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Subsequently, we served the tathāgata named Siṃhavijṛmbhitaprabha who appeared in the world.
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa 'od zer 'bar ba'i gtsug phud ces bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Subsequently, we served the tathāgata named Jñānaraśmijvalanacūḍa who appeared in the world.
Crown Blazing with Lights of Knowledge,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa yon tan 'od zer rgyal mtshan zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Subsequently, we served the tathāgata named Guṇaraśmidhvaja who appeared in the world.
Banner of Lights of Virtue,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa ye shes nyi ma'i gzi brjid ces bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Subsequently, we served the tathāgata named Jñānabhāskaratejas who appeared in the world.
Energy of the Sun of Knowledge,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa sku rin po che'i pad+mo shin tu rgyas pa zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Subsequently, we served the tathāgata named Ratnapadmapraphullitagātra who appeared in the world.
Limbs Like Blooming Jewel Lotuses,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa bsod nams sgron ma'i rgyal mtshan zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Subsequently, we served the tathāgata named Puṇyapradīpadhvaja who appeared in the world.
Lamp of Felicity,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa ye shes 'od zer gyi sprin gyi 'od ces bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Subsequently, we served the tathāgata named Jñānaraśmimeghaprabha who appeared in the world.
Radiance of Multitudes of Rays of Knowledge,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa kun tu rnam par snang ba'i zla ba zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Subsequently, we served the tathāgata named Samantavairocanacandra who appeared in the world.
Moon Shining Everywhere,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa rgyan dang gdugs kyi dbyangs kyi rgyal po zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Subsequently, we served the tathāgata named Ābharaṇacchatranirghoṣarāja[1830] who appeared in the world.
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa ye shes snang bas rnam par gnon pa'i seng+ge zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Subsequently, we served the tathāgata named Samantajñānālokavikramasiṃha who appeared in the world.
Powerful Lion Illumined by Universal Knowledge,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa chos kyi dbyings kyi yul gyi blo gros zla ba zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Subsequently, we served the tathāgata named Dharmadhātuviṣayamaticandra who appeared in the world.
Moon of Cosmic Mind,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa sems can nam mkha'i sems snang ba'i gzugs zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to; ;
“Subsequently, we served the tathāgata named Sattvagaganacittapratibhāsabimba who appeared in the world.
Reflection in the Spacelike Mind of Beings,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa rab tu zhi ba'i spos kyi gtsug bzang po zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Subsequently, we served the tathāgata named Praśamagandhasunābha who appeared in the world.
Tranquil and Well Balanced,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa zhi ba'i dbyangs kun tu bsgrags pa zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Subsequently, we served the tathāgata named Samantānuravitaśāntanirghoṣa who appeared in the world.
Ubiquitous Sound of Silence,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa ye shes rab tu brtan pa'i 'od zer gyi dra ba'i gzugs kyi phung po zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Subsequently, we served the tathāgata named Sudṛḍhajñānaraśmijālabimbaskandha who appeared in the world.
Cluster of Images in a Network of Light Rays of Stable Knowledge,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa bdud rtsi'i ri bo'i gzi brjid ces bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Subsequently, we served the tathāgata named Amṛtaparvataprabhātejas who appeared in the world.
Radiance of the Mountain of Immortality,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa chos rgya mtsho'i 'brug sgra sgrog pa'i dbyangs zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Subsequently, we served the tathāgata named Dharmasāgaranigarjitaghoṣa who appeared in the world.
Thunder of the Ocean of Truths,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa sangs rgyas nam mkha' snang ba'i gtsug phud ces bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Subsequently, we served the tathāgata named Buddhagaganaprabhāsacūḍa who appeared in the world.
Crown of Light in the Sky of Buddhas,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa 'od zer zla ba mdzod spu'i sprin ces bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Subsequently, we served the tathāgata named Raśmicandrorṇamegha who appeared in the world.[1831]
Moon of Light Beams,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa ye shes kyi zhal shin tu rgyas pa zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur te/ /
“Subsequently, we served the tathāgata named Suparipūrṇajñānamukhaktra who appeared in the world.
Face of Complete Knowledge,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa ye shes shin tu rnam par dag pa'i me tog snang ba zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Subsequently, we served the tathāgata named Suviśuddhajñānakusumāvabhāsa who appeared in the world.
Luster of Flowers of Pure Knowledge,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa rin chen 'od 'phro'i ri bo dpal gyi gzi brjid kyi rgyal po zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Subsequently, we served the tathāgata named Ratnārciḥparvataśrītejorāja who appeared in the world.
Glorious Light of a Mountain of Jewel Flowers,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa yon tan rgya chen po gzi brjid kyi 'od ces bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Subsequently, we served the tathāgata named Vipulaguṇajyotiḥprabha who appeared in the world.
Light of Myriad Stars of Virtue,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa ting nge 'dzin gyi ri rab mngon par 'phags pa'i ye shes zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Subsequently, we served the tathāgata named Samādhimervabhyudgatajñāna who appeared in the world.
Knowledge Emerging from the Heights of Concentration,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa rin chen zla ba'i rgyal mtshan zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Subsequently, we served the tathāgata named Ratnacandradhvaja who appeared in the world.
Jewel Moon,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa sku 'od 'phro ba'i dkyil 'khor zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Subsequently, we served the tathāgata named Arcirmaṇḍalagātra who appeared in the world.
Circle of Flames,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa rin chen mchog gi 'od kyi gzi brjid ces bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Subsequently, we served the tathāgata named Ratnāgraprabhatejas who appeared in the world.
Sublime Jewel Radiance,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa ye shes kyi spyod pa kun tu thogs pa med pa zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Subsequently, we served the tathāgata named Samantajñānacaryāvilamba who appeared in the world.
Unhesitating in Practice of Universal Knowledge,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa 'od 'phro rgya mtsho'i sgo'i sgron ma zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Subsequently, we served the tathāgata named Arciḥsamudramukhavegapradīpa who appeared in the world.
Blazing Lamp Topped with a Sea of Flames,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa rin chen zla ba'i rgyal mtshan zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa chos kyi gzhal med khang gi dbyangs kyi rgyal po zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Subsequently, we served the tathāgata named Dharmavimānanirghoṣarāja[1832] who appeared in the world.
King Proclaiming the Mansion of Truth,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa yon tan mi mtshungs grags pa'i rgyal mtshan zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Subsequently, we served the tathāgata named Asadṛśaguṇakīrtidhvaja who appeared in the world.
Famed for Peerless Virtue,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa phyag rab tu brkyang ba zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Subsequently, we served the tathāgata named Pralambabāhu who appeared in the world.
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa sngon gyi smon lam gyis 'phrul pa'i zla ba zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Subsequently, we served the tathāgata named Pūrvapraṇidhinirmāṇacandra who appeared in the world.
Moon Reflecting Past Vows,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa nam mkha'i ye shes don gyi sgron ma zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Subsequently, we served the tathāgata named Ākāśajñānārthapradīpa who appeared in the world.
Lamp of Meaning with Spacelike Knowledge,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa chos kyis 'phags pa'i nam mkha'i dbang phyug ces bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Subsequently, we served the tathāgata named Dharmodgatanabheśvara who appeared in the world.
Lord of the Sky, Born of Truth,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa rnam par snang mdzad dpal gyi snying po rgyal po zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Subsequently, we served the tathāgata named Vairocanaśrīgarbharāja who appeared in the world.
King Filled with Shining Light,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa chos mthu bo che'i dpal zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Subsequently, we served the tathāgata named Dharmanārāyaṇaketu who appeared in the world.
Paragon of Spirituality,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa ye shes dpal zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Subsequently, we served the tathāgata named Jñānaketu who appeared in the world.
Chief in Knowledge,
de'i 'og tu de bzhin gshegs pa chos rgya mtsho'i pad+mo zhes bya ba bsnyen bkur to/ /
“Subsequently, we served the tathāgata named Dharmasāgarapadma who appeared in the world.
Lotus in the Ocean of Truth.

rigs kyi bu/ de ltar de bzhin gshegs pa de dag la sogs pa 'jig rten gyi khams der sangs rgyas bye ba khrag khrig brgya stong phrag drug cu byung ste/ de dag thams cad kho mo cag gis na bza' dang / bshos dang / gzims cha dang / snyun gyi rkyen sman dang / yo byad kyis bsnyen bkur to/ / rim gror byas so/ / bsti stang du byas so/ / phu dud du byas so/ / mchod do/ /

“Noble one, those and other tathāgatas numbering altogether sixty sextillion appeared in that world realm. I served them all with clothing, food, alms, bedding, medicine during times of illness, and necessary articles, showed them respect, honored them, venerated them, and made offerings to them.
Beginning with these, there were sixty decillion buddhas in that world whom we honored, served, and provided with food and clothing, medicine and furniture.

rigs kyi bu/ sangs rgyas bye ba khrag khrig brgya stong phrag drug cu po de dag thams cad kyi tha mar de bzhin gshegs pa dgra bcom pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas chos rgya chen po la mos pa yang dag par 'byung ba'i gzi brjid ces bya ba byung ste/ bcom ldan 'das de grong khyer du gshegs pa la kho mo rgyal po'i chung mar gyur te khyim thab dang bcas pas de bzhin gshegs pa'i mchod pa'i sgo rnam pa thams cad du bshams pas mchod pa byas nas bcom ldan 'das de las chos kyi rnam grangs de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad skye ba 'byung ba'i sgron ma zhes bya ba thos so/ / de thos nas kho mos ye shes kyi mig rab tu thob ste byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin gyi tshul rgya mtsho thams cad la rnam par lta ba'i yul 'di yang rab tu thob par gyur to/ /

“Noble one, the last of those sixty hundred thousand trillion buddhas was the Tathāgata Arhat Samyaksaṃbuddha Vipuladharmādhimuktisaṃbhavatejas. When that tathāgata came to the city, I was the king’s wife. Together with householders, we practiced the gateways of every kind of offering, and after making offerings with the offerings for a tathāgata, we heard from that bhagavat the Dharma teaching called The Lamp of the Arising of the Births of All the Tathāgatas. On hearing that, I attained the eyes of wisdom, and I attained this bodhisattva liberation called the range of the view of all the ways of the ocean of the samādhis of the bodhisattvas.

“The last of those sixty decillion buddhas was one named Energy Born of Great Zeal for Truth. When that buddha came to town, I, as wife of the king, together with my husband, made all kinds of offerings and then heard an exposition of the Teaching from the buddha called ‘lamp produced by the emergence of all those who arrive at Thusness,’ on hearing which I attained the eye of knowledge, and attained this enlightening liberation whose sphere is observation of the oceans of concentrations of all enlightening beings.

rigs kyi bu/ de ltar kho mo rnam par thar pa 'di la sgom zhing / byang chub sems dpa' dang lhan cig tu byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa spyod cing bskal pa sangs rgyas kyi zhing brgya phrag stong gi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed cig tu rgyu rgyu ste/ sangs rgyas kyi zhing de snyed kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi bskal pa de dag la de bzhin gshegs pa mtha' dang dbus med pa zhig bsnyen bkur nas bskal pa la la la ni/ de bzhin gshegs pa bskal par bzhugs pa gcig kyang bsnyen bkur to/ / bskal pa la la ni/ de bzhin gshegs pa gnyis kyang bsnyen bkur to/ / bskal pa la la la ni/ de bzhin gshegs pa brjod du med pa'i bar dag kyang bsnyen bkur to/ / bskal pa la la la ni/ de bzhin gshegs pa sangs rgyas kyi zhing gi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyang bsnyen bkur to/ /

“Noble one, meditating on this liberation, I practiced bodhisattva conduct together with the bodhisattva for kalpas as numerous as the atoms in a hundred thousand buddha realms. During those kalpas as numerous as the atoms in that number of buddha realms, I served a vast extent of tathāgatas without end or middle. In some kalpas, I served a single tathāgata who remained for an entire kalpa. In some kalpas, I served two tathāgatas. In some kalpas, I served countless[1833] tathāgatas. In some kalpas, I served as many tathāgatas as there are atoms in a buddha realm.

“Cultivating this liberation for as many eons as atoms in one hundred buddha-lands, carrying out enlightening practice with the enlightening being Vairocana, I associated with countless buddhas during those many eons. In an eon I might serve one buddha or two, up to an inexpressible number of buddhas; some eons I served as many buddhas as atoms in a buddha-land.

de srid du kho mos byang chub sems dpa'i sku yang tshad ni/ ji tsam zhig /dbyibs ni/ ji lta bu zhig /sku mdog ni/ ji 'dra ba zhig yin pa khong du ma chud do/ / sku'i 'phrin las kyang khong du mchud do/ / gsung gi 'phrin las dang / thugs kyi 'phrin las kyang khong du mchud do/ ye shes kyi gzigs pa dang / ye shes kyi spyod yul dang / ye shes kyi ting nge 'dzin gyi yul yang khong du mchud do/ /

“During that time, my bodhisattva bodies’ sizes, shapes, and colors were beyond comprehension. The activities of my bodies were beyond comprehension. The activities of my speech and of my mind were beyond comprehension. My wisdom’s sight, my wisdom’s range of activity, and the scope of my wisdom’s samādhi were also beyond comprehension.

Yet never did I know the size of the enlightening being’s body or what it looked like; nor did I know the enlightening being’s physical, verbal, or mental actions, nor his knowledge and vision, his range of knowledge, or his realm of concentration of knowledge.

rigs kyi bu/ byang chub sems dpa' ji snyed cig gis byang chub sems dpa' byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa mdzad pa mthong nas byang chub sems dpa' la dga' ba'i sems bskyed de brda sna tshogs dang / bsnyen pa sna tshogs kyis mos pa bskyed par gyur pa de dag thams cad kyang byang chub sems dpa'i 'jig rten dang / 'jig rten las 'das pa'i thabs sna tshogs kyis yongs su bzung ste/ byang chub sems dpa'i 'khor du gyur to/ / de dag kyang byang chub sems dpa' byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa mdzad pa'i tshe 'khor du 'grogs 'grogs pas bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub las phyir mi ldog par gyur to/ /

“Noble one, when beings[1834] see a bodhisattva and the practice of bodhisattva conduct, they admire the bodhisattva and with various gestures and approaches are attracted to the bodhisattva who cares for them through various worldly and nonworldly ways, so that they became the bodhisattva’s followers. When they accompany as followers the bodhisattva who practices bodhisattva conduct, they become irreversible in their progress to the highest, complete enlightenment.

As for those who, seeing the enlightening being carrying out the practice of enlightening beings, developed pure faith through various associations, all of them were taken care of by the enlightening being by various worldly and transmundane means, and became associates of the enlightening being. Associating with the enlightening being as he carried on enlightening practice, they never regressed on the way to supreme perfect enlightenment.

rigs kyi bu/ de ltar kho mos de bzhin gshegs pa chos rgya chen po la mos pa yang dag par 'byung ba'i gzi brjid kyi zhal mthong ma thag tu byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin gyi tshul rgya mtsho la rnam par lta ba'i yul 'di thob nas rnam par thar pa 'di sgom zhing / byang chub sems dpa' dang / bskal pa sangs rgyas kyi zhing brgya phrag stong gi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed cig tu 'grogs 'grogs te/ bskal pa sangs rgyas kyi zhing brgya'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed po de dag la de bzhin gshegs pa ji snyed cig byung bar gyur pa de dag thams cad kyang kho mos bsnyen bkur to/ / mchod do/ / rim gror byas so/ / de bzhin gshegs pa de dag thams cad las kyang kho mos chos bstan pa thob ste yongs su blangs so/ / yang dag par bzung ngo/ / sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das de dag thams cad las kyang kho mos rnam par thar pa 'di tshul sna tshogs dang / mdo sde'i tshul gyi gsung sna tshogs dang / rnam par thar pa'i rang bzhin sna tshogs dang / rnam par thar pa'i sgo sna tshogs dang / rnam par thar pa'i rgyud sna tshogs dang / dus la 'jug pa sna tshogs dang / zhing rgya mtsho la 'jug pa sna tshogs dang / sangs rgyas blta ba rgya mtsho rnam par dmigs par bya ba sna tshogs dang / de bzhin gshegs pa'i 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor du 'jug pa sna tshogs dang / byang chub sems dpa'i smon lam rgya mtsho'i tshul gyi lam sna tshogs dang / byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa mngon par sgrub pa sna tshogs dang / byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa 'byams klas pa sna tshogs kyis thob par gyur kyang byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa kun tu bzang po'i tshul ni/ khong du mchud do/ /

“Noble one, in that way, as soon as I saw the Tathāgata Vipuladharmādhimuktisaṃbhavatejas, I attained this bodhisattva liberation called the range of the view of all the ways of the ocean of the samādhis of the bodhisattvas. Meditating on this liberation, I accompanied the bodhisattva for kalpas as numerous as the atoms in a hundred[1835] buddha realms. I served, made offerings to, and venerated all the tathāgatas that appeared during those kalpas as numerous as the atoms in buddha realms. I heard the teaching of the Dharma from all those tathāgatas, obtaining it and keeping it. I also obtained from all those buddha bhagavats this liberation through various ways, through various teachings of the ways of the sūtras, through various natures of liberation, through various entrances to liberation, through various practices of liberation, through various engagements in times, through various entries into realms, through various perceptions of oceans of visions of buddhas, through various entries into the circles of followers of tathāgatas, through various paths of the ways of oceans of bodhisattva prayers, through various accomplishments of bodhisattva conduct, and through various vast extents of bodhisattva liberations. However, I still had not realized the way of completely good bodhisattva conduct.

“Having attained the enlightening liberation whose sphere is observation of the oceans of concentrations of all enlightening beings when I saw the buddha Energy Born of Zeal for Truth, as I cultivated this liberation along with the enlightening being for as many eons as atoms in a hundred buddha-lands, I propitiated, served, and attended all the buddhas who emerged in those ages and heard, took up, and remembered their teachings; and I attained this liberation from all those buddhas, by various methods, by various enunciations of principles and systems of scriptures, by various bodies of liberation, by various doors of liberation, by various liberative meditations and procedures, by various ways of access, by entry into various oceans of buddha-lands, by various visions of oceans of buddhas, by entry into various buddhas’ assemblies, by various paths following the oceans of vows of enlightening beings, by carrying out various paths following the oceans of vows of enlightening beings, by carrying out various practices of enlightening beings, by accomplishing various practices of enlightening beings, by various manifestations of the scope of the endeavor of enlightening beings: yet I still did not enter the enlightening being’s universally good liberation.

de ci'i phyir zhe na/ byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po rnams kyi rnam par thar pa'i tshul ni/ nam mkha'i dbyings kyis klas par tshad med do/ / sems can gyi ming du bya ba thams cad kyi dbyings ltar tshad med do/ / dus gsum gyi rgyud rgya mtsho'i dbyings ltar tshad med do/ / phyogs rgya mtsho'i dbyings ltar tshad med do/ / chos kyi dbyings kyi tshul rgya mtsho'i dbyings ltar tshad med do/ /

“Why is that? Because the way of the liberation of completely good bodhisattvas is as immeasurable as the extent of space, as immeasurable as the extent of the conceptualizations[1836] of beings, as immeasurable as the extent of the ocean of the divisions of the three times, as immeasurable as the extent of the ocean of the directions, and as immeasurable as the extent of the ocean of the ways of the realm of phenomena.

Why? Because the ways of liberation of the universally good enlightening beings are infinite as space, infinite as the thoughts of all sentient beings, infinite as the ocean of time periods of past, present, and future, infinite as the ocean of places, infinite as the ocean of structures of the cosmos;
rigs kyi bu/ byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po rnams kyi rnam par thar pa'i tshul gyi lus ni/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i yul dang mnyam pa'o; ;
“Noble one, the nature of the way of the liberations of the completely good bodhisattvas is the same as the scope of perception of the tathāgatas.
indeed, the ways of liberation of the universally good enlightening beings are equal to the sphere of buddhahood.
de ltar rigs kyi bu/ kho mos bskal pa sangs rgyas kyi zhing gi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed cig tu byang chub sems dpa'i sku la lta lta yang blta bas ma ngoms te/
“In that way, noble one, for kalpas as numerous as the atoms in buddha realms I gazed again and again upon the bodhisattva’s body without ever having enough of seeing it.
“For as many eons as atoms in a buddha-land I gazed at the enlightening being, never tired of seeing him.

rigs kyi bu/ 'di lta ste; dper na/ gcig tu 'dod chags la spyod pa'i skyes pa dang bud med phan tshun nas 'phrad par dus byas pa gnyis la ni/ sems kyi rgyud tshul bzhin ma yin pa yid la byed pa las byung ba gtsang ba'i 'du shes pa dang / rnam par rtog pas mos pa las byung ba tshad med pa zhig skye'o/ /

“Noble one, it was like when a man and woman have arranged to come together purely for the enjoyment of passion, and there arises an immeasurable development of their state of mind through their being intoxicated by the concepts and thoughts of purity that arise from fallacious mental activity.
Just as countless illogical thoughts and illusions rise in the minds of a woman and man full of passion when they get together,

rigs kyi bu/ de bzhin du kho mo byang chub sems dpa'i sku la lta na/ ba spu'i sgo re re nas kyang 'jig rten gyi khams kyi rgyud 'byams klas pa mtha' dang dbus med pa/ tshad med par shin tu bstan pa/ gzhi sna tshogs dang ldan pa/ mtshams kyi rgyan sna tshogs dang ldan pa; dbyibs sna tshogs dang ldan pa/ ri'i rgyan sna tshogs kyis brgyan pa/ sa'i gzhi'i rgyan sna tshogs bstan du yod pa/ sprin sna tshogs dang ldan pa'i nam mkha' kun nas khyab pa'i rgyan dang ldan pa/ tshul dang / ming dang / grangs sna tshogs su brjod pa/ sangs rgyas 'byung ba dang / de bzhin gshegs pa'i rgyud sna tshogs 'byung ba/ snying po byang chub kyi rgyan sna tshogs kyis brgyan pa/ de bzhin gshegs pa chos kyi 'khor lo bskor ba'i rnam par 'phrul pa sna tshogs dang ldan pa/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor gyi rgyan sna tshogs dang ldan pa/ mdo sde'i tshul sna tshogs shin tu bstan pa'i sgra 'byung ba/ theg pa'i tshul sna tshogs mngon par sgrub pa 'byung ba dang ldan pa / yongs su dag pa'i 'od dang / snang ba sna tshogs kyis rab tu snang pa/ mtshan ma sngon chad ma mthong ba dag sems kyi skad cig re re zhing mig lam du snang ngo/ /

“Noble one, in the same way, when I looked upon the bodhisattva’s body, in each instant of mind, from each pore there appeared to my eyes an immeasurable vast extent of groups of world realms without end or middle, with various grounds, various arrays of borders, various shapes, various arrays of mountains, various displays of arrays of grounds, various skies adorned by coverings of clouds, various natures, names, and numbers, and various appearances of buddhas and successions of tathāgatas, adorned by various bodhimaṇḍas, with various miraculous manifestations of the turning of the Dharma wheel by tathāgatas, with various arrays of the circles of followers of tathāgatas, with the various sounds of the teaching of the various ways of the sūtras, with the various accomplishments of the ways of the yānas, with the various illuminations from pure lights and radiances, and with omens that have never been seen before.

as I watched the body of the enlightening being, in every moment of consciousness I perceived infinitely various indications from each of his pores—the range of world systems, their various foundations, various conjoining arrangements, various configurations, various mountain ranges, various arrays of the ground, various arrays of clouds in the sky, various names and numbers of eons, emergence of various buddhas and formation of lineages of buddhas, various adornments of enlightenment sites, various occult powers involved in the buddhas’ teaching procedures, various arrays of buddhas’ audiences, various enunciations of scriptures, productions of various vehicles of emancipation, and various manifestations of pure light, the like of which I had never seen before.

ba spu'i sgo re re nas kyang sangs rgyas rgya mtsho mtha' dang dbus med pa'i snying po byang chub kyi rgyan sna tshogs mnga' ba/ chos kyi 'khor lo bskor ba'i rnam par 'phrul pa sna tshogs dang ldan pa/ mdo sde'i tshul sna tshogs sgrog pa'i rnam par 'phrul pa dang ldan pa dag kyang rgyun mi 'chad pa'i tshul du sems kyi skad cig re re la mig lam du snang ngo/ /

“From each pore there appeared to my eyes oceans of buddhas without end or middle. In each instant of mind, from each pore, there appeared continuously to my eyes the adornment of various bodhimaṇḍas, the miraculous manifestations of the various turnings of the Dharma wheel, and the miraculous manifestations of the sounds of the various ways of the sūtras.

By ceaseless effort, from each of his pores I saw in each moment of consciousness infinite oceans of buddhas, various adornments of enlightenment sites, various mystic operations of the Teaching, and various miraculous proclamations of scriptures.

ba spu'i sgo re re nas kyang sems can rgya mtsho mtha' dang dbus med pa khyim dang / kun dga'i ra ba dang / ri dang / gzhal med khang dang / chu klung dang / rgya mtsho la gnas pa gzugs dang / lus sna tshogs can/ longs spyod kyi yul sna tshogs dang ldan pa/ spyod pa dang / spyod yul dang / sbyor ba sna tshogs dang ldan pa/ dbang po sna tshogs su grub pa'i tshul dang ldan pa dag kyang sems kyi skad cig re re la mig lam du snang ngo/ /

“In each instant of mind, from each pore, there appeared to my eyes a vast ocean of beings without end or middle, with houses, parks, divine palaces, rivers, oceans, and dwellings, with various forms and bodies, with various ranges of enjoyments, with various engagements in conduct and behavior, and with various forms of perfections of faculties.

From each of his pores I saw, in each moment of consciousness, infinite oceans of beings, various houses, gardens, mountains, palaces, rivers, seas, and dwellings, various physical bodies, various goods, various actions and efforts, and various forms of development of faculties.
ba spu'i sgo re re nas kyang dus gsum rgya mtsho la 'jug pa'i tshul mtha' dang dbus med pa zhig mig lam du snang ngo/ /
“From each pore there appeared to my eyes ways of entering an ocean of the three times, without end or middle.
From every one of his pores infinitely various ways of entering past, present, and future became perceptible;
byang chub sems dpa'i smon lam rgya mtsho mtha' dang dbus med pa zhig ni/ rnam par dag par 'gyur ro/ /
“An ocean, without end or middle, of bodhisattva prayers were purified.
infinitely various oceans of vows of enlightening beings were purified,
byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa rnam pa tha dad pa rgya mtsho mtha' dang dbus med pa dag kyang yongs su snang ngo/ /
“There appeared an ocean, without end or middle, of different forms of conduct of the bodhisattva bhūmis.
infinite oceans of differences of the practices of the stages of enlightening beings became perceptible,
byang chub sems dpa'i pha rol tu phyin pa'i tshul rgya mtsho yongs su dag pa mtha' dang dbus med pa dag kyang yongs su snang ngo/ /
“There appeared a pure ocean, without end or middle, of the perfections of the bodhisattvas.
the infinitely various purities of the transcendent ways of enlightening beings became perceptible,
byang chub sems dpa'i sngon gyi sbyor ba rgya mtsho mtha' dang dbus med pa dag kyang yongs su snang ngo/ /
“There appeared an ocean, without end or middle, of the past practices of the bodhisattvas.
infinitely various oceans of past efforts of enlightening beings became perceptible,
sangs rgyas kyi zhing yongs su dag par bya ba'i tshul rgya mtsho mtha' dang dbus med pa dag kyang yongs su snang ngo/ /
“There appeared an ocean, without end or middle, of the ways of purifying buddha realms.
infinitely various oceans of ways of purifying buddha-lands became perceptible;
byang chub sems dpa'i byams pa chen po'i tshul rgya mtsho mtha' dang dbus med pa dag kyang yongs su snang ngo/ /
“There appeared an ocean, without end or middle, of the ways of the great love of bodhisattvas.[1837]
infinitely various oceans of the universal love of enlightening beings,
sems can thams cad yongs su smin par bya ba dang / gdul ba'i mthu dang / thabs rgya mtsho dag la'ang 'jug cing khong du chud do/ /
“I comprehended their entering oceans of the power and methods for ripening and guiding all beings.
oceans of universal love for all beings, and oceans of heroic efforts to develop and guide all beings descended into the world,
byang chub sems dpa'i snying rje chen po'i sprin gyi tshul rgya mtsho mtha' dang dbus med pa dag kyang yongs su 'grub bo/ /
“They accomplished an ocean, without end or middle, of the ways of the clouds of the great compassion of bodhisattvas.
infinite oceans of the universal compassion of enlightening beings arose,
byang chub sems dpa'i dga' ba'i shugs chen po rgya mtsho mtha' dang dbus med pa dag kyang rnam par 'phel te/
“They increased an ocean, without end or middle, of the great power of the joy of bodhisattvas.
infinite oceans of the great joy of enlightening beings grew,
sems kyi skad cig re re la yang sems can thams cad yongs su bsdu ba'i tshul rgya mtsho mtha' dang dbus med pa dag kyang rab tu 'grub bo/ /
“In each instant of mind, they accomplished an ocean, without end or middle, of the methods of gathering all beings.
and in every moment of consciousness infinitely various oceans of efforts to take care of all sentient beings were accomplished.

rigs kyi bu/ de ltar kho mo bskal pa sangs rgyas kyi zhing brgya'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed dag tu byang chub sems dpa'i ba spu'i sgo re re zhing sems kyi skad cig re re la chos kyi tshul rgya mtsho mtha' dang dbus med pa la zhugs te/ khong du chud par byas kyang mthar thug par ma gyur te sngon khong du chud pa la bzlas te khong du chud par byas pa'ang med do/ / sngon thob pa las bzlas te thob par byas pa'ang med do/ /

“Noble one, in that way, for kalpas as numerous as the atoms in a hundred buddha realms, in each instant of mind I perceived and comprehended an ocean, without end or middle, of the ways of the Dharma in each pore of the bodhisattva. Nevertheless, I did not comprehend them in their entirety, even though I never perceived again what I had perceived before, even though I did not hear again what I had already heard before.

“In each moment of consciousness through those eons numerous as atoms in a hundred buddha-lands, I perceived oceans of principles of the Teaching from each pore of the enlightening being, and never reached the end, even though I did not go into what I had already gone into, and did not attain what I had already attained.

rigs kyi bu/ de ltar don thams cad grub pa btsun mo'i 'khor gyi nang na bzhugs shing / bud med kyi tshogs kyis yongs su bskor bar bzhugs pa'i tshe'ang kho mo ni/ ba spu'i sgo re re nas kyang dus gsum gyi tshul rgya mtsho mtha' dang dbus med pa la chos kyi dbyings la 'jug pa'i tshul rgya mtsho khong du chud par bya bas yongs su 'jug go /

“Noble one, in that way, when I was in the harem of Sarvārthasiddha, who had an entourage of a crowd of queens, through an ocean of the ways of comprehending the realm of phenomena I perceived in each of his pores an ocean, without end or middle, of the ways of the three times.

This I did by going into the ocean of various ways of liberation of the enlightening being, even when he was the prince Siddhartha in the royal palace surrounded by women; I perceived infinitely various oceans of principles of past, present, and future through each of his pores, by penetrating the oceans of ways into the realm of reality.

rigs kyi bu/ kho mos byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin gyi tshul rgya mtsho thams cad la rnam par lta ba'i yul 'di shes te mnyam par gzhog par zad na/ kho mos byang chub sems dpa' thabs kyi tshul rgya mtsho mtha' dang dbus med pa la zhugs pa/ sems can thams cad dang mnyam zhing 'dra ba'i dbyibs su gnas pa'i lus rnam par dmigs pa yongs su ston pa/ 'gro ba thams cad kyi bsam pa dang mthun par spyod pa yongs su ston pa/ ba spu'i sgo thams cad nas kha dog mtha' yas pa'i sprul pa'i sprin rab tu 'gyed pa/ lus med pa'i chos nyid kyi ngo bo nyid kyi rang bzhin shin tu rnam par dag pa/ nam mkha'i mtshan nyid du 'gro ba'i rang bzhin khong du chud pas rnam par rtog pa med pa/ thams cad du rjes su song ba'i blo rnam par gdon mi za bas de bzhin gshegs pa dang mnyam par rnam par 'phrul pa la brtson pa/ rnam par thar pa'i yul mtha' dang dbus med pas rnam par 'phrul pa la zhugs pa/ chos kyi dbyings shin tu rgya chen por sems bskyed pas 'jug pa la rnam par spyod cing dbang sgyur ba/ chos kyi gnas sgo thams cad dang ldan pa'i rnam par thar pa rgya mtsho la rnam par rtse ba de dag gi spyod pa shes pa'am/ yon tan gyi gter ma lus par bstan par nus re skan/

“Noble one, I know and practice only this bodhisattva liberation called the miraculous manifestations at the birth of bodhisattvas throughout all the perceptions of countless kalpas. How could I know the conduct, or teach the treasure of qualities, without exception, of the bodhisattvas who engage in an ocean, without end or middle, of the ways of methods; who manifest the perception of bodies in shapes[1838] that accord with those of all beings; who manifest conducts that accord with the aspirations of all beings; who emit clouds of emanations with infinite colors from all their pores; who have the realization, free of thought, of the pure nature of the bodyless essence of the true nature, a nature that has the characteristics of space; who with the certainty of realization at all times are dedicated to miraculous manifestations equal to those of the tathāgatas; who engage in miraculous manifestation through the scope of the liberations, which has no end or middle; who through the generation of motivation have power over entering and remaining in the vast realm of the Dharma; and who revel in an ocean of liberations that possess all the gateways into the levels of the Dharma?

“I only know and have attained this enlightening liberation whose sphere is observation of the oceans of concentrations of all enlightening beings. How can I know the practice, tell of the qualities, or show all the oceans of virtue of the enlightening beings who have gone into the infinitely various oceans of liberative means, who purposely appear physically like all beings, who appear to act in accord with the mentalities of all beings, who emanate infinitely various appearances from all their pores, who realize the purity of essence and nature of all bodies, who are free from discriminatory thought because of awareness of the spacelike quality of the nature of beings, whose intellect reaches everywhere with certain discernment, occupied with spiritual powers equal to those who arrive at Thusness, who produce miraculous displays of infinite spheres of liberation, who have mastered the state where they can enter the vast cosmos of realities in a thought, who roam freely in the ocean of liberation of the all-sided stage of all truths?

song rigs kyi bu/ bcom ldan 'das rnam par snang mdzad kyi zhabs kyi drung 'di nyid na khri rin po che sna tshogs kyi rgyan dang ldan pa/ nor bu rin po che'i rgyal po pad+mo'i snying po can la byang chub sems dpa'i yum lha mo sgyu ma zhes bya ba 'dug gi /de'i gan du song la/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpa'i spyad pa spyod pa'i byang chub sems dpa' rnams 'jig rten gyi chos kyi dri ma thams cad kyis mi gos pa yin pa dang / de bzhin gshegs pa mchod pa'i nan tan la rgyun mi 'chad pa yin pa dang / byang chub sems dpa'i las kyi mtha' thams cad las phyir mi ldog pa yin pa dang / byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa la 'jug pa la sgrib pa thams cad dang bral bar 'gyur ba yin pa dang / byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par spyod pa thams cad la gzhan gyi dring mi 'jog pa yin pa dang / de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad dang mngon du gyur par gnas pa yin pa dang / sems can thams cad yongs su bsdu ba'i nan tan las phyir mi ldog pa yin pa dang / phyi ma'i mtha'i mur thug pa'i bskal par byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa thams cad la gnas par bya ba las phyir mi ldog pa yin pa dang / theg pa chen po'i smon lam las phyir mi ldog pa yin pa dang / 'gro ba thams cad kyi dge ba'i rtsa ba yongs su gzung ba dang / rnam par spel ba la sgyid lug par mi 'gyur pa yin pa dris shig /

“Depart, noble one. Here at the feet of the Bhagavat Vairocana, upon a precious throne with various adornments that has in its center a lotus made of the kings of precious jewels, is the mother of the bodhisattva, whose name is Māyādevī. Go to her and ask her, ‘How are bodhisattvas who practice bodhisattva conduct undefiled by any of the stains of this world? How do bodhisattvas have an uninterrupted dedication to making offerings to the tathāgatas? How are bodhisattvas irreversible from attaining the final accomplishment of their activities? How are they free from obscurations in their entry into bodhisattva liberations? How are they without expectation of a reward from others in all their bodhisattva conduct? How do they have the direct perception of all the tathāgatas? How do they never lapse from their dedication to gathering all beings? How do they never lapse from remaining in all bodhisattva conduct until the last future kalpa? How do they never turn back from the prayers of the Mahāyāna? How do they never lose heart in maintaining and increasing the roots of merit of all beings?’ ”

“Go to Lady Maya, mother of the enlightening being, who is sitting on a great jewel lotus seat near the Blessed Vairocana. Go ask her how enlightening beings become undefiled by the taint of worldly things while they are carrying out the practice of enlightening beings, how they become unflagging in serving all buddhas, how they become undeviating from the ends of the actions of enlightening beings, how they become free from all hindrances to entry into the liberations of enlightening beings, how they become unfixed to all states of enlightening beings, how they come into the presence of all buddhas and do not stop their efforts to take care of all sentient beings, do not cease enlightening practice for all time, do not regress from the undertaking of the Great Vehicle of universal enlightenment, and do not become discouraged in maintaining and increasing the roots of goodness in the world.”
de nas shAkya'i bu mo go pas rnam par thar pa'i sgo'i tshul 'di nyid yongs su bstan pa'i phyir sangs rgyas kyi byin gyi rlabs kyis de'i tshe tshigs su bcad pa 'di dag smras so/ /
Then at that time, Gopā, the Śākya maiden, in order to teach completely this gateway to liberation, through the blessing of the Buddha recited these verses:
Then, by the empowerment of Buddha, Gopa spoke these verses illustrating this way of liberation:
yang dag byang chub spyod la brtson pa yi/ / sems can dam pa sems can sus mthong ba/ / mos pa'i sems can khong khro ldan yang rung / / de yi bsdu bas kun kyang yongs su 'du; ;
“The beings who see the supreme beings Who are dedicated to perfect bodhisattva conduct, Whether they are attracted or in enmity, All become gathered by him. {90}
Those who see the best of people Engaged in the practice of perfect enlightenment All go to join him, Be they friendly or inimical.
zhing brgya'i rdul phran rab tu phra snyed kyi/ / bskal pa mang po kho mos 'di nas dran/ / de yi pha rol bskal pa rnam brgyan la/ / 'jig rten khams rab ri bo'i 'od byung ngo/ /
“I remember as many kalpas As there are atoms in a hundred realms. Beyond those there was the Vyūhasa kalpa, In which was the perfect world realm Meruprabhā. {91}
I remember as many eons as there are atoms In a hundred lands; There was an excellent world of outstanding light, With an age of supreme magnificence.
de la thub pa stong phrag bgrangs pa ni/ / bye ba khrag khrig sum cu drug byung ste/ / de kun tha mar thub dbang byung ba ni/ / 'gro ba'i sgron ma chos kyi rgyal mtshan no/ /
“In that world appeared sages To the number of sixty sextillion. The last of those lords of sages Was the lamp for beings Dharmadhvaja. {92}
In that age, in that world, Were sixty decillion buddhas; The last of them, best of sages, Was a lamp of the world, Spiritual Paragon.
de tshe rgyal po dpal gyi gzi brjid byung / / thub dbang de ni mya ngan yongs 'das nas/ / dgra yi 'khor bcom 'dzam bu'i rgyal mtshan 'dir/ / bka' la thogs med mnga' bdag dam par gyur/ /

“At that time there was the King Śrītejas. After the parinirvāṇa of that lord of sages In this Jambudhvaja, he destroyed the armies of his adversaries And became a supreme sovereign with commands that could not be disobeyed. {93}
At the time of that buddha’s demise There was a glorious king Who had conquered all enemies, A king of kings with unobstructed knowledge.
de la bu ni brgya phrag lnga yod do/ / kun kyang dpa' zhing rtul bod gzugs dang ldan/ / yan lag kun rdzogs rnam par dag pa'i lus/ / gong na med pa'i dpal gyis rab tu brgyan/ /
“He had five hundred sons, who were All courageous, heroic, and handsome, With perfectly formed limbs and pure bodies, And who were unsurpassable and adorned by glory. {94}
He had five hundred sons Who were heroic, brave, and handsome, Physically perfect and pure, Adorned with unexcelled splendor.
rgyal po sras bcas bde gshegs 'dun par gyur; ; rgyal ba'i mchod pa rgya chen rab kyang byas/ / de ni rtag tu dam chos yongs bzung ba'i/ / chos la mngon brtson rab tu brtan par gyur/ /
“The king and his sons had devotion to the Sugata, And they made vast offerings to the Jina. He was always in possession of the good Dharma And unshakably dedicated to the Dharma. {95}
The king and his sons had faith in Buddha And made great offerings to the enlightened; They always followed the true teaching And were unshakable in application of its practice.
rgyal po de sras 'od zer bzang po ni/ / sems can rnam dag gzhon nu 'khrungs gyur pa/ / shin tu blta mdzes yid 'ong gzugs ldan te/ / yan lag mtshan rab sum cu rtsa gnyis brgyan/ /
“To that king was born a son Named Prince Suraśmi, a pure being Who was a delight to see and had a beautiful form And was adorned by the thirty-two supreme signs. {96}
The king had a brilliant son, A pure being, Adorned with the thirty-two Marks of a great man.
rgyal srid yongs su spangs nas mi yi 'khor/ / bye ba lngas bskor de tshe rab tu byung / / rab tu byung nas brtson 'grus brtan ldan te/ / rgyal po'i chos kyang yongs su bzung bar gyur/ /

“He abandoned the kingdom and entered homelessness Accompanied by an entourage of fifty million men. As a mendicant, he was dedicated with unwavering diligence And gained completely the Dharma of the Jina. {97}
Giving up his kingship, he left home Together with five million people; Having gone forth, he worked with firmness and energy To preserve the teaching of the Buddha.
pho brang dam pa sdong po ldan pa ni/ / grong mchog bye ba stong gis kun nas bskor/ / nags tshal yal ga sna tshogs der byung ba/ / rab tu sgra zhi bla na med pa'i dpal/ /
“There was the city[1839] named Drumāvatī Encircled by ten billion excellent towns. There were forests with a variety of branches, Peaceful and silent, with unsurpassable splendor. {98}
There was a city full of trees, Best of a billion cities; There was a forest there of various trees, Quiet and most beautiful.
de ni 'od bzang brtul zhugs rab ldan pa/ / 'jigs med shes rab spobs dang ldan pa bzhugs/ / des ni sems can nyon mongs sbyangs pa'i phyir/ / rgyal ba'i chos kyang yongs su bstan pa mdzad/ /
“There, with perfect discipline, dwelled Suraśmi, Who was fearless, wise, and eloquent. He was teaching the Dharma of the Jina In order to purify defiled beings. {99}
There the king’s son sojourned, Experienced, intelligent, clear-minded; He elucidated the Buddha’s teaching To purify the spirit of defiled beings.
shes rab ldan pa de ni bsod snyoms la/ / spyod lam mdzes shing cha byad zhi ba dang / / mi g.yeng spyan gyis dgongs pa mkhyen bzhin du/ / tshul zab bstan par bzhud pas grong du byon/ /
“That wise one, when seeking alms, Had a beautiful conduct and peaceful appearance. He went into town in an unwavering, profound manner With mindfulness and undistracted eyes. {100}
Gathering wise people, he entered the city, Composed, of noble mien and serene appearance, His gaze steady, mindful, aware, His action profound, walking steadily.
grong mchog dga' ba'i rgyal mtshan zhes bya bar/ / tshong dpon legs pa'i snyan grags der byung ste/ / kho mo de yi bu mo yid 'ong gyur/ / gzugs mdzes ldan te nyi ma'i 'od ces bya/ /
“In the best of towns, Nandīdhvaja, There was the head merchant Suvighuṣṭakīrti. I was his charming, beautiful daughter By the name of Bhānuprabhā. {101}
There was an excellent town, Banner of Joy, And a grandee there named Resounding Fame; I was his beloved daughter, Named Shining Light, more beautiful.
khyim gyi dam pa de yi sgo gnas su/ / 'od zer bzang po 'khor bcas kho mos mthong / / yan lag mtshan brgyan shin tu mdzes pa ste/ / de la kho mo mos pa mchog cig skyes/ /
“At the gateway of our perfect house, I saw Suraśmi and his entourage, Handsome, his body adorned by the signs, And I was greatly attracted to him. {102}
I saw the shining prince and his retinue As I stood in the door of my house; He was handsome, with the marks of greatness, And I became very happy on seeing him.
de ni kho mo'i khyim gyi sgor byon nas/ / nor bu de yi lhung bzed nang du gsol/ / rgyan rnams kun kyang bkrol te mos sems kyis/ / shin tu 'dun par de la bdag gis phul/ /
“He came to the gateway to my home, And I placed a jewel[1840] in his alms bowl. I also removed all my jewelry, And with adoration I offered them to him. {103}
When he passed my door, I put a pearl in his bowl; Then, taking off all my jewelry, Full of love I gave it to him.
bde gshegs sras po 'od zer bzang dpal la/ / 'dod chags sems kyis mchod pa rnams bsgrubs pas/ / bskal pa'i dam pa nyis brgya lnga bcur yang / / ngan song gang du'ang song bar ma gyur to/ /
“Because of making an offering through passion To that son of the buddhas, Suraśmiketu, For two hundred and fifty of the longest kalpas I was not reborn in the lower existences. {104}
With an impassioned heart I made a gift to that enlightening being, And for two hundred and fifty eons Did not fall into evil states.
lha yi yul du lha rigs ldan par skyes/ / mi yi yul du rgyal po'i sras mor gyur/ / kha dog mtha' yas sku yi mdog mnga' bas/ / kun tu kho mo mngon par zhal yang bstan/ /

“I was born into divine families in the realms of the devas And in the human world as the daughters of kings. In all those lives he revealed himself to me In bodies that had endless different forms.[1841] {105}
I was born among celestials, Or as a human princess, And in endless forms I always saw the prince.
bskal pa nyis brgya la bcu 'das gyur nas/ / sbrul tshong gtso mo blta na sdug pa ste/ / mi 'jigs byed pa'i bu mor skyes par gyur/ / de tshe shin tu sbyangs zhes bya ba yin/ /
“After two hundred and fifty kalpas had passed, I was born as the fearless daughter Of the preeminent courtesan Sudarśanā And at that time was known as Saṃcālitā. {106}
rgyal bu gzi brjid 'od kyis bdag mthong nas/ / kho mos de la dga' bas mchod pa byas/ / bdag nyid de la yongs su dbul byas nas/ / kho mo de yi dbang gyur chung mar gyur/ /
“When I saw Prince Tejodhipati, I joyfully made offerings to him. I offered myself to him And became his obedient[1842] wife. {107}
Then I was born to a courtesan, Saw the prince and fell in love, Made myself known to him, And became his obedient wife.
drang srong chen po sku mchog nyi ma la'ang / / bdag cag bsdongs te legs par mchod pa byas/ / mos pas sangs rgyas de yi zhal bltas nas/ / bdag gis byang chub mchog tu sems kyang bskyed/ /
“Together we made excellent offerings To the great ṛṣi Sūryagātrapravara. With devotion I looked upon that buddha’s face, And I developed the aspiration for supreme enlightenment. {108}
He and I together made offerings To the sage Supreme Sun with pure faith, And having seen that buddha, I was inspired to seek supreme enlightenment.
rgyal ba bye ba drug cu tshang ba yang / / bskal pa de la kho mos rim gro byas/ / rgyal ba de dag tha ma'i dus kyi tshe/ / sangs rgyas mos pa'i gzi brjid byung bar gyur/ /
“During that kalpa, I venerated A full six hundred million jinas. In the time of the last of those jinas There appeared the Buddha Adhimuktitejas. {109}
During that eon sixty decillion Buddhas emerged in the world: The last of those buddhas Was Energy of Zeal for Truth.
der ni kho mo'i chos mig rnam par dag / chos kyi rang bzhin bdag gis khong du chud/ / tshul min rnam rtog rab tu zhi bar gyur/ / de tshe tshun chad kho mos snang ba thob / /
“In that time, I gained pure Dharma eyes And comprehended the nature of phenomena. Incorrect thinking completely ceased, And since that time I have attained illumination. {110}
Then my objective eye was clarified And I became aware of the essence of things; My continuous errant conceptions were silenced, And I attained this illumination thenceforth.
rgyal sras rnams kyi ting nge 'dzin gyi yang / / de phyi tshun chad rnam par mthong bar gyur/ / sems kyi skad cig gcig gis rgya mtsho'i zhing / / bsam las rnam 'das phyogs su kho mo 'jug /
“Since that time, I have seen The samādhis of the jinas’ progeny. In each instant of the mind I observe An inconceivable ocean of realms in all directions. {111}
After that I observed the stage Of concentration of enlightening beings; In a mental instant I see unthinkable Oceans of lands in the ten directions.
phyogs rnams kun gyi sna tshogs rnam dag pa'i/ / zhing rnams tshad med rmang byung kho mos mthong / / mthong yang de dag la ni chags pa med/ / nyon mongs bcas la'ang khong khro sdang ba'ang med/ /
“I see in all directions a variety Of countless, marvelous pure realms. I have no attachment to them on seeing them And no aversion toward those that are defiled. {112}
And I see in all directions Various pure worlds, infinitely wondrous; Seeing them, my mind does not cling to them, Nor is it repelled by defiled lands.
zhing rnams de dag ma lus thams cad kyi/ / snying po byang chub sangs rgyas ma lus mthong / / de dag 'od kyi rgya mtsho tshad med pa'ang / / sems kyi skad cig gcig gis rnam par lta/ /
“I see, in every one of those realms, Every buddha in his bodhimaṇḍa. In each instant of mind I look upon Their immeasurable oceans of light. {113}
I also see the enlightenment sites in those lands And all the buddhas there, And I behold in one thought Their measureless oceans of light.
de dag 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor rgya mtsho yang / / sems gcig thogs pa med pas khong du chud/ / rnam par thar pa tshad med thams cad dang / / de dag ting 'dzin ma lus de bzhin gshegs/ /
“In each instant of mind I comprehend, without impediment, The oceans of their circles of followers. In the same way, I know all their samādhis And also their countless liberations. {114}
In the same way I see their oceanic congregations In an instant of awareness, unimpeded, And know all their concentrations, And all their immeasurable liberations.
de dag spyod pa yangs pa'ang khong du chud/ / sa tshul ma lus kun kyang kho mos shes/ / smon lam grangs med rgya mtsho chen po yang / / skad cig re res mtha' yas khong du chud/ /
“I comprehend their vast activities, And I know every manner of the bhūmis. I also know, in each instant, the infinite, Vast ocean of their countless prayers. {115}
I also keep their myriad practices in mind, And penetrate all the principles of the stages; And in each and every instant I enter Into the countless oceans of their vows.
bskal pa mtha' yas spyad pa spyod byed cing / / skyes bu dam pa'i sku la lta lta ste/ / de yi ba spu re re rnam 'phrul pa'ang / / nam yang mur phyin bdag gis ma nus so/ /
“Throughout endless kalpas I gazed upon The body of the supreme being practicing conduct. I could never fully know the extent Of the manifestations from his pores. {116}
Observing the body of the True Man for endless eons And carrying out his practice, I have never seen an end to the mystic projections Emanating from his every hair.
de yi ba spu gcig gi rtse la yang / / zhing mang rgya mtsho grangs las 'das pa mthong / / rlung gi phung po chu bo chen po dang / / sa yi lhun rnams me yis yongs gang mthong / /
“I saw countless oceans of many realms, Even on the tip of a single pore hair. I saw them filled with masses of air, Great rivers, mountains of earth, and fire. {117}

And I see oceans of lands beyond number On the tip of a single hair, With their masses of air and water, fire and earth, On various foundations, with different forms, And diverse patterns of structure,
gzhi rnam sna tshogs rnam phye'i gzugs ldan zhing / / dbyibs tshul sna tshogs khong du chud bya ba; ; dbyibs dang lus kyi rnam pa sna tshogs shing / / lus dang rnam pa mtha' yas gzugs ldan pa'i/ /

“I perceived a variety of grounds Having different forms and various kinds of shapes. They had a variety of elements[1843] and constituents,[1844] Various different kinds of aspects and forms.[1845] {118}
Of various types, according to distribution of elements, With an endless variety of adornments. I see each of the untold realms In the measureless oceans of lands,
brjod yas khams rnams zhing rnams rgya mtsho dag / tshad med rnams su tha dad gsal bar mthong / / chos kyi gsung gis 'gro ba gdul don du/ / brtson pa'i rgyal ba de nyid bzhugs pa mthong / /
“I saw clearly and distinctly countless Oceans of realms, worlds beyond description. I saw the jinas who were engaged In guiding beings through teaching the Dharma. {119}
And I see the buddhas therein Guiding people by articulating truth. I do not understand his activities, His speech, his mind, or its action,
bskal par spyod pa yangs pa spyod pa'i tshe/ / sku yi 'phrin las kho mos de ma shes/ / gsung dang thugs min de gnyis 'phrin las min/ / rdzu 'phrul rnam 'phrul tha dad tshul ma shes/ /
“I cannot comprehend the actions of his body, Or his speech or his mind, or their actions, Or his various miraculous manifestations While practicing his vast conduct for kalpas.” {120}
Or his mystic powers and miracles, or great sublime practice, Though I have been working at this for eons.

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis shAkya'i bu mo go pa'i rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te shAkya'i bu mo go pa la lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas yang bltas te shAkya'i bu mo go pa'i drung nas song ngo// //

Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, bowed his head to the feet of the Śākya maiden Gopā, circumambulated the Śākya maiden Gopā many hundreds of thousands of times, keeping her to his right, and, looking back again and again, departed from the Śākya maiden Gopā.
Then Sudhana paid his respects and took leave of Gopa.
shin tu rgyas pa chen po'i mdo/ sangs rgyas phal po che zhes bya ba las/ sdong pos brgyan pa'i le'u ste/ /bam po brgya dgu pa/
[lha mo sgyu ma]
Chapter 44. Māyādevī
Maya
de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang lha mo sgyu ma'i gan du 'gro bar mngon du bltas nas sangs rgyas kyi spyod yul gyi rgyud kyi ye shes la zhugs pa des 'di snyam du bsam mo/ /
Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, on the way to Māyādevī, undertaking the wisdom of practicing the scope of the activity of the buddhas, thought,
Then Sudhana, turning to go to Lady Maya, having attained knowledge from investigation of the sphere of buddhahood, thought to himself,
bdag gis dge ba'i bshes gnyen 'jig rten thams cad las gyen du 'phags pa'i

“By what means can I see the kalyāṇamitras, honor them, meet them,[1846] accompany them,[1847] learn their qualities, know the field of their speech, understand the succession of their words, and possess the teachings of the kalyāṇamitras
“How can I meet, associate with, and learn from spiritual benefactors
skye mched drug dang ldan pa/
who have six āyatanas that have risen above all worlds;
whose senses are detached from all worlds,
gnas med pa la rab tu gnas pa/
who do not abide anywhere,
chags pa thams cad las yang dag par 'das pa'i lus dang ldan pa/
who have bodies that have transcended all attachments;
whose bodies are beyond all attachments,
chags pa med par 'gro ba'i lam du zhugs pa /
who follow the path of unimpeded movement;
who have set out on the unimpeded path,
chos kyi lus shin tu rnam par dag pa/
who have pure Dharma bodies;
who have purified the spiritual body,
lus kyi lam sgyu mas legs par sprul pa'i lus dang ldan pa/
who have bodies that are manifestations of illusory physical activities;
who skillfully project bodily forms by the illusion of physical action,
ye shes sgyu ma'i rnam par 'jig rten na rnam par spyod pa/
who perform conducts in the world that are the illusions of wisdom;
who observe the world as being within the illusion of knowledge,
smon lam sgyu ma'i gzugs dang lus su ldan pa/
who have forms and bodies[1848] from prayer;[1849]
who are physical embodiments of vows,
sangs rgyas kyi byin gyi rlabs yid kyi rang bzhin gyi lus dang ldan pa/
whose bodies are made of mind by the power of Buddha,
ma skyes ma 'gag pa'i lus dang ldan pa;
who have bodies that are not born and do not cease;
whose bodies are not born and do not perish,
'ong ba med pa'i lus dang ldan pa/
bden pa med pa dang rdzun pa med pa'i lus dang ldan pa/
who have bodies that are neither true nor false;
whose bodies are neither real nor unreal,
ma 'phos ma zhig pa'i lus dang ldan pa/
who have bodies that do not pass away or perish;
whose bodies neither come nor go,
ma byung mi 'jig pa'i lus dang ldan pa/
who have bodies that do not originate and are not destroyed;
whose bodies neither become nor disintegrate,
mtshan nyid med par mtshan nyid gcig pa'i lus dang ldan pa/
who have bodies that have the single characteristic of having no characteristics;
whose bodies are of one form which is formless,
gnyis la chags pa dang bral ba'i lus dang ldan pa/
who have bodies that have no attachment to duality;
whose bodies are nondual and freed from attachments,
kun gzhi med pa la gnas pa'i lus dang ldan pa/
who have bodies that are based on having no basis;
whose bodies have no resting place,
mi zad cing nyams pa med pa'i lus dang ldan pa/
who have bodies that do not decay[1850] or diminish;
whose bodies have no extinction,
gzugs brnyan ltar rnam par rtog pa med pa'i lus dang ldan pa/
who have bodies without thoughts, like reflections;
whose bodies are like reflections and have no difference,
rmi lam dang mnyam par rnam par rgyu ba'i lus dang ldan pa/
who have active bodies that are like dreams;
whose bodies are like dreams in action,
me long gi dkyil 'khor ltar 'pho ba med pa'i lus dang ldan pa/
who have bodies that do not depart, like the surface of a mirror;
whose bodies are like images in a mirror,
phyogs med pa ltar rab tu zhi ba khong du chud pa'i lus dang ldan pa/
who have bodies that are established in peace, like the absence of directions;
whose bodies stand tranquilly everywhere equally,
/phyogs kun tu rgyas par 'gengs pa'i lus dang ldan pa/
who have bodies that pervade all directions;
whose bodies are emanations pervading all directions,
dus gsum du tha mi dad pa'i lus dang ldan pa/
who have bodies that have no differentiation between the three times;
whose bodies are continuous through past, present, and future,
lus med pa'i sems kyi lus rnam par mi rtog pa'i lus dang ldan pa/
who have bodiless bodies of mind that are bodies without thought;
whose bodies are neither physical nor mental and are indivisible,
'jig rten thams cad kyi mig gi lam las yongs su 'das pa'i lus dang ldan pa/
who have bodies that have transcended the path of sight in all worlds;
whose bodies are beyond the range of vision of all worldlings,
kun tu bzang po'i mig gi rgyud kyis rnam par shes par bya bas 'dul ba'i lus dang ldan pa/
who have bodies that have been tamed through the path of completely good vision;
whose secret being can only be known to the vision of the eye of universal good,
chags pa med pa nam mkha'i spyod yul dang ldan pa rnams mthong bar bya ba'am/
and who have the unimpeded field of activity of space?”
