whose realm of action is unobstructed like space?”

bsnyen bkur bar bya ba'am/ mngon sum du 'phrad par bya ba'am/ 'grogs par bya ba'am/ mtshan ma gzung bar bya ba'am/ dbyangs kyi dkyil 'khor rnam par rig par bya ba'am/ tshig gi rgyud yongs su shes par bya ba'am/ gdams ngag yongs su gzung bar bya bar thabs ji lta bu zhig tu nus par 'gyur snyam nas
[…see above…]
[…see above…]

de ltar sems shing yid la byed pa la brtson par gnas pa'i tshe grong khyer gyi lha mo rin chen mig ces bya ba/ nam mkha'i lha mo'i tshogs kyis yongs su bskor ba zhig gis bdag gi lus rgyan sna tshogs kyis yongs su brgyan pa/ bdag gi lus rgyan gyis rnam par klubs par nam mkha' la 'dug par nye bar bstan nas lha rdzas kyi me tog rnam pa dang / kha dog du ma can snyim pa nas mngon par gtor te

While he was dedicated to contemplating and pondering this, Ratnanetrā, the goddess of the city, appeared in the sky encircled by a crowd of sky goddesses. Her body was adorned by varieties of jewelry, her body was covered in adornments, and she scattered handfuls of divine flowers of many shapes and colors.

As he was engaged in such thoughts, a city goddess named Jewel Eyes, surrounded by a group of sky goddesses, showed herself in the sky, her body adorned with various adornments, holding a basket of celestial flowers of many shapes and colors,
tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la 'di skad ces smras so/ / rigs kyi bu; khyod kyis 'khor ba'i yid la dga' bar mi gnas pas sems kyi grong khyer yongs su srung ba la brtson par gyis shig /
She said to Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, “Noble one, you should be dedicated to protecting the city of the mind by not dwelling in delight in saṃsāra’s field of perception.
and spoke to Sudhana in these terms as she scattered them before him: “You should guard the city of mind, by not dwelling on enjoyment of mundane objects.
rigs kyi bu/ khyod kyis de bzhin gshegs pa'i stobs bcu la dmigs pas sems kyi grong khyer brgyan pa la brtson par gyis shig /
“Noble one, you should be dedicated to adorning the city of the mind through focusing on the ten strengths of the tathāgatas.
You should adorn the city of mind, by concentrating on the ten powers of the enlightened.
rigs kyi bu /khyod kyis phrag dog dang / ser sna dang / g.yo dang bral bas sems kyi grong khyer yongs su sbyangs pa la brtson par gyis shig /
“Noble one, you should be dedicated to purifying the city of the mind through being free of envy, greed, and deception.
You should clean the city of mind, by getting rid of jealousy, envy, and guile.
rigs kyi bu/ khyod kyis chos thams cad kyi rang bzhin nges par rtogs par bya bas sems kyi grong khyer gyi yongs su gdung ba rab tu zhi bar bya ba la brtson par gyis shig /
“Noble one, you should be dedicated to pacifying the torment of the city of the mind through realizing the nature of all phenomena.
You should extinguish the burning of the city of mind, by meditating on all truths.
rigs kyi bu/ khyod kyis thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi tshogs la brtson 'grus chen po'i shugs rnam par spel bas sems kyi grong khyer rnam par spel ba la brtson par gyis shig /
“Noble one, you should be dedicated to increasing the city of the mind through increasing the power of great dedication to the accumulation of omniscience.
You should expand the city of mind, by increasing the flow of great energy in preparing for omniscience.

rigs kyi bu/ khyod kyis ting nge 'dzin dang / snyoms par 'jug pa dang / bsam gtan dang / rnam par thar pa dang / chos kyi gzhal med khang yangs pa'i rnam par spyod pa la dbang sgyur bas sems kyi grong khyer dang / gnas kyi mdzod brgyan pa dang / srung ba la brtson par gyis shig /

“Noble one, you should be dedicated to protecting the city of the mind’s treasury of buildings through gaining power over dwelling in the vast divine palaces of the samādhis, samāpattis, dhyānas, liberations, and the Dharma.
You should protect the dwellings, storehouses, and facilities of the city of mind, by command of the vast spiritual palace of all concentrations, attainments, meditations, and liberations.

rigs kyi bu; khyod kyis de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor yang dag par sgrub pa'i sa thams cad kyi shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa rab tu thob par 'tshal bas sems kyi grong khyer snang bar bya ba la brtson par gyis shig /

“Noble one, you should be dedicated to illuminating the city of the mind through seeking the attainment of the perfection of wisdom of all the levels of the established circles of followers of all the tathāgatas.
You should illumine the city of mind, by absorbing universal transcendent wisdom in the assemblies gathered around all buddhas.

rigs kyi bu/ khyod kyis de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad yang dag par byung ba'i thabs kyi lam gyis rang gi sems kyi grong khyer du gzhol bar bya bas sems kyi grong khyer nye bar brtan pa la brtson par gyis shig /
“Noble one, you should be dedicated to strengthening the city of the mind through entering the city of your own mind through the path of the method of the arising of all the tathāgatas.
You should make the city of mind firm, by putting the paths of means produced by all buddhas into the city of your own mind.

rigs kyi bu/ khyod kyis byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po'i spyod pa dang / smon lam mngon par sgrub pa'i sems rnam par dag pas sems kyi grong khyer gyi ra ba brtan pa mngon par sgrub par gyis shig /
“Noble one, you should be dedicated to creating the strong walls of the city of the mind through a pure mind that accomplishes the completely good conduct and prayers of the bodhisattvas.
You should build strong walls about the city of mind, by purification of mind in carrying out the vow of practice of universal good.

rigs kyi bu/ khyod kyis nyon mongs pa dang / bdud kyi ris kyi sdig to'i grogs po dang / bdud kyi 'khor gyis mi chom par bya bas sems kyi grong khyer rgal dka' ba dang / bshig par dka' ba mngon par sgrub pa la brtson par gyis shig /

“Noble one, you should be dedicated to accomplishing the inapproachability and indestructibility of the city of the mind through crushing the army of the māras, the friends of wickedness, who are on the side of the māras and the kleśas.
You should make the city of mind invincible and impregnable, by being invulnerable to all afflictions and bad influences.
rigs kyi bu/ khyod kyis sems can thams cad de bzhin gshegs pa'i ye shes snang bas khong du chud par bya ba'i phyir sems kyi grong khyer snang bar bya ba la brtson par gyis shig /
“Noble one, you should be dedicated to illuminating the city of the mind through enlightening all beings with the illumination from the knowledge of the tathāgatas.
You should light up the city of mind, by illumining all beings with the knowledge of the enlightened.
rigs kyi bu/ khyod kyis de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi chos kyi sprin gyi char yongs su bzung bas sems kyi grong khyer mngon par brlan pa la brtson par gyis shig /
“Noble one, you should be dedicated to moistening the city of the mind through acquiring the rain from the clouds of the Dharma of all the tathāgatas.
You should irrigate the city of mind, by receiving the clouds of teaching of all buddhas.
rigs kyi bu/ khyod kyis de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi bsod nams rgya mtsho rang gi sems kyis yang dag par blangs pas sems kyi grong khyer brtan pa la brtson par gyis shig /
“Noble one, you should be dedicated to strengthening the city of the mind through your mind’s acquisition of the ocean of merit of all the tathāgatas.
You should firmly brace the city of mind, by absorbing into your own mind the oceans of virtues of all buddhas.
rigs kyi bu/ khyod kyis byams pa chen pos 'gro ba thams cad rgyas par dgang bas sems kyi grong khyer rab tu rgyas par bya ba la brtson par gyis shig /
“Noble one, you should be dedicated to increasing the city of the mind through great love pervading all beings.
You should broaden the city of mind, by suffusing all beings with great love.
rigs kyi bu/ khyod kyis mi dge ba'i chos kyi gnyen po chos kyi gdugs yangs par sgrub pas sems kyi grong khyer yongs su dag pa la brtson par gyis shig /
“Noble one, you should be dedicated to purifying[1851] the city of the mind through establishing the vast parasol of the Dharma as the remedy for bad qualities.
You should provide shelter, by producing the shield of all good ways in the vast canopy of the Teaching.
rigs kyi bu/ khyod kyis snying rje chen po shin tu yangs pas 'gro ba thams cad kyi don du sems g.yo par bya bas sems kyi grong khyer rab tu bskyob pa la brtson par gyis shig /
“Noble one, you should be dedicated to making the city of the mind tremble[1852] through the mind trembling with vast, great compassion for the sake of all beings.
You should water the city of mind, by feeling great compassion for all beings.
rigs kyi bu/ khyod kyis phyi nang gi dngos po 'gro ba thams cad la yongs su bstan pa'i phyir sems kyi grong khyer gyi sgo dbye ba la brtson par gyis shig /
“Noble one, you should be dedicated to opening the gates to the city of the mind through[1853] providing[1854] all beings with outer and inner things.
You should open the doors of the city of mind, by giving of yourself and giving goods to all beings.
rigs kyi bu/ khyod kyis 'khor ba'i yul thams cad la dga' ba las phyin phyogs su blta bas sems kyi grong khyer rnam par dag par bya ba la brtson par gyis shig /
“Noble one, you should be dedicated to purifying the city of the mind through turning away[1855] from delighting in the sensory range of all of saṃsāra.
You should purify the city of mind, by turning away from passion for ephemeral things.
rigs kyi bu/ khyod kyis mi dge ba'i chos kyi rgyud thams cad mi srid par bya bas sems kyi grong khyer gyi srog rab tu mkhrang ba mngon par sgrub pa la brtson par gyis shig /
“Noble one, you should be dedicated to strengthening the heart[1856] of the city of the mind through making the continuity of bad actions impossible.
You should make the city of mind steadfast and strong, by excluding all unhealthy elements from your body-mind continuum.
rigs kyi bu/ khyod kyis thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi tshogs yang dag par sgrub pa'i brtson 'grus las phyir mi ldog par bya bas sems kyi grong khyer brtan par bya ba la brtson par gyis shig /
“Noble one, you should be dedicated to making the city of the mind strong through never lapsing from the diligence that accomplishes the accumulation of omniscience.
You should energize the city of mind, by maintaining the energy to produce the provisions for omniscience.
rigs kyi bu/ khyod kyis dus gsum gyi de bzhin gshegs pa'i dkyil 'khor thams cad dran pa shin tu snang bar byas pas sems kyi grong khyer rab tu gsal bar bya ba la brtson par gyis shig /
“Noble one, you should be dedicated to illuminating the city of the mind through the illumination of remembering the field of all the tathāgatas of the three times.
You should illuminate the city of mind, by the illumination of recollection of the spheres of the buddhas of past, present, and future.

rigs kyi bu/ khyod kyis de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi chos kyi 'khor lo'i mdo sde sna tshogs kyi chos kyi sgo rab tu dbye ba'i ye shes la mngon par mkhas par bya bas sems kyi grong khyer rnam par dbye ba'i tshul la mkhas par gyis shig /

“Noble one, you should be dedicated to being skilled in the ways of analyzing the city of the mind through being skilled in the wisdom that analyzes the Dharma gateways of the various sūtras of the Dharma wheel of all the tathāgatas.
You should know how to stock the city of mind, by examination, learning, and higher knowledge of the various doors of truth in the scriptures of the cycles of teaching of all buddhas.

rigs kyi bu/ khyod kyis 'gro ba thams cad mngon sum du gnas pa'i thams cad mkhyen pa'i sgo dang / lam gyi tshul yongs su brtan pa'i phyir sems kyi grong khyer dmigs par bya ba la brtson par gyis shig /
“Noble one, you should be dedicated to the perception of the city of the mind through teaching the way of the path and gateways to omniscience that are directly perceivable by all beings.
You should know how to govern the city of mind, by showing all beings the path of entries into omniscience in various ways.

rigs kyi bu/ khyod kyis dus gsum gyi de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi smon lam rgya mtsho rang gi smon lam du mngon par sgrub pa rnam par dag par bya ba'i phyir sems kyi grong khyer byin gyis brlab pa'i tshul la mkhas par gyis shig /

“Noble one, you should be dedicated to being skilled in the ways of blessing the city of the mind through the pure accomplishment of the ocean of prayers of all the tathāgatas in the three times within your own prayer.
You should know how to support the city of mind, by perfection of accomplishment of the vows of all buddhas of past, present, and future.

rigs kyi bu/ khyod kyis chos kyi dbyings thams cad du bsod nams dang / ye shes kyi tshogs rgya chen po rnam par spel bas sems kyi grong khyer gyi tshogs kyi mthu rnam par 'phel bar bya ba'i thabs la mkhas par gyis shig /

“Noble one, you should be dedicated to increasing the power of the accumulations of the city of the mind through increasing the great, vast accumulations of merit and wisdom in the entire realm of the Dharma.
You should know how to increase the power to provide for the city of mind, by increasing the great stores of virtue and knowledge from all realms of truth.

rigs kyi bu/ khyod kyis sems can thams cad kyi sems dang / bsam pa dang / dbang po dang / mos pa dang / kun nas nyon mongs pa dang / rnam par byang ba shes par bya bas sems kyi grong khyer nas 'od kun tu dgye ba'i thabs la mkhas par gyis shig /

“Noble one, you should be dedicated to being skilled in the method for emitting light from the city of the mind through knowing the minds, thoughts, faculties, aspirations, defilements, and purification of all beings.
You should know how to emanate light throughout the entire city of mind, by higher knowledge of the science of stripping away defilements from the minds, senses, and interests of all sentient beings.
rigs kyi bu/ khyod kyis chos kyi dbyings kyi tshul thams cad yang dag par bsdu bas sems kyi grong khyer du dbang sgyur ba'i tshul la mkhas par gyis shig /
“Noble one, you should be dedicated to being skilled in the way of gaining power over the city of the mind through gathering all the ways of the realm of the Dharma.
You should know how to control the city of mind, by embracing all the principles of the realm of reality.
rigs kyi bu/ khyod kyis de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad dran zhing snang bar bya bas sems kyi grong khyer 'od gsal bar bya ba la brtson par gyis shig /
“Noble one, you should be dedicated to illuminating the city of the mind through remembering and illuminating all the tathāgatas.
You should make the city of mind light, by the light of mindfulness of all buddhas.
rigs kyi bu/ khyod kyis lus med pa'i chos kyi tshul thams cad khong du chud par bya bas sems kyi grong khyer gyi rang bzhin yongs su shes par bya ba la brtson par gyis shig /
“Noble one, you should be dedicated to knowing the nature of the city of the mind through realizing all the ways of the bodyless Dharma.
You should know the essence of the city of mind, by penetrating the principle of nonsubstantiality of all things.
rigs kyi bu/ khyod kyis thams cad mkhyen pa'i chos kyi grong khyer du 'gro bar bya bas sems kyi grong khyer sgyu ma lta bur brtag pa la brtson par gyis shig /
“Noble one, you should be dedicated to examining as an illusion the city of the mind through going to the city of the Dharma of omniscience.
You should observe the illusoriness of the city of mind, by going to the spiritual city of omniscience.
rigs kyi bu/ khyod kyis de ltar sems kyi grong khyer yongs su sbyangs pa la brtson pa'i byang chub sems dpa'i dge ba'i rtsa ba thams cad yongs su sgrub pa thob par nus so/ /
“Noble one, in that way the bodhisattva who is dedicated to the purification of the city of the mind will be able to attain the accomplishment of all roots of merit.
“By thus purifying the city of mind, an enlightening being can produce all good.

de ci'i phyir zhe na/ de ltar sems kyi grong khyar yongs su dag pa'i byang chub sems dpa' de'i mdun na ni/ sangs rgyas mthong bar bya ba la sgrib pa'am/ chos mnyan par bya ba la sgrib pa'am/ de bzhin gshegs pa mchod cing rim gror bya ba la sgrib pa'am/ sems can yongs su bsdu ba'i sbyor ba la sgrib pa dang / sangs rgyas kyi zhing yongs su dag par bya ba la sgrib pa yang rung ste/ sgrib pa thams cad mi gnas so/ /

“Why is that? Because bodhisattvas who thus purify the city of the mind have before them no obscurations: there are no obscurations to seeing the buddhas, no obscurations to hearing the Dharma, no obscurations to venerating and making offerings to the tathāgatas, no obscurations to engaging in gathering beings, and no obscurations to purifying buddha realms.

Why? Because no obstacles stand before an enlightening being whose mind-city is thus purified—no obstacles to seeing buddhas, or obstacles to hearing the Teaching, or obstacles to serving buddhas, or obstacles to efforts to save sentient beings, or obstacles to purifying buddha-lands.

rigs kyi bu/ sgrib pa thams cad dang bral ba'i sems dang / lhag pa'i bsam par dge ba'i bshes gnyen yongs su btsal ba la mngon par brtson pa'i byang chub sems dpas ni/ las gron chung dus dge ba'i bshes gnyen mthong bar 'gyur te/
“Noble one, bodhisattvas who are dedicated to seeing kalyāṇamitras with a mind free of all obscurations and with a higher motivation will with little difficulty see a kalyāṇamitra.
Spiritual friends are easily perceptible to an enlightening being looking for spiritual friends when the mind is free from obstacles;
rigs kyi bu; dge ba'i bshes gnyen la rag las pa yang byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi thams cad mkhyen pa nyid do/ /
“Noble one, the omniscience of bodhisattvas depends on the kalyāṇamitras.”
and omniscience for enlightening beings comes through the help of spiritual friends.”

de nas lus kyi ris su gtogs pa'i lha mo chos kyi pad+mo dpal gyi dkyil 'khor ces bya ba dang / ngo tsha shes pa'i dpal gyi dog pa'i 'od ces bya ba gnyis shig lha mo'i tshogs tshad med pas yongs su bskor nas lha mo sgyu ma'i legs pa rjod cing snying po byang chub nas thon te tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gi mdun gyi nam mkha' la 'khod nas rang rang gi rin po che'i rna cha las 'od zer gyi dra ba rin po che'i kha dog tu 'dug pa du ma dang / spos dang / bdug pa dri ma med pa 'od 'phro ba'i kha dog tu 'dug pa du ma dang / sems dang / bsam pa mos par byed pa'i kha dog dang; sems kyi dga' ba'i shugs rnam par 'phel bar byed pa'i kha dog dang / lus kyi gdung ba sim par byed pa'i kha dog dang / lus rnam par dag pa yongs su ston pa'i kha dog dang / lus kyi mthu thogs pa med par 'byung ba'i yul dang ldan pa'i 'od zer gyi dra ba mang po bkye bas/ zhing rgya chen po snang bar byas nas

Then two of the family of goddesses of the body, who were named Dharmapadmaśrīkuśalā and Hrīśrīmañjariprabhāvā,[1857] encircled by an innumerable assembly of goddesses, emerged from the bodhimaṇḍa, uttering praises of Māyādevī. They arranged themselves in the sky before Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, and emitted from their precious earrings[1858] a net of many light rays the colors of jewels; many pure perfumes and incenses the colors of shining lights; colors attractive to mind and thought; colors that increased the power of joy in the mind; colors that eased the pains of the body; colors that revealed pure bodies; and nets of light rays that were a field of perception that gave rise to an unimpeded prowess of the body and illuminated vast realms.

Then a goddess, Spiritual Lotus, surrounded by innumerable goddesses radiant with modesty and beauty, came forth from the enlightening site praising Lady Maya and stopped in the sky in front of Sudhana, each goddess emanating webs of light of many jewel colors, colors of pure flames of incense of many fragrances, colors soothing the mind, colors increasing the flow of joy in the mind, colors cooling the fever of the body, colors showing physical purity, webs of light produced by the motion of unattached, unimpeded bodies. Illumining a multitude of lands,

tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi sku thams cad du khyab pa thams cad la mngon du gyur pa yongs su bstan nas 'jig rten thams cad la g.yas phyogs su bskar ba byas te tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gi spyi bo'i gtsug tu shar nas spyi bo'i gtsug man chad ba spu'i bu ga thams cad du zhugs te lus kun tu khyab par gyur to; ;

They revealed to Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, all the bodies of all tathāgatas, which are present everywhere and facing everywhere. Then they completely circled, to their right, the entire world, and then shone upon the crown of the head of Sudhana, the head merchant’s son. They completely pervaded him, from the crown of his head to the pores of his body.
revealing to Sudhana the forms of all buddhas everywhere, the lights then circled the whole world and descended into Sudhana’s head, and from his head entered into all of his pores.

de ltar lha mo de dag gi 'od zer gyis tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la phog ma thag tu de'i mod la mun pa thams cad dang mi gnas pa'i mig rdul dang bral ba'i 'od snang ba zhes bya ba thob par gyur to/ / sems can gyi rang bzhin khong du chud par byed pa'i mig rab rib dang bral ba'i 'od snang ba zhes bya ba thob par gyur to/ / sems can gyi rang bzhin khong du chud par byed pa'i mig rab rib dang bral ba zhes bya ba thob par gyur to/ / chos thams cad kyi rang bzhin gyi dkyil 'khor la rnam par lta ba'i mig rdul dang bral bas dbang bsgyur ba zhes bya ba thob par gyur to/ / zhing thams cad la rnam par lta ba'i mig rnam par dag pa la dbang bsgyur ba zhes bya ba thob par gyur to/ / de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi chos kyi sku la rnam par lta ba'i mig rnam par snang ba zhes bya ba thob par gyur to/ / de bzhin gshegs pa'i gzugs kyi sku yongs su grub pa rnam par phye ba bsam gyis mi khyab pa la rnam par lta ba'i mig rnam par dag pa'i blo gros zhes bya ba thob par gyur to/ / zhing rgya mtsho 'byams klas pa thams cad kyi 'jig rten gyi khams 'byung ba dang / 'jig pa rnam par phye ba la rnam par lta ba'i mig chags pa med pa'i 'od ces bya ba thob par gyur to/ / de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi chos kyi 'khor lo'i mdo sde'i tshul mngon par sgrub pa'i phyogs la rnam par lta ba'i mig kun tu snang ba zhes bya ba thob par gyur to/ / sangs rgyas kyi rnam par 'phrul pa dang / sems can 'dul ba'i byin gyi rlabs la rnam par lta ba'i mig kun nas yul du 'gyur ba zhes bya ba thob par gyur to/ / sangs rgyas kyi zhing thams cad du byung ba'i sangs rgyas skyes pa la rnam par lta ba'i mig kun tu lta ba zhes bya ba thob par gyur to/ /

As soon as the light rays from those goddesses touched Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, in that instant he attained the eyesight called the dust-free illuminations, which was free from all blinding darkness. He attained the eyesight called free from the obscuration of sight, through which he perceived the nature of beings. He attained the eyesight called the lord of freedom from dust, through which he looked at the field of the nature of all phenomena. He attained the eyesight called lord of purity, through which he looked at the character[1859] of all realms. He attained the eyesight called shining light, through which he looked upon the Dharma bodies of all tathāgatas. He attained the eyesight called pure intelligence,[1860] through which he looked upon the countless categories of the created form bodies of the tathāgatas.[1861] He attained the eyesight called unimpeded light, through which he looked upon the categories of the origination and destruction of world realms throughout the vast extent of the ocean of realms. He attained the eyesight called complete light, through which he looked upon the aspect of the creation of the way of the sūtras in the Dharma wheel of all the tathāgatas. He attained the eyesight called the complete field of perception, through which he looked upon the miracles of the buddhas and their blessings that guide beings. He attained the eyesight called complete sight, through which he looked upon the births of buddhas that occurred in all buddha realms.

As soon as the light rays of the goddesses touched Sudhana, he acquired an eye called ‘dispassionate light,’ with which no darkness can coexist; he acquired an eye called ‘unobscured,’ whereby he saw the essence of beings; he acquired an eye called ‘dispassionate sovereign,’ whereby he viewed the sphere of essence of all phenomena; he acquired an eye called ‘pure state,’ whereby he viewed the nature of all lands; he acquired an eye called ‘shining light,’ whereby he viewed the reality body of those who arrive at Thusness; he acquired an eye called ‘universal light,’ whereby he viewed the inconceivable perfection of the physical embodiment of those who arrive at Thusness; he acquired an eye called ‘unobstructed light,’ whereby he viewed the becoming and disintegration of worlds in all universes; he acquired an eye called ‘total illumination,’ whereby he observed the manner of extraction of the principles of the scripture in the teachings of all buddhas; he acquired an eye called ‘universal scope,’ whereby he viewed the infinite variety of mystic powers used by buddhas to guide beings; he acquired an eye called ‘all-seeing,’ whereby he observed the emergence of buddhas in all lands.

de nas byang chub sems dpa' yang dag par 'gro ba'i khang pa'i sgo srung srin po'i dbang po srin po stong phrag bcu'i gtso bo mig bzang zhes bya ba chang mar bcas/ bu dang bcas/ rang gi gnyen bshes dang 'khor du bcas pas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la me tog kha dog sna tshogs yid du 'ong bas mngon par gtor te 'di skad ces smras so/ /

Then the guardian at the door of the meeting hall of the bodhisattvas, the leader of ten thousand rākṣasas, whose name was Sunetra, with his wives, children, relatives, and entourage, threw flowers of many beautiful colors over Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, and said to him,

Then a supernatural being named Fine Eye, doorkeeper of the hall of assembly of enlightening beings, at the head of ten thousand supernatural beings, together with his wife and son and clan, sprinkled Sudhana with flowers of various colors and pleasant fragrances, and said,

rigs kyi bu/ chos bcu dang ldan pa'i byang chub sems dpas ni/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen thams cad dang nye bar bsnyen pa yin te/ bcu gang zhe na/ 'di ltar bsam pa yongs su dag pa g.yo dang sgyu med pa dang / 'gro ba thams cad yongs su sdud pa la tha mi dad pa'i snying rje chen po dang / sems can thams cad la sems can med pa'i rang bzhin nges par rtsogs pa'i rab tu rtog pa dang / lhag pa'i bsam pa'i stobs thams cad mkhyen par 'gro ba las phyir mi ldog pa dang / de bzhin gshegs pa'i dkyil 'khor la mngon par 'dun pa'i mos pa'i stobs dang / chos thams cad kyi rang bzhin dri ma med pas rnam par dag pa'i mig dang / sems can gyi dkyil 'khor thams cad la tha mi dad pa'i byams pa chen po dang / sgrib pa thams cad rnam par 'thor ba'i ye shes kyi snang ba dang / 'khor ba'i sdug bsngal thams cad kyi gnyen po gdugs su gyur pa'i chos kyi sprin chen po dang / chos kyi dbyings kyi rgyud thams cad la rab tu zhugs shing dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi rjes su 'brang ba mngon du gyur pa'i ye shes kyi mig ste/

“Noble one, a bodhisattva who has ten qualities will be near to all kalyāṇamitras. What are these ten? They are (1) a pure motivation without deception or guile, (2) a compassion that gathers all beings without discrimination, (3) the insight that realizes that the nature of all beings is that there are no beings, (4) a superior motivation for proceeding irreversibly toward omniscience, (5) the strength of the aspiration that is directed toward the field of the tathāgatas, (6) the vision of the purity of the stainlessness of the nature of all phenomena, (7) the great love without discrimination for the field of beings, (8) the light of wisdom, which dispels all obscurations, (9) the great cloud of the Dharma, which is a parasol that counters all the suffering of saṃsāra, and (10) the eyes of wisdom that are focused on following the kalyāṇamitras and enter into all the streams within the realm of the Dharma.

“An enlightening being imbued with ten qualities can approach all spiritual friends. What are these ten? A pure mind free from guile and deceit; great compassion taking in all beings as a whole; meditation on the unreality of self-existence of all beings; the willpower to proceed unswervingly toward omniscience; the power of attention to the spheres of all buddhas; clear perception of the purity of essence of all phenomena; great kindness to all beings as a whole; the light of knowledge that dissolves all barriers; the great body of teachings that acts as a shield against the miseries of the mundane whirl; the eye of knowledge of all currents of reality, directed toward the path of spiritual friends.
rigs kyi bu/ chos bcu po de dag dang ldan pa'i byang chub sems dpa' ni/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen thams cad dang nye bar bsnyen pa yin no/ /
“Noble one, the bodhisattva who has these ten qualities will be near to all kalyāṇamitras.
“Having attained these ten things, enlightening beings can approach all spiritual friends;
ting nge 'dzin la nges par gzhag pa'i sgo bcus rnam par lta ba'i byang chub sems dpa' ni/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen thams cad dang mngon du gyur pa 'thob pa yin te/ bcu gang zhe na/
“The bodhisattva who sees the ten entryways to resting in samādhi will attain the direct perception of all kalyāṇamitras. What are those ten? They are
and by observation through ten ways of concentrated meditation they can come face to face with all spiritual friends. What are the ten?
ting nge 'dzin la nges par gzhag pa'i sgo chos thams cad nam mkha' ltar rdul dang bral bar rnam par dpyod pa'i dkyil 'khor dang /
(1) the entryway to resting in the samādhi of the field of analyzing all phenomena as being like dust-free space,
Meditation on the purity of the sky of reality;
ting nge 'dzin la nges par gzhag pa'i sgo phyogs rgya mtsho thams cad mngon du gyur pa'i mig dang /
(2) the entryway to resting in the samādhi of the vision that directly perceives the ocean of all directions,
meditation viewing the ocean of all realms;
ting nge 'dzin la nges par gzhag pa'i sgo dmigs pa thams cad la rnam par mi rtog rnam par mi dpyod pa dang /
(3) the entryway to resting in the samādhi of the nonexamination and nonanalysis of all perception,
meditation without discrimination or thought of any objects;
ting nge 'dzin la nges par gzhag pa'i sgo phyogs thams cad du de bzhin gshegs pa'i sprin yongs su 'byung ba dang /
(4) the entryway to resting in the samādhi of the arising of the clouds of tathāgatas in all directions,
meditation on the appearance of the multitudes of buddhas of all realms;
ting nge 'dzin la nges par gzhag pa'i sgo thams cad mkhyen pa'i ye shes dang / bsod nams rgya mtsho gsog pa'i snying po dang /
(5) the entryway to resting in the samādhi of the essence of the accumulation of an ocean of omniscient wisdom and merit,
meditation on the multitude of virtues of omniscience;
ting nge 'dzin la nges par gzhag pa'i sgo sems bskyed pa thams cad la dge ba'i bshes gnyen 'byung ba dang 'bral ba med cing nye bar gyur pa dang /
(6) the entryway to resting in the samādhi of the development of all aspirations to be inseparably near to the occurrence of kalyāṇamitras,
meditation with every thought constantly on spiritual friends;
ting nge 'dzin la nges par gzhag pa'i sgo de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi yon tan dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi khar las pas yongs su 'grub pa dang /
(7) the entryway to resting in the samādhi of all the qualities of the tathāgatas originating from the mouths[1862] of the kalyāṇamitras,
meditation on the virtues of all buddhas deriving from spiritual friends;
ting nge 'dzin la nges par gzhag pa'i sgo dge ba'i bshes gnyen thams cad dang yongs su mi 'bral ba dang /
(8) the entryway to resting in the samādhi of inseparability from all the tathāgatas,
meditation on being with all spiritual friends forever;
ting nge 'dzin la nges par gzhag pa'i sgo dge ba'i bshes gnyen thams cad mnyam pa nyid kyis rtag par kun tu nye bar 'gro ba'i sbyor ba dang /
(9) the entryway to resting in the samādhi of being engaged in being near, always and equally, to all kalyāṇamitras, and
meditation on always going to all spiritual friends everywhere equally;
ting nge 'dzin la nges par gzhag pa'i sgo dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi thabs kyi spyod pa thams cad kyis dub pa med pa'i sbyor ba ste/
(10) the entryway to resting in the samādhi of engaging without weariness in all the conduct of methods of the kalyāṇamitras.
meditation devoted to tireless application of the techniques of all spiritual friends.

rigs kyi bu/ ting nge 'dzin la nges par gzhag pa'i sgo bcu po de dag dang ldan pa'i byang chub sems dpa' ni/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen thams cad dang mngon du gyur pa 'thob pa yin te/ ting nge 'dzin gyi rnam par thar ba de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi chos kyi 'khor lo dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi kha nas grags pa zhes bya ba yang 'thob pas/ de la zhugs pa'i byang chub sems dpa' ni/ sangs rgyas thams cad tha mi dad cing mnyam pa nyid du gyur pa yang rab tu 'thob bo/ / dge ba'i bshes gnyen tha mi dad cing thams cad du khyab pa 'di rab tu thob par 'gyur ro/ /

“Noble one, the bodhisattva who has those ten qualities will attain the direct perception of all kalyāṇamitras. The bodhisattva who attains the liberation of the samādhi called the Dharma wheels of all the tathāgatas proclaimed from the mouth of the kalyāṇamitra will, by entering it, attain the undifferentiated equality of all buddhas and the undifferentiated omnipresence of the kalyāṇamitras.”

The enlightening being who has accomplished these ten kinds of concentrated meditation comes face to face with all spiritual friends and attains a liberation through concentration called ‘enunciation of the teachings of all buddhas by spiritual friends,’ practicing which the enlightening being realizes the indivisible sameness of all buddhas and finds spiritual friends everywhere in contact.”
srin po'i dbang po mig bzang gis de skad ces smras pa dang /
That is what Sunetra, the lord of the rākṣasas, said.
Having been told this by the supernatural being,

tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis nam mkha'i dbyings la bltas te 'di skad ces smras so/ / 'phags pa/ bdag la thugs brtse bar mdzad de/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen bsten pas sman yon btags pa ma nongs so/ / da dung yang dge ba'i bshes gnyen blta ba'i slad du ji ltar brtson par bgyi ba dang / phyogs gang logs su mchi bar bgyi ba dang / gnas gang zhig tu yongs su btsal ba dang / dmigs pa gang zhig bsam par bgyi ba'i thabs kyi sgo ma nor bar bstan du gsol/

Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, stared into the sky and said, “Ārya,[1863] you have regarded me with compassion and without error taught[1864] the kalyāṇamitras in order to benefit[1865] me. In addition, I pray that you teach me without error the entrance ways to methods concerning how to apply myself to seeing the kalyāṇamitras, in what direction I should go, in what places I should search, and upon what goal I should focus my thoughts.”

Sudhana looked up to the sky and said, “Bravo, O noble one, sympathetic one; you are trying to help me and show me spiritual friends. Tell me, in the right way, how to proceed; where should I go? Where should I search? What should I meditate on to see spiritual friends?”

smras pa/ rigs kyi bu/ de bas na/ phyogs kun tu rab tu 'dud pa'i lus dang / dmigs pa thams cad du dge ba'i bshes gnyen dran pa dang 'brel ba'i bsam pa dang / kun tu 'gro ba'i ting nge 'dzin gyi rjes su 'brang ba dang / sems kyi shugs rmi lam lta bu dang / yid kyi lus gzugs brnyan lta bus rnam par rgyu ste 'gro bas dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi gan du song zhig /

Sunetra, the lord of the rākṣasas, replied, “Noble one, you should go to the kalyāṇamitras by going with a body that bows down in every direction, with thoughts that are fastened on remembering the kalyāṇamitras as their object, following the samādhi that goes everywhere, with strength of mind that is like a dream, and traveling with a body of the mind that is like a reflection.”

The supernatural being said, “One may go into the presence of spiritual friends by an attitude of universal respect, by mental focus on remembering spiritual friends in all things, by concentration speeding everywhere by dreamlike speed of mind, by realizing mind and body as like reflections.”

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis srin po'i dbang po mig bzang gis ji skad du gtam pa de ltar nan tan du byas pa dang / mdun gyi sa'i nang nas pad+mo chen po rdo rje rin po che thams cad las grub pa'i chu ba can; nang rim rin po che'i rgyal po 'gro ba rgya mtsho sna tshogs las byas pa/ rin po che'i rgyal po thams cad las 'dab ma'i phreng ba grub pa/ rin po che'i rgyal po rnam par snang ba'i snying po can/ spos kyi rin po che'i rgyal po rin po che thams cad gyi mdog gi ze ba dang ldan pa/ rin po che'i dra ba grangs med pas kun nas yog pa byung ba mthong ngo/ /

Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, practicing as he had been told by Sunetra, the lord of the rākṣasas, saw rising from the ground before him a great lotus with a stem made entirely from diamond jewels, with sepals made from a variety of kings of jewels of the world’s[1866] oceans, with a circle of petals formed from all kings of jewels, with a pericarp made of shining kings of jewels, with filaments the colors and aromas of all the precious kings of jewels, and covered by a net of countless jewels.[1867]
Then Sudhana, practicing as he had been taught by the supernatural being Fine Eye, saw a great jewel lotus spring up from the ground in front of him.

rin po che'i rgyal po'i pad+mo chen po de'i snying po la'ang khang pa brtsegs pa chos kyi phyogs su yang dag par gzhol ba'i snying po zhes bya ba/ shin tu spa la blta na sdug pa; sa'i gzhi rnam par snang ba'i dbyibs dang ldan pa/ rin po che rgyal po thams cad las byas pa'i ka ba stong tshang bas mdzes par brgyan pa/ rgyan thams cad du rin po che thams cad bkram pa/ 'dzam bu chu klung gi gser dri ma med pa'i lha rdzas kyi gzhi bting ba/ mu tig gi phreng ba sna tshogs kyi dra ba grangs med pa kun nas bres pa; rin po che'i rgyal po sna tshogs rab tu spa bar spel bas brgyan pa/ dzam+bu chu klung gi nor bu rin po ches kun nas rnam par phye ba/ rin po che'i khri 'phang grangs med pas kun nas bskor ba/ phyogs thams cad nas rin po che rgyal po'i them skas mdzes par bkye ba gnas par mthong ngo/ /

He saw on the pericarp of that great lotus made of the kings of jewels a kūṭāgāra called Dharmadhātudiksamavasaraṇagarbha, which was well adorned and beautiful, with a base that was the shape of a shining vajra.[1868] A full thousand pillars made from the kings of jewels beautifully adorned it. Every kind of jewel was displayed as every kind of adornment. Its floor was made of divine Jambu River gold. Countless nets of various strings of pearls were spread upon it. It was adorned by a beautifying blend of various kings of jewels. It had a complete array[1869] of the precious jewels of Jambudhvaja.[1870] It was encircled by countless precious balconies. On all sides, stairways made of kings of jewels were beautifully arranged.
In the heart of the lotus he saw a tower called ‘chamber containing the cosmos,’ beautifully made of gold and jewels.
khang pa brtsegs pa de'i dbus na yang khri nor bu rin po che yid bzhin gyi pad+mo'i snying po can/
He saw in the center of the kūṭāgāra a throne of wish-fulfilling jewels with a lotus on its center.
Inside the tower he saw a lotus calyx throne made of wish-fulfilling jewels,
nor bu rin po che'i gzugs 'jig rten gyi dbang po'i dbyibs lta bu'i rten gyis bzung ba/
It was composed of precious jewels, and its base had the representations of all[1871] the lords of the world.
set on jewel figurines of the chiefs of all realms of being,
nor bu rin po che'i 'bru thams cad kyi kha dog tu 'dug pa/
It had the colors of all gems of precious jewels.
arrayed with many kinds of precious adornments
dbang po'i rgyal mtshan rab tu snang ba'i dbyibs su 'dug pa/
It had the shape of Indra’s radiant banner.
rdo rje rin po che'i 'khor lo'i sa la brten pa/
It was set upon the surface of a ground that was a circle of precious diamonds.
rin po che'i rgyal po sna tshogs kyi phreng bas brgyan pa;
It had an array of rows of various kings of jewels.
rin po che'i khri 'phang du ma las blangs pa/
It was encircled by many precious platforms.
rin po che'i rgyal po snang ba'i rgyal mtshan gyis rab tu spras pa/
It was decorated by shining banners of kings of jewels.
rin po che sna tshogs kyi rgyan gyis shin tu brgyan pa/
It was beautified by an array of various jewels.
rin po che'i rgyal po'i stan lha rdzas las 'das pa legs par bting ba/
Upon it was placed a cushion that was superior to divine material.
gos rin po che kha dog mtha' yas pa sna tshogs kyis gzhi thams cad du bkram pa/
Its surface was covered with precious cloths of various infinite colors.
rin po che'i gos thams cad kyi gnam yol bres pas nam mkha' rab tu brgyan pa/
Decorative canopies of all kinds of precious cloth adorned the sky.
rin po che thams cad kyi dra ba kun tu bres pa/
It was draped in nets of all jewels.
phyogs kun nas rin po che'i rgyal mtshan dkrigs pa'i sgra 'byung ba;
In all directions there was the sound of the flapping of arrayed precious banners.
rin po che thams cad kyi snam bu'i rgyal mtshan phur lab tu lding ba/
Banners of cloth made of all jewels fluttered.
spos rin po che thams cad kyi rgyal mtshan rnam par bres pas kun nas brgyan pa/
It was adorned by an arrangement of banners of all precious aromatic jewels.
me tog thams cad kyi rgyal mtshan las me tog gi klong sna tshogs char du mngon par 'brul ba/
Banners made of all flowers emitted a rain of showers of various flowers.
rin po che'i dril bu'i rgyal mtshan 'khrol ba'i sgra yid bde ba'i dbyangs snyan par grags pa/
Banners of precious bells emitted melodious, beautiful sounds.
and bells which emanated sounds
khang pa'i kha thams cad nas rin po che sna tshogs kyi phreng ba rab tu dpyangs pa/
All the entrances[1872] of the building were decorated[1873] with strings of various jewels.
rin po che'i gzugs sna tshogs kyi kha nas spos chu kha dog du ma dang ldan pa'i char 'bab pa/
From various precious jewels in the form of spouts issued a rain of scented water in many different colors.
nor bu rin po che'i rgyal po rnam par snang ba las glang po dam pa'i gzugs su byas pa'i kha nas pad+mo'i dra ba 'byung ba dang ldan pa/
From the mouths of elephant lords formed from shining kings of precious jewels came[1874] networks of lotuses.
rdo rje sna tshogs kyi seng+ge'i kha nas spos kyi sprin kha dog mtha' yas pa rab tu 'byung ba/
From the mouths of lions made of a variety of diamonds came[1875] clouds of incense in endless colors.
rin po che'i rgyal po rnam par snang ba tshangs pa'i gzugs su 'dug pa'i kha nas byams pa chen po'i tshul tshangs pa'i dbyangs kyi nga ror sgrog pa dang ldan pa/
From the mouths of statues of Brahmā made from shining kings of jewels there resounded in a loving manner the sound of the voice of Brahmā.
telling of the principle of universal love,
rin po che sna tshogs shin tu mdzes pa'i gzugs kyi kha nas dkar po'i phyogs kyi legs pa rab tu rjod pa'i nga ro 'byung ba/
From the mouths of beautiful statues made of various jewels resounded the beautiful sounds of praises of goodness.
dus gsum gyi sangs rgyas kyi mtshan gser gyi dril gyi phreng ba las sgra snyan pa'i dbyangs su 'byung ba dang ldan pa/
From strings of golden bells were emitted the pleasant sounds of the names of the buddhas in the three times.
the names of the buddhas of past, present, and future,
nor bu rin po che dam pa'i dril gyi phreng ba las sangs rgyas thams cad kyi chos kyi 'khor lo'i sgra yid du 'ong ba 'byung ba dang /
From strings of bells made of excellent precious jewels came the beautiful sounds of the Dharma wheels of all the buddhas.
the teachings of all buddhas,
rdo rje'i dril sna tshogs las byang chub sems dpa'i smon lam thams cad kyi sgra rab tu 'byung ba/
From a variety of diamond bells came the sounds of all bodhisattva prayers.
and the vows of all enlightening beings.
rin po che'i rgyal po zla ba'i rgyal mtshan gyi phreng bas sangs rgyas thams cad kyi gzugs brnyan rab tu 'byung ba'i dbyings sna tshogs tu sgrog pa/
Various voices resounded from the images of all the buddhas that arose from strings of moonstone[1876] kings of jewels.
nor bu rin po che'i rgyal po snying po dag pa'i phreng bas dus gsum du gshegs pa'i de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi sku tshe gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa'i gzugs brnyan rnam par dmigs par bya ba/
From strings of emerald[1877] kings of precious jewels came manifestations of images of the successive lives of all the tathāgatas in the three times.
It was also arrayed with rows of jewels which reflected the manifestations of buddhas and the succession of births of all buddhas of past, present, and future,
rin po che'i rgyal po nyi ma'i snying po'i phreng bas nam mkha'i dbyings kyi mthas klas pa'i phyogs bcu'i sangs rgyas kyi zhing sna tshogs kyi dbyings su 'od zer yongs su bstan pa/
From strings of sunstone[1878] kings of jewels appeared light rays of the range of various buddha realms throughout the ten directions as far as the limits of the realm of space.
rows of radiant jewels showing the lights of the activities in all buddha-lands throughout space and the effecting of all miracles,
rin po che'i rgyal po snang ba'i rgyal mtshan gyi phreng bas de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi 'od kyi dkyil 'khor snang ba rab tu dbye ba/
From strings of avabhāsadhvaja kings of jewels shone the illumination of the halos of light of all the tathāgatas.
emanating the auras of light of all buddhas,
nor bu rin po che'i rgyal po snang ba'i phreng bas sprul pa'i sprin 'gro ba thams cad kyi dbang po lta bu/ de bzhin gshegs pa la mchod cing rim gro byed pa'i 'od rab tu dgye ba/
From strings of vairocana kings of jewels radiated light rays in the forms of emanated clouds of all the lords of worlds, who made offerings to and venerated the tathāgatas.
emanating apparitions like the chiefs of all worlds making offerings to buddhas,
rin po che'i rgyal po yid bzhin gyi phreng bas byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po'i rnam par 'phrul bas skad cig re re la chos kyi dbyings su rgyas par dgang ba/
From strings of wish-fulfilling kings of jewels there spread throughout the realm of phenomena in each instant the completely good miraculous manifestations of the bodhisattvas.
and jewels filling the cosmos in every moment with the mystic projections of the universally good enlightening being.

rin po che'i rgyal po ri bo'i rgyal mtshan gyi phreng bas lha'i dbang po thams cad kyi khyim gyi lha mo'i dbyangs snyan pa rab tu sgrog pa dang ldan zhing / khri de dmigs pa thams cad du de bzhin gshegs pa la bstod pa'i sprin 'gyed pas yon tan dang / legs pa bsam gyis mi khyab pa brjod du yod pa dang /

From strings of vairocana kings of jewels resounded the sound of the voices of all the apsarases in the palaces of all the lords of devas emitting clouds of praises of all perceived tathāgatas, describing their inconceivable good qualities.
Every object on the throne of inconceivable qualities emanated celestial eulogies of the enlightened.
rin po che'i rgyan grangs med pa'i 'khor gyi stan gyis bskor bar mthong ngo/ /
The throne was encircled by an array of seats made of countless jewels.
The throne was also surrounded by an inconceivable number of seats arrayed with jewels.
khri de la lha mo sgyu ma 'jig rten gsum las yang dag par 'das pa'i gzugs
He saw upon that throne Māyādevī. She had a form that transcended the three worlds.
Sudhana saw Lady Maya sitting on that throne, her physical form transcending all in the triple world, having gone beyond all states of being;
'jig rten thams cad la mngon par gnas pa dang / srid pa'i rgyud thams cad las gyen du 'phags pa'i gzugs
She had a form that resided in all worlds and was above all existences.
facing all beings, appearing according to their mentalities;
'gro ba thams cad kyis rnam par dmigs su yod pa dang / 'jig rten thams cad kyis ma gos pa'i gzugs
She had a form that was perceived by all beings according to their aspirations[1879] but was unstained by any world.
unstained by any world, being made of myriad virtues;
bsod nams yangs pas byung ba dang / 'gro ba thams cad dang mnyam zhing 'dra ba'i gzugs
She had a form that originated from vast merit and could resemble that of all beings.
in the likeness of all beings, appearing in such a way as to please all beings;
sems can thams cad la bzhin mngon par ston pa dang / 'gro ba thams cad yongs su smin par bya ba dang / gdul bar mthun pa'i gzugs
She had a form that appeared to all beings but in a way that would accord with ripening and guiding all beings.
adapted to develop and guide all beings, descending into the presence of all beings;
sems can thams cad dang mngon sum du 'dal ba dang / dus thams cad 'gro ba nam mkha' la rnam par dmigs pa tha mi dad pa'i gzugs
She had a form that was directly perceived by all beings but was at all times[1880] no different from beings’ perception of space.
appearing continuously to beings at all times like the sky, appearing to all beings to be permanent;
'gro ba thams cad kyi mthas klas par dmigs su yod par byin gyis rlob pa dang / 'gro ba med pa'i gzugs
She had a form that had the power to be present[1881] as perceivable throughout the extent of all beings without going anywhere.
not going anywhere, not passing away from all worlds,
'jig rten gyi lam gyi rgyud thams cad 'gag pa dang / 'ong ba med pa'i gzugs
She had a form that neither ceased nor came into existence within worlds.
not coming anywhere, not coming into existence in any world;
'gro ba thams cad du ma byung ba dang / ma skyes pa'i gzugs
She had a form that did not originate in and was not born in any world.
unoriginated, absorbed in the equanimity of nonorigination;
mi skye bar mnyam pa'i chos la brtson pa dang / ma 'gag pa'i gzugs
She had a form that was dedicated to having a quality the same as birthlessness but was also unceasing.
unextinguished,
'jig rten gyi rnam par spyod pa thams cad la gzhol ba dang / yang dag par dmigs pa'i gzugs
She had a form that engaged in all conducts within the world and was truly perceived.[1882]
involved in the affairs of all worlds;
bden pa med pa dang / 'jig rten gyis rnam par dmigs pa'i gzugs
She had a form that was not real but was perceived by the world.[1883]
not real, having attained suchness;
rdzun pa med pa dang / 'pho ba med pa'i gzugs
She had a form that was not false and did not pass away.[1884]
not false, appearing in accord with the world;
shi 'pho ba dang skye ba las 'das pa dang / mi 'jig pa'i gzugs
She had a form that transcended death and birth and was indestructible.
not in motion, being divorced from death and birth;
chos kyi dbyings kyi rang bzhin gyis 'jig pa med pa dang / mtshan nyid med pa'i gzugs
She had a form that had the indestructible nature of the realm of the Dharma and had no characteristics.
not annihilated, because of the nonannihilation of the nature of reality;
dus gsum tshig gi lam du gzhol ba dang / mtshan nyid gcig pa'i gzugs
She had a form that mastered the languages of the three times and had a single characteristic.
undefinable, being beyond any manner of speaking;
mtshan nyid med pas byung ba dang / gzugs brnyan lta bu'i gzugs
She had a form that came forth with the excellent characteristic[1885] of the absence of characteristics and was like a reflection.
uniform, her auspicious characteristics issuing from indefinability; like a reflection,
'gro ba thams cad kyi sems dang / bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du dmigs pa dang / sgyu ma lta bu'i gzugs
She had a form that was perceived by all beings in accordance with their motivations and aspirations and was like an illusion.
appearing according to the minds of all beings; like magic,
ye shes sgyu mas yongs su grub pa dang / smig rgyu lta bu'i gzugs
She had a form that was created by the illusion of wisdom and was like a mirage.
made of the magic of knowledge; like specks of light,
'gro ba'i 'du shes bzhin du byin gyis rlob pa la gzhol ba dang / grib ma lta bu'i gzugs
She had a form that was intent on being present[1886] in the perception of beings in each instant[1887] and was like a shadow.
moment to moment sustained by the thoughts of beings; like a shadow,
sngon gyi smon lam gyis 'gro ba thams cad kyi rjes su 'brang ba dang / rmi lam lta bu'i gzugs
She had a form that followed beings in accordance with her past prayers and was like a dream.
bound to all beings by commitment; dreamlike,
bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du 'gro bas dmigs pa la ma 'dres pa dang / chos kyi dbyings thams cad du gzhol ba'i gzugs
She had a form that was perceived separately by beings according to their dispositions and was active in the entire realm of phenomena.
appearing to beings according to their mentalities without being mixed up; reaching throughout all universes,
nam mkha'i dbyings ltar rang bzhin yongs su dag pa dang / snying rje chen pos byung ba'i gzugs
She had a form that had a pure nature like the realm of space and arose from great compassion.
being in nature pure as space; issuing from universal compassion,
sems can gyi rgyud thams cad yongs su bskyang ba la brtson pa dang / chags pa med pa'i sgos byung ba'i gzugs
She had a form that was dedicated to protecting all the classes of beings and arose through the gateway of the absence of attachment.
engaged in the protection of the community of beings; issuing from the door of nonobstruction,
skad cig re res chos kyi dbyings rgyas par 'gengs pa dang / mtha' dang dbus med pa'i gzugs
She had a form that pervaded in each instant the entire realm of phenomena and had no end or middle.
pervading the cosmos in each instant; infinite,
rnyog pa med par 'gro ba thams cad la brten pa dang / tshad med pa'i gzugs
She had a form that was dependent on all beings without being polluted by them and was immeasurable.
dwelling in all worlds without defilement; measureless,
tshig gi lam thams cad las yang dag par 'das pa dang / mi gnas pa'i gzugs
She had a form that transcended all words and had no location.
transcending all manner of verbal expression; nondwelling,
'gro ba thams cad gdul ba'i byin gyi rlabs kyis grub pa dang / byin gyis ma brlabs pa'i gzugs
She had a form that was an accomplished presence[1888] that guided all beings and had no presence.[1889]
manifesting to guide all beings; unfixed,
byin gyi rlabs kyis 'gro ba'i don la brtson pa dang / ma byung ba'i gzugs
She had a form that through its presence was dedicated to benefiting beings and did not occur.[1890]
appearing magically in the body of a living being; not really existing,
smon lam sgyu mas yongs su grub pa dang / zil gyis mi non pa'i gzugs
She had a form that was created through the conjured illusion of prayer and was unsurpassable.
made by the magic of aspiration; unsurpassed,
'jig rten thams cad las mngon par 'phags pa dang / yang dag pa ma yin pa'i gzugs
She had a form that was above all worlds and was not what it seemed to be.
being beyond all worlds; unreal,
zhi gnas kyi snang bas rnam par dmigs pa dang / mi 'byung ba'i gzugs
She had a form that was perceived through the light of śamatha and was without origin.
being a manifestation of tranquillity; unproduced,

'gro ba'i las ji lta ba bzhin du rjes su 'brang ba dang / rin po che yid bzhin gyi rgyal po ltar bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du sems can thams cad kyi bsam pa yongs su rdzogs par bya ba'i smon lam yongs su grub pa dang / rnam par mi rtog pa'i gzugs
She had a form that followed beings in accordance with their karma and accomplished the prayers to fulfill the wishes of all beings like the king of wish-fulfilling jewels, without thought.
'gro ba thams cad kyi yongs su rtog pa bzhin du nye bar gnas pa dang / mi rtog pas rtog pa med pa'i gzugs
She had a form that was present in accordance with the conceptions of all beings and, having no thought, was nonconceptual.
based on the thoughts of all beings; beyond conception,
'gro ba thams cad kyi rnam par dmigs pa dang / thogs pa med pa'i gzugs
She had a form that was perceived by all beings and was without impediment.
unknowable to all beings;
'khor ba las bzlog pa la rab tu brtson pa dang / rnam par dag pa'i gzugs
She had a form that was dedicated to turning beings away from saṃsāra and was completely pure.
based on resolve, never leaving the mundane;
de bzhin nyid dang mnyam par rnam par mi rtog pa dang / rnam pa de lta bu'i gzugs
She had a form that, like the true nature, was without conceptualization and had that kind of mode.
pure, nonconceptual like Thusness.
gzugs med par gzugs su snang ba dang / tshor ba med pa'i gzugs kyis
She had a form that appeared as form without having form and was without sensation.
In this form did Sudhana see Lady Maya, manifesting a physical body that was not form, being a reflection of form; not feeling,
'jig rten gyi sdug bsngal gyi tshor ba rab tu zhi bar bya ba la brtson pa dang / 'du shes kyi rnam pa thams cad las gyen du 'phags pa'i gzugs
She had a form that was dedicated to the cessation of the sensations of worldly suffering and was above all the conceptualizations of beings.
being the ultimate cessation of painful feelings of the world; outside the thoughts of all beings,
sems can thams cad kyi 'du shes kyi rnam pas rnam par dmigs pa dang / mngon par 'du bya ba med pa'i chos nyid kyis byung ba'i gzugs
She had a form that was perceived by the perceptions of all beings and arose through the nature of not being formed.
but appearing in their thoughts; issuing from the unfabricated nature of reality,
chos sgyu ma'i rnam pas grub pa dang / rnam par shes pa'i yul las yongs su 'das pa'i gzugs
She had a form that occurred through the quality of illusory conjuration and transcended being an object of consciousness.
detached from illusory action; transcending the sphere of discriminatory consciousness,
byang chub sems dpa'i smon lam gyi ye shes las byung ba dang / rang bzhin med pa'i gzugs
She had a form that arose from the wisdom of bodhisattva prayer and had no nature of its own.
born of the knowledge of vows of enlightening beings; having no intrinsic essence,
'gro ba thams cad kyi tshig gi lam la gzhol ba dang / gdung ba yongs su bsal ba'i gzugs
She had a form that engaged in the languages of all beings and dispelled pain.
being beyond the range of all verbal expression; free from the burning of the mundane whirl,

chos kyi sku bsil ba dam pa dang ldan pas lha mo sgyu ma bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du 'gro ba'i gzugs kyi lus yongs su ston pa dang / sems can gyi bsam pa'i dbang du 'gro ba thams cad dang mnyam zhing 'dra ba'i gzugs kyi lus 'gro ba thams cad kyi gzugs kyi lus las 'phags pa ston cing 'dug pa mthong ngo/ /

Through possessing the supreme coolness of the Dharma body, Māyādevī revealed a form body in accordance with the aspirations of beings. In accordance with the aspirations of beings, she manifested bodies that resembled those of all beings and were superior to the form bodies of all beings.

having arrived at the state of supreme coolness of the reality-body—she was appearing physically to beings in accord with their minds by mastery of their minds, appearing in forms resembling all beings but superior to the physical forms of all beings.
de la sems can la las ni/ lha mo sgyu ma de bdud kyi bu mo'i gzugs su 'dug la/ bdud kyi bu mo'i gzugs pas kyang lhag par mthong ngo/ /
Some beings saw Māyādevī in the form of a daughter of Māra but superior to the form of a daughter of Māra.
Some beings saw her in the form of a devil woman, with a form superlative among devil women;
la las ni/ dbang sgyur gyi lha'i bu mo'i gzugs pas kyang lhag par mthong ngo/ /
Some saw her as superior through having the form of one of Vaśavartin’s apsarases.
some saw her in forms superlative among the goddesses of various heavens;
la las ni/ rab 'phrul dga'i lha'i bu mo'i gzugs pas kyang lhag par mthong ngo/ /
Some saw her as superior through having the form of one of Sunirmita’s apsarases.
la las ni/ rab dga' ldan gyi lha'i bu mo'i gzugs pas kyang lhag par mthong ngo/ /
Some saw her as superior through having the form of one of Saṃtuṣita’s apsarases.
la las ni/ rab mtsho ma'i lha'i bu mo'i gzugs pas kyang lhag par mthong ngo/ /
Some saw her as superior through having the form of one of Suyāma’s apsarases.
some saw her in forms superlative among the females of the various kinds of beings;
la las ni/ sum cu rtsa gsum gyi lha'i bu mo'i gzugs pas kyang lhag par mthong ngo/ /
Some saw her as superior through having the form of a Trāyastriṃśa apsaras.
la las ni/ rgyal po chen po bzhi'i ris kyi lha'i bu mo'i gzugs pas kyang lhag par mthong ngo/ /
Some saw her as superior through having the form of a Caturmahārājika apsaras.
la las ni/ grul bum gyi bu mo'i gzugs pas kyang lhag par mthong ngo/ /
Some saw her as superior through having the form of a daughter of a lord of kumbhāṇḍas.
la las ni/ lto 'phye chen po'i dbang po'i bu mo'i gzugs pas kyang lhag par mthong ngo/ /
Some saw her as superior through having the form of a daughter of a lord of mahoragas.
sems can la las ni/ lha mo sgyu ma de mi'i dbang po'i bu mo'i gzugs pas kyang lhag par mthong ngo/ /
Some beings saw her as superior through having the form of a daughter of a lord of humans.
some saw her in the form of a most beautiful human princess.

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang 'gro ba thams cad kyi gzugs kyi 'du shes dang bral yang sems can pha rol gyi bsam pa la 'jug pa des sems can thams cad kyi bsam pa'i rnam pa la lha mo sgyu ma 'gro ba thams cad nye bar 'tsho ba'i bsod nams dang ldan pa/ thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi bsod nams kyis bsgrubs pa'i lus dang ldan pa/

Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, although devoid of the concepts of the forms of all beings, was comprehending the thoughts of other beings, and he saw that in the thoughts of all beings Māyādevī had the merit to care for all beings; she had a body created by the merit of omniscience;

Then Sudhana, emptied of notions of the forms of all beings, penetrating the minds of other beings, saw Lady Maya in the minds of all beings, her virtue sustaining all beings, her body an accumulation of the virtues of omniscience;
sbyin pa'i pha rol tu phyin pa'i sbyor ba tha mi dad pa dang ldan pa/ 'gro ba thams cad la mnyam pa nyid kyis zhugs pa/ snying rje chen po'i lus su sems can thams cad yongs su sdud pa/
she was engaged in nondiscriminatory perfect giving, impartial toward all beings, having united all beings in the fellowship of universal compassion;
de bzhin gshegs pa'i yon tan thams cad nan tan du byas pas byung ba/
she manifested from the practice of all the qualities of the tathāgatas;
she had set out to actualize the virtues of all buddhas;
bzod pa thams cad kyi tshul rgya mtsho la zhugs pa/
she had entered an ocean of all the ways of patience;
she had entered the ocean of all ways of tolerance;
thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi brtson 'grus kyi shugs kyis sems rnam par spel ba/
she increased mentation[1891] through the power of the diligence of omniscience;
her mind was expanded with a flood of energy of omniscience;
chos kyi dkyil 'khor thams cad yongs su dag par bya ba la phyir mi ldog pa'i brtson 'grus dang ldan pa/
she possessed the constant diligence that purified the entire field of phenomena;
she was indefatigable in clarification of all spheres of truth;
chos thams cad kyi rang bzhin nges par rtogs pas byung ba/
she had arisen from the realization of the nature of phenomena;
she was adept in meditation on the essence of all things;
bsam gtan gyi yan lag dang tshul thams cad las yongs su grub pa'i sems dang ldan pa/
she possessed a mind that had accomplished all the ways of the branches of dhyāna;
her mind was accomplished in all branches of meditation;
bsam gtan gyi yan lag tha mi dad pa'i yul yongs su 'dzin pa'i de bzhin gshegs pa'i bsam gtan gyi dkyil 'khor snang ba rab tu thob pa/
she had attained the illumination of the field of dhyāna of the tathāgatas that possesses the undifferentiated range of the branches of dhyāna;
she was engaged in all branches of meditation without confusion and had perceived the unique sphere of meditation of those who arrive at Thusness;
sems can thams cad kyi nyon mongs pa rgya mtsho bskam pa la shin tu gdon mi za bar byas pa'i nges par rtogs pa sna tshogs la gnas pa;
she dwelled in various realizations of how to definitively dry up the ocean of the kleśas of all beings;
she was intent on various meditations to evaporate the ocean of afflictions of all beings;
de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi chos kyi 'khor lo rnam par dbye ba'i tshul la mkhas pa/
she had skill in the way of differentiating the Dharma wheels of all tathāgatas;
she knew how to analyze the teachings of all buddhas;
chos thams cad kyi tshul rgya mtsho rnam par dpyad pa'i shes rab dang ldan pa/
she had the wisdom to analyze the ocean of all the ways of the Dharma;
she had the wisdom to consider all the designs of reality;
de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad mthong bas ma ngoms pa/
she never had enough of seeing all the tathāgatas;
she gazed tirelessly on all buddhas;
dus gsum gyi de bzhin gshegs pa gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa la rnam par lta ba'i rgyun mi gcod pa/
she had the continuous vision of the successions of the tathāgatas in the three times;
she ceaselessly observed the succession of buddhas of past, present, and future;
sangs rgyas thams cad lta ba'i sgo la mngon du gyur pa/
she faced the gateway to seeing all the buddhas;
she faced the door of vision of all buddhas;
de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyis yongs su bsgrubs pa'i lam yongs su dag par bya ba; rnam pa tha dad pa'i tshul la mkhas pa/
she was skilled in the different ways of purifying the path accomplished by all the tathāgatas;
she knew the variety of techniques to perfectly accomplish the path of attainment of all buddhas;
de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi spyod yul nam mkha' dang mnyam pa/
she had the field of activity of the tathāgatas, which is as extensive as space;
she coursed in the space of all who realize Thusness;
sems can thams cad yongs su bsdu ba'i thabs kyi tshul la mkhas pa/
she was skilled in the ways of the method of gathering all beings;
she knew how to take care of all beings;
'gro ba mtha' dang dbus med pa bsam pa ji lta ba bzhin du yongs su smin par bya ba dang gdul ba'i snang ba rab tu thob pa/
she had appearances that ripened and guided the vast extent of beings, without end or middle, in accordance with their aspirations;
she appeared in an infinite variety of reflections to develop and guide beings according to their mentalities;
sangs rgyas thams cad kyi sku rnam par dag pa rnam pa tha dad pa la zhugs pa/
she comprehended the different pure bodies of all buddhas;
she comprehended the variety of purities of all buddha-bodies;
zhing rgya mtsho thams cad yongs su dag par bya ba'i smon lam dang ldan pa/
she had the prayer to purify the ocean of all realms;
she had vowed to purify all lands;
sems can gyi khams thams cad rnam par gdul ba'i byin gyi rlabs mthar thug par bya ba'i smon lam yongs su dag pa/
she had the pure prayer to reach the conclusion of having the presence with the power to guide all realms of beings;
she had perfected the vow to guide all beings to ultimate liberation;
de bzhin gshegs pa'i yul thams cad mchod pas rgyas par dgang ba'i sems dang ldan pa/
she had a mind that fills with offering the field of all buddhas;
her mind pervaded the spheres of all buddhas with respect;
byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par 'phrul pa thams cad la brtson pas byung ba/
she had arisen from dedication to all the miraculous manifestations of bodhisattvas;
she had the energy to produce all the miracles of enlightening beings;
chos kyi sku bla na med pa yongs su dag pa dang ldan pa/
she possessed the pure, unsurpassable Dharma body;
she had purified the supreme spiritual body;
gzugs kyi lus mtha' yas pa yongs su ston pa/
she manifested endless form bodies;
she manifested infinite physical bodies;
bdud kyi dpung thams cad rab tu 'joms pa/
she defeated all the armies of Māra;
she crushed the power of all demons;
dge ba'i rtsa ba shin tu rgya chen po'i stobs dang ldan pa/
she possessed the strength of vast roots of merit;
she was imbued with the power of great roots of goodness;
chos kyi stobs rab tu sgyes pa'i blo can/ sangs rgyas kyi stobs snang ba rab tu thob pa/
she had a mind that generated the strength of the Dharma; she had attained the illumination of the strengths of the buddhas;
with intellect born of the power of truth she perceived the power of buddhas;
byang chub sems dpa'i dbang thams cad kyi stobs yongs su rdzogs pa/
she had perfected the strength of all the powers of a bodhisattva;
she had perfected all powers of mastery of enlightening beings;
thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi shugs kyi stobs yongs su skyes pa/
she had developed the strength of the power of omniscience;
she was flooded with the power of omniscience;
de bzhin gshegs pa'i ye shes glog gi shes rab snang bar byas pa/
she had illuminated wisdom with the lightning of the wisdom of the tathāgatas;
her wisdom was illumined by the lightning of the knowledge of all buddhas;
sems can mtha' dang dbus med pa'i sems rgya mtsho rnam par dpyad pa la mkhas pa;
she was skilled in examining the ocean of the minds of the vast, centerless, endless extent of beings;
her knowledge contemplated the infinite ocean of minds of beings;
'gro ba shin tu mang ba'i bsam pa la zhugs pa/
she comprehended the aspirations of the multitudes of beings;
she comprehended the myriad mentalities of beings;
sems can pha rol gyi dbang po rnam pa tha dad pa shes par bya ba'i tshul la mkhas pa/
she was skilled in the ways of knowing the different capabilities of other beings;
she was expert in knowledge of the differences in faculties of others;
sems can mtha' yas pa'i mos pa rnam pa tha dad pa'i rgyus la mkhas par khong du chud pa/
she had realized the skill in knowing the various aspirations of infinite beings;
she was skilled in knowledge of the differences in interests of infinite beings;
phyogs bcu'i zhing rgya mtsho tshad med pa lus kyis rgyas par 'gengs pa/
she filled the measureless ocean of realms in the ten directions with her bodies;
her body pervaded infinite oceans of lands in the ten directions;
'jig rten gyi khams rnam pa tha dad pa thams cad shes par bya ba'i tshul dang rnam pa la mkhas pa/
she was skilled in the aspects and ways of knowing all the different world realms;
she was expert in knowledge of the differences in all worlds;
zhing tha dad pa'i tshul thams cad shes par bya ba'i tshul la mkhas pa'i rjes su song ba/
she had acquired skill in the ways of knowing all the modes of different realms;
she was skilled in the means of knowing the junction and disjunction of all lands;
ye shes kyis lta ba phyogs rgya mtsho thams cad du rab tu 'dal ba/
she spread the view of wisdom throughout the ocean of all directions;
she saw throughout all realms by knowledge;
dus rgya mtsho thams cad du khyab pa'i blo dang ldan pa/
she had the understanding that pervades all the ocean of all time;
she was aware of all times;
sangs rgyas rgya mtsho thams cad la mngon sum du 'dud pa'i lus can/
she had bodies that bow down directly to the ocean of all buddhas;
she bowed to all buddhas;
chos kyi sprin rgya mtsho'i char thams cad yang dag par gzung ba la mngon du gyur pa'i sems dang ldan pa/
she had a mind that directly acquired all the rain from the ocean of the clouds of the Dharma;
her mind was directed toward reception of the ocean of all buddha-teachings;
de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi yon tan rab tu rdzogs par bya ba'i nan tan gyis 'byung ba la rab tu brtson pa/
she was dedicated to coming forth through the practice of completing the qualities of all the tathāgatas;
she was engaged in accomplishing fulfillment of all qualities of buddhas;
byang chub sems dpa'i tshogs thams cad yongs su sgrub pa la rab tu zhugs pa'i blo dang ldan pa/
she had the understanding that engaged in accomplishing all the accumulations of the bodhisattvas;
her intellect was applied to the production of all the provisions for enlightenment;
byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi rab tu 'jug pa la rnam par dpyod pa'i mthu yod pa/
she possessed the power of analyzing the progress of all bodhisattvas;
she boldly considered and carried out all the undertakings of enlightening beings;
byang chub kyi sems kyi yan lag thams cad yongs su grub pa/
she accomplished all the aspects of the aspiration to enlightenment;
she had completed all the elements of development of the will for enlightenment;
byang chub sems dpa' thams cad yongs su bskyang ba la rab tu brtson pa/
she was engaged in protecting all bodhisattvas;
she was engaged in protecting all beings;
sangs rgyas thams cad kyi legs pa'i sprin kun tu snang ba rab tu ston pa/
she manifested the light of the clouds of the goodness of all buddhas;
she undertook to be the mother of all enlightening beings and buddhas.
byang chub sems dpa' dang / rgyal ba thams cad skyed pa'i smon lam gyis byung ba dang /
and she had arisen from the prayers that give birth to all bodhisattvas and jinas.
de dag la sogs pa mthong ba'i tshul 'dzam bu'i gling gi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi lha mo sgyu ma tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis mthong bar gyur to/ /
Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, saw Māyādevī in those ways and in other ways as numerous as the atoms in Jambudvīpa.
Beginning with these, Sudhana saw Lady Maya in as many ways as atoms in the continent:

des de mthong nas lha mo sgyu ma ji snyed yod pa de snyed du bdag gi lus byin gyis brlabs nas phyogs thams cad la mngon du bltas pa'i lha mo sgyu ma la thams cad du khyab pa'i lus kyis phyag byas so/ /
Having seen that, he blessed his own body to be as numerous as those of Māyādevī and bowed down to them with bodies that spread among them all.
seeing her, he magically made his body as extensive as Lady Maya, and with this omnipresent body bowed to the ubiquitous Maya.

des de ltar phyag byas ma thag tu ting nge 'dzin gyi sgo mtha' dang dbus med pa thob par gyur te/ des ting nge 'dzin gyi sgo de dag la rnam par bltas nas mtshan mar bya ba dang / bsgom pa dang / lhur blang ba dang / rjes su dran par bya ba dang / rgyas par dgang ba dang / rab tu rgya cher bya ba dang / blta ba dang / rnam par spel ba dang / mngon par bsgrub pa dang / rgyas gdab par byas te

The instant he bowed down, he attained a vast extent, without middle or end, of entrances to samādhi. He looked upon those entrances to samādhi, identified their characteristics, meditated on them, devoted himself to them, remembered them, pervaded them, made them vast, viewed them, increased them, accomplished them, and sealed them.

As he was bowing, an infinite variety of concentrations entered into him. Observing those concentrations, making them externally undetectable, cultivating them, mastering them, remembering them, making them all-pervasive, expanding them, watching them, increasing them, accomplishing them, and fixing their impression,

ting nge 'dzin gyi sgo de dag las langs nas lha mo sgyu ma 'khor dang bcas/ gnas dang bcas/ stan dang bcas pa la g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas te mdun du 'dug nas thal mo sbyar te 'di skad ces smras so/ /

He arose from those entrances to samādhi and circumambulated Māyādevī and her entourage, keeping her to his right, and their residence and seats. Then he stood before her with hands together in homage and said,
he rose from those concentrations and circled Lady Maya, her retinue, her abode and seat, and then stood respectfully before her and said,

'phags ma/ bdag ni/ 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pas bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed de/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen bsnyen bkur ba la yongs su bskul ba bgyis pa ste/ de ltar bdag dge ba'i bshes gnyen nas dge ba'i bshes gnyen du bsnyen bkur bgyid cing / mthar gyis khyod kyi zhabs kyi drung 'di'i bar du mchis pa lags na/

“Āryā, through Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta I have developed the aspiration for the highest, complete enlightenment and was inspired to honor the kalyāṇamitras. In that way, I have honored one kalyāṇamitra after another and have finally come to your feet.

“Noble one, Manjushri inspired me to seek supreme perfect enlightenment and directed me to attend spiritual benefactors. So I have been approaching spiritual friends, benefactors, and in the course of doing so I have come to you.
'phags ma/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab na/ rnam pa thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du 'grub pa lags/
“Āryā, how does a bodhisattva train in bodhisattva conduct and accomplish omniscience?”
Now please tell me, noble one, how an enlightening being may achieve omniscience while carrying out the practice of enlightening beings.”
des smras pa/ rigs kyi bu/ kho mo ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa smon lam chen po'i ye shes sgyu ma'i rnam pas rnam par brgyan pa thob pa ste/
Māyādevī answered, “Noble one, I have attained the bodhisattva liberation called the display of the illusory conjurations of wisdom of the great prayers.
She said, “I have attained an enlightening liberation, ‘magical manifestation of knowledge of great vows.’

rigs kyi bu/ kho mo rnam par thar pa de dang ldan pas 'jig rten gyi khams rgya mtsho 'di'i 'jig rten gyi khams thams cad kyi 'dzam bu'i gling thams cad na bcom ldan 'das rnam par snang mdzad kyi byang chub sems dpa'i srid pa'i tha ma la skye ba'i rnam par 'phrul pa ji snyed cig yod pa'i byang chub sems dpa' srid pa'i tha ma pa de dag thams cad so so'i mar gyur pa ste/ byang chub sems dpa' de dag thams cad kyang kho mo'i lto na gnas pa/ kho mo'i lto g.yas pa nas 'byung ngo/ /

“Noble one, through possessing that liberation, I have become the mother of each one of all the bodhisattvas in their final existences who are the Bhagavat Vairocana’s miraculous manifestations of being born into the final existences of a bodhisattva in all the Jambudvīpas in all the world realms in this ocean of world realms. All those bodhisattvas have resided in my belly and emerged from the right side of my belly.

Imbued with this liberation, I am the mother of all the enlightening beings in their final existence in all the worlds in this world-ocean where Vairocana Buddha’s miraculous manifestation of birth as an enlightening being in the final existence takes place. All those enlightening beings grow in my belly and come forth from my right side.

rigs kyi bu/ skal pa dang ldan pa'i gling bzhi pa 'di nyid kyi grong khyer chen po ser skya'i gnas su yang rgyal po zas gtsang ma'i btsun mo'i rigs dang ldan pa'i tshul gyis byang chub sems dpa' don grub byang chub sems dpa' skye ba'i rnam par 'phrul pa rgya chen po bsam gyis mi khyab pas bskyed do/ /

“Noble one, in the location of the great city of Kapilavastu in this fortunate four-continent world, as a queen in the family of King Śuddhodana, I gave birth to the bodhisattva Siddhārtha in an inconceivable, vast, miraculous manifestation of a bodhisattva’s birth.

So here too in this great city of Kapilavastu, as wife of the king Shuddhodana, I became the mother of the enlightening being Siddhartha, by the great inconceivable miracle of the birth of an enlightening being.

rigs kyi bu/ de ltar kho mo rgyal po zas gtsang ma'i pho brang na 'dug 'dug pa las/ byang chub sems dpa' dga' ldan gyi pho brang nas 'pho ba'i dus la bab pa dang / ba spu'i sgo thams cad kyi ba spu'i sgo re re nas kyang 'od zer de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi yum gyi yon tan gyi dkyil 'khor las byung ba'i snang ba zhes bya ba mang po byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi yum gyi yon tan gyi rgyan sangs rgyas kyi zhing brjod du med pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed thon nas 'jig rten gyi khams thams cad snang bar byas te kho mo'i lus la shar nas spyi bo man chad ba spu'i bu ga thams cad du 'phros par gyur to/ /

“Noble one, while I was living in the palace of King Śuddhodana, the time came for the bodhisattva to leave Tuṣita.
