From all his pores, from each of his pores, shone many light rays, as numerous as the atoms in countless buddha realms, called the illumination that comes from the field of the qualities of the mothers of all tathāgatas, which were a display of the qualities of the mothers of all bodhisattvas. They illuminated all world realms and shone upon me, spreading through me from the crown of my head to all the pores of my body.

“At that time I was in the house of king Shuddhodana, and when the time of the enlightening being’s descent from the heaven of contentment had arrived, from every pore the enlightening being emanated as many rays of light as atoms in untold buddha-lands, arrayed with the qualities of the birth of all enlightening beings, known as the light originating from the qualities of birth of all buddhas; those rays of light illumined the whole world, then descended on my body and entered into every pore of my body, beginning with my head.

rigs kyi bu/ de ltar byang chub sems dpa'i 'od zer ming gcig la byang chub sems dpa'i yum gyi rnam par 'phrul pa dang rgyan dang rnam par thar pa sna tshogs rab tu 'gyed pa de dag kho mo'i lus su dong ma thag tu de'i mod la kho mo'i lus su byang chub sems dpa'i 'od zer gyi sgo'i dkyil 'khor gyis rnam par dmigs par byas te byang chub sems dpa'i skye ba'i rnam par 'phrul pa'i tshul dang / rgyan thams cad yongs su snang bar gyur to/ / khyim dang 'khor la yang de bzhin du snang bar gyur to/ /

“Noble one, in that way, the bodhisattva light rays with one name[1892] radiated various miraculous manifestations, displays, and liberations of the mothers of bodhisattvas. The instant that they entered my body, I perceived in my body the displays and modes of the miraculous births of all bodhisattvas, visible in the fields of the tips[1893] of the light rays from the bodhisattva. Their residences and their entourages also appeared in that way.

As soon as those light rays of the enlightening being, with various names, emanating magical projections of the various miracles attending the birth of an enlightening being, had entered me, they caused the spheres of light at the front of the enlightening being’s light rays to be manifest in my body, and the supernal manifestations of miracles attending the birth of all enlightening beings were visible.

rigs kyi bu/ de ltar byang chub sems dpa'i 'od zer de dag kho mo'i lus su dong ma thag tu de'i mod la byang chub sems dpa'i 'od zer gyi sgo'i dkyil 'khor de dag gis byang chub sems dpa' gang dag gi skye ba'i tshul dang / rnam par 'phrul pa rnam par dmigs par byas pa de dag thams cad kyang kho mos mthong bar gyur te/ de dag thams cad kyang snying po byang chub du gshegs nas seng+ge'i gdan la bzhugs shing / byang chub sems dpa'i 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor gyis bskor te 'jig rten gyi dbang po rnams kyis bskor cing chos kyi 'khor lo bskor ba mang po mthong ngo/ /

“Noble one, in that way, the instant those light rays from the bodhisattva entered my body, the field of the tips of the light rays from the bodhisattva made visible to me the miracles and modes of the lives of bodhisattvas, and I saw them all. I saw them all going to their bodhimaṇḍas, sitting on their lion thrones encircled by assembled entourages of bodhisattvas, encircled by lords of the world, and turning the wheel of the Dharma.

And as soon as those light rays of the enlightening being had entered my body, I saw all the enlightening beings whose birth-miracles were shown in the spheres at the front of the enlightening being’s light rays, as they sat on the Buddha’s lion throne at the site of enlightenment, surrounded by congregations of enlightening beings, honored by the leaders of the worlds, turning the wheel of the teaching.

de bzhin gshegs pa de dag gis sngon byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa mdzad pa'i tshe de bzhin gshegs pa ji snyed cing bsnyen bkur ba de dag thams cad kyang kho mos dang po thugs bskyed pa dang / skye ba'i rnam par 'phrul pa dang bcas mngon par rdzogs par byang chub pa dang / chos kyi 'khor lo bskor ba dang / mya ngan las 'das pa'i rnam par 'phrul pa dang bcas/ sangs rgyas kyi zhing yongs su dag pa'i rgyan dang bcas par mthong ngo/ /

“I also saw those tathāgatas performing bodhisattva conduct in the past, all their service to tathāgatas, their first development of aspiration to enlightenment, the miracles of their birth, their complete enlightenment, their turning the wheel of the Dharma, the miraculous manifestation of their passing into nirvāṇa, and the display of their pure buddha realms.

I also saw all the buddhas with whom those buddhas associated as they carried out enlightening practices in the past. I also saw mystical projections of their initial inspiration, attainment of enlightenment, turning of the wheel of the teaching, final extinction, and the pure arrays of all buddha-lands,
de bzhin gshegs pa de dag gi sprul pa'i dkyil 'khor sems kyi skad cig re re la chos kyi dbyings thams cad rgyas par 'gengs pa de dag thams cad kyang kho mos mthong bar gyur to/ /
“I also saw all the field of the emanations of those tathāgatas filling all the realms of phenomena in each instant.
as well as the multitudes of emanations of those buddhas pervading the cosmos in each moment of consciousness.

rigs kyi bu/ de ltar kho mo'i lus su byang chub sems dpa'i 'od zer de dag dong ma thag tu kho mo'i lus kyang 'gro ba thams cad las mngon par 'phags par gyur te/ rum nam mkha'i dbyings ltar yangs par gyur kyang mi'i lus las lhag par yang mi snang ngo/ /

“Noble one, in that way, the instant those light rays from the bodhisattva entered my body, my own body became superior to those of all beings. My womb became as vast as space, but my body did not appear to transcend being a human body.
When those rays of light of the enlightening being entered my body, my body outreached all worlds, and my belly became as vast as space, and yet did not go beyond the human physical size.

phyogs bcu na byang chub sems dpa'i mngal gyi gnas dang / khang khyim dang / rgyan ji snyed cig yod pa de dag thams cad kyang kho mo'i lus kyi khongs su chud pa dang / kho mo'i lus su shod bar gyur par snang bar gyur to/ /
“All the displays and residences of the wombs in which dwelled bodhisattvas in the ten directions appeared contained within my body.
The supernal manifestations of the enlightening beings’ abode in the womb everywhere in the ten directions all appeared in my body.

rigs kyi bu/ de ltar kho mo'i lus su byang chub sems dpa'i mngal gyi gnas dang / khang khyim dang / rgyan dang / longs spyod byung bar gyur pa dang / de'i mod la byang chub sems dpa' sangs rgyas kyi zhing bcu'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi byang chub sems dpa' smon lam gcig pa/ skal pa mnyam par spyod spyod pa/ dge ba'i rtsa ba gcig pa/ rgyan gcig pa/ rnam par thar pa gcig la rnam par spyod pa/ ye shes kyi sa gcig la gnas pa/ rnam par 'phrul pa gcig gis byung ba/ smon lam gcig gis grub pa/ spyod pa gcig gis byung ba/ chos kyi lus yongs su dag pa/ gzugs kyi lus mtha' dang dbus med pa'i byin gyi rlabs dang ldan pa/ byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po'i spyod pa dang / smon lam dang / rnam par 'phrul pas byung ba dag dang / rin po che klu'i dbang po'i snying po'i khang pa brtsegs pa na 'khod cing klu'i rgyal po gang chen mtsho la sogs pa klu'i dbang po stong phrag brgyad cu dang / 'jig rten gyi dbang po thams cad kyis kyang mngon par mchod cing byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par 'phrul pa/

“Noble one, in that way, there appeared in my body the wombs in which the bodhisattvas resided, together with their residences and their enjoyments. In that instant, the bodhisattva and bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha realms who had the same prayer, the same practice of conduct, the same roots of merit, the same displays; who were dwelling in the same liberation, residing on the same level of wisdom, coming forth through the same miraculous manifestations, accomplishing the same prayers, coming forth through the same conduct; having purified Dharma bodies and the powerful presence of a vast, centerless, endless extent, of form bodies coming forth through the completely good bodhisattva conduct, prayers, and miraculous manifestations, were seated in the center of the precious kūṭāgāras of the lords of nāgas. The nāga king Sāgara and eighty thousand other nāga kings and all lords of the world made offerings to them.

“Upon the appearance in my body of the furnishings of the enlightening being’s abode in the womb, the enlightening being, together with as many enlightening beings as atoms in ten buddha-lands, all with the same vow, the same practice, the same roots of goodness, the same state of liberation and the same stage of knowledge, adept at the same mystic projection, having accomplished the same endeavor, adept at the same practice, having purified the same spiritual body, able to assume an infinite variety of physical forms, expert in the projection of the endeavors of universally good enlightening beings, respectfully attended by chiefs of all worlds,

dga' ldan gyi pho brang thams cad nas shi 'pho yongs su ston pas dga' ldan gyi gnas re re nas kyang 'jig rten gyi khams thams cad du 'dal ba'i gling bzhi par skye ba len pa yongs su ston pa/ sems can yongs su smin par bya ba'i thabs kyi tshul bsam gyis mi khyab pa la mkhas pa'i rjes su song ba dang / sems can bag med pa thams cad yongs su skul zhing mngon par zhen pa thams cad las gyen du bskyod pa dang / 'od zer gyi dra ba chen po rab tu dgye bas 'jig rten gyi mun pa thams cad rnam par sel ba dang / ngan song thams cad kyi sdug bsngal zhi bar byed pa dang / sems can dmyal ba'i lam gyi rgyud thams cad nas rnam par zlog pa dang / sems can thams cad kyi sngon gyi las yongs su skul ba dang / sems can gyi khams thams cad yongs su skyob pa dang / sems can thams cad la lus mngon par ston pas

“They displayed the miraculous manifestations of passing away from all the Tuṣita palaces, displayed taking birth from each Tuṣita into a four-continent world throughout all the world realms, acted in accordance with their skill in the inconceivable methods for ripening beings, inspired beings who were careless, brought them up out of all attachments, spread a great network of light rays that dispelled the darkness in all worlds, ended the sufferings in all lower existences, prevented all existences in hells, invoked the past karma of all beings, protected all realms of beings, and displayed their bodies to all beings.

descended from the heaven of contentment by the great miracle of enlightening beings; appearing to pass away from all heavens of contentment, appearing to become regenerated in all worlds, from each heaven of contentment to early existence, following skill in means of developing inconceivable numbers of sentient beings to maturity, alerting all intoxicated, deluded beings, detaching from all attachments, emanating a great network of light beams dispelling the darkness from all worlds, stopping all evils and miseries, putting an end to all hellish ways of being, making all beings aware of their past deeds, rescuing all beings, appearing in the presence of all beings,

dga' ldan gyi pho brang nas 'phos te 'khor dang bcas par kho mo'i lus su zhugs nas de dag thams cad kyang kho mo'i khong na gom pa stong gsum gyi stong chen po'i 'jig rten gyi khams tsam du yangs pa nas 'jig rten gyi khams sangs rgyas kyi zhing brjod du med pa'i rdul shin tu phra ba snyed du yangs pa'i 'gros kyis rgyu zhing spyod do/ /

“Together they departed from their Tuṣita palaces and with their entourages entered my body. All of them moved and walked within my body, their steps ranging from being as wide as a great world realm of a thousand million worlds up to being as wide as world realms as numerous as the atoms in countless buddha realms.

he descended from the heaven of contentment with his retinue and entered my belly. “Once all of them were in my belly, they walked around in strides as big as a billion-world universe, even as big as worlds as numerous as atoms in untold buddha-lands.

phyogs bcu'i 'jig rten gyi khams 'byams klas pa thams cad kyi de bzhin gshegs pa'i zhabs kyi drung gi byang chub sems dpa'i 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor brjod du med pa dag kyang sems kyi skad cig re re la byang chub sems dpa'i mngal gyi gnas dang / rnam par 'phrul ba blta ba'i phyir kho mo'i khong du 'dong ngo/ /

“The countless assembled entourages of bodhisattvas at the feet of tathāgatas in all the vast extent of world realms in the ten directions in each instant came into my body in order to see the miraculous manifestation of the bodhisattva’s residence in the womb.

Also all the untold congregations of enlightening beings at the feet of all buddhas in all worlds in the ten directions entered my belly in every moment of thought to see the miracle of the enlightening being’s dwelling in the womb.

rgyal po chen po bzhi dang / brgya byin dang / rab mtshe ma dang / rab dga' ldan dang / rab 'phrul dga' dang / dbang sgyur gyi lha'i dbang po rnams dang / tshangs pa rnams kyang mngal gyi gnas na bzhugs pa'i byang chub sems dpa' la blta ba dang / phyag bya ba dang / bsnyen bkur ba dang / chos nyan pa'i gtam nyams su myong bar bya ba'i phyir nye bar 'dong yang kho mo'i rum 'dis de snyed kyi 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor zhig yongs su bzung yang yangs par gyur pa yang med/ mi'i lus tha mal pa las kho mo'i lus khyad par can du gyur pa yang med mod kyi/ 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor de snyed kyang yongs su bzung ngo/ /

“The Four Mahārājas, Śakra, Suyāma, Saṃtuṣita, Sunirmita, Vaśavartin, the lords of the devas, and the lords of Brahmā devas also entered in order to see the bodhisattva dwelling in a womb, to pay homage to him, honor him, and hear him speak the Dharma. My womb, although it held all those assembled entourages, did not become vast. My body was not different from an ordinary human body, and yet it held all those assembled entourages.

The chief gods of all the heavens also came to the enlightening being in the womb, to see and honor him, to listen to the Teaching and hear his discourse. Yet even though it took in all those multitudes, my belly was not enlarged, nor did this body of mine become any more than a human body. Yet it received so many multitudes;
lha dang mi de dag thams cad kyis kyang byang chub sems dpa'i longs spyod sna tshogs dang / rgyan yongs su dag pa yang mthong bar gyur to/ /
“All those devas and humans saw the bodhisattva’s various pure enjoyments and displays.
and all the celestials and humans saw the various pure arrays of the enlightening beings’ surroundings.
de ci'i phyir zhe na/ de ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa smon lam chen po'i ye shes sgyu ma'i rnam pa 'di nyid shin tu bsgoms pa'i phyir ro/ /
Why is that? Because I meditated on this bodhisattva liberation called the illusory conjurations of the wisdom of great prayer.
Why was this? Because of the development of this enlightening liberation of the magic of knowledge of great vows.

rigs kyi bu/ ji ltar kho mo skal pa dang ldan pa'i gling bzhi pa 'di'i 'dzam bu'i gling na byang chub sems dpa' khong na yongs su 'dzin pa de bzhin du/ stong gsum gyi stong chen po'i 'jig rten gyi khams kyi gling bzhi pa thams cad kyi 'dzam bu'i gling dag na'ang rnam par 'phrul pa'i rgyan gyi tshul 'di nyid kyis yongs su 'dzin par byed de/ byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa smon lam chen po'i ye shes sgyu ma'i rnam pa 'di nyid shin tu bsgoms pa'i phyir kho mo'i lus 'di gnyis su gyur pa'ang med/ mi gnyis pa'ang med/ gcig la gnas pa'ang med/ mang po la gnas pa'i med do/ /

“Noble one, just as I held in my body the bodhisattva in the Jambudvīpa of this fortunate four-continent world, in the same way I have held him in this miraculous manner in all the four-continent worlds of the great world realm of a thousand million worlds. Because I have meditated on this bodhisattva liberation called the illusory conjurations of the wisdom of great prayer, my body is neither dual nor nondual, and it is neither single nor multiple.

“Just as I received the enlightening being in my belly in this world, so did I likewise do so in all worlds in the billion-world universe, and with this same miraculous manifestation; yet this body of mine is neither dual nor nondual, neither single nor multiple; this is because of the development of this enlightening liberation of the magic of knowledge of great vows.

rigs kyi bu/ ji ltar kho mo bcom ldan 'das rnam par snang mdzad 'di'i yum du gyur pa de bzhin du/ sngon gyi de bzhin gshegs pa mtha' dang dbus med pa dag gi yang yum du gyur to/ / la la zhig tu byang chub sems dpa' pad+mo'i spubs nas rdzus te skye ba zhig tu gyur na yang pad+mo'i tshal gyi lha mor gyur cing / kho mos byang chub sems dpa' len te/ 'jig rten rnams kyis kyang kho mo ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i yum yin par shes so/ / la la zhig tu thu bar skye bar gyur na yang de dag tu yang kho mos thu bar blangs te byang chub sems dpa'i yum du gyur to/ / la la zhig tu sangs rgyas kyi zhing du de bzhin 'byung bar gyur na'ang de dag tu'ang kho mo snying po byang chub kyi lha mor gnas gnas so/ /

“Noble one, just as I have been the mother of this Buddha Vairocana, in the same way I have been the mother of a vast extent, without middle or end, of past tathāgatas. If a bodhisattva was born miraculously from the center of a lotus, I was a goddess of that lotus bed, I acquired that bodhisattva, and I was known in the world as being the bodhisattva’s mother. If a bodhisattva was born upon my lap, I acquired them from my lap and was the bodhisattva’s mother. If a bodhisattva were in that way born spontaneously in a buddha realm, I would be living there as the goddess of the bodhimaṇḍa.

And just as I was the mother of this buddha Vairocana, so was I the mother of infinite buddhas before. Whenever an enlightening being was spontaneously born in the calyx of a lotus, there I became a lotus-pond goddess and received the enlightening being, and the world recognized me as the progenetrix of the enlightening being; in whatever buddha-land an enlightening being appeared, I became an enlightenment-site goddess there:
rigs kyi bu/ thabs kyi sgo ji snyed cig gis byang chub sems dpa' srid pa'i tha ma pa 'jig rten du 'byung ba yongs su ston pa de snyed kyi thabs kyi sgos kho mo byang chub sems dpa'i yum du gyur te/
“Noble one, through various methods I became the mother of the bodhisattvas when they appeared in various ways in the world as their last existence as bodhisattvas.
thus in whatever ways enlightening beings manifested birth in the world in their final existence, in so many ways did I become the mother of the enlightening beings.

rigs kyi bu/ kho mo 'jig rten gyi khams 'di na bcom ldan 'das rnam par snang mdzad kyi byang chub sems dpa'i skye ba'i rnam par 'phrul pa yongs su bstan pa dag tu yum du gyur pa de bzhin du/ bcom ldan 'das de bzhin gshegs pa log par dad sel dang / gser thub dang / bsod skyabs kyi yum du 'ang gyur to/ /

“Noble one, in this world realm I have been the mother who manifested the miraculous bodhisattva birth of the Bhagavat Vairocana. In the same way, I was the mother of the tathāgatas Krakucchanda, Kanakamuni, and Kāśyapa. In the same way, I will be the mother of all the future tathāgatas in this Bhadra kalpa.

“Just as I was the mother of this buddha in this world in all his manifestations of miracles of birth as an enlightening being, so was I the mother of the buddhas Krakucchanda, Kanakamuni, and Kashyapa; and so will I be the mother of all the buddhas of this eon.

de bzhin du ma byon pa'i de bzhin gshegs pa bskal pa bzang po pa rnams kyi'ang yum du 'gyur te/ 'di ltar byang chub sems dpa' byams pa dga' ldan gyi gnas na bzhugs shing shi 'pho yongs su ston pa'i dus la bab pa dang / 'od zer byang chub sems dpa' thams cad skye bar 'byung zhing / mngal na bzhugs pa'i rnam par 'phrul pa yongs su ston pa'i 'od bkye nas chos kyi dbyings thams cad kyi tshul dang / gzhi rab tu snang bar byas te chos kyi dbyings kyi tshul dang / gzhi ji snyed cig tu byang chub sems dpa' byams pas mi'i 'jig rten gyi mi'i dbang po'i rigs su cher skye ba yongs su bstan pas sems can gdul bar bya ba ji snyed cig yod pa de dag thams cad du'ang kho mo byang chub sems dpa'i yum du 'gyur ro/ /

Thus, when the time comes for the bodhisattva Maitreya, who dwells in the Tuṣita palace, to manifest passing away, he will radiate the light ray of the lights that reveal the miraculous event of the birth, appearance, and dwelling in a womb of all bodhisattvas. The light will go throughout the lands and ways of the entire realm of phenomena and will manifest as that bodhisattva Maitreya who will be born in a human world in the family of a lord of humans in all the lands and ways of the entire realm of phenomena in order to guide beings, and I will be the mother of all those bodhisattvas.

“When the time comes for the enlightening being Maitreya, now in the heaven of contentment, to manifest descent from heaven, and emanate the lights of the manifestation of the miracles of enlightening beings abiding in the womb whence they are born, I will see all realms in all universes which are illumined thereby, where Maitreya will be born in a royal family in the human world and will guide sentient beings, and everywhere therein I will be the mother of the enlightening being.

grags pa dang / sman gyi rgyal po dang / rin chen mchog dang / blo gros rdo rje dang /
Yaśas, Auṣadhirāja, Ratnavara, Mativajra,[1903]
dkar po'i dpal dang / gzhi shin tu sbyangs pa dang / rin chen rgyal po dang / grags pa chen po dang /
Sitaśrī, Nirghautālaya, Maṇirāja, Mahāyaśas,
shugs drag 'dzin pa dang / mi dpog 'od dang / 'od 'phro chen pos bzhugs pa dang / don yod pa'i chos la mnga' ba dang /

brtson 'grus ma nyams pa dang / dag pa'i lha dang / 'od brtan pa dang / kun gyi bshes gnyen dang /

rnam par grol ba'i dbyangs dang / rnam par bsgrags pa'i rgyal po dang / tshig gcod pa dang / tsam+pa ka dri ma med pa'i 'od dang /
Vimuktighoṣa, Vinarditarāja, Vākyaccheda, Campakavimalaprabha,
kha na mi tho ba mi mnga' ba dang / zla ba rnam par 'phags pa dang / sgron ma 'dzin pa dang / sku rnam par mdzes pa dang /

brjod du med par 'phags pa dang / 'gro ba'i bshes gnyen dang / 'od zer mang po dang / dbyangs kyi yan lag dpa' bo dang /
Anabhilāpyodgata, Jaganmitra, Prabhūtaraśmi, Svarāṅgaśūra,
chu lha'i spyan dang / mos pa'i blo gros mnga' ba'i gzi brjid dang / me tog kun da'i dpal dang / mchod pa'i zla ba dang /
Varuṇākṣa,[1904] Dhṛtamatitejas, Kundaśrī, Arciścandra,
blo mi mnga' ba dang / chags pa mi mnga' ba dang / mi dmigs pa'i blo gros dang / phung po bsags pa dang /
Anihitamati, Anunayavigata, Anilambhamati, Upacitaskandha,
ngan song rab tu 'joms pa dang / me tog dam pa dang / seng+ge rnam par sgrog pa dang / don mi dma' ba dang /
Apāyapramathana, Adīnakusuma, Siṃhavinardita, Anihānārtha,
bsgribs pa med par gzigs pa dang / pha rol gyi tshogs 'joms pa dang / rlung gi mu khyud dang / snying po mi g.yo ba dang /
Anāvaraṇadarśin, Paragaṇamathana, Anilanema, Akampitagarbha,[1905]
snying po bzang po dang / gzhan gyis mi thub pa'i ri bo dang / mi gnas ye shes dang / mtha' yas bzhugs pa dang /
Śobhanasāgara, Aparājitameru, Anilayajñāna, Anantāsana,
g.yul du brtan pa dang / spyod pas grub pa dang / bla mas bon pa dang / mchog tu dga' ba dang /
Ayudhiṣṭhira, Caryāgata, Uttaradatta, Atyantacandramas,
rjes su 'dzin pa'i zla ba dang / lhun mi g.yo ba dang / thugs drag po dang / thugs brtse ba'i blo gros dang /
Anugrahacandra, Acalaskandha, Agrasānumati, Anugrahamati,

Abhyuddhara, Arcitanama, Anupagamanāman, Nihatatejas,

Viśvavarṇa, Animittaprajña, Acaladeva, Acintyaśrī,
rnam par thar pa'i zla ba dang / bla na med pa'i rgyal po dang / zla ba'i phung po dang / mchod pa'i tshangs pa dang /
Vimokṣacandra, Anuttararāja, Candraskandha, Arcitabrahman,
spyan mi 'gyur ba dang / byams pa'i rigs dang / 'phrin las 'phags pa dang / gnyer ba'i chos kyi blo gros dang /
Akampyanetra, Anunayagātra, Abhyudgatakarman, Anudharmamati,
bla na med pa'i dpal dang / tshangs pa'i lha dang / yon tan bsam gyis mi khyab pa'i 'od dang / bla na med pa'i chos kyi spyod yul dang /
Anuttaraśrī, Brahmadeva, Acintyaguṇaprabha,[1906] Anuttaradharmagocara,
mtha' yas bzang po dang / tshul dang 'dra ba'i gsung dang / byang chub sems dpa' shin tu mtho ba'i lha dag ste/
Aparyantabhadra, Anurūpasvara, and the bodhisattva Abhyuccadeva.

rigs kyi bu/ de ltar stong gsum gyi stong chen po'i 'jig rten gyi khams 'di'i ma byon pa'i de bzhin gshegs pa byams pa la sogs te/ smos pa 'di dag la sogs pa bskal pa bzang po pa'i de bzhin gshegs pa dgra bcom pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas thams cad kyi yum du'ang kho mo nyid 'gyur ro/ /

“Noble one, in that way I will be the mother of all the future tathāgatas, such as Maitreya and the others I have mentioned, and all the other tathāgata arhat samyaksaṃbuddhas of this Bhadra kalpa in this great world realm of a thousand million worlds.
“And just as I will be the mother of Maitreya, so will I be the mother of all buddhas in this eon in this universe,
'jig rten gyi khams 'dir ji lta ba de bzhin du/ phyogs bcu'i 'jig rten gyi khams tshad med pa'i chos kyi dbyings kyi tshul mtha' dang dbus med pa la zhugs te/
“As it is in this world realm, I will in the same way enter countless world realms in the ten directions throughout the vast extent, without middle or center, of the ways of the realm of phenomena.
and in all universes of the ten directions, penetrating endless universes.

ji ltar de bzhin gshegs pa byams pa'i yum du yon tan gyi khyad par brjod du med par 'gyur ba de bzhin du/ yon tan gyi khyad par brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa'i de bzhin gshegs pa seng+ge nas de bzhin gshegs pa snang ba'i bar gyi yum du 'gyur ro/ /

“In the same way that I will be the mother, with countless special qualities, of the Tathāgata Maitreya, I will be the mother, with countless numbers of countless special qualities, of the Tathāgata Siṃha, and so on until the Tathāgata Roca.
And just as I will be the mother of Maitreya, by untold virtues,
ji ltar de bzhin gshegs pa bskal pa bzang po pa rnams kyi yum du 'gyur ba
“Just as I am the mother of the tathāgatas of the Bhadra kalpa,

de bzhin du/ 'jig rten gyi khams rgya mtsho gzhi dang snying po me tog gi rgyan gyis brgyan pa 'di thams cad kyi 'jig rten gyi khams kyi rgyud thams cad dang / 'jig rten gyi khams 'byams klas thams cad kyi 'jig rten gyi khams thams cad na 'dzam bu'i gling yod pa thams cad du phyi ma'i mtha'i mur thug pa'i bskal par byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po'i spyad pa spyod cing / bskal pa thams cad du sems can thams cad yongs su smin par bya ba dang / gdul bar byin gyis brlabs te/ ma byon pa'i de bzhin gshegs pa byang chub sems dpar gyur pa thams cad kyi yum du'ang 'gyur ro/ / de skad ces smras pa dang /

in the same way, in all the Jambudvīpas in all the world realms in the entirety of this ocean of world realms called Kusumatalagarbhavyūhālaṃkāra, and in all the world realms throughout the vast extent of world realms, until the last of future kalpas, I will practice the completely good conduct of the bodhisattva and be present in all kalpas in order to ripen and guide beings, and I will be the mother of all the tathāgatas as bodhisattvas in the future.”

so shall I be the mother of all the buddhas in this eon, and in endless billions of eons in all the worlds in all world systems in this flower treasury ocean of worlds, I will be the mother of all the buddhas of the future when they are enlightening beings, carrying on the practice of universally good enlightening beings, establishing guidance for the perfection of all beings in all ages.”

tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis lha mo sgyu ma la 'di skad ces smras so/ / 'phags ma/ khyod kyis byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa smon lam chen po'i ye shes sgyu ma'i rnam pas rnam par brgyan pa 'di brnyes nas ji snyed cig lags/

After she had spoken, Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, asked Māyādevī, “Āryā, how long has it been since you attained this bodhisattva liberation called the illusory conjurations of the wisdom of great prayer?”
Then Sudhana asked Lady Maya, “How long ago did you attain this enlightening liberation of magical manifestations of knowledge of great vows?”

smras pa/ rigs kyi bu/ sngon 'das pa'i dus bskal pa bsam gyis mi khyab pa sems kyi yul las 'das par rigs dang ldan pa'i byang chub sems dpa'i mig gi lam gyis rnam par dmigs pa/ rnam par shes pas bgrang ba las yongs su 'das pa'i pha rol cig tu bskal pa dge ba'i 'od ces bya ba zhig byung ste/ bskal pa dge ba'i 'od de la 'jig rten gyi khams ri bo shin tu mtho ba'i dpal zhes bya ba rnam par dag la kun nas nyon mongs pa/ rin po che du ma las grub pa/ khor yug dang bcas pa/ ri rab dang rgya mtshor bcas pa/ 'gro ba lnga'i rgyud dang bcas pa sna tshogs blta na mdzes pa zhig byung ste/ 'jig rten gyi khams ri bo shin tu mtho ba'i dpal der gling bzhi pa bye ba brgya phrag bcu byung ste/ gling bzhi pa bye ba brgya phrag bcu po de dag gi dbus na gling bzhi pa dbu ma seng+ge rgyal mtshan dam pa'i gzi brjid ces bya ba zhig yod par gyur te/ gling bzhi pa der rgyal po'i gnas bye ba brgya phrag brgyad cu byung bar gyur to/ / rgyal po'i gnas bye ba brgya phrag brgyad cu po de dag gi dbus su rgyal po'i gnas dbu ma rgyal mtshan gyi dam pa dang ldan pa zhes bya ba byung ste/ der 'khor los bsgyur ba'i rgyal po gzi brjid chen po'i mthu zhes bya ba byung ngo/ / rgyal po'i gnas rgyal mtshan gyi dam pa dang ldan pa der snying po byang chub yal ga sna tshogs kyi 'od ces bya ba zhig byung ste/ de na snying po byang chub kyi lha mo mig gi dpal zhes bya ba 'dug 'dug go /

Māyādevī answered, “Noble one, in the past, in time gone by, countless kalpas ago, beyond the scope of the mind, beyond kalpas that are beyond the number that can be perceived and known by the vision of wise bodhisattvas, there was a kalpa called Śubhaprabha. In that Śubhaprabha kalpa there was a world realm called Merūdgataśrī, which was both pure and defiled, formed from many jewels, and endowed with Cakravāla mountain ranges, Sumeru mountains, and oceans, the five classes of beings, and a variety of beauties. In that Merūdgataśrī world realm there were ten thousand million four-continent worlds. In the center of those ten thousand million four-continent worlds was the central four-continent world called Siṃhadhvajāgratejas. In that four-continent world there were eighty thousand million royal cities. In the center of those eighty thousand million royal cities there was the central royal city, called Dhvajāgravatī, in which there was a cakravartin king called Mahātejaḥparākrama. By that royal city of Dhvajāgravatī there was a bodhimaṇḍa called Citramañjariprabhāsa, where dwelled a bodhimaṇḍa goddess by the name of Netraśrī.

Maya replied, “Inconceivable eons ago, beyond the range of mind, beyond conscious calculation, there was an age called Pure Light. In that age of Pure Light there was a world called Elevated, which was pure with some defilement, made of many jewels, with surrounding mountains, polar mountains, and oceans, containing realms of celestials, humans, animals, ghosts, and hells, variegated and pleasant to see. In that world were a billion sets of four continents, in the middle of which was a group of four continents called Supreme Lionlike Majesty, in which there were eighty billion metropolises, among which was one called Possessed of the Best of Banners. There in that metropolis was a king called Great Energetic Power, a sovereign ruler. There was also an enlightenment site in that metropolis called Conspicuous Rays of Light, wherein there was a deity called Radiant Eyes.

snying po byang chub yal ga sna tshogs kyi 'od de la byang chub sems dpa' rgyal mtshan dri ma med pa zhes bya ba zhig thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi chos khong du chud par bya ba'i phyir 'dug pa las/ de'i thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi chos khong du chud par bya ba la bar chad bya ba'i phyir bdud kha dog bzang po'i 'od ces bya ba bdud kyi sde chen po'i 'khor dang ldan pa zhig lus mi snang bar ma byas par drung du phyin par gyur ro/ /

“In that bodhimaṇḍa called Citramañjariprabhāsa, the bodhisattva Vimaladhvaja sat in order to realize omniscience. In order to prevent his realization of omniscience, a māra by the name of Suvarṇaprabha, together with an entourage of a great army of māras, made himself visible[1907] and came before him.

Furthermore, at that enlightenment site an enlightening being named Pure Standard sat, to attain omniscience. A demon named Golden Light, along with a great army of cohorts, had come invisibly to prevent the enlightening being from attaining omniscience;

'khor los bsgyur ba gzi brjid chen po'i mthu de yang byang chub sems dpa'i dbang thob pa'i rdzu 'phrul chen po'i rnam par 'phrul pas byung ba zhig ste/ des bdud kyi sde de bas kyang 'phags la ches mang ba'i dpung gi tshogs chen po mngon par sprul te bdud kyi sde pham par bya ba'i phyir snying po byang chub de'i 'khor kun nas yongs su bskor ba dang / des bdud kyi sde chen po de yang rnam par gtor bar gyur to/ / bcom ldan 'das de bzhin gshegs pa rgyal mtshan dri ma med pa des kyang bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu mngon par rdzogs par sangs rgyas so/ /

“The cakravartin Mahātejaḥparākrama had attained the power of a bodhisattva and displayed manifestations of great miraculous powers. He manifested a great army that was far more numerous than the māra’s army, and in order to defeat the māra’s army, it surrounded the bodhimaṇḍa and scattered the great army of the māra. Then the Bhagavat, the Tathāgata Vimaladhvaja, attained the highest, complete enlightenment of buddhahood.

but the king Great Energetic Power, who had attained the mastery which enlightening beings realize, issued a great magical projection, producing a great army, more numerous than and superior to that of the demons, to surround the enlightenment site and fight off the demon army. The demon army was thereby scattered, and the blessed Pure Standard realized perfect enlightenment.

de nas snying po byang chub kyi lha mo mig gi dpal gyis 'khor los bsgyur ba'i rgyal po gzi brjid chen po'i mthu la bu'i 'du shes bskyed nas de bzhin gshegs pa de'i zhabs gnyis la phyag 'tshal nas smon lam btab pa/ bcom ldan 'das/ bdag gang dang gang du skyes pa de dang der 'khor los bsgyur ba gzi brjid chen po'i mthu 'di bdag gi bur gyur cig /nam 'di bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu mngon par 'tshang rgya bar 'gyur ba de'i tshe 'ang bdag nyid de'i mar gyur cig /ces nas des smon lam de skad du btab ste/

“Netraśrī, the bodhimaṇḍa goddess, looked upon the cakravartin king Mahātejaḥparākrama as her son. She bowed to the feet of the Bhagavat and made this prayer: ‘Bhagavat, wherever I am reborn, may the cakravartin Mahātejaḥparākrama always be my son! May I be his mother when he attains the highest, complete enlightenment at buddhahood.’

“The goddess of the enlightenment site, Radiant Eyes, looking upon the king as her son, then prostrated herself before the buddha and made a vow: ‘Wherever I may be born, may the king Great Energetic Power be my son; and when he attains supreme perfect enlightenment, I will be his mother then too.’ Having made this vow,
snying po byang chub yal ga sna tshogs kyi 'od de nyid la gnas shing bskal pa 'od bzang po 'di nyid la de bzhin gshegs pa khrag khrig phrag bcu bsnyen bkur to/ /
“She dwelled at the Citramañjariprabhāsa bodhimaṇḍa serving a trillion tathāgatas during the Śubhaprabha kalpa.
she attended ten decillion buddhas at that enlightenment site during that eon.

rigs kyi bu /de la ji snyam du sems/ de'i tshe de'i dus na snying po byang chub kyi lha mo mig gi dpal zhes bya bar gyur pa de gzhan zhig yin pa snyam du sems na ni/ rigs kyi bu khyod kyis de ltar mi blta ste/ kho mo ni/ de'i tshe de'i dus na snying po byang chub kyi lha mo mig gi dpal zhes bya bar gyur to/ /

“What do you think, noble one? At that time, in that time, who was Netraśrī, the bodhimaṇḍa goddess? Noble one, do not think that it was anyone else, for at that time, in that time, I was Netraśrī, the bodhimaṇḍa goddess.
“Now, who do you think that goddess was? It was I myself who was the enlightenment-site goddess Radiant Eyes at that time.

rigs kyi bu/ de la ji snyam du sems/ de'i tshe de'i dus na 'khor los bsgyur ba'i gzi brjid chen po'i mthu zhes bya ba/ byang chub sems dpa'i dbang thob pa/ rdzu 'phrul chen po'i rnam par 'phrul pas byung ba/ bdud kyi sde chen po rnam par mthor bar byed pa de gzhan zhig yin pa snyam du sems na ni/ de ltar mi blta ste/ bcom ldan 'das de bzhin gshegs pa dgra bcom pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas rnam par snang mdzad 'di ni/ de'i tshe de'i dus na 'khor los bsgyur ba'i rgyal po gzi brjid chen po'i mthu zhes bya bar gyur to/ /

“What do you think, noble one? At that time, in that time, who was the cakravartin king Mahātejaḥparākrama, who had attained the power of a bodhisattva, displayed manifestations of great miraculous powers, and scattered the army of that māra? Do not think that it was anyone else, for at that time, in that time, the Tathāgata Arhat Samyaksaṃbuddha Vairocana was Mahātejaḥparākrama, the cakravartin king.

As for the king Great Energetic Power, who had the mastery of an enlightening being and destroyed the demon army by means of a magical projection, it was none other than this present buddha, the blessed Vairocana, the saint, the perfectly enlightened one, who was at that time the king Great Energetic Power.

rigs kyi bu; de ltar kho mo de nas nye bar bzung nas gang dang gang du skyes pa de dag thams cad du'ang 'di ni/ kho mo'i bur gyur te/ sangs rgyas kyi zhing thams cad du byang chub sems dpa'i spyad pa spyod cing / 'gro ba'i rgyud kyi sgo thams cad dang / skye gnas kyi sgo thams cad dang / dge ba'i rtsa ba'i sgo thams cad dang / byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa'i rgyud kyi tshul thams cad dang / skyes pa'i rabs kyi tshul thams cad dang / lha'i dbang po'i tshe thams cad dang / 'jig rten gyi dbang po'i 'gro ba'i rgyud thams cad dang / dbang phyug gis thams cad dang / 'gro ba'i rgyud du snang ba thams cad gang dang gang du sems can yongs su smin par bya ba'i don du skyes par gyur pa de dag thams cad du yang kho mo nyid 'di'i yum du gyur te/ srid pa thams cad du 'ang kho mo nyid dang bral ba med par yum du gyur to/ / byang chub sems dpa'i skye ba'i sgo thams cad du skad cig skad cig cing byang chub sems dpa'i skye ba'i rnam par 'phrul pa bstan par gyur to/ / de dag thams cad du yang kho mo nyid 'di'i yum du gyur to/ /

“Noble one, in that way, from that time onward, wherever I was reborn, in all those lives he has been my son. Wherever he was reborn, practicing bodhisattva conduct in all buddha realms, in all the entrances to roots of merit, in all the ways of bodhisattva conduct, in all the ways of rebirth, in all lifetimes as a lord of devas, as a lord of the world, on the level of a supreme deity, as a light among the classes of beings, wherever he was reborn in order to ripen beings, in all those lifetimes I was his mother. In all existences I have inseparably been his mother. I have been his mother in all the miraculous bodhisattva births manifested in each instant through the gateways of bodhisattva births.

Ever since then, wherever I have been, he has come as my son, carrying out the practice of enlightening beings in all buddha-lands, in all states of being, in all lifetimes, based on all that is good, in all undertakings through which enlightening practice is carried out. Wherever he emerged to develop and perfect sentient beings, there I was his mother, and in his final existence too, I was his mother, everywhere. In all modes of birth as an enlightening being, moment to moment, however many miracles of birth as an enlightening being he displayed, in every case I was his mother.

'das pa'i de bzhin gshegs pa mtha' dang dbus med pa tshad med pa dag gi yum du'ang kho mo gyur to/ / phyogs bcu'i de bzhin gshegs pa da ltar byung ba mtha' dang dbus med pa tshad med pa dag gi yum du'ang kho mo gyur te/ de bzhin gshegs pa ji snyed cig gi srid pa tha ma la kho mo byang chub sems dpa'i yum du gyur pa'i de bzhin gshegs pa de dag thams cad kyi sku lte ba'i dkyil 'khor nas 'od zer mang po byung zhing / kho mo'i lus dang sems rab tu snang bar mdzad do/ /

“I have been the mother of the immeasurable vast extent, without middle or end, of the tathāgatas of the past. I am the mother of the immeasurable vast extent, without middle or end, of the tathāgatas in the ten directions who have appeared in the present time. In that way, I have been the mother of a bodhisattva for all tathāgatas in their final lifetime, and from the navel of all those tathāgatas shone many light rays that illuminated my body and mind.

In the same way I was the mother of infinite buddhas of the past, and I am mother to the infinite buddhas of the ten directions in the present. And all the buddhas I was mothers to in their last existence as an enlightening being emanated lights from their navels and illumined this great body and this seat.

rigs kyi bu/ kho mos byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa smon lam chen po ye shes sgyu ma'i rnam pas rnam par brgyan pa 'di shes par zad na; kho mos byang chub sems dpa'i snying rje chen po'i snying po dang ldan pa/ thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du yongs su smin par bya ba dang / gdul bas mi ngoms pa'i lta can/ de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi rnam par 'phrul ba ba spu'i rtse mo las 'byung bar ston pa la dbang sgyur ba de dag gi spyod pa shes pa'am/ yon tan brjod par nus re skan/

“Noble one, I know only this bodhisattva liberation called the illusory conjurations of the wisdom of great prayer. How could I know or describe the qualities of the bodhisattvas who possess the essence of great compassion, who within themselves are never satisfied in ripening and guiding beings to omniscience, and who manifest from the tips of their body hairs the miraculous manifestations of all tathāgatas?

“I only know this enlightening liberation of magical manifestation of knowledge of great vows—how can I know the practice or tell of the virtues of the enlightening beings who are filled with great compassion, who never tire of guiding to perfection of omniscience, who are able to display projections of the miracles of all buddhas from every pore?

song rigs kyi bu/ sum cu rtsa gsum gyi dbang po'i gnas de nyid na lha'i bu dran pa dang ldan pa'i bu mo lha dbang 'od ces bya ba 'dug gi /de'i gan du song la ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bya ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bya ba dris shig/

“Depart, noble one. In the paradise of the lord of Trāyastriṃśa resides Surendrābhā, the daughter of the deva Smṛtimat. Go to her and ask her, ‘How should a bodhisattva train in and practice bodhisattva conduct?’ ”

“In the thirty-three-fold heaven of this world is a goddess named Surendrabha, who is the daughter of a god named Smrtimati. Go ask her how to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings.”

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis lha mo sgyu ma'i rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas yang dang yang bltas te/ lha mo sgyu ma'i drung nas song ngo/ /

Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, bowed his head to the feet of Māyādevī, circumambulated her many hundreds of thousands of times, keeping her to his right, and, looking back again and again, departed from Māyādevī.
So then Sudhana paid his respects and left Lady Maya.
shin tu rgyas pa chen po'i mdo/ sangs rgyas phal po che zhes bya ba las/ sdong pos brgyan pa'i le'u ste/ ` bam po brgya bcu pa/

Chapter 45. Surendrābhā
Surendrabha

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang sum cu rtsa gsum gyi dbang ba'i gnas gang na ba dang / lha'i bu dran pa dang ldan pa'i bu mo lha dbang 'od gang na ba der song ste phyin nas lha'i bu mo lha dbang 'od kyi rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te; lha'i bu mo lha dbang 'od la lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas lha'i bu mo lha dbang 'od kyi mdun du 'dug ste thal mo sbyar nas 'di skad ces smras so/ /

Sudhana went to the paradise of the lord of Trāyastriṃśa and approached the deva maiden Surendrābhā, the daughter of the deva Smṛtimat. He bowed his head to the feet of the deva maiden Surendrābhā, circumambulated the deva maiden Surendrābhā many hundreds of thousands of times, keeping her to his right, and then stood before the deva maiden Surendrābhā with his palms together in homage and said,
Then Sudhana went to the thirty-three-fold heaven, and went to the goddess Surendrabha. Paying his respects to the goddess, Sudhana stood before her and said,

'phags ma lha mo/ bdag gis bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed na/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bgyi ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bgyi ba ma 'tshal te/ 'phags ma ni/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams la gdams ngag dang / rjes su bstan pa mdzad do/ /zhes bdag gis thos na/ 'phags ma lha mo/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bgyi ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bgyi ba bdag la bstan du gsol/

“Āryā, goddess, I have developed the aspiration for the highest, complete enlightenment, but I do not know how bodhisattvas should train in bodhisattva conduct and in what way they should practice it. Āryā, I have heard that you give instruction and teachings to bodhisattvas! I pray that you explain to me how bodhisattvas should train in bodhisattva conduct and how they should practice it!”

“Noble one, I have set my mind on supreme perfect enlightenment, but I do not know how to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings. I hear you give instruction to enlightening beings, so please tell me how to learn and practice.”
de skad ces smras pa dang / lha'i bu mo lha dbang 'od kyis tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la 'di skad ces smras so/ /
When he had said that, the deva maiden Surendrābhā said to Sudhana, the head merchant’s son,
Surendrabha replied,
rigs kyi bu/ kho mo ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa dran pa thogs pa med pa/ rnam par dag pas brgyan pa zhes bya ba thob pa ste/
“Noble one, I have attained the bodhisattva liberation called the display of pure, unimpeded memory.
“I have attained an enlightening liberation called pure manifestation of unimpeded recollection.

rigs kyi bu/ kho mos mngon par dran pa bskal pa ut+pa la zhes bya ba zhig byung ba la kho mos de bzhin gshegs pa chu klung gang+gA'i bye ma snyed cig bsnyen bkur te/ de dag mngon par ma byung ba'i tshe yang yongs su srung ba byas so/ / mchod pa byas so/ / longs spyod pa'i don du bza' shing gi ra ba gsol to/ /

“Noble one, I remember a kalpa called Utpala in which I served as many tathāgatas as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River. When they set forth, I protected them, made offerings to them, and gave them parks to enjoy.

I am aware that there was an age called Flowering, in which I served as many buddhas as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River. When they went forth from their customary surroundings, I protected them, provided for them, and made parks for their use.

sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das de dag byang chub sems dpar gyur te/ yum gyi sku na bzhugs pa dang / bltams pa dang / gshegs stabs mdun du bzhud pa dang / seng+ge'i nga ro chen po sgrog pa dang / gzhon nu'i sa la bzhugs pa dang / btsun mo'i 'khor gyi nang na bzhugs pa dang / mngon par byung ba dang / byang chub tu mngon par rdzogs par 'tshang rgya ba dang / chos kyi 'khor lo bskor ba dang / sangs rgyas kyi rnam par 'phrul pa thams cad yongs su ston pa mdzad pa'i tshe sems can yongs su smin pa dang / rnam par gdul bar mdzad pa de dag thams cad kyang thugs dang po bskyed pa nas nye bar bzung ba tshun chad dam pa'i chos mthar thug par zad kyi bar du kho mos shes so/ / dran no/ / rjes su dran no/ / bzung ngo/ / yongs su bzung ngo/ / nye bar bzung ngo/ / rjes su 'brang bar byed do/ /

“I know when those buddha bhagavats were bodhisattvas, were within the bodies of their mothers, were born, took their first seven steps, roared the lion’s roar, were youths, were within their harems, set forth into homelessness, attained the enlightenment of buddhahood, turned the wheel of the Dharma, and displayed all the miraculous manifestations of a buddha, and when they ripened and guided beings, throughout all those times, from their first development of the aspiration for enlightenment until their final Dharma teaching. I remember that, recollect that, grasp that, retain that, reflect upon that, and follow that.

And all the developmental guidance of sentient beings performed by those buddhas—while they were enlightening beings, while in the womb of the mother, while being born, while taking seven steps, while roaring the lion’s roar, during childhood, during life at home, when leaving home, when awaking at the site of enlightenment, while teaching, while displaying the miracles of buddhas—all that, from their first inspiration to the final ending of their true teaching, I know and remember, recall and keep in mind, reflect on and follow.
bskal pa sa bzang po zhes bya ba zhig byung ba de la kho mos de bzhin gshegs pa chu klung gang+gA bcu'i bye ma snyed cig bsnyen bkur to/ /
“There was a kalpa called Subhūti, in which I served as many tathāgatas as there are grains of sand in ten Ganges Rivers.
“There was an eon called Well-Being, in which I served as many buddhas as sand grains in ten Ganges Rivers;
bskal pa grags pa bzang po zhes bya ba zhig byung ba de la kho mos de bzhin gshegs pa sangs rgyas kyi zhing gi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed cig bsnyen bkur to; ;
“There was a kalpa called Subhaga, in which I served as many tathāgatas as there are atoms in a buddha realm.
there was an eon called Good Fortune, in which I served as many buddhas as atoms in a buddha-land;
bskal pa dmigs su med pa zhes bya ba zhig byung ba de la kho mos sangs rgyas bye ba khrag khrig brgya stong phrag brgyad cu rtsa bzhi bsnyen bkur to; ;
“There was a kalpa called Anilambha, in which I served eighty-four hundred thousand quintillion tathāgatas.
there was an eon called No Attainment, in which I served eighty-four thousand duodecillion buddhas;
bskal pa 'od bzang po zhes bya ba zhig byung ba de la kho mos de bzhin gshegs pa dzam+bu'i gling gi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed cig bsnyen bkur to/ /
“There was a kalpa called Suprabha, in which I served as many tathāgatas as there are atoms in Jambudvīpa.
there was an eon called Beautiful Light, in which I served as many buddhas as atoms in this continent;
bskal pa 'od gzhal du med pa zhes bya ba zhig byung ba de la kho mos de bzhin gshegs pa chu klung gang+gA nyi shu'i bye ma snyad cig bsnyen bkur to/ /
“There was a kalpa called Atulaprabha, in which I served as many tathāgatas as there are grains of sand in twenty Ganges Rivers.
there was an eon called Peerless Light, in which I served as many buddhas as sand grains in twenty Ganges Rivers;
bskal pa dpal shin tu 'bar ba zhes bya ba zhig byung ba de la kho mos de bzhin gshegs pa chu klung gang+gA'i bye ma snyed cig bsnyen bkur to/ /
“There was a kalpa called Uttaptaśrī, in which I served as many tathāgatas as there are grains of sand in one Ganges River.
there was an eon called Blazing Glory, in which I served as many buddhas as sand grains in the Ganges River;
bskal pa snying rje bzang po zhes bya ba zhig byung ba de la kho mos de bzhin gshegs pa chu klung gang+gA brgyad cu'i bye ma snyed cig bsnyen bkur to/ /
“There was a kalpa called Sūryodaya, in which I served as many tathāgatas as there are grains of sand in eighty Ganges Rivers.
there was an eon called Sunrise, in which I served as many buddhas as sand grains in eighty Ganges Rivers;
bskal pa rgyal bar gyur pa zhes bya ba zhig byung ba de la kho mos de bzhin gshegs pa chu klung gang+gA drug cu'i bye ma snyed cig bsnyen bkur to/ /
“There was a kalpa called Jayaṃgama, in which I served as many tathāgatas as there are grains of sand in sixty Ganges Rivers.
there was an eon called Victorious March, in which I served as many buddhas as sand grains in sixty Ganges Rivers;
bskal pa zla ba bzang po zhes bya ba zhig byung ba de la kho mos de bzhin gshegs pa chu klung gang+gA bdun cu'i bye ma snyed cig bsnyen bkur to/ /
“There was a kalpa called Sucandra, in which I served as many tathāgatas as there are grains of sand in seventy Ganges Rivers.
there was an eon called Beautiful Moon, in which I served as many buddhas as sand grains in seventy Ganges Rivers.

rigs kyi bu/ de ltar tshul bzhin du kho mos rtag tu rgyun ma chad par de bzhin gshegs pa dgra bcom pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas rnams dang bral bar ma gyur pa ni/ bskal pa chu klung gang+gA'i bye ma snyed cig dran te/ kho mos de bzhin gshegs pa de dag thams cad las byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa dran pa thogs pa med la rnam par dag pas brgyan pa 'di thos so/ / thos nas kyang yongs su bzung ngo/ / ji skad du gsungs pa bzhin du khong du chud do/ / rnam par thar pa 'di nyid la kho mo rtag tu rgyun ma chad par rjes su zhugs par gnas gnas te/ de bzhin gshegs pa de dag gis byang chub sems dpa'i sa nye bar bzung ba nas dam pa'i chos gnas pa zad pa'i mthar thug gi bar gyi sangs rgyas kyi rnam par 'phrul pa ji snyed pa de dag thams cad kyang byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa dran pa thogs pa med la rnam par dag pas brgyan pa 'dis dran no/ / rjes su dran no/ / bzung ngo/ / yongs su bzung ngo/ / nye bar bzung ngo/ / rjes su 'brang bar byed do/ /

“Noble one, in that way, I remember never being apart from the tathāgata arhat samyaksaṃbuddhas throughout kalpas as numerous as the grains of sand in the Ganges River. I heard from all those tathāgatas this bodhisattva liberation called the display of pure, unimpeded memory. I heard it and retained it. I comprehended whatever they said. I have constantly, always remained within this liberation. Through this bodhisattva liberation called the display of pure, unimpeded memory, I remember those tathāgatas from the time they attained the level of a bodhisattva until the time their Dharma ceased to exist. I recollect that, grasp that, retain that, reflect upon that, and follow that.

“In this way, I remember as many eons as sand grains in the Ganges River, during which I was always with buddhas, and I heard of this enlightening liberation of pure manifestation of unimpeded recollection from those buddhas, and practiced it as they told me. Thus, constantly engrossed in this liberation, I recollect, remember, keep in mind, reflect on, and recall the supernal manifestations of all those buddhas from their stages of enlightening to the end of the duration of their true teachings, by means of this enlightening liberation of pure manifestation of unimpeded recollection.

rigs kyi bu; kho mos byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa 'di shes par zad na/ kho mos byang chub sems dpa' mun pa'i mun nag dang bral ba/ 'khor ba'i nam nangs pa/ sgrib pa dang bral ba/ gnyid med pa la mos shing dga' ba/ snyom pa dang le lo rnam par spangs pa/ lus kyi 'du byed shin tu byang ba/ rtag par chos thams cad kyi rang bzhin khong du chud pas shin tu dag pa/ stobs bcu rnam par dag pa khong du chud pa de dag gi spyod pa shes pa'am/ yon tan brjod par nus re skan/

“Noble one, I know only this bodhisattva liberation called the display of pure, unimpeded memory. How could I know or describe the qualities of the bodhisattvas who are free from the blindness of darkness, who have risen out of saṃsāra, who are free of obscurations, who aspire not to be asleep, who are free of apathy and idleness, whose body formations are purified, who continuously understand the nature of all phenomena, and who have realized the pure ten strengths?

“I only know this enlightening liberation—how can I know the practice, or tell the virtues, of the enlightening beings who are free from all obscurity and darkness, who light up the night of the mundane whirl, who are rid of all obstacles, who do not slumber, who are rid of apathy and indolence, who have stopped compulsive actions based on conditioning, who have purified awareness of the essence of all things, who awaken others to the purity of the ten powers?

song rigs kyi bu/ grong khyer chen po ser skya'i gnas na byis pa'i slob dpon kun gyi bshes gnyen zhes bya ba 'dug gi/ de'i gan du song la ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bya ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bya ba dris shig /

“Depart, noble one. In the great city of Kapilavastu resides a teacher of children by the name of Viśvāmitra. Go to him and ask him, ‘How should a bodhisattva train in and practice bodhisattva conduct?’ ”
“In the city of Kapilavastu there lives a boy named Vishwamitra who is a teacher. Go ask him how to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings.”

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang dga' rangs te mgu zhing nyams bde la tshim zhing yid bde ba skyes nas dge ba'i rtsa ba bsam gyis mi khyab pa'i shugs drag po rnam par 'phel bas/ lha'i bu mo lha dbang 'od kyi rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te/ lha'i bu mo lha dbang 'od la lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas yang dang yang bltas te lha'i bu mo lha dbang 'od kyi drung nas song ngo/ /

Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, filled with joy, delighted, elated, pleased, and happy, bowed his head to the feet of the deva maiden Surendrābhā. He circumambulated the deva maiden Surendrābhā many hundreds of thousands of times, keeping her to his right, and, looking back at her again and again, departed from the deva maiden Surendrābhā.
Then Sudhana paid his respects and left the goddess Surendrabha.

Sudhana descended from the paradise of the lord of Trāyastriṃśa and eventually came to Viśvāmitra, the teacher of children, in the city of Kapilavastu. When he came to him, he bowed his head to the feet of Viśvāmitra, the teacher of children; circumambulated Viśvāmitra, the teacher of children, many hundreds of thousands of times, keeping him to his right; and then stood before Viśvāmitra, the teacher of children, with his palms together in homage and said,
Descending from the thirty-three-fold heaven, Sudhana made his way to Kapilavastu, where he went to see the young teacher Vishwamitra. Paying his respects, he stood before the teacher and said,

Ārya, I have heard that you give instruction and teachings to bodhisattvas! Ārya, I pray that you explain to me how bodhisattvas should train in bodhisattva conduct and how they should practice it!”

“Noble one, I have set my mind on supreme perfect enlightenment, but I do not know how to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings. I hear you give enlightening beings instruction, so please tell me how to learn and practice.”

When he had said that, Viśvāmitra, the teacher of children, said to Sudhana, the head merchant’s son,
Vishwamitra said,

rigs kyi bu/ tshong dpon gyi bu bzo mngon par shes pa zhes bya ba 'di ni/ byang chub sems dpa' las yi ge'i shes pa slob slob pa yin gyi/ 'di'i gan du song ste dris dang / 'di ni/ khyod la ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bya ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bya ba ston par 'gyur ro/ /zhes nas

“Noble one, Śilpābhijña, a head merchant’s son here, has studied the knowledge of words from bodhisattvas. You should go to him and ask him, and he will teach you how bodhisattvas should train in bodhisattva conduct and how they should practice it.”
“I learned the science of writing from a young enlightening being named Shilpabhijna. Go ask him and he will tell you how the practice of enlightening beings is to be learned and carried out.”

Shilpabhijna

Then Sudhana went to the youth Shilpabhijna, paid his respects, and said to him,

'phags pa/ bdag gis bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed na/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bgyi ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bgyi ba ma 'tshal te/ 'phags pa ni/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams la gdams ngag dang / rjes su bstan pa mdzad do/ /zhes bdag gis thos na/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bgyi ba dang / ji ltar nan tan du bgyi ba 'phags pas bdag la bka' stsal du gsol/
