don thams cad yang dag par len du 'jug pa'o/ /
They bring the acquisition of all benefits.
inspire us to our goals,
nan tan la gzengs bstod pa'o/ /
They inspire practice.
enhance efforts and attainments,
'byung ba'i sgo ston pa'o/ /
They reveal the door to setting forth.
show the ways to emancipation,
lam gol ba las yongs su srung ba'o/ /
They guard others from taking wrong paths.
protect us from the paths of destruction,
chos snang ba'i sgo snang bar byed pa'o/ /
They bring illumination from the gateways to the light of the Dharma.
illumine the ways to perceive truth,
chos kyi sgo mngon par rlan par byed pa'o/ /
They bring saturation from the doors of the Dharma.
chos thos par bya ba'i sprin gyi char rab tu 'bebs pa'o/ /
They send down a rain from clouds of hearing the Dharma.
shower multitudes of teachings,
nyon mongs pa thams cad zhi bar byed pa'o/ /
They cause all kleśas to cease.
extinguish all afflictions,
lta ba'i rnam pa thams cad las zlog pa'o/ /
They turn others away from all wrong views.
stop the formation of views,
sangs rgyas kyi chos thams cad la gnas par byed pa'o/ /
They establish others in all the Dharmas of the buddhas.
and introduce us to all aspects of enlightenment.
'di ltar yang rigs kyi bu/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen ni/ sangs rgyas kyi rigs su skyed bas ma lta bu'o/ /
“Noble one, in that way, the kalyāṇamitras are like mothers because they give birth to the family of the buddhas.
“Moreover, spiritual benefactors are mothers, giving birth to the family of buddhas;
dge ba'i bshes gnyen ni/ phan pa rgya chen po sgrub pas pha lta bu'o/ /
The kalyāṇamitras are like fathers because they accomplish great benefits.
they are fathers, producing great benefit;
dge ba'i bshes gnyen ni/ sdig pa thams cad las srung bas ma ma lta bu'o/ /
The kalyāṇamitras are like nannies because they guard from all bad actions.
they are nurses, protecting us from all evils;
dge ba'i bshes gnyen ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i bslab pa khong du chud par byed pas slob dpon lta bu'o/ /
The kalyāṇamitras are like teachers because they bring understanding of bodhisattva training.
they are mentors, elucidating the learning of enlightening beings;
dge ba'i bshes gnyen ni/ pha rol tu phyin pa'i lam du 'dzud pas lam mkhan lta bu'o/ /
The kalyāṇamitras are like guides because they bring others onto the bodhisattva path.
they are guides, leading us into the path of transcendence;
dge ba'i bshes gnyen ni/ nyon mongs pa'i nad las thar par byed pas sman pa lta bu'o/ /
The kalyāṇamitras are like doctors because they free others from the illness of the kleśas.
they are physicians, relieving us of the maladies of afflictions;
dge ba'i bshes gnyen ni/ ye shes kyi sman rnam par 'phel bar byed pas gangs kyi ri lta bu'o/ /
The kalyāṇamitras are like the Himalayas because they multiply the medicinal herbs of wisdom.
they are like the Himalaya Mountains, growing the herb of knowledge;
dge ba'i bshes gnyen ni/ 'jigs pa thams cad las srung bas dpa' bo lta bu'o/ /
The kalyāṇamitras are like heroes because they guard from all fears.
they are heroic warriors, protecting us from all perils;
dge ba'i bshes gnyen ni/ 'khor ba'i chu bo chen po las sgrol bas mnyan pa lta bu'o; ;
The kalyāṇamitras are like ferry captain because they bring others across the great river of saṃsāra.
they are ferrymen, ferrying us across the torrents of the mundane whirl;
dge ba'i bshes gnyen ni/ thams cad mkhyen pa'i ye shes rin po che'i gling du phyin par byed pas skye ba 'dzin pa lta bu'o/ /
The kalyāṇamitras are like sea captains because they take others to the island of the jewels of omniscient wisdom.
they are helmsmen, delivering us to the treasure island of omniscience.
rigs kyi bu/ de lta bas na/ de ltar yid la bya ba rgyun ma chad pas khyod kyi dge ba'i bshes gnyen bsnyen par gyis shig /khur thams cad bkur bas yongs su mi skyo ba'i phyir sa lta bu'i sems dad/
“Noble one, you should approach the kalyāṇamitras continuously, thinking in this way: You should approach the kalyāṇamitras with a mind like the earth for carrying all burdens without weariness,
“Therefore, thinking in this way, you should continue to approach spiritual benefactors, with a mind like the earth, bearing all burdens unbendingly;
mi phyed pa'i phyir rdo rje lta bu'i sems dang /
with a mind like a vajra because it is indestructible,
with a mind like adamant, having an unbreakable will;
sdug bsngal thams cad kyis mi sgul ba'i phyir khor yug lta bu'i sems dang /
with a mind like the Cakravāla mountain range because it is unaffected by any suffering,
with a mind like a mountain range, impenetrable to all miseries;
ci dga' bar bka' nyan pas bran lta bu'i sems dang /
with a mind like a slave because it gladly obeys,
with a mind like a servant, doing whatever is bidden;
ngag thams cad mi gcog pas slob ma lta bu'i sems dang /
with a mind like a pupil because it does not disobey instructions,
with a mind like a student, following all instructions;
las thams cad nyams su blang ba la mi smad pas 'jig rten gyi bran lta bu'i sems dang /
with a mind like a slave of the world because it takes on all tasks without resentment,
with a mind like a slave, willing to take on all tasks;
nyon mongs pa thams cad kyis mi skyo ba'i phyir ma ma lta bu'i sems dang /
with a mind like a nanny because it is unwearied by any kleśa,
with a mind like a nurse, not overcome by afflictions;
bya'o cog la mthun par gzung bas g.yog lta bu'i sems dang /
with a mind like a servant because it is prepared to do any kind of work,
with a mind like a servant, taking up any task obediently;
nga rgyal dang / mtho ba'i nga rgyal spangs pas phyag dar ba lta bu'i sems dang /
with a mind like a street sweeper because it is devoid of pride and arrogance,
with a mind like a street cleaner, getting rid of pride and conceit;
dus dang / dus ma yin par mtho dman du 'gyur bas zla ba nya lta bu'i sems dang /
with a mind like a full moon because it is lofty at the appropriate time and low at the inappropriate time,
with a mind like the full moon, appearing at the proper times;
mi srun pa thams cad rnam par spangs pas rta cang shes lta bu'i sems dang /
with a mind like a thoroughbred stallion because it is devoid of unruliness,
with a mind like a good horse, avoiding all unruliness;
khur lci ba bkur bas theg pa lta bu'i sems dang /
with a mind like a carriage because it can carry a heavy load,
with a mind like a vehicle, carrying a precious cargo;
dul ba dang / cang shes kyi bsam pas glang po lta bu'i sems dang /
with a mind like an elephant because it is tamed and well bred,
with a mind like an elephant, tame and docile;
mi sgul mi bskyod pas ri lta bu'i sems dang /
with a mind like a mountain because it is immovable and unshakable,
with a mind like a mountain, unshakable;
mi khro bas khyi lta bu'i sems dang /
with a mind like a dog because it is not angered,
with a mind like a dog, not getting angry;
nga rgyal dang dus med pas gdol ba lta bu'i sems dang /
with a mind like a caṇḍāla because it is without pride or egoism,[1966]
with a mind like an outcaste youth, free from arrogance and egotism;
dregs pa thams cad med pas khyu mchog ra bcad pa lta bu'i sems dang /
with a mind like a hornless bull because it is without arrogance,
with a mind like a bull with its horns cut off, stripped of all haughtiness;
rlom sems med pas mtshan bu lta bu'i sems dang /
with a mind like an in-house pupil[1967] because it has no haughtiness,
with a mind like an apprentice, free from inflated ideas of your own worth;
'gro zhing 'ong bas mi skyo bas gru lta bu'i sems dang /
with a mind like a boat because it is unwearied by coming and going,
with a mind like a ship, coming and going tirelessly;
dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi ngag gi mthar phyin par byed pas zam pa lta bu'i sems dang /
with a mind like a bridge because it reaches the conclusion of the kalyāṇamitra’s instruction,
with a mind like a bridge, crossing over with the directions of spiritual benefactors;
dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi ngor lta bas bu mdzangs ba lta bu'i sems dang /
with a mind like an excellent son[1968] because it looks up at the face of the kalyāṇamitra,
with a mind like a good son, looking up to the countenance of spiritual benefactors;
chos kyi rgyal po'i bka' las mi 'gal bar bya bas rgyal po gzhon nu lta bu'i sems kyis dge ba'i bshes gnyen la bsnyen par bya'o/ /
and with a mind like a prince because it does not disobey the king of the Dharma.
with a mind like a prince, carrying out the directives of the spiritual king.

rigs kyi bu; khyod kyis bdag la nad par 'du shes bskyed do/ / dge ba'i bshes gnyen la ni/ sman pa'i 'du shes dang / gdams ngag la ni/ sman gyi 'du shes dang / nan tan nyams su blang ba la ni/ nad 'tsho ba'i 'du shes bskyed par bya'o/ /

“Noble one, you should think of yourself as a sick person, think of the kalyāṇamitra as a doctor, think of the instructions as medicine, and think of dedication to their practice as being healed from illness.
“Think of yourself as sick, and think of spiritual benefactors as physicians; think of their instructions as medicines, and think of the practices as getting rid of disease.

rigs kyi bu/ khyod kyis bdag la ni/ 'gron po'i 'du shes bskyed pa'o/ / dge ba'i bshes gnyen la ni/ lam mtshon pa'i 'du shes dang / gdams ngag la ni/ lam gyi 'du shes dang / nan tan la ni/ phyogs bde bar 'gro ba'i 'du shes bskyed par bya'o/ /
“Noble one, you should think of yourself as a traveler, think of the kalyāṇamitra as a guide, think of the instructions as the path, and think of their practice as traveling safely.
Think of yourself as a traveler, and think of spiritual benefactors as guides; think of their instructions as the road, and think of the practices as going to the land of your destination.

rigs kyi bu/ khyod kyis bdag la ni/ pha rol tu 'gro ba'i 'du shes bskyed par bya'o/ / dge ba'i bshes gnyen la ni/ mnyan pa'i 'du shes dang / rjes su bstan pa la ni/ mu stegs kyi 'du shes dang / nan tan la ni/ gru'i 'du shes bskyed par bya'o/ /

“Noble one, you should think of yourself as someone crossing to the opposite shore, think of the kalyāṇamitra as a ferry captain, think of the teachings as the jetty, and think of their practice as the boat.
Think of yourself as crossing over to the other shore, and think of spiritual benefactors as boatmen; think of their instructions as a ford, and think of the practices as a boat.

rigs kyi bu/ khyod kyis bdag la ni/ zhing pa'i 'du shes bskyed par bya'o/ / dge ba'i bshes gnyen la ni/ klu'i dbang po'i 'du shes dang / gdams ngag la ni/ char pa'i 'du shes dang / nan tan la ni/ lo tog 'grub pa'i 'du shes bskyed par bya'o/ /
“Noble one, you should think of yourself as a farmer, think of the kalyāṇamitra as a nāga[1969] lord, think of the instructions as rain, and think of their practice as cultivating a harvest.
Think of yourself as a farmer, and think of spiritual benefactors as water spirits; think of their instructions as rain, and think of the practices as the ripening of the crops.

rigs kyi bu/ khyod kyis bdag la ni/ dbul po'i 'du shes bskyed par bya'o/ / dge ba'i bshes gnyen la ni/ ngal bso ba'i 'du shes dang / gdams ngag la ni/ nor dang / don gyi 'du shes dang / nan tan la ni/ dbul ba sel ba'i 'du shes bskyed par bya'o/ /

“Noble one, you should think of yourself as a poor person, think of the kalyāṇamitra as Vaiśravaṇa, think of the instructions as wealth and gifts, and think of their practice as becoming free from poverty.
Think of yourself as a pauper, and think of spiritual benefactors as the givers of wealth; think of their instructions as wealth, and think of the practices as getting rid of poverty.

rigs kyi bu/ khyod kyis bdag la ni/ slob ma'i 'du shes bskyed par bya'o; ; dge ba'i bshes gnyen la ni/ slob dpon gyi 'du shes dang / gdams ngag la ni/ bzo'i 'du shes dang / nan tan la ni/ bzo khong du chud pa'i 'du shes bskyed par bya'o/ /
“Noble one, you should think of yourself as a pupil, think of the kalyāṇamitra as a teacher, think of the instructions as the arts, and think of their practice as learning the arts.
Think of yourself as an apprentice, and think of spiritual benefactors as mentors; think of their instructions as arts, and think of the practices as accomplishments.

rigs kyi bu/ khyod kyis bdag la ni/ 'jigs pa'i 'du shes bskyed par bya'o/ / dge ba'i bshes gnyen la ni/ dpa' bo'i 'du shes dang / gdams ngag la ni/ mtshon cha'i 'du shes dang / nan tan la ni/ dgra sel ba'i 'du shes bskyed par bya'o/ /
“Noble one, you should think of yourself as someone in danger, think of the kalyāṇamitra as a hero, think of the instructions as weapons, and think of their practice as the elimination of enemies.
Think of yourself as fearless, and think of spiritual benefactors as heroic warriors; think of their instructions as attack, and think of the practices as vanquishing enemies.

rigs kyi bu/ khyod kyis bdag la ni/ tshong pa'i 'du shes bskyed par bya'o/ / dge ba'i bshes gnyen la ni/ skya ba 'dzin pa'i 'du shes dang / gdams ngag la ni/ rin po che'i 'du shes dang / nan tan la ni/ rin po che'i sdud pa'i 'du shes bskyed par bya'o/ /
“Noble one, you should think of yourself as a merchant, think of the kalyāṇamitra as a sea captain, think of the instructions as jewels, and think of their practice as gathering jewels.
Think of yourself as a merchant, and think of spiritual benefactors as ship captains; think of their instructions as treasure, and think of the practices as obtaining treasures.

rigs kyi bu/ khyod kyis bdag la ni/ bu dam pa'i 'du shes bskyed par byed pa'o/ / dge ba'i bshes gnyen la ni/ pha ma'i 'du shes dang / rjes su bstan pa la ni/ rigs kyi tshul gyi 'du shes dang / nan tan la ni/ tshul ma nyams pa'i 'du shes bskyed par bya'o/ /

“Noble one, you should think of yourself as a good son, think of the kalyāṇamitra as your parents, think of the instructions as the behavior of someone from a good family, and think of their practice as keeping to that good behavior.

Think of yourself as a good son, and think of spiritual benefactors as parents; think of their instructions as the family business, and think of the practices as the perpetuation of the family business.

rigs kyi bu/ khyod kyis bdag la ni; rgyal po gzhon nu'i 'du shes bskyed par bya'o/ / dge ba'i bshes gnyen la ni chos kyi rgyal po dang / blon po dam pa'i 'du shes dang / gdams ngag la ni/ rgyal po'i khrims kyi 'du shes dang / nan tan la ni/ ye shes kyi rgyal po'i cod pan dang / rgyan dang / chos kyi thabs mgo la bcing ba dang / chos kyi rgyal po'i grong khyer la rnam par lta ba'i 'du shes bskyed par bya ste/

“Noble one, you should think of yourself as a prince, think of the kalyāṇamitra as a Dharma king and the prime minister, think of the instructions as the king’s law, and think of their practice as looking at the crown and adornments of the king of wisdom, the turban of the Dharma bound upon his head, and the Dharma king’s city.

Think of yourself as a prince, and think of spiritual benefactors as the chief ministers of a spiritual king; think of their instructions as the precepts of kingship, and think of the practices as putting on the turban of truth adorned with the crest of knowledge and overseeing the capital of the spiritual sovereign.
rigs kyi bu/ khyod kyis de lta bu'i 'du shes yid la bya ba yongs su bsgoms te dge ba'i bshes gnyen rnams la nye bar bsnyen par gyis shig/
“Noble one, you should approach the kalyāṇamitras meditating on those thoughts and perceptions of the kalyāṇamitras.
“You should approach spiritual benefactors with these thoughts in mind.

de ci'i phyir zhe na/ rigs kyi bu/ de ltar dge ba'i bshes gnyen la lhag pa'i bsam pa yongs su dag pa'i byang chub sems dpa' rnams ni/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi ngag thams cad nyams su len pa'i tshe gangs kyi ri la brten pa'i dang / gel pa dang / sman dang / nags tshal lta bu dge ba'i rtsa ba thams cad kyis rnam par 'phel lo/ /

“Why is that? Noble one, it is because when a bodhisattva, who has a pure superior motivation toward the kalyāṇamitras, is practicing all the instructions of the kalyāṇamitras, all the bodhisattva’s roots of merit will increase like the grass, bushes, herbs, and forests that depend on the Himalayas.

Why? With their attitude toward spiritual benefactors purified in this way, practicing the instructions of spiritual benefactors, enlightening beings grow in goodness, like plants, bushes, and trees growing up the mountains;
rgya mtsho chen po chu'i snod du gyur pa ltar chos thams cad kyi snod du 'gyur ro/ /
The bodhisattva becomes a container of all Dharmas just as the great ocean is a container of water.
they become vessels of all buddha-teachings, as the oceans are of water;
gang chen mtsho chen po rin po che mang po'i 'byung gnas su gyur pa ltar yon tan thams cad kyi 'byung gnas su 'gyur ro/ /
The bodhisattva becomes the source of many qualities just as the great ocean is a source of many jewels.
they become repositories of all virtues, as the seas are of pearls;
me'i drod kyis gser yongs su 'byang ba ltar byang chub kyi sems yongs su byang bar 'gyur ro/ /
The bodhisattva purifies just as the heat of fire purifies gold.
they purify the determination for enlightenment, as fire does gold;
rgya mtsho chen po las 'phags pa'i ri rab ltar 'jig rten las mngon par 'phags par 'gyur ro/ /
The bodhisattva is higher than the world just as Sumeru is higher than the ocean.
they rise above the world, like the polar mountain over the sea;
pad+mo la chus mi chags pa ltar 'jig rten gyi chos kyis mi gos par 'gyur ro/ /
The bodhisattva is unstained by the worldly qualities just as water does not cling to lotuses.
they become unstained by things of the world, like a lotus in water;
rgya mtsho chen po ro rul pa dang mi 'grogs pa ltar spyod pa ngan pa thams cad dang mi 'grogs so/ /
The bodhisattva does not keep company with bad behavior just as the ocean does not keep a corpse.
they reject all bad actions, as the ocean throws up a corpse;
yud du yar gyi zla ba ltar chos dkar pos rnam par 'phel bar 'gyur ro/ /
The bodhisattva increases good qualities just like the phase of the waxing moon.
they increase in good qualities, as the moon grows brighter as it waxes;
dzam+bu'i gling snang bar byed pa'i nyi ma ltar chos kyi dbyings su snang bar 'gyur ro/ /
The bodhisattva illuminates the realm of the Dharma just as the sun illuminates the world.
they illumine the reality realm, as the sun does the earth;
pha ma dang 'grogs pa'i bu ltar byang chub sems dpa'i smon lam gyi lus thams cad yang dag par skye bar 'gyur ro/ /
The bodhisattva has bodies that are all born from prayer just as a son is associated with his parents.
they grow the bodies of vows of enlightening beings, just as children grow in the care of their parents.

de ltar mdor na/ rigs kyi bu/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi gdams ngag la zhugs pa'i byang chub sems dpa' rnams ni/ yon tan bye ba khrag khrig brgya stong brjod du med pa phrag bcu ni/ rab tu 'dzin par 'gyur ro/ /
“In brief, noble one, the bodhisattvas who follow thus the instructions of the kalyāṇamitras possess uncountable millions of quintillions of qualities.
“In short, enlightening beings who have put the instruction of spiritual benefactors into effect embody untold virtues,
de'i lhag pa'i bsam pa bye ba khrag khrig brgya stong phrag bcu ni/ rab tu 'phel bar 'gyur ro/ /
They purify millions of quintillions of higher motivations.
purify untold resolutions,
byin gyi rlabs bye ba khrag khrig brgya stong phrag bcu ni/ rnam par sbyong bar 'gyur ro/ /
They increase millions of quintillions of bodhisattva powers.
develop untold enlightening faculties,
sgrib pa'i chos bye ba khrag khrig brgya stong phrag bcu ni/ yongs su spyod par 'gyur ro/ /
They purify[1970] millions of quintillions of empowerments.
purify untold mystic powers,
sgrib pa'i chos grangs med pa brgya stong phrag bcu ni/ yongs su dag par 'gyur ro/ /
They purify away millions of quintillions of obscurations.
perfect untold worthy practices,
bdud grangs med pa brgya stong phrag bcu las ni/ yang dag par 'dam par 'gyur ro/ /
They transcend millions of quintillions of māras.
get beyond untold demons,
chos kyi sgo grangs med pa brgya stong phrag bcu la ni/ rab tu 'jug par 'gyur ro/ /
They enter millions of quintillions of Dharma gateways.
abide by untold ways to truth,
tshogs rnam par dag pa'i sgo grangs med pa bye ba khrag khrig brgya stong phrag bcu ni/ yongs su rdzogs par 'gyur ro/ /
They complete millions of quintillions of accumulations.
fulfill untold ways of purifying virtue and knowledge,
spyod pa grangs med pa brgya stong phrag bcu ni/ kun nas dag par 'gyur ro/ /
They purify millions of quintillions of conducts.
fulfill untold deeds,
smon lam chen po grangs med pa brgya stong phrag bcu ni/ mngon par grub par 'gyur ro/ /
They accomplish millions of quintillions of great prayers.
purify untold modes of conduct, carry out untold vows.
rigs kyi bu/ de ltar mdor na/ byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa thams cad dang /
“Thus, noble one, in brief, all bodhisattva conduct,
“In sum, all practices of enlightening beings,
byang chub sems dpa'i pha rol tu phyin pa thams cad dang /
all bodhisattva perfections,
all transcendent ways of enlightening beings,
byang chub sems dpa'i sa thams cad dang /
all bodhisattva bhūmis,
all stages of enlightening beings,
byang chub sems dpa'i bzod pa la 'jug pa thams cad dang /
all bodhisattva entries into patience,
byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin gyi sgo thams cad dang /
all bodhisattva gateways to samādhi,
all concentrations of enlightening beings,
byang chub sems dpa'i mngon par shes pa'i ye shes kyi rnam par 'phrul pa thams cad dang /
all bodhisattva miraculous manifestations through the wisdom of higher cognition,
all mystic knowledges and spiritual powers of enlightening beings,
byang chub sems dpa'i gzungs dang spobs pa'i snang ba thams cad dang /
all the bodhisattva illumination through mental retention and eloquence,
all manifestations of mental command and intellectual power of enlightening beings,
byang chub sems dpa'i bsngo ba'i ye shes dang / mngon par shes pa tshad med pa thams cad dang /
all limitless ripened[1971] wisdom and higher cognition,
all knowledge of dedication and infinity of superknowledge of enlightening beings,
byang chub sems dpa'i smon lam mngon par sgrub pa thams cad dang /
all the accomplishment of bodhisattva prayers,
all accomplishments of vows of enlightening beings,
sangs rgyas kyi chos thams cad rab tu thob cing yongs su grub pa rnams ni/
and all attainment and accomplishment of buddha qualities
and all perfections of attainments of all aspects of buddhahood,
dge ba'i bshes gnyen la rag las pa dang /
depend on the kalyāṇamitras,
derive from spiritual benefactors,
go ;dge ba'i bshes gnyen rtsa bar gyur pa dag go /
have the kalyāṇamitras as their root,
are rooted in spiritual benefactors,
dge ba'i bshes gnyen las byung ba dag go /
come from the kalyāṇamitras,
dge ba'i bshes gnyen skye gnas su gyur pa dag go /
have the kalyāṇamitras as their source,
dge ba'i bshes gnyen skye mched du gyur pa dag go /
have the kalyāṇamitras as their origin,[1972]
dge ba'i bshes gnyen las yongs su skyes pa dag go /
are born from the kalyāṇamitras,
are born of spiritual benefactors,
dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyis yongs su spel ba dag go /
are increased by the kalyāṇamitras,
are fostered by spiritual benefactors,
dge ba'i bshes gnyen la rab tu brten pa dag go /
are based on the kalyāṇamitras,
are based on spiritual benefactors,
dge ba'i bshes gnyen rgyur gyur pa'o/ /
have the kalyāṇamitras as their cause,
are caused by spiritual benefactors,
dge ba'i bshes gnyen las rab tu skyes pa dag go /
and arise from the kalyāṇamitras.”
are produced by spiritual benefactors.”

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis rnam pa de lta bu'i dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi yon tan dang / bsngags pa rjes su bstan pa dang / byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa tshad med pa dang / sangs rgyas kyi chos rgya chen po thos nas dga' rangs te mgu zhing nyams bde la tshim zhing yid bde ba skyes nas khye'u dpal 'byung dang / bu mo dpal gyi blo gros ma gnyis kyi rkang pa la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te khye'u dpal 'byung ba dang / bu mo dpal gyi blo gros ma gnyis la lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas khye'u dpal 'byung ba dang / bu mo dpal gyi blo gros ma'i drung nas song ngo// //

Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, having listened to the teaching that praised the qualities of the kalyāṇamitras, having listened to limitless bodhisattva conduct and the vast qualities of the buddhas, was filled with joy, delighted, elated, pleased, and happy, and he bowed his head to the feet of the boy Śrīsaṃbhava and the girl Śrīmati. He circumambulated the boy Śrīsaṃbhava and the girl Śrīmati many hundreds of thousands of times, keeping them to his right, and, looking back at them again and again, he departed from the boy Śrīsaṃbhava and the girl Śrīmati.

Now Sudhana, hearing about the virtues and qualities of spiritual benefactors, about the infinity of practice of enlightening beings, and the vastness of the buddha-teaching, was thoroughly delighted and uplifted in mind. He then paid his respects again to the boy Shrisambhava and the girl Shrimati and took his leave.
shin tu rgyas pa chen po'i mdo/ sangs rgyas phal po che zhes bya ba las/ sdong pos brgyan pa'i le'u ste; ; bam po brgya bcu gcig pa/
[byang chub sems dpa' byams pa]
Chapter 54. Maitreya
Maitreya

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi gdams ngag gis sems mngon par brlan pa de/ byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa rjes su bstan pa de ni/ rjes su rnam par sems/ sngon gyi mtha'i lus mang po yang dag pa'i spyod pa nyams su ma blangs par chud zos pa la bsam pas ni/ lus kyi stobs rab tu brtan par byed/

Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, his mind moistened by the instructions of the kalyāṇamitra, contemplated bodhisattva conduct. Thinking of how his many bodies in the past had failed to practice perfect conduct, he made resolute the strength of his body.

Then Sudhana, his mind enriched by the instructions of spiritual benefactors, went to the region of Samudrakaccha, contemplating that instruction in the conduct of enlightening beings, strengthening his body by thinking of past activities inconsistent with proper conduct,
sngon gyi mtha'i mur thug pa'i lus dang / sems yongs su dag kyang don med par 'khor ba'i sems kyi rgyud du gyur pa la bsam pas ni; sems dang yid la bya ba rab tu sbyong /
Thinking of how his body and mind throughout the past, even though pure, were the worthless continuation of a saṃsāric mind, he applied the attention of his mind to conduct.
controlling his thoughts by thinking of past mundane mental behavior not conducive to purification of body and mind,

sngon gyi mtha'i mur thug pa'i las yang dag pa ma yin pas 'jig rten gyi don du g.yen spyo ste mi gces par sha thang pa la bsam pas ni/ da ltar byung ba'i don shin tu gces pa la legs par sgrub pa rnam par sems/
Thinking how his actions throughout the past had been impure, had been devoted to the world, and were worthless hardships, he contemplated accomplishing in the present that which is very meaningful.
contemplating the greater common weal in the present by thinking of the vanity of past involvement in harmful mundane activities,

sngon gyi mtha'i mur thug pa'i yongs su rtog pa yang dag pa ma yin par rnam par brtags pa las byung ba/ phyin ci log gis yid la bya ba'i kun nas glags pa la bsam pas ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa thams cad yang dag pa'i rtog pas mngon par 'du bya ba'i stobs yang dag par skyed/
Thinking how throughout the past he had developed thoughts through incorrect examination, he generated the strength to create the correct examination of bodhisattva conduct.
establishing the power of forming correct ideas of the practice of enlightening beings by thinking of former untrue notions based on mere fancy,

'das pa'i lus kyis bdag gi don gyi sbyor pa la rtsom rtsom pa'i yul la yongs su bsam pas ni/ sems can thams cad kyi sbyor ba las khyad par du 'phags par lhag pa'i bsam pas ni/ stobs rab tu brtan par byed/

Thinking how his past bodies had a range of activity[1973] dedicated to engaging in self-benefit, he made firm the strength of his superior, higher motivation to engage in benefiting[1974] all beings.
strengthening the will based on the excellence of striving for the welfare of all beings by thinking of the ills of past striving for his own personal benefit,

sngon 'dod pa yongs su tshol tshol ba'i spyod pa ro med pa la yongs su bsam pas ni/ sangs rgyas kyi chos thams cad 'thob pa'i sbyor bas dbugs phyin pa chen po 'thob pa'i dbang po'i shugs drag po rnam par 'phel bar byed/

Thinking how in the past he had the flavorless conduct of continually seeking what was desired, he increased the great force of the power for attaining relief through engaging in obtaining the Dharma of the buddhas.
increasing the energy of his faculties with great inspiration to strive to attain all elements of buddhahood by thinking of past indulgence in pleasure seeking;

'das pa'i dus kyi lhag pa'i bsam pa phyin ci log dang ldan pa'i sbyor ba la yongs su bsam pas ni/ da ltar byung ba'i dus su phyin ci log med pa dang ldan pa'i yang dag pa'i lta ba dang / byang chub sems dpa'i smon lam la yi dam bca' bas sems kyi rgyud yongs su rgyas par byed/

Thinking how in the past he had engaged in conduct through an incorrect motivation, he purified[1975] the flow of his mind in the present with a correct view that was free of error and with dedication to bodhisattva prayer.

purifying his being with the vow of enlightening beings connected with correct perception in the present free from delusion by thinking of past endeavors made up of error inextricably bound up with delusion;

sngon gyi mtha'i brtson 'grus brtsams pa mi cha la don ma yin pa dang / yongs su ma grub pa'i brtson 'grus nyams su blangs pa la yongs su bsam pas ni/ da ltar byung ba'i dus su sangs rgyas kyi chos yongs su bsdu ba la sta gon du gnas pa'i brtson 'grus chen po rtsom pa'i rnam par gnon pas lus dang sems kyi gzengs mtho ba yang dag par skyed/

Thinking how in the past he fruitlessly had no diligence in his undertakings and practiced without diligence, in the present he motivated his mind and body by generating the diligence for remaining prepared to gather the Dharmas of the buddhas.
unifying body and mind with great vigor in action by thinking of past accomplishment of tasks through exertion of great vigor and striving for the attainment of complete buddhahood in the present;

sngon gyi mtha'i mur thug pa'i 'gro ba lnga'i rgyud kyi ngan song du bdag dang gzhan bor ba la brtag pas lus 'tsho ba med pa yongs su bzung ba la yang dag par bsam pas ni/ sangs rgyas kyi chos thams cad yongs su sgrub pa dang / 'gro ba thams cad nye bar 'tsho ba dang / dge ba'i bshes gnyen thams cad bsnyen bkur bar nus pa'i lus yongs su bzung bas dga' ba dang / mos pa'i shugs drag po rgya chen po rnam par 'phel bar byed/

Examining how he and others had been lost in the lower realms and[1976] the five classes of beings, and thinking how in the past he had not taken care of his body, he increased a vast, powerful rejoicing and aspiration for maintaining a body with the power to accomplish all the Dharmas of the buddhas, take care of all beings, and serve all kalyāṇamitras.

developing great joy and happiness by thinking how it would be to go on forever as in the past—helpless amid the ills of unenlightened life—and instead dedicating himself to the aid and benefit of all beings by establishing all the teachings of enlightenment,

da ltar byung ba'i tsher mngon par grub kyang dga' ba dang / na ba dang / 'chi ba dang / mya ngan gyi 'byung gnas su gyur te/ 'du ba dang 'bral ba'i gter du gyur pa'i lus kyang phyi ma'i mtha'i bskal pa'i mur thug par byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa spyad pa la brtson pa dang / sems can yongs su smin par bya ba dang / sangs rgyas kyi chos yongs su bsdu ba la brtson pa dang / de bzhin gshegs pa'i zhal lta zhing zhing thams cad du rgyu ba dang / chos smra ba thams cad la rim gror bya ba dang / de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi bstan pa yongs su bzung ba la brtson pa dang / chos thams cad yongs su btsal ba'i grogs su gyur pa dang / dge ba'i bshes gnyen thams cad mthong bar bya ba dang / sangs rgyas kyi chos thams cad yang dag par bsdu ba la brtson pa'i byang chub sems dpa'i smon lam dang / ye shes kyi lus kyi rgyu dang rkyen du gyur pa la bltas shing / dge ba'i rtsa ba'i dbang po dang / shugs bsam gyis mi khyab pa rnam par 'phel bar byed cing

He looked upon the body he had attained at that present time as the basis for illness, death, and misery, as a treasure that comes together and comes apart, and as the cause and condition for dedication to the practice of bodhisattva conduct until the last future kalpa; for dedication to ripening beings and possessing[1977] the Dharma of the buddhas; for dedication to seeing the tathāgatas, going to all realms, venerating all dharmabhāṇakas, and acquiring the teachings of all the tathāgatas; for help in the search for all Dharmas; for dedication to seeing all kalyāṇamitras and gathering all the Dharma of the buddhas; and for bodhisattva prayers and a body of wisdom.[1978] Thus he increased the inconceivable power and force of his roots of merit.

developing energy in his faculties rooted in inconceivable good by seeing this present life as a cause of old age, sickness, death, and grief, an abode of assemblage and disintegration, and yet the basis and condition of carrying out the practice of enlightening beings forever, absorbing the buddha-teachings that mature sentient beings, seeing the buddhas and going to all their lands, attending all teachers of truth, keeping the instructions of all buddhas, seeking all truths, meeting all spiritual friends, realizing all elements of buddhahood, and embodying the vows of enlightening beings.
de lta bu'i sems dang / de lta bu'i yid la bya ba dang / tshul bzhin de lta bu la rab tu brtson pa dang / byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi mos pas yang dag par bsgrubs pa'i dad pa dang /
With such a motivation, such thoughts, and such fundamental dedication, with the faith that is created by the belief of all bodhisattvas,
In this frame of mind, with these thoughts, engaged in such reasoning, with faith in the grace of all enlightening beings,

byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi bsam pas yongs su bsgrubs pa'i nye bar sems pa dang / byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi lhag pa'i bsam pas sgro btags pa'i rim gro dang / byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi dbang po dang bar sgro btags pa'i phu dud dang / byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi ston pa la mos pas yang dag par bsgrubs pa'i dbang po dang ba'i shugs dang /

with the regard that is created by the aspirations of all bodhisattvas, with the respect that is created by the higher motivation of all bodhisattvas, with the reverence that is created by the power of the belief of all bodhisattvas, with the strength of the power of belief that is created by the aspiration to buddhas[1979] by all bodhisattvas,

with admiration for the determination of all enlightening beings, with respect for the determination of all enlightening beings, with reverence for the purity of the senses of all enlightening beings, with the powers of purity of sense derived from attentiveness to the teachings of all enlightening beings,

byang chub sems dpa' thams cad la rim gros byung ba'i sems kyi mos pa dang / byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi dad pa las yongs su byung ba'i dge ba'i rtsa ba'i tshogs dang / byang chub sems dpa'i mngon par 'du bya ba thams cad las yongs su grub pa'i mchod pa rnam pa tha dad pa dang / byang chub sems dpa' thams cad dang mnyam pa'i lus kyi thal mo sbyar ba dang /

with the mind’s belief that comes forth from the veneration of all bodhisattvas, with the accumulation of roots of merit that arise from the faith of all bodhisattvas, with the different kinds of offerings that are created from all the activities of all the bodhisattvas, with the body having the hands placed together in homage in the same way as that of all bodhisattvas,

with clarity of mind deriving from respecting all enlightening beings, with provisions of roots of goodness deriving from faith in all enlightening beings, with varieties of offerings deriving from the accomplishments of all enlightening beings, with expressions of respect made equally to all enlightening beings,
'gro ba'i lus thams cad du yongs su byung ba'i mig rnam pa sna tshogs kyis blta ba dang /
looking with the different kinds of vision of the bodies of all beings,
with observations of the variety of eyes developed in the bodies of all beings,

'gro bar ming btags pa thams cad du sgro btags pa'i byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi chos mnyam pa nyid rnams dang / byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi smon lam gyis sprul pa las byung bar sgro btags pa'i lus kyis 'dud cing phyag bya ba tshad med pa dang /

with the equality of the Dharma of all who are designated as bodhisattvas for all who are designated as beings, with countless designated bodies bowing and paying homage that come from the miraculous manifestations through the prayers of all bodhisattvas,[1980]

byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi dbyangs kyi yan lag rnam par dag pa las byung ba'i legs pa brjod pa'i rgyan mngon par sgrub pa dang / sngon gyi mtha' dang / da ltar byung ba'i dus su byung ba'i sems can gyi gnas kyi gnas thams cad yongs su rgyas pa'i de bzhin gshegs pa'i pho brang mngon du byas pa'i 'du shes kyi rnam pa dang / de bzhin gshegs pa dang / byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par 'phrul pas mngon par rdzogs par 'tshang rgya ba thams cad du khyab pa dang /

with the accomplishment of the display of recited praises that come from the aspects of the voices of all bodhisattvas, filled with the blessing of all the bodhisattvas in the past and present,[1981] with the direct perception of the residence of the tathāgatas, with the all-pervading enlightenment miraculously manifested by the tathāgatas and bodhisattvas,

with productions of arrays of descriptions of the conceptual worlds of all beings made with the clarity of expression of all enlightening beings, with perception of the state of presence in the abodes of all buddhas by fulfillment of the mystic power of all enlightening beings of past and present, with awareness of the miracles of buddhas and enlightening beings everywhere,

skra'i rtse mo gcig las kyang lhag pa med par byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyis rgyas par 'gengs pa'i rjes su song ba dang / byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi mig gi lam rnam par dag par sgro btags pa'i mngon par shes pa snang bas rnam par dmigs pa dang / phyogs kyi dra ba tha dad pa thams cad kyi rjes su song ba'i yid kyi skye mched dang / chos kyi dbyings kyi gzhi tha dad pa rgyas par 'gengs pa'i smon la ma mngon par sgrub pa'i stobs dang /

following the bodies of all bodhisattvas pervading nothing greater than a single hair, with the perception illuminated by the higher cognition that conceives of the pure path of vision of all bodhisattvas, with the mental āyatana that follows all the different networks of the directions, with the strength that accomplishes the prayer that pervades all the different surfaces in the realm of phenomena,

following the all-pervasiveness of the bodies of all buddhas and enlightening beings in every single point, with perception of the light of superknowledge of the purity of vision of all enlightening beings, with a mind sense comprehending the network of all places as a whole, pervading all levels of the cosmos,

chos thams cad la 'jug pa'i sgo nam mkha'i dbyings kyis klas te mthas gtugs par thams cad du khyab la/ dus gsum du tha mi dad cing rgyun mi 'chad pa dang / dad pa dang / mos pa la 'jug pa'i stobs dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi gdams ngag snang ba'i phyogs la zhugs pas yul rgya mtsho'i 'gram gang na ba der phyin te/

with the gateways for entering all the Dharma pervading everywhere to the ends of the realm of space, continuously and with no difference in the three times, with the strength of entering faith and aspiration, and with the illumination of the instructions of the kalyāṇamitras spreading into the directions reaching the shore of the ocean of realms,

with the power of accomplishment of vows, extending everywhere throughout the entirety of space, continuous through past, present, and future, ceaselessly penetrating all truths, entering all areas illumined by the instructions of all spiritual benefactors, by the penetrating power of faith and resolve,

de ltar tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang rim gro dang phu dud dang / mchod pa dang / bstod pa dang / phyag bya ba dang / blta ba'i byin gyi rlabs dang / smon lam dang / 'du shes kyi rjes su song ba de lta bu'i yid dang ldan pa dang / ye shes kyi spyod yul tshad med pa'i sa de lta bu la zhugs pa'i ye shes kyi mig gis khang pa brtsegs pa chen po rnam par snang mdzad kyi rgyan gyis brgyan pa'i snying po'i sgo nas lus thams cad kyis phab ste phyag byas so/ /

Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, in that way, with a mind following such a perception of respect, veneration, offering, praise, homage, the blessing of seeing, and prayer, with the eyes of wisdom that comprehended such a level of the immeasurable field of activity of wisdom, prostrated himself at the door of the great kūṭāgāra called Vairocanavyūhālaṃkāragarbha.

Sudhana, his mind pursuing such thoughts of respect, reverence, honor, submission, regard, empowerment, and determination, with the eye of knowledge intent upon the ground of the realm of such infinite knowledge, prostrated himself in front of the door of the great tower, chamber of the adornments of Vairocana, the illuminator.

des rnam pa de lta bu'i mngon par sgrub pa'i tshul yud tsam du rnam par dpyad de mos pa dang / dad pa las byung ba'i lhag pa'i bsam pa dang / smon lam gyis mngon par bsgrubs pa'i mthus de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi zhabs kyi drung du bdag nyid rgyun mi 'chad par byin gyis brlabs so/ /

In that way, for a moment he examined that kind of accomplishment and, through the power of accomplishment through the higher motivation and prayer that arise from aspiration and faith, was empowered to continuously be at the feet of all the tathāgatas.

Contemplating such application of accomplishment for a while, by the power of effectuation of resolute vows, deriving from intense faith, Sudhana projected himself continuously into the presence of all buddhas,

de bzhin du byang chub sems dpa' thams cad dang mngon sum du gnas pa dang / dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyis gnas thams cad dang / de bzhin gshegs pa'i mchod rten thams cad dang / de bzhin gshegs pa'i sku gzugs thams cad dang / sangs rgyas dang byang chub sems dpa'i pho brang thams cad dang / chos rin po che'i gnas thams cad dang / nyan thos dang / rang sangs rgyas thams cad kyi gnas dang / mchod rten thams cad mngon sum du gnas pa nas 'phags pa'i tshogs dang / sbyin pa'i gnas dang / bla ma dang / pha ma thams cad kyi bar gyi 'gro ba'i tshogs thams cad dang / mngon sum du gnas pa rgyun mi 'chad par ye shes kyi lus tha mi dad pa'i tshul la 'jug pa thams cad kyi rjes su song ba dang / 'du shes kyi byin gyi rlabs dang / ye shes yid la bya bas byin gyis brlabs so/ /

In the same way, he was empowered to be directly before all bodhisattvas, before the locations of all kalyāṇamitras, before all the caityas of the tathāgatas, before all the statues of the tathāgatas, before all the palaces of the buddhas and bodhisattvas, before all the locations of the precious Dharma, and before the locations and caityas of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas. He was continuously and directly present in all the gatherings of beings up to the gatherings of the āryas, in the places of offering, and before gurus and parents, through the way of undifferentiated wisdom bodies going everywhere with empowered perception and empowered by the mental activity of wisdom.

and likewise into the presence of all enlightening beings, to the abodes of all spiritual benefactors, to all monuments of buddhas, to all statues of buddhas, to the abodes of all enlightening beings and buddhas, to the locations of all treasures of true teaching, to the presence of all monuments to saints and individual illuminates, to the vicinities of all groups of sages, worthies, and parents: he continuously projected himself into the presence of all beings, by entering into the totality of the body of knowledge, extending everywhere, by focusing attention through knowledge of control of formation of mental images.

khang pa brtsegs pa chen po rnam par snang mdzad kyi rgyan gyis brgyan pa'i snying po'i sgo nas ji lta ba de bzhin du gong du brjod pa'i dmigs pa thams cad la yang chos kyi dbyings thams cad rgyas par 'gengs pas 'dud cing phyag bya bar byin gyis brlab so/ /

Just as there were those perceptions at the door of the great Vairocanavyūhālaṃkāragarbha kūṭāgāra, which have just been described, he was empowered in the same way to bow down and pay homage throughout the entire realm of phenomena.

And just as he prostrated himself before the great tower of the chamber of the adornments of Vairocana, in the same way he prostrated himself before all the aforementioned beings and objects throughout the cosmos.

de bzhin du phyi ma'i mtha'i mur thug par rgyun 'chad pa med par byin gyis brlabs te/ nam mkha'i dbyings tshad med pa dang mnyam pa nyid dang / chos kyi dbyings sgrib pa med pa dang mnyam pa nyid dang / yang dag pa'i mtha' thams cad kyi rjes su song ba dang mnyam pa nyid dang / de bzhin nyid rnam par mi rtog pa dang mnyam pa nyid dang / grib ma lta bu'i ye shes dang 'du shes kyis rgyas par dgang ba mnyam pa nyid dang / rmi lam lta bu'i rnam par dpyod pa dang mnyam pa nyid dang / gzugs brnyan lta bur 'jig rten dang 'gro ba thams cad rnam par dmigs pa'i mnyam pa nyid dang / rgyu dang rkyen las byung bas sgra brnyan lta bu'i mnyam pa nyid dang / 'byung ba dang 'jig pa mi skye ba dang mnyam pa'i mnyam pa nyid dang / rkyen dang rten pa'i rgyud dngos pa med pa'i rang bzhin dang mnyam pa'i mnyam pa nyid kyis las ji lta ba bzhin du yongs su byung ba'i rnam par smin pa la ni/ mos par byed/

He was thus empowered continuously, throughout the future, by sameness with the extent of the measureless realm of space, by sameness with the realm of phenomena without obscuration, by sameness with reaching the limits of existences, by sameness with the nonconceptual true nature,[1982] by sameness with the pervasion of shadow-like knowledge and perceptions, by sameness with dream-like analysis, by sameness with reflection-like perception of all worlds and beings, by sameness with echo-like origination from causes and conditions, by sameness with birthlessness, by sameness with origination and destruction,[1983] and by sameness with causes and conditions that have the same nature as nonexistence, so that he was aspiring to ripening that occurs in accordance with karma;

“In this way, continuously mystically manifesting the eons of the endless future, by equanimity like the infinity of space, equanimity like the nonobstruction of the reality realm, equanimity toward the omnipresent ultimate limit of reality, the equanimity of absence of false notions in those who realize Thusness, the pervasiveness of perceptions of reflectional knowledge, equanimity toward thoughts as being like dreams, equanimity toward the representations of all worlds as being like reflections, equanimity toward conditional origins being like echoes, equanimity toward nonorigination, equanimity toward formation and disintegration, and equanimity toward the evolution of causal conditions as being equal to nonexistence, believing that development takes place according to actions,

rgyu ji lta ba bzhin du yongs su byung ba'i 'bras bu la ni/ mos par byed/ bsags pa ji lta ba bzhin du yongs su byung ba'i bya ba thams cad la ni/ mos par byed/ dad pa las yongs su byung ba'i de bzhin gshegs pa 'byung ba thams cad la ni/ mos par byed/ mos pa ji lta ba bzhin du yongs su byung ba'i sangs rgyas mchod pa'i sprul pa thams cad la ni/ mos par byed/

believing that results come about according to causes, believing that all Three Vehicles come to be according to accumulation of spiritual practices, believing that the appearance of all buddhas comes from faith, believing that all creations of offerings to buddhas come from devotion,

rim gro las byung ba'i de bzhin gshegs pa'i sprul pa thams cad la ni/ mos par byed/ dge ba'i rtsa ba'i tshogs las yongs su 'byung ba'i sangs rgyas thams cad kyi chos nyid la ni/ mos par byed/ shes rab dang thabs las yongs su byung ba'i rgyan yid kyi rang bzhin du sgrub pa thams cad la ni/ mos par byed/ smon lam las yongs su byung ba'i sangs rgyas kyi chos thams cad la ni/ mos par byed/

believing that all projections of buddhas derive from respect, believing that the nature of all buddhas derives from the accumulation of virtues, believing that all arrays of mental adornments derive from wisdom and technique, believing that all buddha-teachings derive from vows,

bsngo ba las yongs su byung ba'i byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa thams cad dang / chos kyi dbyings thams cad mkhyen pa'i yul du gyur pa rnam par sgrub pas rgyas par dgang pa'i rgyan la ni/ mos par byed cing /

aspiring to all bodhisattva conduct and its all-pervasive display of the accomplishment of the entire realm of phenomena as the field of perception of omniscience, which occur according to prayers of dedication,[1984]
believing all the arrays of adornments spreading throughout the realm of realities, the sphere of omniscience, by the practices of all enlightening beings, derive from dedication;

yongs su bsngo ba'i ye shes tshad med pa'i 'du shes dang bral ba dang / skye ba med pa'i ye shes rtog pa'i 'du shes med pa dang / yang dag pa'i spyod pa la 'jug cing / rgyu nye bar gsog pa'i ye shes rgyu dang bya ba'i lta ba med pa dang /

and with the wisdom of prayers of dedication, which is free from the conception of nothingness;[1985] with the wisdom of birthlessness, which is free from the conception of eternality;[1986] with the wisdom of entry into correct conduct and the accumulation of causes, which is free from false views concerning causes and actions;[1987]

and by elimination of nihilism by knowledge of dedication, by elimination of the notion of permanence by knowledge of nonorigination, by elimination of erroneous views of causality by knowledge of causality,
phyin ci log med pa'i ye shes phyin ci log gi lta ba dang bral ba dang /
with the nonerroneous[1988] wisdom that is free from erroneous views;

gzhan gyi dring mi 'jog pa'i ye shes dbang phyug tu lta ba med pa dang / rten pa la 'jug pa'i ye shes bdag dang phyi rol gyi 'du shes kyi lta ba dang bral ba dang / chos kyi dbyings mtha' dang dbus med pa la 'jug pa'i ye shes mthar 'dzin pa'i lta ba dang bral ba dang / gzugs brnyan lta bur mngon par grub pa'i ye shes 'pho ba'i lta ba med pa dang /

by elimination of false views by independent knowledge, by elimination of notions of self and others by knowledge of interdependence, by elimination of views attached to extremes by knowledge of the reality realm without extremes or mean, by elimination of the notion of transmigration by knowledge of the equal extinction of all abodes,

mi skye mi 'gag pa'i ye shes skye ba dang 'jig pa'i lta ba dang bral ba dang / stong pa nyid kyis mi skye ba'i ye shes lta ba'i rnam pa thams cad dang bral ba dang / smon lam mngon par sgrub pa'i ye shes kyi stobs dbang phyug med pa'i chos nyid rab tu rtogs pa dang / mtshan ma med pa'i mtha'i sgo dang ldan pa'i ye shes mtshan ma thams cad dang bral bas

by elimination of notions of becoming and decay by knowledge of nonorigination and nonextinction, by elimination of all views by knowledge of the nonorigination of emptiness, by dealing with the nonindependent nature of things with the power of knowledge of how to accomplish vows, by detachment from all notions of appearances by knowledge of the signless ultimate,

sa bon las myu gu chud mi za ba'i chos nyid dang / rgya las rgya'i gzugs brnyan 'byung ba'i chos nyid dang / gzugs las gzugs brnyan 'byung ba'i chos nyid dang / sgra brnyan dang sgrar mnyam pa rnam par dmigs pa'i chos nyid dang /

due to the nature of things being unperishing like seeds producing sprouts, due to the nature of things being like the impression of a stamp, due to the nature of things being like seeing reflected images, due to the nature of things as being represented by sounds that are like echoes,
rnam par dpyod pa dang rmi lam du mnyam par rnam par dmigs pa'i chos nyid dang /
through the nature of phenomena that analysis is perceived to be the same as a dream;[1993]
through the nature of phenomena that the production of actions is the same as conjured illusions;
due to the nature of things as arising from acts that are like illusions,

sems gzugs med pas 'jig rten yongs su bskyed pa'i chos nyid dang / rkyen dang rgyu ji ltar bsags pa bzhin du 'bras bu 'byung ba'i chos nyid dang / las ji ltar bsags pa dang mnyam par rnam par sbyin pa 'byung ba'i chos nyid dang /

due to the nature of things as rousing the formless world of mind, due to the nature of things as results conforming to the accumulation of causes and conditions, due to the nature of things as like developments according to accumulation of acts,

thabs mkhas pas rnam par bsgrubs pa'i chos nyid dang / chos dang chos ma yin pa mnyam pa nyid kyis mngon par brlan pa'i chos nyid dang / ye shes kyi rjes su 'jug pa de lta bus mngon par bsgrubs pa'i 'du shes dang yid la bya bas/

due to the nature of things as outgrowths of skill in means, due to the nature of things as flowing into the transcendent equality of reality and unreality—with conscious thought accomplishing entry into knowledge thus,
tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis khang pa brtsegs pa rnam par snang mdzad kyi rgyan gyis brgyan pa'i snying po'i sgo nas rnam pa de lta bur btud de phyag 'tshal nas
Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, bowed down and paid homage at the door of the great Vairocanavyūhālaṃkāragarbha kūṭāgāra.
Sudhana prostrated himself before the great tower, the chamber of adornments of Vairocana.

yun ring mo zhig lon pa dang / dge ba'i rtsa ba'i shugs bsam gyis mi khyab pas mngon par brlan pa'i sems dang ldan pa/ lus dang sems shin tu sim par gyur pa de khang pa brtsegs pa'i gnas nas langs te yud tsam zhig tu khang pa brtsegs pa chen po rnam par snang mdzad kyi rgyan gyis brgyan pa'i snying po de la mig mi 'gengs pas bltas nas thal mo sbyar te lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas

Then, for a long time, with his mind saturated by the inconceivable force of his roots of merit, with well-being of body and mind, he stood at the gateway of the kūṭāgāra and for a little while gazed unblinking at the Vairocanavyūhālaṃkāragarbha kūṭāgāra. Then with palms together in homage, he circumambulated it many hundreds of thousands of times.

After a long while, his being flooded by the energy of inconceivable roots of goodness, his body and mind refreshed, he rose from the doorstep of the tower, gazed with unblinking eyes at the great tower containing the adornments of Vairocana, circled it respectfully hundreds of thousands of times,

de lta bu'i 'du shes dang yid la bya bas bskul ba'i sems dang ldan pas tshig tu brjod pa/ 'di ni/ stong pa nyid dang / mtshan ma med pa dang / smon pa med pa'i gnas la rnam par spyod pa rnams kyi gnas so/ /

Then, with his mind inspired by that kind of perception and mentation, he said these words: “This is the dwelling of those who are present within the dwelling of emptiness, the absence of characteristics, and the absence of aspiration;
and voiced these thoughts: “This is abode of those who dwell in the state of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness;
'di ni/ chos thams cad la rnam par mi rtog pa'i gnas la rnam par spyod pa rnams kyi gnas so/ /
this is the abode of those who dwell in the state of nonconceptualization of all things,

chos kyi dbyings tha mi dad pa'i gnas la rnam par spyod pa/ sems can gyi khams mi dmigs pa'i gnas la rnam par spyod pa/ chos thams cad gnas med pa'i gnas la rnam par spyod pa/ 'jig rten thams cad gnas med pa'i gnas la rnam par spyod pa/

of those who are present within the dwelling of the indivisibility of the realm of the Dharma; of those who are present within the dwelling of the imperceptibility of the realm of beings; of those who are present within the dwelling of the birthlessness of all phenomena; of those who are present within the dwelling of the locationlessness of all worlds;

those who dwell in the state of the unity of the cosmos, those who dwell in the state of ungraspability of the realm of beings, those who dwell in the state of the nonorigination of all things, those who dwell in the state of nonattachment to all worlds,
'gro ba thams cad kyi gnas gnas med pa'i gnas la rnam par spyod pa/
of those who are present within the dwelling of the baselessness of all beings;
those who dwell in the state of nonreliance on what all worldlings rely on,

gnas thams cad rnam par bsgoms pa'i gnas la rnam par spyod pa/ brten pa thams cad la mi rten pa'i gnas la rnam par spyod pa/ lus thams cad la mi rten pa'i gnas la rnam par spyod pa/ 'du shes kyi rnam pa thams cad bsal ba'i gnas la rnam par spyod pa rnams kyi gnas so/ /

of those who are present within the dwelling of meditation on all locations; of those who are present within the dwelling of nondependence on any source of dependence; of those who are present within the dwelling of nonreliance on any body; of those who are present within the dwelling of the elimination of all conceptions;[1994]

those who dwell in the state of having shed everything those who dwell in the state of independence from all supports, those who dwell in the state of independence of all bodily existence, those who dwell in the state of annihilation of all afflictive notions, those who dwell in the state of the essence of all things,
'di ni/ chos thams cad rang bzhin med pa'i gnas la rnam par spyod pa rnams kyi gnas so/ /
of those who are present within the dwelling of the absence in all phenomena of a nature of their own;
those who dwell in the state of freedom from false imaginings,
rtog pa dang / rnam par rtog pa dang / yongs su rtog pa thams cad du rnam par mi rtog pa'i gnas la rnam par spyod pa;
of those who are present within the dwelling of not conceiving any illusory thoughts, ideas, or concepts;
those who dwell in the state of detachment from all thought,
'du shes dang / sems dang / yid thams cad kyis rnam par dben pa'i gnas la spyod pa/
of those who are present within the dwelling of the absence of conception, mind, and mentation;
lam thams cad blang ba med pa dang / dor ba med pa'i gnas la rnam par spyod pa;
of those who are present within the dwelling of neither adopting nor rejecting any path;
those who dwell in the state of neither entering nor leaving all perceptions,

shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa zab mo la 'jug pa'i gnas la rnam par spyod pa/ sgo kun nas chos kyi dbyings rgyas par 'gengs pa'i thabs kyi gnas la rnam par spyod pa/ nyon mongs pa thams cad zhi zhing nye bar zhi ba'i gnas la rnam par spyod pa/ lta ba dang / sred pa dang / nga rgyal thams cad spangs pa'i shes rab shas che ba'i gnas la rnam par spyod pa/

those who dwell in the state of entry into profound transcendent wisdom, those who dwell in the state of capacity to penetrate the realm of reality in all its aspects, those who dwell in the state of ability to extinguish all afflictions, those who dwell in the higher state of wisdom free from all views, cravings, and conceits,

bsam gtan dang / rnam par thar pa dang / ting nge 'dzin dang / snyoms par 'jug pa dang / mngon par shes pa dang / rigs pa skyed pa thams cad la rnam par rol pa'i gnas la rnam par spyod pa/ byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi ting nge 'dzin gyi spyod yul sgom pa'i gnas la rnam par spyod pa rnams kyi gnas so/ /

and of those who are present within the dwelling of delighting in the arising of all dhyānas, liberations, samādhis, samāpattis, higher cognitions, and knowledges; and this is the dwelling of those who are present within the dwelling of meditation on the field of activity of the samādhis of all bodhisattvas.

those who dwell in the state of freedom arising from higher knowledge of all meditations, liberations, concentrations and spiritual attainments, those who dwell in the state of development of all spheres of concentration of enlightening beings,
'di ni/ sangs rgyas thams cad kyi zhabs kyi drung na nye bar gnas pa'i gnas la rnam par spyod pa rnams kyi gnas so/ /
“This is the dwelling of those who are present in the location of being present at the feet of all the buddhas.
those who dwell in the state of presence with all buddhas.
'di ni/ gang de dag bskal pa gcig la bskal pa thams cad dang / bskal pa thams cad la bskal pa gcig tu 'jug pa'i gnas la rnam par spyod pa/
“This is the dwelling of those who are present in the location of entering all kalpas within one kalpa and one kalpa within all kalpas;
This is the abode of those who dwell in the state where one eon enters all eons and all eons enter one eon;
gang de dag zhing gcig dang zhing thams cad du zhing thams cad dang zhing gcig tu tha mi dad pa'i gnas la rnam par spyod pa/
of those who are present in the location where there is no difference between all realms and one realm or between one realm and all realms;
those who dwell in the state of the totality of one land and all lands as one land;
gang de dag chos gcig dang chos thams cad du chos thams cad dang chos gcig tu mi 'gal ba'i gnas la rnam par spyod pa/
of those who are present in the location of compliance with all Dharmas in one Dharma and with one Dharma in all Dharmas;
those who dwell in the state where one thing and all things, all things and one thing, harmonize without conflict;
gang de dag sems can gcig dang sems can thams cad du sems can thams cad dang sems can gcig tu tha mi dad pa'i gnas la rnam par spyod pa/
of those who are present in the location where there is no difference between all beings and one being or between one being and all beings;
those who dwell in the state of the unity of one being and all beings as one being;
gang de dag sangs rgyas gcig dang sangs rgyas thams cad du sangs rgyas thams cad dang sangs rgyas gcig tu mi gnas la rnam par spyod pa/
of those who are present in the location where there is no duality between all buddhas and one buddha, or between one buddha and all buddhas;
those who dwell in the state of nonduality of one buddha and all buddhas, all buddhas and one buddha;
gang de dag dus thams cad la skad cig gcig gis 'jug pa'i gnas la rnam par spyod pa/
of those who are present in the location where they enter all times in one instant;
those who dwell in the state of instantaneous penetration of all meanings;
gang de dag sems bskyed pa gcig gis zhing thams cad du 'gro ba'i gnas la rnam par spyod pa/
of those who are present in the location where with a single motivation they go to all realms;
those who dwell in the state of going to all lands in a single mental pulse;
gang de dag sems can thams cad kyi gnas su gzugs brnyan snang ba'i gnas la rnam par spyod pa/
of those who are present in the location where their images appear in the locations of all beings;
those who dwell in the state of appearance in the abodes of all beings;
gang de dag 'jig rten thams cad la phan pa dang bde ba'i sems kyi gnas la rnam par spyod pa/
of those who are present in the location where there is the motivation to bring benefit and happiness to all worlds;
those who dwell in the state of willing welfare and happiness for all beings;
gang de dag thob par bya ba thams cad rang la rag las pa'i gnas la rnam par spyod pa de dag gi gnas so/ /
of those who are present in the location where all attainments are dependent on oneself;
those who dwell in the state of attainment of complete independence.
'di ni/ gang de dag 'jig rten gyi gnas thams cad las gyen du 'phags kyang sems can thams cad yongs su smin par bya ba'i phyir 'gro ba thams cad kyi gnas na snang ba dang /
of those who, though they have transcended all worldly locations, appear in the locations of all beings in order to ripen all beings;
“This is the abode of those who have dropped all attachments to the world yet appear in the abodes of all beings in order to develop them to maturity;
gang de dag zhing thams cad la mi gnas kyang de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad la mchod pa bya ba'i phyir zhing thams cad du rjes su spyod pa dang /
of those who, though they do not dwell in any realm, are present in all realms in order to make offerings to all the tathāgatas;
those who are not attached to any land but travel in all lands in the service of buddhas,
gang de dag sangs rgyas kyi zhing thams cad kyi rgyan yongs su gzung ba'i phyir zhing thams cad du rjes su spyod kyang gnas nas g.yo ba med pa dang /
of those are present in all buddha realms in order to perceive the displays of all buddha realms without moving from their locations;
those who travel in all lands to encompass the arrangement of all buddha-lands, without leaving where they are;
gang de dag de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi zhabs kyi drung na 'dug kyang sangs rgyas kyi 'du shes su mngon par zhen pa dang bral ba dang /
of those who though they are present at the feet of all tathāgatas are free from attachment to the concept of buddhas;
those who are in the presence of all buddhas while free from attachment to the conception of Buddha;
gang de dag dge ba'i bshes gnyen thams cad la brten pa'i gnas la rnam par spyod kyang 'gro ba thams cad na de'i ye shes la mnyam zhing 'dra ba med pa dang /
of those who are present in all the locations where there is reliance on all kalyāṇamitras but there is no wisdom among beings that is equal or similar to theirs;
those who continue to associate with spiritual friends, even though they have no peer in any world in terms of knowledge;
gang de dag bdud kyi gnas thams cad na spyod kyang 'dod pa'i yon tan gyi dga' ba dang bral ba dang /
of those who, though they are present in the dwellings of māras, are free of delighting in sensory pleasures;
those who dwell in the abodes of all demons while yet being detached from passion;
gang de dag 'du shes kyi rnam pa'i gnas thams cad la rnam par spyod kyang 'du shes kyi rnam pa thams cad rnam par bsal ba'i yid dang ldan pa dang /
of those who, though they are present in the locations of entry into all conceptual identifications, have minds that have dispelled all conceptual identifications;
those who dwell in the state of comprehension of all ideas while their minds are clear of all ideas;
gang de dag 'gro ba thams cad du khyab pa'i lus dang ldan yang bdag dang sems can du gnyis su bya bar mi spyod pa dang /
of those who, though they possess bodies that spread throughout all beings, do not roam with the duality of self and beings;
those who adapt to all beings without duality between self and other;
gang de dag 'jig rten gyi khams thams cad kyi khong du chud pa'i lus dang ldan yang chos kyi dbyings tha dad du bya ba'i gnas la rnam par mi spyod pa dang /
of those who, though they possess bodies that enter all world realms, do not roam through the realm of phenomena as differentiated locations;
those who are physically present in all worldly realms without being cut off from the realm of reality;
gang de dag ma 'ongs pa'i bskal pa thams cad du gnas par bya ba'i smon lam dang ldan yang bskal pa ring pa dang thung ba'i 'du shes kyi rnam pas rnam par mi spyod pa dang /
of those who, though they pray to be present in all future kalpas, do not dwell in the conceptions of long or short kalpas;
those who vow to remain in the world for all time without dwelling on the idea of long or short periods;
gang de dag skra'i rtse mo gcig nas mi g.yo yang 'jig rten gyi khams thams cad du snang ba
and of those who, without deviating from the tip of a single hair, appear in all world realms.
those who appear in all worlds without moving from one spot.
de lta bur sgrub dka' ba'i chos kyi phyogs la 'jug par rnam par spyod pa de dag gi gnas so/ /
“This is the dwelling of those who dwell in the location of entering such a difficult direction of the Dharma.
“This is the abode of those who abide in the state of entering everywhere into the recondite realms of truth;
those who dwell in the state hard to know;
'di ni/ zab mo'i gnas la rnam par spyod pa/
“This is the dwelling of those who dwell in profound locations,
those who dwell in the profound state;
mi gnyis pa'i gnas la rnam par spyod pa/
who dwell in nondual locations,
those who dwell in the nondual state;
mtshan nyid med pa'i gnas la rnam par spyod pa/
who dwell in locations without characteristics,
those who dwell in the signless state;
gnyen po med pa'i gnas la rnam par spyod pa/
who dwell in locations without negations,
those who dwell in the unopposed state;
mi dmigs pa'i gnas la rnam par spyod pa/
who dwell in locations without objects of perception,
those who dwell in the ungraspable state;
spros pa med pa'i gnas la rnam par spyod pa/
who dwell in locations without conceptual elaborations,
those who dwell in the nonconceptual state;
byams pa chen po dang snying rje chen po'i gnas la rnam par spyod pa/
who dwell in locations of great love and great compassion,
nyan thos dang rang sangs rgyas thams cad kyis chud par dka' ba'i gnas la rnam par spyod pa/
who dwell in locations that śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas are unable to enter,
those who dwell in the state inconceivable to all individual illuminates;
bdud kyi yul thams cad las yang dag par 'das pa'i gnas la rnam par spyod pa/
who dwell in locations that transcend the scope of all māras,
those who dwell in the state that is beyond the sphere of all demons;
'jig rten gyi yul thams cad kyis ma gos pa'i gnas la rnam par spyod pa/
who dwell in locations that are unstained by the scope of all worlds,
those who dwell in the state that is undefiled by any worldly objects;
byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi gnas kyi pha rol tu phyin pa'i gnas la rnam par spyod pa/
who dwell in the locations of the perfections of the bodhisattvas,
those who dwell in the state of the transcendent ways of enlightening beings;
sangs rgyas thams cad kyi gnas dang mthun pa'i gnas la rnam par spyod pa rnams kyi gnas so/ /
and who dwell in the locations that correspond to the locations of all the buddhas.
those who dwell in the state of conformity to the state of all buddhas.
gang de mtshan ma thams cad dang bral ba'i gnas la rnam par spyod kyang nyan thos kyi skyon med par mi 'jug pa dang /
“They who dwell in the location free of all characteristics do not enter the faultlessness of the śrāvakas.
“This is the abode of those who dwell in the state that is void of signs yet do not enter the unchangeability of individual illuminates;
gang de dag chos thams cad skye ba med pa'i gnas la rnam par spyod kyang mi skye ba'i chos nyid du mi ltung ba dang /
They who dwell in the location of the birthlessness of all phenomena do not fall into the nature of birthlessness.
those who dwell in the abode of nonorigination of all things and yet do not fall into the condition of nonorigination;
gang de dag mi sdug pa'i gnas la rnam par spyod kyang 'dod chags dang bral ba'i chos nyid mngon du mi byed do/ 'dod chags kyi chos dang yang lhan cig mi gnas pa dang /
They who dwell in the location of unattractiveness do not manifest the nature of freedom from desire, nor do they dwell together with the qualities of desire.
those who dwell in contemplation of impurity yet do not make the condition of dispassion their final realization, nor do they live with elements of passion;
gang de dag byams pa'i gnas la rnam par spyod kyang zhe sdang gi dri ma'i rjes su stong ba'i sems med pa dang /
They who dwell in the location of love do not have minds that follow the stains of anger.
those who dwell in the state of love, their minds not stained by hatred;
gang de dag rten cing 'brel pa'i gnas la rnam par spyod kyang chos thams cad la shin tu rmongs pa med pa dang /
They who dwell in the location of dependent origination have no ignorance in relation to all phenomena.
those who dwell on interdependent origination, ultimately free from delusion in regard to all things;
gang de dag bsam gtan bzhi'i gnas la rnam par spyod kyang bsam gtan gyi dbang gis mi skye ba dang /
They who dwell in the location of the four dhyānas do not arise through the power of dhyāna.
those who dwell in the four meditation states, yet do not come under the sway of meditation;
gang de dag tshad med pa bzhi'i gnas la rnam par spyod kyang sems can yongs su smin par bya ba'i don du gzugs kyi khams kyi lam gyi rgyud du mi 'dong ba dang /
They who dwell in the location of the four immeasurables do not proceed upon the path of the realm of form, so that they may ripen all beings.
those who dwell on the four immeasurables, yet do not go to the world of pure form, so that they may develop all sentient beings;
gang de dag gzugs med pa'i snyoms par 'jug pa bzhi'i gnas la rnam par spyod kyang snying rje chen pos yongs su zin pas gzugs med pa'i khams kyi lam gyi rgyud du mi 'dong ba dang /
They who dwell in the location of the four formless samāpattis do not proceed upon the path of the formless realm, because of their possession of great compassion.
those who dwell in the states of the four formless attainments, yet do not go to the formless world, because of universal compassion;
gang de dag zhi gnas dang lhag mthong gi gnas la rnam par spyod kyang sems can yongs su smin par bya ba'i phyir bdag gis rig pa'i rnam par grol ba mngon du mi byed pa dang /
They who dwell in the location of śamatha and vipaśyanā do not manifest the liberation of their own wisdom, so as to ripen all beings.
those who dwell in the state of tranquillity and insight, yet do not realize knowledge and liberation for themselves alone, so that they may develop all sentient beings;
gang de dag btang snyoms chen po'i gnas la rnam par spyod kyang sems can gyi khams yongs su mi gtong ba dang /
They who dwell in the location of great equanimity do not abandon the realm of beings.
those who dwell in the state of universal equanimity, yet do not abandon the realm of sentient beings;
gang de dag stong pa nyid kyi gnas la rnam par spyod kyang lta ba'i rnam pa la mi gnas pa dang /
They who dwell in the location of emptiness do not depend on views.
those who dwell in the state of emptiness yet do not stick to it as a view;
gang de dag mtshan ma med pa'i spyod yul dang ldan yang mtshan ma la spyod pa'i sems can rnam par gdul ba la brtson pa dang /
They who dwell in the location of characteristiclessness are nevertheless dedicated to guiding beings whose conduct has characteristics.
those whose sphere is not in appearances yet who confront the guidance of beings who act on appearances;
gang de dag smon lam thams cad dang bral ba yin yang byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa'i smon lam gyi rgyun mi 'chad pa dang /
They who are free of all aspirations nevertheless have the continuous aspiration of bodhisattva conduct.
those who have no wishes at all, yet do not give up the vows of enlightening beings;
gang de dag las dang nyon mongs pa thams cad la dbang bsgyur yang sems can yongs su smin par bya ba'i don du las dang nyon mongs pa'i rjes su 'brang bar snang ba dang /
They who have power over all karma and kleśas nevertheless, in order to ripen beings, appear to follow karma and kleśas.
those who can control all active afflictions, yet for the sake of developing sentient beings appear to act under the influence of afflictions;
gang de dag shi 'pho dang skye ba yongs su shes kyang tshe'i shi 'pho dang skye ba yongs su ston pa dang /
They who know death, transference, and rebirth nevertheless manifest the death, transference, and rebirth of lives.
those who have ended death and birth by perfect knowledge, yet appear to be born and die;
gang de dag 'gro ba thams cad las rnam par log kyang sems can gdul ba'i dbang gis 'gro ba thams cad du 'dong ba dang /
They who have turned away from the existences of beings nevertheless, in order to guide beings, proceed throughout all the existences of beings.
those who are detached from all conditions of existence, yet go into all conditions of existence by the power to guide all beings;
gang de dag byams pa la rnam par spyod kyang gang la yang chags par rnam par spyod pa med pa dang /
They who dwell in love nevertheless do not dwell in attachment toward anything.
those who dwell in love but have no emotional attachment;
gang de dag snying rje la rnam par spyod kyang gang la yang chags par lta bas rnam par spyod pa ma yin pa dang /
They who dwell in compassion nevertheless do not dwell in the view of attachment to anything.
those who dwell in compassion but show no hesitation;
gang de dag dga' ba la rnam par spyod kyang sems can sdug bsngal ba la rnam par lta bas rtag tu mi dga' ba dang /
They who dwell in rejoicing nevertheless are always unhappy to view the suffering of beings.
those who dwell in joy but are always grieving because they watch all who are suffering;
gang de dag btang snyoms la rnam par spyod kyang gzhan gyi don la rtag tu 'bad pa dang /
They who dwell in equanimity nevertheless always strive for the benefit of others.
those who dwell in equanimity while working for others;
gang de dag mthar gyis gnas pa'i snyoms par 'jug pa dgu la rnam par spyod kyang 'dod pa'i khams su skye ba la mi smod pa dang /
They who dwell in the nine successive states of samāpatti nevertheless do not denigrate birth in the desire realm.
those who dwell in the attainments of the nine successive stages of meditation, yet do not disdain the realm of desire;
gang de dag skye ba thams cad la mi gnas par rnam par spyod kyang yang dag pa'i mtha' mngon du bya ba la rnam par mi spyod pa dang /
They who dwell in nondependence on all births nevertheless do not dwell in the manifestation of the final conclusion of existence.
those who are independent of all becoming yet do not dwell in the experience of the absolute;
gang de dag rnam par thar pa gsum la rnam par spyod kyang nyan thos kyi rnam par thar pa thob par bya ba la rnam par mi spyod pa dang /
They who dwell in the three doors to liberation nevertheless do not dwell in the attainment of the śrāvaka liberation.
those who dwell in the three liberations but do not dwell in the feeling of liberation of individual saints;
gang de dag 'phags pa'i bden pa bzhi rnam par blta ba la rnam par spyod kyang 'bras bu mngon du bya ba'i phyir rnam par mi spyod pa dang /
They who dwell in the view of the four truths of the āryas nevertheless do not dwell in the manifestation of their result.
those who observe the four holy truths but do not dwell in the experience of the result;
gang de dag rten cing 'brel bar 'byung ba zab mo brtag pa la rnam par spyod kyang shin tu 'gog par ltung ba la rnam par mi spyod pa dang /
They who dwell in the analysis of profound dependent origination nevertheless do not dwell in the fall into cessation.
those who dwell in profound contemplation of interdependent origination but do not dwell in attachment to the ultimate;
gang de dag 'phags pa'i lam gyi yan lag brgyad sgom pa la rnam par spyod kyang shin tu 'byung ba la rnam par mi spyod pa dang /
They who dwell in meditation on the eightfold path nevertheless do not dwell in the ultimate departure.
those who practice the eightfold holy path but do not dwell in ultimate emancipation;
gang de dag so so'i skye bo'i sa las shin tu 'das par rnam par spyod kyang nyan thos dang / rang sangs rgyas kyi sar ltung ba la rnam par mi spyod pa dang /
They who dwell in transcendence from ordinary beings nevertheless do not dwell in the fall to the levels of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.
those who transcend the states of sentient beings but do not dwell in attachment to individual liberation;
gang de dag nye bar len pa'i phung po lnga yongs su shes pa la rnam par spyod kyang phung po shin tu 'gog par ltung ba la rnam par mi spyod pa dang /
