“Just as a fisher with knowledge of sea monsters is free from fear of any creatures of the sea and is safe from harm even in the mouth of a whale, in the same way the enlightening being with the knowledge of the powerful determination of the aspiration for enlightenment is free from fear of all the actions and afflictions of the mundane whirl and cannot be annihilated even in the midst of realization of individual liberation, because of not falling into the extinction produced by witness of ultimate reality.

rigs kyi bu/ 'di lta ste/ dper na/ bdud rtsi'i chu 'thungs pa'i skyes bu ni/ gzhan gyis gnod par bya ba thams cad kyis mi 'chi'o/ / de bzhin du byang chub sems dpa' thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du sems bskyed pa'i bdud rtsi'i chu 'thungs pa yang nyan thos dang / rang sangs rgyas thams cad kyi sar mi 'chi'o/ / byang chub sems dpa'i snying rje chen po'i smon lam las kyang rgyun 'chad par mi 'gyur ro/ /

“Noble one, a person who drinks amrita will not die as the result of any harm from others. In the same way, the bodhisattva who drinks the amrita of the development of the aspiration to omniscience will not die on the level of any śrāvaka or pratyekabuddha and will not cease the continuous bodhisattva prayers of great compassion.

“Just as one who has drunk the elixir of immortality does not die from the attacks of others, in the same way the enlightening being who has drunk the immortality elixir of the aspiration for omniscience does not die in the stages of learners of individual salvation and does not cease acting on the vow of universal compassion of enlightening beings.

rigs kyi bu/ 'di lta ste/ dper na/ bsku ba grub pa'i skyes bu ni/ mi'i gnas thams cad rnam par spyod kyang mi kun gyis mi mthong ngo/ / de bzhin du byang chub sems dpa' byang chub tu sems bskyed pa'i shes rab dang / smon lam gyis nye bar brtan pa bdud kyi yul thams cad la rnam par spyod kyang bdud thams cad kyis mi mthong ngo/ /

“Noble one, a person who has the magical accomplishment of collyrium can be active within all human habitations but will be seen by no one. In the same way, the bodhisattva who relies[2112] on the wisdom and prayer of the development of the aspiration to enlightenment, although active in all the realms of the māras, will not be seen by any māra.

“Just as a man who has perfected the ointment of invisibility can wander through people’s houses unseen by anyone, the enlightening being grounded on the wisdom and commitment of the determination for enlightenment can roam in the realms of all demons without being seen by any demons.

rigs kyi bu/ 'di lta ste/ dper na rgyal po chen po la brtan pa'i skyes bu ni/ skye bo ma rabs thams cad kyis mi 'jigs so/ / de bzhin du byang chub sems dpa' thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du sems bskyed pa chos kyi rgyal po chen po la brten pa yang sgrib pa dang / bar chad dang / ngan song thams cad kyis mi 'jigs so/ /

“Noble one, a person who is supported by a great king has no fear of ordinary people. In the same way, the bodhisattva who is supported by the great king of the Dharma, which is the development of the aspiration to enlightenment, has no fear of all obscurations, obstacles, and lower realms.

“Just as a person who cleaves to a great king does not fear ordinary people, the enlightening being who cleaves to the spiritual king of the determination for omniscience does not fear any obstacles, hindrances, or states of misery.

rigs kyi bu/ 'di lta ste/ dper na/ sa phug gi khyim na gnas na/ sa'i gseb thams cad rlan gyis yangs su gang bas me'i 'jigs pa med do/ / de bzhin du byang chub sems dpa' sems kyi rgyud byang chub sems kyi dge ba'i rtsa bas mngon par brlan pa la'ang nyan thos dang / rang sangs rgyas kyi rnam par grol ba'i ye shes kyi mes 'jigs pa med do/ /

“Noble one, if something lives in a hole in the ground and that gap in the earth is saturated with water, it has no fear of fire. In the same way, the bodhisattva whose mind is saturated by the roots of merit of the aspiration to enlightenment has no fear of the fire of the wisdom of liberation of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.

“Just as someone in water is in no danger from fire, the enlightening being who is soaked in the virtue of the aspiration for enlightenment is in no danger from the fire of knowledge of individual liberation.

rigs kyi bu/ 'di lta ste/ dper na/ dpa' bo la brten pa'i mi ni/ dgra thams cad kyis mi 'jigs so/ / de bzhin du byang chub sems dpa' thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du sems bskyed pa'i dpa' bo la brtan pa yang spyod pa ngan pa'i dgra thams cad kyis mi 'jigs so/ /

“Noble one, a person who is supported by a hero has no fear of any enemy. In the same way, the bodhisattva who is supported by the hero that is the development of the aspiration to omniscience has no fear of the enemy that is bad conduct.

“Just as a person who cleaves to a heroic warrior does not fear enemies, the enlightening being who cleaves to the heroic warrior of the determination for omniscience does not fear the enemies that are evil actions.

rigs kyi bu/ 'di lta ste/ dper na/ lha'i dbang po brgya byin rdo rje'i lag cha thogs pa ni/ lha ma yin gyi tshogs thams cad rab tu 'joms so/ / de bzhin du byang chub sems dpa' thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du sems bskyed pa brtan pa'i lhag pa'i bsam pa rdo rje'i lag cha thogs pa yang bdud dang phas kyi rgol ba'i lha ma yin gyi tshogs thams cad rab tu 'joms so/ /

“Noble one, Śakra, the lord of the devas, wielding the weapon of the vajra, defeats the entire host of asuras. In the same way, the bodhisattva who wields the vajra weapon of the higher motivation that is dependent on the development of the aspiration to omniscience defeats the entire host of the asuras who are māras and adversaries.

“Just as the king of gods with the thunderbolt weapon crushes all the titans, the enlightening being with the thunderbolt of the steadfast will of the aspiration for omniscience crushes all the titans of demons and false teachers.

rigs kyi bu/ 'di lta ste/ dper na/ rtsi ro'i bcud 'thungs pa'i skyes bu ni/ tshe shin tu ring par gnas so; ; nyam chung bar mi 'gyur ro/ / rga bar mi 'gyur ro/ / de bzhin du byang chub sems dpa' thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du sems bskyed pa'i ro'i bcud kyi tshogs 'thungs pa yang bskal pa grangs med par 'khor ba na 'khor yang yongs su skyo ba med la 'khor ba'i skyon gyis mi gos so/ /

“Noble one, a person who drinks the elixir of life will have a very long life, will not become weak, and will not grow old. In the same way, the bodhisattva who drinks the accumulated life-elixir of the development of the aspiration to omniscience will continue in saṃsāra for countless kalpas without ever wearying or becoming stained by the defects of saṃsāra.

“Just as a person who takes the elixir of life lives for a long time and does not grow weak, the enlightening being who uses the elixir of the aspiration for omniscience goes around in the mundane whirl for countless eons without becoming exhausted and without being stained by the ills of the mundane whirl.

rigs kyi bu/ 'di lta ste/ dper na/ sman gyi ro sbyar ro cog thams cad du chu ni/ sngon du 'gro ba ste/ gang la yang skyon du mi 'gyur ro/ / de bzhin du byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa dang / smon lam gyi tshogs sbyar ba thams cad du thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du sems bskyed pa ni/ sngon du 'gro ba ste/ gang la yang skyon du mi 'gyur ro/ /

“Noble one, in all preparations of herbal medicines, one first needs water, and then they will not turn bad. In the same way, in practicing an accumulation of all bodhisattva conduct and prayer, one first needs to have the development of the aspiration to omniscience, and then they will not turn bad.

“Just as in all compounds of herbal extracts potable water is primary, never spoiling, in the same way in the application of preparations of all enlightening beings’ practices and vows the determination for omniscience is primary, never becoming corrupt.

rigs kyi bu/ 'di lta ste/ dper na/ mi'i don du bya ba thams cad la ni; srog gi dbang po sngon du 'gro'o/ / de bzhin du byang chub sems dpas sangs rgyas kyi chos thams cad yang dag par blang ba la'ang byang chub kyi sems sngon du 'gro'o/ /

“Noble one, in all accomplishment of human goals, there must first be the faculty of life. In the same way, the bodhisattva must first have the aspiration to enlightenment in order to acquire all the Dharmas of the buddhas.
“Just as in all of a person’s doing the faculty of life is the primary necessity, for an enlightening being to absorb the buddha-teachings the aspiration for enlightenment is the primary necessity.

rigs kyi bu/ 'di lta ste/ dper na/ skyes bu srog gi dbang po dang bral ba ni/ las thams cad la mthu med pas pha ma dang / gnyen bshes kyi tshogs kyis kyang nye bar 'tsho bar byar med do/ / de bzhin du byang chub sems dpa' thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du sems bskyed pa dang bral ba yang sangs rgyas kyi ye shes thob par bya ba la mthu med pas/ sems can thams cad kyis kyang thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi yon tan gyis nye bar 'tsho bar byar med do/ /

“Noble one, a person who is deprived of the faculty of life has no power to perform any action and cannot be brought to life even by parents and a host of relatives. In the same way, bodhisattvas who are separate from the development of the aspiration to omniscience will have no power to attain the wisdom of the buddhas, and all beings cannot bring them to life with the qualities of omniscience.

“Just as a person who has lost the faculty of life has no way to live, being unable to do anything for his people, in the same way an enlightening being without the life root of the determination for omniscience has no way to live, being unable to obtain enlightened knowledge for all beings.

rigs kyi bu/ 'di lta ste/ dper na/ rgya mtsho chen po ni/ dug thams cad kyis gdug par mi nus so/ / de bzhin du thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du sems skyed pa'i rgya mtsho chen po yang las dang / nyon mongs pa dang / nyan thos dang rang sangs rgyas su sems bskyed pa'i dug thams cad kyis gdug bar mi nus so/ /

“Noble one, the great ocean cannot be poisoned by any poisons. In the same way, the great ocean of the development of the aspiration to omniscience cannot be poisoned by any of the poisons of karma, kleśas, or the aspirations to enlightenment of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.

“Just as the ocean cannot be ruined by any poisons, the ocean of aspiration for omniscience cannot be ruined by any of the poisons of compulsive actions, afflictions, or aspirations for personal liberation alone.

rigs kyi bu/ 'di lta ste/ dper na/ nyi ma'i dkyil 'khor ni skar ma thams cad kyi 'od kyis thub par mi nus so/ / de bzhin du thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du sems bskyed pa'i nyi ma'i dkyil 'khor yang nyan thos dang / rang sangs rgyas kyi skar ma thams cad kyi yon tan zag pa med pa'i 'od kyis mi thub bo/ /

“Noble one, the light of all the stars cannot overwhelm the disk of the sun. In the same way, the sun disk of the development of aspiration to omniscience cannot be overwhelmed by the immaculate qualities of all śrāvaka and pratyekabuddha stars.
“Just as the sun is not outshone by the lights of all the stars, the sun of aspiration to omniscience is not outshone by the taintless virtues of those who are personally liberated.

rigs kyi bu/ 'di lta ste/ dper na/ rgyal po'i bu skyes nas yun ring du ma lon pa yang blon po'i mchog tu bya ba nas rgan pa thams cad rigs su rigs dang ldan par skyes pa dang / dbang gis zil gyis gnon to/ / de bzhin du byang chub sems dpa' byang chub tu sems bskyed nas ring po ma lon pa / chos kyi rgyal po de bzhin gshegs pa'i rigs su skyes pa'i las dang po pa yang yun ring po nas tshangs par spyod spyod pa'i nyan thos nas rgan pa thams cad byang chub kyi sems kyi snying rje chen po'i dbang gis zil gyis gnon to/ /

“Noble one, not long after a prince has been born, he outshines the highest ministers who are his seniors through being of noble birth and sovereignty. In the same way, not long after bodhisattvas have developed the aspiration for enlightenment, through being born in the family of the Dharma kings, the tathāgatas, even though they are beginners, through the sovereignty of the great compassion of the aspiration to enlightenment, they outshine all the śrāvakas who are their seniors in having practiced celibacy for a long time.

“Just as a newborn prince is not inferior to fully grown ministers, because of his superior birth, a beginning enlightening being, born in the family of the enlightened spiritual kings, is not inferior to Buddhist disciples with long experience in religious practice, because of the superiority of universal compassion of the aspiration for enlightenment.

rigs kyi bu/ 'di lta ste/ dper na/ blon po ji tsam du rgan pas kyang rgyal bu gzhon nu ji tsam du chung ba la'ang phyag bya dgos so/ / rgyal po'i bus kyang blon po rgan po la rim gro mi bya ba ma yin no/ / de bzhin du nyan thos dang / rang sangs rgyas ji tsam du rgan la/ ji tsam du tshangs pa'i spyod pa ring du spyod spyod pa rnams kyis kyang byang chub sems dpa' las dang po pa la 'dud bar bya'o/ / byang chub sems dpas kyang nyan thos dang / rang sangs rgyas rnams la rim gro med par bya ba ma yin no/ /

“Noble one, all ministers have to pay homage to a prince, however young he is and however senior to him they are, and yet the prince does not disrespect the senior ministers. In the same way, however senior the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas may be, however long they have been practicing celibacy, they should bow down to a beginner bodhisattva. Also, the bodhisattvas should not disrespect the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.

“Just as a minister, no matter how old, should pay respect to a prince, no matter how young, and a prince need not honor a minister, in the same way Buddhist disciples and self-illuminates, no matter how long they have performed religious practice, should pay respect to even a beginning enlightening being, and the enlightening being need not honor those who are enlightened only for themselves.

rigs kyi bu/ 'di lta ste/ dper na/ rgyal po'i bu thams cad kyis mi dgos par bya ba zhig na'ang rgyal po'i mtshan dang ldan na/ rigs kyi btsun pas rgyal po'i blon po dam par bya ba thams cad dang yang mi mnyam mo/ / de bzhin du byang chub sems dpa' las dang po las dang nyon mongs pa'i nye bar len pa thams cad kyis non pa yang thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du sems bskyed pa'i mtshan dang ldan na/ sangs rgyas kyi rigs kyi btsun zhing che bas nyan thos dang / rang sangs rgyas mchog tu phyin pa thams cad dang yang mi mnyam mo/ /

“Noble one, even though a prince is not needed by anyone,[2113] because he has the royal title and because of the nobility of his family, none of the king’s ministers is his equal. In the same way, even though beginner bodhisattvas are oppressed by result-causing karma and kleśas, they have the title of having developed the aspiration to omniscience and have the nobility and greatness of the family of the buddhas, and therefore none of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas that have reached complete attainment are their equals.

“Just as a prince, without any power yet never without the character of royalty, is not equaled even by the ministers who have gained eminence, because of his superior birth, in the same way a beginning enlightening being, no matter how much under the sway of action and affliction, is never without the character of the aspiration for omniscience, and is not equaled even by eminent Buddhist disciples and self-illuminates, because of being of the family of enlightened ones.

rigs kyi bu/ 'di lta ste/ dper na/ nor bu rin po che yongs su dag pa ni mig la rab rib kyi skyon yod na/ yongs su ma dag par snang ngo/ / de bzhin du thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du sems bskyed pa rin po che rang bzhin gyis yongs su dag pa yang sems can dang pha'i mig mi shes pa'i rab rib kyi skyon dang ldan pa rnams la yongs su ma dag par snang ngo/ /

“Noble one, a completely pure, precious jewel will appear impure to someone who has the visual defect of cataracts. In the same way, the nature of the jewel of the development of the aspiration to omniscience is pure, but it appears impure to those whose eyes of faith have the defect of the cataracts of ignorance.
“Just as a clear jewel appears impure to a clouded eye, the inherently pure jewel of the aspiration to omniscience is perceived as impure by those whose eye of unbelief is beclouded by ignorance.

rigs kyi bu/ 'di lta ste/ dper na/ rtsi'i gzungs sngags dang rtsi thams cad bsdus te byas pa ni reg gam/ mthong ngam/ 'grogs na yang sems can gyi nad rab tu zhi bar byed do/ / de bzhin du byang chub kyi sems kyi smon lam dang / ye shes kyi lus dge ba'i rtsa ba'i tshogs dang / shes rab dang / thabs kyi sngags dang / rtsi thams cad las bsgrubs pa byang chub kyi sems dang ldan pa ni/ thos sam/ mthong ngam/ 'grogs sam/ rjes su dran pa'i tshul gyis kyang sems can gyi nyon mongs pa'i nad rab tu zhi bar byed do/ /

“Noble one, when all mantras and elixirs have been gathered together and prepared, they heal the illness of beings through being touched or seen, or through being in their presence. In the same way, the body of the prayer and wisdom of the aspiration to enlightenment is created from all the mantras and elixirs of the accumulation of roots of merit and of wisdom and method. Hearing, seeing, being in the presence of, or thinking of someone who possesses that aspiration to enlightenment heals the illness of the kleśas of beings.

“Just as a body of medicine endowed with all medical knowledge and medicinal herbs curse the diseases of sentient beings by sight, contact, and association, in the same way the body of vows and knowledge of enlightening beings, sustained by the knowledge and medicine of wisdom and means assembling all roots of goodness, endowed with the will for enlightenment, cures sentient beings’ diseases of afflictions by hearing, seeing, association, recollection, and application.

rigs kyi bu/ 'di lta ste/ dper na/ gos dang ba'i mtshan nyid can ni/ 'dam gyi nyes pa thams cad kyis mi gos so/ / de bzhin du byang chub kyi sems kyi gos dang ba'i mtshan nyid can ni/ 'khor ba'i nyon mongs pa'i 'dam gyi skyon thams cad kyis kun nas nyon mongs par mi 'gyur ro/ /

“Noble one, clothing that has the characteristic of duck feathers[2114] is unstained by the defect of mud. In the same way, the aspiration to enlightenment that is the clothing that has the characteristic of duck feathers is not afflicted by the defect of the mud of the kleśas of saṃsāra.
“Just as a goose-feather robe is not stained by any dirt, the goose-feather robe of the aspiration for enlightenment is not stained by the dirt of afflictions of the mundane whirl.

rigs kyi bu/ 'di lta ste/ dper na/ shing gi gzugs mgo gzer gyis btab pa ni/ yongs su 'gyes par mi 'gyur te/ bya ba thams cad kyang byed do/ / de bzhin du thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du smon pa'i ye shes kyi lus kyi spyi bo byang chub tu sems bskyed pa'i smon lam gyi gzer gyis btab pa yang byang chub sems dpa'i bya ba thams cad la mthu yod de/ thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi smon lam gyi ye shes las lus su grub pa yin pas yongs su 'gyes par mi 'gyur ro/ /

“Noble one, a wooden figure that has its head shaft will not fall apart but be able to perform all functions. In the same way, if in the head of the body of the wisdom of the prayer[2115] for omniscience there is the shaft of the prayer for the development of the aspiration to enlightenment, it will have the power for all bodhisattva activities, and because the body is created from the wisdom of the prayer for omniscience, it will not fall apart.

“Just as a wooden figure held together by the main pin does not fall apart and can perform any kind of movement, in the same way the body of the vow and knowledge of omniscience, held together by the main pin of the vow of enlightenment, can perform the tasks of enlightening beings, and does not fall apart as the embodiment of the vow of omniscience.

rigs kyi bu/ 'di lta ste/ dper na/ gzer dang mi ldan pa'i 'khrul 'khor ni/ shing gi yan lag de nyid yin yang dgos pa bya ba'i mthu med do/ / de bzhin du byang chub sems dpa' thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du sems bskyed pa'i lhag pa'i bsam pa dang mi ldan na/ byang chub kyi yan lag gi tshogs de nyid yin yang sangs rgyas kyi chos sgrub pa la mthu med do/ /

“Noble one, a machine that does not have a shaft, even though it possesses wooden limbs, will not have the power for necessary actions. In the same way, if bodhisattvas do not possess the higher motivation of the aspiration to omniscience, even though they have the accumulation of the limbs of enlightenment, they will not have the power to accomplish the Dharma of the buddhas.

“Just as a machine without its pins cannot work, even though the parts are the same, similarly, the enlightening being without the commanding will of the aspiration to omniscience cannot attain buddhahood, even though the preparations of the parts of enlightenment be the same.

rigs kyi bu/ 'di lta ste/ dper na/ 'khor los bsgyur ba'i rgyal po la rin po che a ga ru nag po glang po'i snying po zhes bya ba yod pa des bcugs ma thag tu rgyal po 'khor los bsgyur ba'i yan lag bzhi pa'i dpung gi tshogs thams cad kyang nam mkha' la gnas par 'gyur ro/ / de bzhin du thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du sems bskyed pa a ga rus bdugs pa'i byang chub sems dpa'i dge ba'i rtsa ba thams cad kyang khams gsum pa thams cad las rnam par 'das te/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i ye shes nam mkha'i spyod yul 'dus ma byas pa thams cad kyi mthar thug par 'gyur ro/ /

“Noble one, a cakravartin has the precious black agarwood called essence of the elephant. As soon as that incense is lit, all four branches of the cakravartin’s army rise up into the sky. In the same way, all the bodhisattva’s roots of merit, which are the agarwood incense of the development of the aspiration to omniscience, rise above all the three realms and fully accomplish the noncomposite field of activity that is the sky of the wisdom of the tathāgatas.

“Just as a sovereign ruler has a precious incense by the perfume of which his four armies are levitated into the air, in the same way the roots of goodness of an enlightening being, perfumed by the incense of the determination for omniscience, leave the mundane and end up in the unconditioned realm of the sky of enlightened knowledge.

rigs kyi bu/ 'di lta ste/ dper na/ rdo rje ni/ rin po che ma rabs kyi 'byung khungs nas mi 'byung gi /rdo rje'i 'byung khungs sam/ gser gyi 'byung khungs nas 'byung ngo/ / de bzhin du thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du sems bskyed pa rdo rje lta bu'ang sems can gyi bsam pa'i dge ba'i rtsa ba ma rabs kyi rin po che'i 'byung gnas nas mi skye ste/ gzhan du na sems can yongs su skyob pa'i snying rje chen po'i rdo rje'i 'byung khungs sam/ thams cad mkhyen pa'i ye shes la lhag par dmigs pa'i gser gyi 'byung khungs chen po nas 'byung ngo/ /

“Noble one, diamonds do not come from inferior jewel mines but from diamond mines or from gold mines. In the same way, the development of the aspiration to omniscience is like a diamond. It does not arise in the jewel mines of the lesser roots of merit of the aspirations of beings, but from the diamond mines of the great compassion that protects beings or from the great gold mines of the higher focus on the omniscient wisdom.

“Just as diamond comes from nowhere else but a jewel mine, from a diamond or gold mine, in the same way the diamondlike aspiration for omniscience comes from nowhere else but the jewel mine of roots of goodness in sentient beings’ minds, from the diamond mine of universal compassion saving all beings, or from the gold mine of concentration on omniscience.

rigs kyi bu/ 'di lta ste; dper na/ shing gi rigs rtsa ba med pa zhes bya ba yod de/ de'i rtsa ba mthar thug pa mi dmigs mod kyi/ shing rnams la yal ga dang / lo ma dang / 'dab ma dang / me tog shin tu rgyas pa dra ba lta bur gyur pa snang ngo/ / de bzhin du thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du sems bskyed pa'i dge ba'i rtsa ba'i mthar thug pa'ang mi dmigs mod kyi/ 'jig rten gyi skye gnas thams cad du'ang thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi bsod nams dang / ye shes dang / mngon par shes pa'i me tog shin tu rgyas pa smon lam chen po'i dra bar gyur pa'ang yongs su snang ngo/ /

“Noble one, the class of trees called without a root ultimately has no visible roots, and yet the trees are seen to be covered like a net with branches, leaves, foliage, and flowers. In the same way, there are ultimately no visible roots of merit of the development of the aspiration to omniscience, and yet in all existences in all worlds there appear the extensive flowers of its merit, wisdom, and higher cognitions, as a net of great prayers.

“Just as there is a kind of tree called ‘rootless’ whose roots cannot be found, yet branches, leaves, and flowers appear luxuriantly on the tree, in the same way the root of the aspiration for omniscience cannot be found, yet it appears in all worlds, blooming with all virtues, knowledge, and mystic capacities, forming a web of vows.

“Noble one, if a diamond is placed in a poor container, it does not appear to be beautiful, and a vessel with cracks or holes cannot contain it, only a vessel in perfect condition. In the same way, the great diamond of the development of the aspiration to omniscience will not have beauty in the vessels of beings who have weak aspiration, are miserly, have bad conduct, are malevolent, are lazy, have disrupted mindfulness, or have wrong understanding. It cannot be contained within beings who are vessels with unstable minds and who follow erroneous higher motivations, but only in the precious vessels of a bodhisattva’s higher motivation.

“Just as a diamond does not shine beautifully in another kind of vessel, and cannot be held in an imperfect, perforated vessel, only in a perfect vessel, in the same way the diamond of the aspiration for omniscience does not shine in the vessels of people with inferior resolutions, in the envious, in the immoral, in the mentally corrupt, in the lazy, in the heedless, or in the stupid, and it cannot be held by a vessel of a wavering, inconstant mind with defective will, only in the precious vessel of the powerful will of an enlightening being.

rigs kyi bu/ 'di lta ste/ dper na/ rdo rje ni/ rin po che thams cad 'bigs so/ / de bzhin du/ thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du sems bskyed pa'i rdo rje yang sangs rgyas kyi chos rin po cha thams cad 'bigs par khong du chud par byed do/ /
“Noble one, a diamond can pierce all other jewels. In the same way, the diamond of the development of the aspiration to omniscience can pierce and comprehend all the precious Dharmas of the buddhas.
“Just as diamond pierces all jewels, the diamond of the determination for omniscience pierces the jewels of all truth.

rigs kyi bu/ 'di lta ste/ dper na/ rdo rje ni/ brag thams cad shigs par 'dzems so/ / de bzhin du thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du sems bskyed pa'i rdo rje yang lta ba'i rnam pa thams cad kyi brag shigs par 'joms so/ /
“Noble one, a diamond can cut through and overcome all stones. In the same way, the diamond of the development of the aspiration to omniscience can cut through and overcome the stone of false views.
“Just as adamant splits all mountains, the adamant of the aspiration for omniscience splits the mountains of all views.

rigs kyi bu/ 'di lta ste/ dper na/ rdo rje rin po che ni/ chag kyang thams cad las khyad par du 'phags pa'i gser gyi rgyan zil gyis gnon to/ / de bzhin du thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du sems bskyed pa'i rdo rje rin po che bsam pa log par zhugs pas chag par gyur kyang nyan thos dang / rang sangs rgyas thams cad kyi yon tan gyi gser gyi rgyan zil gyis gnon to/ /

“Noble one, even if a diamond is broken, it is superior to all other jewels and outshines ornaments of gold. In the same way, even if the diamond jewel of the development of the aspiration to omniscience becomes broken through one’s following erroneous thoughts, it still outshines the golden adornments that are the qualities of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.

“Just as even a cracked diamond is better than an ornament of gold, the finest of precious metals, in the same way the diamond of the aspiration for omniscience is better than the gold ornaments of the virtues of hearers and individual illuminates, even if the will is broken by adversity.

rigs kyi bu/ 'di lta ste/ dper na/ rdo rje rin po che ni/ chag kyang phongs pa thams cad rnam par sel to/ / de bzhin du thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du sems bskyed pa'i rdo rje rin po che nan tan med pas chag par gyur kyang 'khor ba'i phongs pa thams cad rnam par sel to/ /

“Noble one, even if a diamond is broken, it will dispel all poverty. In the same way, even if the diamond jewel of the development of the aspiration to omniscience becomes broken through not being practiced, it can still dispel the poverty that is saṃsāra.
“Just as a diamond, even if cracked, relieves poverty, in the same way the diamond of the determination for omniscience, even if split, relieves the poverty of the mundane whirl.

rigs kyi bu/ 'di lta ste/ dper na/ rdo rje'i khams ni/ ji tsam zhig tu chung yang nor bu dang rdo thams cad gcog pa'i mtshan nyid do/ / de bzhin du dmigs pa ji tsam du chung ba la zhugs kyang thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du sems bskyed pa'i rdo rje'i khams ni/ mi shes pa thams cad 'jig par byed pa'i mtshan nyid do/ /

“Noble one, however small a diamond element may be, it still has the characteristic of being able to cut all jewels and stones. In the same way, however minor the engagement in the diamond element of the development of the aspiration to omniscience, it still has the characteristic of destroying all ignorance.
“Just as a diamond, however little, breaks all gems and stones, in the same way the diamond of the aspiration for omniscience, focused on however small an object, breaks all ignorance.

rigs kyi bu/ 'di lta ste/ dper na/ rdo rje rin po che ni/ skye bo ma rabs kyi lag tu phyin par mi 'gyur ro/ / de bzhin du thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du sems bskyed pa'i rdo rje rin po che yang ma rabs kyi bsam pa dang ldan pa dge ba'i rtsa ba ngan don can gyi lha dang mi'i lag tu phyin par mi 'gyur ro; ;

“Noble one, a diamond jewel does not come into the hands of lesser people. In the same way, the diamond jewel of the development of the aspiration to omniscience does not come into the hands of devas and humans who have inferior aspiration and poor roots of merit.

“Just as a diamond does not come into the hands of an ordinary man, the diamond of the determination for omniscience does not come into the hands of those of low intentions and poor roots of goodness.

rigs kyi bu/ 'di lta ste/ dper na/ rin po che yongs su brtag pa la mi mkhas pa'i skyes bu ni/ rdo rje rin po che'i yon tan nyams su myong bar mi 'gyur ro/ / de bzhin du shes rab 'chal ba'i ngang tshul dang ldan pa'i skyes bu gang zag kyang byang chub kyi sems rdo rje rin po che chen po'i yon tan la mi mkhas pas kyang de'i yon tan gyi khyad par nyams su myong bar mi 'gyur ro/ /

“Noble one, a person who is not skilled in examining jewels will not know the qualities of a diamond jewel and therefore will not experience its qualities. In the same way, a person whose understanding is confused is not skilled in the qualities of the great diamond jewel of the development of the aspiration to omniscience and therefore will not experience its qualities.

“Just as someone who has no knowledge of gems does not recognize the qualities of diamonds or understand their excellence, in the same way a stupid person does not know the qualities of the diamond of wisdom of the aspiration for enlightenment and does not understand its excellence.
rigs kyi bu/ 'di lta ste/ dper na/ rdo rje ni/ zhu bar mi nus so/ / de bzhin du thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi rgyur gyur pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed pa'i rdo rje yang zhu bar mi nus so/ /
“Noble one, a diamond cannot be dissolved.[2116] In the same way, the diamond of the aspiration to enlightenment, which is the cause of omniscience, cannot be dissolved.
“Just as a diamond cannot be worn out, the diamond of the aspiration for enlightenment, the basis of omniscience, cannot be worn out.

rigs kyi bu/ 'di lta ste/ dper na/ rdo rje'i lag cha chen po ni/ gzhan du na mthu bo che chen po'i stobs ltar khyad par du 'phags pa'i mthu stobs kyi shugs drag po ma gtogs par stobs po che chen pos kyang gzung bar mi nus so/ / de bzhin du thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du sems bskyed pa'i rdo rje'i lag cha chen po yang gzhan du na byang chub sems dpa' chen po thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi rgyu'i stobs kyi brtan pa dge ba'i rtsa ba chad med pa'i mthu bo che chen po'i stobs ltar khyad par du 'phags pa stobs kyi shugs chen po rab tu thob pa ma gtogs par nyan thos dang / rang sangs rgyas stobs po che thams cad kyis kyang yongs su gzung bar mi nus so/ /

“Noble one, the great diamond weapon can only be held by someone who has the superior powerful strength and might of the great Nārāyaṇa, and not by another strongman. In the same way, the great diamond weapon of the development of the aspiration to omniscience can only be acquired by a great bodhisattva whose limitless roots of merit are made firm by the power of the cause of omniscience, which has superior powerful strength and might like that of the great Nārāyaṇa. Otherwise, it cannot be held by any other strongmen, who are the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.

“Just as the thunderbolt weapon cannot be held even by a strong man unless he has superhuman strength, likewise the thunderbolt of the aspiration for enlightenment cannot be held even by the mighty saints and sages, only by the great enlightening beings with great illumination, excelling in the superhuman might of infinite roots of goodness based on the power of the cause of omniscience.

rigs kyi bu; 'di lta ste/ dper na/ mtshon cha thams cad kyis mi tshugs pa gang du yang rdo rjes mi tshugs pa med de/ kha mi 'bab bo/ / de bzhin du sems can yongs su smin par bya ba dang / gdul ba'am/ dus gsum gyi bskal par spyad pa'i sdug bsngal dang 'grogs par bya ba gang du nyan thos dang / rang sangs rgyas kyi smon lam dang / ye shes kyi mtshon chas rdugs pa/ thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du sems bskyed pa'i rdo rje'i mtshon cha chen po thogs pa'i byang chub sems dpa' yongs su skyo ba'i yid med pas ni/ mi bzod pa med de/ kha mi 'bab bo/ /

“Noble one, a diamond can pierce what no other weapon can pierce, without itself being damaged. In the same way, wherever the weapons of the prayers and wisdom of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas are ineffective in ripening and guiding beings, or in associating with the suffering that is experienced during the kalpas of the three times, there the bodhisattva who wields the great diamond weapon of the development of the aspiration to omniscience is effective without weariness of mind, and without it being unendurable, and without being adversely affected by it.

“Just as a thunderbolt can prevail where all other weapons cannot, and will not be destroyed, in the same way where the weapons of vows and knowledge of all Buddhist disciples and self-enlightened ones cannot prevail, in developing and guiding people or living through the toils of practice through the ages of past, present, and future, there the enlightening being who holds the great thunderbolt weapon of the determination for omniscience, indefatigable, prevails unharmed.

rigs kyi bu/ 'di lta ste/ dper na/ rdo rje ni/ gzhan du na rdo rje nyid las gyur pa'i gzhi ma gtogs par sa'i phyogs gang gis kyang gzung bar mi nus so/ / de bzhin du byang chub sems dpa'i 'byung ba'i smon lam gyi tshogs kyi rdo rje ni/ gzhan du na lhag pa'i bsam pas byang chub tu sems bskyed pa'i rdo rje brtan pa'i sa'i gzhi ma gtogs par nyan thos dang / rang sangs rgyas thams cad kyis gzung bar mi nus so/ /

“Noble one, a diamond can only be contained in a ground made of diamond and not in any other place. In the same way, only the strong diamond ground of the development of the aspiration to omniscience can contain the diamond of the accumulations of the prayers that arise from a bodhisattva, so that śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas cannot possess it.

“Just as adamant cannot be held on any spot on the earth except on an adamantine surface, in the same way the adamant vows of emancipation of enlightening beings cannot be held by those whose goal is personal salvation only; it can only be supported by the adamantine ground of the resolute determination for universal enlightenment.

rigs kyi bu/ 'di lta ste/ dper na/ rgya mtsho chen po'i snod rdo rje'i gzhi sra zhing gseb med pas/ chu gsang du 'dzag par mi 'gyur ro/ / de bzhin du byang chub sems dpa'i dge ba'i rtsa ba byang chub kyi sems kyi rdo rje gseb med pa yongs su bsngos pa'i gzhi can la gnas pa yang srid par skyes pa thams cad kyis zad par mi 'gyur ro/ /

“Noble one, the container of the great ocean is the diamond ground that is solid and without fissures so that water cannot leak through the cracks.[2117] In the same way, the roots of merit of a bodhisattva that rest on the uncracked ground of dedication of the diamond of the development of the aspiration to enlightenment will never be exhausted throughout all existences.

“Just as the ocean does not leak any water because it is a solid container with an unyielding ground, in the same way the roots of goodness of an enlightening being, grounded on adamant, solid, unyielding dedication to enlightening, do not die out in any states of existence.

rigs kyi bu/ 'di lta ste/ dper na/ rdo rje'i gzhi la brtan pa'i sa chen po ni/ 'jig par mi 'gyur ro/ / dma' bar mi 'gyur ro/ / de bzhin du byang chub tu sems bskyed pa'i rdo rje sra ba'i gzhi la brtan pa'i byang chub sems dpa'i smon lam rnams kyang khams gsum thams cad du 'jig par mi 'gyur ro/ / dma' bar mi 'gyur ro/ /

“Noble one, the great earth that rests on a foundation of diamond will never be destroyed and will never degenerate. In the same way, the bodhisattva prayers that are based upon the solid diamond ground of the development of the aspiration to enlightenment will never be destroyed and will never degenerate.

“Just as earth set on an adamantine base does not collapse or sink, in the same way the vows of enlightening beings, grounded on the adamantine base of the determination for enlightenment, are not rent apart and do not collapse in any mundane realm.

rigs kyi bu/ 'di lta ste/ dper na/ rdo rje ni/ chus bangs pa'am rul bar mi 'gyur ro/ / de bzhin du byang chub tu sems bskyed pa'i rdo rje yang las dang / nyon mongs pa thams cad kyi chur bskal par gnas kyang rul bar ma 'gyur/ bangs par mi 'gyur ro/ /

“Noble one, a diamond will not rot if immersed in water. In the same way, the diamond of the development of the aspiration to enlightenment will not become rotten even if it remains for a kalpa in the water of all karma and kleśas.
“Just as a diamond does not rot in water, the diamond of the aspiration for enlightenment does not decompose or soften even though it remain in the water of action and affliction for all ages.

rigs kyi bu/ 'di lta ste/ dper na/ rdo rje ni/ me thams cad kyi drod kyis kyang tshig par mi 'gyur/ yongs su gdung bar yang mi 'gyur ro/ / de bzhin du thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du sems bskyed pa'i rdo rje yang 'khor ba thams cad kyi sdug bsngal gyi me'i drod thams cad kyis mi tshig go / nyon mongs pa thams cad kyi me'i gdung bas gdungs par mi 'gyur ro/ /

“Noble one, a diamond will not be burned or scorched by the heat of fire. In the same way, the diamond of the development of the aspiration to omniscience will not be burned by the heat of the fire of the sufferings of all saṃsāra and will not be scorched by the burning fire of all the kleśas.

“Just as a diamond is not burnt or heated by fire, the diamond of the determination for omniscience is not burnt by the fires of suffering of the mundane whirl and is not heated up by the fires of afflictions.

rigs kyi bu/ 'di lta ste/ dper na/ de bzhin gshegs pa dgra bcom pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas snying po byang chub la bzhugs shing bdud rgol du gzhug pa mdzad pa dang / thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du mngon par rdzogs par 'tshang rgya ba rnams kyi gdan ni/ gzhan du na stong gsum gyi stong chen po'i 'jig rten gyi khams kyi rdo rje'i lte ba'i sa'i gzhi ma gtogs par sa'i phyogs gzhan gyis gzung bar mi nus so/ / de bzhin du byang chub sems dpa' bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu smon lam 'debs pa dang / spyad pa spyod pa dang / pha rol tu phyin pa yongs su rdzogs par byed pa dang / bzod pa la 'jug pa dang / sa thob par byed pa dang / dge ba'i rtsa ba yongs su rdzogs par byed pa dang / lung bstan pa yongs su nod pa dang / byang chub sems dpa'i lam gyi tshogs thams cad nye bar ston pa dang / de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad la mchod pa byed pa dang / chos kyi sprin chen po yongs su 'dzin pa rnams kyi dge ba'i rtsa ba'i stobs dang / shugs dang / drag shul de dag kyang gzhan du na thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du sems bskyed pa smon lam thams cad kyi ye shes rdo rje sra ba'i lte ba can ma gtogs par sems gzhan gyis yongs su gzung bar mi nus so/ /

“Noble one, when a tathāgata arhat samyaksaṃbuddha sits on the bodhimaṇḍa, overcomes the māras, and attains omniscient buddhahood, no place can be its location other than the ground that is the diamond center of a world realm of a billion worlds. In the same way, all the strength, power, and might of the bodhisattvas’ roots of merit from their prayers for the attainment of the highest, complete enlightenment, their entry into patience, their attainment of the bhūmis, their completion of the roots of merit, their receiving their prophecy, their reliance[2118] on all the accumulations of the bodhisattva path, their making offerings to all the tathāgatas, and their holding all the great clouds of the Dharma can only be located on the solid diamond center of the wisdom of all the prayers for the development of the aspiration to omniscience, and other beings will not be able to possess it.

“Just as the seat of buddhas sitting on the site of enlightenment battling the devil and awakening to omniscience cannot be supported by any spot on earth except the earth surface of the adamantine center of the universe, in the same way the great force of power of the roots of goodness of enlightening beings aspiring to perfect enlightenment, carrying out the practice, fulfilling the transcendent ways, entering into tolerance, attaining spiritual station, dedicating roots of goodness, receiving assurance of buddahood, providing the necessities for the path of enlightening beings, and holding the multitudes of teachings of all buddhas, cannot be sustained by mind other than the mind set on omniscience, the adamantine core of all vows and knowledge.

rigs kyi bu/ de ltar thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du sems bskyed pa ni/ yon tan de dag dang / gzhan tshad med pa nas yon tan gyi khyad par brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa dang ldan pa ste/ sems can gang gis bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed pa de dag kyang yon tan gyi chos de lta bu dang ldan par gyur to/ / ldan par 'gyur ro/ /

“Noble one, the development of the aspiration to omniscience has those qualities and countless others; it possesses an indescribable extent of indescribable special qualities. Any being who develops the aspiration to the highest, complete enlightenment possesses the phenomena of such qualities and will possess them going forward.

“The aspiration for omniscience has these and untold other extraordinary virtues; and those who have set their minds on supreme perfect enlightenment are, have been, and will be endowed with such virtues.

de bas na/ rigs kyi bu/ de ltar khyod bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed de/ yon tan 'di dag rab tu thob par bya ba'i phyir byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa yongs su tshol ba ni/ khyod kyis thob par bya ba legs par thob bo/ /

“Therefore, noble one, you have gained an excellent attainment in developing the aspiration to the highest, complete enlightenment, and in order to attain these qualities you have sought bodhisattva conduct.
Therefore you have made a great gain in having aspired to supreme perfect enlightenment and seeking the practice of enlightening beings, because of attainment of these virtues.
rigs kyi bu/ khyod na re/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la spyad par bya/ ji ltar nan tan du bya zhes zer ba ni/
“Noble one, you asked, ‘How does one perform bodhisattva conduct? How does one practice it?’
“Also, you ask how an enlightening being is to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings.

rigs kyi bu/ khang pa brtsegs pa chen po rnam par snang mdzad kyi rgyan gyis brgyan pa'i snying po 'di nyid kyi nang du song ste ltos shig dang / der khyod kyis ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bya ba dang / bslab nas kyang yon tan ji lta bu yongs su 'grub par 'gyur ba shes par 'gyur ro/ /

“Noble one, go inside the great kūṭāgāra called Vairocanavyūhālaṃkāragarbha and look! You will then know how a bodhisattva should train in bodhisattva conduct and, having trained, what kind of qualities will be accomplished.”

Go into this great tower containing the adornments of Vairocana and look—then you will know how to learn the practice of enlightening beings, and what kind of virtues are perfected in those who learn this.”

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis byang chub sems dpa' byams pa la g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas te 'di skad ces smras so; ;'phags pa/ pho brang brtsegs pa'i chab sgo dbyer gsol nang du mchi'o/ /
Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, circumambulated the bodhisattva Maitreya, keeping him to his right, and then said, “Ārya, open the door of the kūṭāgāra. I am going to enter.”
Then Sudhana respectfully circumbulated the enlightening being Maitreya and said, “Please open the door of the tower, and I will enter.”

de nas byang chub sems dpa' byams pas khang pa brtsegs pa rnam par snang mdzad kyi rgyan gyis brgyan pa'i snying po'i sgo drung du phyin te/ lag pa g.yas pas se gol gtogs te sgra byung ba dang / de'i sgo de'ang rang bye bar gyur pa dang / des smras pa/ rigs kyi bu/ da khang pa brtsegs pa 'dir song zhig /

The bodhisattva Maitreya came in front of the door of the Vairocanavyūhālaṃkāragarbha kūṭāgāra. With his right hand he snapped his fingers, and with that sound the door opened. He said, “Noble son, enter the kūṭāgāra.”
Then Maitreya went up to the door of the tower containing the adornments of Vairocana, and with his right hand snapped his fingers; the door of the tower opened, and Maitreya bade Sudhana to enter.
de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang ngo mtshar chen po thob par gyur te/ khang pa brtsegs pa de'i nang du phyin pa dang / phyin ma thag tu sgo de yang rang chad par gyur to/ /
Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, was greatly amazed, and he entered the kūṭāgāra. The instant he entered, the door closed by itself.
Then Sudhana, in greatest wonder, went into the tower. As soon as he had entered, the door shut.

des mthong ba khang pa brtsegs pa de shin tu rgya che zhing yangs la/ rgyar dpag tshad brgya stong mang po dang ldan pa/ nam mkha'i dbyings kyi tshad kyis gzhal ba/ 'khor thams cad du nam mkha'i dbyings ltar yangs pa/
He saw the tower immensely vast and wide, hundreds of thousands of leagues wide, as measureless as the sky, as vast as all of space,

gdugs dang / rgyal mtshan dang / ba dan gyi rgyan grangs med pas brgyan pa/ rin po che grangs med pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa/ mu tig gi phreng ba grangs med pa rab tu dbyangs pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa/ rin po che'i phreng ba grangs med pa rab tu dpyangs pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa/
adorned with countless attributes; countless canopies, banners, pennants, jewels, garlands of pearls and gems,

mu tig dmar po'i phreng ba grangs med pa rab tu dpyangs pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa/ seng+ge'i mu tig gi phreng ba grangs med pa rab tu dpyangs pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa/ seng+ge'i rgyal mtshan grangs med pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa/

zla ba dang zla gam grangs med pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa/ dar gyi lnga ldi sna tshogs grangs med pa rab tu dpyangs pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa/ dar gyi ba dan sna tshogs grangs med pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa/ rin po che mang po grangs med pa'i 'od kyi rgyan gyis brgyan pa/ gser gyi dra ba grangs med pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa/
moons and half moons, multicolored streamers, jewel nets, gold nets,

rin po che'i snam bu grangs med pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa/ gser gyi lcags bod rin po ches spras pa grangs med pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa/ dril bu sgra snyan pa'i byung ba grangs med pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa/ rin po che'i dril bu g.yer kha'i dra ba bskyod na yid du 'ong ba'i sgra 'byung ba grangs med pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa/
strings of jewels, jewels on golden threads, sweetly ringing bells and nets of chimes,

lha rdzas kyi me tog mang po'i char mngon par 'bab pa grangs med pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa/ lha rdzas kyi phreng ba'i lnga ldi mngon par dpyangs pa grangs med pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa/ gam yo nas smos kyi snod nas bdug spos 'thul ba'i yo byad grangs med pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa/ gser gyi phye ma'i char rab tu 'bab pa grangs med pa'i rgyan gyi brgyan pa/
flowers showering, celestial garlands and streamers, censers giving off fragrant fumes, showers of gold dust,
pu shu'i dra ba grangs med pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa/ skar khung grangs med pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa/ rta babs grangs med pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa/ ba gam grangs med pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa;
networks of upper chambers, round windows, arches, turrets,

me long gi dkyil 'khor grangs med pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa/ rin po che'i pha gu grangs med pa gtams pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa/ rin po che'i rtsig pa grangs med pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa/ rin po che'i ka ba grangs med pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa/
mirrors, jewel figurines of women, jewel chips, pillars,

rin po che'i gos kyi sprin grangs med pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa/ rin po che'i shing grangs med pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa; rin po che'i khri 'phang grangs med pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa/ rin po che'i lam grangs med pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa/
clouds of precious cloths, jewel trees, jewel railings, jeweled pathways,

rin po che grangs med pa'i ba dan gyi rgyan gyis brgyan pa/ sa'i gzhi rgyan sna tshogs grangs med pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa/ rin po che grangs med pa las brtsegs pa'i khang pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa/ rin po che'i khri grangs med pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa/
jeweled awnings, various arrays of the floor, chambers of jewels, jeweled promenades,
rin po che'i bu mo grangs med pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa/ rin po che'i snam bu grangs med pa bting ba'i 'chag sa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa;
adorned by countless precious statues of females; adorned by countless walkways overhung with precious streamers;
'dzam bu chu klung gi gser gyi chu shing gi ka ba shin tu rnam par phye ba grangs med pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa/
adorned by countless beautifully arranged pillars of banana trees made of Jambu River gold;
rows of golden banana trees,

rin po che thams cad kyi gzugs grangs med pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa/ byang chub sems dpa'i lus grangs med pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa/ bya'i tshogs sna tshogs yid du 'ong ba'i sgra 'byin pa grangs med pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa/ rin po che'i pad+mo grangs med pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa/
statues made of all kinds of jewels, images of enlightening beings, singing birds, jewel lotuses,
rin po che'i srog shing 'dzin pa grangs med pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa/ rdzing bu grangs med pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa/
adorned by countless precious supporting columns; adorned by countless pools;
me tog puN+Da rI ka grangs med pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa/ rin po che'i them skas grangs med pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa/
adorned by countless white lotuses; adorned by countless stairways;
lotus ponds, jewel stairways,
rin po che'i stegs bu rnam par bkod pa grangs med pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa;
adorned by countless arrangements of daises;[2121]

rin po che sna tshogs grangs med pas spras pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa/ nor bu rin po che chen po'i 'od grangs med pa rab tu 'gyed pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa/ rin po che thams cad rnam par phye ba grangs med pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa/
ground of masses of various jewels, radiant gems, arrays of all kinds of jewels.
yon tan dang legs pa phun sum tshogs pa grangs med pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa 'dug par mthong ste/
and adorned by countless perfect qualities and excellences.

khang pa brtsegs pa de'i nang na yang khang pa brtsegs pa gzhan brgya stong 'di lta bu'i rgyan dang / / lhab lhub kyis brgyan pa/ rin po che'i gdugs dang / rgyal mtshan dang / lha'i bdag grangs med pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa nas yon tan dang legs pa phun sum tshogs pa grangs med pa'i bar gyi rgyan gyis brgyan pas gang bar mthong ngo/ /

He saw within the kūṭāgāra another hundred thousand with this kind of an array of adornments: adorned by countless precious parasols, banners, and flags, and so on, adorned by countless perfect excellent qualities.
Also, inside the great tower he saw hundreds of thousands of other towers similarly arrayed;
khang pa brtsegs pa de dag thams cad kyang de ltar rgya che zhing yangs pa/ de ltar tshad med de nam mkha'i mdzod du gyur pa kun nas shin tu spa bar 'khod par mthong ngo/ /
He saw that all those kūṭāgāras were in that way vast, immense, and immeasurable; were treasuries of space; and had been completely, beautifully adorned.
he saw those towers as infinitely vast as space, evenly arrayed in all directions,

des khang pa brtsegs pa rnam par phye ba de dag thams cad kyang dmigs pa gcig la phan tshun ma 'dres pa dang / phan tshun ma 'dzings pa dang / phan tshun sa la gsal bor 'dug par gzugs brnyan gyi tshul du de la snang bar gyur te/ dmigs pa gcig la ji lta ba de bzhin du dmigs pa ma lus pa de dag thams cad la'ang snang bar mthong ngo/ /

He saw that these kūṭāgāras were perfectly arranged so that in a single perception they appeared in the manner of reflections that were separate from one another, not mingled with one another, and distinct from one another, and so that they appeared with all of them without exception being perceived in a single perception.
yet these towers were not mixed up with one another, being each mutually distinct, while appearing reflected in each and every object of all the other towers.

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis khang pa brtsegs pa chen po rnam par snang mdzad kyi rgyan gyis brgyan pa'i snying po'i yul dang / rnam par 'phrul pa bsam gyis mi khyab pa rnam pa de lta bu dag mthong nas dga' ba'i thugs dpag tu med pa rnam par 'phel ba'i spro ba dang / mos pa chen pos lus dang sems mngon par brlan pa dang / 'du shes kyi rnam pa thams cad rnam par bsal pa'i yid dang / sgrib pa thams cad rnam par zlog pa'i sems dang / rmongs pa thams cad dang rnam par bral ba dang / 'khrul pa med pa'i phyogs la rab tu gzhol ba dang / thams cad la thogs pa med pa'i dran pas rnam par dmigs pa'i rna ba dang ldan pa dang / yid la bya ba'i rnam par 'khrug pa thams cad dang bral ba dang / rnam par thar pa sgrib pa med pa'i tshul gyi rjes su 'brang ba'i blo dang / dmigs pa thams cad la sgrib pa med par mig rab tu 'gro bar gyur nas phyogs kyi rgyud thams cad la mngon du bltas pa'i lus kyis phyag bya bar mngon par sgrub pa'i stobs thams cad du khyab pa dang ldan pa'i lus thams cad kyis phab ste phyag byas so/ /

Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, having seen in that way the inconceivable field of perception and miraculous manifestations of the Vairocanavyūhālaṃkāragarbha kūṭāgāra, had great delight, and his enthusiasm and aspiration increased by an immeasurable power of joy, which saturated his mind and body; his mind was clarified of all conceptualizations; his mind dispelled all obscurations; he was freed from all ignorance; he entered the direction of the absence of delusion;[2122] he had hearing that perceived with the unimpeded memory of all sounds; he had mentation that was free of all confusion; he had the power of understanding that followed the way of unobscured liberation; he had eyesight that reached all perceptions without obscuration; and with the accomplishment of paying homage with his body while facing all directions he paid homage by prostrating with the full length of his all-pervading body.

Then Sudhana, seeing this miraculous manifestation of the inconceivable realm of the great tower containing the adornments of Vairocana, was flooded with joy and bliss; his mind was cleared of all conceptions and freed from all obstructions. Stripped of all delusion, he became clairvoyant without distortion, and could hear all sounds with unimpeded mindfulness. He was freed from all scattering of attention, and his intellect followed the unobstructed eye of liberation. With physical tranquillity, seeing all objects without hindrance, by the power of production everywhere he bowed in all directions with his whole body.

de ltar tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis phyag byas ma thag tu byang chub sems dpa' byams pa'i byin gyi rlabs kyi mthus khang pa brtsegs pa de dag thams cad kyi nang du bdag nyid phyin par shes par gyur to; ; khang pa brtsegs pa de dag thams cad du'ang rnam par 'phrul ba bsam gyis mi khyab pa'i yul can rnam pa sna tshogs rnam pa tha dad pa mang po yang mthong bar gyur to/ khang pa brtsegs pa la lar ni/ byang chub sems dpa' byams pas thog ma rigs ni/ gang du skyes te/ ming ci zhes bya bar gyur pa zhig gis dge ba'i rtsa ba gang dang / yongs su bskul ba gang dang / dge ba'i bshes gnyen gang gis yang dag par bskul ba dang / tshe'i tshad ni/ ji tsam zhig tu/ bskal pa'i ming ni/ ci zhes bya bar/ de bzhin gshegs pa ni/ gang la/ rgyan ni/ ji lta bu zhig dang ldan pa'i zhing du/ 'khor ni/ ji lta bu zhig tu/ smon lam gyi khyad par ni/ ji lta bu zhig mngon par bsgrubs te bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu smon lam gyi sems bskyed pa de dag thams cad kyang mthong bar gyur to/ / shes par gyur to/ / khong du chud par gyur to/ /

As soon as Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, bowed down he perceived that he had entered all those kūṭāgāras through the power of the bodhisattva Maitreya’s blessing. He saw the many different and various miraculous manifestations and inconceivable objects of perception inside those kūṭāgāras. Inside some kūṭāgāras he perceived and comprehended where the bodhisattva Maitreya first developed the prayer for the highest, complete enlightenment: his birth into a family, what name he had, what roots of merit he was inspired to, which kalyāṇamitras inspired him, his lifespan, the name of the kalpa, and under which tathāgata in a realm with what kinds of displays and in what kind of assembly he made which particular prayers.

The moment he bowed, by the power of Maitreya, Sudhana perceived himself in all of those towers; and in all those towers he saw various diverse inconceivable miraculous scenes. In one tower he saw where the enlightening being Maitreya first aspired to supreme perfect enlightenment, what his family was, what his basic goodness was, how he was inspired, how he was encouraged by spiritual friends, how long he lived, what age he lived in, what buddha he met, what land he adorned, what assembly he was in, and what kind of special vows he undertook.

de'i tshe sems can de dag dang / de bzhin gshegs pa de'i sku tshe'i tshad dang / tshe'i tshad ji srid gcig tu gyur pa de tsam gyi dus su de bzhin gshegs pa de'i zhabs kyi drung na bdag nyid 'dug par yang shes par gyur te/ bya ba de dag thams cad kyang mthong bar gyur to/ /
He also perceived himself, during the entire lifetime of that tathāgata and of those beings, to be at the feet of that tathāgata in that time, and he saw all those activities.
He also perceived the length of life of the beings and the buddha of that time, and saw himself in the presence of that buddha, and saw all of his works.

khang pa brtsegs pa la lar ni/ byang chub sems dpa' byams pas thog ma gang du byams pa'i ting nge 'dzin thob par gyur pa dang / dus gang nas bzung ste de'i ming byams pa zhes bya bar gyur pa de dag mthong bar gyur to/ /
In some kūṭāgāras he saw the bodhisattva Maitreya at the time that he first attained the samādhi of love.
In one tower he saw where Maitreya first attained absorption in love, whence came his name, “The Loving One.”

la lar ni/ gang du spyod pa spyad pa dang / la lar ni/ gang du pha rol tu phyin pa yongs su rdzogs par byas pa dang / la lar ni/ gang du bzod pa la zhugs pa dang / la lar ni/ gang du sa non pa dang / la lar ni/ gang du sangs rgyas kyi zhing gi rgyan yongs su bzung ba dang / la lar ni/ gang du de bzhin gshegs pa'i bstan pa yongs su bzung ba dang / la lar ni/ gang du mi skye ba'i chos la bzod pa thob par gyur pa dang / la lar ni/ gang du bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu lung bstan pa dang / rnam pa ni/ ji lta bu zhig tu lung bstan pa dang / lung ni/ sus bstan pa dang / yun ni/ ji srid gcig gis lung bstan pa de dag thams cad kyang mthong bar gyur to/ /

In some, he saw where he practiced conduct; in some, where he completed the perfections; in some, where he entered the state of patience; in some, where he ascended the bhūmis; in some, where he gained the displays of buddha realms; in some, where he obtained the teaching of tathāgatas; in some, where he attained the patience of the birthlessness of phenomena; and in some, where he received the prophecy of his highest, complete enlightenment, and everything about what kind of prophecy he received, who gave the prophecy, and the length of time that was prophesied.

In another he saw where he carried out spiritual practice; in another, where he fulfilled the transcendent ways; in another, where he attained acceptance of things as unoriginated; in another, where he was assured of supreme perfect enlightenment, how he was assured, by whom, and how long it was predicted it would be before he was enlightened.
khang pa brtsegs pa la lar ni/ byang chub sems dpa' byams pa 'khor los bsgyur ba'i rgyal por gyur te sems can rnams dge ba bcu'i las kyi lam la rab tu 'god pa mthong bar gyur to/ /
In some kūṭāgāras he saw the bodhisattva Maitreya being a cakravartin establishing beings on the path of the ten good actions.
In one tower he saw Maitreya as a sovereign king directing people to virtuous action;

la lar ni/ 'jig rten gyi mgon por gyur te/ 'jig rten gyi phan pa dang / bde ba thams cad kyis sems can rnams la nye bar sdud pa dang / la lar ni; brgya byin du gyur te/ 'dod par yon tan gyi dga' ba las sems can rnams rnam par zlog pa dang / la lar ni/ tshangs par gyur te bsam gtan dang / tshad med pa'i dga' ba sems can rnams la yongs su rjod pa dang / la lar ni/ lha'i dbang po rab mtsho mar gyur te tshad med pa'i yon tan sems can rnams la yongs su rjod pa dang / la lar ni/ lha'i dbang po rab dga' ldan du gyur te/ byang chub sems dpa' tshe gcig gis thogs pa'i yon tan rjod pa dang / la lar ni/ lha'i rgyal po rab 'phrul dga' bar gyur te/ lha'i 'khor du byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi sprul pa'i rgyan yongs su ston pa dang / la lar ni/ lha'i rgyal po dbang sgyur du gyur te/ lha rnams la chos thams cad la dbang sgyur ba yang dag par ston pa dang / la lar ni/ bdud du gyur te lha rnams la phun sum tshogs pa thams cad mi rtag par ston pa dang / la lar ni/ lha ma yin gyi dbang po'i gnas su skyes te lha ma yin gyi 'khor na nga rgyal dang / dregs pa dang / rlom pa thams cad rab tu spang ba dang / ye shes kyi rgya mtsho chen por 'jug par bya ba dang / chos kyi ye shes kyi rgyu thob par bya ba'i phyir chos ston pa mthong ngo/ /

In some, he saw him being a lord of the world, benefiting the world and gathering beings through all kinds of happiness; in some, being a Śakra, turning beings away from delighting in sensory pleasures; in some, being a Brahmā, describing to beings dhyāna and immeasurable joy; in some, being a Suyāma deva lord, describing limitless qualities to beings; in some, being a Saṃtuṣita deva lord, describing the qualities of a bodhisattva with one life remaining; in some, being a Sunirmita deva lord, manifesting the array of emanations of all bodhisattvas to his retinue; in some, being a Vaśavartin deva lord, displaying to the devas power over all phenomena; in some, being a Māra, teaching to devas the impermanence of all good fortune; and in some, being born in the dwelling of the lord of the asuras, teaching the Dharma to his retinue of asuras in order that they forsake all pride, arrogance, and conceit, enter the great ocean of wisdom,[2123] and attain the illusory powers[2124] of the wisdom of the Dharma.

in another he saw Maitreya as a world guardian bestowing well-being and happiness on the world; in another he saw Maitreya as Indra, fostering detachment in those obsessed with pleasure; in another he saw Maitreya as Brahma, describing to people the measureless pleasure of meditation; in another he saw Maitreya as the chief of the gods of timely portion, describing to people the virtues of attentiveness and diligence; in another he saw Maitreya as the chief of the heaven of contentment, revealin the virtues of enlightening beings bound to become buddhas in one lifetime; in another he saw Maitreya as a king of the heaven of good emanations, showing a company of celestials the array of emanations of all enlightening beings; in another he saw Maitreya as a lord of the heaven of control, explaining to the gods control over all phenomena; in another he saw Maitreya causing the devil to act, showing the gods the impermanence of all states of being; in another he saw Maitreya born in the palace of titans, teaching the titans truth so that they might do away with all conceit, pride, and arrogance, plunge into the ocean of knowledge, enter the ocean of spiritual knowledge, and attain the magic of knowledge of truth.

khang pa brtsegs pa la lar ni/ gshin rje'i 'jig rten mthong bar gyur te/ de na byang chub sems dpa' byams pa 'od kyis sems can dmyal ba thams cad snang bar byed cing / sems can dmyal bar skyes pa'i sems can rnams kyi sems can dmyal ba'i sdug bsngal thams cad rab tu zhi bar byed pa mthong ngo/ /

In some kūṭāgāras he saw the realm of Yama, in which the light of the bodhisattva Maitreya illuminated all the beings in the hells, so that all the sufferings of the hells ceased for the beings who had been reborn in the hells.
In one tower he saw the underworld and saw Maitreya illumine the great hells with light and relieve the hellish pains of the beings in hell.

khang pa brtsegs pa la lar ni/ yi kyi gnas mthong bar gyur te; de na byang chub sems dpa' byams pa sems can yi kyi gnas su skyes pa rnams la kha zas dang / btung ba mang po nye bar sgrub cing bkres pa dang / skom pa rab tu zhi bar byed pa mthong ngo/ /
In some kūṭāgāras he saw the realm of the pretas, in which the bodhisattva Maitreya created much food and drink for the beings who had been reborn in the preta realms, ending their hunger and thirst.
In another tower he saw the ghost world and saw Maitreya giving much food and drink to the ghosts, relieving their hunger and thirst.
khang pa brtsegs pa la lar ni/ byol song gi skye gnas na skye ba'i skye mched rnam pa tha dad pa sna tshogs kyis byol song gi skye gnas su gtogs pa'i sems can mang po 'dul ba mthong ngo/ /
In some kūṭāgāras he saw the worlds of animals, in which through taking birth in their various kinds of physical existences he guided those beings who had been reborn as animals.
In another tower he saw Maitreya guiding the beings in the animal realm.

khang pa brtsegs pa la lar ni/ rgyal po chen po'i khams su gtogs pa'i lha'i 'khor na 'jig rten gyi mgon po rnams la chos ston pa mthong ngo/ / la lar ni/ lha'i dbang po brgya byin gyi 'khor na/ la lar ni/ lha'i rgyal po rab mtshe ma'i 'khor na/ la lar ni/ lha'i rgyal po rab dga' ldan gyi 'khor na/ la lar ni/ lha'i rgyal po rab 'phrul dga'i 'khor na/ la lar ni/ lha'i rgyal po dbang sgyur gyi 'khor na/ la lar ni/ bdud kyi 'khor na/ khang pa brtsegs pa la lar ni/ tshangs pa'i dbang po'i 'khor na byang chub sems dpa' byams pa chos ston pa mthong ngo/ /

In some kūṭāgāras he saw him in the deva retinues of the realms of the Mahārājas, where he taught the Dharma to the world lords; in some, he was in the retinue of a Śakra deva lord; in some, in the retinue of a Suyāma deva king; in some, in the retinue of a Saṃtuṣita deva king; in some, in the retinue of a Sunirmita deva king; in some, in the retinue of a Vaśavartin deva king; in some, in the retinue of a Māra; and in some kūṭāgāras he saw the bodhisattva Maitreya teaching the Dharma in the retinue of a Brahmā lord.

In one tower he saw Maitreya expounding the Teaching to world guardians in an assembly of celestial kings; in another he saw him in a group of chief gods of the thirty-three-fold heavens; in another he saw him in a group of chiefs of the heaven of timely portion; in another he saw him in a group of lords of the heaven of contentment; in another he saw him in a group of chiefs of the heaven of good emanations; in another he saw him in a group of kings, of the heaven of control; in another tower he saw Maitreya as a Great Brahma in a group of Brahma lords, expounding the Teaching.

la lar ni/ klu dang lto 'phye chen po'i 'khor na; la lar ni/ gnod sbyin dang srin po'i 'khor na/ la lar ni/ dri za dang mi 'am ci'i 'khor na/ la lar ni/ lha ma yin dang gsod 'phrog gi dbang po'i 'khor na/ la lar ni/ nam mkha' lding gi dbang po chen po'i 'khor na/ la lar ni/ mi'i 'khor na/ khang pa brtsegs pa la lar ni/ lha dang / klu dang / gnod sbyin dang / dri za dang / lha ma yin dang / nam mkha' lding dang / mi 'am ci dang / lto 'phye chen po dang / mi dang mi ma yin pa'i 'khor na byang chub sems dpa' byams pa chos ston pa mthong ngo/ /

In some kūṭāgāras, he saw the bodhisattva Maitreya teaching the Dharma in the retinues of great nāgas and mahoragas; in some, in the retinues of yakṣas and rākṣasas; in some, in the retinues of gandharvas and kinnaras; in some, in the retinues of the lords of the asuras and dānavas; in some, in the retinues of great lords of the garuḍas; in some, in the retinues of humans; in some, in the retinues of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, and nonhumans;

In one tower he saw Maitreya in a group of dragons and serpents; in another, in a group of goblins and fiends; in another, in a group of titans and demons; in another, in a group of giant serpents; in another, in a group of human chiefs; in another tower, he saw the enlightening being Maitreya in a group of gods, dragons, goblins, fiends, cherubs, titans, birds, minotaurs, serpents, humans, and nonhumans, expounding the Teaching to them.

la lar ni/ nyan thos kyi 'khor na/ la lar ni/ rang sangs rgyas kyi 'khor na/ la lar ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i 'khor na/ khang pa brtsegs pa la lar ni/ byang chub sems dpa' sems thog ma bskyed pa las dang po pa rnams la byang chub sems dpa' byams pa chos ston pa mthong ngo/ /

in some, in the retinues of śrāvakas; in some, in the retinues of pratyekabuddhas; and in some, in the retinues of bodhisattvas. In some kūṭāgāras, he saw the bodhisattva Maitreya teaching the Dharma to beginner bodhisattvas who had developed the aspiration to enlightenment for the first time;

In one tower he saw Maitreya in a group of hearers; in another, in a group of individual illuminates; in another, in a group of enlightening beings; in another tower, he saw Maitreya expounding the Teaching to beginning enlightening beings who had just set their minds on enlightenment.

la lar ni/ spyod pa la zhugs pa rnams la/ la lar ni/ bzod pa thob cing phyir mi ldog pa rnams la/ la lar ni/ tshe gcig gis thogs shing dbang bskur pa rnams la/ khang pa brtsegs pa la lar ni/ byang chub sems dpa' sa dang po la gnas pa rnams la sa'i khyad par yongs su brjod pa mthong ngo/ /

in some, to those who were engaged in bodhisattva conduct; in some, to those who had attained patience and were irreversible; and in some, to those who were in their last lifetime and had been consecrated by the buddhas. In some kūṭāgāras, he saw him describing the particular qualities of a bhūmi to bodhisattvas who were on the first bhūmi,

In another tower he saw Maitreya extolling the excellences of the stages to those who had undertaken practice; in another, to those who had attained tolerance and were irreversible; in another, to those bound to be enlightened in one lifetime who had attained coronation; in another tower, to enlightening beings in the first stage.
la lar ni/ sa bcu la gnas pa'i bar gyi byang chub sems dpa' rnams dang lhan cig tu byang chub sems dpa' byams pa sa thams cad kyi khyad par yang dag par bgro ba byed pa mthong ngo/ /
and in some he saw the bodhisattva Maitreya discussing all the particular qualities of the bhūmis with bodhisattvas on all ten bhūmis;
In another tower he saw Maitreya with enlightening beings in stages up to the tenth, extolling the excellence of all the stages.
la lar ni/ pha rol tu phyin pa thams cad yongs su rdzogs par bya ba dang /
in some, he had the completion of all the perfections;
In another tower he saw Maitreya speaking of the infinity of fulfillment of the transcendent ways;
la lar ni/ bslab pa thams cad la mngon du 'jug par bya ba kun tu mtha' yas pa dang /
in some, he had infinite[2125] entries into all trainings;
in another, of impartiality in approaching and entering into all studies;
la lar ni/ ting nge 'dzin gyi sgo la 'jug pa rgya chen po dang /
in some, he had vast entries through the gateways of all samādhis;
in another, of breadth of entry into concentration;

la lar ni/ rnam par thar pa'i tshul zab mo dang / la lar ni/ bsam gtan dang / ting nge 'dzin dang / snyoms par 'jug pa dang / mngon par shes pa zhi ba'i yul gyis rgyas par dgang ba dang / la lar ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa dang / 'dul ba dang / thabs kyi sgo la 'jug pa dang / la lar ni/ smon lam mngon par sgrub pa rgya che ba dang /

khang pa brtsegs pa la lar ni/ byang chub sems dpa' byams pa skal pa mthun par spyod pa'i byang chub sems dpa' rnams dang 'grogs shing 'jig rten la phan par bya ba'i don du bzo'i gnas sna tshogs dang / gtsug lag gi khyad par sems can thams cad la phan pa dang / bde bar 'gyur ba dang / 'byor pa rnams yang dag par bgro ba mthong ngo/ /

In some kūṭāgāras, he saw the bodhisattva Maitreya accompanying bodhisattvas who followed the same kind of conduct and spoke in unison[2126] about engaging, in order to benefit beings, in the various specific kinds of arts and treatises that bring benefit, happiness, and wealth to all beings.

in another tower he saw Maitreya with a group of enlightening beings engaged in the same practice as he, speaking of the relevance of providing for the welfare and happiness of all beings, of the various arts and sciences to be employed for the benefit of the world.
la lar ni/ byang chub sems dpa' tshe gcig gis thogs pa rnams dang 'grogs shing / sangs rgyas thams cad kyi ye shes la dbang bskur ba'i sgo yang dag par bgro ba mthong ngo/ /
In some, he saw him speaking in unison[2127] with bodhisattvas with one lifetime remaining about entering the gateway of the wisdom consecration of all the buddhas.
In another tower he saw Maitreya with a group of enlightening beings bound to be enlightened in one life, telling them about coronation with the knowledge of all buddhas.
khang pa brtsegs ba la lar ni/ byang chub sems dpa' byams pa 'chag pa byed cing lo brgya stong du mar mi gtong ba la brtson pa mthong ngo/ /
In some kūṭāgāras, he saw the bodhisattva Maitreya dedicated to walking[2128] for many hundreds of thousands of years.
In another tower he saw Maitreya perambulating ceaselessly for hundreds of thousands of years;

la lar ni/ lung 'bog pa dang / kha ton bya ba la brtson par/ la lar ni/ chos kyi sgo rab tu brtag pa la brtson par; la lar ni/ dam pa'i chos bgro ba la brtson pa/ la lar ni/ dam pa'i chos bri ba la brtson par/

la lar ni/ byams pa la mnyam par bzhag par/ la lar ni/ bsam gtan dang tshad med pa thams cad la mnyam par bzhag par/ la lar ni/ rgyas pa'i skye mched dang / rnam par thar pa thams cad la mnyam par bzhag pa dang /
khang pa brtsegs pa la lar ni/ byang chub sems dpa' byams pa byang chub sems dpa'i mngon par shes pa sgrub pa'i thabs kyi ting nge 'dzin la mnyam par bzhag pa mthong ngo/ /
and in some, he was resting in meditation in the samādhi of the method for accomplishing the higher cognitions of a bodhisattva.
in another tower he saw Maitreya absorbed in the practice of bringing forth the higher knowledge of enlightening beings.

khang pa brtsegs pa la lar ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin sprul pa yod pa la mnyam par bzhag pa'i byang chub sems dpa' mang po mthong ste/ de dag gi lus thams cad dang / ba spu'i sgo thams cad nas sprul pa thams cad kyi sprin mang po 'byung ba mthong ngo/ /
In some kūṭāgāras, he saw many bodhisattvas resting in the bodhisattva samādhi of emanations, and he saw many clouds of all emanations coming from all the pores of all their bodies.
In one tower he saw enlightening beings absorbed in an enlightening concentration which emanated phantoms, and saw multitudes of all kinds of emanations coming from every pore of their bodies.

la lar ni/ lus dang ba spu'i sgo thams cad nas ni/ lha'i ris kyi sprin mang po 'byung ba mthong ngo/ / la la'i lus dang ba spu'i sgo thams cad nas ni/ klu dang / gnod sbyin dang / dri za dang / lha ma yin dang / nam mkha' lding dang / mi 'am ci dang / lto 'phye chen po dang / brgya byin dang / tshangs pa dang / 'jig rten gyi mgon po dang / 'khor los bsgyur ba'i sprin mang po 'byung ba dang / la la'i lus dang ba spu'i sgo thams cad nas ni/ khams kyi rgyal po'i sprin mang po 'byung ba dang / la la'i lus dang ba spu'i sgo thams cad nas ni/ rgyal bu gzhon nu'i sprin mang po 'byung ba dang / la la'i lus dang ba spu'i sgo thams cad nas ni/ tshong dpon dang / blon po dang / khyim bdag gi sprin mang po dang / la la'i lus dang ba spu'i sgo thams cad nas ni/ nyan thos dang / rang sangs rgyas dang / byang chub sems dpa'i sprin mang po dang / la la'i lus dang ba spu'i sgo thams cad nas ni/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i sku'i sprin mang po dang / la la'i lus dang ba spu'i sgo thams cad nas ni/ sems can thams cad du sprul pa'i sprin tshad med pa 'byung ba mthong ngo/ /

From some of them, he saw many clouds of devas arising from all their bodies and pores. From some of them, he saw many clouds of nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, Śakras, Brahmās, world lords, and cakravartins arising from all their bodies and pores; from some of them, many clouds of kings of realms from all their bodies and pores; from some of them, many clouds of young princes from all their bodies and pores; from some of them, many clouds of head merchants, ministers, and householders from all their bodies and pores; from some of them, many clouds of śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and bodhisattvas from all their bodies and pores; from some of them, many clouds of the bodies of tathāgatas from all their bodies and pores; and from some of them, measureless clouds of emanated beings arising from all their bodies and pores.

From the pores of some he saw multitudes of celestial hosts emerging; from some he saw multitudes of dragons, goblins, cherubs, titans, birds, minotaurs, serpents, Indras, Brahmas, world guardians, and emperors; from some he saw multitudes of princes; from some he saw multitudes of grandees, ministers, and gentlemen; from some he saw multitudes of hearers, individual illuminates, and enlightening beings; from some he saw multitudes of buddha-bodies; from the pores of some he saw measureless multitudes of phantoms of all sentient beings emerge.
