la la'i lus dang ba spu'i sgo thams cad nas ni/ chos kyi sgo rnam pa sna tshogs 'byung ba thos par gyur te/ 'di ltar byang chub sems dpa'i yon tan bsngags pa'i sgo dang / sbyin pa'i pha rol tu phyin pa'i sgo dang / tshul khrims dang / bzod pa dang / brtson 'grus dang / bsam gtan dang / shes rab dang / thabs dang / smon lam dang / stobs dang / ye shes kyi pha rol tu phyin pa'i sgo dang / bsdu ba'i dngos po dang / bsam gtan dang / tshad med pa dang / ting nge 'dzin dang / snyoms par 'jug pa dang / mngon par shes pa dang / rig pa dang / gzungs dang / spobs pa dang / bden pa dang / tha dad pa yang dag par shes pa dang / zhi gnas dang / lhag mthong dang / rnam par thar pa'i sgo dang / rten cing 'brel par 'byung ba dang / rten pa dang / chos kyi mdo dang / dran pa nye bar gzhag pa dang / yang dag par spong ba dang / rdzu 'phrul gyi rkang pa dang / dbang po dang / stobs dang / byang chub kyi yan lag dang / lam dang / nyan thos kyi theg pa'i gtam dang / rang sangs rgyas kyi theg pa'i gtam dang / theg pa chen po'i gtam dang / sa dang / bzod pa dang / spyod pa dang / smon lam gyi sgo dang / de bzhin du chos thams cad kyi sgor 'jug pa'i sgra mang po 'byung ba thos so/ /

From some of them, he heard various Dharma gateways coming from all their bodies and pores, which means he heard the many sounds of entering all Dharma doors such as the door of praising the qualities of bodhisattvas; the door of the perfection of generosity; the doors of the perfections of conduct, patience, diligence, dhyāna, wisdom, method, prayer, strength, and knowledge; the doors of the methods of gathering pupils, the dhyānas, the immeasurables, the samādhis, the samāpattis, the higher cognitions, gnosis, the retentions, the eloquences, the truths, the discernments, śamatha, vipaśyanā, and liberation; and the doors of dependent origination, elimination, the bases of miraculous powers, the powers, the strengths, the aspects of enlightenment, the paths, the teaching of the Śrāvakayāna, the teaching of the Pratyekabuddhayāna, the teaching of the Mahāyāna, the bhūmis, patience, conduct, and prayer.

He heard various aspects of the Teaching being broadcast from the pores of some of the enlightening beings—teachings of the virtues of enlightening beings, transcendent generosity, discipline, tolerance, vigor, meditation, wisdom, methods, vows, power, knowledge, the means of integration, the immeasurables, concentrations, trance, superknowledge, mystic spells, intellectual powers of analysis and exposition, tranquillity and observation, means of liberation, interdependent origination, the reliances, summarization of teachings, the points of mindfulness, the right efforts, the bases of mystic powers, the religious faculties and powers, the limbs of enlightenment, the paths, explanation of the vehicle of hearers, explanation of the vehicle of individual illuminates, explanation of the Great Vehicle, the stages, tolerances, practices, and vows—in this way he heard voices expressing all the ways into the Teaching being broadcast.

khang pa brtsegs pa la lar ni/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor du kun nas 'dus par mthong ste/ de bzhin gshegs pa de dag gi rnam pa tha dad pa rnam pa sna tshogs skye ba dang / rigs rnam pa tha dad pa dang / sku rnam par phye ba tshad med pa rnam pa tha dad pa dang / sku tshe rnam pa tha dad pa dang / zhing rnam pa tha dad pa dang / bskal pa rnam pa tha dad pa dang / chos bstan pa rnam pa tha dad pa dang / 'byung ba'i sgo rnam pa tha dad pa dang / dam pa'i chos gnas pa rnam pa tha dad pa nas 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor rnam pa thams cad du rnam pa tha dad pa dag kyang ma lus par mthong bar gyur to/ /

In some kūṭāgāras, he saw the gathered assemblies of followers of tathāgatas. He saw the various different births of those tathāgatas, their different families, their countless different lifetimes,[2129] their different realms, their different kalpas, their different teachings of the Dharma, their different gateways of emanations,[2130] the different durations of their Dharmas, and so on, up to all the different forms of their assemblies of followers without exception.

In another tower he saw gatherings of the audiences of buddhas, as well as the various differences among those buddhas, their different families, the infinite variety of their physical adornments, the variety of their life spans, the differences in their lands and eras, the variety of their teachings, the variety of the outwardness of their projected manifestations, the differences in the duration of their true teachings, and all the differences in their assemblies.

khang pa brtsegs pa chen po rnam par snang mdzad kyi rgyan gyis brgyan pa'i snying po de'i dbus su khang pa brtsegs pa gcig cig gzhan pas che la yangs shing khang pa brtsegs pa gzhan thams cad kyi rgyan ma lus pa thams cad pas kyang ches lhag par 'phags pa'i rgyan gyis yang dag par brgyan pa zhig 'dug par mthong ste/

He saw in the center of the Vairocanavyūhālaṃkāragarbha kūṭāgāra one kūṭāgāra that was greater and vaster than the others and was adorned with adornments that were greatly superior to all the adornments, without exception, of all the other kūṭāgāras.
In the middle of the great tower containing the adornments of Vairocana he saw one tower which was bigger than all the others and arrayed with adornments surpassing all the other towers.

khang pa brtsegs pa de'i nang na stong gsum gyi stong chen po'i 'jig rten gyi khams 'dug pa mthong ngo/ / stong gsum gyi stong chen po'i 'jig rten gyi khams de na yang gling bzhi pa bye ba phrag brgya dang / 'dzam bu'i gling bye ba phrag brgya dang / dga' ldan gyi gnas bye ba phrag brgya 'khod par mthong ngo/ /
He saw within that kūṭāgāra a billion-world world realm. He saw in that billion-world world realm the billion four-continent worlds and a billion Jambudvīpas and a billion Tuṣita paradises.
In that tower he saw a billion-world universe, in which he saw a hundred million sets of four continents, with a hundred million Jambudvipas and a hundred million heavens of contentment.

'dzam bu'i gling de dag thams cad na'ang byang chub sems dpa' byams pa pad+mo'i nang nas skye ba dang / brgya byin dang / tshangs pas yongs su blangs pa dang / gom pa bdun du 'gro ba dang / phyogs bcur rnam par bltas pa dang / seng+ge'i nga ro chen po sgrog pa dang / gzhon nu'i sa thams cad yongs su ston pa dang / btsun mo'i 'khor gyi nang na gnas pa dang / bza' shing gi ra bar 'gro ba dang / thams cad mkhyen pa nyid la mngon du phyogs te mngon par byung nas rab tu 'byung ba dang / dka' ba'i spyod pa yongs su ston pa dang / zas za ba dang / snying po byang chub tu 'gro ba dang; bdud rgol du 'jug pa dang / byang chub tu rnam par 'tshang rgya ba dang / byang chub kyi shing la mig mi 'gebs pas lta ba dang / changs pa chen pos gsol ba gdab pa dang / mngon par rdzogs par sangs rgyas te chos kyi 'khor lo bskor ba'i yul sna tshogs yongs su bstan pa rnam pa tha dad pa dang / tshul dang ming rnam pa sna tshogs bstan pa rnam pa tha dad pa dang / tshe'i tshad sna tshogs rnam pa tha dad pa dang / 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor gyi rgyan sna tshogs rnam pa tha dad pa dang / sangs rgyas kyi zhing rnam par dag pa'i tshul bstan pa rnam pa sna tshogs rnam pa tha dad pa dang / spyod pa dang / smon lam brjod pa sna tshogs rnam pa tha dad pa dang / chos bstan cing rnam par dgod pa dang / sems can yongs su smin par bya ba'i thabs sna tshogs rnam pa tha dad pa dang / ring bsrel bgo ba dang / bstan pa gnas pa'i byin gyi rlabs yongs su bstan pa sna tshogs rnam pa tha dad pas chos kyi 'khor lo bskor zhing / lha'i gnas su 'gro ba mthong ste/

He saw within those Jambudvīpas the bodhisattva Maitreya being born from within a lotus; being taken up by Śakra and Brahmā, walking seven steps, gazing into the ten directions, and emitting the lion’s roar; manifesting all the stages of youth; being within the harem; going to the park; turning toward omniscience; setting forth and entering homelessness; manifesting the practice of asceticism; eating food; going to the bodhimaṇḍa; engaging in subjugating the māras; attaining the enlightenment of buddhahood; gazing without closing the eyes at the Bodhi tree; being supplicated by Mahābrahmā; turning the wheel of the Dharma; and passing away to divine abodes, which was done through various different manifestations of the range of attainments of buddhahood, followed by turning the wheel of the Dharma in different ways, names, and forms, with various different lifespans, with various different assemblies of followers, with various different manifestations of pure buddha realms, with various different conduct and prayers, with various methods for presenting and teaching the Dharma and for ripening beings, and with various different manifestations of the distribution of relics and the power of the duration of the teachings.

In those Jambudvipa continents he saw the enlightening being Maitreya being born in a lotus calyx; he also saw Maitreya taking seven steps as Indra and Brahma watched, looking over the ten directions, making the lion roar, showing all the stages of childhood, in the palace, out in the garden, setting out for omniscience, appearing to undertake ascetic practice, finally eating food, going to the site of enlightenment, conquering the devil, awakening to enlightenment, steadily gazing on the tree of enlightenment, being asked by Brahma to teach, and turning the wheel of the teaching, going into the celestial abodes, with various different manifestations of enlightening teaching, using various names of eras in different ways, with various different spans of life, various different arrays of gatherings, with various demonstrations of ways of purification of lands, carrying out various practices and vows, with various structures of teaching used as means to develop and mature all concerned, showing various distributions of relics and bases of maintaining the teachings.
de dag thams cad na yang tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang nyid rkang pa'i drung na 'dug par rang gis shes par gyur to/ /
Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, perceived himself to be at the feet of them all.
And everywhere there Sudhana perceived himself at Maitreya’s feet.

de 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor thams cad dang / bya ba thams cad yongs su bstan pa dang / tshe'i tshad rnam pa tha dad pa thams cad la dran pa ma nyams pa'i byin gyi rlabs kyis 'du shes kyi rnam pa thams cad khong du chud pa'i ye shes kyi sa la gnas pas

Through the blessing of the unfailing memory, all the steadfast knowledge of all those assemblies of followers, all those manifestations of activities, and all those different lifespans remained within his level of comprehending knowledge.

In all those assemblies, in all the manifestations of works, in the varieties of spans of life, by means of the knowledge based on clear recollection, standing on the ground of knowledge, sure to reach omniscience,

khang pa brtsegs pa de dag gi dril dang / dril bu g.yer kha'i dra ba dang / rol mo dang / glu la sogs pa'i dmigs pa ji snyed cig yod pa de dag thams cad las chos kyi sprin gyi 'brug sgra bsam gyis mi khyab pa 'byung ba thos par gyur te/
From all the nets of strings of bells and jingle bells, and from the music and songs and all other perceived sounds, he heard the inconceivable thunder from the clouds of the Dharma being emitted.
Sudhana heard, from all the objects in all those towers, the nets of bells and chimes, the drums and songs, and so on, and from the beings therein, the thunder of inconceivable multitudes of voices.

la la las ni/ byang chub kyi sems rnam pa tha dad pa dang / la la las ni/ pha rol tu phyin pa'i spyod pa dang / smon lam rnam pa tha dad pa dang / la la las ni/ sa tshad med pa rnam pa tha dad pa dang / la la las ni/ mngon par shes pa bsam gyis mi khyab pa'i rnam par 'phrul pa rnam pa tha dad pa dang / la la las ni/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i mchod pa sna tshogs rnam pa tha dad pa dang / la la las ni/ sangs rgyas kyi zhing gi rgyan rnam pa tha dad pa dang / la la las ni/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i chos kyi sprin tshad med pa rnam pa tha dad pa dang / de bzhin du chos thams cad kyi sgra gong du ji skad du brjod pa thams cad thos par gyur to/ /

He heard from them all the sounds of all the Dharma just as it had been previously taught: from some he heard the different kinds of aspiration to enlightenment; from some, the different kinds of conduct and prayer of the perfections; from some, the different kinds of countless bhūmis; from some, the different kinds of miraculous manifestation from inconceivable higher cognitions; from some, the different kinds of various offerings to the tathāgatas; from some, the different kinds of displays of buddha realms; and from some, the different kinds of measureless clouds of the Dharma of the tathāgatas.

From some he heard of the variety of aspirations for enlightenment; from some, about the variety of offerings to buddhas; from some, about the variety of arrays of buddha-lands; from some, about the infinite variety of teachings of buddhas—thus he heard the voices of all the teachings as they had been expounded in the past.

la la las ni/ thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du 'jug pa'i sgra thos te/ 'jig rten gyi khams che ge mo zhig ces bya bar byang chub sems dpa' ming dang che ge mo zhig gis chos kyi sgo ni/ che ge mo zhig ces bya ba thos/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen ni/ che ge mo zhig gis yang dag par bskul/ de bzhin gshegs pa ni/ che ge mo zhig gi zhabs kyi drung du/ bskal pa'i ming ni/ 'di zhes bya bar/ sangs rgyas kyi zhing ni/ 'di lta bu zhig tu/ 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor ni/ 'di lta bu zhig na 'dug 'dug ste/ dge ba'i rtsa ba ni/ 'di lta bu zhig bskyed nas de bzhin gshegs pa'i yon tan ni/ 'di lta bu dag cig thos te/ lhag pa'i bsam pa ni/ 'di lta bu dang / smon lam gyi rnam pa ni; 'di 'dra ba zhig gis byang chub tu sems bskyed nas des bskal pa ni/ 'di snyed cig tu byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa spyad de/ bskal pa 'di snyed cig gis bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu mngon par rdzogs par 'tshang rgya bar 'gyur ro/ / mtshan ni/ 'di zhes bya/ sku tshe'i tshad ni/ 'di tsam zhig ste; sangs rgyas kyi zhing gi yon tan dang / rgyan phun sum tshogs pa 'di 'dra ba dang / smon lam gyi khyad par 'di lta bu zhig dang / sems can rnam par gdul pa 'di 'dra ba zhig dang / nyan thos dang rang sangs rgyas kyi 'khor kun nas 'dus pa 'di 'dra ba zhig go / de yongs su mya ngan las 'das nas kyang bskal pa 'di snyed cig tu dam pa'i chos gnas par 'gyur ro/ / sems can gyi don ni/ 'di tsam zhig tu 'gyur ro/ / zhes bya ba'i sgra thos so/ /

From some, he heard the words concerning entering into omniscience: that in a world realm of such and such a name, a bodhisattva with such and such a name hears such and such a Dharma gateway, is inspired by such and such a kalyāṇamitra, and at the feet of such and such a tathāgata hears that in a kalpa with a certain name he will be present in a certain realm, in a certain circle of followers, and having generated certain roots of merit and having heard of certain buddha qualities will develop a certain aspiration, and through a certain kind of prayer will develop the aspiration to enlightenment and will practice bodhisattva conduct for a certain number of kalpas, and will then attain the highest, complete enlightenment of buddhahood, when he will have a certain name and a certain lifespan and have a certain perfection of qualities and arrays of a buddha realm, and through certain specific prayers will guide beings in a certain way and will gather a certain following of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, and when he has passed into nirvāṇa his Dharma will remain for a certain number of kalpas, and he will thus benefit beings in that way.

He also heard about setting out for omniscience—in such-and-such a land the enlightening being so-and-so aspired to enlightenment, heard such-and-such a teaching, was inspired by the spiritual benefactor so-and-so, went to such-and-such a congregation at the foot of the buddha so-and-so in such-and-such a land in such-and-such an age, planted such-and-such roots of goodness, heard about such-and-such qualities of buddhahood, undertook such-and-such a variety of vows with such-and-such an intention, will realize supreme perfect enlightenment in so many eons after having carried out practice for so many eons, will be named so-and-so, will live so long, in a buddha-land with such-and-such qualities, with such-and-such higher commitments, such-and-such guidance of beings, such-and-such a congregation of disciples, individual illuminates, and enlightening beings, the true teaching to last for so many ages after the death of the Buddha, with such-and-such benefits.

la la las ni/ 'jig rten gyi khams che ge mo zhig na byang chub sems dpa' ming dang / che ge mo zhig sbyin pa'i pha rol tu phyin pa la spyod na/ gtang bar dka' ba 'di lta bu'i yongs su gtong ba brgya ni/ byed do; ; byang chub sems dpa' che ge mo zhig ni/ tshul khrims srung ngo/ / bzod pa sgom mo/ / brtson 'grus rtsom mo/ / bsam gtan la snyoms par 'jug go / shes rab kyis rnam par dbye ba la brtson no/ / byang chub sems dpa' che ge mo zhig ni/ dam pa'i chos yongs su btsal ba'i don du rgyal po'i srid yongs su gtong bar byed do/ / rin po che yongs su gtong ba dang / bu yongs su gtong ba dang / chung ma yongs su gtong ba dang / rkang lag dang / mig dang / mgo yongs su gtong bar byed do; ; mer mchong bar byed do/ / byang chub sems dpa' ming dang / che ge mo zhig gis ni/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i bstan pa bzung ste chos smra ba byed do/ / chos kyi sbyin pa gtong ngo/ / chos kyi mchod sbyin byed do/ / chos kyi rgyal mtshan sgreng ngo/ / chos kyi rnga rdung ngo/ / chos kyi dung 'bud do/ / chos kyi char 'bebs so/ / de bzhin gshegs pa'i bstan pa 'dzin to/ / de bzhin gshegs pa'i mchod rten brgyan pa byed do/ / de bzhin gshegs pa'i sku gzugs brgyan pa byed do/ / sems can la bde ba'i yo byad kyis sdud do/ / dam pa'i chos kyi mdzod srung ngo/ / zhes bya ba'i sgra thos so/ /

From some, he heard that in a world realm of such and such a name, a bodhisattva with such and such a name practices the perfection of generosity, making a hundred gifts in a certain way of that which it is hard to give away; that a bodhisattva with such and such a name maintains correct conduct, meditates on patience, engages in diligence, rests in dhyāna, or practices the analysis of wisdom; that a bodhisattva with such and such a name gives away his kingdom in order to search for the Dharma; that he gives away his jewels, gives away his children, gives away his wives, gives away his hands and feet, gives away his head, and jumps into fire; that a bodhisattva with such and such a name holds the teaching of a tathāgata, recites the Dharma, makes a gift of the Dharma, makes an offering of the Dharma, raises the banner of the Dharma, beats the drum of the Dharma, blows the conch of the Dharma, sends down a rain of the Dharma, holds the teaching of a tathāgata, adorns the caitya of the Tathāgata, adorns the image of the Tathāgata, gathers the articles that will bring happiness to beings, and guards the treasure of the Dharma.

He heard another voice saying that in such-and-such a world the enlightening being so-and-so makes so many hundreds of difficult sacrifices in the practice of transcendent giving; the enlightening being so-and-so keeps the precepts, cultivates tolerance, acquires vigor, attains meditations, engages in the investigation of wisdom; the enlightening being so-and-so, in search of truth, relinquishes kingship, wealth, family, hands and feet, eyes and head, and practices self-mortification by fire; the enlightening being so-and-so, advanced in the teaching of those who arrive at Thusness, works as a spiritual preacher, giving the gift of religion, performs the service of religion, raises the banner of religion, beats the drum and blows the horn of religion, showers the rain of religion, preserves the teaching of the enlightened, adorns monuments to the enlightened, has images of buddhas made, comforts beings, and guards the treasury of truth.

la la las ni/ 'jig rten gyi khams che ge mo zhig ces bya ba na de bzhin gshegs pa mtshan che ge mo zhig dbang bskur ba ming dang che ge mo zhig gis 'khor 'di lta bu zhig na sangs rgyas kyi zhing 'di lta bu zhig dang / bskal pa 'di lta bu zhig la sku tshe'i tshad 'di tsam zhig dang / chos bstan pa 'di lta bu dang / sems can 'dul ba 'di 'dra ba dang / 'di lta bu'i smon lam gyis mngon par 'tshang rgya bas da ltar bzhugs shing 'tsho skyong ngo/ / zhes bya ba dang /

From some, he heard that in a world realm of such and such a name, there resided, lived, and remained a tathāgata with such and such a name, teaching the Dharma through a consecration with a certain name, to a certain assembly, in a certain buddha realm, in a certain kalpa, with a certain lifespan, with certain Dharma teachings, guiding beings in a certain way, and having attained buddhahood through certain prayers.

He heard another voice say that the buddha so-and-so now is in such-and-such a world, currently existing and expounding the Teaching, with such-and-such an initiation, in such-and-such an assembly in such-and-such a land in such-and-such an age, with such-and-such a life span, with such-and-such a doctrine guiding people in such-and-such a way, realizing such-and-such vows.

de bzhin du dril dang / dril bu dang / g.yer kha'i dra ba dang / rol mo la sogs pa'i dmigs pa thams cad las chos kyi sgo rnam pa tha dad pa tshad med pa'i sgra thos par gyur te/ sgra de dag thams cad thos pas/ tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang dga' ba'i shugs rgya chen pos mngon par brlan pa'i sems kyis chos kyi sgo de dag thos nas la lar ni/ gzungs kyi sgo mang po thob par gyur to/ / la lar ni/ spobs pa'i sgo mang po thob par gyur to/ / la lar ni/ bzod pa'i sgo mang po thob par gyur to/ / la lar ni/ spyod pa'i sgo mang po thob par gyur to/ / la lar ni/ smon lam gyi sgo mang po thob par gyur to/ / la lar ni/ pha rol tu phyin pa'i sgo mang po thob par gyur to/ / la lar ni/ mngon par shes pa'i sgo mang po thob par gyur to/ / la lar ni/ rig pa dang ye shes snang ba'i sgo mang po thob par gyur to/ / la lar ni/ rnam par thar pa'i sgo mang po thob par gyur to/ / la lar ni/ ting nge 'dzin gyi sgor 'jug pa mang po thob par gyur to/ /

In that way, he heard from all the perceived networks of bells and jingle bells, music, and so on the words of countless different kinds of Dharma doors. On hearing all those words, the mind of Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, became saturated with the vast power of joy and attained, through hearing, those Dharma doors. On hearing some, he attained many doors of eloquence. On hearing some, he attained many doors of the power of patience. On hearing some, he attained many doors of conduct. On hearing some, he attained many doors of prayer. On hearing some, he attained many doors of the perfections. On hearing some, he attained many doors of the higher cognitions. On hearing some, he attained many doors of gnosis and knowledge. On hearing some, he attained many doors of liberations. On hearing some, he attained many doors of samādhis.

In this manner, from each object Sudhana heard articulations of an infinite variety of aspects of the Teaching, and by listening to all those voices he heard those facets of the Teaching with a mind flooded with joy. From some he got facets of mental command; from others, facets of commitment, tolerance, conduct, transcendence, higher perceptions, mystic knowledge, liberation, and concentration.
shin tu rgyas pa chen po'i mdo/ sangs rgyas phal po che zhes bya ba las/ sdong pos brgyan pa'i le'u ste/ ` /bam po brgya bcu bzhi pa/

me long gi dkyil 'khor de dag las kyang gzugs brnyan gyi rgyan rnam par dmigs pa tshad med pa mthong bar gyur te/ la lar ni/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor gyi gzugs brnyan rnam par dmigs pa mthong ngo/ /
He saw in the mirrors countless reflections of images. In some he saw the perception of the reflections of the assemblies of followers of tathāgatas;
He also saw measureless arrays of reflections in the mirrors, reflections of assemblies of buddhas,
la lar ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor gyi gzugs brnyan rnam par dmigs pa dang /
in some he saw the perception of the reflections of the assemblies of followers of bodhisattvas;
circles of enlightening beings,
la lar ni/ nyan thos kyi 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor gyi gzugs brnyan rnam par dmigs pa dang / la lar ni/ rang sangs rgyas kyi 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor gyi gzugs brnyan rnam par dmigs pa dang /
in some, the perception of the reflections of the assemblies of followers of śrāvakas; in some, the perception of the reflections of the assemblies of followers of pratyekabuddhas;
congregations of disciples, groups of self-illuminates,
la lar ni/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor gyi gzugs brnyan rnam par dmigs pa dang /
in some, the perception of the reflections of the assemblies of followers of tathāgatas;

la lar ni; kun nas nyon mongs pa'i zhing gi gzugs brnyan rnam par dmigs pa dang / la lar ni/ rnam par dag pa'i zhing gi gzugs brnyan rnam par dmigs pa dang / la lar ni/ kun nas nyon mongs shing rnam par dag pa'i zhing gi gzugs brnyan rnam par dmigs pa dang /
defiled lands, pure lands, defiled and pure lands,
la lar ni/ rnam par dag cing kun nas nyon mongs pa'i zhing gi gzugs brnyan rnam par dmigs pa dang /
in some, the perception of the reflections of purified defiled realms;
la lar ni/ sangs rgyas dang bcas pa'i 'jig rten gyi khams kyi gzugs brnyan rnam par dmigs pa dang / la lar ni/ sangs rgyas mi bzhugs pa'i 'jig rten gyi khams kyi gzugs brnyan rnam par dmigs pa dang /
in some, the perception of the reflections of world realms with buddhas; in some, the perception of the reflections of world realms without the presence of a buddha;
reflections of all buddhas in one world, worlds with buddhas,

la lar ni/ chung ba'i 'jig rten gyi khams kyi gzugs brnyan rnam par dmigs pa dang / la lar ni/ che ba'i 'jig rten gyi khams kyi gzugs brnyan rnam par dmigs pa dang / la lar ni/ phra ba'i 'jig rten gyi khams kyi gzugs brnyan rnam par dmigs pa dang / la lar ni/ rgya che ba'i 'jig rten gyi khams kyi gzugs brnyan rnam par dmigs pa dang /
small worlds, large worlds, subtle worlds, gross worlds,
la lar ni/ mig 'phrul gyis 'jug pa'i 'jig rten gyi khams kyi gzugs brnyan gyi rnam par dmigs pa dang /
in some, the perception of the reflections of world realms that were within magical illusion;
worlds in the cosmic net of Indra,
la lar ni/ snrel zhi'i 'jig rten gyi khams kyi gzugs brnyan rnam par dmigs pa dang /
in some, the perception of the reflections of world realms that were sideways;
la lar ni/ spyi'u tshugs kyi 'jig rten gyi khams kyi gzugs brnyan rnam par dmigs pa dang / la lar ni; sa'i gzhi mnyam par 'dug pa'i 'jig rten gyi khams kyi gzugs brnyan rnam par dmigs pa dang /
in some, the perception of the reflections of world realms that were upside-down; in some, the perception of the reflections of world realms that were level;
inverted worlds, level worlds,

la lar ni/ sems can dmyal ba dang / byol song dang / yi kyi gnas kyi 'jig rten gyi khams kyi gzugs brnyan rnam par dmigs pa dang / la lar ni/ lha dang mis gang ba'i 'jig rten gyi khams kyi gzugs brnyan rnam par dmigs pa mthong bar gyur to/ /

in some, the perception of the reflections of world realms that were the abodes of the hell beings, animals, and pretas; and in some, the perception of the reflections of world realms filled with devas and humans.
worlds of hells, animals, and ghosts, worlds full of celestials and humans.

'chags de dag dang / gnas de dag dang / stan de dag la byang chub sems dpa' grangs med pa dgos pa sna tshogs la brtson pa dag kyang mthong bar gyur te/ la lar ni/ 'chag pa dang / la lar ni/ bsam gtan byed pa dang / la lar ni/ lta ba dang / la lar ni/ sems can rnams la snying rje chen pos rgyas par 'gengs pa dang / la lar ni/ gtsug lag gi tshul sna tshogs 'jig rten gyi don du 'gyur ba sgrub pa dang / la lar ni/ lung nod pa dang / la lar ni/ kha ton byed pa dang / la lar ni/ yi ge 'bri ba dang / la lar ni/ dri ba yongs su 'dri ba dang / la lar ni/ phung po gsum pa'i bshags pa dang / yongs su bsngo ba la brtson pa dang / la lar ni/ smon lam mngon par sgrub par byed par mthong ngo/ /

He also saw countless bodhisattvas on the walkways and seated[2132] on the thrones dedicated to a variety of necessities: some were walking, some were in meditation, some were looking, some were filled great compassion for beings, some were composing treatises on various subjects in order to benefit the world, some were receiving scriptural transmission, some were chanting it, some were writing it,[2133] some were asking questions, some were dedicated to The Confession of the Three Heaps and to dedication prayers, and some were accomplishing prayers.

He also saw countless enlightening beings on the promenades or sitting on their seats, engaged in various activities. Some were walking around, some were doing spiritual exercises, some were practicing observation, some were projecting universal compassion, some were working on various sciences having to do with the welfare of the world, some were instructing, some were reciting, some were writing, some were asking questions, some were engaged in ripening conduct, concentration, and knowledge, some were undertaking vows.

ka ba de dag las kyang rin po che'i rgyal po thams cad kyi 'od kyi dra ba mang po 'byung ba mthong ste/ la la las ni/ kha dog sngon po dang / la la las ni/ kha dog ser po dang / la la las ni/ kha dog dmar po dang / la la las ni/ kha dog dkar po dang / la la las ni/ shel gyi kha dog dang / la la las ni/ gser gyi kha dog dang / la la las ni/ in+d+ra nI la'i kha dog dang / la la las ni/ 'ja'i kha dog dang / la la las ni/ 'dzam bu chu klung gi gser gyi kha dog dang / la la las ni/ 'od thams cad du sna tshogs pa'i kha dog lus dang sems kyi bde ba skyed pa/ blta na mchog tu mdzes pa mthong bar gyur to/ /

He saw many nets of light of all the kings of jewels coming from the pillars: from some came blue lights; from some, yellow; from some, red; from some, white; from some, the color of crystal; from some, the color of gold; from some, the color of sapphire; from some, the colors of the rainbow; from some, the color of Jambu River gold; and from some, lights in every color; which brought happiness to the body and mind and were supremely beautiful.

He saw webs of jewel lights coming from the pillars, some sapphire, some topaz, some ruby, some white, some crystal, some golden, some emerald, some diamond, some rainbow, some the colors of all lights, delightful to the body and mind, supremely pleasant to the eye.

'dzam bu chu klung gi gser gyi chu shing gi ka ba de dag dang / rin po che thams cad kyi gzugs de dag kyang lag nas me tog gi sprin mngon par sbyong bar mthong ste/ lag nas phreng ba'i lda ldi dang / lag nas gos dang / lag nas gdugs dang / rgyal mtshan dang / ba dan dang / lag nas spos dang / gdug spos dang / byug pa dang / lag nas nor bu rin po che'i dra ba dang / lag nas rin po che sna tshogs dang / gser gyi lcags pod sna tshogs dang / lag nas mu tig sna tshogs kyi se mo do dang / lag nas rin po che sna tshogs kyi se mo do mngon par sbyong ba dang / lag nas rgyan thams cad thogs par mthong ngo/ /

He saw that the pillars of banana trees made of Jambu River gold and the hands of the statues made of all precious materials were hung[2134] with clouds of flowers, and he saw that the hands were hung with wreaths of garlands; the hands were draped with cloths; the hands held parasols, banners, and flags; the hands held perfumes, incense, and ointments; the hands were hung with nets of strings of precious jewels;[2135] the hands were hung with various jewels on various cords of gold; the hands were hung with long necklaces of various pearls; the hands were hung with long necklaces of various jewels; the hands were holding all kinds of adornments.

He also saw the golden statues of women and all the jewel statues with their hands extended downward, holding myriads of flowers, garlands, parasols, banners and pennants, incense and perfume, various jewels on gold strings, various pearl necklaces, garlands of various jewels, holding all kinds of ornaments in their hands.
la lar ni/ gtsug gi rin po che dang / cod pan gyis 'dud cing mig mi 'gebs par lta ba dang / thal mo sbyor zhing phyag 'tshal bar mthong ngo/ /
He saw that some were bowing down their topknot jewels and crowns, staring with unblinking eyes, and paying homage with their palms placed together.
He saw some figures bowing, crowned with jewels, with steady gaze, palms joined, in gestures of respect.
mu tig gi phreng ba de dag las kyang spos sna tshogs kyis dri zhim por byas pa'i chu yan lag brgyad dang ldan pa'i char gyi rgyun phra mo 'bab par mthong ngo/ /
He saw that from the strings of pearls fell a gentle rain of water with the eight good qualities that had the lovely aroma of various scents.
He also saw delicate clouds of pure water imbued with all fragrances coming from the pearl necklaces,
rin po che bai DUr+ya'i phreng ba'i dra ba de dag las kyang mar [?] me'i phreng ba rab tu 'bar ba mang po mthong bar gyur to/ /
He saw many shining rows of lamps come from the nets of strings of beryl jewels.
and saw long streams flowing from the webs of strings of lapis lazuli.

rin po che'i gdugs de dag kyang rgyan dang / lhab lhub thams cad kyis mdzes par brgyan te/ rin po che'i dril dang / dril bu g.yer kha'i dra ba dang / dar gyi lda ldi dang / chun po dang / rin po che'i shar bu dang / nor bu rin po che sna tshogs kyi sgo ngas yongs su brgyan pa'i snying po dang ldan par mthong ngo/ /

He saw the precious parasols adorned by every kind of adornment and decoration. He saw their interiors adorned by precious bells, nets of jingle bells, silk streamers and tassels, precious tablets,[2136] and eggs[2137] made of various kinds of precious jewels.

He also saw all the jewel parasols embellished with all kinds of ornaments, and he saw the inner chamber adorned with jewel bells, sets of chimes, silk streamers, strings of bells, slivers of jewels, and heaps of various gems.

rdzing de dag nas kyang rin po che'i me tog pad+mo dang / ut+pa la dang / ku mu da dang / puN+Da ri ka grangs med pa mngon par thon par mthong ste/ la la ni/ mtho gang 'khor ba tsam/ la la ni/ 'dom gang 'khor ba tsam/ la la ni/ shing rta'i 'khor lo tsam ste; de dag la yang gzugs sna tshogs kyi rgyan mang po 'khod par mthong ste/ 'di ltar bud med kyi gzugs dang / skyes pa'i gzugs dang / khye'u'i gzugs dang / bu mo'i gzugs dang / brgya byin gyi gzugs dang / tshangs pa'i gzugs dang / 'jig rten gyi mgon po'i gzugs dang / lha dang / klu dang / gnod sbyin dang / dri ba dang / lha ma yin dang / nam mkha' lding dang / mi 'am ci dang / lto 'phye chen po'i gzugs dang / nyan thos dang / rang sangs rgyas dang / byang chub sems dpa'i gzugs dang / 'gro ba thams cad kyi gzugs kyi dbyibs su 'dug pa'i lus kha dog sna tshogs rnam pa du ma dang ldan pa mang po thal mo sbyar te lus 'dud cing phyag 'tshal bar 'khod pa mthong ngo/ /

He saw the ponds in which arose countless precious red lotuses, blue lotuses, night lotuses, and white lotuses. He saw that some were a hand span in size, some were a fathom in circumference, some were the size of carriage wheels, on which were arrayed the adornments of various statues. He saw that there were statues of women, statues of men, statues of boys, statues of girls, statues of Śakra, statues of Brahmā, statues of the world lords, and statues of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and bodhisattvas, and also statues in the form of all beings with their many various colors and bodies, all arranged paying homage, with their palms together and bowing their bodies.

He saw countless superb red, blue, and white lotuses growing in the lotus ponds, some a foot across, some a fathom across, some as big as a wagon wheel; and in them he saw arrays of various figures—figures of women, men, boys, girls, Indra, Brahma, the world guardians, gods, dragons, goblins, cherubs, titans, birds, centaurs, serpents, sages, saints, and enlightening beings—bodies in the forms of all living beings, various in appearance, joining their palms and bowing in gestures of respect.
de bzhin gshegs pa'i sku gzugs mi chen po'i mtshan sum cu rtsa gnyis kyis brgyan pa skyil mo krung du bcas te bzhugs pa dag kyang mthong ngo/ /
He also saw statues of tathāgatas adorned with the thirty-two signs of a great being and sitting cross-legged.
He also saw figures of buddhas adorned with the thirty-two marks of great people, sitting in the lotus posture.

sa chen po'i gzhi bai DUr+ya las grub pa mig mang ris su 'dug pa'i mig mang ris re re nas kyang gzugs brnyan rnam par dmigs pa bsam gyis mi khyab pa mang po mthong bar gyur te/ khang pa brtsegs pa la la las ni/ zhing gi gzugs brnyan rnam par dmigs pa/ la la las ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i gzugs brnyan rnam par dmigs pa/ la la las ni/ sangs rgyas kyi gzugs brnyan rnam par dmigs par mthong bar gyur te/

He saw that the floor was a great ground made of beryl with a checkerboard pattern, and within each of the squares there were countless perceptions of reflections. [2138] In some,[2139] he saw the perception of reflections of realms; in some, the perception of reflections of bodhisattvas; and in some, the perception of reflections of buddhas.
Also, on the checkerboard lapis-lazuli surface of the ground, he saw inconceivable reflections in each square; here he saw the reflection of a land, there the reflection of a buddha.
khang pa brtsegs pa de dag gi rgyan dang / lhab lhub ji snyed pa de dag thams cad kyang mig mang ris re re la gzugs brnyan du snang bar mthong ngo/ /
He saw that reflections of the entire array of the adornments in the kūṭāgāras appeared in each of the squares.
All the arrays of adornments in those towers he saw reflected in each of the squares.

rin po che'i shing rin po che'i me tog dang 'bras bu'i mdzod sna tshogs dang ldan pa de dag thams cad las kyang lus phyed tsam byung ba'i gzugs dbyibs sna tshogs dang / kha dog sna tshogs su 'dug pa mang po thon par mthong ste/ la la las ni/ sangs rgyas kyi sku phyed tsam byung ba dang / la la las ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i lus phyed tsam byung ba dang / la la las ni/ lha dang / klu dang / gnod sbyin dang / dri za dang / lha ma yin dang / nam mkha' lding dang / mi 'am ci dang / lto 'phye chen po'i lus phyed tsam byung ba dang / la la las ni/ brgya byin dang / tshangs pa dang / 'jig rten gyi mgon po'i lus phyed tsam byung ba dang / la la las ni/ 'khor los bsgyur ba dang / mi'i dbang po'i lus phyed tsam byung ba dang / la la las ni/ rgyal bu gzhon nu dang / tshong dpon dang / khyim bdag dang / blon po dang / skyes pa dang / bud med dang / khye'u dang / bu mo dang / dge slong dang / dge slong ma dang / dge bsnyen dang / dge bsnyen ma'i lus phyed tsam byung ba mthong ste/

He saw that from out of the entire treasury of the various flowers and fruits of the precious trees emerged the upper halves of many bodies with various shapes and various colors. He saw that from some emerged the upper halves of the bodies of buddhas; from some emerged the upper halves of the bodies of bodhisattvas; from some emerged the upper halves of the bodies of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas; from some emerged the upper halves of the bodies of Śakra, Brahmā, and world lords; from some emerged the upper halves of the bodies of cakravartins and lords of humans; from some emerged the upper halves of the bodies of young princes, head merchants, householders, ministers, men, women, boys, girls, bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās.

Also, in all the flowers, fruits, and buds of the jewel trees he saw golden busts of all kinds of beings—buddhas, enlightening beings, gods, dragons, goblins, cherubs, titans, birds, serpents, Indras, Brahmas, the world guardians, human emperors, princes, grandees, ministers, women, men, boys, girls, monks, nuns, male and female devotees,

la la'i lag nas ni/ me tog gi phreng ba sbyong ba dang / la la'i lag nas ni/ rin po che'i phreng ba mngon par sbyong ba dang / la la'i lag nas ni/ rgyan thams cad mngon par thogs pa dang / la la ni/ lus 'dud cing thal mo sbyar te mig mi 'gebs par lta zhing phyag 'tshal ba dang / la la ni/ mngon par bstod pa dang / la la ni/ mnyam par bzhag pa dang / la la ni/ gser gyi kha dog tu 'dug pa dang / la la ni/ dngul gyi kha dog tu 'dug pa dang / la la ni/ byi ru'i kha dog tu 'dug pa dang / la la ni/ rin po che bai DUr+ya sngon po'i kha dog tu 'dug pa dang / la la ni/ rin po che in+d+ra nI la'i kha dog tu 'dug pa dang / la la ni/ nor bu rin po che rnam par snang ba'i kha dog tu 'dug pa dang / la la ni/ rin po che thams cad kyi kha dog tu 'dug pa dang / la la ni/ me tog tsam pa ka'i kha dog tu 'dug pa dang / la la ni/ 'od kyi lus dang / la la ni/ mtshan gyis rnam par bris pa'i lus su mthong bar gyur to/ /

He saw that some of them had flower garlands hanging[2140] from their hands; some of them had strings of jewels hanging from their hands; some of them had all adornments held in their hands; some were bowing, with palms together, and gazing with unblinking eyes; some were praising; some were resting in meditation; some were the color of gold; some were the color of silver; some were the color of coral; some were the color of blue beryl; some were the color of sapphires; some were the color of the radiance of vairocana jewels; some were the color of magnolia flowers; some had bodies of light; and some were beautified by the signs of a great being.

some with flower garlands hanging from their hands, some with strings of jewels hanging from their hands, some holding all kinds of ornaments, some bowing with their palms joined and gaze steady, paying respect, some singing hymns of praise, some in trance, some with a golden luster, some with a silver luster, some with a frosty luster, some with a sapphire luster, some with a shining jewel luster, some shining with the colors of all jewels, some with a saffron luster, some shining like bodies of light, some with bodies adorned with the marks of greatness.
zla gam de dag las kyang nyi zla dang / gza' skar gyi gzugs brnyan grangs med pa mang po thon te phyogs bcur snang bar byed pa mthong bar gyur to/ /
He saw that from the half moons emerged countless reflections of suns, moons, planets, and stars.
From the crescents adorning the towers he saw reflections of countless moons, suns, stars, and planets emerge and illumine the ten directions.
khang pa dang / gzhal med khang dang / khang pa brtsegs pa'i rtsig ngos de dag thams cad kyang rin po che thams cad kyis mig mang ris sna tshogs su bris par mthong ste/
He saw that on all the walls of the buildings, divine palaces, and kūṭāgāras there were checkerboard patterns made of all jewels.
He also saw the walls of the palatial towers resplendent with checkerboards of all jewels,

rin po che'i mig mang ris de dag thams cad las kyang byang chub sems dpa' byams pas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa rim pas ji ltar spyad pa'i byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa thams cad rim par mthong bar gyur to/ /
He saw within[2141] those jewel checkerboard patterns all the bodhisattva Maitreya’s stages of bodhisattva conduct in his past practice of bodhisattva conduct;
and in all of the jewel square he saw Maitreya carrying out all the practices of enlightening beings, as he had done while performing enlightening practice in the past:
mig mang ris la la las ni/ byang chub sems dpa' byams pas mgo byin pa mthong ngo/ /
in some of the squares he saw the bodhisattva Maitreya giving away his head;
in one square he saw Maitreya giving away his head;
la la las ni/ mig byin pa dang / la la las ni/ lag pa byin pa dang /
in some, giving away his eyes; in some, giving away his hands;
la la las ni/ gtsug gi rin po che byin pa dang / la la las ni/ thor pag dang bcas pa'i gtsug gi rin po che byin pa dang /
la la las ni/ so byin pa dang / la la las ni/ lce byin pa dang / la la las ni/ rna ba byin pa dang / la la las ni/ sna byin pa dang /
la la las ni/ snying byin pa dang / la la las ni/ sha dang rkang byin pa dang / la la las ni/ khrag byin pa dang / la la las ni/ pags pa dang phri byin pa dang /

la la las ni/ sen mo sha dang bcas par byin pa dang / la la las ni/ dra bar 'brel pa dang bcas pa'i sor mo byin pa dang / la la las ni/ bu dang / bu mo dang / chung ma byin pa dang / la la las ni/ rin po che'i phung po byin pa dang /
la la las ni/ grong dang / grong khyer dang / ljongs dang / yul dang / khams dang / rgyal po'i gnas byin pa dang / la la las ni/ 'dzam bu'i gling byin pa dang /
in some, giving away villages, towns, districts, regions, realms, and royal capitals; in some, giving away Jambudvīpa;
in another, giving away village, town, city, and country; in another, giving away the continent;
la la las ni/ gling bzhi byin pa dang /
in another, giving away four continents;
la la las ni/ rgyal srid kyi dbang phyug byin pa dang / la la las ni/ rgyal po'i khri byin pa dang /
in some, giving away the power of sovereignty; in some, giving away the royal throne;
in another, giving away all powers of rulership; in another, giving away the throne;

la la las ni/ bran pho mo byin pa dang / la la las ni; btsun mo'i 'khor byin pa dang / la la las ni/ bza' shing gi ra ba dang / dka' thub kyi nags tshal byin pa dang / la la las ni/ gdugs dang / rgyal mtshan dang / ba dan byin pa dang /

la la las ni/ me tog dang / phreng ba dang / byug pa byin pa dang / la la las ni/ nad kyi rtsi byin pa dang / la la las ni/ kha zas dang / skom gyi rnam pa mang po byin pa dang / la la las ni/ yo byad thams cad byin pa dang /

la la las ni/ gnas thams cad byin pa dang / la la las ni/ gzhal ba'i snod rin po ches bkang ba byin pa dang / la la las ni/ rin po che'i shing rta byin pa dang / la la las ni/ btson ra na 'khod pa thar par byed pa dang /
la la las ni/ gsad par chad pa las thar par byed pa dang / la la las ni/ byis pa gso ba byed pa dang /
in some, freeing those condemned to death; in some, curing children;
in another, freeing the condemned; in another, giving medical care to the young;
la la las ni; lam stor ba la lam ston pa dang / la la las ni/ mnyan par gyur te chu klung gi rgyud la gru 'dor ba dang /
and in some, showing the way to those who were lost; in some, he was a ferryman who sailed his boat across the river;
in another, showing the right path to those on the path of destruction; in another, navigating the rivers as a boatman;

la la las ni/ rta'i rgyal po stobs kyis sgrol bar gyur te/ rgya mtsho chen po'i srin po'i gling du phyin par gyur pa'i sems can yongs su skyob pa dang / la la las ni/ drang srong chen por gyur te bstan pa mngon par sgrub pa dang / la la las ni/ 'khor los bsgyur bar gyur te/ sems can dge ba bcu'i las kyi lam la 'god pa dang / la la las ni/ sman par gyur te na ba'i gsos byed pa dang /

la la las ni/ pha ma la phu dud byed pa dang / la la las ni/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen la rim gro byed pa dang / la la las ni/ nyan thos kyi kha dog dang / gzugs kyis sems can 'dul ba la brtson pa dang / la la las ni/ rang sangs rgyas kyi kha dog dang / gzugs kyis sems can 'dul ba la brtson pa dang /
la la las ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i kha dog dang / gzugs kyis sems can 'dul ba la brtson pa dang / la la las ni/ sangs rgyas kyi sku mdog dang; sku gzugs kyis sems can 'dul ba la brtson pa dang /
in some, he was dedicated to guiding beings in the appearance and form of a bodhisattva; in some, he was dedicated to guiding beings in the appearance and form of a buddha;
in another in the form of an enlightening being, in another in the form of a buddha, engaged in teaching people;
la la las ni/ skyes pa'i rabs kyi khyad par thams cad kyis skye ba yongs su bstan te sems can yongs su smin par byed pa dang /
in some, he ripened beings through manifesting being reborn in any of the particular births of beings;
in another, manifesting existence as paragons of types of beings, developing beings to maturity;

la la las ni/ chos smra ba'i gzugs kyis de bzhin gshegs pa'i bstan pa la zhugs te lung 'bog pa dang / kha ton bya ba dang / tshul bzhin du dpyad par bya ba la brtson pa dang / de bzhin gshegs pa'i mchod rten la rgyan gyis brgyan par byed pa dang / de bzhin gshegs pa'i sku gzugs byed du 'jug pa dang / sangs rgyas mchod pa la sems can yongs su bskul ba dang / spos dang byug pa gsol zhing 'bru mar dri zhim pos byug pa dang / dril bu dang me tog gi phreng ba gsol pa la sogs pa dang / sangs rgyas kyi mchod pa rnam pa thams cad la brtson pa dang / dge ba bcu'i las kyi lam la sems can rab tu 'god pa dang / bslab pa'i gnas lnga dang / gso sbyong gi yan lag brgyad dang / sangs rgyas dang / chos dang / dge 'dun la skyabs btsal ba dang / rab tu 'byung ba dang / chos mnyan pa dang / lung mnod pa dang / kha ton bya ba dang / tshul bzhin yid la bya ba la sems can 'god par byed pa dang / chos kyi gtam bya ba'i phyir seng+ge'i stan la 'dug cing sangs rgyas kyi byang chub rnam par 'grel ba dang /

in some, in the form of a dharmabhāṇaka, he entered the teachings of a tathāgata, received the transmission of the teachings, recited the teachings, correctly analyzed them, adorned the caitya of the Tathāgata, had statues of the Tathāgata made, inspired beings to make offerings to the Tathāgata, anointed them with perfumes and ointments, dressed them in bells and garlands, and so on, and he was dedicated to making offerings to the Buddha and established beings on the path of the ten good actions, established beings in the five precepts, the eight poṣadha vows, taking refuge in the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha, entering mendicancy, hearing the Dharma, receiving the transmission of the Dharma, reciting the Dharma, and contemplating it correctly; and in order to talk about the Dharma he sat upon a lion throne and explained the enlightenment of the buddhas.

in another, as a religious preacher expounding experience of the teachings of buddhas, reciting the teachings, reflecting deeply on them, decorating monuments of buddhas, having statues of buddhas made, enjoining people to honor the buddhas, giving out perfumes, making all kinds of offerings to buddhas, leading people into paths of actions based on virtuous ways, directing people to the precepts, to refuge in the Buddha, the Teaching, and the Community, to listening to the Teaching, to discussion, recital, and profound contemplation of the Teaching, sitting on the lion seat to talk of the Teaching, revealing the enlightenment of buddhas.

de ltar byang chub sems dpa' byams pas bskal pa bye ba khrag khrig brgya stong grangs med par pha rol tu phyin pa drug la spyad pa de dag thams cad tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis mig mang ris de dag las rnam pa gzhan dang gzhan mthong bar gyur to/ /

In that way, the bodhisattva Maitreya practiced the six perfections for countless hundreds of thousands of quintillions of kalpas. Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, saw all of that in various ways within each square of the checkerboard patterns.
Thus Sudhana saw Maitreya’s practices of the six ways of transcendence over countless eons, projected from each of the squares of the checkerboard walls.

des khang pa brtsegs pa la la las ni/ byang chub sems dpa' byams pas dge ba'i bshes gnyen ji snyed cig bsnyen bkur ba de dag thams cad kyi rnam par 'phrul pa'i rgyan thams cad kyang mthong bar gyur te/
He saw in some kūṭāgāras the bodhisattva Maitreya serving as many kalyāṇamitras as there are, and all the array of miraculous manifestations that came from that.
In one tower he saw magical arrays of all the spiritual benefactors whom Maitreya attended,

dge ba'i bshes gnyen de dag thams cad kyi drung du bdag nyid phyin cing / tshur shog nor bzang legs par 'ongs sam/ mi ngal lam/ 'di re byang chub sems dpa'i rgyan dang / yul rnam par sprul pa bsam gyis mi khyab pa 'di dag la ltos shig /ces bsgo zhing gtam byed par shes par gyur te/

Sudhana went before all those kalyāṇamitras, and he perceived them speaking to him and giving an instruction: “Come here, Sudhana! Welcome! Are you well? Look at this inconceivable range and display of miraculous manifestations of the bodhisattva!”[2148]
and he perceived himself in the presence of all those spiritual benefactors, being welcomed and told not to be weary, to behold this wonder of the enlightening being.

de ltar tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis khang pa brtsegs pa de dag re re dang / dmigs pa de dag re re las kyang bsam gyis mi khyab pa'i rgyan dang / yul rnam par sprul pa 'di dag dang / gzhan dag kyang grangs med pa mang po mthong bar gyur te/ dran pa'i mthu nyams pa med pa dang / mig yongs su dag pa phyogs kun rnam par lta ba dang / lhag mthong la lta ba'i ye shes sgrib pa med pa dang / byang chub sems dpa'i ye shes dang / byin gyi rlabs kyi dbang rab tu thob pas byang chub sems dpa'i 'du shes kyi rnam pa la zhugs pa'i ye shes kyi sa la gnas te mtha' yas pa'i rgyan dang / yul rnam par sprul pa de dag thams cad mthong bar gyur to/ /

Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, saw in each of the kūṭāgāras, and in each object of perception, this and other ranges and displays of miraculous manifestations. Because of his unfailing power of memory, his pure vision, his view of all directions, and his unobscured wisdom of view in vipaśyanā, he was established on the level of wisdom that comes from the understanding of a bodhisattva, and therefore he saw all that infinite range and display of miraculous manifestations.

So Sudhana saw these and other inconceivable projections of magnificent scenes from each of the towers and each object in the towers. By the power of unwavering mindfulness, by all-encompassing purity of vision, by unobstructed knowledge of observational skill, by attainment of control over the basis of knowledge of enlightening beings, standing on the ground of knowledge issuing from the perceptions of enlightening beings, he saw this whole endless manifestation of marvelous scenes.

'di lta ste/ dper na/ skyes bu gnyid kyis log pa'i rmi lam du gzugs kyi dmigs pa'i khyad par sna tshogs mang po zhig mthong bar gyur te/ 'di ltar khyim dang gzhal med khang mdangs dga' ba'am/ grong dang / grong khyer dang / ljongs dang / yul mdangs dga' ba'am/ bza' shing gi ra ba dang / kun dga'i ra ba dang / dka' thub kyi nags tshal mdangs dga' ba'am/ shing dang / chu klung dang / rdzing dang / ri mdangs dga' ba'am/ gos dang / kha zas dang / btung ba'i longs spyod nyams su bde ba'am/ glu dang / sil snyan dang / rol mo'i sgra snyan pa sna tshogs kyis rtse ba nyams su dga' ba zhig mthong ngam/ pha ma dang / gnyen bshes dang / bdag nyid 'grogs par shes par gyur pa'am/ rgya mtsho chen po dang / ri'i rgyal po ri rab dang / lha'i gnas thams cad dam/ 'dzam bu'i gling dag na bdag dpag tshad brgya phrag du mar gnas par shes par gyur la/ khyim mam/ gnas de'ang shin tu yangs shing yon tan dang / rgyan thams cad kyis yongs su brgyan par mthong ste/ nyin par zhig yin par shes kyang nam de yang ring ba dang / thung bar bye brag mi 'byed la/ rmi lam yin pa tsam du'ang mi shes so/ / bdag nyid kyang bde ba'i yo byad thams cad dang ldan zhing / lus kyi 'du byed zo bdog bde la snyom pa dang / gnyid med de mi dga' ba thams cad yongs su bsal bas dga' ba dang / bde ba rgya chen po nyams su myong ste/ yun kyang ring mo zhig lon pa snyam nas nyin gcig gam/ nyin bdun nam/ zla ba phyed dam/ zla ba gcig gam/ lo gcig gam/ lo brg+ya'am/ de bas kyang ring ba zhig lon pa tsam du shes par gyur nas sad na/ de thams cad kyang rjes su dran no/ /

It was like when a person goes to sleep and in a dream sees many various particular perceived forms, such as delightful houses and divine palaces; delightful villages, towns, districts, and regions; delightful parks, gardens, and forest groves; delightful trees, rivers, pools, and mountains; delightful clothes, food, drink, and enjoyments; and the enjoyment of the pleasures of delightful songs, instrumental music, and percussive music. He perceives himself in the company of his father, mother, friends, family, and relatives. He sees the great ocean. He perceives Sumeru, the king of mountains, all divine realms, and Jambudvīpas, in which he himself is many hundreds of yojanas[2149] tall. He sees his house and environs as vast. He perceives them to be adorned with all qualities and adornments. Even though he knows it is daytime, he cannot tell if that day is long or short, or even know that this is a dream. He perceives having all things that are pleasant, and he has the appearance of his composite body being in a state of happiness, not sleeping and free of all that is unpleasant, experiencing vast joy and happiness. He thinks this lasts a long time: for a day, a week, a fortnight, a month, a year, a hundred years, or longer, and when he wakes he remembers it all.

It was like someone asleep seeing various things in a dream—nice houses and mansions, charming villages, towns, and cities, agreeable clothing, food and drink, or delightful performances of music, song, and dance; or as one might see pleasant parks, gardens, and retreats, trees, rivers, lotus ponds, and mountains, or perceive oneself together with family and friends, or as one might see the ocean, or the polar mountain, or the celestial abodes on the highest mountains, or the whole continent, or perceive oneself to be many miles tall, in which case one would see one’s house and surroundings as enormous; one sees all the elements arrayed together, as if it were daytime, and one does not know the length or brevity of the night, nor realize one is asleep. If one sees oneself in a pleasant situation, one’s body will be at rest, one will be free from torpor and drowsiness, with all attachments removed, feeling great joy and bliss; it will seem to last long—a day, a week, a fortnight, a year, a century, or even more—and when one awakes, one will remember it all.

de bzhin du tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis kyang byang chub sems dpa'i byin gyi rlabs dang / khams gsum pa thams cad rmi lam lta bur yang dag par gzhol ba'i ye shes kyis chung ba'i 'du shes 'gags pa'i sems dang ldan par gyur te/ byang chub sems dpa'i 'du shes kyi rnam pa yangs shing rgya che ba dang / sgrib pa med pa la gnas shing / byang chub sems dpa'i rgyan gyi yul khong du chud la byang chub sems dpa'i tshul la 'jug pa bsam gyis mi khyab pa'i rjes su 'brangs pa'i blo dang ldan pas/ rgyan rnam par sprul pa de dag thams cad kyang mthong bar gyur to/ / shes par gyur to/ / nyams su myong bar gyur to/ / rnam par dpyad par gyur to/ / mtshan mar byas par gyur to/ / dmigs kyis rtogs par gyur to/ / bdag nyid kyang de dag na 'dug par shes par gyur to/ /

In that way, Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, through the blessing of the bodhisattva Maitreya, and through a knowledge that was free from a limited perception, like that of someone who has entered a dream of the three realms, was dwelling in the vast, extensive, unobscured perception of a bodhisattva and possessed the comprehension that could follow the inconceivable entry into the way of the bodhisattva and comprehend the scope of the displays of a bodhisattva, and therefore he saw all of those displays of miraculous manifestations, knew them, experienced them, examined them, identified them, and beheld them. He also perceived himself to be present among them.

In the same way Sudhana, by the power of the enlightening being, by the knowledge of the collection of dreams that constitutes the world, the notion of smallness gone from his mind, abiding in the immensely vast unobstructed perception of enlightening beings, with the mental scope of enlightening beings, his intellect having entered into the inconceivable wisdom of enlightening beings, saw the whole supernal manifestation, was perfectly aware of it, understood it, contemplated it, used it as a means, beheld it, and saw himself there.

'di lta ste/ dper na/ mi nad pa sems kyi rgyud tha ma byung bar gyur te/ de ma thag tu skye ba'i sems nye bar gags nas las kyi srid pa mngon du gyur na/ las ji lta bur byas shing bsags pa'i rnam par smin pas las mi dge ba'i rkyen gyis ni/ sems can dmyal ba dang / byol song gi skye gnas dang / yi kyi yul lam/ gshin rje'i mi lag cha gnyems pa thogs pa gshe zhing khro ba dag kyang mthong bar gyur/ sems can dmyal ba pa'i dud mo dang / 'o dod kyi sgra yang thos par gyur la ba chu de dag mthong ste/ spu gri'i so gshibs pa'i ri de dag dang / lcags kyi shal ma li'i sdong po de dag dang / ral gri'i so'i nags tshal de dag kyang mthong bar gyur tam/ sems can dmyal ba de dag kyang kun nas 'bar zhing yongs su 'bar ba dang / rab tu 'bar ba dang / lcags kyi bum pa gcig tu 'bar ba dag kyang mthong bar gyur la/ gnod pa de dag thams cad kyis kyang gnod par bya zhing / tshor ba de dag kyang nyams su myong ba tsam du shes par gyur te/ sems can dmyal ba de dag kyang me'i gdung bas sdug bsngal ba zhig tu mthong ngam/ bdag gis myong bar gyur tam/

This is like when a sick person is in the final phase of his mind. In the instant that occurs, his existing karma manifests: there is the ripening of whatever kind of karma he has accumulated, so that on the basis of bad karma he sees the hells, birth as an animal, the realm of the pretas, or the servants of Yama holding menacing weapons and furiously shouting abuse; he hears the sounds of the wailing and cries of the beings in the hells; he sees the rivers of acid; he sees the mountains of rows of razor-blade edges, the iron cotton trees, and the forests of sword blades; and he sees the beings in hell on fire, burning, being incinerated, and all burning inside one iron pot. He perceives those harms being inflicted and those sensations being experienced, and he sees and feels the suffering of the hell beings being burned by fire.

It was like the case of a dying man hovering in his final mental state, on the brink of the mental state immediately preceding rebirth, faced with the state of being which is caused by his actions, as a result of the accumulation of whatever actions he has done; he will see hell if he has done evil, or the state of animals, ghosts, or the underworld, and may see angry, abusive henchmen of the underworld carrying weapons, and hear the cries of lament and anger of the beings in hell. He will also see the great hells burning, blazing masses of flames, and will see the copper cauldrons and the tortures being carried out, and will perceive those undergoing them. He will also see and feel the pains of the burning of the fires of hell.

las dge ba'i tshogs kyis lha'i khang pa dang / gnas shig mthong bar gyur tam/ lha'i 'khor dang / lha mo'i tshogs dang / rgyan rnam par phye ba thams cad kyang mthong bar gyur te/ bza' shing gi ra ba dang / dka' thub kyi nags tshal dang / chu klung dang / rdzing dang / rin po che'i ri dang / yid bzhin gyi shing dang / longs spyod mang po mthong ngam nyams su myong bar gyur te/ tshe'i yun kyang de dang mnyam par shes par gyur na/

Through good karma he sees the palaces and dwellings of devas: he sees the retinue of a deva, the groups of apsarases, and all the arrayed adornments; he sees and experiences parks, forest groves, rivers, ponds, precious mountains, wish-fulfilling trees, and many enjoyments, and he perceives them to last for a lifetime.

But by accumulation of good actions one will see heaven, and will see the assemblies of gods and goddesses and all the magnificent arrays of heaven; one will see and experience the enjoyments of the parks, palaces, rivers, lotus ponds, mountains of jewels, and wish-fulfilling trees.

de ni/ 'di nas kyang 'phos pa med/ der yang skyes pa med de/ mi snang bar ma gyur bzhin du/ las kyi yul bsam gyis mi khyab pas bya ba'i rnam pa de lta bu dag shes shing mthong la nyams su myong bar rung ngo/ /

Even though he has not passed away from this world and has not been reborn elsewhere, because of the inconceivable scope of karma, those kinds of appearances are not imperceptible but are perceived and experienced.

At the end of one’s life one will feel one has passed away from this world and been reborn in the next, even though one has not yet died; thus by the wonder of the mental realms caused by actions one will see and experience these events.
de bzhin du tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis byang chub sems dpa'i las kyi yul bsam gyis mi khyab pa'i phyir rgyan rnam par sprul pa de dag thams cad kyang mthong bar gyur to/ /
In the same way, Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, because of the inconceivable scope of a bodhisattva’s karma, saw all that display of miraculous manifestations.
In the same way Sudhana, by the wonder of the states caused by the actions of an enlightening being, saw that whole supernal manifestation of the tower of Vairocana.

'di lta ste/ dper na/ skyes bu 'byung po'i gdon gyis non pa ni/ gzugs kyi rnam pa sna tshogs mang po mthong ste/ ci dris pa de dag gi lung yang ston to/ / de bzhin du tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis byang chub sems dpa'i ye shes dang / byin gyi rlabs kyi mthus rgyan de dag thams cad mthong bar gyur to/ /

By analogy, when a person is overpowered by a demon spirit, they will see many various kinds of forms, and whatever questions they ask, it will reveal an answer to them. In the same way, Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, saw all those arrays through the power of the blessing of the bodhisattva.
Just as a man possessed by a spirit sees various things, and tells of what he is asked about, in the same way Sudhana, by the power of knowledge of an enlightening being, saw all those arrays.

'di lta ste/ dper na/ klu'i khang par byin pa'i skyes bus ni/ klu'i 'du shes kyi rnam pa la zhugs pas/ nyi ma gcig gam/ nyi ma bdun nam/ zla ba phyed dam/ zla ba gcig gam/ lo gcig gam/ lo brgyar yang 'du shes kyi rnam pas shes te/ klu'i 'du shes kyi rnam pa dang bral nas mi'i 'du shes kyi rnam par na yud tsam las ma lon par mthong ngo/ / de bzhin du tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang byang chub sems dpa'i 'du shes kyi rnam pas ma btang ba'i blo dang ldan pas kyang byang chub sems dpa' byams pa'i byin gyi rlabs kyis yud tsam gcig po de yang bskal pa bye ba khrag khrig brgya stong mang por shes par gyur to/ /

By analogy, a person who goes into the dwelling of a nāga will enter into a nāga’s perception and will have the perception of a day, a week, a fortnight, a month, a year, or a hundred years passing, but when they separate from the nāga’s perception, they will see that in terms of human perception only a moment[2150] has passed. In the same way, Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, having a mind that maintained the perception of a bodhisattva and the blessing of the bodhisattva Maitreya, perceived in one moment many hundreds of thousands of quintillions of kalpas.

Just as a man who has entered the abode of water spirits, by entering into the perception of water spirits, thinks a day or a week or a fortnight or a month or a year or a century has passed, merely in his perception, and when leaving the perception of water spirits for the perception of humans sees that it was only a short time, in the same way, with the mindfulness of the perception of an enlightening being, by the power of Maitreya, in that short time Sudhana had the sense of the passage of billions of eons.

'di lta ste/ dper na/ tshangs pa chen po'i gzhal med khang 'gro ba thams cad na rgyan gyi dam pa phul zhes bya ba yod de; de'i nang du stong gsum gyi stong chen po'i 'jig rten gyi khams thams cad kyang gzugs brnyan gyi tshul du dmigs pa thams cad dang ma 'dres par gsal bar snang ngo/ / de bzhin du tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis kyang rgyan de dag thams cad dmigs pa thams cad du phan tshun ma 'dres pa dang / phan tshun ma 'dzings par gzugs rab tu byung ba mthong ngo/ /

By analogy, within Mahābrahmā’s divine palace, called Sarvajagadvaravyūhagarbha, the perceived reflections of all the world realms in the billion-world universe appear clearly and distinctly. In the same way, Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, saw the arising of all those displays, all those perceptions, unmixed with one another and unmingled with one another.

There is a celestial mansion called “chamber of the finest ornaments of all worlds,” wherein the whole universe is seen by reflection, with all objects clearly defined; in the same way Sudhana saw all those arrays, unconfused, reflected in all the objects.

'di lta ste/ dper na/ rgyal ba'i skye mched kyi snyoms par 'jug pa la rnam par spyod pa'i dge slong ni/ gcig pu gnyis su med pa'i khang bu'am/ 'chag sa'am/ 'dug pa'i gnas na 'dug gam/ bskyed gang rung ste/ 'jig rten thams cad rgyas pa'i skye mched gang la snyoms par zhugs pa'i yul bzhin du bsam gtan pa'i yul bsam gyis mi khyab par mthong zhing nyams su myong ngo/ / de bzhin du tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis kyang yul gang la zhugs pa'i tshul bzhin du/ rgyan de dag thams cad mthong zhing shes te nyams su myong bar gyur to/ /

By analogy, a monk dwelling in the samāpatti of a meditative state of totality in a singleness without duality, whether in his cell or on a walkway,[2151] seated on a seat or standing up, perceives, sees, and experiences the entire world as the inconceivable scope of his meditation, the scope of his samāpatti of whichever meditative state of totality. In the same way, Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, saw and experienced those displays according to whatever scope of perception he engaged in.

Just as a monk in the trance of absorption in one of the points of totality is single-minded and undivided whether walking, standing still, sitting, or reclining, and sees and experiences the whole world through entry into the sphere of total absorption in whatever point of totality he is focused on, by the marvel of meditation, in the same way Sudhana saw all those arrays whatever object he immersed himself in.
'di lta ste/ dper na/ dri za'i grong khyer rnams kyi rgyan dang / lhab lhub thams cad nam mkha'i dbyings la byung ba ni/ yongs su snang yang ci la yang sgrib par mi 'gyur ro/ /
It was like the display and ornamentation of a gandharva city that appears in the sky, which occurs without any obscuration.
Just as all the adornments of the cities of celestial musicians are visible in the sky, without constituting a barrier to anyone,

'di lta ste/ dper na/ gnod sbyin gyi gzhal med khang mi'i khang pa na 'dug pa'am/ mi'i khang pa gnod sbyin gyi khang pa'i khongs na 'dug pa ni/ phan tshun tha mi dad de/ las kyi yul rnam pa ji ltar dag pa'i tshul bzhin du snang ngo/ /

It was like the palace of a yakṣa being within a human palace, or a human palace being within a yakṣa palace; they are inseparable but are perceived in accordance with the purity of the scope of perception of a person’s karma.[2152]
just as human abodes within demonic abodes, each distinct within the demonic abodes, are visible according to the purity of the objects of desire,
'di lta ste/ dper na/ rgya mtsho chen po la stong gsum gyi stong chen po'i 'jig rten gyi khams thams cad kyang rgya'i gzugs brnyan ltar snang ngo/ /
It was like all the world realms of a billion-world universe appearing upon a great ocean as reflections on the ocean.[2153]
just as reflections of the worlds of the universe are seen in the ocean,

'di lta ste/ dper na/ sgyu ma'i mkhan po ni; sngags dang / rig sngags dang / rtsi'i mthu dang / byin gyi rlabs kyis gzugs kyi rnam pa thams cad dang / bya ba thams cad kyang yongs su ston to/ / de bzhin du tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis kyang byang chub sems dpa' byams pa'i byin gyi rlabs ye shes sgyu ma bsam gyis mi khyab pa la zhugs pas byang chub sems dpa'i dbang dang / byin gyi rlabs kyi ye shes chos thams cad shes pa'i sgyu ma'i stobs kyis mngon par bsgrubs pa'i mthus rgyan gyi yul rnam par sprul pa de dag mthong bar gyur to/ /

By analogy, a conjurer manifests all kinds of forms and activities through the blessings of the power of mantras, spells, and potions. In the same way, Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, saw all the displays of miraculous manifestations because of the bodhisattva Maitreya’s engagement in inconceivable conjurations from blessing and wisdom. This was because of his accomplishment of the power of conjuration from the knowledge of all phenomena and because of conjuration through a bodhisattva’s power of blessing and wisdom.

just as a magician sees all forms and activities by the power of spells and drugs, in the same way Sudhana, by the inconceivable direction of the magic of the enlightening mystic knowledge of Maitreya, saw all those miraculous displays, by bringing forth the power of magic of knowledge of truth, by the power of mystic knowledge mastered by the enlightening being.

de nas byang chub sems dpa' byams pas khang pa brtsegs pa de'i nang du song ste byin gyi rlabs de dag brtul nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang la se gol gyi sgra byas te 'di skad ces smras so/ / rigs kyi bu/ 'di ni/ chos rnams kyi chos nyid yin gyi/ longs/ rigs kyi bu/ chos thams cad ni/ rnam par bsgrubs na/ nye bar 'grub pa'i mtshan nyid de/ byang chub sems dpa'i ye shes kyi byin gyis brlabs pa'i rang bzhin de lta bu ste/ yongs su ma grub pa'o/ / sgyu ma dang / rmi lam dang / gzugs brnyan lta bu'o/ /

Then the bodhisattva Maitreya entered the kūṭāgāra and, diminishing those blessings, he snapped his fingers, saying to Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, “Arise, noble one![2154] Noble one, this is the nature of phenomena. This is the blessing of the wisdom of a bodhisattva. It is the characteristic of accomplishment from the practice of all Dharmas. They thus have no existing nature of their own. They are like conjurations, dreams, and reflections.”

Then the enlightening being Maitreya, entering the tower and relaxing his magical force, snapped his fingers and said to Sudhana, “Arise. This is the nature of things; characterized by nonfixity, all things are stabilized by the knowledge of enlightening beings, thus they are inherently unreal, and are like illusions, dreams, reflections.”

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang se gol gyi sgra des ting nge 'dzin de las langs par gyur pa dang / de la byang chub sems dpa' byams pas smras pa/ rigs kyi bu/ khyod kyis byang chub sems dpa'i byin gyi rlabs rnam par 'phrul ba mthong mod/ khyod kyis byang chub sems dpa'i tshogs kyi mthu dang / rgyu mthun pa mthong mod/ khyod kyis byang chub sems dpa'i smon lam gyi ye shes kyis rnam par bsgrubs pa mthong mod/ khyod kyis byang chub sems dpa'i gnas mdangs dga' ba mthong mod/ khyod kyis byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa yongs su bsdu ba mthong mod/ khyod kyis byang chub sems dpa'i 'byung ba'i sgra thos mod/ khyod kyis sangs rgyas kyi zhing gi yon tan dang / rgyan tshad med pa mthong mod/ khyod kyis de bzhin gshegs pa'i smon lam rnam pa tha dad pa'i khyad par mthong mod; khyod kyis byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa bsam gyis mi khyab pa'i rjes su 'brang ba byas mod/ khyod kyis byang chub sems dpa'i ting nge 'dzin gyi dga' ba dang bde ba myong mod/

Then, with that finger snap, Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, arose from samādhi. The bodhisattva Maitreya then said to him, “Noble one, you have seen the miraculous manifestations of the blessing of a bodhisattva. You have seen the power and natural result of the accumulations of a bodhisattva. You have seen accomplishments through the wisdom of the prayers of a bodhisattva. You have seen the delightful abodes of a bodhisattva. You have seen the accumulated conduct of a bodhisattva. You have heard the doors through which the bodhisattvas come forth. You have seen the immeasurable qualities and displays of the buddha realms. You have seen the specific different prayers of the tathāgatas. You have followed the inconceivable liberation of the bodhisattva. You have experienced the delight and bliss of the bodhisattva’s samādhi.”

Then, at a finger snap, Sudhana emerged from that trance and Maitreyasaid to him, “Did you see the miraculous display of the magical power of enlightening beings? Did you see the results of the power of enlightening beings’ preparations for enlightenment? Did you see the creations of the vows and knowledge of enlightening beings? Did you see the practices and attainments of enlightening beings? Did you hear the enlightening beings’ ways of emancipation? Did you see the infinity of adornments of buddha-lands? Did you see the excellence of the vows and expertise of buddhas? Did you realize the inconceivability of the liberation of enlightening beings? Did you experience enlightening beings’ bliss of absorption?”

nor bzang gis smras pa/ 'phags pa/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi byin gyi rlabs dang / dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyis dgongs pa dang / dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi mthus mthong ngo/ / 'phags pa/ rnam par thar pa 'di'i ming ci zhes bgyi/ smras pa/ rigs kyi bu/ rnam par thar pa 'di ni/ dus gsum gyi dmigs pa thams cad la shes pa rab tu zhugs pa'i dran pa nyams pa med pas brgyan pa'i snying po zhes bya ba ste/

Sudhana said, “Ārya, I have seen them through the blessing of the kalyāṇamitra, through the intention of the kalyāṇamitra, and through the power of the kalyāṇamitra. Ārya, what is this liberation called?” Maitreya answered, “Noble one, this liberation is called the essence of the display of the unfailing memory that engages with the knowledge of all objects of perception in the three times.

Sudhana said, “I saw, noble one, by the empowerment and spiritual force of the benefactor. And what is this liberation called?” Maitreyasaid, “This liberation is called the sanctum of supernal manifestations of unconfused recollection entering into knowledge of all objects of past, present, and future.
rigs kyi bu/ rnam par thar pa 'di lta bu brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa dag ni; tshe gcig gis thogs pa'i byang chub sems dpas thob bo/ /
“Noble one, this[2155] kind of liberation, which is inexpressibly inexpressible, is the attainment of a bodhisattva with one lifetime remaining.”
And an enlightening being assured of enlightenment in one lifetime attains untold liberations like this.”
nor bzang gis smras pa/ 'phags pa/ rgyan de dag gang du mchis/ smras pa/ gang nas 'ongs pa der ro/
Sudhana asked, “Ārya, where is this display?” The bodhisattva Maitreya answered, “It is where it comes from.”
Sudhana said, “Where has that magnificent display gone?” Maitreyasaid, “Where it came from.”
nor bzang gis smras pa/ gang nas mchis/
Sudhana asked, “Where does it come from?”
Sudhana said, “Where did it come from?”

smras pa/ byang chub sems dpa'i ye shes kyi byin gyi rlabs mngon par bsgrubs pa las 'ongs so/ / de ni/ byin gyi rlabs de nyid la gnas shing gang du yang song ba med la 'phos pa med do/ / phung por gyur pa med do/ / tshogs su gyur pa med do/ / brtsegs par gnas pa med do/ / dngos por gnas pa med do/ / yul na gnas pa ma yin no/ / phyogs na gnas pa ma yin no/ /

The bodhisattva Maitreya answered, “It comes from the accomplishment of the blessing of the wisdom of a bodhisattva. It dwells within that blessing. It does not come or go from anywhere. It does not accumulate. It does not come together. It does not amass. It has no location as a thing. It has no location as an object of perception. It has no location in any direction.

Maitreyasaid, “It came from the effectuation of the magical power of knowledge of enlightening beings, and it resides in that very magical power. It does not go or come at all, it is not an aggregate or an accumulation, it is not uniform and unchangeable, it is not abiding or fixed in existence, it is not located in any place.

rigs kyi bu/ 'di lta ste/ dper na/ klu rnams kyi sprin gyi dra ba ni lus la yang mi gnas/ sems la yang mi gnas/ nang na yang mi gnas mod kyi/ klu'i sems kyi dbang dang / klu'i dbang bsam gyis mi khyab pas char gyi rgyun tshad med pa bkye ba ni med pa ma yin te snang ngo/ / rigs kyi bu/ de bzhin du rgyan de dag kyang nang na gnas pa yang ma yin/ phyi rol na gnas pa yang ma yin te/ byang chub sems dpa'i byin gyi rlabs kyi dbang dang / khyod kyi snod bzang ba'i phyir mi snang ba'ang ma yin no/ /
