“By analogy, noble one, the net of clouds of the nāgas is not located in the body, is not located in the mind, is not located internally, and yet through the power of a nāga’s mind and through the inconceivable power of a nāga there is emitted a measureless flow of rain, which is not nonexistent and appears. In the same way, noble one, those displays are not located internally and are not located externally, but they become visible through the power of a bodhisattva’s blessing and through your being a good vessel.

It is like the network of clouds of the water spirits which do not appear from body or mind and yet are indeed seen in masses; by the mental power of the water spirits measureless clouds emerge, by the wonder of the realm of the water spirits. In the same way, those supernal manifestations are not internal or external, yet it is not that they are not seen, by the magical power of the enlightening being, and because of your own capacity.

rigs kyi bu/ 'di lta ste/ dper na/ sgyu ma'i mkhan pos ni yul thams cad yongs su bstan kyang gang nas kyang 'ongs pa med/ bshig kyang gang du yang 'gro ba med de/ 'pho ba med mod kyi sngags dang rtsi'i mthus yongs su mi snang ba ma yin no/ / rigs kyi bu/ de bzhin du rgyan de dag kyang gang du yang song ba med/ gang nas kyang 'ong ba med la/ gang du yang phung por gyur ba med mod kyi/ byang chub sems dpa'i ye shes sgyu ma bsam gyis mi khyab pa la shin tu bslab pa dang / sngon gyi smon lam gyi byin gyi rlabs dang / ye shes kyi dbang gis yongs su mi snang ba ma yin no/ /

“By analogy, noble one, a conjurer displays the entire range of illusions, but they do not come from anywhere, do not go anywhere, and are not transferred to anywhere, but through the power of mantra and concoctions, they are perceived. In the same way, noble one, those displays do not go anywhere, have not come from anywhere, and are not transferred anywhere, but they are perceived through having trained in the inconceivable wisdom conjurations of a bodhisattva and through the power of wisdom and the blessing of past prayers.”

“Just as the illusions of a magician manifesting illusory objects do not come from anywhere or go away, nor are they in transit, yet they appear by the power of spells and drugs, in the same way those supernal arrays have never gone or come, nor accumulated, but they appear by proper learning of the inconceivable magic of knowledge of enlightening beings, by mastery of knowledge empowered by past vows.”

nor bzang gis smras pa/ 'phags pa/ shul ji srid cig nas gshegs/ smras pa/ rigs kyi bu/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams 'gro ba ni 'ong ba med par 'gro'o/ / g.yo ba dang gnas pa med par 'gro'o; ; gnas dang rten med par 'gro'o/ / shi 'pho dang skye ba med par 'gro'o/ / gnas pa dang 'pho ba med par 'gro'o/ / g.yo ba dang ldang ba med par 'gro'o/ / ltos pa dang gnas med par 'gro'o/ / las dang rnam par smin pa med par 'gro'o/ / mi skye ba dang mi 'gag par 'gro'o/ / rtag pa med pa dang chad pa med par 'gro'o/ /

Sudhana asked, “Ārya, from how far have you come?” The bodhisattva Maitreya answered, “Noble one, the movement of bodhisattvas has no coming or going; their motion is without movement or stillness. Their motion is without basis or location. Their motion is without passing away or rebirth. Their motion is without remaining or going elsewhere. Their motion is without movement or rising. Their motion is without dependence or location. Their motion is without karma or its ripening. Their motion is without creation or cessation. Their motion is without permanence or annihilation.

Sudhana said, “From how far away do you come?” Maitreyasaid, “In the state where there is no coming; the state of enlightening beings is the state of neither motion nor stasis, the state of no support or abode, the state of no passing away or rebirth, the state neither static nor transient, the state of no stirring or arising, the state of no concern or attachment, the state of no deeds or fruition, the state of no origination or destruction, the state of no annihilation or eternity.

gzhan yang rigs kyi bu; byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi 'gro ba ni 'dul ba'i sems can la lta bas snying rje chen po'o/ / byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi 'gro ba ni sdug bsngal ba'i sems can yongs su skyob pas byams pa'o/ / byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi 'gro ba ni gang du dga' bar skye bas tshul khrims so/ / byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi 'gro ba ni sngon gyi byin gyis rlabs kyis smon lam mo/ / byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi 'gro ba ni thams cad de bzhin yongs su ston pas mngon par shes pa'o/ / byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi 'gro ba ni/ de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi zhabs kyi drung nas g.yo ba med pas mngon par 'du bya ba med pa'o/ / byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi 'gro ba ni/ lus dang sems yongs su mi gtong bas len pa dang 'dor ba med pa'o/ / byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi 'gro ba ni/ sems can thams cad kyi rjes su 'brang bas shes rab dang thabs so/ / byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi 'gro ba ni/ mig yor dang / gzugs brnyan dang / sprul pa lta bu yin pas sprul pa yongs su ston pa'o/ /

“Moreover, noble one, the motion of bodhisattvas is great compassion because it observes beings to be guided. The motion of bodhisattvas is great[2156] love because it saves beings from suffering. The motion of bodhisattvas is correct conduct because it regards everyone kindly. The motion of bodhisattvas is prayer because of the blessings of the past. The motion of bodhisattvas is higher cognition because it manifests itself[2157] to all. The motion of bodhisattvas has no formation, as there is no movement from being at the feet of all the tathāgatas. The motion of bodhisattvas has no acquisition or rejection, because it is not focused on a body or mind. The motion of bodhisattvas is wisdom and method because it follows all beings. The motion of bodhisattvas is the manifestation of emanations because it is like a mirage, a reflection, or an illusory manifestation.

Furthermore, great compassion is the state of enlightening beings, as they attend to sentient beings who can be guided; great kindness is the state of enlightening beings, as they rescue suffering beings; discipline is the state of enlightening beings, as they become reconstituted according to will; commitment is the state of enlightening beings, based on past vows; spiritual power is the state of enlightening beings, as they manifest all that is pleasant; nondoing is the state of enlightening beings, as they do not leave the presence of all buddhas; neither grasping nor rejecting is the state of enlightening beings, as they are not obsessed with body or mind; wisdom and means is the state of enlightening beings, as they adapt to sentient beings, manifesting emanations is the state of enlightening beings, their bodies being equivalent to reflected images.

rigs kyi bu/ gzhan yang khyod lam ji srid cig nas 'ongs zhes khyod kyis smras pa ni/ rigs kyi bu/ nga ni/ tshe'i sa yul phreng ba stobs kyi grong rdal khang khyim can zhes bya ba de na tshong dpon sa skyong zhes bya ba zhig yod de/ de sangs rgyas kyi chos la bzhag nas tshe'i sa'i mi rnams la snod kyi tshul bzhin du chos bstan pa byas te/ pha ma dang / bram ze dang / khyim bdag gnyen bshes su 'ong ba rnams theg pa chen po la yang dag par bskul nas 'dir 'ongs so/ /

“Moreover, noble one, you asked, ‘From how far have you come?’[2158] Noble son, I come here from a hamlet called Kuṭi in the land of the Māladas, which is the place of my birth.[2159] In that place there was a head merchant by the name of Gopālaka. After I had established him in the Buddha’s Dharma, I taught the Dharma, in accordance with the nature of the recipients, to the people of my birthplace. After I had inspired my parents, family, and relatives[2160] and brahmins and householders to enter the Mahāyāna, I came here.”

“And you ask how far away I come from—I come here from the village of Kuti in the territories of the Malada people, land of my birth. There is a gentleman there named Gopalaka, who guides people into the buddha-teachings, teaches the native people according to their capacities, and establishes family and relatives, priests and householders, in the Great Vehicle.”
nor bzang gis smras pa/ 'phags pa; byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi tshe'i sa gang lags/
Sudhana asked, “Ārya, where are the birthplaces of the bodhisattvas?”
Sudhana asked, “What are the native lands of enlightening beings?”
smras pa/ rigs kyi bu/ bcu po 'di dag ni/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi tshe'i sa ste/ bcu gang zhe na/
Maitreya replied, “Noble one, there are ten birthplaces of the bodhisattvas. What are the ten?
Maitreyasaid, “There are ten native lands of enlightening beings. What are they?

'di lta ste/ byang chub kyi sems ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i rigs su skyes pas byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi tshe'i sa'o/ / lhag pa'i bsam pa ni/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi rigs su skyes pas byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi tshe'i sa'o/ / sa la gnas pa ni/ pha rol tu phyin pa'i rigs su skyes pas byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi tshe'i sa'o/ / smon lam mngon par sgrub pa ni/ spyod pa'i rigs su skyes pas byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi tshe'i sa'o/ / snying rje chen po ni/ bsdu ba'i dngos po thams cad kyi rigs su skyes pas byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi tshe'i sa'o/ / yang dag pa ji lta ba bzhin du chos rtogs par bya ba ni/ shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa'i rigs su skyes pas byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi tshe'i sa'o/ / theg pa chen po ni/ thabs mkhas pa'i rigs su skyes pas byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi tshe'i sa'o/ / sems can yongs su smin par bya ba ni/ mngon par rdzogs par 'tshang rgya ba'i rigs su skyes pas byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi tshe'i sa'o/ / thabs dang shes rab gnyis ni/ mi skye ba'i chos kyi bzod pa'i rigs su skyes pas byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi tshe'i sa'o/ / rigs kyi bu/ chos thams cad kyi nan tan ni/ 'das pa dang / ma byon pa dang / da ltar byung ba'i de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi rigs su skyes pas byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi tshe'i sa te/ /rigs kyi bu/ bcu po de dag ni/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi tshe'i sa'o/ /

(1) “The aspiration to enlightenment is a birthplace of the bodhisattvas because it is birth into the family of bodhisattvas. (2) The higher motivation is a birthplace of the bodhisattvas because it is birth into the family of kalyāṇamitras. (3) Being upon the bhūmis is a birthplace of the bodhisattvas because it is birth into the family of the perfections. (4) The accomplishment of prayer is a birthplace of the bodhisattvas because it is birth into the family of bodhisattva conduct. (5) Great compassion is a birthplace of the bodhisattvas because it is birth into the family of all the methods of gathering pupils. (6) The correct realization of the nature of phenomena is a birthplace of the bodhisattvas because it is birth into the family of the perfection of wisdom. (7) The Mahāyāna is a birthplace of the bodhisattvas because it is birth into the family of skillful methods. (8) Ripening beings is a birthplace of the bodhisattvas because it is birth into the family of complete buddhahood. (9) Method and wisdom are a birthplace of the bodhisattvas because they are birth into the family of patience from the birthlessness of phenomena. (10) Noble one, the practice of the Dharma is a birthplace of the bodhisattvas because it is birth into the family of all past, future, and present tathāgatas. Noble one, those ten are the birthplaces of the bodhisattvas.

The arousal of the aspiration for enlightenment is a native land of enlightening beings, causing one to be born in the family of enlightening beings. Strong will is a native land of enlightening beings, causing one to be born in the family of spiritual friends. The stages are a native land of enlightening beings, causing one to be born in the family of the transcendent ways. Carrying out vows is a native land of enlightening beings, causing one to be born in the family of sublime acts. Universal compassion is a native land of enlightening beings, causing one to be born in the house of means of salvation. Profound contemplation is a native land of enlightening beings, causing one to be born in the house of transcendent wisdom. The Great Vehicle is a native land of enlightening beings, causing one to be born in the house of skill in means. Educating sentient beings is a native land of enlightening beings, causing one to be born in the house of buddhas. Knowledge and means is a native land of enlightening beings, causing one to be born in the house of tolerance of things as unoriginated. Practicing and realizing all truths is a native land of enlightening beings, causing one to be born in the house of all buddhas of past, future, and present.

rigs kyi bu/ thabs mkhas pa ni/ byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi pha'o/ / shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa ni; ma'o/ / sbyin pa'i pha rol tu phyin pa ni/ 'o ma'o/ / tshul khrims kyi pha rol tu phyin pa ni/ ma ma'o/ / bzod pa'i pha rol tu phyin pa ni/ lhab lhub dang rgyan to/ / brtson 'grus kyi pha rol tu phyin pa ni/ skyed pa'o/ / bsam gtan gyi pha rol tu phyin pa ni/ spyod pa rnam par dag par byed pa'o/ / dge ba'i bshes gnyen rnams ni/ bslab pa la spyod du 'jug pa'o/ / byang chub kyi yan lag thams cad ni/ grogs po'o/ / dge ba'i rtsa ba'i chos thams cad ni/ gnyen bshes so/ / byang chub sems dpa' thams cad ni/ phu nu bo'o/ / byang chub kyi sems ni/ rigs so/ / nan tan ni/ rigs kyi chos so/ / sa'i gnas ni/ rigs kyi gnas so/ / bzod pa thob pa ni/ rigs su rigs dang ldan par skyes pa'o/ / smon lam mngon par sgrub pa ni/ rigs kyi gzhung thob pa'o/ / spyod pa rnam par dag pa ni/ rigs kyi chos kyi rjes snyegs pa'o/ / theg pa chen po la yang dag par skul ba ni/ rigs kyi rgyun mi gcod pa'o/ / dbang bskur nas tshe gcig gis thogs pa ni/ chos kyi rgyal po'i sras kyi thu bo'o/ / de bzhin gshegs pa nyid du yang dag par sgrub pa ni/ rigs kyi bu rgyud yongs su dag pa ste/

“Noble one, method and wisdom are the father of the bodhisattvas; the perfection of wisdom is their mother; the perfection of generosity is their wet nurse; the perfection of conduct is their nanny; the perfection of patience is their adornment and jewelry; the perfection of diligence is their growing up; the perfection of meditation is their correct conduct; the kalyāṇamitras are their training in conduct; all the aspects of enlightenment are their companions; all the qualities of the roots of merit are their friends; all the bodhisattvas are their brothers; the aspiration to enlightenment is their family; their practice is the qualities of their family; being upon the bhūmis is being in their family; attaining patience is being born into the family; accomplishing prayer is inheriting the knowledge of the family; pure conduct is gaining the qualities of the family; inspiring others to the Mahāyāna is maintaining the continuity of the family; being consecrated as having one life remaining is being the senior son of a Dharma king; and attaining becoming a tathāgata is purifying the lineage of the family.

“Transcendent wisdom is the mother of enlightening beings, skill in means is the father of enlightening beings, transcendent generosity is the milk of enlightening beings, transcendent discipline is their nurse, transcendent tolerance is their adornment, transcendent vigor is what makes them grow, transcendent meditation purifies their practice, spiritual friends teach them, the elements of enlightenment are their companions, all enlightening beings are their siblings, the determination for enlightenment is their family, practice is the rule of their family, the stages are their residence, attainment of tolerance is birth in the family, carrying out vows is acquisition of the knowledge of the family, purity of conduct is following the rule of the family, promoting the Great Vehicle is preserving the continuity of the family, consecration as one bound to attain buddhahood in one life is princehood among spiritual kings, and the attainment of all who arrive at Thusness is complete purification of the family.

rigs kyi bu/ de ltar na/ byang chub sems dpa' byis pa tha dad pa'i skye bo'i sa las shin tu 'das pa yin/ byang chub sems dpa'i skyon med par zhugs pa yin/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i rigs su yang dag par byung ba yin no/ / de bzhin gshegs pa'i rgyud la rab tu gnas pa yin/ dkon mchog gsum gyi rigs rgyun mi gcad pa la zhugs pa yin/ byang chub sems dpa'i rigs yongs su bsdu ba la mngon par brtson pa yin; rigs dang rus kyis yongs su dag pa yin/ gnad kyi rgyud kyis smad du med pa yin/ lha dang bcas pa'i 'jig rten dang / bdud dang bcas pa dang / tshangs pa dang bcas pa dang / dge sbyong dang / bram zer bcas pa'i skye rgu'i nang na rigs la smos pa'i skyon thams cad kyi kha na ma tho ba med pa yin te/ sangs rgyas kyi rigs dam par skyes la; smon lam chen po'i lus dang ldan pas rigs kyis btsun pa yin/

“Noble one, in that way, the bodhisattvas transcend the level of different foolish beings; enter the faultlessness of a bodhisattva; enter the family of the tathāgatas; are within the lineage of the tathāgatas; practice to maintain the continuity of the family of the Three Jewels; are dedicated to protecting[2161] the family of the bodhisattvas; make the family and clan pure; do not cause the vital lineage to decline; have no fault of transgression in the family that could be criticized by any of the beings in the world including its devas, its māras, its Brahmā deities, and its śramaṇas and brahmins; and have the nobility of their family because through being born in the supreme family of the buddhas they possess a body of great prayer.

“Thus the enlightening being has gone beyond the stage of the ignorant and has entered the certainty of enlightening beings, has been born in the family of buddhas, has been established in the lineage of buddhas, has become capable of perpetuating the three treasures, has become involved in protecting the family of enlightening beings, has become socially pure and impeccable, blameless among all people, has become well born in the highest family of buddhas, the body a repository of great vows.

rigs kyi bu/ rgyud kyi rigs de lta bu dang ldan pa'i byang chub sems dpa' rnams ni/ chos thams cad gzugs brnyan lta bur yongs su shes pas 'jig rten gyi skye gnas thams cad du smad pa med pa yin te/ srid pa'i skye gnas thams cad sprul pa lta bur yongs su shes pas srid pa'i lam gyi rgyud du skye zhing gnas pa thams cad kyis kun nas nyon mongs par mi 'gyur ro/ / chos thams cad bdag med par khong du chud pas sems can thams cad yongs su smin par bya ba dang / gdul bas yongs su mi skyo'o/ / byams pa chen po dang / snying rje chen po'i lus dang ldan pa'i phyir sems can thams cad la phan gdags pas ngal bar mi 'gyur ro/ / 'khor ba thams cad rmi lam lta bur yongs su rtogs pas bskal pa thams cad du gnas pas sgyid lug par mi 'gyur ro/ / phung po thams cad sgyu ma lta bur yongs su shes pas skye ba dang / 'chi 'pho dang / 'chi ba yongs su bstan pa thams cad kyis dub par mi 'gyur ro; ; khams dang / skye mched chos kyi dbyings kyi rang bzhin tu rab tu rtogs pas yul thams cad kyis rma mi 'byung ngo/ / 'du shes kyi rnam pa thams cad smig rgyu lta bur shin tu bsgoms pas 'khor ba'i dga' ba thams cad kyis mos par mi 'gyur ro/ / sgyu ma lta bu'i chos thams cad la rnam par rtse bas bdud kyi yul thams cad kyis mi gos so/ / chos kyi lus su byung bas nyon mongs pa thams cad du smos su med do/ / skye ba la dbang rab tu thob pas 'gro ba'i rgyud thams cad rtogs par khong du chud pa yin no/ /

“Noble one, the bodhisattvas who have such a family lineage know all phenomena to be like reflections, so they are not revolted by births in all worlds. Knowing that all births in existences are like magical illusions, they are born in and remain within the various modes of existence without being afflicted by them. They have comprehended the absence of a self in everything and therefore do not become wearied in ripening and guiding beings. They possess bodies of great love and great compassion and therefore do not become fatigued in benefiting beings. They have realized that all saṃsāra is like a dream and therefore do not become disheartened in remaining in it throughout all kalpas. They know that all the skandhas are like conjured illusions, and therefore they are not made despondent by all manifestations of birth, passing away, and death. They have realized the dhātus[2162] and āyatanas to have the nature of the realm of phenomena and are therefore not wounded by anything in the range of sensory possessions. They meditate on all forms of perception as being like mirages and therefore have no aspiration for any of the joys of saṃsāra. They play with all phenomena as being like conjured illusions and therefore are unstained[2163] by any scope of the māras. They have Dharma bodies[2164] and therefore are not brought down by the kleśas. And they have attained power over rebirth and therefore realize and comprehend all classes of existence.

“Enlightening beings who have succeeded in being born in the family this way do not shrink away from existence in any world, because they realize all things are like reflections; they are not defiled by life in any state of existence, because they realize birth in all states of being is phantomlike; they are tireless in guiding and perfecting all beings, because they are aware all is selfless; they never cease taking care of all beings, because they embody universal love and compassion; they do not fear living through all ages, because they believe the mundane whirl is like a dream; they are not afflicted by the appearance of birth and death, because they realize the clusters of mental and physical elements are illusory; they are not injured in the midst of all objects, because they realize they are of the nature of the reality realm; they are not deluded by any of the states of the mundane whirl, because they have thoroughly realized they are like mirages; they are unaffected by any bedeviling objects because they are familiar with the illusoriness of all things; they are incapable of being deceived by any afflictions, because they have mastered the spiritual body; they reach their goal in all states of being, because they have attained control over becoming.

rigs kyi bu/ de ltar nga ni/ 'jig rten gyi khams thams cad kyi skye gnas kyi khongs su chud pa'i lus dang / 'gro ba thams cad kyi gzugs dang mnyam pa'i kha dog gi khyad par dang / sems can thams cad dang mnyam pa'i nges pa'i tshig gi bye brag dang / 'gro ba thams cad dang mnyam pa'i ming rnam pa tha dad pa dang / sems can thams cad kyi mos pa dang mnyam pa'i spyod lam dang / 'gro ba rnam par gdul ba thams cad dang mnyam pa'i 'jig rten gyi rjes su 'brang ba dang / sems can rnam par dag par bya ba thams cad dang mnyam pa'i tshe dang / rigs su skye ba yongs su bstan pa dang / byis pa'i spyod pa thams cad dang mnyam pa'i bya ba la 'jug pa'i sgo dang / sems can gyi 'du shes kyi rnam pa thams cad dang / mnyam pa'i yongs su shes par bya ba la 'jug pa dang / byang chub sems dpa'i smon lam gyi sprul pa thams cad dang mnyam pa'i lus yongs su bstan cing brjod pas/ chos kyi dbyings thams cad rgyas par bkang ste/

“Noble son, in that way, I have spread throughout the realm of phenomena with a body that enters birth in all world realms, with the particular appearances[2165] that are congruent with the forms of all beings, with specific definitions that are congruent[2166] with all beings, with various names that are congruent[2167] with all beings, with conduct that is congruent with the aspirations of all beings, with a conformity to worlds that is congruent[2168] with guiding all beings, with the manifestations of lifespans and births in families that are congruent with the beings who are to be purified, with gateways of entry into activities that are congruent with all the conducts of foolish beings,[2169] with an engagement in knowledge that is congruent with all the forms of perception of beings,[2170] and with the manifestations and splendor[2171] of bodies that are congruent with all the emanations from the prayers of bodhisattvas.

“With a body existing in all worlds, in forms like all beings, with different powers, with distinct forms of speech like those of all beings, with modes of conduct like those approved by all beings, with adaptations to the world as extensive as the precepts of all beings, appearing to be born in families consonant with all kinds of purity, by entries into the perceptions and ideas of all beings through engagement in activity, by powers of physical manifestation equal to the creations of vows of all enlightening beings, I pervade all universes,

sngon skal pa mnyam par spyod spyod pa'i sems can byang chub kyi sems stor bar gyur pa rnams yongs su smin par bya ba dang / 'dzam bu'i gling du skyes pa'i tshe yongs su bstan pa dang / lho phyogs kyi rgyud 'di'i yul phreng ba stobs kyi grong rdal khang khyim dang ldan pa zhes bya ba 'di'i bram ze'i rigs su skyes pa rnams dang / pha ma dang gnyen bshes su 'ong ba rnams rnam par gdul ba dang / bram ze'i rigs dang rgyud kyi khyad par gyis rigs kyi nga rgyal can du gyur pa 'di dag nga rgyal med par byas te/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i rigs su bskyed pa'i don du 'dir skyes so/ /

“Noble one, in order to ripen those beings who in the past practiced in the same way as I did but lost aspiration for enlightenment, and in order to manifest a birth and life in Jambudvīpa, I was born in the brahmin castes in this hamlet called Kuṭi in the lands of the Māladas in this southern region. I was born here so as to guide my father, mother, family, and relatives, to dispel arrogance among those in the particular brahmin castes who were proud of their birth into those castes, and so that they would be born in the family of the tathāgatas.

and arrived here in the south, in the village of Kuta in the Malada region, in order to develop to maturity those who carried out the same practices as I in the past but have lost the aspiration for enlightenment, and to manifest birth on this continent, to guide parents and relatives born in the priestly caste, and to generate the family of enlightened ones so as to free them from the pride and conceit of the superiority of the priestly caste.

rigs kyi bu/ de ltar nga lho phyogs kyi rgyud 'di na thabs rnam pa 'di lta bus sems can bsam pa'i tshul ji lta bu dang ldan pa dang / rnam pa ji lta bus 'dul ba rnams yongs su smin par bya ba dang / gdul ba byed cing / khang pa brtsegs pa chen po rnam par snang mdzad kyi rgyan gyis brgyan pa'i snying po 'di na 'dug go /

“Noble one, in that way, I dwell in this Vairocanavyūhālaṃkāragarbha kūṭāgāra here in this southern region, ripening and guiding beings in whatever way is necessary and according to their aspirations through these kinds of methods.
“Here in the south, by that means guiding beings according to their mentalities and according to their capacity for being taught, I live in this tower containing the adornments of Vairocana.

'di nas shi 'phos nas kyang bsam pa'i tshul ji lta ba bzhin du sems can rnams kyi rjes su 'brang bar bya ba dang / dga' ldan gyi ris su gtogs pa'i lha'i bu skal pa mnyam par spyod spyod pa rnams yongs su smin par bya ba dang / 'dod pa'i khams nas yongs su 'das pa thams cad la'ang byang chub sems dpa'i bsod nams dang / ye shes dang / sprul pa'i rgyan yongs su bstan pa dang / 'dod pa'i dga' ba'i sred pa las rnam par bzlog pa dang / 'du byed thams cad mi rtag pa nyid du bstan pa dang / lhar skyes pa thams cad kyang mthar rgud par 'gyur ba yongs su bstan pa dang / ye shes chen po'i chos kyi sgo 'chi 'pho'i rnam pa zhes bya ba tshe gcig gis thogs pa'i byang chub sems dpa' rnams dang yang dag par bgro bar bya ba dang / lhan cig yongs su smin par gyur pa rnams der skye bar yongs su bsdu bar bya ba dang / de bzhin gshegs pa shAkya thub pas bkye ba'i pad+mo rnams kyang kha dbye ba'i phyir dga' ldan gyi gnas su skye ba yongs su ston te/ dus la bab la bsam pa yongs su rdzogs nas ni/ thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyang thob par byed kyi/ ngas byang chub mthong nas kyang rigs kyi bu khyod dang / 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur par bcas pas da dung yang mthong bar 'gyur ro/ /

“When I die and pass away from here, I will manifest taking birth in the Tuṣita paradise in order to take care of beings in accordance with their aspirations; in order to ripen the Tuṣita devas whose conduct accords with mine; in order to manifest a bodhisattva’s merit, wisdom, and display of miracles to all those who have transcended the realm of desire; in order to dispel craving for desired pleasures; in order to teach the impermanence of all that is composite;[2172] in order to teach their eventual decline to all those who have been born as devas; in order to discuss,[2173] together with bodhisattvas who have one lifetime remaining, the Dharma gateway to great wisdom; in order to gather together those born there who have been ripened together with me; and in order to cause the lotuses of the guidance sent forth by the Tathāgata Śākyamuni to blossom. When the time has come for my intentions to be fulfilled, I will set out to attain omniscience, and when I have attained enlightenment, you will see me again, together with the kalyāṇamitra Mañjuśrī.

When I have passed away from here, I will manifest birth in Tushita, the celestial abode of happiness and contentment, in order to adapt to beings according to mentality, and to mature the celestials of that heaven engaged in the same practice, to manifest supernal arrays of emanations of the virtue and knowledge of enlightening beings beyond all realms of desire, to dispel all craving for sensual enjoyment, to make it clear that all mundane routines are impermanent, to show that all celestial existence ultimately declines and passes away, to join with the enlightening beings bound for buddhahood in one life in proclaiming the teaching of great knowledge called ‘appearance of descent from heaven into rebirth on earth,’ to take care of those matured together in that state of existence, and to enlighten those sent forth by Shakyamuni when the time comes to be guided. At that time I will realize omniscience, the fulfillment of my aspiration; and when I have attained enlightenment, you will see me again, with the spiritual benefactor Manjushri.

song rigs kyi bu/ da dung yang 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pa'i gan du song la/ ji ltar byang chub sems dpas byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la bslab par bya ba dang / ji ltar kun tu bzang po'i spyod pa'i dkyil 'khor la 'jug par bya ba dang / ji ltar mngon par bsgrub pa dang / ji ltar smon par bya ba dang / ji ltar rgyas par bya ba dang / ji ltar rjes su 'brang bar bya ba dang / ji ltar yongs su sbyang bar bya ba dang / ji ltar khong du chud par bya ba dang / ji ltar yongs su rdzogs par bya ba dris shig dang / dge ba'i bshes gnyen des khyod la ston par 'gyur ro/ /

“Depart, noble one. Go again into the presence of the bodhisattva Mañjuśrī and ask him, ‘How should bodhisattvas train in bodhisattva conduct? How should they practice it? How should they comprehend the field of completely good conduct? How should they accomplish it? How should they pray for it? How should they increase it? How should they follow it? How should they master[2174] it? How should they enter it? How should they perfect it?’ Then that kalyāṇamitra will teach you.

“Now go back to Manjushri and ask him how an enlightening being is to learn and carry out the practice of enlightening beings, enter the sphere of universally good practice, undertake and carry it out, expand it, follow it, purify it, enter fully into it, and fulfill it. He will show you the real benefactor.
de ci'i phyir zhe na/ 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pas spyod pa mngon par sgrub pa de lta bu'i smon lam gyi khyad par ni/ byang chub sems dpa' bye ba khrag khrig brgya phrag stong la yang med do/ /
“Why is that? Because Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta has a special prayer for the accomplishment of that conduct, which a hundred thousand quintillion bodhisattvas do not have.
Why? The best of vows of decillions of enlightening beings is Manjushri’s; vast is the outcome of the practice of Manjushri;
'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pa'i smon lam mngon par sgrub pa ni/ tshad med do/ /
Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta has accomplished countless prayers.
measureless is the accomplishment of vows of Manjushri;
'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pa'i byang chub sems dpa'i yon tan gyi khyad par thams cad mngon par sgrub pa ni/ tshad med do/ /
Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta has accomplished countless special bodhisattva qualities.
ceaseless is Manjushri’s achievement of the best of virtues of all enlightening beings;
'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pa ni/ sangs rgyas bye ba khrag khrig brgya phrag stong gi yum lta bu'o/ /
Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta is like a mother for a hundred thousand quintillion buddhas.
Manjushri is the mother of decillions of buddhas;
'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pa ni/ byang chub sems dpa' bye ba khrag khrig brgya phrag stong la gdams ngag ston pa'o/ /
Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta teaches instructions to a hundred thousand quintillion bodhisattvas.
Manjushri is the teacher of decillions of enlightening beings;
'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pa ni/ sems can gyi khams thams cad yongs su smin par bya ba dang / gdul ba la rab tu brtson pa'o/ /
Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta is dedicated to ripening and guiding all realms of beings.
Manjushri is engaged in the perfection of all beings;
'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pa ni/ phyogs bcu'i 'jig rten gyi khams su ming gi 'khor los rnam par rgyas par gyur pa'o/ /
Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta has spread the wheel of his name throughout the world realms of the ten directions.
widespread is the name of Manjushri in all worlds of the ten directions;
'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pa ni/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor thams cad du gtam gyi skyes bur gyur pa'o/ /
Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta is a person who has spoken to all the assembled followers of the tathāgatas.
Manjushri is the interlocutor in the assemblies of untold buddhas;
'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pa ni/ de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyis bsngags shing bstod pa'o/ /
Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta is extolled and praised by all the tathāgatas.
Manjushri is praised by all buddhas;
'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pa ni/ chos thams cad yang dag pa ji lta ba bzhin du mthong ba ste/ chos zab mo'i ye shes la rnam par spyod pa'o/ /
Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta sees all phenomena exactly as they are and practices the wisdom of the profound Dharma.
abiding in the knowledge of profound truth, Manjushri sees all things according to their true significance;
'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pa ni/ rnam par thar pa thams cad kyi tshul thams cad la ring du song ba'i spyod yul dang ldan pa ste/ byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa kun tu bzang po la zhugs pa'o/ /
Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta has the scope of conduct that has gone far in the ways of all liberations and follows the completely good bodhisattva conduct.
Manjushri has ranged far into all modes of liberation; he is immersed in the practice of universally good enlightening beings.

rigs kyi bu/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen de ni/ khyod de bzhin gshegs pa'i rigs su skyed pa'o/ / dge ba'i rtsa ba thams cad yongs su 'phel bar byed pa'o/ / byang chub sems dpa'i tshogs mang po rab tu sgrub pa'o/ / yang dag pa'i dge ba'i bshes gnyen ston pa'o/ / yon tan thams cad la yang dag par skul ba'o/ / smon lam chen po'i dra ba thams cad du 'jug pa'o/ / smon lam mngon par sgrub pa thams cad la rab tu gzhog pa'o/ / byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi gsang ba thos par byed pa'o/ / byang chub sems dpa'i bsam gyis mi khyab pa thams cad yang dag par ston pa'o/ / sngon gyi tshe'i gnas su skal pa mthun par spyod pa'o/ /

“Noble one, that kalyāṇamitra is the one who has given birth to you into the family of the tathāgatas; he is the one who has increased your roots of merit;[2175] he is the one who has caused you to look for[2176] bodhisattva accumulations; he is the one who has revealed[2177] the kalyāṇamitras to you; he is the one who has inspired you toward all qualities; he is the one who caused you to enter the net of great prayers; he is the one who has established you in the accomplishment of prayers; he is the one who caused you to hear the secrets of all the bodhisattvas; he is the one who has taught you all the inconceivabilities of the bodhisattvas; and he is the one who has practiced together with you in your past lives.[2178]

He is the progenitor of spiritual benefactors, who makes you grow in the family of the enlightened, causes you to establish roots of goodness, shows you the provisions for enlightenment, introduces you to true benefactors, immerses you in all virtues, establishes you in the network of universal vows, causes you to hear of the accomplishment of all vows, shows the secrets of all enlightening beings, and has similarly practiced the wonder of all enlightening beings together with you in past lives.

rigs kyi bu/ de bas na; khyod da ltar yang 'jam dpal gyi rkang pa'i drung na 'dug gi /yon tan gyi gdams ngag thams cad thob par bya ba dang / yongs su skyo ba ma skyed cig /yongs su sgyid lug par ma byed cig /
“Therefore, noble one, be again at the feet of Mañjuśrī, and do not weary or be disheartened while receiving all the instructions for the qualities.
“Therefore when you go to Manjushri, do not be faint-hearted, do not become weary in receiving instruction in all virtues.

de ci'i phyir zhe na/ nor bzang / khyod kyis dge ba'i bshes gnyen ji snyed cig mthong ba dang / spyod pa'i sgo ji snyed cig thos pa dang / rnam par thar pa'i tshul ji snyed cig la zhugs pa dang / smon lam gyi khyad par ji snyed cig khong du chud pa de dag thams cad kyang 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pa'i mthu dang / byin gyi rlabs su blta ste/ 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pa ni/ thams cad la'ang pha rol tu phyin pa'i mchog thob pa'o/ /

Why is that? It is because, Sudhana, you should see that all the kalyāṇamitras that you have seen, all the gateways to conduct that you have heard, however many liberations you have engaged in, and whatever specific prayers you have been immersed in are all because of the power and blessing of Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta.”

Why? All the spiritual benefactors you have seen, all the ways of practice you have heard, all the modes of liberation you have entered, all the vows you have plunged into, should all be looked upon as the empowerment of Manjushri; and Manjushri has reached the ultimate perfection.”

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis byang chub sems dpa' sems dpa' chen po byams pa'i rkang pa gnyis la spyi bos phyag 'tshal te lan brgya stong du mar g.yas phyogs su bskor ba byas nas yang dang yang bltas te byang chub sems dpa' byams pa'i drung nas song ngo/ /

Then Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, bowed his head to the feet of the bodhisattva mahāsattva Maitreya, circumambulated him many hundreds of thousands of times, keeping him to his right, and, looking back again and again, departed from the bodhisattva Maitreya.
Then Sudhana paid his respects to Maitreya the enlightening being and went on.
[jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pa]
Chapter 55. Mañjuśrī
Manjushri

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang grong khyer brgya rtsa bcu kun tu rgyus te phyogs kyi gnas yid bde ba mngon du gyur pa zhes bya ba zhig na 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pa la sems shing rnam par lta bas 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pa mthong bar mos shing smon la phrad par dga' bas sdod cing 'dug 'dug pa dang /

Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, after passing through a hundred and ten towns, came to the district called Sumanāmukha, where, while thinking of and looking for Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, he was aspiring and praying to see Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta and continually yearning to meet him.
Then Sudhana, passing more than one hundred and ten cities, went to Sumanamukha and stayed there thinking about Manjushri, wishing to see and meet with Manjushri.

de nas 'jam dpal gzhon nur gyur pas dpag tshad brgya rtsa bcu bzhi'i pha rol nas lag pa brkyang ste tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang grong khyer yid bde ba mngon du gyur pa na 'dug pa'i spyi bor bzhag ste 'di skad ces smras so/ /

Then Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, from a distance of a hundred and ten yojanas, extended his hand and placed it upon the head of Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, who was in the town of Sumanāmukha, and said,
Then Manjushri extended his hand over a hundred and ten leagues and laid it on the head of Sudhana, who was standing in the city of Sumanamukha, and said,

rigs kyi bu/ legs so/ /legs so/ / dad pa'i dbang po dang mi ldan pa/ sems skyo ba can/ bsam pa zhum pa can/ sbyor ba bor ba/ brtson 'grus ldog pa/ yon tan cung zad kyis dga' bar rtsi ba/ dge ba'i rtsa ba gcig la zhen par gnas pa/ spyod pa dang / smon lam mngon par sgrub pa la mi mkhas pa/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyis yongs su ma bzung ba/ sangs rgyas kyis ma dgongs pa rnams kyis ni/ chos nyid 'di lta bu yongs su shes par bya ba dang / tshul 'di lta bu dang / spyod yul 'di lta bu dang / gnas 'di lta bu yongs su shes par bya ba dang / rnam par shes par bya ba'am/ khong du chud par bya ba'am/ 'jug par bya ba'am/ yid ches par bya ba'am/ brtag par bya ba'am/ rtog par bya ba'am/ thob par bya bar mi nus so/ /zhes te/

“Well done, well done, noble one! Someone who does not have the power of faith, who has a mind that wearies, who has thoughts of despondency, who abandons practice, who turns away from diligence, who is pleased by having a few qualities, who remains clinging to a single root of merit, who is not skilled in accomplishing the conduct and prayer, who is not in the care of a kalyāṇamitra, and who does not consider the buddhas is unable to know the true nature of phenomena in this way, or to know this kind of way and this kind of range of activity, or to know this kind of place or enter it, or to believe in it or examine it or understand it or attain it.”

“Good, good! Those without the faculty of faith, those who are weary or sluggish in mind, those who have not accumulated efforts, those whose vigor recedes, those who are satisfied with meager virtues, those imbued with only one root of goodness, those unskilled in carrying out practical vows, those who are not in the care of spiritual benefactors, those who are not minded by the buddhas, cannot know this true nature, this principle, this sphere, this abode—they are unable to know, to fathom, to penetrate, to believe, to conceive, to know exactly, or to attain.”

des de la chos kyi gtam gyis yang dag par bstan pa dang / yang dag par bskul ba dang / gzengs bstod pa dang / dga' bar byas te chos kyi sgo grangs med pa dang ldan par byas nas ye shes mtha' yas pa'i snang ba chen po thob par byas te byang chub sems dpa'i gzungs dang / spobs pa dang / ting nge 'dzin dang / mngon par shes pa dang / ye shes mtha' yas pa'i byin gyis byin du brlabs par byas te kun tu bzang po'i spyod pa'i dkyil 'khor la bzhag nas bdag gi yul la'ang rab tu bzhag ste/ tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gi drung nas song ngo/ /

Then Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta taught Sudhana by speaking of the Dharma and, having inspired him, extolled him, and gladdened him, made him the possessor of countless Dharma gateways, so that he attained the great illumination of infinite wisdom. He blessed him with a bodhisattva’s retention, eloquence, samādhi, higher cognitions, and infinite wisdom and established him in the field of completely good conduct, and he remained in his own region and departed from the presence of Sudhana, the head merchant’s son.

Having caused Sudhana to see by means of his spiritual talk, having directed him, inspired him, gladdened him, imbued him with countless facets of truth, illumined him with the great light of infinite knowledge, led him into the endless mental command, presence of mind, concentration, and superknowledge of enlightening beings, plunged him into the sphere of universally good practice, and established him in his own place, Manjushri left the presence of Sudhana.
shin tu rgyas pa chen po'i mdo/ sangs rgyas phal po che zhes bya ba las/ sdong pos brgyan pa'i le'u ste/ bzhi bcu rtsa lnga pa'o// ;;
shin tu rgyas pa chen po'i mdo/ / sangs rgyas phal po che zhes bya ba las/ sdong pos brgyan pa'i le'u ste/ bam po brgya bco lnga pa ste/ tha ma/

d.crumb: [nor bzang gis dge ba'i bshes gnyen bsnyen bkur ba'i spyod pa]

f.d: [nor bzang gis dge ba'i bshes gnyen bsnyen bkur ba'i spyod pa]

d.crumb: 56. Samantabhadra and “The Prayer for Completely Good Conduct”

f.d: Chapter 56. Samantabhadra and “The Prayer for Completely Good Conduct”

d.crumb: The Vow of Practice of Universal Good

f.d: The Vow of Practice of Universal Good

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang dge ba'i bshes gnyen stong gsum gyi stong chen po'i 'jig rten gyi khams kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed bsnyen bkur ba/ thams cad mkhyen pa nyid du tshogs bsags pa'i sems dang ldan pa/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen thams cad kyi gdams ngag dang / rjes su bstan pa la mthun par 'dzin pas zhugs pa/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen thams cad kyi drung du bsam pa mnyam pas 'gro ba/

Then Sudhana, attending as many spiritual benefactors as atoms in a billion-world universe, his mind having accumulated the provisions for omniscience, acting on the instructions of all spiritual benefactors with correct understanding, his mind equally attentive to all spiritual friends,

dge ba'i bshes gnyen thams cad dga' bar bya bas yid mi dbyung ba'i blo dang ldan pa/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen thams cad kyi gdams ngag dang / rjes su bstan pa'i tshul rgya mtsho'i rjes su song ba/ snying rje chen po'i bsam pa rgya mtsho las yang dag par byung ba'i snying po dang ldan pa; byams pa chen po'i tshul gyi sprin gyis 'gro ba thams cad rnam par snang bar byed pa/ dga' ba chen po'i shugs rnam par 'phel ba'i lus dang ldan pa/

his intellect in harmony with all spiritual friends without emotion, following the ocean of principles of the advice and instruction of all spiritual friends, filled with universal compassion, illumining all beings with universal love, physically blissful,

byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa rgya chen po la rab tu zhi bar rnam par spyod pa/ sgo thams cad nas lhag par 'phro ba'i gtong ba'i mig dang ldan pa/ de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi yon tan rgya mtsho'i nan tan rab tu rdzogs pa/ de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi mos pa'i lam du zhugs pa/

who was active[2179] in complete peace within the vast bodhisattva liberations; who had the vision focused on whatever emanates from all gateways;[2180] who had perfected the practice of the ocean of the qualities of all tathāgatas;[2181] who had followed the path of aspiration of all the tathāgatas;[2182]

abiding at peace in the vast liberation of enlightening beings, his equanimous vision attentive to all dimensions, having accomplished the ocean of virtues of all buddhas, on the path of resolve of all buddhas,

thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi tshogs la brtson 'grus kyi shugs rnam par 'phel bas byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi sems dang / bsam pas shin tu sbyangs pa'i blo dang ldan pa/ dus gsum gyi de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa la zhugs pa/ sangs rgyas thams cad kyi chos kyi tshul rgya mtsho khong du chud pa/

strengthened by the energy of vigor of preparation for omniscience, his mind thoroughly dedicated to the will of all enlightening beings, comprehending the succession of all buddhas of past, present, and future, awake to the ocean of principles of all enlightened teachings,

de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi 'khor lo'i rgya mtsho'i rjes su song ba/ 'jig rten gyi skye gnas thams cad du gzugs brnyan yongs su ston pa'i spyod yul dang ldan pa/ byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi smon lam gyi tshul rgya mtsho la zhugs pa/ bskal pa thams cad du byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la rab tu zhugs pa/

following the ocean of principles of the wheels of teaching of all buddhas, in the realm of manifesting reflections of life in all worlds, immersed in the principles of the vows of all enlightening beings, set out to carry on enlightening practice throughout all ages,
thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi yul snang ba rab tu thob pa/ byang chub sems dpa'i dbang po thams cad rnam par 'phel ba/ thams cad mkhyen pa'i lam snang ba rab tu thob pa/
seeing the realm of omniscience, having developed all the faculties of enlightening beings, aware of the path of omniscience,
phyogs thams cad du sgrib pa med pa'i snang ba rab tu thob pa/
who had attained the unobscured illumination of all directions;
chos kyi dbyings thams cad kyi tshul la rab tu zhugs pa'i blo dang ldan pa/
who had the realization that pervades the ways of the entire realm of phenomena;
his intellect focused on all the principles of the reality realm,

zhing gi tshul thams cad la snang ba rab tu grub pa/ sems can 'byams klas pa thams cad kyi don bya ba la rgyud dang mi mthun pa med par rjes su song ba/ sgrib pa'i g.yang sa'i ri thams cad rnam par 'thor ba/ sgrib pa med pa'i chos kyi rjes su song ba/

illumining the principles of all lands, following the course of beneficial action extending to all beings, shattering the precipitous mountains of spiritual impediments, according with the unimpeded nature of reality,

byang chub sems dpa'i rnam par thar pa sa'i gzhi kun tu gnas pa'i chos kyi dbyings kyi snying po can la rab tu zhi bar rnam par dpyod pa/ de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi spyod yul rjes su tshol ba/ de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyis byin gyis brlabs pa
abiding at peace in the liberation of enlightening beings containing the universal reality realm, investigating the realm of all buddhas, empowered by all buddhas,
de byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po'i spyod yul la rnam par dpyod cing 'dug par gyur te/
who was established in being active[2184] in the range of activity of a bodhisattva;
stood contemplating the realm of the enlightening being Universally Good.

byang chub sems dpa' sems dpa' chen po kun tu bzang po'i ming thos pa dang / byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa thos pa dang / smon lam gyi khyad par thos pa dang / tshogs yongs su sgrub pa la 'jug pa dang / gnas pa'i khyad par thos pa dang /

Having heard the name of the enlightening being Universally Good, his practice of enlightenment, the excellence of his vow, the excellence of basing his undertaking on the provisions for enlightenment,
mngon par sgrub pa dang / 'byung ba'i lam gyi khyad par thos pa dang / kun tu bzang po'i sa'i tshul gyi rgyud thos pa dang / sa'i tshogs thos pa dang / sa thob par byed pa'i shugs thos pa dang /
the excellence of his expertise in accomplishment, his conduct in the stage of universal good, his preparations for the stages, the excellence of his attainment,
sa yongs su gnon pa thos pa dang / sa la gnas pa thos pa dang / sa sngon du 'dor bas gnon pa thos pa dang / sa'i spyod yul thos pa dang /
the speed of his attainment of the stages, his entry into the stages, his stabilization in the stages, his progress through the stages,
sa'i byin gyi rlabs thos pa dang / sa la yang dag par gnas pa thos nas
who had heard of the blessings of that level; who had heard of his dwelling on that level;
his importance in the stages, his mastery of the stages, and his abiding in the stages,
byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po mthong bar dga' zhing skom ste
and who yearned and thirsted for the sight of the bodhisattva Samantabhadra;
Sudhana, eager to see the enlightening being Samantabhadra, Universally Good,
sat on a lotus seat of jewels facing the lionthrone of the Buddha on the enlightenment site there filled with oceans of diamonds,

nam mkha'i dbyings ltar shin tu yangs pa'i sems mngon par zhen pa thams cad las gyen du 'phags pa dang / zhing gi 'du shes shin tu bsgoms pa dang / chags pa thams cad las yang dag par 'das pa'i sems chos thams cad la sgrib pa med pa'i spyod yul can dang /

with a mind as vast as space and free from all attachments, with perception of all lands well developed, with a mind having transcended all barriers and clingings, with a mind unimpeded, in the realm of nonobstruction in the midst of all things,

thogs pa med pa'i sems phyogs rgya mtsho thams cad rgyas par 'gengs pa dang / sgrib pa med pa'i sems thams cad mkhyen pa nyid yul yongs su gnon pa dang / shin tu rnam par dag pa'i sems snying po byang chub kyi rgyan lhag mthong gis yongs su dag pa dang / shin tu rnam par phye ba'i sems sangs rgyas thams cad kyi chos rgya mtsho la zhugs pa dang /

with a mind freely pervading everywhere without hindrance, with a pure mind entering the realm of omniscience, with a well-ordered mind purified by observing the ornaments of the site of enlightenment, with a broad mind immersed in the ocean of all enlightened teachings,
shin tu yangs pa'i sems sems can gyi khams thams cad yongs su smin par bya ba dang / gdul ba rgyas par 'gengs pa dang /
with a vast mind that pervaded all realms of beings in order to ripen and guide them;
with a vast mind pervading all realms of beings to guide them to perfection,
shin tu che ba'i sems sangs rgyas kyi zhing thams cad yongs su dag par byed pa dang /
with an immense[2186] mind that purified all buddha realms;
with an immeasurable mind purifying all buddha-lands,
tshad med pa'i sems sangs rgyas thams cad kyi 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor du gzugs brnyan rab tu 'byung ba dang /
with a measureless mind that manifested his appearance within the assemblies of the followers of all buddhas;
with an infinite mind reflected in the circles of all buddhas,
bskal pa thams cad du gnas pas mi zad cing mthar thug pa med pa'i sems/ de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi stobs dang / mi bsnyengs pa dang / sangs rgyas kyi chos kyi ma 'dres pa'i mthar thug pas
and with an inexhaustible and endless mind that dwelled in all kalpas and had the conclusive strengths, fearlessnesses, and unique qualities of all the tathāgatas,
abiding indefatigably for all ages, until the ultimate realization of the power, expertise, and unique qualities of all buddhas.
snying po byang chub rdo rje dam pa'i snying po can de la pad+mo'i stan rin po che thams cad kyi lhun can zhig la de bzhin gshegs pa'i gdan seng+ge'i khri la mngon par bltas te 'dug go /
Sudhana, in the bodhimaṇḍa, which had the supreme vajra as its essence, was seated upon a lotus seat that was a mass of all jewels, gazing at the lion throne that was the seat of the Tathāgata.

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang de lta bu'i bsam pa dang / yid la bya ba la brtson par gnas pa'i sngon gyi dge ba'i rtsa ba'i rlan dang / de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi byin gyi rlabs dang / byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po dang / sngon gyi dge ba'i rtsa ba'i skal pa mthun pas byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po mthong bar 'gyur bar sngon gyi ltas bcu byung ngo/ /

Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, who was dedicated to that kind of aspiration and attention, was saturated by previous roots of merit, was blessed by the tathāgatas, and had the equivalent roots of merit in the past as the bodhisattva Samantabhadra, and therefore there appeared ten omens of the appearance of the bodhisattva Samantabhadra.

Furthermore, to Sudhana, engaged in these meditations, there appeared ten signs prefiguring the vision of the enlightening being Universally Good, by virtue of the empowerment of all buddhas having nourished his past roots of goodness, and by virtue of having past roots of goodness equivalent to those of the enlightening being Universally Good.

bcu gang zhe na/ 'di lta ste/ sangs rgyas kyi zhing thams cad de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi snying po byang chub kyi rgyan rnam par dag pas rnam par dag par gyur to/ / sangs rgyas kyi zhing thams cad mi khom pa dang / ngan song dang / ngan 'gro'i lam thams cad rnam par bsal bas rnam par dag par gyur to/ / sangs rgyas kyi zhing thams cad pad+mo'i tshal gyi rgyan ltar sangs rgyas kyi zhing rnam par dag pas rnam par dag par gyur to/ / sangs rgyas kyi zhing thams cad sems can thams cad kyi lus dang / sems dga' zhing sim par byed pas rnam par dag par gyur to/ / sangs rgyas kyi zhing thams cad rin po che thams cad kyi rang bzhin du kun tu gnas pas rnam par dag par gyur to/ / sangs rgyas kyi zhing thams cad sems can gyi khams kun mtshan dang dpe byad bzang pos rab tu brgyan par kun nas gnas pas rnam par dag par gyur to/ / sangs rgyas kyi zhing thams cad rgyan dang lhab lhub kyi sprin gyis kun tu khebs par kun tu gnas pas rnam par dag par gyur to/ / sangs rgyas kyi zhing thams cad sems can gyi khams thams cad phan tshun byams pa'i sems dang / phan pa'i sems dang / gnod sems med pa'i sems dang ldan par kun nas gnas pas rnam par dag par gyur to/ / sangs rgyas kyi zhing thams cad snying po byang chub kyi rgyan gyis brgyan par kun nas gnas pas rnam par dag par gyur to/ / sangs rgyas kyi zhing thams cad sems can thams cad sangs rgyas rjes su dran pa yid la bya ba la brtson par kun nas gnas pas rnam par dag par gyur te/ byang chub sems dpa' sems dpa' chen po kun tu bzang po mthong bar 'gyur ba'i sngon gyi ltas bcu po de dag byung bar gyur to/ /

What were those ten? They were that (1) all buddha realms were purified through having pure adornments at the bodhimaṇḍas of all tathāgatas; (2) all buddha realms were purified through the elimination of all their unfortunate states, lower existences, and lower realms; (3) all buddha realms were purified through becoming pure buddha realms with arrays of lotus[2187] beds; (4) all buddha realms were purified through the bodies and minds of all their beings becoming joyous and happy; (5) all buddha realms were purified through becoming made of all precious materials; (6) all buddha realms were purified through all their realms of beings becoming adorned by the signs and features of a great being; (7) all buddha realms were purified through being covered by clouds of adornments and decorations; (8) all buddha realms were purified through all their beings having a nature that was mutually loving, altruistic, and without malice; (9) all buddha realms were purified through their bodhimaṇḍas becoming adorned by adornments; and (10) all buddha realms were purified through all their beings becoming dedicated to remembering and focusing on the buddhas. Those were the ten omens of the appearance of the bodhisattva mahāsattva Samantabhadra.

What were those ten signs? All buddha-lands were purified by purification with the adornments of the sites of enlightenment of all buddhas. All buddha-lands were purified by removal of all evils and miserable states and conditions inopportune for enlightenment. All buddha-lands were purified by purification of buddha-lands with arrays of spiritual lotus ponds. All buddha-lands were purified by cooling and refreshing the bodies and minds of all beings. All buddha-lands were purified by becoming made of jewels. All buddha-lands were purified by all the beings becoming adorned with the marks and embellishments of greatness. All buddha-lands were purified by formation of masses of all adornments. All buddha-lands were purified by all the beings becoming kind, benevolent, and friendly to each other. All buddha-lands were purified by becoming arrayed with the adornments of sites of enlightenment. All buddha-lands were purified by all the beings becoming consciously absorbed in mindfulness of Buddha. These ten signs appeared foreshadowing the vision of the great enlightening being Universally Good.
gzhan yang byang chub sems dpa' sems dpa' chen po mthong bar 'gyur ba'i sngon gyi ltas snang ba chen po bcu byung bar gyur te/
There also appeared ten lights that were omens of the appearance of the bodhisattva Samantabhadra.
After that, ten great lights appeared, foreshadowing the manifestation of the great enlightening being Universally Good.
bcu gang zhe na; 'di lta ste/
What were those ten? They were that
What were the ten?
'jig rten gyi khams thams cad kyi rdul shin tu phra ba rnams las shin tu phra ba re re zhing yang de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi 'od zer gyi dra ba mang po rnam par snang bar gyur to/ /
(1) from each atom of the atoms of all world realms shone a multitude of nets of light rays from all tathāgatas;
In each atom of all worlds the network of all buddhas shone.

'jig rten gyi khams thams cad kyi rdul shin tu phra ba rnams las rdul shin tu phra ba re re las kyang sangs rgyas thams cad kyi 'od kyi dkyil 'khor mang po thon te/ kha dog gcig pa dang / kha dog sna tshogs dang / kha dog brgya stong du mar chos kyi dbyings thams cad rgyas par 'gengs par gyur to/ /

(2) from each atom of the atoms of all world realms emerged a multitude of halos of buddhas, some of a single color, some of various colors, some with many hundreds of thousands of colors, spreading throughout the entire realm of phenomena;
The auras of light of all buddhas emanated from each atom of all worlds, with hundreds of thousands of various colors, and pervaded the whole cosmos.

'jig rten gyi khams thams cad kyi rdul shin tu phra ba rnams las rdul shin tu phra ba re re las kyang rin po che thams cad kyi sprin de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi gzugs brnyan rnam par dmigs par byed pa mang po thon te chos kyi dbyings thams cad rgyas par 'gengs par gyur to/ /
(3) from each atom of the atoms of all world realms emerged clouds of all jewels creating the perception of the images of all tathāgatas spreading throughout the entire realm of phenomena;
Clouds of jewels manifesting reflections of all buddhas emanated from each atom of all worlds and pervaded the cosmos.

'jig rten gyi khams thams cad kyi rdul shin tu phra ba rnams las rdul shin tu phra ba re re las kyang de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi 'od 'phro ba'i 'khor lo dang / dkyil 'khor gyi sprin mang po thon te chos kyi dbyings thams cad rgyas par 'gengs par gyur to/ /
(4) from each atom of the atoms of all world realms emerged wheels, and circles of the light radiated from all tathāgatas spreading throughout the entire realm of phenomena;
Multitudes of circles of flames of all buddhas emanated from each atom of all worlds and pervaded the cosmos.

'jig rten gyi khams thams cad kyi rdul shin tu phra ba rnams las rdul shin tu phra ba re re las kyang spos dang / me tog dang / phreng ba dang / byug pa dang / bdug pa'i sprin mang po thon te byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po'i yon tan gyi chos rgya mtsho'i sprin thams cad kyi 'brug sgra rab tu sgrog cing / phyogs bcu'i chos kyi dbyings thams cad rgyas par 'gengs par gyur to/ /

(5) from each atom of the atoms of all world realms emerged a multitude of clouds of perfume, flowers, garlands, ointments, and incense that resounded with thunder from all the clouds that proclaimed the ocean of the phenomena of the qualities of the bodhisattva Samantabhadra, spreading throughout the entire realm of phenomena;

Multitudes of all kinds of fragrant flowers, garlands, perfumes, and incenses emanated from each atom of all worlds and pervaded the cosmos radiating the light of the enlightening being Universally Good.

'jig rten gyi khams thams cad kyi rdul shin tu phra ba rnams las rdul shin tu phra ba re re las kyang nyi ma dang / zla ba dang / skar ma'i sprin mang po thon te byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po'i 'od rab tu 'gyed cing / chos kyi dbyings thams cad rgyas par 'gengs par gyur to/ /

(6) from each atom of the atoms of all world realms emerged multitudes of clouds of suns, moons, and stars, emanating the light of the bodhisattva Samantabhadra, spreading throughout the entire realm of phenomena;

'jig rten gyi khams thams cad kyi rdul shin tu phra ba rnams las rdul shin tu phra ba re re las kyang lus thams cad kyi dbyibs ltar 'dug pa'i mar me'i sprin mang po thon nas sangs rgyas kyi 'od zer ltar rab tu snang bar byed cing / chos kyi dbyings thams cad rgyas par 'gengs par gyur to/ /

(7) from each atom of the atoms of all world realms emerged multitudes of clouds of lamps in the shapes of all bodies,[2188] shining like the light rays of buddhas and spreading throughout the entire realm of phenomena;
Multitudes of lamps in the forms of all beings emanated from each atom of all worlds and pervaded the cosmos.

'jig rten gyi khams thams cad kyi rdul shin tu phra ba rnams las rdul shin tu phra ba re re las kyang nor bu rin po che'i gzugs de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi skur snang ba'i sprin mang po thon nas phyogs bcu'i 'jig rten gyi khams thams cad rgyas par 'gengs par gyur to/ /

(8) from each atom of the atoms of all world realms emerged multitudes of clouds of figures made of precious jewels that represent the bodies of the tathāgatas, spreading throughout all the world realms in the ten directions;

'jig rten gyi khams thams cad kyi rdul shin tu phra ba rnams las rdul shin tu phra ba re re las kyang 'od zer gyi gzugs de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi sku'i dbyibs su snang ba'i sprin mang po thon te sangs rgyas thams cad kyi byin gyi rlabs dang / smon lam gyi sprin gyi char mngon par 'bebs shing / chos kyi dbyings thams cad rgyas par 'gengs par gyur to/ /

(9) from each atom of the atoms of all world realms emerged multitudes of clouds of figures made of light rays that appeared in the forms of the bodies of all the tathāgatas, sending down rain from the clouds of the blessings and prayers of all the buddhas and spreading throughout the entire realm of phenomena; and
Multitudes of figures of light beams in the forms of the bodies of all buddhas emanated from each atom of all worlds and pervaded the cosmos showing the basic vows of all buddhas.

'jig rten gyi khams thams cad kyi rdul shin tu phra ba rnams las rdul shin tu phra ba re re las kyang byang chub sems dpa'i lus kyi gzugs brnyan gzugs kyi rnam pa thams cad kyi kha dog tu snang ba'i sprin rgya mtsho sems can thams cad gdon pa'i sbyor ba dang ldan pa/ sems can thams cad kyi chos kyi bsam pa yongs su rdzogs par sgrub pa mang po thon te chos kyi dbyings thams cad rgyas par 'gengs par gyur to/ /

(10) from each atom of the atoms of all world realms emerged an ocean of clouds of the images with the appearance of all kinds of forms of the bodies of bodhisattvas, engaged in liberating[2189] all beings and accomplishing the fulfillment of the Dharma aspirations of all beings and spreading throughout the entire realm of phenomena.

Oceans of multitudes of reflections of enlightening beings of all forms and appearances, representations of phantom bodies of all beings, fulfilling the wishes of all beings, emanated from each point of all worlds and pervaded the cosmos.
byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po mthong bar 'gyur ba'i sngon gyi ltas snang ba chen po bcu po de dag byung bar gyur to/ /
Those were the ten great lights that were omens of the appearance of the bodhisattva mahāsattva Samantabhadra.
These ten great lights appeared foreshadowing the manifestation of Universally Good.

de nas tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis sngon gyi ltas su snang ba bcu po de dag mthong nas byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po mthong bar 'gyur ba'i skabs ni/ bye/ rang gi dge ba'i rtsa bas ni/ brtan/ de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi byin gyis ni/ brlabs/ sangs rgyas thams cad kyi chos kyi snang ba ni/ yang dag par skyes/ byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po'i spyod pa la ni/ mngon du gyur/ byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po ni smon lam gyi byin gyis ni/ byin du brlabs/ de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi spyod yul la ni/ mngon par mos/ byang chub sems dpa'i spyod yul rlabs po che la shin tu nges pa'i stobs dang shugs ni/ rab tu thob/ byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po mthong na/ thams cad mkhyen pa nyid thob pa dang 'dra bar ni/ sems/ byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po mthong bar bya ba la dbang po ni/ mngon du gyur/ byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po mthong bar bya ba la brtson 'grus kyi shugs chen po ni/ thob/ byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po yongs su btsal ba la brtson 'grus phyir mi ldog pa'i sbyor ba dang ni/ ldan/

When Sudhana, the head merchant’s son, had seen those ten great lights as omens, he gained the opportunity to see Samantabhadra. He had the support of his own roots of merit. He had the blessing of all the tathāgatas and had given rise to the illumination of the Dharma of all the buddhas. He was focused on the conduct of the bodhisattva Samantabhadra. He was blessed by the prayers of the bodhisattva Samantabhadra. He aspired to the range of conduct of all the tathāgatas. He had attained the strength and power of certainty in the immense field of activity of the bodhisattva. He thought that seeing the bodhisattva Samantabhadra would be the same as attaining omniscience. His faculties were directed to seeing the bodhisattva Samantabhadra. He had gained the great power of diligence for seeing the bodhisattva Samantabhadra. He applied himself with unflagging diligence in seeking the sight of the bodhisattva Samantabhadra.

Then Sudhana, having seen these ten foreshadowing lights, had the opportunity to see the enlightening being Universally Good, supported by the power of his own roots of goodness, a living manifestation of all buddha-teachings, empowered by all buddhas, immersed in the vows of the enlightening being Universally Good, in the presence of the realm of all buddhas, having the power of certainty of the lofty realm of enlightening beings, perceiving the attainment of the light of omniscience in the sight of the enlightening being Universally Good, his senses directed toward vision of the enlightening being Universally Good, flooded with great energy for the vision of the enlightening being Universally Good, striving unremittingly in the search for the enlightening being Universally Good,

phyogs thams cad du mngon du gyur pa'i dbang po'i 'khor lo dang / kun tu lta bas yul yongs su gnod pa'i byang chub sems dpa'i lus dang / sangs rgyas ma lus pa'i zhabs kyi drung na byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po'dug pa'i rjes su 'brang ba'i sems de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad dmigs par bya ba la yang dag par btang ba dang / byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po'i dmigs pa yongs su btsal ba dang mi 'bral ba'i bsam pa dang / byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po mthong bar bya ba'i 'du shes kyi rnam pa'i snying po dang ldan pa'i ye shes kyi mig byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po'i lam la zhugs pa dang / nam mkha'i dbyings ltar yangs pa'i bsam pa dang / snying rje chen po'i rdo rje thogs pa'i lhag pa'i bsam pa dang /

With the wheel of his faculties facing in all directions; with the body of a bodhisattva that has reached the all-seeing[2190] range of perception; with a mind fixed on the bodhisattva Samantabhadra as being present at the feet of all buddhas without exception; with a focus on all buddhas as the object of his perception; with an aspiration that never ceased to seek the bodhisattva Samantabhadra as an object of perception; with the eyes of wisdom that follow the path of the bodhisattva Samantabhadra having as their essence the idea of seeing the bodhisattva Samantabhadra; with an aspiration that was as vast as space; with a higher motivation that possessed the thunderbolt of great compassion;

with the sphere of his senses turned to all directions, with the body of an enlightening being entering the sphere of the eye of universal good, with a mind directed toward all buddhas and aware of the enlightening being Universally Good in the presence of all buddhas, with a will seeking unremittingly for the enlightening being Universally Good, inwardly perceiving the vision of the enlightening being Universally Good in all objects, with the eye of knowledge on the path of the enlightening being Universally Good, with a mind as vast as space, with a powerful resolve supported by indestructible universal compassion,
with a vow to accompany the enlightening being Universally Good throughout all time, with purity of manner equally following the practice of the enlightening being Universally Good,
byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po'i sa la gnas pa'i ye shes la rnam par spyod pa/ de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi yul la yang dag par gnas pa dang ni ldan pa
abiding in knowledge based on the state of the enlightening being Universally Good, dwelling in the sphere of all those who realize Thusness,
des byang chub sems dpa' kun tu bzang po
he saw the bodhisattva Samantabhadra,
he saw the enlightening being Universally Good
sitting on a lion seat in the calyx of a great jewel lotus in front of Vairocana Buddha, the perfectly enlightened one, in an ocean of enlightening beings,

de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad nas mnyam pa nyid rjes su thob pa/ dus gsum mnyam pa nyid kyi rjes su song ba/ bsam gyis mi khyab pa'i yul dang ldan pa/ mi 'phrog pa'i spyod yul can/ mu med pa'i ye shes kyi yul dang ldan pa/ byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyis rnam par blta ba/ 'jig rten thams cad kyis zil gyis mi non pa/ 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor thams cad kyi rjes su 'brang na mngon par 'phags pa'i lus dang ldan pa de/

who had attained equality with all tathāgatas, who followed the three times equally, who possessed an inconceivable field of perception, who had an inviolable conduct, who had a limitless field of perception of wisdom, who was looked upon by all bodhisattvas, who could not be surpassed by all worlds, who was followed by all assemblies of followers, and who possessed a superior field of perception.

his body standing out among the whole assembly, unexcelled by any worldlings, looking over all the enlightening beings, his knowledge endless, his range insuperable, his sphere inconceivable, having arrived at equality of past, present and future and attained equality with all buddhas.

bcom ldan 'das de bzhin gshegs pa rnam par snang mdzad kyi spyan snga na byang chub sems dpa'i 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor rgya mtsho na ni/ 'dug /byang chub sems dpa'i tshogs kyis ni/ yongs su bskor/ byang chub sems dpa'i dge 'dun na/ mdun du byas shing / seng+ge'i khri rin po che'i pad+mo chen po'i snying po can zhig la 'dug pa mthong ste/

He was seated on a great precious lotus on the center of a lion throne in front of the Tathāgata Arhat Samyaksaṃbuddha, the Bhagavat Vairocana, with an ocean of an assembly of bodhisattva followers, at the head of a gathering of bodhisattvas.
[*see above]

des de'i ba spu'i bu ga thams cad kyi ba spu'i sgo re re nas kyang 'jig rten gyi khams thams cad kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi 'od zer gyi sprin mang po thon nas 'jig rten gyi khams chos kyi dbyings kyis klas pa/ nam mkha'i mthas gtugs pa thams cad rab tu snang bar byas nas sems can rnams kyi sdug bsngal rab tu zhi bar byed pa mthong ngo/ /

He saw that from all the pores on his body, from each of those pores, emerged multitudes of clouds of light rays that illuminated all world realms throughout the extent of the realm of phenomena to its limits and brought an end to the suffering of beings.

He saw clouds of light rays as numerous as atoms in all buddha-lands emanate from each of Universally Good’s pores and illumine all worlds throughout the space of the cosmos, relieving the pain of all beings.
des de'i lus las 'od kyi dkyil 'khor sangs rgyas kyi zhing thams cad kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed kyi sprin mang po kha dog sna tshogs can mang po thon te/
He saw as many auras of light as atoms in all buddha-lands emanate from Universally Good’s body,
byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi dga' ba dang / mos pa'i shugs rgya chen po rnam par 'phel bar byed pa mthong ngo/ /
He saw him increasing the vast power of joy and aspiration in all bodhisattvas.
increasing the ecstasy of all enlightening beings.

spyi po dang phrag pa'i lhun gnyis dang / ba spu'i sgo thams cad nas kyang spos 'od 'phro ba'i sprin gyi char kha dog sna tshogs su 'dug pa mang po mngon par thon nas de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor rgyas par bkang ste mngon par 'bab pa mthong ngo/ /

He saw emanating from the crown of his head, his two shoulders, and all his pores a multitude of clouds of perfumes and lights of various colors, which spread throughout the assemblies of the followers of all tathāgatas and let fall their rain.
He saw clouds of fragrant flames of various colors emanate from Universally Good’s head and pores, pervading the audiences of all buddhas and showering on them.

ba spu'i bu ga thams cad las ba spu'i sgo re re nas kyang me tog thams cad kyi sprin gyi char sangs rgyas kyi zhing thams cad kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed mang po mngon par thon nas de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor rgyas par bkang ste mngon par 'bab pa mthong ngo/ /

He saw that from all the pores on his body, from each of those pores, emerged multitudes of clouds of all flowers, which were as numerous as the atoms in all buddha realms and which spread throughout the assemblies of the followers of all tathāgatas and let fall their rain.
He saw as many clouds of all kinds of flowers as atoms in all buddha-lands emanate from each of Universally Good’s pores, filling the audiences of all buddhas and showering on them.

ba spu'i bu ga thams cad las ba spu'i sgo re re las kyang spos sna tshogs kyi shing gi sprin mang po sangs rgyas kyi zhing thams cad kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed mngon par thon nas chos kyi dbyings nam mkha'i dbyings kyi mthas klas pa thams cad rgyas par bkang nas spos kyi shing gi sprin gyi rgyan gyis brgyan par byas te spos dang / phye ma dang / bdug pa'i mdzod zad mi shes pa'i char rab tu 'gyed cing / de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor rgyas par bkang ste mngon par 'bab par byed pa mthong ngo/ /

He saw that from all the pores on his body, from each of those pores, emerged multitudes of clouds of various aromatic trees, which were as numerous as the atoms in all buddha realms and which spread throughout the realm of phenomena, throughout the entire realm of space to its limits, adorning it with the clouds of aromatic trees, letting fall a rain of an inexhaustible treasure of perfume, aromatic powders, and incense and spreading throughout the assemblies of the followers of all tathāgatas and letting fall their rain.

He saw as many clouds of all kinds of fragrant trees as atoms in all buddha-lands emanate from each of Universally Good’s pores, adorning all universes throughout space with fragrant trees budding with inexhaustible aromatic powders and oils, showering on the audiences of all buddhas.

ba spu'i sgo thams cad las ba spu'i sgo re re nas kyang gos sna tshogs kyi sprin mang po mngon par thon te/ chos kyi dbyings nam mkha'i dbyings kyi mthas klas pa thams cad kun nas yog par byas nas brgyan par mthong ngo/ /

He saw that from all the pores on his body, from each of those pores, emerged multitudes of clouds of various clothes, which spread over and adorned the entire realm of phenomena, the entire realm of space.
He saw clouds of all kinds of cloth emanate from every pore, covering all universes throughout space and decorating them.

ba spu'i bu ga thams cad las ba spu'i sgo re re nas kyang dar sna tshogs kyi lda ldi'i sprin dang / phreng ba sna tshogs kyi sprin dang / mu tig sna tshogs kyi sprin dang / nor bu rin po che yid bzhin gyi sprin gyi char sangs rgyas kyi zhing thams cad kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed mngon par thon nas de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor rgyas par bkang ste mngon par 'bab pa mthong ngo/ /

He saw that from all the pores on his body, from each of those pores, emerged clouds of streamers of silks in various colors, clouds of various garlands, clouds of various pearls, and clouds of wish-fulfilling precious jewels, which were as numerous as the atoms in all buddha realms and which spread throughout the assemblies of the followers of all tathāgatas and let fall their rain.

He saw clouds of streamers, ornaments, strings of pearls, and wish-fulfilling jewels, numerous as atoms in all buddha-lands, emanate from every pore, filling the assemblies of all buddhas and showering on them to fulfill the wishes of all beings.

ba spu'i bu ga thams cad las ba spu'i sgo'i re re nas kyang sems can thams cad kyi bsam pa yongs su rdzogs par bsgrub pa'i phyir rin po che'i shing gi sprin sangs rgyas kyi zhing thams cad kyi rdul shin tu phra ba snyed mngon par thon te chos kyi dbyings nam mkha'i mthas klas pa thams cad rgyas par bkang nas rin po che'i shing las rin po che'i mdzod rnam par 'phro ba'i rgyan gyis brgyan par byas te/ de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi 'khor gyi dkyil 'khor dag tu rin po che'i char chen po mngon par 'bab par byed pa mthong ngo/ /
