gang rnams phyogs bcu'i 'jig rten sgron ma dag / byang chub rim par sangs rgyas ma chags brnyes; ; mgon po de dag bdag gis thams cad la/ / 'khor lo bla na med pa bskor bar bskul/ /
I make the request to all the lords, The lamps of the worlds in the ten directions, Who have attained without impediment the enlightenment of buddhahood, That they turn the unsurpassable wheel. {10}
And all the Lamps of the Worlds in the ten directions Who have realized enlightenment and attain nonobstruction I seek as guides, that they may turn The supreme wheel of teaching.
mya ngan 'da' ston gang bzhed de dag la/ / 'gro ba kun la phan zhing bde ba'i phyir/ / bskal pa zhing gi rdul snyed bzhugs par yang / / bdag gis thal mo rab sbyar gsol bar bgyi/ /

With palms placed together, I supplicate Those who wish to manifest passing into nirvāṇa That they remain for as many kalpas as there are atoms in the realms, For the benefit and happiness of all beings. {11}
And those who wish to manifest extinction I petition respectfully to remain For eons as many as atoms in the land For the welfare and happiness of all beings.
phyag 'tshal ba dang mchod cing bshags pa dang / / rjes su yi rang bskul zhing gsol ba yi/ / dge ba cung zad bdag gis ci bsags pa/ / thams cad bdag gi byang chub phyir bsngo 'o/ /
Whatever little virtue[2211] I have accumulated Through homage, offering, confession, Rejoicing, supplication, and entreating, I dedicate it all to enlightenment. {12}
By honor, service, and direction, By appreciating, seeking, and requesting teachings, Whatever good I have accumulated, I dedicate it all to enlightenment.
'das pa'i sangs rgyas rnams dang phyogs bcu yi/ / 'jig rten dag na gang bzhugs mchod par gyur/ / gang yang ma byon de dag rab myur bar/ / bsam rdzogs byang chub rim par sangs rgyas spyon/ /

May the buddhas of the past and those who are present In the worlds of the ten directions be offered to. May those in the future swiftly fulfill Their aspirations for the enlightenment of buddhahood. {13}
May the buddhas of the past be honored, As well as those now in the worlds of the ten directions, And may those of the future be at ease, Filled with joy, having realized enlightenment.
phyogs bcu ga la'i zhing rnams ji snyed pa/ / de dag rgya cher yongs su dag par gyur/ / byang chub shing dbang drung gshegs rgyal ba dang / / sangs rgyas sras kyis rab tu gang bar shog /
May the realms that are in the ten directions Become purified and sublime.[2212] May they become filled with jinas, who have come To the Bodhi tree, the lord of trees, and with bodhisattvas. {14}
May all the lands of the ten directions Be purified, supreme, and filled With buddhas and enlightening beings At the tree of enlightenment.
phyogs bcu'i sems can gang rnams ji snyed pa/ / de dag rtag tu nad med bde bar gyur/ / 'gro ba kun gyi chos kyi don rnams ni/ / mthun par gyur cing re ba'ang 'grub par shog /
However many beings there are in the ten directions, May they all be always happy and healthy. May all beings be successful in their Dharma goals, And may their wishes be fulfilled. {15}
May all beings in the ten directions By happy and well; May all beings’ righteous aim be successful, May their hope be realized.
byang chub spyod pa dag ni bdag spyod cing / / 'gro ba kun tu skye ba dran par gyur/ / tshe rabs kun tu 'chi 'pho skye ba na/ / rtag tu bdag ni rab tu 'byung bar shog /
May I practice the conduct of enlightenment And remember my lives in all existences. May I always practice mendicancy In all my lifetimes of deaths and rebirths. {16}
As I am carrying out enlightenment practice, May I recall my lives in all states; In every lifetime, as I die and am reborn, May I always transcend the mundane.
rgyal ba kun gyi rjes su slob gyur te/ / bzang po spyod pa yongs su rdzogs byed cing / / tshul khrims spyod pa dri med yongs dag par/ / rtag tu ma nyams skyon med spyod par shog /
Following the teaching of all the jinas And perfecting my good conduct, May I always practice stainless, pure, Correct conduct that is flawless and unblemished. {17}
Learning from all buddhas, Fulfilling the practice of good, I will practice pure conduct, Always free from defect.
lha yi skad dang klu dang gnod sbyin skad/ / grul bum dag dang mi yi skad rnams dang / / 'gro ba kun gyi sgra rnams ji tsam par/ / thams cad skad du bdag gis chos bstan to/ /
May I teach the Dharma in all languages, Whatever the languages of beings: Through the languages of devas, the languages of nāgas, The languages of yakṣas, kumbhāṇḍas, and humans. {18}
I will expound the Teaching In the languages of gods and dragons, In the languages of demons and humans, And of all living beings.
des shing pha rol phyin la rab brtson te/ / byang chub sems ni nam yang brjed ma gyur/ / sdig pa gang rnams sgrib par 'gyur ba dag / de dag ma lus yongs su byang bar shog /
May one who is gentle[2213] and dedicated to the perfections Never forget the aspiration to enlightenment. May the obscurations of bad karma Be purified without any remainder. {19}
May those engaged in the ways of transcendence Not stray from enlightenment; And may all evils to be inhibited Be thoroughly extinguished.
las dang nyon mongs bdud kyi las rnams las/ / grol zhing 'jig rten 'gro ba rnams su yang / / ji ltar pad+mo rgyus mi chags pa bzhin/ / nyi zla nam mkhar thogs pa med ltar spyad/ /
May my conduct, even in the worldly existences, Be free of karma, kleśas, and the actions[2214] of Māra, Just as the lotus is unstained by water And the sun and moon are unobstructed in the sky. {20}
I will traverse the paths of the world Free from compulsion, affliction, and delusion, Like a lotus unstained by water, Like the sun and moon unattached in the sky.
zhing gi khyon dang phyogs rnams ji tsam par/ / ngan song sdug bsngal rab tu zhi bar byed; ; bde ba dag la 'gro ba kun 'god cing / / 'gro ba thams cad la ni phan par spyad/ /

May I end all the sufferings of lower existences And establish all beings in happiness, Practicing a conduct that brings benefit to all beings Throughout the directions and the extent[2215] of realms. {21}
Extinguishing all the miseries of bad states And bringing all beings to happiness, I will act for the welfare of all beings In all lands everywhere.
byang chub spyod pa yongs su rdzogs byed cing / / sems can dag gi spyod dang mthun par 'jug / bzang po spyod pa dag ni rab ston cing / / ma 'ongs bskal pa kun tu spyod par gyur/ /
May I practice this conduct in all future kalpas, Conforming with the conduct of beings, Perfecting the conduct of enlightenment, And teaching good conduct.[2216] {22}
According with the conduct of sentient beings While fulfilling the practice of enlightenment, And cultivating the practice of good, Thus will I act throughout future eons.
bdag gi spyod dang mtshungs par gang spyod pa/ / de dag dang ni rtag tu 'grogs par shog / lus dang ngag rnams dang ni sems kyis kyang / / spyod pa dag dang smon lam gcig tu spyad/ /
May I always be in the company of those Whose conduct is in harmony with my conduct. May my body, my speech, and also my mind Practice the same conduct and have the same prayer.[2217] {23}
May I always be in communion With those who share my practice; Physically, verbally, and mentally, I will carry out vows as one practice.
bdag la phan par 'dod pa'i grogs po dag / bzang po spyod pa rab tu ston pa rnams/ / de dag dang yang rtag tu phrad par shog / de dag bdag gis nam yang yid mi dbyung / /
May I always associate With friends who wish to benefit me And teach me the correct conduct, And may I never displease them. {24}
sangs rgyas sras kyis bskor ba'i mgon po rnams; ; mngon sum rtag tu bdag gis rgyal ba blta/ / ma 'ongs bskal pa kun tu mi skyo bar/ / de dag la yang mchod pa rgya cher bgyi/ /
May I always see before me the jinas, The lords who are encircled by bodhisattvas, And may I make vast[2218] offerings to them, Without wearying, throughout all future kalpas. {28}
May I always see the buddhas face to face, Surrounded by enlightening beings; I will make fine offerings to them Forever, unwearied.
rgyal ba rnams kyi dam pa'i chos 'dzin cing / / byang chub spyod pa kun tu snang bar byed/ / bzang po spyod pa rnam par spyod pa yang / / ma 'ongs bskal pa kun tu spyad par bgyi/ /
Keeping the good Dharma of the jinas, Expounding[2219] the conduct of enlightenment, And purifying the good conduct, May I practice that conduct in all future kalpas. {26}
Preserving the true teaching of buddhas, Illumining the practice of enlightenment, And purifying the practice of good, I will practice for all future eons.
srid pa thams cad du yang 'khor ba na/ / bsod nams ye shes dag ni mi zad rnyed/ / thabs dang shes rab ting 'dzin rnam thar dang / / yon tan kun gyi mi zad mdzod du gyur/ /
While circling through all existences, May I obtain inexhaustible merit and knowledge. May I be[2220] an inexhaustible treasure of wisdom, Methods, samādhis, liberations, and all good qualities. {27}
Migrating through all states of being, Having acquired inexhaustible virtue and knowledge, May I become an inexhaustible treasury of wisdom and means, Concentration, liberation, and all virtues.
rdul gcig steng na rdul snyed zhing rnams te/ / zhing der bsam gyis mi khyab sangs rgyas rnams/ / sangs rgyas sras kyi dbus na bzhugs pa la/ / byang chub spyad pa spyod cing blta bar bgyi/ /
There are realms as numerous as atoms in each atom, And while practicing the conduct of enlightenment, May I see in those realms countless buddhas Who are seated in the midst of bodhisattvas. {28}
As I carry on the practice of enlightenment, May I see the inconceivable buddhas sitting among enlightening beings In the lands as numerous as atoms That are in each atom.
de ltar ma lus thams cad phyogs su yang / / skra tsam khyon la dus gsum tshad snyed kyi/ / sangs rgyas rgya mtsho zhing rnams rgya mtsho dang / / bskal pa rgya mtshor spyod cing rab tu 'jug /

May I engage in practicing conduct for an ocean of kalpas Within every hair’s breadth in every direction, Without exception, in which there are an ocean Of buddhas of the three times, and an ocean of realms. {29}
Thus may I perceive the oceans Of buddhas and lands of all times In each point in the ten directions As I practice for myriad eons.
gsung gcig yan lag rgya mtsho'i sgra skad kyi/ / rgyal ba kun dbyangs yan lag rnam dag pa/ / 'gro ba kun gyi bsam pa ji bzhin dbyangs/ / sangs rgyas gsung la rtag tu 'jug par bgyi/ /

May I always comprehend[2221] the speech of the buddhas, Which, through having an ocean of languages in a single syllable, Has the purity of the aspects of the speech of all the jinas And words that accord with the aspirations of all beings.[2222] {30}

May I ever penetrate the eloquence of buddhas, The voices of all buddhas which adapt to mentalities, The purity of articulation of all buddhas, By the sounds of the ocean of tones in a single utterance.
dus gsum gshegs pa'i rgyal ba thams cad dag / 'khor lo tshul rnams rab tu bskor ba yi/ / de dag gi yang gsung dbyangs mi zad la/ / blo yi stobs kyis bdag kyang rab tu 'jug /
May I comprehend, through the power of the mind, The unceasing sounds of the voices Of the jinas in[2223] the three times, Who are turning the wheel in various ways.[2224] {31}
Into those infinite voices Of all buddhas of all times May I enter by buddha-power, Turning the wheel of teaching.
ma 'ongs bskal pa thams cad 'jug par yang / / skad cig gcig gis bdag kyang 'jug par bgyi/ / gang yang bskal pa dus gsum tshad de dag / skad cig cha shas kyis ni zhugs par spyad/ /
May I enter all the future kalpas, Entering them in a single instant, And in a fraction of an instant practice The conduct throughout the kalpas of the three times. {32}
May I enter all eons Of the future instantly, And may I act in all eons Of all times within an instant.
dus gsum gshegs pa mi yi seng+ge dag / de dag skad cig gcig la bdag gis blta/ / rtag tu de dag gi ni spyod yul la/ / sgyu mar gyur pa'i rnam thar stobs kyis 'jug /
May I in a single instant see The lions among humans in[2225] the three times. Through the power of the liberation of being an illusion, May I always enter into their conduct. {33}
May I see all buddhas of all times In one instant And always enter their sphere By the magical power of liberation.
gang yang dus gsum dag gi zhing bkod pa/ / de dag rdul gcig steng du mngon par sgrub/ / de ltar ma lus phyogs rnams thams cad du/ / rgyal ba rnams kyi zhing gi rgyan la 'jug /
May the displays of realms in the three times Be accomplished within a single atom. May I perceive such displays of the realms of the jinas That are in every direction without exception. {34}
May I produce the arrays of all lands Of all times in an atom, May I thus perceive all the arrays Of buddha-lands in all the ten directions.
gang yang ma byon 'jig rten sgron ma rnams/ / de dag rim par 'tshang rgya 'khor lo bskor/ / mya ngan 'das pa rab tu zhi mtha' ston/ / mgon po kun gyi drung du bdag mchi'o/ /
May I go into the presence of all those lords, Those future lamps of the world, who will successively Attain enlightenment, turn the wheel, And demonstrate the final peace of entering nirvāṇa. {35}
Learning the teachings of The Lamps of the Worlds to come, I visit all the Guides Who have passed away to eternal rest.
kun tu myur ba'i rdzu 'phrul stobs rnams dang / / kun nas sgo yi theg pa'i stobs dag dang / / kun tu yon tan spyod pa'i stobs rnams dang / / kun tu khyab pa byams pa dag gi stobs/ /

Through the power of miracles that has complete speed, Through the power of yānas[2226] that possesses every gateway, Through the power of conduct that has the complete qualities, Through the power of love that is universal, {36}
By occult powers, swift in all ways, By the power of knowledge, all-sided, By the power of practice, with all virtues, By the power of universal love,
kun tu dge ba'i bsod nams stobs rnams dang / / chags pa med par gyur pa'i ye shes stobs/ / shes rab thabs dang ting 'dzin stobs dag gis/ / byang chub stobs rnams yang dag sgrub par byed/ /

Through the power of merit that has complete goodness, Through the power of knowledge that is without impediment, Through the power of wisdom, methods, and samādhi, May I accomplish the power of enlightenment. {37}
By the power of goodness, all pure, By the power of knowledge, unobstructed, Gathering the power of enlightenment, Clearing away the power of acts,
las kyi stobs rnams yongs su dag byed cing / / nyon mongs stobs rnams kun tu 'joms par byed/ / bdud kyi stobs rnams stobs med rab byed cing / / bzang po spyod pa'i stobs ni rdzogs par bgyi/ /
May I purify the power of karma, Destroy the power of the kleśas, Render powerless the power of the māras, And make complete all the powers of good conduct. {38}
Destroying the power of afflictions, Vitiating the power of demons, May I fulfill all powers Of the practice of good.
zhing rnams rgya mtsho rnam par dag byed cing / / sems can rgya mtsho dag ni rnam par sgrol/ / chos rnams rgya mtsho rab tu mthong byed cing / / ye shes rgya mtsho rab tu rtogs par byed/ /
May I purify an ocean of realms, Liberate an ocean of beings, See an ocean of the Dharma, And realize[2227] an ocean of knowledge. {39}
Purifying oceans of lands, Liberating oceans of beings, Observing oceans of truths, Plumbing oceans of knowledge,
spyod pa rgya mtsho rnam par dag byed cing / / smon lam rgya mtsho rab tu rdzogs par byed/ / sangs rgyas rgya mtsho rab tu mchod byed cing / / bskal pa rgya mtshor mi skyo spyad par bgyi/ /
May I purify an ocean of conduct, Fulfill an ocean of prayers, Make offerings to an ocean of buddhas, And have tireless conduct for an ocean of kalpas. {40}
Perfecting oceans of practices, Fulfilling oceans of vows, Serving oceans of buddhas, May I practice, untiring, for oceans of eons.
gang yang dus gsum gshegs pa'i rgyal ba yi/ / byang chub spyod pa'i smon lam bye brag rnams/ / bzang po spyod pas byang chub sangs rgyas nas/ / de kun bdag gis ma lus rdzogs par bgyi/ /
May I, through good conduct, realize enlightenment And fulfill, without exception, All the specific prayers of enlightened conduct That are made by the jinas in the three times. {41}
The lofty vows of enlightenment practice Of the buddhas of past, present, and future May I fulfill completely, Practice what is good, and realize enlightenment.
rgyal ba kun gyi sras kyi thu bo pa/ / gang gi ming ni kun tu bzang zhes bya; ; mkhas pa de dang mtshungs par spyad pa'i phyir/ / dge ba 'di dag thams cad rab tu bsngo/ /
I dedicate all this virtue So that I may have the same conduct as that wise one, The eldest son of all the jinas, Whose name is Samantabhadra.[2228] {42}
All who share in the practice Of the sage of Universal Good, The foremost offspring of all buddhas, I name them good.
lus dang ngag dang yid kyang rnam dag cing / / spyod pa rnam dag zhing rnams yongs dag dang / / bsngo ba bzang po mkhas pa ci 'dra ba/ / de 'drar bdag kyang de dang mtshungs par shog /
Just as the good wise one made a dedication For a pure body, speech, and mind, A pure conduct, and a pure realm, May it be the same for me. {43}
Pure in body, speech, and mind, Pure in conduct, with a pure land, As the sage is named Good, May I become thus equally.
kun nas dge ba bzang po spyad pa'i phyir/ / 'jam dpal gyi ni smon lam spyad par bgyi/ / ma 'ongs bskal pa kun tu mi skyo bar/ / de yi bya ba ma lus rdzogs par bgyi/ /
May I practice the conduct of Mañjuśrī’s prayer For good conduct, for complete goodness, Without weariness throughout the kalpas to come. May I complete all those activities without exception. {44}
May I carry out the vow of Manjushri To totally purify the practice of good; Tireless through all future ages, May I fulfill all those tasks.
spyod pa dag ni tshad yod ma gyur cig / yon tan rnams kyang tshad gzung med par shog / spyod pa tshad med pa la gnas nas kyang / / de dag 'phrul pa thams cad 'tshal bar bgyi/ /
May there be no limits to practice, And no limit to virtues; Persisting in infinite practices, I know all their miraculous creations.
nam mkha'i mthar thug gyur pa ji tsam par/ / sems can ma lus mtha' yang de bzhin te; ; ji tsam las dang nyon mongs mthar gyur pa/ / bdag gi smon lam mtha' yang de tsam mo/ /
If there were an end to space, There would be an end to all beings. Only when their karma and kleśas end Will my prayers also come to an end. {46}
As long as the earth exists, As long as all beings exist, As long as acts and afflictions exist, So long will my vow remain.
gang yang phyogs bcu'i zhing rnams mtha' yas pa/ / rin chen brgyan te rgyal ba rnams la phul; ; lha dang mi yi bde ba mchog rnams kyang / / zhing gi rdul snyed bskal par phul ba bas/ /
If someone offered to the jinas the endless realms In the ten directions adorned with jewels And the most excellent pleasures of devas and humans For kalpas as numerous as the atoms in a realm, {47}
Let me give the buddhas all worlds In the ten directions adorned with jewels, Let me give celestials and humans supreme happiness For eons as many as atoms.
gang gis bsngo ba'i rgyal po 'di thos nas/ / byang chub mchog gi rjes su rab mos shing / / lan gcig tsam yang dad pa bskyed pa ni/ / bsod nams dam pa'i mchog tu 'di 'gyur ro/ /
Someone who has faith just once On hearing this king of dedications And aspires to attain perfect enlightenment Will have a higher, superior merit. {48}
Those who develop respect and devotion On hearing this supreme dedication, Seeking supreme enlightenment, Will be most blessed.
gang gis bzang spyod smon lam 'di btab pa/ / des ni ngan song thams cad spong bar 'gyur/ / des ni grogs po ngan pa'ang spangs pa yin/ / snang ba mtha' yas de yang des myur mthong / /
Whoever recites this prayer for good conduct Will be free from all[2229] lower existences, Will be free from bad companions, And will quickly see Amitābha. {49}
They will have abandoned all evils And all bad associates And will quickly see Infinite Light, If they have this vow of enlightening practice.
de dag rnyed pa rab rnyed bde bar 'tsho/ / mi tsho 'dir yang de dag legs par 'ongs; ; kun tu bzang po de yang ci 'dra bar/ / de dag ring por mi thogs de bzhin 'gyur/ /
They will have in this life the good fortune Of obtaining success, a happy life, And will soon become The same as Samantabhadra. {50}
Great is their gain, worthwhile their life, Auspicious their birth as humans; They will soon be like The universally Good enlightening being.
mtshams med lnga po dag gi sdig pa rnams/ / gang gis mi shes dbang gis byas pa dag / de yis bzang po'i spyod pa 'di brjod na/ / myur du ma lus yongs su byang bar 'gyur/ /

If someone through the power of ignorance Has the bad karma of the five actions with immediate results, They will be purified of it, without any remainder Through reciting this prayer for good conduct. {51}
Those who have committed hellish crimes Under the sway of ignorance Will quickly put an end to them all When this practice of good is expounded.
ye shes dang ni gzugs dang mtshan rnams dang / / rigs dang kha dog rnams dang ldan par 'gyur; ; bdud dang mu stegs mang pos de mi thub/ / 'jig rten gsum po kun na'ang mchod par 'gyur/ /
They will have the wisdom, form, Features, family, and color, Be invincible to hosts of māras and tīrthikas, And be offered to by the entire three realms. {52}
Endowed with knowledge, distinction, and nobility, Invulnerable to false teachers and demons, They will be honored By all in the triple world.
byang chub shing dbang drung du de myur 'gro / song nas sems can phan phyir de 'dug ste; ; byang chub sangs rgyas 'khor lo rab tu bskor/ / bdud rnams sde dang bcas pa thams cad btul/ /

They will soon go to the Bodhi tree, the lord of trees, And having reached there be seated for the benefit of beings, Become enlightened in buddhahood, turn the wheel of the Dharma, And overpower Māra and his entire army. {53}

They will quickly go to the Tree of enlightenment And sit there for the benefit Of all living beings; They will realize enlightenment, Turn the wheel of teaching, And conquer the devil And all its cohorts.
gang yang bzang po spyod pa'i smon lam 'di/ / 'chang ba dang ni ston tam klog na yang / / de yi rnam par smin pa sangs rgyas mkhyen/ / byang chub mchog la som nyi ma byed cig /
The Buddha knows the result that ripens For the one who possesses, recites, Or teaches this prayer for good conduct. Do not doubt the supreme enlightenment! {57}
Buddha knows those who hold this vow to practice good, Who cause it to be told of and taught; The fruit of this is supreme enlightenment— Do not entertain any doubt.
'jam dpal ji ltar mkhyen cing dpa' ba dang / / kun tu bzang po de yang de bzhin te/ / de dag gi ni rjes su bdag slob cing / / dge ba 'di dag thams cad rab tu bsngo/ /
Just as the hero Mañjuśrī knows, In that way[2230] so does Samantabhadra.[2231] In practicing in the same way as they do, I am dedicating all this merit. {55}
As the hero Manjushri knows, so too does Universal Good; As I learn from them I dedicate all this virtue.
dus gsum gshegs pa'i rgyal ba thams cad kyis/ / bsngo ba gang la mchog tu bsngags pa des/ / bdag gi dge ba'i rtsa ba 'di kun kyang / / bzang po spyod phyir rab tu bsngo bar bgyi/ /
With the prayer that is praised as supreme By all the jinas in the three times, I am dedicating all this merit For the supreme good conduct. {56}
By the supreme dedication praised by the buddhas of all times I dedicate all this virtue to the practice of highest good.
bdag ni 'chi ba'i dus byed gyur pa na/ / sgrib pa thams cad bdag ni phyir bsal te/ / mngon sum snang ba mtha' yas de mthong nas/ / bde ba can gyi zhing der rab tu 'gro /
When the time has come for me to die, May I dispel all obscurations, See Amitābha before me, And go to the Sukhāvatī realm. {57}
Acting in accord with the time, may I remove all obstructions, May I see Infinite Light face to face and go to the land of bliss.
der song nas ni smon lam 'di dag kyang / / thams cad ma lus mngon du gyur par shog / de dag ma lus bdag gis yongs su bkang / / 'jig rten ji srid sems can phan par bgyi/ /
When I have gone there, may these prayers All become completely manifest. May I fulfill them all without exception And benefit beings for as long as there are worlds. {58}
There, may all these vows be complete; Having fulfilled them, I will work for the weal of all beings in the world.
rgyal ba'i dkyil 'khor bzang zhing dga' ba der/ / pad+mo dam pa shin tu mdzes las skyes/ / snang ba mtha' yas rgyal bas mngon sum du/ / lung bstan pa yang bdag gis der thob shog /
May I be born from a beautiful, perfect lotus In that pleasant, beautiful circle of the jinas, And there obtain my prophecy Directly from the Jina Amitābha. {59}
Let me abide in the circle of that buddha, born in a beautiful lotus, And receive the prophecy of buddhahood there in the presence Of the buddha of Infinite Light.
der ni bdag gis lung bstan rab thob nas/ / sprul pa mang po bye ba phrag brgya yis/ / blo yi stobs kyis phyogs bcu rnams su yang / / sems can rnams la phan pa mang po bgyi/ /
Having obtained there the prophecy, May I through the power of mind Bring many benefits to beings in the ten directions Through many billions of emanations. {60}
Having received the prophecy there, with millions of emanations I will work for the weal of beings everywhere, by the power of Buddha.
gang gis bzang po spyod pa ston pa yis/ / dge ba cung zad bdag gis ci bsags pa/ / des ni 'gro ba'i smon lam dge ba rnams; ; skad cig gcig gis thams cad 'byor par shog /
May what little merit I have accumulated Through reciting the good conduct prayer Cause the virtuous prayers of beings All to be fulfilled in an instant. {61}
By whatever virtue I accumulate, having invoked the vow to practice good, May the pure aspiration of the world be at once all fulfilled.
gang yang bzang po spyod pa bsngos pa yis/ / bsod nams mtha' yas dam pa thob pa des/ / 'gro ba sdug bsngal chu bor bying ba rnams/ / 'od dpag med pa'i gnas rab 'gro bar shog /
Through the sublime, endless merit attained By my dedicating the good conduct, May the beings drowning in a river of suffering Depart to the supreme residence of Amitābha. {62}
By the endless surpassing blessing realized from dedication To the practice of good, May worldlings submerged in the torrent of passion Go to the higher realm of Infinite Light.

The Buddha said, “Sudhana, those enlightening beings led by Manjushri, the monks developed by Manjushri, Maitreya, and all the enlightening beings of the age of virtue, the great enlightening beings gathered in various worlds, as numerous as atoms, led by Universally Good, appointed inheritors of spiritual sovereignty, the great disciples led by Shariputra and Maudgalyayana and their circle, as well as celestial and human beings, were elated and they applauded what the blessed enlightening being Universally Good had said.”
shin tu rgyas pa chen po'i mdo/ sangs rgyas phal po che zhes bya ba las/ byang chub sems dpa'i sde snod kyi nang nas sdong pos brgyan pa zhes bya ba

The compilation of Sudhana’s conduct of honoring kalyāṇamitras from the great Dharma teaching entitled “Stem Array” from within the “Bodhisattvapiṭaka,” “The Mahāvaipulya Sūtra Entitled ‘A Multitude of Buddhas,’ ” is concluded.
chos kyi rnam grangs chen po las nor bzang gis dge ba'i bshes gnyen bsnyen bkur ba'i spyod pa phyogs gcig pa ste/ ji snyed pa rdzogs so;; //
This concludes the episodes of Sudhana’s conduct of honoring kalyāṇamitras from the great Dharma teaching, “The Stem Array.”
['gyur byang]
Colophon
lots+tsha ba bai ro tsan rak+Shi tas zhu chen bgyis te gtan la phab pa'o// //
It was translated and revised by the chief editor Lotsawa Vairocana­rakṣita.
[sde dge]
sde dge
rgya gar gyi mkhan po dzi na mi tra dang / su ren+d+ra bo d+hi dang / zhus chen gyi lo tsA ba ban+de ye shes sde/ la sogs pas bsgyur cing zhus te gtan la phab pa'o// //
This was translated and revised by the Indian upādhyāyas Jinamitra and Surendrabodhi and by the chief editor Lotsawa Bandé Yeshé Dé and others.[2232]
[mjug byang]
Tibetan Editor’s Colophon (Tashi Wangchuk)

de ltar bde bar gshegs pa'i bka' 'khor lo rim pa gsum las/ 'dir tha ma don dam rnam par nges pa'i 'khor lo'i snying po phul du byung ba sangs rgyas phal po che mtshan gyi rnam grangs shin tu rgyas pa chen po'i sde snod/ snyan gyi gong rgyan/ pad+ma'i rgyan sogs du ma dang ldan pa la/

A Multitude of Buddhas is the marvelous essence of the final, ultimate, definitive wheel from among the three wheels of the Sugata’s teaching. It has many other titles, such as The Mahāvaipulya Basket, The Earring, The Lotus Adornment, and so on.

de bzhin gshegs pa phal po che'i le'u/ rdo rje rgyal mtshan gyi bsngo ba/ sa bcu bstan pa/ kun tu bzang po'i spyod pa bstan pa/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i skye ba dang 'byung ba bstan pa/ 'jig rten las 'das pa'i le'u/ sdong pos brgyan pa'i le'u ste bdun la so so'i nang gses kyi dbye bas le'u bzhi bcu rtsa lnga/

It has seven sections:[2233] A Multitude of Tathāgatas,[2234] The Vajra Banner Dedication,[2235] The Teaching of the Ten Bhūmis,[2236] The Teaching of Completely Good Conduct,[2237] The Teaching of the Birth and Appearance of the Tathāgatas,[2238] The Transcendence of the World,[2239] and Stem Array.[2240] These are subdivided into forty-five chapters.

sh+lo lo ka sum khri/ dgu stong sum cu/ bam po brgya sum cu dang shO lo ka sum cu yod par bu ston rin po che sogs bzhed cing / tshal pa bka' 'gyur gyi dkar chag tu bam po brgya dang bco lnga/ ldan dkar mar bam po brgya dang nyi shu rtsa bdun du mdzad/ deng sang gi dpe rnams la'ang bam grangs mang nyung ci rigs yod par snang /

According to Butön Rinpoché and others, it contains thirty-nine thousand and thirty verses, a hundred and thirty fascicles, and an additional thirty verses. In the Tshalpa Kangyur edition there are a hundred and fifteen fascicles, the Denkarma edition has a hundred and twenty-seven fascicles,[2241] and present-day editions have various numbers of fascicles.[2242]

'di thog mar 'phags pa klu sgrub la/ paN+Di ta byang chub bzang po dang paN+Di ta dga' ba gnyis kyis zhus/ de gnyis kas rgya nag tu 'gyur mdzad/ rgya nag gi 'gyur la/ su ren+t+ra bo d+hi dang / be+e ro tsa na rak+Shi tas zhus chen mdzad par bshad cing /

This sūtra was first received from Ārya Nāgārjuna by Paṇḍita Buddhabhadra and Paṇḍita Śikṣānanda (652–710), and they both translated it into Chinese. It is taught that Surendrabodhi and Vairocanarakṣita became principal editors for a Chinese translation.

lung gi brgyud rim la'ang rgya nag nas 'gyur ba'i brgyud pa ni/ rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas/ 'phags pa 'jam dpal/ mgon po klu sgrub/ gong gi paN+Di ta gnyis/ de nas hwa shang thu thu zhun sogs rim par brgyud de/ hwa shang gying ju la dbus pa sangs rgyas 'bum gyis gsan/ de nas lo tsA ba mchog ldan nas deng sang gi bar du brgyud pa dang /

As for the lineage of the text, there is the lineage from China: The perfect Buddha, Ārya Mañjuśrī, Lord Nāgārjuna, the two paṇḍitas mentioned above, and Heshang Tushun. Then the lineage continued through others until Üpa Sangyé Bum received it from Heshang Gying-ju. Then that lineage was passed on through Lotsawa Chokden and has continued up to the present time.

rgya gar nas 'gyur ba'i brgyud pa ni/ klu sgrub nas/ aR+Ya de wa/ 'jam dpal grags pa sogs nas rim bzhin/ rdo rje gdan ba ri lo tsA bas gsan/ de nas mchims brtson seng / rje btsun sa skya pa chen po sogs brgyud par bshad do/ /

The lineage from India is as follows: It was passed from Nāgārjuna to Āryadeva, and then Mañjuśrīkīrti, and so on, until Bari Lotsawa received it from Vajrāsana. It is taught that the lineage then continued through Chim Tsöndrü Sengé, the great Sakya Lord,[2243] and so on.
'on kyang gong gi 'gyur byang 'di las lo paN gzhan gyis bsgyur tshul lo rgyus dang / dpe rnams la ma mthong ngo / /
However, I have not seen any other text or history of a translation made by any other lotsawa or paṇḍita other than those listed in the colophon to this translation into Tibetan.

'di nyid tshal ba bka' 'gyur gyi ma phyi byas nas 'jang sa tham rgyal pos bka' 'gyur ro cog par du bsgrubs pa deng sang li thang mchal bar du grags pa khungs thub kyi tshad mar bzung nas ma phyi byas pa yin kyang / skabs 'dir chad lhag dang brda ma dag pa mang ba 'dug pas/ slar yig rnying dag pa mang du btsal nas zhu dag bgyis pa yin la/

The king of Jangsa Tham[2244] had a complete Kangyur made that was based on the Tshalpa Kangyur. At the present time this is known as the Lithang Tshalpa Kangyur (1609–14). I considered this to be a reliable source and so have made it the basis for this edition. However, it has many omissions, accretions, and misspellings, and therefore I have at this time corrected it by seeking out many older editions.
de'ang rgya dpe mi gcig pa dang / 'gyur mi mthun pa ni don gyi khog gcig kyang tshig la zhu dag mi btub na'ang / 'di'i dpe phal cher zhu dag pher ba kho na 'dug la

There are variant Indian texts and conflicting translations, and I have not been able to ascertain from them a definitive single meaning or correct words. Nevertheless, this text is nothing but a valid edition.

'on kyang rgyan la bkod pa dang / 'byam klas la rab 'byams dang / so so yang dag par rig pa la/ tha dad pa yang dag par shes pa dang / thugs la dgongs pa dang / nyin mtshan dang zla ba yar kham mar kham dang zhes pa la/ nyin mtshan dang yud du yan man dang zhes dang / tha snyad la rnam par dpyod pa zhes pa rnams 'gyur khyad lta bur 'dug pa don la mi 'gal bas rang sor bzhag /

There are varying translations of terms that have been left unrevised, as there is no contradiction in meaning. For example, it has rgyan instead of bkod pa;[2245] ’byam klas instead of rab ’byams;[2246] so so yang dag par rig pa instead of tha dad pa yang dag par shes pa;[2247] thugs for dgongs pa;[2248] nyin mtshan dang zla ba yar kham mar kham dang instead of nyin mtshan dang yud du yan man dang;[2249] and tha snyad instead of rnam par dpyod pa.[2250]

rgya skad la rang bzhin rkyen/ rnam 'gyur gyi tshul du ma yod pa/ bod la lo paN chos kyi spyan ldan rnams kyis don 'gyur mdzad pa 'ga' zhig / dus dang rnam dbye sogs shin tu rtogs dka' bas dpe mthun shas che ba gtso bor bzung / gzhan dogs gnas cung zad yod pa rnams/ bod kyi brda'i bstan bcos rnams dang go bstun/

Sanskrit words have many cases and tenses, so that although the Tibetan lotsawas and paṇḍitas, who had the eyes of the Dharma, translated their meaning, their tenses, cases, and so on are difficult to discern. Those are the majority of the examples of uncertainty, and there are also a few other kinds, but they are nevertheless in accord with Tibetan grammar.

dpe phal cher la brda rnying shas che ba dang / 'gyur bcos mdzad pa'i gsal kha mi snang bas/ bod kyi brda rnying pa sha stag zhig byung na 'brel chags pa 'dra yang phyis su brda gsar rnying 'dres nyams che ba dang / shad bar gcod mtshams 'khrugs pa mang du snang yang cung zad skyon chung ba'i dbang du byas nas btang snyoms su bzhag / de min mon pa'i rdo gcod zhu dag gi dpe zlar ma song bar nan tan chen pos shin tu dag khul du bgyis pa

In most texts there are many archaic words, so that the meaning of the translation is not clear, but there is a consistency when those words are all in archaic Tibetan. However, there appears to have occurred in later times a strong adulteration of the text so that there is a mixture of archaic and modern forms. There are also unreliable placements of the shad mark that differentiates clauses, but all these have been left as they are because these faults are few and minor. Therefore, this revision has been diligently edited without becoming analogous to knocking down the ancient megaliths of the southern regions.
'di/ sangs rgyas kyi bstan pa rin po che dang ris med pa'i 'gro ba yongs kyi bsod nams kyi dpal du bskal ba ji srid gnas kyi bar du khor yug ri bo'i khongs 'dir/ nyi zla ltar gsal bar gyur cig / ces

May this remain for the entire kalpa within the circle of the Cakravāla Mountains, as bright as the sun and moon, as the glory of the merit of nonsectarian beings and the precious teaching of the Buddha.

bod chen po'i yul ljongs sde bzhi'i 'byung gnas dge bcu'i khrims lugs kyis mngon par mtho ba'i nor 'dzin yangs pa chos bzhin du skyong ba'i lha chos rgyal byang chub sems dpa'i mi'i dbang po bstan pa tshe rings kyi zhal snga nas/ dge byed ces pa chu stag lor gsung rab 'di nyid par du bsgrub par

This was printed in the water tiger year called dge byed (1722),[2251] in the presence of Tenpa Tsering (1678–1738), the divine Dharma king who rules in accordance with the Dharma, who has the vast, superior wealth of the ten good actions, and who is a bodhisattva as a ruler of humans and the source of happiness in the four regions of greater Tibet.
mdzad pa'i skabs zhu dag las 'phros te 'di nyid kyi do dam par bkas gnang ba'i zhabs 'bring ba dge slong bkra shis dbang phyug gis gleng ba dza yan+tu// //
This was written by the attendant Gelong Tashi Wangchuk, who in the process of revision was commanded to become its supervisor.
yed+har+m+mA he tu prab+ha wA he tun+te ShAn+ta thA ga to h+ya wad ta/ / he ShAny+tsa lo ni ro d+ha e waM bA dI ma hA shra ma NaH//

Ye dharmahetuprabhavā hetun teṣān tathāgato hy avadat. Teṣāñ ca yo nirodha evaṃ vādī mahāśramanaḥ. (The Tathāgata has taught those causes that are the causes for the arising of phenomena, and the great Śramaṇa, in that way, taught that which is their cessation.)
